english_verse: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
translation_verse: Mɔlebɛbo ne Nyamenle bɔle anwuma nee aze.

english_verse: The earth was barren, with no form of life; it was under a roaring ocean covered with darkness. But the Spirit of God was moving over the water. The First Day
translation_verse: Ɛnee azɛlɛ ye ɛnzɔho ɛhwee, yɛɛ debie biala ɛnle zolɛ; awozinli ɛheda buma ne anye, na Nyamenle Sunsum ne luolua nzule ne anye.

english_verse: God said, “I command light to shine!” And light started shining.
translation_verse: Na Nyamenle zele kɛ, “Wienyi ɛrɛla”; na wienyi rale.

english_verse: God looked at the light and saw that it was good. He separated light from darkness
translation_verse: Nyamenle nwunle kɛ wienyi ne le kpalɛ, na ɔdele wienyi ne ɔvile awozinli ne anwo.

english_verse: and named the light “Day” and the darkness “Night.” Evening came, then morning—that was the first day. The Second Day
translation_verse: Nyamenle vɛlɛle wienyi ne “Alehyenlɛ” yɛɛ ɔvɛlɛle awozinli ne “Aledwolɛ”. Akee aleɛ dwole na aleɛ hyenle. Ɛhye a le kenle ne mɔɔ lumua la.

english_verse: God said, “I command a dome to separate the water above it from the water below it.”
translation_verse: Na Nyamenle zele kɛ, “Anwomanyunlu ɛrɛla ɛrade nzule ne mɔ avinli.”

english_verse: and named it “Sky.” Evening came, then morning—that was the second day. The Third Day
translation_verse: Na ɔvɛlɛle anwomanyunlu “Anwuma.” Aleɛ dwole na aleɛ hyenle; kenle ne mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nwiɔ la ɛne.

english_verse: God said, “I command the water under the sky to come together in one place, so there will be dry ground.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Na Nyamenle zele kɛ, “Nzule mɔɔ wɔ ewiade la ɛhɔ ɛleka ko ɛye ɛleka resee ɛdo ɛkɛ.” Na ɔyɛle zɔhane.

english_verse: God named the dry ground “Land,” and he named the water “Ocean.” God looked at what he had done and saw that it was good.
translation_verse: Nyamenle vɛlɛle ɛleka resee ne “Azɛlɛ”, yɛɛ ɔvɛlɛle nzule ne mɔ mɔɔ hɔle ɛleka ko la “Nyevile”. Na Nyamenle nwunle kɛ ɔle kpalɛ.

english_verse: God said, “I command the earth to produce all kinds of plants, including fruit trees and grain.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Na Nyamenle zele kɛ, “Ɛbɔ ɛrɛla azɛlɛ ye azo; ndile nee mbaka mɔɔ so ma, yɛɛ nzoleɛ mbaka mɔɔ ma wɔ bɛ nzoleɛ ne mɔ anu la, ko biala nee ye ɛsaso ɛrɛla.” Na ɔyɛle zɔhane.

english_verse: The earth produced all kinds of vegetation. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Ndile nee mbaka ngakyile kɔsɔɔti mɔɔ so ma, yɛɛ nzoleɛ mbaka mɔɔ ma wɔ bɛ nzoleɛ ne mɔ anu la, ko biala nee ye ɛsaso, fifile azɛlɛ ye azo. Na Nyamenle nwunle kɛ ɔle kpalɛ.

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the third day. The Fourth Day
translation_verse: Aleɛ dwole na aleɛ hyenle; kenle ne mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nsa la ɛne.

english_verse: God said, “I command lights to appear in the sky and to separate day from night and to show the time for seasons, special days, and years.
translation_verse: Na Nyamenle zele kɛ, “Ahɛnlaneɛ ɛrɛla anwomanyunlu anwuma lɔ, ɛrade alehyenlɛ nee aledwolɛ avinli, na bɛyɛ sɛkɛlɛneɛ mɔɔ kile ɛlobɔ, kenle, nee ɛvolɛ a,

english_verse: I command them to shine on the earth.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: na bɛda anwomanyunlu anwuma lɔ bɛmaa wienyi ɛrɛla azɛlɛ ye azo.” Na ɔyɛle zɔhane.

english_verse: God made two powerful lights, the brighter one to rule the day and the other to rule the night. He also made the stars.
translation_verse: Na Nyamenle yɛle anwuma ahɛnlaneɛ mgbole nwiɔ ne, ɔyɛle kpole kpalɛ ne, sɛnzɛne ne, kɛ ɔda alehyenlɛ nu; akee ɔyɛle kpole ekyi ne, siane ne, kɛ ɔda aledwolɛ nu. Ɔyɛle nwɔlɔra noko.

english_verse: Then God put these lights in the sky to shine on the earth,
translation_verse: Ɔyɛle ɛhye mɔ ɔzieziele anwomanyunlu anwuma lɔ kɛ bɛda bɛmaa wienyi ɛrɛla azɛlɛ ye azo.

english_verse: to rule day and night, and to separate light from darkness. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Ɔyɛle kɛ bɛda alehyenlɛ nee aledwolɛ nu, amaa bɛade wienyi ne bɛavi awozinli ne anwo. Na Nyamenle nwunle mɔɔ yeyɛ la kɛ ɔle kpalɛ.

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the fourth day. The Fifth Day
translation_verse: Aleɛ dwole na aleɛ hyenle; kenle ne mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nna la ɛne.

english_verse: God said, “I command the ocean to be full of living creatures, and I command birds to fly above the earth.”
translation_verse: Na Nyamenle zele kɛ, “Nzule nu anyewɔzo abɔdeɛ ngakyile muala ɛrɛla, na nloma mɔɔ tu dua anwomanyunlu la ɛrɛla.”

english_verse: So God made the giant sea monsters and all the living creatures that swim in the ocean. He also made every kind of bird. God looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Nyamenle bɔle nyevile nu abɔdeɛ mgbole anwo ɛzulolɛ muala nee nzule nu anyewɔzo abɔdeɛ biala nee bɛ ɛsaso, nee nloma kɔsɔɔti nee bɛ ɛsaso. Na Nyamenle nwunle kɛ ɔle kpalɛ.

english_verse: Then he gave the living creatures his blessing—he told the ocean creatures to increase and live everywhere in the ocean and the birds to increase everywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Nyamenle yilale bɛ muala na ɔzele kɛ, “Bɛlɔ, bɛyɛ dɔɔnwo bɛyi azule nee nyevile,” na ɔzele nloma noko kɛ, “Bɛdabɛ bɛda, bɛyɛ mɔnwo mɔnwo wɔ azɛlɛ ye azo.”

english_verse: Evening came, then morning—that was the fifth day. The Sixth Day
translation_verse: Aleɛ dwole na aleɛ hyenle; kenle ne mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nnu la ɛne.

english_verse: God said, “I command the earth to give life to all kinds of tame animals, wild animals, and reptiles.” And that's what happened.
translation_verse: Akee Nyamenle zele kɛ, “Anyewɔzo abɔdeɛ ɛrɛla azɛlɛ ye azo, biala nee ye ɛsaso: nlankɛ nee ninyɛne mɔɔ twenle bɛ nwo aze la amuala nee nanemgbole, ko biala nee ye ɛsaso.” Na ɔyɛle zɔhane.

english_verse: God made every one of them. Then he looked at what he had done, and it was good.
translation_verse: Na Nyamenle bɔle azɛlɛ ye azo nanemgbole, ko biala nee ye ɛsaso: nlankɛ nee ninyɛne mɔɔ twenle bɛ nwo aze la amuala, ko biala nee ye ɛsaso. Na Nyamenle nwunle kɛ ɔle kpalɛ.

english_verse: God said, “Now we will make humans, and they will be like us. We will let them rule the fish, the birds, and all other living creatures.”
translation_verse: Akee Nyamenle zele kɛ, “Bɛmaa yɛyɛ sonla kɛ yɛdayɛ yɛ ɛsaso yɛmaa ɔzɔho yɛ, na yɛmaa bɛnlea azule nee nyevile nu fɛlɛ, nloma mɔɔ wɔ anwomanyunlu, nyɛmoa nee nanemgbole nee debie biala mɔɔ twenle ɔ nwo aze wɔ azɛlɛ ye azo la anwo zo.”

english_verse: So God created humans to be like himself; he made men and women.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Nyamenle bɔle sonla kɛ ɔdaye ye ɛsaso la; ɔdaye Nyamenle mumua ne ye ɛsaso a ɔnleanle ɔbɔle sonla a. Ɔbɔle bɛ nrenya nee raalɛ.

english_verse: God gave them his blessing and said: Have a lot of children! Fill the earth with people and bring it under your control. Rule over the fish in the ocean, the birds in the sky, and every animal on the earth.
translation_verse: Na Nyamenle yilale bɛ, na ɔzele kɛ, “Bɛlɔ, bɛyɛ mɔnwo mɔnwo, bɛyi azɛlɛ ye na bɛzie azɛlɛ ye. Eza bɛzie azule nee nyevile nu fɛlɛ, anwomanyunlu nloma nee azɛlɛ ye azo abɔdeɛ biala mɔɔ die ɛnwomenle la.”

english_verse: And I have given the green plants as food for everything else that breathes, including animals, both wild and tame, and birds. And so it was.
translation_verse: Meva ndile muala noko memaa debie biala mɔɔ lɛ ngoane wɔ ye nuhua: azɛlɛ ye azo nane kɔsɔɔti nee anwomanyunlu nloma nee ninyɛne mɔɔ twenle bɛ nwo aze la amuala kɛ bɛli.” Na ɔyɛle zɔhane.

english_verse: God looked at what he had done. All of it was very good! Evening came, then morning—that was the sixth day.
translation_verse: Na Nyamenle nwunle kɛ debie biala mɔɔ yeyɛ la le kpalɛ kpole. Aleɛ dwole na aleɛ hyenle; kenle ne mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nsia la ɛne.

english_verse: So the heavens and the earth and everything else were created. The Seventh Day
translation_verse: Ɛnee kɛ Nyamenle zile bɔle anwuma nee aze, nee ninyɛne mɔɔ wɔ nu la amuala la ɛne.

english_verse: That's how God created the heavens and the earth. The Garden of Eden When the Lord God made the heavens and the earth,
translation_verse: Ɛnee kɛ Nyamenle zile bɔle anwuma nee aze la ɛne. Yidɛn tola ne Mekɛ mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle bɔle anwuma nee azɛlɛ ye la,

english_verse: no grass or plants were growing anywhere. God had not yet sent any rain, and there was no one to work the land.
translation_verse: ɛnee baka biala ɛngyi azɛlɛ ye azo, yɛɛ ndile biala ɛtɛfifile, ɔluakɛ ɛnee Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle ɛtɛmanle ezule ɛtɛtɔle azɛlɛ ye azo, yɛɛ ɛnee sonla ɛnle zolɛ na yeazo zolɛ ɛya.

english_verse: But streams came up from the ground and watered the earth.
translation_verse: Noko ɛnee nzule vi azɛlɛ bo finde bu azɛlɛ ne azo amuala tɛloo.

english_verse: The Lord God took some soil from the ground and made a man. God breathed life into the man, and the man started breathing.
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle vale ndɛtɛlɛ nwonle sonla na ɔliele ngoane ɛnwomenle ɔguale ɔ bonyi nu, na sonla nyianle ngoane.

english_verse: The Lord made a garden in a place called Eden, which was in the east, and he put the man there.
translation_verse: Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle hyele tola wɔ Yidɛn, wɔ aduduleɛ nehane, na ɔmanle sonla ne mɔɔ yebɔ la dɛnlanle ɛkɛ.

english_verse: The Lord God filled the garden with all kinds of beautiful trees and fruit trees. Two other trees were in the middle of the garden. One of these gave life—the other gave the wisdom to know the difference between right and wrong.
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle manle mbaka kɔsɔɔti mɔɔ le ngɛnlɛma nee mɔɔ bɛdi a ɔyɛ boɛ la fifile; ɔmanle ngoane baka ne yɛɛ baka ne mɔɔ maa ɛkola ɛnwu kpalɛ nee ɛtane la ɔdaye bɛfifile tola ne anu.

english_verse: From Eden a river flowed out to water the garden, then it divided into four rivers.
translation_verse: Azule la Yidɛn na ɔse ɔdoɔloa tola ne anu. Azule ne dwu tola ne anu a, ɔkpakye nna.

english_verse: The first one is the Pishon River that flows through the land of Havilah,
translation_verse: Bɛfɛlɛ azule ne asa ɛhane ne mɔɔ lumua la Paehyɔn; ɔse ɔdua Havelaa azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ ezukoa nvutuke wɔ zolɛ la azo.

english_verse: The second is the Gihon River that winds through Ethiopia.
translation_verse: Azule ne asa ɛhane ne mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nwiɔ la, bɛfɛlɛ ye Gaehyɔn; ɔse ɔdua Kɛhye azɛlɛ ne azo.

english_verse: The Tigris River that flows east of Assyria is the third, and the fourth is the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nsa la, bɛfɛlɛ ye Taegelese; ɔse ɔdua Aselea maanle ne aduduleɛ, yɛɛ mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nna la, bɛfɛlɛ ye Yufileti.

english_verse: The Lord God put the man in the Garden of Eden to take care of it and to look after it.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle manle sonla hɔdɛnlanle Yidɛn tola ne anu kɛ ɔyɛ nu egyinli na ɔziezie ɛkɛ.

english_verse: But the Lord told him, “You may eat fruit from any tree in the garden,
translation_verse: Ɔzele ye kɛ, “Ɛkola ɛdi bakama biala mɔɔ wɔ tola ye anu la bie,

english_verse: except the one that has the power to let you know the difference between right and wrong. If you eat any fruit from that tree, you will die before the day is over!”
translation_verse: na kpalɛ nee ɛtane ɛnwunlɛ baka ne, yemɔ mmadi ye ma ne bie, ɔluakɛ kenle ko ne mɔɔ ɛkɛli bie la, ɛbawu.”

english_verse: The Lord God said, “It isn't good for the man to live alone. I will make a suitable partner for him.”
translation_verse: Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle zele kɛ, “Ɔnle kpalɛ kɛ menwɔmaa sonla angomekye kɛdɛnla; mebabɔ ye ɛsaso boavolɛ meamaa ye.”

english_verse: So the Lord took some soil and made animals and birds. He brought them to the man to see what names he would give each of them. Then the man named the tame animals and the birds and the wild animals. That's how they got their names. None of these was the right kind of partner for the man.
translation_verse: Sonla totonle nyɛmoa ne mɔ aluma ngoko ngoko, ɔtotonle nloma mɔɔ tu dua anwomanyunlu la aluma yɛɛ ɔtotonle nanemgbole mɔɔ wɔ ɛbɔ nu la aluma. Na ɔdaye sonla ɛdeɛ, yeannyia ye ɛsaso boavolɛ biala.

english_verse: So the Lord God made him fall into a deep sleep, and he took out one of the man's ribs. Then after closing the man's side,
translation_verse: Yemɔti Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle manle sonla lafele kpole bie na ɔyele ɔ nvenle foa bowule ko na ɔvale nwonane ɔduale ɔ bo zo ne.

english_verse: the Lord made a woman out of the rib. The Lord God brought her to the man,
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle vale bowule ne mɔɔ ɔyele la ɔyɛle sonla raalɛ na ɔvale ye ɔrɛlɛle nrenya ne.

english_verse: and the man exclaimed, “Here is someone like me! She is part of my body, my own flesh and bones. She came from me, a man. So I will name her Woman!”
translation_verse: Na nrenya ne zele kɛ, Ɛhye le me mbowule nu bowule, ɔle me nwonane nu nwonane; bɛbavɛlɛ ye “Raalɛ”, ɔboalekɛ ɔvi sonla nrenya nu a ɔrale a.

english_verse: That's why a man will leave his own father and mother. He marries a woman, and the two of them become like one person.
translation_verse: Yemɔti a nrenya fi ɔ ze nee ɔ nli anwo na ɔfa ɔ nwo ɔbɔ ɔ ye anwo kyengye, na bɛ mu nwiɔ bɛbɔ nu bɛyɛ nwonane ko a.

english_verse: Although the man and his wife were both naked, they were not ashamed.
translation_verse: Ɛnee nrenya ne nee ɔ ye ne lɛ bɛ nwo zɔ, noko bɛnze nwolɛ nyiane.

english_verse: The snake was sneakier than any of the other wild animals that the Lord God had made. One day it came to the woman and asked, “Did God tell you not to eat fruit from any tree in the garden?”
translation_verse: Ɛwɔlɛ le mɛlɛbɛla tɛla ɛbɔ nu nane biala mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle bɔle la. Ɔbizale raalɛ ne kɛ, “Yemɔti Nyamenle ɛze bɛ kɛ, ‘Bɛmmadi mbakama mɔɔ wɔ tola ye anu la biala bie’ ɔ?”

english_verse: The woman answered, “God said we could eat fruit from any tree in the garden,
translation_verse: Raalɛ ne buale ɛwɔlɛ ne kɛ, “Yɛkola yɛdi mbakama mɔɔ wɔ tola ye anu la biala bie;

english_verse: except the one in the middle. He told us not to eat fruit from that tree or even to touch it. If we do, we will die.”
translation_verse: na Nyamenle zele yɛ kɛ, ‘Bɛmmadi baka ne mɔɔ gyi tola ne avinli lɔ la ma ne bie, eza bɛmmafa bɛ sa bɛka ye anrɛɛ bɛkɛwu.’ ”

english_verse: “No, you won't!” the snake replied.
translation_verse: Ɛwɔlɛ ne hanle hilele raalɛ ne kɛ, “Bɛnrɛwu.

english_verse: “God understands what will happen on the day you eat fruit from that tree. You will see what you have done, and you will know the difference between right and wrong, just as God does.”
translation_verse: Nyamenle ze kɛ saa bɛdi baka ne ma ne bie a bɛ nye babuke na bɛayɛ kɛ ɔdaye Nyamenle la, na bɛanwu mɔɔ le kpalɛ, bɛannwu mɔɔ le ɛtane la.”

english_verse: The woman stared at the fruit. It looked beautiful and tasty. She wanted the wisdom that it would give her, and she ate some of the fruit. Her husband was there with her, so she gave some to him, and he ate it too.
translation_verse: Yemɔti mɔɔ raalɛ ne nwunle kɛ baka ne ma ne le kɛnlɛma, na bɛdi a ɔle kpalɛ, na ɔwɔ kɛ sonla di bie na ɔnwu nrɛlɛbɛ la, ɔdele bie ɔlile, na ɔdele bie ɔhɔmanle ɔ hu lile.

english_verse: At once they saw what they had done, and they realized they were naked. Then they sewed fig leaves together to cover themselves.
translation_verse: Ɛkɛ ne ala bɛ mu nwiɔ bɛ nye dele na bɛnwunle kɛ bɛlɛ bɛ nwo zɔ; bɛkpomgbale feege nya bɛwowale bɛ nwo.

english_verse: Late in the afternoon, when the breeze began to blow, the man and woman heard the Lord God walking in the garden. So they hid behind some trees. Sin Brings a Curse
translation_verse: Nzinlii mɔɔ aleɛ ne bɔle ɔ nloa aze la, bɛdele Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle agyakɛ abo kɛ ɔlɛkpɔsa tola ne anu, na bɛnriandile bɛhɔveale tola ne anu mbaka ne mɔ anu, amaa yeannwu bɛ.

english_verse: The Lord God called out to the man and asked, “Where are you?”
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle vɛlɛle nrenya ne na ɔbizale ye kɛ, “Ɛwɔ nienwu?”

english_verse: The man answered, “I was naked, and when I heard you walking through the garden, I was frightened and hid!”
translation_verse: Nrenya ne buale kɛ, “Mendele ɛ gyakɛ abo wɔ tola ne anu, na ɛnee mesulo, ɔboalekɛ melɛ me nwo zɔ, yɛɛ menveale a.”

english_verse: “How did you know you were naked?” God asked. “Did you eat any fruit from that tree in the middle of the garden?”
translation_verse: Nyamenle bizale ye kɛ, “Nwane a hanle hilele wɔ kɛ ɛlɛ ɛ nwo zɔ a? Ɛnee wɔli bakama ne mɔɔ menduale wɔ kɛ ɛmmadi bie la bie ɔ?”

english_verse: “It was the woman you put here with me,” the man said. “She gave me some of the fruit, and I ate it.”
translation_verse: Nrenya ne buale kɛ, “Raalɛ ne mɔɔ ɛvale ye ɛmanle me la, yemɔ a vale manle me a, yɛɛ menlile a.”

english_verse: The Lord God then asked the woman, “What have you done?” “The snake tricked me,” she answered, “and I ate some of that fruit.”
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle bizale raalɛ ne kɛ, “Duzu debie a wɔyɛ la?” Raalɛ ne buale kɛ, “Ɛwɔlɛ ne bɛlɛbɛlale me, lile me adwenle yɛɛ menlile bie a.” Nyamenle bua ndɛne

english_verse: So the Lord God said to the snake: “Because of what you have done, you will be the only animal to suffer this curse— For as long as you live, you will crawl on your stomach and eat dirt.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle zele ɛwɔlɛ ne kɛ, “Ɔlua ɛhye mɔɔ wɔyɛ la ati, munzule ɛha wɔ wɔ nyɛmoa nee nanemgbole kɔsɔɔti avinli. Ɔvi ɛnɛ mɔɔ kɔ la ɛbahwenle ɛ ko aze na wɔali ndɛtɛlɛ kɔkpula mekɛ mɔɔ ɛkɛwu la.

english_verse: You and this woman will hate each other; your descendants and hers will always be enemies. One of hers will strike you on the head, and you will strike him on the heel.”
translation_verse: Mebava ɛkpɔlɛ meado wɔ nee raalɛ ne, nee ɛ ra nee raalɛ ne ara avinli. Raalɛ ne ara bagelegele ɛ ti na ɛdawɔ wɔaha ɔ gyakɛ anzi.”

english_verse: Then the Lord God said to the woman, “You will suffer terribly when you give birth. But you will still desire your husband, and he will rule over you.”
translation_verse: Akee ɔzele raalɛ ne kɛ, “Mebamaa wɔade nyane kpalɛ wɔ awolɛ nu; ɛbade nyane wɔ wɔ ralɛ ɛwolɛ nu, noko ɛ nwo balɔ ɛ hu na yeazie wɔ.”

english_verse: The Lord said to the man, “You listened to your wife and ate the fruit I told you not to eat. And so, the ground will be under a curse because of what you did. As long as you live, you will have to struggle to grow enough food.
translation_verse: Na ɔzele Adam kɛ, “Kɛmɔ wɔdie ɛ ye aneɛ na wɔli bakama ne mɔɔ menzele wɔ kɛ ɛmmadi la bie la ati, ɔlua ɛ ti, munzule ɛha azɛlɛ ye; ɛtɛwule a ɛbavɛ na wɔanyia aleɛ wɔali.

english_verse: Your food will be plants, but the ground will produce thorns and thistles.
translation_verse: Mbaka nee ndile mɔɔ anwo le mbowule la bafifi azɛlɛ ye azo, noko ɛbɔ nu ala a ɛbadidi a.

english_verse: You will sweat all your life to earn a living; you were made out of soil, and you will once again turn into soil.”
translation_verse: Ɛbahwi ɛ ti anwo na wɔanyia aleɛ wɔali, kɔkpula mekɛ mɔɔ ɛkɛzia ɛkɛhɔ azɛlɛ ye anu bieko la, ɔluakɛ nuhua yɛɛ ɛvi ɛrale a; ɛle ndɛtɛlɛ na ɛbazia wɔahɔ ndɛtɛlɛ nu.”

english_verse: The man Adam named his wife Eve because she would become the mother of all who live.
translation_verse: Ɛhye anzi, nrenya ne donle ɔ ye duma na ɔvɛlɛle ye Yive, ɔboalekɛ ɔle menli kɔsɔɔti bɛ nli.

english_verse: Then the Lord God made clothes out of animal skins for the man and his wife.
translation_verse: Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle kpomgbale nane nwoma adɛladeɛ manle Adam nee ɔ ye Yive wulale. Bɛvoa Adam nee Yive bɛvi tola ne anu

english_verse: The Lord said, “They now know the difference between right and wrong, just as we do. But they must not be allowed to eat fruit from the tree that lets them live forever.”
translation_verse: Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle zele kɛ, “Bɛnlea, kɛkala sonla ɛyɛ kɛ yɛ nuhua ko la, yenwu kpalɛ nee ɛtane. Saa yɛannea ye boɛ a ɔbali ngoane baka ne ɔdaye ye ma ne bie na yeadɛnla ngoane nu dahuu.”

english_verse: So the Lord God sent them out of the Garden of Eden, where they would have to work the ground from which the man had been made.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle voanle ye vile Yidɛn tola ne anu kɛ ɔhɔ ɔhɔyɛ azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ ɔvi nu ɔrale la azo egyinli.

english_verse: Then God put winged creatures at the entrance to the garden and a flaming, flashing sword to guard the way to the life-giving tree.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle voanle sonla vile tola ne anu, na ɔvale tease abɔdeɛma nee dadeɛ mɔɔ ɛlɛsɔ na ɔpɛnepɛne ɔ nwo ɛleka biala la ɔrazinzale Yidɛn tola ne aduduleɛ adenle ne mɔɔ kɔ ngoane baka ne anwo la.

english_verse: Adam and Eve had a son. Then Eve said, “I'll name him Cain because I got him with the help of the Lord.”
translation_verse: Adam nee ɔ ye Yive lale, na Yive vale ɛkolɛ na ɔwole ralɛ nrenya. Bɛdonle ye Keen. Yive edwɛkɛ a le kɛ, “Ɔlua Ɛdɛnkɛma moalɛ zo mewo ralɛ nrenya.”

english_verse: Later she had another son and named him Abel. Abel became a sheep farmer, but Cain farmed the land.
translation_verse: Nzinlii Yive wole Keen anzi ralɛ nrenya, na bɛdonle ye Ebɛle. Ebɛle ɛnee sie mboane, yɛɛ Keen yɛ egyinli.

english_verse: One day, Cain gave part of his harvest to the Lord,
translation_verse: Mekɛ hɔle bie la, Keen vale ye egyinli ne anu aleɛ ne bie bɔle azu manle Ɛdɛnkɛma.

english_verse: and Abel also gave an offering to the Lord. He killed the first-born lamb from one of his sheep and gave the Lord the best parts of it. The Lord was pleased with Abel and his offering,
translation_verse: Ebɛle noko hyele mboane mralɛ mɔɔ ye mboane ne mɔ bie lumuale wole bɛ la, na ɔvale bɛ nee bɛ ɛleka mɔɔ ɛlɔ kpalɛ la ɔbɔle azu ɔmanle Ɛdɛnkɛma. Ɛdɛnkɛma anye zɔle Ebɛle azubɔdeɛ ne,

english_verse: but not with Cain and his offering. This made Cain so angry that he could not hide his feelings.
translation_verse: na ɔ nye anzɔ Keen azubɔdeɛ ɛdeɛ ne. Ɛhye manle Keen ati zile aze na ɛya hunle ye kpole.

english_verse: The Lord said to Cain: What's wrong with you? Why do you look so angry?
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma bizale Keen kɛ, “Duzu ati a ɛ nyunlu ɛyɛ kpundikpundi na wɔva ɛya ɛ?

english_verse: If you had done the right thing, you would be smiling. But you did the wrong thing, and now sin is waiting to attack you like a lion. Sin wants to destroy you, but don't let it!
translation_verse: Asoo saa ɛyɛle ye boɛ a, anrɛɛ ɛ nyunlu ɛnrɛra anyia? Na wɔanyɛ ye boɛ la, ɛtane ɛhɔ ɛ nwo nzia; ɔkpondɛ kɛ ɔfo ɛ nwo zo, na wɔmɔ yɛɛ ɔwɔ kɛ ɛfo ɔ nwo zo a.”

english_verse: Cain said to his brother Abel, “Let's go for a walk.” And when they were out in a field, Cain attacked and killed him.
translation_verse: Ɛhye anzi Keen zele ɔ diema Ebɛle kɛ, “Maa yɛhɔ ɛbɔ nu.” Bɛhɔle la, Keen holole ɔ diema Ebɛle anwo zo na ɔhunle ye.

english_verse: Afterwards the Lord asked Cain, “Where is Abel?” “How should I know?” he answered. “Am I supposed to look after my brother?”
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma bizale Keen kɛ, “Ɛ diema Ebɛle wɔ nienwu?” Keen buale kɛ, “Menze, mame a menea me diema ne anwo zo a?”

english_verse: Then the Lord said: Why have you done this terrible thing? You killed your own brother, and his blood flowed onto the ground. Now his blood is calling out for me to punish you.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma bizale ye kɛ, “Duzu debie a wɔyɛ la? Ɛ diema ne mogya ne mɔɔ gua azɛlɛ ne anwo la ɛlɛsu avɛlɛ me.

english_verse: When you try to farm the land, it won't produce anything for you. From now on, you'll be without a home, and you'll spend the rest of your life wandering from place to place.
translation_verse: Ɔvi ɛnɛ mɔɔ kɔ la, debie biala mɔɔ ɛkɛlua ye azɛlɛ ye azo la ɛnrɛyɛ kpalɛ ɛnrɛmaa wɔ ɛlɛ; ɛkɛdɔ ɛ bɔ nu na mgbɔsamgbɔsa adɔ ɛ nwo wɔ azɛlɛ ye azo.”

english_verse: “This punishment is too hard!” Cain said.
translation_verse: Na Keen hanle hilele Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ, “Me ndeanlɛ ne bo me nwo zo.

english_verse: “You're making me leave my home and live far from you. I will have to wander about without a home, and just anyone could kill me.”
translation_verse: Wɔye me sa wɔvi azɛlɛ ye mɔɔ medidi zolɛ la anwo; wɔvoa me wɔvi ɛ nye zo. Mebadɔ ɛbɔ nu, na eza mgbɔsamgbɔsa adɔ me nwo wɔ azɛlɛ ye azo; saa awie biala nee me yia a, ɔbahu me.”

english_verse: “No!” the Lord answered. “Anyone who kills you will be punished seven times worse than I am punishing you.” So the Lord put a mark on Cain to warn everyone not to kill him.
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele ye kɛ, “Kyɛkyɛ, ɔnle zɔhane! Awie biala mɔɔ kɛhu Keen la, bɛbali ye nzenralɛ fane nsuu bɛazie ɔ bo zo.” Na Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛle Keen nzonlɛ, amaa awie biala mɔɔ nee ye kɛyia la angu ye.

english_verse: But Cain had to go far from the Lord and live in the Land of Wandering, which is east of Eden. More and More People
translation_verse: Akee Keen vile Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlu na ɔhɔdɛnlanle Nɔɔdo wɔ Yidɛn tola ne aduduleɛ. Keen abo zo amra

english_verse: Later, Cain and his wife had a son named Enoch. At the time Cain was building a town, and so he named it Enoch after his son.
translation_verse: Keen vale ɔ ye na ɔ ye wole ralɛ nrenya, bɛdonle ye Yinɔko. Keen kyekyele suakpole ko na ɔvale ɔ ra ne duma ɔdole zolɛ.

english_verse: Then Enoch had a son named Irad, who had a son named Mehujael, who had a son named Methushael, who had a son named Lamech.
translation_verse: Yinɔko wole ralɛ nrenya, bɛfɛlɛ ye Ayelade; Ayelade wole Mɛhugyeeyɛle. Mɛhugyeeyɛle wole Mɛtuhyeeyɛle, yɛɛ Mɛtuhyeeyɛle wole Leemɛke.

english_verse: Lamech and Adah had two sons, Jabal and Jubal. Their son Jabal was the first to live in tents and raise sheep and goats. Jubal was the first to play harps and flutes.
translation_verse: Gyeebale adiema nrenya a le Dwubale. Dwubale abo zo amra a le menli mɔɔ vale getaa nee fulutu bɔle edwɛne a.

english_verse: Lamech and Zillah had a son named Tubal Cain who made tools out of bronze and iron. They also had a daughter, whose name was Naamah.
translation_verse: Raalɛ Zela wole Tubale Keen, mɔɔ ɔ bo zo amra a vale mbulalɛ nee kɔbele yɛle ɛyazonlɛ nee konle ninyɛne la. Ɔ diema raalɛ a le Neeyama.

english_verse: One day, Lamech said to his two wives, “A young man wounded me, and I killed him.
translation_verse: Leemɛke zele ye mraalɛ ne mɔ kɛ, “Eda nee Zela, bɛdie me aneɛ; me ye mɔ, bɛdie mɔɔ melɛka la: Mehu kpavolɛ bie mɔɔ bɔle me, bodale me la.

english_verse: Anyone who tries to get even with me will be punished ten times more than anyone who tries to get even with Cain.”
translation_verse: Saa mɔɔ kɛhu Keen la bɛkɛli ye nzenralɛ fane nsuu a, ɛnee mɔɔ kɛhu medame Leemɛke la, bɛkɛli ye nzenralɛ fane abulasuu nee nsuu.” Sɛte nee Yinɔhye

english_verse: Adam and his wife had another son. They named him Seth, because they said, “God has given us a son to take the place of Abel, who was killed by his brother Cain.”
translation_verse: Adam nee ɔ ye wole ralɛ nrenya bieko. Ɔ ye hanle kɛ, “Nyamenle ɛmaa me ralɛ nrenya ɛmaa meva mezie Ebɛle, mɔɔ Keen hunle ye la abo zo.” Na ɔdonle ye Sɛte.

english_verse: Later, Seth had a son and named him Enosh. About this time people started worshiping the Lord.
translation_verse: Sɛte wole ralɛ nrenya na ɔdonle ye Yinɔhye. Mekɛ ne anu menli bɔle ɔ bo kɛ bɛsonle Ɛdɛnkɛma.

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Adam lile ɛvolɛ ɛya ngɔnla abulasa, na ɔwule.

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Sɛte lile ɛvolɛ ɛya ngɔnla ɛvolɛ bulu nee nwiɔ, na ɔwule.

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Yinɔhye lile ɛvolɛ ɛya ngɔnla ɛvolɛ nnu, na ɔwule.

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Kinan lile ɛvolɛ ɛya ngɔnla ɛvolɛ bulu, na ɔwule.

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Mahalalile lile ɛvolɛ ɛya mɔtwɛ ɛvolɛ abulahɔnla nee nnu, na ɔwule.

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Gyɛlɛde lile ɛvolɛ ɛya ngɔnla abulasia nee nwiɔ, na ɔwule.

english_verse: and God took him away at the age of
translation_verse: Yinɔko nee Nyamenle luale na yeanwu, ɔminliminlinle, ɔboalekɛ Nyamenle vale ye hɔle.

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Yemɔti Mɛtusɛla lile ɛvolɛ ɛya ngɔnla abulasia nee ngɔnla, na ɔwule.

english_verse: Lamech said, “I'll name him Noah because he will give us comfort, as we struggle hard to make a living on this land that the Lord has put under a curse.”
translation_verse: Ɔhanle kɛ, “Nyamenle ɛmaa munzule ɛha azɛlɛ ye. Ɔlua zo ɛnɛ yɛyɛ zolɛ egyinli a yɛnwu nyane kpalɛ. Noko kakula ɛhye bamaa yɛ nyanenwunlɛ ne aha aze.” Ɛhye ati ɔdonle ye Nowa.

english_verse: and died at the age of
translation_verse: Leemɛke lile ɛvolɛ ɛya nsuu abulasuu nee nsuu, na ɔwule.

english_verse: More and more people were born, until finally they spread all over the earth. Some of their daughters were so beautiful that supernatural beings came down and married the ones they wanted.
translation_verse: anwomanyunlu menli bie nwunle kɛ menli amra mraalɛ ne mɔ anwo yɛ fɛ; yemɔti bɛvale mɔɔ bɛdabɛ bɛkulo la bɛgyale bɛ.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “I won't let my life-giving breath remain in anyone forever. No one will live for more than
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele kɛ, “Menrɛmaa sonla ɛnrɛdɛnla aze dahuu, ɔluakɛ ɔle nwonane. Ɔvi ɛnɛ mɔɔ kɔ la sonla ɛnrɛli ɛvolɛ mɔɔ bo ɛya ko abulanwiɔ la.”

english_verse: The children of the supernatural beings who had married these women became famous heroes and warriors. They were called Nephilim and lived on the earth at that time and even later.
translation_verse: Mekɛ zɔhane anu, yɛɛ nzinlii bɔbɔ, anwomanyunlu menli zɔhane nee mralɛ mraalɛ ne mɔ wole mralɛ. Na bɛmɛ bɛ mra a le menli kakanyinlima ne mɔ mɔɔ mɔmoane ne bɛliele duma la.

english_verse: The Lord saw how bad the people on earth were and that everything they thought and planned was evil.
translation_verse: Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma nwunle kɛ sonla amumuyɛyɛlɛ ne ɛyɛ kpole kpalɛ wɔ azɛlɛ ye azo, na ɛtane ngome ɛyi ye adwenle nee ye ahonle nu tɛkɛɛ.

english_verse: He was sorry that he had made them,
translation_verse: Na ɔyɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma nyane kɛ yebɔ sonla yedo azɛlɛ ye azo a. Ɔyɛle ye nyane somaa,

english_verse: and he said, “I'm going to destroy every person on earth! I'll even wipe out animals, birds, and reptiles. I'm sorry I ever made them.”
translation_verse: na ɔhanle kɛ, “Mebɔ sonla mɔɔ mebɔ la abo zo bɔkɔɔ wɔ azɛlɛ ye azo. Mesɛkye debie biala mɔɔ mebɔ la, sonla, nane, ninyɛne mɔɔ twenle bɛ nwo aze la, yɛɛ nloma muala. Menlu me nwo bɔbɔ kɛ mebɔ bɛ a.”

english_verse: But the Lord was pleased with Noah,
translation_verse: Noko Nowa ɛdeɛ, Ɛdɛnkɛma hulole ye. Nowa

english_verse: Get some good lumber and build a boat. Put rooms in it and cover it with tar inside and out.
translation_verse: Yemɔti fa gɔfa baka bobɔ ɛlɛnemgbole; kyɛ nuhua ekpumgbunli ekpumgbunli na fa bilewu ka nuhua nee nwolɛ amuala.

english_verse: Noah did everything God told him to do.
translation_verse: Nowa yɛle ɛhye mɔ na ɔyɛle debie biala mɔɔ Nyamenle zele ye la.

english_verse: I'm going to send a flood that will destroy everything that breathes! Nothing will be left alive.
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ mebamaa ezule kpole bie adɔ toonwo abu aze, yeazɛkye debie biala mɔɔ die ɛnwomenle mɔɔ wɔ aleɛabo la amuala; debie biala mɔɔ wɔ azɛlɛ ye azo la bawu.

english_verse: But I solemnly promise that you, your wife, your sons, and your daughters-in-law will be kept safe in the boat.
translation_verse: Na wɔmɔ, me nee wɔ bayɛ ngyekyeleɛ. Ɛ nee ɛ mra mrenya, nee ɛ ye, yɛɛ ɛ mra mrenya mraalɛ ne mɔ bavo ɛlɛne ne anu.

english_verse: Take into the boat with you a male and a female of every kind of animal and bird, as well as a male and a female of every reptile. I don't want them to be destroyed.
translation_verse: Ɛbava nane biala nee debie biala mɔɔ twenle ɔ nwo aze la, nloma nee abɔdeɛ mɔɔ wɔ aleɛabo la amuala, ko biala nyinli nee belɛ, wɔahɔ ɛlɛne ne anu, amaa bɛanwu.

english_verse: Store up enough food both for yourself and for them.
translation_verse: Ɛbava aleɛ kɔsɔɔti bie wɔazie na bɛ nee nane nee nloma ne mɔ ali.”

english_verse: The Lord told Noah: Take your whole family with you into the boat, because you are the only one on this earth who pleases me.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Nowa kɛ, “Ɛ nee wɔ sua nu amra amuala bɛvo ɛlɛne ne anu, ɔluakɛ menwu kɛ ɛ ngomekye ala a ɛdi pɛlepɛle wɔ ewiade ye amuala anu a.

english_verse: Take seven pairs of every kind of animal that can be used for sacrifice and one pair of all others.
translation_verse: Fa nane ko biala mɔɔ anwo te la, nyinli nee belɛ nsuu, nuhua mɔɔ anwo ɛnde la, yemɔ fa nyinli nee belɛ ala.

english_verse: Also take seven pairs of every kind of bird with you. Do this so there will always be animals and birds on the earth.
translation_verse: Fa nloma bɛdabɛ noko, ko biala nyinli nee belɛ nsuu. Sesa ɛhye mɔ amuala kɔ ɛlɛne ne anu, amaa nzinlii bɛanyia bɛ ɛsaso wɔ azɛlɛ ye azo amuala.

english_verse: Seven days from now I will send rain that will last for
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ ɛnɛ anwo zo kenle nsuu, mebamaa ezule kpole bie adɔ nɔɔzo nee ewiazo kenle abulanla, azɛkye ninyɛne mɔɔ mebɔ la amuala.”

english_verse: Seven days later a flood began to cover the earth.
translation_verse: Ɛhye anzi kenle nsuu, azuyilɛ ne vale azɛlɛ ye.

english_verse: The water under the earth started gushing out everywhere, the sky opened like windows, and rain poured down for
translation_verse: ɔdɔle bilididi nɔɔzo nee ewiazo toonwo kenle abulanla, ɔbule aze na ɔyɛle azɛlɛ ye azo faanwo.

english_verse: On that day Noah and his wife went into the boat with their three sons, Shem, Ham, and Japheth, and their wives.
translation_verse: Kenle ko ne mɔɔ ezule ne dukuele la, Nowa nee ɔ ye nee ɔ mra mrenya ne mɔ, Hyɛm, Ham, yɛɛ Gyeefɛte nee bɛ mraalɛ nsa ne,

english_verse: Noah took a male and a female of every living creature with him,
translation_verse: Ɔvale abɔdeɛ ngakyile ne mɔ mɔɔ die ɛnwomenle la ko biala, nyinli nee belɛ,

english_verse: just as God had told him to do. And when they were all in the boat, the Lord closed the door.
translation_verse: kɛmɔ Nyamenle zele ye la ɔvole ɛlɛne ne anu. Na Ɛdɛnkɛma dole ɛlɛne ne anlenkɛ ne anu.

english_verse: Finally, the mighty flood was so deep that even the highest mountain peaks were about seven meters below the surface of the water.
translation_verse: Nzule ne monlɔmonlanle awoka ne mɔ na ɔhɔle anwuma kɛyɛ mita nsuu.

english_verse: Not a bird, animal, reptile, or human was left alive anywhere on earth.
translation_verse: Abɔdeɛ biala mɔɔ wɔ azɛlɛ ye azo la, nloma, nyɛmoa, nanemgbole nee ngɛkɛba, yɛɛ menli kɔsɔɔti wule.

english_verse: A hundred fifty days later, the water started going down.
translation_verse: Ɔlile kenle kɔkɔlɛ ɛya ko abulanlu kolaa na nzule ne abɔ ɔ bo kɛ ɔsesa.

english_verse: God did not forget about Noah and the animals with him in the boat. So God made a wind blow, and the water started going down.
translation_verse: Nyamenle arɛle anvi Nowa nee nane nee nyɛmoa ne mɔ mɔɔ Nowa nee bɛ wɔ ɛlɛne ne anu la; ɔmanle anwoma bie vɛlɛle, na azule ne bɔle ɔ bo kɛ ɔsesa.

english_verse: God stopped up the places where the water had been gushing out from under the earth. He also closed up the sky, and the rain stopped.
translation_verse: Ɔzile nzudenle ne mɔ mɔɔ azɛlɛ bo nzule ne mɔ dua nu bu azɛlɛ ye azo la, ɔmanle maanle nu dele na ezule ne gyakyile ɛdɔlɛ.

english_verse: Then on the seventeenth day of the seventh month of the year, the boat came to rest somewhere in the Ararat mountains.
translation_verse: Na siane nsuu ne anu, kenle ne mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ bulu nee nsuu la, ɛlɛne ne ranwenle Arelalate awoka ne mɔ ko azo.

english_verse: The water kept going down, and the mountain tops could be seen on the first day of the tenth month.
translation_verse: Nzule ne hɔle zolɛ sesanle, na ɔkadwu siane bulu ne kenle ne mɔɔ lumua la azo la, ɛnee awoka ne mɔ ati ɛvindevinde.

english_verse: Forty days later Noah opened a window to send out a raven, but it kept flying around until the water had dried up.
translation_verse: na ɔzoanle kɔkɔsɛlɛ. Kɔkɔsɛlɛ dule hɔle na yeanzia yeamba; ɔdule ɔkpɔsale ɔbɔle ahɔnlɔma toonwo ɔhɔkpulale mekɛ mɔɔ nzule ne wiele sesa bɔkɔɔ la.

english_verse: Noah wanted to find out if the water had gone down, so he sent out a dove.
translation_verse: Eza Nowa zoanle abubule ɔdaye noko kɛ ɔhɔnlea saa nzule ne ɛsesa a;

english_verse: Deep water was still everywhere, and when the dove could not find a place to land, it flew back to the boat. Then Noah held out his hand and helped it back in.
translation_verse: na abubule ne annyia ɛleka andɛnla, ɔluakɛ ɛnee nzule dɔɔnwo tɛbɔ aze. Ɔziale ɔhɔle ɛlɛne ne anwo, na Nowa dendenle ɔ sa hyele ye vale ye hɔle ɛlɛne ne anu.

english_verse: Seven days later Noah sent the dove out again.
translation_verse: Nowa hendɛle kenle nsuu bieko na ɔzoanle abubule ne bieko.

english_verse: It returned in the evening, holding in its beak a green leaf from an olive tree. Noah knew the water was finally going down.
translation_verse: Ye nɔsolɛ nu, abubule ne ziale rale; ɔkara la ɔlɛ ɔlivi nya amolɛ ɔ nloa anu. Ɛhye manle Nowa nwunle kɛ nzule ne ɛwie sesa.

english_verse: He waited seven more days before sending the dove out again, and this time it did not return.

english_verse: The smell of the burning offering pleased the Lord, and he said: Never again will I punish the earth for the sinful things its people do. All of them have evil thoughts from the time they are young, but I will never destroy everything that breathes, as I did this time.
translation_verse: Nowa azu ne zɔle Ɛdɛnkɛma anye, na ɔzele kɛ, “Ɔvi ɛnɛ mɔɔ kɔ la menrɛdoa sonla nyɛleɛ menrɛmaa munzule mɔɔ le zɛhae la ɛnrɛha azɛlɛ ye bieko; menrɛzɛkye ewiade abɔdeɛ muala, kɛmɔ meyɛ la bieko. Meze kɛ sonla yemɔ, ye ngakula nu amuala ɛnee ye adwenle nee ye ahonle nu le bile.

translation_verse: Mɔɔ ɔka ekyii na Ebilam adwu Yigyibiti maanle ne anu la, ɔzele ɔ ye Sɛleeyae kɛ, “Meze kɛ ɛle raalɛ mɔɔ anwo yɛ fɛ a.

english_verse: The king's officials told him about her, and she was taken to his house.

english_verse: The king was good to Abram because of Sarai, and Abram was given sheep, cattle, donkeys, slaves, and camels.

english_verse: where he had earlier camped and built an altar. There he worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Ɔhɔle ɛleka ne mɔɔ ɔlumuale ɔzile ye azukponle ne la, na ɔzonlenle Ɛdɛnkɛma.

english_verse: Lot, who was traveling with him, also had sheep, goats, and cattle, as well as his own family and slaves.
translation_verse: Lɔɔto noko mɔɔ nee Ebilam hɔle la, ɔdaye ɔnyianle mboane, mbɔnkye, nlankɛ, yɛɛ ndanlɛ azua.

english_verse: Abram said to Lot, “We are close relatives. We shouldn't argue, and our men shouldn't be fighting one another.
translation_verse: Ebilam zele Lɔɔto kɛ, “Mmamaa yɛmaa kpolera tɔ yɛ mu nwiɔ yɛ avinli, anzɛɛ wɔ menli nee me menli mɔɔ nea yɛ nyɛmoa ne mɔ la avinli, ɔboalekɛ yɛle abusua ko.

english_verse: There is plenty of land for you to choose from. Let's separate. If you go north, I'll go south; if you go south, I'll go north.”
translation_verse: Azɛlɛ tɛtɛtɛlɛlɛ a la yɛ nyunlu lɔ la. Te ɛ nwo. Saa ɛkɔ bɛne zo a, mebahɔ fema zo, yɛɛ saa ɛkɔ fema zo noko a, mebahɔ bɛne zo.”

english_verse: This happened before the Lord had destroyed the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah. And when Lot looked around, he saw there was plenty of water in the Jordan Valley. All the way to Zoar the valley was as green as the garden of the Lord or the land of Egypt.
translation_verse: Lɔɔto dole ɔ nye nleanle azɛlɛ ne na ɔnwunle kɛ Dwɔdan Bɔnza ne anu, toonwo mɔɔ kɔdwu Zowaa la lɛ nzule dɔɔnwo kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma tola ne anu nee Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo la.

english_verse: So Lot chose the whole Jordan Valley for himself, and as he started out toward the east, he and Abram separated.
translation_verse: Na Lɔɔto vale Dwɔdan Bɔnza na ɔvale ɔ ti ɔbɔle aduduleɛ ɔdele ɔ nwo ɔvile Ebilam anwo.

english_verse: Abram stayed in the land of Canaan. But Lot settled near the cities of the valley and put up his tents not far from Sodom,
translation_verse: Ebilam dɛnlanle Keena azɛlɛ zo, na Lɔɔto hɔdɛnlanle azuamgbole ne mɔ mɔɔ wɔ Bɔnza ne anu la bie mɔ azo na akee ɔdule ɔhɔdɛnlanle Sodɔm.

english_verse: where the people were evil and sinned terribly against the Lord. Abram Moves to Hebron
translation_verse: Sodɔmma le amumuyɛ; bɛyɛle ɛtane mgbole bɛtiale Ɛdɛnkɛma. Ebilam tu ahɔ Hibulɔn

english_verse: After Abram and Lot had gone their separate ways, the Lord said to Abram: Look around to the north, south, east, and west.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Lɔɔto dele ɔ nwo vile Ebilam anwo la, Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Ebilam kɛ, “Gyinla ɛleka mɔɔ ɛwɔ la, na maa ɛ nye zo nea ɛbɔ nu afoa nu, nyevile nu afoa nu, yɛɛ aduduleɛ nee adɔleɛ afoa nu,

english_verse: I will give you and your family all the land you can see. It will be theirs forever!
translation_verse: ɔluakɛ mebava azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ ɛ nye dua ye la amuala meamaa wɔ nee ɛ bo zo amra, meamaa yeayɛ bɛ ɛdeɛ bɔkɔɔ.

english_verse: Now walk back and forth across the land, because I am going to give it to you.
translation_verse: Dwazo na kpɔsa kɔ azɛlɛ ne ati nee ɔ bo, kpɔsa nwu azɛlɛ ne tɛtɛlɛ nee ye tendenle, ɔluakɛ mebava meamaa wɔ.”

english_verse: Abram took down his tents and went to live near the sacred trees of Mamre at Hebron, where he built an altar in honor of the Lord.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Ebilam dudule ye ndanlɛ sua ne na ɔhɔdɛnlanle Mameli oku mbaka ne mɔ mɔɔ wɔ Hibulɔn la anwo. Na ɛkɛ ne, ɔzile azukponle ɔmanle Ɛdɛnkɛma.

english_verse: About this time, King Amraphel of Babylonia, King Arioch of Ellasar, King Chedorlaomer of Elam, and King Tidal of Goiim
translation_verse: Arelemgbunli nna ɛhye mɔ, Babelonia Belemgbunli Ameleefɛle, Ɛleesaa Belemgbunli Aleyɔko, Yilam Belemgbunli Kɛdɔleewomɛ, yɛɛ Goyem Belemgbunli Taedale,

english_verse: attacked King Bera of Sodom, King Birsha of Gomorrah, King Shinab of Admah, King Shemeber of Zeboiim, and the king of Bela, a city also known as Zoar.
translation_verse: nee arelemgbunli nnu bie nyianle konle. Arelemgbunli nnu ne mɔ a le Sodɔm Belemgbunli Bila, Gomɔla Belemgbunli Bɛhya, Adomaa Belemgbunli Hyaenabe, Zɛboyem Belemgbunli Hyɛmibɛ, yɛɛ Bila anzɛɛ Zowaa belemgbunli ne.

english_verse: King Chedorlaomer and his allies had ruled these last five kings for twelve years, but in the thirteenth year the kings rebelled and joined forces in Siddim Valley, which is now covered by the southern part of the Dead Sea.
translation_verse: Ɛnee arelemgbunli nnu ɛhye mɔ wɔ Belemgbunli Kɛdɔleewomɛ abo, bɛzonle ye toonwo ɛvolɛ bulu nee nwiɔ. Ye ɛvolɛ bulu nee nsa ne anu, bɛdele atua.

english_verse: A year later King Chedorlaomer and his allies attacked and defeated the Rephaites in Ashteroth-Karnaim, the Zuzites in Ham, and the Emites in Shaveh-Kiriathaim.
translation_verse: Ye ɛvolɛ bulu nee nna ne anu Belemgbunli Kɛdɔleewomɛ nee arelemgbunli mɔɔ ɔ nee bɛ lɛ konle nu agɔnwolɛyɛlɛ la vale bɛ ɛlɔne hɔhanle Relɛfeeyemma mɔɔ wɔ Ahyetɛlo Kaneeyem, Zuzemma mɔɔ wɔ Ham, yɛɛ Yimemma mɔɔ wɔ Hyeevi Keleateeyem la senle dwɛɛ lile bɛ nwo zo konim.

english_verse: They also defeated the Horites in the hill country of Edom, as far as El-Paran, near the desert.
translation_verse: Eza bɛhanle Hɔlaema mɔɔ wɔ Yidɔm awoka ne mɔ azo la senle, na bɛvoanle bɛ toonwo bɛhɔdwule Ɛlepɛlan, mɔɔ wɔ ɛsɛlɛ ne anloa la,

english_verse: They went back to the city of Enmishpat, better known as Kadesh. Then they captured all the land that belonged to the Amalekites, and they defeated the Amorites who were living in Hazazon-Tamar.
translation_verse: na bɛziale bɛ nzi bɛrale Keedɛhye mɔɔ ɛnee bɛfɛlɛ ye Ɛnemehyepate la, bɛrahanle Amalɛkema nee Amɔlema mɔɔ de Heezazɔn Teemaa la senle, bɛlile bɛ muala bɛ nwo zo konim.

english_verse: At Siddim Valley, the armies of the kings of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, Zeboiim, and Bela fought the armies of King Chedorlaomer of Elam, King Tidal of Goiim, King Amraphel of Babylonia, and King Arioch of Ellasar. The valley
translation_verse: Na Sodɔm, Gomɔla, Ademaa, Zɛboyem, yɛɛ Bila arelemgbunli vale bɛ ɛlɔnema dwazole na bɛ nee Yilam Belemgbunli Kɛdɔleewomɛ, Babelonia Belemgbunli Ameleefɛle, Ɛleesaa Belemgbunli Aleyɔko, yɛɛ Goyem Belemgbunli Taedale ɛlɔnema ne bɔle ye zo wɔ Sedem Bɔnza. Bɛle arelemgbunli nnu yɛɛ bɛ nee arelemgbunli nna ɛlɛko a.

english_verse: was full of tar pits, and when the troops from Sodom and Gomorrah started running away, some of them fell into the pits. Others escaped to the hill country.
translation_verse: Sedem Bɔnza ne anu le bilewu ahuma ngome, yemɔti mɔɔ Sodɔm nee Gomɔla arelemgbunli nriandi ahɔ la, bɛhɔfolofolole ahuma ne bie mɔ anu, na arelemgbunli mɔɔ hale la nriandile hɔle awoka ne mɔ azo.

english_verse: Their enemies took everything of value from Sodom and Gomorrah, including their food supplies.
translation_verse: Yemɔti ɛlɔnema ne sesale Sodɔmma nee Gomɔlama ninyɛne ne kɔsɔɔti nee bɛ aleɛ hɔle.

english_verse: They also captured Abram's nephew Lot, who lived in Sodom. They took him and his possessions and then left.
translation_verse: Eza bɛhyele Lɔɔto, mɔɔ le Ebilam adiema nrenya ne ara nrenya ne, mɔɔ ɛnee de Sodɔm la, na bɛvale ye nee ɔ nwo ninyɛne kɔsɔɔti bɛhɔle.

english_verse: At this time Abram the Hebrew was living near the oaks that belonged to Mamre the Amorite. Mamre and his brothers Eshcol and Aner were Abram's friends. Someone who had escaped from the battle told Abram
translation_verse: Na awie ko mɔɔ vile ɛsalɛ la nriandile rahanle hilele Hibulunli Ebilam. Ebilam ɛnee de ɛleka bie mɔɔ bikye Amɔlenli Mameli oku mbaka ne mɔ mɔɔ bɛyɛ ɛzonlenlɛ wɔ bɛ bo la. Mameli amediema mrenya a le Ɛhyekɔlo nee Enɛ, yɛɛ bɛmɛ nsa bɛle Ebilam konle nu agɔnwolɛma.

english_verse: that his nephew Lot had been taken away. Three hundred and eighteen of Abram's servants were fighting men, so he took them and followed the enemy as far north as the city of Dan.
translation_verse: Ebilam dele kɛ bɛhye ye awozoa ne nuokɛ bɛ nee ye ɛlɛkɔ la, ɔvale ye menli ɛya nsa bulu nee mɔtwɛ ne mɔɔ wɔ ye sua nu ɛkɛ mɔɔ yetete bɛ wɔ konle nu la, na ɔ nee bɛ voanle arelemgbunli nna ne toonwo ɔhɔdwule Dan.

english_verse: That night, Abram divided up his troops, attacked from all sides, and won a great victory. But some of the enemy escaped to the town of Hobah north of Damascus,
translation_verse: Ɔhyɛle ye ɛlɔnema ne anu na ɔvale bɛ ɔhɔle ye kpɔvolɛma ne anwo zo nɔɔzo, ɔtetale bɛ na ɔvoanle bɛ toonwo ɔhɔdwule Hobaa, wɔ Dɛmasekɛse sɔlɔ.

english_verse: and Abram went after them. He brought back his nephew Lot, together with Lot's possessions and the women and everyone else who had been captured. Abram Is Blessed by Melchizedek
translation_verse: Akee ɔvale ninyɛne ne amuala, ye busuanli Lɔɔto nee ɔ nwo ninyɛne, mraalɛ ne mɔ nee menli mɔɔ bɛhyele bɛ nuokɛ la amuala ɔziale ɔrale. Mɛlekezɛdɛke Yila Ebilam

english_verse: Abram returned after he had defeated King Chedorlaomer and the other kings. Then the king of Sodom went to meet Abram in Shaveh Valley, which is also known as King's Valley.
translation_verse: Mekɛ mɔɔ Ebilam vi konle ne mɔɔ ɔlile Belemgbunli Kɛdɔleewomɛ nee arelemgbunli mɔɔ nee ye lua la anwo zo konim la anloa ziale rale la, Sodɔm belemgbunli ne hɔyiale ye wɔ Hyeevi Bɔnza, .

english_verse: King Melchizedek of Salem was a priest of God Most High. He brought out some bread and wine
translation_verse: Na Seelɛm Belemgbunli Mɛlekezɛdɛke rɛlɛle ye kpanwo nee nwanye. Mɛlekezɛdɛke le Anwuma Anwuma Nyamenle ne sɛlɛvolɛ.

english_verse: and said to Abram: “I bless you in the name of God Most High, Creator of heaven and earth.
translation_verse: Na ɔyilale Ebilam ɔzele kɛ, “Ebilam, Anwuma Anwuma Nyamenle ne, mɔɔ bɔle anwuma nee aze la ɛyila wɔ.

english_verse: All praise belongs to God Most High for helping you defeat your enemies.” Then Abram gave Melchizedek a tenth of everything.
translation_verse: Ayɛlɛyelɛ ɛha Anwuma Anwuma Nyamenle ne mɔɔ ɛye wɔ kpɔvolɛma ne ɛmaa wɔli bɛ nwo zo konim la.” Na Ebilam hyɛle debie biala mɔɔ ɔnyianle la anu bulu na ɔdule ɛkpɔ ko ɔmanle Mɛlekezɛdɛke.

english_verse: The king of Sodom said to Abram, “All I want are my people. You can keep everything else.”
translation_verse: Na Sodɔm belemgbunli ne zele Ebilam kɛ, “Fa menli ne mɔ maa me, na fa ninyɛne ne mɔ yɛ wɔ ɛdeɛ.”

english_verse: Abram answered: The Lord God Most High made the heavens and the earth. And I have promised him
translation_verse: Ebilam zele Sodɔm belemgbunli ne kɛ, “Meha ndane mehile Ɛdɛnkɛma, Anwuma Anwuma Nyamenle ne mɔɔ bɔle anwuma nee aze la,

english_verse: that I won't keep anything of yours, not even a sandal strap or a piece of thread. Then you can never say that you are the one who made me rich.
translation_verse: kɛ menrɛva nyɛma anzɛɛ mgbɔlaboa zo nyɛma mɔɔ le wɔ ɛdeɛ la, na wɔanyia adenle wɔaha kɛ, ‘Medame a memaa Ebilam ɛnyia ɔ nwo a.’

english_verse: Let my share be the food that my men have eaten. But Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre went with me, so give them their share of what we brought back.
translation_verse: Menrɛva ɛhwee kɛ mɔɔ me ɛlɔnema ne ɛli la, yɛɛ menli mɔɔ nee me hɔle la afoa nu ɛdeɛ ne ala. Yemɔti maa Enɛ, Ɛhyekɔlo, yɛɛ Mameli ɛva bɛ afoa nu ɛdeɛ mɔɔ wɔ nu la.”

english_verse: Later the Lord spoke to Abram in a vision, “Abram, don't be afraid! I will protect you and reward you greatly.”
translation_verse: Ɛhye mɔ anzi, Ebilam dele Ɛdɛnkɛma edwɛkɛ ne wɔ ɛnyelɛzodeɛnwunlɛ nu kɛ, “Ebilam, mmasulo, na mebabɔ ɛ nwo bane. Wɔ ahatualɛ bayɛ kpole kpalɛ.”

english_verse: But Abram answered, “Lord All-Powerful, you have given me everything I could ask for, except children. And when I die, Eliezer of Damascus will get all I own.
translation_verse: Ebilam hanle kɛ, “O Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle, duzu yɛɛ ɛbava wɔamaa me a, ɔluakɛ menlɛ ralɛ, yɛɛ sonla mɔɔ kɛkala bali me agya la a le Ɛleyizɛ mɔɔ vi Dɛmasekɛse la.

english_verse: You have not given me any children, and this servant of mine will inherit everything.”
translation_verse: Ɛtɛmanle metɛwole; kanranli mɔɔ bɛwo ye me sua nu ɛke la a bali me agya a.”

english_verse: The Lord replied, “No, he won't! You will have a son of your own, and everything you have will be his.”
translation_verse: Na Ebilam dele kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛlɛtendɛ ahile ye bieko kɛ, “Nrenya ɛhye ɛnrɛli wɔ agya. Ɛdawɔ ɛ kunlu ralɛ nrenya a bali wɔ agya a.”

english_verse: Then the Lord took Abram outside and said, “Look at the sky and see if you can count the stars. That's how many descendants you will have.”
translation_verse: Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma vale ye vindele na ɔzele ye kɛ, “To ɛ nye anwomanyunlu na nea saa ɛkɛhola nwɔlɔra ne mɔ tia a. Zɔhane ala yɛɛ ɛ bo zo amra bayɛ a.”

english_verse: Abram believed the Lord, so the Lord was pleased with him and accepted him. The Lord Makes Another Promise to Abram
translation_verse: Ebilam liele Ɛdɛnkɛma lile, na ɛhye manle ɔzɔle Ɛdɛnkɛma anye na ɔliele ye ɔdole nu.

english_verse: The Lord said to Abram, “I brought you here from Ur in Chaldea, and I gave you this land.”
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Ebilam kɛ, “Medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma mɔɔ nee wɔ vi Yule mɔɔ wɔ Babelonia la rale kɛ mefa azɛlɛ ɛhye meamaa wɔ kɛ wɔ ɛdeɛ ɔ la.”

english_verse: Abram asked, “Lord God, how can I know the land will be mine?”
translation_verse: Na Ebilam bizale kɛ, “O Awulae Nyamenle, na kɛ menwɔzi menwɔyɛ na meanwu kɛ azɛlɛ ne bayɛ me ɛdeɛ ɛ?”

english_verse: Then the Lord told him, “Bring me a three-year-old cow, a three-year-old female goat, a three-year-old ram, a dove, and a young pigeon.”
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma buale kɛ, “Fa ɛnlankɛ mɔɔ ɛli ɛvolɛ nsa, abɔnkye belɛ mɔɔ ɛli ɛvolɛ nsa, boane nyinli mɔɔ ɛli ɛvolɛ nsa, abubule yɛɛ mɔlɔnoma kakula bɛla.”

english_verse: Abram obeyed the Lord. Then he cut the animals in half and laid the two halves of each animal opposite each other on the ground. But he did not cut the doves and pigeons in half.
translation_verse: Ebilam sesale bɛ rale, ɔhunle bɛ ɔkpukekpukele bɛ nu nwiɔ nwiɔ, na ɔvale ko biala ebule ɔdole ye ebule ko ne anwo. Nloma ne mɔ ɛdeɛ, yeamkpukekpuke bɛ nu nwiɔ nwiɔ.

english_verse: And when birds came down to eat the animals, Abram chased them away.
translation_verse: Saa nloma mɔɔ di nane funli la ba nwolɛ a, ɛnee yevoa bɛ.

english_verse: As the sun was setting, Abram fell into a deep sleep, and everything became dark and frightening.
translation_verse: Sɛnzɛne ne ɛlɛkɔ ahɔdɔ la, nafelɛ kpole vale Ebilam, na awozinli kpole anu ɛzulolɛ bie rahedale ɔ nwo zo.

english_verse: Four generations later, your descendants will return here and take this land, because only then will the people who live here be so sinful that they deserve to be punished.
translation_verse: Ɛ bo zo amra awolɛndoazo fane nna ne azo amra bazia ara ɛke, ɔluakɛ Amɔlema amumuyɛ ne ɛtɛwiele munli di mɔɔ metea bɛ a.”

english_verse: Sometime after sunset, when it was very dark, a smoking cooking pot and a flaming fire passed between the two halves of each animal.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ sɛnzɛne ne dɔle na maanle nu yɛle awozinli la, senle siase mɔɔ ɛlɛkpu esike nee tɛkɛ mɔɔ ɛlɛsɔ gbolamgbolam la razenle nane ebule ebule ne mɔ avinli.

english_verse: At that time the Lord made an agreement with Abram and told him: I will give your descendants the land east of the Shihor River on the border of Egypt as far as the Euphrates River.
translation_verse: Na kenle ko ne Ɛdɛnkɛma nee Ebilam yɛle ngyekyeleɛ. Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Ebilam kɛ, “Meva azɛlɛ ɛhye memaa ɛ bo zo amra. Azɛlɛ ne vi Yigyibiti ɛweɛne zo kɔdwu Azukpole Yufileti ne anloa.

english_verse: the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Rephaites,
translation_verse: Hɛtema, Pɛlɛzema, Relɛfeeyemma,

english_verse: the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Girgashites, and the Jebusites.
translation_verse: Amɔlema, Keenama, Gɛgahyema, yɛɛ Gyibɛsema azɛlɛ ne mɔ amuala boka nwolɛ.”

english_verse: Abram's wife Sarai had not been able to have any children. But she owned a young Egyptian slave woman named Hagar,
translation_verse: Ebilam aye Sɛleeyae anwo ralɛ. Ɔlɛ ye Yigyibitinli sonvolɛ raalɛ bie, bɛfɛlɛ ye Heega.

english_verse: and Sarai said to Abram, “The Lord has not given me any children. Sleep with my slave, and if she has a child, it will be mine.” Abram agreed,
translation_verse: Na Sɛleeyae hanle hilele Ebilam kɛ, “Nea, Ɛdɛnkɛma ammaa meanwo. Yemɔti ɛ nee me sonvolɛ raalɛ ne ɛhɔla. Wɔannea a ɔkɛyɛ kɛ yemɔ ɔbawo mralɛ yeamaa me.” Na Ebilam diele ɔ ye Sɛleeyae ane.

english_verse: and Sarai gave him Hagar to be his wife. This happened after Abram had lived in the land of Canaan for ten years.
translation_verse: Yemɔti mɔɔ Ebilam lile ɛvolɛ bulu wɔ Keena azɛlɛ zo la, ɔ ye Sɛleeyae vale ye Yigyibitinli sonvolɛ raalɛ ne manle ɔ hu yɛle ɔ ye.

english_verse: Later, when Hagar knew she was going to have a baby, she became proud and treated Sarai hatefully.
translation_verse: Ebilam nee Heega lale, na ɔnrenzɛle. Na mɔɔ Heega nwunle kɛ yenrenzɛ la, ɛnee akee ɔmbu ɔ menle raalɛ ne bie.

english_verse: Then Sarai said to Abram, “It's all your fault! I gave you my slave woman, but she has been hateful to me ever since she found out she was pregnant. You have done me wrong, and you will have to answer to the Lord for this.”
translation_verse: Na Sɛleeyae zele Ebilam kɛ, “Abule mɔɔ ɛbu me la ɛbu ɛdawɔ. Menvale me sonvolɛ raalɛ memanle wɔ kɛ ɛ nee ye bɛla, na yenwu kɛ yenrenzɛ la, akee yeyɛ mɔɔ ɔwowɔ me nye mbaka a! Ɛdɛnkɛma ɔdaye ɔbua yɛ mu nwiɔ ndɛne!”

english_verse: Abram said, “All right! She's your slave—do whatever you want with her.” Then Sarai began treating Hagar so harshly that she finally ran away.
translation_verse: Ebilam buale ye kɛ, “Ayi, wɔ sonvolɛ raalɛ ne wɔ ɛ sa nu, debie biala mɔɔ fɛta la fa yɛ ye.” Yemɔti Sɛleeyae hilele Heega abodelɛ, na ɔnriandile.

english_verse: Hagar stopped to rest at a spring in the desert on the road to Shur. While she was there, the angel of the Lord came to her
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma soanvolɛ hɔdole ye wɔ ɛsɛlɛ ne azo nzubula bie mɔɔ wɔ Hyulu adenle zo la anwo,

english_verse: and asked, “Hagar, where have you come from, and where are you going?” She answered, “I'm running away from Sarai, my owner.”
translation_verse: na ɔbizale ye kɛ, “Sɛleeyae sonvolɛ raalɛ Heega, nienwu a ɛvi wɔra ɛke a, yɛɛ nienwu ɛleka a ɛlɛkɔ a?” Ɔbuale ye kɛ, “Melɛnriandi meavi me menle raalɛ Sɛleeyae anwo.”

english_verse: The angel said, “Go back to Sarai and be her slave.

english_verse: But your son will live far from his relatives; he will be like a wild donkey, fighting everyone, and everyone fighting him.”
