translation_verse: Na Gyekɔbo vi nafelɛ nu dunwuele na ɔhanle kɛ, “Amgba, Ɛdɛnkɛma wɔ ɛke, yɛɛ menze a.”

english_verse: Then Jacob became frightened and said, “What a frightening place! It must be the house of God and the gateway to heaven.”
translation_verse: Ɛzulolɛ kpole hanle ye na ɔhanle kɛ, “Ɛke yɛ ɛzulolɛ kpole kpalɛ! Ɛke a le Nyamenle sua nu a, na anuhɔlɛ mɔɔ bɛfa nu bɛkɔ anwuma maanle nu la a le ɛke.”

english_verse: When Jacob got up early the next morning, he took the rock that he had used for a pillow and stood it up as a place of worship. Then he poured olive oil on the rock to dedicate it to God,
translation_verse: Yemɔti Gyekɔbo dwazole nwonlomɔ mangyee ne ala, ɔvale bolɛ ne mɔɔ ɔvale ɔzɔle ɔ ti la ɔkpɔnlanle ye sika na ɔguale nwole zolɛ.

english_verse: Jacob solemnly promised God, “If you go with me and watch over me as I travel, and if you give me food and clothes
translation_verse: Akee Gyekɔbo bɔle ɛwɔkɛ kɛ, “Saa Nyamenle nee me dua, ɔnea me nwo zo wɔ ɛleka mɔɔ melɛkɔ la, na ɔmaa menyia aleɛ medi, menyia ɛdanlɛ mekeda,

english_verse: and bring me safely home again, you will be my God.
translation_verse: na mesia meba Egya sua nu anzonudwolɛ nu a, yemɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma bayɛ me Nyamenle,

english_verse: This rock will be your house, and I will give back to you a tenth of everything you give me.”
translation_verse: yɛɛ bolɛ ɛhye mɔɔ mekpɔnla ye sika wɔ ɛke la, bayɛ Nyamenle sua nu. Na debie biala mɔɔ ɛdawɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛkɛmaa menwɔnyia la, menwɔhyɛ nu bulu menwɔdu ɛkpɔ ko menwɔmaa wɔ.”

english_verse: As Jacob continued on his way to the east,
translation_verse: Akee Gyekɔbo zɔle ye adendulɛ ne azo na ɔhɔdwule menli mɔɔ wɔ aduduleɛ la azɛlɛ zo.

english_verse: he looked out in a field and saw a well where shepherds took their sheep for water. Three flocks of sheep were lying around the well, which was covered with a large rock.
translation_verse: Ɔdole ɔ nye la, ɔnwunle bula bie wɔ ɛya bie anu na mboane ekpunli nsa gugua nwolɛ, ɔluakɛ bula zɔhane azo yɛɛ bɛmaa bɛ nzule a. Bolɛ ne mɔɔ heda bula ne azo la le kpole,

english_verse: Shepherds would roll the rock away when all their sheep had gathered there. Then after the sheep had been watered, the shepherds would roll the rock back over the mouth of the well.
translation_verse: yemɔti mboane ne mɔ bagua ɛkɛ, na saa bɛ nloa wie yia na mboaneneavolɛma ne mɔ ba a, bɛ muala bɛabɔ nu bɛahundo bolɛ ne na bɛamaa mboane ne mɔ nzule. Bɛwie a ɛnee eza bɛhundo bolɛ ne bɛheda bula ne azo.

english_verse: Jacob asked the shepherds, “Where are you from?” “We're from Haran,” they answered.
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo bizale bɛ kɛ, “Me mediema, nienwu a bɛvi a?” Bɛbuale ye kɛ, “Yɛvi Hɛlan.”

english_verse: Then he asked, “Do you know Nahor's grandson Laban?” “Yes we do,” they replied.
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo bizale bɛ kɛ, “Bɛze Neehɔ ara Leeban ɔ?” Bɛbuale ye kɛ, “Yɛze ye.”

english_verse: “How is he?” Jacob asked. “He's fine,” they answered. “And here comes his daughter Rachel with the sheep.”
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo bizale bɛ kɛ, “Ɔte kpɔkɛ ɔ?” Bɛbuale ye kɛ, “Ɔte kpɔkɛ. Nea, ɔ ra raalɛ Relahyɛle a nee ye mboane ne mɔ ɛlɛba la.”

english_verse: Jacob told them, “Look, the sun is still high up in the sky, and it's too early to bring in the rest of the flocks. Water your sheep and take them back to the pasture.”
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo zele kɛ, “Bɛnlea, ewia ne gyi zo ɛsesebɛ. Ɔtɛdwule mɔɔ bɛmaa nyɛmoa ne mɔ kuohua bɛ nloa ɛleka ko a. Bɛmaa mboane ne mɔ nzule na bɛva bɛ bɛhɔ adidi.”

english_verse: But they replied, “We can't do that until they all get here, and the rock has been rolled away from the well.”
translation_verse: Bɛbuale kɛ, “Yɛngola yɛnyɛ ye zɔhane, kyesɛ mboane ekpunli ekpunli ne mɔ anloa yia kolaa na yeahundo bolɛ ne yeavi bula ne azo, na yɛamaa nyɛmoa ne mɔ nzule.”

english_verse: While Jacob was still talking with the men, his cousin Rachel came up with her father's sheep.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ ɔ nloa wɔ zolɛ ɔ nee mboaneneavolɛma ne mɔ ɛlɛtendɛ la, yɛɛ Relahyɛle nee ɔ ze mboane ne mɔ rale a, ɔluakɛ ɛnee ɔdaye a ɔnea bɛ a.

english_verse: When Jacob saw her and his uncle's sheep, he rolled the rock away and watered the sheep.
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo nwunle ɔ nli adiema Leeban ara raalɛ Relahyɛle nee mboane ne mɔ ala la, ɔhɔle ɔhɔhundole bolɛ ne ɔyele ye wɔ bula ne azo na ɔmanle ɔ wuvuanyi ne mboane ne mɔ nzule.

english_verse: He then kissed Rachel and started crying because he was so happy.
translation_verse: Akee Gyekɔbo vole Relahyɛle anvoka anwo na ɔdukuele nu ɔzunle.

english_verse: He told her that he was the son of her aunt Rebekah, and she ran and told her father about him.
translation_verse: Na Gyekɔbo hanle hilele Relahyɛle kɛ ɔle ɔdaye Relahyɛle ɔ ze busuanli, na ɔ nli a le Relɛbɛka. Na Relahyɛle nriandile hɔhanle edwɛkɛ ne hilele ɔ ze Leeban.

english_verse: As soon as Laban heard the news, he ran out to meet Jacob. He hugged and kissed him and brought him to his home, where Jacob told him everything that had happened.
translation_verse: Leeban dele ye awozoa ne nganeɛ la, ɔnriandile ɔrayiale ye, ɔyɛle ye atuu, ɔvole ɔ nvoka anwo, na ɔ nee ye rale sua nu. Gyekɔbo hanle edwɛkɛ biala hilele Leeban,

english_verse: Laban said, “You are my nephew, and you are like one of my own family.” Jacob Marries Leah and Rachel After Jacob had been there for a month,
translation_verse: na Leeban zele Gyekɔbo kɛ, “Amgba, ɛle me dehelɛ bɔkɔɔ!” Na ɔ nee ye dɛnlanle siane ko. Gyekɔbo sonle Leeban agya Relahyɛle nee Liya

english_verse: Laban said to him, “You shouldn't have to work without pay, just because you are a relative of mine. What do you want me to give you?”
translation_verse: Akee Leeban zele Gyekɔbo kɛ, “Me busuanli a le wɔ suzuamgba ɛdeɛ, noko ɔnle kɛ ɛyɛ gyima ɛmaa me mɔɔ mendua wɔ kakɛ a. Ka mɔɔ kenle ko ɛkɛlie la kile me.”

english_verse: Laban had two daughters. Leah was older than Rachel, but her eyes didn't sparkle, while Rachel was beautiful and had a good figure.
translation_verse: Liya anye le monzomonzo, na Relahyɛle gyi zo sengɔɔnwo, yɛɛ ɔ nwo yɛ fɛ kpalɛ.

english_verse: Since Jacob was in love with Rachel, he answered, “If you will let me marry Rachel, I'll work seven years for you.”
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo kulo Relahyɛle, yemɔti ɔhanle kɛ, “Mesonle wɔ ɛvolɛ nsuu na meagya ɛ ra raalɛ ekyi ne, Relahyɛle.”

english_verse: Laban replied, “It's better for me to let you marry Rachel than for someone else to have her. So stay and work for me.”
translation_verse: Leeban buale kɛ, “Ɔle kpalɛ kɛ menwɔva ye menwɔmaa wɔ tɛla kɛ menwɔva ye menwɔmaa awie gyɛne la. Ɛ nee me ɛdɛnla.”

english_verse: Jacob worked seven years for Laban, but the time seemed like only a few days, because he loved Rachel so much.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Relahyɛle ati, Gyekɔbo zonlenle ɛvolɛ nsuu, noko mekɛ ne yɛle ɔ nye zo kenle kɛyɛ nsa bie, ɔluakɛ ɛnee ɔkulo Relahyɛle kpole kpalɛ.

english_verse: Jacob said to Laban, “The time is up, and I want to marry Rachel now!”
translation_verse: Akee Gyekɔbo zele Leeban kɛ, “Fa me ye ne maa me maa me nee ye ɛhɔla, ɔluakɛ me mekɛ ne ɛdwu.”

english_verse: So Laban gave a big feast and invited all their neighbors.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Leeban dole ɔ sa vɛlɛle menli dɔɔnwo na ɔdole ɛkponle kpole bie wɔ ye awuke nu ɛkɛ.

english_verse: But that evening he brought Leah to Jacob, who married her and spent the night with her.
translation_verse: Noko nɔe ne ɔvale ɔ ra raalɛ Liya a ɔhɔmanle Gyekɔbo a, na Gyekɔbo nee ye lale.

english_verse: The next morning Jacob found out that he had married Leah, and he asked Laban, “Why did you do this to me? Didn't I work to get Rachel? Why did you trick me?”
translation_verse: Na aleɛ hyenle la, Gyekɔbo nwunle kɛ tɛ Relahyɛle ɔ, na Liya ɔ. Gyekɔbo bizale Leeban kɛ, “Na duzu edwɛkɛ a ɛ nee me ɛli la? Meanga kɛ mesonle wɔ meagya Relahyɛle ɔ? Duzu ati yɛɛ wɔbɛlɛbɛla me zɛhae ɛ?”

english_verse: After you spend this week with Leah, you may also marry Rachel. But you will have to work for me another seven years.”
translation_verse: Kendɛ na ɛ nee ɛhye bɛwie bɛ dapɛne ko anyelielɛ ne, na nzinlii yɛanlea na saa ɛkɛzonle me ɛvolɛ nsuu bieko a, meava ɔdaye noko meamaa wɔ.”

english_verse: At the end of the week of celebration, Laban let Jacob marry Rachel, and he gave her his servant woman Bilhah. Jacob loved Rachel more than he did Leah, but he had to work another seven years for Laban.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Gyekɔbo nee ɔdaye noko lale, na ɔhulole Relahyɛle dɔɔnwo ɔdɛlale Liya. Na Relahyɛle ati ɔzonlenle Leeban ɛvolɛ nsuu bieko. Gyekɔbo amra mɔɔ ɔwole bɛ la

english_verse: The Lord knew that Jacob loved Rachel more than he did Leah, and so he gave children to Leah, but not to Rachel.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma nwunle kɛ Gyekɔbo ɛngulo Liya la, ɔmanle ɔ ko lale ɛkɛ, na Relahyɛle yɛle mota.

english_verse: She had a second son and named him Simeon, because she said, “The Lord has heard that my husband doesn't love me.”
translation_verse: Ɔnrenzɛle bieko na eza ɔwole ralɛ nrenya, na ɔzele kɛ, “Kɛmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛnwu kɛ bɛngulo me la ati yɛɛ yemaa me ralɛ nrenya ɛhye noko a;” na ɔdonle ye Semɛyɔn.

english_verse: When Leah's third son was born, she said, “Now my husband will hold me close.” So this son was named Levi.
translation_verse: Ɔnrenzɛle bieko na ɔwole ralɛ nrenya, na ɔzele kɛ, “Kɛkala ɛdeɛ, akee me hu nee me bayɛ ko, ɔboalekɛ mewo mrenya nsa memaa ye.” Yemɔti ɔdonle ye Livae.

english_verse: She had one more son and named him Judah, because she said, “I'll praise the Lord!”
translation_verse: Ɔnrenzɛle bieko na ɔwole ralɛ nrenya na ɔzele kɛ, “Kɛkala ɛdeɛ, mebaye Ɛdɛnkɛma ayɛlɛ.” Yemɔti ɔdonle ye Dwuda. Akee ye awolɛ tikale.

english_verse: Rachel was very jealous of Leah for having children, and she said to Jacob, “I'll die if you don't give me some children!”
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Relahyɛle nwunle kɛ ɔ nee Gyekɔbo anwo la, ɔ nye bolole ɔ diema raalɛ ne, na ɔzele Gyekɔbo kɛ, “Maa menwo mralɛ anrɛɛ menwɔwu.”

english_verse: But Jacob became upset with Rachel and answered, “Don't blame me! I'm not God.”
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo vale Relahyɛle anwo ɛya na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Mele Nyamenle mezɔ wɔ awodeɛ ne anloa kɛ ɛmmawo mralɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: “Here, take my servant Bilhah,” Rachel told him. “Have children by her, and I'll let them be born on my knees to show that they are mine.”
translation_verse: Relahyɛle zele kɛ, “Me sonvolɛ raalɛ Belehaa ɛne, ɛ nee ye ɛla maa ɔwo ralɛ ɔdo me gyakɛ azo, na eza ɔlua ɔ nwo zo meanyia mralɛ.”

english_verse: and they had a son.
translation_verse: Belehaa nrenzɛle na ɔwole ralɛ nrenya ɔmanle Gyekɔbo.

english_verse: Rachel named him Dan, because she said, “God has answered my prayers. He judged in my favor and has given me a son.”
translation_verse: Akee Relahyɛle hanle kɛ, “Nyamenle ɛli me edwɛkɛ ɛmaa me, na yedie me ne, na yemaa me ralɛ nrenya.” Yemɔti ɔdonle ye Dan.

english_verse: When Bilhah and Jacob had a second son,
translation_verse: Relahyɛle sonvolɛ raalɛ Belehaa eza nee Gyekɔbo nrenzɛle na ɔwole ralɛ nrenya bieko.

english_verse: Rachel said, “I've struggled hard with my sister, and I've won!” So she named the boy Naphtali.
translation_verse: Na Relahyɛle hanle kɛ, “Me nee me diema raalɛ ne yɛpele kpole kpalɛ, na meli konim.” Yemɔti ɔdonle ye Nafetalae.

english_verse: When Leah realized she could not have any more children, she let Jacob marry her servant Zilpah,
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Liya nwunle kɛ ye awolɛ ne ɛtika la, ɔvale ye sonvolɛ raalɛ Zelepa ɔmanle Gyekɔbo kɛ ɔ ye ɔ.

english_verse: and they had a son.
translation_verse: Liya sonvolɛ raalɛ Zelepa nee Gyekɔbo wole ralɛ nrenya.

english_verse: “I'm really lucky,” Leah said, and she named the boy Gad.
translation_verse: Na Liya hanle kɛ, “Meyɛ saleɛnli”, yemɔti ɔdonle ye Gaade.

english_verse: When they had another son,
translation_verse: Liya sonvolɛ raalɛ Zelepa eza nee Gyekɔbo wole ralɛ nrenya.

english_verse: Leah exclaimed, “I'm happy now, and all the women will say how happy I am.” So she named him Asher. Love Flowers
translation_verse: Na Liya hanle kɛ, “Fɛlɛko ɛyi me! Ɔluakɛ mraalɛ bavɛlɛ me fɛlɛko;” yemɔti ɔdonle ye Ahya.

english_verse: During the time of the wheat harvest, Reuben found some love flowers and took them to his mother Leah. Rachel asked Leah for some of them,
translation_verse: Mekɛ dwule mɔɔ bɛte hwiiti la, Wulubɛn hɔnwunle baka bie mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye mandileki la wɔ ɛya ne anu, na ɔdudule ɔrɛlɛle ɔ nli Liya. Na Relahyɛle hanle hilele Liya kɛ, “Mebodo wɔ, maa me ɛ ra nrenya ne mandileki ne bie.”

english_verse: but Leah said, “It's bad enough that you stole my husband! Now you want my son's love flowers too.” “All right,” Rachel answered. “Let me have the flowers, and you can sleep with Jacob tonight.”
translation_verse: Liya bizale ye kɛ, “Ɛdwenle kɛ ɔle nzɛmedɛ kɛ wɔza me wɔlie me hu la ɔ? Yeanga ye zɔhane, eza ɛbalie me ra ye mandileki ne noko.” Relahyɛle buale ye kɛ, “Ɛ ra ne mandileki ne ati, ɛnɛ nɔe Gyekɔbo nee wɔ bala.”

english_verse: That evening when Jacob came in from the fields, Leah told him, “You're sleeping with me tonight. I hired you with my son's love flowers.” They slept together that night,
translation_verse: Mɔɔ aleɛ muanle nwolɛ, na Gyekɔbo vi ɛbɔ nu ɛlɛba la, Liya hɔyiale ye adenle na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Ɔwɔ kɛ ɛba me ɛkɛ ne ɛnɛ, ɔluakɛ meva me ra ne mandileki mebɔ wɔ ɛkpa.” Yemɔti ɔ nee ye hɔlale kenle ko ne nɔe ne.

english_verse: and God answered Leah's prayers by giving her a fifth son.
translation_verse: Na Nyamenle diele Liya nzɛlɛlɛ. Ɔnrenzɛle na ɔ nee Gyekɔbo wole ɔ ra nrenya mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nnu la.

english_verse: Leah shouted, “God has rewarded me for letting Jacob marry my servant,” and she named the boy Issachar.
translation_verse: Liya hanle kɛ, “Nyamenle ɛdua me ɛkpabɔdeɛ ne ɛmaa me, ɔluakɛ menvale me sonvolɛ raalɛ ne memanle me hu.” Yemɔti ɔdonle ye Yesakaa.

english_verse: she exclaimed, “God has given me a wonderful gift, and my husband will praise me for giving him six sons.” So she named the boy Zebulun.
translation_verse: Na ɔzele kɛ, “Nyamenle ɛlo me agyalɛ nu ahyɛlɛdeɛ mɔɔ le kpalɛ a. Kɛkala akee me hu bali me eni, ɔboalekɛ mewo mralɛ mrenya nsia memaa ye.” Yemɔti ɔdonle ye Zɛbulɛn.

english_verse: Later, Leah had a daughter and named her Dinah.
translation_verse: Nzinlii ɔwole ralɛ raalɛ na ɔdonle ye Daena.

english_verse: Finally, God remembered Rachel—he answered her prayer by giving her a son. “God has taken away my disgrace,” she said.
translation_verse: Ɔnrenzɛle na ɔwole ralɛ nrenya. Na ɔhanle kɛ, “Nyamenle ɛkpa me nyiane.”

english_verse: “I'll name the boy Joseph, and I'll pray that the Lord will give me another son.” Jacob and Laban
translation_verse: Ɔdonle ye Dwosefi na ɔhanle kɛ, “Mesɛlɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ ɔmaa me ralɛ nrenya bieko.” Gyekɔbo nee Leeban ngyehyɛlɛ ne

english_verse: After Joseph was born, Jacob said to Laban, “Release me from our agreement and let me return to my own country.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Relahyɛle wole Dwosefi la, Gyekɔbo zɛlɛle Leeban kɛ ɔmaa ye adenle ɔmaa ɔhɔ ye sua zo.

english_verse: You know how hard I've worked for you, so let me take my wives and children and leave.”
translation_verse: Ɔzele ye kɛ, “Maa menva me mraalɛ ne mɔ nee me mra ne mɔ, mɔɔ bɛ ti menzonlenle wɔ la mengɔ. Ɛdawɔ ɛze ɛzonlenlɛ mɔɔ meva mezonle wɔ la.”

english_verse: Jacob answered: You've seen how hard I've worked for you, and you know how your flocks and herds have grown under my care.
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo hanle kɛ, “Ɛdawɔ ɛze kɛ mezi mezonle wɔ nee kɛ wɔ nlankɛ nee mboane ɛzi ɛda me mekɛ zo la.

english_verse: You didn't have much before I came, but the Lord has blessed everything I have ever done for you. Now it's time for me to start looking out for my own family.
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ ɛnee wɔ nyɛmoa le ekyi bie yɛɛ membale a, kɛkala bɛ nwo ɛzo dɔɔnwo kpalɛ, yɛɛ medame me ti, Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛyila wɔ wɔ debie biala anu. Na kɛkala menea a akee yedwu mekɛ mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ medwenle me sua nu amra anwo a.”

english_verse: “How much do you want me to pay you?” Laban asked. Then Jacob told him: I don't want you to pay me anything. Just do one thing, and I'll take care of your sheep and goats.
translation_verse: Leeban bizale ye kɛ, “Duzu yɛɛ menva memaa wɔ a?” Gyekɔbo buale ye kɛ, “Menlie debie. Saa ɛkɛyɛ ɛhye ɛkɛmaa me a, anrɛɛ menwɔnlea wɔ mboane ne mɔ bieko.

english_verse: Let me go through your flocks and herds and take the sheep and goats that are either spotted or speckled and the black lambs. That's all you need to give me.
translation_verse: Maa meneɛnlea wɔ mboane ne mɔ anu ɛnɛ demua ye ala, na menye boane anwo ndeta biala nee boane ralɛ anwo bile biala, yɛɛ abɔnkye anwo ndeta biala, na fa bɛmɛ yɛ me ahatualɛ.

english_verse: In the future you can easily find out if I've been honest. Just look and see if my animals are either spotted or speckled, or if the lambs are black. If they aren't, they've been stolen from you.
translation_verse: Ɛhye yɛɛ saa kenle bie ɛkpondɛ me nɔhalɛ a ɔbamaa wɔanwu ye a. Ɛbanleɛnlea mɔɔ wɔva wɔmaa me la anu na abɔnkye biala mɔɔ anwo ɛnle ndeta anzɛɛ boane anzɛɛ boane ralɛ biala mɔɔ anwo ɛnle ndeta anzɛɛ boane ralɛ biala mɔɔ anwo ɛnle bile mɔɔ ɛkɛnwu ye wɔ me mboane nee me mbɔnkye ɛdeɛ ne mɔ anu la kile kɛ menwuale.”

english_verse: “I agree to that,” was Laban's response.
translation_verse: Leeban zele ye kɛ, “Ɔle kpalɛ! Yɛ ye kɛ mɔɔ wɔha la.”

english_verse: Before the end of the day, Laban had separated his spotted and speckled animals and the black lambs from the others and had put his sons in charge of them.
translation_verse: Na kenle ko ne, Leeban yeyele mbɔnkye nyinli nee mbelɛ anwo ndetɛndeta nee mboane mralɛ mɔɔ le bile la ɔmanle ɔ mra mrenya ne mɔ kɛ bɛhɔzie.

english_verse: Then Laban made Jacob keep the rest of the sheep and goats at a distance of three days' journey.
translation_verse: Ɔ nee bɛ hɔle ɛleka mɔɔ saa ɛvi Gyekɔbo anwo ɛkɛ ne ɛkɔ lɔ a bɛtia kenle nsa la. Na Gyekɔbo nleanle Leeban mboane ne mɔɔ hale la.

english_verse: Jacob cut branches from some poplar trees and from some almond and evergreen trees. He peeled off part of the bark and made the branches look spotted and speckled.
translation_verse: Akee Gyekɔbo hɔpɛle “alemɔndo”, “pɔpola”, yɛɛ “pilen” mbaka amolɛ na ɔyeyele bɛ nwo abonle ne bie ndenrɛndenra, ɔmanle mbaka ne mɔ anwo yɛle ndetɛndeta.

english_verse: Then he put the branches where the sheep and goats would see them while they were drinking from the water trough. The goats mated there
translation_verse: Ɔvale mbaka ne mɔ mɔɔ yezunzo nwolɛ abonle ne bie mɔ la ɔhɔguale mboane ne mɔ nee mbɔnkye ne mɔ ahyɛnze anzɛɛ ninyɛne mɔɔ bɛno nu nzule la anu. Ɔyɛle ɛhye, ɔluakɛ saa nyɛmoa ne mɔ ba kɛ bɛbanlo nzule a, yɛɛ bɛfola bɛ nwo a.

english_verse: Some of the sheep that Jacob was keeping for Laban were already spotted. And when the others were ready to mate, he made sure that they faced in the direction of the spotted and black ones. In this way, Jacob built up a flock of sheep for himself and did not put them with the other sheep.
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo yele mboane mralɛ ne mɔ vile mbɔnkye ne mɔ anu na ɔmanle bɛ nye hɔle Leeban nyɛmoa anwo bile nee ndetɛndeta ne mɔ anwo. Ɔyele ye nyɛmoa ɛdeɛ ne ɔvile Leeban ɛdeɛ ne anu. Yeanva bɛ yeambɔ Leeban ɛdeɛ ne anu.

english_verse: When the stronger sheep were mating near the drinking place, Jacob made sure that the spotted branches were there.
translation_verse: Saa ayɛmoa bie mɔɔ anwo yɛ se la ɛlɛnrenzɛ a, Gyekɔbo fa mbaka ne mɔ gua ɛleka mɔɔ ayɛmoa ne mɔ no nzule la, amaa yeawo ndeta.

english_verse: But he would not put out the branches when the weaker animals were mating. So Jacob got all of the healthy animals, and Laban got what was left.
translation_verse: Na saa ayɛmoa ne anwo ɛnyɛ se a, yemɔ ɔnyɛ ye zɔhane. Yemɔti ɛnee nyɛmoa ne mɔ mɔɔ anwo yɛ se la amuala le Gyekɔbo ɛdeɛ, yɛɛ mɔɔ anwo ɛnyɛ se la amuala le Leeban ɛdeɛ.

english_verse: Jacob soon became rich and successful. He owned many sheep, goats, camels, and donkeys, as well as a lot of slaves.
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo yɛle ye zɛhae na ɔnyianle ɔ nwo kpole kpalɛ; ɔnyianle nyɛmoa, sonvolɛ mrenya nee mraalɛ, afunlumu nee asoaso dɔɔnwo.

english_verse: Jacob heard that Laban's sons were complaining, “Jacob is now a rich man, and he got everything he owns from our father.”
translation_verse: Na Gyekɔbo dele kɛ Leeban amra mrenya ne mɔ ɛlɛkeha kɛ, “Gyekɔbo ɛva yɛ ze agyadeɛ ne amuala ɛyɛ ye ɛdeɛ, na yelua yɛ ze anwo zo yenyia ɔ nwo.”

english_verse: Jacob also noticed that Laban was not as friendly as he had been before.
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo eza nwunle kɛ Leeban ɛmbu ye, kɛmɔ alumua ne ɔbu ye la.

english_verse: One day the Lord said, “Jacob, go back to your relatives in the land of your ancestors, and I will be with you.”
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Gyekɔbo kɛ, “Sia kɔ ɛ ze nee ɛ nwo amra sua zo, na me nee wɔ balua.”

english_verse: Jacob sent for Rachel and Leah to meet him in the pasture where he kept his sheep,
translation_verse: Yemɔti Gyekɔbo zoanle manle bɛhɔvale Relahyɛle nee Liya bɛrale ɛya ne mɔɔ ye mboane ne mɔ wɔ nuhua la anu.

english_verse: and he told them: Your father isn't as friendly with me as he used to be, but the God my ancestors worshiped has been on my side.
translation_verse: Ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Menwu kɛ bɛ ze anye ɛnlie me nwo kɛ alumua ne la. Noko me ze mɔ Nyamenle ne nee me lua.

english_verse: years to buy your sheep and goats. During that time you kept changing my wages.
translation_verse: Bɛdabɛ bɛze kɛ meva me anwosesebɛ muala mezonle bɛ ze.

english_verse: and that he keeps cheating me by changing my wages time after time. But God has protected me.
translation_verse: Noko bɛze ɛli me ndunlumi, yehakyi me ahatualɛ ne fane bulu, na Nyamenle ammaa ye adenle yeammaa yeanva ɔ sa yeanga me.

english_verse: When your father said the speckled sheep would be my wages, all of them were speckled. And when he said the spotted ones would be mine, all of them were spotted.
translation_verse: Saa ɔka kɛ, ‘Wɔ ahatualɛ a le nyɛmoa anwo ndetɛndeta ne’ a, ɛnee nyɛmoa ne mɔ ɛlɛwo anwo ndeta; yɛɛ saa ɔka kɛ, ‘Wɔ ahatualɛ a le anwo meɛbea ne’ a, ɛnee nyɛmoa ne mɔ wo anwo meɛbea.

english_verse: That's how God has taken sheep and goats from your father and given them to me.
translation_verse: Zɛhae yɛɛ Nyamenle ɛyɛ ɛlie bɛ ze mboane nee nlankɛ ɛmaa me a.

english_verse: Once, when the flocks were mating, I dreamed that all the rams were either spotted or speckled.
translation_verse: “Mekɛ mɔɔ nyɛmoa ne mɔ fa nrenzɛ la anu, menganle ɛlalɛ, na ɛlalɛ ne anu memanle me nye zo la, menwunle kɛ mbɔnkye nyinli mɔɔ kola fola la amuala le ndeta nee meɛbea.

english_verse: Then God's angel called me by name. I answered,
translation_verse: Na Nyamenle soanvolɛ ne vɛlɛle me, ‘Gyekɔbo!’ Membuale kɛ, ‘Mewɔ ɛke!’

english_verse: and he said, “Notice that all the rams are either spotted or speckled. I know everything Laban is doing to you,
translation_verse: Na ɔzele me kɛ, ‘Maa ɛ nye zo nea nehane. Mbɔnkye nyinli mɔɔ kola fola la amuala le ndeta nee meɛbea, ɔluakɛ menwu mɔɔ Leeban ɛlɛfa ayɛ wɔ la amuala.

english_verse: and I am the God you worshiped at Bethel, when you poured olive oil on a rock and made a promise to me. Leave here at once and return to the land where you were born.”
translation_verse: Mame a mele Bɛtɛle, ɛleka mɔɔ ɛkpɔnlanle bolɛ sika ne, ɛguale nwole zolɛ, ɛbɔle me ɛwɔkɛ ne la Nyamenle ne. Dwazo, ɛvi maanle ɛhye anu tu, na sia kɔ azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ bɛwole wɔ zolɛ la azo.’ ”

english_verse: He treats us like foreigners and has even cheated us out of the bride price that should have been ours.
translation_verse: Ɔbu yɛ kɛ yɛle nyɛvolɛ, ɔluakɛ yedɔne yɛ, yɛɛ ezukoa biala mɔɔ bɛkɛva bɛkɛmaa ye mɔɔ le yɛ ɛdeɛ la ɛnee yeva yebɔ ɔ nwo.

english_verse: So do whatever God tells you to do. Even the property God took from our father and gave to you really belongs to us and our children.
translation_verse: Agyadeɛ ɛhye mɔ amuala mɔɔ Nyamenle ɛlie ɛvi yɛ ze asa anu la le yɛ nee yɛ mra ɛdeɛ. Yemɔti kɛkala, yɛ mɔɔ Nyamenle ɛze wɔ la.”

english_verse: Before Rachel left, she stole the household idols while Laban was out shearing his sheep.
translation_verse: Ɛnee Leeban ɛhɔ kɛ ɔkapepɛ ye mboane nwo enrinli, na Relahyɛle wuale ɔ ze sua nu mmonle ne mɔ.

english_verse: long years to earn your two daughters and another
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo anga angile Leeban kɛ ɔwɔ ye adwenle nu kɛ ɔbanriandi.

english_verse: When Jacob crossed the Euphrates River and headed for the hill country of Gilead, he took with him everything he owned. Laban Catches Up with Jacob
translation_verse: Na ɔvale ye debie biala ɔnriandile. Ɔpɛle Azule Yufileti ne na ɔbɔle ɔ ti Geleade maanle nu awoka ne mɔ azo. Leeban foa Gyekɔbo

english_verse: Three days later Laban found out that Jacob had gone.
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo nriandile la, ye kenle nsa yɛɛ bɛhɔbɔle Leeban amaneɛ a.

english_verse: So he took some of his relatives along and chased after Jacob for seven days, before catching up with him in the hill country of Gilead.
translation_verse: Leeban vale ɔ nwo amra na bɛdinle Gyekɔbo toonwo kenle nsuu na bɛkpumgbunle ye wɔ Geleade maanle nu awoka ne mɔ anu.

english_verse: But God appeared to Laban in a dream that night and warned, “Don't say a word to Jacob. Don't make a threat or a promise.”
translation_verse: Na Nyamenle rale Arelamenli Leeban anwo nɔɔzo wɔ ɛlalɛ nu na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Nea boɛ na wɔanga edwɛkɛ biala, kpalɛ o, ɛtane o, wɔangile Gyekɔbo.”

english_verse: Jacob had set up camp in the hill country of Gilead, when Laban and his relatives came and set up camp in another part of the hill country. Laban went to Jacob
translation_verse: Na Leeban hɔdole Gyekɔbo. Ɛnee Gyekɔbo ɛyɛ ye azokoɛleɛ wɔ awoka ne mɔ anu, na Leeban ɔdaye ɔ nee ɔ nwo amra bɛrayɛle bɛ azokoɛleɛ wɔ Geleade awoka ne mɔ anu.

english_verse: and said: Look what you've done! You've tricked me and run off with my daughters like a kidnapper.
translation_verse: Leeban bizale Gyekɔbo kɛ, “Duzu debie a wɔyɛ la, kɛ wɔbɛlɛbɛla me, na wɔva me mra mraalɛ ne mɔ ɛlɛkɔ kɛ menli mɔɔ bɛhye bɛ nuokɛ wɔ konle nu a?

english_verse: Why did you sneak away without telling me? I would have given you a going-away party with singing and with music on tambourines and harps.
translation_verse: Duzu ati a ɛbɛlɛbɛlale me, ɛveale ɛ nwo ɛnriandile, na wɔanga wɔangile me, wɔammaa meanva anyelielɛ, edwɛndolɛ, aweɛne, nee getaa ɛbɔlɛ meangyakyi wɔ adenle a?

english_verse: You didn't even give me a chance to kiss my own grandchildren and daughters goodbye. That was really foolish.
translation_verse: Na duzu ati bɔbɔ yɛɛ wɔammaa meanvo me nlɔnra nee me mra mraalɛ ne mɔ anvoka anwo, me nee bɛ anli nrɛlaleɛ ɛ? Mɔɔ wɔyɛ la, wɔanyɛ ye boɛ fee.

english_verse: I could easily hurt you, but the God your father worshiped has warned me not to make any threats or promises.
translation_verse: Anrɛɛ mekola me nee wɔ di ye pɛsɛɛ, na ɛ ze Nyamenle ne dendɛle hilele me nɔe kɛ, ‘Nea boɛ na wɔanga edwɛkɛ biala, kpalɛ o, ɛtane o, wɔangile Gyekɔbo.’

english_verse: I can understand why you were eager to return to your father, but why did you have to steal my idols?
translation_verse: Kɛmɔ ɛ nwo ɛlɛdɔ ɛ ze sua nu la ati yɛɛ ɛlɛkɔ a, na duzu ati a ɛwuale me mmonle ne mɔ ɛ?”

english_verse: Jacob answered, “I left secretly because I was afraid you would take your daughters from me by force.
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo buale kɛ, “Ɛnee medwenle kɛ ɛbaza me wɔalie ɛ mra mraalɛ ne mɔ, yemɔti menzulole.

english_verse: If you find that any one of us has taken your idols, I'll have that person killed. Let your relatives be witnesses. Show me what belongs to you, and you can take it back.” Jacob did not realize that Rachel had stolen the household idols.
translation_verse: Awie mɔɔ ɛkɛnwu wɔ mmonle ne mɔ wɔ ye ɛkɛ ne la, bava ye ngoane adua. Yɛ nwo amra a ɛbɔ yɛ ɛyia la; debie biala mɔɔ le wɔ ɛdeɛ na ɛkɛnwu ye me ninyɛne ye anu la, ka na fa.” Ɛnee Gyekɔbo ɛnze kɛ Relahyɛle yɛɛ ɛwua mmonle ne a.

english_verse: Laban searched the tents of Jacob, Leah, and the two servant women, but did not find the idols. Then he went to Rachel's tent.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Leeban wolole Gyekɔbo ndanlɛ sua ne anu, ɔhɔle Liya ndanlɛ sua ne anu, ɔhɔle sonvolɛ mraalɛ nwiɔ ne ndanlɛ sua ne mɔ anu na yeannwu ɛhwee. Akee ɔvi Liya ndanlɛ sua ne anu ɔvindele ɔhɔwolole Relahyɛle ndanlɛ sua ɛdeɛ ne anu.

english_verse: She had already hidden them in the cushion she used as a saddle and was sitting on it. Laban searched everywhere and did not find them.
translation_verse: Relahyɛle sesale awuke ne anu mmonle ne mɔ la, ɔvale bɛ ɔguale ebia mɔɔ bɛfa bɛsie afunlumu nwo zo bɛtɛnla zolɛ la anu na ɔdɛnlanle zolɛ. Leeban nleɛnleanle ndanlɛ sua ne anu ɛleka biala, na yeannwu ye mmonle ne.

english_verse: Rachel said, “Father, please don't be angry with me for not getting up; I'm having my period.” Laban kept on searching, but still did not find the idols.
translation_verse: Ɔradwule Relahyɛle anwo ɛkɛ ne la, Relahyɛle hanle hilele ye kɛ, “Egya mmafa ɛya kɛ yera me nwo na menrɛdwazo a, ɔboalekɛ mebu me sa.” Yemɔti Leeban nleɛnleanle ɛkɛ ne amuala, na yeannwu mmonle ne mɔ.

english_verse: Jacob became very angry and said to Laban: What have I done wrong? Have I committed some crime? Is that why you hunted me down?
translation_verse: Akee Gyekɔbo vale ɛya na ɔhwile Leeban anyunlu; ɔzele ye kɛ, “Duzu ɛtane a meyɛ a? Duzu munzule yɛɛ mebɔ, mɔɔ yemɔti wɔvoa me ndinlizo a?

english_verse: After searching through everything I have, did you find anything of yours? If so, put it here, where your relatives and mine can see it. Then we can decide what to do.
translation_verse: Wɔnleɛnlea me ninyɛne ne mɔ amuala anu wɔwie, duzu debie yɛɛ wɔnwu ye nu mɔɔ le wɔ ɛdeɛ a? Mɔɔ wɔnwu ye la fa finde ɛke maa yɛ nwo amra ye ɛli nwolɛ daselɛ na bɛha mɔɔ bɛka la bɛhile yɛ.

english_verse: If a wild animal killed one of your sheep or goats, I paid for it myself. In fact, you demanded the full price, whether the animal was killed during the day or at night.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ nanemgbole hyele ye hunle ye bɔbɔ la, meanva ye funli meambɛlɛ wɔ, mefa bie mesie ɔ bo zo. Saa bɛwua bie ewiazo anzɛɛ nɔɔzo a, ɛdie bie ɛfi me ɛkɛ ne.

english_verse: I sweated every day, and I couldn't sleep at night because of the cold.
translation_verse: Ewia bɔ me alehyenlɛ nu, ɛyɛlɛ ku me nɔɔzo, me nye ɛnze nafelɛ.

english_verse: If the fearsome God worshiped by Abraham and my father Isaac had not been on my side, you would have sent me away without a thing. But God saw my hard work, and he knew the trouble I was in, so he helped me. Then last night he told you how wrong you were. Jacob and Laban Make an Agreement
translation_verse: Saa tɛ me ze Nyamenle ne, Ebileham Nyamenle ne, yɛɛ Ayezeke Ɛzulolɛ ne mɔɔ gyi me nzi la a, anrɛɛ nɔhalɛ, wɔmaa melɛ me sa mgbane mezia mehɔ. Nyamenle nwunle me amaneɛnwunlɛ nee ɛvɛlɛ mɔɔ mevɛ la ati yɛɛ nɔe ɔhwile ɛ nyunlu a.” Gyekɔbo nee Leeban ngyehyɛlɛ ne

english_verse: Laban said to Jacob, “Leah and Rachel are my daughters, and their children belong to me. All these sheep you are taking are really mine too. In fact, everything you have belongs to me. But there is nothing I can do to keep my daughters and their children.
translation_verse: Akee Leeban zele Gyekɔbo kɛ, “Ngakula mraalɛ ne mɔ le me mra, ngakula ne mɔ le me ngakula, mboane ne mɔ le me mboane, yɛɛ debie biala mɔɔ ɛnwu ye ɛke la le me ɛdeɛ. Noko kɛkala menlɛ edwɛkɛ biala menga wɔ me mra mraalɛ ne mɔ anzɛɛ bɛ kunlu mralɛ mɔɔ bɛwo bɛ la anwo.

english_verse: So I am ready to make an agreement with you, and we will pile up some large rocks here to remind us of the agreement.”
translation_verse: Yemɔti maa yɛyɛ ngyehyɛlɛ yɛhye ɔ bo, mɔɔ kyekye wɔ nee medame a, na ɔyɛ daselɛ ɔgyinla yɛ mu nwiɔ yɛ avinli.”

english_verse: After Jacob had set up a large rock,
translation_verse: Na Gyekɔbo vale bolɛ kpɔnlanle ye sika.

english_verse: he told his men to get some more rocks and pile them up next to it. Then Jacob and Laban ate a meal together beside the rocks.
translation_verse: Akee ɔzele ɔ nwo amra ne mɔ kɛ, “Bɛsesa awolɛ bɛhua ye edukue.” Na bɛsesale awolɛ bɛhuanle ye edukue na bɛlile debie wɔ awolɛ edukue ne anwo.

english_verse: Laban named the pile of rocks Jegar Sahadutha. But Jacob named it Galeed.
translation_verse: Leeban donle ye Gyigaa Seehaduta, na Gyekɔbo donle ye Geelide.

english_verse: Laban said to Jacob, “This pile of rocks will remind us of our agreement.” That's why the place was named Galeed.
translation_verse: Leeban zele kɛ, “Ɛnɛ, awolɛ edukue ɛhye le daselɛ wɔ yɛ mu nwiɔ yɛ avinli.” Yemɔti bɛvɛlɛle awolɛ edukue ne Geelide,

english_verse: Laban also said, “This pile of rocks means that the Lord will watch us both while we are apart from each other.” So the place was also named Mizpah.
translation_verse: na bɛvɛlɛle bolɛ sika ne Mezepa. Na Leeban hanle kɛ, “Saa yɛ mu nwiɔ yɛkpakye a, Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛzinza wɔ nee medame.

english_verse: Then Laban said: If you mistreat my daughters or marry other women, I may not know about it, but remember, God is watching us!
translation_verse: Saa ɛkile me mra mraalɛ ne mɔ nyane anzɛɛ ɛgyakyi bɛ ɛkɛ ɛgya mraalɛ gyɛne a, kakye kɛ awie ɛngyi yɛ mu nwiɔ yɛ avinli bɔbɔ ɛdeɛ, noko Nyamenle di yɛ mu nwiɔ daselɛ.

english_verse: Both this pile of rocks and this large rock have been set up between us as a reminder. I must never go past them to attack you, and you must never come past them to attack me.
translation_verse: Awolɛ edukue ne le daselɛ yɛɛ bolɛ sika ne le daselɛ, kɛ menrɛbɔ menrɛdɛla edukue ɛhye menrɛra ɛ nwo zo, yɛɛ ɛdawɔ noko ɛnrɛbɔ ɛnrɛdɛla edukue ne nee bolɛ sika ne ɛnrɛra me nwo zo kɛ ɛbayɛ me ɛtane.

english_verse: My father Nahor, your grandfather Abraham, and their ancestors all worshiped the same God, and he will make sure that we each keep the agreement. Then Jacob made a promise in the name of the fearsome God his father Isaac had worshiped.
translation_verse: Ebileham Nyamenle ne, Neehɔ Nyamenle ne, bɛ ze mɔ Nyamenle ne ɛli yɛ daselɛ.” Yemɔti Gyekɔbo ɔdaye ɔvale ɔ ze Ayezeke Ɛzulolɛ ne ɔhanle ndane.

english_verse: Jacob killed an animal and offered it as a sacrifice there on the mountain, and he invited his men to eat with him. After the meal they spent the night on the mountain.
translation_verse: Akee Gyekɔbo bɔle azu wɔ boka ne azo, na ɔvɛlɛle ɔ nwo amra ne kɛ bɛrakpula bɛ sa. Bɛlile debie, na bɛlale boka ne azo kenle ko ne nɔe ne.

english_verse: Early the next morning, Laban kissed his daughters and his grandchildren goodbye, then he left to go back home.
translation_verse: Aleɛ hyenle nwonlomɔ mangyee ne la, Leeban dwazole, ɔvole ɔ mra mraalɛ nwiɔ ne nee ye nlɔnra ne mɔ anvoka anwo ɔ nee bɛ lile nrɛlaleɛ; ɔyileyilale bɛ na ɔziale ɔhɔle ye sua zo.

english_verse: As Jacob was on his way back home, some of God's angels came and met him.
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo zɔle ye adendulɛ ne azo, na ɔkɔ la ɔ nee Nyamenle soanvolɛma yiale.

english_verse: When Jacob saw them, he said, “This is God's camp.” So he named the place Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo nwunle bɛ la ɔhanle kɛ, “Nyamenle ɛlɔnema ɛne!” Yemɔti ɔvɛlɛle ɛleka ne Meehaneeyem.

english_verse: Jacob sent messengers on ahead to Esau, who lived in the land of Seir, also known as Edom.
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo zoanle menli manle bɛlumuale ɔ nyunlu wɔ ɔ diema Yisɔ anwo lɔ wɔ Siyɛ azɛlɛ zo, wɔ Yidɔm maanle nu.

english_verse: Jacob told them to say to Esau, “Master, I am your servant! I have lived with Laban all this time,
translation_verse: Ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛhɔha bɛhile me menle Yisɔ kɛ, medame ye akɛlɛ Gyekɔbo, mengɔle Leeban anwo lɔ, na nehane a mewɔ toonwo mɔɔ yeradwu bekezɛ a.

english_verse: and now I own cattle, donkeys, and sheep, as well as many slaves. Master, I am sending these messengers in the hope that you will be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Melɛ nlankɛ, asoaso, mboane nee mbɔnkye, yɛɛ sonvolɛ mraalɛ nee mrenya. Na mezoa bɛ kɛ bɛraha bɛhile ye, amaa yealie me gyɛlɛɛnye.”

english_verse: When the messengers returned, they told Jacob, “We went to your brother Esau, and now he is heading this way with
translation_verse: Menli mɔɔ ɔzoanle bɛ la hɔle rale na bɛrahanle bɛhilele Gyekɔbo kɛ, “Yɛhɔdole ɛ diema Yisɔ, ɔlɛba yearayia wɔ, na menli ɛya nna li ɔ nzi.”

english_verse: He thought, “If Esau attacks one group, perhaps the other can escape.”
translation_verse: na ɔdwenlenle nwolɛ kɛ, “Saa Yisɔ nee bɛ yia na ɔbɔ ekpunli ko abo zo a, ekpunli ko ne mɔɔ ɛha la banriandi.”

english_verse: Then Jacob prayed: You, Lord, are the God who was worshiped by my grandfather Abraham and by my father Isaac. You told me to return home to my family, and you promised to be with me and make me successful.

translation_verse: Akee ɔzele Gyekɔbo kɛ, “Gyakyi me maa mengɔ, na aleɛ ɛlɛkye.” Gyekɔbo hanle kɛ, “Menrɛgyakyi wɔ menrɛmaa ɛnrɛhɔ, kyesɛ ɛyila me.”

english_verse: Then the man asked, “What is your name?” “Jacob,” he answered.
translation_verse: Nrenya ne bizale Gyekɔbo kɛ, “Kɛ bɛfɛlɛ wɔ ɛ?” Ɔbuale kɛ, “Bɛfɛlɛ me Gyekɔbo.”

english_verse: The man said, “From now on, your name will no longer be Jacob. You will be called Israel, because you have wrestled with God and with men, and you have won.”
translation_verse: Nrenya ne zele kɛ, “Bɛnrɛvɛlɛ wɔ Gyekɔbo bieko, bɛbavɛlɛ wɔ Yizilayɛ ɔluakɛ ɛ nee Nyamenle nee menli ɛpele, na wɔli konim.”

english_verse: Jacob said, “Now tell me your name.” “Don't you know who I am?” he asked. And he blessed Jacob.
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo bizale ye kɛ, “Mebodo wɔ, bɔ wɔ duma kile me.” Nrenya ne bizale ye kɛ, “Duzu ati yɛɛ ɛbiza me duma a?” Akee ɔyilale Gyekɔbo.

english_verse: The sun was coming up as Jacob was leaving Peniel. He was limping because he had been struck on the hip,
translation_verse: Mɔɔ sɛnzɛne ne dudule la yɛɛ Gyekɔbo vi Pɛneɛle dule ɔ bo a, na ɛnee ye ɛzɔlɛ ne ati ɔtia ɔtɔ zo.

english_verse: and the muscle on his hip joint had been injured. That's why even today the people of Israel don't eat the hip muscle of any animal.
translation_verse: Yemɔti ɛnɛ nee ɛnɛ, Yizilayɛma ɛnli adwongu ndinli ne mɔɔ zɔ bowule ne mɔɔ wɔ ɛzɔlɛ ne anu la, ɔboalekɛ nrenya ne vale ɔ sa hanle Gyekɔbo adwongu ndinli ne.

english_verse: The two servant women, Zilpah and Bilhah, together with their children went first, followed by Leah and her children, then by Rachel and Joseph.
translation_verse: Ɔmanle ye sonvolɛ mraalɛ nwiɔ ne nee bɛ mra ne mɔ lumuale, Liya nee ɔ mra ne mɔ doa bɛ, yɛɛ Relahyɛle nee Dwosefi li bɛ nzi.

english_verse: Jacob himself walked in front of them all, bowing to the ground seven times as he came near his brother.
translation_verse: Ɔdaye mumua ne ɔzenle ɔlile bɛ nyunlu, na mɔɔ ɔbikyele ɔ diema Yisɔ la, ɔvale ɔ nyunlu ɔbutule aze fane nsuu kolaa na yeahɔdo ɔ diema ne.

english_verse: But Esau ran toward Jacob and hugged and kissed him. Then the two brothers started crying.
translation_verse: Na Yisɔ nriandile rayiale ye, yɛle ye atuu, ɔbɛkale ɔ kɔme na ɔvole ɔ nvoka anwo, na bɛ mu nwiɔ bɛzunle.

english_verse: When Esau noticed the women and children he asked, “Whose children are these?” Jacob answered, “These are the children the Lord has been kind enough to give to me, your servant.”
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Yisɔ manle ɔ nye zo na ɔnwunle mraalɛ ne mɔ nee ngakula ne mɔ la, ɔbizale Gyekɔbo kɛ, “Nwane mɔ a le ɛhye mɔ mɔɔ ɛ nee bɛ lua la?” Gyekɔbo buale kɛ, “Ngakula ɛhye mɔ a Nyamenle ɛlolɛ nu yeva yemaa wɔ sonvolɛ a.”

english_verse: Then the two servant women and their children came and bowed down to Esau.
translation_verse: Akee ye sonvolɛ mraalɛ ne nee bɛ mra ne mɔ rabɔle bɛ ti aze manle Yisɔ;

english_verse: Next, Leah and her children came and bowed down; finally, Joseph and Rachel also came and bowed down.
translation_verse: Liya nee ɔ mra ne mɔ yɛle ye zɔhane ala, yɛɛ akee Dwosefi nee Relahyɛle bɛdabɛ noko bɛrabɔle bɛ ti aze bɛmanle Yisɔ.

english_verse: Esau asked Jacob, “Why did you send those herds I met along the road?” “Master,” Jacob answered, “I sent them so you would be friendly to me.”
translation_verse: Yisɔ bizale ye kɛ, “Na ekpunli ɛhendeɛ ne mɔ mɔɔ me nee bɛ yiale la abo a le duzu?” Gyekɔbo buale kɛ, “Bɛle me menle ɛdeɛ, amaa meazɔ ɛ nye.”

english_verse: “But, brother, I already have plenty,” Esau replied. “Keep them for yourself.”
translation_verse: Yisɔ zele ye kɛ, “Me diema, mɔɔ melɛ la zonle, yemɔti maa ɔwɔ ɛkɛ. Fa wɔ debie.”

english_verse: “No!” Jacob said. “Please accept them as a sign of your friendship for me. When you welcomed me and I saw your face, it was like seeing the face of God.
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo buale kɛ, “Kyɛkyɛ, mebodo mesɛlɛ wɔ, saa mezɔ ɛ nye ɛdeɛ a, ɛnee die me ahyɛlɛdeɛ ne. Ɔluakɛ ɛ nyunlu mɔɔ menwu, nee ɛ nye mɔɔ mezɔ la le kɛ menwu Nyamenle.

english_verse: Please accept these as gifts I brought to you. God has been good to me, and I have everything I need.” Jacob kept insisting until Esau agreed.
translation_verse: Mebodo mesɛlɛ wɔ, die me ahyɛlɛdeɛ ne mɔɔ meva merɛlɛ wɔ la, ɔboalekɛ Nyamenle ɛlo me kpole, yɛɛ mɔɔ melɛ la zonle.” Gyekɔbo hanle toonwo manle Yisɔ liele ahyɛlɛdeɛ ne.

english_verse: “Let's get ready to travel,” Esau said. “I'll go along with you.”
translation_verse: Akee Yisɔ zele Gyekɔbo kɛ, “Maa yɛzɔ yɛ adendulɛ ne azo. Mebalumua na bɛadoa me.”

english_verse: But Jacob answered, “Master, you know traveling is hard on children, and I have to look after the sheep and goats that are nursing their young. If my animals travel too much in one day, they will all die.
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo buale kɛ, “Me menle ɔdaye ɔze kɛ ngakula ne mɔ anwo ɛnyɛ se, yɛɛ eza ɔwɔ kɛ menea nlankɛ nee mboane mralɛ ne mɔ mɔɔ no nyɛfonlɛ la. Saa bɛtia kpole bɛmaa ɔbo zolɛ a, bɛ muala bɛbawie wu.

english_verse: Why don't you go on ahead and let me travel along slowly with the children, the herds, and the flocks. We can meet again in the country of Edom.”
translation_verse: Mesɛlɛ wɔ, dumua na medame noko mebayɛ ye bɛtɛbɛtɛ, kɛmɔ nyɛmoa ne mɔ nee ngakula ne mɔ anwosesebɛ si de la, na me nee bɛ ara ɛ nwo lɔ wɔ Yidɔm.”

english_verse: Esau replied, “Let me leave some of my men with you.” “You don't have to do that,” Jacob answered. “I am happy, simply knowing that you are friendly to me.”
translation_verse: Yisɔ zele ye kɛ, “Ɛnee maa mengyakyi me menli ye mɔ bie ɛ nwo ɛke.” Gyekɔbo buale kɛ, “Saa ɛ kunlu ɛdwo me nwo ɛdeɛ a, ɛnee noko ɛhye mɔ ɛngyia biala.”

english_verse: So Esau left for Edom.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Yisɔ ziale hɔle Yidɔm kenle ko ne ala.

english_verse: But Jacob went to Succoth, where he built a house for himself and set up shelters for his animals. That's why the place is called Succoth. Jacob Arrives at Shechem
translation_verse: Na Gyekɔbo vale ɔ ti bɔle Sɛko adenle zo. Ɔzile sua ɔlale nu na ɔsisile kpɔda ɔmanle ye nlankɛ ne mɔ. Ɛhye ati bɛfɛlɛ ɛkɛ ne Sɛko.

english_verse: After leaving northern Syria, Jacob arrived safely at Shechem in Canaan and set up camp outside the city.
translation_verse: Na Gyekɔbo dwule suakpole Hyikɛm azo anzonudwolɛ nu, wɔ Keena azɛlɛ zo. Ɔvi Mɛsɔpɔteemea a ɔradwule ɛkɛ ne a. Ɔyɛle ye azokoɛleɛ wɔ suakpole ne kandiba.

english_verse: The land where he camped was owned by the descendants of Hamor, the father of Shechem. So Jacob paid them
translation_verse: Ɔdɔle azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ ɔdɛnlanle zolɛ la dwɛtɛ fufule ɛya ko ɔvile Hyikɛm ɔ ze Heemɔ abo zo amra ne mɔ lɔ.

english_verse: then he set up his tents and built an altar there to honor the God of Israel.
translation_verse: Ɔzile azukponle wɔ ɛkɛ ne na ɔdonle ye Ɛle-Ɛlohee Yizilayɛ.

english_verse: Dinah, the daughter of Jacob and Leah, went to visit some of the women who lived nearby.
translation_verse: Kenle ko Daena, Gyekɔbo nee ɔ ye Liya ara raalɛ ne, hɔle sua zo kɛ ɔkakpɔlɔkpɔla mraalɛ mɔɔ wɔ ɛkɛ ne la.

english_verse: She was seen by Hamor's son Shechem, the leader of the Hivites, and he grabbed her and raped her.
translation_verse: Haevaenli Heemɔ, mɔɔ di belemgbunli wɔ sua ne azo la ara Hyikɛm nwunle ye la, ɔhyele ye mialera nu ɔ nee ye lale, ɔguale ɔ nyunlu aze.

english_verse: But Shechem was attracted to Dinah, so he told her how much he loved her.
translation_verse: Na Hyikɛm ahonle vale Gyekɔbo ara Daena. Ɔhulole ye na ɔdendɛle bɛtɛɛ ɔhilele ye.

english_verse: Shechem even asked his father to arrange for him to marry her.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Hyikɛm hanle hilele ɔ ze Heemɔ kɛ, “Gya bɛlɛra ɛhye maa me.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, Jacob heard what had happened. But his sons were out in the fields with the cattle, so he did not do anything at the time.
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo dele kɛ bɛgua ɔ ra raalɛ ne anyunlu aze, noko kɛmɔ ɛnee ɔ mra mrenya ne mɔ wɔ namule nu ɛlɛnea ye nlankɛ ne mɔ la ati, yeanga ɛhwee toonwo ɔhɔkpulale mekɛ mɔɔ bɛrale la.

english_verse: just as Jacob's sons were coming in from work. When they learned that their sister had been raped, they became furiously angry, because nothing is more disgraceful than rape, and it must not be tolerated.
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo amra mrenya ne mɔ dele edwɛkɛ ne la, bɛziale bɛrale sua zo. Bɛvale ɛya na bɛyɛle kɛ bɛnrɛkponle, ɔboalekɛ yebɔ munzule wɔ Yizilayɛ kɛ ɔ nee Gyekɔbo ara raalɛ ɛla a. Ɔnle kɛ debie zɛhae si Yizilayɛ maanle nu fee.

english_verse: Hamor said to Jacob and his sons: My son Shechem really loves Dinah. Please let him marry her.
translation_verse: Noko Heemɔ nee bɛ dendɛle na ɔzele kɛ, “Me ra Hyikɛm ahonle ɛva bɛ ra raalɛ ne somaa. Mebodo bɛ, bɛva ye bɛmaa ɔgya.

english_verse: Why don't you start letting your families marry into our families and ours marry into yours?
translation_verse: Bɛragya yɛ bie mɔ na bɛdabɛ noko bɛmaa yɛgya bɛ bie mɔ.

english_verse: You can share this land with us. Move freely about until you find the property you want; then buy it and settle down here.
translation_verse: Bɛ nee yɛ ɛdɛnla, na azɛlɛ ne ɛla ɛkɛ ne ɛmaa bɛ. Bɛdɛnla zolɛ na bɛli bɛ gua, bɛnyia agyadeɛ dɔɔnwo.”

english_verse: Ask anything, no matter how expensive. I'll do anything, just let me marry Dinah.”
translation_verse: Bɛva bɛlɛra ne bɛmaa mengya ye na debie biala mɔɔ agyalɛ ne ati bɛkɛbiza, nee ahyɛlɛdeɛ biala mɔɔ fɛta la, menwɔva menwɔmaa bɛ.”

english_verse: Jacob's sons wanted to get even with Shechem and his father because of what had happened to their sister.
translation_verse: Kɛmɔ ɛnee Hyikɛm ɛgua bɛ diema raalɛ Daena anyunlu aze la ati, Gyekɔbo amra mrenya ne mɔ liele Hyikem nee ɔ ze Heemɔ ɛdwɛkɛ ne dole nu egyele zo.

english_verse: So they tricked them by saying: You're not circumcised! It would be a disgrace for us to let you marry Dinah now.
translation_verse: Bɛzele Hyikɛm nee ɔ ze Heemɔ kɛ, “Yɛnrɛhola yɛnrɛva yɛ diema raalɛ yɛnrɛmaa nrenya mɔɔ ɛtɛyɛle ye mrenyanu nzonlɛ la. Ɔle anyiemgba ɔmaa yɛ.

english_verse: But we will let you marry her, if you and the other men in your tribe agree to be circumcised.
translation_verse: Yemɔti saa bɛkɛyɛ kɛ yɛdayɛ la, na bɛ mrenya ne mɔ kɛyɛ bɛ mrenyanu nzonlɛ ɛdeɛ a, yemɔ yɛkɛkponle zolɛ.

english_verse: Then your families can marry into ours, and ours can marry into yours, and we can live together like one nation.
translation_verse: Yɛkɛkponle zolɛ yɛkɛmaa bɛkɛgya yɛ mra mraalɛ na yɛdayɛ noko yɛagya bɛ mra mraalɛ ne mɔ bie, na yɛ nee bɛ adɛnla yɛayɛ menli ko.

english_verse: But if you don't agree to be circumcised, we'll take Dinah and leave this place.
translation_verse: Na saa bɛnrɛkponle, bɛnrɛyɛ bɛ mrenyanu nzonlɛ ɛdeɛ a, yɛbarava kakula raalɛ ne na yɛahɔ.”

english_verse: Hamor and Shechem liked what was said.
translation_verse: Mgbavolɛ ne mɔ edwɛkɛ ne zɔle Heemɔ nee ɔ ra Hyikɛm anye.

english_verse: Shechem was the most respected person in his family, and he was so in love with Dinah that he hurried off to get everything done.
translation_verse: Na Hyikɛm angyinla nwolɛ fee, ɔboalekɛ ɔ nye die Gyekɔbo ara raalɛ ne anwo. Hyikɛm le sonla mɔɔ bɛdi ye eni kpalɛ wɔ bɛ abusua ne anu a.

english_verse: These people really are friendly. Why not let them move freely about until they find the property they want? There's enough land here for them and for us. Then our families can marry into theirs, and theirs can marry into ours.
translation_verse: “Menli ɛhye mɔ le agɔnwolɛma. Bɛmaa bɛ adenle bɛmaa bɛdɛnla azɛlɛ ye azo na bɛli bɛ gua, ɔluakɛ azɛlɛ ye le kpole maa bɛ. Bɛmaa yɛgya bɛ mra ne mɔ bie na bɛdabɛ noko bɛgya yɛ mra mraalɛ ne mɔ bie.

english_verse: We have to do only one thing before they will agree to stay here and become one nation with us. Our men will have to be circumcised just like theirs.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ menli ɛhye mɔ kpondɛ na bɛadɛnla yɛ avinli bɛ nee yɛ ayɛ ko la a le kɛ, yɛ mrenya ne mɔ, ko biala kɛyɛ ye mrenyanu nzonlɛ, kɛmɔ bɛyɛ bɛ ɛdeɛ ne la.

english_verse: Just think! We'll get their property, as well as their flocks and herds. All we have to do is to agree, and they will live here with us.
translation_verse: Yɛyɛ ye zɔhane a bɛ nlankɛ, bɛ agyadeɛ nee bɛ nyɛmoa ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti bayɛ yɛ ɛdeɛ. Bɛmaa yɛkponle zolɛ yɛmaa bɛ na bɛ nee yɛ ɛdɛnla.”

english_verse: Three days later the men who had been circumcised were still weak from pain. So Simeon and Levi, two of Dinah's brothers, attacked with their swords and killed every man in the town,
translation_verse: Ye kenle nsa ne azo mɔɔ ɛnee bɛ nganlɛ ne mɔ ɛlɛfofo bɛ la, Gyekɔbo amra ne mɔ anu nwiɔ, Semɛyɔn nee Livae, Daena amediema mrenya ne mɔ, vale bɛ dadeɛ na bɛhɔle bɛ nwo zo wɔ suakpole ne azo arɛlevilɛ nu, na bɛhunle mrenya mɔɔ wɔ sua ne azo la amuala.

english_verse: including Hamor and Shechem. Then they took Dinah and left.
translation_verse: Bɛhunle Heemɔ nee ɔ ra Hyikɛm noko, na bɛvale Daena bɛvile Hyikɛm sua nu ɛkɛ ne bɛhɔle.

english_verse: Jacob's other sons came and took everything they wanted. All this was done because of the horrible thing that had happened to their sister.
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo amra mrenya mɔɔ hale la rale menli mɔɔ bɛhu bɛ la avinli, na bɛwuale suakpole ne azo debie biala, ɔboalekɛ bɛgua bɛ diema raalɛ ne anyunlu aze.

english_verse: They took sheep, goats, donkeys, and everything else that was in the town or the countryside.
translation_verse: Bɛvale bɛ nyɛmoa, bɛ nlankɛ, bɛ asoaso, yɛɛ debie biala mɔɔ wɔ suakpole ne azo, nee bɛ ɛya avule ne mɔ anu la amuala;

english_verse: After taking everything of value from the houses, they dragged away the wives and children of their victims.
translation_verse: bɛ anwonyia muala, bɛ mra ndetendete, bɛ mraalɛ, yɛɛ debie biala mɔɔ bɛ sa dɔle zolɛ wɔ bɛ azua nu la, bɛvale bɛ muala.

english_verse: Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “Look what you've done! Now I'm in real trouble with the Canaanites and Perizzites who live around here. There aren't many of us, and if they attack, they'll kill everyone in my household.”
translation_verse: Na Gyekɔbo zele Semɛyɔn nee Livae kɛ, “Bɛhwe dwɛwɔlɛ bɛmaa me, bɛmaa meyɛ Pɛlɛzema nee Keenama mɔɔ wɔ azɛlɛ ye azo la kpɔvolɛ. Yɛ nwo anzo, na saa bɛboɔboa bɛ nloa na bɛfa konle bɛtoa me a, bɛbabɔ medame nee me sua nu amra abo zo bɔkɔɔ.”

english_verse: They answered, “Was it right to let our own sister be treated that way?”
translation_verse: Na mgbavolɛ ne mɔ zele kɛ, “Ɛnee yemɔti yɛmaa ɔyɛ yɛ diema raalɛ ye kɛ ɔle tuutuunli ɔ?”

english_verse: Afterwards, we'll go to Bethel. I will build an altar there for God, who answered my prayers when I was in trouble and who has always been at my side.
translation_verse: Akee bɛdwazo bɛmaa yɛhɔ Bɛtɛle, amaa meazi azukponle meamaa Nyamenle ne mɔɔ diele me nzɛlɛlɛ wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɛnee mewɔ anwongyelelɛ nu la. Yemɔ yɛɛ ɔ nee me ɛlua ɛleka biala mɔɔ mehɔ la a.”

english_verse: So everyone gave Jacob their idols and their earrings, and he buried them under the oak tree near Shechem.
translation_verse: Yemɔti bɛyeyele bɛ mmonle mɔɔ bɛlɛ nee bɛ nzo nu asomadeɛ ne mɔ amuala bɛmanle Gyekɔbo. Na Gyekɔbo vunle bɛ wulale oku baka kpole ne mɔɔ wɔ Hyikɛm kandiba la abo.

english_verse: While Jacob and his family were traveling through Canaan, God terrified the people in the towns so much that no one dared bother them.
translation_verse: Bɛzile nu mɔɔ bɛkɔ la, ɛzulolɛ kpole dɔle azuamgbole mɔɔ zuozua Hyikɛm la amra anwo zo, yemɔti bɛ biala anga ɛlalɛ kɛ ɔkɛkpo Gyekɔbo amra ne mɔ.

english_verse: Jacob built an altar there and called it “God of Bethel,” because that was the place where God had appeared to him when he was running from Esau.
translation_verse: Ɔzile azukponle wɔ ɛkɛ ne na ɔvɛlɛle ɛleka ne Bɛtɛle Nyamenle, ɔboalekɛ ɛkɛ ne a mekɛ mɔɔ ɔnriandi ɔ diema Yisɔ la Nyamenle yele ɔ nwo hilele ye a.

english_verse: While they were there, Rebekah's personal servant Deborah died. They buried her under an oak tree and called it “Weeping Oak.” God Blesses Jacob at Bethel
translation_verse: Ɛkɛ ne a Dɛbola, mɔɔ nea Relɛbɛka la wule a. Bɛziele ye wɔ oku baka bie abo wɔ Bɛtɛle nyiakɛ, na bɛvɛlɛle ɛkɛ ne “Ɛzunlɛ oku Baka.”

english_verse: After Jacob came back to the land of Canaan, God appeared to him again. This time he gave Jacob a new name and blessed him by saying: I am God All-Powerful, and from now on your name will be Israel instead of Jacob. You will have many children. Your descendants will become nations, and some of the men in your family will even be kings.
translation_verse: Na Nyamenle zele ye kɛ, “Mame a mele Nyamenle Bedevinli ne a. Ɛbanyia ɛ bo zo amra dɔɔnwo na bɛ nwo azo. Ɛbayɛ maanle na maanle maanle dɔɔnwo vi wɔ nuhua bavinde, na arelemgbunli vi wɔ nuhua avinde.

english_verse: I will give you the land that I promised Abraham and Isaac, and it will belong to your family forever.
translation_verse: Mebava azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ menvale memanle Ebileham nee Ayezeke la meamaa wɔ. Mebava azɛlɛ ne meamaa ɛ bo zo amra mɔɔ vi ɛ nzi bara la.”

english_verse: Jacob set up a large rock, so that he would remember what had happened there. Then he poured wine and olive oil on the rock to show that it was dedicated to God,
translation_verse: Na Gyekɔbo kpɔnlanle bolɛ sika wɔ ɛleka mɔɔ Nyamenle dendɛle hilele ye la, ɔguale nza zolɛ ɔbɔle azu, na ɔguale ɔlivi nwole zolɛ.

english_verse: and he named the place Bethel. Benjamin Is Born
translation_verse: Yemɔti Gyekɔbo vɛlɛle ɛleka mɔɔ Nyamenle dendɛle hilele ye la, Bɛtɛle. Relahyɛle ewule ne

english_verse: Jacob and his family had left Bethel and were still a long way from Ephrath, when the time came for Rachel's baby to be born.
translation_verse: Akee bɛvi Bɛtɛle bɛdule bɛ bo. Bɛhɔle bie, noko mɔɔ ɛnee bɛ nee Yifelate avinli tɛwa la, Relahyɛle ako hanle ye, na ɔyɛle se kpalɛ.

english_verse: She was having a rough time, but the woman who was helping her said, “Don't worry! It's a boy.”

translation_verse: Ɛnee Gyekɔbo kulo Dwosefi tɛla ɔ mra mɔɔ ɛha la amuala, ɔboalekɛ ɔyɛle ɛrelera la yɛɛ ɔwole ye a. Ɔkpomgbale tɛladeɛ tendenle mɔɔ lɛ ɔ sa ndendenle la ɔmanle ye.

english_verse: One day, Joseph told his brothers what he had dreamed, and they hated him even more.
translation_verse: Kenle ko Dwosefi hanle ɛlalɛ, na mɔɔ ɔhanle ɔhilele ɔ mediema ne mɔ la, akee bɛhyile ye bɔkɔɔ.

english_verse: Joseph said, “Let me tell you about my dream.
translation_verse: Ɔhanle ɔhilele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛdie ɛlalɛ bie mɔɔ meha la:

translation_verse: Ɛnee ɔle kɛ yɛwɔ ɛya nu yɛlɛkyekye hwiiti mɔɔ yɛpɛ la avile avile. Na nea, me file ɛdeɛ ne dwazole gyinlanle senze, na bɛ ɛdeɛ ne mɔ rabɔle yiale ye na bɛbɔle bɛ ti aze bɛmanle me ɛdeɛ ne.”

english_verse: His brothers asked, “Do you really think you are going to be king and rule over us?” Now they hated Joseph more than ever because of what he had said about his dream.
translation_verse: Ɔ mediema ne mɔ bizale ye kɛ, “Ɛnee ɛdwenle kɛ ɛbali yɛ nwo zo belemgbunli ɔ? Anzɛɛ ɛdwenle kɛ wɔmɔ yɛɛ ɛbazie yɛ a?” Yemɔti ye ɛlalɛ ne mɔɔ ɔhanle nee ɔ nloa edwɛkɛ ne ati, bɛhyile ye bɔkɔɔ.

english_verse: Joseph later had another dream, and he told his brothers, “Listen to what else I dreamed. The sun, the moon, and eleven stars bowed down to me.”
translation_verse: Dwosefi eza hanle ɛlalɛ bieko, na ɔhanle ɔhilele ɔ mediema ne mɔ. Ɔse, “Bɛdie, meha ɛlalɛ bieko. Menwunle kɛ sɛnzɛne ne, yɛɛ siane ne, yɛɛ nwɔlɔra bulu nee ko ɛlɛbɔ bɛ ti aze amaa me.”

english_verse: When he told his father about this dream, his father became angry and said, “What's that supposed to mean? Are your mother and I and your brothers all going to come and bow down to you?”
translation_verse: Ɔhanle ɛlalɛ ne ɔhilele ɔ ze nee ɔ mediema ne mɔ la, ɔ ze hwile ɔ nyunlu, na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Duzu ɛlalɛ a wɔha la? Ɛkpondɛ wɔaze kɛ medame, ɛ nli, yɛɛ ɛ mediema mrenya ne mɔ yɛbaradu yɛagua ɛ nyunlu yeabɔ yɛ ti aze yɛamaa wɔ ɔ?”

translation_verse: Gyekɔbo zele ye kɛ, “Kɔ kɔnlea ɛ mediema ne mɔ saa bɛ nwo le kpalɛ a, na wɔanlea kɛ mboane ne mɔ noko si de la, na sia baha kile me.” Yemɔti Dwosefi ɔ ze zoanle ye vi Hibulɔn Bɔnza na ɔhɔle Hyikɛm. Dwosefi dwule Hyikɛm

translation_verse: Medean gualilɛma ne radwule ɛkɛ ne la, bɛyele Dwosefi bɛvile kuma ne anu, na bɛdɔnenle ye dwɛtɛ fufule abulanwiɔ bɛmanle Yehyemeeyɛlema, na bɛ nee ye hɔle Yigyibiti.

english_verse: After this, they took the coat to their father and said, “We found this! Look at it carefully and see if it belongs to your son.”

english_verse: While there he met the daughter of Shua, a Canaanite man. Judah married her,
translation_verse: Dwuda nwunle Keena bɛlɛra bie wɔ ɛkɛ, bɛfɛlɛ ɔ ze Hyua. Ɔgyale ye na ɔ nee ye lale.

english_verse: and they had three sons. He named the first one Er;

translation_verse: Ɔnrenzɛle bieko na ɔwole nrenya, na ɔdonle ye Onan.

translation_verse: Eza ɔwole nrenya bieko, na ɔdonle ye Hyila. Dwuda wɔ Akezebe la yɛɛ ɔwole ralɛ nrenya ɛhye a.

translation_verse: Na Dwuda gyale raalɛ maanle ɔ ra kpanyinli Ɛɛ. Bɛfɛlɛ raalɛ ne Teemaa.

english_verse: But Er was very evil, and the Lord took his life.
translation_verse: Na Dwuda ara nrenya kpanyinli Ɛɛ le amumuyɛ, yemɔti Ɛdɛnkɛma hunle ye.

english_verse: So Judah told Onan, “It's your duty to marry Tamar and have a child for your brother.”
translation_verse: Na Dwuda zele Onan kɛ, “Ɛ nee ɛ diema ne aye ne ɛhɔla, na bu adiema nrenya amaamuo maa ye, amaa ɛ diema ne anyia ɔ bo zo amra.”

english_verse: Onan knew the child would not be his, and when he had sex with Tamar, he made sure that she would not get pregnant.
translation_verse: Onan nwunle kɛ saa ɔyɛ ye zɔhane a, mralɛ mɔɔ ɔbawo bɛ la ɛnle ye ɛdeɛ. Yemɔti ɔ nee ye hɔlale la, ɔdule ye nlanzule ne ɔguale, ammaa raalɛ ne annrenzɛ na yeanwo mralɛ yeammaa ɔ diema ne.

english_verse: The Lord wasn't pleased with Onan and took his life too.
translation_verse: Na mɔɔ ɔyɛle la anzɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma anye, na ɔhunle ɔdaye noko.

english_verse: Judah did not want the same thing to happen to his son Shelah, and he told Tamar, “Go home to your father and live there as a widow until my son Shelah is grown.” So Tamar went to live with her father.
translation_verse: Akee Dwuda zele ɔ ra ne aye Teemaa kɛ, “Kɔdɛnla ɛ ze sua nu di wɔ kunlane ne, kɔdwu kɛ me ra Hyila kɛnyi la.” Ɔhanle ɛhye, ɔluakɛ ɛnee ɔsulo kɛ Hyila noko kɛwu kɛ ɔ mediema ne mɔ la. Yemɔti Teemaa hɔdɛnlanle ɔ ze sua nu.

english_verse: Some years later Judah's wife died, and he mourned for her. He then went with his friend Hirah to the town of Timnah, where his sheep were being sheared.
translation_verse: Mekɛ guale nu la Hyua ara raalɛ ne mɔɔ Dwuda gya ye la wule. Ɔwiele ye kunlane ne kyi la, ɔhɔle ɛleka mɔɔ bɛpepɛ ye mboane nwo enrinli la wɔ Temenasuazo. Ɔkɔ la ɔ nee ɔ gɔnwo Haela mɔɔ vi Adɔlam la a hɔle a.

english_verse: Tamar found out that her father-in-law Judah was going to Timnah to shear his sheep.
translation_verse: Bɛhanle bɛhilele Teemaa kɛ, “Ɛ hu ɔ ze ɛlɛkɔ Temenasuazo ahɔpepɛ ye mboane nwo enrinli.”

english_verse: She also realized that Shelah was now a grown man, but she had not been allowed to marry him. So she decided to dress in something other than her widow's clothes and to cover her face with a veil. After this, she sat outside the town of Enaim on the road to Timnah.
translation_verse: Yemɔti ɔkpale ye kunlanvolɛ adɛladeɛ ne ɔguale, ɔyɛle ɔ nwo boɛ na ɔvale ɛdanlɛ ɔguale ɔ ti zo, ɔvale bie ɔkyekyele ɔ nwo na ɔhɔdɛnlanle Yineem sua zo, wɔ Temenasuazo adenle nu. Ɔluakɛ ɔnwunle kɛ Hyila ɛnyi yɛɛ bɛtɛmanle ɔtɛgyale ye a.

english_verse: When Judah came along, he did not recognize her because of the veil. He thought she was a prostitute
translation_verse: Dwuda nwunle ye la ɔdwenlenle kɛ awie mɔɔ di tuutuu la ɔ, ɔluakɛ ɛnee yeheda ɔ nyunlu amuala.

english_verse: “One of my young goats,” he answered. “What will you give me to keep until you send the goat?” she asked.
translation_verse: Dwuda buale kɛ, “Mebamaa bɛarɛlɛ wɔ me mboane ne mɔ ko.” Raalɛ ne bizale ye kɛ, “Duzu yɛɛ ɛfa wɔali agyinlanu kɔkpula kɛ bɛ nee boane ne kɛra la a?”

english_verse: “What do you want?” he asked in return. “The ring on that cord around your neck,” was her reply. “I also want the special walking stick you have with you.” He gave them to her, they slept together, and she became pregnant.
translation_verse: Dwuda bizale ye kɛ, “Duzu a menva menli agyinlanu a?” Ɔbuale ye kɛ, “Fa wɔ kpɔdelera ne, wɔ nyɛma ne nee wɔ kpɔma ne mɔɔ ɛlɛ ye ɛ sa nu la.” Yemɔti Dwuda vale ninyɛne ɛhye mɔ manle ye, na ɔ nee ye lale, na raalɛ ne nrenzɛle.

english_verse: After returning home, Tamar took off the veil and dressed in her widow's clothes again.
translation_verse: Raalɛ ne dwazole hɔle, ɔhɔyele ɛdanlɛ ne mɔɔ ɔvale ɔhedale ɔ nyunlu la, na ɔvale ye kunlane adɛladeɛ ne mɔ ɔwulale.

english_verse: Judah asked his friend Hirah take a goat to the woman, so he could get back the ring and walking stick, but she wasn't there.
translation_verse: Nzinlii mɔɔ Dwuda zoanle ɔ gɔnwo Adɔlamenli ne kɛ ɔva abɔnkye ralɛ ne ɔhɔ na ɔlie ninyɛne mɔɔ ɔvale ɔlile agyinlanu wɔ raalɛ ne ɛkɛ ne ɔrɛla la, ɔkpondɛle ye biala na yeannwu ye.

english_verse: Hirah asked the people of Enaim, “Where is the prostitute who sat along the road outside your town?” “There's never been one here,” they answered.
translation_verse: Ɔbizebizale mrenya mɔɔ wɔ ɛkɛ ne la kɛ, “Tuutuunli ne mɔɔ dɛnlanle Yineem adenle ne foa ko ɛkɛ ne la wɔ nienwu?” Bɛbuale ye kɛ, “Tuutuunli biala ɛtɛbale ɛke.”

english_verse: Hirah went back and told Judah, “I couldn't find the woman, and the people of Enaim said no prostitute had ever been there.”
translation_verse: Yemɔti ɔziale ɔhɔzele Dwuda kɛ yeannwu tuutuunli ne, yɛɛ mrenya mɔɔ wɔ sua ne azo la se tuutuunli biala ɛtɛbale ɛkɛ.

english_verse: “If you couldn't find her, we'll just let her keep the things I gave her,” Judah answered. “And we'd better forget about the goat, or else we'll look like fools.”
translation_verse: Na Dwuda zele kɛ, “Maa ɔva ninyɛne ne mɔ ɔyɛ ye ɛdeɛ, anrɛɛ bɛkɛzele yɛ. Ɛdawɔ wɔnwu kɛ menvale abɔnkye ralɛ ye memanle ɛhɔle yɛɛ wɔannwu ye a.”

english_verse: About three months later someone told Judah, “Your daughter-in-law Tamar has behaved like a prostitute, and now she's pregnant!” “Drag her out of town and burn her to death!” Judah shouted.
translation_verse: Ɛhye anzi siane nsa, awie hanle hilele Dwuda kɛ, “Teemaa, mɔɔ le ɛ ra ne aye ne ɛbɔ tuutuu ɛbɛla, na yenrenzɛ.” Dwuda zele kɛ, “Bɛva ye bɛrɛla bɛmaa yɛyela ye.”

english_verse: As Tamar was being dragged off, she sent someone to tell her father-in-law, “The man who gave me this ring, this cord, and this walking stick is the one who got me pregnant.”
translation_verse: Mɔɔ bɛtwili ye bɛahɔyela ye la, ɔvale nrɛlaleɛ ɔhɔmanle ɔ hu ɔ ze Dwuda kɛ, “Ahenle mɔɔ lɛ ninyɛne ɛhye mɔ la a nee me ɛlɛnrenzɛ a. Yemɔti mebodo wɔ, nea bɛ kpalɛ na ɛbanwu ahenle mɔɔ kpɔdelera ne, nyɛma ne, yɛɛ kpɔma ne le ye ɛdeɛ la.”

english_verse: “Those are mine!” Judah admitted. “She's a better person than I am, because I broke my promise to let her marry my son Shelah.” After this, Judah never slept with her again.
translation_verse: Dwuda nwunle ninyɛne ne la, ɔliele ɔdole nu kɛ ɔdaye a ɔlɛ bɛ a na ɔhanle kɛ, “Ɛvalɛ mɔɔ meanva ye meamaa me ra Hyila la ɛmaa yeyɛ sonla tenlene yedɛla me.” Na ɔ nee ye anla bieko.

english_verse: Tamar later gave birth to twins. But before either of them was born, one of them stuck a hand out of her womb. The woman who was helping tied a red thread around the baby's hand and explained, “This one came out first.”
translation_verse: Ɔ ko hanle ye la, ngakula ne mɔ ko vale ɔ sa lumuale, na ahenle mɔɔ die awolɛ ne la vale nyɛma kɔkɔlɛ kyekyele ɔ sa, na ɔhanle kɛ, “Ɛhye a le kpanyinli a.”

english_verse: At once his hand went back in, and the other child was born first. The woman then said, “What an opening you've made for yourself!” So they named the baby Perez.
translation_verse: Noko mɔɔ ɔhwenle ɔ sa ɔhɔle ala la yɛɛ ɔ diema nrenya ne mɔɔ ɔ nee ye la ɛkolɛ ne anu la rale a. Na mɔɔ die awolɛ ne la hanle kɛ, “Na duzu hehɛlɛhehɛlɛ ɔ!” Yemɔti bɛvɛlɛle ye Pɛlɛze.

english_verse: When the brother with the red thread was born, they named him Zerah.
translation_verse: Nzinlii akee ko ne ɔdaye ɔrale, nyɛma kɔkɔlɛ ne bɔ ɔ sa, na bɛdonle ye Zilaa.

english_verse: The Ishmaelites took Joseph to Egypt and sold him to Potiphar, the king's official in charge of the palace guard.
translation_verse: Yehyemeeyɛlema dɔle Dwosefi la, bɛ nee ye hɔle Yigyibiti, na Yigyibitinli bie mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye Pɔtefaa, mɔɔ le Yigyibiti belemgbunli mgbanyima ne mɔ ko, na eza ɔle suakunlu ɛkɛ ne sinzavolɛma safohyenle la, dɔle Dwosefi vile bɛ ɛkɛ.

english_verse: So Joseph lived in the home of Potiphar, his Egyptian owner. Soon Potiphar realized that the Lord was helping Joseph to be successful in whatever he did.
translation_verse: na ɔ menle ne nwunle kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma li Dwosefi anzi, na ɔmanle debie biala mɔɔ ɔvale ɔ sa ɔhanle ye la yɛle kpalɛ.

english_verse: Potiphar liked Joseph and made him his personal assistant, putting him in charge of his house and all of his property.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Pɔtefaa anye liele Dwosefi anwo na ɔmanle ɔzonlenle ɔdaye mumua ne. Eza ɔyɛle Dwosefi kpanyinli kɛ ɔnlea ye sua nu ɛkɛ ne debie biala mɔɔ ɔlɛ la azo.

english_verse: Potiphar left everything up to Joseph, and with Joseph there, the only decision he had to make was what he wanted to eat. Joseph was well-built and handsome,
translation_verse: Yemɔti ɔvale debie biala ɔwulale Dwosefi asa anu na ɔyele ye adwenle wɔ zolɛ. Debie mɔɔ ɔdwenlenle nwolɛ ala la a le ɔdaye Pɔtefaa ye aleɛ mɔɔ ɔdi la. Dwosefi anwo yɛ fɛ na ɔgyi zo sengɔɔnwo.

english_verse: and Potiphar's wife soon noticed him. She asked him to make love to her,
translation_verse: Mekɛ guale nu la, ɔ menle aye ne hulole ye na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Ɛnee me ɛla.”

english_verse: but he refused and said, “My master isn't worried about anything in his house, because he has placed me in charge of everything he owns.
translation_verse: Dwosefi amkponle na ɔhanle ɔhilele ɔ menle aye ne kɛ, “Nea, mewɔ ɛke la ati, me menle ɛndwenle debie biala mɔɔ wɔ sua nu ɛke la anwo. Yeva debie biala mɔɔ wɔ sua nu ɛke la yewula me sa nu.

english_verse: No one in my master's house is more important than I am. The only thing he hasn't given me is you, and that's because you are his wife. I won't sin against God by doing such a terrible thing as this.”
translation_verse: Melɛ tumi wɔ awuke ye anu kɛ ɔdaye ala la, yɛɛ ɔtɛtuale me kɛ memmafa me sa meka debie biala kɛ ɛdawɔ ala, ɔboalekɛ ɔ ye a le wɔ. Duzu ati yɛɛ akee menwɔyɛ amumuyɛ kpole ɛhye, na menwɔyɛ ɛtane menwɔtia Nyamenle ɛ?”

english_verse: She kept begging Joseph day after day, but he refused to do what she wanted or even to go near her.
translation_verse: Raalɛ ne hanle mɔɔ kɛyɛ boɛ alehyenlɛ biala, na Dwosefi andie ye, ɔ nee ye anla, yɛɛ ɔ nee ye andɛnla bɔbɔ.

english_verse: One day, Joseph went to Potiphar's house to do his work, and none of the other servants were there.
translation_verse: Kenle ko Dwosefi hɔle sua nu ɛkɛ ne kɛ ɔkayɛ gyima, ɛnee mgbavolɛ mɔɔ wɔ sua nu ɛkɛ ne la amuala ɛvinde.

english_verse: Potiphar's wife grabbed hold of his coat and said, “Make love to me!” Joseph ran out of the house, leaving his coat there in her hands.
translation_verse: Na Pɔtefaa aye ne hɔzɔle Dwosefi tɛladeɛ ne anu na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Ɛ nee me ɛla.” Na Dwosefi kpolole ye tɛladeɛ ne manle ye na ɔnriandile ɔvile sua nu ɛkɛ.

english_verse: she called in her servants and said, “Look! This Hebrew has come just to make fools of us. He tried to rape me, but I screamed for help.
translation_verse: ɔdeanle nu ɔvɛlɛle mgbavolɛ mɔɔ wɔ ɔdaye ye sua nu ɛkɛ ne la na ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛnlea, Pɔtefaa ɛhɔdwu Hibulunli bie ɛra ɛke kɛ ɔrayɛ mgbane mgbane ɔhile sonla. Ɔrale me ɛkɛ ne kɛ ɔbadoa me ɔ nee me ala, yɛɛ mendeɛdeanle nuhua a.

english_verse: And when he heard me scream, he ran out of the house, leaving his coat with me.”
translation_verse: Na mɔɔ ɔdele kɛ melɛteɛdea nuhua mgbole mgbole la yɛɛ ɔvi sua ye anu ɔnriandile, ɔgyakyile ye tɛladeɛ ye ɛke.”

english_verse: Potiphar's wife kept Joseph's coat until her husband came home.
translation_verse: Ɔvale Dwosefi tɛladeɛ ne ɔguale ɔ nwo ɛkɛ ne toonwo ɔ hu rale sua nu,

english_verse: But when I screamed for help, he left his coat and ran out of the house.”
translation_verse: Na mɔɔ mendeɛdeanle nuhua mgbole mgbole la, ɔvi sua nu ɛke ɔnriandile. Ɔnriandile ɔgyakyile ye tɛladeɛ ne ɛke.”

english_verse: and threw Joseph in the same prison where the king's prisoners were kept. While Joseph was in prison,
translation_verse: Na Pɔtefaa hyele Dwosefi dole efiade ɛleka mɔɔ belemgbunli ne pilizama wɔ la, na ɔhale ɛkɛ ne.

english_verse: the Lord helped him and was good to him. He even made the jailer like Joseph so much that
translation_verse: Na ɛnee Ɛdɛnkɛma nee Dwosefi lua. Ɔhilele ɛhulolɛ dɔɔnwo wɔ ɔ nwo, na ɔmanle ɔzɔle nrenya ne mɔɔ nea pilizama ne mɔ anwo zo la anye.

english_verse: he put him in charge of the other prisoners and of everything that was done in the jail.
translation_verse: Nrenya ne vale debie biala mɔɔ wɔ efiade ɛkɛ ne nee pilizama ne mɔ amuala wulale Dwosefi asa anu. Debie biala mɔɔ bɛyɛle wɔ ɛkɛ ne la, Dwosefi a nleanle manle bɛyɛle a.

english_verse: The jailer did not worry about anything, because the Lord was with Joseph and made him successful in all that he did.
translation_verse: Yeanvane nrenya ne mɔɔ nea pilizama anwo zo la anwo kɛ ɔkɛnlea debie mɔɔ bɛvale bɛwulale Dwosefi asa anu la, ɔboalekɛ ɛnee Ɛdɛnkɛma nee ye a lua a, yɛɛ debie biala mɔɔ ɔyɛle la, Ɛdɛnkɛma manle ɔyɛle kpalɛ.

english_verse: While Joseph was in prison, both the king's personal servant and his chief cook made the king angry. So he had them thrown into the same prison with Joseph.
translation_verse: na ɔhyele bɛ ɔguale efiade wɔ sinzavolɛma safohyenle ne sua nu ɛkɛ ne efiade ne ɛleka mɔɔ Dwosefi la la.

english_verse: They spent a long time in prison, and the official in charge of the palace guard, made Joseph their servant.
translation_verse: Bɛguale efiade ɛkɛ ne bɛhyɛle dɔɔnwo, na sinzavolɛma safohyenle ne yele Dwosefi kɛ ɔzonle bɛ.

english_verse: The next morning, when Joseph went to see the men, he could tell they were upset,
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Dwosefi rale bɛ nwo ɛkɛ ne nwonlomɔ ne la, ɔnwunle kɛ bɛ adwenle ɛzɛkye.

english_verse: “We each had a dream last night,” they answered, “and there is no one to tell us what they mean.” Joseph replied, “Doesn't God know the meaning of dreams? Now tell me what you dreamed.”
translation_verse: Bɛbuale ye kɛ, “Yɛha ɛlalɛ, na yɛnnyia awie ɛngile bɛ bo ɛngile yɛ.” Dwosefi buale bɛ kɛ, “Ɔ bo ɛhilelɛ ne vi Nyamenle ɛkɛ ne a ba a. Mebodo bɛ, bɛha bɛ ɛlalɛ ne mɔ bɛhile me.”

english_verse: with three branches. As soon as it budded, it blossomed, and its grapes became ripe.
translation_verse: Vanye baka ne lɛ ngane nsa. Ɔfefɛle nya ala la yɛɛ ɔbɔle ndotolo, ɔzole na ma ne mɔ bolole a.

english_verse: Joseph said: This is the meaning of your dream. The three branches stand for three days,
translation_verse: Na Dwosefi buale kɛ, “Wɔ ɛlalɛ ne abo ɛne: vanye ngane nsa ne kile kenle nsa.

english_verse: and in three days the king will pardon you. He will make you his personal servant again, and you will serve him his wine, just as you used to do.
translation_verse: Ɛnɛ anwo zo kenle nsa, belemgbunli ne bamaa bɛaraye wɔ wɔ efiade ɛke na bɛava wɔ gyima ne bɛawula ɛ sa nu; ɛbava belemgbunli ne kɔpo ne wɔawula ɔ sa nu, na wɔazu ye nza kɛ dɛba ne ala la.

english_verse: But when these good things happen, please don't forget to tell the king about me, so I can get out of this place.
translation_verse: Na saa ɔyɛ boɛ ɔmaa wɔ a, anrɛɛ kakye me na yɛ boɛ ɛhye maa me. Mebodo wɔ, bɔ me duma kile belemgbunli ne maa ɔye me ɔvi efiade ɛke.

english_verse: I was kidnapped from the land of the Hebrews, and here in Egypt I haven't done anything to deserve being thrown in jail.
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ nɔhalɛ nu, bɛwuale me a bɛ nee me vi Hibulu azɛlɛ zo rale a, yɛɛ ɛke noko, metɛyɛle ɛhwee mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ bɛto me efiade a.”

english_verse: When the chief cook saw that Joseph had given a good meaning to the dream, he told Joseph, “I also had a dream. In it I was carrying three breadbaskets stacked on top of my head.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ sonvolɛ ne mɔɔ to belemgbunli kpanwo ne la nwunle kɛ ɛlalɛ ne abo le kɛnlɛma la, ɔzele Dwosefi kɛ, “Medame noko menganle ɛlalɛ. Ɛnee mezo keeki ahɛndɛne nsa me ti zo.

english_verse: The top basket was full of all kinds of baked things for the king, but birds were eating them.”
translation_verse: Mɔɔ gyi zolɛ kpalɛ anwuma la, aleɛ ngakyile dɔɔnwo mɔɔ bɛdo ye fonlomo nu la wɔ nu mɔɔ mefa meahɔmaa belemgbunli ne a, na ɛnee nloma ɛlɛsuso ye me ti zo ali.”

english_verse: Joseph said: This is the meaning of your dream. The three baskets are three days,
translation_verse: Dwosefi buale kɛ, “Wɔ ɛlalɛ ne abo ɛne: ahɛndɛne nsa ne kile kenle nsa.

english_verse: and in three days the king will cut off your head. He will hang your body on a pole, and birds will come and peck at it.
translation_verse: Ɛnɛ anwo zo kenle nsa belemgbunli ne bamaa bɛaraye ɛ ti ne bɛavi zolɛ. Bɛbahenda wɔ baka zo, na nloma bali wɔ nwonane ne.”

english_verse: Three days later, while the king was celebrating his birthday with a dinner for his officials, he sent for his personal servant and the chief cook.
translation_verse: Kenle nsa ne azo Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne lile ye awolɛ kenle. Ɔdole ɛkponle kpole bie ɔmanle ye sonvolɛma ne amuala. Ɔyele ye sonvolɛ kpanyinli ne mɔɔ nea ye nza nee ye ahyɛnze zo nee sonvolɛ ne mɔɔ to kpanwo la ɔvile efiade.

english_verse: and had the cook put to death. Everything happened just as Joseph had said it would,
translation_verse: Akee ɔhunle sonvolɛ ne mɔɔ to kpanwo ne la, kɛmɔ Dwosefi zile hilele bɛ ɛlalɛ ne mɔ abo ala la.

english_verse: Two years later the king of Egypt dreamed he was standing beside the Nile River.
translation_verse: Ɛvolɛ nwiɔ anzi, Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne hanle ɛlalɛ kɛ ɛnee ɔgyi Azule Naele ne anloa.

english_verse: Suddenly, seven fat, healthy cows came up from the river and started eating grass along the bank.
translation_verse: Ɔnwunle kɛ nlankɛ mgbole, dɔlera nsuu vi azule ne anu ɛvinde na bɛlɛdidi ɛhonle ne mɔɔ wɔ ɛkɛ ne la anu.

english_verse: Then seven ugly, skinny cows came up out of the river and
translation_verse: Ɔnwunle kɛ eza nlankɛ nwanlera, kengamgbaanwo nsuu bɛdabɛ bɛvi azule ne anu bɛvo bɛragyinlegyinla nlankɛ ɛhendeɛ ne mɔ anwo ɛkɛ wɔ azule ne anloa.

english_verse: ate the fat, healthy cows. When this happened, the king woke up.
translation_verse: Na nlankɛ nwanlera, kengamgbaanwo nsuu ne hyele nlankɛ mgbole, dɔlera nsuu ne lile. Na belemgbunli ne dunwuele.

english_verse: The king went back to sleep and had another dream. This time seven full heads of grain were growing on a single stalk.
translation_verse: Eza ɔlafele, na ɔhanle ɛlalɛ bieko. Ɔnwunle kɛ abɛlɛ mbaka mgbole nsuu ɛwɔlɔwɔlɔ abɛlɛ baka ko anwo.

english_verse: Later, seven other heads of grain appeared, but they were thin and scorched by a wind from the desert.
translation_verse: Yeangyɛ biala ɛnee eza abɛlɛ mbaka ɛtane ɛtane, agyendo nsuu bɛdabɛ noko bɛwɔlɔwɔlɔ.

english_verse: The thin heads of grain swallowed the seven full heads. Again the king woke up, and it had only been a dream.
translation_verse: Na abɛlɛ mbaka ɛtane ɛtane, agyendo nsuu ne memenle abɛlɛ mbaka mgbole nsuu ne. Belemgbunli ne dunwuele na ɔnwunle kɛ ɔle ɛlalɛ.

english_verse: The next morning the king was upset. So he called in his magicians and wise men and told them what he had dreamed. None of them could tell him what the dreams meant.
translation_verse: Yemɔti aleɛ hyenle la ɛnee ye adwenle ɛzɛkye. Na ɔzoanle ɔmanle bɛhɔvɛlɛle ngonyiama mɔɔ wɔ Yigyibiti la amuala nee maanle ne anu nrɛlɛbɛvolɛma ne amuala na ɔhanle ye ɛlalɛ ne ɔhilele bɛ. Noko bɛ nuhua ko bɔbɔ angola ɛlalɛ ne abo kile kile belemgbunli ne.

english_verse: The king's personal servant said: Now I remember what I was supposed to do.
translation_verse: Akee sonvolɛ ne mɔɔ nea belemgbunli ne nza nee ye ahyɛnze zo la hanle hilele ye kɛ, “Nana, ɛnɛ mehakye kɛ mevo.

english_verse: When you were angry with me and your chief cook, you threw us both in jail in the house of the captain of the guard.
translation_verse: Mekɛ mɔɔ ɛvale me nee sonvolɛ ne mɔɔ to kpanwo la anwo ɛya, na bɛguale yɛ efiade wɔ belemgbunli sinzavolɛma safohyenle ne sua nu la,

english_verse: One night we both had dreams, and each dream had a different meaning.
translation_verse: kenle ko nɔɔzo me nee sonvolɛ ɛhendeɛ ne yɛhanle ɛlalɛ. Yɛ ɛlalɛ ne mɔ le ngakyile, yɛɛ asolo ko biala abo.

english_verse: A young Hebrew, who was a servant of the captain of the guard, was there with us at the time. When we told him our dreams, he explained what each of them meant,
translation_verse: Mekɛ ne anu ɛnee yɛ nee Hibulunli kpavolɛ bie mɔɔ le sinzavolɛma safohyenle ne sonvolɛ la a gua ɛkɛ a. Yɛhanle yɛ ɛlalɛ ne mɔ yɛhilele ye, na ɔhilele ɛlalɛ ne mɔ abo ɔhilele yɛ, kɛmɔ sonla ko biala ye ɛlalɛ ne de la.

english_verse: and everything happened just as he said it would. I got my job back, and the cook was put to death.
translation_verse: Na kɛ ɔzile ɔhilele ɔ bo ɔhilele yɛ la, zɔhane ala yɛɛ ɔyɛle a. Bɛvale me gyima ne bɛmanle me, yɛɛ bɛhendanle sonvolɛ ne mɔɔ to kpanwo la.”

english_verse: The king sent for Joseph, who was quickly brought out of jail. He shaved, changed his clothes, and went to the king.
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne zoanle manle bɛhɔvale Dwosefi ndɛndɛ zo wɔ efiade ne bɛrale. Ɔkpale ɔ kɛsa, ɔbiale, ɔhakyile ye adɛladeɛ mɔɔ ɔwula la, na akee ɔhɔle belemgbunli anyunlu.

english_verse: The king said to him, “I had a dream, yet no one can explain what it means. I am told that you can interpret dreams.”
translation_verse: Na belemgbunli ne zele Dwosefi kɛ, “Meha ɛlalɛ bie, na awie biala ɛnle ɛkɛ mɔɔ kola kile ɔ bo a. Na mede noko kɛ wɔmɔ, saa bɛka ɛlalɛ bɛkile wɔ a ɛkile ɔ bo.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” Joseph answered, “I can't do it myself, but God can give a good meaning to your dreams.”
translation_verse: Dwosefi buale kɛ, “Nana, medame me ngome mengola. Nyamenle yɛɛ bahile ɔ bo ahile Nana a.”

english_verse: The king told Joseph: I dreamed I was standing on the bank of the Nile River.
translation_verse: Na belemgbunli ne zele Dwosefi kɛ, “Wɔ me ɛlalɛ ne anu, menwunle kɛ ɛnee megyi Azule Naele ne anloa.

english_verse: I saw seven fat, healthy cows come up out of the river, and they began feeding on the grass.
translation_verse: Na nlankɛ mgbole, dɔlera nsuu vi azule ne anu vindele na bɛvole bɛradidile ɛhonle ne anu.

english_verse: Next, seven skinny, bony cows came up out of the river. I have never seen such terrible looking cows anywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Na nlankɛ nwanlera, kengamgbaanwo nsuu bɛdabɛ bɛvi azule ne anu bɛvindele. Nlankɛ zɛhae, metɛnwunle bie ɛlɛ wɔ Yigyibiti maanle ye anu.

english_verse: The skinny cows ate the fat ones.
translation_verse: Na nlankɛ nwanlera, kengamgbaanwo nsuu ne hyele alumua nlankɛ mgbole dɔlera nsuu ne lile.

english_verse: But you couldn't tell it, because these skinny cows were just as skinny as they were before. At once, I woke up.
translation_verse: Noko bɛlile bɛ bɛwiele bɔbɔ la, ɛnee ɛnwu nlankɛ ne mɔ a ɛkɛze kɛ bɛtɛdile ɛhwee, ɔluakɛ ɛnee kɛ bɛde ala la yɛɛ bɛde a. Na mendunwuele.

english_verse: I also dreamed that I saw seven heads of grain growing on one stalk. The heads were full and ripe.
