translation_verse: Meka ɛlalɛ bieko la ɛnee abɛlɛ mbaka mgbole nsuu ɛwɔlɔwɔlɔ abɛlɛ baka ko anwo,

english_verse: These heads of grain swallowed the full ones. I told my dreams to the magicians, but none of them could tell me the meaning of the dreams.
translation_verse: na bɛmemenle abɛlɛ mbaka mgbole nsuu ne. Meha ɛlalɛ ɛhye mehile ngonyiama ne mɔ, noko meannyia bɛ nuhua ko bɔbɔ angile ɔ bo angile me.”

english_verse: Joseph replied: Your Majesty, both of your dreams mean the same thing, and in them God has shown what he is going to do.
translation_verse: Na Dwosefi buale kɛ, “Nana, ɛlalɛ ne le kokye. Nyamenle ɛye mɔɔ ɔbayɛ la ɛhile Nana.

english_verse: The seven good cows stand for seven years, and so do the seven good heads of grain.
translation_verse: Nlankɛ mgbole nsuu ne kile ɛvolɛ nsuu, yɛɛ abɛlɛ mbaka mgbole nsuu ne kile ɛvolɛ nsuu. Bɛ mu nwiɔ bɛ bo le kokye.

english_verse: The seven skinny, ugly cows that came up later also stand for seven years, as do the seven bad heads of grain that were scorched by the desert wind. The dreams mean there will be seven years when there won't be enough grain.
translation_verse: Nlankɛ nwanlera, kengamgbaanwo nsuu ne mɔɔ lile ɛhendeɛ ne mɔ anzi rale yɛɛ abɛlɛ mbaka ɛtane ɛtane, agyendo ne noko kile ɛhɔne ɛvolɛ nsuu.

english_verse: It is just as I said—God has shown what he intends to do.
translation_verse: Ɔle kɛ mɔɔ menganle mengilele Nana la. Nyamenle ɛye mɔɔ ɔbayɛ la ɛhile Nana.

english_verse: For seven years Egypt will have more than enough grain,
translation_verse: Ɛvolɛ nsuu bara mɔɔ aleɛ babu kpole wɔ Yigyibiti azɛlɛ ye azo a.

english_verse: The famine will be so bad that no one will remember that once there had been plenty.
translation_verse: Ɛhɔne ne mɔɔ bara la ati, awie ɛnrɛnwu kɛ ɛnee azɛlɛ ye azo le aleɛ ngome, ɔluakɛ ɛhɔne ne bayɛ kpole kpalɛ.

english_verse: God has given you two dreams to let you know that he has definitely decided to do this and that he will do it soon.
translation_verse: Ɛlalɛ fane nwiɔ ne mɔɔ Nana hanle la kile kɛ Nyamenle ɛbɔ ye kpɔkɛ ɛwie, na ɔnrɛhyɛ biala na yeazi.

english_verse: Your Majesty, you should find someone who is wise and will know what to do, so that you can put him in charge of all Egypt.
translation_verse: “Zɔhane ati Nana, ɔwɔ kɛ ɛye sonla mɔɔ ɔ nye gyi ɔ ti anwo na ɔze nrɛlɛbɛ la, na ɛfa ye ɛsie Yigyibiti azɛlɛ ye kɔsɔɔti anloa.

english_verse: Then appoint some other officials to collect one fifth of every crop harvested in Egypt during the seven years when there is plenty.
translation_verse: Nana ɛbɔ ɔ bo ɛyeye menli mɔɔ banlea azɛlɛ ne mɔ azo la, na ɔlie aleɛ biala mɔɔ kɛvinde Yigyibiti azɛlɛ ye azo la anu ngyɛnu nnu ɛkpɔ ko wɔ ɛvolɛ nsuu ne mɔɔ aleɛ babu la anu.

english_verse: Give them the power to collect the grain during those good years and to store it in your cities.
translation_verse: Maa bɛboɔboa aleɛ mɔɔ bɛbanyia ye wɔ ɛvolɛ kpalɛ ne mɔ anu la anloa, na maa tumi maa bɛva abɛlɛ bɛzie azuamgbole ne mɔ azo, na bɛzinza.

english_verse: It can be stored until it is needed during the seven years when there won't be enough grain in Egypt. This will keep the country from being destroyed because of the lack of food. Joseph Is Made Governor over Egypt
translation_verse: Zɛhae aleɛ ne mɔɔ bɛbaboɔboa ɔ nloa la yɛɛ bayɛ aleɛ mɔɔ bagyinla ɛkɛ amaa ɛvolɛ nsuu ɛhɔne ne mɔɔ bara Yigyibiti amuala la a, amaa saa ɛhɔne ne ba a, ɛhɔne angu maanlema ambɔ bɛ bo zo.” Bɛyɛ Dwosefi amɛnlado wɔ Yigyibiti

english_verse: The king and his officials liked this plan.
translation_verse: Nzuzulɛ ne zɔle Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne nee ye mgbanyima ne mɔ amuala anye.

english_verse: So the king said to them, “Who could possibly handle this better than Joseph? After all, the Spirit of God is with him.”
translation_verse: Na ɔzele ye mgbanyima ne mɔ kɛ, “Bɛnea a awie bie wɔ ɛkɛ tɛla ɛhye mɔɔ Nyamenle Sunsum ne wɔ ye nu la ɔ?”

english_verse: The king told Joseph, “God is the one who has shown you these things. No one else is as wise as you are or knows as much as you do.
translation_verse: Yemɔti belemgbunli ne zele Dwosefi kɛ, “Kɛmɔ Nyamenle ɛye ɛhye mɔ amuala ɛhile wɔ la, awie ɛnle ɛkɛ mɔɔ anye gyi ɔ ti anwo na ɔze nrɛlɛbɛ kɛ ɛdawɔ la.

english_verse: I'm putting you in charge of my palace, and everybody will have to obey you. No one will be over you except me.
translation_verse: Ɛbanlea me sua nu ɛke, na me menli ne amuala bayɛ tieyɛ amaa wɔ. Edwɛkɛ biala mɔɔ ɛkɛha la bɛbali zolɛ. Debie mɔɔ mefa metɛla wɔ la a le me belemgbunli ebia ne mɔɔ mede zolɛ la.”

english_verse: Then the king took off his royal ring and put it on Joseph's finger. He gave him fine clothes to wear and placed a gold chain around his neck.
translation_verse: Akee ɔyele ɔ sa kpɔdelera ne mɔɔ ɔfa ɔsisi ngɛlata zo la ɔwulale Dwosefi asa, na bɛvale adɛladeɛ ngɛnlɛma bɛwulale ye, bɛvale ndweabane bɛdole ɔ kɔme;

english_verse: He also let him ride in the chariot next to his own, and people shouted, “Make way for Joseph!” So Joseph was governor of Egypt.
translation_verse: na ɔmanle ɔdɛnlanle ye konle ehwili ne mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nwiɔ la anu, na ye sonvolɛma deanle nu kɛ, “Bɛhoto ye!” Ɛnee kɛ bɛyɛle bɛvale Dwosefi bɛziele Yigyibiti azɛlɛ ne kɔsɔɔti anloa la ɛne.

english_verse: The king told Joseph, “Although I'm king, no one in Egypt is to do anything without your permission.”
translation_verse: Eza belemgbunli ne zele Dwosefi kɛ, “Mame a mele Yigyibiti belemgbunli a. Mese, saa ɛtɛdiele ɛtɛtole nuhua a, awie biala ɛnlɛ adenle kɛ ɔkɛva ɔ sa ɔkɛha anzɛɛ ɔ gyakɛ ɔkɛtia Yigyibiti azɛlɛ biala azo.”

english_verse: For seven years there were big harvests of grain.
translation_verse: Aleɛ mekɛ ɛvolɛ nsuu ne anu, azɛlɛ ne manle bɛnyianle aleɛ dɔɔnwo kpalɛ.

english_verse: Joseph collected and stored up the extra grain in the cities of Egypt near the fields where it was harvested.
translation_verse: Ɔboɔboale ɛvolɛ nsuu ne anu aleɛ mɔɔ bɛnyianle la anloa, na ɔmanle bɛziele aleɛ mɔɔ bɛnyianle wɔ ɛya avule ne mɔ anu la wɔ azuamgbole ne mɔ azo.

english_verse: In fact, there was so much grain that they stopped keeping record, because it was like counting the grains of sand along the beach.
translation_verse: Dwosefi manle bɛziele abɛlɛ dɔɔnwo mɔɔ nzinlii ɛnee akee bɛngola ye suzu. Yemɔti ɔmanle bɛgyakyile ye ɛzuzulɛ, ɔluakɛ abɛlɛ ne zonle somaa, bɛ somaa kɛyɛ kɛ ɛnweazo anwea.

english_verse: Joseph and his wife had two sons before the famine began.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ ɛhɔne ɛvolɛ nsuu ne kabɔ ɔ bo la ɛnee Dwosefi nee ɔ ye Asɛnate ɛwo mrenya nwiɔ.

english_verse: Their first son was named Manasseh, which means, “God has let me forget all my troubles and my family back home.”
translation_verse: Dwosefi donle ralɛ nrenya kpanyinli ne Manasɛ. Ɔse, “Nyamenle ɛmaa me rɛle ɛvi me nyane nee egya sua nu amra.”

english_verse: His second son was named Ephraim, which means “God has made me a success in the land where I suffered.”
translation_verse: Ralɛ nrenya ne mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nwiɔ la, ɔdonle ye Yifelaem. Ɔluakɛ ɔse, “Nyamenle ɛmaa mebɔ ɛdane wɔ me amaneɛnwunlɛ azɛlɛ zo.”

english_verse: Egypt's seven years of plenty came to an end,
translation_verse: Ɛvolɛ nsuu ne mɔɔ nuhua a Yigyibiti nyianle aleɛ dɔɔnwo la wiele.

english_verse: and the seven years of famine began, just as Joseph had said. There was not enough food in other countries, but all over Egypt there was plenty.
translation_verse: Na ɛhɔne ɛvolɛ nsuu ne bɔle ɔ bo, kɛmɔ Dwosefi hanle ala la. Ɛhɔne zile maanle maanle kɔsɔɔti anu, na Yigyibiti ɛdeɛ, ɛnee aleɛ wɔ ɛkɛ.

english_verse: When the famine finally struck Egypt, the people asked the king for food, but he said, “Go to Joseph and do what he tells you to do.”
translation_verse: Mɔɔ ɛhɔne ne hanle Yigyibiti la, maanlema amuala zunle vɛlɛle bɛ belemgbunli ne kɛ ɔmaa bɛ aleɛ. Na belemgbunli ne zele Yigyibitima amuala kɛ, “Bɛhɔ Dwosefi ɛkɛ, na bɛyɛ debie biala mɔɔ ɔkɛze bɛ la.”

english_verse: The famine became bad everywhere in Egypt, so Joseph opened the storehouses and sold the grain to the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Yemɔti mɔɔ akee ɛhɔne ne rale ye mgbole nu la, Dwosefi manle bɛbukebukele ɛleka ɛleka mɔɔ bɛvale aleɛ bɛziele la amuala, na bɛdɔnenle aleɛ bɛmanle Yigyibitima, ɔluakɛ ɛnee akee ɛhɔne ne ɛyɛ kpole wɔ Yigyibiti.

english_verse: People from all over the world came to Egypt to buy grain, because the famine was so severe in their countries.
translation_verse: Yeanga ye zɔhane angome, eza maanle maanle dɔɔnwo rale Dwosefi anwo ɛkɛ ne wɔ Yigyibiti radɔle abɛlɛ, ɔboalekɛ ɛhɔne ne hanle ewiade amra amuala.

english_verse: When Jacob found out there was grain in Egypt, he said to his sons, “Why are you just sitting here, staring at one another?
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo dele kɛ abɛlɛ wɔ Yigyibiti, na ɔzele ɔ mra ne mɔ kɛ, “Bɛmmatɛnla ɛkɛ bɛneɛnlea bɛ nyunlu.

english_verse: I have heard there is grain in Egypt. Go down and buy some, so we won't starve to death.”
translation_verse: Mede kɛ abɛlɛ wɔ Yigyibiti. Bɛhɔ bɛhɔdɔ bie bɛrɛla na yɛanyia bie yɛali, na yɛanwu.”

english_verse: Ten of Joseph's brothers went to Egypt to buy grain.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Dwosefi amediema ne mɔ anu bulu hɔle Yigyibiti kɛ bɛkadɔ abɛlɛ.

english_verse: But Jacob did not send Joseph's younger brother Benjamin with them; he was afraid that something might happen to him.
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo ammaa Bɛngyaman nee ɔ mediema ne mɔ angɔ, ɔluakɛ ɔnze mɔɔ kɛzi ɔ nwo zo a. Bɛngyaman nee Dwosefi vi ɛkolɛ ko anu.

english_verse: So Jacob's sons joined others from Canaan who were going to Egypt because of the terrible famine.
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo amra ne mɔ nee awie mɔ gyɛne a hɔle kɛ bɛkadɔ abɛlɛ ne a, ɔluakɛ ɛnee ɛhɔne ne ɛyɛ kpole wɔ Keena azɛlɛ zo.

english_verse: Since Joseph was governor of Egypt and in charge of selling grain, his brothers came to him and bowed with their faces to the ground.
translation_verse: Mekɛ ne anu ɛnee Dwosefi a le amɛnlado mɔɔ nea Yigyibiti azɛlɛ ne kɔsɔɔti azo a. Ɔdaye a ɔtɔne abɛlɛ ɔmaa bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛwɔ maanle ne anu la amuala a. Na Dwosefi amediema ne mɔ rabɔle bɛ ti aze manle ye, bɛbutubutule bɛ nyunlu aze.

english_verse: Joseph remembered what he had dreamed about them and said, “You're spies! You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
translation_verse: Na Dwosefi hakyele ɛlalɛ ne mɔɔ ɔhanle wɔ bɛ nwo la, na ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛdabɛ, bɛle busiama mɔɔ ɛra banleɛnlea yɛ maanle ye anu bɛanwu ɛleka mɔɔ yɛtɔ sinli la.”

english_verse: “No sir,” they replied. “We're your servants, and we have only come to buy grain.
translation_verse: Bɛbuale kɛ, “Yɛmenle, kyɛkyɛ, ɔnle zɔhane. Abɛlɛ mɔɔ yɛbadɔ la ati yɛɛ wɔ sonvolɛma yɛra a.

english_verse: We're honest men, and we come from the same family—we're not spies.”
translation_verse: Yɛdayɛ mɔɔ yɛra la yɛ muala yɛ ze ko. Nɔhalɛ a yɛlɛka la. Yɛnle busiama.”

english_verse: “That isn't so!” Joseph insisted. “You've come here to find out where our country is weak.”
translation_verse: Dwosefi zele kɛ, “Kyɛkyɛ, menlie bɛ menli. Bɛra kɛ bɛbali busia bɛanleɛnlea ɛleka mɔɔ yɛ maanle ye tɔ sinli la.”

english_verse: But they explained, “Sir, we come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and one of our brothers is dead.”
translation_verse: Bɛbuale kɛ, “Yɛmenle, wɔ sonvolɛma ye le mediema mrenya bulu nee nwiɔ. Yɛ muala yɛ ze ko, yɛɛ yɛwɔ Keena maanle nu. Nuhua kazima ne wɔ yɛ ze anwo lɔ kɛkala, yɛɛ yɛ nuhua ko ɛwu.”

english_verse: Joseph replied: It's like I said. You're spies,
translation_verse: Dwosefi zele kɛ, “Ɔle kɛ mɔɔ meha ala la. Bɛle busiama.

english_verse: and I'm going to find out the truth. I swear by the life of the king that you won't leave this place until your youngest brother comes here.
translation_verse: Na saa bɛse ɔnle nɔhalɛ a ɛnee yɛfa ɛhye yɛanlea bɛ nɔhalɛ. Meka yɛ belemgbunli ne ati kɛ saa bɛtɛkɔfale bɛ diema ekyi zɔhane bɛtɛbale a, bɛndu bɛ gyakɛ ko bɛnvi ɛke.

english_verse: Choose one of you to go after your brother, while the rest of you stay here in jail. That will show whether you are telling the truth. But if you are lying, I swear by the life of the king that you are spies!
translation_verse: Bɛzoa bɛ nuhua ko bɛmaa ɔhɔva bɛ diema ne ɔrɛla. Bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛha la, bɛbagua bɛ efiade, na bɛbagua ɛkɛ ne toonwo kɔkpula kɛ yɛkɛnwu nɔhalɛ mɔɔ wɔ bɛ edwɛkɛ ne anu la. Tɛ ye zɔhane ɛdeɛ a, meka yɛ belemgbunli ne ati kɛ bɛle busiama.”

english_verse: Joseph kept them all under guard for three days,
translation_verse: Na ɔvale bɛ ɔguale efiade kenle nsa.

english_verse: before saying to them: Since I respect God, I'll give you a chance to save your lives.
translation_verse: Ye kenle nsa ne azo, Dwosefi zele ɔ mediema ne mɔ kɛ, “Bɛyɛ ɛhye na bɛkɛnyia bɛ ti, ɔluakɛ mele sonla mɔɔ mesulo Nyamenle a.

english_verse: If you are honest men, one of you must stay here in jail, and the rest of you can take the grain back to your starving families.
translation_verse: Saa bɛdabɛ bɛse bɛle menli mɔɔ ka nɔhalɛ a, ɛnee bɛgyakyi bɛ nuhua ko wɔ efiade ɛke, na bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛha la bɛva abɛlɛ ne bɛhɔ bɛmaa bɛ sua nu amra ɛnyia bie ɛli.

english_verse: But you must bring your youngest brother to me. Then I'll know that you are telling the truth, and you won't be put to death. Joseph's brothers agreed
translation_verse: Na akee bɛva bɛ diema nrenya kakula ne bɛrɛla, amaa meanwu kɛ bɛ edwɛkɛ ne le nɔhalɛ na bɛangu bɛ.” Na bɛkponlenle zolɛ.

english_verse: and said to one another, “We're being punished because of Joseph. We saw the trouble he was in, but we refused to help him when he begged us. That's why these terrible things are happening.”
translation_verse: Akee bɛhanle bɛhilele bɛ nwo ngoko kɛ, “Nɔhalɛ, yɛdi fɔlɛ bɔkɔɔ wɔ mɔɔ yɛvale yɛyɛle yɛ diema nrenya ne la anwo. Yɛdayɛ yɛnwunle ye ɛbolɛ mɔɔ ɛnee ɛlɛte, wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɛnee ɔlɛkpa yɛ kyɛlɛ la, noko yɛandie ye. Yemɔti a abodelɛ ɛhye ɛra yɛ nwo zo la.”

english_verse: Reuben spoke up, “Didn't I tell you not to harm the boy? But you wouldn't listen, and now we have to pay the price for killing him.”
translation_verse: Wulubɛn buale bɛ kɛ, “Se menganle mengilele bɛ kɛ bɛmmafa bɛ sa bɛka kakula ne. Noko bɛandie. Ye mogya ne anwo kakɛ a bɛlɛtua yɛ la.”

english_verse: They did not know that Joseph could understand them, since he was speaking through an interpreter.
translation_verse: Ɛnee bɛnze kɛ Dwosefi te aneɛ ne mɔɔ bɛlɛka la, ɔluakɛ ɛnee awie a tendɛ bɛ nloa zo a.

english_verse: Joseph turned away from them and cried, but soon he turned back and spoke to them again. Then he had Simeon tied up and taken away while they watched. Joseph's Brothers Return to Canaan
translation_verse: Na Dwosefi gyakyile bɛ ɛkɛ ne hɔle na ɔhɔzunle. Ɔziale ɔrale bɛ nwo ɛkɛ ne na ɔradendɛle ɔhilele bɛ. Akee ɔyele Semɛyɔn na ɔmanle bɛkyekyele ye wɔ bɛ muala bɛ nye zo ɛkɛ ne. Dwosefi amediema ne mɔ sia ahɔ Keena

english_verse: Joseph gave orders for his brothers' grain sacks to be filled with grain and for their money to be put in their sacks. He also gave orders for them to be given food for their journey home. After this was done,
translation_verse: Dwosefi manle bɛvale abɛlɛ bɛguale bɛ ahodoku ne mɔ anu, eza ɔmanle bɛvale ko biala ezukoa bɛziale bɛwulale ye kodoku ne anu. Eza ɔmanle bɛmanle bɛ aleɛ mɔɔ bɛbali wɔ adenle nu la.

english_verse: they each loaded the grain on their donkeys and left.
translation_verse: Akee bɛvale abɛlɛ ne bɛguale bɛ asoaso ne mɔ azo na bɛhɔle.

english_verse: When they stopped for the night, one of them opened his sack to get some grain for his donkey, and at once he saw his moneybag.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ bɛkɔ na bɛhɔdwule adenle nu la, bɛ nuhua ko yɛle kɛ ɔmaa ye asoaso ne aleɛ, yemɔti ɔdele ye kodoku ne anloa, na nea, ye ezukoa ye a la kodoku ye anloa la.

english_verse: “Here's my money!” he told his brothers. “Right here in my sack.” They were trembling with fear as they stared at one another and asked themselves, “What has God done to us?”
translation_verse: Ɔzele ɔ mediema ne mɔ kɛ, “Bɛnlea, bɛziane me ezukoa ne; yemɔ a zia me kodoku ye anloa la!” Bɛnwunle ɛhye la, bɛ nwo bubule bɛ na bɛvale anwowozolɛ bɛbizebizale bɛ nwo kɛ, “Duzu munzule a Nyamenle ɛlɛmaa yeara yɛ nwo zo a?”

english_verse: When they returned to the land of Canaan, they told their father Jacob everything that had happened to them:
translation_verse: Bɛdwule sua nu wɔ Keena la, bɛhanle mɔɔ ɛzi bɛ nwo zo la amuala bɛhilele bɛ ze Gyekɔbo, na bɛhanle kɛ,

english_verse: But we told him, “We're honest men, not spies.
translation_verse: Na yɛhanle yɛhilele ye kɛ yɛnle busiama. Yɛle menli mɔɔ di nɔhalɛ a.

english_verse: We come from a family of twelve brothers. The youngest is still with our father in Canaan, and the other is dead.”
translation_verse: Yɛlua mediema mrenya bulu nee nwiɔ, yɛ ze ko. Ko ɛwu, yɛɛ kazima ne wɔ yɛ ze anwo lɔ kɛkala wɔ Keena.

english_verse: Then the governor of Egypt told us, “I'll find out if you really are honest. Leave one of your brothers here with me, while you take the grain to your starving families.
translation_verse: Na nrenya ne mɔɔ nea azɛlɛ ne azo la zele kɛ, saa ɔkɛnwu yɛ nɔhalɛ, na amgba yɛlɛka nɔhalɛ a, ɛnee yɛgyakyi yɛ nuhua ko ɔ nwo ɛkɛ ne, na yɛva abɛlɛ ne yɛrɛlɛ sua nu amra.

english_verse: But bring your youngest brother to me, so I can be certain that you are honest men and not spies. After that, I'll let your other brother go free, and you can stay here and trade.”
translation_verse: Na saa yɛsia yɛahɔ a, ɛnee yɛva yɛ diema kazima ne yɛrɛla. Saa yɛyɛ ye zɔhane a yɛɛ ɔkɛnwu kɛ yɛnle busiama, na yɛlɛka nɔhalɛ a. Ɛhye bahile yɛ nɔhalɛlilɛ na yeaye yɛ diema ne yeamaa yɛ, na yɛali gua wɔ maanle ne anu.”

english_verse: When the brothers started emptying their sacks of grain, they found their moneybags in them. They were frightened, and so was their father Jacob,
translation_verse: Mɔɔ bɛtulutulule bɛ ahodoku ne mɔ, bɛwolɔwolale bɛ abɛlɛ ne la, bɛnwunle kɛ bɛ nuhua ko biala ezukoa bɔlɛ mɔɔ ɔ nee ye hɔle la wɔ ye kodoku ne anu. Mɔɔ bɛ nee bɛ ze bɛnwunle ezukoa ne mɔ la, bɛ rɛle bɔle kpole.

english_verse: who said, “You have already taken my sons Joseph and Simeon from me. And now you want to take away Benjamin! Everything is against me.”
translation_verse: Na bɛ ze zele kɛ, “Bɛmaa me mra ne mɔ ɛvi me sa. Dwosefi ɛwu, yɛɛ Semɛyɔn ɛvi me sa; eza bɛbava Bɛngyaman ɔdaye noko bɛahɔ. Duzu edwɛkɛ bɔbɔ yɛɛ akee ɛlɛsisi me nwo zo a?”

english_verse: Reuben spoke up, “Father, if I don't bring Benjamin back, you can kill both of my sons. Trust me with him, and I'll bring him back.”
translation_verse: Na Wulubɛn hanle kɛ, “Egya, saa meanva Bɛngyaman meanzia meamba a, ku me mra mrenya nwiɔ ne sie ɔ bo zo. Fa ye wula me sa nu, na me nee ye bara.”

english_verse: But Jacob said, “I won't let my son Benjamin go down to Egypt with the rest of you. His brother is already dead, and he is the only son I have left. I am an old man, and if anything happens to him on the way, I'll die from sorrow, and all of you will be to blame.”
translation_verse: Na Gyekɔbo zele kɛ, “Me ra ne nee bɛ ɛnrɛhɔ ɛnɛ nee ɛhyema. Ɔluakɛ ɔ diema ne ɛwu ɛmaa yeha ɔ ngome. Kɛkala mɔɔ mewie kpanyinli yɛ la, saa munzule bie to ye adenle nu wɔ bɛ adendulɛ ye anu a, bɛkɛmaa menwɔva nyane menwɔhɔ ewule nu.”

english_verse: The famine in Canaan got worse,
translation_verse: Akee ɛhɔne ne yɛle kpole wɔ Keena.

english_verse: until finally, Jacob's family had eaten all the grain they had bought in Egypt. So Jacob said to his sons, “Go back and buy some more grain.”
translation_verse: Yemɔti mɔɔ bɛwiele abɛlɛ ne mɔɔ bɛhɔdɔle wɔ Yigyibiti la di la, Gyekɔbo hanle hilele ɔ mra ne mɔ kɛ, “Bɛhɔ bieko, bɛhɔdɔ aleɛ ekyi bɛrɛlɛ yɛ.”

english_verse: Judah replied, “The governor strictly warned us that we would not be allowed to see him unless we brought our youngest brother with us. If you let us take Benjamin along, we will go and buy grain. But we won't go without him!”
translation_verse: Na saa ɛnrɛmaa ɔnrɛhɔ ɛdeɛ a, ɛnee yɛnrɛhɔ, ɔluakɛ nrenya ne se, ‘Saa bɛanva bɛ diema ne bɛamba a, bɛnrɛnwu me nyunlu.’ ”

english_verse: Jacob asked, “Why did you cause me so much trouble by telling the governor you had another brother?”
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo mɔɔ ɛnee bɛfɛlɛ ye Yizilayɛ la zele kɛ, “Duzu ati a bɛhanle bɛhilele nrenya ne kɛ bɛlɛ bɛ diema kakula bieko wɔ ɛkɛ a? Bɛ nee me anli ye boɛ fee.”

english_verse: They answered, “He asked a lot of questions about us and our family. He wanted to know if you were still alive and if we had any more brothers. All we could do was answer his questions. How could we know he would tell us to bring along our brother?”
translation_verse: Bɛbuale kɛ, “Nrenya ne bizebizale yɛ edwɛkɛ dɔɔnwo mɔɔ fane yɛ nee yɛ nwo amra anwo. Ɔbizale yɛ kɛ, ‘Asoo bɛ ze tɛte aze? Bɛlɛ adiema bieko wɔ ɛkɛ ɔ?’ Mɔɔ ɔbizebizale yɛ la yɛɛ yɛmanle ye nwolɛ mualɛ a. Yɛnze kɛ ɔkɛha ɔkɛhile yɛ kɛ, ‘Bɛva bɛ diema ko ne bɛrɛla.’ ”

english_verse: Then Judah said to his father, “Let Benjamin go with me, and we will leave at once, so that none of us will starve to death.
translation_verse: Dwuda hanle hilele ɔ ze kɛ, “Maa me nee kakula ne ɛhɔ, amaa yɛanyia aleɛ yɛali, na ɛdawɔ nee yɛdayɛ nee ngakula ngyikyi ne mɔ anwu. Mefa me nwo meabɔ agyinlanu meamaa ye.

english_verse: I promise to bring him back safely, and if I don't, you can blame me as long as I live.
translation_verse: Saa edwɛkɛ bie a, biza medame. Saa meanva ye meanzia meamba, meanva ye meambanwula ɛ sa nu a, ɛnee fa nwolɛ ngyelelɛ ne kyele me dahuu.

english_verse: If we had not wasted all this time, we could already have been there and back twice.”
translation_verse: Saa tɛ ɛhye mɔɔ ɛzi yɛ aze la a, anrɛɛ yɛhɔ yɛra fane nwiɔ.”

english_verse: Their father said: If Benjamin must go with you, take the governor a gift of some of the best things from our own country, such as perfume, honey, spices, pistachio nuts, and almonds.
translation_verse: Akee Gyekɔbo zele bɛ kɛ, “Saa zɛhae ala a ɔwɔ kɛ ɔyɛ a, ɛnee bɛyɛ ɛhye: bɛva maanle ye anu nzoleɛ kpalɛ ne mɔ bie wɔ bɛ ahodoku ne mɔ anu, ayile nwole evuanlɛ ekyi, wolɛ ekyi, ɛyɛlɛ, alufuanlɛ, ‘pesetakayo’ ma, yɛɛ ‘alemɔndo’ bɛhɔmaa nrenya ne kɛ ye ahyɛlɛdeɛ ɔ.

english_verse: Also take along twice the amount of money for the grain, because there must have been some mistake when the money was put back in your sacks.
translation_verse: Ezukoa ne mɔɔ bɛvale bɛguale bɛ ahodoku ne mɔ anloa la, bɛva ye mɔnwo, ɔkɛyɛ kɛ anyefo ɔ.

english_verse: Take Benjamin with you and leave at once.
translation_verse: Akee bɛva bɛ diema ekyi ne na bɛha bɛ nwo bɛhɔ nrenya ne ɛkɛ.

english_verse: When you go in to see the governor, I pray that God All-Powerful will be good to you and that the governor will let your other brother and Benjamin come back home with you. But if I must lose my children, I suppose I must.
translation_verse: Nyamenle Bedevinli ne ɛmaa nrenya ne ɛnwu bɛ anwunvɔne na ɔmaa bɛ nee bɛ diema ko ne nee Bɛngyaman ɛzia ɛrɛla. Saa me mra ne mɔ fi me sa ala a, ɛnee mewie ala ɛne.”

english_verse: The brothers took the gifts, twice the amount of money, and Benjamin. Then they hurried off to Egypt. When they stood in front of Joseph,
translation_verse: Yemɔti mgbavolɛ ne mɔ vale ahyɛlɛ ninyɛne ne, bɛvale ezukoa ne mɔnwo, bɛvale Bɛngyaman, na bɛzile nu bɛhɔle Yigyibiti, na bɛhɔle Dwosefi sua nu.

english_verse: he saw Benjamin and told the servant in charge of his house, “Take these men to my house. Slaughter an animal and cook it, so they can eat with me at noon.”
translation_verse: Dwosefi nwunle Bɛngyaman la, ɔzele sonvolɛ ne mɔɔ nea sua nu ɛkɛ ne la kɛ, “Fa menli ne mɔ bɛla sua nu, ku nane to aleɛ na me nee bɛ bakpula yɛ sa ɛnɛ ewia ye.”

english_verse: The servant did as he was told and took the brothers to Joseph's house.
translation_verse: Nrenya ne yɛle mɔɔ Dwosefi zele ye la na ɔvale mgbavolɛ ne mɔ ɔhɔle Dwosefi sua nu.

english_verse: But on the way they got worried and started thinking, “We are being taken there because of the money that was put back in our sacks last time. He will arrest us, make us his slaves, and take our donkeys.”
translation_verse: Bɛ nee bɛ dwule Dwosefi sua nu ɛkɛ ne la, ɛzulolɛ hanle bɛ na bɛhanle kɛ, “Ezukoa ne mɔɔ bɛziale bɛvale bɛsisianle yɛ ahodoku ne mɔ anloa la ati deenyi yɛɛ ɛmaa bɛva yɛ bɛra ɛke a. Ɔyɛ ɛhye, amaa yeanyia edwɛkɛ yeatia yɛ na yeaza yɛ yɛalie yɛ asoaso ne mɔ, na yeayɛ yɛ ahanra.”

english_verse: So when they arrived at Joseph's house, they said to the servant in charge,
translation_verse: Yemɔti bɛhɔle sonvolɛ ne mɔɔ nea Dwosefi sua nu ɛkɛ ne la anwo ɛkɛ na bɛ nee ye gyinlanle anlenkɛ ne anloa dendɛle, na bɛzele ye kɛ,

english_verse: “Sir, we came to Egypt once before to buy grain.
translation_verse: “Yɛmenle, yɛlumua yɛra ɛke ko yɛradɔ aleɛ yɛhɔ.

english_verse: But when we stopped for the night, we each found in our grain sacks the exact amount we had paid. We have brought that money back,
translation_verse: Mɔɔ yɛhɔdwule ɛleka mɔɔ yɛsokoɛ la, yɛzianyizianyinle yɛ ahodoku ne mɔ anloa, na yɛnwunle kɛ awie biala ezukoa ne mɔɔ ɔduale la, bɛzia bɛva bɛzia ye kodoku ne anloa. Yemɔti yɛzia yɛva ezukoa ne yɛra.

english_verse: together with enough money to buy more grain. We don't know who put the money in our sacks.”
translation_verse: Yɛ nee ezukoa fofolɛ mɔɔ yɛfa yɛadɔ aleɛ la noko ɛra. Yɛnze ahenle mɔɔ vale ezukoa ne wulowulale yɛ ahodoku ne mɔ anu a.”

english_verse: “It's all right,” the servant replied. “Don't worry. The God you and your father worship must have put the money there, because I received your payment in full.” Then he brought Simeon out to them.
translation_verse: Sonvolɛ ne zele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛmmasulo, bɛha bɛ ahonle bɛgua azule nu. Bɛ Nyamenle ne nee bɛ ze Nyamenle ne a kɛbezɛ ɛva ezukoa ne ɛwulowula bɛ ahodoku ne mɔ anu a. Bɛ ezukoa ɛdeɛ ne, me sa hanle ye bɔkɔɔ.” Akee ɔvale Semɛyɔn ɔvindele ɔrɛlɛle bɛ.

english_verse: The servant took them into Joseph's house and gave them water to wash their feet. He also tended their donkeys.
translation_verse: Sonvolɛ ne mɔɔ vale mgbavolɛ ne mɔ hɔle Dwosefi sua nu la manle bɛ nzule bɛnrinzinrinzinle bɛ gyakɛ anwo. Akee bɛmanle bɛ asoaso ne mɔ aleɛ.

english_verse: The brothers got their gifts ready to give to Joseph at noon, since they had heard they were going to eat there.
translation_verse: Bɛwiele la, bɛboɔboale ahyɛlɛ ninyɛne ne mɔ mɔɔ bɛ nee bɛ hɔle kɛ bɛfa bɛahɔmaa Dwosefi la anloa na bɛhendɛle kɛ saa ɔba ewia ne a bɛava bɛamaa ye, ɔluakɛ bɛdele kɛ ɔba a ɔ nee bɛ bakpula bɛ sa.

english_verse: When Joseph came home, they gave him the gifts they had brought, and they bowed down to him.
translation_verse: Dwosefi dwule sua nu la, bɛvale ninyɛne ne mɔɔ bɛ nee bɛ hɔle la bɛrale sua ne anu, bɛbɔle bɛ ti aze bɛmanle ye na bɛvale ninyɛne ne mɔ bɛmanle ye.

english_verse: After Joseph had asked how they were, he said, “What about your elderly father? Is he still alive?”
translation_verse: Ɔbizale bɛ agbɔkɛ nu na ɔbizale kɛ, “Bɛ ze te kpɔkɛ ɔ, meka nrenya kpanyinli ne mɔɔ bɛhanle ye edwɛkɛ la? Ɔtɛte ngoane nu ɔ?”

english_verse: They answered, “Your servant our father is still alive and well.” And again they bowed down to Joseph.
translation_verse: Bɛbuale kɛ, “Wɔ sonvolɛ ne, mɔɔ le yɛ ze, te kpɔkɛ; ɔtɛte ngoane nu.” Na bɛbɔle bɛ ti aze na bɛbutubutule ɔ nyunlu ɛkɛ.

english_verse: When Joseph looked around and saw his brother Benjamin, he said, “This must be your youngest brother, the one you told me about. God bless you, my son.”
translation_verse: Dwosefi manle ɔ nye zo la, ɔnwunle ɔ diema Bɛngyaman, ɔ nli ara ne, na ɔbizale kɛ, “Bɛ diema ekyi ne mɔɔ bɛhanle ye edwɛkɛ la, yemɔ ɛhye ɔ? Me ra nrenya, Nyamenle ɛnwu wɔ anwunvɔne!”

english_verse: Then, because of his love for Benjamin, he rushed off to his room and cried.
translation_verse: Na Dwosefi dwazole ndɛndɛ hɔle kɛ ɔkakpondɛ ɛleka yeavea yeazu, ɔluakɛ ɛnee ɔ nwo ɛlɛdɔ ɔ diema ne. Na ɔwolole ye suakunlu ɛkɛ ne na ɔzunle.

english_verse: After washing his face and returning, he was able to control himself and said, “Serve the meal!”
translation_verse: Akee ɔnrinzinle ɔ nyunlu, ɔzɔle ɔ nwo, na ɔvindele ɔrahanle kɛ, “Bɛziezie aleɛ ne.”

english_verse: Joseph was served at a table by himself, and his brothers were served at another. The Egyptians sat at yet another table, because Egyptians felt it was disgusting to eat with Hebrews.
translation_verse: Bɛzieziele ye aleɛ ɛdeɛ ngome na bɛzieziele mgbavolɛ ne mɔ ɛdeɛ ngome, yɛɛ Yigyibitima noko mɔɔ wɔ ɛkɛ ne bie la ɛdeɛ ngome. Ɔboalekɛ ɔnle kɛ Yigyibitima nee Hibuluma bɔ nu di aleɛ. Ɔle bɛkyi ɔmaa Yigyibitima.

english_verse: To the surprise of Joseph's brothers, they were seated in front of him according to their ages, from the oldest to the youngest.
translation_verse: Bɛmanle mediema ne mɔ dɛnlɛdɛnlanle aze, bɛ nee Dwosefi bɛ nye bɔ zolɛ. Bɛdɛnlanle ye kɛmɔ bɛ awolɛ nu gyinlabelɛ si de la, kpanyinli ne lumua yɛɛ kakula ne li amozi. Na mgbavolɛ ne mɔ vale azibɛnwo nleɛnleanle bɛ nyunlu.

english_verse: They were served food from Joseph's table, and Benjamin was given five times as much as each of the others. So Joseph's brothers ate and drank with him and had a good time.
translation_verse: Bɛvale aleɛ bɛvile Dwosefi ɛkponle zo a bɛrɛlɛle bɛ a, na ko biala ɛdeɛ mɔɔ ɔnyianle la, Bɛngyaman nyianle ye mɔnwo nnu. Na bɛ nee Dwosefi nlonle na bɛ nye liele.

english_verse: Later, Joseph told the servant in charge of his house, “Fill the men's grain sacks with as much as they can hold and put their money in the sacks. Also put my silver cup in the sack of the youngest brother.” The servant did as he was told.
translation_verse: Fa me dwɛtɛ fufule kɔpo ne sia bɛ diema ekyi ne kodoku ne anloa, na fa ye ezukoa ne mɔɔ ɔvale ɔrale kɛ ɔfa yearadɔ abɛlɛ la boka nwolɛ.” Na sonvolɛ ne yɛle, kɛmɔ Dwosefi zele ye la.

english_verse: Early the next morning, the men were sent on their way with their donkeys.
translation_verse: Bɛvale mgbavolɛ ne mɔ asoaso ne mɔ bɛmanle bɛ nwonlomɔ mangyee ne ala, na bɛguale bɛ adenle.

english_verse: But they had not gone far from the city when Joseph told the servant, “Go after those men! When you catch them, say, ‘My master has been good to you. So why have you stolen his silver cup?
translation_verse: Mɔɔ bɛvi suakpole ne azo bɛyele bɛ nwo na bɛhɔle moa ekyii la, Dwosefi zoanle ye sonvolɛ ne kɛ, “Ka ɛ nwo toa menli ne mɔ. Saa ɛto bɛ a, biza bɛ kɛ, ‘Duzu ati a bɛva ɛtane bɛdua kpalɛ kakɛ ɛ?

english_verse: Not only does he drink from his cup, but he also uses it to learn about the future. You have done a terrible thing.’ ”
translation_verse: Duzu ati a bɛwua me menle kɔpo ne a? Yemɔ anu a ɔno a, yɛɛ yemɔ a ɔnea nu ɔfa ɔnwu mɔɔ bazi la a. Bɛyɛ ɛtane kpole!’ ”

english_verse: When the servant caught up with them, he said exactly what Joseph had told him to say.
translation_verse: Sonvolɛ ne zile nu na ɔhɔdole bɛ adenle nu, na ɔhanle edwɛkɛ ne ɔhilele bɛ.

english_verse: But they replied, “Sir, why do you say such things? We would never do anything like that!
translation_verse: Na bɛzele ye kɛ, “Duzu ati a yɛmenle kɛraha edwɛkɛ zɛhae kɛhile yɛ ɛ? Ɔkɛbɔ yɛ tɔ kɛ wɔ sonvolɛma, yɛkɛbɔ ɛbɛla mɔɔ le zɛhae a.

english_verse: We even returned the money we found in our grain sacks when we got back to Canaan. So why would we want to steal any silver or gold from your master's house?
translation_verse: Nea, ɛkenle ezukoa ne bɔbɔ mɔɔ ɛnee wɔ yɛ ahodoku ne mɔ anloa la, yɛhɔdwule Keena na yɛnwunle ye la, yɛvale yɛziale yɛrale. Ɛnee akee duzu ati yɛɛ yɛkɛwua dwɛtɛ fufule anzɛɛ ezukoa nvutuke wɔ ɛ menle ne sua nu a?

english_verse: If you find that one of us has the cup, then kill him, and the rest of us will become your slaves.”
translation_verse: Wɔ sonvolɛma ye ɛ, nuhua ko biala mɔɔ ɛkɛnwu kɔpo ne wɔ ye ɛkɛ ne la, ku ye, na maa yɛdayɛ noko mɔɔ yɛha la yɛyɛ wɔ ahanra.”

english_verse: “Good!” the man replied, “I'll do what you have said. But only the one who has the cup will become my slave. The rest of you can go free.”
translation_verse: Sonvolɛ ne zele kɛ, “Mɔɔ bɛha la ɛyɛ ɛkɛ. Bɛ nuhua ko biala mɔɔ menwɔnwu kɔpo ne wɔ ye ɛkɛ ne la bayɛ me kanranli. Bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛkɛha la bɛnli ɛzonle biala.”

english_verse: Each of the brothers quickly put his sack on the ground and opened it.
translation_verse: Yemɔti ɛkɛ ne ala bɛzokoɛzokoɛle bɛ ninyɛne ne mɔ bɛziele aze, na bɛtulutulule bɛ ahodoku ne mɔ anloa.

english_verse: Joseph's servant started searching the sacks, beginning with the one that belonged to the oldest brother. When he came to Benjamin's sack, he found the cup.
translation_verse: Sonvolɛ ne bɔle ɔ bo kpanyinli ne anwo zo ɔnleɛnleanle bɛ ninyɛne ne mɔ anu na ɔrawiele ye wɔ kakula ne anwo zo. Na bɛnwunle kɔpo ne wɔ Bɛngyaman kodoku ɛdeɛ ne anu.

english_verse: This upset the brothers so much that they began tearing their clothes in sorrow. Then they loaded their donkeys and returned to the city.
translation_verse: Mediema ne mɔ suosuanle bɛ adɛladeɛ ne mɔ anu, bɛkyekyele bɛ ninyɛne ne bɛzoale bɛ asoaso ne mɔ, na bɛziale bɛhɔle suakpole ne azo.

english_verse: When Judah and his brothers got there, Joseph was still at home. So they bowed down to Joseph,
translation_verse: Dwuda nee ɔ mediema ne mɔ hɔdwule Dwosefi sua nu ɛkɛ ne la, ɛnee ɔtɛbɔ ɛkɛ; na bɛdule bɛguale aze wɔ ɔ nyunlu.

english_verse: who asked them, “What have you done? Didn't you know I could find out?”
translation_verse: Dwosefi bizale bɛ kɛ, “Na duzu ɛbɛla a bɛbɔ la? Bɛnze kɛ sonla le kɛ medame, mekola meye ngonyia menwu mɔɔ bazi la ɔ?”

english_verse: “Sir, what can we say?” Judah replied. “How can we say we are innocent, when God has shown we are guilty? And now all of us are your slaves, especially the one who had the cup.”
translation_verse: Dwuda buale kɛ, “Na yɛnwu mɔɔ yɛka yɛahile yɛ menle bɔbɔ a? Duzu edwɛkɛ yɛɛ yɛlɛ yɛka a? Anzɛɛ kɛ yɛzi yɛye ɛzonle ɛhye wɔ yɛ nwo zo ɛ? Nyamenle ɛmaa yɛ fɔlɛlilɛ ɛla ali wienyi. Kɛkala yɛle wɔ ahanra. Yɛdayɛ yɛ muala nee ahenle mɔɔ bɛnwunle kɔpo ne wɔ ye ɛkɛ ne la, yɛle wɔ ahanra.”

english_verse: Joseph told them, “I would never punish all of you. Only the one who was caught with the cup will become my slave. The rest of you are free to go home to your father.” Judah Pleads for Benjamin
translation_verse: Dwosefi zele kɛ, “Ɔkɛbɔ me tɔ kɛ menwɔyɛ debie zɛhae a. Ahenle ne mɔɔ vale me kɔpo ne la, yemɔ ala a bayɛ me kanranli a. Bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛha la, bɛzia bɛhɔ bɛ ze anwo lɔ anzonudwolɛ nu.” Dwuda kpa Bɛngyaman ati kyɛlɛ

english_verse: Judah went over to Joseph and said: Sir, you have as much power as the king himself, and I am only your slave. Please don't get angry if I speak.
translation_verse: Akee Dwuda hwenle bikyele Dwosefi na ɔhanle kɛ, “O me menle, mebodo wɔ, maa wɔ sonvolɛ, menva me edwɛkɛ mendo ɛ nyunlu. Mmafa me nwo ɛya, ɔluakɛ ɛle kɛ belemgbunli ne ala la.

english_verse: You asked us if our father was still alive and if we had any more brothers.
translation_verse: Me menle, ɛbizale wɔ sonvolɛma ye kɛ, ‘Bɛ ze wɔ ɛkɛ ɔ? Bɛlɛ bɛ diema nrenya bie wɔ ɛkɛ ɔ?’

english_verse: So we told you, “Our father is a very old man. In fact, he was already old when Benjamin was born. Benjamin's brother is dead. Now Benjamin is the only one of the two brothers who is still alive, and our father loves him very much.”
translation_verse: Na yɛbuale wɔ kɛ, ‘Yɛ ze wɔ ɛkɛ, yeyɛ kpanyinli, yɛɛ yɛlɛ yɛ diema nrenya ekyi ko wɔ ɛkɛ. Egya wole ye wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɛnee yewie ɛrelera yɛ la. Kakula zɔhane adiema nrenya mɔɔ ɔ nee ye vi ɛkolɛ ko anu la ɛwu. Ɔ nli akunlu ɛdeɛ ne, ɔdaye ɔ ngome a yeha a, yɛɛ ɔ ze kulo ye kpalɛ.’

english_verse: You ordered us to bring him here, so you could see him for yourself.
translation_verse: Na ɛzele wɔ sonvolɛma ye kɛ, ‘Bɛva ye bɛrɛla bɛmaa menwu ye.’

english_verse: But you warned us that we could never see you again, unless our youngest brother came with us.
translation_verse: Na ɛzele yɛ kɛ, ‘Saa bɛanva bɛ diema nrenya ekyi ne bɛamba a, bɛnrɛnwu me nyunlu bieko.’

english_verse: So we returned to our father and reported what you had said.
translation_verse: “Yɛdwule sua nu la, wɔ sonvolɛma, yɛbɔle yɛ ze amaneɛ na yɛhanle wɔ edwɛkɛ ne amuala yɛhilele ye.

english_verse: Later our father sent us back here to buy more grain.
translation_verse: Yemɔti mɔɔ egya hanle kɛ, ‘Bɛhɔ bieko bɛhɔdɔ aleɛ ekyi bɛrɛla’ la,

english_verse: But we told him, “We can't go back to Egypt without our youngest brother. We will never be let in to see the governor, unless he is with us.”
translation_verse: yɛbuale kɛ, ‘Yɛnrɛhɔ. Saa yɛ diema ekyi ne kɔ bie a yɛɛ yɛkɛhɔ a, ɔluakɛ saa yeangɔ bie a nrenya ne ɛnrɛnlea yɛ nyunlu.’

english_verse: Sir, our father then reminded us that his favorite wife had given birth to two sons.
translation_verse: Na egya zele yɛ kɛ, ‘Bɛdabɛ bɛze kɛ me ye wole mralɛ mrenya nwiɔ.

english_verse: One of them was already missing and had not been seen for a long time. My father thinks the boy was torn to pieces by some wild animal,
translation_verse: Ko ɛgyakyi me ɛhɔ, na menganle kɛ nanemgbole bie a ɛhu ye a. Metɛnwunle ye toonwo a yeradwu ɛnɛ a.

english_verse: and he said, “I am an old man. If you take Benjamin from me, and something happens to him, I will die of a broken heart.”
translation_verse: Kɛkala mɔɔ mewie kpanyinli yɛ la, saa bɛfa ɛhye noko bɛkɔ, na edwɛkɛ bie si ɔ nwo zo a, ɛnee ɔkile kɛ mefa nyane a meahɔ ɛbolɔ a.’

english_verse: I promised my father that I would bring him safely home. If I don't, I told my father he could blame me the rest of my life.
translation_verse: Menvale me nwo membɔle agyinlanu memanle kakula ne wɔ egya ɛkɛ na menganle kɛ, ‘Saa meanva ye meambɛlɛ wɔ a, ɛnee fa ɛzonle ne amuala soa me wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ mede ngoane nu la.’

english_verse: Sir, I am your slave. Please let me stay here in place of Benjamin and let him return home with his brothers.
translation_verse: Yemɔti mebodo mesɛlɛ wɔ, maa wɔ sonvolɛ, menga ɛke kɛ wɔ kanranli, na maa kakula ne nee ɔ mediema ne mɔ ɛhɔ.

english_verse: How can I face my father if Benjamin isn't with me? I couldn't bear to see my father in such sorrow.
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ saa kakula ne ɛmboka nwolɛ a ɛnee kɛ mesi meazia meahɔ egya anwo lɔ ɛ? Mesulo mɔɔ kɛzi egya anwo zo la.”

english_verse: Since Joseph could no longer control his feelings in front of his servants, he sent them out of the room. When he was alone with his brothers, he told them, “I am Joseph.”
translation_verse: Akee Dwosefi nea a ɛnee ɔngola ɔ nwo sɔ wɔ menli mɔɔ ɛrayia ɛkɛ ne la anyunlu; na ɔdeanle nu kɛ, “Awie biala vi me nwo ɛke ɛhɔ.” Yemɔti bɛ muala bɛvindele na ɔhale Dwosefi angome, na ɔhilele ɔ nwo ɔmanle ɔ mediema ne mɔ nwunle ye sonla holɛ.

english_verse: Then he cried so loudly that the Egyptians heard him and told about it in the king's palace.
translation_verse: Na ɔzunle kpole kpalɛ ɔmanle Yigyibitima ne dele, yɛɛ belemgbunli ne sua nu amra dele.

english_verse: Joseph asked his brothers if his father was still alive, but they were too frightened to answer.
translation_verse: Na Dwosefi hanle hilele ɔ mediema ne mɔ kɛ, “Medame a mele Dwosefi. Egya tɛte aze ɔ?” Na ɔ mediema ne mɔ angola bɛ nloa anu tɛ, ɔluakɛ ɛnee bɛ ahonle ɛdu.

english_verse: Joseph told them to come closer to him, and when they did, he said: Yes, I am your brother Joseph, the one you sold into Egypt.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Dwosefi zele ɔ mediema ne mɔ kɛ, “Mebodo bɛ bɛbikye me.” Na bɛhwenle bɛbikyele ye. Na ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛ diema Dwosefi, mɔɔ bɛdɔnenle ye bɛmanle bɛ nee ye hɔle Yigyibiti la, yemɔ a le me.

english_verse: Don't worry or blame yourselves for what you did. God is the one who sent me ahead of you to save lives.
translation_verse: Bɛmmamaa ɔyɛ bɛ nyane, yɛɛ bɛmmafa bɛ nwo ɛya kɛ bɛdɔnenle me bɛmanle bɛ nee me rale ɛke a, ɔluakɛ Nyamenle a zoanle me kɛ menlumua bɛ nyunlu na memanlie menli dɔɔnwo ngoane a.

english_verse: There has already been a famine for two years, and for five more years no one will plow fields or harvest grain.
translation_verse: Ɛhɔne ne mɔɔ ɛra la, bɔ zo mɔɔ yenyia ɛvolɛ nwiɔ ɔ. Ɛvolɛ nnu ɛhɔne bieko tɛdi ɔ nzi mɔɔ awie ɛnrɛzo ɛya na yealua na yeabu a.

english_verse: But God sent me on ahead of you to keep your families alive and to save you in this wonderful way.
translation_verse: Nyamenle zoanle me manle menlumuale bɛ nyunlu amaa mealie bɛ nee bɛ bo zo amra mɔɔ bara la ngoane.

english_verse: After all, you weren't really the ones who sent me here—it was God. He made me the highest official in the king's court and placed me over all Egypt.
translation_verse: Yemɔti tɛ bɛmɛ yɛɛ bɛmanle membale ɛke a, Nyamenle ɔ. Yemɔ yɛɛ yemaa meyɛ belemgbunli ne sonvolɛ kpanyinli mɔɔ nea ye sua nu ɛke nee Yigyibiti maanle ye kɔsɔɔti a.

english_verse: Now hurry back and tell my father that his son Joseph says, “God has made me ruler of Egypt. Come here as quickly as you can.
translation_verse: “Yemɔti bɛha bɛ nwo waa bɛhɔ egya ɛkɛ na bɛhɔze ye kɛ, ‘Ɛ ra Dwosefi se: Nyamenle ɛyɛ me Yigyibitima kpanyinli na bɛla. Mmasi aze fee.

english_verse: You will live near me in the region of Goshen with your children and grandchildren, as well as with your sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else you own.
translation_verse: Saa ɛba a ɛ nee ɛ mra nee wɔ nlɔnra nee wɔ mboane nee wɔ nlankɛ ne mɔ amuala nee debie biala mɔɔ bɛlɛ la badɛnla Gohyɛn, amaa bɛabikye me.

english_verse: I will take care of you there during the next five years of famine. But if you don't come, you and your family and your animals will starve to death.”
translation_verse: Saa bɛwɔ Gohyɛn a, yɛɛ me nye bado bɛ nwo zo, wɔ ɛhɔne ɛvolɛ nnu ne mɔɔ ɛha la anu a. Saa tɛ ye zɔhane ɛdeɛ a, yemɔ ɛdawɔ nee wɔ sua nu amra bali ehyia na debie biala mɔɔ bɛlɛ la abo zo aminli bɔkɔɔ.’

english_verse: All of you, including my brother Benjamin, can tell by what I have said that I really am Joseph.
translation_verse: “Na kɛkala, bɛdabɛ bɛnwu debie, me diema Bɛngyaman bɔbɔ nwu debie, na bɛnwu kɛ medame Dwosefi yɛɛ melɛtendɛ meahile bɛ la.

english_verse: Tell my father about my great power here in Egypt and about everything you have seen. Hurry and bring him here.
translation_verse: Bɛha me tumi mɔɔ melɛ la anwo edwɛkɛ bɛhile egya. Bɛha bɛ nwo bɛhɔva egya bɛrɛla ɛke.”

english_verse: Joseph was still crying as he kissed each of his other brothers. After this, they started talking with Joseph.
translation_verse: Na Dwosefi vole ɔ mediema ne mɔ anvoka anwo, na ɔzunle ɔguale bɛ nwo zo. Ɛhye anzi, akee ɔ mediema ne mɔ nee ye dendɛle.

english_verse: When it was told in the palace that Joseph's brothers had come, the king and his officials were happy.
translation_verse: Nrɛlaleɛ hɔdole belemgbunli ne kɛ, “Dwosefi amediema mrenya ne mɔ ɛra.” Na belemgbunli ne nee ye mgbanyima ne mɔ anye liele kpalɛ.

english_verse: So the king said to Joseph: Tell your brothers to load their donkeys and return to Canaan.
translation_verse: Na belemgbunli ne zele Dwosefi kɛ, “Ka kile ɛ mediema ne mɔ kɛ, bɛyɛ ɛhye: Bɛva aleɛ bɛgua bɛ asoaso ne mɔ azo na bɛzia bɛhɔ Keena;

english_verse: Tell them to bring their father and their families here. I will give them the best land in Egypt, and they can eat and enjoy everything that grows there.
translation_verse: bɛhɔva bɛ ze nee bɛ sua nu amra amuala bɛrɛla, na mebamaa bɛ azɛlɛ kpalɛ bɛadɛnla zolɛ wɔ Yigyibiti ɛke. Saa bɛwɔ ɛke a bɛbanyia debie biala mɔɔ bɛkpondɛ wɔ azɛlɛ ne azo la.

english_verse: Also tell your brothers to take some wagons from Egypt for their wives and children to ride in. And be sure they bring their father.
translation_verse: Eza ka kile bɛ maa bɛyɛ ɛhye: Bɛva ehwili bɛvi ɛke bɛhɔ na bɛava ngakula ne mɔ nee bɛ ye mɔ, na bɛva bɛ ze bɛrɛla.

english_verse: They can leave their possessions behind, because they will be given the best of everything in Egypt.
translation_verse: Bɛmmadwenle bɛ ninyɛne ne mɔ anwo, ɔluakɛ debie kpalɛ biala mɔɔ wɔ Yigyibiti la le bɛ ɛdeɛ.”

english_verse: Jacob's sons agreed to do what the king had said. And Joseph gave them wagons and food for their trip home, just as the king had ordered.
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo amra ne mɔ yɛle mɔɔ bɛzele bɛ la. Dwosefi manle bɛ ehwili, kɛmɔ belemgbunli ne hanle la, na ɔmanle bɛ aleɛ mɔɔ bɛbali wɔ adenle nu la.

english_verse: Joseph gave some new clothes to each of his brothers, but to Benjamin he gave five new outfits and
translation_verse: Ɔmanle ko biala ɛvoyialilɛ adɛladeɛ ngɛnlɛma na ɔmanle Bɛngyaman adɛladeɛ ngɛnlɛma ngakyile nnu yɛɛ dwɛtɛ fufule ɛya nsa.

english_verse: To his father he sent ten donkeys loaded with the best things in Egypt, and ten other donkeys loaded with grain and bread and other food for the return trip.
translation_verse: Ɔnwanle ɔ ze noko Yigyibiti ninyɛne ngɛnlɛma asoaso bulu adesoa, asoaso mbelɛ bulu mɔɔ zozo abɛlɛ, kpanwo, yɛɛ akee aleɛ mɔɔ saa ɔ ze ɛlɛba a ɔbali ye wɔ adenle nu la.

english_verse: Then he sent his brothers off and told them, “Don't argue on the way home!”
translation_verse: Akee ɔgyakyile ɔ mediema ne mɔ adenle, na mɔɔ bɛkɔ la ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛmmakɔdi butule wɔ adenle nu o!”

english_verse: Joseph's brothers left Egypt, and when they arrived in Canaan,
translation_verse: Yemɔti mediema ne mɔ vi Yigyibiti hɔle na bɛradwule bɛ ze Gyekɔbo anwo ɛkɛ wɔ Keena.

english_verse: they told their father that Joseph was still alive and was the ruler of Egypt. But their father was so surprised that he could not believe them.
translation_verse: Na bɛhanle bɛhilele ye kɛ, “Dwosefi tɛte aze, na yemɔ yɛɛ ɔnea Yigyibiti azɛlɛ ne kɔsɔɔti azo a.” Na Gyekɔbo anwo golole ye, ɔluakɛ ɛnee ɔnlie bɛ ɔnli.

english_verse: Then they told him everything Joseph had said. When he saw the wagons Joseph had sent, he felt much better
translation_verse: Na mɔɔ bɛhanle mɔɔ Dwosefi hanle hilele bɛ la amuala bɛhilele ye, na ɔnwunle ehwili ne mɔ mɔɔ Dwosefi ɛmaa bɛ nee bɛ ɛra kɛ bɛva bɛrava ye la, Gyekɔbo anwo gyinlanle ye,

english_verse: and said, “Now I can believe you! My son Joseph must really be alive, and I will get to see him before I die.”
translation_verse: na ɔhanle kɛ, “Yeyɛ boɛ. Me ra Dwosefi tɛte aze. Mekɔ meahɔnwu ye kolaa na meawu.”

english_verse: Jacob packed up everything he owned and left for Egypt. On the way he stopped near the town of Beersheba and offered sacrifices to the God his father Isaac had worshiped.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Yizilayɛ vale mɔɔ ɔlɛ la amuala na ɔzile nu kɛ ɔkɔ. Ɔhɔdwule Biyɛhyiba la, ɔbɔle azu ɔmanle ɔ ze Ayezeke Nyamenle ne.

english_verse: That night, God spoke to him in a dream and said, “Jacob! Jacob!” “Here I am,” Jacob answered.
translation_verse: Na nɔe ne Nyamenle dendɛle hilele ye wɔ ɛnyelɛzodeɛnwunlɛ nu, na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Gyekɔbo, Gyekɔbo!” Gyekɔbo liele zolɛ kɛ, “Mewɔ ɛke.”

english_verse: God said, “I am God, the same God your father worshiped. Don't be afraid to go to Egypt. I will give you so many descendants that one day they will become a nation.
translation_verse: Na Nyamenle zele ye kɛ, “Medame Nyamenle, mɔɔ le ɛ ze mɔ Nyamenle ne la ɔ. Mmasulo kɛ ɛkɛhɔ Yigyibiti, ɔluakɛ mebayɛ wɔ maanle wɔ ɛkɛ ne.

english_verse: I will go with you to Egypt, and later I will bring your descendants back here. Your son Joseph will be at your side when you die.”
translation_verse: Me nee wɔ bahɔ Yigyibiti, na eza meava wɔ meazia meara. Dwosefi banwu wɔ ewule nu.”

english_verse: When Jacob went to Egypt, his children who were born in northern Syria also went along with their families. Jacob and his wife Leah had a total of
translation_verse: Ɛhye mɔ a le mralɛ mrenya mɔɔ Gyekɔbo nee ɔ ye Liya wole bɛ wɔ Mɛsɔpɔteemea a. Bɛ ra raalɛ a le Daena. Ɛka bɛ muala ɛbɔ nu a, ɛnee mralɛ nee nlɔnra mraalɛ nee mrenya mɔɔ Gyekɔbo luale ɔ ye Liya anwo zo nyianle la le abulasa nee nsa.

english_verse: The king will call you in and ask what you do for a living.
translation_verse: Na saa belemgbunli ne fɛlɛ bɛ na ɔbiza bɛ kɛ, ‘Duzu gyima a bɛyɛ a?’

english_verse: Jacob and Zilpah, the servant woman Laban had given his daughter Leah, had a total of
translation_verse: Liya sonvolɛ raalɛ Zelepa abo zo amra ne mɔɔ ɔ nee Gyekɔbo nyianle la le bulu nee nsia.

english_verse: Jacob and Bilhah, the servant woman Laban had given his daughter Rachel, had seven children and grandchildren. Their son Dan took his son Hushim. Their son Naphtali took his sons Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.
translation_verse: Relahyɛle sonvolɛ raalɛ Belehaa, mɔɔ Leeban vale manle ye la abo zo amra mɔɔ ɔ nee Gyekɔbo nyianle la ɛne.

english_verse: Jacob had sent his son Judah ahead of him to ask Joseph to meet them in Goshen.
translation_verse: Akee Gyekɔbo zoanle Dwuda kɛ ɔhɔbɔ Dwosefi amaneɛ kɛ ɔ nee ye ɛyia Gohyɛn, na bɛhɔdwule Gohyɛn.

english_verse: So Joseph got in his chariot and went to meet his father. When they met, Joseph hugged his father around the neck and cried for a long time.
translation_verse: Na Dwosefi boɔboale ɔ nwo ɔvole ye konle ehwili nu ɔhɔyiale ɔ ze Gyekɔbo wɔ Gohyɛn. Ɔvale ɔ nwo ɔhilele ɔ ze, na ɔdule ɔdɔle ɔ kɔme nu ɔzunle ɔguale ɔ nwo ɔhyɛle kpalɛ.

english_verse: Jacob said to Joseph, “Now that I have seen you and know you are still alive, I am ready to die.”
translation_verse: Na Gyekɔbo hanle kɛ, “Kɛkala mɔɔ menwu ɛ nyunlu na menwu kɛ ɛtɛte ngoane nu la, mewu bɔbɔ a ɔnyɛ ɛhwee.”

english_verse: Then Joseph said to his brothers and to everyone who had come with them: I must go and tell the king that you have arrived from Canaan.
translation_verse: Dwosefi hanle hilele ɔ ze nee ɔ mediema ne mɔ kɛ, “Mekɔ belemgbunli ne ɛkɛ meahɔbɔ ye amaneɛ kɛ, ‘Me mediema mrenya ne mɔ nee egya sua nu amra mɔɔ anrɛɛ wɔ Keena la ɛra me nwo ɛke.

english_verse: I will tell him that you are shepherds and that you have brought your sheep, goats, cattle, and everything else you own.
translation_verse: Mebaha kɛ menli ne le mboaneneavolɛma, ɔluakɛ bɛsie nlankɛ; na bɛva bɛ mboane nee bɛ nlankɛ, nee bɛ debie biala mɔɔ bɛlɛ la bɛra.’

english_verse: When he does, be sure to say, “We are shepherds. Our families have always raised sheep.” If you tell him this, he will let you settle in the region of Goshen. Joseph wanted them to say this to the king, because the Egyptians did not like to be around anyone who raised sheep.
translation_verse: bɛha kɛ, ‘Wɔ sonvolɛma sie nlankɛ, na yemɔ a le gyima mɔɔ sumunli yɛ ngakula nu yɛ nee egya yɛyɛ toonwo mɔɔ yeradwu ɛnɛ a.’ Saa bɛka ye zɔhane a yɛɛ bɛbamaa bɛadɛnla Gohyɛn a, ɔluakɛ mboaneneavolɛ biala le kyibadeɛ maa Yigyibitima.”

english_verse: who asked them, “What do you do for a living?” “Sir, we are shepherds,” was their answer. “Our families have always raised sheep.
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne bizale Dwosefi amediema ne mɔ kɛ, “Duzu gyima a bɛyɛ a.” Bɛbuale kɛ, “Wɔ sonvolɛma le mboaneneavolɛma, kɛmɔ ɛnee yɛ ze mɔ de la.

english_verse: But in our country all the pastures are dried up, and our sheep have no grass to eat. So we, your servants, have come here. Please let us live in the region of Goshen.”
translation_verse: Yɛra wɔ maanle ye anu, ɔluakɛ yɛnnyia adidileka yɛmmaa yɛ mboane ne mɔ. Ɛhɔne mɔɔ ɛra Keena la bo zolɛ. Yɛbodo wɔ, maa wɔ sonvolɛma adenle maa bɛdɛnla Gohyɛn.”

english_verse: The king said to Joseph, “It's good that your father and brothers have arrived.
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne zele Dwosefi kɛ, “Ɛ ze nee ɛ mediema ne mɔ ɛra ɛ nwo.

english_verse: I will let them live anywhere they choose in the land of Egypt, but I suggest that they settle in Goshen, the best part of our land. I would also like for your finest shepherds to watch after my own sheep and goats.”
translation_verse: Yigyibiti azɛlɛ ne a la ɛkɛ ne la. Maa ɛ ze nee ɛ mediema ne mɔ ɛdɛnla ɛleka mɔɔ ɛdawɔ ɛnea a ɔle kpalɛ la. Maa bɛdɛnla Gohyɛn azɛlɛ zo, na saa bie mɔ wɔ nuhua mɔɔ kɛhola a, maa bɛnlea me nlankɛ ne mɔ azo.”

english_verse: Then Joseph brought his father Jacob and introduced him to the king. Jacob gave the king his blessing,
translation_verse: Akee Dwosefi vale ɔ ze Gyekɔbo rahilele belemgbunli ne. Na Gyekɔbo yileyilale belemgbunli ne.

english_verse: and the king asked him, “How old are you?”
translation_verse: Akee belemgbunli ne bizale Gyekɔbo kɛ, “Wɔli ɛvolɛ nyɛ?”

english_verse: Then Jacob gave the king his blessing once again and left.
translation_verse: Akee Gyekɔbo Yileyilale belemgbunli ne bieko na ɔhɔle.

english_verse: Joseph obeyed the king's orders and gave his father and brothers some of the best land in Egypt near the city of Rameses.
translation_verse: Na Dwosefi bɔle ɔ ze nee ɔ mediema ne mɔ atɛnlase, na ɔmanle bɛ azɛlɛ kpalɛ wɔ Yigyibiti ɔmanle bɛvale bɛyɛle bɛ ɛdeɛ, kɛmɔ Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne hanle la. Azɛlɛ ne bikye Yigyibiti suakpole ne mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye Relamɛsize la.

english_verse: The famine was bad everywhere in Egypt and Canaan, and the people were suffering terribly.
translation_verse: Akee ɛhɔne ne anu yɛle ɛsesebɛ, ɔluakɛ ɛnee aleɛ fee ɛnle maanle ne anu. Yemɔti menli mɔɔ wɔ Yigyibiti nee Keena la anwo bɛlɛle bɛ na bɛnwanle.

english_verse: So Joseph sold them the grain that had been stored up, and he put the money in the king's treasury.
translation_verse: Dwosefi diedianle ezukoa mɔɔ ɔnyianle ye wɔ abɛlɛ ne mɔɔ ɔdɔnenle ɔmanle Yigyibitima nee Keenama la amuala, na ɔvale ɔhɔmanle belemgbunli ne.

english_verse: But when everyone had run out of money, the Egyptians came to Joseph and demanded, “Give us more grain! If you don't, we'll soon be dead, because our money's all gone.”
translation_verse: Akee mɔɔ menli mɔɔ wɔ yigyibiti nee Keena la ezukoa wiele la, Yigyibitima kɔsɔɔti rale Dwosefi ɛkɛ ne na bɛzele ye kɛ, “Yɛ ezukoa ɛwie! Maa yɛ aleɛ. Yemɔti ɛnea yɛ wɔamaa yɛawu ɔ?”

english_verse: “If you don't have any money,” Joseph answered, “give me your animals, and I'll let you have some grain.”
translation_verse: Dwosefi buale bɛ kɛ, “Saa bɛ ezukoa ɛwie a ɛnee bɛva bɛ nlankɛ bɛrɛla bɛralie aleɛ.”

english_verse: Then the people came to him and said: Sir, there's no way we can hide the truth from you. We are broke, and we don't have any more animals. We have nothing left except ourselves and our land.
translation_verse: Ɛvolɛ zɔhane zenle la, ye ɛvolɛ ne mɔɔ doa ye la anu, menli ne razele Dwosefi kɛ, “Ɛhye ɛnle nyiane debie mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ yɛfa yɛfea yɛ menle a. Yɛ ezukoa ɛwie, yɛɛ yɛ nyɛmoa kɔsɔɔti ɛyɛ yɛ menle ɛdeɛ. Yɛnlɛ ɛhwee kɛ yɛ sonlabaka ne yɛɛ yɛ azɛlɛ ala.

english_verse: Don't let us starve and our land be ruined. If you'll give us grain to eat and seed to plant, we'll sell ourselves and our land to the king. We'll become his slaves.
translation_verse: Duzu ati a ɛnea yɛ wɔamaa yɛawu, yɛ azɛlɛ ye azɛkye ɛ? Tɔ yɛ nee yɛ azɛlɛ ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti na maa yɛ aleɛ, na yɛ muala yɛkɛyɛ belemgbunli ne ahanra. Eza maa yɛ ma maa yɛlua na azɛlɛ ye anla mgbane, na maa yɛ aleɛ na yɛanwu.”

english_verse: The famine became so severe that Joseph finally bought every piece of land in Egypt for the king
translation_verse: Yemɔti Dwosefi dɔle Yigyibiti azɛlɛ ne kɔsɔɔti manle belemgbunli ne. Yigyibitima dɔnenle bɛ azɛlɛ ne mɔ, ɔluakɛ ɛnee ɛhɔne ne anu ɛyɛ ɛsesebɛ kpole kpalɛ.

english_verse: except the priests. The king gave the priests a regular food allowance, so they did not have to sell their land.
translation_verse: Ahɔmenle ne mɔ azɛlɛ ɛdeɛ ne ala yɛɛ Dwosefi andɔ a. Ɔluakɛ ɛnee belemgbunli ne maa ahɔmenle ne mɔ ezukoa mɔɔ bɛfa bɛbɔ bɛ nwo mgbɔlɔka a. Yemɔti bɛandɔne bɛ azɛlɛ ne.

english_verse: Then Joseph said to the people, “You and your land now belong to the king. I'm giving you seed to plant,
translation_verse: Akee Dwosefi zele menli ne kɛ, “Bɛnwu ye kɛ, ɛnɛ kenle ye, medɔ bɛ nee bɛ azɛlɛ ne mɔ memaa belemgbunli ne. Memaa bɛ ma, na ɔwɔ kɛ bɛso ɛya na bɛdua.

english_verse: but one fifth of your crops must go to the king. You can keep the rest as seed or as food for your families.”
translation_verse: Saa bɛbu bɛ bɛyɔba ne a, ɔwɔ kɛ bɛkyɛ nu nnu na bɛtu ɛkpɔ ko bɛbɛlɛ belemgbunli ne na bɛdabɛ bɛfa nna. Bɛ ɛdeɛ ɛkpɔ nna ne, bie yɛɛ bɛbava bɛalua ɛya fofolɛ a, bɛbali bie na bɛamaa bɛ mra nee bɛ mbusua ne mɔ bie bɛali.”

english_verse: “Sir, you have saved our lives!” they answered. “We are glad to be slaves of the king.”
translation_verse: Na bɛbuale kɛ, “Wɔlie yɛ ngoane. Yɛmenle, maa yɛzɔ ɛ nye na yɛyɛ belemgbunli ne ahanra.”

english_verse: Then Joseph made a law that one fifth of the harvest would always belong to the king. Only the priests did not lose their land. Jacob Becomes an Old Man
translation_verse: Yemɔti Dwosefi lile mɛla kɛ Yigyibiti azɛlɛ ne kɔsɔɔti le belemgbunli ne ɛdeɛ. Mɛla ɛhye tɛbɔ ɛkɛ ne kɛkala kɛ, aleɛ biala mɔɔ kɛvinde azɛlɛ ne azo la, ɔwɔ kɛ bɛkyɛ nu nnu na belemgbunli ne nyia ɛkpɔ ko. Ahɔmenle ne mɔ azɛlɛ ɛdeɛ ne ala yɛɛ anyɛ belemgbunli ne ɛdeɛ a. Gyekɔbo ɛbizalɛdeɛ mɔɔ li amozi

english_verse: The people of Israel made their home in the land of Goshen, where they became prosperous and had large families.
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo nee ye sua nu amra dɛnlanle Yigyibiti, wɔ Gohyɛn azɛlɛ zo, na bɛnyianle bɛ nwo. Bɛwole mralɛ na bɛyɛle dɔɔnwo kpalɛ.

english_verse: When Jacob knew he did not have long to live, he called in Joseph and said, “If you really love me, you must make a solemn promise not to bury me in Egypt.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ ɔka ekyii Gyekɔbo wu la, ɔvɛlɛle ɔ ra Dwosefi na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Saa amgba ɛ nye sɔ me a, ɛnee fa ɛ sa fula me ɛzɔlɛ nu na bɔ ɛwɔkɛ kɛ ɛbali nɔhalɛ wɔamaa me. Mmasie me Yigyibiti ɛke;

english_verse: Instead, bury me in the place where my ancestors are buried.” “I will do what you have asked,” Joseph answered.
translation_verse: mekpondɛ kɛ ɛfa me ɛkɔ ɛleka mɔɔ egya mɔ wɔ la. Saa mewu a, ye me funli ne fi Yigyibiti ɛke na kɔzie me ɛleka mɔɔ bɛziele egya mɔ la.” Dwosefi buale kɛ, “Mebayɛ, kɛmɔ wɔha la.”

english_verse: “Will you give me your word?” Jacob asked. “Yes, I will,” Joseph promised. After this, Jacob bowed down and prayed at the head of his bed.
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo zele ye kɛ, “Ɛnee ka ndane.” Dwosefi hanle ndane, na Gyekɔbo butule ye ɛkpa ne ati sɔlɔ na ɔyɛle Nyamenle mo.

english_verse: Joseph was told that his father Jacob had become very sick. So Joseph went to see him and took along his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.
translation_verse: Ɛhye anzi bɛhanle bɛhilele Dwosefi kɛ, “Nea, ɛ ze ɛnde kpɔkɛ.” Yemɔti ɔvale ɔ mra mrenya nwiɔ ne, Yifelaem nee Manasɛ ɔhɔle kɛ ɔkakpɔla ye.

english_verse: When Joseph arrived, someone told Jacob, “Your son Joseph has come to see you.” Jacob sat up in bed, but it took almost all his strength.
translation_verse: Na bɛhanle bɛhilele Gyekɔbo kɛ, “Ɛ ra Dwosefi ɛra bakpɔla wɔ.” Yemɔti ɔmianle ɔ nye ɔdwazole ɔdɛnlanle ye ɛkpa ne azo.

english_verse: Jacob told Joseph: God All-Powerful appeared to me at Luz in the land of Canaan, where he gave me his blessing
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo zele Dwosefi kɛ, “Nyamenle Bedevinli ne yele ɔ nwo hilele me wɔ Lɛze mɔɔ wɔ Keena maanle nu la na ɔyilale me, ɔzele me kɛ,

english_verse: and promised, “I will give you a large family with many descendants that will grow into a nation. And I am giving you this land that will belong to you and your family forever.”
translation_verse: ‘Mebamaa wɔawo, na ɛ nwo azo. Mebamaa wɔanyia menli dɔɔnwo; mebamaa bɛayɛ ɛlɔne; mebava azɛlɛ ɛhye meamaa ɛ bo zo amra ayɛ bɛ ɛdeɛ bɔkɔɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Then Jacob went on to say: Joseph, your two sons Ephraim and Manasseh were born in Egypt, but I accept them as my own, just as Reuben and Simeon are mine.
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo zɔle zolɛ hanle kɛ, “Kɛkala, ɛ mra nwiɔ ne mɔɔ ɛwole bɛ wɔ Yigyibiti ɛke kolaa na meara la le me ɛdeɛ. Yifelaem nee Manasɛ le me mra, kɛmɔ Wulubɛn nee Semɛyɔn de ala la.

english_verse: Any children you have later will be considered yours, but their inheritance will come from Ephraim and Manasseh.
translation_verse: Ngakula mɔɔ ɛbawo bɛ wɔ ɛhye mɔ anzi la le wɔ ɛdeɛ. Saa bɛnyia agyadeɛ bie a, bɛbava bɛ mediema ɛhye mɔ aluma a bɛado zolɛ a.

english_verse: Unfortunately, your mother Rachel died in Canaan after we had left northern Syria and before we reached Bethlehem. And I had to bury her along the way.
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ mevi Peedan mendule me bo la yɛɛ Relahyɛle wule nyane nyane wɔ Keena adenle ne anu, mɔɔ ɛnee ɔka ekyii yɛdwu Yifelate la; ɔmanle menziele ye Yifelate adevinli ne.”

english_verse: Jacob was very old and almost blind. He did not recognize the two boys, and so he asked Joseph, “Who are these boys?” Joseph answered, “They are my sons. God has given them to me here in Egypt.” “Bring them to me,” Jacob said. “I want to give them my blessing.” Joseph brought the boys to him, and he hugged and kissed them.
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo ɛyɛ kpanyinli la ati ɔ nye ɛyɛ, yemɔti ɔnnwu debie kpalɛ. Dwosefi vale ngakula ne mɔ bikyele ɔ ze, na ɔ ze vole bɛ nvoka anwo na ɔvale bɛ ɔbɔle ye ɛbolɛ.

english_verse: Jacob turned to Joseph and told him, “For many years I thought you were dead and that I would never see you again. But now God has even let me live to see your children.”
translation_verse: Na Yizilayɛ zele Dwosefi kɛ, “Meanla meandwenle kɛ menwɔnwu ɛ nyunlu, noko nea, Nyamenle ɛmaa menwu ɛ mra noko.”

english_verse: Then Joseph made his sons move away from Jacob's knees, and Joseph bowed down in front of him with his face to the ground.
translation_verse: Na Dwosefi manle ngakula ne mɔ zo vile ɔ ze agyakɛ azo, na ɔbutule ɔ ze anyunlu ɔvale ɔ nye ɔbutule aze.

english_verse: After Joseph got up, he brought his two sons over to Jacob again. He led his younger son Ephraim to the left side of Jacob and his older son Manasseh to the right.
translation_verse: Akee Dwosefi dwule ngakula nwiɔ ne, Yifelaem wɔ ye fema zo, mɔɔ kile kɛ ɔwɔ Gyekɔbo bɛne zo, yɛɛ Manasɛ wɔ ye bɛne zo, mɔɔ kile kɛ ɔwɔ Gyekɔbo fema zo la, na ɔvale bɛ ɔbikyele ɔ ze.

english_verse: But before Jacob gave them his blessing, he crossed his arms, putting his right hand on the head of Ephraim and his left hand on the head of Manasseh.
translation_verse: Na Yizilayɛ denrɛle ɔ sa kɛ ɔyileyila bɛ, ɔdole ɔ sa ɔbɛkale nu, ɔvale ɔ sa fema ne ɔdole Yifelaem mɔɔ le kakula la ati zo, na yeava ɔ sa bɛne ne yeado Manasɛ mɔɔ le kpanyinli la ati zo.

english_verse: Then he gave Joseph his blessing and said: My grandfather Abraham and my father Isaac worshiped the Lord God. He has been with me all my life,
translation_verse: Na ɔyileyilale Dwosefi, ɔhanle kɛ: “Nyamenle ne mɔɔ me ze mɔ Ebileham nee Ayezeke zonlenle, Nyamenle ne mɔɔ ɛli me nyunlu wɔ me ɛbɛlabɔlɛ nu toonwo yeradwu ɛnɛ,

english_verse: and his angel has kept me safe. Now I pray that he will bless these boys and that my name and the names of Abraham and Isaac will live on because of them. I ask God to give them many children and many descendants as well.
translation_verse: Nyamenle soanvolɛ ne mɔɔ ɛlie me ɛvi munzule kɔsɔɔti anu la, Ɛyila mgbavolɛ ɛhye mɔ; na ɔlua bɛ nwo zo bɛbɔ me nee me ze mɔ Ebileham nee Ayezeke aluma atɛnlase; Na bɛ nwo ɛzo bɛyɛ ɛlɔne wɔ azɛlɛ ye azo!”

english_verse: Joseph did not like it when he saw his father place his right hand on the head of the younger son. So he tried to move his father's right hand from Ephraim's head and place it on Manasseh.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Dwosefi nwunle kɛ ɔ ze ɛva ɔ sa fema ne ɛdo Yifelaem ati zo la, yeanyɛ ye fɛ, yemɔti ɔyele ɔ ze asa wɔ Yifelaem ati zo kɛ ɔfa yeado Manasɛ ati zo.

english_verse: Joseph said, “Father, you have made a mistake. This is the older boy. Put your right hand on him.”
translation_verse: Ɔhanle ɔhilele ɔ ze kɛ, “Kyɛkyɛ, egya, mmayɛ ye zɔhane, ɔluakɛ ɛhye a le kpanyinli a na fa ɛ sa fema ne to ɔ ti zo.”

english_verse: But his father said, “Son, I know what I am doing. It's true that Manasseh's family will someday become a great nation. But Ephraim will be even greater than Manasseh, because his descendants will become many great nations.”
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo amkponle na ɔbuale kɛ, “Me ra, meze ye zɔhane. Ɔdaye noko ɔbayɛ ɛlɔne, eza ɔbayɛ kpole. Noko ɔ diema kakula ye bayɛ sonlakpole adɛla ye, yɛɛ ɔ bo zo amra bayɛ maanle maanle dɔɔnwo.”

english_verse: Jacob told him that in the future the people of Israel would ask God's blessings on one another by saying, “I pray for God to bless you as much as he blessed Ephraim and Manasseh.” Jacob put Ephraim's name first to show that he would be greater than Manasseh.
translation_verse: Yemɔti ɔyileyilale ngakula ne mɔ kenle ko ne ɔzele kɛ, “Bɛ duma nu yɛɛ Yizilayɛma balua ayila menli na bɛaha kɛ, ‘Nyamenle ɛmaa bɛyɛ kɛ Yifelaem nee Manasɛ la.’ ” Gyekɔbo luale adenle zɛhae azo vale Yifelaem yɛle Manasɛ kpanyinli.

english_verse: After that, Jacob said, “Joseph, you can see that I won't live much longer. But God will be with you and will lead you back to the land he promised our family long ago.
translation_verse: Akee Yizilayɛ zele Dwosefi kɛ, “Kɛmɔ wɔnwu ye la, ɔka ekyii mɔɔ mekɔ me ɛkɛla nzi a. Nyamenle nee bɛ badɛnla, na yeava bɛ gyɛlɛɛnye yeazia yeahɔ bɛ ze mɔ azɛlɛ ne azo.

english_verse: Jacob called his sons together and said: My sons, I am Jacob, your father Israel.
translation_verse: Akee Gyekɔbo vɛlɛle ɔ mra mrenya ne mɔ na ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛvɛlɛvɛlɛ bɛ nwo bɛrɛla bɛmaa menga mɔɔ kenle bie bazi bɛ nwo zo la mengile bɛ.

english_verse: Come, gather around, as I tell your future.
translation_verse: “Bɛbɔ nu bɛrɛla, Gyekɔbo amra mrenya. Bɛradie mɔɔ bɛ ze Yizilayɛ ka ahile bɛ la.

english_verse: Reuben, you are my oldest, born at the peak of my powers; you were an honored leader.
translation_verse: “Wulubɛn, wɔmɔ a ɛle me ra kpanyinli a, Me anwosesebɛ nee me kpoleyɛlɛ nu ralɛ mɔɔ lumua. Wɔlie duma adubɛnwo nu, wɔlie duma anwosesebɛ nu.

english_verse: Uncontrollable as a flood, you slept with my wife and disgraced my bed. And so you no longer deserve the place of honor.
translation_verse: Noko ɛse kɛ azule, yemɔti ɛnrɛnyia duma, Ɔboalekɛ ɛlale ɛ ze ɛkpa zo, Ɛvale ɔ ye; ɛguale nwolɛ evinli!

english_verse: Simeon and Levi, you are brothers, each a gruesome sword.
translation_verse: “Semɛyɔn nee Livae le mediema; Bɛ ayedɛ ɛnze kyɛ.

english_verse: I never want to take part in your plans or deeds. You slaughtered people in your anger, and you crippled cattle for no reason.
translation_verse: O me ɛkɛla, ɛ nee bɛ mmafa adwenle! O me sunsum, ɛ nee bɛ mmatu; Ɔluakɛ bɛfa ɛya a bɛku menli, Bɛ nwo tɛ bɛ a bɛbubu nlankɛ ndwɛlɛ.

english_verse: Now I place a curse on you because of your fierce anger. Your descendants will be scattered among the tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Munzule ɛha bɛ ɛyavalɛ, Ɔluakɛ bɛ ɛya nloa yɛ se. Munzule ɛha bɛ ahonle ɛfutulɛ, Ɔluakɛ ɔle amumuyɛ! Mebahyɛ bɛ nuhua na meabɔ bɛ asande wɔ Yizilayɛ.

english_verse: Judah, you will be praised by your brothers; they will bow down to you, as you defeat your enemies.
translation_verse: “Dwuda, ɛ mediema mrenya ne mɔ baye wɔ ayɛlɛ; Ɛbali wɔ kpɔvolɛma anwo zo konim. Ɛ ze amra mrenya babɔ bɛ ti aze amaa wɔ.

english_verse: My son, you are a lion ready to eat your victim! You are terribly fierce; no one will bother you.
translation_verse: Me ra Dwuda le kɛ awenade ralɛ, Ɔku ye kpɔvolɛ ne na ɔsia ɔbada. Ɔda na ɔtenrɛ ɔ nwo a, awenade belɛ ɔ, Nwane a kola tunwue ye a?

english_verse: You will have power and rule until nations obey you and come bringing gifts.
translation_verse: Belemgbunlililɛ ɛnrɛvi Dwuda sua nu, Yɛɛ mɛlalilɛma ɛnrɛkpa ye belemgbunli ebia bo, Kɔkpula kɛ ɔkɛdwu mɔɔ lɛ ye la ɛkɛ ne. Maanle maanle kɔsɔɔti badie ye.

english_verse: You will tie your donkey to a choice grapevine and wash your clothes in wine from those grapes.
translation_verse: Ɔkenda ye asoaso ralɛ wɔ vanye baka nwo, Ɔkenda ye asoaso wɔ vanye baka kpole nwo. Ɔfa nwanye ɔnrinzi ye adɛladeɛ nu, Na ɔkpo ye anwuma tɛladeɛ wɔ vanye ma nzule nu.

english_verse: Your eyes are darker than wine, your teeth whiter than milk.
translation_verse: Nwanye bamaa ɔ nye ayɛ yɔɔnwo, Na meleke amaa ɔ gye ayɛ nwohyee.

english_verse: Zebulun, you will settle along the seashore and provide safe harbors as far north as Sidon.
translation_verse: “Zɛbulɛn badɛnla nyevile nloa; Ɔbayɛ ahonle mɔɔ meli gyinla zo a, Yɛɛ ye ɛweɛne badwu Saedɛn.

english_verse: Issachar, you are a strong donkey resting in the meadows.
translation_verse: “Yesakaa le asoaso mɔɔ anwo yɛ se a, Ɔla mboane tunli ne mɔ avinli.

english_verse: You found them so pleasant that you worked too hard and became a slave.
translation_verse: Ɔnwunle kɛ ɛnwomenlelielɛ ɛleka le kpalɛ, Yɛɛ azɛlɛ ne noko le kɛnlɛma; Yemɔti ɔhanle ɔ nwo aze ɔzoale adesoa, Na ɔyɛle gyima ɛsesebɛ ɛyɛlɛ nu kanra.

english_verse: Dan, you are the tribe that will bring justice to Israel.
translation_verse: “Dan babua ye menli ne ndɛne, Kɛ Yizilayɛ mbusua ekpunli ne mɔ anu ko.

english_verse: You are a snake that bites the heel of a horse, making its rider fall.
translation_verse: Dan bayɛ ɔ nwo ɛwɔlɛ ala adenle nu, Ɛkyenlebenle mɔɔ la adehane, ɔkeka mgbɔnwɔ ne mɔ agyakɛ, Ɔmaa mɔɔ de zo la tu tɔ alɛnranyunlu.

english_verse: Our Lord, I am waiting for you to save us.
translation_verse: “O Ɛdɛnkɛma, melɛkendɛ wɔ ngoanelielɛ ne.

english_verse: Gad, you will be attacked, then attack your attackers.
translation_verse: “Nwule bawua Gaade, Na ɔbavoa bɛ ndinlizo.

english_verse: Asher, you will eat food fancy enough for a king.
translation_verse: “Ahya azɛlɛ bahye aleɛ amaa ye, Na yeado ɛkponle kɛ arelemgbunli.

english_verse: Naphtali, you are a wild deer with lovely fawns.
translation_verse: “Nafetalae le kɛ kutu mɔɔ ɛhwee ɛngyegye ye, Na ɔwo mralɛ ngɛnlɛma.

english_verse: Joseph, you are a fruitful vine growing near a stream and climbing a wall.
translation_verse: “Dwosefi le kɛ baka mɔɔ so na ɔgyi azule nloa la, Ye ngane ne mɔ twenlehwenle bane ti.

english_verse: Enemies attacked with arrows, refusing to show mercy.
translation_verse: Ɛdadolɛma tetale ye, bɛtotole ye ɛda, Na bɛgyegyele ye kpole kpalɛ.

english_verse: But you stood your ground, swiftly shooting back with the help of Jacob's God, the All-Powerful One— his name is the Shepherd, Israel's mighty rock.
translation_verse: Noko ye ɛda ɛdeɛ ne andɔ aze. Ɔ sa nu yɛle ɛsesebɛ wɔ Gyekɔbo Nyamenle Bedevinli ne tumi nu, Wɔ Mboaneneavolɛ Yizilayɛ Pepɛdievolɛ ne duma nu.

english_verse: Your help came from the God your father worshiped, from God All-Powerful. God will bless you with rain and streams from the earth; he will bless you with many descendants.
translation_verse: Ɛ ze Nyamenle ne ɛnlea ɛ nwo zo, Nyamenle Bedevinli ne ɛdɔ nyilalɛ dɔɔnwo vi anwuma ɛgua ɛ nwo zo. Ɔva nyilalɛ ɔvi azɛlɛ buma nu ɔrɛlɛ wɔ, Ɔmaa wɔ nyɛfonlɛ nloa nee ɛkolɛ nu nyilalɛ.

english_verse: My son, the blessings I give are better than the promise of ancient mountains or eternal hills. Joseph, I pray these blessings will come to you, because you are the leader of your brothers.
translation_verse: Ɛ ze nyilalɛ ne mɔ, Mɔɔ yɛ ɛnlomboɛ tɛla me awovolɛma ɛdeɛ ne, ɛnyi ɛyɛ kɛ awoka mɔɔ ɛndudu ɛlɛ, Ɛrɛla Dwosefi anwo zo, na ɔgua mɔɔ bɛdu ye bɛzie ahane, Bɛvi ɔ mediema ne mɔ anu la, anwo zo.

english_verse: Benjamin, you are a fierce wolf, destroying your enemies morning and evening.
translation_verse: “Bɛngyaman le kɛ bɛdi mɔɔ kpondɛ nane ali; Ɔdi mɔɔ ɔkɛhye ye nwonlomɔ ne la, Ɔdwu nɔsolɛ a yeahye fofolɛ yeali.”

english_verse: These are the twelve tribes of Israel, and this is how Jacob gave each of them their proper blessings. Jacob's Death
translation_verse: Ɛhye mɔ amuala a le Yizilayɛ mbusua ekpunli ekpunli bulu nee nwiɔ ne a; yɛɛ mɔɔ bɛ ze hanle hilele bɛ wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɔyileyila bɛ la ɛne. Ɔvale ko biala nyilalɛ mɔɔ ɔfɛta la ɔmanle ye. Gyekɔbo ewule nee ye ɛzielɛ

english_verse: Both the cave and the land that goes with it were bought from the Hittites.
translation_verse: Azɛlɛ ne nee bolɛ bɔne ne mɔɔ wɔ nu la, bɛdɔle bɛvile Hɛtema lɔ.”

english_verse: When Jacob had finished giving these instructions to his sons, he lay down on his bed and died.
translation_verse: Gyekɔbo wiele tendɛ kile ɔ mra mrenya ne mɔ la, ɔnyenyanle ɔ nwo ɔlale, na ɔgule ye ɛnwomenle mɔɔ li amozi la, na ɔwule.

english_verse: Joseph started crying, then leaned over to hug and kiss his father.
translation_verse: Akee Dwosefi dule dɔle ɔ ze anwo zo na ɔzunle, na ɔvole ɔ nvoka anwo.

english_verse: When the time of mourning was over, Joseph said to the Egyptian leaders, “If you consider me your friend, please speak to the king for me.
translation_verse: Mekɛ mɔɔ bɛfa bɛazu ye la pɛle nu la, Dwosefi hanle hilele bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛwɔ belemgbunli ne sua nu la kɛ, “Saa mezɔ bɛ nye ɛdeɛ a, ɛnee mebodo bɛ, bɛha bɛhile belemgbunli ne bɛmaa me kɛ

english_verse: Just before my father died, he made me promise to bury him in his burial cave in Canaan. If the king will give me permission to go, I will come back here.”
translation_verse: egya manle menganle ndane kɛ saa ɔwu a, menwɔzie ye wɔ ɔdaye ye nla mɔɔ yepɛ wɔ Keena la anu. Ɛhye ati mesɛlɛ ye na meahɔ meahɔzie egya, na meazia meara.”

english_verse: The king answered, “Go to Canaan and keep your promise to your father.”
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne manle ye adenle, ɔse, “Kɔ na kɔzie ɛ ze, kɛmɔ wɔ ndane ne mɔɔ ɛhanle la se la.”

english_verse: After crossing the Jordan River, Joseph stopped at Atad's threshing place, where they all mourned and wept seven days for Jacob.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ bɛradwule Etade ɛleka mɔɔ bɛwozo ma ne, wɔ azule Dwɔdan ne anloa la, bɛzunle nyane nyane bie bɛyele awolɛ kpalɛ. Dwosefi manle bɛzunle ɔ ze wɔ ɛkɛ ne toonwo kenle nsuu.

english_verse: The Canaanites saw this and said, “The Egyptians are in great sorrow.” Then they named the place “Egypt in Sorrow.”
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Keenama mɔɔ wɔ maanle ne anu la nwunle kɛ bɛlɛsi bɛdi nyane bɛsu wɔ Etade ma ɛwozolɛ ɛleka ne la, bɛhanle kɛ, “Yigyibitima nyanelilɛ ɛhye le kpole.” Yemɔti bɛdonle ɛkɛ ne Ebɛle Mezeleeyem.

english_verse: So Jacob's sons did just as their father had instructed.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Gyekɔbo amra ne mɔ yɛle mɔɔ bɛ ze kpondɛ la manle ye.

english_verse: They took him to Mamre in Canaan and buried him in Machpelah Cave, the burial place Abraham had bought from Ephron the Hittite.
translation_verse: Bɛvale ye funli ne bɛhɔle Keena na bɛhɔziele ye bolɛ bɔne nu wɔ Makepilaa azɛlɛ zo, wɔ Mameli aduduleɛ. Ebileham dɔle azɛlɛ ne vile Hɛtenli Yifolɔn ɛkɛ, kɛ ɔfa yeayɛ ye azie.

english_verse: After the funeral, Joseph, his brothers, and everyone else returned to Egypt. Joseph's Promise to His Brothers
translation_verse: Dwosefi ziele ɔ ze wiele la akee ɔ nee ɔ mediema ne mɔ nee menli mɔɔ hɔzɔhonle ye la amuala ziale rale Yigyibiti. Dwosefi si ɔ mediema ne mɔ ahonle

english_verse: After Jacob died, Joseph's brothers said to each other, “What if Joseph still hates us and wants to get even with us for all the cruel things we did to him?”
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Dwosefi amediema ne mɔ nwunle kɛ bɛ ze ɛwu la, bɛhanle kɛ, “Ɔkɛyɛ kɛ Dwosefi akee bakpo yɛ, na yeadua yɛ munzule ɛbɛla ne mɔɔ yɛbɔle la anwo kakɛ.”

english_verse: So they sent this message to Joseph: Before our father died,
translation_verse: Yemɔti bɛzoanle bɛmanle bɛvale nrɛlaleɛ bɛhɔmanle Dwosefi kɛ, “Ɛ ze bawu la,

english_verse: he told us, “You did some cruel and terrible things to Joseph, but you must ask him to forgive you.” Now we ask you to please forgive the terrible things we did. After all, we serve the same God that your father worshiped. When Joseph heard this, he started crying.
translation_verse: ɔhanle kɛ, ‘Bɛha bɛhile Dwosefi kɛ, mebodo wɔ, fa ɛ mediema ne mɔ mɛladonlɛ nee bɛ ɛtane kyɛ bɛ, ɔboalekɛ bɛyɛle wɔ ɛtane.’ Zɔhane ati kɛkala, yɛbodo wɔ, fa ɛ ze Nyamenle ne sonvolɛma mɛladonlɛ kyɛ bɛ.” Bɛhanle ɛhye bɛhilele Dwosefi la, ɔzunle.

english_verse: Right then, Joseph's brothers came and bowed down to the ground in front of him and said, “We are your slaves.”
translation_verse: Akee ɔ mediema ne mɔ radule guale ɔ nyunlu na bɛzele kɛ, “Yɛra kɛ yɛle wɔ ahanra.”

english_verse: But Joseph told them, “Don't be afraid! I have no right to change what God has decided.
translation_verse: Na Dwosefi zele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛmmasulo; na tɛ mame a megyi Nyamenle agyakɛ anu a!

english_verse: You tried to harm me, but God made it turn out for the best, so that he could save all these people, as he is now doing.
translation_verse: Bɛmɛ ɛdeɛ, ɛnee bɛkpondɛ me nee munzule, na Nyamenle kpondɛle me nee saleɛ, amaa yeara ye zɔhane na mealie menli dɔɔnwo ngoane, kɛmɔ ɛnɛ bɛde la.

english_verse: Don't be afraid! I will take care of you and your children.” After Joseph said this, his brothers felt much better. Joseph's Death
translation_verse: Yemɔti bɛmmasulo; mebanlea bɛ nee bɛ mra ne mɔ amuala.” Ɔzile bɛ ɛbolɛ na ɔkyekyele bɛ rɛle. Dwosefi ewule ne

english_verse: Joseph lived in Egypt with his brothers until he died at the age of
translation_verse: Dwosefi nee ɔ ze sua nu amra dɛnlanle Yigyibiti. Ɔlile ɛvolɛ ɛya ko ɛvolɛ bulu na yeawu.

english_verse: Joseph lived long enough to see Ephraim's children and grandchildren. He also lived to see the children of Manasseh's son Machir, and he welcomed them into his family.
translation_verse: Dwosefi nwunle Yifelaem amra nee nlɔnra yɛɛ Manasɛ ara Meekɛ amra mɔɔ ɔwole bɛ ɔguale ɔdaye Dwosefi ɔ gyakɛ azo la.

english_verse: Before Joseph died, he told his brothers, “I won't live much longer. But God will take care of you and lead you out of Egypt to the land he promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
translation_verse: Na Dwosefi zele ɔ mediema ne mɔ kɛ, “Ɔka ekyii mewu; Nyamenle banlea bɛ na yeaye bɛ yeavi azɛlɛ ɛhye azo yeahɔ azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ ɔhanle ndane ɔhilele bɛ ze mɔ Ebileham, Ayezeke nee Gyekɔbo kɛ ɔbava yeamaa bɛ la azo.”

english_verse: Now promise me that you will take my body with you when God leads you to that land.”
translation_verse: Na Dwosefi manle ɔ mediema ne mɔ bɔle ɛwɔkɛ na ɔzele kɛ, “Bɛbɔ me ɛwɔkɛ kɛ, saa Nyamenle baye bɛ fi azɛlɛ ɛhye azo kɛ ɔ nee bɛ kɔ a, bɛkɛva me mbowule bɛkɛhɔ.”

english_verse: After Joseph, his brothers, and everyone else in that generation had died,
translation_verse: Mekɛ ne hɔle bie la Dwosefi, ɔ mediema mrenya ne mɔ nee awolɛndoazo zɔhane anu amra kɔsɔɔti wule.

english_verse: the people of Israel became so numerous that the whole region of Goshen was full of them.
translation_verse: Noko Yizilayɛ abo zo amra ne dale, yɛle mɔnwo mɔnwo, bɛnyinle anwosesebɛ nu na bɛvale Yigyibiti maanle ne anu amuala.

english_verse: Many years later a new king came to power. He did not know what Joseph had done for Egypt,
translation_verse: Na belemgbunli fofolɛ mɔɔ ɛnze Dwosefi la ralile Yigyibiti ebia ne.

english_verse: and he told the Egyptians: There are too many of those Israelites in our country, and they are becoming more powerful than we are.
translation_verse: Ɔhanle ɔhilele ye menli ne kɛ, “Bɛnlea, Yizilayɛma ɛzo somaa yɛɛ bɛ nwo yɛ se.

english_verse: If we don't outsmart them, their families will keep growing larger. And if our country goes to war, they could easily fight on the side of our enemies and escape from Egypt.
translation_verse: Bɛmaa yɛbɔ bɛ nye anrɛɛ bɛkɛzo bɛkɛbo zolɛ. Saa yɛanyɛ ye zɔhane na yɛ nee awie mɔ nyia konle a bɛkɛboa yɛ kpɔvolɛma ne bɛkɛho bɛkɛtia yɛ na bɛanyia adenle bɛanriandi bɛavi maanle ye anu.”

english_verse: The Egyptians put slave bosses in charge of the people of Israel and tried to wear them down with hard work. Those bosses forced them to build the cities of Pithom and Rameses, where the king could store his supplies.
translation_verse: Yemɔti bɛyele menli mɔɔ nea gyima zo la bɛmanle bɛ, bɛhyele Yizilayɛma mialera nu bɛmanle bɛyɛle gyima mɔɔ bo bɛ nwo zo la. Bɛmanle bɛkyekyele azuamgbole Paetɔm nee Releeyamesizi bɛmanle belemgbunli ne vale yɛle ye ninyɛnezielɛ ɛleka.

english_verse: But even though the Israelites were mistreated, their families grew larger, and they took over more land. Because of this, the Egyptians feared them worse than before
translation_verse: Noko mekɛ mɔɔ bɛlɛkile Yizilayɛma abodelɛ la ɛnee bɔ zo mɔɔ bɛlɛso kpalɛ na bɛlɛtende bɛahɔ moa bɛahɔva azɛlɛ ne dɔɔnwo a. Yemɔti Yigyibitima zulole Yizilayɛma kpole kpalɛ.

english_verse: that their lives were miserable. The Egyptians were cruel to the people of Israel and forced them to make bricks and to mix mortar and to work in the fields.
translation_verse: Yemɔti bɛyɛle Yizilayɛma kpoyokpoyo bɛmanle bɛyɛle anwunvɔne. Bɛmanle bɛguale belekese, bɛsisile azua na bɛyɛle gyima wɔ Yigyibitima egyinli ne mɔ anu.

english_verse: Finally, the king called in Shiphrah and Puah, the two women who helped the Hebrew mothers when they gave birth.
