translation_verse: Akee Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne hanle hilele Hibulu mraalɛ nwiɔ ne mɔɔ die awolɛ la, Hyɛfela nee Pua kɛ,

english_verse: He told them, “If a Hebrew woman gives birth to a girl, let the child live. If the baby is a boy, kill him!”
translation_verse: “Saa bɛlɛdie Hibulu raalɛ biala awolɛ na bɛnwu kɛ adɔma ne le nrenya a, bɛhu ye, na saa ɔle raalɛ a, bɛmmaku ye.”

english_verse: But the two women were faithful to God and did not kill the boys, even though the king had told them to.
translation_verse: Noko awolɛdievolɛma ne mɔ le menli mɔɔ sulo Nyamenle a, yemɔti bɛanyɛ mɔɔ Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne hanle hilele bɛ la, bɛangu ngakula mrenya ne mɔ.

english_verse: The king called them in again and asked, “Why are you letting those baby boys live?”
translation_verse: Yemɔti Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne vɛlɛle awolɛdievolɛma ne mɔ na ɔbizale bɛ kɛ, “Duzu ati a bɛyɛ ɛhye, na bɛammaa mralɛ mrenya ne mɔ anga nzule nu a?”

english_verse: They answered, “Hebrew women have their babies much quicker than Egyptian women. By the time we arrive, their babies are already born.”
translation_verse: Awolɛdievolɛma ne mɔ hanle hilele belemgbunli ne kɛ, “Ɔboalekɛ Hibulu mraalɛ ɛnle kɛ Yigyibiti mraalɛ la; bɛkola bɛ nwo sɔ; toonwo mɔ awolɛdievolɛma ne kadwu ɛkɛ la ɛnee bɛwo dɛbadɛba.”

english_verse: God was good to the two women because they truly respected him, and he blessed them with children of their own. The Hebrews kept increasing
translation_verse: Yemɔti Nyamenle yɛle awolɛdievolɛma ne mɔ boɛ. Kɛmɔ bɛsulo Nyamenle la ati, ɔmanle bɛdabɛ bɛbɔle ɛdane. Na akee Yizilayɛma yɛle mɔnwo mɔnwo na bɛ nwo yɛle se.

english_verse: until finally, the king gave a command to everyone in the nation, “As soon as a Hebrew boy is born, throw him into the Nile River! But you can let the girls live.”
translation_verse: Na akee belemgbunli ne yɛle ye mɛla manle maanlema kɛ, “Ralɛ nrenya biala mɔɔ Hibulunli biala kɛwo ye la, bɛvuandi ye bɛdo Azule Naele ne anu, na saa raalɛ a, bɛmmato ye nu.”

english_verse: A man from the Levi tribe married a woman from the same tribe,
translation_verse: Mekɛ ne anu nrenya bie mɔɔ vi Livae abusua ekpunli ne anu la gyale raalɛ wɔ abusua ekpunli ko ne ala anu.

english_verse: and she later had a baby boy. He was a beautiful child, and she kept him inside for three months.
translation_verse: Raalɛ ne vale ɛkolɛ na ɔwole ralɛ nrenya; na mɔɔ ɔnwunle kɛ ralɛ ne anwo si yɛ fɛ la, ɔvale ye ɔveale toonwo siane nsa.

english_verse: But when she could no longer keep him hidden, she made a basket out of reeds and covered it with tar. She put him in the basket and placed it in the tall grass along the edge of the Nile River.
translation_verse: Na mɔɔ ɛnee akee ɔfa ye ɔfea bieko a ɔnyɛ boɛ la, ɔvale ndɔ ɔnwonle kɛndɛne, ɔvale bilewu ɔfɔlele nuhua, amaa nzule angɔ nu, ɔvale kakula ne ɔdole nuhua na ɔvale ɔhɔziele ndɔ ne anu wɔ azule ne anloa.

english_verse: The baby's older sister stood off at a distance to see what would happen to him.
translation_verse: Akee kakula ne adiema raalɛ gyinlanle moa ekyii zinzale ye, amaa yeanwu edwɛkɛ mɔɔ kɛzi kakula ne anwo zo la.

english_verse: About that time one of the king's daughters came down to take a bath in the river, while her servant women walked along the river bank. She saw the basket in the tall grass and sent one of them to pull it out of the water.
translation_verse: Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne ara raalɛ ne nee ye sonvolɛma hɔle azule ne anu kɛ ɔkabia, ɛnee ye sonvolɛ mraalɛ ne mɔ luolua azule ne anloa. Mɔɔ ɔlɛbia la ɔnwunle kɛ kɛndɛne ne gyi ndɔ ne anu; ɔmanle ye sonvolɛ raalɛ ko hɔvale rale.

english_verse: When the king's daughter opened the basket, she saw the baby crying and felt sorry for him. She said, “This must be one of the Hebrew babies.”
translation_verse: Ɔdukuele zolɛ la ɔnwunle kakula ne, na alɔbɔlɛ, ɛnee kakula ne ɛlɛsu. Ɔlile kakula ne anwo nyane na ɔhanle kɛ, “Hibuluma ne amra ne mɔ ko ɛne.”

english_verse: At once the baby's older sister came up and asked, “Do you want me to get a Hebrew woman to take care of the baby for you?”
translation_verse: Ɔ diema raalɛ ne bizale belemgbunli ara raalɛ ne kɛ, “Mengɔnvɛlɛ Hibulu mraalɛ ne mɔ ko memaa ɔrava kakula ne ɔhɔli ye adane ɔmaa wɔ ɔ?”

english_verse: “Yes,” the king's daughter answered. So the girl brought the baby's mother,
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ara raalɛ ne zele ye kɛ, “Ɛhɛe, kɔ.” Yemɔti kakula raalɛ ne hɔvɛlɛle kakula ne ɔ nli.

english_verse: and the king's daughter told her, “Take care of this child, and I will pay you.” The baby's mother carried him home and took care of him.
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ara raalɛ ne zele ye kɛ, “Fa kakula ɛhye kɔ, kɔli ye adane maa me na mebadua wɔ kakɛ.” Yemɔti raalɛ ne vale kakula ne hɔlile ye adane.

english_verse: And when he was old enough, she took him to the king's daughter, who adopted him. She named him Moses because she said, “I pulled him out of the water.” Moses Escapes from Egypt
translation_verse: Kakula ne nyinle, ɔ nli vale ye rɛlɛle belemgbunli ara raalɛ ne, na ɔrayɛle ɔ ra. Ɔdonle ye Mosisi, na ɔzele kɛ, “Ɔboalekɛ menyele ye menvile nzule nu.” Mosisi nriandi ahɔ Medean

english_verse: After Moses had grown up, he went out to where his own people were hard at work, and he saw an Egyptian beating one of them.
translation_verse: Mosisi nyinle la, kenle ko ɔhɔkpɔlale ye menli ne, ɔhɔnleanle gyima ɛsesebɛ mɔɔ bɛlɛyɛ la, na ɔnwunle kɛ Yigyibitinli bie ɛlɛbo ye menli Hibuluma ne mɔ ko.

english_verse: Moses looked around to see if anyone was watching, then he killed the Egyptian and hid his body in the sand.
translation_verse: Ɔdole ɔ nye bɛne nee fema na yeannwu awie biala la, ɔhunle Yigyibitinli ne na ɔvunle ye ɔveale ɛnwea ne anu.

english_verse: When Moses went out the next day, he saw two Hebrews fighting. So he went to the man who had started the fight and asked, “Why are you beating up one of your own people?”
translation_verse: Aleɛ hyenle na eza ɔhɔle bɛ ɛkpɔlalɛ bieko la, ɛnee Hibuluma nwiɔ ɛlɛko. Ɔzele nuhua ne mɔɔ anyɛ ye boɛ la kɛ, “Duzu ati a wɔbɔ ɛ gɔnwo ɛ?”

english_verse: The man answered, “Who put you in charge of us and made you our judge? Are you planning to kill me, just like you killed that Egyptian?” This frightened Moses because he was sure that people must have found out what had happened.
translation_verse: Nrenya ne buale ye kɛ, “Nwane a yɛle wɔ yɛ nwo zo neavolɛ nee ndɛnebuavolɛ a? Wɔdwenle nwo kɛ ɛku me, kɛmɔ ɛhunle Yigyibitinli ne la ɔ?” Akee Mosisi zulole na ɔhanle ɔhilele ɔ nwo kɛ, “Nɔhalɛ, edwɛkɛ ne ɛla ali.”

english_verse: Some shepherds tried to chase them away, but Moses came to their rescue and watered their animals.
translation_verse: Mboaneneavolɛma bie ravoanle bɛ; na Mosisi dwazole boale bɛ na ɔnleanle ɔmanle mboane ne mɔ nzule.

english_verse: When Jethro's daughters returned home, their father asked, “Why have you come back so early today?”
translation_verse: Mɔɔ bɛziale bɛhɔle la bɛ ze Riliwɛle bizale bɛ kɛ, “Duzu ati a ɛnɛ bɛra sua nu ndɛndɛ zɛhae a?”

english_verse: They answered, “An Egyptian rescued us from the shepherds, and he even watered our sheep and goats.”
translation_verse: Bɛhanle kɛ, “Yigyibitinli bie liele yɛ ti wɔ mboaneneavolɛma ne asa anu, ɔsesale nzule ne bie ɔmanle yɛ na eza ɔnleanle ɔmanle mboane nee mbɔnkye ne mɔ nlonle nzule.”

english_verse: “Where is he?” Jethro asked. “Why did you leave him out there? Invite him to eat with us.”
translation_verse: Riliwɛle bizale ɔ mra mraalɛ ne mɔ kɛ, “Na ɔwɔ nienwu? Duzu ati a bɛgyakyi ye nehane ɛ? Bɛvɛlɛ ye bɛmaa ɔrali debie.”

english_verse: Moses agreed to stay on with Jethro, who later let his daughter Zipporah marry Moses.
translation_verse: Na Mosisi kponlenle zolɛ ɔ nee nrenya ne dɛnlanle. Ɔvale ɔ ra raalɛ Zepɔla ɔmanle Mosisi gyale.

english_verse: And when she had a son, Moses said, “I will name him Gershom, since I am a foreigner in this country.”
translation_verse: Ɔ nee ye wole ralɛ nrenya. Mosisi hanle hilele ɔ nwo kɛ, “Mele ɛyɛvolɛ wɔ awie mɔ maanle nu” Yemɔti ɔdonle ye Gɛhyɔm.

english_verse: After the death of the king of Egypt, the Israelites still complained because they were forced to be slaves. They cried out for help,
translation_verse: Mekɛ ne hɔle bie kpalɛ la Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne wule. Akee Yizilayɛma nwunle amaneɛ kpole kpalɛ wɔ akɛlɛzonlenlɛ nu. Bɛzunle bɛvɛlɛle moalɛ, na bɛ ɛzunlɛ ne dwule Nyamenle anyunlu.

english_verse: and God heard their loud cries. He did not forget the promise he had made to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob,
translation_verse: Nyamenle dele bɛ ɛzunlɛ ne na ɔhakyele ye ngyekyeleɛ ne mɔɔ ɔ nee Ebileham, Ayezeke, nee Gyekɔbo kyekyele la.

english_verse: and because he knew what was happening to his people, he felt sorry for them.
translation_verse: Na Nyamenle nwunle Yizilayɛma tɛnlabelɛ nu, na nyane hanle ye.

english_verse: One day, Moses was taking care of the sheep and goats of his father-in-law Jethro, the priest of Midian, and Moses decided to lead them across the desert to Sinai, the holy mountain.
translation_verse: Ɛnee Mosisi nea Sɛlɛvolɛ Gyɛtulo, ɔ ye ɔ ze ne mɔɔ vi Medean la nyɛmoa. Kenle ko ɔhanle nyɛmoa ne mɔ ɔhɔle fienemgbole ne aduduleɛ na ɔrale Nyamenle Boka Saenae abo.

english_verse: There an angel of the Lord appeared to him from a burning bush. Moses saw that the bush was on fire, but it was not burning up.
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma soanvolɛ yɛle kɛ senle mɔɔ ɛlɛsɔ la na ɔyele ɔ nwo ɔhilele ye wɔ kpɔkɛ ne anu. Ɔnleanle, na ɔnwunle kɛ kpɔkɛ ne ɛlɛsɔ, noko ɔnyela.

english_verse: “This is strange!” he said to himself. “I'll go over and see why the bush isn't burning up.”
translation_verse: Na Mosisi zele kɛ, “Megyinla ahane meanlea nwanwane deɛ ɛhye, kɛ ɔyɛ mɔɔ kpɔkɛ ne ɛlɛsɔ, noko ɔnyela la.”

english_verse: When the Lord saw Moses coming near, he called him by name from the bush, and Moses answered, “Here I am.”
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma nwunle kɛ yehwe ahane kɛ ɔnea la, Nyamenle vɛlɛle ye wɔ kpɔkɛ ne anu, “Mosisi! Mosisi!” Na Mosisi zulole zolɛ kɛ, “Mewɔ ɛke.”

english_verse: God replied, “Don't come any closer. Take off your sandals—the ground where you are standing is holy.
translation_verse: Na Nyamenle zele kɛ, “Mmabikye me; yeye mgbɔlaboa ne mɔɔ ɛwula la, ɔluakɛ azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ ɛgyi zolɛ la le nwuanzanwuanza.”

english_verse: I am the God who was worshiped by your ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.” Moses was afraid to look at God, and so he hid his face.
translation_verse: Eza ɔzele kɛ, “Mame a mele ɛ ze mɔ Nyamenle ne, Ebileham Nyamenle ne, Ayezeke Nyamenle ne, nee Gyekɔbo Nyamenle ne.” Na Mosisi hedale ɔ ti zo, ɔluakɛ ɔsulo kɛ ɔkɛnlea Nyamenle.

english_verse: The Lord said: I have seen how my people are suffering as slaves in Egypt, and I have heard them beg for my help because of the way they are being mistreated. I feel sorry for them,
translation_verse: Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma zele kɛ, “Menwu me menli mɔɔ wɔ Yigyibiti la amaneɛnwunlɛ ne, eza mede bɛ ɛzunlɛ ne, ɔlua abodelɛ mɔɔ bɛ gyima zo neavolɛma ne ɛlɛfa ahile bɛ la.

english_verse: and I have come down to rescue them from the Egyptians. I will bring my people out of Egypt into a country where there is a lot of good land, rich with milk and honey. I will give them the land where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
translation_verse: Meze bɛ amaneɛnwunlɛ ne, na mera kɛ mebalie bɛ meavi Yigyibitima asa anu, meaye bɛ meavi azɛlɛ ɛhye azo me nee bɛ ahɔ azɛlɛ kpalɛ mɔɔ tɛlɛ, azɛlɛ kpalɛ mɔɔ kye aleɛ mɔɔ Keenama, Hɛtema, Amɔlema, Pɛlɛzema, Haevaema, yɛɛ Gyibɛsema a de zolɛ la azo.

english_verse: My people have begged for my help, and I have seen how cruel the Egyptians are to them.
translation_verse: Kɛkala, Yizilayɛma ɛzunlɛ ne ɛdwu me nwo ɛke, yɛɛ menwu ɛsisilɛ mɔɔ Yigyibitima fa sisi bɛ la.

english_verse: Now go to the king! I am sending you to lead my people out of his country.
translation_verse: Bɛla, mesoa wɔ wɔ Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne ɛkɛ amaa wɔahɔye me menli, Yizilayɛma wɔavi Yigyibiti.”

english_verse: But Moses said, “Who am I to go to the king and lead your people out of Egypt?”
translation_verse: Na Mosisi hanle hilele Nyamenle kɛ, “Na nwane bɔbɔ a le medame, mɔɔ mekɔ Yigyibiti belemgbunli anyunlu, meahɔye Yizilayɛma meavi Yigyibiti a?”

english_verse: God replied, “I will be with you. And you will know that I am the one who sent you, when you worship me on this mountain after you have led my people out of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Nyamenle zele ye kɛ, “Me nee wɔ balua, na ɛhye bayɛ sɛkɛlɛneɛ amaa wɔ kɛ medame a mezoa wɔ a. Mekɛ mɔɔ ɛ nee menli ne kɛvi Yigyibiti la, bɛbarazonle Nyamenle wɔ boka ɛhye azo.”

english_verse: Moses answered, “I will tell the people of Israel that the God their ancestors worshiped has sent me to them. But what should I say, if they ask me your name?”
translation_verse: Mosisi bizale Nyamenle kɛ, “Saa mekɔ Yizilayɛma ɛkɛ ne na meka mekile bɛ kɛ, ‘Bɛ ze mɔ Nyamenle ne ɛzoa me bɛ nwo ɛke’, na bɛbiza me kɛ, ‘Kɛ bɛfɛlɛ ye?’ a, duzu edwɛkɛ a menga mengile bɛ a?”

english_verse: God said to Moses: I am the eternal God. So tell them that the Lord, whose name is “I Am,” has sent you. This is my name forever, and it is the name that people must use from now on.
translation_verse: Ka ɛhye kile Yizilayɛma kɛ, ‘Ɛdɛnkɛma, bɛ ze mɔ Nyamenle ne, Ebileham Nyamenle ne, Ayezeke Nyamenle ne, nee Gyekɔbo Nyamenle ne ɛzoa me bɛ nwo ɛke! Ɛhye a le me duma wɔ melɛ mɔɔ ɛnlɛ awieleɛ, na ɛhye yɛɛ ɔwɔ kɛ awolɛndoazo kɔsɔɔti fa fɛlɛ me a.

english_verse: Call together the leaders of Israel and tell them that the God who was worshiped by Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob has appeared to you. Tell them I have seen how terribly they are being treated in Egypt,
translation_verse: Kɔboɔboa Yizilayɛ mgbanyima kɔsɔɔti anloa na ka kile bɛ kɛ: Ɛdɛnkɛma, bɛ ze mɔ Nyamenle ne, Ebileham Nyamenle ne, Ayezeke Nyamenle ne, nee Gyekɔbo Nyamenle ne ɛye ɔ nwo ɛhile me. Ka kile bɛ kɛ menwu mɔɔ bɛva bɛyɛ bɛ wɔ Yigyibiti la,

english_verse: and I promise to lead them out of their troubles. I will give them a land rich with milk and honey, where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites now live.
translation_verse: na mebɔ ɛwɔkɛ kɛ mebaye bɛ meavi bɛ amaneɛnwunlɛ nu wɔ Yigyibiti na me nee bɛ ahɔ Keenama, Hɛtema, Amɔlema, Pɛlɛzema, Haevaema, nee Gyibɛsema azɛlɛ zo. Ɛkɛ ne azɛlɛ ne le kpalɛ na ɔkye aleɛ.’

english_verse: The leaders of Israel will listen to you. Then you must take them to the king of Egypt and say, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Let us walk three days into the desert, where we can offer a sacrifice to him.”
translation_verse: “Me menli ne badie ɛ ne; na ɛdawɔ nee Yizilayɛ mgbanyima bahɔ Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne ɛkɛ bɛahɔze ye kɛ, ‘Ɛdɛnkɛma, Hibuluma Nyamenle ne nee yɛ ɛyɛ nyianu, yemɔti yɛsɛlɛ wɔ, maa yɛ adenle maa yɛdia kenle nsa adenle yɛhɔ fienemgbole ne anu, amaa yɛabɔ azu yɛamaa Ɛdɛnkɛma, yɛ Nyamenle ne.’

english_verse: But I know that the king of Egypt won't let you go unless something forces him to.
translation_verse: Meze kɛ Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne ɛnrɛmaa bɛ adenle, kyesɛ tumi kpole bie kolo ɔ nwo zo.

english_verse: So I will use my mighty power to perform all kinds of miracles and strike down the Egyptians. Then the king will send you away.
translation_verse: Yemɔti mebadenrɛ me sa meayɛ nwanwane ninyɛne meadua Yigyibiti kakɛ, na ɛhye anzi, ɔbamaa bɛahɔ.

english_verse: Every Israelite woman will go to her Egyptian neighbors or to any Egyptian woman living with them and ask them for gold and silver jewelry and for their finest clothes. The Egyptians will give them to you, and you will put these fine things on your sons and daughters. Carry all this away when you leave Egypt.
translation_verse: Yizilayɛnli raalɛ biala bahɔ ye manivolɛ Yigyibitinli raalɛ mɔɔ ɔ nee ye de nee mɔɔ ɛradɛnla ye sua nu la ɛkɛ ahɔlie dwɛtɛ fufule nee ezukoa nvutuke anwoneɛ nee ndanlɛ, na bɛava bɛaziezie bɛ mra mrenya nee mraalɛ. Na ɛhye bamaa bɛakpokpo Yigyibitima.”

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord, “Suppose everyone refuses to listen to my message, and no one believes that you really appeared to me?”
translation_verse: Akee Mosisi buale kɛ, “Bɛnrɛlie me bɛnrɛli anzɛɛ bɛnrɛdie me, bɛbaha kɛ, ‘Ɛdɛnkɛma anye ɔ nwo angile wɔ.’ ”

english_verse: The Lord answered, “What's that in your hand?” “A walking stick,” Moses replied.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma bizale ye kɛ, “Duzu a ɛlɛ ye ɛ sa nu la?” Mosisi buale ye kɛ, “Kpɔma ɔ.”

english_verse: “Throw it down!” the Lord commanded. So Moses threw the stick on the ground. It immediately turned into a snake, and Moses jumped back.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele ye kɛ, “Fuandi to azɛlɛ ne anwo.” Mosisi vuandinle dole azɛlɛ ne anwo, na ɔhakyile ɛwɔlɛ. Mosisi bɔle nguku hɔle ɔ nzi.

english_verse: “Pick it up by the tail!” the Lord told him. And when Moses did this, the snake turned back into a walking stick.
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Tenrɛ ɛ sa sɔ ɔ dua ne anu” Ɔzɔle nuhua, na ɔhakyile kpɔma wɔ ɔ sa nu.

english_verse: “Do this,” the Lord said, “and the Israelites will believe that you have seen me, the God who was worshiped by their ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.”
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele ye kɛ, “Ɛhye bamaa bɛalie bɛali kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, bɛ ze mɔ Nyamenle ne, Ebileham Nyamenle ne, Ayezeke Nyamenle ne, nee Gyekɔbo Nyamenle ne ɛye ɔ nwo ɛhile wɔ.”

english_verse: Next, the Lord commanded Moses, “Put your hand inside your shirt.” Moses obeyed, and when he took it out, his hand had turned white as snow—like someone with leprosy.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele ye bieko kɛ, “Fa ɛ sa wula wɔ tɛladeɛ ne anu.” Mosisi vale ɔ sa wulale ye tɛladeɛ ne anu; na mɔɔ ɔyele ɔ sa la, ɛnee kokobɛ ɛdila ɔ sa ɛmaa yeyɛ fufule nwohyee kɛ ezukɔtweaba.

english_verse: “Put your hand back inside your shirt,” the Lord told him. Moses did so, and when he took it out again, it was as healthy as the rest of his body.
translation_verse: Eza Nyamenle zele ye kɛ, “Fa ɛ sa wula wɔ tɛladeɛ ne anu.” Yemɔti ɔvale ɔ sa ɔwulale ye tɛladeɛ ne anu; na mɔɔ ɔyele ɔ sa la, ɛnee kokobɛ ne ɛhɔ na nwonane ne ɛyɛ kɛ ye dɛba ne ala la.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “If no one believes either of these miracles, take some water from the Nile River and pour it on the ground. The water will immediately turn into blood.”
translation_verse: Saa bɛnrɛlie sɛkɛlɛneɛ nwiɔ ye bɛnrɛli, anzɛɛ bɛnrɛdie ɛ ne a, sa Azule Naele ne nzule ne bie wola gua azɛlɛ resee ne azo, na nzule ne mɔɔ ɛbaza wɔ azule ne anu la bahakyi mogya wɔ azɛlɛ ne anwo.”

english_verse: Moses replied, “I have never been a good speaker. I wasn't one before you spoke to me, and I'm not one now. I am slow at speaking, and I can never think of what to say.”
translation_verse: Na Mosisi hanle hilele Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ, “O me Awulae, sumunli kɛ bɛwole me toonwo mɔɔ yeradwu ɛnɛ, yɛɛ kɛkala bɔbɔ mɔɔ wɔdendɛ wɔhile wɔ sonvolɛ la, me nloa ɛnde, yɛɛ me ɛdendɛlɛ le bɛtɛɛ.”

english_verse: But the Lord answered, “Who makes people able to speak or makes them deaf or unable to speak? Who gives them sight or makes them blind? Don't you know that I am the one who does these things?
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele ye kɛ, “Nwane a bɔle sonla nloa a? Nwane a maa ɔyɛ mumule anzɛɛ anzondiliravolɛ, anzɛɛ nwane a maa ɔnwu debie anzɛɛ ɔyɛ anyenzinliravolɛ a? Asoo tɛ medame, Ɛdɛnkɛma ɔ?

english_verse: Now go! When you speak, I will be with you and give you the words to say.”
translation_verse: Yemɔti kɔ na mebade ɛ nloa na meahilehile wɔ mɔɔ ɛbaha la.”

english_verse: Moses begged, “Lord, please send someone else to do it.”
translation_verse: Na Mosisi hanle kɛ, “O me Awulae, soa sonla fofolɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord became angry with Moses and said: What about your brother Aaron, the Levite? I know he is a good speaker. He is already on his way here to visit you, and he will be happy to see you again.
translation_verse: Ɛhye manle Ɛdɛnkɛma vale Mosisi anwo ɛya na ɔzele kɛ, “Ɛ diema Aalɔn, Livaenli ne ɛnle ɛkɛ ɔ? Meze kɛ ɔ nloa ɛde kpalɛ; nea, ɔlɛba yearayia wɔ, na saa ɔnwu wɔ a ɔbali fɛlɛko wɔ ye ahonle nu.

english_verse: Now take this walking stick and use it to perform miracles. Moses Returns to Egypt
translation_verse: Fa kpɔma ɛhye kɔ na wɔava wɔayɛ nwanwane sɛkɛlɛneɛ ne mɔ.” Mosisi sia ahɔ Yigyibiti

english_verse: Moses went to his father-in-law Jethro and asked, “Please let me return to Egypt to see if any of my people are still alive.” “All right,” Jethro replied. “I hope all goes well.”
translation_verse: Mosisi ziale hɔle ɔ ye ɔ ze Gyɛtulo ɛkɛ hɔhanle hilele ye kɛ, “Mesɛlɛ wɔ, maa me adenle maa menzia mengɔ Yigyibiti mengɔnea saa me nwo amra tɛte ngoane nu a.” Na Gyɛtulo kponlenle zolɛ kɛ Mosisi ɛhɔ anzonudwolɛ nu.

english_verse: But even before this, the Lord had told Moses, “Leave the land of Midian and return to Egypt. Everyone who wanted to kill you is now dead.”
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi wɔ Medean kɛ, “Sia kɔ Yigyibiti, ɔluakɛ menli mɔɔ ɛnee ɛlɛkpondɛ wɔ ahu wɔ la amuala ɛwie wu.”

english_verse: So Moses put his wife and sons on donkeys and headed for Egypt, holding the walking stick that had the power of God.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Mosisi vale ɔ ye nee ɔ mra mrenya ne mɔ vole asoaso zo zile nu hɔle Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo; Mosisi eza vale kpɔma ne mɔɔ Nyamenle zele ye kɛ ɔva la.

english_verse: On the way the Lord said to Moses: When you get to Egypt, go to the king and work the miracles I have shown you. But I will make him so stubborn that he will refuse to let my people go.
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Saa ɛsia ɛkɔ Yigyibiti a, yɛ nwanwane ninyɛne ne mɔ mɔɔ meva nwolɛ tumi memaa wɔ la kile belemgbunli ne. Noko akee mebamaa yeayɛ dapele, yemɔti ɔnrɛmaa menli ne ɛnrɛhɔ.

english_verse: Then tell him that I have said, “Israel is my first-born son,
translation_verse: Na ɛbaze ye kɛ, ‘Kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma se la ɛne: Yizilayɛ a le me belamunli ralɛ nrenya a, yemɔti medame Ɛdɛnkɛma, mese,

english_verse: and I commanded you to release him, so he could worship me. But you refused, and now I will kill your first-born son.” Zipporah's Son Is Circumcised
translation_verse: maa me ra nrenya ne ɛhɔ amaa yeazonle me. Saa ɛkpo kɛ ɛnrɛmaa ɔnrɛhɔ a, mebahu wɔ belamunli ralɛ nrenya ne.’ ”

english_verse: One night while Moses was in camp, the Lord was about to kill him.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Mosisi kɔ Yigyibiti na ɔhɔdwule adenle nu azokoɛleɛ bie la, Ɛdɛnkɛma yiale ye na ɔyɛle kɛ ɔku ye.

english_verse: So the Lord did not harm Moses. Then Zipporah said, “Yes, my dear, you are safe because of this circumcision.” Aaron Is Sent To Meet Moses
translation_verse: Na Mosisi aye Zepɔla vale ɛtwɛlɛboɔ yɛle ɔ ra nrenya ne mrenyanu nzonlɛ na ɔvale ɔhanle Mosisi agyakɛ, ɔzele kɛ, “Nɔhalɛ, ɛle mogya kunli ɛmaa me!” Yemɔti Ɛdɛnkɛma gyakyile Mosisi, kɛmɔ ɔ ye hanle kɛ, “Ɛle mogya kunli ɛmaa me” la, ɔboalekɛ bɛbu mrenyanu nzonlɛyɛlɛ amaamuo ne.

english_verse: The Lord sent Aaron to meet Moses in the desert. So Aaron met Moses at Mount Sinai and greeted him with a kiss.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Aalɔn kɛ, “Kɔ fienemgbole ne anu kɔyia Mosisi.” Yemɔti Aalɔn hɔle hɔyiale Mosisi wɔ Nyamenle Boka, ɔyɛle ye atuu na ɔvole ɔ nloa anwo.

english_verse: Moses told Aaron what God had sent him to say; he also told him about the miracles God had given him the power to perform.
translation_verse: Na Mosisi hanle edwɛkɛ mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛva ɛzoa ye la amuala hilele Aalɔn na ɔhanle sɛkɛlɛneɛ mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛze ye kɛ ɔyɛ la amuala ɔbokale nwolɛ.

english_verse: Later they brought together the leaders of Israel,
translation_verse: Akee Mosisi nee Aalɔn hɔle hɔboɔboale Yizilayɛ mgbanyima kɔsɔɔti anloa.

english_verse: and Aaron told them what the Lord had sent Moses to say. Then Moses worked the miracles for the people,
translation_verse: Na Aalɔn hanle mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma hanle hilele Mosisi la amuala hilele bɛ na ɔyɛle nwanwane sɛkɛlɛneɛ ne mɔ wɔ menli ne anyunlu ɛkɛ ne.

english_verse: and everyone believed. They bowed down and worshiped the Lord because they knew that he had seen their suffering and was going to help them.
translation_verse: Na menli ne liele lile. Mɔɔ bɛdele kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛrakpɔla ye menli Yizilayɛma na yenwu bɛ amaneɛnwunlɛ ne la, bɛbɔle bɛ ti aze bɛyeyɛle ye.

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king of Egypt and told him, “The Lord God says, ‘Let my people go into the desert, so they can honor me with a celebration there.’ ”
translation_verse: Nzinlii Mosisi nee Aalɔn hɔle Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne ɛkɛ hɔzele ye kɛ, “Kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne se la ɛne, ‘Maa me menli ne ɛhɔ, amaa bɛali ɛvoyia wɔ fienemgbole ne anu bɛawula me anyunlunyia.’ ”

english_verse: “Who is this Lord and why should I obey him?” the king replied. “I refuse to let you and your people go!”
translation_verse: Na belemgbunli ne bizale bɛ kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma a le nwane, mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ metie ye na memaa Yizilayɛma kɔ a? Menze Ɛdɛnkɛma; yɛɛ akee bɔbɔ menrɛmaa Yizilayɛma ɛnrɛhɔ fee.”

english_verse: They answered, “The Lord God of the Hebrews has appeared to us. Please let us walk three days into the desert where we can offer sacrifices to him. If you don't, he may strike us down with terrible troubles or with war.”
translation_verse: Mosisi nee Aalɔn buale kɛ, “Hibuluma Nyamenle ne nee yɛ ɛyɛ nyianu; yɛsɛlɛ wɔ, maa yɛ adenle maa yɛdia kenle nsa adenle yɛhɔ fienemgbole ne anu yɛhɔbɔ azu yɛmaa Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛ Nyamenle ne, anrɛɛ ɔkɛde ewule ɔkɛkponde yɛ nwo ɔkɛhu yɛ anzɛɛ ɔkɛhwe yɛ nwo dadeɛ.”

english_verse: The king said, “Moses and Aaron, why are you keeping these people from working? Look how many you are keeping from doing their work. Now everyone get back to work!”
translation_verse: Na belemgbunli ne hanle kɛ, “Bɛnlea, akee menli ne ɛzo somaa na bɛkulo kɛ bɛgyakyi gyimayɛlɛ!”

english_verse: That same day the king gave orders to his Egyptian slave bosses and to the Israelite men directly in charge of the Israelite slaves. He told them:
translation_verse: Kenle ko ne ala Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne zele gyima zo neavolɛma nee gyima nu mgbanyinli ne mɔ kɛ,

english_verse: Don't give the slaves any more straw to put in their bricks. Force them to find their own straw wherever they can,
translation_verse: “Ɔvi ɛnɛ mɔɔ kɔ la, bɛmmamaa menli ne atoko gyakɛ bɛmaa bɛfa bɛgua belekese ne mɔ; bɛmaa bɛdabɛ mumua ne bɛhɔkpondɛ bie.

english_verse: but they must make the same number of bricks as before. They are lazy, or else they would not beg me to let them go and sacrifice to their God.
translation_verse: Kenle ko biala belekese dodo mɔɔ bɛgua la, bɛva bie bɛgua zolɛ, ɔluakɛ bɛ gyima ne anzo la ati, bɛsu kɛ, ‘Maa yɛ adenle maa yɛhɔbɔ azu yɛmaa yɛ Nyamenle ne!’

english_verse: Make them work so hard that they won't have time to listen to these lies.
translation_verse: Bɛzoa bɛ adesoa ɛnlomboɛ kpalɛ kpalɛ bɛmaa ɔhola bɛ, amaa bɛandie adalɛ edwɛkɛ biala.”

english_verse: The slave bosses and the men in charge of the slaves went out and told them, “The king says he will not give you any more straw.
translation_verse: Yemɔti gyima zo neavolɛma ne nee Yizilayɛ mgbanyinli mɔɔ nea gyimayɛlɛ ne la hɔhanle hilele menli ne kɛ, “Kɛ belemgbunli ne se la ɛne, ‘Menrɛmaa bɛ atoko gyakɛ.

english_verse: Go and find your own straw wherever you can, but you must still make as many bricks as before.”
translation_verse: Ɛleka biala mɔɔ bɛdabɛ bɛkɛhɔ na bɛanyia bie la bɛhɔ bɛhɔkpondɛ bie, yɛɛ bɛ gyima ne ɛdeɛ, bɛnrɛde zolɛ nretee zɛhae.’ ”

english_verse: The slaves went all over Egypt, looking for straw.
translation_verse: Yemɔti menli ne kpondenle Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo luoluale nuhua kpondɛle atoko gyakɛ.

english_verse: But the slave bosses were hard on them and kept saying, “Each day you have to make as many bricks as you did when you were given straw.”
translation_verse: Gyima zo neavolɛma ne hanle bɛ nuhua kɛ, “Ɔwɔ kɛ bɛwie gyima ne. Ɔwɔ kɛ bɛyɛ gyima ne kɛmɔ bɛmaa bɛ atoko gyakɛ a bɛyɛ la.”

english_verse: The bosses beat the men in charge of the slaves and said, “Why didn't you force the slaves to make as many bricks yesterday and today as they did before?”
translation_verse: Bɛbole Yizilayɛ mgbanyinli mɔɔ belemgbunli ne gyima zo neavolɛma ne yele bɛ kɛ bɛnlea bɛ menli ne anwo zo la, na bɛbizale bɛ kɛ, “Duzu ati a bɛanwie bɛ belekese gyima ne yɛ ɛnɛ, kɛmɔ bɛyɛ ye dɛba ne la ɛ?”

english_verse: Finally, the men in charge of the slaves went to the king and said, “Why are you treating us like this?
translation_verse: Na Yizilayɛ mgbanyinli mɔɔ bɛyele bɛ kɛ bɛnlea bɛ menli ne anwo zo la razunle vuale belemgbunli ne kɛ, “Duzu ati a ɛbu wɔ sonvolɛma amaamuo zɛhae ɛ?

english_verse: No one brings us any straw, but we are still ordered to make the same number of bricks. We are beaten with whips, and your own people are to blame.”
translation_verse: Bɛmmaa wɔ sonvolɛma atoko gyakɛ, noko bɛse yɛ kɛ, ‘Bɛgua belekese,’ na bɛbo yɛ ɛbolɛ mɔɔ ɛnfɛta la. Nvonleɛ ne vi wɔ menli ne mɔ.”

english_verse: The king replied, “You are lazy—nothing but lazy! That's why you keep asking me to let you go and sacrifice to your Lord.
translation_verse: Na ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛle mgbovonle, bɛle mgbovonle somaa, yemɔti dahuu bɛse, ‘Maa yɛ adenle maa yɛhɔbɔ azu yɛmaa Ɛdɛnkɛma!’

english_verse: Get back to work! You won't be given straw, but you must still make the same number of bricks.”
translation_verse: Bɛdwazo ɛkɛ ne bɛhɔyɛ gyima; awie biala ɛnrɛmaa bɛ atoko gyakɛ tanye, yɛɛ ɔwɔ kɛ bɛgua belekese dodo mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ kenle ko biala bɛgua la.”

english_verse: The men knew they were in deep trouble when they were ordered to make the same number of bricks each day.
translation_verse: Yizilayɛ mgbanyinli mɔɔ nea gyimayɛvoma ne anwo zo la nwunle kɛ munzule ɛdo bɛ wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ bɛhanle bɛhilele bɛ kɛ, “Ɔwɔ kɛ bɛgua belekese dodo mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ kenle ko biala bɛgua la.”

english_verse: After they left the king, they went to see Moses and Aaron, who had been waiting for them.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ bɛvi belemgbunli ne ɛkɛ bɛlɛba la, bɛyiale Mosisi nee Aalɔn mɔɔ ɛnee ɛlɛkendɛ bɛ la.

english_verse: Then the men said, “We hope the Lord will punish both of you for making the king and his officials hate us. Now they even have an excuse to kill us.” The Lord's Promise to Moses
translation_verse: Na bɛhanle bɛhilele Mosisi nee Aalɔn kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛnlea na ɔbua bɛ ndɛne, ɔboalekɛ bɛmaa yɛyɛ ɛtane wɔ belemgbunli nee ye mgbanyima anyunlu, na bɛva yɛ ɛhunlɛ dadeɛ bɛwula bɛ sa nu.” Mosisi bɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma somolɛ

english_verse: Moses left them and prayed, “Our Lord, why have you brought so much trouble on your people? Is that why you sent me here?
translation_verse: Na Mosisi hakyile ɔ nwo zele Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ, “O Ɛdɛnkɛma, duzu ati a wɔmaa munzule ɛdo menli ɛhye mɔ a? Duzu ati a ɛzoanle me bɔbɔ a?

english_verse: Ever since you told me to speak to the king, he has caused nothing but trouble for these people. And you haven't done a thing to help.”
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ sumunli kɛ membale belemgbunli ne ɛkɛ kɛ melua wɔ duma nu mebadendɛ la, ɛtane ala a yeva yeyɛ menli ne a, yɛɛ ɛtɛdiele bɛ fee.”

english_verse: The Lord God told Moses: Soon you will see what I will do to the king. Because of my mighty power, he will let my people go, and he will even chase them out of his country.
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Akee ɛbanwu debie mɔɔ mebava meahile belemgbunli ne la, ɔluakɛ ɔlua tumi kpole zo ɔbamaa bɛahɔ, ɛhɛe, ɔlua tumi kpole zo akee bɔbɔ ɔbavoa bɛ kɛ bɛvi ye maanle ne anu bɛhɔ.” Nyamenle fɛlɛ Mosisi

english_verse: My name is the Lord.
translation_verse: Na Nyamenle zele Mosisi kɛ, “Medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a.

english_verse: But when I appeared to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, I came as God All-Powerful and did not use my name.
translation_verse: Menyele me nwo mengilele Ebileham, Ayezeke, nee Gyekɔbo kɛ Tumivolɛ Nyamenle, noko me duma, Ɛdɛnkɛma ne, meammaa bɛannwu ye.

english_verse: I made an agreement and promised them the land of Canaan, where they were living as foreigners.
translation_verse: Eza me nee bɛ kyekyele ngyekyeleɛ kɛ mebava Keena azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ bɛdɛnlanle zolɛ kɛ nyɛvolɛ la meamaa bɛ.

english_verse: Now I have seen how the people of Israel are suffering because of the Egyptians, and I will keep my promise.
translation_verse: Eza mede Yizilayɛma mɔɔ Yigyibitima ɛyɛ bɛ ahanra la ɛzunlɛ ne, na mehakye me ngyekyeleɛ ne.

english_verse: Here is my message for Israel: “I am the Lord! And with my mighty power I will punish the Egyptians and free you from slavery.
translation_verse: Yemɔti ka kile Yizilayɛma kɛ, ‘Medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma ne a. Mebazokoɛ bɛ adesoa ne mɔɔ Yigyibitima ɛva ɛzoa bɛ la, mebaye bɛ meavi akɛlɛzonlenlɛ nu. Mebava tumi kpole mealie bɛ na meadua Yigyibitima kakɛ.

english_verse: I will accept you as my people, and I will be your God. Then you will know that I was the one who rescued you from the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Mebava bɛmɛ Yizilayɛma meayɛ me menli, na meayɛ bɛ Nyamenle, na bɛanwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne mɔɔ ɛye bɛ ɛvi Yigyibitima adesoa ne mɔ abo la.

english_verse: I will bring you into the land that I solemnly promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and it will be yours. I am the Lord!”
translation_verse: Mebava bɛ meahɔ azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ menganle ndane kɛ mebava meamaa Ebileham, Ayezeke, nee Gyekɔbo la azo. Mebava meamaa bɛ meamaa yeayɛ bɛ ɛdeɛ bɔkɔɔ. Medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a.’ ”

english_verse: When Moses told this to the Israelites, they were too discouraged and mistreated to believe him.
translation_verse: Mosisi hanle ɛhye hilele Yizilayɛma, noko bɛandie ye, ɔboalekɛ bɛ nwo ɛvɔ yɛɛ bɛtɛbɔ atisesebɛ akɛlɛzonlenlɛ nu.

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ,

english_verse: to demand that the king of Egypt let the Israelites leave.
translation_verse: “Kɔ kɔze Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne kɛ ɔmaa Yizilayɛma ɛvi ye maanle ne anu ɛhɔ.”

english_verse: But Moses replied, “I'm not a powerful speaker. If the Israelites won't listen to me, why should the king of Egypt?”
translation_verse: Na Mosisi hanle hilele Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ, “Yizilayɛma bɔbɔ andie me, kɛ ɔkɛyɛ na belemgbunli ne adie me ɛ, nwane a le mame, mɔɔ menze tendɛ la?”

english_verse: But the Lord sent Aaron and Moses with a message for the Israelites and for the king. He also ordered Aaron and Moses to free the people from Egypt. Family Record of Aaron and Moses
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi nee Aalɔn kɛ, “Bɛha bɛhile Yizilayɛma nee Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne kɛ memaa bɛdabɛ, Mosisi nee Aalɔn tumi kɛ bɛrava Yizilayɛma bɛvi Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo bɛhɔ.” Mosisi nee Aalɔn mbusua ekpunli ne mɔ anu edwɛkɛ

english_verse: The following men were the heads of their ancestral clans: The sons of Reuben, Jacob's oldest son, were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.
translation_verse: Mbusua mgbanyinli mɔɔ gyigyi bɛ ze mɔ awuke ne mɔ ati la ɛne: Wulubɛn, Gyekɔbo ara nrenya kpanyinli ne wole mrenya nna: Heenɔko, Palu, Hɛzelɔn, yɛɛ Kaamae.

english_verse: The sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jachin, Zohar, and Shaul, the son of a Canaanite woman.
translation_verse: Semɛyɔn wole mrenya nsia: Gyɛmuwɛle, Gyeemen, Ohade, Gyeeken, Zohaa, yɛɛ Hyeewulu. Bɛ nli le Keenanli.

english_verse: Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. All of the above were from the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Mɛlɛlae wole mrenya nwiɔ: Maalae nee Muhyae. Livae mbusua ne mɔ, kɛmɔ bɛ awolɛndoazo ne mɔ de la ɛne.

english_verse: Izhar's sons were Korah, Nepheg, and Zichri.
translation_verse: Yezehaa wole mrenya nsa: Kɔla, Nɛfɛge, yɛɛ Zekelae.

english_verse: Uzziel's sons were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri.
translation_verse: Ɛzeɛle noko wole mrenya nsa: Maehyeeyɛle, Ɛlezeefan, yɛɛ Setelae.

english_verse: Aaron married Elisheba. She was the daughter of Amminadab and the sister of Nahshon; they had four sons, Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
translation_verse: Aalɔn gyale Amenadabe ara raalɛ Yilaehyɛba mɔɔ ɔ diema raalɛ a le Nahyɔn la. Yilaehyɛba wole Needabe, Abaehu, Ɛlieza, yɛɛ Yetamaa.

english_verse: Korah's sons were Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph.
translation_verse: Kɔla wole mrenya nsa: Asɛ, Ɛlekana, yɛɛ Abayasafe. Kɔla mbusua ne ɛne.

english_verse: Aaron's son Eleazar married one of Putiel's daughters, and their son was Phinehas. This ends the list of those who were the heads of clans in the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Aalɔn ara nrenya Ɛlieza gyale Puteɛle ara raalɛ na ɔwole Fenɛhaze. Ɛhye mɔ a le Livae abusua ekpunli ne anu mbusua mgbanyinli a.

english_verse: The Lord had commanded Aaron and Moses to lead every family and tribe of Israel out of Egypt,
translation_verse: Aalɔn nee Mosisi a Ɛdɛnkɛma zele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛye Yizilayɛ ɛlɔne ne amuala bɛvi Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo” la.

english_verse: and so they told the king of Egypt to set the people of Israel free. The Lord Commands Moses and Aaron To Speak to the King
translation_verse: Mosisi ɛhye nee Aalɔn ɛhye a hanle Yizilayɛma ɛvilɛ mɔɔ bɛfi Yigyibiti la anwo edwɛkɛ hilele Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne a. Ɛdɛnkɛma kɔ zolɛ azoa Mosisi nee Aalɔn

english_verse: When the Lord spoke to Moses in the land of Egypt,
translation_verse: Kenle ko ne mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele Mosisi wɔ Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo la,

english_verse: he said, “I am the Lord. Tell the king of Egypt everything I say to you.”
translation_verse: ɔzele Mosisi kɛ, “Medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a. Ka edwɛkɛ mɔɔ melɛka meahile wɔ la amuala kile Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne.”

english_verse: But Moses answered, “You know I am a very poor speaker, and the king will never listen to me.”
translation_verse: Mosisi hanle hilele Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ, “Ɛdawɔ ɛze kɛ me nloa ɛnde, kɛ ɔkɛyɛ na belemgbunli ne adie me ɛ?”

english_verse: The Lord said: I am going to let your brother Aaron speak for you. He will tell your message to the king, just as a prophet speaks my message to the people.
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Nea, meyɛ wɔ kɛ ɛle Nyamenle wɔ belemgbunli ne anye zo, na ɛ diema Aalɔn ayɛ wɔ kpɔmanvolɛ.

english_verse: Tell Aaron everything I say to you, and he will order the king to let my people leave his country.
translation_verse: Ɛbaha mɔɔ mebaha meahile wɔ la amuala wɔahile ɛ diema Aalɔn na ɔdaye noko yeaha yeahile belemgbunli ne kɛ ɔmaa Yizilayɛma ɛvi ye azɛlɛ ne azo ɛhɔ.

english_verse: When this happens, the Egyptians will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Saa mefa tumi kpole metea Yigyibitima, meye me menli Yizilayɛma mefi Yigyibiti a bɛanwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron obeyed the Lord
translation_verse: Na Mosisi nee Aalɔn yɛle ye zɔhane, kɛmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma zele bɛ la.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Moses, when the king asks you and Aaron to perform a miracle, command Aaron to throw his walking stick down in front of the king, and it will turn into a snake.”
translation_verse: “Saa Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne se bɛ kɛ bɛyɛ nwanwane debie bɛhile kɛ bɛle nɔhalɛ a, wɔmɔ Mosisi, ka kile Aalɔn kɛ, ‘Fuandi wɔ kpɔma ne to belemgbunli ne anyunlu ɛkɛ maa ɔhakyi ɛwɔlɛ.’ ”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king and his officials and did exactly as the Lord had commanded—Aaron threw the stick down, and it turned into a snake.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Mosisi nee Aalɔn hɔle belemgbunli ne ɛkɛ hɔyɛle mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma zele bɛ la. Aalɔn vuandinle ye kpɔma ne dole belemgbunli nee ye mgbanyima ne mɔ anyunlu ɛkɛ na ɔhakyile ɛwɔlɛ.

english_verse: Then the king called in the wise men and the magicians, who used their secret powers to do the same thing—
translation_verse: Akee belemgbunli ne vɛlɛle ye nrɛlɛbɛvolɛma nee ngonyiama mɔɔ wɔ Yigyibiti la, na bɛdabɛ noko bɛyele ngonyia ko ne ala bie.

english_verse: they threw down sticks that turned into snakes. But Aaron's snake swallowed theirs.
translation_verse: Bɛvuandinle bɛ agbɔma ne mɔ bɛguale aze na agbɔma ne mɔ hakyile nwɔlɛ. Na Aalɔn ɛwɔlɛ ɛdeɛ ne memenle bɛ nwɔlɛ ne mɔ.

english_verse: The king behaved just as the Lord had said and stubbornly refused to listen. The Nile River Turns into Blood
translation_verse: Noko belemgbunli ne akee yɛle dapele kpole kpalɛ, na kɛmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma hanle la, akee bɔbɔ ɔnrɛdie bɛ edwɛkɛ fee. Anwubɛnyunlu to Yigyibitima Mogya

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: The Egyptian king stubbornly refuses to change his mind and let the people go.
translation_verse: Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Belemgbunli ɛyɛ dapele, yedu ɔ gye kɛ ɔnrɛmaa menli ne ɛnrɛhɔ.

english_verse: Tomorrow morning take the stick that turned into a snake, then wait beside the Nile River for the king.
translation_verse: Nwonlomɔ kɔ belemgbunli ne ɛkɛ, wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɔlɛkɔ Azule Naele ne anu la. Kendɛ ye wɔ azule ne anloa. Anrɛɛ fa wɔ kpɔma ne mɔɔ hakyile ɛwɔlɛ ne la dɛ ɛ sa nu.

english_verse: Tell him, “The Lord God of the Hebrews sent me to order you to release his people, so they can worship him in the desert. But until now, you have paid no attention.
translation_verse: Na se ye kɛ, ‘Ɛdɛnkɛma, Hibuluma Nyamenle ne zoanle me manle membanzele wɔ kɛ: Maa me menli ne ɛhɔ, amaa bɛazonle me wɔ fienemgbole ne anu, na sumunli kɛ de la, wɔduodua ɛ nzo.’

english_verse: “The Lord is going to do something to show you that he really is the Lord. I will strike the Nile with this stick, and the water will turn into blood.
translation_verse: Yemɔti kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma se la ɛne, ‘Ɛhye bamaa wɔanwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a. Mefa kpɔma ye mɔɔ melɛ la meabɔ azule Naele ye anu, na ɔbahakyi mogya.

english_verse: The fish will die, the river will stink, and none of you Egyptians will be able to drink the water.”
translation_verse: Fɛlɛ mɔɔ wɔ nu la amuala bawu, nzule ne babɔ nvoanvoa bie, na Yigyibitima ɛnrɛnlo ye fee.’ ”

english_verse: Moses, then command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. And when he does, every drop of water in Egypt will turn into blood, including rivers, canals, ponds, and even the water in buckets and jars.
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Ka kile Aalɔn maa ɔva ye kpɔma ne ɔdende ye Yigyibiti nzule ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti azo, bɛ azule ne mɔ, azudenle ne mɔ mɔɔ menli ɛpɛ la, nee bɛ nzubula ne mɔ amuala azo ɔmaa bɛ kɔsɔɔti bɛhakyi mogya. Mogya bava Yigyibiti azɛlɛ ne kɔsɔɔti, mogya bagyinlegyinla mbaka nee awolɛ muala akunlu kuloonwu nu!”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron obeyed the Lord. Aaron held out his stick, then struck the Nile, as the king and his officials watched. The river turned into blood,
translation_verse: Mosisi nee Aalɔn yɛle mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma zele bɛ la. Wɔ belemgbunli ne nee ye mgbanyima ne mɔ anyunlu, Aalɔn vale ye kpɔma ne bɔle Azule Naele ne anu, na azule ne hakyile mogya.

english_verse: the fish died, and the water smelled so bad that none of the Egyptians could drink it. Blood was everywhere in Egypt.
translation_verse: Fɛlɛ mɔɔ wɔ azule ne anu la wule, azule ne bɔnle nvoanvoa mɔɔ Yigyibitima no a ɔnyɛ boɛ a. Yigyibiti ɛleka biala yɛle mogya.

english_verse: But the Egyptian magicians used their secret powers to do the same thing. The king did just as the Lord had said—he stubbornly refused to listen.
translation_verse: Yigyibiti ngonyiama yele ngonyia ko ne ala bie, yemɔti belemgbunli ahonle akee solole na ye dapele ne yɛle kpole, na kɛmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma hanle la, yeandie bɛ fee.

english_verse: Then he went back to his palace and never gave it a second thought.
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne ziale hɔle sua nu, yeanva ye adwenle yeangɔ ɛhye azo fee.

english_verse: The Egyptians had to dig holes along the banks of the Nile for drinking water, because water from the river was unfit to drink. Frogs
translation_verse: Yigyibitima amuala bobɔle bula wɔ azule Naele ne anloa, ɔluakɛ bɛno Naele ne anu nzule ne a ɔnyɛ boɛ fee.

english_verse: Seven days after the Lord had struck the Nile,
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zɛkyele azule Naele ne la, kenle nsuu pɛle nu na yeayɛ kpalɛ.

english_verse: he said to Moses: Go to the palace and tell the king of Egypt that I order him to let my people go, so they can worship me.
translation_verse: Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Kɔ kɔze Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne kɛ, ‘Kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma se la ɛne: Maa me menli ne ɛhɔ, amaa bɛazonle me.

english_verse: If he refuses, I will cover his entire country with frogs.
translation_verse: Saa wɔammaa bɛangɔ a, nea, mebava ahɛlɛne meazɛkye wɔ maanle ne.

english_verse: Warn the king that the Nile will be full of frogs, and from there they will spread into the royal palace, including the king's bedroom and even his bed. Frogs will enter the homes of his officials and will find their way into ovens and into the bowls of bread dough.
translation_verse: Azule Naele ne bawula ahɛlɛne ngome, bɛbayi wɔ suakunlu ɛkɛ, wɔ sua ne mɔɔ ɛda nu la akunlu, wɔ ɛsokpa ne azo, wɔ mgbanyima nee wɔ menli ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti azua nu yɛɛ bɛ fonlomo ne mɔ nee bɛ ahyɛnze mɔɔ bɛfa bɛto kpanwo bɔbɔ la, ahɛlɛne bayiyi bɛ tetɛkɛɛ.

english_verse: Frogs will be crawling on everyone—the king, his officials, and every citizen of Egypt.
translation_verse: Ahɛlɛne bavo wɔ, wɔ menli ne, yɛɛ wɔ mgbanyima ne mɔ anwo.’ ”

english_verse: Moses, now command Aaron to hold his stick over the water. Then frogs will come from all rivers, canals, and ponds in Egypt, and they will cover the land.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Ka kile Aalɔn kɛ, ‘Fa wɔ kpɔma ne tende azule ne mɔ, azudenle mɔɔ bɛdudu, nee nzubula ne mɔ azo ye ahɛlɛne maa bɛva Yigyibiti azɛlɛ ne.’ ”

english_verse: But the magicians used their secret powers to do the same thing.
translation_verse: Na ngonyiama ne noko yele ngonyia yele ahɛlɛne guale Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “If you ask the Lord to take these frogs away from me and my people, I will let your people go and offer sacrifices to him.”
translation_verse: Akee belemgbunli ne vɛlɛle Mosisi nee Aalɔn na ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛzɛlɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛmaa ɔye ahɛlɛne ne mɔ ɔvi me nee me menli ne anwo ɛke, na mebamaa menli ne ahɔbɔ azu amaa Ɛdɛnkɛma.”

english_verse: “All right,” Moses answered. “You choose the time when I am to pray for the frogs to stop bothering you, your officials, and your people, and for them to leave your houses and be found only in the river.”
translation_verse: Mosisi hanle hilele belemgbunli ne kɛ, “Si ahonle, kile mekɛ mɔɔ menzɛlɛ memaa wɔ nee wɔ mgbanyima nee wɔ menli ne, amaa bɛaye ahɛlɛne ne mɔ bɛavi bɛ nee bɛ azua nu na yeaha Azule Naele ne anu ɛdeɛ ne mɔ ala la.”

english_verse: “Do it tomorrow!” the king replied. “As you wish,” Moses agreed. “Then everyone will discover that there is no god like the Lord,
translation_verse: Na belemgbunli ne hanle kɛ, “Ɛhyema.” Mosisi hanle kɛ, “Ɔyɛ zɔhane, kɛmɔ ɛdawɔ ɛse la, amaa wɔanwu kɛ nyamenle biala ɛnle ɛkɛ ne kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, yɛ Nyamenle ne ala.

english_verse: and frogs will no longer be found anywhere, except in the Nile.”
translation_verse: Ahɛlɛne ne mɔ bavi wɔ, wɔ mgbanyima, nee wɔ menli ne mɔ azua nu ahɔ, na yeaha mɔɔ wɔ Naele ne anu la ala.”

english_verse: After Moses and Aaron left the palace, Moses begged the Lord to do something about the frogs he had sent as punishment for the king.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Mosisi nee Aalɔn vi belemgbunli ɛkɛ ne hɔle. Mosisi zɛlɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma, kɛmɔ ɔ nee belemgbunli ne hyehyɛle mɔɔ fane ahɛlɛne ne mɔ ɛyelɛ nwo la.

english_verse: The Lord listened to Moses, and the frogs died everywhere—in houses, yards, and fields.
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛle mɔɔ Mosisi zɛlɛle ye la, ahɛlɛne ne mɔ wule wɔ azua nu, awuke ne mɔ, nee ɛya avule ne mɔ anu.

english_verse: The dead frogs were placed in piles, and the whole country began to stink.
translation_verse: Bɛhuohuanle bɛ nloa edukue edukue, akee maanle ne anu bɔnle nvoanvoa.

english_verse: But when the king saw that things were now better, he again did just as the Lord had said he would and stubbornly refused to listen to Moses and Aaron. Gnats
translation_verse: Na mɔɔ belemgbunli ne nwunle kɛ ahɛlɛne ne mɔ ɛwu la, ɔyɛle dapele bieko, yeandie mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma hanle la. Ngɔkɔwule

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Command Aaron to strike the ground with his walking stick, and everywhere in Egypt the dust will turn into gnats.”
translation_verse: Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Ka kile Aalɔn kɛ, ‘Tende wɔ kpɔma ne na fa fi azɛlɛ nwo maa ɔye ngɔkɔwule ɔmaa bɛva Yigyibiti maanle ne kɔsɔɔti.’ ”

english_verse: They obeyed, and when Aaron struck the ground with the stick, gnats started swarming on people and animals. In fact, every speck of dust in Egypt turned into a gnat.
translation_verse: Na bɛyɛle ye zɔhane; Aalɔn dendenle ye kpɔma ne finle aze, na ngɔkɔwule vale menli nee nyɛmoa; Yigyibiti azɛlɛ mumua ne azo yɛle ngɔkɔwule ngome.

english_verse: When the magicians tried to use their secret powers to do this, they failed, and gnats stayed on people and animals.
translation_verse: Ngonyiama ne bɔle mɔdenle kɛ bɛdabɛ bɛye ngɔkɔwule ne mɔ bie, noko bɛangola. Yemɔti ngɔkɔwule vale menli nee nyɛmoa.

english_verse: The magicians told the king, “God has done this.” But, as the Lord had said, the king was too stubborn to listen. Flies
translation_verse: Ngonyiama ne hanle hilele belemgbunli ne kɛ, “Nyamenle asa ɛrɛlɛsɛka ko bɔbɔ ɛhye o! Nyamenle a ɛyɛ ɛhye a.” Na belemgbunli ne zile ye ɛbolɛ na ɔyɛle dapele. Yeammaa menli ne angɔ, kɛmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma hanle la. Nrɛzenra

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Early tomorrow morning, while the king is on his way to the river, go and say to him, “The Lord commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him.
translation_verse: Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Dwazo nwonlomɔ mangyee ne na kendɛ belemgbunli ne. Saa ɔse yeahɔ azule ne anu a ka kile ye kɛ, ‘Kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma se la ɛne: Maa me menli ne ɛhɔ, amaa bɛazonle me.

english_verse: If you don't, he will send swarms of flies to attack you, your officials, and every citizen of your country. Your houses will be full of flies, and the ground will crawl with them.
translation_verse: Saa wɔammaa me menli ne angɔ a, nea, mebamaa nrɛzenra adɔka ara ɛdawɔ, wɔ mgbanyima, nee wɔ menli ne mɔ anwo zo; bɛbayiyi bɛ azua ne mɔ, Yigyibitima kɔsɔɔti azua ne mɔ anu bayɛ nrɛzenra adɔka, akee azɛlɛ mumua ne mɔɔ bɛgyi zolɛ la, nrɛzenra bava ye bɔkɔɔ.

english_verse: The Lord kept his promise—the palace and the homes of the royal officials swarmed with flies, and the rest of the country was infested with them as well.
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛle ye zɔhane; nrɛzenra adɔka ravale belemgbunli ne nee ye mgbanyima ne mɔ azua ne. Nrɛzenra ne mɔ zɛkyele Yigyibiti azɛlɛ ne.

english_verse: Then the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Go ahead and sacrifice to your God, but stay here in Egypt.”
translation_verse: Akee belemgbunli ne vɛlɛle Mosisi nee Aalɔn na ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛhɔ bɛhɔbɔ azu bɛmaa bɛ Nyamenle ne wɔ maanle ye anu.”

english_verse: “That's impossible!” Moses replied. “Any sacrifices we offer to the Lord our God would disgust the Egyptians, and they would stone us to death.
translation_verse: Na Mosisi hanle kɛ, “Ɔnle kpalɛ kɛ yɛkɛyɛ ye zɔhane, ɔluakɛ saa yɛyɛ a yɛkɛva Yigyibiti bɛkyi azubɔdeɛ ne mɔ bie yɛkɛbɔ azu yɛkɛmaa Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛ Nyamenle ne. Saa yɛfa azubɔdeɛ mɔɔ Yigyibitima kyi la yɛbɔ azu wɔ bɛ nye zo ɛke a, bɛkɛkpa yɛ awolɛ.

english_verse: No indeed! The Lord has ordered us to walk three days into the desert before offering sacrifices to him, and that's what we have to do.”
translation_verse: Ɔwɔ kɛ yɛtia kenle nsa adenle yɛkɔ fienemgbole ne anu yɛkɔbɔ azu yɛmaa Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛ Nyamenle ne, kɛmɔ ɔdaye ɔkɛhile yɛ la.”

english_verse: Then the king told him, “I'll let you go into the desert to offer sacrifices, if you don't go very far. But in the meantime, pray for me.”
translation_verse: Yemɔti belemgbunli ne hanle kɛ, “Memaa bɛahɔ bɛahɔbɔ azu bɛamaa Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne wɔ fienemgbole ne anu, na moa yɛɛ ɔnle kɛ bɛkɔ a. Bɛzɛlɛ bɛmaa me.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty,” Moses replied, “I'll pray for you as soon as I leave, and by tomorrow the flies will stop bothering you, your officials, and the citizens of your country. Only make sure that you're telling the truth this time and that you really intend to let our people offer sacrifices to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Akee Mosisi hanle kɛ, “Nea, mevi ɛ nwo ɛke melɛkɔ, na mebazɛlɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ nrɛzenra adɔka ne ɛvi belemgbunli, ye mgbanyima, nee ye menli ne anwo zo ɛhyema; na Nana, mmabɛlɛbɛla yɛ bieko kɛ ɛnrɛmaa me menli ne ɛnrɛhɔbɔ azu ɛnrɛmaa Ɛdɛnkɛma.”

english_verse: After leaving the palace, Moses prayed,
translation_verse: Yemɔti Mosisi vi belemgbunli ne anwo ɛkɛ ne hɔzɛlɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma.

english_verse: and the Lord answered his prayer. Not a fly was left to pester the king, his officials, or anyone else in Egypt.
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛle mɔɔ Mosisi bizale ye la, na ɔmanle nrɛzenra adɔka ne vile belemgbunli, ye mgbanyima, nee ye menli ne anwo zo; ko bɔbɔ anga ɛkɛ.

english_verse: But the king turned stubborn again and would not let the people go.
translation_verse: Na belemgbunli ne zile ye ɛbolɛ, na ye dapele ne akee yɛle kpole kpalɛ.

english_verse: The Lord sent Moses with this message for the king of Egypt: The Lord God of the Hebrews commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him.
translation_verse: Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Kɔ belemgbunli ne ɛkɛ kɔze ye kɛ, ‘Kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, Hibuluma Nyamenle ne se la ɛne: Maa me menli ne ɛhɔ, amaa bɛazonle me.

english_verse: he will bring a terrible disease on your horses and donkeys, your camels and cattle, and your sheep and goats.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma asa ɛnlomboɛ ne badɔ bɛ nlankɛ ne mɔ mɔɔ wɔ bɛ ɛya nu, bɛ mgbɔnwɔ, asoaso, afunlumu, mbɔnkye, yɛɛ mboane ne mɔ anwo zo, yeaye ewule yeado bɛ nwo yeamaa bɛawu.

english_verse: But the Lord will protect the animals that belong to the people of Israel, and none of theirs will die.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma bava ɛweɛne ado Yizilayɛma nee Yigyibitima nlankɛ ne mɔ avinli, na Yizilayɛma nlankɛ ne mɔ anu ko bɔbɔ ɛnrɛwu.’ ”

english_verse: Tomorrow is the day the Lord has set to do this.
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma hilele mekɛ, ɔse, “Ɛhyema Ɛdɛnkɛma bayɛ ɛhye wɔ azɛlɛ ne azo.”

english_verse: It happened the next day—all of the animals belonging to the Egyptians died, but the Israelites did not lose even one.
translation_verse: Aleɛ hyenle la Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛle ɛhye, ɔmanle Yigyibiti nlankɛ ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti wule, na Yizilayɛma nlankɛ ne mɔ, ɛdwoba ko bɔbɔ anwu.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses and Aaron: Take a few handfuls of ashes from a stove and you, Moses, throw them into the air. Be sure the king is watching.
translation_verse: Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi nee Aalɔn kɛ, “Bɛvula anyevinli nzonle bɛ sa ngoko na Mosisi ɛkponde bɛ anwomanyunlu wɔ belemgbunli ne anyunlu ɛkɛ.

english_verse: The ashes will blow across the land of Egypt, causing sores to break out on people and animals.
translation_verse: Ɔbazande kɛ munlutu kɛnlɛma bie wɔ Yigyibiti azɛlɛ ne kɔsɔɔti azo, na yeamaa nyila anwunwu menli nee nyɛmoa na bɛakpukekpuke bɛayɛ nganlɛ.”

english_verse: So they took a few handfuls of ashes and went to the king. Moses threw them into the air, and sores immediately broke out on the Egyptians and their animals.
translation_verse: Yemɔti bɛvulale anyevinli nzonle na bɛhɔle belemgbunli ne anyunlu. Mosisi vuandinle nzonle ne anwoma ne anu, na ɔmanle nyila nwunwunle menli nee nyɛmoa na bɛkpukekpukele bɛyɛle nganlɛ.

english_verse: The magicians were suffering so much from the sores, that they could not even come to Moses.
translation_verse: Na nyila ne mɔ ati ngonyiama ne angola Mosisi anyunlu gyinla, ɔluakɛ ɛnee nyila ɛnwunwu bɛ nee Yigyibitima kɔsɔɔti.

english_verse: Everything happened just as the Lord had told Moses—he made the king too stubborn to listen to Moses and Aaron. Hailstones
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma manle belemgbunli ne ahonle yɛle se, yeandie bɛ edwɛkɛ, kɛmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma hanle hilele Mosisi ala la. Ezuawolɛ

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to get up early the next morning and say to the king: The Lord God of the Hebrews commands you to let his people go, so they can worship him!
translation_verse: Eza Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Dwazo nwonlomɔ mangyee ne kɔ belemgbunli ne anyunlu kɔze ye kɛ, ‘Kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, Hibuluma Nyamenle ne se la ɛne: Maa me menli ne ɛhɔ, amaa bɛazonle me.

english_verse: If you don't, he will send his worst plagues to strike you, your officials, and everyone else in your country. Then you will find out that no one can oppose the Lord.
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ akee mebava me ndeanlɛ kɔsɔɔti meagua ɛ nwo zo, nee wɔ mgbanyima nee wɔ menli ne anwo zo, amaa wɔanwu kɛ awie biala mɔɔ le kɛ medame la ɛnle azɛlɛ ye azo ɛleka biala.

english_verse: In fact, he could already have sent a terrible disease and wiped you from the face of the earth.
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ kɛkala, saa medenrɛ me sa kɛ memaa ewulenzane adɔ wɔ nee wɔ mgbanyima avinli a, anrɛɛ mezɛkye bɛ muala mevi azɛlɛ ye azo.

english_verse: But he has kept you alive, just to show you his power and to bring honor to himself everywhere in the world.
translation_verse: Na mevavi wɔ, memaa wɔdɛnla ngoane nu kɛ mefa meahile me tumi ne, na wɔakponde me duma wɔ azɛlɛ ye kɔsɔɔti azo.

english_verse: You are still determined not to let the Lord's people go.
translation_verse: Noko ɛtɛmemaa ɛ nwo zo ɛtɛkile me menli ne, ɛnrɛmaa bɛnrɛhɔ.

english_verse: All right. At this time tomorrow, he will bring on Egypt the worst hailstorm in its history.
translation_verse: Nea, ɛhyema bekezɛ mebamaa ezuawolɛ mɔɔ sumunli kɛ bɛkyekyele Yigyibiti maanle ne toonwo mɔɔ yeradwu ɛnɛ la bie ɛtɛtɔle ɛlɛ la adɔ.

english_verse: You had better give orders for every person and every animal in Egypt to take shelter. If they don't, they will die.
translation_verse: Yemɔti soa maa bɛhɔyeye wɔ nyɛmoa nee wɔ ninyɛne mɔɔ wɔ ɛya ne mɔ anu la amuala bɛzie azua nu, ɔluakɛ ezuawolɛ badɔ menli nee nyɛmoa mɔɔ wɔ ɛya avule nu na bɛamba sua zo la anwo zo, na bɛawu.’ ”

english_verse: Some of the king's officials were frightened by what the Lord had said, and they hurried off to make sure their slaves and animals were safe.
translation_verse: Na awie biala mɔɔ wɔ belemgbunli nee mgbanyima ne mɔ anu na ɔzulole Ɛdɛnkɛma anloa edwɛkɛ ne la, manle ye sonvolɛma nee ye nyɛmoa nriandile hɔle sua bo.

english_verse: But others paid no attention to his threats and left their slaves and animals out in the open.
translation_verse: Bɛdabɛ noko mɔɔ bɛambu Ɛdɛnkɛma edwɛkɛ ne bie la gyakyile bɛ sonvolɛma nee bɛ nyɛmoa wɔ bɛ ɛya avule ne mɔ anu.

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sky, so that hailstones will fall on people, animals, and crops in the land of Egypt.”
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Tende ɛ sa anwomanyunlu maa ezuawolɛ ɛdɔ Yigyibiti azɛlɛ ye kɔsɔɔti azo ɔgua menli nee nyɛmoa nee aleɛ mɔɔ wɔ ɛbɔ nu la azo.”

english_verse: Moses pointed his walking stick toward the sky, and hailstones started falling everywhere. Thunder roared, and lightning flashed back and forth, striking the ground. This was the worst storm in the history of Egypt.
translation_verse: ezuawolɛ dɔle, ahumu kpole dule, anwomanyunlu kpale senle vedele ndoɔdoazo, na ezuawolɛ ne dɔle kpole kpalɛ mɔɔ sumunli kɛ Yigyibiti yɛle maanle la bie ɛtɛtɔle ɛlɛ a.

english_verse: People, animals, and crops were pounded by the hailstones, and bark was stripped from trees.
translation_verse: Ezuawolɛ ne hanle debie biala mɔɔ wɔ wienyi nu la wɔ Yigyibiti maanle ne kɔsɔɔti anu, menli nee nyɛmoa; ɔhanle aleɛ biala mɔɔ wɔ ɛbɔ nu la, ɔzɛkyele dɔɔnwo.

english_verse: Only Goshen, where the Israelites lived, was safe from the storm.
translation_verse: Gohyɛn azɛlɛ zo, ɛleka mɔɔ Yizilayɛma wɔ la yɛɛ ezuawolɛ ne bie andɔ a.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Now I have really sinned! My people and I are guilty, and the Lord is right.
translation_verse: Akee belemgbunli zoanle menli manle bɛhɔvɛlɛle Mosisi nee Aalɔn na ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Meyɛ ɛtane. Ɛdɛnkɛma di benle. Me nee me menli ne yɛdi fɔlɛ.

english_verse: We can't stand any more of this thunder and hail. Please ask the Lord to make it stop. Your people can go—you don't have to stay in Egypt any longer.”
translation_verse: Bɛzɛlɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛmaa maanle nu ɛhululɛ nee ezuawolɛ ɛdɔlɛ ne ɛgyakyi na memaa bɛahɔ; menrɛmaa bɛnrɛdɛnla ɛke bieko.”

english_verse: Moses answered, “As soon as I leave the city, I will lift my arms in prayer. When the thunder and hail stop, you will know that the earth belongs to the Lord.
translation_verse: Mosisi hanle kɛ, “Saa meye me nwo suakpole ye azo a, mebamaa me sa zo meazɛlɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, na maanle nu ɛhululɛ ne bagyakyi, yɛɛ ezuawolɛ ne ɛnrɛdɔ bieko, amaa wɔanwu kɛ azɛlɛ ye le Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛdeɛ.

english_verse: But I am certain that neither you nor your officials really fear the Lord God.”
translation_verse: Na wɔmɔ, ɛ nee wɔ mgbanyima, meze kɛ bɛnzulo Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle ne.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, the flax and barley crops had been destroyed by the storm because they were ready to ripen.
translation_verse: Bolɔfodɔ nee baale zɛkyele, ɔluakɛ ɛnee baale ɛtulutulu na bolɔfodɔ ɛlɛwula nya.

english_verse: But the wheat crops ripen later, and they were not damaged.
translation_verse: Na hwiiti anzɛkye, ɔluakɛ bɛnlua bɛ ndɛ la ati bɛanfifi ndɛ.

english_verse: After Moses left the royal palace and the city, he lifted his arms in prayer to the Lord, and the thunder, hail, and drenching rain stopped.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Mosisi vi belemgbunli ne anwo ɛkɛ hɔle na ɔyele ɔ nwo suakpole ne azo. Ɔdɛlɛle ɔ sa nu ɔzɛlɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma na maanle nu ɛhululɛ ne gyakyile, ezuawolɛ ne gyakyile ɛdɔlɛ, na ezule ɛdɔlɛ bilididi andɔ azɛlɛ ne azo bieko.

english_verse: When the king realized that the storm was over, he disobeyed once more. He and his officials were so stubborn
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne nwunle kɛ ezule ne nee ezuawolɛ ne nee maanle nu ɛhululɛ ne ɛgyakyi la, ɔyɛle ɛtane bieko, na ɔ nee ye mgbanyima ne mɔ dapele ne akee yɛle kpole.

english_verse: that he refused to let the Israelites go. This was exactly what the Lord had said would happen.
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne ahonle yɛle se, yemɔti yeammaa Yizilayɛma angɔ, kɛmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma luale Mosisi anwo zo hanle la.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: Go back to the king. I have made him and his officials stubborn, so that I could work these miracles.
translation_verse: Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Kɔ belemgbunli ne ɛkɛ, ɔluakɛ memaa ye nee ye mgbanyima ne mɔ ahonle ɛyɛ se, amaa meahile bɛ me sɛkɛlɛneɛ ɛhye mɔ wɔ bɛ avinli,

english_verse: I did this because I want you to tell your children and your grandchildren about my miracles and about my harsh treatment of the Egyptians. Then all of you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: na wɔabɔ ye nolo wɔahile ɛ mra nee ɛ mra amra, kɛ menzile menyɛle Yigyibitima nee sɛkɛlɛneɛ mɔɔ menyɛle wɔ bɛ avinli la, na ɛdawɔ noko wɔanwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the king and told him that the Lord God of the Hebrews had said: How long will you stubbornly refuse to obey? Release my people so they can worship me.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Mosisi nee Aalɔn hɔle belemgbunli ne ɛkɛ hɔzele ye kɛ, “Kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, Hibuluma Nyamenle ne se la ɛne, ‘Kenlenzu yɛɛ ɛkɛkpo kɛ ɛnrɛmemaa ɛ nwo zo ɛnrɛhile me a? Maa me menli ne ɛhɔ, amaa bɛazonle me.

english_verse: Do this by tomorrow, or I will cover your country with so many locusts
translation_verse: Saa ɛkpo na wɔammaa me menli ne angɔ a, ɛnee nea kɛ, ɛhyema mebamaa abɛbɛ arava wɔ maanle ne,

english_verse: that you won't be able to see the ground. Most of your crops were ruined by the hailstones, but these locusts will destroy what little is left, including the trees.
translation_verse: na bɛaheda azɛlɛ ne azo bɔkɔɔ mɔɔ awie biala ɛnnwu azɛlɛ ne a. Bɛbali debie biala mɔɔ ezuawolɛ ne dɔle wiele na ɔhale la amuala; bɛbali aleɛ biala mɔɔ wɔ ɛbɔ nu la.

english_verse: Your palace, the homes of your officials, and all the other houses in Egypt will overflow with more locusts than have ever been seen in this country. After Moses left the palace,
translation_verse: Bɛbava wɔ, wɔ mgbanyima nee Yigyibitima kɔsɔɔti azua ne mɔ; na ɛhye, sumunli kɛ bɛ ze mɔ nee bɛ nlenya mɔ rale azɛlɛ ye azo toonwo mɔɔ yeradwu ɛnɛ la, bɛtɛnwunle bie ɛlɛ.’ ” Na Mosisi nee Aalɔn hakyile bɛ nwo hɔle.

english_verse: the king's officials asked, “Your Majesty, how much longer is this man going to be a troublemaker? Why don't you let the people leave, so they can worship the Lord their God? Don't you know that Egypt is a disaster?”
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne mgbanyima ne mɔ hanle hilele ye kɛ, “Kenlenzu yɛɛ nrenya ɛhye kɛgyakyi yɛ ɛgyegyelɛ a? Maa menli ne ɛhɔ ɛ, amaa bɛazonle Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne. Asoo ɛtɛnwunle kɛ Yigyibiti ɛbɔ bɔkɔɔ ɔ?”

english_verse: The king had Moses and Aaron brought back, and he said, “All right, you may go and worship the Lord your God. But first tell me who will be going.”
translation_verse: Yemɔti bɛhɔvale Mosisi nee Aalɔn bɛrale belemgbunli ne anyunlu, na ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛhɔzonle Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne; na nwane mɔ a kɔ a?”

english_verse: “Everyone, young and old,” Moses answered. “We will even take our sheep, goats, and cattle, because we want to hold a celebration in honor of the Lord.”
translation_verse: Mosisi buale kɛ, “Yɛ nee ngakula nee mgbanyinli, yɛ mra mrenya nee mraalɛ, yɛ mboane nee yɛ nyɛmoa muala, ɔluakɛ ɔwɔ kɛ yɛdi ɛvoyia yɛwula Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlunyia.”

english_verse: The king replied, “The Lord had better watch over you on the day I let you leave with your families! You're up to no good.
translation_verse: Na belemgbunli ne zele bɛ kɛ, “Meka Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ menrɛmaa bɛ nee mraalɛ nee ngakula ne mɔ ɛnrɛhɔ fee. Bɛlɛ adwenle ɛtane wɔ bɛ ti anu.

english_verse: Do you want to worship the Lord? All right, take only the men and go.” Then Moses and Aaron were chased out of the palace.
translation_verse: Telekɔ! Maa mrenya ne mɔ angome ɛhɔzonle Ɛdɛnkɛma, ɔluakɛ ɛhye ala a ɛnee ɛkpondɛ a.” Na bɛvoanle Mosisi nee Aalɔn bɛvile belemgbunli ne anyunlu.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward Egypt. Swarms of locusts will come and eat everything left by the hail.”
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Maa ɛ sa zo wɔ Yigyibiti azɛlɛ ye azo maa abɛbɛ ɛrɛla ɛrali aleɛ biala mɔɔ wɔ azɛlɛ ne azo mɔɔ ezuawolɛ ne anzɛkye ye la.”

english_verse: Moses held out his walking stick, and the Lord sent an east wind that blew across Egypt the rest of the day and all that night. By morning, locusts
translation_verse: Yemɔti Mosisi manle ɔ sa zo wɔ Yigyibiti azɛlɛ ne azo, na Ɛdɛnkɛma manle aduduleɛ anwoma dule azɛlɛ ne azo ewia ne nee nɔe ne; ye nwonlomɔ ne ɛnee aduduleɛ anwoma ne ɛmaa abɛbɛ ɛbu azɛlɛ ne azo.

english_verse: were swarming everywhere. Never before had there been so many locusts in Egypt, and never again will there be so many.
translation_verse: Abɛbɛ ne mɔ rale Yigyibiti azɛlɛ ne azo, bɛvale maanle ne ɛleka biala na bɛbɔle bɛ nwo atɛnlase. Bɛ pinopino ɛdeɛ, bieko ɛtɛbale, yɛɛ bieko ɛnrɛra ɛlɛ.

english_verse: The ground was black with locusts, and they ate everything left on the trees and in the fields. Nothing green remained in Egypt—not a tree or a plant.
translation_verse: Bɛvale azɛlɛ ne bɔkɔɔ, na azɛlɛ ne azo yɛle fii kokye. Bɛlile aleɛ nee mbakama mɔɔ ezuawolɛ ne gyakyile la; debie amunli kokye bɔbɔ anga, yɛɛ nzoleɛ biala anga baka kpole anzɛɛ ekyi bɔbɔ azo wɔ ɛya anzɛɛ kpɔkɛ nu wɔ Yigyibiti maanle ne kɔsɔɔti anu.

english_verse: At once the king sent for Moses and Aaron. He told them, “I have sinned against the Lord your God and against you.
translation_verse: Na ndɛndɛ ne ala belemgbunli ne vɛlɛle Mosisi nee Aalɔn na ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Meyɛ ɛtane metia Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne nee bɛdabɛ.

english_verse: Forgive me one more time and ask the Lord to stop these insects from killing every living plant.”
translation_verse: Yemɔti mesɛlɛ bɛ, bɛva me ɛtane ko ye bɛhyɛ me na bɛzɛlɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne kɛ ɔye ewule ɛhye ɔvi me nwo zo.”

english_verse: Moses left the palace and prayed.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Mosisi vile belemgbunli ne anwo ɛkɛ na ɔhɔzɛlɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma.

english_verse: Then the Lord sent a strong west wind that swept the locusts into the Red Sea. Not one locust was left anywhere in Egypt,
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma manle adɔleɛ anwoma ɛsesebɛ bie dule na ɔpiepianle abɛbɛ ne mɔ ɔhɔguale Suwɛze Ebolo ne anu; kokye anga Yigyibiti maanle ne anu.

english_verse: but the Lord made the king so stubborn that he still refused to let the Israelites go. Darkness
translation_verse: Na eza Ɛdɛnkɛma manle belemgbunli ne ahonle yɛle se bieko, yemɔti yeammaa Yizilayɛma angɔ. Awozinli

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sky, and everything will be covered with darkness thick enough to touch.”
translation_verse: Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Tende ɛ sa anwomanyunlu maa awozinli kabikabi mɔɔ kɛde menli ne kpalɛ kpalɛ la ɛva Yigyibiti azɛlɛ ne.”

english_verse: Moses stretched his arm toward the sky, and Egypt was covered with darkness for three days.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Mosisi dendenle ɔ sa anwomanyunlu na awozinli kabikabi vale Yigyibiti maanle ne kenle kɔkɔlɛ nsa.

english_verse: During that time, the Egyptians could not see each other or leave their homes, but there was light where the Israelites lived.
translation_verse: Yigyibitinli biala annwu ɔ gɔnwo, yɛɛ Yigyibitinli biala anvinde toonwo kenle nsa. Na ɛleka mɔɔ Yizilayɛma de la ɛdeɛ, wienyi dale ɛkɛ.

english_verse: The king sent for Moses and told him, “Go worship the Lord! And take your families with you. Just leave your sheep, goats, and cattle.”
translation_verse: Akee belemgbunli ne vɛlɛle Mosisi na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Bɛhɔ na bɛhɔzonle Ɛdɛnkɛma, bɛ nee bɛ mra nee bɛ mraalɛ ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti bɛhɔ. Na bɛgyakyi bɛ mboane nee bɛ nyɛmoa ne mɔ ɛke.”

english_verse: “No!” Moses replied. “You must let us offer sacrifices to the Lord our God,
translation_verse: Na Mosisi hanle kɛ, “Eza ɔwɔ kɛ yɛnyia azubɔdeɛ nee ɛyelalɛ azubɔdeɛ, amaa yɛava yɛabɔ azu yɛamaa Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛ Nyamenle ne.

english_verse: and we won't know which animals we will need until we get there. That's why we can't leave even one of them here.”
translation_verse: Ɔwɔ kɛ yɛ nee yɛ nlankɛ ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti kɔ. Yɛnrɛgyakyi ɛnlankɛ gyakɛ mgbɔlaboa mgbane ko bɔbɔ ɛke. Ɔwɔ kɛ yɛnyia bɛ na yɛava yɛazonle Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛ Nyamenle ne. Yɛtɛnwunle debie mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ yɛfa yɛsonle Ɛdɛnkɛma a, kyesɛ yɛdwu nehane kolaa.”

english_verse: This time the Lord made the king so stubborn
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma manle belemgbunli ne ahonle yɛle se, yemɔti yeammaa bɛangɔ.

english_verse: that he said to Moses, “Get out and stay out! If you ever come back, you're dead!”
translation_verse: Akee belemgbunli ne zele ye kɛ, “Ɛvi me nyunlu ɛkɛ ne kɔ! Dwenle ɛ nwo, mmamaa menwu ɛ nyunlu bieko! Kenle biala mɔɔ menwɔnwu ɛ nyunlu la, ɛbawu!”

english_verse: “Have it your way,” Moses answered. “You won't see me again.”
translation_verse: Mosisi hanle kɛ, “Kɛmɔ wɔha la, ɛnrɛnwu me nyunlu bieko.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses: I am going to punish the king of Egypt and his people one more time. Then the king will gladly let you leave his land. In fact, he will even chase you out.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Akee yeha ewule ko mɔɔ meye meado belemgbunli ne nee Yigyibitima anwo a; ɛhye anzi belemgbunli ne bamaa bɛahɔ. Ɔnrɛha ye kɛ bɛhɔ ala na ɔbavoa bɛ.

english_verse: Now go and tell my people to ask their Egyptian neighbors for gold and silver jewelry.
translation_verse: Bɔ wɔ menli ne amaneɛ kɛ, nrenya biala ɛbiza ye manivolɛ yɛɛ raalɛ biala ɛbiza ye manivolɛ raalɛ ɛlie dwɛtɛ fufule nee ezukoa nvutuke anwoneɛ.”

english_verse: So the Lord made the Egyptians greatly respect the Israelites, and everyone, including the king's officials, considered Moses an important leader.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma manle Yigyibitima lile Yizilayɛma ne eni. Ɛnee Mosisi mumua ne ɛyɛ sonlakpole wɔ Yigyibiti maanle ne anu, wɔ belemgbunli mgbanyima ne nee menli ne mɔ anye zo.

english_verse: Moses went to the king and said: I have come to let you know what the Lord is going to do. About midnight he will go through the land of Egypt,
translation_verse: Na Mosisi hanle kɛ, “Kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma se la ɛne: Alevinli mu nwiɔ avinli, mebazi mealɔ Yigyibitima nu.

english_verse: and wherever he goes, the first-born son in every family will die. Your own son will die, and so will the son of the lowest slave woman. Even the first-born males of your cattle will die.
translation_verse: Yigyibitinli biala belamunli ralɛ nrenya bawu, ɔvi belemgbunli ne mɔɔ de ebia ne azo la ara belamunli ralɛ nrenya ne anwo zo toonwo mɔɔ kɔdwu sonvolɛ raalɛ ne bɔbɔ mɔɔ ɛlɛkyiba melahyinli ne mɔɔ ti abɛlɛ la belamunli ralɛ nrenya ne anwo zo. Nlankɛ ne mɔ amra mɔɔ lumua la kɔsɔɔti bawu.

english_verse: Everywhere in Egypt there will be loud crying. Nothing like this has ever happened before or will ever happen again.
translation_verse: Na ɛzunlɛ nee awolɛyelɛ bazi Yigyibiti maanle ne anu kɔsɔɔti; ɛhye le debie mɔɔ bie ɛtɛsile ɛlɛ yɛɛ bie ɛnrɛzi ɛlɛ.

english_verse: But there won't be any need for the Israelites to cry. Things will be so quiet that not even a dog will be heard barking. Then you Egyptians will know that the Lord is good to the Israelites, even while he punishes you.
translation_verse: Na wɔ Yizilayɛma anu, twea ɛnrɛkpo sonla na yeayɛ nane bɔbɔ, amaa wɔanwu kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛgya ɛweɛne ɛdo Yizilayɛma nee Yigyibitima avinli.

english_verse: Your leaders will come and bow down, begging me to take my people and leave your country. Then we will leave. Moses was very angry; he turned and left the king.
translation_verse: Wɔ mgbanyima ɛhye mɔ kɔsɔɔti bara arabɔ bɛ ti aze amaa me na bɛaze kɛ, ‘Ɛ nee ɛ sa zo ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti bɛvi ɛke bɛhɔ.’ Na ɛhye anzi mebavi maanle ye anu meahɔ.” Na Mosisi vale ɛya kpole, na ɔvile belemgbunli ne anyunlu ɛkɛ ne ɔhɔle.

english_verse: What the Lord had earlier said to Moses came true. He had said, “The king of Egypt won't listen. Then I will perform even more miracles.”
translation_verse: Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Belemgbunli ne ɛnrɛdie wɔ, amaa meayɛ nwanwane ninyɛne mɔnwo mɔnwo wɔ Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo.”

english_verse: So the king of Egypt saw Moses and Aaron work miracles, but the Lord made him stubbornly refuse to let the Israelites leave his country.
translation_verse: Mosisi nee Aalɔn yɛle nwanwane ninyɛne ɛhye mɔ kɔsɔɔti wɔ belemgbunli ne anye zo, na Ɛdɛnkɛma manle belemgbunli ne ahonle yɛle se, yemɔti yeammaa Yizilayɛma anvi maanle ne anu angɔ.

english_verse: Some time later the Lord said to Moses and Aaron:
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi nee Aalɔn wɔ Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo kɛ,

english_verse: This month is to be the first month of the year for you.
translation_verse: “Siane ɛhye bayɛ bɛ siane mɔɔ lumua a; ɔbayɛ bɛ ɛvolɛ ne anu siane mɔɔ lumua la.

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel that on the tenth day of this month the head of each family must choose a lamb or a young goat for his family to eat.
translation_verse: Ka kile Yizilayɛma ɛlɔne ne amuala kɛ siane ɛhye, ye kenle mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ bulu la, nrenya biala nee ye awuke nu amra ɛva boane anzɛɛ abɔnkye ralɛ ko.

english_verse: Each family must take care of its animal until the evening of the fourteenth day of the month, when the animals are to be killed.
translation_verse: Bɛbava bɛazie toonwo siane ɛhye ye kenle bulu nee nna ne azo, akee Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti bahu bɛ mboane ne mɔ kenle ko ne nɔsolɛ nu.

english_verse: Some of the blood must be put on the two doorposts and above the door of each house where the animals are to be eaten.
translation_verse: Bɛbava nane ne mogya ne bie bɛaha azua mɔɔ bɛkɛli nane ne wɔ nu la nlenkɛ ne felɛmo nwiɔ ne nee ɔ ti zo ɛdeɛ ne mɔ anwo.

english_verse: That night the animals are to be roasted and eaten, together with bitter herbs and thin bread made without yeast.
translation_verse: Bɛbava kpanwo mɔɔ mgbɔvonle ɛnle nu nee nya nya ɛnwonle bɛali nane ne ndondo.

english_verse: Don't eat the meat raw or boiled. The entire animal, including its head, legs, and insides, must be roasted.
translation_verse: Bɛmmadi bie amolɛ anzɛɛ bɛmmato na bɛali. Bɛli ye ndondo, ɔ ti o, ye ndwɛlɛ o, ɔ kunlu ɔ kunlu ne mɔ o, bɛdondo.

english_verse: Eat what you want that night, and the next morning burn whatever is left.
translation_verse: Bɛmmagyakyi bie bɛmaa aleɛ kye zolɛ. Biala mɔɔ aleɛ kɛhye zolɛ la, bɛyela ye.

english_verse: When you eat the meal, be dressed and ready to travel. Have your sandals on, carry your walking stick in your hand, and eat quickly. This is the Passover Festival in honor of me, your Lord.
translation_verse: Akee adenle mɔɔ bɛpe nu bɛli la ɛne: bɛhye bɛ adɛladeɛ ne mɔ azo, bɛwula bɛ mgbɔlaboa ne mɔ, na bɛva bɛ agbɔma ne mɔ bɛlɛ bɛ sa nu, na bɛli ye ndɛndɛ. Ɔle Ɛdɛnkɛma Akpabɛnwo Ɛvoyia.

english_verse: That same night I will pass through Egypt and kill the first-born son in every family and the first-born male of all animals. I am the Lord, and I will punish the gods of Egypt.
translation_verse: “Ɔluakɛ mebapɛ nu Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo kenle ko ne nɔe ne. Mebahu Yigyibiti belamunli mralɛ muala, menli nee nyɛmoa, na meabua Yigyibiti awozonle kɔsɔɔti ndɛne. Medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a.

english_verse: The blood on the houses will show me where you live, and when I see the blood, I will pass over you. Then you won't be bothered by the terrible disasters I will bring on Egypt.
translation_verse: Mogya ne bayɛ azua mɔɔ bɛwɔ nu la sɛkɛlɛneɛ, ɛleka biala mɔɔ menwɔnwu mogya la, mebapɛ nu, amaa saa melɛku Yigyibitima a meangu bɛ.

english_verse: Remember this day and celebrate it each year as a festival in my honor.
translation_verse: Kenle zɔhane bayɛ ngakyelɛ kenle amaa bɛ, na bɛbazie ye kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma Ɛvoyia kenle. Awolɛndoazo kɔsɔɔti bazie kenle ne na bɛali ɛvoyia ne.” Angye Ɛvoyia ne

english_verse: For seven days you must eat bread made without yeast. And on the first of these seven days, you must remove all yeast from your homes. If you eat anything made with yeast during this festival, you will no longer be part of Israel.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele kɛ, “Bɛbali kpanwo mɔɔ mgbɔvonle ɛnle nu la kenle nsuu. Kenle ne mɔɔ lumua la, bɛye mgbɔvonle biala bɛvi bɛ azua nu, ɔluakɛ ɔvi kenle ne mɔɔ lumua la toonwo mɔɔ kɔdwu kenle nsuu ne la, saa awie biala di debie mɔɔ mgbɔvonle wɔ nu la a, bɛbaye ye bɛavi Yizilayɛma anu.

english_verse: Meet together for worship on the first and seventh days of the festival. The only work you are allowed to do on either of these two days is that of preparing the bread.
translation_verse: Kenle ne mɔɔ lumua la, bɛyia na bɛzonle, yɛɛ kenle nsuu ne azo bɛyia na bɛzonle. Kenle nwiɔ zɔhane ɔnle kɛ bɛyɛ gyima, debie mɔɔ bɛdi la, yemɔ ala a ɔwɔ kɛ bɛyɛ a.

english_verse: Celebrate this Festival of Thin Bread as a way of remembering the day that I brought your families and tribes out of Egypt. And do this each year.
translation_verse: Ɔwɔ kɛ bɛdi Angye Ɛvoyia ne, ɔluakɛ kenle ɛhye anu yɛɛ menyele bɛ muala menvile Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo a. Yemɔti ɔwɔ kɛ bɛ awolɛndoazo kɔsɔɔti di ɛvoyia ɛhye.

english_verse: Begin on the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month by eating bread made without yeast. Then continue this celebration until the evening of the twenty-first day.
translation_verse: Siane ne mɔɔ lumua la anu kenle ne mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ bulu nee nna ne la nɔsolɛ nu toonwo mɔɔ kɔdwu kenle abulanwiɔ nee ko ne azo nɔsolɛ nu la, bɛbali kpanwo mɔɔ mgbɔvonle ɛnle nu la.

english_verse: Moses called the leaders of Israel together and said: Each family is to pick out a sheep and kill it for Passover.
translation_verse: Akee Mosisi vɛlɛle Yizilayɛ mgbanyima ne mɔ amuala na ɔhanle ɔhilele bɛ kɛ, “Awie biala ɛhɔhye boane ko ɛhu ye ɛmaa ye awuke nu amra ɛva ɛli Akpabɛnwo ne.

english_verse: Make a brush from a few small branches of a hyssop plant and dip the brush in the bowl that has the blood of the animal in it. Then brush some of the blood above the door and on the posts at each side of the door of your house. After this, everyone is to stay inside until morning.
translation_verse: Bɛva nyinlanyinla bɛbɔ boane mogya ne mɔɔ wɔ kyɛnze ne anu la anu, na bɛva bɛha bɛ felɛmo ne mɔ ati zo nee bɛ mbaka nwiɔ ne anwo, yɛɛ bɛ biala mmafinde toonwo nwonlomɔ.
