english_verse: During that night the Lord will go through the country of Egypt and kill the first-born son in every Egyptian family. He will see where you have put the blood, and he will not come into your house. His angel that brings death will pass over and not kill your first-born sons.
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma barapɛ nuhua yeahɔhu Yigyibitima. Saa ɔnwu mogya ne mɔɔ wɔ felɛmo ne anwo la a ɔbapɛ nuhua; ɔnrɛmaa sɛkyevolɛ ne ɛnrɛwolo bɛ azua nu ɛnrɛhu bɛ.

english_verse: After you have entered the country promised to you by the Lord, you and your children must continue to celebrate Passover each year.
translation_verse: Saa bɛdwu azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛva ɛbɔ bɛ ɛwɔkɛ la azo a, bɛyɛ ɛzonlenlɛ ɛhye.

translation_verse: Na kɛmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi nee Aalɔn la, zɔhane ala yɛɛ Yizilayɛma yɛle a. Belamunli mralɛ ewule

english_verse: At midnight the Lord killed the first-born son of every Egyptian family, from the son of the king to the son of every prisoner in jail. He also killed the first-born male of every animal that belonged to the Egyptians.
translation_verse: Alevinli mu nwiɔ avinli Ɛdɛnkɛma hunle belamunli mralɛ kɔsɔɔti mɔɔ wɔ Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo la, ɔvi belemgbunli ne mɔɔ de ebia ne azo la belamunli ralɛ ne anwo zo toonwo kɔdwu sonla mɔɔ la efiade la belamunli ralɛ ne anwo zo; ɔhunle nyɛmoa kɔsɔɔti amra mɔɔ lumua la.

english_verse: That night the king, his officials, and everyone else in Egypt got up and started crying bitterly. In every Egyptian home, someone was dead. The People of Israel Escape from Egypt
translation_verse: Na belemgbunli nee ye mgbanyima nee Yigyibitima amuala dwazole nɔe ne zunle yele awolɛ, ɔluakɛ awuke biala ɛnle ɛkɛ mɔɔ awie anwu nuhua a.

english_verse: During the night the king sent for Moses and Aaron and told them, “Get your people out of my country and leave us alone! Go and worship the Lord, as you have asked.
translation_verse: Na belemgbunli ne vɛlɛle Mosisi nee Aalɔn nɔe ne na ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛha bɛ nwo bɛhɔ, bɛdabɛ nee Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti, bɛvi me menli Yigyibitima avinli bɛhɔ; bɛhɔzonle Ɛdɛnkɛma, kɛmɔ bɛdabɛ bɛha la.

english_verse: Take your sheep, goats, and cattle, and get out. But ask your God to be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Bɛva bɛ nlankɛ nee bɛ nyɛmoa kɔsɔɔti bɛhɔ. Anrɛɛ bɛzɛlɛ bɛmaa medame noko.”

english_verse: The Egyptians did everything they could to get the Israelites to leave their country as quickly as possible. They said, “Please hurry and leave. If you don't, we will all be dead.”
translation_verse: Yigyibitima hanle Yizilayɛma nu kɛ bɛmaa bɛ nwo ɛyɛ ndɛ bɛvi maanle ne anu; ɔluakɛ bɛse, “Anrɛɛ yɛ kɔsɔɔti yɛyɛ avunli ala ɛne.”

english_verse: So the Israelites quickly made some bread dough and put it in pans. But they did not mix any yeast in the dough to make it rise. They wrapped cloth around the pans and carried them on their shoulders.
translation_verse: Yemɔti menli ne mɔ kyekyele bɛ ɛdɔkɛ ne mɔ mɔɔ mgbɔvonle ɛnle nu la nee bɛ ahyɛnze mɔɔ bɛfa bɛto kpanwo la wɔ ndanlɛ nu guale bɛ kɔme zo.

english_verse: The Israelites had already done what Moses had told them to do. They had gone to their Egyptian neighbors and asked for gold and silver and for clothes.
translation_verse: Ɛnee Yizilayɛma ɛyɛ mɔɔ Mosisi hanle hilele bɛ la. Bɛbizale Yigyibitima bɛliele dwɛtɛ fufule nee ezukoa nvutuke anwoneɛ nee ndanlɛ.

english_verse: The Lord had made the Egyptians friendly toward the people of Israel, and they gave them whatever they asked for. In this way they carried away the wealth of the Egyptians when they left Egypt.
translation_verse: Ɛnee Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛmaa Yizilayɛma anyunlu ɛra anyia wɔ Yigyibitima anyunlu, yemɔti debie biala mɔɔ bɛbizale la, Yigyibitima vale manle bɛ. Ɛhye manle bɛkpokpole Yigyibitima bɔkɔɔ. Yizilayɛma fi Yigyibiti

english_verse: The Israelites walked from the city of Rameses to the city of Succoth. There were about
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma vi Relamɛsizi maanzinli nu zile nu hɔle Sɛko. Bɛkɛyɛ menli apenle ngoko ɛya nsia, bɛandia mraalɛ nee ngakula bɛamboka nwolɛ.

english_verse: Many other people went with them as well, and there were also a lot of sheep, goats, and cattle.
translation_verse: Menli gyɛne gyɛne dɔɔnwo nee bɛ hɔle; bɛvale bɛ nlankɛ, mboane yɛɛ mbɔnkye noko bɛhɔle.

english_verse: They left Egypt in such a hurry that they did not have time to prepare any food except the bread dough made without yeast. So they baked it and made thin bread.
translation_verse: Bɛloale ɛdɔkɛ ne mɔɔ bɛanwula ye mgbɔvonle, mɔɔ bɛ nee ye vi Yigyibiti la tata. Bɛanwula ye mgbɔvonle, ɔluakɛ bɛdule bɛ arɛlevilɛ nu, bɛannyia adenle bɛanva aleɛ biala bɛanzia bɛ nwo.

english_verse: On that night the Lord kept watch for them, and on this same night each year Israel will always keep watch in honor of the Lord. Instructions for Passover
translation_verse: Kenle ko ne nɔe ne Ɛdɛnkɛma zinzale ye menli ne manle bɛvile Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo. Yemɔti wɔ bɛ awolɛndoazo muala anu, saa ɔdwu kenle zɔhane nɔɔzo a, Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti si epe ye Ɛdɛnkɛma ayɛlɛ. Akpabɛnwo ne anwo ngyehyɛlɛ

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following instructions for celebrating Passover: Only Israelites may eat the Passover meal.
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi nee Aalɔn kɛ, “Akpabɛnwo ne anwo ngyehyɛlɛ ɛne: Ɛyɛvolɛ biala ɛnli ye aleɛ ne bie,

english_verse: Your slaves may eat the meal if they have been circumcised,
translation_verse: noko kanranli biala mɔɔ bɛva ezukoa bɛdɔ ye la, saa bɛyɛ ye mrenyanu nzonlɛ a ɔdi aleɛ ne bie.

english_verse: but no foreigners who work for you are allowed to have any.
translation_verse: Adendulɛnli anzɛɛ ɛkpanli biala ɛnli aleɛ ne bie.

english_verse: The entire meal must be eaten inside, and no one may leave the house during the celebration. No bones of the Passover lamb may be broken.
translation_verse: Awuke ko mɔɔ bɛkɛdo aleɛ ne wɔ nu la, ɔwɔ kɛ bɛdi ɔ muala wɔ nu; ɔnle kɛ bɛfa bie bɛpɛ gua, yɛɛ bɛmmabɔ bowule biala anu.

english_verse: And all Israelites must take part in the meal.
translation_verse: Ɔwɔ kɛ Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti di ɛvoyia ne.

english_verse: If anyone who isn't an Israelite wants to celebrate Passover with you, every man and boy in that family must first be circumcised. Then they may join in the meal, just like native Israelites. No uncircumcised man or boy may eat the Passover meal!
translation_verse: Saa sonla gyɛne bie nee bɛ rale na ɔkulo kɛ ɔdi ɛvoyia ne bie a, ɔwɔ kɛ nrenya biala mɔɔ wɔ ye awuke nu ɛkɛ ne la yɛ ye mrenyanu nzonlɛ kolaa na yeabikye bɛ yeali ɛvoyia ne bie; ɛnee yeyɛ kɛ sonla mɔɔ vi maanle ne anu la. Awie biala mɔɔ bɛtɛyɛle ye mrenyanu nzonlɛ la, ɔnle kɛ ɔdi bie.

english_verse: This law applies both to native Israelites and to those foreigners who live among you.
translation_verse: Mɛla ko ne ala a wɔ ɛkɛ maa sonla mɔɔ vi maanle ne anu nee ɛyɛvolɛ mɔɔ nee bɛ rale la a.”

english_verse: The Israelites obeyed everything the Lord had commanded Moses and Aaron to tell them.
translation_verse: Ɛhye yɛɛ Yizilayɛma yɛle a; kɛmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi nee Aalɔn la, zɔhane ala a bɛyɛle a.

english_verse: And on that same day the Lord brought Israel's families and tribes out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Na kenle ko zɔhane, Ɛdɛnkɛma yele Yizilayɛma ɛwolaa ne vile Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ,

english_verse: “Dedicate to me the first-born son of every family and the first-born males of your flocks and herds. These belong to me.” The Festival of Thin Bread
translation_verse: “Tu belamunli mralɛ kɔsɔɔti maa me, sonla o, nane o, biala mɔɔ kɛlumua kɛkpakye awodeɛ wɔ Yizilayɛ maanle nu la le me ɛdeɛ.” Angye Ɛvoyia ne

english_verse: The Lord promised your ancestors that he would bring you into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites. It is a land rich with milk and honey. Each year during the month of Abib, celebrate these events in the following way:
translation_verse: Na saa Ɛdɛnkɛma fa bɛ dwu Keena mɔɔ le Hɛtema, Amɔlema, Haevaema, yɛɛ Gyibɛsema azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ ɔvale ɔbɔle bɛ ze mɔ ɛwɔkɛ, na ɔle azɛlɛ kɛnlɛma mɔɔ kye aleɛ la azo a, bɛli ɛvoyia ɛhye wɔ siane ɛhye anu.

english_verse: For seven days you are to eat bread made without yeast, and on the seventh day you are to celebrate a festival in honor of the Lord.
translation_verse: Bɛli kpanwo mɔɔ mgbɔvonle ɛnle nu la kenle nsuu, ye kenle nsuu ne azo bɛli ɛvoyia ne bɛwula Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlunyia.

english_verse: During those seven days, you must not eat anything made with yeast or even have yeast anywhere near your homes.
translation_verse: Bɛbali kpanwo mɔɔ mgbɔvonle ɛnle nu la kenle nsuu; ɔnle kɛ bɛnwu mgbɔvonle wɔ bɛ nwo wɔ maanle ye kɔsɔɔti anu.

english_verse: Then on the seventh day you must explain to your children that you do this because the Lord brought you out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Kenle ko ne bɛha bɛhile bɛ mra mrenya ne mɔ kɛ, ‘Debie mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛle manle me wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ menvile Yigyibiti la ati ɔ.’

english_verse: This celebration will be like wearing a sign on your hand or on your forehead, because then you will pass on to others the teaching of the Lord, whose mighty power brought you out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Na ɔbayɛ kɛ sɛkɛlɛneɛ mɔɔ wɔ bɛ sa anwo na yeayɛ kɛ ngakyedeɛ wɔ bɛ nwoma azo, amaa Ɛdɛnkɛma mɛla ne ala bɛ nloa, ɔluakɛ ɔlua tumi kpole zo, Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛye bɛ ɛvi Yigyibiti.

english_verse: Celebrate this festival each year at the same time.
translation_verse: Yemɔti bɛzie maamɛla ɛhye ɛvolɛ biala wɔ ye mekɛ ne anloa. Belamunli mralɛ

english_verse: The Lord will give you the land of the Canaanites, just as he promised you and your ancestors.
translation_verse: “Na saa Ɛdɛnkɛma fa bɛ dwu Keena azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ ɔvale ɔbɔle bɛ nee bɛ ze mɔ ɛwɔkɛ la azo, na ɔfa ɔmaa bɛ a,

english_verse: From then on, you must give him every first-born son from your families and every first-born male from your animals, because these belong to him.
translation_verse: debie biala mɔɔ kɛlumua kɛkpakye awodeɛ la bɛdu bɛzie ahane bɛmaa Ɛdɛnkɛma. Ɛnlankɛ biala ara nyinli mɔɔ lumua la le Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛdeɛ.

english_verse: You can spare the life of a first-born donkey by sacrificing a lamb; if you don't, you must break the donkey's neck. You must spare every first-born son.
translation_verse: Asoaso biala ara mɔɔ lumua la, bɛbava boane ralɛ bɛahakyi ye, na saa ɔ menle ɛngulo kɛ ɔkɛhakyi ye a ɛnee ɔwɔ kɛ bɛbu ɔ kɔme. Ɔwɔ kɛ bɛkpɔne belamunli ralɛ nrenya biala.

english_verse: In the future your children will ask what this ceremony means. Explain it to them by saying, “The Lord used his mighty power to rescue us from slavery in Egypt.
translation_verse: Saa kenle bie bɛ mra biza bɛ kɛ, ‘Ɛhye abo a le duzu?’ a, bɛha bɛhile bɛ kɛ, ‘Ɛdɛnkɛma vale tumi kpole a yele yɛ vile Yigyibiti wɔ akɛlɛzonlenlɛ nu a.

english_verse: The king stubbornly refused to set us free, so the Lord killed the first-born male of every animal and the first-born son of every Egyptian family. This is why we sacrifice to the Lord every first-born male of every animal and save every first-born son.”
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ mɔɔ Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne zile ye ahonle yɛle dapele na ɔdule ɔ gye kɛ ɔnrɛmaa yɛnrɛhɔ la, Ɛdɛnkɛma hunle belamunli mralɛ kɔsɔɔti mɔɔ wɔ Yigyibiti azɛlɛ ne azo la; ɔhunle menli belamunli mralɛ, ɔhunle nyɛmoa amra mɔɔ lumua. Yemɔti yɛfa belamunli ralɛ nrenya biala mɔɔ kɛkpakye awodeɛ la yɛbɔ azu yɛmaa Ɛdɛnkɛma, na yɛ mra mrenya belamunli mralɛ mrenya ne mɔ, yɛkpɔne bɛ.’

english_verse: This ceremony will serve the same purpose as a sign on your hand or on your forehead to tell how the Lord's mighty power rescued us from Egypt. The Lord Leads His People
translation_verse: Ɔbayɛ ngakyedeɛ nee sɛkɛlɛneɛ yeamaa bɛ wɔ bɛ sa anwo anzɛɛ bɛ nwoma azo; ɔluakɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma vale tumi kpole a yele yɛ vile Yigyibiti a.” Amungu mpila nee senle mpila ne

english_verse: After the king had finally let the people go, the Lord did not lead them through Philistine territory, though that was the shortest way. God had said, “If they are attacked, they may decide to return to Egypt.”
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne manle menli ne adenle kɛ bɛhɔ la, Nyamenle ammaa bɛampe Filisitiama azɛlɛ zo wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɛkɛ ne a le adenle sikalɛ la, ɔluakɛ Nyamenle hanle kɛ, “Saa menli ne mɔ dua ɛkɛ na bɛkɔtɔ konle nu a bɛkɛvu bɛ nwo na bɛkɛzia bɛkɛhɔ Yigyibiti bieko.”

english_verse: So he led them around through the desert and toward the Red Sea. The Israelites left Egypt, prepared for battle.
translation_verse: Na Nyamenle manle bɛbɔle fienemgbole ne mgbɔlɔka bɛvale Ndɔ Nyevile ne adenle zo. Yizilayɛma vile Yigyibiti wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɛnee bɛwie bɛ nwo boɔboa wɔ konle nu la.

english_verse: Moses had them take the bones of Joseph, whose dying words had been, “God will come to your rescue, and when he does, be sure to take my bones with you.”
translation_verse: Na Mosisi zale Dwosefi mbowule ne hɔle, ɔluakɛ ɛnee Dwosefi ɛha ndane ɛdo Yizilayɛma anwo na yeze bɛ kɛ, “Nyamenle baralie bɛ, na saa bɛlɛkɔ a bɛmmagyakyi me mbowule ne ɛke.”

english_verse: The people of Israel left Succoth and camped at Etham at the border of Egypt near the desert.
translation_verse: Na bɛvi Sɛko bɛdule bɛ bo bɛhɔyɛle azokoɛleɛ wɔ Yitam, wɔ fienemgbole ne anloa.

english_verse: At Etham the Lord said to Moses:
translation_verse: Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ,

english_verse: Tell the people of Israel to turn back and camp across from Pi-Hahiroth near Baal-Zephon, between Migdol and the Red Sea.
translation_verse: “Ka kile Yizilayɛma ne mɔ kɛ bɛzia bɛ nzi bɛhɔyɛ azokoɛleɛ wɔ Pae Hahaelo, wɔ Megedɔlo nee Ndɔ Nyevile ne avinli, mɔɔ bikye Beeyale Zifɔn la.

english_verse: The king will think you were afraid to cross the desert and that you are wandering around, trying to find another way to leave the country.
translation_verse: Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne baha kɛ, ‘Yizilayɛma ɛminli fienemgbole ne anu na bɛlɛdi ahyimango.’

english_verse: I will make the king stubborn again, and he will try to catch you. Then I will destroy him and his army. People everywhere will praise me for my victory, and the Egyptians will know that I really am the Lord. The Israelites obeyed the Lord and camped where he told them.
translation_verse: Mebamaa belemgbunli ne ahonle ayɛ se, na yeadoa bɛ, na meanyia anyunlunyia wɔ belemgbunli ne nee ye ɛlɔnema ne kɔsɔɔti anyunlu, amaa Yigyibitima anwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a.” Na Yizilayɛma yɛle mɔɔ bɛhanle bɛhilele bɛ la.

english_verse: When the king of Egypt heard that the Israelites had finally left, he and his officials changed their minds and said, “Look what we have done! We let them get away, and they will no longer be our slaves.”
translation_verse: Mɔɔ bɛbɔle Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne amaneɛ kɛ menli ne ɛnriandi ɛhɔ la, ɔ nee ye mgbanyima ne mɔ nyianle Yizilayɛma ne anwo adwenle ngakyile na bɛhanle kɛ, “Duzu a yɛyɛ la, kɛ yɛmaa Yizilayɛma ɛgyakyi yɛ ɛzonlenlɛ ɛhɔ a?”

english_verse: The king got his war chariot and army ready.
translation_verse: Yemɔti ɔvale ye konle ehwili ne nee ye ɛlɔnema ne;

english_verse: The Lord made the king so stubborn that he went after them, while the Israelites proudly went on their way.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma manle Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne ahonle yɛle se. Ɔbulule debie biala azo na ɔdoale Yizilayɛma wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɛnee bɛlua adenle nu konimlilɛ nu bɛlɛkɔ la.

english_verse: But the king's horses and chariots and soldiers caught up with them while they were camping by the Red Sea near Pi-Hahiroth and Baal-Zephon.
translation_verse: Yigyibitima, belemgbunli ne mgbɔnwɔ ne mɔ, ye konle ehwili ne mɔ, menli mɔɔ ka mgbɔnwɔ nee ɛlɔnema ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti belele zile Yizilayɛma zo na bɛhɔdole bɛ kɛ bɛzokoɛ Ndɔ Nyevile ne anloa, wɔ Pae Hahaelo nee Beeyale Zifɔn avinli.

english_verse: When the Israelites saw the king coming with his army, they were frightened and begged the Lord for help.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ belemgbunli ne kpumgbunle bɛ na Yizilayɛma manle bɛ nye zo nwunle kɛ Yigyibitima ɛlɛba bɛ nwo zo la, ɛzulolɛ hanle bɛ. Yizilayɛma zunle vɛlɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma,

english_verse: They also complained to Moses, “Wasn't there enough room in Egypt to bury us? Is that why you brought us out here to die in the desert? Why did you bring us out of Egypt anyway?
translation_verse: na bɛhanle bɛhilele Mosisi kɛ, “Anzɛɛ azie biala ɛnle Yigyibiti mɔɔ yemɔti wɔva yɛ wɔra ɛmaa yɛarawu yɛagua fienemgbole ye anu a? Wɔye yɛ wɔvi Yigyibiti la, se wɔnwu ɛbɛla mɔɔ wɔbɔ la?

english_verse: While we were there, didn't we tell you to leave us alone? We'd rather be slaves in Egypt than die in this desert!”
translation_verse: Anzɛɛ yɛanze wɔ kɛ, ‘Gyakyi yɛ koonwu maa yɛzonle Yigyibitima ɔ?’ Ɔluakɛ ɔle kpalɛ kɛ anrɛɛ ɛnee yɛkɛzonle Yigyibitima tɛla kɛ yɛkɛwu yɛkɛgua fienemgbole ye anu.”

english_verse: But Moses answered, “Don't be afraid! Be brave, and you will see the Lord save you today. These Egyptians will never bother you again.
translation_verse: Na Mosisi zele menli ne kɛ, “Bɛmmasulo, bɛgyinla kpundii na bɛnlea kɛ ɛnɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma bazi alie bɛ la. Ɔluakɛ Yigyibitima mɔɔ bɛnwu bɛ ɛnɛ la, bɛnrɛnwu bɛ bieko ɛlɛ.

english_verse: The Lord will fight for you, and you won't have to do a thing.”
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma baho amaa bɛ; bɛmɛ, bɛzie bɛ nwo diinyi.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Why do you keep calling out to me for help? Tell the Israelites to move forward.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Duzu ati a bɛlɛsu bɛavɛlɛ me a? Ka kile Yizilayɛma kɛ bɛhɔ bɛ nyunlu.

english_verse: Then hold your walking stick over the sea. The water will open up and make a road where they can walk through on dry ground.
translation_verse: Maa wɔ kpɔma ne zo; tende ɛ sa nyevile ne anu maa nuhua ɛhyɛ nwiɔ ɛmaa Yizilayɛma ɛlua azɛlɛ resee zo ɛpɛ.

english_verse: I will make the Egyptians so stubborn that they will go after you. Then I will be praised because of what happens to the king and his chariots and cavalry.
translation_verse: Mebamaa Yigyibitima ahonle ayɛ se, bɛbadoa bɛ na ɛhye bamaa meali konim meanyia me nyunlu wɔ Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne nee ye ɛlɔnema, ye konle ehwili ne mɔ, nee ye konlema mɔɔ ka mgbɔnwɔ la ɛkɛ.

english_verse: All this time God's angel had gone ahead of Israel's army, but now he moved behind them. A large cloud had also gone ahead of them,
translation_verse: Akee Nyamenle soanvolɛ ne mɔɔ li Yizilayɛma pemgbenleamgbe ne anyunlu la zenle lile bɛ nzi. Amungu mpila ne mɔɔ li bɛ nyunlu la zenle ralile bɛ nzi,

english_verse: but now it moved between the Egyptians and the Israelites. The cloud gave light to the Israelites, but made it dark for the Egyptians, and during the night they could not come any closer.
translation_verse: na ɔragyinlanle Yigyibitima nee Yizilayɛma avinli. Amungu ne yele awozinli kabikabi manle Yigyibitima, na wienyi dale Yizilayɛma anyunlu. Yemɔti nɔe ne, ɛlɔnema ekpunli nwiɔ ne ambikye nwolɛ fee.

english_verse: Moses stretched his arm over the sea, and the Lord sent a strong east wind that blew all night until there was dry land where the water had been. The sea opened up,
translation_verse: Akee Mosisi dendenle ɔ sa nyevile ne anu, na Ɛdɛnkɛma manle aduduleɛ anwoma anu ɛsesebɛ bie bɔle nɔe ne amuala, na ɔhyɛle nyevile ne anu ɔyele azɛlɛ resee ɔdole nyevile ne avinli.

english_verse: and the Israelites walked through on dry land with a wall of water on each side.
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma luale nyevile ne anu azɛlɛ resee ne azo; nyevile ne dwazole bolonwonwo wɔ foa ko nee foa ko yɛle kɛ bane wɔ bɛ fema zo nee bɛ bɛne zo.

english_verse: But before daylight the Lord looked down at the Egyptian army from the fiery cloud and made them panic.
translation_verse: Aleɛbahye ne Ɛdɛnkɛma luale amungu nee senle mpila ne anu nleanle Yigyibitima na Yigyibiti ɛlɔnema ne anye zo danle bɛ.

english_verse: Their chariot wheels got stuck, and it was hard for them to move. So the Egyptians said to one another, “Let's leave these people alone! The Lord is on their side and is fighting against us.”
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma manle bɛ konle ehwili ne mɔ agyakɛ miminle mɔɔ bɛtwe bɛ nwo fee a ɔnyɛ boɛ a. Na Yigyibitima hanle kɛ, “Bɛmaa yɛnriandi yɛvi Yizilayɛma anyunlu, ɔluakɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛlɛko atia yɛ amaa bɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses, “Stretch your arm toward the sea—the water will cover the Egyptians and their cavalry and chariots.”
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Tende ɛ sa nyevile ne anu maa nyevile ne ɛha ɛbɔ nu ɛva Yigyibitima, bɛ konle ehwili ne mɔ, nee menli mɔɔ ka mgbɔnwɔ ne mɔ la anwo zo.”

english_verse: Moses stretched out his arm, and at daybreak the water rushed toward the Egyptians. They tried to run away, but the Lord drowned them in the sea.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Mosisi dendenle ɔ sa nyevile ne anu, na nwonlomɔ ne, nyevile ne yile rale ɔ bo zo ne. Yigyibitima bɔle mɔdenle kɛ bɛnriandi, na Ɛdɛnkɛma hanle bɛ guale nyevile ne anu.

english_verse: The water came and covered the chariots, the cavalry, and the whole Egyptian army that had followed the Israelites into the sea. Not one of them was left alive.
translation_verse: Nyevile ne yile bɔle nu monlanle konle ehwili ne mɔ, menli mɔɔ ka mgbɔnwɔ ne mɔ, nee Yigyibitima pemgbenleamgbe ne mɔɔ ɛlɛfoa Yizilayɛma la; bɛ nuhua ko bɔbɔ anga.

english_verse: But the sea had made a wall of water on each side of the Israelites, so they walked through on dry land.
translation_verse: Nyevile ne dwazole bolonwonwo yɛle bane wɔ Yizilayɛma fema zo nee bɛ bɛne zo, na bɛluale azɛlɛ resee zo bɛpɛle nyevile ne.

english_verse: On that day, when the Israelites saw the bodies of the Egyptians washed up on the shore, they knew that the Lord had saved them.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma liele Yizilayɛma kenle ko ne vile Yigyibitima asa anu. Na Yizilayɛma nwunle Yigyibitima avunli ne mɔ wɔ nyevile ne anloa.

english_verse: Because of the mighty power he had used against the Egyptians, the Israelites worshiped him and trusted him and his servant Moses.
translation_verse: Eza Yizilayɛma nwunle gyima kpole mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma lile tiale Yigyibitima la. Menli ne zulole Ɛdɛnkɛma na bɛliele Ɛdɛnkɛma nee ye sonvolɛ Mosisi bɛlile.

english_verse: Moses and the Israelites sang this song in praise of the Lord: I sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.
translation_verse: Akee Mosisi nee Yizilayɛma dole edwɛne ɛhye yeyɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma: “Mebado edwɛne meayeyɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, ɔluakɛ yeli konim anyunlunyia nu; ɛkpɔnwɔ nee ye kavolɛ ne, yevuandi bɛ yegua nyevile nu.

english_verse: The Lord is my strength, the reason for my song, because he has saved me. I praise and honor the Lord— he is my God and the God of my ancestors.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma le me anwosesebɛ nee me edwɛne, yɛɛ yeyɛ me ngoanedievolɛ. Me Nyamenle ne ɛne, mebaye ye ayɛlɛ, me ze Nyamenle ne, mebayeyɛ ye.

english_verse: The Lord is his name, and he is a warrior!
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma le ɛlɔnenli; ye duma a le Ɛdɛnkɛma.

english_verse: He threw the chariots and army of Egypt's king into the Red Sea, and he drowned the best of the king's officers.
translation_verse: “Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne konle ehwili nee ye ɛlɔnema, yevuandi bɛ yegua nyevile nu; ye safohyenlema kpalɛ ne, Ndɔ Nyevile ne ɛva bɛ.

english_verse: They sank to the bottom just like stones.
translation_verse: Azuyilɛ ne ɛheda bɛ nwo zo; bɛnlomanle azule bo kɛ bolɛ.

english_verse: With the tremendous force of your right arm, our Lord, you crushed your enemies.
translation_verse: “O Ɛdɛnkɛma, ɛ sa fema le tumi kpole; O Ɛdɛnkɛma, ɛ sa fema bubu kpɔvolɛ.

english_verse: What a great victory was yours, when you defeated everyone who opposed you. Your fiery anger wiped them out, as though they were straw.
translation_verse: Wɔ wɔ konimlilɛ kpole nu, ɛfuandi wɔ kpɔvolɛma ɛgua; ɛmaa wɔ ɛya dwu aze, yela bɛ kɛ ndile.

english_verse: You were so furious that the sea piled up like a wall, and the ocean depths curdled like cheese.
translation_verse: Wɔ ɛnwomenle ko pɛ manle nyevile ne dwazole bolonwonwo, azuyilɛ ne hɔle anwuma yɛle kɛ bane; azule buma ne bɔle kunguma.

english_verse: Your enemies boasted that they would pursue and capture us, divide up our possessions, treat us as they wished, then take out their swords and kill us right there.
translation_verse: Kpɔvolɛ ne hanle kɛ, ‘Meti bɛ, mekye bɛ; mekyɛ bɛ nwo ninyɛne, meadu me ahunlundwolɛ ɛdeɛ; metwe me dadeɛ ne, meabɔ bɛ bo zo.’

english_verse: But when you got furious, they sank like lead, swallowed by ocean waves.
translation_verse: Ɛmanle anwoma dule, nyevile ne monlanle bɛ; bɛnlomanle kɛ sumi wɔ azubuma ne anu.

english_verse: Our Lord, no other gods compare with you— Majestic and holy! Fearsome and glorious! Miracle worker!
translation_verse: “O Ɛdɛnkɛma, nwane a le kɛ ɛdawɔ wɔ awozonle avinli a? Nwane a le kɛ wɔmɔ, mɔɔ le kpole wɔ nwuanzanwuanzayɛlɛ nu, ye ayɛlɛyelɛ le kpole na ɔyɛ nwanwane ninyɛne a?

english_verse: When you signaled with your right hand, your enemies were swallowed deep into the earth.
translation_verse: Ɛmanle ɛ sa fema zo, na azɛlɛ menle bɛ.

english_verse: The people you rescued were led by your powerful love to your holy place.
translation_verse: Wɔ anwunvɔnezelɛ ne ati, wɔli menli mɔɔ wɔlie bɛ ngoane la ati; wɔva wɔ tumi ne wɔzinza bɛ ɛ nee bɛ ɛra wɔ ɛleka nwuanzanwuanza ne.

english_verse: Nations learned of this and trembled— Philistines shook with horror.
translation_verse: Maanle maanle ɛde, bɛsulo; ɛzulolɛ ɛha Filisitiama.

english_verse: The leaders of Edom and of Moab were terrified. Everyone in Canaan fainted,
translation_verse: Akee Yidɔm arelemgbunli ahonle ɛdu; Mowabe katakyiema anwo ɛlɛwozo bɛ; Keena maanlema amuala ɛnwenwe.

english_verse: struck down by fear. Our Lord, your powerful arm kept them still as a rock until the people you rescued to be your very own had marched by.
translation_verse: Ɛzulolɛ nee ahunlundetelɛ tɔ bɛ nwo; wɔ tumi ne kpole ti, bɛnga bɛ nwo fee, bɛyɛle kɛ awolɛ kɔkpula kɛ, O Ɛdɛnkɛma, wɔ menli ne mɔɔ wɔkpɔne bɛ la ɛpɛ nu.

english_verse: You will let your people settle on your own mountain, where you chose to live and to be worshiped.
translation_verse: O Ɛdɛnkɛma, ɛbava bɛ wɔara, na wɔalua bɛ wɔ wɔ boka ne azo, ɛleka mɔɔ wɔziezie kɛ ɛbadɛnla, wɔ wɔ Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne mɔɔ ɛdawɔ wɔzi la anu.

english_verse: Our Lord, you will rule forever! The Song of Miriam
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma bali belemgbunli wɔ melɛ mɔɔ ɛnlɛ awieleɛ.” Meleam edwɛne ne

english_verse: The Lord covered the royal Egyptian cavalry and chariots with the sea, after the Israelites had walked safely through on dry ground.
translation_verse: Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne mgbɔnwɔ, ye konle ehwili ne mɔ, nee ye menli mɔɔ ka mgbɔnwɔ la hɔle nyevile ne anu la, Ɛdɛnkɛma manle nyevile ne hedale bɛ nwo zo; na Yizilayɛma ne mɔ luale nyevile ne anu azɛlɛ resee zo hɔle.

english_verse: Miriam the sister of Aaron was a prophet. So she took her tambourine and led the other women out to play their tambourines and to dance.
translation_verse: Na Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ raalɛ Meleam, Aalɔn adiema raalɛ ne vale akɛya, na mraalɛ ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti doale ye, wozole akɛya, zile agole.

english_verse: Then she sang to them: “Sing praises to the Lord for his great victory! He has thrown the horses and their riders into the sea.” Bitter Water at Marah
translation_verse: Meleam dole edwɛne manle bɛ kɛ: “Bɛdo edwɛne bɛyeyɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, ɔluakɛ yeli konim anyunlunyia nu; ɛkpɔnwɔ nee ye kavolɛ ne, yevuandi bɛ yegua nyevile nu.” Nzule ɛnwonle ne

english_verse: After the Israelites left the Red Sea, Moses led them through the Shur Desert for three days, before finding water.
translation_verse: Akee Mosisi lile Yizilayɛma ati ɔ nee bɛ vi Ndɔ Nyevile ne anloa hɔle Hyɔɔ fienemgbole ne anu. Bɛdiale toonwo kenle nsa, na bɛannwu nzule nwo.

english_verse: They did find water at Marah, but it was bitter, which is how that place got its name.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ bɛradwule Mɛɛla la, bɛangola ɛkɛ ne nzule no, ɔboalekɛ nzule ne yɛ ɛnwonle; yemɔti bɛvɛlɛle ye Mɛɛla.

english_verse: The people complained and said, “Moses, what are we going to drink?”
translation_verse: Na menli ne dendɛle bɛ nzo abo tiale Mosisi zele kɛ, “Duzu a yɛno a?”

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord for help, and the Lord told him to throw a certain piece of wood into the water. Moses did so, and the water became fit to drink. At Marah the Lord tested his people and also gave them some laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Mosisi zɛlɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma, na Ɛdɛnkɛma hilele ye baka bie, ɔvuandinle baka ne ɔdole nzule ne anu, na nzule ne yɛle nzukpa. Ɛdɛnkɛma manle bɛ mɛla nee ngyehyɛlɛ na ɔzɔle bɛ ɔnleanle.

english_verse: Then he said, “I am the Lord your God, and I cure your diseases. If you obey me by doing right and by following my laws and teachings, I won't punish you with the diseases I sent on the Egyptians.”
translation_verse: Ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Saa bɛtie medame Ɛdɛnkɛma, bɛ Nyamenle ne me ne, bɛyɛ debie mɔɔ sɔ me nye, bɛdi me mɛla nee me ngyehyɛlɛ ne mɔ azo a, ewule ngakyile mɔɔ memanle ɔrale Yigyibitima anwo zo la, menrɛmaa bie ɛnrɛra bɛ nwo zo; ɔluakɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma mɔɔ metondo bɛ ewule a.”

english_verse: Later the Israelites came to Elim, where there were twelve springs and
translation_verse: Akee bɛrale Yilem, nzufeanvea bula bulu nee nwiɔ nee mrɛlɛ abulasuu wɔ ɛkɛ, na bɛyɛle azokoɛleɛ wɔ nzule ne mɔ anloa.

english_verse: On the fifteenth day of the second month after the Israelites had escaped from Egypt, they left Elim and started through the western edge of the Sinai Desert in the direction of Mount Sinai.
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti vi Yilem rale fienemgbole ne mɔɔ wɔ Yilem nee Saenae avinli la anu. Bɛdule bɛ bo wɔ Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo la, ye siane mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nwiɔ, ye kenle bulu nee nnu ne azo yɛɛ bɛdwule ɛkɛ ne a.

english_verse: There in the desert they started complaining to Moses and Aaron,
translation_verse: Na Yizilayɛma amuala dendɛle bɛ nzo abo tiale Mosisi nee Aalɔn wɔ fienemgbole ne anu.

english_verse: “We wish the Lord had killed us in Egypt. When we lived there, we could at least sit down and eat all the bread and meat we wanted. But you have brought us out here into this desert, where we are going to starve.”
translation_verse: Bɛzele Mosisi nee Aalɔn kɛ, “Ɔle kpalɛ kɛ anrɛɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma hunle yɛ wɔ Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo. Ɛkɛ ne, yɛdɛnlanle aze yɛlile nane nee aleɛ yɛ ko yile tɛkɛɛ. Bɛva yɛ bɛragua fienemgbole ye anu bɛmaa ɛhɔne ahu menli pemgbenleamgbe ɛhye.”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “I will send bread down from heaven like rain. Tell the people to go out each day and gather only enough for that day. That's how I will see if they obey me.
translation_verse: Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Nea, mebamaa aleɛ vi anwuma adɔ kɛ ezule. Kenle ko biala menli ne bahɔsesa mɔɔ sa bɛ di kenle ko la ala, amaa meazɔ bɛ meanlea saa bɛkɛli me mɛla ne azo anzɛɛ bɛnrɛli zolɛ.

english_verse: But on the sixth day of each week they must gather and cook twice as much.”
translation_verse: Kenle nsia ne azo, bɛva kenle ko aleɛ ne fane nwiɔ na bɛrado.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron told the people, “This evening you will know that the Lord was the one who rescued you from Egypt.
translation_verse: Na Mosisi nee Aalɔn hanle hilele menli ne kɔsɔɔti kɛ, “Nɔsolɛ nu bɛbanwu kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma a yele bɛ vile Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo a.

english_verse: And in the morning you will see his glorious power, because he has heard your complaints against him. Why should you grumble to us? Who are we?”
translation_verse: Na ye nwonlomɔ nu, bɛbanwu Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlunyia ne, ɔboalekɛ yede bɛ ɛdendɛlɛ mɔɔ bɛdendɛ bɛtia ye la. Ɔluakɛ yɛmɛ, yɛle duzu mɔɔ yemɔti ɔwɔ kɛ bɛtendɛ bɛtia yɛ a?”

english_verse: Then Moses continued, “You will know it is the Lord when he gives you meat each evening and more than enough bread each morning. He is really the one you are complaining about, not us—we are nobodies—but the Lord has heard your complaints.”
translation_verse: Na Mosisi hanle kɛ, “Nɔsolɛ nu Ɛdɛnkɛma bamaa bɛ nane bɛali na nwonlomɔ nu yeamaa bɛ kpanwo bɛali bɛ ko ayi, ɔboalekɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛde bɛ ɛdendɛlɛ mɔɔ bɛtendɛ bɛtia ye la, na yɛmɛ, yɛle duzu? Tɛ yɛmɛ yɛɛ bɛtendɛ bɛatia yɛ a, bɛtendɛ bɛtia Ɛdɛnkɛma.”

english_verse: Moses turned to Aaron and said, “Bring the people together, because the Lord has heard their complaints.”
translation_verse: Na Mosisi hanle hilele Aalɔn kɛ, “Ka kile Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti kɛ bɛrɛla Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlu ɛke, ɔluakɛ yede ɛdendɛlɛ mɔɔ bɛlɛtendɛ bɛatia ye la.”

english_verse: Aaron was speaking to them, when everyone looked out toward the desert and saw the bright glory of the Lord in a cloud.
translation_verse: Na mɔɔ Aalɔn dendɛle hilele Yizilayɛma ne la, bɛdole bɛ nye fienemgbole ne anu lɔ, na nea, Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlunyia ne dale amungu ne anu.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ,

english_verse: “I have heard my people complain. Now tell them that each evening they will have meat and each morning they will have more than enough bread. Then they will know that I am the Lord their God.”
translation_verse: “Mede Yizilayɛma ɛdendɛlɛ mɔɔ bɛtendɛ bɛtia me la; ka kile bɛ kɛ: Nɔsolɛ nu bɛbali nane na nwonlomɔ bɛali kpanwo; akee bɛbanwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne a.”

english_verse: That evening a lot of quails came and landed everywhere in the camp, and the next morning dew covered the ground.
translation_verse: Ɔdwule nɔsolɛ nu la nloma kyelɛwele kpolane ravale azokoɛleɛ ne, na ye nwonlomɔ ne ɛbɔlɛ dɔle azokoɛleɛ ne ɛleka biala.

english_verse: After the dew had gone, the desert was covered with thin flakes that looked like frost.
translation_verse: Na mɔɔ ɛbɔlɛ ne wele la, bɛnwunle kɛ debie ahunguma ngyikyi nwonwohyee kɛ ɛbɔndwoba la dɔɔnwo gua ndile ne azo wɔ fienemgbole ne anu.

english_verse: The people had never seen anything like this, and they started asking each other, “What is it?” Moses answered, “This is the bread that the Lord has given you to eat.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Yizilayɛma ne nwunle ye la, bɛbizebizale bɛ nwo ngoko kɛ, “Duzu debie ɛ?” Ɔluakɛ ɛnee bɛnze ye deɛ holɛ. Na Mosisi zele bɛ kɛ, “Ɔle kpanwo mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛva ɛmaa bɛ kɛ bɛli a.

english_verse: And he orders you to gather about two liters for each person in your family—that should be more than enough.”
translation_verse: Na mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛha ye wɔ nwolɛ la ɛne: ‘Awie biala ɛsesa dɔɔnwo biala mɔɔ kɛza ye di la, menli mɔɔ wɔ ye awuke ne anu la, ko biala ɛdeɛ litili nwiɔ.’ ”

english_verse: They did as they were told. Some gathered more and some gathered less.
translation_verse: Na Yizilayɛma ne yɛle ye zɔhane, bie mɔ sesale dɔɔnwo, bie mɔ noko sesale ekyi.

english_verse: Moses told them not to keep any overnight.
translation_verse: Na Mosisi hanle hilele bɛ kɛ, “Awie biala mmafa bie sie ɔmaa aleɛ kye zolɛ.”

english_verse: Some of them disobeyed, but the next morning what they kept was stinking and full of worms, and Moses was angry.
translation_verse: Noko bɛandie Mosisi, bie mɔ gyakyile bie manle aleɛ hyenle zolɛ, na bɛlɔle azonlɛ, bɛbɔnle nvoanvoa, na Mosisi vale bɛ nwo ɛya kpole.

english_verse: Each morning everyone gathered as much as they needed, and in the heat of the day the rest melted.
translation_verse: Nwonlomɔ biala bɛsesale bie. Awie biala sesale mɔɔ kɛza ye di la, yɛɛ kɛ ewia ne fi la ɛnee yeholo.

english_verse: However, on the sixth day of the week, everyone gathered enough to have four liters, instead of two. When the leaders reported this to Moses,
translation_verse: Kenle nsia ne azo bɛsesale kpanwo ne mɔnwo, sonla ko biala ɛdeɛ litili nna. Na mɔɔ mgbanyima ne mɔ rahanle hilele Mosisi la,

english_verse: he told them that the Lord had said, “Tomorrow is the Sabbath, a sacred day of rest in honor of me. So gather all you want to bake or boil, and make sure you save enough for tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Mosisi zele bɛ kɛ, “Kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma se la ɛne: ‘Ɛhyema le ɛnwomenlelielɛ kenle nwuanzanwuanza maa Ɛdɛnkɛma; bɛdondo mɔɔ bɛtondo la na bɛdo mɔɔ bɛto bɛali la. Biala mɔɔ kɛha la bɛva bɛzie ɛhyema.’ ”

english_verse: The people obeyed, and the next morning the food smelled fine and had no worms.
translation_verse: Na kɛmɔ Mosisi hanle hilele bɛ la, bɛvale bie bɛziele bɛmanle aleɛ hyenle; yeambɔ nvinli yɛɛ yeanlɔ azonlɛ.

english_verse: “You may eat the food,” Moses said. “Today is the Sabbath in honor of the Lord, and there won't be any of this food on the ground today.
translation_verse: Mosisi zele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛli ɛhye ɛnɛ, ɔboalekɛ ɛnɛ le Ɛdɛnkɛma Ɛnwomenlelielɛ Kenle. Bɛnrɛnyia aleɛ biala wɔ ɛleka biala.

english_verse: You will find it there for the first six days of the week, but not on the Sabbath.”
translation_verse: Bɛsesa aleɛ kenle nsia. Kenle nsuu ne le Ɛnwomenlelielɛ Kenle, yemɔti bɛnrɛnyia aleɛ biala.”

english_verse: A few of the Israelites did go out to look for some, but there was none.
translation_verse: Na kenle nsuu ne azo menli ne bie mɔ hɔle kɛ bɛkasesa aleɛ, na bɛannyia bie.

english_verse: Then the Lord said, “Moses, how long will you people keep disobeying my laws and teachings?
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Kenlenzu yɛɛ bɛkɛkpo kɛ bɛnrɛli me mɛla ne mɔ azo a?

english_verse: Remember that I was the one who gave you the Sabbath. That's why on the sixth day I provide enough bread for two days. Everyone is to stay home and rest on the Sabbath.”
translation_verse: Bɛnlea! Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛmaa bɛ ɛnwomenlelielɛ kenle, yemɔti kenle nsia ne azo ɔmaa bɛ kenle nwiɔ aleɛ, zɔhane ati kenle nsuu ne azo, awie biala ɛdɛnla ye sua nu; yɛɛ awie biala mmatu ɔ gyakɛ.”

english_verse: And so they rested on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Yemɔti menli ne liele bɛ ɛnwomenle kenle nsuu ne.

english_verse: The Israelites called the bread manna. It was white like coriander seed and delicious as wafers made with honey.
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma ne vɛlɛle aleɛ ne mana. Ɔle kɛ ma fufule ekyi bie, yɛɛ ye fɛlɛko le kɛ belɛde mɔɔ bɛva wolɛ bɛyɛ la.

english_verse: Moses told the people that the Lord had said, “Store up two liters of this manna, because I want future generations to see the food I gave you during the time you were in the desert after I rescued you from Egypt.”
translation_verse: Na Mosisi hanle kɛ, “Kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma se la ɛne! ‘Bɛva mana ne litili nwiɔ bɛzie, amaa bɛ awolɛndoazo ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti anwu aleɛ ne mɔɔ menvale menlile bɛ adane wɔ fienemgbole ne anu wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ menyele bɛ menvile Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo la.’ ”

english_verse: Then Moses told Aaron, “Put some manna in a jar and store it in the place of worship for future generations to see.”
translation_verse: Na Mosisi hanle hilele Aalɔn kɛ, “Fa dwora, na fa mana litili nwiɔ gua nu na sie ye Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlu ɛkɛ maa wɔ awolɛndoazo kɔsɔɔti.”

english_verse: Aaron followed the Lord's instructions and put the manna in front of the sacred chest for safekeeping.
translation_verse: Na kɛmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi la, Aalɔn vale ziele Ɛdɛnkɛma Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne anyunlu.

english_verse: The Israelites left the desert and moved from one place to another each time the Lord ordered them to. Once they camped at Rephidim, but there was no water for them to drink.
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti vile fienemgbole ne anu zɔle bɛ adendulɛ ne azo ngyikyi ngyikyi, kɛmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ngyehyɛlɛ ne se la, na bɛyɛle azokoɛleɛ wɔ Relɛfedem, na ɛnee nzule mɔɔ bɛno la ɛnle ɛkɛ.

english_verse: The people started complaining to Moses, “Give us some water!” Moses replied, “Why are you complaining to me and trying to put the Lord to the test?”
translation_verse: Yemɔti menli ne hɔle Mosisi anwo zo na bɛzele ye kɛ, “Maa yɛ nzule yɛnlo.” Na Mosisi hanle hilele bɛ kɛ, “Duzu ati a bɛra me nwo zo bɛbabɔ me somolɛ a? Duzu ati a bɛlɛsɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛanlea a?”

english_verse: But the people were thirsty and kept on complaining, “Moses, did you bring us out of Egypt just to let us and our families and our animals die of thirst?”
translation_verse: Nzuhɔne hunle menli ne na bɛdendɛle bɛtiale Mosisi, bɛhanle kɛ, “Duzu ati a ɛvale yɛ ɛvile Yigyibiti, kɛ ɛ nee yɛ ba wɔamaa nzuhɔne ahu yɛ, ahu yɛ mra nee yɛ nlankɛ ɛ?”

english_verse: Then Moses prayed to the Lord, “What am I going to do with these people? They are about to stone me to death!”
translation_verse: Na Mosisi zunle zɛlɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ, “Menli ɛhye mɔ, kɛ menyɛ bɛ ɛ? Asɛɛ bɛzi me awolɛ bɛwie.”

english_verse: The Lord answered, “Take some of the leaders with you and go ahead of the rest of the people. Also take along the walking stick with which you struck the Nile River.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Fa Yizilayɛ mgbanyima ne mɔ bie na ɛ nee bɛ ɛze ɛli menli ne anyunlu. Fa kpɔma ne mɔɔ ɛvale ɛbɔle Azule Naele ne anu la kɔ.

english_verse: When you get to the rock at Mount Sinai, I will be there with you. Strike the rock with the stick, and water will pour out for the people to drink.” Moses did this while the leaders watched.
translation_verse: Nea, mebagyinla bodane bie azo wɔ ɛ nyunlu wɔ Saenae Boka; ɛbava wɔ kpɔma ne wɔabɔ bolɛ ne, na nzule vi nu bara, amaa menli ne anyia bie anlo.” Na Mosisi yɛle ye zɔhane wɔ Yizilayɛ mgbanyima ne mɔ anyunlu.

english_verse: The people had complained and tested the Lord by asking, “Is the Lord really with us?” So Moses named that place Massah, which means “testing” and Meribah, which means “complaining.” Israel Defeats the Amalekites
translation_verse: Na ɔvɛlɛle ɛleka zɔhane Masa nee Mɛleba ɔboalekɛ Yizilayɛma ne mɔ bɔle tokule zɔle Ɛdɛnkɛma nleanle, na bɛhanle kɛ, “Asoo Ɛdɛnkɛma wɔ yɛ avinli anzɛɛ ɔnle yɛ avinli?” Bɛ nee Amalɛkema konle ne

english_verse: When the Israelites were at Rephidim, they were attacked by the Amalekites.
translation_verse: Amalɛkema nee Yizilayɛma hɔhonle wɔ Relɛfedem.

english_verse: So Moses told Joshua, “Have some men ready to attack the Amalekites tomorrow. I will stand on a hilltop, holding this walking stick that has the power of God.”
translation_verse: Na Mosisi hanle hilele Dwɔhyua kɛ, “Ye menli, ɛ nee bɛ nee Amalɛkema ɛhɔho. Ɛhyema mebalɛ Nyamenle kpɔma ne me sa nu meahɔgyinla boka ne azo.”

english_verse: Joshua led the attack as Moses had commanded, while Moses, Aaron, and Hur stood on the hilltop.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Dwɔhyua yɛle mɔɔ Mosisi hanle hilele ye la na ɔ nee Amalɛkema hɔhonle. Na Mosisi, Aalɔn, yɛɛ Hɛɛle hɔle boka ne azo.

english_verse: The Israelites out-fought the Amalekites as long as Moses held up his arms, but they started losing whenever he lowered them.
translation_verse: Na mekɛ biala mɔɔ Mosisi kɛmaa ɔ sa zo la, ɛnee Yizilayɛma asa ɛla Amalɛkema anwo zo; saa ɔgua ɔ sa aze a, ɛnee Amalɛkema asa ɛla Yizilayɛma anwo zo.

english_verse: After a while, his arms were so tired that Aaron and Hur got a rock for him to sit on. Then they stood beside him and supported his arms in the same position until sunset.
translation_verse: Na Mosisi asa akee bule, yemɔti bɛvale bolɛ bɛdole ɛkɛ bɛmanle ɔdɛnlanle zolɛ. Akee Aalɔn nee Hɛɛle sosɔle ɔ sa, ko lɛ fema ne yɛɛ ko lɛ bɛne ne. Yemɔti yeanga ɔ sa aze toonwo sɛnzɛne ne dɔle.

english_verse: That's how Joshua defeated the Amalekites.
translation_verse: Na Dwɔhyua vale ye konle dadeɛ ne biale Amalɛkema takaa.

english_verse: Afterwards, the Lord said to Moses, “Write an account of this victory and read it to Joshua. I want the Amalekites to be forgotten forever.”
translation_verse: Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Kɛlɛ ɛhye wɔ buluku nu maa ɔyɛ ngakyelɛ na kenga kile Dwɔhyua kɛ: Mebanunu Amalɛkema abo zo bɔkɔɔ wɔ aleɛabo.”

english_verse: Moses built an altar and named it “The Lord Gives Me Victory.”
translation_verse: Na Mosisi zile azukponle, na ɔdonle ye “Ɛdɛnkɛma le me Fɛlɛnra.”

english_verse: Then Moses explained, “This is because I depended on the Lord. But in future generations, the Lord will fight the Amalekites again and again.”
translation_verse: Ɔse, “Bɛmaa Ɛdɛnkɛma fɛlɛnra ne zo! Ɔvi awolɛndoazo mɔɔ kɔ awolɛndoazo la, Ɛdɛnkɛma baho atia Amalɛkema.”

english_verse: While Israel was camped in the desert near Mount Sinai, Jethro sent Moses this message: “I am coming to visit you, and I am bringing your wife and two sons.”
translation_verse: Awie hɔhanle hilele Mosisi kɛ, “Nea, ɛ ye ɔ ze Gyɛtulo nee ɛ ye nee ɛ mra mrenya nwiɔ ne ɛlɛba.”

english_verse: When they arrived, Moses went out and bowed down in front of Jethro, then kissed him. After they had greeted each other, they went into the tent,
translation_verse: Yemɔti Mosisi vale ɛnriandilɛ hɔyiale ye, ɔbɔle ɔ ti aze ɔmanle ye, ɔyɛle ye akoaba na ɔvole ɔ nvoka anwo. Bɛbizebizale bɛ agbɔkɛ nu nee kɛ ɛbɛlabɔlɛ nu si kɔ ye la. Akee bɛhɔwolole Mosisi ndanlɛ sua ne anu.

english_verse: where Moses told him everything the Lord had done to protect Israel against the Egyptians and their king. He also told him how the Lord had helped them in all of their troubles.
translation_verse: Na Mosisi hanle ninyɛne mɔɔ ɔlua Yizilayɛma ati Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛva ɛyɛ Yigyibitima nee bɛ belemgbunli ne la, amaneɛ mɔɔ bɛnwunle ye wɔ bɛ adendulɛ ne anu nee kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛzi ɛlie bɛ la amuala hilele ɔ ye ɔ ze Gyɛtulo.

english_verse: Now I know that the Lord is the greatest God, because he has rescued Israel from their arrogant enemies.”
translation_verse: Na kɛkala, menwu kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma le kpole tɛla nyamenle biala, ɔboalekɛ ɔliele menli ne ɔvile Yigyibitima asa anu wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɛnee bɛlɛyɛ bɛ mgbane mgbane la.”

english_verse: Jethro offered sacrifices to God. Then Aaron and Israel's leaders came to eat with Jethro there at the place of worship. Judges Are Appointed (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Na Mosisi aye ɔ ze Gyɛtulo bɔle ɛyelalɛ azu manle Ɛdɛnkɛma. Aalɔn nee Yizilayɛ mgbanyima ne mɔ amuala rale na bɛ nee Gyɛtulo ralile debie wɔ Nyamenle anyunlu. Bɛye Ndɛnebuavolɛma (Mɛla

english_verse: You and the people who come to you will soon be worn out. The job is too much for one person; you can't do it alone.
translation_verse: Ɛ nee menli ne bɛku bɛ nwo ɛvɛlɛ mgbane, ɔluakɛ gyima ne bo ɛ nwo zo. Ɛ ngomekye ɛnrɛhola ɔ muala yɛ.

english_verse: The next morning Moses sat down at the place where he decided legal cases for the people, and everyone crowded around him until evening.
translation_verse: Aleɛ hyenle la menli ne yiale. Bɛgyinlanle nzisi na Mosisi dɛnlanle aze kɛ ɔsiezie edwɛkɛ ngyikyi mɔɔ wɔ menli ne avinli la. Ɔbɔle ɔ bo nwonlomɔ toonwo aleɛ dwole bɔkɔɔ.

english_verse: Jethro saw how much Moses had to do for the people, and he asked, “Why are you the only judge? Why do you let these people crowd around you from morning till evening?”
translation_verse: Na mɔɔ Mosisi aye ne ɔ ze nwunle mɔɔ Mosisi ɛlɛyɛ amaa menli ne la ɔhanle kɛ, “Duzu a ɛlɛyɛ wɔamaa menli ne la? Duzu ati a ɛdawɔ ɛ ngomekye ɛkɛdɛnla aze na menli ne amuala kɛgyinla, kɛbɔ wɔ mgbɔlɔka kɛyia toonwo aledwolɛ ɛ?”

english_verse: Moses answered, “Because they come here to find out what God wants them to do.
translation_verse: Na Mosisi buale Gyɛtulo kɛ, “Ɔboalekɛ menli ne ba kɛ membiza Ɛdɛnkɛma memaa bɛ.

english_verse: They bring their complaints to me, and I make decisions on the basis of God's laws.”
translation_verse: Saa bɛnyia edwɛkɛ a bɛba na mesiezie bɛ avinli, na memaa bɛnwu Nyamenle mɛla ne nee ye ngyehyɛlɛ ne mɔ.”

english_verse: Jethro replied: That isn't the best way to do it.
translation_verse: Na Gyɛtulo zele ye kɛ, “Tɛ adenle kpalɛ ne a ɛlua nu la.

english_verse: God will help you if you follow my advice. You should be the one to speak to God for the people,
translation_verse: Tie mɔɔ meka la; memaa wɔ adwenle, na Nyamenle nee wɔ balua! Ɛbagyinla menli ne agyakɛ anu wɔ Nyamenle anyunlu.

english_verse: and you should teach them God's laws and show them what they must do to live right.
translation_verse: Ɛbahilehile bɛ mɛla ne nee ngyehyɛlɛ ne mɔ, na wɔamaa bɛanwu adenle mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ bɛdua nu nee debie mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ bɛyɛ la.

english_verse: These judges can handle the ordinary cases and bring the more difficult ones to you. Having them to share the load will make your work easier.
translation_verse: Na maa mekɛ biala bɛziezie menli ne mɔ edwɛkɛ. Saa edwɛkɛ ne le edwɛkɛ kpole bo bɛ nwo zo a, maa bɛva bɛrɛlɛ wɔ; edwɛkɛ ngyebangyeba ne mɔ, maa bɛdabɛ bɛli. Ɛhye bade wɔ ɛvɛlɛ zo na bɛ nee wɔ azoa adesoa ne.

english_verse: This is the way God wants it done. You won't be under nearly as much stress, and everyone else will return home feeling satisfied.
translation_verse: Saa ɛyɛ ɛhye na Nyamenle kponle zolɛ maa wɔ a, ɛbahyɛ na menli ne mɔ noko ahɔ bɛ azua nu anzonudwolɛ nu.”

english_verse: He chose some competent leaders from every tribe in Israel and put them over groups of
translation_verse: Ɔyele Yizilayɛma bie mɔ mɔɔ bɔ mɔdenle kpalɛ la na ɔyɛle bɛ mgbanyinli wɔ menli ne anwo zo, bie sie menli apenle, bie menli ɛya, bie menli abulanlu, yɛɛ bie menli bulu.

english_verse: They served as judges, deciding the easy cases themselves, but bringing the more difficult ones to Moses.
translation_verse: Na mekɛ biala bɛzieziele menli ne avinli. Edwɛkɛ ne mɔɔ yɛ se la, bɛvale bɛrɛlɛle Mosisi, na bɛzieziele edwɛkɛ ngyebangyeba ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti.

english_verse: After Moses and his father-in-law Jethro had said goodbye to each other, Jethro returned home.
translation_verse: Akee Mosisi guale ɔ ye ɔ ze ne adenle manle ɔhɔle ye maanle nu.

english_verse: The Israelites left Rephidim and arrived at the desert. Then two months after leaving Egypt, they arrived at the desert near Mount Sinai, where they set up camp at the foot of the mountain. This was two months after they had left Egypt.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Yizilayɛma vile Yigyibiti la, ye siane nsa ne na ye kenle ne mɔɔ lumua la bɛdwule Saenae fienemgbole ne anu. Akee mɔɔ bɛvi Relɛfedem bɛrale Saenae fienemgbole ne anu la, bɛrazokoɛle Boka Saenae abo ɛkɛ.

english_verse: Moses went up the mountain to meet with the Lord God, who told him to say to the people:
translation_verse: Na Mosisi vole boka ne kɛ ɔkayia Nyamenle. Ɛdɛnkɛma vɛlɛle ye boka ne azo zele ye kɛ, “Ɛhye yɛɛ ɛbaha wɔahile Gyekɔbo abo zo amra ne a: Ka kile Yizilayɛma ne kɛ,

english_verse: You saw what I did in Egypt, and you know how I brought you here to me, just as a mighty eagle carries its young.
translation_verse: ‘Bɛnwunle mɔɔ medame Ɛdɛnkɛma menvale menyɛle Yigyibitima, na menvale bɛ wɔ kɔleɛ ndɛbalɛ zo membale me nwo ɛke la.

english_verse: Now if you will faithfully obey me, you will be my very own people. The whole world is mine,
translation_verse: Yemɔti saa bɛtie me ne na bɛdi me ngyekyeleɛ ne azo a, bɛbayɛ me ɛdeɛ wɔ maanle maanle kɔsɔɔti avinli, ɔluakɛ azɛlɛ ne kɔsɔɔti le me ɛdeɛ.

english_verse: but you will be my holy nation and serve me as priests. Moses, that is what you must tell the Israelites.
translation_verse: Bɛbayɛ me maanle nwuanzanwuanza na bɛazonle me kɛ bɛle me sɛlɛvolɛma. Ɛhye a le edwɛkɛ mɔɔ ɛbaha wɔahile Yizilayɛma a.’ ”

english_verse: After Moses went back, he reported to the leaders what the Lord had said,
translation_verse: Yemɔti Mosisi ziale rale; ɔvɛlɛle Yizilayɛ mgbanyima ne mɔ na ɔvale mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛha ɛhile ye la ɔdole bɛ nyunlu.

english_verse: and they all promised, “We will do everything the Lord has commanded.” So Moses told the Lord about this.
translation_verse: Na menli ne kɔsɔɔti anloa hɔle ko hanle kɛ, “Debie biala mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛha la, yɛbayɛ.” Na Mosisi hanle mɔɔ menli ne hanle la hilele Ɛdɛnkɛma.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “I will come to you in a thick cloud and let the people hear me speak to you. Then they will always trust you.” Again Moses reported to the Lord what the people had said.
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Nea, mebalua amungu kumɔɔnwo bie anu meara, amaa saa me nee wɔ ɛlɛtendɛ a, menli ne ade me ne na bɛalie wɔ bɛali dahuu.” Akee Mosisi hanle mɔɔ menli ne hanle la hilele Ɛdɛnkɛma.

english_verse: Once more the Lord spoke to Moses: Go back and tell the people that today and tomorrow they must get themselves ready to meet me. They must wash their clothes
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Kɔ na kɔnlua menli ne ɛnɛ nee ɛhyema, bɛkpo bɛ nwo ninyɛne,

english_verse: and be ready by the day after tomorrow, when I will come down to Mount Sinai, where all of them can see me.
translation_verse: na maa bɛboɔboa bɛ nwo ɛhyema anzi, ɔluakɛ ye kenle nsa ne azo medame Ɛdɛnkɛma, mebadwu aze wɔ Boka Saenae azo, wɔ menli ne kɔsɔɔti anye zo.

english_verse: Warn the people that they are forbidden to touch any part of the mountain. Anyone who does will be put to death,
translation_verse: Gya anyiane, amaa menli ne ambɔ andɛla, na ka kile bɛ kɛ, ‘Bɛnlea boɛ na bɛ biala anvo boka ne azo anzɛɛ ambikye nwolɛ bɔbɔ. Awie biala mɔɔ kɛzie ɔ ti boka ne anwo la, bɛkɛhu ye.

english_verse: either with stones or arrows, and no one must touch the body of the person being put to death in this way. Even an animal that touches this mountain must be put to death. You may go up the mountain only after a signal is given on the trumpet.
translation_verse: Bɛbazi ye awolɛ anzɛɛ bɛbado ye ɛda na awie biala ɛnrɛzɔ ye, saa sonla anzɛɛ nane o, ɔwɔ kɛ ɔwu.’ Na saa bɛbɔ aweɛne tendenle ne anu tendenle ko a, bɛvo boka ne azo.”

english_verse: After Moses went down the mountain, he gave orders for the people to wash their clothes and make themselves acceptable to worship God.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Mosisi vi boka ne azo dwule rale menli ne anwo ɛkɛ na ɔranluanle bɛ, na bɛkpole bɛ nwo ninyɛne.

english_verse: He told them to be ready in three days and not to have sex in the meantime. The Lord Comes to Mount Sinai
translation_verse: Ɔzele menli ne kɛ, “Bɛboɔboa bɛ nwo toonwo ɛhyema anzi; awie biala mmakɔ raalɛ nwo.”

english_verse: On the morning of the third day there was thunder and lightning. A thick cloud covered the mountain, a loud trumpet blast was heard, and everyone in camp trembled with fear.
translation_verse: Kenle nsa ne azo nwonlomɔ ne, ezule hulule na maanle nu vedevedele. Amungu kumɔɔnwo hedale boka ne azo, bɛwule aweɛne tendenle ne anu tendenle bie, na menli ne mɔɔ wɔ azokoɛleɛ ɛkɛ ne la amuala anwo wozole bɛ.

english_verse: Moses led them out of the camp to meet God, and they stood at the foot of the mountain.
translation_verse: Akee Mosisi vale menli ne kɔsɔɔti vile azokoɛleɛ ɛkɛ ne hɔle kɛ bɛkayia Nyamenle. Awie biala kpondɛle ɛleka gyinlanle wɔ boka ne abo.

english_verse: Mount Sinai was covered with smoke because the Lord had come down in a flaming fire. Smoke poured out of the mountain just like a furnace, and the whole mountain shook.
translation_verse: Na esike hedale Boka Saenae azo, ɔboalekɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma dwule zo kɛ senle la, na esike ne hɔle anwuma kɛ fonlomo esike la, na boka mumua ne kpusule kpole bie.

english_verse: The trumpet blew louder and louder. Moses spoke, and God answered him with thunder.
translation_verse: Mekɛ mɔɔ ɛnee aweɛne tendenle ne ane ɛlɛkɔ anwuma kpalɛ la, Mosisi dendɛle, na Nyamenle vale ɛhululɛ liele ye zo.

english_verse: The Lord came down to the top of Mount Sinai and told Moses to meet him there.
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma dwule Boka Saenae azo. Ɔvɛlɛle Mosisi na Mosisi hɔle boka ne azo.

english_verse: Then he said, “Moses, go and warn the people not to cross the boundary that you set at the foot of the mountain. They must not cross it to come and look at me, because if they do, many of them will die.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Sia kɔ aze na bɔ menli ne kɔkɔ, anrɛɛ bɛkɛtele zolɛ kɛ bɛbanlea Ɛdɛnkɛma na bɛ dɔɔnwo awu.

english_verse: Only the priests may come near me, and they must obey strict rules before I let them. If they don't, they will be punished.”
translation_verse: Eza maa sɛlɛvolɛma ne mɔ mɔɔ bikye Ɛdɛnkɛma la ɛnlua bɛ nwo na anrɛɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛdua bɛ kakɛ.”

english_verse: Moses replied, “The people cannot come up the mountain. You warned us to stay away because it is holy.”
translation_verse: Na Mosisi hanle hilele Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ, “Menli ne mɔ ba Boka Saenae azo a ɔnyɛ boɛ, ɔluakɛ ɛdawɔ mumua ne ɛzele yɛ kɛ, ‘Bɛgya boka ne anyiane na bɛdu bɛmaa me.’ ”

english_verse: Then the Lord told Moses, “Go down and bring Aaron back here with you. But the priests and people must not try to push their way through, or I will rush at them like a flood!”
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele yɛ kɛ, “Dwu aze na ɛ nee Aalɔn bɛrɛla. Mmamaa sɛlɛvolɛma nee menli ne tɛla anyiane ne ba medame Ɛdɛnkɛma me nwo ɛke, anrɛɛ menwɔdua bɛ kakɛ.”

english_verse: After Moses had gone back down, he told the people what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Mosisi dwule aze hɔhanle edwɛkɛ mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma hanle la hilele menli ne.

english_verse: God said to the people of Israel:
translation_verse: Na Nyamenle dendɛle zele kɛ,

english_verse: But when Moses went near the thick cloud where God was, the people stayed a long way off. Idols and Altars
translation_verse: Menli ne gyinlanle moa moa na Mosisi bikyele awozinli kabikabi ne, ɛleka mɔɔ Nyamenle wɔ la. Azukponle nwo mɛla

english_verse: I am the Lord your God, the one who brought you out of Egypt where you were slaves.
translation_verse: “Mame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne, mɔɔ yele bɛ vile Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo, vile akɛlɛzonlenlɛ nu la.

english_verse: Do not worship any god except me.
translation_verse: “Bɛmmasonle nyamenle gyɛne biala kɛ me ngome ala.

english_verse: Do not make idols that look like anything in the sky or on earth or in the ocean under the earth.
translation_verse: “Bɛmmayɛ ananze, anzɛɛ debie biala mɔɔ wɔ anwuma anzɛɛ aze anzɛɛ nzule nu wɔ azɛlɛ bo la sɔhovolɛ.

english_verse: But if you love me and obey my laws, I will be kind to your families for thousands of generations.
translation_verse: na mekile me ɛhulolɛ kpundii ne memaa awolɛndoazo apenle apenle mɔɔ kulo me na bɛdi me mɛla zo la.

english_verse: Do not misuse my name. I am the Lord your God, and I will punish anyone who misuses my name.
translation_verse: “Bɛmmabɔ medame Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne duma mgbane mgbane, ɔluakɛ medame Ɛdɛnkɛma, menrɛmaa mɔɔ bɔ me duma mgbane mgbane la ɛnrɛva ɔ nwo dwɔɔ.

english_verse: Remember that the Sabbath Day belongs to me.
translation_verse: “Bɛhakye kɛ bɛkɛzie Ɛnwomenlelielɛ Kenle ne nwuanzanwuanza.

english_verse: You have six days when you can do your work,
translation_verse: Bɛva kenle nsia bɛyɛ gyima, bɛyɛ bɛ gyima muala,

english_verse: but the seventh day of each week belongs to me, your God. No one is to work on that day—not you, your children, your slaves, your animals, or the foreigners who live in your towns.
translation_verse: na kenle nsuu ne le Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne Ɛnwomenlelielɛ Kenle; bɛmmayɛ gyima biala, bɛdabɛ anzɛɛ bɛ mra mrenya, anzɛɛ bɛ mra mraalɛ, bɛ sonvolɛ mrenya, anzɛɛ bɛ sonvolɛ mraalɛ, anzɛɛ bɛ nlankɛ, anzɛɛ nyɛvolɛ mɔɔ wɔ bɛ azua ne mɔ azo la.

english_verse: In six days I made the sky, the earth, the oceans, and everything in them, but on the seventh day I rested. That's why I made the Sabbath a special day that belongs to me.
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ medame Ɛdɛnkɛma, menvale kenle nsia a membɔle anwuma nee aze a, nyevile nee nuhua ninyɛne muala, na menliele me ɛnwomenle wɔ kenle nsuu ne azo. Yemɔti medame Ɛdɛnkɛma, menyilale Ɛnwomenlelielɛ Kenle ne na menyɛle ye nwuanzanwuanza.

english_verse: Respect your father and your mother, and you will live a long time in the land I am giving you.
translation_verse: “Bɛli bɛ ze mɔ nee bɛ nli mɔ eni, amaa bɛ mekɛ awa wɔ azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ medame Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne melɛfa meamaa bɛ la azo.

english_verse: Do not murder.
translation_verse: “Bɛmmaku sonla.

english_verse: Be faithful in marriage.
translation_verse: “Bɛmmafa awuvolɛ.

english_verse: Do not tell lies about others.
translation_verse: “Bɛmmadi daselɛ adalɛ bɛtia bɛ gɔnwo.

english_verse: Do not desire to possess anything that belongs to another person—not a house, a wife, a husband, a slave, an ox, a donkey, or anything else. The People Are Afraid (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: “Bɛmmamaa bɛ nye bolo bɛ gɔnwo sua nu; bɛmmamaa bɛ nye bolo bɛ gɔnwo aye, anzɛɛ ye sonvolɛ nrenya, anzɛɛ ye sonvolɛ raalɛ, anzɛɛ ye ɛnlankɛ nyinli, anzɛɛ ye asoaso, anzɛɛ bɛ gɔnwo debie biala.” Menli ne ɛzulolɛ (Mɛla

english_verse: So you must never make idols of silver or gold to worship in place of me.
translation_verse: Bɛmmafa dwɛtɛ fufule bɛyɛ awozonle bɛboka me nwo, anzɛɛ bɛmmafa ezukoa nvutuke bɛyɛ awozonle bɛmaa bɛ nwo.

english_verse: The people trembled with fear when they heard the thunder and the trumpet and saw the lightning and the smoke coming from the mountain. They stood a long way off
translation_verse: Mɔɔ menli ne kɔsɔɔti dele ɛhululɛ nee ye ɛvedevedelɛ ne nee aweɛne tendenle ne ane, na bɛnwunle boka ne azo esike ne la, ɛzulolɛ hanle bɛ na bɛ nwo wozole bɛ.

english_verse: and said to Moses, “If you speak to us, we will listen. But don't let God speak to us, or we will die!”
translation_verse: Bɛgyinlanle moa moa na bɛhanle bɛhilele Mosisi kɛ, “Wɔmɔ tendɛ kile yɛ na yɛbade. Mmamaa Nyamenle tendɛ kile yɛ, anrɛɛ yɛkɛwu.”

english_verse: “Don't be afraid!” Moses replied. “God has come only to test you, so that by obeying him you won't sin.”
translation_verse: Na Mosisi hanle hilele menli ne kɛ, “Bɛmmasulo, ɔluakɛ Nyamenle ɛra kɛ ɔbazɔ bɛ yeanlea, amaa bɛazulo ye dahuu na bɛanyɛ ɛtane.”

english_verse: The Lord told Moses to say to the people of Israel: With your own eyes you saw me speak to you from heaven.
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Ɛhye yɛɛ ɛbaha wɔahile Yizilayɛma a: Bɛdabɛ bɛnwu ye bɛ nye zo kɛ mevi anwuma me nee wɔ ɛdendɛ.

english_verse: Build an altar out of earth, and offer on it your sacrifices of sheep, goats, and cattle. Wherever I choose to be worshiped, I will come down to bless you.
translation_verse: Bɛzi ndɛtɛlɛ azukponle bɛmaa me na bɛva bɛ mboane nee nlankɛ azubɔdeɛ ne mɔ bɛbɔ ɛyelalɛ azu nee anzonudwolɛ azu wɔ zolɛ bɛmaa me. Ɛleka biala mɔɔ menwɔze bɛ kɛ bɛzonle me la, mebara mearayila bɛ.

english_verse: If you ever build an altar for me out of stones, do not use any tools to chisel the stones, because that would make the altar unfit for use in worship.
translation_verse: Saa bɛfa awolɛ a bɛazi azukponle bɛamaa me a, anrɛɛ bɛmmafa bulalɛ bɛkyekyɛ nwolɛ, ɔluakɛ saa bɛfa bulalɛ bɛkyekyɛ nwolɛ a, ɛnee bɛgua nwolɛ evinli.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for attacking your father or mother.
translation_verse: “Awie biala mɔɔ kɛbɔ ɔ ze anzɛɛ ɔ nli la, bɛhu ye.

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses the following laws for his people:
translation_verse: “Fa mɛla ɛhye mɔ maa Yizilayɛma:

english_verse: If you buy a Hebrew slave, he must remain your slave for six years. But in the seventh year you must set him free, without cost to him.
translation_verse: Saa bɛtɔ Hibulunli kanra a, ɔwɔ kɛ ɔsonle ɛvolɛ nsia. Ɛvolɛ nsuu ne azo ɔwɔ kɛ ɔnyia fanwodi na ɔkɔ, mɔɔ ɔndua ɛhwee a.

english_verse: If he was single at the time you bought him, he alone must be set free. But if he was married at the time, both he and his wife must be given their freedom.
translation_verse: Saa ɔba la ɔrale ye baholɛ a, ɔwɔ kɛ ɔkɔ ye baholɛ; saa ɔ nee ɔ ye a, ɔwɔ kɛ ɔ nee ɔ ye kɔ.

english_verse: If you give him a wife, and they have children, only the man himself must be set free; his wife and children remain the property of his owner.
translation_verse: Saa ɔ menle ne gya raalɛ maa ye na ɔ nee ye wo mralɛ mrenya anzɛɛ mralɛ mraalɛ na saa ɔnyia ye fanwodi, na ɔlɛkɔ a, raalɛ ne nee mralɛ ne mɔ le ɔ menle ne ɛdeɛ. Ɔ ngomekye a ɔwɔ kɛ ɔkɔ a.

english_verse: But suppose the slave loves his wife and children and his owner so much that he won't leave them.
translation_verse: Na saa kanranli ne ka ye wienyi kɛ, ‘Mekulo me menle ne, me ye nee me mra ne; menrɛhɔ’ a,

english_verse: Then he must stand beside either the door or the doorpost at the place of worship, while his owner punches a small hole through one of his ears with a sharp metal rod. This makes him a slave for life.
translation_verse: ɛnee ɔ menle ne ɛva ye ɛhɔ Nyamenle ɛzonlenlɛ ɛleka ne anlenkɛ ne anwo anzɛɛ anlenkɛ ne felɛmo ne anwo na ɔ menle ne ɛva ketera ɛfiti ɔ nzo na akee ɔzonle ɔ menle ne toonwo ɔwu.

english_verse: A young woman who was sold by her father doesn't gain her freedom in the same way that a man does.
translation_verse: “Saa nrenya tɔne ɔ ra raalɛ kɛ kanranli a, ɔnle kɛ ɔnyia fanwodi kɛ mrenya ne mɔ la.

english_verse: If she doesn't please the man who bought her to be his wife, he must let her be bought back. He cannot sell her to foreigners; this would break the contract he made with her.
translation_verse: Saa ɔ menle ne mɔɔ dɔle ye kɛ ɔfa ye yeayɛ ɔ ye la anye ɛnlie ɔ nwo a, ɔmaa bɛkpɔne ye; ɔnlɛ adenle ɔndɔne ye ɔmmaa maanle gyɛne nu sonla, ɔluakɛ yeanyɛ ye boɛ yeammaa ye.

english_verse: If he selects her as a wife for his son, he must treat her as his own daughter.
translation_verse: Saa ɔfa ye ɔmaa ɔ ra nrenya gya ye a, ɔwɔ kɛ ɔfa ye ɔyɛ ɔ ra raalɛ.

english_verse: If the man later marries another woman, he must continue to provide food and clothing for the one he bought and to treat her as a wife.
translation_verse: Saa ɔgya raalɛ bieko ɔboka ɔ nwo a, ɔnlɛ adenle ɔnde ye aleɛ, ndanlɛ nee agyalɛ gyinlabelɛ biala mɔɔ ɔlɛ la azo.

english_verse: If he fails to do any of these things, she must be given her freedom without paying for it. Murder and Other Violent Crimes The Lord said:
translation_verse: Saa yeanyɛ ninyɛne nsa ɛhye mɔ yeammaa ye a, raalɛ ne lɛ adenle fa ɔ nwo di, mɔɔ ɔndua ɛhwee a. Kpukpokpukpo nyɛleɛ nwo mɛla

english_verse: But if you did not intend to kill someone, and I, the Lord, let it happen anyway, you may run for safety to a place that I have set aside.
translation_verse: Na saa yeandwenle nwolɛ yeanzie dɛba, na Nyamenle a ɛmaa yedɔ ɔ sa nu a, ahenle kola nriandi kɔ ɛleka mɔɔ menwɔhile la, amaa yeanyia ɔ ti.

english_verse: If you plan in advance to murder someone, there's no escape, not even by holding on to my altar. You will be dragged off and killed.
translation_verse: Na saa sonla anye fuu teta ɔ gɔnwo ku ye a, bɛhɔhwe ye bɛvi me azukponle ne anwo bɛhu ye.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for kidnapping. If you sell the person you kidnapped, or if you are caught with that person, the penalty is death.
translation_verse: “Awie biala mɔɔ kɛwua sonla kɛ ɔtɔne ye anzɛɛ bɛkɛnwu kɛ yeva ye yevea la, bɛhu ye.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for cursing your father or mother.
translation_verse: “Awie biala mɔɔ kɛwa ɔ ze anzɛɛ ɔ nli amonle la, bɛhu ye.

english_verse: and later has to use a stick when walking outside, you must pay for the loss of time and do what you can to help until the injury is completely healed. That's your only responsibility.
translation_verse: “Saa menli nwiɔ ko na ko fa bolɛ anzɛɛ sua kutuku bɔ ɔ gɔnwo ne to aze, na yeanwu na ɔbɔ ye anwonyane ala a, ɔnle kɛ bɛtua ye nwolɛ kakɛ. Saa ahenle dwazo na ɔkola ɔtia kpɔma nwo a, ɔwɔ kɛ nuhua ne mɔɔ bɔle ɔ gɔnwo ne la tua ye adondohonle kakɛ ne nee mekɛ dodo mɔɔ yeanva yeanyɛ gyima la kakɛ.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for beating to death any of your slaves.
translation_verse: “Saa awie bɔ ye kanranli, nrenya anzɛɛ raalɛ maa ɔka ɔ sa nu a, ɔwɔ kɛ bɛtea ye.

english_verse: However, if the slave lives a few days after the beating, you are not to be punished. After all, you have already lost the services of that slave who was your property.
translation_verse: Na saa kanranli ne di kenle ko anzɛɛ kenle nwiɔ na yeawu a, ɔnle kɛ bɛtea ye, ɔluakɛ kanranli ne le ye ezukoa.

english_verse: Suppose a pregnant woman suffers a miscarriage as the result of an injury caused by someone who is fighting. If she isn't badly hurt, the one who injured her must pay whatever fine her husband demands and the judges approve.
translation_verse: Saa mrenya nwiɔ ɛlɛko na bɛsi raalɛ nrenzɛvolɛ, na ɔ ko ne kpɔne, na nrenzɛvolɛ mumua ne amboda a, ɔwɔ kɛ bɛtwe ahenle mɔɔ zile ye la anzo. Ezukoa bolɛ biala mɔɔ nrenzɛvolɛ ne ɔ hu kɛbɔ la, saa ndɛnebuavolɛma die to nu a, ɔwɔ kɛ ahenle ne tua.

english_verse: But if she is seriously injured, the payment will be life for life,
translation_verse: Na saa nrenzɛvolɛ ne anwo bu ɛbonle a, ɛnee yemɔ, ɔbayɛ mɔɔ ɛku ɛ gɔnwo a bɛku wɔ,

english_verse: If you hit one of your slaves and cause the loss of an eye, the slave must be set free.
translation_verse: “Saa awie kpakye ye kanranli nrenya anzɛɛ raalɛ anye zo maa ɔ nye bɔ a, ɔ nye ne ati, kanranli ne fa ɔ nwo di.

english_verse: The same law applies if you knock out a slave's tooth—the slave goes free.
translation_verse: Saa ɔbɔ ye kanranli nrenya anzɛɛ raalɛ ne ɔmaa ɔ gye tu a, ɔ gye ne ati, ɔwɔ kɛ ɔfa ɔ nwo ɔdi. Menlenlɛma gyima

english_verse: A bull that kills someone with its horns must be killed and its meat destroyed, but the owner of the bull isn't responsible for the death.
translation_verse: “Saa ɛnlankɛ nyinli fa ye mɛne wɔ awie, nrenya anzɛɛ raalɛ ku ye a, ɔwɔ kɛ bɛsi ye awolɛ bɛku ye, ɔnle kɛ bɛdi ye nane; ɔnle kɛ bɛyɛ ɔ menle ne ɛhwee.

english_verse: Suppose you own a bull that has been in the habit of attacking people, but you have refused to keep it fenced in. If that bull kills someone, both you and the bull must be put to death by stoning.
translation_verse: Na saa ɔle ɛnlankɛ nyinli ne gyima mɔɔ ɔdi ye dɛba, na bɛbɔ ɔ menle kɔkɔ, na yeanva ye yeanzie, na ɔku sonla nrenya anzɛɛ raalɛ a, ɔwɔ kɛ bɛsi ɛnlankɛ ne awolɛ bɛku ye na bɛku ɔ menle ne ɔdaye.

english_verse: pieces of silver for the loss of the slave, and the bull must be killed by stoning.
translation_verse: Na saa bɛse ye kɛ ɔdua ezukoa ɔdɔ ye ngoane a, yemɔ bolɛ biala mɔɔ bɛkɛbɔ la, ɔwɔ kɛ ɔtua.

english_verse: This same law applies if the bull gores someone's son or daughter.
translation_verse: Saa ɛnlankɛ ne ku awie ara nrenya anzɛɛ raalɛ a, mɛla ko ne ala azo yɛɛ ɔwɔ kɛ bɛgyinla bɛ nee ye di a.

english_verse: Suppose someone's ox or donkey is killed by falling into an open pit that you dug or left uncovered on your property.
translation_verse: “Saa awie angeda ye kuma mɔɔ yevu la azo, anzɛɛ ɔfu kuma na yeandua ye na ɛnlankɛ nyinli anzɛɛ asoaso tɔ nu a,

english_verse: You must pay for the dead animal, and it becomes yours.
translation_verse: ɔwɔ kɛ ahenle mɔɔ vunle kuma ne la tua ɛnlankɛ ne kakɛ maa ɔ menle na ɔfa nane funli ne.

english_verse: If your bull kills someone else's, yours must be sold. Then the money from your bull and the meat from the dead bull must be divided equally between you and the other owner.
translation_verse: Saa awie ɛnlankɛ nyinli ku awie ɛnlankɛ a, ɔwɔ kɛ bɛtɔne ɛnlankɛ nyinli anyewɔzo ne na bɛkyɛ ezukoa ne, na eza bɛkyɛ nane ne mɔɔ ɛwu la nane ne.

english_verse: If you refuse to fence in a bull that is known to attack others, you must replace any animal it kills, but the dead animal will belong to you.
translation_verse: “Na saa bɛnwu kɛ ɔle ɛnlankɛ nyinli ne gyima kɛ ɔsisi awie mɔ nlankɛ yɛɛ ɔ menle ne anva ye anzie ɛdeɛ a, ɔbava ɛnlankɛ ne bie yeazie mɔɔ ɛwu la abo zo na yeava ɛnlankɛ funli ne.

english_verse: If you steal an ox and slaughter or sell it, you must replace it with five oxen; if you steal a sheep and slaughter it or sell it, you must replace it with four sheep.
translation_verse: “Saa awie wua ɛnlankɛ nyinli anzɛɛ boane na ɔku ye anzɛɛ ɔtɔne ye a, ɔbava nlankɛ nyinli nnu yeazie ɛnlankɛ ko ne abo zo, anzɛɛ mboane nna yeazie boane ko ne abo zo.

english_verse: But if you cannot afford to replace the animals, you must be sold as a slave to pay for what you have stolen. If you steal an ox, donkey, or sheep, and are caught with it still alive, you must pay the owner double. If you happen to kill a burglar who breaks into your home after dark, you are not guilty. But if you kill someone who breaks in during the day, you are guilty of murder.
translation_verse: Ɔwɔ kɛ ɔfa bie ɔsie mɔɔ yewua la abo zo; saa ɔnlɛ ɛhwee a, ɔwɔ kɛ bɛtɔne ye kɛ kanra la bɛtua mɔɔ ɔwuale la. Saa bɛnwu nane ne mɔɔ ɔwuale la anyewɔzo, ɛnlankɛ nyinli, asoaso, anzɛɛ boane ne wɔ ye ɛkɛ ne a, ɔwɔ kɛ ɔtua ye mɔnwo. “Saa bɛkye awule kɛ ɔlɛbu sua nɔɔzo, na bɛbɔ ye debie na ɔwu a, ahenle mɔɔ bɔle ye la ɛnli fɔlɛ kɛ yeyɛ kɔdiawu.

english_verse: If you allow any of your animals to stray from your property and graze in someone else's field or vineyard, you must repay the damage from the best part of your own harvest of grapes and grain.
translation_verse: “Saa awie maa ye nyɛmoa kɔdidi awie vanye egyinli nu, anzɛɛ gyakyi ye nyɛmoa maa bɛkɔdi ɔ gɔnwo ɛya nu bɛyɔba a, ɔwɔ kɛ ɔfa ɔdaye ye ɛya nu bɛyɔba kpalɛ kpalɛ ne mɔ bie ɔsie bɛ bo zo.

english_verse: If you carelessly let a fire spread from your property to someone else's, you must pay the owner for any crops or fields destroyed by the fire.
translation_verse: “Saa awie to senle na ɔmaa ɔsɔ ɔkɔyela awie abɛlɛ mɔɔ yebu yehua anzɛɛ gyigyi anzɛɛ ɔyela ɛya avule a, ahenle mɔɔ dole senle ne la ɔwɔ kɛ sie ye kɔsɔɔti abo zo.

english_verse: Suppose a neighbor asks you to keep some silver or other valuables, and they are stolen from your house. If the thief is caught, the thief must repay double.
translation_verse: “Saa awie fa ezukoa anzɛɛ ninyɛne maa ɔ gɔnwo kɛ ɔva ɔzie na awie wua na bɛkye ye a, ɔwɔ kɛ ɔtua ye mɔnwo.

english_verse: But if the thief isn't caught, some judges will decide if you are the guilty one.
translation_verse: Saa bɛannwu awule ne a, ɔwɔ kɛ awuke menle ne kɔ Nyamenle anyunlu, ɛleka mɔɔ bɛsonle la, na ɔkɔdi amonle kɛ amgba tɛ ɔdaye a ɔwuale ɔ gɔnwo ne ninyɛne ne a.

english_verse: Suppose two people claim to own the same ox or donkey or sheep or piece of clothing. Then the judges must decide the case, and the guilty person will pay the owner double.
translation_verse: “Mɔɔ fane ninyɛne nwo kpolerazulɛ nwo, saa ɛnlankɛ nyinli o, asoaso o, boane o, ndanlɛ o, anzɛɛ debie biala mɔɔ kɛminli la anwo, na nuhua ko ɛlɛka kɛ, ‘Me ɛdeɛ ɔ’ la, menli nwiɔ ne mɔɔ ɛlɛsu kpolera ne la ɔwɔ kɛ kɔ Nyamenle anyunlu. Nuhua ne mɔɔ Nyamenle kɛbua ye fɔlɛ la ɔwɔ kɛ tua ye mɔnwo maa ɔ gɔnwo ne.

english_verse: Suppose a neighbor who is going to be away asks you to keep a donkey or an ox or a sheep or some other animal, and it dies or gets injured or is stolen while no one is looking.
translation_verse: “Saa awie kponle zolɛ kɛ ɔkɛzie ɔ gɔnwo asoaso anzɛɛ ɛnlankɛ nyinli anzɛɛ boane anzɛɛ ayɛmoa biala ɔkɛmaa ye, na saa ɔwu, ɔboda anzɛɛ bɛwua, mɔɔ awie biala ɛnli nwolɛ daselɛ la a,

english_verse: If you swear with me as your witness that you did not harm the animal, you do not have to replace it. Your word is enough.
translation_verse: ɔwɔ kɛ ahenle kɔdi amonle wɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlu kɛ amgba tɛ ɔdaye a ɔwuale ɔ gɔnwo ne agyadeɛ ne a. Saa nane ne, tɛ ɛwualɛ yɛɛ bɛwuale a, ahenle mɔɔ lɛ agyadeɛ ne la ɔwɔ kɛ kponle zolɛ; yemɔti ɔnlie bie ɔnzie ɔ bo zo.

english_verse: But if the animal was stolen while in your care, you must replace it.
translation_verse: Na saa bɛwuale nane ne ɛdeɛ a, yemɔ neavolɛ ne ɔwɔ kɛ fa bie sie ɔ bo zo maa ɔ menle.

english_verse: If the animal was attacked and killed by a wild animal, and you can show the remains of the dead animal to its owner, you do not have to replace it.
translation_verse: Saa nanemgbole bie ku ye a, ɔwɔ kɛ ɔfa ye funli ne ɔbadi daselɛ, amaa yeanzie ɔ bo zo.

english_verse: Suppose you borrow an animal from a neighbor, and it gets injured or dies while the neighbor isn't around. Then you must replace it.
translation_verse: “Saa awie fɛne ɔ gɔnwo ayɛmoa na bɛboda ye anzɛɛ ɔwu wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɔ menle ne ɛnle ɛkɛ ne la a, ɔwɔ kɛ ɔsie ɔ bo zo.

english_verse: But if something happens to the animal while the owner is present, you do not have to replace it. If you had leased the animal, the money you paid the owner will cover any harm done to it. Laws for Everyday Life The Lord said:
translation_verse: Na saa ɔ menle wɔ ɛkɛ na ɛhye si a, ɔnle kɛ ahenle sie ɔ bo zo. Saa bɛbɔle ye ɛkpa a, ɔwɔ ye ɛkpabɔlɛ ezukoa ne anu. Subane nee nyamenlezonlenlɛ nwo mɛla

english_verse: Suppose a young woman has never had sex and isn't engaged. If a man talks her into having sex, he must pay the bride price and marry her.
translation_verse: “Saa nrenya bɔ belamunli raalɛ mɔɔ bɛtɛyiale ye la anzɔne na ɔ nee ye da a, ɔwɔ kɛ ɔsu ɔ ti asoa na ɔgya ye.

english_verse: But if her father refuses to let her marry the man, the bride price must still be paid.
translation_verse: “Saa raalɛ ne ɔ ze kpo kɛ ɔnrɛmaa ɔnrɛgya ye a, ɔwɔ kɛ nrenya ne tua ezukoa mɔɔ nee raalɛ belamunli ati asoa sɛ la maa ɔ ze.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for witchcraft.
translation_verse: “Bɛhu raalɛ biala mɔɔ ye ngonyia la.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for having sex with an animal.
translation_verse: “Bɛhu nrenya biala mɔɔ nee nane kɛla la.

english_verse: Death is the punishment for offering sacrifices to any god except me.
translation_verse: “Bɛhu awie biala mɔɔ kɛbɔ azu kɛmaa bozonle biala la; Ɛdɛnkɛma angomekye yɛɛ bɛbɔ azu bɛmaa ye a.

english_verse: Do not mistreat or abuse foreigners who live among you. Remember, you were foreigners in Egypt.
translation_verse: “Bɛmmayɛ ɛyɛvolɛ biala ɛtane anzɛɛ bɛmmasisi ye, ɔluakɛ ɛnee bɛdabɛ bɛle nyɛvolɛ wɔ Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo.

english_verse: Do not mistreat widows or orphans.
translation_verse: Bɛmmakile kunlanvolɛ raalɛ anzɛɛ arisa biala nyane.

english_verse: If you do, they will beg for my help, and I will come to their rescue.
translation_verse: Saa bɛkile bɛ nyane na bɛsu bɛfɛlɛ me a, nɔhalɛ, mebadie bɛ ɛzunlɛ ne;

english_verse: In fact, I will get so angry that I will kill your men and make widows of their wives and orphans of their children.
translation_verse: mebava bɛ nwo ɛya na meamaa bɛahu bɛ wɔ konle nu, na bɛ ye mɔ ayɛ ahunlanvolɛ na bɛ mra ayɛ nrisa.

english_verse: Don't charge interest when you lend money to any of my people who are in need.
translation_verse: “Saa bɛbɔ me menli ehyianvolɛma ne mɔ bie bosea a, bɛmmayɛ kɛ menli mɔɔ bɔ bosea die nzinwo la, yɛɛ bɛmmadie ye nzinwo.

english_verse: Before sunset you must return any coat taken as security for a loan,
translation_verse: Saa ɛdie ɛ gɔnwo tɛladeɛ awoba a, fa ye debie maa ye kolaa na sɛnzɛne adɔ,

english_verse: because that is the only cover the poor have when they sleep at night. I am a merciful God, and when they call out to me, I will come to help them.
translation_verse: ɔluakɛ ɛhye ala a ɔwula a, ye tɛladeɛ mɔɔ ɔfa ɔkeda ye sonlabaka ne anwo la ɛne. Duzu yɛɛ ɔva ɔla a? Saa ɔsu ɔfɛlɛ me a, mebadie ye, ɔluakɛ mese anwunvɔne.

english_verse: Don't speak evil of me or of the ruler of your people.
translation_verse: “Bɛmmatendɛ bɛtia Nyamenle anzɛɛ bɛmmawa sonla mɔɔ sie bɛ menli ne la amonle.

english_verse: Don't fail to give me the offerings of grain and wine that belong to me. Dedicate to me your first-born sons
translation_verse: “Bɛmmatwenlehwenle bɛ bo aze wɔ bɛ bɛyɔba azubɔlɛ ne mɔ anwo. “Bɛva bɛ mra mrenya mɔɔ lumua la bɛmaa me.

english_verse: and the first-born of your cattle and sheep. Let the animals stay with their mothers for seven days, then on the eighth day give them to me, your God.
translation_verse: Zɔhane ala yɛɛ bɛyɛ bɛ nlankɛ nee bɛ mboane amra mɔɔ bɛkɛlumua bɛkɛwo bɛ la a. Bɛmaa bɛ nyɛmoa ne mɔ amra mɔɔ lumua la biala ɛli kenle nsuu wɔ ɔ nli anwo ɛkɛ, ye kenle mɔtwɛ ne azo, bɛva ye bɛmaa me.

english_verse: You are my chosen people, so don't eat the meat of any of your livestock that was killed by a wild animal. Instead, feed the meat to dogs.
translation_verse: “Bɛbayɛ menli mɔɔ bɛdu bɛ bɛmaa me, yemɔti bɛmmadi nane mɔɔ ɛbɔ nu nane ɛhu ye la; bɛva bɛmaa ahwea ɛli.

english_verse: Always tell the truth in court, even if everyone else is dishonest and stands in the way of justice.
translation_verse: Bɛmmadi menli dɔɔnwo anzi bɛyɛ ɛtane; yɛɛ bɛmmatoa menli ne dɔɔnwo ti bɛkyea nɔhalɛ nye wɔ bɛ daselɛlilɛ nu bɛsɛkye pɛlepɛlelilɛ.

english_verse: And don't favor the poor, simply because they are poor.
translation_verse: Bɛdi ehyianli edwɛkɛ a, bɛmmadi mɔguazo.

english_verse: If you find an ox or a donkey that has wandered off, take it back where it belongs, even if the owner is your enemy.
translation_verse: “Saa ɛnwu kɛ wɔ kpɔvolɛ ɛnlankɛ anzɛɛ asoaso ɛde ɛlɛkɔ a, kye ye kɔmaa ye.

english_verse: If a donkey is overloaded and falls down, you must do what you can to help, even if it belongs to someone who doesn't like you.
translation_verse: Saa ɛnwu kɛ adesoa ɛdɔ wɔ kpɔvolɛ asoaso nwo zo a, boa ye maa ɔdwazo ye; mmapɛ nu ɛkɔ.
