english_verse: Then he said to Korah, “Tomorrow you and your followers must go with Aaron to the Lord's sacred tent.
translation_verse: Mosisi hanle hilele Kɔla kɛ, “Ɛhyema fa ɛ sa zo ne mɔ finde Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlu; Aalɔn noko bara.

english_verse: Each of you take along your fire pan with incense in it and offer the incense to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Awie biala ɛva ye ɛyɛlɛkpunlɛ kyɛnze ne, ɔva ɛyɛlɛ ɔgua nu na ɔva ɔrɛla Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlu ɛke, bɛdabɛ menli ɛya nwiɔ abulanlu ne, ɛdawɔ, yɛɛ Aalɔn.”

english_verse: The next day the men placed incense and coals in their fire pans and stood with Moses and Aaron at the entrance to the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Yemɔti awie biala vale ye ɛyɛlɛkpunlɛ kyɛnze ne, ɔvale senle ɔguale nu, ɔvale ɛyɛlɛ ɔguale nu na ɔragyinlanle Mosisi nee Aalɔn anwo ɛkɛ wɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma Ndanlɛ Sua ne anlenkɛ ne anloa.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Korah had convinced the rest of the Israelites to rebel against their two leaders. When that happened, the Lord appeared in all his glory
translation_verse: Kɔla boɔboale menli ne kɔsɔɔti anloa na bɛragyinlanle Ɛdɛnkɛma Ndanlɛ Sua ne anlenkɛ ne anloa, bɛ nye kpɔnla Mosisi nee Aalɔn anyunlu. Na arɛlevilɛ nu, Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlunyia ne dale menli ne kɔsɔɔti anwo zo,

english_verse: and said to Moses and Aaron,
translation_verse: na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi nee Aalɔn kɛ,

english_verse: “Get away from the rest of the Israelites so I can kill them at once!”
translation_verse: “Bɛhwe bɛ nwo bɛvi menli ɛhye mɔ avinli, na mesɛkye bɛ kɛkala.”

english_verse: But the two men bowed down and prayed, “Our God, you gave these people life. Why would you punish everyone here when only one man has sinned?”
translation_verse: Na Mosisi nee Aalɔn dule guale mutule nu na bɛhanle kɛ, “O Nyamenle, menli kɔsɔɔti bɛ Nyamenle, na saa sonla ko yɛ ɛtane a, ɛnee ɔwɔ kɛ ɛfa ɛlɔne ne anwo ɛya ɔ?”

english_verse: The Lord answered Moses,
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ,

english_verse: “Tell the people to stay away from the tents of Korah, Dathan, and Abiram.”
translation_verse: “Ka kile menli ne kɛ bɛhwe bɛ nwo bɛvi Kɔla, Deetan, yɛɛ Abaelam ndanlɛ azua ne mɔ anwo.”

english_verse: Moses walked over to Dathan and Abiram, and the other leaders of Israel followed.
translation_verse: Na Yizilayɛ mgbanyima ne mɔ hɔzɔhonle Mosisi wɔ Deetan nee Abaelam ɛkɛ.

english_verse: Then Moses warned the people, “Get away from the tents of these sinful men! Don't touch anything that belongs to them or you'll be wiped out.”
translation_verse: Ɔhanle ɔhilele menli ne kɛ, “Mebodo bɛ, bɛhwe bɛ nwo bɛvi amumuyɛma ɛhye mɔ ndanlɛ azua ne mɔ anwo, yɛɛ bɛmmafa bɛ sa bɛka bɛ debie biala, anrɛɛ bɛkɛva bɛ bɛkɛfonla, bɛkɛbɔ bɛ bo zo wɔ bɛ ɛtane ne mɔ ati.”

english_verse: Moses said to the crowd, “The Lord has chosen me and told me to do these things—it wasn't my idea. And here's how you will know:
translation_verse: Mosisi hanle hilele menli ne kɛ, “Ɛhye bamaa bɛanwu kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛɛ ɛzoa me kɛ membanyɛ gyima ɛhye mɔ a, na tɛ medame me tumi zo ɔ.

english_verse: But suppose the Lord does something that has never been done before. For example, what if a huge crack appears in the ground, and these men and their families fall into it and are buried alive, together with everything they own? Then you will know they have turned their backs on the Lord!”
translation_verse: Na saa Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛ debie ɛzulolɛ kpole bie mɔɔ bɛtɛtele bie ɛlɛ, na saa azɛlɛ kpakye, me bɛ nee bɛ nwo ninyɛne, na bɛdwu Ɛbolɔ anyewɔzo a, yɛɛ bɛbanwu kɛ menli ɛhye mɔ ɛkpo Ɛdɛnkɛma a.”

english_verse: As soon as Moses said this, the ground under the men opened up
translation_verse: Mɔɔ ɔwiele edwɛkɛ ne ka ala la, azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ Deetan nee Abaelam gyi zolɛ la kpakyele nwiɔ

english_verse: and swallowed them alive, together with their families and everything they owned. Then the ground closed back up, and they were gone.
translation_verse: Yemɔti bɛ nee bɛ nwo ninyɛne kɔsɔɔti hɔle Ɛbolɔ anyewɔzo. Azɛlɛ ne hedale bɛ nwo zo na bɛ bo zo minlinle.

english_verse: The rest of the Israelites heard their screams, so they ran off, shouting, “We don't want that to happen to us!”
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti mɔɔ wɔ ɛkɛ na bɛdele menli ne ɛdeɛdeanlɛ ne la nriandile, na bɛhanle kɛ, “Angɔ a angɔ o! Anrɛɛ azɛlɛ ne kɛme yɛdayɛ noko o!”

english_verse: Then the Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ,

english_verse: “Tell Aaron's son Eleazar to take the fire pans from the smoldering fire and scatter the coals. The pans are now sacred,
translation_verse: “Ka kile Sɛlɛvolɛ Aalɔn ara nrenya Ɛlieza kɛ ɔyeye kɔbele ɛyɛlɛkpunlɛ ahyɛnze ne mɔ ɔvi menli mɔɔ ɛyela la avinli na ɔkpokpo nuhua nzonle ne ɔgua ɛleka bie, ɔboalekɛ ɛyɛlɛkpunlɛ ahyɛnze ne mɔ le nwuanzanwuanza.

english_verse: because they were used for offering incense to me. Have them hammered into a thin layer of bronze as a covering for the altar. Those men died because of their sin, and now their fire pans will become a warning for the rest of the community.”
translation_verse: Mekɛ mɔɔ bɛ nee bɛ hɔle Ɛdɛnkɛma azukponle ne anwo la yɛɛ bɛyɛle nwuanzanwuanza a. Yemɔti fa menli ɛhye mɔ mɔɔ bɛhunle bɛ wɔ bɛ ɛtane ti la ɛyɛlɛkpunlɛ ahyɛnze ne mɔ, bolo bɛ ndɛtɛlɛ ndɛtɛlɛ na bɛava bɛaheda azukponle ne azo. Ɛhye bayɛ kɔkɔbɔlɛ amaa Yizilayɛma.”

english_verse: Eleazar collected the pans and had them hammered into a thin layer of bronze as a covering for the altar,
translation_verse: Yemɔti Sɛlɛvolɛ Ɛlieza vale ɛyɛlɛkpunlɛ ahyɛnze ne mɔ bolole bɛ ndɛtɛlɛ ndɛtɛlɛ yɛɛ bɛfa bɛkeda azukponle ne azo a.

english_verse: just as the Lord had told Moses. The pans were a warning to the Israelites that only Aaron's descendants would be allowed to offer incense to the Lord. Anyone else who tried to would be punished like Korah and his followers. The Israelites Rebel and Are Punished
translation_verse: Ɛhye yɛle kɔkɔbɔlɛ manle Yizilayɛma kɛ, ɔnle kɛ awie biala mɔɔ ɛnle Aalɔn abo zo sonla la ba azukponle ne anwo bayela ɛyɛlɛ maa Ɛdɛnkɛma. Anrɛɛ bɛkɛzɛkye ye kɛ bɛzɛkyele Kɔla nee ye menli ne la. Ɛlieza yɛle ɛhye mɔ amuala, kɛmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma luale Mosisi anwo zo zele ye la. Aalɔn die menli ne ngoane

english_verse: The next day the people of Israel again complained against Moses and Aaron, “The two of you killed some of the Lord's people!”
translation_verse: Aleɛ hyenle bieko la, menli ne kɔsɔɔti dendɛle tiale Mosisi nee Aalɔn hanle kɛ, “Bɛhu Ɛdɛnkɛma menli ne bie mɔ.”

english_verse: As the people crowded around them, Moses and Aaron turned toward the sacred tent, and the Lord appeared in his glory in the cloud covering the tent.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ bɛ kɔsɔɔti bɛyiale nu kɛ bɛko bɛatia Mosisi nee Aalɔn la, bɛdole bɛ nye wɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma Ndanlɛ Sua ne anwo, na bɛnwunle kɛ amungu ne ɛheda zolɛ na Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlunyia ne ɛlɛta.

english_verse: So Moses and Aaron walked to the front of the tent,
translation_verse: Mosisi nee Aalɔn hɔgyinlanle Ndanlɛ Sua ne anyunlu,

english_verse: where the Lord said to them,
translation_verse: na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ,

english_verse: “Stand back! I am going to wipe out these Israelites once and for all.” They immediately bowed down and prayed.
translation_verse: “Ɛvi menli ɛhye mɔ avinli twe ɛ nwo, na mesɛkye bɛ wɔ ɛleka mɔɔ bɛgyi ala la!” Bɛ mu nwiɔ bɛdule bɛguale mutule nu,

english_verse: Then Moses told Aaron, “Grab your fire pan and fill it with hot coals from the altar. Put incense in it, then quickly take it to where the people are and offer it to the Lord, so they can be forgiven. The Lord is very angry, and people have already started dying!”
translation_verse: na Mosisi hanle hilele Aalɔn kɛ, “Fa wɔ ɛyɛlɛkpunlɛ kyɛnze ne, fa senle wɔ azukponle ne azo gua nuhua, na fa ɛyɛlɛ gua senle ne anu. Akee ka ɛ nwo ndɛndɛ fa kɔ menli ne anwo lɔ na kɔyɛ mgbɔdalɛ nzɛlɛlɛ maa bɛ. Maa ɔyɛ ndɛ! Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛya ne ɛdwu aze, yɛɛ ewulenzane ɛbɔ ɔ bo.”

english_verse: Aaron walked back and stood with Moses at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ ewulenzane ne gyakyile la, Aalɔn ziale hɔle Mosisi anwo lɔ wɔ Ndanlɛ Sua ne anlenkɛ ne anloa.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses:
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ,

english_verse: Place these sticks in the tent right in front of the sacred chest where I appear to you.
translation_verse: Fa kɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma Ndanlɛ Sua ne anu kɔgua bɛ wɔ Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne anyunlu, ɛleka mɔɔ me nee wɔ yia la.

english_verse: I will then choose a man to be my priest, and his stick will sprout. After that happens, I won't have to listen to any more complaints about you.
translation_verse: Na sonla ne mɔɔ menlea nu meye ye la baka ɛdeɛ ne bafifi. Ɔlua adenle ɛhye azo, mebadua Yizilayɛma mɔɔ tendɛ tia wɔ dahuu la.”

english_verse: Moses told the people what the Lord had commanded, and they gave him the walking sticks from the twelve tribal leaders, including Aaron's from the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Mosisi hanle edwɛkɛ ne hilele Yizilayɛma ne, na bɛ mgbanyima ne mɔ vale bɛ mbaka ne mɔ manle Mosisi, abusua kpanyinli biala ɛdeɛ ko, bɛ muala bɛle bulu nee nwiɔ. Aalɔn baka ɛdeɛ ne boka nwolɛ.

english_verse: Moses took them and placed them in the Lord's sacred tent.
translation_verse: Akee Mosisi vale mbaka ne mɔ hɔguale Ɛdɛnkɛma Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne anyunlu wɔ Ndanlɛ Sua ne anu.

english_verse: Moses brought the twelve sticks out of the tent and showed them to the people. Each of the leaders found his own and took it.
translation_verse: Mosisi vale mbaka ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti vindele na ɔvale ɔhilele Yizilayɛma ne. Bɛdabɛ bɛnwunle mɔɔ ɛzi la, na abusua kpanyinli biala yele ye baka ɛdeɛ ne.

english_verse: But the Lord told Moses, “Put Aaron's stick back! Let it stay near the sacred chest as a warning to anyone who might think of rebelling. If these people don't stop their grumbling about me, I will wipe them out.”
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Fa Aalɔn baka ɛdeɛ ne sia kɔdo Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne anyunlu. Bɛva bɛzie bɛmaa ɔyɛ kɔkɔbɔlɛ ɔmaa Yizilayɛma mɔɔ te atua la kɛ, saa bɛangyakyi bɛ ɛdendɛlɛ mɔɔ bɛtendɛ bɛtia me la a, bɛbawu.”

english_verse: Moses did what he was told.
translation_verse: Na Mosisi yɛle mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma zele ye kɛ ɔyɛ la.

english_verse: The Israelites cried out to Moses, “We're done for
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma ne hanle hilele Mosisi kɛ, “Kɛkala ɛdeɛ, yɛ awieleɛ ne ala ɛne!

english_verse: The Levites are your relatives and are here to help you in your service at the tent.
translation_verse: Saa ɛ nee ɛ mra mrenya ɛlɛyɛ gyima wɔ Ndanlɛ Sua ne anu a, maa ɛ nwo amra mɔɔ le Livae abusua ekpunli ne ɛboa bɛ.

english_verse: You must see that they perform their duties. But if they go near any of the sacred objects or the altar, all of you will die.
translation_verse: Bɛbazonle wɔ na bɛayɛ bɛ gyima ne wɔ Ndanlɛ Sua ne anu, noko ɔnle kɛ bɛbikye ninyɛne nwuanzanwuanza ne mɔ mɔɔ wɔ Ɛleka Nwuanzanwuanza ne la, anzɛɛ azukponle ne anrɛɛ bɛkɛhu bɛ nee ɛdawɔ.

english_verse: No one else is allowed to take care of the sacred tent or do anything connected with it.
translation_verse: Ɔwɔ kɛ bɛ nee wɔ yɛ gyima na bɛyɛ bɛ gyima mɔɔ bɛyɛ wɔ Ndanlɛ Sua ne anu la amuala. Ɔnle kɛ sonla gyɛne biala yɛ gyima ne bie.

english_verse: Follow these instructions, so I won't become angry and punish the Israelites ever again.
translation_verse: Ɔwɔ kɛ ɛdawɔ nee ɛ mra mrenya angomekye a yɛ gyima wɔ Ɛleka Nwuanzanwuanza ne nee azukponle ne anwo a, amaa meanva Yizilayɛma anwo ɛya bieko.

english_verse: I alone chose the Levites from all the other tribes to belong to me, and I have given them to you as your helpers.
translation_verse: Na nea, meye ɛ mediema Livaema mevi Yizilayɛma avinli kɛ bɛle wɔ ahyɛlɛdeɛ, bɛdu bɛ bɛmaa medame Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ bɛyɛ gyima wɔ Ndanlɛ Sua ne anu.

english_verse: But only you and your sons can serve as priests at the altar and in the most holy place. Your work as priests is a gift from me, and anyone else who tries to do that work must be put to death. The Priests' Share of Offerings Given to the Lord (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Na ɛdawɔ nee ɛ mra mrenya noko bayɛ bɛ sɛlɛvolɛ gyima ne mɔɔ fane azukponle ne nee Nwuanzanwuanza Nu Nwuanzaanwu ɛleka ne anwo la. Ɛhye mɔ le bɛ gyima, ɔboalekɛ meva sɛlɛvolɛlilɛ ne kɛ ahyɛlɛdeɛ la memaa bɛ. Awie gyɛne biala mɔɔ kɛbikye ninyɛne nwuanzanwuanza ne mɔ la, ɔwɔ kɛ bɛku ye.” Sɛlɛvolɛma ne kyɛfoa

english_verse: You are allowed to eat the meat of those animals, just as you can eat the choice ribs and the right hind leg of the special sacrifices.
translation_verse: Bɛ nane ne le bɛ ɛdeɛ, kɛmɔ bɛ kɛnrazo ne mɔɔ bɛkɛdo ye ehono nee bɛ ɛzɔlɛ fema ne le bɛ ɛdeɛ la.

english_verse: The Lord said to Aaron: I have put you in charge of the sacred gifts and sacrifices that the Israelites bring to me. And from now on, you, your sons, and your descendants will receive part of the sacrifices for sin, as well as part of the grain sacrifices, and the sacrifices to make things right. Your share of these sacrifices will be the parts not burned on the altar.
translation_verse: Azubɔdeɛ nwuanzanwuanza kpalɛ kpalɛ ne mɔ mɔɔ bɛanyela bɛ wɔ azukponle ne azo, bɛ azubɔdeɛ biala, bɛ ma azubɔdeɛ ne mɔ, mɔɔ bɛva bɛmaa me la le nwuanzanwuanza maa wɔ nee ɛ mra mrenya ne mɔ.

english_verse: Since these things are sacred, they must be eaten near the sacred tent, but only men are allowed to eat them.
translation_verse: Nwu ye kɛ bɛle nwuanzanwuanza, yemɔti ɔwɔ kɛ bɛdi ɛhye mɔ wɔ ɛleka mɔɔ le nwuanzanwuanza la, yɛɛ mrenya ala a ɔwɔ kɛ di bie a.

english_verse: You will also receive part of the special gifts and offerings that the Israelites bring to me. Any member of your family who is clean and acceptable for worship can eat these things.
translation_verse: “Eza ahyɛlɛdeɛ ngakyile biala mɔɔ Yizilayɛma kɛva kɛmaa me, nee ehono azubɔdeɛ biala le bɛ ɛdeɛ. Meva memaa wɔ, ɛ mra mrenya nee ɛ mra mraalɛ wɔ mekɛ kɔsɔɔti mɔɔ bara la. Wɔ busuanli biala mɔɔ evinli ɛnle ɔ nwo la kola di bie.

english_verse: For example, when the Israelites bring me the first batches of oil, wine, and grain, you can have the best parts of those gifts.
translation_verse: “Ɛvolɛ biala egyinli nu bɛyɔba mɔɔ Yizilayɛma kɛlumua kɛbu na bɛkɛva bɛkɛmaa me la, ɔlivi nwole kpalɛ, nwanye nee abɛlɛ, meva memaa wɔ.

english_verse: And the first part of the crops from their fields and vineyards also belongs to you. The people will offer this to me, then anyone in your family who is clean may have some of it.
translation_verse: Nzoleɛ biala mɔɔ bɛkɛlumua bɛkɛde wɔ azɛlɛ ne azo na bɛkɛva bɛkɛrɛlɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma la le wɔ ɛdeɛ. Wɔ busuanli biala mɔɔ evinli ɛnle ɔ nwo la kola di bie.

english_verse: Everything in Israel that has been completely dedicated to me will now belong to you.
translation_verse: “Debie biala mɔɔ wɔ Yizilayɛ azɛlɛ zo, mɔɔ bɛboɔboa bɛva bɛmaa me la le wɔ ɛdeɛ.

english_verse: The first-born son in every Israelite family, as well as the first-born males of their flocks and herds, belong to me. But every first-born son and first-born donkey must be bought back from me.
translation_verse: “Debie biala, sonla anzɛɛ nane mɔɔ kɛlumua kɛbɔ ɛkolɛ na bɛkɛdu bɛkɛmaa Ɛdɛnkɛma la le wɔ ɛdeɛ; noko akee sonla belamunli ralɛ ɛdeɛ, maa bɛkpɔne ye. Nane biala mɔɔ anwo ɛnde la ara mɔɔ lumua la, maa bɛkpɔne ye.

english_verse: The price for a first-born son who is at least one month old will be five pieces of silver, weighed according to the official standards.
translation_verse: Kakula mɔɔ kɛli siane ko la, bɛkpɔne ye dwɛtɛ fufule nnu, kɛmɔ bɛ ezukoa awolɛ si to kɔ la.

english_verse: However, all first-born cattle, sheep, and goats belong to me and cannot be bought back. Splatter their blood on the altar and send their fat up in smoke, so I can smell it and be pleased.
translation_verse: Na nlankɛ, mboane, yɛɛ mbɔnkye amra mɔɔ lumua la ɛdeɛ ɔnle kɛ bɛkpɔne bɛ; bɛva bɛ bɛbɔ azu, bɛle nwuanzanwuanza. Bɛdo bɛ mogya ne bɛgua azukponle ne anwo na bɛyela bɛ ɛnlome ne kɛ ɔle ɛyelalɛ azubɔdeɛ mɔɔ ye evuanlɛ sɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma anye a.

english_verse: From now on, the sacred offerings that the Israelites give to me will belong to you, your sons, and your daughters. This is my promise to you and your descendants, and it will never change.
translation_verse: “Azubɔdeɛ nwuanzanwuanza biala mɔɔ sonle bolɛ, mɔɔ Yizilayɛma kɛva kɛmaa medame Ɛdɛnkɛma la, mefa memaa wɔ, ɛ mra mrenya nee ɛ mra mraalɛ kɛ ɔle bɛ ɛdeɛ dahuu. Ɛhye le ngyekyeleɛ mɔɔ me nee wɔ nee ɛ bo zo amra ɛkyekye mɔɔ bɛntulu ye ɛlɛ a.”

english_verse: You will not receive any land in Israel as your own. I am the Lord, and I will give you whatever you need. What the Levites Receive The Lord said to Aaron:
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Aalɔn kɛ, “Ɛnrɛnyia agyadeɛ biala wɔ bɛ azɛlɛ ne azo, yɛɛ ɛnrɛnyia kyɛfoa biala wɔ bɛ avinli. Medame a mele wɔ kyɛfoa nee wɔ agyadeɛ wɔ Yizilayɛma avinli a.” Livaema ne kyɛfoa

english_verse: Ten percent of the Israelites' crops and one out of every ten of their newborn animals belong to me. But I am giving all this to the Levites as their pay for the work they do at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele kɛ, “Meva debie biala ngyɛnu bulu ɛkpɔ ko ne mɔɔ Yizilayɛma kɛva kɛrɛlɛ me la memaa Livaema. Ɛhye le gyima mɔɔ bɛyɛ wɔ Ndanlɛ Sua ne anu la kakɛdualɛ.

english_verse: They are the only ones allowed to work at the tent, and they must not let anyone else come near it. Those who do come near must be put to death, and the Levites will also be punished. This law will never change. Since the Levites won't be given any land in Israel as their own,
translation_verse: Livaema bayɛ Ndanlɛ Sua ne anwo gyima na bɛdabɛ bɛali bɛ ɛtane nwo ɛzonle. Ɛhye le mɛla mɔɔ bala ɛkɛ amaa bɛ bo zo amra dahuu a. Livaema ɛnrɛnyia agyadeɛ biala wɔ Yizilayɛma avinli.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ,

english_verse: to say to the Levites: When you receive from the people of Israel ten percent of their crops and newborn animals, you must offer a tenth of that to me.
translation_verse: “Ka kile Livaema kɛ saa bɛ sa ka Yizilayɛma ngyɛnu bulu ɛkpɔ ngoko ne mɔ mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma se ɔle bɛ ɛdeɛ la a, bɛdabɛ noko bɛhyɛ nu bulu bɛdu ɛkpɔ ko bɛyɛ azubɔdeɛ bɛmaa Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ ahyɛlɛdeɛ mɔɔ sonle bolɛ la.

english_verse: Just as the Israelites give me part of their grain and wine, you must set aside part of what you receive
translation_verse: Azubɔdeɛ ɛhye bayɛ kɛ ma fofolɛ nee nwanye azubɔdeɛ mɔɔ ɛyazonlɛnli fa maa Ɛdɛnkɛma la.

english_verse: so the best of what you receive will be mine.
translation_verse: Bɛva mɔɔ bɛkɛnyia ye la anu kpalɛ kpalɛ ne mɔɔ nwolɛ te na ɔle Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛdeɛ la bɛmaa me.

english_verse: After you have dedicated the best parts to me, you can eat the rest, just as the Israelites eat part of their grain and wine after offering them to me.
translation_verse: Saa bɛfa nuhua kpalɛ kpalɛ ne bɛmaa Ɛdɛnkɛma a, bɛva mɔɔ kɛha la bɛzie bɛmaa Livaema ne kɛ ɔle ma mɔɔ vi ma ɛwozolɛ ɛleka ne, nee nwanye mɔɔ vi nwanyeyɛlɛ ɛleka ne la.

english_verse: Your share may be eaten anywhere by anyone in your family, because it is your pay for working at the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Bɛ nee bɛ mbusuafoɔ bɛli mɔɔ kɛha la wɔ ɛleka biala, ɔboalekɛ ɔle gyima mɔɔ bɛyɛ wɔ Ndanlɛ Sua ne anu la anwo kakɛdualɛ.

english_verse: You won't be punished for eating it, as long as you have already offered the best parts to me. The gifts and sacrifices brought by the people must remain sacred, and if you eat any part of them before they are offered to me, you will be put to death.
translation_verse: Sumunli kenle ala mɔɔ bɛlumua bɛva nuhua kpalɛ kpalɛ ne bɛmaa medame Ɛdɛnkɛma la, saa bɛdi a bɛnli fɔlɛ, yɛɛ bɛmmagua Yizilayɛma azubɔdeɛ nwuanzanwuanza ne mɔ anwo evinli, kɛ bɛkɛlumua bɛkɛli bie kolaa na bɛava nuhua kpalɛ kpalɛ ne bɛahɔmaa Ɛdɛnkɛma. Saa bɛyɛ ye zɔhane a, bɛkɛhu bɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord gave Moses and Aaron the following law: The people of Israel must bring Moses a reddish-brown cow that has nothing wrong with it and that has never been used for plowing.
translation_verse: “Mɛla mɔɔ medame Ɛdɛnkɛma mehyehyɛ la ɛne: Bɛha bɛhile Yizilayɛma kɛ bɛva ɛnlankɛ belɛ kɔkɔlɛ mɔɔ anwo ɛnlɛ dɛne yɛɛ bɛtɛfale bɛtɛyɛle gyima biala la

english_verse: Moses will give it to Eleazar the priest, then it will be led outside the camp and killed while Eleazar watches.
translation_verse: bɛmaa Sɛlɛvolɛ Ɛlieza; bɛva ye bɛhɔ azokoɛleɛ ne anzi lɔ na bɛhu ye wɔ Sɛlɛvolɛ Ɛlieza anyunlu ɛkɛ.

english_verse: He will dip his finger in the blood and sprinkle it seven times in the direction of the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Akee Ɛlieza ɛva ɔ sa ɛrɛlɛsɛka ɛbɔ ye mogya ne anu na ɔkponde ye wɔ Ndanlɛ Sua ne anyunlu fɔɔnwo fane nsuu.

english_verse: Then the whole cow, including its skin, meat, blood, and insides must be burned.
translation_verse: Ɔwɔ kɛ bɛyela ɛnlankɛ ne wɔ sɛlɛvolɛ ne anye zo ɛkɛ; bɛyela ye nwoma ne, ye nane ne, ye mogya ne, yɛɛ ɔ kunlu ninyɛne ne amuala.

english_verse: A priest is to throw a stick of cedar wood, a hyssop branch, and a piece of red yarn into the fire.
translation_verse: Sɛlɛvolɛ ne bava sida baka, nyinlanyinla nee nyɛma kɔkɔlɛ avuandi agua senle ne mɔɔ ɛnlankɛ ne la nu la anu.

english_verse: After the ceremony, the priest is to take a bath and wash his clothes. Only then can he go back into the camp, but he remains unclean and unfit for worship until evening.
translation_verse: Ɔyɛ ɛhye ɔwie a akee ɔkpo ye adɛladeɛ ne mɔ, ɔbia ɔ nwo na ɔzia ɔhɔ azokoɛleɛ ne bieko, noko ɛnee ɔtɛbɔ evinli nu, kyesɛ nɔsolɛ nu kolaa na yeawie ye evinli ne tu.

english_verse: The man who burned the cow must also wash his clothes and take a bath, but he is also unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Ɔwɔ kɛ ahenle ne mɔɔ yelale ɛnlankɛ ne la ɔdaye noko ɔkpo ye adɛladeɛ ne mɔ, ɔbia ɔ nwo, noko ɛnee ɔtɛbɔ evinli nu, kyesɛ nɔsolɛ nu kolaa na yeawie ye evinli ne tu.

english_verse: A man who isn't unclean must collect the ashes of the burnt cow and store them outside the camp in a clean place. The people of Israel can mix these ashes with the water used in the ceremony to wash away sin.
translation_verse: Akee sonla mɔɔ evinli ɛnle ɔ nwo la kuohua nzonle ne anloa na ɔfa ɔsie ɛleka gyɛlɛɛnye wɔ azokoɛleɛ ne anzi. Bɛfa bɛsie na Yizilayɛma ava akpoto nzule mɔɔ bɛfa bɛanlua evinli la anu.

english_verse: The man who collects the ashes must wash his clothes, but will remain unclean until evening. This law must always be obeyed by the people of Israel and the foreigners living among them. What Must Be Done after Touching a Dead Body The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ɔwɔ kɛ ahenle mɔɔ kɛhuohua nzonle ne anloa la kpo ye adɛladeɛ ne mɔ, noko akee ɛnee evinli tɛbɔ ɔ nwo, kyesɛ nɔsolɛ nu kolaa na yeawie ye evinli ne tu. Mɛla ɛhye gyi ɛkɛ maa Yizilayɛma nee nyɛvolɛ mɔɔ de bɛ avinli la, wɔ mekɛ biala anu. Saa awie anwo ka funli a

english_verse: If you touch a dead body, you will be unclean for seven days.
translation_verse: “Awie biala mɔɔ kɛva ɔ sa kɛha funli la ɛnee evinli ɛha ye toonwo kenle nsuu.

english_verse: But if you wash with the water mixed with the cow's ashes on the third day and again on the seventh day, you will be clean and acceptable for worship. You must wash yourself on those days; if you don't, you will remain unclean.
translation_verse: Ɔwɔ kɛ ɔfa nzule ɔbia ɔ nwo wɔ kenle nsa ne nee kenle nsuu ne azo kolaa na ɔ nwo evinli ne adu. Na saa kenle nsa ne nee kenle nsuu ne azo yeanva nzule yeambia ɔ nwo a, evinli ne ɛnrɛdu.

english_verse: Suppose you touch a dead body, but refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes. You will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean and will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Awie biala mɔɔ kɛva ɔ sa kɛha funli na yeambia ɔ nwo la anwo ɛnde. Ɔgua Ɛdɛnkɛma Ndanlɛ Sua ne anwo evinli, yɛɛ ɔnle kɛ ɔboa Nyamenle menli ne mɔ avinli, ɔboalekɛ bɛtɛwolale nzule ne mɔɔ bɛfa bɛnua evinli la bie bɛtɛguale ɔ nwo.

english_verse: If someone dies in a tent while you are there, you will be unclean for seven days. And anyone who later enters the tent will also be unclean.
translation_verse: “Saa awie wu ndanlɛ sua nu a, awie mɔɔ ye ewule nu ɔwɔ ɛkɛ ne anzɛɛ awie mɔɔ kɛwolo ndanlɛ sua ne anu la ɛnee evinli ɛha ye toonwo kenle nsuu.

english_verse: If you touch the body of someone who died or was killed, or if you touch a human bone or a grave, you will be unclean for seven days.
translation_verse: Saa awie fa ɔ sa ka sonla mɔɔ bɛhu ye anzɛɛ ɛwu ɔ ti anwo ewule wɔ ɛbɔ nu anzɛɛ saa awie fa ɔ sa ka sonla funli bowule anzɛɛ ɔfa ɔ sa ɔka sɛka a, ɛnee evinli ɛha ye toonwo kenle nsuu.

english_verse: Before you can be made clean, someone who is clean must take some of the ashes from the burnt cow and stir them into a pot of spring water. That same person must dip a hyssop branch in the water and ashes, then sprinkle it on the tent and everything in it, including everyone who was inside. If you have touched a human bone, a grave, or a dead body, you must be sprinkled with that water.
translation_verse: Akee sonla mɔɔ evinli ɛnle ɔ nwo la ɛva nyinlanyinla ɛbɔ nzule ne anu ɛkponde ndanlɛ sua ne nee ninyɛne mɔɔ bɛva bɛziezie nu, menli mɔɔ wɔ ɛkɛ, yɛɛ ahenle ne mɔɔ vale ɔ sa hanle sonla funli bowule ne, anzɛɛ sonla ne mɔɔ bɛhunle ye, anzɛɛ funli ne, anzɛɛ sɛka ne la kɔsɔɔti anwo.

english_verse: If this is done on the third day and on the seventh day, you will be clean. Then after you take a bath and wash your clothes, you can worship that evening.
translation_verse: Kenle nsa ne nee kenle nsuu ne azo yɛɛ awie mɔɔ evinli ɛnle ɔ nwo la fa nzule ne kponde ahenle ne mɔɔ evinli ɛha ye la anwo a. Ye kenle nsuu ne azo, ɔnua ye na ahenle ne kpo ye adɛladeɛ na ɔbia ɔ nwo. Ye nɔsolɛ nu ɛnee ɔ nwo evinli ne ɛdu.

english_verse: If you are unclean and refuse to be made clean by washing with the water mixed with ashes, you will be guilty of making my sacred tent unclean, and you will no longer belong to the people of Israel.
translation_verse: “Awie biala mɔɔ evinli ɛha ye, na ɔtɛnuanle ɔ nwo la tɛbɔ evinli nu. Bɛnva ye kɛ ɔle Nyamenle menli ne mɔ ko, ɔluakɛ yegua Ɛdɛnkɛma Ndanlɛ Sua ne anwo evinli.

english_verse: These laws will never change. The man who sprinkled the water and the ashes on you when you were unclean must also wash his clothes. And whoever touches this water is unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Bɛli mɛla ɛhye mɔ kɔsɔɔti azo wɔ melɛ tendenle mɔɔ bara la amuala. Ahenle ne mɔɔ kponde ɛnluanlɛ nzule ne la, ɔdaye noko ɔwɔ kɛ ɔkpo ye adɛladeɛ ne mɔ, awie biala mɔɔ kɛva ɔ sa kɛha nzule ne la ɛnee evinli ɛha ye toonwo ɔkɔdwu nɔsolɛ.

english_verse: When you are unclean, everything you touch becomes unclean, and anyone who touches you will be unclean until evening.
translation_verse: Debie biala mɔɔ sonla mɔɔ evinli ɛha ye la kɛzɔ nu la ɛnee evinli ɛha ye, yɛɛ awie mɔɔ kɛva ɔ sa kɛha deɛ ne la anwo ɛnde toonwo ɔkɔdwu nɔsolɛ.”

english_verse: The people of Israel arrived at the Zin Desert during the first month and set up camp near the town of Kadesh. It was there that Miriam died and was buried.
translation_verse: Siane ne mɔɔ lumua la anu Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti hɔle Zen fienemgbole ne anu na bɛyɛle azokoɛleɛ wɔ Keedɛhye. Ɛkɛ ne yɛɛ Meleam wule na bɛziele ye a.

english_verse: The Israelites had no water, so they went to Moses and Aaron
translation_verse: Ɛleka mɔɔ bɛyɛle azokoɛleɛ ne la, ɛnee nzule ɛnle ɛkɛ, yemɔti menli ne bɔle yiale Mosisi nee Aalɔn

english_verse: and complained, “Moses, we'd be better off if we had died along with the others in front of the Lord's sacred tent.
translation_verse: na bɛhehanle ɛtane ɛtane bɛtietiale bɛ kɛ, “Saa yɛ nee yɛ mediema Yizilayɛma wule Ɛdɛnkɛma Ndanlɛ Sua ne anyunlu a anrɛɛ ɔle kpalɛ.

english_verse: You brought us into this desert, and now we and our livestock are going to die!
translation_verse: Duzu ati a bɛva Ɛdɛnkɛma menli ye nee yɛ nyɛmoa bɛragua fienemgbole ye anu, bɛmaa yɛawu a?

english_verse: Egypt was better than this horrible place. At least there we had grain and figs and grapevines and pomegranates. But now we don't even have any water.”
translation_verse: Duzu ati a bɛye yɛ bɛvi Yigyibiti bɛ nee yɛ ɛra munzule azɛlɛ ɛhye azo a? Ɔnle azɛlɛ bɔbɔ mɔɔ fifi ma, anzɛɛ feege, anzɛɛ vanye, anzɛɛ ma mɔɔ le kɛ akutue la; yɛɛ yɛnnyia nzule yɛnno.”

english_verse: Moses and Aaron went to the entrance to the sacred tent, where they bowed down. The Lord appeared to them in all of his glory
translation_verse: Mosisi nee Aalɔn hwenle bɛ nwo vile menli ne avinli na bɛhɔgyinlanle Ndanlɛ Sua ne anlenkɛ ne anloa. Bɛdule bɛguale bɛbutubutule bɛ nye aze, na Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlunyia ne dale bɛ nwo zo.

english_verse: and said, “Moses, get your walking stick. Then you and Aaron call the people together and command that rock to give you water. That's how you will provide water for the people of Israel and their livestock.”
translation_verse: “Fa kpɔma ne na ɛ nee ɛ diema Aalɔn bɛboɔboa menli ne anloa. Wɔ bɛ nye zo ɛkɛ ne, ka kile bodane ne mɔɔ la bɛ nyunlu ɛkɛ ne la kɛ ɔkpu nzule, na nzule vi nuhua bara na wɔanyia nzule wɔamaa menli ne nee bɛ nyɛmoa anlo.”

english_verse: Moses obeyed and took his stick from the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Na kɛmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma hanle la, Mosisi vale kpɔma ne.

english_verse: After he and Aaron had gathered the people around the rock, he said, “Look, you rebellious people, and you will see water flow from this rock!”
translation_verse: Mosisi nee Aalɔn boɔboale ɛlɔne ne anloa wɔ bodane ne anwo na bɛzele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛmɛ atuadelɛma, bɛdie! Yɛmaa nzule ɛvi bodane ɛhye anu ɛrɛla ɛmaa bɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: He raised his stick in the air and struck the rock two times. At once, water gushed from the rock, and the people and their livestock had water to drink.
translation_verse: Akee Mosisi manle ɔ sa zo na ɔvale ye kpɔma ne ɔfinle bodane ne fane nwiɔ, na nzule vi nuhua rale dɔɔnwo manle menli ne nee bɛ nyɛmoa ne mɔ nlonle bie.

english_verse: But the Lord said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you refused to believe in my power, these people did not respect me. And so, you will not be the ones to lead them into the land I have promised.”
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi nee Aalɔn kɛ, “Kɛmɔ bɛanlie me bɛanli, bɛammaa Yizilayɛma annwu me kpoleyɛlɛ ne bɛdabɛ bɛ nye zo la, bɛnrɛli menli ɛhye mɔ ati bɛ nee bɛ ɛnrɛdwu azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ meva memaa bɛ la azo.”

english_verse: The Israelites had complained against the Lord, and he had shown them his holy power by giving them water to drink. So they named the place Meribah, which means “Complaining.” Israel Isn't Allowed To Go through Edom
translation_verse: Ɛhye zile wɔ Mɛleba; ɛkɛ ne a Yizilayɛma dendɛle tiale Ɛdɛnkɛma na ɔhilele bɛ kɛ ɔle nwuanzanwuanza a. Yidɔm belemgbunli ne tu ɔ gye kɛ ɔnrɛmaa Yizilayɛma adenle

english_verse: Moses sent messengers from Israel's camp near Kadesh with this message for the king of Edom: We are Israelites, your own relatives, and we're sure you have heard the terrible things that have happened to us.
translation_verse: Mosisi zoanle menli wɔ Yidɔm belemgbunli ne ɛkɛ manle bɛhɔzele ye kɛ, “Nrɛlaleɛ ɛhye vi ɛ mediema Yizilayɛma ɛkɛ. Ɛze anwubɛnyunlu mɔɔ ɛdo yɛ,

english_verse: Our ancestors settled in Egypt and lived there a long time. But later the Egyptians were cruel to us,
translation_verse: kɛ ɔzile mɔɔ yɛ mgbanyima ne mɔ hɔle Yigyibiti, na yɛdɛnlanle Yigyibiti ɛvolɛ dɔɔnwo la. Yigyibitima hilele yɛ mgbanyima nee yɛdayɛ nyane kpalɛ.

english_verse: and when we begged our Lord for help, he answered our prayer and brought us out of that land. Now we are camped at the border of your territory, near the town of Kadesh.
translation_verse: Yɛzunle yɛzɛlɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma moalɛ, na ɔzoanle Nyamenle soanvolɛ ɔmanle ɔrayele yɛ ɔvile Yigyibiti. Na kɛkala, yɛradwu Keedɛhye, suakpole mɔɔ wɔ wɔ maanzinli ne ɛweɛne zo la.

english_verse: Please let us go through your country. We won't go near your fields or vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. We will stay on the main road until we leave your territory.
translation_verse: Nana, yɛsɛlɛ wɔ, maa yɛ adenle maa yɛraze wɔ azɛlɛ ne azo yɛhɔ. Yɛdua ademgbole ne ala anu. Yɛnrɛze egyinli anzɛɛ vanye ɛya biala anu, bula nu nzule bɔbɔ, yɛnrɛnlo bie. Yɛnrɛmakyi bɛne anzɛɛ fema toonwo yɛkɛpɛ nu wɔ maanzinli ne anu.”

english_verse: But the king of Edom answered, “No, I won't let you go through our country! And if you try, we will attack you.”
translation_verse: Na Yidɔm belemgbunli ne buale ye kɛ, “Bɛmmafa bɛ gyakɛ bɛtia azɛlɛ ye azo, anrɛɛ menwɔva konle menwɔyia bɛ adenle.”

english_verse: Moses sent back this message: “We promise to stay on the main road, and if any of us or our livestock drink your water, we will pay for it. We just want to pass through.”
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma hanle kɛ, “Yɛbava ademgbole ne ala anu. Saa yɛdayɛ anzɛɛ yɛ nyɛmoa no bɛ nzule bɔbɔ a, yɛkɛdua ye kakɛ, mɔɔ yɛkpondɛ ala la a le kɛ yɛkɛze wɔ azɛlɛ ne azo.”

english_verse: But the king insisted, “You can't go through our land!” Then Edom sent out its strongest troops
translation_verse: Yidɔmma ne zile zolɛ kɛ, “Yɛmkponle, bɛnva ɛke bɛnze!” Na bɛvale ɛlɔnema mɔɔ anwo yɛ se kpalɛ la bɛraduale Yizilayɛma adenle.

english_verse: to keep Israel from passing through its territory. So the Israelites had to go in another direction. Aaron Dies
translation_verse: Kɛmɔ Yidɔmma ammaa Yizilayɛma adenle bɛammaa bɛanze bɛ maanzinli ne anu la ati, bɛziale bɛhɔpenle ɛleka fofolɛ. Aalɔn ewule ne

english_verse: After the Israelites had left Kadesh and had gone as far as Mount Hor
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti vile Keedɛhye hɔle Hɔɔ Boka,

english_verse: “Aaron, this is where you will die. You and Moses disobeyed me at Meribah, and so you will not enter the land I promised the Israelites.
translation_verse: “Aalɔn ɛnrɛvo azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ meva memaa Yizilayɛma la azo, ɔbawu, ɔluakɛ bɛ mu nwiɔ bɛbulule me mɛla zo wɔ Mɛleba azule ne anloa.

english_verse: Moses, go with Aaron and his son Eleazar to the top of the mountain.
translation_verse: Fa Aalɔn nee ɔ ra nrenya Ɛlieza bɛla Hɔɔ Boka ye azo.

english_verse: Then take Aaron's priestly robe from him and place it on Eleazar. Aaron will die there.”
translation_verse: Yeye Aalɔn sɛlɛvolɛ adɛladeɛ ne mɔ fa wula ɔ ra Ɛlieza, na Aalɔn bawu ɛkɛ.”

english_verse: Moses obeyed, and everyone watched as he and Aaron and Eleazar walked to the top of Mount Hor.
translation_verse: Mosisi yɛle mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma zele ye la. Bɛvole Hɔɔ Boka ne azo wɔ menli ne kɔsɔɔti anye zo.

english_verse: Moses then took the priestly robe from Aaron and placed it on Eleazar. Aaron died there. When Moses and Eleazar came down,
translation_verse: Mosisi yeyele Aalɔn sɛlɛvolɛ adɛladeɛ ne mɔ na ɔvale ɔwulale ɔ ra nrenya Ɛlieza. Na Aalɔn wule boka ne azo. Akee Mosisi nee Ɛlieza vi boka ne azo tolole rale.

english_verse: the people knew that Aaron had died, and they mourned his death for
translation_verse: Na mɔɔ menli ne nwunle kɛ Aalɔn ɛwu la, bɛ kɔsɔɔti bɛzunle ye toonwo kenle kɔkɔlɛ abulasa.

english_verse: The Israelites had to go around the territory of Edom, so when they left Mount Hor, they headed south toward the Red Sea. But along the way, the people became so impatient
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma vile Hɔɔ Boka na bɛvale Akaba Ebolo adenle zo, amaa bɛabu bɛahoane Yidɔm maanzinli ne. Na mɔɔ bɛlua adenle zo bɛlɛkɔ la, menli ne annyia abotane

english_verse: that they complained against God and said to Moses, “Did you bring us out of Egypt, just to let us die in the desert? There's no water out here, and we can't stand this awful food!”
translation_verse: na bɛdendɛle bɛtiale Nyamenle nee Mosisi kɛ, “Duzu ati yɛɛ bɛva yɛ bɛvi Yigyibiti bɛmaa yɛarawu fienemgbole ye anu a? Ɔluakɛ aleɛ ɛnle ɛke yɛɛ nzule bɔbɔ, bie ɛnle ɛke. Aleɛ funli ɛhye, yɛnrɛhola bieko di.”

english_verse: Then the Lord sent poisonous snakes that bit and killed many of them.
translation_verse: Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma manle nwɔlɛ anwo ɛzulolɛ bie rakekale Yizilayɛma ne hunle bie mɔ.

english_verse: Some of the people went to Moses and admitted, “It was wrong of us to insult you and the Lord. Now please ask him to make these snakes go away.” Moses prayed,
translation_verse: Na menli ne rale Mosisi anwo ɛkɛ, na bɛhanle kɛ, “Yɛyɛ ɛtane, ɔluakɛ yɛdendɛ yɛtia Ɛdɛnkɛma nee ɛdawɔ. Sɛlɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma maa ɔmaa nwɔlɛ ɛhye mɔ ɛhɔ.” Yemɔti Mosisi zɛlɛle manle menli ne.

english_verse: and the Lord answered, “Make a snake out of bronze and place it on top of a pole. Anyone who gets bitten can look at the snake and be saved from death.”
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Fa kɔbele yɛ ɛwɔlɛ na kenda ye baka zo, amaa awie biala mɔɔ nwɔlɛ ne mɔ bie kɛha ye la, kɛ ɔto ɔ nye yeanlea kɔbele ɛwɔlɛ ne la ɛnee yede kpɔkɛ.”

english_verse: Moses obeyed the Lord. And all of those who looked at the bronze snake lived, even though they had been bitten by the poisonous snakes. Israel's Journey to Moab
translation_verse: Yemɔti Mosisi yɛle kɔbele ɛwɔlɛ na ɔhendanle ye baka zo. Awie biala mɔɔ ɛwɔlɛ hale ye na ɔdole ɔ nye ɔnleanle ye la dele kpɔkɛ. Bɛvi Hɔɔ Boka bɛhɔle Mowabe Bɔnza

english_verse: As the Israelites continued their journey to Canaan, they camped at Oboth,
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma zɔle bɛ adendulɛ ne azo na bɛrazokoɛle Obo.

english_verse: and then in the Zered Gorge.
translation_verse: Akee bɛvile ɛkɛ bɛhɔyɛle azokoɛleɛ wɔ Zɛlɛde Bɔnza ne anu.

english_verse: After that, they crossed the Arnon River gorge and camped in the Moabite desert bordering Amorite territory. The Arnon was the border between the Moabites and the Amorites.
translation_verse: Eza bɛvi ɛkɛ ne bɛdule bɛ bo bɛrazokoɛle Azule Anɔn ne sɔlɔ afoa nu fienemgbole ne mɔɔ di kɔ Amɔle maanzinli nu la anu.

english_verse: A song in The Book of the Lord's Battles mentions the town of Waheb with its creeks in the territory of Suphah. It also mentions the Arnon River,
translation_verse: Ɛhye ati a Ɛdɛnkɛma Konle ne mɔ Buluku ne ka kɛ, “… Weehɛbe mɔɔ wɔ Sufa, nee Azule Anɔn mbɔnza ne mɔ,

english_verse: with its valleys that lie alongside the Moabite border and extend to the town of Ar.
translation_verse: nee mbɔnza ne mɔ ndololeɛ nu mɔɔ tɛlɛ dwu Aale sua zo mɔɔ kɔdwu Mowabe ɛweɛne zo,” la.

english_verse: From the Arnon, the Israelites went to the well near the town of Beer, where the Lord had said to Moses, “Call the people together, and I will give them water to drink.”
translation_verse: Bɛvi ɛkɛ ne la, bɛhɔle Biiyɛ, yemɔ a le bula ne mɔɔ ɛkɛ ne a Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Boɔboa menli ne anloa na menwɔmaa bɛ nzule la.”

english_verse: That's also the same well the Israelites sang about in this song: Let's celebrate! The well has given us water.
translation_verse: Na akee Yizilayɛma dole edwɛne ɛhye: “Bula, maa nzule ɛrɛla; Bɛdo edwɛne bɛmaa ye!

english_verse: With their royal scepters, our leaders pointed out where to dig the well. The Israelites left the desert and camped near the town of Mattanah,
translation_verse: Bula mɔɔ arelemgbunli Nee menli ne mgbanyima Vale dehelɛ tumi dadeɛ Nee bɛ agbɔma bɔle la.” Bɛvile fienemgbole ne anu bɛhɔle Mateena,

english_verse: then at Nahaliel, and then at Bamoth.
translation_verse: bɛvi Mateena bɛhɔle Nahaleɛle, yɛɛ bɛvi Nahaleɛle bɛhɔle Beemo.

english_verse: Finally, they reached Moabite territory, where they camped near Mount Pisgah in a valley overlooking the desert north of the Dead Sea. Israel Defeats King Sihon the Amorite (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Akee bɛvi Beemo la, bɛhɔle bɔnza ne mɔɔ wɔ Mowabe maanzinli ne mɔɔ wɔ Pesega Boka ne mɔɔ wɔ ɛsɛlɛ ne anloa la anu. Belemgbunli Saehɔn nee Belemgbunli Ɔɔgo anwo zo konimlilɛ (Mɛla

english_verse: King Sihon had ruled from Heshbon, after defeating the Moabites and taking over their land north of the Arnon River gorge.
translation_verse: Hɛhyebɔn le Amɔle Belemgbunli Saehɔn mɔɔ honle vale Mowabe belemgbunli dɛba ne na ɔvale ye azɛlɛ ne kɔsɔɔti toonwo ɔhɔdwule Azule Anɔn ne anloa la suakpole.

english_verse: The Israelites sent this message to King Sihon of the Amorites:
translation_verse: Akee Yizilayɛma zoanle menli wɔ Amɔle Belemgbunli Saehɔn ɛkɛ manle bɛhɔzele ye kɛ,

english_verse: Please let us pass through your territory. We promise to stay away from your fields and vineyards, and we won't drink any water from your wells. As long as we're in your land, we'll stay on the main road.
translation_verse: “Maa yɛ adenle maa yɛraze wɔ azɛlɛ ne azo yɛhɔ. Yɛdua ademgbole ne ala anu. Yɛnrɛmakyi ɛya anzɛɛ vanye egyinli biala anu, yɛnrɛnlo bula nu nzule biala. Yɛnrɛmakyi bɛne anzɛɛ fema zo toonwo yɛkɛpɛ nu wɔ maanzinli ne anu.”

english_verse: But Sihon refused to let Israel travel through his land. Instead, he called together his entire army and marched into the desert to attack Israel near the town of Jahaz.
translation_verse: Na Saehɔn ammaa Yizilayɛma adenle yeammaa bɛanlua ye maanzinli ne anu. Ɔboɔboale ye ɛlɔnema ne anloa ɔhɔle Gyeehaze fienemgbole ne anu na ɔvale konle ɔdoale Yizilayɛma.

english_verse: Israel defeated them and took over the Amorite territory from the Arnon River gorge in the south to the Jabbok River gorge in the north. Beyond the Jabbok was the territory of the Ammonites, who were much stronger than Israel.
translation_verse: Na Yizilayɛma ne hunle ye na bɛvale ye maanle ne, ɔvi Azule Anɔn ne anloa ɔhɔdwule Azule Gyabɔko ne anloa, toonwo bɛdwule Amɔlema ɛweɛne zo wɔ Gyeezɛ, ɔboalekɛ Amɔlema azɛlɛ ne anloa pɛ Gyeezɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites settled in the Amorite towns, including the capital city of Heshbon with its surrounding villages.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Yizilayɛma vale Amɔlema azuamgbole ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti na bɛdɛnlanle zolɛ, Hɛhyebɔn nee azua mɔɔ zuozua ye la kɔsɔɔti boka nwolɛ.

english_verse: That's why the Amorites had written this poem about Heshbon: Come and rebuild Heshbon, King Sihon's capital city!
translation_verse: Ɛhye ati a edwɛkɛdwɛndolɛma edwɛne se kɛ, “Bɛla Hɛhyebɔn, bɛkyekye ye bieko. Maa bɛkyekye Saehɔn suakpole.

english_verse: His armies marched out like fiery flames, burning down the town of Ar and destroying the hills along the Arnon River.
translation_verse: Kenle ko bie, Hɛhyebɔn suakpole ye azo, Saehɔn ɛlɔnema ne dule kɛ senle Hɔzɛkyele suakpole Aale mɔɔ wɔ Mowabe, Na ɔzɛkyele Anɔn sɔlɔ awoka ne mɔ.

english_verse: You Moabites are done for! Your god Chemosh deserted your people; they were captured, taken away by King Sihon the Amorite.
translation_verse: Munzule ɛha wɔ, O Mowabe! Bɛmɛ mɔɔ bɛsonle Kimɔhye! Bɛ awieleɛ ɛwie bɛ! Yemaa ɔ mra mrenya ɛyɛ nriandivoma, Na ɔ mra mraalɛ ɛdɔ donvula Wɔ Amɔle Belemgbunli Saehɔn asa anu.

english_verse: We completely defeated Moab. The towns of Heshbon and Dibon, of Nophah and Medeba are ruined and gone.
translation_verse: Yemɔti bɛ bo zo amra abo dule Hɛhyebɔn, Toonwo ɔhɔdwule Daebɔn, Ɔvi Nahyem ɔkɔdwu Nofa mɔɔ zua Midɛba.”

english_verse: After the Israelites had settled in the Amorite territory,
translation_verse: Yemɔti Yizilayɛma dɛnlanle Amɔlema maanle ne anu.

english_verse: Moses sent some men to explore the town of Jazer. Later, the Israelites captured the villages surrounding it and forced out the Amorites who lived there. Israel Defeats King Og of Bashan (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Na Mosisi zoanle menli kɛ bɛhɔkpondɛ adenle mɔɔ bɛpe nu bɛateta suakpole Gyeezɛ la. Yizilayɛma vale suakpole ne nee azua mɔɔ zuozua ye la, na bɛvoanle Amɔlema mɔɔ de ɛkɛ la.

english_verse: The Israelites headed toward the region of Bashan, where King Og ruled, and he led his entire army to Edrei to meet Israel in battle.
translation_verse: Akee Yizilayɛma ziale hɔvale Beehyan adenle zo, na Beehyan Belemgbunli Ɔɔgo nee ye ɛlɔnema ne vindele ratetale bɛ wɔ Ɛdelɛyae.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “Don't be afraid of Og. I will help you defeat him and his army, just as you did King Sihon who ruled in Heshbon. Og's territory will be yours.”
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Mmasulo ye. Memaa wɔali ye nee ye menli ne kɔsɔɔti anwo zo konim na wɔava azɛlɛ ne. Yɛ ye kɛ ɛyɛle Amɔle Belemgbunli Saehɔn mɔɔ ziele Hɛhyebɔn la.”

english_verse: So the Israelites wiped out Og, his family, and his entire army—there were no survivors. Then Israel took over the land of Bashan.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Yizilayɛma hunle Ɔɔgo, ɔ mra mrenya yɛɛ ye menli ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti, ko bɔbɔ anga, na bɛvale ye azɛlɛ ne bɛdɛnlanle zolɛ.

english_verse: Israel moved from there to the hills of Moab, where they camped across the Jordan River from the town of Jericho. King Balak of Moab Hires Balaam To Curse Israel
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma dule denrɛle bieko na bɛrayɛle azokoɛleɛ wɔ Mowabe fienemgbole ne mɔɔ wɔ Dwɔdan aduduleɛ afoa nu na ɔ nee Gyɛleko bɛ nye bɔ zo la anu.

english_verse: They said to the Midianite leaders, “That huge mob of Israelites will wipe out everything in sight, like a bull eating grass in a field.” So King Balak
translation_verse: Mowabema hanle hilele Medean mgbanyima ne mɔ kɛ, “Menli ɛwolaa ɛhye mɔ bali debie biala mɔɔ ɛbɔ yɛ ɛyia la kɛ ɛnlankɛ nyinli di ndile la.” Yemɔti Belemgbunli Beelake

english_verse: sent a message to Balaam son of Beor who lived among his relatives in the town of Pethor near the Euphrates River. It said: I need your help. A large group of people has come here from Egypt and settled near my territory.
translation_verse: zoanle menli kɛ bɛhɔva Biyɔ ara nrenya Beelam mɔɔ wɔ Pito, mɔɔ zua Azule Yufileti, mɔɔ wɔ Amawo azɛlɛ zo la. Bɛvale nrɛlaleɛ ɛhye bɛhɔmanle ye: “Memaa wɔade kɛ maanle mumua vi Yigyibiti ɛdu bɛ bo ɛra; bɛ dodo ɛva azɛlɛ ye amuala na bɛradɛnla yɛ kandiba ɛke.

english_verse: They are too powerful for us to defeat, so would you come and place a curse on them? Maybe then we can run them off. I know that anyone you bless will be successful, but anyone you curse will fail.
translation_verse: Bɛzonle bɛtɛla yɛ, yemɔti, mesɛlɛ wɔ, bɛla na bahye bɛ sili maa me. Wɔannea a ɔkɛyɛ kɛ menwɔli bɛ nwo zo konim na meavoa bɛ meavi azɛlɛ ye azo. Ɔluakɛ meze kɛ mɔɔ ɛkɛyila ye la, bɛyila ye, yɛɛ mɔɔ ɛkɛwa ye amonle la, munzule ka ye.”

english_verse: The leaders of Moab and Midian left and took along money to pay Balaam. When they got to his house, they gave him Balak's message.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Mowabe nee Medean mgbanyima ne mɔ vale silihyelɛ ne anwo ezukoa bɔle bɛ nwo, na bɛhɔle Beelam ɛkɛ bɛhɔhanle Beelake nrɛlaleɛ ne bɛhilele ye.

english_verse: “Spend the night here,” Balaam replied, “and tomorrow I will tell you the Lord's answer.” So the officials stayed at his house.
translation_verse: Beelam hanle hilele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛla ɛke ɛnɛ nɔe, ɛhyema mebaha edwɛkɛ biala mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛha kɛhile me la meahile bɛ.” Yemɔti Mowabe mgbanyima ne mɔ nee Beelam lale.

english_verse: During the night, God asked Balaam, “Who are these people at your house?”
translation_verse: Nyamenle rale Beelam anwo ɛkɛ na ɔbizale ye kɛ, “Nwane mɔ a nee wɔ wɔ ɛke la?”

english_verse: “They are messengers from King Balak of Moab,” Balaam answered. “He sent them
translation_verse: Beelam buale Nyamenle kɛ, “Zepɔ ara nrenya Beelake, Mowabe belemgbunli ne ɛzoa ɛmaa bɛraha bɛhile me kɛ

english_verse: to ask me to go to Moab and put a curse on the people who have come there from Egypt. They have settled everywhere around him, and he wants to run them off.”
translation_verse: maanle mumua vi Yigyibiti ɛrava ye aze na bɛva maanle ne amuala. Ɔkpondɛ kɛ meyɛ nwolɛ debie, amaa ɔ nee bɛ aho na yeadu bɛ ye maanle ne anu.”

english_verse: But God replied, “Don't go with Balak's messengers. I have blessed those people who have come from Egypt, so don't curse them.”
translation_verse: Nyamenle zele Beelam kɛ, “Ɛ nee bɛ mmakɔ; mmayɛ nwolɛ ɛhwee, ɔluakɛ bɛyila bɛ.”

english_verse: The next morning, Balaam said to Balak's officials, “Go on back home. The Lord says I cannot go with you.”
translation_verse: Yemɔti Beelam dwazole nwonlomɔ ne na ɔhanle ɔhilele mgbanyima ne mɔɔ Beelake zoanle bɛ la kɛ, “Bɛzia bɛhɔ bɛ sua zo, ɔluakɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma se me nee bɛ mmakɔ.”

english_verse: The officials left and told Balak that Balaam refused to come.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Mowabe mgbanyima ne mɔ ziale hɔle, na bɛhɔhanle bɛhilele Beelake kɛ, “Beelam ɛkpo kɛ ɔ nee yɛ ɛnrɛra.”

english_verse: Then Balak sent a larger group of officials, who were even more important than the first ones.
translation_verse: Eza Beelake zoanle mgbanyima fofolɛ, mgbanyima mɔɔ le titile na eza bɛ nwo zonle tɛla alumua mgbanyima ne mɔ la.

english_verse: They went to Balaam and told him that Balak had said, “Balaam, if you come to Moab,
translation_verse: Bɛhɔle Beelam ɛkɛ na bɛhɔzele ye kɛ, “Zepɔ ara nrenya Beelake se: Mmamaa debie biala si wɔ aze fee kɛ ɛkɛra!

english_verse: I'll pay you very well and do whatever you ask. Just come and place a curse on these people.”
translation_verse: Mebamaa wɔ ahyɛlɛdeɛ kpole kpalɛ, yɛɛ debie biala mɔɔ ɛkɛze me la, mebayɛ. Mesɛlɛ wɔ, bɛla na bahye menli ne mɔ sili maa me.”

english_verse: Balaam answered, “Even if Balak offered me a palace full of silver or gold, I wouldn't do anything to disobey the Lord my God.
translation_verse: Na Beelam buale kɛ, “Saa Beelake fa dwɛtɛ fufule nee ezukoa nvutuke mɔɔ wɔ ye suakunlu ɛkɛ ne la kɔsɔɔti yeamaa me bɔbɔ a, wɔ adenle biala anu, menrɛdu Ɛdɛnkɛma me Nyamenle ne anloa menrɛdo ɛlɛ.

english_verse: You are welcome to spend the night here, just as the others did. I will find out if the Lord has something else to say about this.”
translation_verse: Mebodo bɛ, bɛla ɛke ɛnɛ nɔe amaa meade saa Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛha edwɛkɛ ngakyile bie kɛhile me a.”

english_verse: So Balaam got up the next morning and saddled his donkey, then left with the Moabite officials. Balaam and His Donkey Meet an Angel
translation_verse: Yemɔti aleɛ hyenle la, Beelam vole ye asoaso ne azo na ɔ nee bɛ hɔle. Beelam nee ye asoaso ne

english_verse: Balaam was riding his donkey to Moab, and two of his servants were with him. But God was angry that Balaam had gone, so one of the Lord's angels stood in the road to stop him.
translation_verse: Na Nyamenle vale ɛya kɛ Beelam nee bɛ ɛlɛkɔ a. Mɔɔ Beelam de ye asoaso ne azo ɛlɛkɔ, na ye sonvolɛma nwiɔ ne li ɔ nzi la, Ɛdɛnkɛma soanvolɛ ragyinlanle ademgbole ne anu duale adenle ne.

english_verse: When Balaam's donkey saw the angel standing there with a sword, it walked off the road and into an open field. Balaam had to beat the donkey to get it back on the road.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ asoaso ne nwunle Nyamenle soanvolɛ ne kɛ ɔgyi adenle ne anu na yehwe konle dadeɛ la, ɔbɔle ɔ ti kpɔkɛ nu. Beelam finle asoaso ne na ɔmanle ɔrale adenle ne anu.

english_verse: Then the angel stood between two vineyards, in a narrow path with a stone wall on each side.
translation_verse: Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma soanvolɛ ne hɔgyinlanle vanye ɛya avule nwiɔ avinli, ɛleka mɔɔ adenle ne kye na bane wɔ ye foa nee ye foa la.

english_verse: When the donkey saw the angel, it walked so close to one of the walls that Balaam's foot scraped against the wall. Balaam beat the donkey again.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ asoaso ne nwunle Ɛdɛnkɛma soanvolɛ ne la, ɔhɔluale bane ne anwo kpalɛ na ɔmianle Beelam agyakɛ wɔ bane ne anwo. Na Beelam eza finle asoaso ne.

english_verse: The angel moved once more and stood in a spot so narrow that there was no room for the donkey to go around.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma soanvolɛ ne eza hɔle ɔ nyunlu na ɔhɔgyinlanle ɛleka mɔɔ adenle ne le feɔ mɔɔ ɛfa ye foa ko ɛleka biala, bɛne zo anzɛɛ fema zo a ɔnyɛ boɛ la.

english_verse: So it just lay down. Balaam lost his temper, then picked up a stick and whacked the donkey.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ asoaso ne nwunle Ɛdɛnkɛma soanvolɛ ne la, ɔbutule. Beelam vale ɛya kpole kpalɛ na ɔvale ye kpɔma ne ɔfinle asoaso ne.

english_verse: When that happened, the Lord told the donkey to speak, and it asked Balaam, “What have I done that made you beat me three times?”
translation_verse: Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma dele asoaso ne anloa manle ɔdendɛle ɔhanle ɔhilele Beelam kɛ, “Duzu bɔbɔ yɛɛ meyɛ, mɔɔ yemɔti wɔfi me fane nsa ɛhye a?”

english_verse: “You made me look stupid!” Balaam answered. “If I had a sword, I'd kill you here and now!”
translation_verse: Beelam buale asoaso ne kɛ, “Ɔboalekɛ wɔyɛ me koasea! Saa melɛ dadeɛ a anrɛɛ mehu wɔ”

english_verse: “But you're my owner,” answered the donkey, “and you've ridden me many times. Have I ever done anything like this before?” “No,” Balaam admitted.
translation_verse: Na asoaso ne buale Beelam kɛ, “Na tɛ asoaso ko ye ala mɔɔ sumunli wɔ ɛbɛlabɔlɛ nu wɔdɛnla zolɛ toonwo la a le me ɔ? Asoo meyɛ wɔ zɛhae ɛlɛ?” Beelam buale kɛ, “Kyɛkyɛ.”

english_verse: Just then, the Lord let Balaam see the angel standing in the road, holding a sword, and Balaam bowed down.
translation_verse: Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma manle Beelam anye zo dele, ɔnwunle kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma soanvolɛ gyi adenle ne anu na yehwe konle dadeɛ. Beelam bɔle ɔ ti aze na ɔbutule ɔ nye aze.

english_verse: The angel said, “You had no right to treat your donkey like that! I was the one who blocked your way, because I don't think you should go to Moab.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma soanvolɛ ne bizale ye kɛ, “Duzu ati a wɔfi asoaso ye fane nsa ɛ? Mera kɛ mebazi wɔ aze, ɔboalekɛ me nye ɛnlie wɔ adenle ne mɔɔ ɛlɛtu la anwo.

english_verse: If your donkey had not seen me and stopped those three times, I would have killed you and let the donkey live.”
translation_verse: Wɔ asoaso ne nwunle me na ɔhwenle ahane fane nsa. Saa yeanyɛ ye zɔhane a anrɛɛ mehu wɔ na megyakyi yemɔ.”

english_verse: Balaam replied, “I was wrong. I didn't know you were trying to stop me. If you don't think I should go, I'll return home at once.”
translation_verse: Beelam buale kɛ, “Meyɛ ɛtane. Menze kɛ ɛgyi adenle ne anu kɛ ɛsi me aze. Na kɛkala, saa ɛnea na ɔnle kpalɛ kɛ mekɔ a, ɛnee mesia meahɔ sua nu.”

english_verse: “It's all right for you to go,” the Lord's angel answered. “But you must say only what I tell you.” So Balaam went on with Balak's officials. King Balak Meets Balaam
translation_verse: Na Nyamenle soanvolɛ ne hanle kɛ, “Ɛ nee menli ne ɛhɔ, na mɔɔ menwɔha menwɔhile wɔ la, yemɔ ala a ka a.” Yemɔti Beelam nee menli ne hɔle. Beelake die Beelam

english_verse: When Balak heard that Balaam was coming, he went to meet him at the town of Ir on the Arnon River, which is the northern border of Moab.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Beelake dele kɛ Beelam ɛlɛba la, ɔhɔyiale ye adenle wɔ Aale; Aale le suakpole mɔɔ wɔ Mowabe ɛweɛne zo wɔ Azule Anɔn ne anloa.

english_verse: Balak asked, “Why didn't you come when I invited you the first time? Did you think I wasn't going to pay you?”

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ,

english_verse: “In my anger, I would have wiped out the Israelites if Phinehas had not been faithful to me.
translation_verse: “Ɔlua mɔɔ Sɛlɛvolɛ Aalɔn ara Ɛlieza ara Fenɛhaze ɛyɛ la ati, megyakyi Yizilayɛma anwo ɛya ne mɔɔ menvale la anu. Ɔliele me ti nungule ɔhwenle, yemɔti a meambɔ Yizilayɛma abo zo wɔ me ɛyavalɛ nu a.

english_verse: But instead of punishing them, I forgave them. So because of the loyalty that Phinehas showed, I solemnly promise that he and his descendants will always be my priests.”
translation_verse: ɔdaye nee ɔ bo zo amra bayɛ sɛlɛvolɛma mɔɔ ɛmbɔ aze ɛlɛ a, ɔboalekɛ ɔhwenle ye Nyamenle ne ati nungule ɔvale ɔkpɔdale Yizilayɛma ati.”

english_verse: The Israelite man that was killed was Zimri son of Salu, who was one of the leaders of the Simeon tribe.
translation_verse: Bɛfɛlɛ Yizilayɛnli ne mɔɔ bɛhunle ye nee Medean raalɛ ne la Zemelae. Ɔ ze a le Seelu mɔɔ le Semɛyɔn abusua ekpunli ne anu abusua ekpulike ko abusua kpanyinli la.

english_verse: And the Midianite woman killed with him was Cozbi, the daughter of a Midianite clan leader named Zur.
translation_verse: Bɛfɛlɛ Medean raalɛ ne noko Kɔzobae. Ɔ ze Zɛɛ le Medean mbusua ekpulike ne mɔ anu ko abusua kpanyinli.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses,
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ,

english_verse: “The Midianites are now enemies of Israel, so attack and defeat them! They tricked the people of Israel into worshiping their god at Peor, and they are responsible for the death of Cozbi, the daughter of one of their own leaders.”
translation_verse: ɔboalekɛ bɛyɛle wɔ ɛtane kɛ bɛbɛlɛbɛlale wɔ wɔ Piyɔ, yɛɛ Kɔzobae, Medean belemgbunli ne ara raalɛ ne mɔɔ bɛhunle ye wɔ Piyɔ wɔ ewulenzane mekɛ ne anu la ati.”

english_verse: After the Lord had stopped the deadly disease from killing the Israelites, he said to Moses and Eleazar son of Aaron,
translation_verse: Ewulenzane ne anzi Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi nee Sɛlɛvolɛ Aalɔn ara Ɛlieza kɛ,

english_verse: “I want you to find out how many Israelites are in each family. Then make a list of every man
translation_verse: “Bɛdia Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti mɔɔ ɛli ɛvolɛ abulanwiɔ mɔɔ kɔ na bɛkola ɛlɔne nloa kɔ la, mbusua ekpulike ekpulike.”

english_verse: Pallu was the father of Eliab
translation_verse: Palu abo zo amra ne a le Yilayabe

english_verse: and the grandfather of Nemuel, Dathan, and Abiram. These are the same Dathan and Abiram who had been chosen by the people, but who followed Korah and rebelled against Moses, Aaron, and the Lord.
translation_verse: nee ɔ mra mrenya Nɛmuwɛle, Deetan, yɛɛ Abaelam. (Deetan nee Abaelam ɛhye mɔ a menli ne dule bɛ na bɛkpole Mosisi nee Aalɔn, na bɛdoale Kɔla nee ye ɛdoavolɛma ne wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ bɛdele Ɛdɛnkɛma anwo atua la.

english_verse: That's when the Lord made the earth open up and swallow Dathan, Abiram, and Korah. At the same time, fire destroyed
translation_verse: Na azɛlɛ ne kpakyele nwiɔ na ɔmenle bɛ nee Kɔla nee ye ɛdoavolɛma ne, menli zɔhane wule wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ senle yelale menli ɛya nwiɔ abulanlu ne la, na bɛyɛle kɔkɔbɔlɛ bɛmanle menli ne.

english_verse: But the Korahite clan wasn't destroyed.
translation_verse: Kɔla amra mrenya ne mɔ, bɛmɛ bɛanwu.)

english_verse: None of the people that Moses and Aaron had counted in the Sinai Desert were still alive,
translation_verse: Menli mɔɔ Mosisi nee Aalɔn dianle bɛ wɔ alumua menli ɛdianlɛ ne anu wɔ Saenae Fienemgbole ne anu la, ɛdwoba ko bɔbɔ anga.

english_verse: Aaron was the father of Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.
translation_verse: Aalɔn wole mrenya nna, Needabe, Abaehu, Ɛlieza, yɛɛ Yetamaa.

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses,
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ,

english_verse: “Divide the land of Canaan among these tribes, according to the number of people in each one,
translation_verse: “Kyɛ azɛlɛ ne maa mbusua ekpunli ekpunli ne, kɛmɔ bɛ dodo de la.

english_verse: I will show you what land to give each tribe, and they will receive as much land as they need, according to the number of people in it.”
translation_verse: Gua nzeleba na wɔahyɛ azɛlɛ ne, abusua ekpunli mɔɔ anwo zonle la, maa ye azɛlɛ kpole, mɔɔ anwo anzo la, maa ye azɛlɛ ekyi.”

english_verse: The tribe of Levi included the clans of the Gershonites, Kohathites, Merarites,
translation_verse: Mbusua ekpulike ekpulike mɔɔ wɔ Livae abusua ekpunli ne anu la a le Gɛhyɔn, Kohate, yɛɛ Mɛlɛlae.

english_verse: as well as the clans of Libni, Hebron, Mahli, Mushi, and Korah. Kohath the Levite was the father of Amram,
translation_verse: Lebenae, Hibulɔn, Maalae, Muhyae, yɛɛ Kɔla le bɛ bo zo amra. Amelam ɔ ze a le Kohate,

english_verse: the husband of Levi's daughter Jochebed, who was born in Egypt. Amram and Jochebed's three children were Aaron, Moses, and Miriam.
translation_verse: ɔgyale Livae ara raalɛ Dwɔkɛbɛde mɔɔ bɛwole ye Yigyibiti la. Dwɔkɛbɛde nee ɔ hu Amelam wole mralɛ mrenya nwiɔ, Aalɔn nee Mosisi, yɛɛ raalɛ ko, Meleam.

english_verse: But Nadab and Abihu had died when they offered fire that was unacceptable to the Lord.
translation_verse: Needabe nee Abaehu vale senle mɔɔ ɛnle nwuanzanwuanza la bɔle azu manle Ɛdɛnkɛma, yemɔti bɛwule.

english_verse: Moses and Eleazar counted the Israelites while they were camped in the hills of Moab across the Jordan River from Jericho.
translation_verse: Mosisi nee Ɛlieza a dianle menli ɛhye mɔ kɔsɔɔti wɔ Mowabe ɛsɛlɛ ne anzi, wɔ Azule Dwɔdan ne anzi wɔ Gyɛleko afoa nu a.

english_verse: except Caleb son of Jephunneh and Joshua son of Nun. The Lord had said that everyone else would die there in the desert.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele kɛ menli ɛhye mɔ kɔsɔɔti bawu fienemgbole ne anu. Gyɛfɛni ara Kalɛbe nee Nɛn ara Dwɔhyua ala a hale a. Bɛ muala bɛwule.

english_verse: One day his daughters went to the sacred tent, where they met with Moses, Eleazar, and some other leaders of Israel, as well as a large crowd of Israelites. The young women said:
translation_verse: Bɛhɔle Mosisi, Sɛlɛvolɛ Ɛlieza, mgbanyima ne mɔ, yɛɛ menli ne kɔsɔɔti anyunlu wɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma Ndanlɛ Sua ne anlenkɛ ne anloa bɛhɔhanle kɛ,

english_verse: You know that our father died in the desert. But it was for something he did wrong, not for joining with Korah in rebelling against the Lord. Our father left no sons
translation_verse: “Egya anwo mralɛ mrenya yɛɛ ɔwule fienemgbole ne anu a. Ɔmboka Kɔla ɛdoavolɛma ne mɔ mɔɔ honle tiale Ɛdɛnkɛma la anwo, ɔdaye ye ɛtane ti a ɔwule a.

english_verse: to carry on his family name. But why should his name die out for that reason? Give us some land like the rest of his relatives in our clan, so our father's name can live on.
translation_verse: Kɛmɔ yeanwo mralɛ mrenya la ati, ɛnee ɔwɔ kɛ egya duma minli ye abusua ekpulike ne anu ɔ? Egya anwo amra agyadeɛ ne, bɛva ye afoa nu ɛdeɛ bɛmaa yɛ.”

english_verse: Moses asked the Lord what should be done,
translation_verse: Mosisi vale bɛ edwɛkɛ ne dole Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlu.

english_verse: and the Lord answered:
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele ye kɛ,

english_verse: Zelophehad's daughters are right. They should each be given part of the land their father would have received.
translation_verse: “Zilɔfɛhade amra mraalɛ ne mɔ edwɛkɛ ne le fɔɔnwo, fa bɛ ze anwo amra ne agyadeɛ ne bie maa bɛ. Maa bɛ ze agyalilɛ ne ɛpɛ ɛli bɛ lɔ.

english_verse: If he has no daughter, his brothers will inherit the land.
translation_verse: Saa ɔnlɛ ralɛ raalɛ a, ɛnee fa ye agyadeɛ ne maa ɔ mediema mrenya.

english_verse: But if he has no brothers, his father's brothers will inherit the land.
translation_verse: Saa ɔnlɛ ɔ mediema mrenya a, ɛnee fa ye agyadeɛ ne maa ɔ ze amediema mrenya.

english_verse: And if his father has no brothers, the land must be given to his nearest relative in the clan. This is my law, and the Israelites must obey it. Joshua Is Appointed Israel's Leader (Deuteronomy
translation_verse: Saa ɔ ze ɛnlɛ mediema mrenya a, ɛnee fa ye agyadeɛ ne maa ye busuanli biala mɔɔ bikye ye kpalɛ kpalɛ la maa ɔyɛ ye agyadeɛ bɔkɔɔ. Ɛhye le mɛla maa Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti, kɛmɔ medame Ɛdɛnkɛma, meze Mosisi la.” Bɛye Dwɔhyua kɛ ɔdi Mosisi agya (Mɛla

english_verse: The Lord said to Moses, “One day you will go up into the Abarim Mountains, and from there you will see the land I am giving the Israelites.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Fo Boka Abalem azo na nea azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ meva memaa Yizilayɛma la.

english_verse: After you have seen it, you will die, just like your brother Aaron,
translation_verse: Saa ɛnwu ye a ɛbazia wɔahɔ wɔ ɛkɛla nzi ɛ nee ɛ ze mɔ ahɔla, kɛmɔ ɛ diema nrenya Aalɔn hɔle la.

english_verse: because both of you disobeyed me at Meribah near the town of Kadesh in the Zin Desert. When the Israelites insulted me there, you didn't believe in my holy power.”
translation_verse: Ɔboalekɛ bɛ mu nwiɔ bɛbulule me mɛla zo wɔ Zen fienemgbole ne anu. Mekɛ mɔɔ menli ne kɔsɔɔti dendɛle tiale me wɔ Mɛleba la, bɛkpole kɛ bɛnrɛmaa menli ne ɛnrɛnwu me tumi nwuanzanwuanza ne.”

english_verse: Moses replied,
translation_verse: Mosisi zɛlɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ,

english_verse: “You are the Lord God, and you know what is in everyone's heart. So I ask you to appoint a leader for Israel.
translation_verse: “Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle, ngoane muala menle, mesɛlɛ wɔ, ye sonla maa ɔnlea menli ne anwo zo,

english_verse: Your people need someone to lead them into battle, or else they will be like sheep wandering around without a shepherd.”
translation_verse: mɔɔ kɛli bɛ nyunlu ɔ nee bɛ kɛhɔ, ɔ nee bɛ kɛra la, amaa menli ne anyɛ kɛ mboane mɔɔ ɛnlɛ neavolɛ la.”

english_verse: The Lord answered, “Joshua son of Nun can do the job. Place your hands on him to show that he is the one to take your place.
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ, “Ye Nɛn ara Dwɔhyua, ɔle sonla mɔɔ sunsum ne wɔ ye nu. Fa ɛ sa gua ɔ ti zo.

english_verse: Then go with him and tell him to stand in front of Eleazar the priest and the Israelites. Appoint Joshua as their new leader
translation_verse: Maa ɔgyinla Sɛlɛvolɛ Ɛlieza nee menli ne kɔsɔɔti anyunlu na kpakye nu ka maa bɛde kɛ yemɔ yɛɛ ɔbali ɛ gyakɛ anu a.

english_verse: and tell them they must now obey him, just as they obey you.
translation_verse: Fa wɔ tumi ne bie maa ye, amaa Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti ayɛ tieyɛ amaa ye.

english_verse: But Joshua must depend on Eleazar to find out from me what I want him to do as he leads Israel into battle.”
translation_verse: Na ɔbahɔ Sɛlɛvolɛ Ɛlieza anyunlu na Ɛlieza ava Yulem nee Tɛmem abiza ɔ ti amaa ye, amaa saa ɔse bɛ kɛ bɛhɔ a, bɛahɔ, ɔse bɛ kɛ bɛrɛla a, bɛara. Ɛlieza bahile Dwɔhyua nee Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti adenle.”

english_verse: Moses followed the Lord's instructions and took Joshua to Eleazar and the people,
translation_verse: Na Mosisi yɛle mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma zele ye la. Ɔmanle Dwɔhyua gyinlanle Sɛlɛvolɛ Ɛlieza nee ɛlɔne ne anyunlu,

english_verse: then he placed his hands on Joshua and appointed him Israel's leader.
translation_verse: ɔvale ɔ sa ɔguale ɔ ti zo na ɔbɔle ye nolo kɛ yemɔ yɛɛ ɔle ye agyadivo a, kɛmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma zele ye la.

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams.
translation_verse: yɛɛ boane edonraa ko biala, bɛva esamo kilo ko.

english_verse: This sacrifice to please me was first offered at Mount Sinai.
translation_verse: Ɛhye le dahuu ɛyelalɛ azubɔdeɛ mɔɔ bɛhyehyɛle wɔ Saenae Boka, mɔɔ ye evuanlɛ sɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma anye a.

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams. The smell of the smoke from these sacrifices will please me.
translation_verse: yɛɛ boane edonraa ko biala, bɛva esamo kilo ko bɛyɛ ma azubɔdeɛ. Ɛyelalɛ azubɔdeɛ ɛhye mɔ evuanlɛ sɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma anye.

english_verse: The Lord told Moses
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Mosisi kɛ,

english_verse: to say to the people of Israel: Offer sacrifices to me at the appointed times of worship, so that I will smell the smoke and be pleased.
translation_verse: “Ka kile Yizilayɛma kɛ, ‘Me azubɔlɛ ne, aleɛ mɔɔ bɛfa bɛabɔ ɛyelalɛ azu mɔɔ sɔ me nye bɛamaa me la, bɛyɛ bɛ wɔ bɛ mekɛ nloa.’

english_verse: Each day offer two rams a year old as sacrifices to please me. The animals must have nothing wrong with them;
translation_verse: “Ka kile bɛ kɛ, ɛyelalɛ azubɔdeɛ ɛhye mɔ a bɛva bɛrɛlɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma a: Kenle ko biala bɛva mboane mralɛ nyinli nwiɔ mɔɔ ɛli ɛvolɛ ngoko, mɔɔ anwo ɛnlɛ dɛne la bɛbɔ azu.

english_verse: Finally, along with each of these two sacrifices, a liter of wine must be poured on the altar as a drink offering.
translation_verse: Boane ko biala, fa nza anu ɛsesebɛ litili ko yɛ azubɔdeɛ gua ye aze wɔ ɛleka nwuanzanwuanza ne maa Ɛdɛnkɛma.

english_verse: On the first day of each month, bring to the altar two bulls, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old that have nothing wrong with them. Then offer these as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: “Siane biala mɔlebɛbo, bɛbɔ ɛyelalɛ azu bɛmaa Ɛdɛnkɛma. Bɛva nlankɛ ndonrandonra nwiɔ, boane nyinli ko, mboane nyinli ndonrandonra mɔɔ ɛli ɛvolɛ ngoko mɔɔ bɛ nwo ɛnlɛ dɛne la nsuu bɛyɛ ɛyelalɛ azubɔdeɛ bɛmaa Ɛdɛnkɛma.

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with each bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram,
translation_verse: Eza bɛva esamo kilo nsa, mɔɔ bɛva ɔlivi nwole bɛfɔtɔ la bɛyɛ ma azubɔdeɛ bɛboka ɛnlankɛ nyinli ko biala anwo; yɛɛ boane nyinli ko biala, bɛva esamo kilo ko bɛyɛ ma azubɔdeɛ;

english_verse: Celebrate Passover in honor of me on the fourteenth day of the first month of each year.
translation_verse: “Siane ne mɔɔ lumua la, ye kenle bulu nee nna ne le Ɛdɛnkɛma Akpabɛnwo Ɛvoyia.

english_verse: The following day will begin the Festival of Thin Bread, which will last for a week. During this time you must honor me by eating bread made without yeast.
translation_verse: Ye kenle bulu nee nnu ne yɛɛ bɛbɔ ɛvoyia ne ɛlilɛ bo a, yɛɛ bɛli kpanwo mɔɔ mgbɔvonle ɛnle nu la toonwo kenle nsuu.

english_verse: On the first day of this festival, you must rest from your work and come together for worship.
translation_verse: Kenle ne mɔɔ lumua ɛvoyialilɛ ne anyunlu la, ɔwɔ kɛ bɛyia nu bɛyɛ nzɛlɛlɛ, ɔnle kɛ bɛyɛ gyima ɛsesebɛ biala.

english_verse: Bring to the altar two bulls, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old that have nothing wrong with them. And then offer these as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: Bɛva nlankɛ nyinli ndonrandonra nwiɔ, boane nyinli ko, yɛɛ mboane nyinli ndonrandonra nsuu mɔɔ ɛli ɛvolɛ ngoko na bɛ nwo ɛnlɛ dɛne la bɛbɔ ɛyelalɛ azu bɛmaa Ɛdɛnkɛma.

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with each bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram,
translation_verse: Eza bɛva esamo mɔɔ bɛva ɔlivi nwole bɛfɔtɔ la bɛyɛ ma azubɔdeɛ bɛmaa Ɛdɛnkɛma: ɛnlankɛ nyinli ko biala, bɛva esamo kilo nsa, boane nyinli ko biala, bɛva esamo kilo nwiɔ,

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams.
translation_verse: yɛɛ boane edonraa ko biala, bɛva esamo kilo ko.

english_verse: All of these are to be offered each day of the festival in additional to the regular sacrifices, and the smoke from them will please me.
translation_verse: Zɔhane ala yɛɛ bɛbɔ aleɛ ɛyelalɛ azu mɔɔ ye evuanlɛ sɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma anye la bɛmaa ye toonwo kenle nsuu a. Bɛyɛ ɛhye bɛboka dahudahu ɛyelalɛ azu ne nee nwanye azubɔlɛ ne anwo.

english_verse: Then on the last day of the festival, you must once again rest from work and come together for worship. The Sacrifices during the Harvest Festival (Leviticus
translation_verse: Ye kenle nsuu ne azo bɛyia nu bɛyɛ nzɛlɛlɛ; bɛmmayɛ gyima ɛsesebɛ biala. Bɛyɔba Ɛvoyia ne azubɔdeɛ ne mɔ (Sɛlɛ

english_verse: On the first day of the Harvest Festival, you must rest from your work, come together for worship, and bring a sacrifice of new grain.
translation_verse: “Kenle ne mɔɔ lumua Bɛyɔba Ɛvoyia ne anyunlu la, saa bɛfa ma fofolɛ bɛarɛlɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma a, bɛlumua bɛyia nu bɛyɛ nzɛlɛlɛ, yɛɛ bɛmmayɛ gyima ɛsesebɛ biala.

english_verse: Offer two young bulls, one full-grown ram, and seven rams a year old as sacrifices to please me.
translation_verse: Bɛbɔ ɛyelalɛ azu mɔɔ ye evuanlɛ sɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma anye la bɛmaa Ɛdɛnkɛma. Bɛva nlankɛ nyinli ndonrandonra nwiɔ, boane nyinli ko, yɛɛ mboane nyinli ndonrandonra mɔɔ ɛli ɛvolɛ ngoko na bɛ nwo ɛnlɛ dɛne la nsuu.

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with each bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram,
translation_verse: Bɛ ma azubɔdeɛ ne, bɛva esamo mɔɔ bɛva ɔlivi nwole bɛfɔtɔ la: ɛnlankɛ nyinli ko biala, bɛva esamo kilo nsa, boane nyinli ko biala, bɛva esamo kilo nwiɔ,

english_verse: Also offer a goat as a sacrifice for sin.
translation_verse: Eza bɛbɔ menli ne ati bɛva abɔnkye nyinli ko bɛyɛ ɛtane azubɔdeɛ bɛyɛ mgbɔdalɛ nzɛlɛlɛ bɛmaa bɛ.

english_verse: The animals must have nothing wrong with them and are to be sacrificed along with the regular daily sacrifices.
translation_verse: Bɛyɛ ɛhye mɔ nee nwanye azubɔdeɛ ne bɛboka dahudahu ɛyelalɛ azubɔdeɛ ne nee ma azubɔdeɛ ne anwo. Bɛnlea kɛ nane ne mɔ anwo ɛnlɛ dɛne.

english_verse: On the first day of the seventh month, you must rest from your work and come together to celebrate at the sound of the trumpets.
translation_verse: “Siane nsuu ne, ye kenle ne mɔɔ lumua la azo, ɔwɔ kɛ bɛyia nu bɛyɛ nzɛlɛlɛ, yɛɛ ɔnle kɛ bɛyɛ gyima ɛsesebɛ biala. Kenle zɔhane, ɔwɔ kɛ bɛwu aweɛne ndendenle ne mɔ anu.

english_verse: Three kilograms of your finest flour mixed with olive oil must be offered with the bull as a grain sacrifice. Two kilograms of flour mixed with oil must be offered with the ram,
translation_verse: Bɛ ma azubɔdeɛ ne, bɛva esamo kpalɛ mɔɔ bɛva ɔlivi nwole bɛfɔtɔ la kilo nsa bɛzua ɛnlankɛ ne: boane nyinli ne, bɛva esamo kilo nwiɔ,

english_verse: and one kilogram of flour mixed with oil must be offered with each of the young rams.
translation_verse: yɛɛ boane edonraa ko biala, bɛva esamo kilo ko.
