translation_verse: Gɛhyɔn asa azo ne noko nyianle azuamgbole bulu nee nsa, nee nwolɛ adidileka.

english_verse: The Lord gave the Israelites the land he had promised their ancestors, and they captured it and settled in it.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Ɛdɛnkɛma vale azɛlɛ ne amuala manle Yizilayɛma, kɛmɔ ɔvale ɔbɔle bɛ nlenya mɔ ɛwɔkɛ la. Akee mɔɔ bɛ sa hanle ye la, bɛdɛnlanle ɛkɛ ne kpɔkpɔ.

english_verse: There still were enemies around Israel, but the Lord kept his promise to let his people live in peace. And whenever the Israelites did have to go to war, no enemy could defeat them. The Lord always helped Israel win.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma manle bɛ anzonudwolɛ wɔ bɛ azɛlɛ ne azo, kɛmɔ ɛwɔkɛ ne mɔɔ ɔbɔle bɛ nlenya mɔ la se la. Bɛ kpɔvolɛma ne anu ko bɔbɔ angola bɛ nyunlu gyinla, ɔboalekɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma manle bɛlile konim wɔ bɛ muala bɛ nwo zo.

english_verse: The Lord promised to do many good things for Israel, and he kept his promise every time.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma lile ɛwɔkɛ biala mɔɔ ɔbɔle Yizilayɛma la azo.

english_verse: Joshua held a meeting with the men of the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh, and he told them:
translation_verse: Akee Dwɔhyua vɛlɛle Wulubɛn, Gaade, yɛɛ Manasɛ Aduduleɛ mbusua ekpunli ne mɔ manle bɛyiale.

english_verse: You have obeyed every command of the Lord your God and of his servant Moses. And you have done everything I've told you to do. It's taken a long time, but you have stayed and helped your relatives.
translation_verse: Mekɛ ɛhye amuala, kenle ko bɔbɔ ɛnle ɛkɛ mɔɔ bɛhakyile bɛ nzi bɛzile bɛ mediema Yizilayɛma a. Bɛli Ɛdɛnkɛma, bɛ Nyamenle ne edwɛkɛ zo.

english_verse: The Lord promised to give peace to your relatives, and that's what he has done. Now it's time for you to go back to your own homes in the land that Moses gave you east of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Kɛkala, Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne ɛmaa Yizilayɛma anzo nu ɛdwo bɛ, kɛmɔ ye ɛwɔkɛ ne se la. Yemɔti bɛhɔ sua nu, wɔ azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ bɛ sa ɛha ye la azo, wɔ Dwɔdan aduduleɛ lɔ. Ɛdɛnkɛma sonvolɛ Mosisi a vale manle bɛ a.

english_verse: Moses taught you to love the Lord your God, to be faithful to him, and to worship and obey him with your whole heart and with all your strength. So be very careful to do everything Moses commanded.
translation_verse: Bɛnlea boɛ na bɛli mɛla ne mɔɔ Mosisi ɛva ɛmaa bɛ la azo. Bɛhulo Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne, bɛyɛ ye ɛhulolɛdeɛ, bɛli ye mɛla ne mɔ azo, bɛli nɔhalɛ bɛmaa ye, na bɛva bɛ ahonle nee bɛ ɛkɛla muala bɛzulo ye.”

english_verse: The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh reached the western side of the Jordan River valley and built a huge altar there beside the river. When the rest of the Israelites heard what these tribes had done,
translation_verse: Awie hɔhanle hilele Yizilayɛma mɔɔ hale la kɛ, “Bɛdie, Wulubɛnema, Gaadema, nee Manasɛ Aduduleɛ amra ɛzi azukponle bie wɔ Gɛlaelo, mɔɔ nee Keena anye bɔ zolɛ la wɔ Dwɔdan adɔleɛ nehae.”

english_verse: the Israelite men met at Shiloh to get ready to attack the two and a half tribes.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Yizilayɛma ne dele ɛhye la, bɛ muala bɛyiale Hyaelo na bɛyɛle kɛ bɛ nee aduduleɛ mbusua ekpunli ekpunli ne mɔ kaho.

english_verse: But first they sent a priest, Phinehas the son of Eleazar, to talk with the two and a half tribes.
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma zoanle sɛlɛvolɛ Ɛlieza ara Fenɛhaze wɔ Wulubɛn, Gaade, yɛɛ Manasɛ Aduduleɛ mbusua ne mɔ anwo ɛkɛ wɔ Geleade.

english_verse: Each of the ten tribes at Shiloh sent the leader of one of its families along with Phinehas.
translation_verse: Mgbanyinli bulu a nee Fenɛhaze hɔle a, abusua ekpunli ko biala anu sonla ko, yɛɛ yemɔ a ɔle abusua ne kpanyinli a.

english_verse: Phinehas and these leaders went to Gilead and met with the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh. They said:
translation_verse: Bɛrale Wulubɛn, Gaade, yɛɛ Manasɛ Aduduleɛ mbusua ekpunli ne mɔ ɛkɛ wɔ Geleade maanzinli nu.

english_verse: All of the Lord's people have gathered together and have sent us to find out why you are unfaithful to our God. You have turned your backs on the Lord by building that altar. Why are you rebelling against him?
translation_verse: Bɛgyinlanle Ɛdɛnkɛma menli ne mɔ amuala agyakɛ anu bɛbizale bɛ kɛ, “Duzu munzule debie a bɛyɛ bɛtia Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne la? Saa bɛzi azukponle ɛhye bɛmaa bɛ nwo a ɛnee bɛkpo Ɛdɛnkɛma! Bɛkpo kɛ bɛnrɛdoa ɔ bo zo bieko!

english_verse: Wasn't our people's sin at Peor terrible enough for you? The Lord punished us by sending a horrible sickness that killed many of us, and we still suffer because of that sin.
translation_verse: Bɛkakye ɛtane mɔɔ yɛyɛle wɔ Piyɔ la. Mekɛ ne anu Ɛdɛnkɛma vale ewule nzane a deanle ɔdaye ye menli ne a. Ɛnɛ nee ɛnɛ ala yɛtɛnwu nwolɛ amaneɛ. Ɛtane zɔhane, yɛyɛ bie yɛvɛ!

english_verse: Now you are turning your backs on the Lord again. If you don't stop rebelling against the Lord at once, he will be angry with the whole nation.
translation_verse: Yemɔti ɛnɛ noko eza bɛkpo kɛ bɛnrɛdoa ye ɔ? Saa bɛkpo Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛnɛ a, ɛhyema ɔbava Yizilayɛnli biala anwo ɛya.

english_verse: If you don't think your land is a fit place to serve God, then move across the Jordan and live with us in the Lord's own land, where his sacred tent is located. But don't rebel against the Lord our God or against us by building another altar besides the Lord's own altar.
translation_verse: Saa bɛnea na bɛ azɛlɛ ne ɛnle ɛleka mɔɔ bɛtɛnla bɛsonle Nyamenle a, ɛnee bɛrɛla Ɛdɛnkɛma azɛlɛ ye azo, ɛleka mɔɔ ye Ndanlɛ Sua ne wɔ la na bɛralie yɛ azɛlɛ ne bie. Bɛmmasi azukponle bɛboka Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛ Nyamenle ne ɛdeɛ ne anwo. Bɛmmako bɛtia Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛɛ bɛmmamaa yɛte atua.

english_verse: Don't you remember what happened when Achan was unfaithful and took some of the things that belonged to God? This made God angry with the entire nation. Achan died because he sinned, but he also caused the death of many others.
translation_verse: Bɛhakye Zila ara Ekan. Yeanli mɛla ne mɔɔ fane ninyɛne mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ bɛsɛkye bɛ la azo la, ɔmanle Yizilayɛma amuala nyianle nwolɛ ndeanlɛ. Tɛ Ekan angome a wule wɔ ye ɛtane ne mɔɔ ɔyɛle la ati a.”

english_verse: The tribes of Reuben, Gad, and East Manasseh answered:
translation_verse: Wulubɛn nee Gaade nee Manasɛ Aduduleɛ amra buale mbusua mgbanyinli mɔɔ vi adɔleɛ rale la kɛ,

english_verse: The Lord is the greatest God! We ask him to be our witness, because he knows whether or not we were rebellious or unfaithful when we built that altar. If we were unfaithful, then we pray that God won't rescue us today. Let us tell you why we built that altar,
translation_verse: “Tumivolɛ Kokye ne ala a le Nyamenle a! Yemɔ a ɔle Ɛdɛnkɛma a! Tumivolɛ Kokye ne ala a le Nyamenle a! Yemɔ a ɔle Ɛdɛnkɛma a! Ɔze deɛ mɔɔ yemɔti yɛyɛle ɛhye la, na yɛmaa bɛdabɛ noko bɛanwu ye! Saa yɛanli nɔhalɛ yɛammaa Ɛdɛnkɛma na yɛhakyi yɛ nzi yɛzi ye, yɛde ɔ nwo atua a, ɛnee bɛhu yɛ!

english_verse: and we ask the Lord to punish us if we are lying. We didn't build it so we could turn our backs on the Lord. We didn't even build it so we could offer animal or grain sacrifices to please the Lord or ask his blessing.
translation_verse: Saa yɛdule Ɛdɛnkɛma anloa yɛdole yɛɛ yɛzi yɛdayɛ yɛ ti anwo azukponle mɔɔ yɛyela azubɔdeɛ wɔ zolɛ anzɛɛ yɛfa yɛabɔ aleɛ ɛnyianlɛ anzɛɛ agɔnwolɛyɛlɛ azu a, ɛnee Ɛdɛnkɛma ɔdaye ɔdua yɛ kakɛ.

english_verse: We built that altar because we were worried. Someday your descendants might tell our descendants, “The Lord made the Jordan River the boundary between us Israelites and you people of Reuben and Gad. The Lord is Israel's God, but you're not part of Israel, so you can't take part in worshiping the Lord.” Your descendants might say that and try to make our descendants stop worshiping and obeying the Lord.
translation_verse: Ɔvale Dwɔdan ɔyɛle ɛweɛne ɔdole yɛ nee bɛmɛ Wulubɛn nee Gaade amra avinli. Bɛ nee Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛnlɛ ngitanwolilɛ biala.’ Ɛnee akee wɔannea a bɛ bo zo amra bamaa yɛmɛ yɛ bo zo amra ne mɔ agyakyi Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛzonlenlɛ.

english_verse: That's why we decided to build the altar. It isn't for offering sacrifices, not even sacrifices to please the Lord.
translation_verse: Yemɔti yɛanzi azukponle ne kɛ yɛyela nane anzɛɛ yɛbɔ azu wɔ zolɛ,

english_verse: Phinehas and the clan leaders left Gilead and went back to Canaan to tell the Israelites about their meeting with the Reuben and Gad tribes.
translation_verse: Akee Fenɛhaze nee mbusua mgbanyinli ne mɔ vile bɛ mediema Wulubɛn nee Gaade amra anwo ɛkɛ ne wɔ Geleade na bɛhɔle Keena; bɛhɔdole Yizilayɛma mɔɔ ɛha la na bɛbɔle bɛ amaneɛ bɛhilele bɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites were happy and praised God. There was no more talk about going to war and wiping out the tribes of Reuben and Gad.
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma ne akunlu dwole na bɛyele Nyamenle ayɛlɛ. Bɛanli konle nwo adwelie bieko kɛ bɛkɔ bɛahɔzɛkye azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ Wulubɛn nee Gaade amra de zolɛ la.

english_verse: The people of Reuben and Gad named the altar “A Reminder to Us All That the Lord Is Our God.”
translation_verse: Wulubɛn nee Gaade amra zele kɛ, “Azukponle ɛhye le daselɛ maa yɛ muala kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ala a le Nyamenle a.” Yemɔti bɛvɛlɛle ye “Daselɛ.”

english_verse: The Lord let Israel live in peace with its neighbors for a long time, and Joshua lived to a ripe old age.
translation_verse: Mekɛ ne hɔle bie la, Ɛdɛnkɛma bɔle Yizilayɛma anwo bane wɔ bɛ kpɔvolɛma mɔɔ ɛbɔ ɛyia bɛ la asa anu. Mekɛ ne anu ɛnee Dwɔhyua ɛyɛ kpanyinli,

english_verse: One day he called a meeting of the leaders of the tribes of Israel, including the old men, the judges, and the officials. Then he told them: I am now very old.
translation_verse: yemɔti ɔvɛlɛle Yizilayɛma amuala, bɛ mgbanyima, bɛ mbusua mgbanyinli, ndɛnebuavolɛma, nee bɛ mbɔlɔba ne mɔ amuala na ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Kɛkala, akee meyɛ kpanyinli.

english_verse: You have seen how the Lord your God fought for you and helped you defeat the nations who lived in this land.
translation_verse: Bɛdabɛ bɛnwu debie mɔɔ bɛmɛ bɛ ti Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne ɛva ɛyɛ maanle maanle ɛhye mɔ la. Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne a ɛho ɛmaa bɛ a.

english_verse: There are still some nations left, but the Lord has promised you their land. So when you attack them, he will make them run away. I have already divided their land among your tribes, as I did with the land of the nations I defeated between the Jordan River and the Mediterranean Sea.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne bamaa maanle maanle zɔhane mɔ agua ndwɛlɛ aze na yeavoa bɛ, wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ bɛmɛ bɛkɛze kɛ bɛko bɛahɔ bɛ nyunlu la. Bɛ azɛlɛ ne bayɛ bɛ ɛdeɛ, kɛmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma vale bɔle bɛ ɛwɔkɛ la.

english_verse: Be sure that you carefully obey everything written in The Book of the Law of Moses and do exactly what it says.
translation_verse: Yemɔti bɛnlea boɛ na bɛli debie biala mɔɔ bɛhɛlɛ ye wɔ Mosisi Mɛla ne anu la azo. Bɛmmabu bɛ nye bɛgua ye kpɔkɛ ko bɔbɔ azo.

english_verse: Don't have anything to do with the nations that live around you. Don't worship their gods or pray to their idols or make promises in the names of their gods.
translation_verse: Akee menli ɛhye mɔ mɔɔ de bɛ avinli la, bɛ nee bɛ mmatu fane biala, bɛmmabɔ bɛ awozonle ne mɔ aluma, bɛmmafa bɛ bɛka ndane, bɛmmasonle bɛ yɛɛ bɛmmabɔ bɛ ti aze bɛmaa bɛ.

english_verse: Be as faithful to the Lord as you have always been.
translation_verse: Bɛli nɔhalɛ bɛmaa Ɛdɛnkɛma, kɛmɔ bɛyɛ toonwo yeradwu ɛnɛ la.

english_verse: When you attacked powerful nations, the Lord made them run away, and no one has ever been able to stand up to you.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma voanle maanle mgbole mgbole mɔɔ anwo yɛ se la wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ bɛzele kɛ bɛba bɛ nyunlu la. Maanle maanle zɔhane mɔ anu menli, ko bɔbɔ angola bɛ nyunlu gyinla.

english_verse: Any one of you can defeat a thousand enemy soldiers, because the Lord God fights for you, just as he promised.
translation_verse: Bɛmɛ, bɛ nuhua ko biala kola maa menli apenle gua ndwɛlɛ aze, ɔboalekɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne a ɛlɛko amaa bɛ a, kɛmɔ ye ɛwɔkɛ ne se la.

english_verse: Be sure to always love the Lord your God.
translation_verse: Zɔhane ati bɛnlea bɛ nwo boɛ na bɛhulo Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne.

english_verse: Don't ever turn your backs on him by marrying people from the nations that are left in the land. Don't even make friends with them. I tell you that if you are friendly with those nations, the Lord won't chase them away when you attack. Instead, they'll be like a trap for your feet, a whip on your back, and thorns in your eyes. And finally, none of you will be left in this good land that the Lord has given you.
translation_verse: ɛnee bɛnwu ye kɛ, Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne ɛnrɛdu menli ɛhye mɔ wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ bɛ nee bɛ kɛnyia konle la. Menli zɔhane anwo bayɛ ɛzulolɛ kɛ ɛhane anzɛɛ kuma la amaa bɛ; na nyane mɔɔ bɛbanwu ye la bayɛ kɛ bɛlɛ empele bɛlɛbila bɛ nzi kuma nu anzɛɛ bɛlɛ mbowule bɛlɛwowɔ bɛ nye zo la. Na ɛhye bahɔ zolɛ toonwo kɔkpula kɛ bɛ muala bɛkɛwie azɛlɛ kpalɛ ɛhye mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne ɛva ɛmaa bɛ la azo.

english_verse: I will soon die, as everyone must. But deep in your hearts you know that the Lord has kept every promise he ever made to you. Not one of them has been broken.
translation_verse: “Akee me ewule mekɛ asɛɛ ɛdwu. Bɛ nuhua ko biala ze ye wɔ ye ahonle nu na ɔdie ɔto nu kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne ɛva ninyɛne kpalɛ ne mɔɔ ɔvale ɔbɔle bɛ ɛwɔkɛ la ɛmaa bɛ. Ɛwɔkɛ biala mɔɔ ɔbɔle la yeli zolɛ; kokye anga nu.

english_verse: Joshua called the tribes of Israel together for a meeting at Shechem. He asked the leaders, including the old men, the judges, and the officials, to come up and stand near the sacred tent.
translation_verse: Dwɔhyua manle Yizilayɛ mbusua ekpunli ekpunli ne mɔ amuala yiale Hyikɛm. Ɔvɛlɛle mgbanyima ne mɔ, mbusua mgbanyinli nee, ndɛnebuavolɛma ne mɔ, yɛɛ Yizilayɛ mbɔlɔba kɔsɔɔti ɔmanle bɛrayiale Nyamenle duma nu wɔ Hyikɛm.

english_verse: Then Joshua told everyone to listen to this message from the Lord, the God of Israel: Long ago your ancestors lived on the other side of the Euphrates River, and they worshiped other gods. This continued until the time of your ancestor Terah and his two sons, Abraham and Nahor.
translation_verse: Dwɔhyua zele menli ne amuala kɛ, “Kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne se la ɛne: ‘Mekɛ bie mɔɔ ɛraze ɛhɔ la bɛ nlenya mɔ dɛnlanle Azule Yufileti anzi lɔ na bɛzonlenle awozonle. Bɛ nlenya mɔ zɔhane anu ko a le Ebileham nee Neehɔ bɛ ze Tilaa.

english_verse: But I brought Abraham across the Euphrates River and led him through the land of Canaan. I blessed him by giving him Isaac, the first in a line of many descendants.
translation_verse: Na menyele bɛ nlenya Ebileham menvile azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ la Azule Yufileti ne anzi lɔ la azo, na mengilele ye Keena azɛlɛ ye amuala. Memanle ɔ sa zo dale. Memanle ɔwole Ayezeke,

english_verse: Then I gave Isaac two sons, Jacob and Esau. I gave Esau the hill country of Mount Seir, but your ancestor Jacob and his children went to live in Egypt.
translation_verse: na Ayezeke wole Gyekɔbo nee Yisɔ. Menvale Yidɔm azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ la awoka ne mɔ azo lɔ la memanle Yisɔ kɛ ɔva ɔdɛnla zolɛ, na bɛ nlenya Gyekɔbo nee ɔ mra ne mɔ hɔle Yigyibiti.

english_verse: Later I sent Moses and his brother Aaron to help your people, and I made all those horrible things happen to the Egyptians. I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, but the Egyptians got in their chariots and on their horses and chased your ancestors, catching up with them at the Red Sea.
translation_verse: menyele bɛ nlenya mɔ menvile Yigyibiti, na Yigyibitima vale ɛlɔnema mɔɔ dede mgbɔnwɔ zo nee konle ehwili nu la doale bɛ ndinlizo. Mɔɔ bɛ nlenya mɔ dwule Ndɔ Nyevile ne anloa la

english_verse: Your people cried to me for help, so I put a dark cloud between them and the Egyptians. Then I opened up the sea and let your people walk across on dry ground. But when the Egyptians tried to follow, I commanded the sea to swallow them, and they drowned while you watched. You lived in the desert for a long time,
translation_verse: bɛzunle bɛvɛlɛle me kɛ memboa bɛ, na menvale awozinli mendole bɛ nee Yigyibitima avinli. Memanle nyevile azɛlɛkye bule guale bɛ nwo zo na bɛwule. Bɛze mɔɔ menvale menyɛle Yigyibitima la. “ ‘Bɛdɛnlanle ɛsɛlɛ ne azo bɛhyɛle dɔɔnwo.

english_verse: then I brought you into the land east of the Jordan River. The Amorites were living there, and they fought you. But with my help, you defeated them, wiped them out, and took their land.
translation_verse: Akee menvale bɛ membale Amɔlema azɛlɛ zo wɔ Dwɔdan aduduleɛ. Amɔlema nee bɛ honle, noko memanle bɛlile Amɔlema anwo zo konim. Bɛvale Amɔlema azɛlɛ ne, na mɔɔ bɛkɛze kɛ bɛkɔ bɛ nyunlu la ɛnee melɛsɛkye bɛ kpɔvolɛma ne meamaa bɛ.

english_verse: King Balak decided that his nation Moab would go to war against you, so he asked Balaam to come and put a curse on you.
translation_verse: Akee Zepɔ ara Balake, mɔɔ le Mowabe belemgbunli ne, ɔdaye ɔ nee bɛ rahonle. Ɔmanle Biyɔ ara Beelam dele na ɔzɛlɛle ye kɛ ɔhye bɛ sili.

english_verse: But I wouldn't listen to Balaam, and I rescued you by making him bless you instead of curse you.
translation_verse: Na meandie Beelam, yemɔti ɔyilale bɛ; adenle ɛhye azo yɛɛ mempenle menliele bɛ ngoane wɔ Balake asa anu a.

english_verse: You crossed the Jordan River and came to Jericho. The rulers of Jericho fought you, and so did the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites. I helped you defeat them all.
translation_verse: Bɛpɛle Azule Dwɔdan ne bɛrale Gyɛleko. Gyɛlekoma nee bɛ honle; zɔhane ala yɛɛ Amɔlema, Pɛlɛzema, Keenama, Hɛtema, Gɛgahyema, Haevaema, yɛɛ Gyibɛsema noko nee bɛ honle a. Na memanle bɛlile bɛ muala bɛ nwo zo konim.

english_verse: Your enemies ran from you, but not because you had swords and bows and arrows. I made your enemies panic and run away, as I had done with the two Amorite kings east of the Jordan River.
translation_verse: Mekɛ mɔɔ bɛ nee Amɔle arelemgbunli nwiɔ ne ko la, membɔle bɛ ɛlɔnema ne asande, amaa bɛadu bɛ ɛkɛ ne. Tɛ bɛ anwosesebɛ anzɛɛ asɛɛ bɛze konle nye zo la ati ɔ.

english_verse: You didn't have to work for this land—I gave it to you. Now you live in towns you didn't build, and you eat grapes and olives from vineyards and trees you didn't plant.
translation_verse: Memanle bɛ azɛlɛ mɔɔ tɛ bɛ a bɛbule ye ɛhoayelɛ la, nee azuamgbole mɔɔ tɛ bɛ a bɛkyekyele la. Kɛkala, bɛde zolɛ yɛɛ bɛlɛdi vanye ma nee ɔlivi ma wɔ mbaka mɔɔ tɛ bɛ a bɛluale la azo.’ ”

english_verse: Then Joshua told the people: Worship the Lord, obey him, and always be faithful. Get rid of the idols your ancestors worshiped when they lived on the other side of the Euphrates River and in Egypt.
translation_verse: Dwɔhyua vale zɔle zolɛ kɛ, “Ye zɔhane ati bɛli Ɛdɛnkɛma eni na bɛzonle ye nɔhalɛ nu. Awozonle ne mɔ mɔɔ bɛ nlenya mɔ zonlenle bɛ wɔ Mɛsɔpɔteemea nee Yigyibiti la, bɛgua bɛ lɔ na bɛzonle Ɛdɛnkɛma angomekye.

english_verse: But if you don't want to worship the Lord, then choose here and now! Will you worship the same idols your ancestors did? Or since you're living on land that once belonged to the Amorites, maybe you'll worship their gods. I won't. My family and I are going to worship and obey the Lord!
translation_verse: Saa bɛ kunlu ɛndwo kɛ bɛkɛzonle ye a, ɛnee ɛnɛ demua ye, bɛhile mɔɔ bɛkɛzonle ye la, awozonle ne mɔ mɔɔ bɛ nlenya mɔ zonlenle bɛ wɔ Mɛsɔpɔteemea la anzɛɛ saa Amɔlema mɔɔ bɛ azɛlɛ zo a bɛde la awozonle ne mɔ a. Na mame, me nee me sua nu amra, yɛbazonle Ɛdɛnkɛma.”

english_verse: The people answered: We could never worship other gods or stop worshiping the Lord.
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma ne buale kɛ, “Yɛnrɛgyakyi Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛnrɛzonle awozonle fee!

english_verse: The Lord is our God. We were slaves in Egypt as our ancestors had been, but we saw the Lord work miracles to set our people free and to bring us out of Egypt. Even though other nations were all around us, the Lord protected us wherever we went.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛ Nyamenle ne a yele yɛ nlenya mɔ nee yɛdayɛ vile ahanra ɛzonlenlɛ nu wɔ Yigyibiti a, yɛɛ yɛnwunle nwanwane ninyɛne mɔɔ ɔyɛle la. Ɛdɛnkɛma bɔle yɛ nwo bane wɔ maanle maanle mɔɔ yɛluale bɛ avinli yɛrale la asa anu.

english_verse: And when we fought the Amorites and the other nations that lived in this land, the Lord made them run away. Yes, we will worship and obey the Lord, because the Lord is our God.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ yɛba maanle ye anu la, Ɛdɛnkɛma lumuale yɛ nyunlu, ɔvoanle Amɔlema mɔɔ de ɛke la amuala. Yemɔti yɛdayɛ yɛbazonle Ɛdɛnkɛma; yemɔ a ɔle yɛ Nyamenle a.”

english_verse: If you turn your backs on the Lord and worship the gods of other nations, the Lord will turn against you. He will make terrible things happen to you and wipe you out, even though he had been good to you before.
translation_verse: yemɔti saa bɛgyakyi ye na bɛkɔsonle nyamenle gyɛne biala anzɛɛ awozonle a, ɔbahakyi ɔ nzi yeazi bɛ na yeadea bɛ. Ɔnvane ɔ nwo kɛ yeyɛ kpalɛ yemaa bɛ ɛlɛ, ɔbazɛkye bɛ.”

english_verse: But the people shouted, “We won't worship any other gods. We will worship and obey only the Lord!”
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma ne hanle hilele Dwɔhyua kɛ, “Yɛmɛ, yɛtua yɛ nzo! Yɛbazonle Ɛdɛnkɛma.”

english_verse: Joshua said, “You have heard yourselves say that you will worship and obey the Lord. Isn't that true?” “Yes, it's true,” they answered.
translation_verse: Dwɔhyua zele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛdabɛ bɛdi daselɛ kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ala a bɛbazonle ye a.” Bɛbuale ye kɛ, “Ɛhɛe, yɛdi daselɛ.”

english_verse: Joshua said, “But you still have some idols, like those the other nations worship. Get rid of your idols! You must decide once and for all that you really want to obey the Lord God of Israel.”
translation_verse: Dwɔhyua zele bɛ kɛ, “Ɛnee bɛvuandi awozonle ne mɔ mɔɔ bɛlɛ la bɛgua, na bɛvua bɛhile Ɛdɛnkɛma, Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne kɛ bɛbali nɔhalɛ bɛamaa ye.”

english_verse: The people said, “The Lord is our God, and we will worship and obey only him.”
translation_verse: Menli ne zele Dwɔhyua kɛ, “Yɛbazonle Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛ Nyamenle ne. Yɛbali ye mɛla ne mɔ azo.”

english_verse: Joshua helped Israel make an agreement with the Lord that day at Shechem. Joshua made laws for Israel
translation_verse: Kenle ko ne Dwɔhyua nee menli ne yɛle ngyehyɛlɛ wɔ Hyikɛm na ɔvale mɛla ɔmanle bɛ kɛ bɛli zolɛ.

english_verse: and wrote them down in The Book of the Law of God. Then he set up a large stone under the oak tree at the place of worship in Shechem
translation_verse: Dwɔhyua hɛlɛle mɛla ne mɔ wɔ Nyamenle Mɛla Buluku ne anu. Akee ɔvale bolɛ ko ɔdole oku baka kpole ne mɔɔ gyi Ɛdɛnkɛma Ɛleka Nwuanzanwuanza ne la abo,

english_verse: and told the people, “Look at this stone. It has heard everything that the Lord has said to us. Our God can call this stone as a witness if we ever reject him.”
translation_verse: na ɔzele Yizilayɛma amuala kɛ, “Bolɛ ɛhye bayɛ yɛ daselɛ. Yede edwɛkɛ mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛha ɛhile yɛ la amuala. Zɔhane ati ɔbayɛ daselɛ yeatia bɛ kɛ bɛkɛho bɛkɛtia bɛ Nyamenle ne a.”

english_verse: Joshua sent everyone back to their homes. Joshua, Joseph, and Eleazar Are Buried
translation_verse: Na Dwɔhyua manle menli ne mɔ hɔle, awie biala ziale hɔle ɔdaye ye sua zo. Dwɔhyua nee Ɛlieza ewule

english_verse: Not long afterwards, the Lord's servant Joshua died at the age of
translation_verse: Ɛhye anzi, Ɛdɛnkɛma sonvolɛ Dwɔhyua, Nɛn ara ne wule. Ɔlile ɛvolɛ ɛya, ɛvolɛ bulu.

english_verse: The Israelites buried him in his own land at Timnath-Serah, north of Mount Gaash in the hill country of Ephraim.
translation_verse: Bɛziele ye wɔ ɔdaye ye azɛlɛ ɛdeɛ ne azo wɔ Temenate Sila, wɔ Geeyahye Boka ne sɔlɔ, wɔ Yifelaem maanzinli nu awoka ne mɔ azo.

english_verse: As long as Joshua lived, Israel worshiped and obeyed the Lord. There were other leaders old enough to remember everything that the Lord had done for Israel. And for as long as these men lived, Israel continued to worship and obey the Lord.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ ɛnee Dwɔhyua de aze la, Yizilayɛma zonlenle Ɛdɛnkɛma, ye ewule ne anzi, mɔɔ ɛnee mgbanyinli ne mɔ mɔɔ nwunle debie biala mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛle manle Yizilayɛma la de aze la, menli ne hɔle zolɛ zonlenle Ɛdɛnkɛma.

english_verse: When the people of Israel left Egypt, they brought the bones of Joseph along with them. They took the bones to the town of Shechem and buried them in the field that Jacob had bought for
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma vale Dwosefi mbowule vile Yigyibiti rale, na bɛraziele ye wɔ Hyikɛm wɔ azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ Gyekɔbo dɔle wɔ Heemɔ amra mrenya ne mɔ lɔ la azo. Heemɔ le Hyikɛm ɔ ze, na bɛdɔle azɛlɛ ne dwɛtɛ fufule ɛya. Azɛlɛ zɔhane, Dwosefi abo zo amra a vale a.

english_verse: When Eleazar the priest died, he was buried in the hill country of Ephraim on a hill that belonged to his son Phinehas.
translation_verse: Aalɔn ara Ɛlieza wule na bɛziele ye wɔ Gebɛya. Gebɛya le sua wɔ Yifelaem maanzinli nu awoka ne mɔ azo. Ɛkɛ ne azɛlɛ ne, bɛvale bɛmanle ɔ ra Fenɛhaze.

english_verse: After the death of Joshua, the Israelites asked the Lord, “Which of our tribes should attack the Canaanites first?”
translation_verse: Dwɔhyua wule la, Yizilayɛma bizale Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ, “Nwane yɛɛ ɛlumua ɛhɔteta Keenama ɔ nee bɛ ɛho a?”

english_verse: “Judah!” the Lord answered. “I'll help them take the land.”
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma buale kɛ, “Dwuda yɛɛ balumua a; bɛnlea, meye maanle ne memaa ye.”

english_verse: The people of Judah went to their relatives, the Simeon tribe, and said, “Canaanites live in the land God gave us. Help us fight them, and we will help you.” Troops from Simeon came to help Judah.
translation_verse: Na Dwuda zele ɔ diema Semɛyɔn kɛ, “Maa yɛhɔ maanle ne mɔɔ bɛva bɛmaa yɛ la anu yɛ nee Keenama ɛhɔho, na yɛwie a medame noko me nee wɔ ahɔ wɔ maanle ɛdeɛ ne mɔɔ bɛva bɛmaa wɔ la anu.” Yemɔti Semɛyɔn nee

english_verse: After that, they attacked the Canaanites who lived at Hebron, defeating the three clans called Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai. At that time, Hebron was called Kiriath-Arba.
translation_verse: Na Dwudama hɔtetale Keenama mɔɔ wɔ Hibulɔn mɔɔ ɛnee bɛfɛlɛ ye Keleate Aaba la, na bɛlile Hyihyae, Ahaeman, yɛɛ Talemae asa azo ne mɔ anwo zo konim. Ɔteneɛle di suakpole Dibɛ anwo zo konim (Dwɔ

english_verse: The king tried to escape, but soldiers from Judah caught him. They cut off his thumbs and big toes,
translation_verse: Adonaebizɛke nriandile, na bɛvoanle ye dedee bɛhyele ye, na bɛpepɛle ɔ sa nee ɔ gyakɛ ahohotile ne mɔ.

english_verse: They attacked Jerusalem, captured it, killed everyone who lived there, and then burned it to the ground.
translation_verse: Dwudama nee Gyɛlusalɛmma honle na bɛbole Gyɛlusalɛmma bɛvale sua ne. Bɛhunle menli mɔɔ wɔ zolɛ la na bɛyelale suakpole ne.

english_verse: Judah's army fought the Canaanites who lived in the hill country, the Southern Desert, and the foothills to the west.
translation_verse: Nzinlii Dwudama hɔle na bɛ nee Keenama mɔɔ gua awoka ne mɔ azo, awoka ne mɔ ndololeɛ nu, yɛɛ azɛlɛ fɛɛnye ne azo la hɔhonle.

english_verse: From Hebron, Judah's army went to attack Debir, which at that time was called Kiriath-Sepher.
translation_verse: Bɛvi ɛkɛ ne la Dwuda nee ye ɛlɔnema hɔtetale Dibɛ. Duma mɔɔ dɛba ne bɛfa bɛfɛlɛ Dibɛ la a le Keleate Sifɛ.

english_verse: Caleb told his troops, “The man who captures Kiriath-Sepher can marry my daughter Achsah.”
translation_verse: Na Kalɛbe hanle kɛ, “Awie biala mɔɔ kɛteta Keleate Sifɛ na ɔkɛli konim la menwɔva me ra raalɛ Akesa menwɔmaa ɔkɛgya ye.”

english_verse: Caleb's nephew Othniel captured Kiriath-Sepher, so Caleb let him marry Achsah. Othniel was the son of Caleb's younger brother Kenaz.
translation_verse: Na Kalɛbe adiema kakula ne mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye Kinaze la ara nrenya Ɔteneɛle hɔhonle vale sua ne, na Kalɛbe vale ɔ ra raalɛ Akesa manle ɔgyale ye.

english_verse: Right after the wedding, Achsah started telling Othniel that he ought to ask her father for a field. She went to see her father, and while she was getting down from her donkey, Caleb asked, “What's bothering you?”
translation_verse: Wɔ atɔfolɛlielɛ ne anu, Ɔteneɛle zele ɔ ye kɛ ɔbiza ɔ ze ɔlie azɛlɛ. Zɔhane ati Akesa vi ye asoaso ne azo dwule aze, na Kalɛbe bizale ye kɛ, “Duzu a ɛkpondɛ a?”

english_verse: She answered, “I need your help. The land you gave me is in the Southern Desert, so please give me some spring-fed ponds for a water supply.” Caleb gave her a couple of small ponds named Higher Pond and Lower Pond.
translation_verse: Ɔbuale kɛ, “Maa me ahyɛlɛdeɛ. Kɛmɔ wɔva nyiakɛ azɛlɛ azo resee ne wɔmaa me la ɛnee maa me ɛleka mɔɔ nzule wɔ la.” Na Kalɛbe vale sua ne sɔlɔ nee nyiakɛ nzubula ne mɔ manle ye. Dwuda nee Bɛngyaman mbusua ekpunli ne mɔ konimlilɛ

english_verse: The people who belonged to the Kenite clan were the descendants of the father-in-law of Moses. They left Jericho with the people of Judah and settled near Arad in the Southern Desert of Judah not far from the Amalekites.
translation_verse: Kinanli ne mɔɔ Mosisi gya ɔ ra raalɛ la abo zo amra nee Dwudama vi suakpole Gyɛleko, suakpole mɔɔ mrɛlɛ nee mrelehyia ngome la azo, na bɛhɔle azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ ɛhwie, mɔɔ zua Ɛlade la azo na bɛ nee menli ne hɔdɛnlanle.

english_verse: Judah's army helped Simeon's army attack the Canaanites who lived at Zephath. They completely destroyed the town and renamed it Hormah.
translation_verse: Dwuda nee ɔ diema Semɛyɔn hɔle Zifate na bɛhɔlile Keenama mɔɔ wɔ ɛkɛ ne la anwo zo konim na bɛbɔle sua ne bɔkɔɔ. Yemɔti bɛvɛlɛle suakpole ne Hɔɔma.

english_verse: The Lord helped the army of Judah capture Gaza, Ashkelon, Ekron, and the land near those towns. They also took the hill country. But the people who lived in the valleys had iron chariots, so Judah was not able to make them leave or to take their land.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma lile Dwuda anzi manle ɔvale maanle ne mɔɔ gua awoka ne mɔ azo la amuala, noko yeangola menli mɔɔ wɔ fienemgbole ne anu la tu, ɔluakɛ bɛlɛ mbulalɛ ehwili mɔɔ bɛfa bɛko la.

english_verse: The Jebusites were living in Jerusalem, and the Benjamin tribe did not defeat them or capture the town. That's why Jebusites still live in Jerusalem along with the people of Benjamin. The Ephraim and Manasseh Tribes Capture Bethel
translation_verse: Bɛngyaman asa azo ɛdeɛ ne, bɛandu Gyibɛsema mɔɔ wɔ Gyɛlusalɛm la; yemɔti Gyibɛsema nee Bɛngyamanema ɛdɛnla toonwo a yeradwu ɛnɛ a. Yifelaem nee Manasɛ mbusua ekpunli ne mɔ di Bɛtɛle anwo zo konim

english_verse: The Ephraim and Manasseh tribes were getting ready to attack Bethel, which at that time was called Luz. And the Lord helped them when they sent spies to find out as much as they could about Bethel.
translation_verse: Yifelaem abusua ekpunli ne noko hɔtetale Bɛtɛlema, na Ɛdɛnkɛma lile bɛ nzi. Dwosefi asa azo ne mɔ lumuale zoanle menli kɛ bɛhɔli busia bɛnlea kɛ Bɛtɛle azɛlɛ ne si de la. .

english_verse: While the spies were watching the town, a man came out, and they told him, “If you show us how our army can get into the town, we will make sure that you aren't harmed.”
translation_verse: Busiama ne nwunle kɛ nrenya bie vi suakpole ne azo ɛvinde ɛlɛba. Bɛzele nrenya ne kɛ, “Yɛsɛlɛ wɔ, kile yɛ suakpole ne azo adenle ne na yɛbayɛ wɔ boɛ.”

english_verse: The man showed them, and the two Israelite tribes attacked Bethel, killing everyone except the man and his family. The two tribes made the man and his family leave,
translation_verse: Nrenya ne hilele bɛ suakpole ne azo adenle. Bɛhunle ezuavolɛ ne kɔsɔɔti na bɛgyakyile nrenya ne nee ɔ ye nee ɔ mra.

english_verse: so they went to the land of the Hittites, where he built a town. He named the town Luz, and that is still its name. Israel Does Not Get Rid of All the Canaanites
translation_verse: Nrenya ne akee hɔle Hɛtema maanle nu, ɔhɔkyekyele sua bieko na ɔdonle ye Lɛɛze, na ɛnɛ nee ɛnɛ ala kɛ bɛfɛlɛ sua ne la ɛne. Menli mɔɔ Yizilayɛma andu bɛ la

english_verse: The Ephraim tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Gezer, so the Canaanites lived there with Israelites all around them.
translation_verse: Yifelaem abusua ekpunli ne anu amra noko andu Keenama mɔɔ wɔ Gizɛ la. Keenama dɛnlanle Gizɛ ɛkɛ ne ala.

english_verse: The Zebulun tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Kitron and Nahalol, and the Canaanites stayed there with Israelites around them. But the people of Zebulun did force the Canaanites into slave labor.
translation_verse: Zɛbulɛn abusua ekpunli ne anu amra andu menli mɔɔ wɔ Ketelɔn la. Eza bɛandu Neehalɔnoma. Bɛ nee Keenama ne dɛnlanle na bɛmanle bɛyɛle akɛlɛ gyima.

english_verse: The Asher tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Acco, Sidon, Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik, and Rehob, and the Asher tribe lived with Canaanites all around them.
translation_verse: Ahya abusua ekpunli ne anu amra dɛnlanle Keenama mɔɔ de maanle ne anu la avinli. Bɛandu bɛ.

english_verse: The Naphtali tribe did not get rid of the Canaanites who lived in Beth-Shemesh and Beth-Anath, but they did force the Canaanites into slave labor. The Naphtali tribe lived with Canaanites around them.
translation_verse: Nafetalae abusua ekpunli ne anu amra andu menli mɔɔ wɔ Bɛte Hyimɛhye la yɛɛ bɛandu Bɛtanatema. Nafetalaema nee Keenama mɔɔ de azɛlɛ ne azo la dɛnlanle na bɛmanle Bɛte Hyimɛhyema nee Bɛtanatema yɛle akɛlɛ gyima manle Yizilayɛma.

english_verse: The Amorites were strong enough to keep the tribe of Dan from settling in the valleys, so Dan had to stay in the hill country.
translation_verse: Amɔlema voanle Dan abusua ekpunli ne anu amra manle bɛhɔle azua mɔɔ gua awoka ne mɔ azo la azo, ɔluakɛ bɛammaa bɛ adenle bɛammaa bɛamba azɛlɛ fɛɛnye ne azo.

english_verse: The Amorites on Mount Heres and in Aijalon and Shaalbim were also determined to stay. Later on, as Ephraim and Manasseh grew more powerful, they forced those Amorites into slave labor. The Amorite-Edomite Border
translation_verse: Amɔlema bɔle mɔdenle kɛ bɛtɛnla Hilɛse Boka ne azo wɔ Ayegyalɔn nee Hyeeyalebem, na Yifelaem abo zo amra asa homonle bɛ nwo zo na bɛmanle bɛyɛle akɛlɛ gyima.

english_verse: The old Amorite-Edomite border used to go from Sela through Scorpion Pass into the hill country.
translation_verse: Yidɔmma ɛweɛne ne vi Akelabem anwuma, ɔlua Silaa ɔkɔ ye sɔlɔ lɔ.

english_verse: The Lord's angel went from Gilgal to Bochim and gave the Israelites this message from the Lord: I promised your ancestors that I would give this land to their families, and I brought your people here from Egypt. We made an agreement that I promised never to break,
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma soanvolɛ vi Gelegale hɔle Bokem. Ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Menyele bɛ menvile Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo, me nee bɛ rale azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ menvale membɔle bɛ mgbanyima ɛwɔkɛ la azo. Menganle kɛ, ‘Menrɛtulu ngyekyeleɛ ne mɔɔ me nee bɛ kyekyele la ɛlɛ,

english_verse: and you promised not to make any peace treaties with the other nations that live in the land. Besides that, you agreed to tear down the altars where they sacrifice to their idols. Why haven't you kept your promise?
translation_verse: yɛɛ bɛdabɛ noko bɛ nee menli mɔɔ de azɛlɛ ye azo la mmayɛ ngyehyɛlɛ biala, na bɛbubu bɛ azukponle ne mɔ.’ Noko bɛanli me mɛla ne azo. Bɛdabɛ bɛnlea bɛ nyɛleɛ mɔɔ bɛyɛ la.

english_verse: And so, I'll stop helping you defeat your enemies. Instead, they will be there to trap you into worshiping their idols.
translation_verse: Zɔhane ati mese, menrɛvoa menli ɛhye mɔ. Bɛbayɛ bɛ nwo ɛlɔne, na bɛ awozonle ne mɔ bayɛ ngane amaa bɛ.”

english_verse: and they offered sacrifices to the Lord. From then on, they called that place “Crying.” Israel Stops Worshiping the Lord
translation_verse: Na bɛvɛlɛle ɛleka zɔhane Bokem, na bɛbɔle azu wɔ ɛkɛ ne bɛmanle Ɛdɛnkɛma. Dwɔhyua ewule

english_verse: Joshua had been faithful to the Lord. And after Joshua sent the Israelites to take the land they had been promised, they remained faithful to the Lord until Joshua died at the age of
translation_verse: Bɛziele ye wɔ ɔdaye ye azɛlɛ zo wɔ Temenate Sila wɔ Yifelaem maanzinli nu, Geeyahye boka ne sɔlɔ.

english_verse: After a while the people of Joshua's generation died, and the next generation did not know the Lord or any of the things he had done for Israel.
translation_verse: Na awolɛndoazo zɔhane anu amra amuala wule, na awolɛndoazo fofolɛ mɔɔ ɛnze Ɛdɛnkɛma anzɛɛ ɛnze gyima mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛli ɛmaa Yizilayɛma la dwazole. Yizilayɛma gyakyi Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛzonlenlɛ

english_verse: with the Israelites that he let other nations raid Israel and steal their crops and other possessions. Enemies were everywhere, and the Lord always let them defeat Israel in battle. The Lord had warned Israel he would do this, and now the Israelites were miserable. The Lord Chooses Leaders for Israel
translation_verse: Kɛmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma kɔkɔ ne mɔɔ ɔbɔle bɛ, nee ye ndane ne mɔɔ ɔhanle ɔdole zolɛ la se la, mekɛ biala mɔɔ Yizilayɛma kɛhɔ konle nloa la, Ɛdɛnkɛma ko tia bɛ wɔ bɛ munzule ɛbɛla ne ati, na bɛnwunle amaneɛ kpole.

english_verse: From time to time, the Lord would choose special leaders known as judges. These judges would lead the Israelites into battle and defeat the enemies that made raids on them.
translation_verse: Nzinlii akee Ɛdɛnkɛma manle Yizilayɛma nyianle menli lile bɛ ti na bɛliele bɛ bɛvile nwule ne mɔ asa anu.

english_verse: In years gone by, the Israelites had been faithful to the Lord, but now they were quick to be unfaithful and to refuse even to listen to these judges. The Israelites disobeyed the Lord, and instead of worshiping him, they worshiped other gods.
translation_verse: Noko bɛandie menli mɔɔ lile bɛ ti la aneɛ. Bɛanli nɔhalɛ bɛammaa Ɛdɛnkɛma. Bɛhɔlile nyamenle gyɛne bie mɔ anzi na bɛzonlenle bɛ. Bɛanva adenle ne mɔɔ bɛ mgbanyima ne mɔ luale nu zonlenle Ɛdɛnkɛma la anu. Bɛ ze mɔ lile Ɛdɛnkɛma mɛla ne mɔ azo, na bɛmɛ, bɛanli zo fee.

english_verse: When enemies made life miserable for the Israelites, the Lord felt sorry for them. He would choose a judge and help that judge rescue Israel from its enemies. The Lord was kind to Israel as long as that judge lived.
translation_verse: Mekɛ biala mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛmaa bɛ sonla kɛ ɔli bɛ ti la, ɔ nee ye dua na ɔdie Yizilayɛma ɔfi bɛ kpɔvolɛma asa anu, wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ahenle mɔɔ li bɛ ti la de aze la. Ɔluakɛ ɔyɛ na bɛkile bɛ nyane nee abodelɛ na bɛse kɛ bɛsu a ɛnee ɔyɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma alɔbɔlɛ.

english_verse: But afterwards, the Israelites would become even more sinful than their ancestors had been. The Israelites were stubborn—they simply would not stop worshiping other gods or following their teachings. The Lord Lets Enemies Test Israel
translation_verse: Noko mekɛ biala mɔɔ ahenle mɔɔ li bɛ ti la kɛwu la, ɛnee bɛzia bɛ nzi bɛlɛbɔ bɛ munzule ɛbɛla ne bieko, na bɛyɛ bɔbɔ bɛmaa ɔtɛla dɛba ne mɔɔ bɛ ze mɔ yɛle la. Bɛtoɔdoa nyamenle gyɛne gyɛne, bɛsonle bɛ, na bɛbɔ bɛ ti aze bɛmaa bɛ. Bɛangyakyi bɛ ninyɛndane nee anzosesebɛ ne mɔ ɛyɛlɛ.

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel and said: The Israelites have broken the agreement I made with their ancestors. They won't obey me,
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma vale Yizilayɛma anwo ɛya na ɔzele kɛ, “Kɛmɔ menli ɛhye mɔ ɛtulu me ngyekyeleɛ ne mɔɔ me nee bɛ ze mɔ kyekyele, na bɛandie me ne la,

english_verse: so I'll stop helping them defeat their enemies. Israel still had a lot of enemies when Joshua died,
translation_verse: menrɛli bɛ nyunlu menrɛdu menli mɔɔ ɛha azɛlɛ ne azo mɔɔ Dwɔhyua wule gyakyile bɛ ɛkɛ ne la,

english_verse: and I'm going to let those enemies stay. I'll use them to test Israel, because then I can find out if Israel will worship and obey me as their ancestors did.
translation_verse: amaa meava meazɔ Yizilayɛma meanlea kɛ bɛkɛli medame Ɛdɛnkɛma, me mɛla zo, kɛmɔ bɛ ze mɔ lile zolɛ la anzɛɛ bɛnrɛyɛ.”

english_verse: That's why the Lord had not let Joshua get rid of those enemy nations all at once.
translation_verse: Zɔhane ati Ɛdɛnkɛma gyakyile maanle maanle zɔhane mɔ wɔ azɛlɛ ne azo. Yeandu bɛ ɛkɛ ne ala, yɛɛ yeanva bɛ yeanwula Dwɔhyua tumi ne abo.

english_verse: And the Lord had another reason for letting these enemies stay. The Israelites needed to learn how to fight in war, just as their ancestors had done. Each new generation would have to learn by fighting
translation_verse: Ɔyɛle ɛhye kɛ ɔfa yeahile Yizilayɛma awolɛndoazo ne mɔ konle deɛ holɛ, na bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛtɛnwunle konle ɛlɛ la anwu kɛ konle si de la.

english_verse: the Philistines and their five rulers, as well as the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites that lived in the Lebanon Mountains from Mount Baal-Hermon to Hamath Pass.
translation_verse: Maanle maanle ne mɔ ɛne: Filisitia arelemgbunli nnu ne, Keenama amuala, Saedɛnema, yɛɛ Haevaema mɔɔ gua Lɛbanɔn Boka ne azo la, ɔvi Beeyale Hɛmɔn Boka toonwo mɔɔ kɔdwu Heemate Ademgbolezo la.

english_verse: Moses had told the Israelites what the Lord had commanded them to do, and now the Lord was using these nations to find out if Israel would obey.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛle ɛhye mɔ amuala kɛ ɔfa yeazɔ Yizilayɛma yeanlea saa bɛkɛli mɛla ne mɔ mɔɔ ɔluale Mosisi anwo zo ɔvale ɔmanle bɛ ze mɔ la azo a.

english_verse: But they refused. And some of them even married Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites who lived all around them. That's how they started worshiping foreign gods. Othniel
translation_verse: na bɛgyale menli ne mɔ amra mraalɛ, na bɛdabɛ noko bɛvale bɛ mra mraalɛ bɛmanle menli ne mɔ amra mrenya gyale bɛ; na Yizilayɛma zonlenle menli ne mɔ nyamenle ne mɔ. Ɔteneɛle

english_verse: The Israelites sinned against the Lord by forgetting him and worshiping idols of Baal and Astarte.
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma arɛle vile Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne. Bɛbɔle munzule ɛbɛla bɛtiale Ɛdɛnkɛma na bɛzonlenle awozonle Beeyale nee Ahyela ananze ne mɔ.

english_verse: This made the Lord angry, so he let Israel be defeated by King Cushan Rishathaim of northern Syria, who ruled Israel eight years and made everyone pay taxes.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Ɛdɛnkɛma vale Yizilayɛma anwo ɛya kpole kpalɛ. Ɔsɛmanle bɛ ɔwulale Kuhyan Relehyateeyem, mɔɔ le Mɛsɔpɔteemea belemgbunli ne asa anu. Na Yizilayɛma zonlenle Kuhyan Relehyateeyem toonwo ɛvolɛ mɔtwɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites begged the Lord for help, and so he chose Othniel to rescue them. Othniel was the son of Caleb's younger brother Kenaz.
translation_verse: Na Yizilayɛma zunle vɛlɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma, na Ɛdɛnkɛma yele Kinaze ara Ɔteneɛle, mɔɔ le Kalɛbe adiema kakula la manle ɔliele bɛ.

english_verse: and Israel was at peace until Othniel died about
translation_verse: Na akee anzonudwolɛ rale maanle ne anu ɛvolɛ abulanla. Na Kinaze ara Ɔteneɛle wule. Yihɛde

english_verse: Once more the Israelites started disobeying the Lord. So he let them be defeated by King Eglon of Moab,
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma ɛtane mɔɔ yɛle la akee bole zolɛ wɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlu. Zɔhane ati Ɛdɛnkɛma kpogyale Mowabe Belemgbunli Ɛgelɔn asa zo.

english_verse: who had joined forces with the Ammonites and the Amalekites to attack Israel. Eglon and his army captured Jericho.
translation_verse: Ɛgelɔn nee Amɔnoma nee Amalɛkema bɔle nu na bɛvale konle bɛdoale Yizilayɛma, bɛhanle bɛ senle dwɛɛ, na bɛvale Gyɛleko mɔɔ ɛkɛ ne le mrɛlɛ nee mrelehyia ngome la.

english_verse: Then he ruled Israel for
translation_verse: Na Yizilayɛma zonlenle Mowabe Belemgbunli Ɛgelɔn ɛvolɛ bulu nee mɔtwɛ.

english_verse: Ehud and some other Israelites took the taxes to Eglon, who was a very fat man. As soon as they gave the taxes to Eglon, Ehud said it was time to go home.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Yihɛde vale adwule anzɛɛ ahyɛlɛdeɛ ne manle ye la, ɔmanle menli mɔɔ zoale ninyɛne ne rale la ziale bɛ nzi hɔle.

english_verse: Ehud went with the other Israelites as far as the statues at Gilgal. Then he turned back and went upstairs to the room where Eglon had his throne. Ehud said, “Your Majesty, I need to talk with you in private.” Eglon replied, “Don't say anything yet!” His officials left the room, and Eglon stood up as Ehud came closer. “Yes,” Ehud said, “I have a message for you from God!”
translation_verse: Akee ɔhale belemgbunli ne angome wɔ ye ekpumgbunli ɛdeɛ ne anu. Ye ekpumgbunli ɛdeɛ ne wɔ sua ne ati zo, na ɛkɛ ne le fɔɔnwo zɛhae. Yihɛde hɔle ɔ nwo ɛkɛ hɔzele ye kɛ, “Melɛ Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ melɛbɛlɛ wɔ.” Belemgbunli ne vi ye ebia ne anu dwazole,

english_verse: Ehud pulled out the dagger with his left hand and shoved it so far into Eglon's stomach
translation_verse: na Yihɛde nee ye yɛle kyɛlɛ, na ɔvale ɔ sa bɛne ɔhwenle dadeɛ ne wɔ ye ɛzɔlɛ nwo ɔwɔle belemgbunli ne akunlu.

english_verse: and left. When the king's officials came back and saw that the doors were locked, they said, “The king is probably inside relieving himself.”
translation_verse: na ɔhɔle. Nzinlii belemgbunli ne sonvolɛma ne rale, na mɔɔ bɛnwunle kɛ bɛtoto nlenkɛ ne mɔ anu la bɛdwenlenle kɛ, “Kabezɛ ɔlɛsɔho ɔ gyakɛ.”

english_verse: They stood there waiting until they felt foolish, but Eglon still didn't open the doors. Finally, they unlocked the doors and found King Eglon lying dead on the floor.
translation_verse: Akee bɛzule bɛ sa toonwo ɔhɔdwule mekɛ mɔɔ bɛnea a kabezɛ yewie na yevinde la, na bɛhɔdukuedukuele nlenkɛ ne mɔ. Na nea, belemgbunli ne a la azɛlɛ ne anwo la; yewu!

english_verse: But by that time, Ehud had already escaped past the statues. Ehud went to the town of Seirah
translation_verse: Mekɛ mɔɔ bɛlɛkendɛ bɛamaa belemgbunli ne avinde la ɛnee Yihɛde ɛhɔ dɛbadɛba; yepɛ nu ɛleka mɔɔ awolɛ ananze ne mɔ wɔ la, yenriandi yehɔ Siayela.

english_verse: in the hill country of Ephraim and started blowing a trumpet as a signal to call the Israelites together. When they came, he shouted, “Follow me! The Lord will help us defeat the Moabites.” The Israelites followed Ehud down to the Jordan valley, and they captured the places where people cross the river on the way to Moab. They would not let anyone go across,
translation_verse: Ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛdoa me, ɔluakɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛye bɛ kpɔvolɛma, mɔɔ le Mowabema ne ɛmaa bɛ.” Yemɔti bɛ nee ye hɔle bɛhɔduale Mowabema adenle wɔ Dwɔdan ne anloa ɛleka mɔɔ bɛkola bɛwudwu bɛpɛ la. Bɛammaa awie ko bɔbɔ ampɛ nu.

english_verse: and before the fighting was over, they killed about
translation_verse: Bɛhunle Mowabema mɔɔ anwo yɛ se la kɛyɛ apenle bulu; kokye bɔbɔ anvi bɛ sa.

english_verse: Moab was so badly defeated that it was a long time before they were strong enough to attack Israel again. And Israel was at peace for
translation_verse: Kenle ko zɔhane Yizilayɛma lile Mowabema anwo zo konim. Na anzonudwolɛ rale maanle ne anu ɛvolɛ abulatwɛ. Hyamega

english_verse: Shamgar the son of Anath was the next to rescue Israel. In one battle, he used a sharp wooden pole to kill
translation_verse: Sonla bieko mɔɔ dwazole Yihɛde anzi lile Yizilayɛma ati la a le Enate ara Hyamega. Ɔdaye noko ɔvale baka mɔɔ bɛfa bɛka nlankɛ la ɔhonle ɔhunle Filisitiama ɛya nsia na ɔliele Yizilayɛma.

english_verse: After the death of Ehud, the Israelites again started disobeying the Lord.
translation_verse: Yihɛde ewule ne anzi, Yizilayɛma bɔle bɛ munzule ɛbɛla ne bieko tiale Ɛdɛnkɛma.

english_verse: “Stand at the entrance to the tent,” Sisera told her. “If someone comes by and asks if anyone is inside, tell them ‘No.’ ”
translation_verse: Sesɛla zele Gyeeyɛle kɛ, “Gyinla ndanlɛ sua ne anlenkɛ ne anloa. Saa awie biala babiza kɛ, ‘Awie wɔ ɛke ɔ?’ a, se ye kɛ, ‘Kyɛkyɛ.’ ”

english_verse: Deborah the wife of Lappidoth was a prophet and a leader of Israel during those days.
translation_verse: Mekɛ ne anu ɛnee Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ raalɛ bie mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye Dɛbola mɔɔ ɔ hu bɛfɛlɛ ye Lapedo la a le Yizilayɛma ndɛnebuavolɛ a.

english_verse: She would sit under Deborah's Palm Tree between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, where Israelites would come and ask her to settle their legal cases.
translation_verse: Ɔta ɔtɛnla “Dɛbola” arɛlɛ bo. Arɛlɛ zɔhane gyi Releema nee Bɛtɛle mɔɔ gua Yifelaem awoka ne mɔ azo la avinli. Ɛkɛ ne yɛɛ saa Yizilayɛma bie mɔ nyia edwɛkɛ a bɛkɔ bɛmaa ɔsiezie ɔmaa bɛ a.

english_verse: One day, Barak the son of Abinoam was in Kedesh in Naphtali, and Deborah sent word for him to come and talk with her. When he arrived, she said: I have a message for you from the Lord God of Israel! You are to get together an army of
translation_verse: Kenle ko ɔzoanle ɔmanle bɛhɔvɛlɛle Abenoam mɔɔ vi Kidɛhye mɔɔ wɔ Nafetalae la ara nrenya Balake na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma, Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne se menze wɔ kɛ, ‘Kɔ kɔboɔboa wɔ ɛlɔnema ne anloa wɔ Teebɔ Boka ne azo. Ye menli apenle bulu fi Nafetalae nee Zɛbulɛn mbusua ekpunli ne mɔ anu.

english_verse: The Lord will trick Sisera into coming out to fight you at the Kishon River. Sisera will be leading King Jabin's army as usual, and they will have their chariots, but the Lord has promised to help you defeat them.
translation_verse: Na mebamaa Safohyenlema Kpanyinli Sesɛla, mɔɔ nea Gyeeben ɛlɔnema ne azo la ava ye ɛlɔnema nee ye konle mbulalɛ ehwili ne mɔ arayia wɔ azule Kaehyɔn ne anloa na meamaa wɔali ɔ nwo zo konim.’ ”

english_verse: “All right, I'll go!” she replied. “But I'm warning you that the Lord is going to let a woman defeat Sisera, and no one will honor you for winning the battle.” Deborah and Barak left for Kedesh,
translation_verse: Dɛbola zele ye kɛ, “Me nee wɔ kɛhɔ; noko akee, ɛnrɛnyia ɛ nyunlu wɔ konimlilɛ ne anzi, ɔluakɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma baye Sesɛla amaa raalɛzinli.” Na Dɛbola dwazole na ɔ nee Balake hɔle Kidɛhye.

english_verse: At this time, Heber of the Kenite clan was living near the village of Oak in Zaanannim, not far from Kedesh. The Kenites were descendants of Hobab, the father-in-law of Moses, but Heber had moved and had set up his tents away from the rest of the clan.
translation_verse: Mekɛ ne anu ɛnee Kinanli Hiba nee Kinama mɔɔ ɛha la avinli ɛtete, na yehɔbɔ ye nzeseɛ wɔ moa moa, baka kpole bie mɔɔ gyi Zeenanem, mɔɔ zua Kidɛhye la abo. Kinama le Hobabe, mɔɔ le Mosisi aye ne adiema nrenya la abo zo amra.

english_verse: When Sisera learned that Barak had led an army to Mount Tabor,
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Sesɛla dele kɛ Abenoam ara Balake ɛboɔboa ɛlɔnema anloa wɔ Teebɔ Boka ne azo la,

english_verse: Deborah shouted, “Barak, it's time to attack Sisera! Because today the Lord is going to help you defeat him. In fact, the Lord has already gone on ahead to fight for you.” Barak led his
translation_verse: Na Dɛbola zele Balake kɛ, “Bɛdwazo bɛhɔ, ɔluakɛ ɛnɛ kenle ye, Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛye Sesɛla ɛmaa bɛ. Ɛdɛnkɛma li bɛ nyunlu.” Zɔhane ati Balake vale ye ɛlɔnema apenle bulu ne lile ɔ nzi vi Teebɔ Boka ne azo tolole rale aze.

english_verse: And during the battle, the Lord confused Sisera, his chariot drivers, and his whole army. Everyone was so afraid of Barak and his army, that even Sisera jumped down from his chariot and tried to escape.
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma manle Balake hanle Sesɛla nee ye ɛlɔnema nee ye konle mbulalɛ ehwili ne mɔ senle dwɛɛ, na bɛhunle bɛ bie mɔ. Sesɛla vi ye konle mbulalɛ ehwili ɛdeɛ ne anu dwule na ɔvale ɔ gyakɛ ɔzɔle zolɛ.

english_verse: Only Sisera escaped. He ran to Heber's camp, because Heber and his family had a peace treaty with the king of Hazor. Sisera went to the tent that belonged to Jael, Heber's wife.
translation_verse: Sesɛla guale ndwɛlɛ aze la, ɔvale ɔ ti ɔbɔle Kinanli Hibɛ aye Gyeeyɛle ndanlɛ sua ne anwo, ɔluakɛ ɛnee anzonudwolɛ wɔ Heezɔ Belemgbunli Gyeeben nee Kinanli Hibɛ awuke nu amra avinli.

english_verse: She came out to greet him and said, “Come in, sir! Please come on in. Don't be afraid.” After they had gone inside, Sisera lay down, and Jael covered him with a blanket.
translation_verse: Gyeeyɛle vindele yiale Sesɛla na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Yɛmenle, mmasulo, bɛla; bawolo me ndanlɛ sua ye anu.” Amgba Sesɛla hɔwolole sua ne anu, na Gyeeyɛle vale ndanlɛ hedale ɔ nwo zo.

english_verse: “Could I have a little water?” he asked. “I'm thirsty.” Jael opened a leather bottle and poured him some milk, then she covered him back up.
translation_verse: Sesɛla zele Gyeeyɛle kɛ, “Mesɛlɛ wɔ, nzuhɔne ɛlɛku me! Maa me nzule ekyi meno.” Na Gyeeyɛle dule meleke nwoma kodoku ko azo manle ɔnlonle, na eza ɔhedale ɔ nwo zo bieko.

english_verse: Sisera was exhausted and soon fell fast asleep. Jael took a hammer and drove a tent-peg through his head into the ground, and he died.
translation_verse: Ɛvɛlɛ ngome manle Sesɛla lafele botoo zɛhae. Na Hibɛ aye Gyeeyɛle vale ndanlɛ sua mbaka adakola ne mɔ ko nee hamenle, ɔyɛle nyaa ɔvale Sesɛla ati ɔdole aze bɛtɛɛ, na ɔbɔle ye takola nu kyengye ɔbetanle azɛlɛ ne anwo. Na Sesɛla wule.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Barak had been following Sisera, and Jael went out to meet him. “The man you're looking for is inside,” she said. “Come in and I'll show him to you.” They went inside, and there was Sisera—dead and stretched out with a tent-peg through his skull.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Balake lɛ ɛnriandilɛ ɛlɛkpondɛ Sesɛla la, Gyeeyɛle yiale ye na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Bɛla, ahenle mɔɔ ɛkpondɛ ye la, mebahile wɔ.” Balake hɔle Gyeeyɛle ndanlɛ sua ne anu, na ɔnwunle kɛ Sesɛla ɛwu, na takola lɛ ye ketekete beta azɛlɛ ne anwo.

english_verse: Jabin grew weaker while the Israelites kept growing stronger, until at last the Israelites destroyed him.
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma asa homonle Keena Belemgbunli Gyeeben anwo zo toonwo hɔkpulale kɛ bɛhunle ɔdaye noko la.

english_verse: After the battle was over that day, Deborah and Barak sang this song:
translation_verse: Akee Dɛbola nee Abenoam ara nrenya Balake dole edwɛne ɛhye kenle ko ne:

english_verse: We praise you, Lord! Our soldiers volunteered, ready to follow you.
translation_verse: Bɛye Ɛdɛnkɛma ayɛlɛ! Yizilayɛ mgbanyima dele bɛ kunlu, menli ne yeyele bɛ kunlu honle.

english_verse: Listen, kings and rulers, while I sing for the Lord, the God of Israel.
translation_verse: Bɛmɛ arelemgbunli, bɛdie! Bɛmɛ maanle mgbanyima, bɛgyele bɛ nzo. Mebado edwɛne, meabɔ agole meamaa Yizilayɛma Nyamenle ne.

english_verse: Our Lord, God of Israel, when you came from Seir, where the Edomites live,
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma, mekɛ mɔɔ ɛvile Siyɛ, na ɛyele ɛ nwo Yidɔm azɛlɛ zo la, azɛlɛ kpusule, ezule dɔle, yɛɛ ezule vi amungu ne anu zonyinle.

english_verse: rain poured from the sky, the earth trembled, and mountains shook.
translation_verse: Awoka ne mɔ kpusule wɔ Saenae Ɛdɛnkɛma, Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne anyunlu.

english_verse: In the time of Shamgar son of Anath, and now again in Jael's time, roads were too dangerous for caravans. Travelers had to take the back roads,
translation_verse: Anate ara Hyamega mekɛ zo, Gyeeyɛle mekɛ zo, adendulɛma kpole ademgbole, bɛbule ahane ahane.

english_verse: and villagers couldn't work in their fields. Then Deborah took command, protecting Israel as a mother protects her children.
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma amuala guale ɛbɔ nu, azua kɔsɔɔti dɔle mgbane, hɔkpulale kɛ Dɛbola dwazole kɛ Yizilayɛ ɔ nli.

english_verse: The Israelites worshiped other gods, and the gates of their towns were then attacked. But they had no shields or spears to fight with.
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma nyianle bɛ nyamenle gyɛne la yɛɛ konle vale bɛ aze a. Ɛlɔnema apenle apenle abulanla, nuhua ko bɔbɔ anva enyinlike na yeayɛ atwɛ.

english_verse: I praise you, Lord, and I am grateful for those leaders and soldiers who volunteered.
translation_verse: Me ahonle la Yizilayɛ safohyenlema anwo, bɛmɛ a bɛdule bɛ nwo bɛmanle menli ne a. Ayɛlɛyelɛ ɛha Ɛdɛnkɛma.

english_verse: Listen, everyone! Whether you ride a donkey with a padded saddle or have to walk.
translation_verse: Bɛmɛ mɔɔ bɛtɛnla asoaso fufule zo, na bɛtɛnla asoaso mbia fondonloo zo, nee bɛmɛ mɔɔ bɛdua aze la, bɛbɔ nolo!

english_verse: Even those who carry water to the animals will tell you, “The Lord has won victories, and so has Israel.” Then the Lord's people marched down to the town gates
translation_verse: Bɛdie edwɛne mɔɔ bɛlɛto ye bula ne mɔ azo, bɛlɛka Ɛdɛnkɛma konimlilɛ nwo edwɛkɛ, Yizilayɛ ɛlɔnema konimlilɛ nwo edwɛkɛ ɔ. Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma menli ne to ɛlɔnwɔne tia kilikili kɔ bɛ sua zo nlenkɛ mgbole nloa.

english_verse: and said, “Deborah, let's go! Let's sing as we march. Barak, capture our enemies.”
translation_verse: Dwazo, Dɛbola, dwazo! Dwazo na kpakye ɛ ne nu to edwɛne! Dwazo, Abenoam ara Balake, fa wɔ menli ne mɔɔ wɔhye bɛ nuokɛ la kɔ.

english_verse: The Lord's people who were left joined with their leaders and fought at my side.
translation_verse: Akɛnrasesebɛma dwazole ye mrenya zo, Ɛdɛnkɛma menli ne diale ye mrenya zo, kɛ bɛ nee katakyie ne kaho.

english_verse: Troops came from Ephraim, where Amalekites once lived. Others came from Benjamin; officers and leaders came from Machir and Zebulun.
translation_verse: Bɛvi Yifelaem bɛrale bɔnza ne anu, bɛdoale wɔmɔ Bɛngyaman nee ɛ nwo amra, safohyenle mgbanyinli vi Meekɛ rale, yɛɛ Zɛbulɛn konle nu mgbanyima rale.

english_verse: The rulers of Issachar came along with Deborah, and Issachar followed Barak into the valley. But the tribe of Reuben was no help at all!
translation_verse: Yesakaa mgbanyima nee Dɛbola rale, na Yesakaa lile nɔhalɛ manle Balake. Bɛ muala bɛlile ɔ nzi bɛhɔle bɔnza ne anu. Noko Wulubɛn abusua ekpunli ne lile abunwiɔ, bɛangola bɛambɔ kpɔkɛ kɛ bɛkɛhɔ.

english_verse: Reuben, why did you stay among your sheep pens? Was it to listen to shepherds whistling for their sheep? No one could figure out why Reuben wouldn't come.
translation_verse: Duzu ati a bɛ nee mboane ne mɔ hale amozi a? Bɛtie mboaneneavolɛma mɔɔ ɛlɛfɛlɛ bɛ mboane la ɔ? Wulubɛn abusua ekpunli ne ɛli abunwiɔ, bɛangola bɛanzi kpɔkɛ kɛ bɛkɛhɔ.

english_verse: The people of Gilead stayed across the Jordan. Why did the tribe of Dan remain on their ships and the tribe of Asher stay along the coast near the harbors?
translation_verse: Gaade abusua ekpunli ne dɛnlanle Dwɔdan Aduduleɛ, Dan abusua ekpunli ne hale nyevile ne anloa, Ahya abusua ekpunli ne noko dɛnlanle ɛnwea ne anloa, na bɛhale nyevile ne anloa.

english_verse: But soldiers of Zebulun and Naphtali risked their lives to attack the enemy.
translation_verse: Na Zɛbulɛn abusua ekpunli ne vale bɛ ngoane dole nzeleba, Nafetalae abusua ekpunli ne yɛle zɔhane ala wɔ konle ne anu.

english_verse: Canaanite kings fought us at Taanach by the stream near Megiddo— but they couldn't rob us of our silver.
translation_verse: Arelemgbunli rale rahonle; Keena arelemgbunli honle wɔ Teeyanake, wɔ Mɛgedo azule ne anloa; noko dwɛtɛ fufule ɔ, bɛannyia bie.

english_verse: From their pathways in the sky the stars fought Sisera,
translation_verse: Anwuma nwɔlɔra honle, bɛlua anwomanyunlu nehane la, ɛnee bɛ nee Sesɛla ɛlɛko.

english_verse: and his soldiers were swept away by the ancient Kishon River. I will march on and be brave.
translation_verse: Kaehyɔn azuyilɛ ne pianle bɛ hɔle, Azule Kaehyɔn ɔ, ye ɛzenlɛ nu yɛ se. Akee mebava anwosesebɛ meaho meahɔ me nyunlu.

english_verse: Sisera's horses galloped off, their hoofs thundering in retreat.
translation_verse: Akee mgbɔnwɔ ne mɔ lɛ ɛnriandilɛ rale, bɛsisi bɛ ndwɛlɛ aze zɛhae ala.

english_verse: The Lord's angel said, “Put a curse on Meroz Town! Its people refused to help the Lord fight his powerful enemies.”
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma soanvolɛ ne zele ɔ, “Abule ɛbu Milɔzo, abule ɛbu menli mɔɔ wɔ zo, ɔboalekɛ bɛambamboa Ɛdɛnkɛma, bɛambamboa Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛantia katakyiema.”

english_verse: But honor Jael, the wife of Heber from the Kenite clan. Give more honor to her than to any other woman who lives in tents. Yes, give more honor to her than to any other woman.
translation_verse: Nyilalɛ ɛha Gyeeyɛle ɛdɛla mraalɛ kɔsɔɔti, Kinanli Hibɛ aye ne. Nyilalɛ ɛha ye ɛdɛla mraalɛ mɔɔ de ndanlɛ azua nu la.

english_verse: Sisera asked for water, but Jael gave him milk— cream in a fancy cup.
translation_verse: Sesɛla zɛlɛle nzule, na Gyeeyɛle manle ye meleke. Ɔmanle ye meleke kpalɛ wɔ dwora kɛnlɛma nu.

english_verse: She reached for a tent-peg and held a hammer in her right hand. And with a blow to the head, she crushed his skull.
translation_verse: Ɔdole ɔ sa ɔvale ndanlɛ sua takola, ɔvale hamenle ɔ sa fema nu; ɔbɔle takola ne ɔmianle Sesɛla ati, ɔgelegelele ɔ ti, ɔbɛtɛle ɔ nwoma.

english_verse: Sisera sank to his knees and fell dead at her feet.
translation_verse: Sesɛla anwo golole ye, ɔdɔle aze, ɔlale kɛnlanana wɔ Gyeeyɛle agyakɛ anu. Ɔgolole ɔguale Gyeeyɛle agyakɛ anu, ɔgolole ɔguale, ɔwule.

english_verse: Sisera's mother looked out through her window. “Why is he taking so long?” she asked. “Why haven't we heard his chariots coming?”
translation_verse: Sesɛla ɔ nli nleanle nvɛnzɛlɛ nu, ɔgyinlanle nvɛnzɛlɛ ne anzi ɔbizale kɛ, “Duzu ati a ye konle ehwili ne mɔ ɛhyɛ zɛhae ɛ? Duzu ati a yɛnde ye konle ehwili ne mgbɔnwɔ ne mɔ nganeɛ ɛ?”

english_verse: She and her wisest women gave the same answer:
translation_verse: Ye mraalɛ mgbanyima ne buale ye, ɔdaye mumua ne ɔzele ɔ nwo kɛ,

english_verse: “Sisera and his troops are finding treasures to bring back— a woman, or maybe two, for each man, and beautiful dresses for those women to wear.”
translation_verse: “Kabezɛ tɛ anwonyia a bɛkpondɛ bɛahyɛ bɛamaa bɛ nwo a, nrenya ko raalɛ ko anzɛɛ nrenya ko mraalɛ nwiɔ. Ndanlɛ mɔɔ sonle bolɛ mɔɔ bɛkpondɛ bɛamaa Sesɛla, nee me kɔme zo aguzo ngɛnlɛma nwiɔ mɔɔ bɛkpondɛ bɛarɛlɛ me.”

english_verse: Our Lord, we pray that all your enemies will die like Sisera. But let everyone who loves you shine brightly like the sun at dawn. Midian Steals Everything from Israel There was peace in Israel for about
translation_verse: O Ɛdɛnkɛma, maa menli mɔɔ kpɔ wɔ la abo zo ɛbɔ, na maa bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛkulo wɔ la ɛda wienyi kɛ mangyee sɛnzɛne. Na anzonudwolɛ rale maanle ne anu ɛvolɛ abulanla.

english_verse: Then once again the Israelites started disobeying the Lord, so he let the nation of Midian control Israel for seven years.
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma eza yɛle ɛtane tiale Ɛdɛnkɛma, na Ɛdɛnkɛma manle Medeanema ziele bɛ ɛvolɛ nsuu.

english_verse: Every time the Israelites planted crops, the Midianites invaded Israel together with the Amalekites and other eastern nations.
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ mekɛ biala mɔɔ Yizilayɛma kɛlua aleɛ na ɔkɛyɛ kpalɛ la, ɛnee Medeanema nee Amalɛkema nee Aduduleɛ ɛsɛlɛ ne azo amra ɛva konle ɛdoa bɛ.

english_verse: They rode in on their camels, set up their tents, and then let their livestock eat the crops as far as the town of Gaza. The Midianites stole food, sheep, cattle, and donkeys. Like a swarm of locusts, they could not be counted, and they ruined the land wherever they went.
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ saa bɛse kɛ bɛba a bɛfa bɛ nlankɛ nee ndanlɛ azua a bɛba a. Bɛ somaa maa bɛyɛ menyemenye kɛ abɛbɛ la. Menli nee afunlumu mɔɔ kɛra maanle ne anu la, awie ɛngola bɛ tia. Saa bɛba a bɛsɛkye debie biala mɔɔ wɔ ɛya ne mɔ anu la.

english_verse: The Midianites took almost everything that belonged to the Israelites, and the Israelites begged the Lord for help.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Yizilayɛma zunle vɛlɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ ɔboa bɛ, ɔlie bɛ wɔ Medeanema asa anu la,

english_verse: I am your God, and I told you not to worship Amorite gods, even though you are living in the land of the Amorites. But you refused to listen. The Lord Chooses Gideon
translation_verse: Na menzele bɛ kɛ, ‘Mame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne a, bɛmmasonle Amɔlema nyamenle ne mɔ biala.’ Noko bɛandie me ne.”

english_verse: One day an angel from the Lord went to the town of Ophrah and sat down under the big tree that belonged to Joash, a member of the Abiezer clan. Joash's son Gideon was nearby, threshing grain in a shallow pit, where he could not be seen by the Midianites.
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma soanvolɛ radɛnlanle baka kpole bie abo wɔ Ɔfela. Baka ɛhye le Dwowahye, mɔɔ le Ebayizɛ abo zo amra ne mɔ bie la ɛdeɛ. Mekɛ ne anu ɛnee Ebayizɛ ara Gedɛyɔn vea nwanyeyɛlɛ sua ne anu ɛlɛwozo atoko.

english_verse: The angel appeared and spoke to Gideon, “The Lord is helping you, and you are a strong warrior.”
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma soanvolɛ ne yele ɔ nwo hilele ye na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Nrenya katakyie, Ɛdɛnkɛma nee wɔ lua.”

english_verse: Gideon answered, “Please don't take this wrong, but if the Lord is helping us, then why have all of these awful things happened? We've heard how the Lord performed miracles and rescued our ancestors from Egypt. But those things happened long ago. Now the Lord has abandoned us to the Midianites.”
translation_verse: Gedɛyɔn zele ye kɛ, “Yɛmenle, mesɛlɛ wɔ, saa Ɛdɛnkɛma nee yɛ a lua a ɛnee duzu ati a ɛhye mɔ kɔsɔɔti ɛsisi yɛ nwo zo a? Ye nwanwane nyɛleɛ ne mɔ mɔɔ egya mɔ hanle nwolɛ edwɛkɛ hilele yɛ kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma a yele bɛ vile Yigyibiti la wɔ nienwu? Kɛkala Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛkpo yɛ na yeye yɛ yemaa Medeanema.”

english_verse: Then the Lord himself said, “Gideon, you will be strong, because I am giving you the power to rescue Israel from the Midianites.”
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma soanvolɛ ne hakyile ɔ nye zele ye kɛ, “Anwosesebɛ totohyia ɛhye mɔɔ kɛkala wɔnyia ye la, fa kɔ kɔlie Yizilayɛma fi Medeanema asa anu. Mame medame a mezoa wɔ a.”

english_verse: Gideon replied, “But how can I rescue Israel? My clan is the weakest one in Manasseh, and everyone else in my family is more important than I am.”
translation_verse: Na Gedɛyɔn buale ye kɛ, “Awulae, mesɛlɛ wɔ, kɛ menwɔzi menwɔyɛ na mealie Yizilayɛma ɛ? Nea, wɔ Manasɛ abusua ekpunli ne anu, me nlenya mɔ ala a ɛnle awie a, yɛɛ wɔ egya sua nu, medame ala a mele ekyi kpalɛ a.”

english_verse: “Gideon,” the Lord answered, “you can rescue Israel because I am going to help you! Defeating the Midianites will be as easy as beating up one man.”
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma soanvolɛ ne zele ye kɛ, “Me nee wɔ bahɔ. Ɛbahu Medeanema kɔsɔɔti kɛ asɛɛ bɛle sonla kokye ala.”

english_verse: Gideon said, “It's hard to believe that I'm actually talking to the Lord. Please do something so I'll know that you really are the Lord.
translation_verse: Na Gedɛyɔn zele ye kɛ, “Saa mezɔ ɛ nye ɛdeɛ a, ɛnee kile sɛkɛlɛneɛ kɛ amgba ɛdawɔ yɛɛ ɛ nee me ɛlɛtendɛ la.

english_verse: And wait here until I bring you an offering.” “All right, I'll wait,” the Lord answered.
translation_verse: Mesɛlɛ wɔ, mmafi ɛke ɛkɔ, kɔkpula mekɛ mɔɔ menwɔva me aleɛ ahyɛlɛdeɛ menwɔrɛlɛ wɔ la.” Ɛdɛnkɛma soanvolɛ ne zele ye kɛ, “Mebahendɛ toonwo kɔkpula mekɛ mɔɔ ɛkɛzia ɛkɛra la.”

english_verse: Gideon went home and killed a young goat, then started boiling the meat. Next, he opened a big sack of flour and made it into thin bread. When the meat was done, he put it in a basket and poured the broth into a clay cooking pot. He took the meat, the broth, and the bread and placed them under the big tree.
translation_verse: Na Gedɛyɔn hɔle sua nu hɔhunle abɔnkye donle subue; ɔvale esamo ɔdonle kpanwo mɔɔ mgbɔvonle ɛnle nu la. Ɔyeyele nane ne ɔguale kɛndɛne nu na ɔvale subue ne ɔguale siase nu, na ɔvale ɔhɔmanle Ɛdɛnkɛma soanvolɛ ne mɔɔ de baka ne abo la.

english_verse: God's angel said, “Gideon, put the meat and the bread on this rock, and pour the broth over them.” Gideon did as he was told.
translation_verse: Na Nyamenle soanvolɛ ne zele ye kɛ, “Yeye nane ne nee kpanwo ne gua bolɛ ɛhye azo, na wola subue ne gua zolɛ.” Na Gedɛyɔn yɛle ye zɔhane.

english_verse: The angel was holding a walking stick, and he touched the meat and the bread with the end of the stick. Flames jumped from the rock and burned up the meat and the bread. When Gideon looked, the angel was gone.
translation_verse: Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma soanvolɛ ne vale ye kpɔma ne mɔɔ ɔlɛ la ati hanle nane ne nee kpanwo ne, na senle vi bolɛ ne anu zɔle yelale nane ne nee kpanwo ne. Na Ɛdɛnkɛma soanvolɛ ne minliminlinle ɔ nye zo.

english_verse: Gideon realized that he had seen one of the Lord's angels. “Oh!” he moaned. “Now I'm going to die.”
translation_verse: Akee Gedɛyɔn liele lile kɛ amgba Ɛdɛnkɛma soanvolɛ ɔ, na ɔzele kɛ, “O, Awulae Nyamenle! Me nee Ɛdɛnkɛma soanvolɛ yɛ nye ɛyɛ nna.”

english_verse: “Calm down!” the Lord told Gideon. “There's nothing to be afraid of. You're not going to die.”
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele ye kɛ, “Ka wɔ ahonle to azule nu. Mmasulo, na ɛnrɛwu.”

english_verse: Gideon built an altar for worshiping the Lord and called it “The Lord Calms Our Fears.” It still stands there in Ophrah, a town in the territory of the Abiezer clan. Gideon Tears Down Baal's Altar
translation_verse: Akee Gedɛyɔn yɛle azukponle manle Ɛdɛnkɛma na ɔvɛlɛle ye “Ɛdɛnkɛma le anzonudwolɛ.” Na ɛnɛ nee ɛnɛ ala, ɔtɛgyi Ɔfela. Ɔfela le Ebayizɛma sua zo.

english_verse: That night the Lord spoke to Gideon again: Get your father's second-best bull, the one that's seven years old. Use it to pull down the altar where your father worships Baal and cut down the sacred pole next to the altar.
translation_verse: Kenle ko ne nɔe ne Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Gedɛyɔn kɛ, “Fa ɛ ze ɛnlankɛ nyinli ne mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nwiɔ mɔɔ ɛli ɛvolɛ nsuu la, bubu ɛ ze mɔ azukponle ne mɔɔ bɛzile bɛmanle Beeyale la, na pɛ bozonle raalɛ Ahyela sɛkɛlɛneɛ baka ne mɔɔ gyi nwolɛ la to.

english_verse: Then build an altar for worshiping me on the highest part of the hill where your town is built. Use layers of stones for my altar, not just a pile of rocks. Cut up the wood from the pole, make a fire, kill the bull, and burn it as a sacrifice to me.
translation_verse: Akee fa awolɛ siezie bɛ gyɛlɛɛnye na si azukponle wɔ ezukue ɛhye azo maa Ɛdɛnkɛma wɔ Nyamenle ne. Fa Ahyela baka ne mɔɔ ɛbapɛ la wuda senle na yela ɛnlankɛ nyinli ne fa bɔ azu maa Ɛdɛnkɛma.”

english_verse: Gideon chose ten of his servants to help him, and they did everything God had said. But since Gideon was afraid of his family and the other people in Ophrah, he did it all at night.
translation_verse: Zɔhane ati Gedɛyɔn yele ye sonvolɛma ne mɔ anu bulu manle bɛyɛle, kɛmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma zele ye la; noko kɛmɔ ɛnee ɔsulo ye sua nu amra ne nee ezuavolɛ ne somasoma la ati, kɛ ɔkɛbɔ azu ne ewiazo la, ɔbɔle ye nɔɔzo.

english_verse: When the people of the town got up the next morning, they saw that Baal's altar had been knocked over, and the sacred pole next to it had been cut down. Then they noticed the new altar covered with the remains of the sacrificed bull.
translation_verse: Nwonlomɔ mangyee ne mɔɔ ezuavolɛ ne vi nla nu dwazole la, bɛnwunle kɛ bɛbubu Beeyale azukponle ne, bɛpɛ Ahyela baka ne mɔɔ gyi nwolɛ la, na bɛva ɛnlankɛ ne mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nwiɔ ne la bɛbɔ azu wɔ azukponle ne mɔɔ bɛzi la azo.

english_verse: “Who could have done such a thing?” they asked. And they kept on asking, until finally someone told them, “Gideon the son of Joash did it.”
translation_verse: Na bɛbizebizale bɛ nwo ngoko kɛ, “Ɛnee nwane yɛɛ ɛli gyima zɛhae a?” Bɛbizebizale dedee la, bɛdele kɛ Dwowahye ara Gedɛyɔn yɛɛ ɛli gyima mɔɔ le zɛhae la.

english_verse: The men of the town went to Joash and said, “Your son Gideon knocked over Baal's altar and cut down the sacred pole next to it. Hand him over, so we can kill him!”
translation_verse: Ezuavolɛ ne zele Dwowahye kɛ, “Fa ɛ ra nrenya ne finde maa yɛhu ye, ɔluakɛ yebubu Beeyale azukponle ne na eza yepɛ Ahyela baka ne mɔɔ gyi nwolɛ la.”

english_verse: The crowd pushed closer and closer, but Joash replied, “Are you trying to take revenge for Baal? Are you trying to rescue Baal? If you are, you will be the ones who are put to death, and it will happen before another day dawns. If Baal really is a god, let him take his own revenge on someone who tears down his altar.”
translation_verse: Na Dwowahye zele menli ne mɔɔ ɛra ɔ nwo zo la kɛ, “Bɛbagyinla Beeyale agyakɛ anu ɔ? Anzɛɛ bɛbalie ɔ ti ɔ? Awie biala mɔɔ kɛzi ye ɛbolɛ kɛ ɔdie Beeyale ati la bɛbahu ye na aleɛ ahye. Bɛbubu Beeyale azukponle ne, saa ɔle nyamenle a, bɛmaa ɔdaye ɔlie ɔ nwo.”

english_verse: That same day, Joash changed Gideon's name to Jerubbaal, explaining, “He tore down Baal's altar, so let Baal take revenge himself.” Gideon Defeats the Midianites
translation_verse: Ɛhye ati ɔvi kenle ko zɔhane bɛdonle Gedɛyɔn, Gyɛlɛbeeyale, ɔboalekɛ Dwowahye zele kɛ, “Bɛmaa Beeyale ɛho ɛmaa ɔ nwo”, kɛmɔ Gedɛyɔn ɛbubu ye azukponle ne ɛgua la.

english_verse: All the Midianites, Amalekites, and other eastern nations got together and crossed the Jordan River. Then they invaded the land of Israel and set up camp in Jezreel Valley.
translation_verse: Akee Medeanema nee Amalɛkema nee Aduduleɛ ɛsɛlɛ zo amra ne mɔ amuala boɔboale bɛ nloa, bɛpɛle Azule Dwɔdan ne, na bɛyɛle bɛ azokoɛleɛ wɔ Gyɛzɛli Bɔnza ne anu.

english_verse: The Lord's Spirit took control of Gideon, and Gideon blew a trumpet as a signal for the men in the Abiezer clan to follow him.
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma Sunsum ne dwule Gedɛyɔn anwo zo. Ɔwule aweɛne nu na Ebayizɛma kɔsɔɔti dwazole doale ye.

english_verse: He also sent messengers to the tribes of Manasseh, Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, telling the men of these tribes to come and join his army. Then they set out toward the enemy camp.
translation_verse: Ɔzoanle menli wɔ Manasɛ, na bɛ kɔsɔɔti bɛralile ɔ nzi. Eza ɔzoanle menli wɔ Ahya, Zɛbulɛn, yɛɛ Nafetalae, na bɛ kɔsɔɔti bɛbɔle nu bɛ nee ye hɔyiale.

english_verse: Gideon prayed to God, “I know that you promised to help me rescue Israel, but I need proof. Tonight I'll spread a sheep skin on the stone floor of that threshing-place over there. If you really will help me rescue Israel, then tomorrow morning let there be dew on the skin, but let the stone floor be dry.”
translation_verse: ɛnee melɛfa dwɛsɛ meagua ɛleka mɔɔ bɛwozo ma ne la. Saa aleɛ kye na ɛbɔlɛ wɔ dwɛsɛ ne azo, na bie ɛnle azɛlɛ ne anwo a, ɛnee menwu kɛ amgba ɛdua me nwo zo wɔalie Yizilayɛma, kɛmɔ ɛdawɔ wɔha la.”

english_verse: And that's just what happened. Early the next morning, Gideon got up and checked the sheep skin. He squeezed out enough water to fill a bowl.
translation_verse: Na ɔyɛle zɔhane. Aleɛ hyenle na Gedɛyɔn hwinle dwɛsɛ ne anu la, ɛbɔlɛ mɔɔ guale aze la yi kanrɛlɛ.

english_verse: But Gideon prayed to God again. “Don't be angry with me,” Gideon said. “Let me try this just one more time, so I'll really be sure you'll help me. Only this time, let the skin be dry and the stone floor be wet.”
translation_verse: Na Gedɛyɔn zɛlɛle Nyamenle kɛ, “Mmafa me nwo ɛya. Maa menga edwɛkɛ kpɔkɛ ko bieko. Mesɛlɛ wɔ, maa menva dwɛsɛ ne menyɛ sɔnea ko bieko. Nzinlii ɛdeɛ ye, mmamaa dwɛsɛ ne doa; maa ɔyɛ resee, na maa ɛbɔlɛ ɛloa azɛlɛ ne anwo.”

english_verse: That night, God made the stone floor wet with dew, but he kept the sheep skin dry.
translation_verse: Na kenle ko ne nɔe ne, Nyamenle yɛle ye kɛmɔ Gedɛyɔn kpondɛ la. Aleɛ hyenle la ɛnee dwɛsɛ ne le resee, na ɛbɔlɛ ɛloa azɛlɛ ne anwo.

english_verse: Early the next morning, Gideon and his army got up and moved their camp to Fear Spring. The Midianite camp was to the north, in the valley at the foot of Moreh Hill.
translation_verse: Gedɛyɔn nee ye ɛlɔnema ne amuala dwazole kenle ko aleɛbahye na bɛhɔdɛle Hɛlɔdo Nzubula ne azo. Medeanema azokoɛleɛ ɛdeɛ ne wɔ Gedɛyɔn ɛdeɛ ne sɔlɔ, wɔ Moli Boka ne foa ko bɔnza ne anu.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Gideon, your army is too big. I can't let you win with this many soldiers. The Israelites would think that they had won the battle all by themselves and that I didn't have anything to do with it.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Gedɛyɔn kɛ, “Wɔ ɛlɔnema mɔɔ meye Medeanema meamaa bɛ la zonle somaa. Saa bɛzonle somaa a bɛbaze kɛ bɛdabɛ bɛ anwosesebɛ a bɛva bɛli konim a, yemɔti bɛnrɛli me eni; bɛbamemaa bɛ nwo zo.

english_verse: So call your troops together and tell them that anyone who is really afraid can leave Mount Gilead and go home.” Twenty-two thousand men returned home, leaving Gideon with only
translation_verse: Zɔhane ati kpakye nuhua wienyi ka kile bɛ kɛ, ‘Awie biala mɔɔ nea a ɔ nwo ɛnva ye ɛngɔ la ɛzia ɛhɔ sua nu.’ ” Gedɛyɔn zɔle bɛ nleanle na bɛ nuhua apenle ngoko abulanwiɔ nee nwiɔ ziale, na ɔhale apenle bulu.

english_verse: but if you're still afraid, you and your servant Purah should sneak down to their camp.
translation_verse: Saa ɛsulo noko a, ɛnee ɛ nee wɔ sonvolɛ Pula bɛhɔbu bɛzia

english_verse: “Gideon,” the Lord said, “you still have too many soldiers. Take them down to the spring and I'll test them. I'll tell you which ones can go along with you and which ones must go back home.”
translation_verse: Eza Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Gedɛyɔn kɛ, “Ɛlɔne mɔɔ ɛha la tɛso somaa. Fa bɛ kɔ Azule ne anloa na medame mebakpa nu meaye bie meamaa wɔ. Bɛ nuhua biala mɔɔ menwɔze wɔ kɛ, ‘sonla ɛhye kɔ bie’ la, ɛ nee ye ɛhɔ. Awie biala mɔɔ menwɔze wɔ kɛ ‘ɔngɔ bie’ la, ɛ nee ye mmakɔ.”

english_verse: When Gideon led his army down to the spring, the Lord told him, “Watch how each man gets a drink of water. Then divide them into two groups—those who lap the water like a dog and those who kneel down to drink.”
translation_verse: Yemɔti Gedɛyɔn vale ɛlɔnema ne hɔle nzubula ne azo. Ɛdɛnkɛma zele ye kɛ, “Menli mɔɔ kɛva bɛ tafinlima kɛnlo nzule ne kɛ twea ɛlɛno nzule la, kpa bɛ ngome sie ahane. Bɛdabɛ noko mɔɔ bɛkɛhoto kolaa na bɛanlo nzule ne la, kpa bɛ sie foa ko.”

english_verse: Three hundred men scooped up water in their hands and lapped it, and the rest knelt to get a drink.
translation_verse: Bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛvale bɛ sa bɛvenle nzule ne bɛnlonle la amuala le ɛya nsa ala. Menli mɔɔ hale la amuala hotole kolaa na bɛanlo nzule ne.

english_verse: The Lord said, “Gideon, your army will be made up of everyone who lapped the water from their hands. Send the others home. I'm going to rescue Israel by helping you and your army of
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Gedɛyɔn kɛ, “Menli ɛya nsa ne mɔɔ vale bɛ sa venle nzule ne nlonle la, bɛmɛ yɛɛ mefa bɛ mealie Yizilayɛma a; memaa bɛali Medeanema anwo zo konim. Yemɔti menli mɔɔ ɛha la, maa biala ɛzia ɛhɔ sua nu.”

english_verse: That night, the Lord said to Gideon. “Get up! Attack the Midianite camp. I am going to let you defeat them,
translation_verse: Kenle ko ne nɔe ne Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Gedɛyɔn kɛ, “Dwazo na ɛ nee wɔ ɛlɔnema ɛhɔ Medeanema anwo zo. Wɔli konim wɔwie.

english_verse: When you hear what the Midianites are saying, you'll be brave enough to attack.” Gideon and Purah worked their way to the edge of the enemy camp, where soldiers were on guard duty.
translation_verse: na bɛbade mɔɔ menli ne ɛlɛka la. Ɛhye bamaa wɔazi ahonle ɛ nee bɛ ahɔho.” Yemɔti Gedɛyɔn nee Pula hɔle Medeanema azokoɛleɛ ne kandiba.

english_verse: The camp was huge. The Midianites, Amalekites, and other eastern nations covered the valley like a swarm of locusts. And it would be easier to count the grains of sand on a beach than to count their camels.
translation_verse: Medeanema, Amalɛkema, yɛɛ Aduduleɛ ɛsɛlɛ ne azo amra ne mɔ ɛyɛ menyemenye kɛ azonlɛ la wɔ bɔnza ne anu, yɛɛ afunlumu mɔɔ bɛlɛ la zonle kɛ ɛnweazo anwea.

english_verse: Gideon overheard one enemy guard telling another, “I had a dream about a flat loaf of barley bread that came tumbling into our camp. It hit the headquarters tent, and the tent flipped over and fell to the ground.”
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Gedɛyɔn hɔdwule la, ɔdele kɛ nrenya bie ɛlɛka ɛlalɛ mɔɔ yeha la yeahile ɔ gɔnwo. Ɔse, “Ayi, meka ɛlalɛ la ɛnee kpanwo mɔɔ bɛva abɛlɛ bɛyɛ la ɛhundo ɛra Medeanema azokoɛleɛ ɛke na yeratia yɛ ndanlɛ azua ne mɔ anu ko yegologolo ye yegua bɔkɔɔ.”

english_verse: The other soldier answered, “Your dream must have been about Gideon, the Israelite commander. It means God will let him and his army defeat the Midianite army and everyone else in our camp.”
translation_verse: Ɔ gɔnwo ne buale kɛ, “Ɛlalɛ ɛhye abo ɛngile debie gyɛne biala. Kpanwo ne kile Yizilayɛnli Dwowahye ara nrenya Gedɛyɔn konle dadeɛ ne. Nyamenle ɛkpogya ɔ sa zo yemaa yeli Medeanema nee yɛ ɛlɔnema ne anwo zo konim.”

english_verse: As soon as Gideon heard about the dream and what it meant, he bowed down to praise God. Then he went back to the Israelite camp and shouted, “Let's go! The Lord is going to let us defeat the Midianite army.”
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Gedɛyɔn dele ɛlalɛ ne nee ɔ bo ɛhilelɛ ne la, ɔyeyɛle Nyamenle. Akee ɔziale ɔhɔle Yizilayɛma azokoɛleɛ lɔ na ɔzele ye ɛlɔnema ne kɛ, “Bɛdwazo, ɔluakɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛye Medeanema pemgbenleamgbe ne ɛmaa bɛ.”

english_verse: Gideon said, “When we get to the enemy camp, spread out and surround it. Then wait for me to blow a signal on my trumpet. As soon as you hear it, blow your trumpets and shout, ‘Fight for the Lord! Fight for Gideon!’ ”
translation_verse: Saa me nee me ekpunli ɛdeɛ ne yɛwu yɛ aweɛne ne mɔ anu a, bɛdabɛ noko bɛwu bɛ ɛdeɛ ne mɔ anu bɛdeɛdea nu kɛ, ‘Ɛdɛnkɛma nee Gedɛyɔn bɛ ɛdeɛ ɛne!’ ”
