english_verse: Gideon and his group reached the edge of the enemy camp a few hours after dark, just after the new guards had come on duty. Gideon and his soldiers blew their trumpets and smashed the clay jars that were hiding the torches.
translation_verse: Gedɛyɔn nee ye ɛlɔnema ɛya nsa ne mɔɔ hale la dwule menli ne mɔ azokoɛleɛ ne kandiba asɛɛ alevinli mu nwiɔ avinli. Ɛnee bɔ zo mɔɔ sinzavolɛma fofolɛ mɔɔ bahakyi dɛba ne mɔ la ɛra ɔ. Akee bɛwule bɛ aweɛne ne mɔ anu na bɛbobɔle dwora ne mɔ mɔɔ bɛdedɛ la.

english_verse: The rest of Gideon's soldiers blew the trumpets they were holding in their right hands. Then they smashed the jars and held the burning torches in their left hands. Everyone shouted, “Fight with your swords for the Lord and for Gideon!”
translation_verse: Ɛlɔnema ekpunli nwiɔ ne noko yɛle zɔhane ala. Bɛlɛ bɛ tɛkɛ ne mɔ bɛ sa bɛne ne mɔ anu, yɛɛ aweɛne ne mɔ mɔɔ bɛlɛwu nuhua la wɔ bɛ sa fema ne mɔ anu, na bɛdeɛdeanle nuhua kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma konle dadeɛ ko, Gedɛyɔn konle dadeɛ ko!”

english_verse: The enemy soldiers started yelling and tried to run away. Gideon's troops stayed in their positions surrounding the camp
translation_verse: Awie biala andu ɔ bo anvi ɛleka mɔɔ ɔgyi la, noko kpɔvolɛma ɛlɔne ne deɛdeanle nuhua na bɛguale ɛbɔ nu.

english_verse: and blew their trumpets again. As they did, the Lord made the enemy soldiers pull out their swords and start fighting each other. The enemy army tried to escape from the camp. They ran to Acacia Tree Town, toward Zeredah, and as far as the edge of the land that belonged to the town of Abel-Meholah near Tabbath.
translation_verse: Mekɛ mɔɔ Gedɛyɔn ɛlɔnema ɛya nsa ne ɛlɛwu bɛ aweɛne ne mɔ anu la, Ɛdɛnkɛma manle kpɔvolɛma ne mɔ pɛle bɛ nwo honle na bɛhunle bɛ nwo. Bɛnriandile toonwo bɛhɔle Bɛte Hyeta wɔ Zalɛtan afoa nu nehane, bɛtelele zolɛ bɛhɔdwule Ebɛle Mɛhɔla mɔɔ zua Tabate ɛweɛne zo la.

english_verse: Gideon sent word for more Israelite soldiers to come from the tribes of Naphtali, Asher, and both halves of Manasseh to help fight the Midianites.
translation_verse: Na bɛvɛlɛle Yizilayɛma mɔɔ wɔ Nafetalae nee Ahya nee Manasɛ la, na bɛbelele bɛzile Medeanema zo.

english_verse: He also sent messengers to tell all the men who lived in the hill country of Ephraim, “Come and help us fight the Midianites! Put guards at every spring, stream, and well, as far as Beth-Barah before the Midianites can get to them. And guard the Jordan River.” Troops from Ephraim did exactly what Gideon had asked,
translation_verse: Gedɛyɔn zoanle menli manle bɛhɔbɔle azua mɔɔ gua Yifelaem awoka ne mɔ azo la amaneɛ kɛ, “Bɛtolo aze bɛ nee Medeanema ɛraho. Bɛzia bɛ wɔ Azule Dwɔdan ne nee azudenle ne mɔ anloa toonwo bɛhɔkpula Bɛtebɛla. Bɛmmamaa bɛ adenle bɛmaa bɛpɛ.” Yemɔti Yifelaemma ravale azudenle ne mɔ amuala nee Azule Dwɔdan ne.

english_verse: and they even helped chase the Midianites on the east side of the Jordan River. These troops captured Raven and Wolf, the two Midianite leaders. They killed Raven at a large rock that has come to be known as Raven Rock, and they killed Wolf near a wine-pit that has come to be called Wolf Wine-Pit. The men of Ephraim brought the heads of the two Midianite leaders to Gideon.
translation_verse: Bɛvoanle bɛ toonwo bɛhyele Medean mgbanyima nwiɔ, mɔɔ le Ɔlɛbe nee Ziibi. Bɛhunle Ɔlɛbe wɔ Ɔlɛbe Bodane ne azo, yɛɛ bɛhunle Ziibi wɔ Ziibi nwanyeyɛlɛ sua ne anu na bɛvale adile nwiɔ ne, Ɔlɛbe nee Ziibi adile ne mɔ bɛrɛlɛle Gedɛyɔn. Mekɛ ne anu ɛnee Gedɛyɔn wɔ Azule Dwɔdan ne anzi mɔɔ di kɔ aduduleɛ la.

english_verse: But the men were really upset with Gideon and complained, “When you went to war with Midian, you didn't ask us to help! Why did you treat us like that?”
translation_verse: Yifelaem ɛlɔnema ne bɔle Gedɛyɔn somolɛ kɛ, “Duzu amaamuo ɛtane a wɔva wɔbu yɛ la. Duzu ati a ɛ nee Medeanema kaho mɔɔ wɔambɔ yɛ amaneɛ a?” Na bɛhwile ɔ nyunlu kpalɛ.

english_verse: Gideon answered: Don't be upset! Even though you came later, you were able to do much more than I did. It's just like the grape harvest: The grapes your tribe doesn't even bother to pick are better than the best grapes my family can grow.
translation_verse: Na ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Mɔɔ meyɛ la nee mɔɔ bɛyɛ la ɛnrɛzɛ. Ekyi bɔbɔ mɔɔ bɛmɛ Yifelaemma bɛyɛ la sɔ ɛnyelɛ tɛla mɔɔ me ɛlɔnema ne amuala ɛyɛ la.

english_verse: Besides, God chose you to capture Raven and Wolf. I didn't do a thing compared to you. By the time Gideon had finished talking, the men of Ephraim had calmed down and were no longer angry with him. Gideon Finishes Destroying the Midianite Army
translation_verse: Ɔlua Nyamenle tumi zo, bɛhu Medean mgbanyima nwiɔ ne, Ɔlɛbe nee Ziibi. Na duzu bɔbɔ yɛɛ meyɛ mɔɔ nee ɛhye sɛ a?” Ɔhanle ɛhye la, bɛ ɛya ne dwole.

english_verse: The town of Succoth was nearby, so he went there and asked, “Please give my troops some food. They are worn out, but we have to keep chasing Zebah and Zalmunna, the two Midianite kings.”
translation_verse: Yemɔti ɔzele menli mɔɔ wɔ Sɛko la kɛ, “Mesɛlɛ bɛ, bɛmaa ɛlɔnema mɔɔ me nee bɛ lua la kpanwo bɛmaa bɛli, ɔluakɛ asɛɛ bɛwie wu. Melua Medean arelemgbunli nwiɔ ne, mɔɔ le Ziba nee Zɛlemɛna ɛhyelɛ.”

english_verse: The town leaders of Succoth answered, “Why should we feed your army? We don't know if you really will defeat Zebah and Zalmunna.”
translation_verse: Na Sɛko mgbanyima zele ye kɛ, “Ziba nee Zɛlemɛna mumua ne ɛ sa ɛzɔ bɛ nu wɔhye bɛ yɛɛ yɛmaa wɔ ɛlɔnema aleɛ a?”

english_verse: “Just wait!” Gideon said. “After the Lord helps me defeat them, I'm coming back here. I'll make a whip out of thorns and rip the flesh from your bones.”
translation_verse: Gedɛyɔn zele kɛ, “Bɛ mo. Saa Ɛdɛnkɛma maa me sa sɔ Ziba nee Zɛlemɛna nu a, bɛmɛ Sɛkoma, mebava fienemgbole nu mbowule mbaka meabila bɛ toonwo bɛ nzi akpakyekpakye.”

english_verse: After leaving Succoth, Gideon went to Penuel and asked the leaders there for some food. But he got the same answer as he did at Succoth.
translation_verse: Ɔvi ɛkɛ la, Gedɛyɔn nee ye ɛlɔnema ne hɔle Pɛnuwɛle na ɔhɔzɛlɛle bɛdabɛ noko aleɛ. Na Pɛnuwɛlema noko buale ye, kɛmɔ Sɛkoma buale ye ala la.

english_verse: “I'll come back safe and sound,” Gideon said, “but when I do, I'm going to tear down your tower!”
translation_verse: Na ɔzele Pɛnuwɛlema kɛ, “Melɛkɔ, na saa mesia meba anzonudwolɛ nu a, mebabubu bɛ tawa ne meagua.”

english_verse: Gideon went to the town officials and said, “Here are Zebah and Zalmunna. Remember how you made fun of me? You said, ‘We don't know if you really will defeat those two Midianite kings. So why should we feed your worn-out army?’ ”
translation_verse: Gedɛyɔn akee rale Sɛko mgbanyima ne mɔ ɛkɛ. Ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛnlea, Ziba nee Zɛlemɛna ɛne! Bɛmɛ bɛ ti a bɛzile me amgbu kɛ, ‘Ziba nee Zɛlemɛna mumua ne, wɔhola bɛ kye na wɔaze yɛ kɛ yɛmaa wɔ ɛlɔnema aleɛ, ɔluakɛ bɛwie wu?’ la.”

english_verse: Gideon reached the enemy camp by going east along Nomad Road past Nobah and Jogbehah. He made a surprise attack,
translation_verse: Gedɛyɔn vale Noba nee Dwobɛha aduduleɛ adenle ne azo na ɔhɔle bɛ kpɔvolɛma ɛlɔne ne anwo zo arɛlevilɛ nu.

english_verse: and the enemy panicked. Zebah and Zalmunna tried to escape, but Gideon chased and captured them.
translation_verse: Ziba nee Zɛlemɛna nriandile; ɔvoanle bɛ toonwo ɔhɔhyele Medean Arelemgbunli Ziba nee Zɛlemɛna, na ɔbɔle bɛ ɛlɔnema ne asande.

english_verse: After the battle, Gideon set out for home. As he was going through Heres Pass,
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Dwowahye ara Gedɛyɔn vi konle ne anloa sia ara la, ɔluale Hilɛse awoka ne mɔ avinli.

english_verse: he caught a young man who lived in Succoth. Gideon asked him who the town officials of Succoth were, and the young man wrote down
translation_verse: Ɔhyele kpavolɛ bie mɔɔ vi Sɛko la na ɔbizale ye edwɛkɛ, na kpavolɛ ne hɛlɛle mgbanyima titile abulasuu nee nsuu ne mɔɔ gyi bɛ ti la aluma manle ye.

english_verse: Gideon made a whip from thorn plants and used it to beat the town officials.
translation_verse: Ɔhyele suakpole Sɛko azo mgbanyima ne mɔ na ɔvale fienemgbole nu mbowule mbaka ɔlile bɛ nwo gyima ɔhilele bɛ debie.

english_verse: Afterwards he went to Penuel, where he tore down the tower and killed all the town officials.
translation_verse: Eza ɔbubule Pɛnuwɛle tawa ne ɔguale na ɔhunle suakpole ne azo mrenya kɔsɔɔti.

english_verse: Then Gideon said, “Zebah and Zalmunna, tell me about the men you killed at Tabor.” “They were a lot like you,” the two kings answered. “They were dignified, almost like royalty.”
translation_verse: Akee ɔbizale Ziba nee Zɛlemɛna kɛ, “Menli mɔɔ bɛhunle bɛ wɔ Teebɔ la kɛ bɛsi bɛde ɛ?” Bɛbuale ye kɛ, “Kɛmɔ ɛde la, zɔhane ala yɛɛ bɛ ko biala de a; ko biala zɔho belemgbunli ra.”

english_verse: “They were my very own brothers!” Gideon said. “I swear by the living Lord that if you had let them live, I would let you live.”
translation_verse: Gedɛyɔn zele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛle me mediema fɔɔnwo mɔɔ me nee bɛ vi ɛkolɛ ko anu a. Meka Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ saa bɛangu bɛ a, anrɛɛ medame noko menrɛhu bɛ.”

english_verse: kilograms. In addition, there was the gold from the camels' ornaments and from the beautiful jewelry worn by the Midianite kings. Gideon also took their purple robes.
translation_verse: Na ɔzele ɔ ra nrenya kpanyinli ne mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye Gyita la kɛ, “Dwazo ku bɛ!” Noko kpavolɛ ne andwe ye dadeɛ ne, ɔluakɛ ɔle kakula, yɛɛ ɔsulo.

english_verse: “What's the matter, Gideon?” Zebah and Zalmunna asked. “Do it yourself, if you're not too much of a coward!” Gideon jumped up and killed them both. Then he took the gold ornaments from the necks of their camels. The Israelites Ask Gideon To Be Their King
translation_verse: Na Ziba nee Zɛlemɛna zele Gedɛyɔn kɛ, “Ɛdawɔ mumua ne ku yɛ, ɔluakɛ kɛ nrenya si de la, zɔhane ala yɛɛ ye anwosesebɛ de a.” Yemɔti Gedɛyɔn hunle Ziba nee Zɛlemɛna, na ɔyeyele agudeɛ mɔɔ bɛyɛ ye kɛ siane ɛbule mɔɔ gugua bɛ afunlumu ne mɔ akɔme la.

english_verse: After the battle with the Midianites, the Israelites said, “Gideon, you rescued us! Now we want you to be our king. Then after your death, your son and then your grandson will rule.”
translation_verse: Akee Yizilayɛma ne zele Gedɛyɔn kɛ, “Ɛdawɔ di yɛ nwo zo kpanyinli. Ɛ ra nee wɔ anlɔnra noko zɔhane ala. Ɔluakɛ wɔlie yɛ wɔvi Medeanema asa anu.”

english_verse: “No,” Gideon replied, “I won't be your king, and my son won't be king either. Only the Lord is your ruler.
translation_verse: Gedɛyɔn buale kɛ, “Menrɛli bɛ nwo zo kpanyinli, yɛɛ me ra noko zɔhane ala. Ɛdɛnkɛma a bali bɛ nwo zo kpanyinli a.”

english_verse: But I will ask you to do one thing: Give me all the earrings you took from the enemy.” The enemy soldiers had been Ishmaelites, and they wore gold earrings.
translation_verse: Akee Gedɛyɔn zele bɛ kɛ, “Mesɛlɛ bɛ debie ko; ninyɛne mɔɔ bɛnyianle la awie biala ɛyeye asomadeɛ mɔɔ wɔ nu la ɛmaa me.”

english_verse: The Israelite soldiers replied, “Of course we will give you the earrings.” Then they spread out a robe on the ground and tossed the earrings on it.
translation_verse: Bɛzele ye kɛ, “Yɛ kunlu fufule nwohyee, yɛfa bɛ muala yɛamaa wɔ.” Bɛdɛlɛle ɛdanlɛ azɛlɛ ne anwo na awie biala yeyele ye ezukoa asomadeɛ mɔɔ ɔnyianle la guale zolɛ.

english_verse: Gideon had many wives and
translation_verse: Gedɛyɔn wole mralɛ mrenya abulasuu, ɔluakɛ ɔgyale mraalɛ dɔɔnwo.

english_verse: He even had a wife who lived at Shechem. They had a son, and Gideon named him Abimelech.
translation_verse: Ɔlɛ ye mgbɔnla wɔ Hyikɛm. Ɔ nee ye wole nrenya ko, na ɔdonle ye Abemɛlɛke.

english_verse: Gideon lived to be an old man. And when he died, he was buried in the family tomb in his hometown of Ophrah, which belonged to the Abiezer clan.
translation_verse: Gedɛyɔn yɛle ɛrelera nwosonwoso na yeawu. Bɛziele ye wɔ ɔ ze Dwowahye nla ne anu wɔ Ɔfela. Ɔfela le Ebayizɛ abo zo amra sua zo.

english_verse: Soon after Gideon's death, the Israelites turned their backs on God again. They set up idols of Baal and worshiped Baal Berith as their god.
translation_verse: Gedɛyɔn wule ala la yɛɛ Yizilayɛma ati hakyile bieko a. Bɛkpole Nyamenle na bɛzonlenle Beeyale ne mɔ na bɛvale Beeyale-bilete bɛyɛle bɛ nyamenle.

english_verse: The Israelites forgot that the Lord was their God, and that he had rescued them from the enemies who lived around them.
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma ne angakye kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne a liele bɛ vile bɛ kpɔvolɛma asa anu wɔ adenle biala anu a.

english_verse: Besides all that, the Israelites were unkind to Gideon's family, even though Gideon had done so much for Israel.
translation_verse: Eza bɛangile ahunlunyele biala bɛammaa Gedɛyɔn abo zo amra wɔ moalɛ mɔɔ ɔvale ɔboale bɛ la anwo.

english_verse: and told them to say to the leaders of Shechem, “Do you think it would be good to have all
translation_verse: bɛbizebiza Hyikɛm ezuavolɛ ne kɛ, “Boni yɛɛ bɛkulo a? Bɛkulo kɛ Gedɛyɔn amra abulasuu ne kɛzie bɛ anzɛɛ sonla kokye ala a kɛzie bɛ a? Eza bɛhakye kɛ bɛ mogya ko ne ala bie a le me.”

english_verse: Abimelech's uncles talked it over with the leaders of Shechem who agreed, “Yes, it would be better for one of our relatives to be king.”
translation_verse: Ɔ nli amediema ne mɔ vale mɔɔ ɔhanle ɔhilele bɛ la hɔbɔle Hyikɛm ezuavolɛ ne amaneɛ. Na bɛ kɔsɔɔti bɛ kunlu dwole fɔɔnwo kɛ Abemɛlɛke ala a sie bɛ a, ɔluakɛ bɛhanle kɛ, “Yɛdayɛ ko ne ala bie a le ye.”

english_verse: Abimelech and his soldiers went to his father's home in Ophrah and brought out Gideon's other sons to a large rock, where they murdered all
translation_verse: Ɔ nee bɛ hɔle ɔ ze awuke nu wɔ Ɔfela na ɔhunle ɔ mediema ne mɔ, mɔɔ le Gedɛyɔn amra mrenya abulasuu ne kɔsɔɔti wɔ bolɛ ko azo; ɔhale Dwotam, mɔɔ le Gedɛyɔn ara kazima ne angomekye, ɔluakɛ ɔnriandile ɔveale.

english_verse: The leaders of Shechem, including the priests and the military officers, met at the tree next to the sacred rock in Shechem to crown Abimelech king.
translation_verse: Hyikɛm ezuavolɛ ne nee Bɛtemelo ezuavolɛ ne kɔsɔɔti bɔle nu na bɛvale Abemɛlɛke bɛziele bɛ belemgbunli wɔ oku baka ne mɔɔ gyi Hyikɛm la abo.

english_verse: Jotham heard what they were doing. So he climbed to the top of Mount Gerizim and shouted down to the people who were there at the meeting: Leaders of Shechem, listen to me, and maybe God will listen to you.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Dwotam dele ɛhye la, ɔhɔle Gɛlaezem Boka ne azo na ɔdeanle nu ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛmɛ Hyikɛm amra, bɛdie me, na Nyamenle adie bɛdabɛ.

english_verse: Once the trees searched for someone to be king; they asked the olive tree, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Kenle ko mbaka kɔsɔɔti hɔle ayia kɛ bɛkaye bɛ nuhua ko bɛazie ye bɛ belemgbunli. Bɛzele ɔlivi baka kɛ, ‘Di yɛ belemgbunli.’

english_verse: But the olive tree replied, “My oil brings honor to people and gods. I won't stop making oil, just so my branches can wave above the other trees.”
translation_verse: Na ɔlivi baka zele bɛ kɛ, ‘Saa menwɔli bɛ belemgbunli a, ɛnee ɔwɔ kɛ megyakyi ma ne mɔɔ meso memaa bɛfa bɛyɛ nwole bɛwula menli nee awozonle ne mɔ anyunlunyia la ɛzolɛ, na meanyia adenle meakpɔsa bɛ nwo zo.’

english_verse: Then they asked the fig tree, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Mbaka ne mɔ hɔzele feege baka kɛ, ‘Bɛla bali yɛ belemgbunli.’

english_verse: But the fig tree replied, “I won't stop growing my delicious fruit, just so my branches can wave above the other trees.”
translation_verse: Na feege baka zele bɛ kɛ, ‘Saa menwɔli bɛ belemgbunli a, ɛnee ɔwɔ kɛ megyakyi me ma fɛlɛko ne mɔɔ meso la.’

english_verse: Next they asked the grape vine, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Eza mbaka ne mɔ hɔzele vanye baka kɛ, ‘Bɛla bali yɛ belemgbunli.’

english_verse: But the grape vine replied, “My wine brings cheer to people and gods. I won't stop making wine, just so my branches can wave above the other trees.”
translation_verse: Na vanye baka zele bɛ kɛ, ‘Saa menwɔli bɛ belemgbunli a, ɛnee ɔwɔ kɛ megyakyi nwanye ne mɔɔ maa awozonle nee menli anye die la ma ne ɛzolɛ.’

english_verse: Finally, they went to the thornbush and asked, “Will you be our king?”
translation_verse: Akee mbaka ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti zele mbowule baka kɛ, ‘Wɔmɔ, bɛla bali yɛ belemgbunli.’

english_verse: The thornbush replied, “If you really want me to be your king, then come into my shade and I will protect you. But if you're deceiving me, I'll start a fire that will spread out and destroy the cedars of Lebanon.” After Jotham had finished telling this story, he said:
translation_verse: Na mbowule baka zele mbaka ne mɔ kɛ, ‘Saa nɔhalɛ nu, bɛ kunlu fufule nwohyee, bɛkulo kɛ medi bɛ belemgbunli a, ɛnee bɛravea me alubo ye anu; saa bɛanyɛ ye zɔhane a, senle vi me mbowule ye anu bazɔ ayela Lɛbanɔn sida mbaka kɔsɔɔti.’

english_verse: My father Gideon risked his life for you when he fought to rescue you from the Midianites. Did you reward Gideon by being kind to his family? No, you did not! You attacked his family and killed all
translation_verse: Noko ɛnɛ bɛho bɛtia egya, bɛhu ɔ mra abulasuu ne amuala wɔ bolɛ ko azo, na bɛva Abemɛlɛke, mɔɔ le akɛlɛ ralɛ la bɛzie Hyikɛm belemgbunli,

english_verse: So, you leaders of Shechem, if you treated Gideon and his family the way you should have, then I hope you and Abimelech will make each other very happy.
translation_verse: ɔboalekɛ ɔle bɛ nwo sonla. Saa bɛdabɛ bɛnea bɛ ti anu, na bɛli nɔhalɛ kɛ bɛwula Gedɛyɔn nee ye awuke nu amra anyunlunyia ɛnɛ ɛdeɛ a, ɛnee Abemɛlɛke ati, bɛli fɛlɛko na ɔdaye noko ɔli fɛlɛko wɔ bɛ ti.

english_verse: But if it was wrong to treat Gideon and his family the way you did, then I pray that Abimelech will destroy you with fire, and I pray that you will do the same to him.
translation_verse: Na saa tɛ ye zɔhane ɛdeɛ a, ɛnee senle vi Abemɛlɛke anu ɛzɔ ɛyela Hyikɛm nee Bɛtemelo amra, na senle noko vi Hyikɛm nee Bɛtemelo ezuavolɛ ne anu ɛzɔ ɛyela Abemɛlɛke.”

english_verse: Jotham ran off and went to live in the town of Beer, where he could be safe from his brother Abimelech. Abimelech Destroys Shechem
translation_verse: Na Dwotam nriandile hɔle Biyɛ, ɔhɔdɛnlanle ɛkɛ, ɔluakɛ ɔsulo ɔ diema Abemɛlɛke.

english_verse: when God decided to punish him and the leaders of Shechem for killing Gideon's
translation_verse: Ɛhye zile, amaa Gedɛyɔn amra abulasuu ne mogya agua Abemɛlɛke nee Hyikɛm amra mɔɔ zile ye adua manle ɔhunle bɛ la ati zo.

english_verse: Then they sent some men to hide on the hilltops and watch for Abimelech and his troops, while they sent others to rob everyone that went by on the road. But Abimelech found out what they were doing.
translation_verse: Na Hyikɛm ezuavolɛ manle menli hɔdɛle Abemɛlɛke wɔ awoka ne mɔ azo, na bɛzale adendulɛma mɔɔ vale adenle ne azo la bɛliele bɛ ninyɛne. Na bɛrabɔle Abemɛlɛke amaneɛ.

english_verse: One day, Gaal son of Ebed went to live in Shechem. His brothers moved there too, and soon the leaders of Shechem started trusting him.
translation_verse: Na Yibɛde ara nrenya Geeyale nee ɔ mediema ne mɔ dule radɛnlanle Hyikɛm, na Hyikɛm amra vale bɛ rɛle wulale ye nu.

english_verse: The time came for the grape harvest, and the people of Shechem went into their vineyards and picked the grapes. They gathered the grapes and made wine. Then they went into the temple of their god and threw a big party. There was a lot of eating and drinking, and before long they were cursing Abimelech.
translation_verse: Bɛ kɔsɔɔti bɛhɔle bɛ vanye ɛya ne mɔ anu bɛhɔtetele vanye ma bɛrayɛle nwanye bɛvale bɛdole ɛkponle kpole bie. Bɛhɔle bɛ nyamenle sua ne abo bɛlile, bɛnlonle na bɛlile Abemɛlɛke ngoamɛ, bɛhehanle ɛtane ɛtane bɛtietiale ye.

english_verse: Gaal said: Hamor was the founder of Shechem, and one of his descendants should be our ruler. But Abimelech's father was Gideon, so Abimelech isn't really one of us. He shouldn't be our king, and we shouldn't have to obey him or Zebul, who rules Shechem for him.
translation_verse: Geeyale zele kɛ, “Abemɛlɛke a le nwane, yɛɛ yɛmɛ Hyikɛm ezuavolɛ, duzu menli a le yɛ mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ yɛsonle ye a? Anzɛɛ tɛ Gedɛyɔn ara ye nee ye abɔlɔba Zibɛle a zonlenle Heemɔ mɔɔ kyekyele Hyikɛm la ɛlɔnema la ɔ? Duzu ati bɔbɔ yɛɛ ɔwɔ kɛ yɛsonle Abemɛlɛke a?

english_verse: If I were the ruler of Shechem, I'd get rid of that Abimelech. I'd tell him, “Get yourself an even bigger army, and we will still defeat you.”
translation_verse: Me kunlu a anrɛɛ menli ɛhye mɔ kɔsɔɔti wɔ me bo, anrɛɛ metu Abemɛlɛke ebia ne azo. Anrɛɛ menwɔze Abemɛlɛke kɛ, ‘Boɔboa wɔ ɛlɔnema ne anloa na finde maamgbole nu maa yɛho.’ ”

english_verse: Zebul was angry when he found out what Gaal had said.
translation_verse: Mekɛ mɔɔ Zibɛle, mɔɔ nea suakpole ne azo la dele edwɛkɛ mɔɔ Yibɛde ara Geeyale hanle la, ɛya hunle ye kpole kpalɛ.

english_verse: This is what I think you should do. Lead your army here during the night and hide in the fields.
translation_verse: Yemɔti ɛnɛ nɔe, ɛ nee wɔ ɛlɔnema bɛrazia adenle nu.

english_verse: Get up the next morning at sunrise and rush out of your hiding places to attack the town. Gaal and his followers will come out to fight you, but you will easily defeat them.
translation_verse: Na ye alehyenlɛ nu, mɔɔ maanle nu kɛtete la wɔahɔnwinwi bɛ wɔ suakpole ne azo; na saa Geeyale nee menli mɔɔ nee ye lua la se kɛ bɛba bɛ nee wɔ araho a, wɔadua bɛ kakɛ, kɛmɔ ɔfɛta la.”

english_verse: So one night, Abimelech led his soldiers to Shechem. He divided them into four groups, and they all hid near the town.
translation_verse: Abemɛlɛke nee ye ɛlɔnema ne dwazole nɔe ne; bɛhyɛle bɛ nwo ekpunli nna na bɛhɔziale Hyikɛm kandiba ne.

english_verse: The next morning, Gaal went out and stood in the opening of the town gate. Abimelech and his soldiers left their hiding places,
translation_verse: Geeyale hɔgyinlanle suakpole ne anlenkɛ kpole ne anloa. Abemɛlɛke nee ye ɛlɔnema ne vi ɛleka mɔɔ bɛvea la vindele.

english_verse: and Gaal saw them. Zebul was standing there with Gaal, and Gaal remarked, “Zebul, that looks like a crowd of people coming down from the mountaintops.” “No,” Zebul answered, “it's just the shadows of the mountains. It only looks like people moving.”
translation_verse: Geeyale nwunle ɛlɔne ne la ɔzele Zibɛle kɛ, “Nea, menli vi awoka ne mɔ azo ɛlɛtolo ara!” Zibɛle zele ye kɛ, “Awoka ne mɔ azo ɛlawolɛ ne mɔ a ɛyɛ ɛ nye zo kɛ menli a.”

english_verse: “But Zebul, look over there,” Gaal said. “There's a crowd coming down from the sacred mountain, and another group is coming along the road from the tree where people talk with the spirits of the dead.”
translation_verse: Geeyale zile zolɛ bieko kɛ, “Nea, menli vi avinli nehane ɛlɛba. Ekpunli bieko noko vi oku baka ne mɔɔ bɛbɔ menli munzule wɔ ɔ bo la anwo ɛlɛba.”

english_verse: Then Zebul replied, “What good is all of your bragging now? You were the one who said Abimelech shouldn't be the ruler of Shechem. Out there is the army that you made fun of. So go out and fight them!”
translation_verse: Akee Zibɛle zele ye kɛ, “Wɔ mgbole ne mɔɔ ɛka la wɔ nienwu? Tɛ wɔmɔ a ɛhanle kɛ, ‘Abemɛlɛke a le nwane, mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ yɛsonle ye la?’ Menli mɔɔ ɛgolole bɛ nwo la a ɛlɛba la. Finde tɛtɛlɛ nu lɔ ɛ nee bɛ ɛhɔho.”

english_verse: Gaal and the leaders of Shechem went out and fought Abimelech.
translation_verse: Na Geeyale lile Hyikɛm ezuavolɛ ne ati na bɛ nee Abemɛlɛke honle.

english_verse: Soon the people of Shechem turned and ran back into the town. However, Abimelech and his troops were close behind and killed many of them along the way.
translation_verse: Geeyale dɔle ɛbɔ nu; Abemɛlɛke belele zile ye zo. Menli ne anu somaa bodɛbodale wɔ suakpole ne anlenkɛ kpole ne anloa.

english_verse: Abimelech stayed at Arumah, and Zebul forced Gaal and his brothers out of Shechem.
translation_verse: Akee Abemɛlɛke dɛnlanle Alɛma. Zibɛle voanle Geeyale nee ɔ mediema ne mɔ; yeammaa bɛandɛnla Hyikɛm bieko.

english_verse: The next morning, the people of Shechem were getting ready to work in their fields as usual, but someone told Abimelech about it.
translation_verse: Aleɛ hyenle la Hyikɛm ezuavolɛ yɛle kɛ bɛfinde bɛahɔ konle ne anloa bieko.

english_verse: Abimelech divided his army into three groups and set up an ambush in the fields near Shechem. When the people came out of the town, he and his army rushed out from their hiding places and attacked.
translation_verse: Abemɛlɛke dele la ɔhyɛle ye ɛlɔnema ne anu ekpunli nsa na bɛhɔziale Hyikɛm amra. Mɔɔ ɔnwunle kɛ bɛvi suakpole ne azo bɛye bɛ ti la, bɛhɔnwinwinle bɛ na bɛhunle bɛ kɔsɔɔti.

english_verse: Abimelech and the troops with him ran to the town gate and took control of it, while two other groups attacked and killed the people who were in the fields.
translation_verse: Abemɛlɛke nee ye ekpunli ɛdeɛ ne hanle bɛ nwo ndɛndɛ hɔvale suakpole ne anlenkɛ kpole ne. Ekpunli nwiɔ ne noko hɔnwinwinle menli ne mɔ wɔ konle ɛleka ne na bɛhunle bɛ kɔsɔɔti.

english_verse: He and his troops fought in Shechem all day, until they had killed everyone in town. Then he and his men tore down the houses and buildings and scattered salt everywhere.
translation_verse: Abemɛlɛke nee suakpole ne azo amra honle toonwo aledwolɛ. Ɔhunle menli mɔɔ wɔ zolɛ la kɔsɔɔti na ɔvale suakpole ne; ɔbɔle ye tɔɔ na ɔvale ngyenle ɔkpondenle zolɛ.

english_verse: Earlier that day, the leaders of the temple of El Berith at Shechem had heard about the attack. So they went into the temple fortress,
translation_verse: Mɔɔ mgbanyima mɔɔ wɔ Hyikɛm aranemgbole ne anu la dele mɔɔ ɛzi la, bɛnriandile bɛhɔveale Beeyale-bilete ɛzonlenlɛ sua ne anu.

english_verse: He led his troops to Mount Zalmon, where he took an ax and chopped off a tree branch. He lifted the branch onto his shoulder and shouted, “Hurry! Cut off a branch just as I did.”
translation_verse: Yemɔti Abemɛlɛke vale ye ɛlɔnema lile ɔ nzi hɔle Zalemɔn Boka ne azo. Ɔvale akuma ɔpɛle baka ko ngane ne mɔ ko ɔdole ɔ kɔme zo na ɔzele ye ɛlɔnema ne kɛ, “Deɛ ɛhye mɔɔ bɛnwu kɛ meyɛ la, awie biala ɛmaa ɔ nwo ɛyɛ ndɛ ɔyɛ bie.”

english_verse: When they all had branches, they followed Abimelech back to Shechem. They piled the branches against the fortress and set them on fire, burning down the fortress and killing about
translation_verse: Yemɔti awie biala pɛle baka ɛhane ko na bɛlile Abemɛlɛke anzi bɛvale bɛhɔguale aranemgbole ne anloa na bɛdole senle nu, na bɛdabɛ mrenya nee mraalɛ kɛyɛ apenle, mɔɔ wɔ Hyikɛm aranemgbole ne anu la kɔsɔɔti dɔle nzonle.

english_verse: After destroying Shechem, Abimelech went to Thebez. He surrounded the town and captured it.
translation_verse: Akee Abemɛlɛke hɔle Tibɛze, bɛhɔbɔle bɛyiale ye na bɛhonle bɛvale.

english_verse: But there was a tall fortress in the middle of the town, and the town leaders and everyone else went inside. Then they barred the gates and went up to the flat roof.
translation_verse: Aranemgbole bie wɔ Tibɛze suakpole ne azo, yemɔti menli ne mɔ, mraalɛ nee mrenya, nriandile hɔveale zolɛ anwuma.

english_verse: Abimelech and his army rushed to the fortress and tried to force their way inside. Abimelech himself was about to set the heavy wooden doors on fire,
translation_verse: Abemɛlɛke hɔle aranemgbole ne anwo na ɔvole ɔhɔle kɛ ɔkado senle wɔ ye anlenkɛ ne anu. Ɔfo la,

english_verse: when a woman on the roof dropped a large rock on his head and cracked his skull.
translation_verse: raalɛ bie gyakyile ɛdibolɛ totohyia bie dole ɔ ti zo manle ɔ ti kpukele.

english_verse: The soldier who carried his weapons was nearby, and Abimelech told him, “Take out your sword and kill me. I don't want people to say that I was killed by a woman!” So the soldier ran his sword through Abimelech.
translation_verse: Abemɛlɛke vɛlɛle ye sonvolɛ ne mɔɔ soa ye konle ninyɛne ne la kɛ, “Ka ɛ nwo, twe wɔ dadeɛ ne ku me ndɛndɛ, anrɛɛ menli kɛze kɛ, ‘Raalɛzinli a hunle ye a.’ ” Amgba noko kpavolɛ ne wɔle Abemɛlɛke dadeɛ hunle ye.

english_verse: And when the Israelite soldiers saw that their leader was dead, they went back home.
translation_verse: Na mɔɔ Yizilayɛma nwunle kɛ Abemɛlɛke ɛwu la, bɛ kɔsɔɔti bɛziale bɛhɔle bɛ sua zo.

english_verse: That's how God punished Abimelech for killing his brothers and bringing shame on his father's family.
translation_verse: Zɛhae adenle zo a Nyamenle vale duale Abemɛlɛke kakɛ wɔ munzule ɛbɛla ne mɔɔ ɔbɔle ɔtiale ɔ ze, kɛ ɔhunle ɔ mediema abulasuu ne la a.

english_verse: God also punished the people of Shechem for helping Abimelech. Everything happened just as Jotham's curse said it would.
translation_verse: Eza Nyamenle manle Hyikɛm amra munzule ne mɔɔ bɛbɔle la bɔle bɛ ti. Ɛhye kile kɛ Dwotam mɔɔ le Gedɛyɔn ara ne amonle mɔɔ wale bɛ la ɛdila.

english_verse: Tola was the next person to rescue Israel. He belonged to the Issachar tribe, but he lived in Shamir, a town in the hill country of Ephraim. His father was Puah, and his grandfather was Dodo.
translation_verse: Abemɛlɛke wule la sonla mɔɔ dwazole kɛ ɔbalie Yizilayɛma la a le Pua ara Tola. Ɔ nlenya a le Dodo, mɔɔ vi Yesakaa abusua ekpunli ne anu la. Ɔvi Hyeemɛ mɔɔ wɔ Yifelaem awoka ne mɔ azo la.

english_verse: Tola was a leader of Israel for
translation_verse: Ɔziele Yizilayɛma ɛvolɛ abulanwiɔ nee nsa. Ɔwule na bɛziele ye wɔ Hyeemɛ. Gyeeyɛɛ

english_verse: The next leader of Israel was Jair, who lived in Gilead. He was a leader for
translation_verse: Tola wule la, Gyeeyɛɛ mɔɔ vi Geleade la dwazole. Ɔdaye ɔziele Yizilayɛma ɛvolɛ abulanwiɔ nee nwiɔ.

english_verse: When he died, he was buried in the town of Kamon. Israel Is Unfaithful to God
translation_verse: Gyeeyɛɛ wule na bɛziele ye wɔ Keemɔn. Gyɛfeta

english_verse: Before long, the Israelites began disobeying the Lord by worshiping Baal, Astarte, and gods from Syria, Sidon, Moab, Ammon, and Philistia.
translation_verse: Eza Yizilayɛma yɛle ɛtane tiale Ɛdɛnkɛma. Bɛzonlenle Beeyale ne mɔ nee Ahyela ne mɔ. Bɛzonlenle Selea, Saedɛn, Mowabe, Amɔn, yɛɛ Filisitia awozonle ne mɔ bɛgyakyile Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛzonlenlɛ.

english_verse: The Lord was angry with Israel and decided to let Philistia and Ammon conquer them.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma vale ɛya na ɔyele Yizilayɛma ɔmanle Filisitiama nee Amɔnoma.

english_verse: So the same year that Jair died, Israel's army was crushed by these two nations. For
translation_verse: Bɛlile Yizilayɛma anwo zo konim na bɛziele Yizilayɛma mɔɔ wɔ Amɔle azɛlɛ zo wɔ Dwɔdan aduduleɛ mɔɔ wɔ Geleade maanle nu la, na bɛyɛle bɛ kpɔdekpɔde dedee ɛvolɛ bulu nee mɔtwɛ.

english_verse: The leaders of Gilead asked each other, “Who can lead an attack on the Ammonites?” Then they agreed, “If we find someone who can lead the attack, we'll make him the ruler of Gilead.”
translation_verse: Na Geleade mgbanyima nee menli ne bizebizale bɛ nwo ngoko kɛ, “Na nwane bɔbɔ yɛɛ di yɛ ti alumua ahɔdo Amɔnoma anwo etu a? Awie biala mɔɔ kɛzi ye ɛbolɛ kɛlumua la, sonla zɔhane yɛɛ kɛzie Geleadema amuala a.”

english_verse: Then the Ammonites began crossing the Jordan and attacking the tribes of Judah, Benjamin, and Ephraim. Life was miserable for the Israelites.
translation_verse: Amɔnoma pɛle Dwɔdan ne na bɛ nee Dwuda abusua ekpunli ne, Bɛngyaman abusua ekpunli ne, yɛɛ Yifelaem abusua ekpunli ne mɔ rahonle. Na Yizilayɛma akee wiele anwunvɔne yɛ.

english_verse: They begged the Lord for help and confessed, “We were unfaithful to you, our Lord. We stopped worshiping you and started worshiping idols of Baal.”
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma zunle vɛlɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ, “Yɛyɛ ɛtane yɛtia wɔ, ɔboalekɛ yɛkpo wɔmɔ mɔɔ ɛle yɛ Nyamenle la, na yɛzonle Beeyale ne mɔ.”

english_verse: But I'm not going to rescue you any more! You've left me and gone off to worship other gods. If you're in such big trouble, go and cry to them for help!
translation_verse: Bɛhɔ na bɛhɔzu bɛvɛlɛ bɛ nyamenle ne mɔ mɔɔ bɛnyia bɛ la na bɛmaa bɛlie bɛ bɛvi bɛ amaneɛnwunlɛ nu.”

english_verse: “We have been unfaithful to you,” the Israelites admitted. “If we must be punished, do it yourself, but please rescue us from the Ammonites.”
translation_verse: Na Yizilayɛma zɛlɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ, “Yɛyɛ ɛtane. Debie biala mɔɔ ɛkulo la fa yɛ yɛ. Na ɛnɛ kenle ye ɛdeɛ, yɛsɛlɛ wɔ, die yɛ.”

english_verse: The rulers of Ammon called their soldiers together and led them to Gilead, where they set up camp. The Israelites gathered at Mizpah and set up camp there.
translation_verse: Amɔn ɛlɔnema ne boɔboale bɛ nloa na bɛyɛle bɛ azokoɛleɛ wɔ Geleade. Yizilayɛma noko boɔboale bɛ ɛlɔnema ne anloa na bɛhɔdɛle Mezepa mɔɔ wɔ Geleade la.

english_verse: “Please come back to Gilead! If you lead our army, we will be able to fight off the Ammonites.”
translation_verse: Bɛzele ye kɛ, “Bɛla bali yɛ ti maa yɛ nee Amɔnoma ɛhɔho.”

english_verse: “Didn't you hate me?” Jephthah replied. “Weren't you the ones who forced me to leave my family? You're only coming to me now because you're in trouble.”
translation_verse: Na Gyɛfeta zele Geleade mgbanyima kɛ, “Na tɛ bɛmɛ a bɛhyile me na bɛdule me bɛvile egya awuke nu la. Duzu ati yɛɛ saa akee edwɛkɛ ɛdo bɛ a ɛnee bɛra bɛbakpo me bo zo a?”

english_verse: “But we do want you to come back,” the leaders said. “And if you lead us in battle against the Ammonites, we will make you the ruler of Gilead.”
translation_verse: Geleade mgbanyima zele Gyɛfeta kɛ, “Ɛhye ala ati yɛɛ yɛra yɛbakpo ɛ bo zo a, amaa wɔali yɛ ti na yɛ nee Amɔnoma ahɔho, na wɔali Geleade amuala kpanyinli.”

english_verse: “All right,” Jephthah said. “If I go back with you and the Lord lets me defeat the Ammonites, will you really make me your ruler?”
translation_verse: Gyɛfeta zele Geleade mgbanyima ne kɛ, “Saa bɛ nee me sia kɔ kɛ me nee Amɔnoma ɛhɔho, na Ɛdɛnkɛma maa medi konim a, mebali bɛ belemgbunli.”

english_verse: “You have our word,” the leaders answered. “And the Lord is a witness to what we have said.”
translation_verse: Geleade mgbanyima buale Gyɛfeta kɛ, “Yɛkponle zolɛ, Ɛdɛnkɛma di daselɛ; debie biala mɔɔ wɔbiza la, yɛbayɛ.”

english_verse: So Jephthah went back to Mizpah with the leaders of Gilead. The people of Gilead gathered at the place of worship and made Jephthah their ruler. Jephthah also made promises to them.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Gyɛfeta nee Geleade mgbanyima hɔle. Menli ne ziele ye belemgbunli na bɛyɛle kɛ ɔli bɛ ti. Gyɛfeta hanle ye edwɛkɛ muala hilele menli ne mɔ wɔ Mezepa wɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlu.

english_verse: After the ceremony, Jephthah sent messengers to say to the king of Ammon, “Are you trying to start a war? You have invaded my country, and I want to know why!”
translation_verse: Akee Gyɛfeta zoanle manle bɛhɔbizale Amɔn belemgbunli ne kɛ, “Duzu semunli yɛɛ me menli ne ɛze wɔ, mɔɔ yemɔti wɔra ɛbadoa bɛ ɛ nee bɛ aho a?”

english_verse: The king of Ammon replied, “Tell Jephthah that the land really belongs to me, all the way from the Arnon River in the south, to the Jabbok River in the north, and west to the Jordan River. When the Israelites came out of Egypt, they stole it. Tell Jephthah to return it to me, and there won't be any war.”
translation_verse: Amɔn belemgbunli ne buale Gyɛfeta soanvolɛma ne kɛ, “Semunli ne a le kɛ, mɔɔ Yizilayɛma vi Yigyibiti rale la, bɛvale me azɛlɛ, ɔvi Azule Gyabɛke ne anloa toonwo ɔkɔgua Azule Dwɔdan ne anloa. Saa bɛkpondɛ anzonudwolɛ a, ɛnee bɛva me azɛlɛ ne bɛmaa me.”

english_verse: Jephthah sent the messengers back to the king of Ammon,
translation_verse: Gyɛfeta eza zoanle menli bieko wɔ Amɔnoma belemgbunli ne ɛkɛ ne kɛ,

english_verse: and they told him that Jephthah had said: Israel hasn't taken any territory from Moab or Ammon.
translation_verse: “Kɛ Gyɛfeta se la ɛne: Yizilayɛma anva Mowabema azɛlɛ yɛɛ bɛanva Amɔnoma azɛlɛ.

english_verse: When the Israelites came from Egypt, they traveled across the desert to the Red Sea and then to Kadesh.
translation_verse: Bɛvi Yigyibiti la, bɛluale fienemgbole ne anu bɛhɔpɛle Ndɔ Nyevile ne na bɛravindele Keedɛhye.

english_verse: They sent messengers to the king of Edom and said, “Please, let us go through your country.” But the king of Edom refused. They also sent messengers to the king of Moab, but he wouldn't let them cross his country either. And so the Israelites stayed at Kadesh.
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma zoanle menli manle bɛhɔzele Yidɔm belemgbunli ne kɛ, ‘Yɛsɛlɛ wɔ, maa yɛ adenle maa yɛpɛ nu wɔ wɔ maanle ne anu.’ Na Yidɔm belemgbunli ne amkponle. Eza bɛzoanle menli wɔ Mowabe belemgbunli ne ɛkɛ, na ɔdaye noko yeammaa adenle. Yemɔti Yizilayɛma dɛnlanle Keedɛhye.

english_verse: A little later, the Israelites set out into the desert, going east of Edom and Moab, and camping on the eastern side of the Arnon River gorge. The Arnon is the eastern border of Moab, and since the Israelites didn't cross it, they didn't even set foot in Moab.
translation_verse: Nzinlii Yizilayɛma vale fienemgbole ne anu bule hoanenle Yidɔm nee Mowabe. Bɛravindele Mowabe foa ko mɔɔ di kɔ aduduleɛ la, na bɛyɛle bɛ azokoɛleɛ wɔ Azule Aanɔn ne anzi lɔ. Bɛangɔ Mowabe, ɔluakɛ Azule Aanɔn ne a le Mowabe ɛweɛne a.

english_verse: The Israelites sent messengers to the Amorite King Sihon of Heshbon. “Please,” they said, “let our people go through your country to get to our own land.”
translation_verse: Akee Yizilayɛma zoanle menli manle bɛhɔle Amɔle belemgbunli Saehɔn mɔɔ ɛnee de Hɛhyebɔn la ɛkɛ ne hɔzele ye kɛ, ‘Yɛsɛlɛ wɔ, maa yɛ adenle maa yɛpɛ nu wɔ wɔ maanle ne anu yɛhɔ yɛ maanle nu.’

english_verse: towns between Aroer and Minnith, and others as far as Abel-Keramim. After that, the Ammonites could not invade Israel any more. Jephthah's Daughter
translation_verse: Ɛnee Saehɔn ɛnlie Yizilayɛma ɛnli biala, yemɔti yeammaa bɛ adenle. Ɔboɔboale ye ɛlɔnema anloa, na ɔhɔdɛle bɛ wɔ Gyeehaze, na ɔ nee bɛ honle.

english_verse: But the Lord God helped Israel defeat Sihon and his army. Israel took over all of the Amorite land where Sihon's people had lived,
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma, Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne, yele Saehɔn nee ye ɛlɔnema manle Yizilayɛma lile bɛ nwo zo konim. Yemɔti Yizilayɛma vale Amɔlema azɛlɛ ne kɔsɔɔti.

english_verse: from the Arnon River in the south to the Jabbok River in the north, and from the desert in the east to the Jordan River in the west.
translation_verse: Bɛvale azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ vi Azule Aanɔn ne anloa toonwo hɔdwule Azule Gyabɛke ne anloa.

english_verse: The messengers also told the king of Ammon that Jephthah had said: The Lord God of Israel helped his nation get rid of the Amorites and take their land. Now do you think you're going to take over that same territory?
translation_verse: Yemɔti kɛkala, Ɛdɛnkɛma mɔɔ le Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne yɛɛ nee Amɔlema ɛho ɛlie bɛ maanle ne ɛmaa ye menli, Yizilayɛma a. Na duzu tumi yɛɛ wɔmɔ ɛdawɔ ɛlɛ ye mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ ɛsa yɛ ɛdie a?

english_verse: If Chemosh your god takes over a country and gives it to you, don't you have a right to it? And if the Lord takes over a country and gives it to us, the land is ours!
translation_verse: Duzu ati yɛɛ bɛnrɛhɔva bɛ maanle ɛdeɛ ne mɔɔ bɛ nyamenle Kimɔhye ne ɛva ɛmaa bɛ la ɛ? Ɔluakɛ azɛlɛ biala mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma, yɛ Nyamenle ne ɛva ɛmaa yɛ la, sinli bɔbɔ, yɛnrɛgyakyi nu.

english_verse: Are you better than Balak the son of Zippor? He was the king of Moab, but he didn't quarrel with Israel or start a war with us.
translation_verse: Anzɛɛ bɛdwenle kɛ bɛle kpalɛ bɛtɛla Zepɔ ara nrenya Balake mɔɔ di belemgbunli wɔ Mowabe la ɔ? Kenle ko bɔbɔ ɔ nee Yizilayɛma ɛtɛpelele debie biala anwo anzɛɛ ɔ nee bɛ ɛtɛkonle.

english_verse: I haven't done anything to you, but it's certainly wrong of you to start a war. I pray that the Lord will show whether Israel or Ammon is in the right.
translation_verse: Metɛfonle bɛ, yemɔti ɔle nvonleɛ kɛ bɛkɛva konle bɛkɛdoa me a. Ɛdɛnkɛma, mɔɔ le Ndɛnebuavolɛ ne, ɛnɛ kenle ko ye babua manzonle mɔɔ la Yizilayɛma nee Amɔnoma avinli la.”

english_verse: But the king of Ammon paid no attention to Jephthah's message.
translation_verse: Noko Amɔn belemgbunli ne anli Gyɛfeta nrɛlaleɛ ne anwo bie.

english_verse: Then the Lord's Spirit took control of Jephthah, and Jephthah went through Gilead and Manasseh, raising an army. Finally, he arrived at Mizpah in Gilead, where
translation_verse: Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma Sunsum ne dwule Gyɛfeta anwo zo. Ɔluale Geleade nee Manasɛ, na ɔtelele zolɛ ɔhɔle Mezepa mɔɔ wɔ Geleade la. Ɔvi Mezepa la ɔhɔvole Amɔnoma akɔme zo.

english_verse: he promised the Lord, “If you will let me defeat the Ammonites
translation_verse: Na Gyɛfeta bɔle ɛwɔkɛ wɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlu kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma, saa ɛmaa medi Amɔnoma anwo zo konim,

english_verse: From Mizpah, Jephthah attacked the Ammonites, and the Lord helped him defeat them.
translation_verse: Gyɛfeta pɛle azule ne na ɔhɔtetale Amɔnoma ɔ nee bɛ honle, na Ɛdɛnkɛma yele bɛ wulale ɔ sa nu.

english_verse: When Jephthah returned to his home in Mizpah, the first one to meet him was his daughter. She was playing a tambourine and dancing to celebrate his victory, and she was his only child.
translation_verse: Akee Gyɛfeta ziale rale ye sua zo Mezepa, na nea, ɔ ra raalɛ ne bɔle akɛya, zile agole vi awuke ne anu vindele kɛ ɔkayia ɔ ze adenle. Ɔ ze ara ala ɛne. Ɔnlɛ ralɛ nrenya anzɛɛ ralɛ raalɛ bieko ɔmboka ɔ nwo.

english_verse: “Oh no!” Jephthah cried. Then he tore his clothes in sorrow and said to his daughter, “I made a sacred promise to the Lord, and I must keep it. Your coming out to meet me has broken my heart.”
translation_verse: Gyɛfeta nwunle ɔ ra raalɛ ne la, ɔsuosuanle ye tɛladeɛ mɔɔ ɔwula la anu na ɔhanle kɛ, “Me ra raalɛ! Duzu ati a wɔde me ɛbolɛ kpole zɛhae ɛ? Mebɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛwɔkɛ mɔɔ hyia a, yɛɛ metwe mesia a ɔnyɛ boɛ.”

english_verse: “Father,” she said, “you made a sacred promise to the Lord, and he let you defeat the Ammonites. Now, you must do what you promised, even if it means I must die.
translation_verse: Ɔ ra raalɛ ne buale ye kɛ, “Egya, saa wɔbuke ɛ nloa wɔbɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛwɔkɛ a, ɛnee fa me yɛ deɛ mɔɔ vi ɛ nloa anu vindele la, ɔluakɛ kɛkala, Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛli Amɔnoma mɔɔ le wɔ kpɔvolɛma la nzenralɛ ne ɛmaa wɔ.”

english_verse: But first, please let me spend two months, wandering in the hill country with my friends. We will cry together, because I can never get married and have children.”
translation_verse: Na ɔzɛlɛle ɔ ze kɛ, “Debie ko ala a mesɛlɛ wɔ a, na yemɔ a le ɛhye: maa me siane nwiɔ maa me nee me gɔnwo mɔ yɛhɔ awoka ne mɔ azo lɔ na mengɔnzu me belamunli nu alɔbɔlɛ ewule.”

english_verse: “Yes, you may have two months,” Jephthah said. She and some other girls left, and for two months they wandered in the hill country, crying because she could never get married and have children.
translation_verse: Ɔ ze kponlenle siane nwiɔ ne azo na ɔzele kɛ ɔhɔ. Ɔ nee ɔ gɔnwo mɔ hɔle awoka ne mɔ azo, na ɔhɔzunle ɔ nwo kɛ yeannwu nrenya yeanwo ralɛ na yeawu a.

english_verse: Then she went back to her father. He did what he had promised, and she never got married. That's why
translation_verse: Siane nwiɔ ne dwule la ɔziale ɔrale ɔ ze anwo ɛkɛ ne, na ɔ ze vale ye yɛle mɔɔ ye ɛwɔkɛ ne se la. Ɛnee ɔ ra raalɛ ne ɛnze nrenya fee. Na ɔrayɛle maamɛla wɔ Yizilayɛ maanle nu

english_verse: every year, Israelite girls walk around for four days, weeping for Jephthah's daughter.
translation_verse: kɛ ɛvolɛ biala dwu a Yizilayɛ mraalɛ kɔsu Geleadenli Gyɛfeta ara raalɛ ne kenle nna.

english_verse: The men of the Ephraim tribe got together an army and went across the Jordan River to Zaphon to meet with Jephthah. They said, “Why did you go to war with the Ammonites without asking us to help? Just for that, we're going to burn down your house with you inside!”
translation_verse: Yifelaemma boɔboale ɛlɔnema anloa. Bɛpɛle Azule Dwɔdan ne bɛhɔle Zeefɔn bɛhɔbizale Gyɛfeta kɛ, “Duzu ati a bɛrazenle bɛ nee Amɔnoma hɔhonle na bɛambɔ yɛ amaneɛ bɛammaa yɛ nee bɛ angɔ ɛ? Yɛyela bɛ sua ye yɛagua bɛ ti zo.”

english_verse: “But I did ask for your help,” Jephthah answered. “That was back when the people of Gilead and I were having trouble with the Ammonites, and you wouldn't do a thing to help us.
translation_verse: Gyɛfeta zele bɛ kɛ, “Me menli ne nee Amɔnoma nyianle konle. Mendole ɛsalɛ menvɛlɛle bɛ la bɛambanlie me.

english_verse: So when we realized you weren't coming, we risked our lives and attacked the Ammonites. And the Lord let us defeat them. There's no reason for you to come here today to attack me.”
translation_verse: Mɔɔ menwunle kɛ bɛnrɛlie me bɛnrɛvi Amɔnoma asa anu la, yɛɛ menvale me ngoane mendole nzeleba a. Mempɛle azule ne mendoale Amɔnoma na Ɛdɛnkɛma yele bɛ manle me. Duzu ati yɛɛ ɛnɛ bɛdwazo kɛ akee bɛ nee me baho a?”

english_verse: The army of Gilead also posted guards at all the places where the soldiers from Ephraim could cross the Jordan River to return to their own land. Whenever one of the men from Ephraim would try to cross the river, the guards would say, “Are you from Ephraim?” “No,” the man would answer, “I'm not from Ephraim.”
translation_verse: Amaa Yifelaemma annyia adenle annriandi la, Geleadema hɔziale Azule Dwɔdan ne anloa, ɛleka mɔɔ bɛpɛ azule ne la. Saa Yifelaemenli nriandi badwu ɛkɛ ne na ɔse kɛ, “Bɛpɛ me azule” a, ɛnee Geleadema ne biza ye kɛ, “Ɛle Yifelaemenli ɔ?” Saa ɔse kɛ, “Kyɛkyɛ” a,

english_verse: The guards would then tell them to say “Shibboleth,” because they knew that people of Ephraim could say “Sibboleth,” but not “Shibboleth.” If the man said “Sibboleth,” the guards would grab him and kill him right there. Altogether,
translation_verse: ɛnee bɛse ye kɛ, “Ka edwɛkɛkpɔkɛ ‘Hyebɔlɛte.’ ” Saa ɔka a ɔse, “Sebɔlɛte,” ɔluakɛ Yifelaemenli ɛnze edwɛkɛkpɔkɛ zɔhane ka. Kɛ bɛnwu kɛ ɔle Yifelaemenli la ɛnee bɛhu ye wɔ Dwɔdan ne anloa ɛkɛ ne ala. Mekɛ zɔhane anu bɛhunle Yifelaemma apenle ngoko abulanla nee nwiɔ

english_verse: Jephthah was a leader of Israel for six years, before he died and was buried in his hometown Mizpah in Gilead. Ibzan
translation_verse: Gyɛfeta ziele Yizilayɛma ɛvolɛ nsia. Na Geleadenli Gyɛfeta wule na bɛziele ye wɔ ye sua zo Geleade. Yebezan, Yilɔn, yɛɛ Abedɛn

english_verse: Ibzan, the next leader of Israel, came from Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Gyɛfeta wule la, Yebezan mɔɔ vi Bɛtelɛhɛm la a ralile Yizilayɛma ati a.

english_verse: before he died and was buried in Bethlehem. Elon
translation_verse: Yebezan wule na bɛziele ye wɔ Bɛtelɛhɛm.

english_verse: Elon from the Zebulun tribe was the next leader of Israel. He was a leader for ten years,
translation_verse: Yebezan wule la, Yilɔn mɔɔ vi Zɛbulɛn abusua ekpunli nu la a lile Yizilayɛma ati a. Ɔlile bɛ ti ɛvolɛ bulu.

english_verse: before he died and was buried in Aijalon that belonged to the Zebulun tribe. Abdon
translation_verse: Yilɔn mɔɔ vi Zɛbulɛn abusua ekpunli ne anu la wule na bɛziele ye wɔ Ayegyalɔn wɔ Zɛbulɛn maanzinli nu.

english_verse: Abdon the son of Hillel was the next leader of Israel. He had
translation_verse: Na Abedɛn wule. Bɛziele ye wɔ Paeleetɔn mɔɔ wɔ Yifelaem azɛlɛ zo, wɔ Amalɛke maanle nu la awoka ne mɔ azo.

english_verse: Once again the Israelites started disobeying the Lord. So he let the Philistines take control of Israel for
translation_verse: Eza Yizilayɛma yɛle ɛtane bieko tiale Ɛdɛnkɛma. Yemɔti Ɛdɛnkɛma vale bɛ wulale Filisitiama abo ɛvolɛ abulanla.

english_verse: Manoah from the tribe of Dan lived in the town of Zorah. His wife was not able to have children,
translation_verse: Mekɛ ɛhye anu ɛnee nrenya bie wɔ Zɔla, bɛfɛlɛ ye Manowa. Ɔvi Dan abusua ekpunli ne anu. Ɔ ye le mota; ɔtɛwole ɛlɛ.

english_verse: but one day an angel from the Lord appeared to her and said: You have never been able to have any children, but very soon you will be pregnant and have a son. He will belong to God from the day he is born, so his hair must never be cut. And even before he is born, you must not drink any wine or beer or eat any food forbidden by God's laws. Your son will begin to set Israel free from the Philistines.
translation_verse: Mmadi debie biala mɔɔ nwolɛ ɛnde la. Ɔluakɛ ɛbanrenzɛ wɔawo ralɛ nrenya. Mmafa dadeɛ dɛma ɛka ɔ ti enrinli, ɔluakɛ kenle ko ne ala mɔɔ bɛkɛwo ye bɛkɛdo aze la, bɛbadu ye bɛazie ahane bɛamaa Nyamenle kɛ ɔle ‘Tusiemaa-Nyamenle’ ralɛ. Na yemɔ yɛɛ ɔbalie Yizilayɛma yeavi Filisitiama asa anu a.”

english_verse: She went to Manoah and said, “A prophet who looked like an angel of God came and talked to me. I was so frightened, that I didn't even ask where he was from. He didn't tell me his name,
translation_verse: Raalɛ ne rabɔle ɔ hu amaneɛ kɛ, “Nyamenle sonla ɛye ɔ nwo ɛhile me. Ɔ nwo yɛ ɛzulolɛ na ɔ nyunlu zɔho Nyamenle soanvolɛ. Meambiza ye ɛleka mɔɔ ɔvi la, yɛɛ ɔdaye noko yeambɔ ye duma yeangile me.

english_verse: but he did say that I'm going to have a baby boy. I'm not supposed to drink any wine or beer or eat any food forbidden by God's laws. Our son will belong to God for as long as he lives.”
translation_verse: Na ɔzele me kɛ, ‘Nea, ɛbava ɛkolɛ na wɔawo ralɛ nrenya; yemɔti mmano nwanye anzɛɛ nza ɛsesebɛ, yɛɛ mmadi debie biala mɔɔ nwolɛ ɛnde la, ɔluakɛ kakula ne le “Tusiemaa-Nyamenle” ralɛ mɔɔ kile kɛ ɔle Nyamenle ɛdeɛ, ɔvi ye awolɛ nu kɔkpula ye ewule nu.’ ”

english_verse: Then Manoah prayed, “Our Lord, please send that prophet again and let him tell us what to do for the son we are going to have.”
translation_verse: Na Manowa zɛlɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ, “O Ɛdɛnkɛma, mesɛlɛ wɔ, maa Nyamenle sonla ne mɔɔ ɛzoanle ye la ɛrɛla bieko, na ɔrahile yɛ kɛ yɛzi yɛyɛ kakula ne mɔɔ bɛbawo ye la.”

english_verse: God answered Manoah's prayer, and the angel went back to Manoah's wife while she was resting in the fields. Manoah wasn't there at the time,
translation_verse: Nyamenle diele Manowa nzɛlɛlɛ ne. Na mekɛ mɔɔ ɛnee raalɛ ne wɔ ye ɛya nu la, Nyamenle soanvolɛ ne ziale rale ɔ nwo ɛkɛ ne bieko. Ɛnee ɔ hu Manowa ɛnle ɔ nwo ɛkɛ.

english_verse: so she found him and said, “That same man is here again! He's the one I saw the other day.”
translation_verse: Yemɔti raalɛ ne vale ɛnriandilɛ hɔbɔle ɔ hu amaneɛ kɛ, “Nea, nrenya ne mɔɔ ɛkenle yele ɔ nwo hilele me la ɛra bieko.”

english_verse: Manoah went with his wife and asked the man, “Are you the one who spoke to my wife?” “Yes, I am,” he answered.
translation_verse: Manowa dwazole lile ɔ ye anzi, na bɛradole nrenya ne la ɔzele ye kɛ, “Wɔmɔ a ɛhanle edwɛkɛ ne ɛhilele raalɛ ye la ɔ?” Nrenya ne buale kɛ, “Ɛhɛe, medame ɔ.”

english_verse: Manoah then asked, “When your promise comes true, what rules must he obey and what will be his work?”
translation_verse: Manowa bizale ye kɛ, “Saa wɔ edwɛkɛ ne yɛ nɔhalɛ a, ɛnee duzu a ɔwɔ kɛ kakula ne yɛ a, yɛɛ duzu ɛbɛla a ɔwɔ kɛ ɔbɔ a?”

english_verse: “Your wife must be careful to do everything I told her,” the Lord's angel answered.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma soanvolɛ ne zele Manowa kɛ, “Edwɛkɛ biala mɔɔ meha mehile raalɛ ne la maa ɔli zolɛ.

english_verse: “She must not eat or drink anything made from grapes. She must not drink wine or beer or eat anything forbidden by God's laws. I told her exactly what to do.”
translation_verse: Debie biala mɔɔ bɛva vanye ma bɛyɛ la, ɔmmafa bie ɔka ɔ nloa. Eza ɔmmano nwanye anzɛɛ nza ɛsesebɛ biala, yɛɛ ɔmmadi debie biala mɔɔ nwolɛ ɛnde la. Ɛhye mɔ kɔsɔɔti mɔɔ meha la ɔwɔ kɛ ɔdi zolɛ.”

english_verse: Manoah didn't realize that he was really talking to one of the Lord's angels. The angel answered, “I can stay for a little while, although I won't eat any of your food. But if you would like to offer the goat as a sacrifice to the Lord, that would be fine.”
translation_verse: Ɛnee Manowa ɛnze kɛ nrenya ne le Ɛdɛnkɛma soanvolɛ, yemɔti ɔzele ye kɛ, “Mesɛlɛ wɔ, kendɛ ekyii maa yɛva abɔnkye yɛbu akposi ekyi yɛmaa wɔ.” Ɛdɛnkɛma soanvolɛ ne zele Manowa kɛ, “Saa ɛkye me ɛsie ɛke bɔbɔ a, menrɛli wɔ aleɛ ne. Na saa ɛkulo a, ɛnee yela nane ne bɔ azu maa Ɛdɛnkɛma.”

english_verse: Manoah said, “Tell us your name, so we can honor you after our son is born.”
translation_verse: Manowa bizale Ɛdɛnkɛma soanvolɛ ne kɛ, “Kɛ bɛfɛlɛ wɔ ɛ, amaa saa wɔ edwɛkɛ ne yɛ nɔhalɛ a yɛawula wɔ anyunlunyia?”

english_verse: “No,” the angel replied. “You don't need to know my name. And if you did, you couldn't understand it.”
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma soanvolɛ ne zele ye kɛ, “Duzu ati a ɛkulo kɛ ɛnwu me duma a? Ɔle duma ɛzulolɛ bie.”

english_verse: Manoah said, “We have seen an angel. Now we're going to die.”
translation_verse: Manowa zele ɔ ye kɛ, “Yɛnwu Nyamenle! Yɛbawu”

english_verse: “The Lord isn't going to kill us,” Manoah's wife responded. “The Lord accepted our sacrifice and grain offering, and he let us see something amazing. Besides, he told us that we're going to have a son.”
translation_verse: Na ɔ ye buale ye kɛ, “Saa Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛhu yɛ a, anrɛɛ yeanlie yɛ sa nu azubɔdeɛ ne; anrɛɛ ɔnrɛhile yɛ ninyɛne ɛhye mɔ anzɛɛ ɔnrɛha ɛhye mɔ amuala ɔnrɛhile yɛ.”

english_verse: Later, Manoah's wife did give birth to a son, and she named him Samson. As the boy grew, the Lord blessed him.
translation_verse: Raalɛ ne wole ralɛ nrenya na bɛdonle ye Samesɛn. Kakula ne nyinle, na Ɛdɛnkɛma yilale ye.

english_verse: Then, while Samson was staying at Dan's Camp between the towns of Zorah and Eshtaol, the Spirit of the Lord took control of him.
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma Sunsum ne manle ye anwosesebɛ. Mekɛ ne anu ɛnee ɔde Dan abusua ekpunli ne azokoɛleɛ ne, wɔ Zɔla nee Yehyeteɔlo avinli.

english_verse: One day, Samson went to Timnah, where he saw a Philistine woman.
translation_verse: Kenle ko Samesɛn hɔle Temena, na ɔnwunle Filisitia bɛlɛra bie.

english_verse: When he got back home, he told his parents, “I saw a Philistine woman in Timnah, and I want to marry her. Get her for me!”
translation_verse: Ɔziale ɔhɔle sua nu la ɔbɔle ɔ ze nee ɔ nli amaneɛ kɛ, “Menwu Filisitia bɛlɛra bie na me ahonle ɛva ye, yemɔti bɛhɔgya ye bɛmaa me.”

english_verse: His parents answered, “There are a lot of women in our clan and even more in the rest of Israel. Those Philistines are pagans. Why would you want to marry one of their women?” “She looks good to me,” Samson answered. “Get her for me!”
translation_verse: Ɔ ze nee ɔ nli zele ye kɛ, “Anzɛɛ raalɛ biala ɛnle yɛ abusua ekpulike ɛdeɛ ye anu mɔɔ ɛgya ye a ɔyɛ boɛ, mɔɔ yemɔti ɛkɔ menli mɔɔ ɛnze Nyamenle la avinli wɔahɔgya raalɛ a?” Samesɛn zele ɔ ze kɛ, “Bɛgya ye bɛmaa me, ɔluakɛ me ahonle ɛva ye kpalɛ.”

english_verse: At that time, the Philistines were in control of Israel, and the Lord wanted to stir up trouble for them. That's why he made Samson desire that woman.
translation_verse: Samesɛn ɔ ze nee ɔ nli ɛnze kɛ ɛhye mɔ kɔsɔɔti Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛɛ ɛlɛyɛ a, ɔluakɛ ɛnee Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛlɛkpondɛ adenle yealua nu yeadua Filisitiama kakɛ. Mekɛ zɔhane anu ɛnee Filisitiama a sie Yizilayɛma a.

english_verse: As Samson and his parents reached the vineyards near Timnah, a fierce young lion suddenly roared and attacked Samson.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Samesɛn nee ɔ ze nee ɔ nli hɔle Temena. Bɛdwule Temena la Samesɛn hɔkpɔsale Temena vanye ɛya ne mɔ anu, na ɔnwunle kɛ awenade ekyi bie ɛlɛkpo nee ye ayia.

english_verse: But the Lord's Spirit took control of Samson, and with his bare hands he tore the lion apart, as though it had been a young goat. His parents didn't know what he had done, and he didn't tell them.
translation_verse: Ɛkɛ ne ala Ɛdɛnkɛma Sunsum ne dwule ɔ nwo zo. Ɔvale ɔ sa mgbane ɔtetele awenade ne kɛ asɛɛ abɔnkye ralɛ bie la. Noko ɛhye mɔɔ ɔyɛle la yeanga yeangile ɔ ze nee ɔ nli.

english_verse: When they got to Timnah, Samson talked to the woman, and he was sure that she was the one for him.
translation_verse: Akee ɔhɔle na ɔ nee raalɛ ne hɔlile adwelie, na Samesɛn anye liele.

english_verse: Later, Samson returned to Timnah for the wedding. And when he came near the place where the lion had attacked, he left the road to see what was left of the lion. He was surprised to see that bees were living in the lion's skeleton, and that they had made some honey.
translation_verse: Yeangyɛ biala yɛɛ Samesɛn hɔgyale bɛlɛra ne a. Mɔɔ ɔlua adenle ne anu ɔlɛkɔ la, ɔdole ɔ nye ɔnleanle awenade funli ne, na ɛnee awenade funli ne ɛlɔ wolɛ.

english_verse: He scooped up the honey in his hands and ate some of it as he walked along. When he got back to his parents, he gave them some of the honey, and they ate it too. But he didn't tell them he had found the honey in the skeleton of a lion.
translation_verse: Ɔvale ɔ sa ɔbule wolɛ ndɛlamoa ne bie, na mɔɔ ɔ gyakɛ wɔ zolɛ la ɛnee ɔlɛdi. Ɔvale bie ɔhɔmanle ɔ ze nee ɔ nli, na bɛdabɛ noko bɛlile. Noko yeanga yeangile bɛ kɛ ɔbule wolɛ ndɛlamoa ne ɔvile awenade funli nu.

english_verse: While Samson's father went to make the final arrangements with the bride and her family, Samson threw a big party, as grooms usually did.
translation_verse: Samesɛn ɔ ze hɔle raalɛ ne sua zo, na Samesɛn dole ɛkponle wɔ ɛkɛ. Ɛhye le amaamuo mɔɔ mgbavolɛ ne mɔ ɔyɛ a bu a.

english_verse: When the Philistines saw what Samson was like, they told
translation_verse: Mɔɔ menli ne mɔ nwunle ye la bɛyele mgbavolɛ abulasa bɛmanle ye kɛ ɔ nee bɛ ɛlua.

english_verse: But if you can't tell me the answer, then each of you will have to give me a shirt and a full change of clothing.” “It's a bet!” the Philistines said. “Tell us the riddle.”
translation_verse: na saa bɛangola ɔ nloa ye a, ɛnee ɔwɔ kɛ bɛdabɛ noko bɛmaa me adɛladeɛ fufule abulasa yɛɛ ɛvoyialilɛ adɛladeɛ abulasa.” Na bɛzele ye kɛ, “Gye wɔ agyebɛ ne maa yɛdie.”

english_verse: Samson said: Once so strong and mighty— now so sweet and tasty! Three days went by, and the Philistine young men had not come up with the right answer.
translation_verse: Na Samesɛn gyele bɛ zɛhae, “Debie mɔɔ bɛdi la vi mɔɔ di debie la anu rale. Debie fɛlɛko vi mɔɔ anwo yɛ se la anu rale.” Kenle kɔkɔlɛ nsa ɛnee awie biala ɛtɛkolale agyebɛ ne anloa ye.

english_verse: Finally, on the seventh day of the party they went to Samson's bride and said, “You had better trick your husband into telling you the answer to his riddle. Have you invited us here just to rob us? If you don't find out the answer, we will burn you and your family to death.”
translation_verse: Ye kenle nna ne azo bɛzele Samesɛn aye ne kɛ, “To ɛ hu agyiba maa ɔye ye agyebɛ ne anloa anrɛɛ yɛyela wɔ nee ɛ ze awuke nu amra amuala. Bɛva yɛ bɛra ɛke kɛ bɛbabɔ yɛ anyiemgba ɔ?”

english_verse: Samson's bride went to him and started crying in his arms. “You must really hate me,” she sobbed. “If you loved me at all, you would have told me the answer to your riddle.” “But I haven't even told my parents the answer!” Samson replied. “Why should I tell you?”
translation_verse: Na Samesɛn aye ne zunle ɔ hu akɔme nu zele kɛ, “Ɛkpɔ me, ɛngulo me. Wɔgye me menli ne agyebɛ na wɔanga ye nyelebɛnloa ne wɔangile me.” Samesɛn zele ɔ ye kɛ, “Duzu ati yɛɛ menga mengile wɔ a? Nea, egya nee ɔmɔ bɔbɔ, metɛkanle metɛkilele bɛ.”

english_verse: For the entire seven days of the party, she had been whining and trying to get the answer from him. But that seventh day she put so much pressure on Samson that he finally gave in and told her the answer. She went straight to the young men and told them.
translation_verse: Ɔ ye zunle ɛhye anwo toonwo kenle nsuu ne mɔɔ bɛvale bɛdole ɛkponle ne la dwule. Kenle nsuu ne azo mɔɔ ɛnee akee ɛzunlɛ ne ɛyɛ ye abodelɛ la, ɔhanle agyebɛ ne nyelebɛnloa ɔhilele ye. Na ɔdaye noko ɔhanle ɔhilele ye menli ne.

english_verse: Before sunset that day, the men of the town went to Samson with this answer: A lion is the strongest— honey is the sweetest! Samson replied, This answer you have given me doubtless came from my bride-to-be.
translation_verse: Kenle nsuu ne azo, suakpole ne azo amra hanle nyelebɛnloa ne hilele Samesɛn kolaa na sɛnzɛne ne adɔ. Bɛyele ɔ nloa zɛhae, “Duzu a yɛ fɛ tɛla wolɛ a? Duzu a anwo yɛ se tɛla awenade a?” Samesɛn buale bɛ kɛ, “Saa bɛanva me ɛnlankɛ bɛangɔ ɛyazonlɛ a, anrɛɛ bɛnrɛnwu me agyebɛ ne anzi ɛlɛ.”

english_verse: The father of the bride made Samson's wife marry one of the
translation_verse: Na bɛvale Samesɛn aye ne bɛmanle mɔɔ kyekyele agyalɛ ne abo la gyale ye.

english_verse: “When you left the way you did, I thought you were divorcing her. So I arranged for her to marry one of the young men who were at your party. But my younger daughter is even prettier, and you can have her as your wife.”
translation_verse: Ɔzele kɛ, “Mekɔ me ye anwo wɔ ye sua kunlu ɛkɛ.” Na ɔ ye ɔ ze ammaa ye adenle. Ɔzele ye kɛ, “Mendwenlenle kɛ ɛngulo ye bieko, yemɔti menvale ye memanle ɛ gɔnwo ne. Ɔ diema raalɛ ekyi ne anwo yɛ fɛ tɛla ye. Mesɛlɛ wɔ, gya yemɔ.”

english_verse: “This time,” Samson answered, “I have a good reason for really hurting some Philistines.” Samson Takes Revenge
translation_verse: Samesɛn zele kɛ, “Ɛnɛ ɛdeɛ, saa mebu Filisitiama amaamuo ɛtane a, awie biala mmafu me.”

english_verse: Then Samson took the foxes into the Philistine wheat fields that were ready to be harvested. He set the rags on fire and let the foxes go. The wheat fields went up in flames, and so did the stacks of wheat that had already been cut. Even the Philistine vineyards and olive orchards burned.
translation_verse: Akee ɔvale senle ɔsosɔle tɛkɛ ne mɔ na ɔgyakyile ɛzonlɛ ne mɔ ɔmanle bɛhɔle Filisitiama abɛlɛ ɛya avule ne mɔ anu. Bɛhɔyelale abɛlɛ mɔɔ bɛbu bɛhua nee mɔɔ bɛtɛbule, nee ɔlivi ɛya avule ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti.

english_verse: Some of the Philistines started asking around, “Who could have done such a thing?” “It was Samson,” someone told them. “He married the daughter of that man in Timnah, but then the man gave Samson's wife to one of the men at the wedding.” The Philistine leaders went to Timnah and burned to death Samson's wife and her father.
translation_verse: Filisitiama ne bizale kɛ, “Ɛnee nwane yɛɛ ɛbɔ ɛbɛla ɛhye a?” Na bɛdele kɛ Samesɛn ɔ, ɔluakɛ ɔ ye ɔ ze ne mɔɔ vi Temena la ɛva ɔ ye ɛmaa ɔdaye Samesɛn ɔ gɔnwo ɛgya ye. Na Filisitiama rale na bɛrayelale ɔ ye nee ɔ ze.

english_verse: When Samson found out what they had done, he went to them and said, “You killed them! And I won't rest until I get even with you.”
translation_verse: Na Samesɛn zele bɛ kɛ, “Saa amaamuo zɛhae yɛɛ bɛbu ɛdeɛ a, ɛnee meka, meka kɛ, saa metɛyɛle bɛ bie metɛsiele ɔ bo zo a, menrɛla.”

english_verse: Then Samson started hacking them to pieces with his sword. Samson left Philistia and went to live in the cave at Etam Rock.
translation_verse: Ɔhɔle bɛ nwo zo na ɔhunle bɛ bie mɔ dɔɔnwo. Akee ɔhɔle na ɔhɔdɛnlanle bolɛ bɔne bie anu wɔ Yitam bodane ne azo. Samesɛn di Filisitiama anwo zo konim

english_verse: But it wasn't long before the Philistines invaded Judah and set up a huge army camp at Jawbone.
translation_verse: Akee Filisitiama raziale Dwuda, na bɛvale konle bɛdoale Lihaema.

english_verse: The people of Judah asked, “Why have you invaded our land?” The Philistines answered, “We've come to get Samson. We're going to do the same things to him that he did to our people.”
translation_verse: Na Dwudama bizale bɛ kɛ, “Duzu ati yɛɛ bɛva konle bɛradoa yɛ a?” Bɛbuale kɛ, “Yɛra kɛ yɛbahye Samesɛn, na mɔɔ yeva yeyɛ yɛ la, yɛdayɛ noko yɛayɛ ye bie.”

english_verse: Three thousand men from Judah went to the cave at Etam Rock and said to Samson, “Don't you know that the Philistines rule us, and they will punish us for what you did?” “I was only getting even with them,” Samson replied. “They did the same things to me first.”
translation_verse: Na Dwudama apenle nsa hɔle Yitam bodane ne bɔne ne mɔɔ Samesɛn wɔ nu la anu na bɛzele ye kɛ, “Ɛnze kɛ Filisitiama a sie yɛ ɔ? Na ɛhye noko mɔɔ wɔhɔhwe wɔra la abo a le duzu?” Samesɛn zele bɛ kɛ, “Amaamuo mɔɔ bɛbule bɛmanle me la yɛɛ menlea zolɛ mebu bie memaa bɛ a.”

english_verse: “We came here to tie you up and turn you over to them,” said the men of Judah. “I won't put up a fight,” Samson answered, “but you have to promise not to hurt me yourselves.”
translation_verse: Na bɛzele ye kɛ, “Yɛra kɛ yɛbakyekye wɔ yɛahɔmaa Filisitiama.” Samesɛn zele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛha ndane kɛ bɛmɛ bɛdabɛ mumua ne bɛnrɛhu me.”

english_verse: “We promise,” the men said. “We will only tie you up and turn you over to the Philistines. We won't kill you.” Then they tied up his hands and arms with two brand-new ropes and led him away from Etam Rock. When the Philistines saw that Samson was being brought to their camp at Jawbone, they started shouting and ran toward him. But the Lord's Spirit took control of Samson, and Samson broke the ropes, as though they were pieces of burnt cloth.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ bɛ nee ye radwule Lihae la, Filisitiama vale ɛwudolɛ nriandile rayiale ye. Na Ɛdɛnkɛma Sunsum ne dwule ɔ nwo zo kpole kpalɛ, na ɔtetele samgbe nyɛma amolɛ nwiɔ ne mɔɔ bɛvale bɛkyekyele ɔ sa la kɛ asɛɛ dwɛsɛ mɔɔ senle ɛdɔ nu la.

english_verse: After the fighting was over, he made up this poem about what he had done to the Philistines: I used a donkey's jawbone to kill a thousand men; I beat them with this jawbone over and over again.
translation_verse: Na Samesɛn zele kɛ, “Meva asoaso awudwelɛ bowule mehuohua bɛ ɛdukue ɛdukue; meva asoaso awudwelɛ bowule mehu menli apenle.”

english_verse: Samson tossed the jawbone on the ground and decided to call the place Jawbone Hill. It is still called that today.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ ɔwiele tendɛ la, ɔvuandinle awudwelɛ bowule ne mɔɔ ɔlɛ la ɔdole; na bɛvɛlɛle ɛleka mɔɔ ɔdɔle la Releemate Lihae.

english_verse: Samson was so thirsty that he prayed, “Our Lord, you helped me win a battle against a whole army. Please don't let me die of thirst now. Those heathen Philistines will carry off my dead body.”
translation_verse: Akee nzuhɔne hunle ye kpole kpalɛ, na ɔzɛlɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ, “Wɔlua wɔ sonvolɛ nwo zo wɔlie wɔ menli ye ngoane. Na nzuhɔne ɛlɛku me yeamaa meadɔ donvula wɔ menli mɔɔ ɛnze Nyamenle la asa anu ɔ?”

english_verse: Samson was tired and weary, but God sent water gushing from a rock. Samson drank some and felt strong again. Samson named the place Caller Spring, because he had called out to God for help. The spring is still there at Jawbone.
translation_verse: Na Nyamenle manle nzule vi azɛlɛ bo vindele kuma bie anu manle ye wɔ Lihae. Samesɛn nlonle bie na ye ahonle gyinlanle na ɔ nwo yɛle se. Yemɔti bɛdonle nzule ne “Hakɔli”. Na ɛnɛ nee ɛnɛ ala ɔtɛbɔ Lihae.

english_verse: years, but the Philistines were still the rulers of Israel.
translation_verse: Samesɛn lile Yizilayɛma ati ɛvolɛ abulanwiɔ wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɛnee bɛwɔ Filisitiama abo la.

english_verse: The people who lived in Gaza found out he was there, and they decided to kill him at sunrise. So they went to the city gate and waited all night in the guardrooms on each side of the gate.
translation_verse: Bɛhanle bɛhilele Gazama kɛ, “Samesɛn ɛra ɛke.” Aledwolɛ ne amuala bɛbɔle bɛyiale sua ne na bɛ bie mɔ hɔdɛle ye wɔ suakpole ne anlenkɛ kpole ne anloa. Bɛyɛle ngungoonwu na bɛzele kɛ, “Bɛmaa yɛdɛ toonwo alehyenlɛ na yɛ sa baha ye yɛahu ye.”

english_verse: Some time later, Samson fell in love with a woman named Delilah, who lived in Sorek Valley.
translation_verse: Ɛhye anzi, Samesɛn nwunle raalɛ bie mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye Dɛlaela la wɔ Sɔlɛke Bɔnza na ɔhulole ye.

english_verse: The Philistine rulers went to Delilah and said, “Trick Samson into telling you what makes him so strong and what can make him weak. Then we can tie him up so he can't get away. If you find out his secret, we will each give you
translation_verse: Filisitia mgbanyima hɔnwunle Dɛlaela na bɛzele ye kɛ, “To Samesɛn agyiba na nwu deɛ holɛ ko ne mɔɔ maa ye anwosesebɛ kpole zɛhae la, nee adenle mɔɔ yɛdua zolɛ a yɛkɛkyekye ye, na yɛkɛbɛlɛ ye aze la, na yɛ nuhua ko biala kɛmaa wɔ dwɛtɛ fufule apenle ko ɛya ko.”

english_verse: The next time Samson was at Delilah's house, she asked, “Samson, what makes you so strong? How can I tie you up so you can't get away? Come on, you can tell me.”
translation_verse: Yemɔti Dɛlaela zele Samesɛn kɛ, “Yɛmenle, kile me deɛ holɛ ko mɔɔ maa wɔ anwosesebɛ kpole ɛhye la, nee adenle mɔɔ bɛdua zolɛ a bɛkɛhola wɔ kyekye na bɛabɛlɛ wɔ aze la.”

english_verse: Samson answered, “If someone ties me up with seven new bowstrings that have never been dried, it will make me just as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Samesɛn zele ye kɛ, “Saa bɛfa ɛda nyɛma amolɛ nsuu mɔɔ bɛtɛrɛlɛle ye fee la bɛkyekye me a me nwo bagolo me, na me anwosesebɛ ne bayɛ kɛ nrenya gyɛne biala anwosesebɛ la.”

english_verse: The Philistine rulers gave seven new bowstrings to Delilah. They also told some of their soldiers to go to Delilah's house and hide in the room where Samson and Delilah were. If the bowstrings made Samson weak, they would be able to capture him. Delilah tied up Samson with the bowstrings and shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson snapped the bowstrings, as though they were pieces of scorched string. The Philistines had not found out why Samson was so strong.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ ɔyɛ ɛhye la, ɛnee menli vea sua ne ekpumgbunli ne bie anu ɛlɛkendɛ. Na ɔzele Samesɛn kɛ, “Samesɛn, Filisitiama ɛva wɔ aze!” Na Samesɛn tetele ɛda nyɛma ne anu kɛ dwɛsɛ mɔɔ senle ɛha ye la. Yemɔti bɛanwu deɛ mɔɔ maa ye anwosesebɛ ne la.

english_verse: “You lied and made me look like a fool,” Delilah said. “Now tell me. How can I really tie you up?”
translation_verse: Dɛlaela zele Samesɛn kɛ, “Wɔyɛ me koasea, wɔanga nɔhalɛ wɔangile me. Ka kɛ bɛkɛzi bɛkɛyɛ na bɛahola wɔ kyekye la kile me.”

english_verse: Samson answered, “Use some new ropes. If I'm tied up with ropes that have never been used, I'll be just as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Ɔzele ye kɛ, “Saa bɛfa samgbe nyɛma fofolɛ mɔɔ bɛtɛfale bɛtɛyɛle debie biala la bɛkyekye me a, me nwo bagolo me, na me anwosesebɛ ne bayɛ kɛ nrenya gyɛne biala anwosesebɛ la.”

english_verse: Delilah got new ropes, and again some Philistines hid in the room. Then she tied up Samson's arms and shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson snapped the ropes as if they were threads.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Dɛlaela vale nyɛma fofolɛ kyekyele ye na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Samesɛn, Filisitiama ɛva wɔ aze!” Ɛnee menli vea ye suakunlu ɛkɛ ɛlɛkendɛ. Na Samesɛn tetele nyɛma ne anu kɛ asɛɛ ɔle melahyinli nyɛma la.

english_verse: “You're still lying and making a fool of me,” Delilah said. “Tell me how I can tie you up!” “My hair is in seven braids,” Samson replied. “If you weave my braids into the threads on a loom and nail the loom to a wall, then I will be as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Na Dɛlaela zele Samesɛn kɛ, “Sumunli kɛ de la, me nwo ala a ɛgolo a. Ɛnga nɔhalɛ ɛngile me. Ka kɛ bɛkɛzi bɛkɛyɛ na bɛahola wɔ kyekye la kile me.” Na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Me enrinli ne mɔɔ bɛbobɔ ye agbɔkɛ nsuu mɔɔ hendɛhenda me ti zo la, saa ɛbɛka bɛ muala ɛbɔ nu, ɛfa pini ɛbɔ nu, ɛbɔ ye kpɔkɛ ɛmia nu a, me nwo bagolo me, na me anwosesebɛ ne bayɛ kɛ nrenya gyɛne biala anwosesebɛ la.”

english_verse: While Samson was asleep, Delilah wove his braids into the threads on a loom and nailed the loom to a wall. Then she shouted, “Samson, the Philistines are attacking!” Samson woke up and pulled the loom free from its posts in the ground and from the nails in the wall. Then he pulled his hair free from the woven cloth.
translation_verse: Yemɔti ɔlafele la, Dɛlaela vulale enrinli ne mɔɔ hendɛhenda ɔ ti zo la, ɔbɛkale ɔmanle ɔmianle ketekete na ɔvale pini ɔbɔle nu, na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Samesɛn, Filisitiama ɛva wɔ aze!” Na ɔvi nafelɛ nu ɔdwazole, ɔdule pini ne na ɔtulutulule ɔ ti ne.

english_verse: “Samson,” Delilah said, “you claim to love me, but you don't mean it! You've made me look like a fool three times now, and you still haven't told me why you are so strong.”
translation_verse: Dɛlaela zele ye kɛ, “Ɛnee kɛ ɛsi ɛka kɛ ɛkulo me ɛ, wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɛhulolɛ ne ɛnvi wɔ ahonle nu la? Wɔgolo me nwo fane nsa. Ɛleka mɔɔ wɔ anwosesebɛ kpole ne vi la ɛtɛkanle ɛtɛkilele me.”

english_verse: Delilah started nagging and pestering him day after day, until he couldn't stand it any longer.
translation_verse: Na ɔhɔle zolɛ ɔbizale ye alehyenlɛ biala ɔmanle akee ɔyɛle Samesɛn abodelɛ mɔɔ ɛnee ɔ kunlu a anrɛɛ yewu bɔbɔ.

english_verse: Finally, Samson told her the truth. “I have belonged to God ever since I was born, so my hair has never been cut. If it were ever cut off, my strength would leave me, and I would be as weak as anyone else.”
translation_verse: Na ɔhanle nɔhalɛ ne kɔsɔɔti ɔhilele ye kɛ, “Dadeɛ dɛma ɛtɛkanle me ti enrinli ɛlɛ, ɔluakɛ mele ‘Tusiemaa-Nyamenle’ ralɛ mɔɔ bɛdule me bɛziele ɛkɛ bɛmanle Nyamenle kolaa na bɛawo me a. Kenle ko ne mɔɔ dadeɛ dɛma kɛha me ti enrinli la, kenle zɔhane, me anwosesebɛ ne kɛvi me nu; me nwo bagolo me, na menwɔyɛ kɛ nrenya gyɛne biala la.”

english_verse: Delilah realized that he was telling the truth. So she sent someone to tell the Philistine rulers, “Come to my house one more time. Samson has finally told me the truth.” The Philistine rulers went to Delilah's house, and they brought along the silver they had promised her.
translation_verse: Dɛlaela nwunle kɛ akee Samesɛn ɛha nɔhalɛ kɔsɔɔ ne ɛhile ye la, ɔzoanle ɔmanle bɛhɔbɔle Filisitia mgbanyima ne amaneɛ kɛ, “Bɛrɛla na akee yeha nɔhalɛ ne mɔɔ vea la.” Filisitia mgbanyima ne vale ɛwɔkɛbɔlɛ ezukoa ne lɛle bɛ sa nu rale.

english_verse: Delilah had lulled Samson to sleep with his head resting in her lap. She signaled to one of the Philistine men as she began cutting off Samson's seven braids. And by the time she was finished, Samson's strength was gone. Delilah tied him up
translation_verse: Ɔmanle Samesɛn lale ɔ gyakɛ azo na ɔbobole ye ɔmanle ɔlafele. Ɔvɛlɛle nrenya bie ɔmanle ɔrakpale ɔ ti enrinli totɔkɔɔ nsuu ne. Akee ɔbɔle ɔ bo kɛ ɔnwonlonwonlo ye. Na Samesɛn anwo golole ye, na ye anwosesebɛ ne vile ye nu.

english_verse: The Philistines grabbed Samson and poked out his eyes. They took him to the prison in Gaza and chained him up. Then they put him to work, turning a millstone to grind grain.
translation_verse: Filisitiama ne hyele ye dudule ɔ nye na bɛ nee ye hɔle Gaza. Bɛvale kɔbele nwɔnzɔnwɔnzɔ bɛguale ye na bɛmanle ɔhyibale abɛlɛ melahyinli, ɔdinle abɛlɛ wɔ efiade ɛkɛ ne.

english_verse: But they didn't cut his hair any more, so it started growing back.
translation_verse: Na ɔ ti enrinli ne mɔɔ bɛkpale la bɔle ɔ bo kɛ ɔfifi bieko. Samesɛn ewule ne

english_verse: The Philistine rulers threw a big party and sacrificed a lot of animals to their god Dagon. The rulers said: Samson was our enemy, but our god Dagon helped us capture him!
translation_verse: Akee Filisitia mgbanyima yiale kɛ bɛbɔ azu bɛamaa bɛ bozonle Deegɔn ne na bɛalie bɛ nye. Bɛzele kɛ, “Yɛ nyamenle ne ɛye yɛ kpɔvolɛ Samesɛn ɛmaa yɛ.”

english_verse: Everyone there was having a good time, and they shouted, “Bring out Samson—he's still good for a few more laughs!” The rulers had Samson brought from the prison, and when the people saw him, this is how they praised their god: Samson ruined our crops and killed our people. He was our enemy, but our god helped us capture him. They made fun of Samson for a while, then they told him to stand near the columns that supported the roof.
translation_verse: Menli ne anye liele kpole kpalɛ, na bɛzele kɛ, “Bɛva Samesɛn bɛrɛla bɛmaa yɛva ye yɛlielie yɛ nye.” Bɛvale Samesɛn bɛvile efiade ne bɛrale, na bɛziele ye wɔ sua ne mpila nwiɔ ne avinli, na bɛvale ye bɛlieliele bɛ nye. Mɔɔ menli ne nwunle ye la, bɛyeyɛle bɛ bozonle ne bɛzele kɛ, “Yɛ nyamenle ne ɛmaa yɛli yɛ kpɔvolɛ ne mɔɔ ɛbɔ yɛ maanle ye ɛhu menli dɔɔnwo la anwo zo konim.”

english_verse: A young man was leading Samson by the hand, and Samson said to him, “I need to lean against something. Take me over to the columns that hold up the roof.”
translation_verse: Samesɛn zele kpavolɛ ne mɔɔ lɛ ɔ sa la kɛ, “Maa mensosɔ sua ye mpila nwiɔ ne mɔɔ lɛ ye la anu na mendudu mengisa bɛ.”

english_verse: Samson prayed, “Please remember me, Lord God. The Philistines poked out my eyes, but make me strong one last time, so I can take revenge for at least one of my eyes!”
translation_verse: Akee Samesɛn vɛlɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma na ɔhanle kɛ, “O Awulae Nyamenle, mesɛlɛ wɔ ko ɛhye ala. Kakye me, O Nyamenle, na maa me anwosesebɛ maa menzenra Filisitiama ye wɔ me nye nwiɔ ye mɔɔ bɛdudu la anwo.”

english_verse: Samson was standing between the two middle columns that held up the roof. He felt around and found one column with his right hand, and the other with his left hand.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Samesɛn sosɔle sua ne avinli mpila nwiɔ ne anu, ɔvale ye anwosesebɛ ne amuala ɔhomonle zolɛ, ɔ sa fema ne lɛ ko anu yɛɛ bɛne ne noko lɛ ko anu.

english_verse: Then he shouted, “Let me die with the Philistines!” He pushed against the columns as hard as he could, and the temple collapsed with the Philistine rulers and everyone else still inside. Samson killed more Philistines when he died than he had killed during his entire life.
translation_verse: Na ɔzele kɛ, “Maa me nee Filisitiama ye ɛwu.” Ɔvale ye anwosesebɛ kɔsɔɔti ɔtiale mpila nwiɔ ne. Sua ne bule guale mgbanyima nee menli mɔɔ wɔ nu la amuala anwo zo. Yemɔti menli mɔɔ ɔhunle bɛ wɔ ye ewule nu la zonle tɛla menli mɔɔ ɔbɔ ɔ bo amuala la yehu bɛ la.

english_verse: His brothers and the rest of his family went to Gaza and took his body back home. They buried him in his father's tomb, which was located between Zorah and Eshtaol. Samson was a leader of Israel for
translation_verse: Ɔ mediema mrenya nee ye mbusua ne ravale ye funli ne hɔziele ye wɔ ɛleka mɔɔ bɛziele ɔ ze Manowa la wɔ Zɔla nee Ɛhyeteeyɔlo avinli. Ɔlile Yizilayɛma ati ɛvolɛ abulanwiɔ.

english_verse: Micah returned the silver to his mother, and she said, “I give this silver to the Lord, so my son can use it to make an idol.” Turning to her son, she said, “Micah, now the silver belongs to you.” But Micah handed it back to his mother. She took
translation_verse: Maeka zianenle ezukoa ne manle ɔ nli la, ɔ nli dele nuhua ɛya nwiɔ manle dwɛtɛ fufule dwinvolɛ; ɔmanle ɔzele ananze, na ɔholole dwɛtɛ fufule ne ɔguale nwolɛ, na bɛvale bɛziele Maeka sua ne anu.

english_verse: He had a shrine for worshiping God there at his home, and he had made some idols and a sacred priestly vest. Micah chose one of his own sons to be the priest for his shrine.
translation_verse: Maeka ɛhye lɛ ye amonle sua. Ɔyɛle mmonle nee ɛzonlenlɛ tɛladeɛ ne mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye “yifɔdo” la bie, na ɔyele ɔ mra mrenya ne mɔ ko kɛ ɔdendɛ ye nyamenle ne anloa azo.

english_verse: This was before kings ruled Israel, so all the Israelites did whatever they thought was right.
translation_verse: Mekɛ ne anu ɛnee belemgbunli biala ɛnle Yizilayɛ maanle ne anu. Awie biala ɔdaye ɔbɔle ye ɛbɛla mɔɔ ɔnea a ɔle kpalɛ la.

english_verse: One day a young Levite came to Micah's house in the hill country of Ephraim. He had been staying with one of the clans of Judah in Bethlehem, but he had left Bethlehem to find a new place to live where he could be a priest.
translation_verse: Ɔvi Bɛtelɛhɛm ɔdule kɛ ɔkakpondɛ ɛleka fofolɛ yeadɛnla. Ɔkɔ na ɔhɔdwule Yifelaem awoka ne mɔ azo azua ne mɔ ko azo la, ɔhɔle Maeka awuke ne anu.

english_verse: “Where are you from?” Micah asked. “I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah,” the man answered, “and I'm on my way to find a new place to live.”
translation_verse: Maeka bizale ye kɛ, “Ɛvi nienwu sua zo?” Na ɔbuale ye kɛ, “Mele Livaenli, mevi Bɛtelɛhɛm mɔɔ wɔ Dwuda la, na meluolua nu kɛ mekpondɛ ɛleka meadɛnla.”

english_verse: Micah said, “Why don't you stay here with me? You can be my priest and tell me what God wants me to do. Every year I'll give you ten pieces of silver and one complete set of clothes, and I'll provide all your food.” The young man went for a walk,
translation_verse: Na Maeka zele ye kɛ, “Maa yɛdɛnla ɛke; yɛ selɛ nee me sɛlɛvolɛ. Ɛvolɛ biala mebadua wɔ dwɛtɛ fufule ngoko bulu. Mebamaa wɔ adɛladeɛ na meali ɛ nloa anu ndɔnie.”

english_verse: then he agreed to stay with Micah and be his priest. He lived in Micah's house, and Micah treated him like one of his own sons.
translation_verse: Na Maeka yɛle Livaenli ne ye sɛlɛvolɛ wɔ ɔdaye Maeka ye awuke nu ɛkɛ.

english_verse: Micah said, “I have a Levite as my own priest. Now I know that the Lord will be kind to me.”
translation_verse: Akee Maeka hanle kɛ, “Kɛkala, akee menwu kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma bamaa meakpazi, ɔboalekɛ menyia Livaenli sɛlɛvolɛ.”

english_verse: These things happened before kings ruled Israel. The Tribe of Dan Takes Micah's Priest and Idols About this time, the tribe of Dan was looking for a place to live. The other tribes had land, but the people of Dan did not really have any to call their own.
