translation_verse: Mekɛ ne anu ɛnee belemgbunli biala ɛnle Yizilayɛ maanle ne anu. Eza mekɛ ne anu ala ɛnee Dan abusua ekpunli ne anu amra ɛnlɛ bɛ ti anwo azɛlɛ ɛnde zolɛ na bɛlɛkpondɛ bie bɛadɛnla zolɛ; ɔluakɛ Yizilayɛ abusua ekpunli ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti lɛ bie. Bɛmɛ ala yɛɛ bɛnlɛ bie a.

english_verse: The tribe chose five warriors to represent their clans and told them, “Go and find some land where we can live.” The warriors left the area of Zorah and Eshtaol and went into the hill country of Ephraim. One night they stayed at Micah's house,
translation_verse: Yemɔti Danema yele mrenya akɛnrasesebɛ nnu wɔ Zɔla nee Ɛhyeteeyɔlo na bɛzoanle bɛ kɛ bɛhɔli busia bɛhɔkpɔla azɛlɛ ne na bɛyɛ bie anyenle. Bɛzele soanvolɛma ne kɛ, “Bɛhɔ na bɛhɔnlea bɛkpondɛ azɛlɛ.” Bɛhɔle sua ne mɔɔ gua Yifelaem boka ne azo la azo. Bɛhɔle Maeka sua nu na bɛhɔzokoɛle ye.

english_verse: because they heard the young Levite talking, and they knew from his accent that he was from the south. They asked him, “What are you doing here? Who brought you here?”
translation_verse: Mɔɔ bɛwɔ Maeka sua nu ɛkɛ ne la, bɛdele Livae kpavolɛ ne ɛdendɛlɛ. Bɛhwenle bɛbikyele ye na bɛbizale ye kɛ, “Nwane a nee wɔ rale ɛke a? Duzu yɛɛ ɛlɛyɛ ye wɔ ɛke a? Duzu gyima yɛɛ ɛdi ye wɔ ɛke a?”

english_verse: The Levite replied, “Micah hired me as his priest.” Then he told them how well Micah had treated him.
translation_verse: Ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Maeka nee me ɛhyehyɛ kɛ menyɛ ye sɛlɛvolɛ na ɔdua me kakɛ.”

english_verse: “Please talk to God for us,” the men said. “Ask God if we will be successful in what we are trying to do.”
translation_verse: Bɛzele kpavolɛ ne kɛ, “Yɛsɛlɛ wɔ, biza Nyamenle, saa yɛ adendulɛ ye kɛyɛ saleɛ kɛmaa yɛ a.”

english_verse: “Don't worry,” answered the priest. “The Lord is pleased with what you are doing.”
translation_verse: Na sɛlɛvolɛ ne zele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛhɔ anzonudwolɛ nu. Ɛdɛnkɛma anye wɔ bɛ nwo zo wɔ bɛ adendulɛ nu.”

english_verse: The five men left and went to the town of Laish, whose people were from Sidon, but Sidon was too far away to protect them. Even though their town had no walls, the people thought they were safe from attack. So they had not asked anyone else for protection, which meant that the tribe of Dan could easily take over Laish.
translation_verse: Akee menli nnu ne zile nu hɔle Leeyehye. Bɛnwunle kɛ menli ne de anzonudwolɛ nu. Bɛde ye kɛ Saedɛnema de ye la. Bɛde anzonudwolɛ nu yɛɛ bɛ nloa beta bɛ ti anwo. Bɛ nee awie biala ɛnlɛ manzonle yɛɛ bɛngyia ɛhwee biala mɔɔ wɔ ewiade ye anu la anwo. Anwonyia a, bɛlɛ bie. Bɛ nee Saedɛnema avinli twe, yɛɛ bɛ nee awie biala ɛnlɛ ngitanwolilɛ.

english_verse: The five men went back to Zorah and Eshtaol, where their relatives asked, “Did you find any land?”
translation_verse: Mɔɔ menli nnu ne ziale hɔle Zɔla nee Ɛhyeteeyɔlo la, bɛ mediema ne mɔ bizale bɛ kɛ, “Duzu kolakola a bɛ nee ye rale a?”

english_verse: “Let's go!” the five men said. “We saw some very good land with enough room for all of us, and it has everything we will ever need. What are you waiting for? Let's attack and take it. You'll find that the people think they're safe, but God is giving the land to us.”
translation_verse: Saa bɛkɔ a, bɛbanwu kɛ menli ne le menli mɔɔ ɛndwenle awie mɔ anwo a. Azɛlɛ ne tɛlɛ. Ɔle azɛlɛ mɔɔ debie biala anwo ɛngyia zolɛ a. Nyamenle yɛɛ ɛye ɛmaa yɛ a.”

english_verse: Six hundred men from the tribe of Dan strapped on their weapons and left Zorah and Eshtaol with their families.
translation_verse: Na Dan abusua ekpunli ne anu amra ɛya nsia vale bɛ konle ninyɛne vi Zɔla nee Ɛhyeteeyɔlo zile nu hɔle.

english_verse: One night they camped near Kiriath-Jearim in the territory of Judah, and that's why the place just west of Kiriath-Jearim is still known as Dan's Camp.
translation_verse: Bɛkɔ la, bɛhɔzokoɛle Keleate Gyialem adɔleɛ afoa nu wɔ Dwuda. Ɛhye ati a ɛnɛ nee ɛnɛ ala bɛtɛfɛlɛ ye Dan Azokoɛleɛ la.

english_verse: Then they went into the hill country of Ephraim. When they came close to Micah's house,
translation_verse: Bɛvile ɛkɛ ne bɛhɔle sua ne mɔɔ gua Yifelaem awoka ne mɔ azo la azo na bɛhɔle Maeka awuke nu.

english_verse: the five men who had been spies asked the other warriors, “Did you know that someone in this village has several idols and a sacred priestly vest? What do you think we should do about it?”
translation_verse: Akee menli nnu ne mɔɔ hɔlile Leeyehye azɛlɛ ne azo busia la zele bɛ mediema ne mɔ kɛ, “Asoo bɛze kɛ azua ɛhye mɔ, mmonle ngyikyi, ananze mɔɔ bɛze nee mɔɔ bɛholo dwɛtɛ fufule bɛgua nwolɛ la, nee nwolɛ ɛzonlenlɛ tɛladeɛ wɔ ko anu ɔ? Yemɔti bɛdwenle mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ bɛyɛ la anwo.”

english_verse: “Quiet!” the men said. “Keep your mouth shut and listen. Why don't you come with us and be our priest, so you can tell us what God wants us to do? You could stay here and be a priest for one man's family, but wouldn't you rather be the priest for a clan or even a whole tribe of Israel?”
translation_verse: Bɛzele ye kɛ, “Yɛ koonwu. Ka ɛ nloa to nuhua na bɛla maa yɛhɔ. Bayɛ selɛ nee yɛ sɛlɛvolɛ. Ɛnea a ɛnee ɔle kpalɛ kɛ ɛkɛyɛ Yizilayɛ mbusua ekpunli ne mɔ ko nee bɛ awuke awuke ne mɔ anu amra sɛlɛvolɛ anzɛɛ ɛkɛyɛ sonla ko awuke nu sɛlɛvolɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: The priest really liked that idea. So he took the vest and the idols and joined the others
translation_verse: Sɛlɛvolɛ ne ahonle dɔle ye azule nu. Ɛhye ati ɔvale ɛzonlenlɛ tɛladeɛ ne nee mmonle ngyikyi ne nee ananze ne mɔ na ɔ nee menli ne hɔle.

english_verse: from the tribe of Dan. Then they turned and left, after putting their children, their cattle, and the rest of their other possessions in front.
translation_verse: Bɛmanle bɛ ngakula ne mɔ, nee nyɛmoa, nee bɛ nwo ninyɛne ne mɔ lumuale bɛ nyunlu, na akee bɛzile nu kɛ bɛkɔ.

english_verse: They had traveled for some time before Micah asked his neighbors to help him get his things back. He and his men caught up with the people of Dan
translation_verse: Mɔɔ bɛhɔle moa bie kpalɛ la, menli mɔɔ zuozua Maeka la dele bɛ kunlu na bɛdule bɛdoale Danema ne.

english_verse: and shouted for them to stop. They turned to face him and asked, “What's wrong? Why did you bring all these men?”
translation_verse: Bɛdeɛdeanle nu bɛvɛlɛle bɛ, na Danema hakyile bɛ nye na bɛzele Maeka kɛ, “Duzu a gyegye wɔ mɔɔ yemɔti wɔva ɛlɔne ɛhye wɔkpo yɛ a?”

english_verse: Micah answered, “You know what's wrong. You stole the gods I made, and you took my priest. I don't have anything left.”
translation_verse: Maeka zele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛva me nyamenle ne mɔ mɔɔ medame meyɛ, nee me sɛlɛvolɛ mɔɔ melɛ la bɛlɛkɔ, na ɛnee bɛdabɛ bɛnea a duzu a ka me sa nu a? Kɛmɔti a bɛbiza me kɛ, ‘Duzu a gyegye wɔ a?’ ”

english_verse: “We don't want to hear any more about it,” the people of Dan said. “And if you make us angry, you'll only get yourself and your family killed.”
translation_verse: Na Danema ne zele ye kɛ, “Mua ɛ nloa! Mmayɛ ɛmaa ahonle futu, na anrɛɛ ɛdawɔ nee wɔ awuke nu amra amuala kɛdɔ.”

english_verse: After saying this, they turned and left. Micah realized there was no way he could win a fight with them, and so he went back home. The Tribe of Dan Captures Laish
translation_verse: Na Danema dule denrɛle. Maeka nwunle kɛ ɔ nee bɛ ɛnrɛhola ko la, ɔziale ɔ nzi koonwu ɔhɔle sua nu.

english_verse: But they named it Dan, after one of Israel's sons, who was the ancestor of their tribe.
translation_verse: Na bɛvale suakpole ne mɔɔ anrɛɛ bɛfɛlɛ ye Leeyehye la bɛdonle bɛ nlenya Dan, mɔɔ bɛwole ye wɔ Yizilayɛ la.

english_verse: Before kings ruled Israel, a Levite was living deep in the hill country of the Ephraim tribe. He married a woman from Bethlehem in Judah,
translation_verse: Mekɛ mɔɔ ɛnee Yizilayɛma ɛnlɛ belemgbunli la, Livaenli bie dule adenle hɔle Yifelaem awoka ne mɔ azo. Ɔvale mgbɔnla wɔ Bɛtelɛhɛm mɔɔ wɔ Dwuda la.

english_verse: but she was unfaithful and went back to live with her family in Bethlehem. Four months later
translation_verse: Ye mgbɔnla ne wulowulale ɔ sa aze, na ɔziale ɔhɔle ɔ ze sua zo Bɛtelɛhɛm mɔɔ wɔ Dwuda la ɔhɔziele ɔ nwo aze siane nna.

english_verse: her husband decided to try and talk her into coming back. So he went to Bethlehem, taking along a servant and two donkeys. He talked with his wife, and she invited him into her family's home. Her father was glad to see him
translation_verse: Ɔ hu dwazole kɛ ɔkakpo ɔ bo zo, yeahɔha ɛdendɛlɛ kpalɛ yeahile ye na ɔ nee ye azia. Ɔvale ye sonvolɛ ne nee asoaso nwiɔ ɔ nee bɛ hɔle ɔ ye ɔ ze sua zo. Ɔdwule la ɔ ye vale ye rale ɔ ze sua nu. Ɔ ye ɔ ze nwunle ye la ɔvale fɛlɛkolilɛ ɔhɔyiale ye adenle.

english_verse: and did not want him to leave. So the man stayed three days, eating and drinking with his father-in-law.
translation_verse: Ɔ ye ɔ ze ne liele ye na ɔ nee ye dɛnlanle kenle nsa, bɛlile bɛnlonle.

english_verse: When everyone got up on the fourth day, the Levite started getting ready to go home. But his father-in-law said, “Don't leave until you have a bite to eat. You'll need strength for your journey.”
translation_verse: Ye kenle nsa ne azo bɛdwazole nwonlomɔ mangyee ne na Livaenli ne boɔboale ɔ nwo kɛ ɔkɔ. Raalɛ ne ɔ ze zele ye kɛ, “Kpula ɛ sa kolaa na wɔahɔ.”

english_verse: The two men sat down together and ate a big meal. “Come on,” the man's father-in-law said. “Stay tonight and have a good time.”
translation_verse: Yemɔti bɛ mu nwiɔ bɛdɛnlanle aze bɛkpulale bɛ sa na bɛnlonle. Akee raalɛ ne ɔ ze zele nrenya ne kɛ, “Maa yɛla na die ɛ nye.”

english_verse: The Levite tried to leave, but his father-in-law insisted, and he spent one more night there.
translation_verse: Livaenli ne nyianle nwolɛ kɛ ɔkɔ la, ɔ ye ɔ ze ne yɛle toonwo manle ɔlale bieko.

english_verse: The fifth day, the man got up early to leave, but his wife's father said, “You need to keep up your strength! Why don't you leave right after lunch?” So the two of them started eating.
translation_verse: Aleɛ hyenle bieko mɔɔ ɛnee nrenya ne ɛli kenle nnu la, ɔdwazole ndɛ kɛ ɔkɔ, na ɔ ye ɔ ze ne zele ye kɛ, “Di debie maa sɛnzɛne ne ɛkpali ekyii na wɔahɔ.” Eza bɛ mu nwiɔ bɛlile debie.

english_verse: Finally, the Levite got up from the meal, so he and his wife and servant could leave. “Look,” his father-in-law said, “it's already late afternoon, and if you leave now, you won't get very far before dark. Stay with us one more night and enjoy yourself. Then you can get up early tomorrow morning and start home.”
translation_verse: Na mɔɔ nrenya ne nee ye mgbɔnla ne nee ye sonvolɛ ne nyianle nwolɛ kɛ bɛkɔ la, ɔ ye ɔ ze ne zele ye kɛ, “Sɛnzɛne ne asɛɛ ɛdɔ; mesɛlɛ wɔ, da. Aleɛ ɛdwo. Die ɛ nye na ɛhyema nwonlomɔ mangyee ne ala ɛkɛhɔ na wɔadwu sua nu.”

english_verse: But the Levite decided not to spend the night there again. He had the saddles put on his two donkeys, then he and his wife and servant traveled as far as Jebus, which is now called Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Nrenya ne amkponle kɛ ɔkɛla bieko. Yemɔti ɔzile nu na ɔradwule Gyibɛse kandiba, ɔdaye, yɛɛ ye sonvolɛ ne nee ye mgbɔnla ne, yɛɛ ye asoaso nwiɔ mɔɔ mbia wɔ zolɛ la.

english_verse: It was beginning to get dark, and the man's servant said, “Let's stop and spend the night in this town where the Jebusites live.”
translation_verse: Mɔɔ bɛbikyele Gyibɛse la, ɛnee mekɛ ne ɛhɔ dɔɔnwo. Na ye sonvolɛ ne zele ye kɛ, “Bɛmaa yɛmakyi Gyibɛsema suakpole ɛhye azo yɛkpondɛ ɛleka yɛhyea.”

english_verse: They walked on and reached Gibeah in the territory of Benjamin just after sunset.
translation_verse: Yemɔti bɛpɛle nuhua bɛhɔle. Sɛnzɛne ne dɔle bɛ wɔ mɔɔ ɛnee bɛbikye Gebɛya, mɔɔ wɔ Bɛngyaman abusua ekpunli ne maanle nu la,

english_verse: They left the road and went into Gibeah. But the Levite couldn't find a house where anyone would let them spend the night, and they sat down in the open area just inside the town gates.
translation_verse: na bɛvole suakpole ne azo kɛ bɛkala. Bɛhɔdɛnlanle suakpole ne gua kpatawienyi ne azo, ɔluakɛ awie biala anva bɛ angɔ ye sua nu.

english_verse: Soon an old man came in through the gates on his way home from working in the fields. Most of the people who lived in Gibeah belonged to the tribe of Benjamin, but this man was originally from the hill country of Ephraim.
translation_verse: Nrenya kpanyinli bie mɔɔ vi ɛbɔ nu ɛlɛba sua zo nɔsolɛ nu la ravindele bɛ nwo zo. Nrenya ne vi sua bie mɔɔ gua Yifelaem awoka ne mɔ azo la azo yɛɛ yeradɛnla Gebɛya a. Gebɛyama le Bɛngyaman abo zo amra.

english_verse: He noticed that the Levite was just in town to spend the night. “Where are you going?” the old man asked. “Where did you come from?”
translation_verse: Nrenya kpanyinli ne nwunle ɛyɛvolɛ ne na ɔbizale ye kɛ, “Ɛvi nienwu, yɛɛ ɛkɔ nienwu?”

english_verse: “We've come from Bethlehem in Judah,” the Levite answered. “We went there on a visit. Now we're going to the place where the Lord is worshiped, and later we will return to our home in the hill country of Ephraim. But no one here will let us spend the night in their home.
translation_verse: Ɛyɛvolɛ ne zele ye kɛ, “Yɛvi Bɛtelɛhɛm mɔɔ wɔ Dwuda la; yɛse yɛahɔ Yifelaem awoka ne mɔ azo lɔ; ɛkɛ ne a mevi a. Mengɔle Bɛtelɛhɛm mɔɔ wɔ Dwuda la yɛɛ mese meahɔ me sua zo a. Na yɛnnyia awie biala ɛnva yɛ ɛngɔ sua nu.

english_verse: We brought food for our donkeys and bread and wine for ourselves, so we don't need anything except a place to sleep.”
translation_verse: Yɛlɛ asoaso ne mɔ anwo ndile nee aleɛ; yɛlɛ kpanwo nee nwanye mɔɔ medame, me mgbɔnla ye nee me sonvolɛ ye yɛdi yɛanlo la. Yɛnrɛhyia debie biala anwo.”

english_verse: The old man said, “You are welcome to spend the night in my home and to be my guest, but don't stay out here!”
translation_verse: Na nrenya kpanyinli ne zele kɛ, “Akoaba. Maa yɛhɔ sua nu. Ɔnle kɛ ɛda gua kpatawienyi ye azo.”

english_verse: The old man brought them into his house and fed their donkeys. Then he and his guests washed their feet and began eating and drinking.
translation_verse: Na ɔvale ye ɔ nee ye hɔle sua nu. Ɔmanle asoaso ne mɔ aleɛ. Akee nyɛvolɛ ne mɔ wowole bɛ gyakɛ anwo, na bɛlile na bɛnlonle.

english_verse: They were having a good time, when some worthless men of that town surrounded the house and started banging on the door and shouting, “A man came to your house tonight. Send him out, so we can have sex with him!”
translation_verse: Na mekɛ mɔɔ bɛlɛdi debie na bɛ nye ɛlie la, arɛlevilɛ nu ala, suakpole ne azo mrenya bie mɔɔ fa bɛ gɔnwo mɔ mrenya la rabɔle yiale sua ne na bɛbɔle anlenkɛ ne anu ndinlizo. Bɛzele nrenya kpanyinli ne kɛ, “Fa nrenya ne mɔɔ wɔ wɔ sua ne anu la finde maa yɛ nee ye ɛyɛ nrenya nee nrenya.”

english_verse: The old man went outside and said, “My friends, please don't commit such a horrible crime against a man who is a guest in my house.
translation_verse: Na awuke menle ne vindele doale bɛ na ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Me mediema, adenle ɛnle ɛkɛ. Bɛmmayɛ amumuyɛ. Nrenya ye le me sokoɛvolɛ. Bɛmmabɔ munzule ɛbɛla biala.

english_verse: Let me send out my daughter instead. She's a virgin. And I'll even send out the man's wife. You can rape them or do whatever else you want, but please don't do such a horrible thing to this man.”
translation_verse: Bɛnlea, me ra raalɛ mɔɔ ɛnze nrenya fee yɛɛ nrenya ne mgbɔnla noko wɔ ɛke. Bɛmaa menva bɛ membɛlɛ bɛ na bɛyɛ bɛ debie biala mɔɔ bɛkulo la. Na nrenya ɛhye, bɛmmayɛ mɔɔ bɛnyɛ la bɛkile ye.”

english_verse: The men refused to listen, so the Levite grabbed his wife and shoved her outside. The men raped her and abused her all night long. Finally, they let her go just before sunrise,
translation_verse: Noko menli ne mɔ amkponle. Yemɔti nrenya ne vale ye mgbɔnla ne vindele rɛlɛle bɛ. Bɛfulofunlanle ye, bɛ nee ye lale bɛ ti ngoko toonwo alehyenlɛ. Aleɛbahye ne mɔɔ maanle nu ɛlɛba aratete la, bɛgyakyile ye kɛ ɔhɔ.

english_verse: and it was almost daybreak when she went back to the house where her husband was staying. She collapsed at the door and lay there until sunrise.
translation_verse: Raalɛ ne rapɛle finle nrenya kpanyinli ne sua ne mɔɔ ɔ hu la nu la anlenkɛ ne anloa, na ɔlale ɛkɛ ne toonwo maanle nu tetele wienyi.

english_verse: About that time, her husband woke up and got ready to leave. He opened the door and went outside, where he found his wife lying at the door with her hands on the doorstep.
translation_verse: Nwonlomɔ ne ala ɔ hu dwazole dukuele anlenkɛ ne kɛ ɔkɔ. Na nea, ye mgbɔnla ye a bea anlenkɛ ye anloa na ɔ sa gua anuhɔlɛ ɛkɛ ne la.

english_verse: “Get up!” he said. “It's time to leave.” But his wife didn't move. He lifted her body onto his donkey and left.
translation_verse: Ɔzele ye kɛ, “Dwazo maa yɛhɔ.” Na raalɛ ne anga ɔ nwo. Nrenya ne vale ye dole ye asoaso ne azo na ɔzile nu ɔhɔle ye sua zo.

english_verse: When he got home, he took a butcher knife and cut her body into twelve pieces. Then he told some messengers, “Take one piece to each tribe of Israel
translation_verse: Ɔdwule sua nu la, ɔvale dadeɛ ɔdudule ye mgbɔnla ne funli ne abɛsa abɛsa. Akee ɔhyɛle ye nwonane ne anu bulu nee nwiɔ, na ɔvale ɔhɔle Yizilayɛ maanle ne anu amuala.

english_verse: and ask everyone if anything like this has ever happened since Israel left Egypt. Tell them to think about it, talk it over, and tell us what should be done.” Everyone who saw a piece of the body said, “This is horrible! Nothing like this has ever happened since the day Israel left Egypt.”
translation_verse: Na bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛnwunle zɛhae debie la hanle kɛ, “Debie zɛhae, bie ɛtɛsile ɛlɛ; yɛɛ ɔvi mekɛ mɔɔ yɛ mgbanyinli, Yizilayɛma vi Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo rale la, yɛtɛtele bie ɛlɛ kɛ ɛnɛ kenle ye ala. Bɛnlea bɛdwenle nwolɛ na mɔɔ bɛka la bɛha.”

english_verse: The husband of the murdered woman answered: My wife and I went into the town of Gibeah in Benjamin to spend the night.
translation_verse: Na Livaenli ne, mɔɔ ɔ ye a bɛhunle ye la yele ɔ nloa kɛ, “Membale Gebɛya mɔɔ wɔ Bɛngyamanema maanle nu la; me nee me mgbɔnla a rale a, kɛ yɛbala ɛkɛ.

english_verse: It was a terrible thing for Israelites to do! So I cut up her body and sent the pieces everywhere in Israel.
translation_verse: Na menvale funli ne mempepɛle nu bulu nee nwiɔ, na mengyɛle memanle Yizilayɛ mbusua ekpunli ekpunli bulu nee nwiɔ ne. Ɔluakɛ bɛyɛ mɔɔ bɛnyɛ la, na bɛbɔ munzule wɔ Yizilayɛ maanle ye anu.

english_verse: You are the people of Israel, and you must decide today what to do about the men of Gibeah.
translation_verse: Bɛmɛ Yizilayɛma mɔɔ bɛyia ɛke la, bɛdabɛ bɛdwenle ɛhye anwo na bɛva nwolɛ adwenle.”

english_verse: The whole army was in agreement, and they said, “None of us will go home.
translation_verse: Na menli ne kɔsɔɔti yɛle ko na bɛzele kɛ, “Yɛ nuhua biala, saa ɛde ndanlɛ sua bo o anzɛɛ ɛde sua nu o, ɛndu ɔ gyakɛ.

english_verse: The tribes of Israel sent messengers to every town and village in Benjamin. And wherever the messengers went, they said, “How could those worthless men in Gibeah do such a disgusting thing?
translation_verse: Yizilayɛ mbusua ekpunli ekpunli ne mɔ zoanle menli wɔ Bɛngyaman maanle ne anu amuala manle bɛhɔbizale bɛ kɛ, “Duzu amumuyɛ ɛbɛla a bɛbɔ la?

english_verse: We can't allow such a terrible crime to go unpunished in Israel! Hand the men over to us, and we will put them to death.” But the people of Benjamin refused to listen to the other Israelites.
translation_verse: Bɛye menli zɔhane mɔ mɔɔ wɔ Gebɛya, mɔɔ bɔle munzule ɛbɛla ne la bɛrɛla bɛmaa yɛhu bɛ, na yɛkpa munzule ɛhye yɛvi Yizilayɛ maanle ye anu.” Na Bɛngyamanema andie bɛ mediema Yizilayɛma ne ane.

english_verse: Men from towns all over Benjamin's territory went to Gibeah and got ready to fight Israel.
translation_verse: Bɛngyamanema vi bɛ azuamgbole ne mɔ azo rale Gebɛya kɛ bɛ nee Yizilayɛma baho.

english_verse: The next morning the Israelite army moved its camp to a place near Gibeah.
translation_verse: Nwonlomɔ ne, Yizilayɛma ne hɔdɛle Gebɛya kandiba.

english_verse: Then they left their camp and got into position to attack the army of Benjamin. The War Between Israel and Benjamin
translation_verse: Na bɛvale konle bɛdoale Bɛngyamanema wɔ ɛleka mɔɔ nee suakpole ne anye bɔ zolɛ la.

english_verse: Benjamin's soldiers came out of Gibeah and attacked, and when the day was over,
translation_verse: Bɛngyamanema ɛlɔne ne vi Gebɛya vindele, na toonwo mɔɔ sɛnzɛne ne kadɔ la ɛnee bɛhu Yizilayɛma apenle ngoko abulanwiɔ nee nwiɔ.

english_verse: The people of Israel went to the place of worship at Bethel, where the sacred chest was being kept. They sat on the ground, crying and not eating for the rest of the day. Then about sunset, they offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask his blessing. Phinehas the priest then prayed, “Our Lord, the people of Benjamin are our relatives. Should we stop fighting or attack them again?” “Attack!” the Lord answered. “Tomorrow I will let you defeat them.”
translation_verse: Mekɛ ne anu ɛnee Nyamenle Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne wɔ ɛkɛ, na Aalɔn ara nrenya Ɛlieza ara Fenɛhaze a le sɛlɛvolɛ a. Na Yizilayɛma bizale Ɛdɛnkɛma bieko kɛ, “Eza yɛva konle yɛhɔdoa yɛ mediema Bɛngyamanema bieko ɔ, anzɛɛ yɛgyakyi?” Ɛdɛnkɛma buale kɛ, “Bɛhɔ bieko, ɔluakɛ ɛhyema mebaye Gebɛyama meamaa bɛ,”

english_verse: The men of Benjamin headed down the road toward the desert, trying to escape from the Israelites. But the Israelites stayed right behind them, keeping up their attack. Men even came out of the nearby towns to help kill the men of Benjamin,
translation_verse: Yemɔti bɛguale ye bɛ nzi na bɛguale ɛbɔ nu wɔ fienemgbole ne anu, noko akee bɛ nwo anza nu. Yizilayɛma ɛlɔne ne mɔɔ vi suakpole ne azo ɛlɛba la nwinwinle bɛ avinli ɛkɛ ne.

english_verse: who were having to fight on all sides. The Israelite soldiers never let up their attack. They chased and killed the warriors of Benjamin as far as a place directly east of Gibeah,
translation_verse: Bɛngyamanema ne dɔle donvula, na Yizilayɛma voanle bɛ ndinlizo bɛtiale bɛ dwɛɛ bɛvi Noha toonwo Gebɛya aduduleɛ lɔ.

english_verse: The Israelites turned back and went to every town in Benjamin's territory, killing all the people and animals, and setting the towns on fire.
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma ne ziale kpole Bɛngyamanema ne; bɛhunle menli nee nyɛmoa mɔɔ bɛnwunle bɛ la kɔsɔɔti na bɛtotole senle wɔ azua mɔɔ bɛnwunle bɛ la kɔsɔɔti azo.

english_verse: When the Israelites had met at Mizpah before the war with Benjamin, they had made this sacred promise: “None of us will ever let our daughters marry any man from Benjamin.”
translation_verse: Akee Yizilayɛma ne hanle ndane wɔ Mezepa kɛ, “Yɛ nuhua ko bɔbɔ ɛnrɛva ɔ ra raalɛ ɛnrɛmaa Bɛngyamanenli agyalɛ ɛlɛ.”

english_verse: After the war with Benjamin, the Israelites went to the place of worship at Bethel and sat there until sunset. They cried loudly and bitterly
translation_verse: Na menli ne rale Bɛtɛle radɛnlanle aze wɔ Nyamenle anyunlu na bɛzunle bɛyele awolɛ.

english_verse: and prayed, “Our Lord, you are the God of Israel. Why did you let this happen? Now one of our tribes is almost gone.”
translation_verse: Bɛzele kɛ, “O Ɛdɛnkɛma, Yizilayɛ Nyamenle, duzu ati yɛɛ ɛhye ɛzi a, kɛ Yizilayɛ mbusua ekpunli ekpunli ne mɔ anu ko ɛnɛ kɛvi nu a?”

english_verse: Early the next morning, the Israelites built an altar and offered sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask his blessing.
translation_verse: Aleɛ hyenle la menli ne dwazole ndɛ yɛle azukponle, bɛyelale nane bɛbɔle azu, eza bɛbɔle anzonudwolɛ azu.

english_verse: Then they asked each other, “Did any of the tribes of Israel fail to come to the place of worship? We made a sacred promise that anyone who didn't come to the meeting at Mizpah would be put to death.”
translation_verse: Na Yizilayɛma ne bizale kɛ, “Yizilayɛ mbusua ekpunli ekpunli ne boni yɛɛ amba Ɛdɛnkɛma nyianu ne bie a?” Ɔluakɛ ɛnee bɛha ndane kpole bɛdo zolɛ kɛ, awie ko biala mɔɔ amba Ɛdɛnkɛma nyianu ne bie wɔ Mezepa la, ɔwɔ kɛ bɛku ye.

english_verse: The Israelites were sad about what had happened to the Benjamin tribe, and they said, “One of our tribes was almost wiped out.
translation_verse: Na Yizilayɛma ne lile nyane wɔ bɛ mediema Bɛngyamanema ati na bɛzele kɛ, “Ɛnɛ Yizilayɛ ɛminli ye mbusua ekpunli ekpunli ne mɔ anu ko.

english_verse: Only a few men of Benjamin weren't killed in the war. We need to get wives for them, so the tribe won't completely disappear. But how can we do that, after promising in the Lord's name that we wouldn't let them marry any of our daughters?”
translation_verse: Kɛ ɔkɛyɛ na yɛanyia mraalɛ yɛamaa bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛha la agya ɛ? Ɔluakɛ yɛli amonle yɛha ndane wɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlu kɛ yɛnrɛva yɛ mra mraalɛ yɛnrɛmaa bɛ agyalɛ ɛlɛ.”

english_verse: The warriors attacked Jabesh in Gilead, and returned to their camp at Shiloh in Canaan with
translation_verse: Bɛnyianle mbɛlɛra mɔɔ ɛtɛnwunle mrenya ɛlɛ la ɛya nna wɔ Gyeebɛhye Geleade, na bɛ nee bɛ hɔle Hyaelo mɔɔ wɔ Keena la.

english_verse: The Israelites met and sent messengers to the men of Benjamin at Rimmon Rock, telling them that the Israelites were willing to make peace with them.
translation_verse: Akee Yizilayɛma amuala vale nrɛlaleɛ hɔmanle Bɛngyamanema mɔɔ wɔ Relemɔn bodane ne azo lɔ la kɛ bɛva bɛ nwo edwɛkɛ bɛhyɛ bɛ.

english_verse: So the men of Benjamin came back from Rimmon Rock, and the Israelites let them marry the young women from Jabesh. But there weren't enough women.
translation_verse: Bɛngyamanema ziale rale sua nu. Yizilayɛma vale mraalɛ ne mɔ mɔɔ bɛangu bɛ wɔ Gyeebɛhye Geleade la manle bɛ, noko bɛ kɔsɔɔti bɛannyia bie.

english_verse: The Israelites were very sad, because the Lord had almost wiped out one of their tribes.
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma lile Bɛngyamanema anwo nyane, ɔluakɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛkpakye Yizilayɛ mbusua ekpunli ekpunli ne mɔ avinli.

english_verse: Then their leaders said: All the women of the Benjamin tribe were killed. How can we get wives for the men of Benjamin who are left?
translation_verse: Akee nyianu ne anu mgbanyima ne zele kɛ, “Bɛngyaman abusua ekpunli ɛdeɛ ne, bɛhu mraalɛ mɔɔ wɔ nu la kɔsɔɔti. Kɛ ɔkɛyɛ na yɛanyia mraalɛ yɛamaa mrenya mɔɔ ɛha la agya ɛ?”

english_verse: If they don't have children, one of the Israelite tribes will die out.
translation_verse: Na bɛzele kɛ, “Ɔwɔ kɛ bɛnyia menli di Bɛngyamanema mɔɔ ɛha la agya. Ɔnle kɛ abusua ekpunli zɔhane abo tu Yizilayɛ maanle ye anu.

english_verse: But we can't let the men of Benjamin marry any of our daughters. We made a sacred promise not to do that, and if we break our promise, we will be under our own curse.
translation_verse: Noko akee yɛngola yɛnva yɛ mra mraalɛ yɛmmaa bɛ agyalɛ.” Ɔluakɛ Yizilayɛma ɛha ndane kɛ, “Munzule ɛha awie biala mɔɔ kɛva ɔ ra raalɛ kɛmaa Bɛngyamanenli kɛgya la.”

english_verse: Then someone suggested, “What about the Lord's Festival that takes place each year in Shiloh? It's held north of Bethel, south of Lebonah, and just east of the road that goes from Bethel to Shechem.”
translation_verse: Yemɔti bɛhanle kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛvoyia ne mɔɔ bɛdi ye wɔ Hyaelo la ɛdwu. Hyaelo wɔ Bɛtɛle sɔlɔ, wɔ Bɛtɛle nee Hyikɛm ademgbole ne aduduleɛ afoa nu wɔ Lɛbona nyiakɛ.”

english_verse: Wait there for the young women of Shiloh to come out and perform their dances. Then rush out and grab one of the young women, then take her home as your wife.
translation_verse: Saa Hyaelo mbɛlɛra ba kɛ bɛbazi agole wɔ ɛvoyialilɛ ne anu a, bɛvinde na awie biala ɛhye ko ɛva ye ɛyɛ ɔ ye, na ɔ nee ye ɛhɔ Bɛngyaman maanle nu.

english_verse: If the fathers or brothers of these women complain about this, we'll say, “Be kind enough to let those men keep your daughter. After all, we couldn't get enough wives for all the men of Benjamin in the battle at Jabesh. And because you didn't give them permission to marry your daughters, you won't be under the curse we earlier agreed on.”
translation_verse: Na saa bɛ ze mɔ anzɛɛ bɛ mediema mrenya babiza nwolɛ edwɛkɛ a, bɛbaze bɛ kɛ, ‘Bɛkponle zolɛ bɛmaa yɛ. Ɔluakɛ yɛangye bɛ donvula wɔ konle nu, yɛɛ tɛ bɛdabɛ noko yɛɛ bɛvale bɛ bɛmanle yɛ a, yemɔti bɛnli fɔlɛ.’ ”

english_verse: The men of Benjamin went to Shiloh and hid in the vineyards. The young women soon started dancing, and each man grabbed one of them and carried her off. Then the men of Benjamin went back to their own land and rebuilt their towns and started living in them again.
translation_verse: Na Bɛngyamanema ne yɛle ye zɔhane. Biala nyianle raalɛ hyele ye wɔ agolezilɛ ne anu. Bɛ nee bɛ ziale hɔle bɛ azua ne mɔ azo; bɛhɔkyekyele bɛ azua ne mɔ na bɛdɛnlanle aze.

english_verse: Afterwards, the rest of the Israelites returned to their homes and families. Israel Was Not Ruled by a King
translation_verse: Mekɛ ne anu Yizilayɛma ne noko ziale hɔle hɔbokale bɛ mbusua ekpunli ekpunli ne mɔ nee bɛ sua nu amra anwo, na bɛhɔle bɛ gyima zo.

english_verse: In those days Israel wasn't ruled by a king, and everyone did what they thought was right.
translation_verse: Mekɛ ne anu ɛnee belemgbunli biala ɛnle Yizilayɛ maanle ne anu; awie biala bɔle ɛbɛla biala mɔɔ ɔdaye ɔkulo la.

english_verse: Before Israel was ruled by kings, Elimelech from the clan of Ephrath lived in the town of Bethlehem. His wife was named Naomi, and their two sons were Mahlon and Chilion. But when their crops failed in Israel, they moved to the country of Moab. And while they were there,
translation_verse: Mekɛ mɔɔ ɛnee maanlebuvolɛma a bu Yizilayɛ maanle ne la, ɛhɔne kpole bie zile maanle ne anu. Zɔhane ati nrenya bie mɔɔ vi Bɛtelɛhɛm mɔɔ wɔ Dwuda maanle nu na ɔbɔ Ɛfelate abusua ne bie la vale ɔ ye nee ɔ mra mrenya nwiɔ mɔɔ ɔlɛ bɛ la lɔle nu hɔle Mowabe maanle nu. Bɛfɛlɛ nrenya ne Yilemɛlɛke, bɛfɛlɛ ɔ ye Nawome yɛɛ ɔ mra mrenya nwiɔ ne noko aluma a le Maalɔn yɛɛ Kaeleɔn. Bɛhɔle Mowabe maanle nu bɛhɔdɛnlanle ɛkɛ ne.

english_verse: Elimelech died, leaving Naomi with only her two sons.
translation_verse: Na Nawome ɔ hu Yilemɛlɛke wule manle ɔhale ye nee ɔ mra mrenya nwiɔ ne.

english_verse: Later, Naomi's sons married Moabite women. One was named Orpah and the other Ruth. About ten years later,
translation_verse: Mgbavolɛ nwiɔ ɛhye gyale Mowabe mraalɛ; bɛfɛlɛ ko Ɔpa yɛɛ bɛfɛlɛ ko Wulutu. Kɛyɛ ɛvolɛ bulu anzi

english_verse: When Naomi heard that the Lord had given his people a good harvest, she and her two daughters-in-law got ready to leave Moab and go to Judah. As they were on their way there,
translation_verse: Yemɔti ɔ nee ahunlanvolɛ mraalɛ nwiɔ ne vile ɛleka mɔɔ bɛde la na bɛzile nuhua kɛ bɛsia bɛahɔ Dwuda maanle nu. Na mɔɔ bɛdwule adenle nu la

english_verse: Naomi said to them, “Don't you want to go back home to your own mothers? You were kind to my husband and sons, and you've always been kind to me. I pray that the Lord will be just as kind to you.
translation_verse: Nawome zele ahunlanvolɛ mraalɛ ne mɔ kɛ, “Bɛzia, awie biala ɛhɔ ɔ nli sua nu. Ɛdɛnkɛma nee bɛ ɛdɛnla gyɛlɛɛnye, kɛmɔ bɛ nee me nee menli mɔɔ ɛwu ɛhɔ la dɛnlanle la.

english_verse: May he give each of you another husband and a home of your own.” Naomi kissed them. They cried
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛmaa bɛnyia mrenya bɛgya, na bɛkyekye awuke.” Akee ɔvale bɛ ɔbɔle ye ɛbolɛ, ɔyɛle bɛ atuu na ɔhɛlale bɛ. Na bɛdukuele nu bɛzunle.

english_verse: and said, “We want to go with you and live among your people.”
translation_verse: Ahunlanvolɛ mraalɛ ne mɔ zele Nawome kɛ, “Kyɛkyɛ, yɛ nee wɔ kɔ ɛleka mɔɔ ɛvi la.”

english_verse: But she replied, “My daughters, why don't you return home? What good will it do you to go with me? Do you think I could have more sons for you to marry?
translation_verse: Nawome zele bɛ kɛ, “Me mra mraalɛ, bɛzia. Duzu ati a bɛ nee me kɔ a? Asoo mebawo mralɛ mrenya bieko na bɛarayɛ bɛ hu mɔ?

english_verse: You must go back home, because I am too old to marry again. Even if I got married tonight and later had more sons,
translation_verse: Me mra mraalɛ, bɛzia bɛhɔ, ɔluakɛ meyɛ kpanyinli, mebo agyalɛhɔlɛ zo. Na saa melɛ anyelazo bɔbɔ yɛɛ megya nrenya na ɛnɛ nɔe ala meawo mralɛ mrenya a,

english_verse: would you wait for them to become old enough to marry? No, my daughters! Life is harder for me than it is for you, because the Lord has turned against me.”
translation_verse: asoo ɛhye ati bɛkɛhendɛ toonwo bɛkɛmaa bɛkɛyɛ mgbanyinli? Ɛhye ati bɛnrɛhɔ agyalɛ ko ɔ? Kyɛkyɛ, me mra mraalɛ, ɔyɛ se ɔmaa me na ɔmaa medi nyane wɔ bɛ ti, kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛmaa menwu me nyunlu totohyia zɛhae a.”

english_verse: They cried again. Orpah kissed her mother-in-law goodbye, but Ruth held on to her.
translation_verse: Na bɛzunle bieko kpole kpalɛ; Ɔpa metanle ɔ hu ɔ nli ne, ɔyɛle ye atuu na ɔziale ɔhɔle. Na Wulutu ɛdeɛ, yeamkponle kɛ ɔkɛzia.

english_verse: Naomi then said to Ruth, “Look, your sister-in-law is going back to her people and to her gods! Why don't you go with her?”
translation_verse: Na Nawome zele Wulutu kɛ, “Nea, ɛ hola ɛzia ɛhɔ ye sua zo ɔkazonle ye abusua bozonle ne mɔɔ ɔsonle ye dɛba la. Ɛdawɔ noko toa ye ɛ nee ye bɛhɔ.”

english_verse: Ruth answered, “Please don't tell me to leave you and return home! I will go where you go, I will live where you live; your people will be my people, your God will be my God.
translation_verse: Wulutu zele ye kɛ, “Mmafoa me kɛ mengyakyi wɔ mengɔ anzɛɛ menzia na memmatoa wɔ. Ɔluakɛ me nee wɔ yɛkɔ ɛleka mɔɔ ɛlɛkɔ la, mebadɛnla ɛleka mɔɔ ɛkɛdɛnla la. Wɔ menli bayɛ me menli, na wɔ Nyamenle ne ayɛ me Nyamenle.

english_verse: I will die where you die and be buried beside you. May the Lord punish me if we are ever separated, even by death!”
translation_verse: Ɛleka mɔɔ ɛkɛwu ɛkɛla la, ɛkɛ ne yɛɛ medame mebawu meala a. Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛdua me kakɛ ɛgua me bie zo kɛ menwɔgyakyi wɔ menwɔzia a, kyesɛ ewule na akpakye yɛ mu nwiɔ yɛ avinli!”

english_verse: When Naomi saw that Ruth had made up her mind to go with her, she stopped urging her to go back.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Nawome nwunle kɛ Wulutu ɛzi ye ɛbolɛ kɛ ɔ nee ye kɔ la, yeandɛ ɔ nloa anu bieko.

english_verse: They reached Bethlehem, and the whole town was excited to see them. The women who lived there asked, “Can this really be Naomi?”
translation_verse: Yemɔti bɛ mu nwiɔ bɛzile nuhua na bɛrale Bɛtelɛhɛm. Na mɔɔ bɛradwule la sua ne azo kpudwule, na mraalɛ ne mɔ zele kɛ, “Nawome ɛhye ɔ?”

english_verse: Then she told them, “Don't call me Naomi any longer! Call me Mara, because God has made my life bitter.
translation_verse: Nawome zele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛmmafɛlɛ me Nawome bieko; bɛvɛlɛ me Maala. Ɔluakɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma nee me ɛli ye ɛnwonle zo kpalɛ kpalɛ.

english_verse: I had everything when I left, but the Lord has brought me back with nothing. How can you still call me Naomi, when God has turned against me and made my life so hard?”
translation_verse: Mekɔ la ɛnee megyi boɛ, na Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛmaa meva me sa mgbane mezia mera. Duzu ati a bɛkɛvɛlɛ me Nawome a, wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma annwu me ɛralɛ nu na Nyamenle Tumivolɛ ne asa ɛyɛ ɛnlomboɛ wɔ me nwo zo la?”

english_verse: When Boaz arrived from Bethlehem and went out to his field, he said to the harvest workers, “The Lord bless you!” They replied, “And may the Lord bless you!”
translation_verse: Bowaze vi Bɛtelɛhɛm rale na ɔrayɛle ye gyimayɛvoma ne mo ɔzele kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma nee bɛ ɛdɛnla.” Bɛliele zolɛ kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛyila wɔ.”

english_verse: Then Boaz asked the man in charge of the harvest workers, “Who is that young woman?”
translation_verse: Akee Bowaze bizale ye sonvolɛ ne mɔɔ nea gyimayɛvoma ne anwo zo la kɛ, “Bɛlɛra ɛhye vi nienwu?”

english_verse: The man answered, “She is the one who came back from Moab with Naomi.
translation_verse: Kpavolɛ ne mɔɔ nea gyimayɛvoma ne anwo zo la buale kɛ, “Mowabe bɛlɛra ne mɔɔ nee Nawome vi Mowabe maanle nu rale la ɛne.

english_verse: She asked if she could pick up grain left by the harvest workers, and she has been working all morning without a moment's rest.”
translation_verse: Ɔrazɛlɛle me kɛ, ‘Mekpa wɔ kyɛlɛ, maa menluolua wɔ gyimayɛvoma ye anzi saa menwɔnyia mgbɛpɛlɛ bie a.’ Ɔrale sumunli nwonlomɔ ye na ɔtɛdiele ye ɛnwomenle bɔbɔ. Kɛkala bie yɛɛ yehɔdɛnla kpɔda ne abo lɔ ekyii a.”

english_verse: Boaz went over to Ruth and said, “I think it would be best for you not to pick up grain in anyone else's field. Stay here with the women
translation_verse: Akee Bowaze zele Wulutu kɛ, “Me ra raalɛ, tie mɔɔ meka meahile wɔ la kpalɛ. Mmakɔ ɛya gyɛne nu ɛkɔkpondɛ mgbɛpɛlɛ, yɛɛ mmafi ɛya ɛhye anu noko ɛkɔ fofolɛ nu. Ɛ nee me sonvolɛ mraalɛ ne mɔ ɛwoa ɛke ala.

english_verse: and follow along behind them, as they gather up what the men have cut. I have warned the men not to bother you, and whenever you are thirsty, you can drink from their water jars.”
translation_verse: Di bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛlɛte ma ne la anzi kpalɛ na toa bɛ kɔ ɛleka mɔɔ bɛkɔ la. Meha mehile mgbavolɛ ne mɔ kɛ awie biala mmafa ɔ sa ka wɔ. Saa nzuhɔne ɛlɛku wɔ a, kɔ ɛleka mɔɔ nzule ne wɔ la na no mɔɔ mgbavolɛ ne mɔ ɛhɔza ɛra la bie.”

english_verse: Ruth bowed down to the ground and said, “You know I come from another country. Why are you so good to me?”
translation_verse: Wulutu dule dɔle Bowaze agyakɛ anu na ɔzele kɛ, “Mele ɛyɛvolɛ, na duzu ati a wɔyɛ ahunlunyele kpole ɛhye wɔmaa me a?”

english_verse: Boaz answered, “I've heard how you've helped your mother-in-law ever since your husband died. You even left your own father and mother to come and live in a foreign land among people you don't know.
translation_verse: Na Bowaze buale ye kɛ, “Mɔɔ wɔyɛ wɔmaa ɛ hu ɔ nli, ɔvi mekɛ mɔɔ ɛ hu wule, nee kɛ wɔzi wɔgyakyi ɛ ze nee ɛ nli, ɛvi wɔ maanle nu wɔra menli mɔɔ ɛnze bɛ la avinli la, bɛha ye kɔsɔɔti bɛhile me.

english_verse: I pray that the Lord God of Israel will reward you for what you have done. And now that you have come to him for protection, I pray that he will bless you.”
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛyila wɔ wɔ mɔɔ wɔyɛ la anwo; Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛlo wɔ molozo na Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne mɔɔ wɔravea ɔ ndɛba abo la ɛva wɔ ɛzie boɛ.”

english_verse: Ruth replied, “Sir, it's good of you to speak kindly to me and make me feel so welcome. I'm not even one of your servants.”
translation_verse: Wulutu zele ye kɛ, “Yɛmenle, wɔlo me somaa. Wɔkyekye me rɛle na wɔdendɛ wɔhile me kɛ wɔ sonvolɛ raalɛ a le me wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ memboka wɔ sonvolɛ mraalɛ ne mɔ anwo la.”

english_verse: At mealtime Boaz said to Ruth, “Come, eat with us. Have some bread and dip it in the sauce.” At once she sat down with the workers, and Boaz handed her some roasted grain. Ruth ate all she wanted and had some left over.
translation_verse: Ɔdwule aleɛlilɛ mekɛ la Bowaze vɛlɛle ye kɛ, “Bɛla, bali debie; anrɛɛ fa wɔ kpanwo ne bɔ subue ye anu.” Yemɔti Wulutu dɛnlanle gyimayɛvoma ne mɔ anwo ɛkɛ ne na Bowaze manle ye abɛlɛ ngyehye manle ɔlile, ɔ ko yile, bie hale.

english_verse: Be sure to pull out some stalks of grain from the bundles and leave them on the ground for her. And don't speak harshly to her!”
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Wulutu dwazole kɛ ɔkakpondɛ mgbɛpɛlɛ bieko la Bowaze zele ye gyimayɛvoma ne kɛ, “Bɛmaa ye adenle bɛmaa ɔluolua aziakɛ ne mɔ mɔɔ bɛkyekye la avinli ɔsesa mgbɛpɛlɛ; anrɛɛ bɛmmatendɛ ye bɛgua ɔ nyunlu aze. Eza anrɛɛ bɛhwehwe mɔɔ bɛkyekye la bie bɛmaa ye.”

english_verse: Ruth worked in the field until evening. Then after she had pounded the grain off the stalks, she had a large basket full of grain.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Wulutu woale ɛya ne anu kpondɛle mgbɛpɛlɛ toonwo aleɛ muanle nwolɛ. Ɔwozole mɔɔ ɔnyianle ye la ɛnee ɔle asɛɛ kilo bulu.

english_verse: She took the grain to town and showed Naomi how much she had picked up. Ruth also gave her the food left over from her lunch.
translation_verse: Wulutu vale mɔɔ ɔnyianle ye la hɔle sua zo na ɔvale ɔhilele Nawome. Eza Wulutu vale aleɛ mɔɔ ɔlile la bie hɔmanle Nawome.

english_verse: Naomi said, “Where did you work today? Whose field was it? God bless the man who treated you so well!” Then Ruth told her that she had worked in the field of a man named Boaz.
translation_verse: Nawome bizale ye kɛ, “Nienwu a ɛnɛ ɛhɔsesale wɔ mgbɛpɛlɛ ne a? Nienwu a ɛlile gyima ɛhye a? Nyamenle ɛyila ahenle mɔɔ yɛle wɔ nyele ɛhye la.” Wulutu zele Nawome kɛ, “Nrenya ne mɔɔ ɛnɛ mengɔle ye ɛya nu la bɛfɛlɛ ye Bowaze.”

english_verse: “The Lord bless Boaz!” Naomi replied. “He has shown that he is still loyal to the living and to the dead. Boaz is a close relative, one of those who is supposed to look after us.”
translation_verse: Nawome buale ɔ ra ne aye ne kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛyila ye kɛ ɔdwenle menli mɔɔ ɛwu ɛhɔ nee anyewɔzoamra anwo la. Nrenya ne le yɛ nwo sonla. Ɔle sonla mɔɔ di agya a ɔyɛ boɛ a.”

english_verse: Ruth told her, “Boaz even said I could stay in the field with his workers until they had finished harvesting all his grain.”
translation_verse: Mowabenli Wulutu zele kɛ, “Eza bɔbɔ ɔhanle ɔhilele me kɛ mendɛnla ye sonvolɛ mraalɛ ne mɔ anwo ɛkɛ kɔkpula mekɛ mɔɔ bɛkɛwie ye bɛyɔba ne bu la.”

english_verse: Naomi replied, “My daughter, it's good that you can pick up grain alongside the women who work in his field. Who knows what might happen to you in someone else's field!”
translation_verse: Nawome zele Wulutu kɛ, “Me ra raalɛ, ɔle kpalɛ kɛ ɛ nee ye sonvolɛ mraalɛ ne mɔ kɛyɛ gyima; saa ɛluolua awie ɛya nu a bɛkɛyɛ wɔ mgbane mgbane.”

english_verse: And so, Ruth stayed close to the women, while picking up grain in his field. Ruth worked in the fields until the barley and wheat were harvested. And all this time she lived with Naomi.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Wulutu woale Bowaze sonvolɛ mraalɛ ne mɔ anwo ɛkɛ ne ɔsesale mgbɛpɛlɛ wɔ ɛya ne anu toonwo ma ɛdelɛ ne pɛle nu. Na akee ɔdɛnlanle aze wɔ ɔ hu ɔ nli ne anwo ɛkɛ.

english_verse: One day, Naomi said to Ruth: It's time I found you a husband, who will give you a home and take care of you.
translation_verse: Akee Nawome zele Wulutu kɛ, “Me ra raalɛ, ɔwɔ kɛ memaa bɛgya wɔ, amaa wɔanyia awie ɛ nee ye adɛnla.

english_verse: You have been picking up grain alongside the women who work for Boaz, and you know he is a relative of ours. Tonight he will be threshing the grain.
translation_verse: Ɛze ɔ? Bowaze mɔɔ ye sonvolɛ mraalɛ a ɛ nee bɛ yɛ gyima la le yɛ hu mɔ busuanli. Ɛnɛ nɔsolɛ ɔbakpogya ma wɔ ɛleka mɔɔ bɛkpogya ye ala la.

english_verse: Now take a bath and put on some perfume, then dress in your best clothes. Go where he is working, but don't let him see you until he has finished eating and drinking.
translation_verse: Zɔhane ati nrinzi ɛ nwo, siezie ɛ nwo, na kɔ ɛleka mɔɔ bɛkpogya ma ne la; na anrɛɛ mmamaa ɔnwu wɔ kɔkpula mekɛ mɔɔ ɔkɛli debie na ɔkɛnlo nwanye la.

english_verse: Watch where he goes to spend the night, then when he is asleep, lift the cover and lie down at his feet. He will tell you what to do.
translation_verse: Yɛ ɛleka mɔɔ ɔbala la nzonlɛ kpalɛ, na saa ɔda a, kɔye ɔ gyakɛ anwo ɛdanlɛ ne na da ɔ gyakɛ anu ɛkɛ, na ɔbahile wɔ debie mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ ɛyɛ la.”

english_verse: Ruth answered, “I'll do whatever you say.”
translation_verse: Na Wulutu zele ye kɛ, “Mɔɔ wɔha la, mebayɛ.”

english_verse: She went out to the place where Boaz was working and did what Naomi had told her.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Wulutu hɔle ɛleka mɔɔ bɛkpogya ma ne la na ɔhɔyɛle kɛmɔ ɔ hu ɔ nli ne zele ye la.

english_verse: After Boaz finished eating and drinking and was feeling happy, he went over and fell asleep near the pile of grain. Ruth slipped over quietly. She lifted the cover and lay down near his feet.
translation_verse: Bowaze wiele debie di na ɔvale nwanye ekyi ɔhanle ɔ nloa na ɔ nye liele la, ɔhɔlale ye ma ne azo lɔ. Wulutu yɛle nyaa nyaa hɔyele Bowaze agyakɛ anwo ɛdanlɛ ne na ɔlale ɔ gyakɛ anu ɛkɛ ne.

english_verse: In the middle of the night, Boaz suddenly woke up and was shocked to see a woman lying at his feet.
translation_verse: Kɛyɛ alevinli mu nwiɔ avinli yɛɛ Bowaze bɔle mgbatike dwazole a. Na ɔdole ɔ nye la ɔnwunle kɛ raalɛ bie la ɔ gyakɛ anu ɛkɛ.

english_verse: “Who are you?” he asked. “Sir, I am Ruth,” she answered, “and you are the relative who is supposed to take care of me. So spread the edge of your cover over me.”
translation_verse: Na ɔbizale kɛ, “Ɛdawɔ nwane a ɛla ɛkɛ ne la?” Wulutu buale ye kɛ, “Yɛmenle, medame, wɔ sonvolɛ raalɛ Wulutu ɔ. Ɛle me hu kɔliagya mɔɔ wɔmɔ a ɔwɔ kɛ ɛnea me a; yemɔti gya me.”

english_verse: Boaz replied: The Lord bless you! This shows how truly loyal you are to your family. You could have looked for a younger man, either rich or poor, but you didn't.
translation_verse: Bowaze zele ye kɛ, “Me ra raalɛ, Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛyila wɔ. Akee wɔhile kɛ ɛlɛ subane kpalɛ wɔdɛla alumua ne kɛ wɔandoɔdoa mgbavolɛ sukoavolɛma anzɛɛ ehyianvolɛma la.

english_verse: Don't worry, I'll do what you have asked. You are respected by everyone in town.
translation_verse: Kɛkala, me ra raalɛ, mmasulo; debie biala mɔɔ wɔbiza la, mebayɛ meamaa wɔ, ɔluakɛ awie biala mɔɔ wɔ sua ye azo la ze kɛ ɛle raalɛ mɔɔ lɛ subane a.

english_verse: It's true that I am one of the relatives who is supposed to take care of you, but there is someone who is an even closer relative.
translation_verse: Ɔle nɔhalɛ kɛ mele kɔliagya, megya wɔ a ɔyɛ boɛ, noko ahenle mɔɔ di agya mumua ne la wɔ ɛkɛ.

english_verse: Stay here until morning, then I will find out if he is willing to look after you. If he isn't, I promise by the living God to do it myself. Now go back to sleep until morning.
translation_verse: Zɔhane ati boa ɛke ɛnɛ nɔe, na saa aleɛ kye na kɔliagya ne se kɛ ɔkɛgya wɔ a, ɛnee ye kpalɛ nu ɔ; maa ɔgya wɔ. Na saa ɔnrɛgya wɔ noko a, ɛnee kɛmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma de aze la, menwɔgya wɔ. Wɔmɔ da na nwonlomɔ.”

english_verse: Ruth lay down again, but she got up before daylight, because Boaz did not want anyone to know she had been there.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Wulutu lale ɔ gyakɛ anu ɛkɛ ne na ɔdwazole nwonlomɔ mangyee ne ala mɔɔ ɛnee maanle nu ɛtɛtetele la kɛ ɔkɔ. Bowaze zele ye kɛ, “Mmamaa awie biala te kɛ raalɛ rale ɛleka mɔɔ bɛkpogya ma ye la.”

english_verse: Then he told her to spread out her cape. And he filled it with grain and placed it on her shoulder. When Ruth got back to town,
translation_verse: Eza ɔzele ye kɛ, “Fa wɔ ɛdanlɛ ne mɔɔ gua ɛ nwo zo la bɛla na tɛlɛ nu.” Wulutu dɛlɛle ye ɛdanlɛ ne anu, na Bowaze zule ma kilo abulanwiɔ guale nuhua na ɔkyekyele ɔzoale ye. Na Wulutu hɔle sua nu.

english_verse: She also said, “Boaz gave me this grain, because he didn't want me to come back without something for you.”
translation_verse: Na ɔvale ɔzɔle zolɛ kɛ, “Ɔzele me kɛ, ‘Menrɛmaa ɛnrɛva ɛ sa mgbane ɛnrɛhɔhile ɛ hu ɔ nli.’ Yemɔti ɔzule ma kilo abulanwiɔ ɔmanle me.”

english_verse: Naomi replied, “Just be patient and don't worry about what will happen. He won't rest until everything is settled today!”
translation_verse: Na Nawome zele ye kɛ, “Me ra raalɛ, sie ɛ nwo diinyi kɔkpula mekɛ mɔɔ yɛkɛnwu edwɛkɛ ne guabelɛ la. Ɔluakɛ nrenya ne ɛnrɛla, kɛ ɔkɛyɛ biala la, ɔwɔ kɛ ɔnwu edwɛkɛ ne guabelɛ ɛnɛ kenle ko ye ala.”

english_verse: In the meanwhile, Boaz had gone to the meeting place at the town gate and was sitting there when the other close relative came by. So Boaz invited him to come over and sit down, and he did.
translation_verse: Bowaze hɔle suakpole ne anlenkɛ kpole ne anloa, ɛleka mɔɔ ɔyɛ a bɛyia la na ɔdɛnlanle aze. Yeangyɛ biala yɛɛ kɔliagya ne mɔɔ Bowaze lile ye edwɛkɛ la rale ɛkɛ ne a. Bowaze zele ye kɛ, “Ayi, bɛla badɛnla aze.” Na ɔradɛnlanle aze.

english_verse: Then Boaz got ten of the town leaders and also asked them to sit down. After they had sat down,
translation_verse: Bowaze vɛlɛvɛlɛle suakpole ne azo mgbanyima bulu na ɔmanle bɛradɛnlanle aze wɔ ɛkɛ ne.

english_verse: he said to the man: Naomi has come back from Moab and is selling the land that belonged to her husband Elimelech.
translation_verse: Akee ɔzele kɔliagya ne kɛ, “Nawome vi Mowabe ɛra, na yeyɛ kɛ ɔtɔne yɛ busuanli Yilemɛlɛke azɛlɛ ne.

english_verse: I'm telling you about this, since you are his closest relative and have the right to buy the property. If you want it, you can buy it now. These ten men and the others standing here can be witnesses. But if you don't want the property, let me know, because I am next in line. The man replied, “I'll buy it!”
translation_verse: Yemɔti medwenle nwolɛ kɛ meka meahile wɔ kɛ tɔ azɛlɛ ne maa menli mɔɔ wɔ ɛke nee mgbanyima mɔɔ mehɔvɛlɛvɛlɛ bɛ la ɛli nwolɛ daselɛ. Saa ɛkɛlie azɛlɛ ne a ɛnee die, saa ɛnrɛlie noko a ɛnee ka kile me maa menwu ye, ɔluakɛ awie bieko ɛnle ɛkɛ ne kɛ wɔmɔ yɛɛ mame.” Na nrenya ne mɔɔ di agya ne la zele Bowaze kɛ, “Mebalie azɛlɛ ne.”

english_verse: “If you do buy it from Naomi,” Boaz told him, “you must also marry Ruth. Then if you have a son by her, the property will stay in the family of Ruth's first husband.”
translation_verse: Bowaze zele ye kɛ, “Saa ɛtɔ azɛlɛ ne na ɛdie ɛfi Nawome asa anu a, ɛnee ɔwɔ kɛ ɛgya Wulutu, Mowabenli kunlanvolɛ ne, amaa mɔɔ lɛ azɛlɛ ne la duma amminli ye agyadeɛ ne anwo.”

english_verse: The man answered, “If that's the case, I don't want to buy it! That would make problems with the property I already own. You may buy it yourself, because I cannot.”
translation_verse: Kɔliagya ne zele Bowaze kɛ, “Saa zɔhane ɛdeɛ a ɛnee mekpɔlɔkpɔla me sa anwo wɔ debie biala anwo. Ɔluakɛ ɔkɛgyegye me mra ne mɔ agyalilɛ. Yemɔti memaa wɔ nwolɛ adenle. Tɔ azɛlɛ ne na mame, menrɛdɔ.”

english_verse: So after the man had agreed to let Boaz buy the property, he took off one of his sandals and handed it to Boaz.
translation_verse: Yemɔti kɔliagya ne yele ye mgbɔlaboa ne na ɔzele Bowaze kɛ, “Kɔdɔ fa.”

english_verse: Boaz told the town leaders and everyone else: All of you are witnesses that today I have bought from Naomi the property that belonged to Elimelech and his two sons, Chilion and Mahlon.
translation_verse: Bowaze zele mgbanyima nee menli mɔɔ wɔ ɛkɛ ne la amuala kɛ, “Bɛdabɛ bɛdi daselɛ kɛ ɛnɛ kenle ye, medɔ debie biala mɔɔ anrɛɛ le Yilemɛlɛke ɛdeɛ la, nee debie biala mɔɔ le Kaeleɔn nee Maalɔn ɛdeɛ la amuala mevi Nawome asa anu.

english_verse: You are also witnesses that I have agreed to marry Mahlon's widow Ruth, the Moabite woman. This will keep the property in his family's name, and he will be remembered in this town.
translation_verse: Bieko, ɛnɛ Mowabenli Wulutu mɔɔ anrɛɛ le Maalɔn aye la le me ye, amaa yeawo mralɛ wɔ agyadeɛ ne mɔɔ melie la duma nu, na mɔɔ ɛwu ɛhɔ la duma amminli ɔ mediema avinli anzɛɛ ye sua zo; bɛ muala bɛdi ɛhye mɔ anwo daselɛ ɛnɛ.”

english_verse: The town leaders and the others standing there said: We are witnesses to this. And we pray that the Lord will give your wife many children, just as he did Leah and Rachel, the wives of Jacob. May you be a rich man in the tribe of Ephrath and an important man in Bethlehem.
translation_verse: Na bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛyiale ɛkɛ ne la amuala nee mgbanyima ne mɔ hanle kɛ, “Ɛhɛe, yɛdi nwolɛ daselɛ. Yɛsɛlɛ kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛmaa raalɛ ne mɔɔ ɛlɛba wɔ sua nu la ɛyɛ kɛ Relahyɛle nee Liya mɔɔ bɛ kunlu mralɛ a kyekyele Yizilayɛ maanle ye la. Nyamenle ɛmaa ɛkpazi wɔ Ɛfelate na ɛyɛ mandimase wɔ Bɛtelɛhɛm ɛke.

english_verse: May the children you have by this young woman make your family as famous as the family of Perez, the son of Tamar and Judah.
translation_verse: Ngakula mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma bava amaa ɛdawɔ nee ɛ ye kakula ɛhye la ɛmaa wɔ sua nu ɛyɛ gbudugbudu kɛ Dwuda nee ɔ ye Teemaa ara Pɛlɛze sua nu la.” Bowaze nee ɔ bo zo amra

english_verse: Boaz married Ruth, and the Lord blessed her with a son.
translation_verse: Na Bowaze vale Wulutu yɛle ɔ ye na ɔ nee ye hɔdɛnlanle. Ɛdɛnkɛma manle ɔvale ɛkolɛ na ɔwole ralɛ nrenya.

english_verse: After his birth, the women said to Naomi: Praise the Lord! Today he has given you a grandson to take care of you. We pray that the boy will grow up to be famous everywhere in Israel.
translation_verse: Mraalɛ mɔɔ wɔ suakpole ne azo la zele Nawome kɛ, “Yɛyɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma mo; ɛnɛ yemaa wɔnyia anlɔnra nrenya. Yɛsɛlɛ kɛ ɔnyia duma kpole wɔ Yizilayɛ.

english_verse: He will make you happy and take care of you in your old age, because he is the son of your daughter-in-law. And she loves you more than seven sons of your own would love you.
translation_verse: Ɛ ra ne aye ne mɔɔ kulo wɔ la ɛyɛ mɔɔ hyia wɔ tɛla mralɛ mrenya nsuu bɔbɔ la ɛmaa wɔ. Kɛkala yemaa wɔ ralɛ nrenya mɔɔ bamaa wɔ sua nu ayɛ gbudugbudu na yeazɔ wɔ, wɔ wɔ mrelera nu a.”

english_verse: Naomi loved the boy and took good care of him.
translation_verse: Na Nawome liele kakula ne bɔle ye ɛbolɛ, na ɔliele ye ɛnleanlɛ ɔdole ɔ nwo zo.

english_verse: The neighborhood women named him Obed, but they called him “Naomi's Boy.” When Obed grew up he had a son named Jesse, who later became the father of King David.
translation_verse: Mraalɛ mɔɔ wɔ kpalɛ ne azo la noko hanle hilele menli kɛ, “Bɛwo ralɛ nrenya bɛmaa Nawome.” Bɛdonle kakula ne Obɛde. Obɛde wole Gyɛsi mɔɔ wole Belemgbunli Devidi la.

english_verse: Here is a list of the ancestors of David: Jesse, Obed, Boaz, Salmon, Nahshon, Amminadab, Ram, Hezron, and Perez.
translation_verse: Akee Pɛlɛze abusuandoazo ne, bɛmɛ ɛne: Pɛlɛze wole Hɛzelɔn, Hɛzelɔn wole Relam, yɛɛ Relam wole Amenadabe. Amenadabe wole Nahyɔn, Nahyɔn wole Salemɔn, Salemɔn wole Bowaze, Bowaze wole Obɛde, Obɛde wole Gyɛsi, yɛɛ Gyɛsi wole Belemgbunli Devidi.

english_verse: Elkanah lived in Ramah, a town in the hill country of Ephraim. His great-great-grandfather was Zuph, so Elkanah was a member of the Zuph clan of the Ephraim tribe. Elkanah's father was Jeroham, his grandfather was Elihu, and his great-grandfather was Tohu.
translation_verse: Nrenya bie mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye Ɛlekana la woale ɛkɛ, ɔvi Yifelaem abusua ekpunli ne anu. Ɔdɛnlanle sua ne mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye Releema, mɔɔ wɔ Yifelaem awoka ne mɔ azo la azo. Bɛfɛlɛ ɔ ze Gyɛloham. Gyɛloham ɔ ze a le Ɛlaehu; Ɛlaehu ɔ ze a le Tohu; Tohu ɔ ze a le Zɛfe.

english_verse: Elkanah had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah. Although Peninnah had children, Hannah did not have any.
translation_verse: Ɛlekana gyale mraalɛ nwiɔ. Bɛfɛlɛ ko Hana yɛɛ bɛfɛlɛ ko Pɛnena. Pɛnena bɔle ɛdane na Hana anwo ralɛ.

english_verse: Once a year Elkanah traveled from his hometown to Shiloh, where he worshiped the Lord All-Powerful and offered sacrifices. Eli was the Lord's priest there, and his two sons Hophni and Phinehas served with him as priests.
translation_verse: Ɛvolɛ biala Ɛlekana vi Releema kɔ Hyaelo. Ɛkɛ ne a sɛlɛvolɛ Yilae amra mrenya nwiɔ ne, Hɔfenae nee Fenɛhaze yɛ bɛ sɛlɛvolɛ gyima ne a. Ɛlekana kɔ ɛkɛ ne ɛvolɛ biala kɔsonle na ɔbɔ azu ɔmaa Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma.

english_verse: Whenever Elkanah offered a sacrifice, he gave some of the meat to Peninnah and some to each of her sons and daughters.
translation_verse: Mekɛ biala mɔɔ Ɛlekana kabɔ azu la, ɔtu ye azubɔdeɛ ne anu ɛkpɔ ko ɔmaa ɔ ye Pɛnena na ɔmaa ɔ mra mrenya nee mraalɛ ne mɔ biala ɛkpɔ ko.

english_verse: But he gave Hannah even more, because he loved Hannah very much, even though the Lord had kept her from having children of her own.
translation_verse: Ɔkulo Hana kpalɛ noko ɛkpɔ ko ala a ɔfa ɔmaa ɔdaye a, ɔluakɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ammaa yeanwo ralɛ.

english_verse: Peninnah liked to make Hannah feel miserable about not having any children,
translation_verse: Dahuu ɔ hola Pɛnena si ye amgbu na ɔfa ye mota ɔse ye, ɔluakɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ammaa yeannyia ɛkolɛ yeanwo ralɛ.

english_verse: especially when the family went to the house of the Lord each year. One day, Elkanah was there offering a sacrifice, when Hannah began crying and refused to eat.
translation_verse: Nyɛleɛ ɛhye hɔle zolɛ ɛvolɛ biala; mekɛ biala mɔɔ bɛkɛhɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu kɛ bɛkazonle la Pɛnena ta Hana anye zo ɔmaa ɔsu toonwo mɔɔ aleɛ bɔbɔ ɔnli bie a.

english_verse: So Elkanah asked, “Hannah, why are you crying? Why won't you eat? Why do you feel so bad? Don't I mean more to you than ten sons?”
translation_verse: Saa ɔba ye zɛhae a ɔ hu Ɛlekana biza ye kɛ, “Hana, duzu ati a ɛlɛsu a? Duzu ati a ɛnrɛli debie a? Duzu ati a dahuu ɛwɔ nyane nu a? Anzɛɛ me nwo ɛnlɛ nvasoɛ ɛmmaa wɔ ɛndɛla mralɛ mrenya bulu ɔ?” Hana nee Yilae

english_verse: “Lord All-Powerful, I am your servant, but I am so miserable! Please let me have a son. I promise to give him to you for as long as he lives, and his hair will never be cut.”
translation_verse: Na Hana bɔle ɛwɔkɛ kɛ, “Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, to ɛ nye nea me, wɔ sonvolɛ; mehyia na kakye me; mmamaa ɛ rɛle fi me. Mebɔ ɛwɔkɛ kɛ saa ɛmaa menyia ɛkolɛ mewo ralɛ nrenya a menwɔdu ye nee ye ɛbɛlabɔlɛ muala menwɔmaa wɔ, na ye enrinli ko bɔbɔ, bɛnrɛde bɛnrɛdo aze.”

english_verse: Hannah prayed silently to the Lord for a long time. But her lips were moving, and Eli thought she was drunk.
translation_verse: Hana andendɛ na ɛnee ɔlɛsɛlɛ ɔ ti anu la ati, ɔ nloa ala a ɔbukebuke a, yemɔti Yilae bule ye kɛ sonla bie mɔɔ ɛbo nza la.

english_verse: “How long are you going to stay drunk?” he asked. “Sober up!”
translation_verse: Yemɔti Yilae zele ye kɛ, “Duzu ati a wɔbo zɛhae ɛ? Gyakyi nzanlonlɛ na yɛ ɛ nye gyɛlɛmgbɛɛnye”

english_verse: “Sir, please don't think I'm no good!” Hannah answered. “I'm not drunk, and I haven't been drinking. But I do feel miserable and terribly upset. I've been praying all this time, telling the Lord about my problems.”
translation_verse: Mmadwenle kɛ wɔ sonvolɛ raalɛ, mele sonlamgbane; melɛ tendenle ye amuala, me nyane nee me anwubɛnyunlu ala yɛɛ melɛye meado Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlu a, ɔluakɛ meyɛ anwunvɔne.”

english_verse: Eli replied, “Go home. Everything will be fine. The God of Israel will answer your prayer.”
translation_verse: Na Yilae zele ye kɛ, “Kɔ anzonudwolɛ nu; wɔ nzɛlɛlɛ ne mɔɔ wɔva wɔdo Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne anyunlu la, ɔyɛ ye zɔhane ɔmaa wɔ.”

english_verse: “Sir, thank you for being so kind to me,” Hannah said. Then she left, and after eating something, she felt much better. Samuel Is Born
translation_verse: Hana buale kɛ, “Maa wɔ sonvolɛ raalɛ ye ɛzɔ ɛ nye dahuu.” Akee Hana hɔle sua nu, ɔlile debie na ɔgyakyile ɔ nwo alɔbɔlɛ ɛyɛlɛ. Samoɛle awolɛ nee ye Ɛdɛnkɛma asa anu ɛduwulalɛ

english_verse: Elkanah and his family got up early the next morning and worshiped the Lord. Then they went back home to Ramah. Later the Lord blessed Elkanah and Hannah
translation_verse: Alehyenlɛ ne anu, ye aleɛbahye ne Ɛlekana nee ye sua nu amra ne dwazole ndɛndɛ na bɛzɛlɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma. Akee bɛziale bɛhɔle bɛ sua zo Releema. Ɛlekana nwunle ɔ ye Hana, na Ɛdɛnkɛma hakyele ye.

english_verse: with a son. She named him Samuel because she had asked the Lord for him. Hannah Gives Samuel to the Lord
translation_verse: Yemɔti yeangyɛ biala yɛɛ Hana vale ɛkolɛ a; ɔwole ralɛ nrenya na bɛdonle ye Samoɛle, ɔluakɛ Hana se, “Menzɛlɛle ye Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛkɛ.”

english_verse: The next time Elkanah and his family went to offer their yearly sacrifice, he took along a gift that he had promised to give to the Lord.
translation_verse: Eza mekɛ ne dwule kɛ ɔwɔ kɛ Ɛlekana nee ye sua nu amra kɔ Hyaelo kɔbɔ bɛ ɛvolɛ azu ne na ɔtua ye ɛwɔkɛbɔlɛ ɔmaa Ɛdɛnkɛma.

english_verse: But Hannah stayed home, because she had told Elkanah, “Samuel and I won't go until he's old enough for me to stop nursing him. Then I'll give him to the Lord, and he can stay there at Shiloh for the rest of his life.”
translation_verse: Hana angɔ bie. Ɔzele ɔ hu kɛ, “Mekendɛ, saa kakula ne pɛ nyɛfonlɛ na ɔ nwo kputi a mebava ye meahɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu, na ɛkɛ ne yɛɛ ɔbadɛnla dahuu a.”

english_verse: “You know what's best,” Elkanah said. “Stay here until it's time to stop nursing him. I'm sure the Lord will help you do what you have promised.” Hannah did not go to Shiloh until she stopped nursing Samuel.
translation_verse: Ɛlekana buale ye kɛ, “Nɔhalɛ, yɛ mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ ɛyɛ la; tɛnla sua nu kɔkpula mekɛ mɔɔ kakula ne kɛpɛ nyɛfonlɛ na ɔ nwo kɛkputi la. Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛmaa wɔ ɛwɔkɛ ne ɛyɛ zɔhane.” Yemɔti Hana dɛnlanle sua nu na ɔlile kakula ne adane.

english_verse: “Sir,” Hannah said, “a few years ago I stood here beside you and asked the Lord
translation_verse: Hana zele ye kɛ, “Yɛmenle, asoo ɛkakye me? Nɔhalɛ, mame a mele raalɛ ne mɔɔ ragyinlanle ɛ nyunlu zɛlɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma la.

english_verse: to give me a child. Here he is! The Lord gave me just what I asked for.
translation_verse: Menzɛlɛle ye kɛ ɔmaa menwo ralɛ, na Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛyɛ me ɛbizalɛdeɛ ɛmaa me.

english_verse: Now I am giving him to the Lord, and he will be the Lord's servant for as long as he lives.” Hannah Prays Elkanah worshiped the Lord there at Shiloh, and
translation_verse: Yemɔti medu ye memaa Ɛdɛnkɛma. Mekɛ dodo mɔɔ ɔdi ye wɔ azɛlɛ ye azo la, ɔle Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛdeɛ.” Na ɔyeyɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma wɔ ɛkɛ ne.

english_verse: Hannah prayed: You make me strong and happy, Lord. You rescued me. Now I can be glad and laugh at my enemies.
translation_verse: Hana zɛlɛle zele kɛ: “Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛmaa me nye ɛlie; Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛmaa me anwosesebɛ kpole! Na yemaa mezele me kpɔvolɛma, me nye ɛlie somaa, ɔboalekɛ wɔboa me.

english_verse: No other god is like you. And with you we are safer than on a high mountain.
translation_verse: “Awie ɛnle nwuanzanwuanza kɛ wɔmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma angome ala, awie ɛnle ɛkɛ kɛ ɛ ngomekye ala; boavolɛ biala ɛnle ɛkɛ kɛ wɔmɔ yɛ Nyamenle ne ala.

english_verse: I can tell those proud people, “Stop your boasting! Nothing is hidden from the Lord, and he judges what we do.”
translation_verse: Bɛmmaka mgbole ko; bɛmmatu bɛ nloa anu ko. Ɔluakɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma le Nyamenle mɔɔ ze debie biala a, ɔbu nyɛleɛ biala anwo mgbonda.

english_verse: Our Lord, you break the bows of warriors, but you give strength to everyone who stumbles.
translation_verse: Anwosesebɛ ɛda ne mɔ ɛbubu, menli mɔɔ le bɛtɛɛ la nyia anwosesebɛ dahuu.

english_verse: People who once had plenty to eat must now hire themselves out for only a piece of bread. But you give the hungry more than enough to eat. A woman did not have a child, and you gave her seven, but a woman who had many was left with none.
translation_verse: Menli mɔɔ anrɛɛ lɛ ye di la ɛnɛ di ɛkpa na bɛali, menli mɔɔ ɛhɔne ku bɛ la ɛnɛ ɛnzu ɛhɔne. Mota raalɛ ne ɛwo awoba nsuu, na mɔɔ ɛwo somaa la asa ɛhondo aze.

english_verse: You take away life, and you give life. You send people down to the world of the dead and bring them back again.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma a ku a yɛɛ ɔdaye a ɔmaa ngoane a; ɔmaa menli kɔ mɔwuamra sua zo, na ɔfa bɛ ɔsia ɔba file zo.

english_verse: Our Lord, you are the one who makes us rich or poor. You put some in high positions and bring disgrace on others.
translation_verse: Ɔmaa bie mɔ di ehyia na bie mɔ nyia bɛ nwo, ɔbɛlɛ bie mɔ aze na ɔkpogya bie mɔ zo.

english_verse: You lift the poor and homeless out of the garbage dump and give them places of honor in royal palaces. You set the world on foundations, and they belong to you.
translation_verse: Ɔye ehyianvolɛma ɔfi bɛ nyane nu, ɔye anwunvɔnema ɔfi bɛ amaneɛnwunlɛ nu. Ɔyɛ bɛ arelemgbunli agɔnwo mɔ na ɔmaa bɛdi bɛ eni dɔɔnwo. Azɛlɛ ye adiabo ne le Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛdeɛ; zolɛ yɛɛ yezie ewiade a.

english_verse: You protect your loyal people, but everyone who is evil will die in darkness. We cannot win a victory by our own strength.
translation_verse: “Ɔsinza menli mɔɔ di nɔhalɛ maa ye la, na ɔmaa amumuyɛma minli esike nu, ɔluakɛ tɛ sonla ɔdaye ye anwosesebɛ yɛɛ ɔfa ɔdi konim a.

english_verse: Our Lord, those who attack you will be broken in pieces when you fight back with thunder from heaven. You will judge the whole earth and give power and strength to your chosen king. Samuel Stays with Eli
translation_verse: Bɛbazɛkye Ɛdɛnkɛma kpɔvolɛma; ɔbadea bɛ nu wɔ anwuma anwuma lɔ. Ɛdɛnkɛma babua aleɛabo amra ndɛne. Ɔbamaa ye belemgbunli ne anwosesebɛ, ɔbamaa ye belemgbunli ne ali konim.”

english_verse: Elkanah and Hannah went back home to Ramah, but the boy Samuel stayed to help Eli serve the Lord. Eli's Sons
translation_verse: Akee Ɛlekana ziale hɔle Releema na kakula Samoɛle hale Hyaelo wɔ sɛlɛvolɛ Yilae anwo ɛkɛ ne na ɔzonlenle Ɛdɛnkɛma. Yilae amra mrenya ne mɔ

english_verse: Eli's sons were priests, but they were dishonest and refused to obey the Lord. So, while people were boiling the meat from their sacrifices, these priests would send over a servant with a large, three-pronged fork.
translation_verse: Amaamuo mɔɔ sɛlɛvolɛ ne fa bu menli ne la a le kɛ, saa bɛlɛbɔ azu bɛamaa awie a, sɛlɛvolɛ ne sonvolɛ ne ba wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ azubɔdeɛ ne gyi senle zo la, na ɔfa faka agye nsa

english_verse: The servant would stick the fork into the cooking pot, and whatever meat came out on the fork was taken back to Eli's two sons. That was how they treated every Israelite who came to offer sacrifices in Shiloh.
translation_verse: ɔwula ɛzɛne anzɛɛ siase anzɛɛ danesɛne ne mɔɔ gyi senle ne azo ɛlɛwu gbodogbodo la anu; debie biala mɔɔ faka ne nee ye kɛvinde la le sɛlɛvolɛ ne ɛdeɛ. Ɛhye yɛɛ bɛvale bɛyɛle Yizilayɛma wɔ Hyaelo a.

english_verse: Sometimes, when people were offering sacrifices, the servant would come over, even before the fat had been cut off and sacrificed to the Lord. Then the servant would tell them, “The priest doesn't want his meat boiled! Give him some raw meat that he can roast!”
translation_verse: Eza saa bɛbava nane ɛnlome bɛayela bɛabɔ azu a ɛnee sɛlɛvolɛ ne sonvolɛ ne base ahenle mɔɔ nee azubɔdeɛ ne ɛra kɛ bɛva bɛbɔ azu ne la kɛ, “Sɛlɛvolɛ ne ɛnrɛlie nane mɔɔ bɛdo la, yemɔti fa amolɛ ne bie maa mengɔmaa ye na ɔdaye yeadondo.”

english_verse: Usually the people answered, “Take what you want. But first, let us sacrifice the fat to the Lord.” “No,” the servant would reply. “If you don't give it to me now, I'll take it by force.”
translation_verse: Saa ahenle mɔɔ lɛ azubɔdeɛ ne la se ye kɛ, “Maa bɛlumua bɛyela nane ɛnlome ne kolaa na wɔava dɔɔnwo biala mɔɔ ɛdawɔ ɛkulo la” a, sonvolɛ ne se ye kɛ, “Kyɛkyɛ, fa maa me kɛkala, saa tɛ ye zɔhane a medame mebava bie.”

english_verse: Eli's sons did not show any respect for the sacrifices that the people offered. This was a terrible sin, and it made the Lord very angry. Hannah Visits Samuel
translation_verse: Yemɔti Yilae amra ne mɔ ɛtane ne yɛle kpole bole zolɛ wɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma anye zo, ɔboalekɛ bɛambu Ɛdɛnkɛma azubɔlɛ ninyɛne ne mɔ bie. Samoɛle wɔ Hyaelo

english_verse: The boy Samuel served the Lord and wore a special linen garment
translation_verse: Kakula nrenya Samoɛle wulale “Lenen” ɛzonlenlɛ tɛladeɛ aguzo.

english_verse: and the clothes his mother made for him. She brought new clothes every year, when she and her husband came to offer sacrifices at Shiloh.
translation_verse: Ɛvolɛ biala saa ɔ ze nee ɔ nli kɔ kɛ bɛkabɔ bɛ ɛvolɛ azu ne a, ɔ nli kɔmaa ye tɛladeɛ ekyi ko mɔɔ yenwo ye woladapi la.

english_verse: Eli always blessed Elkanah and his wife and said, “Samuel was born in answer to your prayers. Now you have given him to the Lord. I pray that the Lord will bless you with more children to take his place.” After Eli had blessed them, Elkanah and Hannah would return home.
translation_verse: Saa bɛwie a Yilae yila Ɛlekana nee ɔ ye na ɔse Ɛlekana kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛmaa ɛ nee ɛ ye ɛhye ɛbɔ ɛdane ɛva ɛzie ko ye mɔɔ wɔdu wɔzie ɛkɛ wɔmaa ye la agyakɛ anu.” Akee saa bɛwie a bɛsia bɛkɔ bɛ sua zo.

english_verse: The Lord was kind to Hannah, and she had three more sons and two daughters. But Samuel grew up at the Lord's house in Shiloh. Eli Warns His Sons
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma lole Hana manle ɔnyianle mralɛ mrenya nsa bieko nee mralɛ mraalɛ nwiɔ. Kakula Samoɛle kawie nyi la ɛnee yebe Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛzonlenlɛ nu. Yilae nee ɔ mra mrenya ne mɔ

english_verse: “Why are you doing these awful things?” he asked them. “I've been hearing nothing but complaints about you from all of the Lord's people.
translation_verse: Me mra, kyɛkyɛ, bɛgyakyi nyɛleɛ ɛhye. Ɔle munzule ɛbɛla, ɔle dumanzɛkyelɛ mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma menli ne ɛlɛbɔ ye nolo wɔ bɛ avinli a.

english_verse: If you harm another person, God can help make things right between the two of you. But if you commit a crime against the Lord, no one can help you!” But the Lord had already decided to kill them. So he kept them from listening to their father. A Prophet Speaks to Eli
translation_verse: Saa sonla fo ɔ gɔnwo a, Nyamenle a di ɔ ti edwɛkɛ maa ye a, na saa sonla fo Ɛdɛnkɛma a ɛnee nwane a di ɔ ti mgbɔdalɛ a?” Noko Yilae amra ne mɔ andie bɛ ze aneɛ, ɔluakɛ ɛnee ɔle Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛhulolɛ kɛ ɔku bɛ.

english_verse: Each day, as Samuel grew older, the Lord was pleased with him, and so were the people.
translation_verse: Kakula Samoɛle ɛdeɛ, ɔnyinle na ɔzɔle Ɛdɛnkɛma nee menli anye. Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ mɔɔ tia Yilae awuke nu amra la

english_verse: One day a prophet came to Eli and gave him this message from the Lord: When your ancestors were slaves of the king of Egypt, I came and showed them who I am.
translation_verse: Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ bie vale Ɛdɛnkɛma nrɛlaleɛ rɛlɛle Yilae kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma se, ‘Mekɛ mɔɔ bɛ nlenya Aalɔn nee ye abusua ne wɔ akɛlɛ ɛzonlenlɛ nu wɔ Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne abo la, menyele me nwo mengilele bɛ.

english_verse: I am the Lord, the God of Israel. I promised to always let your family serve me as priests, but now I tell you that I cannot do this any longer! I honor anyone who honors me, but I put a curse on anyone who hates me.
translation_verse: Zɔhane ati, medame, Yizilayɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle, mese: membɔle ɛwɔkɛ kɛ wɔ abusua ne nee ɛ bo zo amra bayɛ me sɛlɛvolɛma dahuu ɛdeɛ na kɛkala, mese wɔ kɛ ɔnrɛyɛ zɔhane bieko. Mebali menli mɔɔ di me eni la eni; na menrɛbu bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛkpo me la ɛhwee.

english_verse: The time will come when I will kill you and everyone else in your family. Not one of you will live to an old age.
translation_verse: Tie, mekɛ ɛlɛba mɔɔ mebahu mgbavolɛ mɔɔ wɔ wɔ abusua ne anu la nee ɛ bo zo amra amuala a, amaa bɛ nuhua ko bɔbɔ anyɛ ɛrelera.

english_verse: Your family will have a lot of trouble. I will be kind to Israel, but everyone in your family will die young.
translation_verse: Ɛbali nyane na anyebolo badɔ ɛ nwo wɔ nyilalɛ mɔɔ mebava meamaa Yizilayɛma mɔɔ ɛha la anwo, noko, wɔ sua nu amra ɛdeɛ, sonla ko bɔbɔ ɛnrɛyɛ ɛrelera ɛlɛ.

english_verse: If I let anyone from your family be a priest, his life will be full of sadness and sorrow. But most of the men in your family will die a violent death!
translation_verse: Mebagyakyi ɛ bo zo amra ne anu ko mɔɔ ɔbazonle me kɛ me sɛlɛvolɛ. Ɔ nye bazi na yeaminli anyelazo muala, yɛɛ ɛ bo zo amra mɔɔ ɛha la kɔsɔɔti bawu dadeɛ nloa.

english_verse: To prove to you that I will do these things, your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, will die on the same day.
translation_verse: Saa ɛ mra mrenya nwiɔ ne, Hɔfenae nee Fenɛhaze gulu nu wu kenle ko a yɛɛ ɛkɛnwu kɛ edwɛkɛ biala mɔɔ meha la bayɛ zɔhane a.

english_verse: I have chosen someone else to be my priest, someone who will be faithful and obey me. I will always let his family serve as priests and help my chosen king.
translation_verse: Mebaye sɛlɛvolɛ mɔɔ bali nɔhalɛ amaa me na yeayɛ debie biala mɔɔ menwɔze ye kɛ ɔyɛ la. Mebamaa ye nlɔnra mɔɔ dahuu bazonle me wɔ belemgbunli ne mɔɔ mebaye ye la abo a.

english_verse: But if anyone is left from your family, he will come to my priest and beg for money or a little bread. He may even say to my priest, “Please let me be a priest, so I will at least have something to eat.”
translation_verse: Ɛ bo zo amra mɔɔ kɛha la bahɔ sɛlɛvolɛ zɔhane ɛkɛ ahɔzɛlɛ ezukoa nee aleɛ, na bɛabodo ye kɛ ɔmaa bɛboa ye na bɛanyia debie bɛali.’ ”

english_verse: and Samuel was sleeping on a mat near the sacred chest in the Lord's house. They had not been asleep very long
translation_verse: ɛnee bɛtɛnuanle Nyamenle kɛnlaneɛ ne na Samoɛle la Ɛdɛnkɛma Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu, ɛleka mɔɔ Nyamenle Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne gyi la.

english_verse: when the Lord called out Samuel's name. “Here I am!” Samuel answered.
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma vɛlɛle Samoɛle kɛ, “Samoɛle, Samoɛle!” Samoɛle liele zolɛ, “Yɛmenle! Mewɔ ɛke!”

english_verse: Then he ran to Eli and said, “Here I am. What do you want?” “I didn't call you,” Eli answered. “Go back to bed.” Samuel went back.
translation_verse: Ɔnriandile ɔhɔle Yilae anwo ɛkɛ ne na ɔhanle kɛ, “Ɛvɛlɛle me, mera.” Na Yilae zele ye kɛ, “Metɛfɛlɛle wɔ na kɔla.” Yemɔti Samoɛle ziale hɔlale.

english_verse: When the Lord called out his name for the third time, Samuel went to Eli again and said, “Here I am. What do you want?” Eli finally realized that it was the Lord who was speaking to Samuel.
translation_verse: Ye fane nsa ne azo Ɛdɛnkɛma vɛlɛle Samoɛle. Eza ɔdwazole ɔhɔle Yilae anwo ɛkɛ ne na ɔhanle kɛ, “Ɛlɛfɛlɛ me, mera.” Na Yilae nwunle kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛɛ ɛlɛfɛlɛ kakula ne a.

english_verse: So he said, “Go back and lie down! If someone speaks to you again, answer, ‘I'm listening, Lord. What do you want me to do?’ ” Once again Samuel went back and lay down.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Yilae zele Samoɛle kɛ, “Kɔ kɔla na saa ɔfɛlɛ wɔ a ka kɛ, ‘Ɛdɛnkɛma, tendɛ, wɔ sonvolɛ ɛlɛtie.’ ” Yemɔti Samoɛle ziale hɔlale.

english_verse: The Lord then stood beside Samuel and called out as he had done before, “Samuel! Samuel!” “I'm listening,” Samuel answered. “What do you want me to do?”
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma ragyinlanle ɛkɛ ne na kɛmɔ ɔyɛ ye dɛba ne ala la, ɔvɛlɛle Samoɛle bieko, “Samoɛle, Samoɛle!” Samoɛle liele zolɛ, “Tendɛ, wɔ sonvolɛ ɛlɛtie.”

english_verse: The Lord said: Samuel, I am going to do something in Israel that will shock everyone who hears about it!
translation_verse: Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Samoɛle kɛ, “Mebahile Yizilayɛma debie na awie biala mɔɔ kɛde la anwo bawozo ye.

english_verse: I will punish Eli and his family, just as I promised.
translation_verse: Kenle zɔhane, edwɛkɛ biala mɔɔ meha ye wɔ Yilae abusua ne anwo la bayɛ zɔhane, ɔvi ɔ bo yeahɔ ye awieleɛ.

english_verse: He knew that his sons refused to respect me, and he let them get away with it, even though I said I would punish his family forever.
translation_verse: Melumua meha mehile ye kɛ mebadea ye abusua ne ndeanlɛ mɔɔ ɛnlɛ awieleɛ la, ɔboalekɛ ɔ mra ne mɔ dendɛle ɛtane tiale Nyamenle mɔɔ ɔdaye Yilae ɔze a, noko yeandua bɛ.

english_verse: I warned Eli that sacrifices or offerings could never make things right! His family has done too many disgusting things.
translation_verse: Zɔhane ati meka meka kɛ, Yilae abusua ne, azubɔlɛ anzɛɛ azubɔdeɛ biala ɛnrɛmaa ndeanlɛ mɔɔ la bɛ nwo zo la ɛnrɛzi aze ɛlɛ.”

english_verse: The next morning, Samuel got up and opened the doors to the Lord's house. He was afraid to tell Eli what the Lord had said.
translation_verse: Samoɛle lale; ɔdwazole nwonlomɔ ne la ɔdukuedukuele Ɛdɛnkɛma Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne nlenkɛ ne mɔ. Ɛnee Samoɛle sulo kɛ ɔkɛha mɔɔ ɔnwunle ye la ɔkɛhile Yilae.

english_verse: But Eli told him, “Samuel, my boy, come here!” “Yes, sir!” Samuel answered.
translation_verse: Yilae vɛlɛle Samoɛle kɛ, “Me ra Samoɛle!” Samoɛle liele zolɛ, “Mewɔ ɛke.”

english_verse: Eli said, “What did God say to you? Tell me everything. I'll ask God to punish you terribly if you don't tell me every word he said!”
translation_verse: Yilae bizale ye kɛ, “Duzu edwɛkɛ a Ɛdɛnkɛma hanle hilele wɔ a? Mmafa ɛfea me. Debie biala mɔɔ wɔde la saa ɛfa ɛfea me a Nyamenle badua wɔ kakɛ yeagua wɔ bie zolɛ”

english_verse: Samuel told Eli everything. Then Eli said, “He is the Lord, and he will do what's right.” The Lord Helps Samuel
translation_verse: Yemɔti Samoɛle anva debie biala anvea ye; ɔhanle debie biala mɔɔ ɔnwunle ye nee mɔɔ ɔdele la ɔhilele ye. Na Yilae zele ye kɛ, “Ɔdaye a ɔle Ɛdɛnkɛma a; ɔyɛ debie biala mɔɔ ɔdaye ɔnea a ɔle kpalɛ la.”

english_verse: As Samuel grew up, the Lord helped him and made everything Samuel said come true.
translation_verse: Samoɛle dule zolɛ; Ɛdɛnkɛma nee ye luale na ɔmanle edwɛkɛ biala mɔɔ Samoɛle hanle la yɛle nɔhalɛ.

english_verse: From the town of Dan in the north to the town of Beersheba in the south, everyone in the country knew that Samuel was truly the Lord's prophet.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti, ɔvi maanle ne ati mɔɔ kɔdwu ɔ bo la nwunle kɛ amgba Samoɛle le Ɛdɛnkɛma kpɔmanvolɛ.

english_verse: Then Samuel would speak to the whole nation of Israel. The Philistines Capture the Sacred Chest One day the Israelites went out to fight the Philistines. They set up camp near Ebenezer, and the Philistines camped at Aphek.
translation_verse: Mekɛ ne anu, Filisitiama boɔboale bɛ ɛlɔnema anloa kɛ bɛ nee Yizilayɛma baho. Yemɔti Yizilayɛma noko dule bɛ bo kɛ bɛ nee bɛ kaho. Yizilayɛma yɛle azokoɛleɛ wɔ Ɛbɛnizɛ yɛɛ Filisitiama noko yɛle bɛ azokoɛleɛ wɔ Efɛke.

english_verse: The Philistines made a fierce attack. They defeated the Israelites and killed about
translation_verse: Filisitiama tetale Yizilayɛma na bɛhonle ɛsesebɛ bɛlile Yizilayɛma anwo zo konim; bɛhunle Yizilayɛma apenle nna wɔ konle ne anu.

english_verse: The army sent some soldiers to bring back the sacred chest from Shiloh, because the Lord All-Powerful has his throne on the winged creatures on top of the chest. As Eli's two sons, Hophni and Phinehas,
translation_verse: Yemɔti bɛzoanle menli bɛmanle bɛhɔle Hyaelo bɛhɔvale Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne mɔɔ Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma de ye ebia nu wɔ tease abɔdeɛ ne mɔ avinli anwuma la rale. Yilae amra mrenya nwiɔ ne, Hɔfenae nee Fenɛhaze boka nwolɛ a bɛrale a.

english_verse: The Israelite army returned to their camp, and the leaders said, “Why did the Lord let us lose to the Philistines today? Let's get the sacred chest where the Lord's agreement with Israel is kept. Then the Lord will help us and rescue us from our enemies.”
translation_verse: Yizilayɛ ɛlɔnema mɔɔ hale la ziale rale bɛ azokoɛleɛ ne la, bɛ mgbanyima ne bizale kɛ, “Duzu ati a ɛnɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛmaa Filisitiama ɛli yɛ nwo zo konim a? Bɛmaa yɛhɔ Hyaelo yɛhɔva Ɛdɛnkɛma Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne yɛrɛla ɛke, amaa yearadɛnla yɛ avinli na yealie yɛ yeavi yɛ kpɔvolɛma tumi ne abo.”

english_verse: brought the chest into camp, the army cheered so loudly that the ground shook.
translation_verse: Mekɛ mɔɔ bɛ nee Ɛdɛnkɛma Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne dwule azokoɛleɛ ɛkɛ ne la, Yizilayɛma ne wudole kpole bie manle azɛlɛ kpusule.

english_verse: The Philistines heard the noise and said, “What are those Hebrews shouting about?” When the Philistines learned that the sacred chest had been brought into the camp,
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Filisitiama dele ɛwudolɛ kpole ne la, bɛzele kɛ, “Na ɛwudolɛ kpole ɛhye mɔɔ vi Hibuluma azokoɛleɛ ne ba la abo a le duzu?” Na bɛdele kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne ɛdwu azokoɛleɛ ɛkɛ ne.

english_verse: they were scared to death and said: The gods have come into their camp. Now we're in real trouble! Nothing like this has ever happened to us before.
translation_verse: Ɛzulolɛ kpole hanle bɛ; na bɛzele kɛ, “Nyamenle bie ɛra bɛ azokoɛleɛ ɛkɛ. Yɛwie bɔkɔɔ. Debie zɛhae bie ɛtɛsile yɛ nwo zo ɛlɛ.

english_verse: We're in big trouble! Who can save us from these powerful gods? They're the same gods who made all those horrible things happen to the Egyptians in the desert.
translation_verse: Yɛwie! Nwane a kɛhola kɛlie yɛ kɛvi nyamenle anwo ɛzulolɛ ɛhye mɔ asa anu a? Bɛmɛ a bɛhunle Yigyibitima bɔkɔɔ wɔ fienemgbole ne anu la.

english_verse: Philistines, be brave and fight hard! If you don't, those Hebrews will rule us, just as we've been ruling them. Fight and don't be afraid.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Filisitiama, bɛzi ahonle. Bɛho kɛ mrenya na anrɛɛ yɛkɛyɛ ahanra yɛkɛmaa Hibuluma kɛ mɔɔ ɛnee bɛle bɛmaa yɛ la. Yemɔti bɛho bɛhile kɛ bɛle mrenya.”

english_verse: Hophni and Phinehas were killed, and the sacred chest was captured. Eli Dies
translation_verse: Bɛvale Nyamenle Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne donvula na bɛhunle Yilae amra mrenya nwiɔ ne. Yilae ewule ne

english_verse: That same day a soldier from the tribe of Benjamin ran from the battlefront to Shiloh. He had torn his clothes and put dirt on his head to show his sorrow.
translation_verse: Nrenya bie mɔɔ vi Bɛngyaman abusua ekpunli ne anu la vi ɛlɔne ne anloa nriandile hɔdwule Hyaelo kenle ko ne. Nyane mɔɔ ɛnee ɔlɛdi la manle ɔsuosuanle tɛladeɛ mɔɔ ɔwula la anu na ɔvale ndɛtɛlɛ ɔyɛle ɔ ti zo.

english_verse: He went into town and told the news about the battle, and everyone started crying. Eli was afraid that something might happen to the sacred chest. So he was sitting on his chair beside the road, just waiting.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ nrenya ne dwule suakpole ne azo la ɛnee Yilae de ebia nu wɔ adenle ne foa ko na ɔ nye gyi adenle zo, ɔluakɛ ɛnee ye adwenle kɔsɔɔti gyi Nyamenle Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne azo. Mɔɔ nrenya ne bɔle ye amaneɛ ne wiele la, ɛzulolɛ kpole hanle ezuavolɛ ne na bɛdeɛdeanle nuhua.

english_verse: “Israel ran away from the Philistines,” the soldier answered. “Many of our people were killed, including your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas. But worst of all, the sacred chest was captured.”
