translation_verse: Nrenya ne buale ye kɛ, “Yizilayɛma ɛgua ɛbɔ nu wɔ Filisitiama anyunlu, konle ne sinli nyunlu yɛle ɛzulolɛ; ɛ mra nwiɔ ne, Hɔfenae nee Fenɛhaze ɛdɔ amolɛ nu, bɛhu yɛ ɛlɔnema ne bɔkɔɔ, yɛɛ bɛva Nyamenle Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne donvula.”

english_verse: Eli was still sitting on a chair beside the wall of the town gate. And when the man said that the Philistines had taken the sacred chest, Eli fell backwards. He was a very heavy old man, and the fall broke his neck and killed him. He had been a leader of Israel for
translation_verse: Yilae dele amaneɛ ne mɔɔ fane Nyamenle Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne anwo la, ɔvi ebia ne mɔɔ ɔde nu la anu ɔdɔle aze alɛnranyunlu wɔ anlenkɛ kpole ne foa ko; ɔ kɔme bule na ɔwule. Ɔluakɛ ɛnee yeyɛ ɛrelera na ɔ nwo ɛyɛ ɛnlomboɛ. Yilae ziele Yizilayɛma ɛvolɛ abulanla. Fenɛhaze aye kunlanvolɛ ne ewule

english_verse: The wife of Phinehas was about to give birth. And soon after she heard that the sacred chest had been captured and that her husband and his father had died, her baby came. The birth was very hard,
translation_verse: Yilae ara Fenɛhaze aye ne ɛnee ɛva ɛkolɛ na ɔka ekyii ye awolɛ mekɛ dwu. Mɔɔ ɔdele kɛ bɛva Nyamenle Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne donvula na ɔ hu ɔ ze Yilae nee ɔ hu Fenɛhaze ɛwu la, ɔwole mgbemgbene nu.

english_verse: and she was dying. But the women taking care of her said, “Don't be afraid—it's a boy!” She didn't pay any attention to them.
translation_verse: Mekɛ mɔɔ ɔkpondɛ yeaha bɛ sa nu la, mraalɛ mɔɔ ɛlɛdie ye awolɛ la zele ye kɛ, “To wɔ ɛbolɛ azule nu na wɔwo ralɛ nrenya.” Na yeangyea ɔ nye bɔbɔ yɛɛ yeambua.

english_verse: The Philistines took the sacred chest from near Ebenezer to the town of Ashdod.
translation_verse: Mekɛ mɔɔ Filisitiama vale Nyamenle Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne la, bɛ nee ye vi Ɛbɛnizɛ hɔle Ahyedɔdo.

english_verse: They brought it into the temple of their god Dagon and put it next to the statue of Dagon, which they worshiped.
translation_verse: Bɛvale bɛhɔwulale bɛ bozonle Deegɔn ne amonle sua ne anu na bɛziele ye Deegɔn amonle ne anwo ɛkɛ.

english_verse: When the people of Ashdod got up early the next morning, they found the statue lying facedown on the floor in front of the sacred chest. They put the statue back where it belonged.
translation_verse: Ye alehyenlɛ nu nwonlomɔ mangyee ne mɔɔ Ahyedɔdoma dwazole la, bɛnwunle kɛ Deegɔn ananze ne anye ɛbutu aze wɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne anyunlu. Na bɛdenrɛle ye bɛziele ɔ bo zo ne bieko.

english_verse: But early the next morning, it had fallen over again and was lying facedown on the floor in front of the chest. The body of the statue was still in one piece, but its head and both hands had broken off and were lying on the stone floor in the doorway.
translation_verse: Aleɛ hyenle bieko la, nwonlomɔ mangyee ne mɔɔ bɛdwazole la ɛnee Deegɔn anye ɛbutu aze wɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne anyunlu na ɔ ti nee ɔ sa nwiɔ ne ɛbubu ɛgua anlenkɛ ne anloa na yeha ye kungunluminzi ne ala.

english_verse: This is why the priests and everyone else step over that part of the doorway when they enter the temple of Dagon in Ashdod.
translation_verse: Ɛhye ati ɛnɛ nee ɛnɛ ala Deegɔn ahɔmenle nee bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛsonle Deegɔn la kɔ ye amonle sua ne anu wɔ Ahyedɔdo a bɛntia ɛleka mɔɔ ɔdɔle la.

english_verse: The Lord caused a lot of trouble for the people of Ashdod and their neighbors. He made sores break out all over their bodies, and everyone was in a panic.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma duale Ahyedɔdoma kakɛ na ɔhanle bɛ ɛzulolɛ kpole. Ɔvale ewule mutulemutule ɔduale Ahyedɔdoma nee maanlema mɔɔ zua bɛ la kakɛ.

english_verse: Finally, they said, “The God of Israel did this. He is the one who caused all this trouble for us and our god Dagon. We've got to get rid of this chest.”
translation_verse: Ahyedɔdoma nwunle kɛ ninyɛne ɛlɛsi ado ahɔ la, bɛzele kɛ, “Ɔnle kɛ Nyamenle Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne boa yɛ nwo ɛke bieko. Ye tumi ne bo yɛ nee yɛ bozonle Deegɔn bɔbɔ anwo zo.”

english_verse: The people of Ashdod invited all the Philistine rulers to come to Ashdod, and they asked them, “What can we do with the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel?” “Send it to Gath,” the rulers answered. But after they took it there,
translation_verse: Yemɔti bɛzoanle bɛmanle bɛhɔvale Filisitia arelemgbunli ne mɔ na bɛzele bɛ kɛ, “Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne kɛ bɛyɛ ye la bɛyɛ ye. Ɔboa yɛ nwo ɛke bieko a ɔnrɛyɛ boɛ.” Bɛbuale kɛ, “Bɛye ye ɛke bɛhɔ Gate.” Yemɔti bɛvale Ɛlɛka ne bɛhɔle suakpole Gate azo.

english_verse: the Lord made sores break out on everyone in town. The people of Gath were frightened,
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma duale suakpole ne azo amra kakɛ. Ɔhanle bɛ ɛzulolɛ, ɔmanle mutulemutule zanenle suakpole ne azo amra, ngakula nee mgbanyinli kɔsɔɔti.

english_verse: so they sent the sacred chest to Ekron. But before they could take it through the town gates, the people of Ekron started screaming, “They've brought the sacred chest that belongs to the God of Israel! It will kill us and our families too!” The Philistines Send Back the Sacred Chest
translation_verse: Yemɔti bɛyele Nyamenle Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne ɛkɛ bɛhɔle Ɛkelɔn. Ɛkelɔnoma nwunle Nyamenle Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne la, bɛzunle bɛdeɛdeanle nu bɛzele kɛ, “Bɛva Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne bɛra kɛ bɛbahu yɛ kɔsɔɔti.”

english_verse: The people of Ekron called for another meeting of the Philistine rulers and told them, “Send this chest back where it belongs. Then it won't kill us.” Everyone was in a panic, because God was causing a lot of people to die,
translation_verse: Yemɔti bɛzoanle bɛmanle bɛhɔvale Filisitia arelemgbunli ne mɔ na bɛzele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛye Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne ɛke; bɛva bɛhɔzie ɔ bo zo dɛba ne wɔ Yizilayɛ, amaa yeangu yɛ nee yɛ mbusuafoɔ.” Ahunlundetelɛ hanle suakpole ne azo amra kɔsɔɔti, ɔboalekɛ ɛnee Nyamenle ɛmaa bɛ nwo ɛhyele bɛ kpalɛ.

english_verse: and those who had survived were suffering from the sores. They all cried to their gods for help.
translation_verse: Bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛanwu la nyianle mutulemutule, na menli ne zunle manle ɔyɛle alɔbɔlɛ na bɛvɛlɛle bɛ awozonle ne mɔ kɛ bɛralie bɛ.

english_verse: After the sacred chest had been in Philistia for seven months,
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne lile siane nsuu wɔ Filisitia maanle nu.

english_verse: the Philistines called in their priests and fortunetellers, and asked, “What should we do with this sacred chest? Tell us how to send it back where it belongs!”
translation_verse: Filisitiama vɛlɛvɛlɛle bɛ ahɔmenle nee menli mɔɔ bɔ menli munzule la na bɛbizale bɛ kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne kɛ yɛyɛ ye ɛ? Bɛha deɛ holɛ ko mɔɔ saa yɛfa yɛahɔzie ɔ bo zo dɛba ne a yɛva yɛboka nwolɛ la bɛhile yɛ.”

english_verse: “Don't send it back without a gift,” the priests and fortunetellers answered. “Send along something to Israel's God to make up for taking the chest in the first place. Then you will be healed, and you will find out why the Lord was causing you so much trouble.”
translation_verse: Bɛzele kɛ, “Saa bɛfa Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne bɛahɔzie ɔ bo zo ne a ɛnee bɛmmafa ye mgbane bɛkɔ. Wɔ adenle biala anu, ɔwɔ kɛ bɛfa mgbɔdalɛ azubɔdeɛ bɛboka nwolɛ, amaa bɛanyia bɛ ti na bɛanwu debie mɔɔ yemɔti sumunli kɛ de la yedua bɛ kakɛ kpole ɛhye la.”

english_verse: So make five gold models of the sores and five gold models of the rats that are wiping out your crops. If you honor the God of Israel with this gift, maybe he will stop causing trouble for you and your gods and your crops.
translation_verse: Yemɔti bɛyɛ mutulemutule ne nee ahila ne mɔ mɔɔ zɛkyele bɛ maanle ne la ananze bɛwula Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne anyunlunyia, na wɔannea a ɔkɛgyakyi bɛ nee bɛ awozonle ne mɔ nee bɛ maanle ne kakɛdualɛ.

english_verse: Don't be like the Egyptians and their king. They were stubborn, but when Israel's God was finished with them, they had to let Israel go.
translation_verse: Duzu ati a bɛyɛ anzosesebɛ, kɛmɔ Yigyibiti belemgbunli nee Yigyibitima yɛle la ɛ? Bɛhakye kɛ Nyamenle zile dole bɛ agyiba na nzinlii ɔyɛle bɛ koasea ɔmanle Yizilayɛma vile Yigyibiti la.

english_verse: Get a new cart and two cows that have young calves and that have never pulled a cart. Hitch the cows to the cart, but take the calves back to their barn.
translation_verse: Yemɔti bɛbobɔ ehwili ko na bɛziezie nlankɛ mbelɛ nwiɔ mɔɔ bɛtɛfale bɛtɛyɛle gyima ɛlɛ la; bɛva ehwili ne bɛhenda bɛ na bɛha bɛ mra ne mɔ bɛwula tunli nu.

english_verse: Then put the chest on the cart. Put the gold rats and sores into a bag and put it on the cart next to the chest. Then send it on its way.
translation_verse: Akee bɛva Ɛdɛnkɛma Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne bɛzie ehwili ne azo, na bɛva ɛlɛka ne mɔɔ bɛgua ezukoa nvutuke mgbɔdalɛ azubɔdeɛ ne mɔ nu la bɛzie ye foa ko; bɛha nlankɛ ne mɔ bɛmaa bɛ ngome bɛva ehwili ne bɛdɔ adenle zo.

english_verse: Watch to see if the chest goes on up the road to the Israelite town of Beth-Shemesh. If it goes back to its own country, you will know that it was the Lord who made us suffer so badly. But if the chest doesn't go back to its own country, then the Lord had nothing to do with the disease that hit us—it was simply bad luck.
translation_verse: Na akee bɛnlea saa ɔsia ɔkɔ Bɛte Hyimɛhye sua zo a ɛnee Yizilayɛ Nyamenle yɛɛ ɛmaa ewule nzane ne ɛdɔ yɛ nwo a. Saa yeangɔ ɛkɛ ne a ɛnee ɔkile kɛ nzia nee nzia yɛɛ ɛyia nu a.”

english_verse: The Philistines followed their advice. They hitched up the two cows to the cart, but they kept their calves in a barn.
translation_verse: Menli ne yɛle, kɛmɔ bɛhanle bɛhilele bɛ ala la. Bɛvale ehwili ne bɛhendanle nlankɛ mbelɛ nwiɔ ne na bɛhanle bɛ mra ne mɔ bɛwulale tunli nu.

english_verse: Then they put the chest on the cart, along with the bag that had the gold rats and sores in it.
translation_verse: Bɛvale Ɛdɛnkɛma Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne bɛziele ehwili ne azo, bɛvale ɛlɛka ne mɔɔ mutulemutule nee kila ananze ne mɔ wɔ nu la noko bɛziele zolɛ.

english_verse: The cows went straight up the road toward Beth-Shemesh, mooing as they went. The Philistine rulers followed them until they got close to Beth-Shemesh.
translation_verse: Nlankɛ ne mɔ bɔle bɛ ti Bɛte Hyimɛhye adenle zo, bɛammakyi ɛleka biala. Bɛkɔ la ɛnee bɛ ɛzunlɛ ne la zolɛ. Filisitia arelemgbunli ne doale bɛ toonwo bɛdwule Bɛte Hyimɛhye ɛweɛne zo.

english_verse: The people of Beth-Shemesh were harvesting their wheat in the valley. When they looked up and saw the chest, they were so happy that they stopped working and started celebrating.
translation_verse: Mekɛ ne anu ɛnee Bɛte Hyimɛhyema ɛlɛte hwiiti wɔ bɔnza bie anu. Arɛlevilɛ nu bɛkpogyale bɛ ti zo la bɛnwunle Ɛdɛnkɛma Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne na bɛlile fɛlɛko.

english_verse: When the five rulers of the Philistines saw what had happened, they went back to Ekron that same day.
translation_verse: Filisitia arelemgbunli nnu ne nwunle ɛhye la, bɛziale bɛhɔle Ɛkelɔn kenle ko ne ala.

english_verse: That is how the Philistines sent gifts to the Lord to make up for taking the sacred chest. They sent five gold sores, one each for their towns of Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron.
translation_verse: Filisitiama vale ezukoa nvutuke mutulemutule ananze ne yɛle azubɔdeɛ yɛle bɛ ɛtane ne mɔ anwo mgbɔdalɛ manle Ɛdɛnkɛma: Ahyedɔdo ɛdeɛ ko, Gaza ɛdeɛ ko, Ahyekɛlɔn ɛdeɛ ko, Gate ɛdeɛ ko, yɛɛ Ɛkelɔn noko ɛdeɛ ko.

english_verse: They also sent one gold rat for each walled town and for every village that the five Philistine rulers controlled. The huge stone where the Levites set the chest is still there in Joshua's field as a reminder of what happened. The Sacred Chest Is Sent to Kiriath-Jearim
translation_verse: Zɔhane ala yɛɛ bɛyɛle ezukoa nvutuke kila ananze nnu ne mɔ a; azuamgbole nnu ne mɔɔ arelemgbunli nnu ne dede zolɛ mɔɔ bɛlie nwolɛ bane nee mɔɔ bɛtɛdiele nwolɛ bane la ko biala ɛdeɛ ko. Bodane ne mɔɔ bɛziele Ɛdɛnkɛma Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne zolɛ la, ɛnɛ nee ɛnɛ ala tɛbɔ Dwɔhyua mɔɔ vi Bɛte Hyimɛhye la ɛya nu di mɔɔ zile la anwo daselɛ.

english_verse: and they started saying, “No other God is like the Lord! Who can go near him and stay alive? We'll have to send the chest away from here. But where can we send it?”
translation_verse: Yemɔti Bɛte Hyimɛhyema hanle kɛ, “Nwane a kɛhola Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle Nwuanzanwuanza ɛhye anyunlu gyinla a? Yɛɛ ɔvi yɛ ɛke a ɛnee nwane ɛkɛ ne yɛɛ ɔkɔ a?”

english_verse: They sent messengers to tell the people of Kiriath-Jearim, “The Philistines have sent back the sacred chest. Why don't you take it and keep it there with you?”
translation_verse: Yemɔti bɛzoanle menli wɔ Keleate Gyialem bɛhɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Filisitiama ɛziane Ɛdɛnkɛma Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne ɛra. Bɛrɛla bɛrava bɛhɔ.”

english_verse: The people of Kiriath-Jearim got the chest and took it to Abinadab's house, which was on a hill in their town. They chose his son Eleazar to take care of it,
translation_verse: Yemɔti Keleate Gyialemma ravale Ɛdɛnkɛma Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne na bɛ nee ye hɔle Abenadabe mɔɔ de boka ne azo la sua nu. Bɛdule ɔ ra Ɛlieza bɛziele ɛkɛ bɛmanle Ɛdɛnkɛma na bɛzele ye kɛ ɔnlea zolɛ. Samoɛle sie Yizilayɛ

english_verse: One day, Samuel told all the people of Israel, “If you really want to turn back to the Lord, then prove it. Get rid of your foreign idols, including the ones of the goddess Astarte. Turn to the Lord with all your heart and worship only him. Then he will rescue you from the Philistines.”
translation_verse: Samoɛle zele Yizilayɛma kɛ, “Saa bɛfa bɛ ahonle kɔsɔɔti bɛazia bɛara Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛkɛ ne a ɛnee bɛkpo bɛ maanle gyɛne nu nyamenle ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti nee bɛ bozonle raalɛ Asetate ananze ne ɛzonlenlɛ. Bɛdu bɛ nwo kɔsɔɔti bɛmaa Ɛdɛnkɛma na bɛzonle ɔ ngomekye na ɔkɛlie bɛ ɔkɛvi Filisitiama asa anu.”

english_verse: The people got rid of their idols of Baal and Astarte and began worshiping only the Lord.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Yizilayɛma vuandinle Beeyale ne mɔ nee Asetate ananze ne mɔ guale na bɛzonlenle Ɛdɛnkɛma angomekye.

english_verse: Then Samuel said, “Tell everyone in Israel to meet together at Mizpah, and I will pray to the Lord for you.”
translation_verse: Akee Samoɛle zele Yizilayɛma kɛ, “Bɛ kɔsɔɔti bɛhɔyia Mezepa na mebazɛlɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma meamaa bɛ.”

english_verse: When the Philistine rulers found out about the meeting at Mizpah, they sent an army there to attack the people of Israel. The Israelites were afraid when they heard that the Philistines were coming.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Filisitiama dele kɛ Yizilayɛma ɛyia nu wɔ Mezepa la, Filisitia arelemgbunli ne mɔ vale ɛlɔnema kɛ bɛkadoa bɛ bɛ nee bɛ aho. Yizilayɛma dele nwolɛ bie na ɛzulolɛ hanle bɛ.

english_verse: “Don't stop praying!” they told Samuel. “Ask the Lord our God to rescue us.”
translation_verse: Bɛzele Samoɛle kɛ, “Kɔ zolɛ sɛlɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛ Nyamenle ne maa ɔlie yɛ ɔvi Filisitiama asa anu.”

english_verse: Samuel begged the Lord to rescue Israel, then he sacrificed a young lamb to the Lord. Samuel had not even finished offering the sacrifice when the Philistines started to attack. But the Lord answered his prayer and made thunder crash all around them. The Philistines panicked and ran away.
translation_verse: Mekɛ mɔɔ Samoɛle wɔ zolɛ ɔlɛbɔ azu ne la, Filisitiama rale Yizilayɛma anwo zo, na ɛkɛ ne ala Ɛdɛnkɛma kpakyele ɛsɛnlɛmanye guale Filisitiama anwo zo manle bɛ nye zo danle bɛ, na bɛvale sulosulo bɛbɔle asande bɛguale ɛbɔ nu.

english_verse: The men of Israel left Mizpah and went after them as far as the hillside below Beth-Car, killing every enemy soldier they caught.
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma vi Mezepa vindele na bɛbelele bɛzile Filisitiama zo toonwo bɛhɔdwule Bɛtekaa. Bɛhunle awie biala mɔɔ bɛdole ye adenle nu la.

english_verse: The Israelites were even able to recapture their towns and territory between Ekron and Gath. Israel was also at peace with the Amorites. Samuel Is a Leader in Israel
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma liele azuamgbole mɔɔ bɔ ye Ɛkelɔn kɔdwu Gate mɔɔ Filisitiama lile bɛ nwo zo konim vale la amuala. Yemɔti Yizilayɛma asa hanle bɛ maanle ne kɔsɔɔti. Na anzonudwolɛ rale Yizilayɛma nee Keenama avinli.

english_verse: Samuel was a leader in Israel all his life.
translation_verse: Samoɛle ziele Yizilayɛ maanle ne toonwo ɔhɔle ewule nu.

english_verse: Every year he would go around to the towns of Bethel, Gilgal, and Mizpah where he served as judge for the people.
translation_verse: Ɔde aze la ɛvolɛ biala ɔkpɔsa bɛ nwo zo; ɔkɔ Bɛtɛle, Gelegale nee Mezepa na ɔsiezie manzonle manzonle mɔɔ wɔ azuamgbole ɛhye mɔ azo la amuala.

english_verse: Then he would go back to his home in Ramah and do the same thing there. He also had an altar built for the Lord at Ramah.
translation_verse: Ɔwie a akee ɔsia ɔkɔ ye sua zo Releema na ɔkɔtoto ɛkɛ ne noko boɛ. Ɔzile azukponle wɔ Releema ɔmanle Ɛdɛnkɛma.

english_verse: Samuel had two sons. The older one was Joel, and the younger one was Abijah. When Samuel was getting old, he let them be leaders at Beersheba.
translation_verse: Bɛfɛlɛ ɔ ra nrenya kpanyinli ne Dwowɛle yɛɛ bɛfɛlɛ ekyi ne Abaegya; bɛyɛle maanlebuvoma wɔ Biyɛhyiba.

english_verse: But they were not like their father. They were dishonest and accepted bribes to give unfair decisions.
translation_verse: Noko bɛanva bɛ ze agyakɛ. Bɛ nye bolole ezukoa, bɛliele ndoloboa na bɛbule bɛ nye bɛguale pɛlepɛlelilɛ zo.

english_verse: One day the nation's leaders came to Samuel at Ramah
translation_verse: Yizilayɛ mgbanyinli yiale; bɛhɔnwunle Samoɛle wɔ Releema.

english_verse: and said, “You are an old man. You set a good example for your sons, but they haven't followed it. Now we want a king to be our leader, just like all the other nations. Choose one for us!”
translation_verse: Na bɛzele ye kɛ, “Nea, wɔyɛ kpanyinli yɛɛ ɛ mra ne mɔ noko anva ɛ gyakɛ. Yemɔti ye sonla maa ɔli yɛ belemgbunli, kɛmɔ maanle gyɛne gyɛne ne mɔ yɛ ye la.”

english_verse: Samuel was upset to hear the leaders say they wanted a king, so he prayed about it.
translation_verse: Bɛhanle ɛhye la, yeanyɛ Samoɛle fɛ. Yemɔti ɔzɛlɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma,

english_verse: The Lord answered: Samuel, do everything they want you to do. I am really the one they have rejected as their king.
translation_verse: na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Samoɛle kɛ, “Edwɛkɛ biala mɔɔ menli ne kɛha kɛhile wɔ la, tie. Tɛ wɔmɔ yɛɛ bɛkpo wɔ a; mame yɛɛ bɛkpo me kɛ ɛnɛ menle bɛ belemgbunli bieko a.

english_verse: Ever since the day I rescued my people from Egypt, they have turned from me to worship idols. Now they are turning away from you.
translation_verse: Sumunli kɛ menyele bɛ menvile Yigyibiti la, bɛhakyi bɛ nzi bɛzi me na bɛzonle nyamenle ngakyile ngakyile; mɔɔ bɛyɛle bɛmanle me la, zɔhane ala yɛɛ bɛlɛyɛ bɛamaa wɔ a.

english_verse: Do everything they ask, but warn them and tell them how a king will treat them.
translation_verse: Yemɔti, wɔmɔ tie bɛ. Noko bɔ bɛ kɔkɔ ɛsesebɛ, na maa bɛnwu adenle mɔɔ bɛ belemgbunli ne balua nu azie bɛ la.”

english_verse: Samuel told the people who were asking for a king what the Lord had said:
translation_verse: Samoɛle hanle edwɛkɛ biala mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma hanle la hilele menli mɔɔ se bɛkpondɛ belemgbunli la.

english_verse: If you have a king, this is how he will treat you. He will force your sons to join his army. Some of them will ride in his chariots, some will serve in the cavalry, and others will run ahead of his own chariot.
translation_verse: Samoɛle hilele nuhua hilele bɛ kɛ, “Kɛ bɛ belemgbunli ne bazi azie bɛ la ɛne. Ɔbayɛ bɛ mra mrenya ne mɔ ye ɛlɔnema mɔɔ bie mɔ baha ye konle ehwili ne mɔ, bie mɔ baha ye mgbɔnwɔ, na bie mɔ noko anriandi ali ye konle ehwili ne mɔ anyunlu.

english_verse: Your daughters will have to make perfume or do his cooking and baking.
translation_verse: Bɛ mra mraalɛ ne bie mɔ bayɛ sakyeɛ evuanlɛ amaa ye, bie mɔ bado ye aleɛ na bie mɔ ado ye kpanwo.

english_verse: The king will take your best fields, as well as your vineyards, and olive orchards and give them to his own officials.
translation_verse: Ɔbava bɛ ɛya avule, bɛ vanye ɛya avule, yɛɛ bɛ ɔlivi ɛya avule kpalɛ ne mɔ yeamaa ye sonvolɛma.

english_verse: He will also take a tenth of your grain and grapes and give it to his officers and officials.
translation_verse: Ɔbahyɛ awie biala abɛlɛ nee ye vanye ma ne mɔ anu bulu yeadu ɛkpɔ ngoko yeamaa ye suakunlu mgbanyima nee ye sonvolɛma.

english_verse: The king will take your slaves and your best young men and your donkeys and make them do his work.
translation_verse: Ɔbamaa bɛ sonvolɛ mrenya nee mraalɛ kpalɛ ne mɔ, bɛ nlankɛ nee bɛ asoaso kpalɛ ne mɔ ayɛ gyima amaa ye.

english_verse: He will also take a tenth of your sheep and goats. You will become the king's slaves,
translation_verse: Ɔbahyɛ awie biala nyɛmoa ne mɔ anu bulu yeadu ɛkpɔ ko, na bɛdabɛ mumua ne, ɔbayɛ bɛ ye ahanra.

english_verse: and you will finally cry out for the Lord to save you from the king you wanted. But the Lord won't answer your prayers.
translation_verse: Kɛmɔ bɛdabɛ bɛzie bɛ belemgbunli la saa mekɛ zɔhane dwu a bɛbahwi monle, noko Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛnrɛdie bɛ ɛzunlɛ.”

english_verse: The people would not listen to Samuel. “No!” they said. “We want to be like other nations. We want a king to rule us and lead us in battle.”
translation_verse: amaa yeayɛ kɛ maanle maanle mɔɔ ɛha la, na yeazie yɛ, yeali yɛ nyunlu ɔ nee yɛ ahɔ konle.”

english_verse: Samuel listened to them and then told the Lord exactly what they had said.
translation_verse: Samoɛle diele bɛ edwɛkɛ ne amuala na ɔbɔle Ɛdɛnkɛma amaneɛ.

english_verse: “Do what they want,” the Lord answered. “Give them a king.” Samuel told the people to go back to their homes.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Samoɛle kɛ, “Kɛmɔ bɛdabɛ bɛbiza la, yɛ ye zɔhane na ye belemgbunli maa bɛ.” Akee Samoɛle zele Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti kɛ awie biala ɛhɔ ye sua zo.

english_verse: Kish was a wealthy man who belonged to the tribe of Benjamin. His father was Abiel, his grandfather was Zeror, his great-grandfather was Becorath, and his great-great-grandfather was Aphiah.
translation_verse: Nrenya sukoavolɛ bie wɔ ɛkɛ. Bɛfɛlɛ ye Kehye, ɔvi Bɛngyaman abusua ekpunli ne anu. Ɔ ze a le Abayɛle. Abayɛle ɔ ze a le Zilɔ, Zilɔ ɔ ze a le Bɛkɔla, yɛɛ Bɛkɔla ɔ ze a le Afaya.

english_verse: Kish had a son named Saul, who was better looking and more than a head taller than anyone else in all Israel.
translation_verse: Kehye wole ralɛ nrenya na ɔdonle ye Sɔɔlo. Wɔ Yizilayɛ maanle ne anu, nrenya biala anwo ɛnyɛ fɛ nee Sɔɔlo ɛnzɛ. Ɔle nrenya tendenle ɔtɛla awie biala.

english_verse: Kish owned some donkeys, but they had run off. So he told Saul, “Take one of the servants and go look for the donkeys.”
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo ɔ ze Kehye asoaso ne bie mɔ minlinle. Yemɔti Kehye zele Sɔɔlo kɛ, “Fa sonvolɛma ne mɔ ko na ɛ nee ye ɛhɔ bɛhɔkpondɛ asoaso ne mɔ.”

english_verse: Saul and the servant went through the hill country of Ephraim and the territory of Shalishah, but they could not find the donkeys. Then they went through the territories of Shaalim and Benjamin, but still there was no sign of the donkeys.
translation_verse: Bɛhɔluoluale Yifelaem awoka ne mɔ azo nee mbɔnza ne mɔ anu nee Hyalehya maanzinli ne anu, na bɛannwu bɛ. Bɛhɔkpondɛle bɛ wɔ Hyeeyalem azɛlɛ zo, na bɛannwu bɛ. Eza bɛhɔkpondɛle bɛ wɔ Bɛngyaman azɛlɛ zo, na bɛannwu bɛ.

english_verse: Finally they came to the territory where the clan of Zuph lived. “Let's go back home,” Saul told his servant. “If we don't go back soon, my father will stop worrying about the donkeys and start worrying about us!”
translation_verse: Mɔɔ bɛdwule Zɛfe maanle nu la, Sɔɔlo zele ye sonvolɛ ne mɔɔ ɔ nee ye lua la kɛ, “Maa yɛzia yɛhɔ sua nu na anrɛɛ egya akee kɛdwenle yɛ nwo kɛdɛla asoaso ne mɔ.”

english_verse: “Wait!” the servant answered. “There's a man of God who lives in a town near here. He's amazing! Everything he says comes true. Let's talk to him. Maybe he can tell us where to look.”
translation_verse: Na sonvolɛ ne zele ye kɛ, “Nyamenle sonla bie wɔ suakpole ɛhye azo. Awie biala di ye eni, ɔluakɛ edwɛkɛ biala mɔɔ ɔkɛha la yɛ zɔhane. Maa yɛhɔ ɔ nwo ɛkɛ, wɔannea a ɔkɛhola ɔkɛhile yɛ ɛleka mɔɔ yɛkɛnwu asoaso ne mɔ la.”

english_verse: Saul said, “How can we talk to the prophet when I don't have anything to give him? We don't even have any bread left in our sacks. What can we give him?”
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo bizale ye kɛ, “Saa yɛkɔ a, duzu debie yɛɛ yɛbava yɛamaa ye a? Yɛnlɛ aleɛ biala wɔ yɛ bɔlɛ nu, yɛɛ yɛnlɛ debie biala mɔɔ yɛfa yɛamaa ye a.”

english_verse: “I have a small piece of silver,” the servant answered. “We can give him that, and then he will tell us where to look for the donkeys.”
translation_verse: Sonvolɛ ne buale ye kɛ, “Melɛ dwɛtɛ fufule ekyi ko; mebava meamaa ye, na yeahile yɛ ɛleka mɔɔ yɛkɛnwu asoaso ne mɔ la.”

english_verse: As they were going up the hill to the town, they met some young women coming out to get water, and the two men said to them, “We're looking for the man who can see visions. Is he in town?”
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo buale ye kɛ, “Wɔ adwenle ne le kpalɛ, maa yɛhɔ.” Yemɔti bɛhɔle suakpole ne mɔɔ Nyamenle sonla ne wɔ zolɛ la azo. Mɔɔ bɛfo boka ne bɛahɔ sua ne azo la, bɛ nee mbɛlɛra bie mɔɔ ɛlɛkɔ azule la yiale. Bɛbizale mbɛlɛra ne mɔ kɛ, “Sonla ne mɔɔ nwu Nyamenle ɛhulolɛdeɛ la wɔ ɛkɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: They went to the town, and just as they were going through the gate, Samuel was coming out on his way to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Sɔɔlo nee ye sonvolɛ ne hɔle sua ne azo. Mɔɔ bɛfo suakpole ne azo ala la, bɛ nee Samoɛle yiale kɛ ɔlɛkɔ boka ne azo, ɛleka mɔɔ bɛkazonle la.

english_verse: The day before Saul came, the Lord had told Samuel,
translation_verse: Kenle mɔɔ aleɛ kye a Sɔɔlo kɛra la, Ɛdɛnkɛma yele hilele Samoɛle kɛ,

english_verse: “I've seen how my people are suffering, and I've heard their call for help. About this time tomorrow I'll send you a man from the tribe of Benjamin, who will rescue my people from the Philistines. I want you to pour olive oil on his head to show that he will be their leader.”
translation_verse: “Ɛhyema, bekezɛ ala, mebamaa nrenya bie mɔɔ vi Bɛngyaman abusua ekpunli ne anu la ara ɛ nwo ɛke. Kpokpa ye nwole kɛ ɔli belemgbunli ɔzie me menli Yizilayɛma. Ɔbalie bɛ yeavi Filisitiama asa anu. Menwu bɛ amaneɛnwunlɛ ne amuala yɛɛ mede bɛ ɛzunlɛ ne mɔɔ bɛlɛsu bɛabiza moalɛ la.”

english_verse: Samuel looked at Saul, and the Lord told Samuel, “This is the man I told you about. He's the one who will rule Israel.”
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Samoɛle anye bobɔle Sɔɔlo la, Ɛdɛnkɛma zele ye kɛ, “Nrenya ne mɔɔ menganle ye edwɛkɛ la, yemɔ ɛne. Yemɔ yɛɛ ɔbazie me menli Yizilayɛma a.”

english_verse: Saul went over to Samuel in the gateway and said, “A man who can see visions lives here in town. Could you tell me the way to his house?”
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo bikyele Samoɛle wɔ suakpole ne anuhɔlɛ kpole ne anloa na ɔbizale ye kɛ, “Nienwu a sonla ne mɔɔ nwu Nyamenle ɛhulolɛdeɛ la wɔ a?”

english_verse: “I am the one who sees visions!” Samuel answered. “Go on up to the place of worship. You will eat with me today, and in the morning I'll answer your questions.
translation_verse: Samoɛle buale ye kɛ, “Mame a mele sonla ne mɔɔ nwu Nyamenle ɛhulolɛdeɛ la a. Dumua me nyunlu wɔ ɛleka mɔɔ bɛlɛbɔ azu ne la, ɔluakɛ ɛnɛ bɛ nee me bado ɛsalɛ, na aleɛ kye a wɔ edwɛkɛ biala mɔɔ ɛ nee ye rale la mebabua wɔ nwolɛ na meamaa wɔahɔ.

english_verse: Don't worry about your donkeys that ran off three days ago. They've already been found. Everything of value in Israel now belongs to you and your family.”
translation_verse: Wɔ asoaso ne mɔ mɔɔ ɛnɛ kenle nsa minlinle la, mmadwenle nwolɛ na bɛnwu bɛ. Na nwane yɛɛ Yizilayɛma ɛlɛkpondɛ ye ɛsesebɛ a? Ɛdawɔ ɔ, wɔmɔ nee ɛ ze sua nu amra.”

english_verse: “Why are you telling me this?” Saul asked. “I'm from Benjamin, the smallest tribe in Israel, and my clan is the least important in the tribe.” Saul Eats with Samuel and Stays at His House
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo buale kɛ, “Mevi Bɛngyaman abusua ekpunli ne anu. Abusua ɛhye a le Yizilayɛ mbusua ekpunli ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti anu ekyi kpalɛ a, yɛɛ me sua nu amra fɔɔnwo ne noko ɛnlɛ duma fee wɔ Bɛngyaman abusua ekpunli ne anu. Duzu ati a ɛkɛva amaneɛ ɛhye ɛkɛbɔ me ɛ?”

english_verse: Then Samuel told the cook, “I gave you the best piece of meat and told you to set it aside. Bring it here now.” The cook brought the meat over and set it down in front of Saul. “This is for you,” Samuel told him. “Go ahead and eat it. I had this piece saved especially for you, and I invited these guests to eat with you.” After Saul and Samuel had finished eating,
translation_verse: Yemɔti mɔɔ donle aleɛ ne la vale ndwɛlɛ ne mɔ nee ɔ kɔme zo nanenvoka ne mɔ bie raziele Sɔɔlo anyunlu, na Samoɛle zele kɛ, “Nea, mɔɔ bɛvale bɛziele wɔ la ɛne. Di, menvale menziele wɔ, amaa mekɛ ne dwu a ɛ nee menli mɔɔ bɛdole ɛsalɛ bɛvɛlɛle bɛ la ali.” Yemɔti Sɔɔlo nee Samoɛle dole ɛsalɛ kenle ko ne.

english_verse: they went down from the place of worship and back into town. A bed was set up for Saul on the flat roof of Samuel's house,
translation_verse: Mɔɔ bɛvi ɛzonlenlɛ ɛleka ne bɛhɔle sua nu la, bɛzieziele dabelɛ wɔ sua ne ati zo bɛmanle Sɔɔlo,

english_verse: and Saul slept there. About sunrise the next morning, Samuel called up to Saul on the roof, “Time to get up! I'll help you get started on your way.” Saul got up. He and Samuel left together
translation_verse: na ɔlale ɛkɛ ne. Samoɛle kpokpa Sɔɔlo nwole ahile kɛ ɔle belemgbunli Aleɛbahye ne Samoɛle vɛlɛle Sɔɔlo na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Dwazo; maa mengɔgua wɔ adenle.” Sɔɔlo dwazole na ɔ nee Samoɛle vindele gua ne azo.

english_verse: and had almost reached the edge of town when Samuel stopped and said, “Tell your servant go on. Stay here with me for a few minutes, and I'll tell you what God has told me.” Samuel Tells Saul He Will Be King After the servant had gone,
translation_verse: Mɔɔ bɛdwule sua ne kandiba la, Samoɛle zele Sɔɔlo kɛ, “Ka kile wɔ sonvolɛ ne kɛ ɔlumua yɛ nyunlu.” Sonvolɛ ne lumuale na Samoɛle zele Sɔɔlo kɛ, “Kendɛ ekyii maa menga edwɛkɛ mɔɔ Nyamenle ɛha la mengile wɔ.”

english_verse: Samuel took a small jar of olive oil and poured it on Saul's head. Then he kissed Saul and told him: The Lord has chosen you to be the leader and ruler of his people.
translation_verse: Akee Samoɛle vale dwora mɔɔ nwole wɔ nu la, ɔwolale ɔguale Sɔɔlo ati zo, ɔvole ɔ nvoka anwo na ɔzele kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛye wɔ kɛ ɛzie ye menli Yizilayɛma. Ɛbazie bɛ na wɔalie bɛ wɔavi bɛ kpɔvolɛma asa anu. Na ɛhye a le sɛkɛlɛneɛ mɔɔ bahile kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛye wɔ kɛ ɛzie ye menli ne la a.

english_verse: When you leave me today, you'll meet two men near Rachel's tomb at Zelzah in the territory of Benjamin. They'll tell you, “The donkeys you've been looking for have been found. Your father has forgotten about them, and now he's worrying about you! He's wondering how he can find you.”
translation_verse: Saa ɛvi me nwo ɛke ɛnɛ a, ɛ nee mrenya nwiɔ bayia Relahyɛle sɛka ne anwo wɔ Zɛleza mɔɔ wɔ Bɛngyaman maanzinli nu la. Bɛbaze wɔ kɛ asoaso ne mɔ mɔɔ ɛhɔle bɛ ɛkpondɛlɛ la, bɛnwu bɛ, yemɔti ɛ ze ɛndwenle bɛ nwo bieko na wɔmɔ yɛɛ akee ɔlɛdi ɛ nwo nyane a, na ɔbiza ɔ nwo kɛ, ‘Na me ra ne, duzu a menyɛ a?’

english_verse: Go on from there until you reach the big oak tree at Tabor, where you'll meet three men on their way to worship God at Bethel. One of them will be leading three young goats, another will be carrying three round loaves of bread, and the last one will be carrying a clay jar of wine.
translation_verse: Ɛvi ɛkɛ ne a ɛbahɔ toonwo wɔahɔdwu baka bie anwo wɔ Teebɔ. Ɛkɛ ne, ɛ nee mrenya nsa bayia kɛ bɛlɛ bɛ azubɔdeɛ bɛlɛkɔ Bɛtɛle bɛahɔbɔ azu bɛamaa Nyamenle. Ko lɛ mbɔnkye mralɛ nsa, ko lɛ kpanwo ahunguma nsa, yɛɛ ko noko lɛ nwoma kodoku mɔɔ nwanye wɔ nu la.

english_verse: After they greet you, they'll give you two loaves of bread.
translation_verse: Bɛbabiza wɔ ahye na bɛamaa wɔ kpanwo ne nwiɔ, na anrɛɛ die.

english_verse: Next, go to Gibeah, where the Philistines have an army camp. As you're going into the town, you'll meet a group of prophets coming down from the place of worship. They'll be going along prophesying while others are walking in front of them, playing small harps, small drums, and flutes.
translation_verse: Akee ɛbadwu Nyamenle Boka, wɔ Gebɛya, ɛleka mɔɔ Filisitiama azokoɛleɛ ne wɔ la ademgbole ne mɔɔ fa kɔ sua ne azo la anu, ɛbanwu Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛma ekpunli bie mɔɔ vi boka ne azo azukponle ne anwo ɛlɛtolo ara la na bɛlɛka Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ, bɛsi agole na bɛbɔ getaa kpole, akɛya, fulutu, yɛɛ ɛto.

english_verse: The Spirit of the Lord will suddenly take control of you. You'll become a different person and start prophesying right along with them.
translation_verse: Na arɛlevilɛ nu ala, Ɛdɛnkɛma Sunsum ne badwu ɛ nwo zo kpole bie na ɛ nee bɛ aha Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ ne na wɔayɛ sonla ngakyile.

english_verse: After these things happen, do whatever you think is right! God will help you.
translation_verse: Saa sɛkɛlɛneɛ ɛhye mɔ sisi a, debie biala mɔɔ Nyamenle kɛze wɔ kɛ ɛyɛ la, yɛ. Ɔluakɛ Nyamenle nee wɔ a lua a.

english_verse: Then go to Gilgal. I'll come a little later, so wait for me. It may even take a week for me to get there, but when I come, I'll offer sacrifices to please the Lord and to ask for his blessings. I'll also tell you what to do next. Saul Goes Back Home
translation_verse: Ɛbalumua me nyunlu wɔ Gelegale, na mebarayia wɔ ɛkɛ na mearabɔ ɛyelalɛ nee anzonudwolɛ azu. Anrɛɛ kendɛ me ɛkɛ ne kenle nsuu kɔkpula kɛ menwɔrahile wɔ deɛ mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ ɛyɛ la.”

english_verse: As Saul turned around to leave Samuel, God made Saul feel like a different person. That same day, everything happened just as Samuel had said.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Sɔɔlo vile Samoɛle anwo ɛkɛ ne na ɔkɔ la, Nyamenle manle ye ahonle nee ye subane hakyile; edwɛkɛ biala mɔɔ Samoɛle hanle hilele ye la yɛle zɔhane kenle ko ne ala.

english_verse: When Saul arrived at Gibeah, a group of prophets met him. The Spirit of God suddenly took control of him, and right there in the middle of the group he began prophesying.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Sɔɔlo nee ye sonvolɛ ne dwule Gebɛya la, bɛ nee Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛma ekpunli bie yiale. Arɛlevilɛ nu Nyamenle Sunsum ne dwule Sɔɔlo anwo zo kpole bie, na ɔ nee bɛ zile agole na bɛhanle Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ ne.

english_verse: Some people who had known Saul for a long time saw that he was speaking and behaving like a prophet. They said to each other, “What's happened? How can Saul be a prophet?”
translation_verse: Menli mɔɔ ze ye dɛba la nwunle kɛ ɔ nee Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛma ne mɔ ɛlɛka Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ ne la, bɛbizebizale bɛ nwo ngoko kɛ, “Duzu edwɛkɛ a ɛzi Kehye ara ye anwo zo a? Ɛnee Sɔɔlo ɔdaye noko yeyɛ Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: “Why not?” one of them answered. “Saul has as much right to be a prophet as anyone else!” That's why everyone started saying, “How can Saul be a prophet?”
translation_verse: Nrenya ko mɔɔ vi ɛkɛ ne la zele kɛ, “Na Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛma ɛhendeɛ ne mɔ ɛ, bɛnea a ɛnee bɛ ze mɔ a le nwane mɔ?” Yemɔti ɔrayɛle ɛrɛlɛ kɛ, “Na Sɔɔlo ɔdaye noko ɔboka Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛma anwo ɔ?”

english_verse: After Saul stopped prophesying, he went to the place of worship.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Sɔɔlo wiele ye agole ne si, na ɔwiele Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ ne ka la, ɔhɔle azukponle ne anwo wɔ boka ne azo.

english_verse: Later, Saul's uncle asked him, “Where have you been?” Saul answered, “Looking for the donkeys. We couldn't find them, so we went to talk with Samuel.”
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo awuvuanyi ne nwunle Sɔɔlo nee ye sonvolɛ ne; ɔbizale bɛ kɛ, “Nienwu a bɛhɔle a?” Sɔɔlo buale kɛ, “Yɛhɔle asoaso ne mɔ ɛkpondɛlɛ. Mɔɔ yɛkpondɛle bɛ toonwo na yɛannwu bɛ la, yɛhɔle Samoɛle anwo lɔ.”

english_verse: “And what did he tell you?” Saul's uncle asked.
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo awuvuanyi ne bizale ye kɛ, “Mesɛlɛ wɔ, duzu edwɛkɛ a Samoɛle hanle hilele wɔ a?”

english_verse: Saul answered, “He told us the donkeys had been found.” But Saul didn't mention that Samuel had chosen him to be king. The Lord Shows Israel that Saul Will Be King
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo zele ɔ wuvuanyi ne kɛ, “Yɛhɔle la, ɔkpakyele nu wienyi ɔzele yɛ kɛ bɛnwu asoaso ne mɔ.” Na mɔɔ fane ye belemgbunlililɛ ne anwo mɔɔ Samoɛle hanle la, Sɔɔlo ambɔ zolɛ. Bɛzie Sɔɔlo belemgbunli

english_verse: Samuel sent messengers to tell the Israelites to come to Mizpah and meet with the Lord.
translation_verse: Akee Samoɛle vɛlɛle Yizilayɛma amuala manle bɛrale Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛzonlenlɛ ayia wɔ Mezepa;

english_verse: When everyone had arrived, Samuel said: The Lord God of Israel told me to remind you that he had rescued you from the Egyptians and from the other nations that abused you.
translation_verse: ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne se la ɛne, ‘Menyele bɛ menvile Yigyibiti na menliele bɛ menvile Yigyibitima nee maanle maanle mɔɔ sisile bɛ la asa anu.

english_verse: God has rescued you from your troubles and hard times. But you have rejected your God and have asked for a king. Now each tribe and clan must come near the place of worship so the Lord can choose a king.
translation_verse: Mele bɛ Nyamenle mɔɔ die bɛ fi bɛ ngyegyelɛ nee bɛ ngyianlɛ muala anu a. Noko ɛnɛ bɛkpo me na bɛze me kɛ, memaa bɛ belemgbunli.’ Yemɔti bɛ kɔsɔɔti bɛrɛla bɛrayia Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlu ɛke, bɛgua ye mbusua ekpunli ekpunli nee mbusua ekpulike ekpulike, kɛmɔ ko biala dodo de la.”

english_verse: Samuel brought each tribe, one after the other, to the altar, and the Lord chose the Benjamin tribe.
translation_verse: Akee Samoɛle manle mbusua ekpunli ekpunli ne mɔ rale ngoko; bɛguale nzeleba la Ɛdɛnkɛma yele Bɛngyaman abusua ekpunli ne.

english_verse: Next, Samuel brought each clan of Benjamin there, and the Lord chose the Matri clan. Finally, Saul the son of Kish was chosen. But when they looked for him, he was nowhere to be found.
translation_verse: Samoɛle manle Bɛngyaman abusua ekpunli ne anu amra ne rale ye awuke awuke, na nzeleba ne bɔle Meetelae awuke nu amra. Mrenya mɔɔ wɔ Meetelae awuke nu la rale na bɛyele Sɔɔlo mɔɔ ɔ ze a le Kehye la. Bɛkpondɛle Sɔɔlo, na bɛannwu ye,

english_verse: The people prayed, “Our Lord, is Saul here?” “Yes,” the Lord answered, “he is hiding behind the baggage.”
translation_verse: yemɔti bɛbizale Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ, “Awie bieko tɛbɔ ɛkɛ ɔ?” Ɛdɛnkɛma zele kɛ, “Sɔɔlo vea ninyɛne edukue ne anzi nehane.”

english_verse: The people ran and got Saul and brought him into the middle of the crowd. He was more than a head taller than anyone else.
translation_verse: Na bɛnriandile bɛhɔhyele ye bɛrale. Ɔragyinlanle bɛ avinli la ɛnee ɔwale ɔtɛla awie biala mɔɔ wɔ ɛkɛ ne la.

english_verse: “Look closely at the man the Lord has chosen!” Samuel told the crowd. “There is no one like him!” The crowd shouted, “Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Na Samoɛle zele menli ne kɔsɔɔti kɛ, “Sonla ne mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛye ye ɛmaa bɛ la ɛne, bɛnwu ye ɔ? Awie biala ɛnle menli ye avinli mɔɔ nee ye sɛ a.” Na menli ne kɔsɔɔti deanle nuhua kɛ, “Belemgbunli ne ɛnyi ɛhyɛ.”

english_verse: Samuel explained the rights and duties of a king and wrote them all in a book. He put the book in one of the shrines where the Lord was worshiped. Then Samuel sent everyone home.
translation_verse: Akee Samoɛle hanle belemgbunli dibilɛ nee ye gyima hilele menli ne. Ɔhɛlɛle ɛhye mɔ buluku nu, na ɔvale ɔdole ɛleka nwuanzanwuanza wɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlu. Akee Samoɛle manle menli ne kɔsɔɔti hɔle bɛ azua nu.

english_verse: God had encouraged some young men to become followers of Saul, and when he returned to his hometown of Gibeah, they went with him.
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo ɔdaye noko ɔhɔle ye sua zo Gebɛya. Menli mɔɔ anwo yɛ se na Nyamenle asa wɔ bɛ nwo zo la nee ye hɔle.

english_verse: But some worthless fools said, “How can someone like Saul rescue us from our enemies?” They did not want Saul to be their king, and so they didn't bring him any gifts. But Saul kept calm.
translation_verse: Na menli kpamgbanvolɛma bie zele kɛ, “Duzu debie kpaziwɔkɛ bɔbɔ yɛɛ sonla ɛhye kɛhola kɛyɛ kɛmaa yɛ a?” Bɛkpole ye, bɛammaa ye ahyɛlɛdeɛ biala, noko Sɔɔlo andɛne bɛ zo.

english_verse: About this time, King Nahash of Ammon came with his army and surrounded the town of Jabesh in Gilead. The people who lived there told Nahash, “If you will sign a peace treaty with us, you can be our ruler, and we will pay taxes to you.”
translation_verse: Akee Neehahye, Amɔnoma belemgbunli ne vale ɛlɔnema hɔbɛnrale yiale Gyeebɛhye mɔɔ wɔ Geleade maanle nu la. Na Gyeebɛhyema zele Neehahye kɛ, “Ɛ nee yɛ ɛyɛ anzonudwolɛ ngyehyɛlɛ na yɛkɛzonle wɔ.”

english_verse: Nahash answered, “Sure, I'll sign a treaty! But not before I insult Israel by poking out the right eye of every man who lives in Jabesh.”
translation_verse: Neehahye zele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛnwu ye kɛ, mekponle zolɛ me nee bɛ ayɛ ngyehyɛlɛ ne la, ɛnee bɛlie bɛdo nu bɛmaa medu awie biala anye fema ne, amaa yeayɛ anyiemgba yeaha Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti.”

english_verse: The town leaders said, “Give us seven days so we can send messengers everywhere in Israel to ask for help. If no one comes here to save us, we will surrender to you.”
translation_verse: Gyeebɛhye mgbanyima zele ye kɛ, “Maa yɛ kenle nsuu maa yɛzoa menli wɔ Yizilayɛ maanle ye anu amuala. Na saa yɛannyia awie mɔɔ kɛlie yɛ la a, yɛkɛva yɛ nwo yɛkɛmaa wɔ.”

english_verse: Some of the messengers went to Gibeah, Saul's hometown. They told what was happening at Jabesh, and everyone in Gibeah started crying.
translation_verse: Soanvolɛma ne mɔ rale Gebɛya, sua ne mɔɔ Sɔɔlo de zolɛ la azo. Bɛvale amaneɛ ne bɛbɔle ezuavolɛ ne na bɛ muala bɛzunle bɛyele awolɛ.

english_verse: Just then, Saul came in from the fields, walking behind his oxen. “Why is everyone crying?” Saul asked. They told him what the men from Jabesh had said.
translation_verse: Mekɛ ne anu ala ɛnee Sɔɔlo nee ye nlankɛ vi ɛyazonlɛ ɛlɛba sua nu. Na ɔbizale kɛ, “Duzu a ɛlɛgyegye menli ne mɔɔ yemɔti bɛlɛsu a?” Na bɛvale Gyeebɛhye amaneɛ ne bɛbɔle ye.

english_verse: Saul killed two of his oxen, cut them up in pieces, and gave the pieces to the messengers. He told them to show the pieces to everyone in Israel and say, “Saul and Samuel are getting an army together. Come and join them. If you don't, this is what will happen to your oxen!” The Lord made the people of Israel terribly afraid. So all the men came together
translation_verse: Ɔhyele nlankɛ nwiɔ ɔpepɛle bɛ nzokanzoka ɔmanle soanvolɛma vale hɔle Yizilayɛ maanle ne anu amuala na ɔhanle kɛ, “Awie biala mɔɔ andoa Sɔɔlo nee Samoɛle, ɔ nee bɛ angɔ konle ne la, kɛ bɛbapepɛ ye nlankɛ ne mɔ nzokanzoka la ɛne.” Ɛdɛnkɛma anwo ɛzulolɛ dɔle menli ne anwo zo, yemɔti bɛ kɔsɔɔti bɛrale.

english_verse: Saul and his officers sent the messengers back to Jabesh with this promise: “We will rescue you tomorrow afternoon.” The messengers went back to the people at Jabesh and told them that they were going to be rescued. Everyone was encouraged!
translation_verse: Na bɛzele soanvolɛma mɔɔ vi Gyeebɛhye rale la kɛ, “Bɛhɔ bɛhɔze bɛ menli ne kɛ, ‘Ɛhyema, toonwo mɔɔ ɔkadwu sɛnzɛngyinla la ɛnee bɛlie bɛ bɛvi munzule biala anu.’ ” Mɔɔ soanvolɛma ne mɔ vale amaneɛ ɛhye rabɔle Gyeebɛhyema la, ɔyɛle bɛ fɛ somaa.

english_verse: So they told the Ammonites, “We will surrender to you tomorrow, and then you can do whatever you want to.”
translation_verse: Na bɛzele Neehahye kɛ, “Ɛhyema yɛbava yɛ nwo yeamaa wɔ. Debie biala mɔɔ ɛkulo la, fa yɛ yɛ.”

english_verse: The next day, Saul divided his army into three groups and attacked before daylight. They started killing Ammonites and kept it up until afternoon. A few Ammonites managed to escape, but they were scattered far from each other.
translation_verse: Aleɛ hyenle nwonlomɔ mangyee ne la Sɔɔlo hyɛle ye ɛlɔnema ne mɔ anu ekpunli nsa. Bɛhɔholole Amɔnoma anwo zo wɔ bɛ azokoɛleɛ ne; bɛhuhunle bɛ toonwo sɛnzɛngyinla. Bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛvile ɛsalɛ la anye zo danle bɛ, bɛbɔle asande mɔɔ bɛ nuhua nwiɔ bɔbɔ angola ampɛ anli ɛleka ko a.

english_verse: The Israelite soldiers went to Samuel and demanded, “Where are the men who said they didn't want Saul to be king? Bring them to us, and we will put them to death!”
translation_verse: Akee menli ne hanle hilele Samoɛle kɛ, “Nwane mɔ a hanle kɛ, ‘Sɔɔlo ɛnli yɛ nwo zo belemgbunli’ la? Bɛva bɛ bɛrɛla bɛmaa yɛhu bɛ.”

english_verse: “No you won't!” Saul told them. “The Lord rescued Israel today, and no one will be put to death.” Saul Is Accepted as King
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo zele kɛ, “Bɛmmaku awie biala ɛnɛ, ɔluakɛ ɛnɛ a le kenle mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛlie Yizilayɛ ɛzie aze a.”

english_verse: “Come on!” Samuel said. “Let's go to Gilgal and make an agreement that Saul will continue to be our king.”
translation_verse: Na Samoɛle zele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛmaa yɛ kɔsɔɔti yɛhɔ Gelegale yɛhɔzi zolɛ bieko kɛ Sɔɔlo le yɛ belemgbunli.”

english_verse: Everyone went to the place of worship at Gilgal, where they agreed that Saul would be their king. Saul and the people sacrificed animals to ask for the Lord's blessing, and they had a big celebration.
translation_verse: Yemɔti bɛ kɔsɔɔti bɛhɔle Gelegale bɛhɔziele Sɔɔlo belemgbunli wɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlu. Bɛbɔle anzonudwolɛ azu bɛmanle Ɛdɛnkɛma wɔ ɛkɛ ne. Na Sɔɔlo nee menli ne kɔsɔɔti lile fɛlɛko.

english_verse: Samuel told the Israelites: I have given you a king, just as you asked.
translation_verse: Akee Samoɛle zele Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti kɛ, “Mɔɔ bɛzele me kɛ menyɛ la, meyɛ mewie. Memaa bɛ belemgbunli kɛ ɔzie bɛ.

english_verse: You have seen how I have led you ever since I was a young man. I'm already old. My hair is gray, and my own sons are grown. Now you must see how well your king will lead you.
translation_verse: Kɛkala, bɛnyia belemgbunli mɔɔ bali bɛ ti a. Akee meyɛ kpanyinli; me ti zo ɛyɛ nwohyee. Eza bɛnlea, me mra mrenya ne mɔ wɔ bɛ avinli. Sumunli me mgbavolɛ nu, meli bɛ ti toonwo a yeradwu ɛnɛ a.

english_verse: Let me ask this. Have I ever taken anyone's ox or donkey or forced you to give me anything? Have I ever hurt anyone or taken a bribe to give an unfair decision? Answer me so the Lord and his chosen king can hear you. And if I have done any of these things, I will give it all back.
translation_verse: Mame ɛne; saa meyɛ ɛtane metia bɛ a, bɛha ye wɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma nee bɛ belemgbunli ye mɔɔ yeye yemaa bɛ la anyunlu ɛke. Meva awie ɛnlankɛ anzɛɛ meva awie asoaso ɔ? Meli awie ndunlumi ɔ? Mesisi awie anzɛɛ mekpuokpua awie ɔ? Melie awie ndoloboa ɔ? Ninyɛne ɛhye mɔ kɔsɔɔti, saa meyɛ nuhua bie a, bɛha na menwɔzie ɔ bo zo.”

english_verse: “No,” the Israelites answered. “You've never cheated us in any way!”
translation_verse: Menli ne buale kɛ, “Ɛtɛdile yɛ ndunlumi, ɛtɛkpuokpuanle awie biala, ɛtɛsale awie biala ɛtɛdiele ye debie.”

english_verse: Samuel said, “The Lord and his chosen king are witnesses to what you have said.” “That's true,” they replied.
translation_verse: Samoɛle buale kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma nee belemgbunli ne mɔɔ yeye yemaa bɛ la di daselɛ ɛnɛ demua ye kɛ menli fɔlɛ wɔ debie biala anwo.” Bɛbuale kɛ, “Ɛhɛe, Ɛdɛnkɛma di daselɛ.”

english_verse: Then Samuel told them: The Lord brought your ancestors out of Egypt and chose Moses and Aaron to be your leaders.
translation_verse: Na Samoɛle zele menli ne kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma mɔɔ yele Mosisi nee Aalɔn manle bɛvale bɛ mgbanyima bɛvile Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo la di daselɛ.

english_verse: Now the Lord will be your judge. So stand here and listen, while I remind you how often the Lord has saved you and your ancestors from your enemies.
translation_verse: Bɛyɛ koonwu bɛgyinla ɛkɛ, bɛmaa menzɛlɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma memaa bɛ wɔ nyɛleɛ mɔɔ ɔyɛle ɔliele bɛ nee bɛ mgbanyinli la anwo.

english_verse: After Jacob went to Egypt, your ancestors cried out to the Lord for help, and he sent Moses and Aaron. They brought your ancestors out of Egypt and led them here to settle this land.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Gyekɔbo nee ɔ bo zo amra hɔle Yigyibiti na Yigyibitima yɛ bɛ kpɔdekpɔde la, bɛzunle bɛvɛlɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma na ɔzoanle Mosisi nee Aalɔn ɔmanle bɛhɔyele bɛ bɛvile Yigyibiti bɛ nee bɛ rale azɛlɛ ɛhye azo.

english_verse: But your ancestors forgot the Lord, so he let them be defeated by the Philistines, the king of Moab, and Sisera, the commander of Hazor's army.
translation_verse: Noko bɛ rɛle vile Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne, yemɔti ɔyele bɛ ɔmanle Filisitiama nee Mowabe belemgbunli ne nee Sesɛla mɔɔ nea suakpole Heezɔ ɛlɔnema ne anwo zo la, na ɔmanle bɛ nee bɛ mgbanyima ne mɔ honle bɛlile bɛ nwo zo konim.

english_verse: Again your ancestors cried out to the Lord for help. They said, “We have sinned! We stopped worshiping you, our Lord, and started worshiping Baal and Astarte. But now, if you rescue us from our enemies, we will worship you.”
translation_verse: Bɛzunle bɛvɛlɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛzele kɛ, ‘Yɛyɛ ɛtane, ɔboalekɛ yɛkpo Ɛdɛnkɛma na yɛzonle Beeyale nee Asetate ananze ne mɔ. Die yɛ fi yɛ kpɔvolɛma asa anu, na yɛbazonle wɔ.’

english_verse: The Lord sent Gideon, Bedan, Jephthah, and Samuel to rescue you from your enemies, and you didn't have to worry about being attacked.
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma yele Gedeɔn ; nzinlii ɔyele Balake nee Gyɛfeta, yɛɛ akee medame Samoɛle, ɔmanle yɛ nuhua ko biala raliele bɛ vile bɛ kpɔvolɛma asa anu, na bɛdɛnlanle anzonudwolɛ nu.

english_verse: Then you saw that King Nahash of Ammon was going to attack you. And even though the Lord your God is your king, you told me, “This time it's different. We want a king to rule us!”
translation_verse: Na mɔɔ Amɔn Belemgbunli Neehahye vale konle radoale bɛ la, bɛkpole Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ ɔnle bɛ belemgbunli bieko na bɛzele me kɛ, ‘Maa yɛ belemgbunli maa ɔzie yɛ.’

english_verse: If you and your king want to be followers of the Lord, you must worship him and do what he says. Don't be stubborn!
translation_verse: Saa bɛdi Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne eni, bɛsonle ye, bɛtie ɔ ne, bɛdi ye mɛla ne mɔ azo, na bɛ nee bɛ belemgbunli ne toa ɔ bo zo ɛdeɛ a, debie biala bahɔ zolɛ fɔɔnwo amaa bɛ.

english_verse: If you're stubborn and refuse to obey the Lord, he will turn against you and your king.
translation_verse: Na saa bɛandie Ɛdɛnkɛma ane na bɛbulu ye mɛla ne mɔ azo a, ɔ nee bɛ nee bɛ belemgbunli ne bali.

english_verse: Just stand here and watch the Lord show his mighty power.
translation_verse: Yemɔti awie biala ɛzie ɔ nwo diinyi, na ɔnlea nwanwane debie mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma bayɛ la.

english_verse: Isn't this the dry season? I'm going to ask the Lord to send a thunderstorm. When you see it, you will realize how wrong you were to ask for a king.
translation_verse: Bɛ muala bɛze kɛ yɛwɔ wawaa mekɛ nu. Mebazɛlɛ ye meamaa yeamaa maanle nu ahulu na ezule adɔ. Saa ɛhye si a, bɛbanwu kɛ bɛyɛ ɛtane kpole bɛtia Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ bɛdabɛ bɛbizale bɛliele belemgbunli a.”

english_verse: Samuel prayed, and that same day the Lord sent a thunderstorm. Everyone was afraid of the Lord and of Samuel.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Samoɛle zɛlɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma, na kenle ko ne ala maanle nu hulule na ezule dɔle. Na menli ne kɔsɔɔti zulole Ɛdɛnkɛma nee Samoɛle.

english_verse: They told Samuel, “Please, pray to the Lord your God for us! We don't want to die. We have sinned many times in the past, and we were very wrong to ask for a king.”
translation_verse: Na bɛzele Samoɛle kɛ, “Yɛmenle, bodo Ɛdɛnkɛma wɔ Nyamenle ne maa yɛ, amaa yeangu yɛ. Ɔluakɛ yɛnwu ye wienyi kɛ, ɛye ɛtane gyɛne gyɛne mɔɔ yɛyɛ la ɛsie ahane a, mɔɔ yɛyɛ la akee bo zolɛ kɛ yɛdayɛ yɛbizale kɛ ɔmaa yɛ belemgbunli a.”

english_verse: Samuel answered: Even though what you did was wrong, you don't need to be afraid. But you must always follow the Lord and worship him with all your heart.
translation_verse: Na Samoɛle zele menli ne kɛ, “Bɛmmasulo; bɛbɔ munzule bɔbɔ ɛdeɛ, noko bɛmmakpo kɛ bɛnrɛdoa Ɛdɛnkɛma abo zo. Bɛva bɛ ahonle kɔsɔɔti bɛzonle ye.

english_verse: Don't worship idols! They don't have any power, and they can't help you or save you when you're in trouble.
translation_verse: Bɛmmadi adalɛ nyamenle ne mɔ mɔɔ ɛnrɛhola ɛnrɛlie bɛ ngoane la anzi, ɔluakɛ bɛdabɛ mumua ne bɛnlɛ ngoane.

english_verse: But the Lord has chosen you to be his own people. He will always take care of you so that everyone will know how great he is.
translation_verse: Ɔlua ye duma kpole ne ati, Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛnrɛkpo ye menli, ɔboalekɛ ɔdaye ye ɛhulolɛ zo yɛɛ yeva bɛ yeyɛ ye menli a.

english_verse: I would be disobeying the Lord if I stopped praying for you! I will always teach you how to live right.
translation_verse: Na mame, Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛkpa ɛgua kɛ menwɔyɛ ɛtane kɛ menrɛzɛlɛ menrɛmaa bɛ a. Mebahilehile bɛ nɔhalɛ adenle ne nee mɔɔ le kpalɛ kɛ ɔwɔ kɛ bɛyɛ la.

english_verse: You also must obey the Lord—you must worship him with all your heart and remember the great things he has done for you.
translation_verse: Bɛyɛ tieyɛ bɛmaa Ɛdɛnkɛma na bɛva bɛ ahonle muala bɛzonle ye nɔhalɛ nu. Bɛhakye ninyɛne mgbole mɔɔ yeyɛ yemaa bɛ la.

english_verse: But if you and your king do evil, the Lord will wipe you out.
translation_verse: Na saa bɛandie na bɛyɛ ninyɛndane a, ɔbazɛkye bɛ nee bɛ belemgbunli ne bɔkɔɔ.”

english_verse: The messengers then said to the people of Israel, “Saul has destroyed the Philistine army camp at Geba. Now the Philistines really hate Israel, so every town and village must send men to join Saul's army at Gilgal.”
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti dele kɛ Sɔɔlo ɛhu Filisitiama safohyenle kpanyinli ne mɔɔ nea bɛ ɛlɔnema ne anwo zo la, na Filisitiama ɛyɛ Yizilayɛma anwo ɛlɔne, yemɔti bɛ kɔsɔɔti bɛrabokale Sɔɔlo wɔ Gelegale.

english_verse: The Israelite army realized that they were outnumbered and were going to lose the battle. Some of the Israelite men hid in caves or in clumps of bushes, and some ran to places where they could hide among large rocks. Others hid in tombs or in deep dry pits.
translation_verse: Bɛmianle bɛ nwo bɛ nee Yizilayɛma honle kpalɛ. Mɔɔ Yizilayɛma nwunle kɛ konle ne ɛyɛ ɛsesebɛ ɛmaa bɛ la, bie mɔ nriandile hɔveale mbɔne nu, awolɛ nu, adokule nu, bula nu nee sɛka nu.

english_verse: Still others went to Gad and Gilead on the other side of the Jordan River. Saul stayed at Gilgal. His soldiers were shaking with fear,
translation_verse: Bie mɔ pɛle Azule Dwɔdan ne hɔle Gaade nee Geleade maanle ne mɔ anu. Ɛnee Sɔɔlo tɛbɔ Gelegale na ɛzulolɛ ɛha menli mɔɔ nee ye lua la amuala.

english_verse: and they were starting to run off and leave him. Saul waited there seven days, just as Samuel had ordered him to do, but Samuel did not come.
translation_verse: Samoɛle hilele Sɔɔlo kenle nsuu kɛ ɔbara; mɔɔ Sɔɔlo hendɛle Samoɛle toonwo kenle nsuu na yeamba Gelegale la, ye menli ne bɔle ɔ bo kɛ bɛbɔ asande.

english_verse: Finally, Saul commanded, “Bring me some animals, so we can offer sacrifices to please the Lord and ask for his help.” Saul killed one of the animals,
translation_verse: Yemɔti Sɔɔlo zele menli ne kɛ, “Bɛva ɛyelalɛ nee anzonudwolɛ azubɔdeɛ ne mɔ bɛrɛlɛ me.” Na ɔbɔle ɛyelalɛ azu.

english_verse: and just as he placed it on the altar, Samuel arrived. Saul went out to welcome him.
translation_verse: Ɔwiele azu ne bɔ ala la yɛɛ Samoɛle yele ɔ nyunlu a. Sɔɔlo hɔyiale ye na ɔyɛle ye akɔaba.

english_verse: “What have you done?” Samuel asked. Saul answered, “My soldiers were leaving in all directions, and you didn't come when you were supposed to. The Philistines were gathering at Michmash,
translation_verse: Na Samoɛle bizale ye kɛ, “Duzu debie a wɔyɛ la?” Sɔɔlo buale kɛ, “Kɛmɔ kenle ne mɔɔ ɛhilele la dwule na wɔamba, na menli ne kpondɛ abɔ asande, na Filisitiama noko ɛboɔboa bɛ nwo wɔ Mekemahye azokoɛleɛ ne la, yɛɛ menzele kɛ,

english_verse: and I was worried that they would attack me here at Gilgal. I hadn't offered a sacrifice to ask for the Lord's help, so I forced myself to offer a sacrifice on the altar fire.”
translation_verse: ‘Ɔnrɛhyɛ na Filisitiama arateta yɛ wɔ Gelegale ɛke bɛ nee yɛ aho, yɛɛ metɛsɛlɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma moalɛ biala;’ yemɔti menlile me ti anwo membɔle ɛyelalɛ azu ne.”

english_verse: “That was stupid!” Samuel said. “You didn't obey the Lord your God. If you had obeyed him, someone from your family would always have been king of Israel.
translation_verse: Na Samoɛle zele Sɔɔlo kɛ, “Wɔli edwɛkɛ ɛtane. Wɔanli Ɛdɛnkɛma wɔ Nyamenle ne mɛla mɔɔ ɔmanle wɔ la azo; anrɛɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛmaa wɔ nee ɛ bo zo amra kɛzie Yizilayɛ maanle ne dahuu,

english_verse: But no, you disobeyed, and so the Lord won't choose anyone else from your family to be king. In fact, he has already chosen the one he wants to be the next leader of his people.”
translation_verse: na kɛkala, wɔ belemgbunlililɛ ne ɛnrɛhɔ zolɛ bieko. Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛnyia sonla mɔɔ ɔdaye ɔkulo la, yeye ye kɛ ɔzie ye menli ne, ɔboalekɛ wɔdu ɔ nloa wɔdo.”

english_verse: Then Samuel left Gilgal. Part of Saul's army had not deserted him, and he led them to Gibeah in Benjamin to join his other troops. Then he counted them and found that he still had
translation_verse: Samoɛle vile Gelegale hɔle Gebɛya mɔɔ wɔ Bɛngyaman abusua ekpunli ne maanle nu la. Sɔɔlo dianle ye ɛlɔnema mɔɔ nee ye lua la; bɛkɛyɛ ɛya nsia.

english_verse: Saul, Jonathan, and their army set up camp at Geba in Benjamin. Jonathan Attacks the Philistines The Philistine army was camped at Michmash.
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo nee ɔ ra Dwɔnatan nee menli mɔɔ nee ye lua la dɛnlanle Giba mɔɔ wɔ Bɛngyaman abusua ekpunli ne maanle nu la; yɛɛ Filisitiama dɛnlanle bɛ azokoɛleɛ ne wɔ Mekemahye.

english_verse: Each day they sent out patrols to attack and rob villages and then destroy them. One patrol would go north along the road to Ophrah in the region of Shual.
translation_verse: Filisitia ɛlɔnema ne hyɛle bɛ nwo ekpunli nsa. Ekpunli ko hɔle Ɔfela, wɔ Hyuale maanle nu,

english_verse: Another patrol would go west along the road to Beth-Horon. A third patrol would go east toward the desert on the road to the ridge that overlooks Zeboim Valley.
translation_verse: ko hɔle Bɛte Hɔlɔn, yɛɛ ko ne noko hɔle ɛweɛne ne mɔɔ nee Zɛboyem Bɔnza ne nee fienemgbole ne anye bɔ zolɛ la azo, na bɛwuale Yizilayɛma bɛkpokpole bɛ bɔkɔɔ.

english_verse: The Philistines would not allow any Israelites to learn how to make iron tools. “If we allowed that,” they said, “those worthless Israelites would make swords and spears.”
translation_verse: Mekɛ ne anu ɛnee dwinvolɛma mɔɔ fa mbulalɛ di adwinli la bie ɛnle Yizilayɛ maanle ne anu, ɔboalekɛ Filisitiama amkponle Hibuluma ammaa bɛanyɛ bie na bɛava bɛ nee bɛ aho.

english_verse: Whenever the Israelites wanted to get an iron point put on a cattle prod, they had to go to the Philistines. Even if they wanted to sharpen plow-blades, picks, axes, sickles, and pitchforks they still had to go to them. And the Philistines charged high prices.
translation_verse: Bɛsi akuma anzɛɛ bɛyɛ ɛnlankɛ empele ko boɛ a bɛdie dwɛtɛ ekyi ko; yɛɛ saa bɛsi funduazɛlɛ gye anzɛɛ koanlɛ a bɛdie dwɛtɛ ngyikyi nwiɔ.)

english_verse: So, whenever the Israelite soldiers had to go into battle, none of them had a sword or a spear except Saul and his son Jonathan.
translation_verse: Yemɔti kenle ne mɔɔ konle ne zile la, ɛnee Sɔɔlo ɛlɔnema ne biala ɛnlɛ konle debie biala kɛ Sɔɔlo nee ɔ ra Dwɔnatan ala.

english_verse: The Philistines moved their camp to the pass at Michmash,
translation_verse: Filisitiama manle menli hɔzinzale adenle ne mɔɔ la Mekemahye awoka ne mɔ avinli la.

english_verse: Jonathan decided to get to the Philistine camp by going through the pass that led between Shiny Cliff and Michmash to the north and Thornbush Cliff and Geba to the south.
translation_verse: Ko wɔ adenle ne sɔlɔ mɔɔ di kɔ Mekemahye la, yɛɛ ko ne noko wɔ nyiakɛ mɔɔ di kɔ Giba la.

english_verse: Jonathan and the soldier who carried his weapons talked as they went toward the Philistine camp. “It's just the two of us against all those godless men,” Jonathan said. “But the Lord can help a few soldiers win a battle just as easily as he can help a whole army. Maybe the Lord will help us win this battle.”
translation_verse: Dwɔnatan zele kpavolɛ ne mɔɔ soa ye konle ninyɛne ne la kɛ, “Maa yɛhɔ menli ne mɔɔ ɛnze Nyamenle la azokoɛleɛ lɔ; ɔkɛyɛ kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma bayɛ gyima ne amaa yɛ, ɔluakɛ kanzɛ yɛanzo bɔbɔ a, debie biala ɛnle ɛkɛ mɔɔ kola tua Ɛdɛnkɛma adenle mɔɔ ɔnrɛmaa ɔnrɛlie yɛ a.”

english_verse: “Do whatever you want,” the soldier answered. “I'll be right there with you.”
translation_verse: Kpavolɛ ne buale ye kɛ, “Debie biala mɔɔ wɔ adwenle se wɔ la, yɛ; megyi ɛ nzi. Wɔ adenle biala anu, menrɛgyakyi ɛ nzi ɛlilɛ.”

english_verse: “This is what we will do,” Jonathan said. “We will go across and let them see us.
translation_verse: Dwɔnatan zele kɛ, “Mede, yɛkɔ yɛamaa Filisitiama anwu yɛ.

english_verse: If they agree to come down the hill and fight where we are, then we won't climb up to their camp.
translation_verse: Saa bɛnwu yɛ na bɛse yɛ kɛ, ‘Bɛhendɛ bɛmaa yɛrado bɛ’ a, yɛbagyinla yɛ bo zo ne koonwu, yɛnrɛdu yɛ bo.

english_verse: But we will go if they tell us to come up the hill and fight. That will mean the Lord is going to help us win.”
translation_verse: Na saa bɛse yɛ kɛ, ‘Bɛrɛla yɛ nwo ɛke’ a, yɛbahɔ. Ɔluakɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛmaa yɛli bɛ nwo zo konim yɛwie, na ɛhye yɛɛ bayɛ sɛkɛlɛneɛ amaa yɛ a.”

english_verse: Jonathan and the soldier stood at the bottom of the hill where the Philistines could see them. The Philistines said, “Look! Those worthless Israelites have crawled out of the holes where they've been hiding.” Then they yelled down to Jonathan and the soldier, “Come up here, and we will teach you a thing or two!” Jonathan turned to the soldier and said, “Follow me! The Lord is going to let us win.”
translation_verse: Na Filisitia ɛlɔnema ne vɛlɛle Dwɔnatan nee ye sonvolɛ ne kɛ, “Bɛrɛla yɛ nwo ɛke bɛmaa yɛha edwɛkɛ yɛhile bɛ.” Dwɔnatan zele kpavolɛ ne kɛ, “Toa me; Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛmaa Yizilayɛma ɛli bɛ nwo zo konim ɛwie ala ɛne.”

english_verse: Jonathan crawled up the hillside with the soldier right behind him. When they got to the top, Jonathan killed the Philistines who attacked from the front, and the soldier killed those who attacked from behind.
translation_verse: Dwɔnatan vi awoka ne mɔ avinli gongonle vole doale bɛ, ye sonvolɛ ne li ɔ nzi. Dwɔnatan tetale Filisitiama; mɔɔ ɔka bɛ yeagua la ɛnee ye sonvolɛ ne ɛlɛku bɛ.

english_verse: I wish you had eaten some of the food the Philistines left behind. We would have been able to kill a lot more of them.”
translation_verse: Saa menli ne lile bɛ kpɔvolɛma ne anwo zo konim la bɛlile aleɛ mɔɔ bɛnyianle ye la bie a anrɛɛ bɛ nwo kpundinle bɛ; na anrɛɛ Filisitiama mɔɔ bɛkɛhu bɛ ɛnɛ la kɛyɛ ɛzulolɛ.”

english_verse: Saul quickly called his army together, then led them to the Philistine camp. By this time the Philistines were so confused that they were killing each other.
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo boɔboale ye ɛlɔnema ne anloa na ɔvale konle ɔdoale Filisitiama. Mekɛ ne anu ɛnee Filisitiama adwenle ɛha ɛbɔ nu, na anyezota ɛmaa bɛdabɛ bɛ ngome bɛpɛ bɛ nwo bɛlɛko bɛahuhu bɛ nwo.

english_verse: The whole Philistine army panicked—those in camp, those on guard duty, those in the fields, and those on raiding patrols. All of them were afraid and confused. Then God sent an earthquake, and the ground began to tremble. Israel Defeats the Philistines
translation_verse: Ɛzulolɛ kpole hanle Filisitiama mɔɔ wɔ konle azokoɛleɛ ne la kɔsɔɔti. Menli mɔɔ hɔle awule kawua Yizilayɛma akpokpo bɛ la bɔbɔ ahonle dule. Azɛlɛ kpusule, na menli ne anye zo danle bɛ. Filisitiama anwo zo konimlilɛ

english_verse: Saul's lookouts at Geba saw that the Philistine army was running in every direction, like melted wax.
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo menli ne mɔɔ ɛnee wɔ Gebɛya mɔɔ wɔ Bɛngyaman maanle nu, mɔɔ ɛnee ɛlɛtɛ la nwunle kɛ Filisitia ɛlɔnema anye zo ɛda bɛ na bɛbɔ asande.

english_verse: Saul told his officers, “Call the roll and find out who left our camp.” When they had finished, they found out that Jonathan and the soldier who carried his weapons were missing.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Sɔɔlo zele ye menli ne mɔ kɛ, “Bɛdia ɛlɔnema ne na bɛnwu menli mɔɔ ɛnle ɛke la.” Bɛdianle bɛ bɛwiele la, bɛnwunle kɛ Dwɔnatan nee kpavolɛ ne mɔɔ soa ye konle ninyɛne ne mɔ la ɛnle ɛkɛ.

english_verse: Just as Saul finished saying this, he could see that the Philistine army camp was getting more and more confused, and he said, “Ahijah, never mind!”
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Sɔɔlo nee sɛlɛvolɛ ne ɛlɛtendɛ la, alɛra ne mɔɔ ɛnee Filisitiama ɛlɛyɛ wɔ bɛ azokoɛleɛ ne la hɔle anwuma, yemɔti Sɔɔlo zele sɛlɛvolɛ ne kɛ, “Alagye bieko ɛnle ɛkɛ mɔɔ yɛfa yɛbiza Ɛdɛnkɛma edwɛkɛ a.”

english_verse: There were also some hired soldiers in the Philistine camp, who now switched to Israel's side and fought for Saul and Jonathan.
translation_verse: Hibuluma bie mɔ, mɔɔ wɔ Filisitiama afoa na bɛ nee bɛ wɔ bɛ azokoɛleɛ ne la hakyile bɛ adwenle na bɛziale bɛhɔbokale Sɔɔlo nee Dwɔnatan.

english_verse: Many Israelites had been hiding in the hill country of Ephraim. And when they heard that the Philistines were running away, they came out of hiding and joined in chasing the Philistines.
translation_verse: Zɔhane ala yɛɛ Yizilayɛma mɔɔ hɔle afea wɔ Yifelaem awoka ne mɔ anu la, dele kɛ Filisitiama ɛgua ɛbɔ nu la vindele voanle bɛ ndinlizo

english_verse: So the Lord helped Israel win the battle that day. Saul's Curse on Anyone Who Eats Saul had earlier told his soldiers, “I want to get even with those Philistines by sunset. If any of you eat before then, you will be under a curse!” So he made them swear not to eat. By the time the fighting moved past Beth-Aven, the Israelite troops were weak from hunger.
translation_verse: Kenle ko ne Yizilayɛma adwenle zɛkyele, ɔluakɛ Sɔɔlo guale bɛ amonle kɛ, “Toonwo mɔɔ ɔkadwu nɔsolɛ la, awie biala mmadi debie kɔkpula kɛ menwɔli me kpɔvolɛma anwo zo konim la. Ɛdawɔ mɔɔ ɛkɛli debie la, munzule ɛha wɔ.” Yemɔti awie biala anva debie anga ɔ nloa.

english_verse: The army and the people who lived nearby had gone into a forest, and they came to a place where honey was dripping on the ground. But no one ate any of it, because they were afraid of being put under the curse.
translation_verse: Eza bɛnwunle kɛ kpɔkɛ ne anu ɛleka biala mɔɔ bɛkɛva la ɛnee wolɛ ɛlɛpepe aze, noko awie biala anva bie anga ɔ nloa, ɔluakɛ bɛsulo amonle ne mɔɔ Sɔɔlo guale bɛ la.

english_verse: Jonathan did not know about Saul's warning to the soldiers. So he dipped the end of his walking stick in the honey and ate some with his fingers. He felt stronger and more alert.
translation_verse: Ɛnee Dwɔnatan ɛtɛtele kɛ ɔ ze ɛgua menli ne amonle kɛ bɛmmadi debie, yemɔti ɔdwule wolɛ ne mɔ anwo la, ɔvale baka ne mɔɔ ɔlɛ la ati ɔwɔle wolɛ ne anu ɔwokele ndɛlamoa ko ɔlile, na ɔ nwo gyinlanle ye.

english_verse: Then a soldier told him, “Your father swore that anyone who ate food today would be put under a curse, and we agreed not to eat. That's why we're so weak.”
translation_verse: Na menli ne mɔ ko zele ye kɛ, “Ɛ ze ɛgua yɛ amonle kɛ, ‘Ɛnɛ kenle ye, awie biala mɔɔ kɛli debie la, munzule ɛha ye;’ yemɔti ɛhɔne ngome ɛmaa yɛ nwo ɛgolo yɛ.”

english_verse: Jonathan said, “My father has caused you a lot of trouble. Look at me! I ate only a little of this honey, but already I feel strong and alert.
translation_verse: Na Dwɔnatan zele kɛ, “Egya ɛbu amaamuo ɛtane ɛmaa menli ne. Wolɛ ekyi mɔɔ meli la, nea kɛ me nwo ekpundi me bie a.

english_verse: By evening the Israelite army was exhausted from killing Philistines all the way from Michmash to Aijalon.
translation_verse: Kenle ko ne Yizilayɛma lile Filisitiama anwo zo konim. Bɛvi Mekemahye bɛhonle toonwo bɛhɔguale ye Ayegyalɔn. Mekɛ ɛhye anu ɛnee akee ɛhɔne ngome ɛmaa Yizilayɛma anwo ɛwie bɛ golo;

english_verse: They grabbed the food they had captured from the Philistines and started eating. They even killed sheep and cows and calves right on the spot and ate the meat without draining the blood.
translation_verse: yemɔti bɛzile bɛlɔle nu bɛhyele mboane, nlankɛ, mgbole nee ngyikyi, bɛhunle bɛ na bɛlile bɛ nee bɛ mogya ne kɔsɔɔti.

english_verse: Someone told Saul, “Look! The army is disobeying the Lord by eating meat before the blood drains out.” “You're right,” Saul answered. “They are being unfaithful to the Lord! Hurry! Roll a big rock over here.
translation_verse: Bɛhanle bɛhilele Sɔɔlo kɛ, “Menli ne ɛlɛyɛ ɛtane atia Ɛdɛnkɛma. Bɛlɛdi nane nee ye mogya ne.” Sɔɔlo deanle nu, “Bɛle ngunzi; bɛhundo bolɛ kpole ko bɛrɛlɛ me ɛke.”

english_verse: Then tell everyone in camp to bring their cattle and lambs to me. They can kill the animals on this rock, then eat the meat. That way no one will disobey the Lord by eating meat with blood still in it.” That night the soldiers brought their cattle over to the big rock and killed them there.
translation_verse: Ɔzoanle bɛ kɛ, “Bɛhɔze menli ne mɔ kɛ, ‘Awie biala ɛva ye ɛnlankɛ anzɛɛ ye boane na bɛrahu bɛ bɛli wɔ ɛke, na bɛmmayɛ ɛtane bɛtia Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle kɛ bɛkɛli nane mɔɔ mogya wɔ nu la.’ ” Yemɔti kenle ko ne nɔsolɛ, awie biala vale ye ɛnlankɛ rahunle ye wɔ ɛkɛ ne.

english_verse: It was the first altar Saul had built for offering sacrifices to the Lord. The Army Rescues Jonathan
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo zile azukponle manle Ɛdɛnkɛma. Ɛhye a le azukponle mɔɔ lumua mɔɔ Sɔɔlo zile manle Ɛdɛnkɛma a.

english_verse: Saul said, “Let's attack the Philistines again while it's still dark. We can fight them all night. Let's kill them and take everything they own!” The people answered, “We will do whatever you want.” “Wait!” Ahijah the priest said. “Let's ask God what we should do.”
translation_verse: Akee Sɔɔlo zele menli ne kɛ, “Bɛmaa yɛhɔ Filisitiama anwo zo ɛnɛ nɔe toonwo alehyenlɛ, yɛbɔ bɛ bo zo, yɛkpokpo bɛ bɔkɔɔ mɔɔ yɛngyakyi ko bɔbɔ a.” Na bɛzele ye kɛ, “Debie biala mɔɔ ɛkulo la, yɛ.” Na sɛlɛvolɛ ne zele kɛ, “Bɛmaa yɛbiza Nyamenle kolaa.”

english_verse: Saul asked God, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you help us win?” This time God did not answer.
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo bizale Nyamenle kɛ, “Menva konle mengɔndoa Filisitiama ɔ? Ɛkɛye bɛ ɛkɛmaa Yizilayɛma ɔ?” Na kenle ko ne Nyamenle ammaa ye mualɛ.

english_verse: Saul called his army officers together and said, “We have to find out what sin has kept God from answering.
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo zele mgbanyima ne mɔ kɛ, “Bɛrɛla, bɛranlea ɛtane mɔɔ ɛnɛ bɛyɛ la.

english_verse: I swear by the living Lord that whoever sinned must die, even if it turns out to be my own son Jonathan.” No one said a word.
translation_verse: Meka tease Ɛdɛnkɛma mɔɔ ko die Yizilayɛma la kɛ, ahenle mɔɔ vale munzule ɛhye rale la, saa me ra Dwɔnatan bɔbɔ a, ɔwɔ kɛ ɔwu.” Na awie biala ambua ye.

english_verse: Saul told his army, “You stand on that side of the priest, and Jonathan and I will stand on the other side.” Everyone agreed.
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo zele bɛ kɔsɔɔti kɛ, “Bɛgyinla foa ko nehane, na medame me nee me ra Dwɔnatan yɛgyinla foa ko ɛke.” Na menli ne zele Sɔɔlo kɛ, “Debie biala mɔɔ fɛta la, yɛ.”

english_verse: Then Saul prayed, “Our Lord, God of Israel, why haven't you answered me today? Please show us who sinned. Was it my son Jonathan and I, or was it your people Israel?” The answer came back that Jonathan or Saul had sinned, not the army.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Sɔɔlo zɛlɛle kɛ, “O Ɛdɛnkɛma, Yizilayɛ Nyamenle, duzu ati a wɔambua me edwɛkɛ ne anwo ɛnɛ a? Saa ɛtane ɛhye vi me anzɛɛ me ra Dwɔnatan a, ɛnee fa ‘Yulem’ sɛkɛlɛneɛ kile; na saa ɔvi wɔ menli Yizilayɛma ɛdeɛ a, ɛnee fa ‘Tɛmen’ sɛkɛlɛneɛ kile.” Na ɔbɔle Sɔɔlo nee Dwɔnatan; menli ne anwo vile nu.

english_verse: Saul told Ahijah, “Now ask the Lord to decide between Jonathan and me.” The answer came back that Jonathan had sinned.
translation_verse: Eza Sɔɔlo zele kɛ, “Bɛgua medame nee me ra Dwɔnatan yɛ ti nzeleba.” Bɛguale la ɔbɔle Dwɔnatan.

english_verse: “Jonathan,” Saul exclaimed, “tell me what you did!” “I dipped the end of my walking stick in some honey and ate a little. Now you say I have to die!”
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo zele Dwɔnatan kɛ, “Deɛ holɛ ko mɔɔ wɔyɛ la, ka kile me.” Dwɔnatan zele kɛ, “Kpɔma ne mɔɔ ɛnee melɛ la, menvale ɔ ti membɔle wolɛ ne anu mentafele; medame ɛne, mekponle zolɛ kɛ menwɔwu.”

english_verse: “Yes, Jonathan. I swear to God that you must die.”
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo zele kɛ, “Dwɔnatan, saa meammaa bɛangu wɔ a, Nyamenle ɛhu me.”

english_verse: “No!” the soldiers shouted. “God helped Jonathan win the battle for us. We won't let you kill him. We swear to the Lord that we won't let you kill him or even lay a hand on him!” So the army kept Saul from killing Jonathan.
translation_verse: Na menli ne zele Sɔɔlo kɛ, “Ɛmaa bɛahu Dwɔnatan mɔɔ ɛli konim kpole ɛhye ɛmaa Yizilayɛma la ɔ? Nyamenle ɛkpa ɛgua. Yɛka tease Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ, ɔ ti enrinli ko bɔbɔ ɛnrɛde ɛnrɛdɔ aze ɛlɛ. Mɔɔ ɔyɛle ɛnɛ la, Nyamenle ɔ.” Yemɔti menli ne liele Dwɔnatan ngoane.

english_verse: Saul stopped hunting down the Philistines, and they went home. Saul Fights His Enemies
translation_verse: Akee Sɔɔlo amkpo Filisitiama bieko, na Filisitiama hɔle bɛ maanle nu. Sɔɔlo belemgbunlililɛ nee ye sua nu amra

english_verse: Saul was at war with the Philistines for as long as he lived. Whenever he found a good warrior or a brave man, Saul made him join his army.
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo mekɛ zo, ɔ nee Filisitiama honle mgbole mgbole fane dɔɔnwo, yemɔti mekɛ biala mɔɔ ɔkɛnwu katakyie bie la ɔfa ye ɔboka ɔ nwo.

english_verse: One day, Samuel told Saul: The Lord told me to choose you to be king of his people, Israel. Now listen to this message from the Lord:
translation_verse: Samoɛle zele Sɔɔlo kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma zoanle me manle memkpokpale wɔ nwole menziele wɔ Yizilayɛma belemgbunli, zɔhane ati tie Ɛdɛnkɛma nrɛlaleɛ ne.

english_verse: “When the Israelites were on their way out of Egypt, the nation of Amalek attacked them. I am the Lord All-Powerful, and now I am going to make Amalek pay!
translation_verse: Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma se, ‘Mebadua Amalɛkema kakɛ, ɔboalekɛ bɛduale Yizilayɛma adenle wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ bɛvi Yigyibiti bɛlɛba la.

english_verse: “Go and attack the Amalekites! Destroy them and all their possessions. Don't have any pity. Kill their men, women, children, and even their babies. Slaughter their cattle, sheep, camels, and donkeys.”
translation_verse: Yemɔti kɔ na kɔhu Amalɛkema kɔsɔɔti, sɛkye bɛ debie biala mɔɔ bɛlɛ la, mmagyakyi debie biala fee; ku mrenya nee mraalɛ, ngakula nee nlɔma, nlankɛ nee mboane, afunlumu nee asoaso kɔsɔɔti. Mmagyakyi ko bɔbɔ.’ ”

english_verse: Saul sent messengers who told every town and village to send men to join the army at Telaim. There were
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo boɔboale ye ɛlɔnema ne anloa wɔ Tilɛm na ɔdianle bɛ. Yizilayɛ ɛlɔnema mɔɔ dua aze la le apenle ngoko ɛya nwiɔ yɛɛ Dwudama le apenle bulu.

english_verse: then led them to a valley near one of the towns in Amalek, where they got ready to make a surprise attack.
translation_verse: Akee Sɔɔlo hɔle suakpole Amalɛke azo na bɛhɔdɛle bɔnza bie anu.

english_verse: Some Kenites lived nearby, and Saul told them, “Your people were kind to our nation when we left Egypt, and I don't want you to get killed when I wipe out the Amalekites. So stay away from them.” The Kenites left,
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo zele Kina asa zo ne mɔ kɛ, “Bɛvi Amalɛkema avinli bɛhwe bɛ nwo, anrɛɛ menwɔva bɛ menwɔfonla nu menwɔhu bɛ muala. Ɔluakɛ mɔɔ Yizilayɛma vi Yigyibiti ba la bɛyɛle bɛ nyele.” Yemɔti Kinama ne hwenle bɛ nwo vile Amalɛkema maanle ne anu.

english_verse: and Saul attacked the Amalekites from Havilah to Shur, which is just east of Egypt.
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo nee Amalɛkema honle, na ɔlile bɛ nwo zo konim, ɔvi Havela toonwo ɔdwule Hyulu mɔɔ wɔ Yigyibiti aduduleɛ la.

english_verse: Every Amalekite was killed except King Agag.
translation_verse: Ɔhyele Amalɛke belemgbunli Egage anyewɔzo, na ɔhunle menli ne kɔsɔɔti.

english_verse: Saul and his army let Agag live, and they also spared the best sheep and cattle. They didn't want to destroy anything of value, so they only killed the animals that were worthless or weak. The Lord Rejects Saul
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo nee ye menli ne angu Egage, bɛangu mboane kpalɛ ne mɔɔ ɛlɔ la, nlankɛ kpalɛ nee mboane mralɛ ne mɔ, yɛɛ debie biala mɔɔ le kpalɛ la, bɛanzɛkye ye. Ninyɛne mɔɔ ɛnzonle bolɛ la angome a bɛzɛkyele bɛ a. Nyamenle kpo Sɔɔlo kɛ ɔnle belemgbunli bieko

english_verse: “Saul has stopped obeying me, and I'm sorry that I made him king.” Samuel was angry, and he cried out in prayer to the Lord all night.
translation_verse: ɔluakɛ yehakyi ɔ nzi yezi me. Yeanli me mɛla ne mɔ azo.” Samoɛle vale ɛya, na ɔzɛlɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma nɔe ne toonwo alehyenlɛ.

english_verse: Early the next morning he went to talk with Saul. Someone told him, “Saul went to Carmel, where he had a monument built so everyone would remember his victory. Then he left for Gilgal.”
translation_verse: Samoɛle dwazole ndɛ kɛ ɔkayia Sɔɔlo nwonlomɔ ne ala, na bɛhanle bɛhilele Samoɛle kɛ, “Sɔɔlo ɛhɔ Kamɛle ɛhɔzi ngakyelɛ sɛkɛlɛneɛ ɛwula ɔdaye ɔ nwo anyunlunyia, na yetele zolɛ yehɔ Gelegale.”

english_verse: Samuel finally caught up with Saul, and Saul told him, “I hope the Lord will bless you! I have done what the Lord told me.”
translation_verse: Samoɛle hɔle Sɔɔlo anwo ɛkɛ, na Sɔɔlo zele ye kɛ, “O Samoɛle, Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛyila wɔ, meli Ɛdɛnkɛma mɛla ne azo.”

english_verse: “Then why,” Samuel asked, “do I hear sheep and cattle?”
translation_verse: Na Samoɛle zele kɛ, “Na duzu nlankɛ nee mboane ɛzunlɛ a mete la?”

english_verse: “The army took them from the Amalekites,” Saul explained. “They kept the best sheep and cattle, so they could sacrifice them to the Lord your God. But we destroyed everything else.”
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo buale ye kɛ, “Bɛ nee bɛ vi Amalɛkema lɔ a ɛra a, menli ne gyakyile nlankɛ nee mboane kpalɛ ne mɔ kɛ bɛ nee bɛ ba na bɛava bɛabɔ azu bɛamaa Ɛdɛnkɛma wɔ Nyamenle ne, na mɔɔ hale la yɛzɛkye bɛ bɔkɔɔ.”

english_verse: “Stop!” Samuel said. “Let me tell you what the Lord told me last night.” “All right,” Saul answered.
translation_verse: Na Samoɛle zele Sɔɔlo kɛ, “Gyinla; maa menga mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma hanle hilele me ɛnɛ nɔe la mengile wɔ.” Sɔɔlo zele kɛ, “Ka kile me.”

english_verse: Samuel continued, “You may not think you're very important, but the Lord chose you to be king, and you are in charge of the tribes of Israel.
translation_verse: Na Samoɛle zele ye kɛ, “Ɛdawɔ mumua ne ɛmbu ɛ nwo bie, noko wɔmɔ yɛɛ ɛgyi Yizilayɛ mbusua ekpunli ekpunli ne mɔ ati a. Ɛdɛnkɛma ziele wɔ Yizilayɛ belemgbunli,

english_verse: When the Lord sent you on this mission, he told you to wipe out those worthless Amalekites.
translation_verse: yɛɛ ɔzoanle wɔ kɛ, ‘Kɔ kɔzɛkye Amalɛkema ɛtanevolɛma. Ɛ nee bɛ ɛho toonwo kɔkpula kɛ bɛ bo zo kɛbɔ tɔɔ la.’

english_verse: Why didn't you listen to the Lord? Why did you keep the animals and make him angry?”
translation_verse: Na duzu ati yɛɛ wɔandie Ɛdɛnkɛma ane ɛ? Duzu ati yɛɛ ɛvenle bɛ ninyɛne ne mɔ na ɛyɛle ɛtane wɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlu a?”

english_verse: “But I did listen to the Lord!” Saul answered. “He sent me on a mission, and I went. I captured King Agag and destroyed his nation.
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo buale Samoɛle kɛ, “Mendiele Ɛdɛnkɛma ane. Mengɔle ye ɛzoanlɛ ne, mengyele Belemgbunli Egage anyewɔzo membale na mengunle Amalɛkema mɔɔ ɛha la kɔsɔɔti.

english_verse: All the animals were going to be destroyed anyway. That's why the army brought the best sheep and cattle to Gilgal as sacrifices to the Lord your God.”
translation_verse: Me menli ne angu nlankɛ nee mboane kyenlera ne mɔ. Bɛyɛ kɛ bɛ nee bɛ ba Gelegale ɛke bɛarabɔ azu bɛamaa Ɛdɛnkɛma wɔ Nyamenle ne.”

english_verse: “Tell me,” Samuel said. “Does the Lord really want sacrifices and offerings? No! He doesn't want your sacrifices. He wants you to obey him.
translation_verse: Samoɛle zele kɛ, “Ɛnee ɛnea a Ɛdɛnkɛma anye die azubɔdeɛ nee ɛyelalɛ azubɔlɛ nwo kpole tɛla kɛ ɛkɛdie ɔ ne la ɔ? Nea, tieyɛ le kpalɛ tɛla azubɔlɛ, yɛɛ ɛtie Ɛdɛnkɛma ane a ɔle kpalɛ ɔtɛla mboane nyinli mɔɔ ɛwie kye la.

english_verse: Rebelling against God or disobeying him because you are proud is just as bad as worshiping idols or asking them for advice. You refused to do what God told you, so God has decided that you can no longer be king.”
translation_verse: Atuadelɛ le kɛ mizemiza ɛtaneyɛlɛ, yɛɛ anzosesebɛ le ɛtane kɛ amumuyɛ ɛyɛlɛ nee awozonle ɛzonlenlɛ. Kɛmɔ wɔkpo Ɛdɛnkɛma edwɛkɛ ne la, ɔdaye noko yekpo wɔ kɛ ɛnle belemgbunli.”

english_verse: “I have sinned,” Saul admitted. “I disobeyed both you and the Lord. I was afraid of the army, and I listened to them instead.
