english_verse: Abigail quickly got off her donkey and bowed down in front of David.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Abegeli nwunle Devidi la, ɔvi ye asoaso ne azo ɔdwule aze ndɛndɛ, ɔhɔbutule Devidi anyunlu ɛkɛ na ɔbɔle ɔ ti aze ɔmanle ye.

english_verse: Don't pay any attention to that good-for-nothing Nabal. His name means “fool,” and it really fits him! I didn't see the men you sent,
translation_verse: Mmadwenle Neebale nyɛleɛ ne anwo, ɔluakɛ ɔlɛ ahonle, yɛɛ ye duma mumua ne kile ye subane, koasea ɔ. Yɛmenle, mɔɔ wɔ soanvolɛma ne mɔ rale la, ɛnee menle ɛkɛ.

english_verse: Please forgive me if I say a little more. The Lord will always protect you and your family, because you fight for him. I pray that you won't ever do anything evil as long as you live.
translation_verse: Mesɛlɛ wɔ, ɛtane biala mɔɔ meyɛ la, fa kyɛ me. Ɛdɛnkɛma bamaa wɔali belemgbunli, ɛ bo zo amra noko bali belemgbunli, ɔboalekɛ ɛlɛko wɔamaa ye, na melɛ dodo biala mɔɔ ɛbali la, munzule ɛnrɛdo wɔ ɛlɛ.

english_verse: The Lord your God will keep you safe when your enemies try to kill you. But he will snatch away their lives quicker than you can throw a rock from a sling.
translation_verse: Saa awie se kɛ ɔku wɔ a, Ɛdɛnkɛma wɔ Nyamenle ne bava wɔ avea gyɛlɛɛnye, kɛmɔ sonla sinza ye agyadeɛ mɔɔ sonle bolɛ la. Na mɔɔ fane wɔ kpɔvolɛma ne mɔ anwo, ɔbavuandi bɛ yeagua kɛ bɛto totoabɔ la.

english_verse: The Lord has promised to do many good things for you, even to make you the ruler of Israel. The Lord will keep his promises to you,
translation_verse: Akee mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛwie debie kpalɛ biala mɔɔ yeva yebɔ wɔ ɛwɔkɛ la yɛ na yezie wɔ Yizilayɛ belemgbunli yewie la,

english_verse: and now your conscience will be clear, because you won't be guilty of taking revenge and killing innocent people. When the Lord does all those good things for you, please remember me.
translation_verse: debie biala ɛnle ɛkɛ mɔɔ kɛmaa ɛkɛli nyane anzɛɛ kɛmaa ɛ nwo kɛbubu wɔ, kɛ wɔanga mogya mɔɔ ɛnze nwolɛ bie la wɔangua anzɛɛ wɔanli nzenralɛ a. Na akee saa Ɛdɛnkɛma wie wɔ yila a, anrɛɛ mmamaa ɛ rɛle fi me.”

english_verse: David told her: I praise the Lord God of Israel! He must have sent you to meet me today.
translation_verse: Na Devidi zele Abegeli kɛ, “Ayɛlɛyelɛ ɛha Ɛdɛnkɛma, Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne, mɔɔ zoanle wɔ kɛ ɛnɛ demua ye ɛ nee me ɛyia la.

english_verse: And you should also be praised. Your good sense kept me from taking revenge and killing innocent people.
translation_verse: Yɛyɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma mo kɛ yemaa wɔ nrɛlɛbɛ kpalɛ ɛhye, yɛɛ nyilalɛ ɛha ɛdawɔ mumua ne kɛ wɔammaa meanli nzenralɛ meanga mogya meangua a.

english_verse: If you hadn't come to meet me so quickly, every man and boy in Nabal's family and in his servants' families would have been killed by morning. I swear by the living Lord God of Israel who protected you that this is the truth.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛgogo me ahonle, yeammaa meanzɛkye bɛ. Meka Yizilayɛ tease Nyamenle ne kɛ, saa ɛ nwo anyɛ ndɛ ɛ nee me anyia a, anrɛɛ toonwo mɔɔ aleɛ kahye la, ɛnee Neebale menli ne mɔ ɛdɔ amolɛ nu, mɔɔ ko bɔbɔ ɛnrɛha a.”

english_verse: David accepted the food Abigail had brought. “Don't worry,” he said. “You can go home now. I'll do what you asked.”
translation_verse: Akee Devidi liele Abegeli ahyɛlɛdeɛ ne na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Kɔ sua nu anzonudwolɛ nu; medie ɛ ne, na mekponle wɔ modolɛ ne azo.”

english_verse: Abigail went back home and found Nabal throwing a party fit for a king. He was very drunk and feeling good, so she didn't tell him anything that night.
translation_verse: Abegeli ziale hɔle sua nu na ɔhɔdole kɛ Neebale ɛdo ɛkponle kpole bie kɛ asɛɛ belemgbunli bie la, ɔ nye ɛlie na yebo kpole kpalɛ. Yemɔti yeanga ɛhwee yeangile ye hɔkpulale ye alehyenlɛ nu.

english_verse: But when he sobered up the next morning, Abigail told him everything that had happened. Nabal had a heart attack, and he lay in bed as still as a stone.
translation_verse: Aleɛ hyenle na Neebale anye zo tetele ye la, ɔ ye hanle mɔɔ zile la amuala hilele ye, na ɛkɛ ne ala ɔgolole ɔguale na ɔdwidwele.

english_verse: Ten days later, the Lord took his life.
translation_verse: Ye kenle bulu ne azo Ɛdɛnkɛma manle ɔwule.

english_verse: She bowed down and said, “I would willingly be David's slave and wash his servants' feet.”
translation_verse: Abegeli dwazole na ɔbɔle ɔ ti aze na ɔhanle kɛ, “Mele ye sonvolɛ mɔɔ ɛboɔboa ɔ nwo kɛ ɔkɛwowo ye sonvolɛma agyakɛ anwo a.”

english_verse: Abigail quickly got ready and went back with David's messengers. She rode on her donkey, while five of her servant women walked alongside. She and David were married as soon as she arrived.
translation_verse: Ɔdwazole ɔvole ye asoaso ne azo; ɔvale ye sonvolɛ mraalɛ nnu ne na ɔ nee Devidi sonvolɛma ne hɔle na ɔhɔgyale Devidi.

english_verse: David had earlier married Ahinoam from the town of Jezreel, so both she and Abigail were now David's wives.
translation_verse: Devidi ɛnee ɛgya Ahenoam mɔɔ vi Gyɛzɛli la, yemɔti bɛ mu nwiɔ bɛyɛle ye mraalɛ.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Saul had arranged for Michal to marry Palti the son of Laish, who came from the town of Gallim.
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo vale Maekale mɔɔ ɛnee le Devidi aye la manle Leeyehye ara Paletae mɔɔ vi Galem la gyale.

english_verse: Once again, some people from Ziph went to Gibeah to talk with Saul. “David has a hideout on Mount Hachilah near Jeshimon out in the desert,” they told him.
translation_verse: Menli bie vi Zefe rale Sɔɔlo anwo ɛkɛ ne wɔ Gebɛya rahanle hilele ye kɛ Devidi vea Hakaela Boka wɔ Dwuda fienemgbole ne anloa.

english_verse: Saul set up camp on Mount Hachilah, which is across the road from Jeshimon. But David was hiding out in the desert. When David heard that Saul was following him,
translation_verse: Bɛhɔyɛle azokoɛleɛ wɔ ademgbole ne mɔɔ la Hakaela Boka la foa ko. Ɛnee Devidi wɔ fienemgbole ne anu; na mɔɔ ɔdele kɛ Sɔɔlo ɛra bakpondɛ ye la,

english_verse: he sent some spies to find out if it was true.
translation_verse: ɔzoanle menli ɔmanle bɛhɔnleanle na bɛnwunle kɛ amgba Sɔɔlo wɔ ɛkɛ.

english_verse: Then he sneaked up to Saul's camp. He noticed that Saul and his army commander Abner the son of Ner were sleeping in the middle of the camp, with soldiers sleeping all around them.
translation_verse: Ɛkɛ ne ala Devidi hɔle Sɔɔlo azokoɛleɛ ɛkɛ ne hɔnleanle ɛleka fɔɔnwo mɔɔ Sɔɔlo nee Nɛɛ ara Abenɛɛ mɔɔ nea Sɔɔlo ɛlɔnema ne anwo zo la da la. Ɔnwunle kɛ Sɔɔlo la azokoɛleɛ ne avinli na ye ɛlɔnema ɛbɔ ye mgbɔlɔka ɛyia.

english_verse: David asked Ahimelech the Hittite and Joab's brother Abishai, “Which one of you will go with me into Saul's camp?” “I will!” Abishai answered.
translation_verse: Akee Devidi bizale Ahemɛlɛke, Hɛtenli ne nee Dwowabe adiema nrenya Abehyae kɛ, “Bɛ nuhua boni a nee me kɛhɔ Sɔɔlo azokoɛleɛ ne a?” Na Abehyae zele kɛ, “Medame a me nee wɔ kɔ a.”

english_verse: That same night, David and Abishai crept into the camp. Saul was sleeping, and his spear was stuck in the ground not far from his head. Abner and the soldiers were sound asleep all around him.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Devidi nee Abehyae hɔle ɛlɔnema azokoɛleɛ ɛkɛ ne nɔe ne, na bɛhɔnwunle kɛ Sɔɔlo ɛlafe botoo na ye atwɛ ne kpɔnla ɔ ti sɔlɔ; Abenɛɛ nee ɛlɔnema ne noko ɛbɔ ɛyia ye na bɛdabɛ bɛlafe.

english_verse: Abishai whispered, “This time God has let you get your hands on your enemy! I'll pin him to the ground with one thrust of his own spear.”
translation_verse: Na Abehyae zele Devidi kɛ, “Ɛnɛ demua ye, Nyamenle ɛye wɔ kpɔvolɛ ne ɛwula ɛ sa nu, maa menwɔ ye atwɛ na membɔ ye pemgbɛne azɛlɛ ne anwo; mewɔ ye kokye ala, menrɛdia zolɛ nwiɔ.”

english_verse: “Don't kill him!” David whispered back. “The Lord will punish anyone who kills his chosen king.
translation_verse: Na Devidi zele ye kɛ, “Mmafa ɛ sa ɛka ye, ɔluakɛ awie biala mɔɔ kɛva ɔ sa kɛha sonla mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛzie ye belemgbunli la ɛnrɛva ɔ nwo dwɔɔ.”

english_verse: As surely as the Lord lives, the Lord will kill Saul, or Saul will die a natural death or be killed in battle.
translation_verse: Devidi hanle zɔle zolɛ kɛ, “Meka tease Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ, Ɛdɛnkɛma ɔdaye ɔbahu ye; saa konle nu o anzɛɛ ye ewule mekɛ nu o.

english_verse: But I pray that the Lord will keep me from harming his chosen king. Let's grab his spear and his water jar and get out of here!”
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛkpa ɛgua kɛ menwɔva me sa menwɔha sonla mɔɔ ɔdaye yeye ye yezie ye belemgbunli la. Maa yɛdu ye atwɛ ne mɔɔ gyi ɔ ti sɔlɔ la na yɛva ye nzule dwora ne yɛhɔ.”

english_verse: David took the spear and the water jar, then left the camp. None of Saul's soldiers knew what had happened or even woke up—the Lord had made all of them fall sound asleep.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Devidi vale atwɛ ne nee nzule dwora ne wɔ Sɔɔlo ati sɔlɔ ɛkɛ ne, na ɔ nee Abehyae bɛhɔle. Awie biala annwu bɛ yɛɛ awie biala ɛnze mɔɔ zile la yɛɛ bɛ nuhua ko bɔbɔ ambɔ mgbatike andunwue, ɔboalekɛ ɛnee Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛye nafelɛ ɛdo bɛ nwo ɛmaa bɛlafe bubotoo.

english_verse: David and Abishai crossed the valley and went to the top of the next hill, where they were at a safe distance.
translation_verse: Akee Devidi pɛle bɔnza ne hɔle ɔ nzi na ɔhɔvole boka ne mɔɔ nee bɛ avinli twe la azo,

english_verse: “Abner!” David shouted toward Saul's army. “Can you hear me?” Abner shouted back. “Who dares disturb the king?”
translation_verse: na ɔdeanle nu ɔzele Sɔɔlo ɛlɔnema ne nee Abenɛɛ kɛ, “Abenɛɛ, ɛte me ne ɔ?” Abenɛɛ bizale kɛ, “Nwane a ɛlɛteɛdea nu adunwue belemgbunli la?”

english_verse: “Abner, what kind of a man are you?” David replied. “Aren't you supposed to be the best soldier in Israel? Then why didn't you protect your king? Anyone who went into your camp could have killed him tonight.
translation_verse: Devidi zele Abenɛɛ kɛ, “Na ɛnle nrenya ɔ? Yizilayɛ maanle ye anu, nwane a nee wɔ sɛ a? Duzu ati a wɔangola wɔanzinza wɔ belemgbunli ne a? Mekɛ ɛhye ala anu, awie rale bɛ azokoɛleɛ ɛkɛ ne kɛ ɔbahu wɔ belemgbunli ne.

english_verse: You're a complete failure! I swear by the living Lord that you and your men deserve to die for not protecting the Lord's chosen king. Look and see if you can find the king's spear and the water jar that were near his head.”
translation_verse: Nyɛleɛ ɛhye mɔɔ wɔyɛ la ɛnle kpalɛ, ɔluakɛ wɔanli wɔ gyima ne. Abenɛɛ, meka tease Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ, bɛ kɔsɔɔti bɛfɛta ewule, ɔboalekɛ bɛangola bɛanzinza bɛ belemgbunli ne mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛzie ye ɛmaa bɛ la. Nea, belemgbunli ne atwɛ ne wɔ nienwu?”

english_verse: Saul could tell it was David's voice, and he called out, “David, my son! Is that you?” “Yes it is, Your Majesty.
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo ze Devidi ane, yemɔti ɔbizale ye kɛ, “Me ra Devidi, ɛnee ɛ ne a mete la ɔ?” Devidi zele ye kɛ, “Ɛhɛe, Nana, me ne ɔ.”

english_verse: Why are you hunting me down? Have I done something wrong, or have I committed a crime?
translation_verse: Na ɔvale ɔzɔle zolɛ kɛ, “Duzu ati yɛɛ ɛnɛ nee ɛnɛ ala ɛtɛfoa wɔ sonvolɛ ɛ? Duzu a meyɛ a? Duzu munzule a mebɔ a?

english_verse: Please listen to what I have to say. If the Lord has turned you against me, maybe a sacrifice will make him change his mind. But if some people have turned you against me, I hope the Lord will punish them! They have forced me to leave the land that belongs to the Lord and have told me to worship foreign gods.
translation_verse: Nana, yɛ ɛnzolɛ tie me. Saa Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛɛ ɛmaa ɛlɛtu me mgbaliko ɛhye a, ɛnee azubɔlɛ bamaa yeahakyi ye adwenle; na saa ɔle menli ngyehyɛlɛ ɛdeɛ a, ɛnee Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛdua bɛ kakɛ, ɔluakɛ bɛvoa me bɛvi Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛzonlenlɛ ne anwo, na bɛmaa mehɔ ɛleka mɔɔ bɛnzonle Nyamenle la.

english_verse: Don't let me die in a land far away from the Lord. I'm no more important than a flea! Why should the king of Israel hunt me down as if I were a bird in the mountains?”
translation_verse: Mmamaa mekpɔkye me nwo mefi Ɛdɛnkɛma anwo, na mewu maanle gyɛne nu. Duzu ati yɛɛ Yizilayɛ belemgbunli ne kɛdu medame, mɔɔ membɔnle nzule la mgbaliko zɛhae a? Duzu ati a ɔlɛtɛ me kɛ bɛtɛ anloma bɛahye ye la ɛ?”

english_verse: “David, you had the chance to kill me today. But you didn't. I was very wrong about you. It was a terrible mistake for me to try to kill you. I've acted like a fool, but I'll never try to harm you again. You're like a son to me, so please come back.”
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo zele kɛ, “Meyɛ ɛtane, me ra Devidi, sia bɛla. Menrɛdu wɔ mgbaliko bieko, ɔboalekɛ wɔnwu me anwunvɔne, wɔangu me ɛnɛ nɔe. Meyɛ koasea na meyɛ ɛtane.”

english_verse: “Your Majesty, here's your spear! Let one of your soldiers come and get it.
translation_verse: Devidi buale ye kɛ, “Nana, wɔ atwɛ ne ɛne. Maa wɔ menli ne mɔ ko ɛralie.

english_verse: The Lord put you in my power today, but you are his chosen king and I wouldn't harm you. The Lord rewards people who are faithful and live right.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma yila awie biala mɔɔ di pɛlepɛle nee nɔhalɛ la. Ɛdɛnkɛma yele wɔ manle me ɛnɛ nɔe, noko meanyɛ wɔ ɛhwee, ɔluakɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛzie wɔ belemgbunli.

english_verse: I spared your life today, and I pray that the Lord will spare my life and keep me safe.”
translation_verse: Kɛmɔ ɛnɛ meangu wɔ la, zɔhane ala yɛɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛyɛ ɛmaa me na ɔye me ɔvi ngyegyelɛ biala anu a.”

english_verse: “David, my son, I pray that the Lord will bless you and make you successful!” David in Philistia Saul went back home. David also left,
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo zele Devidi kɛ, “Me ra Devidi, Nyamenle ɛyila wɔ. Ɛbayɛ ninyɛne dɔɔnwo na biala anu ɛbali konim.” Yemɔti Devidi hɔle ye ɛleka bie, yɛɛ Sɔɔlo noko ziale hɔle sua nu.

english_verse: but he thought to himself, “One of these days, Saul is going to kill me. The only way to escape from him is to go to Philistia. Then I'll be outside of Israel, and Saul will give up trying to catch me.”
translation_verse: Devidi hanle ye ɔ ti anu kɛ, “Kɛ ɔkɛyɛ biala la, kenle ko Sɔɔlo asa baha me yeahu me. Mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ meyɛ la a le kɛ, meye me nwo zo meahɔ Filisitiama maanle nu. Na saa ɔba ye zɛhae a Sɔɔlo asa anu bado, ɔbagyakyi me ɛkpondɛlɛ wɔ Yizilayɛ maanle ye anu, na meanyia me ti.”

english_verse: When Saul found out that David had run off to Gath, he stopped trying to catch him.
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo dele kɛ Devidi ɛnriandi ɛhɔ Gate la, yeamkpo ye bieko.

english_verse: One day, David was talking with Achish and said, “If you are happy with me, then let me live in one of the towns in the countryside. I'm not important enough to live here with you in the royal city.”
translation_verse: Akee Devidi zele Ekehye kɛ, “Saa wɔnyia me nwo ɛhulolɛ a ɛnee maa me azɛlɛ wɔ azua ngyikyi ne mɔ bie azo maa mengɔndɛnla lɔ tɛla kɛ me nee wɔ kɛdɛnla wɔ dehelɛ suakpole ye azo la.”

english_verse: Achish gave David the town of Ziklag that same day, and Ziklag has belonged to the kings of Judah ever since.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Ekehye vale Zekelage manle Devidi. Ɛhye ati yɛɛ ɛnɛ Zekelage le Dwuda arelemgbunli ɛdeɛ la.

english_verse: David was in Philistia for a year and four months.
translation_verse: Devidi dɛnlanle Filisitia maanle nu ɛvolɛ ko siane nna.

english_verse: The Geshurites, the Girzites, and the Amalekites lived in the area from Telam to Shur and on as far as Egypt, and David often attacked their towns.
translation_verse: Mekɛ ɛhye anu, ɔyɛ a ɛnee Devidi nee ye ɛlɔnema ne ɛva konle ɛhɔdoa Gɛhyɛma, Gɛzaema yɛɛ Amalɛkema mɔɔ de maanzinli ne anu dɛba la. Bɛwuale bɛ azɛlɛ ne azo ninyɛne bɛvi Hyulu toonwo bɛdwule Yigyibiti ɛweɛne zo.

english_verse: Whenever David and his men attacked a town, they took the sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, and the clothing, and killed everyone who lived there. After he returned from a raid, David always went to see Achish,
translation_verse: Devidi hunle awie biala, mraalɛ nee mrenya na bɛvenle bɛ mboane, nlankɛ, asoaso, afunlumu, yɛɛ bɛ nwo ndanlɛ bɔbɔ. Na saa ɔsia ɔba, na Ekehye

english_verse: who would ask, “Where did you attack today?” David would answer, “Oh, we attacked some desert town that belonged to the Judah tribe.” Sometimes David would say, “Oh, we attacked a town in the desert where the Jerahmeel clan lives” or “We attacked a town in the desert where the Kenites live.”
translation_verse: biza ye kɛ, “Nienwu a ɛnɛ bɛwuale bɛdwule a?” Devidi bua ye kɛ bɛhɔle Dwuda nyiakɛ nee Gyɛlamile abusua ne azɛlɛ zo anzɛɛ azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ Kinama de zolɛ la azo.

english_verse: That's why David killed everyone in the towns he attacked. He thought, “If I let any of them live, they might come to Gath and tell what I've really been doing.” David made these raids all the time he was in Philistia.
translation_verse: Devidi angyakyi nrenya ko anzɛɛ raalɛ ko bɔbɔ anyewɔzo. Saa tɛ ye zɔhane a anrɛɛ bɛ bie kɛzia kɛhɔ Gate kɛhɔbɔ Ekehye amaneɛ na bɛkɛha debie mɔɔ Devidi nee ye ɛlɔnema ne ɛyɛ la. Mekɛ tendenle ne mɔɔ Devidi lile wɔ Filisitia la ɛbɛla mɔɔ ɔbɔle la ɛne.

english_verse: But Achish trusted David and thought, “David's people must be furious with him. From now on he will have to take orders from me.”
translation_verse: Ekehye nyianle diedi wɔ Devidi anu na ɔhanle ɔhilele ɔ nwo kɛ, “Ɔdaye ye menli Yizilayɛma kyi ye kɔkɔ, yemɔti ɔbazonle me toonwo yeawu.”

english_verse: The Philistines went to Shunem and set up camp. Saul called the army of Israel together, and they set up their camp in Gilboa.
translation_verse: Filisitiama boɔboale bɛ nwo na bɛrayɛle azokoɛleɛ wɔ Hyunɛm. Sɔɔlo ɔdaye ɔboɔboale Yizilayɛ ɛlɔnema ne anloa na ɔrayɛle azokoɛleɛ wɔ Gelebowa Boka.

english_verse: Saul took one look at the Philistine army and started shaking with fear.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Sɔɔlo nwunle Filisitia ɛlɔnema ne somaa la, ɔ nwo mɔra dule,

english_verse: So he asked the Lord what to do. But the Lord would not answer, either in a dream or by a priest or a prophet.
translation_verse: na ɔbizale Ɛdɛnkɛma nwolɛ bie. Na Ɛdɛnkɛma ambua ye fee; yeanga ye ɛlalɛ bɔbɔ yɛɛ yeangile sɛkɛlɛneɛ biala na yeayɛ Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛma nrɛlaleɛ.

english_verse: Then Saul told his officers, “Find me a woman who can talk to the spirits of the dead. I'll go to her and find out what's going to happen.” His servants told him, “There's a woman at Endor who can talk to spirits of the dead.”
translation_verse: Akee Sɔɔlo zele ye sonvolɛma ne kɛ, “Bɛkpondɛ raalɛ mɔɔ tendɛ nwomenle nloa zo la bɛmaa mengɔ ɔ nwo abisa.” Sonvolɛma ne buale ye kɛ, “Raalɛ bie wɔ Ɛndɔ mɔɔ ɔbɔ mɔdenle a.”

english_verse: That night, Saul put on different clothing so nobody would recognize him. Then he and two of his men went to the woman, and asked, “Will you bring up the ghost of someone for us?”
translation_verse: Yemɔti Sɔɔlo hakyile ɔ nwo, ɔwulale adɛladeɛ ngakyile, ɔvale awozinli ɔwale ɔ nye na ɔ nee ye mgbanyima ne mɔ nwiɔ hɔle raalɛ ne ɛkɛ hɔzele ye kɛ, “Biza mɔwuamra na ka edwɛkɛ mɔɔ bazi la kile me. Fɛlɛ sonla ne mɔɔ menwɔbɔ ye duma la nwomenle maa me nee ye ɛdendɛ.”

english_verse: The woman said, “Why are you trying to trick me and get me killed? You know King Saul has killed everyone who talks to the spirits of the dead!”
translation_verse: Raalɛ ne zele ye kɛ, “Nɔhalɛ, ɛze debie mɔɔ Belemgbunli Sɔɔlo ɛyɛ la, yedu menli mɔɔ bɔ menli munzule nee menli mɔɔ tendɛ nwomenle nloa zo la wɔ maanle ye anu. Duzu ati a ɛkulo kɛ ɛto me agyiba na ɛmaa bɛku me ɛ?”

english_verse: Saul replied, “I swear by the living Lord that nothing will happen to you because of this.”
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo vale Ɛdɛnkɛma lile amonle kɛ, “Meka tease Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ ɛnrɛnyia ɛhye anwo ndeanlɛ biala.”

english_verse: “Who do you want me to bring up?” she asked. “Bring up the ghost of Samuel,” he answered.
translation_verse: Raalɛ ne bizale ye kɛ, “Nwane a menvɛlɛ ye memaa wɔ a?” Sɔɔlo zele kɛ, “Fɛlɛ Samoɛle.”

english_verse: When the woman saw Samuel, she screamed. Then she turned to Saul and said, “You've tricked me! You're the king!”
translation_verse: Raalɛ ne nwunle Samoɛle la, ɔdeanle nu kpole bie na ɔzele Sɔɔlo kɛ, “Duzu ati a wɔbɛlɛbɛla me zɛhae a? Se wɔmɔ a ɛle Belemgbunli Sɔɔlo!”

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Saul replied. “Just tell me what you see.” She answered, “I see a spirit rising up out of the ground.”
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne zele ye kɛ, “Mmasulo; duzu a wɔnwu ye a?” Raalɛ ne buale ye kɛ, “Menwu kɛ sunsum bie vi azɛlɛ ne anu ɛlɛfinde.”

english_verse: “What does it look like?” “It looks like an old man wearing a robe.” Saul knew it was Samuel, so he bowed down low.
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne bizale ye kɛ, “Kɛ ɔsi ɔde ɛ?” Raalɛ ne buale kɛ, “Nrenya akpanyima bie; ɔwula tɛladeɛ kpole bie.” Na Sɔɔlo nwunle kɛ Samoɛle ɔ, na ɔvale enililɛ ɔbɔle ɔ ti aze ɔmanle ye.

english_verse: “Why are you bothering me by bringing me up like this?” Samuel asked. “I'm terribly worried,” Saul answered. “The Philistines are about to attack me. God has turned his back on me and won't answer any more by prophets or by dreams. What should I do?”
translation_verse: Akee Samoɛle zele Sɔɔlo kɛ, “Duzu ati yɛɛ wɔgyegye me zɛhae wɔmaa mezia mera ɛke bieko ɛ?” Sɔɔlo buale ye kɛ, “Kɛkala, edwɛkɛ ɛdo me, ɔluakɛ Filisitiama ɛlɛfa konle aradoa me. Mebiza Nyamenle nwolɛ bie, na yeanga me ɛlalɛ yɛɛ yeammaa Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ bie ambua nwolɛ fee. Yemɔti yɛɛ mevɛlɛ wɔ a, amaa wɔaha mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ meyɛ la wɔahile me.”

english_verse: Samuel said: If the Lord has turned away from you and is now your enemy, don't ask me what to do.
translation_verse: Na Samoɛle zele kɛ, “Duzu ati a ɔwɔ kɛ ɛfɛlɛ me, wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma mumua ne ɛhakyi ɔ nzi ɛzi wɔ na yeyɛ wɔ kpɔvolɛ la a?

english_verse: I've already told you: The Lord has sworn to take the kingdom from you and give it to David. And that's just what he's doing!
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛyɛ mɔɔ ɔluale me nwo zo ɔhanle ɔhilele wɔ la. Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛlie belemgbunlililɛ ne ɛ sa nu yeva yemaa Devidi.

english_verse: When the Lord was angry with the Amalekites, he told you to destroy them, but you didn't do it. That's why the Lord is doing this to you.
translation_verse: Kɛmɔ wɔandie Ɛdɛnkɛma ane, wɔambɔ Amalɛke maanle ne, wɔanzɛkye nuhua debie biala la, yemɔti a ɛnɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛyɛ wɔ zɛhae a.

english_verse: Tomorrow the Lord will let the Philistines defeat Israel's army, then you and your sons will join me down here in the world of the dead.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma baye ɛdawɔ nee Yizilayɛ maanlema awula Filisitiama asa anu. Ɛhyema, ɛdawɔ nee ɛ mra mrenya ne mɔ baraboka me nwo. Ɛdɛnkɛma eza baye Yizilayɛ ɛlɔnema ne awula Filisitiama asa anu.”

english_verse: At once, Saul collapsed and lay stretched out on the floor, terrified at what Samuel had said. He was weak because he had not eaten anything since the day before.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Sɔɔlo dele Samoɛle edwɛkɛ ne la, ɛzulolɛ hanle ye na ɔpɛle ɔfinle; ɔ nwo golole ye, ɔluakɛ ɛnee alehyenlɛ ne nee aledwolɛ ne anu amuala ɔtɛdile ɛhwee.

english_verse: The woman came over to Saul, and when she saw that he was completely terrified, she said, “Your Majesty, I listened to you and risked my life to do what you asked.
translation_verse: Raalɛ ne hɔle Sɔɔlo anwo ɛkɛ ne na ɔnwunle kɛ ɛzulolɛ kpole ɛha ye, yemɔti ɔzele kɛ, “Nana, menvale me ngoane mendole nzeleba yɛɛ menyɛle mɔɔ ɛbizale me la a.

english_verse: Now please listen to me. Let me get you a little something to eat. It will give you strength for your walk back to camp.”
translation_verse: Yemɔti mɔɔ mebiza wɔ la, ɛdawɔ noko yɛ maa me. Maa membɔ akposi ekyi memaa wɔ na di debie maa ɛ nwo ɛgyinla wɔ na wɔahɔ.”

english_verse: “No, I won't eat!” But his officers and the woman kept on urging Saul, until he finally agreed. He got up off the floor and sat on the bed.
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo hɔsɔle ɔ ti na ɔzele kɛ, “Menrɛli debie.” Na ye sonvolɛma ne nee raalɛ ne kponle ye toonwo manle ɔkponlenle. Yemɔti ɔvi azɛlɛ ne anwo ɔdwazole ɔdɛnlanle ɛsokpa ne azo.

english_verse: At once the woman killed a calf that she had been fattening up. She cooked part of the meat and baked some thin bread.
translation_verse: Raalɛ ne lɛ ɛnlankɛ kyenlera ko. Ɔhunle ye ndɛndɛ, ɔvale esamo ɔfetele ye ndɛndɛ na ɔvale ɔdonle kpanwo mɔɔ mgbɔvonle ɛnle nu la.

english_verse: Then she served the food to Saul and his officers, who ate and left before daylight.
translation_verse: Ɔvale ɔmanle Sɔɔlo nee ye mgbanyima ne mɔ lile, na nɔe ne ala bɛhɔle.

english_verse: The Philistine army commanders were angry and shouted: Send David back to the town you gave him. We won't have him going into the battle with us. He could turn and fight against us! Saul would take David back as an officer if David brought him the heads of our soldiers.
translation_verse: Filisitia safohyenlema ne vale Ekehye anwo ɛya kpole na bɛzele ye kɛ, “Maa ɔzia ɔhɔ sua ne mɔɔ ɛvale ɛmanle ye la azo. Yɛ nee ye kɔ konle ne a, ɔnrɛyɛ boɛ. Saa konle ne kyele zolɛ na wɔannea a ɔkɛpɛ ɔ nwo ɔ nee yɛ kɛho. Ɔluakɛ adenle kpalɛ biala ɛnle ɛkɛ mɔɔ ɔkola ɔfa zolɛ ɔ nee ye belemgbunli ne yɛ ko kɛ ɛhye anu ala. Ɔpepɛ yɛ ti yeahɔ na ɔ nee ye belemgbunli ne bɛ avinli azɛ.

english_verse: The Israelites even dance and sing, “Saul has killed a thousand enemies; David has killed ten thousand!”
translation_verse: Tɛ Devidi ɛhye a bɛbɔ ye duma bɛto edwɛne bɛsi ɔ nloa agole kɛ, ‘Sɔɔlo ɛhu apenle, na Devidi ɛhu apenle apenle bulu, la ɔ?’ ”

english_verse: Achish called David over and said: I swear by the living Lord that you've been honest with me, and I want you to fight by my side. I don't think you've done anything wrong from the day you joined me until this very moment. But the other Philistine rulers don't want you to come along.
translation_verse: Belemgbunli Ekehye vɛlɛle Devidi na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Meka Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ wɔli nɔhalɛ wɔmaa me bɔkɔɔ. Ɔhale me ngome a anrɛɛ mese ɛmaa yɛhɔ konle ne, ɔluakɛ sumunli kɛ ɛ nee me radɛnlanle la, metɛnwunle ɛtane biala mɔɔ wɔyɛ me toonwo a yeradwu ɛnɛ demua ye a. Noko akee arelemgbunli mɔɔ ɛha la ɛnlie ɛndo nu kɛ ɛ nee yɛ kɛhɔ.

english_verse: Go on back home and try not to upset them.
translation_verse: Yemɔti sia kɔ sua nu anzonudwolɛ nu, amaa Filisitia arelemgbunli ne mɔ annyia ɛ nwo edwɛkɛ biala anga.”

english_verse: “But what have I done?” David asked. “Do you know of anything I've ever done that would keep me from fighting the enemies of my king?”
translation_verse: Na Devidi zele Ekehye kɛ, “Duzu ɛtane yɛɛ meyɛ a? Kɛmɔ ɛdawɔ wɔha la, sumunli kɛ me nee wɔ radɛnlanle la, saa ɛtɛnwunle ɛtane biala mɔɔ meyɛ la a, ɛnee duzu ati yɛɛ me nee me menli nee me belemgbunli ɛnrɛhɔ konle ne na menrɛho menrɛtia ye kpɔvolɛma ɛ?”

english_verse: Achish said: I believe that you're as good as an angel of God, but our army commanders have decided that you can't fight in this battle.
translation_verse: Na Ekehye buale ye kɛ, “Wɔ me nyunlu a ɛdi nɔhalɛ bɔkɔɔ kɛ Nyamenle soanvolɛ. Noko akee Filisitia safohyenlema ne se bɛ nee wɔ kɔ konle ne a, ɔnrɛyɛ boɛ.

english_verse: You and your troops will have to go back to the town I gave you. Get up and leave tomorrow morning as soon as it's light. I'm pleased with you, so don't let any of this bother you.
translation_verse: Yemɔti, nwonlomɔ anrɛɛ dwazo ndɛ, saa maanle nu tete ala a, fa menli mɔɔ nee wɔ lua la sia kɔ.”

english_verse: David and his men got up early in the morning and headed back toward Philistia, while the Philistines left for Jezreel.
translation_verse: Yemɔti nwonlomɔ mangyee ne ala Devidi nee ye ɛlɔnema ne ziale hɔle Gyɛzɛli.

english_verse: It took David and his men three days to reach Ziklag. But while they had been away, the Amalekites had been raiding in the desert around there. They had attacked Ziklag, burned it to the ground,
translation_verse: Devidi nee ye ɛlɔnema ne zile nu la ye kenle nsa ne azo yɛɛ bɛdwule Zekelage a, na bɛnwunle kɛ Amalɛkema ɛrava Dwuda nyiakɛ maanle ne na bɛbɔ Zekelage, bɛyela sua bɔdenle ne,

english_verse: When David and his men came to Ziklag, they saw the burned-out ruins and learned that their families had been taken captive.
translation_verse: Devidi nee ye ɛlɔnema ne ranwunle kɛ bɛyela sua ne na bɛhye bɛ mraalɛ ne mɔ, bɛ mra mrenya nee mraalɛ bɛhɔ la,

english_verse: They started crying and kept it up until they were too weak to cry any more.
translation_verse: bɛdukuele nuhua bɛzunle toonwo bɛ ɛnwomenle wiele bɔkɔɔ.

english_verse: David was desperate. His soldiers were so upset over what had happened to their sons and daughters that they were thinking about stoning David to death. But he felt the Lord God giving him strength,
translation_verse: Edwɛkɛ dole Devidi, ɔluakɛ ye menli ne yɛle kɛ bɛsi ye awolɛ, ɔboalekɛ awie biala ɛlɛdi nyane kpole kɛ bɛhye ɔ ye nee ɔ mra bɛhɔ a. Na Devidi Ɛdɛnkɛma ye Nyamenle ne manle ye akɛnrazilɛ.

english_verse: and he said to the priest, “Abiathar, let's ask God what to do.” Abiathar brought everything he needed to get answers from God, and he went over to David.
translation_verse: Devidi zele sɛlɛvolɛ Abayata, Ahemɛlɛke ara nrenya ne kɛ, “Fa yifɔdo ne bɛla.” Na Abayata vale yifɔdo ne rɛlɛle Devidi.

english_verse: Then David asked the Lord, “Should I go after the people who raided our town? Can I catch up with them?” “Go after them,” the Lord answered. “You will catch up with them, and you will rescue your families.”
translation_verse: Na Devidi bizale Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ, “Memkpo nwule ne mɔ ɔ? Menwɔhola bɛ kye ɔ?” Ɛdɛnkɛma buale kɛ, “Foa bɛ, ɛbahye bɛ na wɔalie menli mɔɔ bɛhye bɛ la.”

english_verse: Some of David's men found an Egyptian out in a field and took him to David. They gave the Egyptian some bread, and he ate it. Then they gave him a drink of water,
translation_verse: Ɛlɔnema mɔɔ nee Devidi lua la nwunle Yigyibitinli bie wɔ fienemgbole ne anu na bɛvale ye bɛrɛlɛle Devidi. Bɛmanle ye kpanwo ɔlile, bɛmanle ye nzule ɔnlonle,

english_verse: some dried figs, and two handfuls of raisins. This was the first time in three days he had tasted food or water. Now he felt much better.
translation_verse: bɛmanle ye keeki mɔɔ bɛva feege ma bɛyɛ la, yɛɛ vanye ma welera aziakɛ nwiɔ. Mɔɔ ɔlile ɔwiele la, ɔ nwo gyinlanle ye, ɔluakɛ ɛnee kenle kɔkɔlɛ nsa, ɔtɛdile ɛhwee na yeanlo nzule.

english_verse: “Who is your master?” David asked. “And where do you come from?” “I'm from Egypt,” the young man answered. “I'm the servant of an Amalekite, but he left me here three days ago because I was sick.
translation_verse: Devidi bizale ye kɛ, “Ɛ menle a le nwane? Ɛvi nienwu?” Ɔbuale kɛ, “Mele Yigyibitinli, yɛɛ mele Amalɛkenli bie sonvolɛ. Me menle gyakyile me hɔle la ɛnɛ le kenle nsa, ɔboalekɛ me nwo dole me.

english_verse: We had attacked some towns in the desert where the Cherethites live, in the area that belongs to Judah, and in the desert where the Caleb clan lives. And we burned down Ziklag.”
translation_verse: Yɛhɔvale Kɛlɛte maanle ne mɔɔ wɔ Dwuda nyiakɛ la anu ninyɛne kɔsɔɔti nee Kalɛbe abusua ne maanle ne anu debie biala, yɛɛ yɛyelale Zekelage.”

english_verse: “Will you take me to those Amalekites?” David asked. “Yes, I will, if you promise with God as a witness that you won't kill me or hand me over to my master.”
translation_verse: Devidi bizale ye kɛ, “Ɛ nee me kɛhɔ nwule ɛhye mɔ anwo lɔ ɔ?” Yigyibitinli ne buale ye kɛ, “Ka Nyamenle kɛ ɛnrɛhu me yɛɛ ɛnrɛye me ɛnrɛmaa me menle ne, na me nee wɔ kɛhɔ.”

english_verse: He led David to the Amalekites. They were eating and drinking everywhere, celebrating because of what they had taken from Philistia and Judah.
translation_verse: Na ɔlile Devidi anyunlu ɔ nee ye hɔle. Menli ne mɔ ɛde ɛkponde ɛleka mɔɔ bɛwɔ la amuala, bɛlɛdi, bɛanlo na bɛlɛdi wulupe, bɛ nye ɛlie wɔ anwonyia mɔɔ bɛwua bɛvi Filisitia nee Dwuda la anwo.

english_verse: David attacked just before sunrise the next day and fought until sunset. Four hundred Amalekites rode away on camels, but they were the only ones who escaped.
translation_verse: Kenle ko ne aleɛbahye ne, Devidi hɔtetale bɛ, ɔ nee bɛ honle ɔhunle bɛ kɔsɔɔti, ɔhale menli ɛya nna mɔɔ lɛ afunlumu na bɛnriandile la.

english_verse: David rescued his two wives and everyone else the Amalekites had taken from Ziklag.
translation_verse: Debie biala mɔɔ Amalɛkema ne wuale la, Devidi asa hanle bɛ muala, na ɔliele ye mraalɛ nwiɔ ne nee awie biala ɔvile munzule nu.

english_verse: No one was missing—young or old, sons or daughters. David brought back everything that had been stolen,
translation_verse: Debie biala fee amminli. Devidi liele ye menli ne mɔ mraalɛ ne mɔ, bɛ mra mrenya nee mraalɛ nee debie biala mɔɔ Amalɛkema ne wuale la.

english_verse: including their livestock. David also took the sheep and cattle that the Amalekites had with them, but he kept these separate from the others. Everyone agreed that these would be David's reward.
translation_verse: Devidi eza liele mboane, nlankɛ, yɛɛ nyɛmoa kɔsɔɔti. Ye menli ne mɔ hanle bɛ lile bɛ nyunlu na bɛzele kɛ, “Ɛhye mɔ kɔsɔɔti le Devidi ɛdeɛ.”

english_verse: Some of David's men were good-for-nothings, and they said, “Those men didn't go with us to the battle, so they don't get any of the things we took back from the Amalekites. Let them take their wives and children and go!”
translation_verse: Menli amumuyɛ nee agbamgbanvolɛ bie mɔ mɔɔ nee Devidi hɔle la zele kɛ, “Bɛ nee yɛ angɔ la ati, debie biala mɔɔ yɛnyianle nee bɛ ninyɛne bɔbɔ mɔɔ yɛza menli ne mɔ yɛlie la, yɛnrɛmaa bɛ. Mɔɔ yɛyɛ yɛamaa bɛ la a le kɛ, awie biala ɛva ɔ ye nee ɔ mra na ɔhɔ.”

english_verse: But David said: My friends, don't be so greedy with what the Lord has given us! The Lord protected us and gave us victory over the people who attacked.
translation_verse: Devidi zele bɛ kɛ, “Me mediema, bɛmmayɛ ɛhye wɔ debie mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛva ɛmaa yɛ la anwo; yezinza yɛ na yeye nwule ne mɔ mɔɔ rawuale yɛ la yemaa yɛ.

english_verse: Who would pay attention to you, anyway? Soldiers who stay behind to guard the camp get as much as those who go into battle.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ bɛlɛka la awie biala nee bɛ ɛnrɛyɛ adwenle. Mɔɔ ɛlɔnenli biala mɔɔ hɔle konle ne bie la kɛnyia ye la, zɔhane ala yɛɛ mɔɔ zinzale ninyɛne la ɔwɔ kɛ nyia ye a. Ɔwɔ kɛ bɛkyɛ ye pɛpɛ.”

english_verse: David made this a law for Israel, and it has been the same ever since.
translation_verse: Devidi lile ɛhye anwo mɛla na ɔvi mekɛ ne anu mɔɔ ɛradwu ɛnɛ la kɛ ɔde ala la ɛne wɔ Yizilayɛ maanle ne anu.

english_verse: David went back to Ziklag with everything they had taken from the Amalekites. He sent some of these things as gifts to his friends who were leaders of Judah, and he told them, “We took these things from the Lord's enemies. Please accept them as a gift.”
translation_verse: Devidi ziale hɔle Zekelage la, ɔvale ninyɛne mɔɔ bɛnyianle bɛ wɔ konle ne anu la bie ɔhɔmanle ɔ gɔnwo mɔ Dwuda mgbanyima na ɔzele kɛ, “Ninyɛne mɔɔ yɛnyianle bɛ wɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma kpɔvolɛma ne mɔ lɔ la bɛdabɛ noko bɛ ahyɛlɛdeɛ ɛne.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, the Philistines were fighting Israel at Mount Gilboa. Israel's soldiers ran from the Philistines, and many of them were killed.
translation_verse: Filisitiama nee Yizilayɛma honle wɔ Gelebowa Boka. Bɛhunle Yizilayɛma somaa ne ala wɔ ɛkɛ. Mɔɔ hale la nee Belemgbunli Sɔɔlo nee ɔ mra mrenya ne mɔ nriandile.

english_verse: The Philistines closed in on Saul and his sons, and they killed his sons Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua.
translation_verse: Filisitiama voanle bɛ hɔhyele bɛ na bɛhunle Sɔɔlo amra mrenya nsa ne, Dwɔnatan, Abenadabe, yɛɛ Malekehyua.

english_verse: The fighting was fierce around Saul, and he was badly wounded by enemy arrows.
translation_verse: Konle ne hyelele Sɔɔlo anwo zo, na ɛda wɔle ye manle ɔbodale kpole bie.

english_verse: Saul told the soldier who carried his weapons, “Kill me with your sword! I don't want these worthless Philistines to torture and make fun of me.” But the soldier was afraid to kill him. Saul then took out his own sword; he stuck the blade into his stomach, and fell on it.
translation_verse: Yemɔti ɔzele kpavolɛ ne mɔɔ soa ye konle ninyɛne ne la kɛ, “Twe wɔ dadeɛ ne ku me, amaa Filisitiama mɔɔ ɛnze Nyamenle la ambangolo me nwo, angu me.” Ɛzulolɛ hanle kpavolɛ ne, yemɔti yeangola ye ku. Sɔɔlo yele ye dadeɛ ne na ɔdaye ɔ ngome ɔdɔle zolɛ ɔhunle ɔ nwo.

english_verse: When the soldier knew that Saul was dead, he killed himself in the same way.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ kpavolɛ ne nwunle kɛ Sɔɔlo ɛwu la, ɔdaye noko ɔyele ye dadeɛ ne ɔdɔle zolɛ ɔ nee Sɔɔlo wule.

english_verse: Saul was dead, his three sons were dead, and the soldier who carried his weapons was dead. They and all his soldiers died on that same day.
translation_verse: Ɛnee kɛ Sɔɔlo, ɔ mra mrenya nsa ne nee kpavolɛ ne mɔɔ soa Sɔɔlo konle ninyɛne ne la zile wule la ɛne. Sɔɔlo ɛlɔnema ne kɔsɔɔti wule konle ne anu kenle ko ne.

english_verse: The Israelites on the other side of Jezreel Valley and the other side of the Jordan learned that Saul and his sons were dead. They saw that the Israelite army had run away. So they ran away too, and the Philistines moved into the towns the Israelites had left behind.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Yizilayɛma mɔɔ wɔ Gyɛzɛli Bɔnza ne anzi lɔ mɔɔ di kɔ Azule Dwɔdan aduduleɛ la dele kɛ Yizilayɛ ɛlɔnema ne ɛgua ɛbɔ nu na bɛhu Sɔɔlo nee ɔ mra ne mɔ la, bɛvile bɛ azua ne mɔ azo bɛguale ɛbɔ nu. Na Filisitiama radɛnlanle azua ne mɔ azo.

english_verse: The day after the battle, when the Philistines returned to the battlefield to take the weapons of the dead Israelite soldiers, they found Saul and his three sons lying dead on Mount Gilboa.
translation_verse: Bɛhonle bɛwiele na ye alehyenlɛ nu, Filisitiama hɔle kɛ bɛkawua avunli ne mɔ anwo ninyɛne. Bɛnwunle Sɔɔlo nee ɔ mra nsa ne mɔ avunli wɔ Gelebowa Boka.

english_verse: The Philistines cut off Saul's head and pulled off his armor. Then they put his armor in the temple of the goddess Astarte, and they nailed his body to the city wall of Beth-Shan. They also sent messengers everywhere in Philistia to spread the good news in the temples of their idols and among their people.
translation_verse: Akee bɛvale ye konle ninyɛne ne mɔ bɛhɔguale bɛ bozonle raalɛ Asetate ɛzonlenlɛ sua ne anu. Bɛbɔle ye sonlabaka ne pɛlɛko bɛmetanle Bɛte Hyan suakpole bane ne anwo.

english_verse: The people who lived in Jabesh in Gilead heard what the Philistines had done to Saul's body.
translation_verse: Gyeebɛhyema mɔɔ wɔ Geleade la dele mɔɔ Filisitiama ɛva ɛyɛ Sɔɔlo la,

english_verse: So one night, some brave men from Jabesh went to Beth-Shan. They took down the bodies of Saul and his sons, then brought them back to Jabesh and burned them.
translation_verse: bɛ nuhua mrenya katakyiema zile nu nɔɔzo hɔle Bɛte Hyan. Bɛyeyele Sɔɔlo nee ɔ mra ne mɔ avunli wɔ bane ne anwo, bɛ nee bɛ rale Gyeebɛhye na bɛyelale bɛ ɛkɛ ne.

english_verse: They buried the bones under a small tree in Jabesh, and for seven days, they went without eating to show their sorrow.
translation_verse: Akee bɛsesale bɛ mbowule ne mɔ na bɛziele bɛ wɔ “tamaleseke” baka bie mɔɔ gyi sua ne azo la abo, na bɛhyele ɛhɔne kenle nsuu.

english_verse: Saul was dead. Meanwhile, David had defeated the Amalekites and returned to Ziklag.
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo ewule ne anzi, Devidi hɔlile Amalɛkema anwo zo konim, ɔhunle bɛ bie mɔ dɔɔnwo kpalɛ na ɔziale ɔrale Zekelage ɔralile kenle nwiɔ wɔ ɛkɛ.

english_verse: Three days later, a soldier came from Saul's army. His clothes were torn, and dirt was on his head. He went to David and knelt down in front of him.
translation_verse: Ye kenle nsa ne azo, nrenya bie vi Sɔɔlo konle azokoɛleɛ ne rale. Ɔkile ye nyane mɔɔ ɔlɛdi la, ɛnee yesuosua ye tɛladeɛ ne mɔɔ ɔwula la anu na yeva ndɛtɛlɛ yeyɛ ɔ ti zo. Ɔradwule Devidi anyunlu la, ɔdule ɔdɔle ɔ gyakɛ anu ɔbizale ye ahye.

english_verse: David asked, “Where did you come from?” The man answered, “From Israel's army. I barely escaped with my life.”
translation_verse: Devidi bizale ye kɛ, “Ɛvi nienwu a wɔra a?” Nrenya ne buale ye kɛ, “Mevi Yizilayɛma azokoɛleɛ ne a menriandi mera a.”

english_verse: “Who won the battle?” David asked. The man said, “Our army turned and ran, but many were wounded and died. Even King Saul and his son Jonathan are dead.”
translation_verse: Devidi bizale ye kɛ, “Kɛ konle ne zile wiele ye ɛ? Ka kile me.” Nrenya ne buale kɛ, “Yɛ ɛlɔnema ne ɛgua ɛbɔ nu, yɛɛ dɔɔnwo noko ɛho ɛdɔ. Sɔɔlo nee ɔ ra Dwɔnatan noko ɛwu.”

english_verse: David asked, “How do you know Saul and Jonathan are dead?”
translation_verse: Devidi bizale kpavolɛ ne mɔɔ rabɔle amaneɛ ne la kɛ, “Kɛ ɛzile ɛnwunle kɛ Sɔɔlo nee ɔ ra Dwɔnatan ɛwu ɛ?”

english_verse: The young man replied: I was on Mount Gilboa and saw King Saul leaning on his spear. The enemy's war chariots and cavalry were closing in on him.
translation_verse: Kpavolɛ ne buale kɛ, “Ɔrale ye kɛ ɛnee mewɔ Gelebowa Boka, na menwunle kɛ Sɔɔlo hisa ye atwɛ ne na kpɔvolɛma ne konle ehwili ne mɔ nee menli mɔɔ ka mgbɔnwɔ la ɛkpumgbu ye kpalɛ.

english_verse: When he turned around and saw me, he called me over. I went and asked what he wanted.
translation_verse: Ɔdole ɔ nye na ɔnwunle me la, ɔvɛlɛle me. Menzele ye kɛ, ‘Medame ɛ, mera.’

english_verse: Saul asked me, “Who are you?” “An Amalekite,” I answered.
translation_verse: Ɔbizale me kɛ, ‘Na ɛdawɔ nwane ɔ?’ Mengilele nu mengilele ye kɛ mele Amalɛkenli.

english_verse: Then he said, “Kill me! I'm dying, and I'm in terrible pain.”
translation_verse: Na ɔzele me kɛ, ‘Twe bikye me na ku me. Meboda kpole somaa; me nye gyi ɛbolɔ.’

english_verse: So I killed him. I knew he was too badly wounded to live much longer. Then I took his crown and his arm-band, and I brought them to you, Your Majesty. Here they are.
translation_verse: Yemɔti mendwenle membikyele ye na mengunle ye, ɔboalekɛ menwunle ye wienyi kɛ ɔnle lɔ ɔnde kpɔkɛ bieko. Mendule ye belemgbunli kyɛlɛ ne, menyele ɔ sa akɔme nu ngɛba ne yɛɛ melɛfa mearɛlɛ wɔ a.”

english_verse: At once, David and his soldiers tore their clothes in sorrow.
translation_verse: Devidi vale nyane ngome suosuanle ye tɛladeɛ ne anu, na ye menli mɔɔ nee ye lua la yɛle zɔhane ala.

english_verse: They cried all day long and would not eat anything. Everyone was sad because Saul, his son Jonathan, and many of the Lord's people had been killed in the battle.
translation_verse: Bɛlile nyane, bɛhyele ɛhɔne kenle ko ne na bɛzunle Sɔɔlo nee ɔ ra Dwɔnatan nee Ɛdɛnkɛma menli Yizilayɛma kɛ bɛhu bɛ dɔɔnwo wɔ konle ne anu a.

english_verse: David asked the young man, “Where is your home?” The man replied, “My father is an Amalekite, but we live in Israel.”
translation_verse: Akee Devidi bizale kpavolɛ ne mɔɔ rabɔle amaneɛ ne la kɛ, “Ɛvi nienwu?” Kpavolɛ ne buale kɛ, “Mele Amalɛkenli bie ara, na kɛkala, mede maanle ye anu.”

english_verse: David said to him, “Why weren't you afraid to kill the Lord's chosen king? And you even told what you did. It's your own fault that you're going to die!” Then David told one of his soldiers, “Come here and kill this man!” David Sings in Memory of Saul
translation_verse: Akee Devidi zele ye kɛ, “Wɔ mogya ɛgua ɛdawɔ ɛ ngome ɛ ti zo, ɔluakɛ ɛdawɔ ɛ nloa ɛli daselɛ ɛtia wɔ kɛ wɔhu sonla mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛkpokpa ye nwole la.”

english_verse: David sang a song in memory of Saul and Jonathan,
translation_verse: Devidi dole awolɛyelɛ edwɛne ɛhye vale zunle Sɔɔlo nee ɔ ra Dwɔnatan,

english_verse: Israel, your famous hero lies dead on the hills, and your mighty warriors have fallen!
translation_verse: “Yɛ mgbanyima ɛwu ɛgua Yizilayɛ awoka zo! Yɛ ɛlɔne nu katakyiema ɛho ɛdɔ!

english_verse: Don't tell it in Gath or spread the news on the streets of Ashkelon. The godless Philistine women will be happy and jump for joy.
translation_verse: Bɛmmabɔ ye nolo wɔ Gate, anzɛɛ Ahyekɛlɔn mgbata ne mɔ azo. Anrɛɛ Filisitia mraalɛ kɛli fɛlɛko, anrɛɛ mraalɛ mɔɔ ɛnze Nyamenle la anye kɛlie.

english_verse: Don't let dew or rain fall on the hills of Gilboa. Don't let its fields grow offerings for God. There the warriors' shields were smeared with mud, and Saul's own shield was left unpolished.
translation_verse: “Ezule anzɛɛ ɛbɔlɛ mmatɔ Gelebowa awoka zo; ye azɛlɛ ɛhwie dahuu! Ɔluakɛ katakyiema enyinlike gua ɛkɛ ne anyiemgba nu; Sɔɔlo enyinlike ɔ, ɛnɛ awie ɛnvɔ ye nwole.

english_verse: The arrows of Jonathan struck, and warriors died. The sword of Saul cut the enemy apart.
translation_verse: Dwɔnatan ɛda nloa yɛ nla, Sɔɔlo konle dadeɛ ɛnze anwunvɔne, ɔka mgbolema ɔgua, ɔku kpɔvolɛma.

english_verse: It was easy to love Saul and Jonathan. Together in life, together in death, they were faster than eagles and stronger than lions.
translation_verse: “Sɔɔlo nee Dwɔnatan, bɛ ɛhulolɛ yɛ nwanwane; bɛde aze la bɛle ko, bɛ ewule nu, bɛ avinli antete, bɛ nwo ndɛne tɛla kɔleɛ, bɛ anwosesebɛ tɛla awenade.

english_verse: Women of Israel, cry for Saul. He brought you fine red cloth and jewelry made of gold.
translation_verse: “Yizilayɛ mraalɛ, bɛzu Sɔɔlo! Yemɔ mɔɔ ɔhedale bɛ ndakpa, na ɔvale mgbɔba ɔzieziele bɛ a.

english_verse: Our warriors have fallen in the heat of battle, and Jonathan lies dead on the hills of Gilboa.
translation_verse: “Ɛlɔne nu katakyiema ɛho ɛdɔ, bɛhunle bɛ wɔ konle nu. Dwɔnatan ɛwu la awoka avinli.

english_verse: Jonathan, I miss you most! I loved you like a brother. You were truly loyal to me, more faithful than a wife to her husband.
translation_verse: “Mesu wɔ, me diema Dwɔnatan; ɛsonle bolɛ ɛmaa me somaa! Ɛhulole me ɛmanle ɔyɛle nwanwane, ɔdɛlale mraalɛ ɛhulolɛ bɔbɔ.

english_verse: Our warriors have fallen, and their weapons are destroyed.
translation_verse: Ɛlɔne nu katakyiema ɛho ɛdɔ, bɛ konle ninyɛne ɛyɛ mgbane!”

english_verse: Later, David asked the Lord, “Should I go back to one of the towns of Judah?” The Lord answered, “Yes.” David asked, “Which town should I go to?” “Go to Hebron,” the Lord replied.
translation_verse: Ɛhye anzi, Devidi bizale Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ, “Mengɔ Dwuda azuamgbole ne mɔ bie azo ɔ?” Ɛdɛnkɛma zele ye kɛ, “Kɔ.” Devidi bizale kɛ, “Boni azo a mengɔ a?” Ɛdɛnkɛma buale ye kɛ, “Kɔ Hibulɔn.”

english_verse: David went to Hebron with his two wives, Ahinoam and Abigail. Ahinoam was from Jezreel, and Abigail was the widow of Nabal from Carmel.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Devidi nee ye mraalɛ nwiɔ ne, Ahenoam mɔɔ vi Gyɛzɛli yɛɛ Abegeli mɔɔ anrɛɛ Neebale mɔɔ vi Kamɛle mɔɔ ɛha ɛleka bie la gya ye la hɔle Hibulɔn.

english_verse: David also told his men and their families to come and live in the villages near Hebron.
translation_verse: Devidi vale ye ɛlɔnema ne, bɛ mraalɛ nee bɛ awuke nu amra kɔsɔɔti nee bɛ nwo ninyɛne, ɔ nee bɛ hɔle Hibulɔn.

english_verse: David sent messengers to tell them: The Lord bless you! You were kind enough to bury Saul your ruler,
translation_verse: ɔzoanle ɔmanle bɛhɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛyila bɛ kɛ bɛli nɔhalɛ ɛhye bɛmaa bɛ Belemgbunli Sɔɔlo na bɛzie ye a.

english_verse: and I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you. I will be your friend because of what you have done.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛhile ye ɛhulolɛ kpole ne nee ye kpalɛyɛlɛ ne wɔ bɛ nwo zo. Ɛhye mɔɔ bɛyɛ la ati, medame noko mebayɛ bɛ boɛ.

english_verse: Saul is dead, but the tribe of Judah has made me their king. So be strong and have courage. Ishbosheth Becomes King of Israel
translation_verse: Bɛgyinla kpundii na bɛmia bɛ nwo. Bɛ Belemgbunli Sɔɔlo ɛwu, na Dwudama ɛzie me belemgbunli.” Bɛzie Yehyebɔhyɛte Yizilayɛ belemgbunli

english_verse: Abner the son of Ner had been the general of Saul's army. He took Saul's son Ishbosheth across the Jordan River to Mahanaim
translation_verse: Nɛɛ ara nrenya Abenɛɛ mɔɔ nea Sɔɔlo ɛlɔnema ne anwo zo la ɛva Sɔɔlo ara nrenya Yehyebɔhyɛte ɛnriandi ɛhɔpɛ Azule Dwɔdan ne ɛhɔ Meehaneeyem;

english_verse: and made him king of Israel, including the areas of Gilead, Asher, Jezreel, Ephraim, and Benjamin.
translation_verse: na yehɔzie ye Geleade, Ahya, Gyɛzɛli, Yifelaem, Bɛngyaman nee Yizilayɛ maanle ne kɔsɔɔti belemgbunli.

english_verse: and he ruled from Hebron for seven and a half years. The War between David and Ishbosheth
translation_verse: na ɔdɛnlanle Hibulɔn ɔziele Dwuda ɛvolɛ nsuu nee foa. Yizilayɛ nee Dwuda konle ne

english_verse: One day, Abner and the soldiers of Ishbosheth left Mahanaim and went to Gibeon.
translation_verse: Nɛɛ ara Abenɛɛ nee Sɔɔlo ara Yehyebɔhyɛte mgbanyima ne mɔ vi Meehaneeyem hɔle Gebɛyɔn.

english_verse: Meanwhile, Joab the son of Zeruiah was leading David's soldiers, and the two groups met at the pool in Gibeon. Abner and his men sat down on one side of the pool, while Joab and his men sat on the other side.
translation_verse: Dwowabe mɔɔ ɔ nli a le Zɛluaya la nee Devidi mgbanyima ne mɔ noko hɔyiale bɛ wɔ Gebɛyɔn nzubula ne azo na bɛdɛnlanle aze. Ekpunli ko wɔ nzubula ne anzi foa ko yɛɛ ekpunli ko noko wɔ ye foa ko.

english_verse: Abner yelled to Joab, “Let's get some of our best soldiers to stand up and fight each other!” Joab agreed,
translation_verse: Abenɛɛ zele Dwowabe kɛ, “Maa yɛmaa yɛ mgbavolɛ ne bie mɔ ɛraho ye menli nwiɔ nwiɔ, ko ɛvi wɔ ekpunli ne anu na ko noko ɛvi me ekpunli ye anu na yɛnlea.” Dwowabe buale kɛ, “Maa bɛrɛla.”

english_verse: and twelve of Ishbosheth's men from the tribe of Benjamin got up to fight twelve of David's men.
translation_verse: Yemɔti menli bulu nee nwiɔ ragyinlanle Yehyebɔhyɛte nee Bɛngyaman mbusua ne agyakɛ anu, yɛɛ menli bulu nee nwiɔ noko vi Devidi afoa nu vindele.

english_verse: They grabbed each other by the hair and stabbed each other in the side with their daggers. They all died right there! That's why the place in Gibeon is called “Field of Daggers.”
translation_verse: Bɛgyinlanle ye nwiɔ nwiɔ, ko biala nee ye sonla, na akee bɛbɔle ye zo. Ko biala zɔle ɔ gɔnwo ati na ɔvale ye konle dadeɛ ne ɔwɔle ɔ nvenle. Na bɛdabɛ menli abulanwiɔ nee nna ne, bɛgulule nu bɛguale aze bɛwule. Yemɔti Gebɛyɔn ɛleka zɔhane, bɛfɛlɛ ye “Dadeɛ Azɛlɛ.”

english_verse: Then everyone started fighting. Both sides fought very hard, but David's soldiers defeated Abner and the soldiers of Israel.
translation_verse: Kenle ko ne konle ne yɛle ɛzulolɛ. Devidi ɛlɔnema ne lile Abenɛɛ nee Yizilayɛ ɛlɔnema ne anwo zo konim.

english_verse: Zeruiah's three sons were there: Joab, Abishai, and Asahel. Asahel could run as fast as a deer in an open field,
translation_verse: Ɛnee Zɛluaya amra mrenya nsa ne, Dwowabe, Abehyae nee Asahɛle wɔ ɛkɛ ne. Asahɛle anwo yɛ ndɛ tɛla ɛhoayelɛ nu kɛtɛboɛ.

english_verse: When Abner turned and saw him, he said, “Is that you, Asahel?” Asahel answered, “Yes it is.”
translation_verse: Abenɛɛ dole ɔ nye ɔ nzi na ɔhanle kɛ, “Asahɛle, wɔmɔ ɛhye ɔ?” Na ɔbuale ye kɛ, “Ɛhɛe, medame ɛ!”

english_verse: Abner said, “There are soldiers all around. Stop chasing me and fight one of them! Kill him and take his clothes and weapons for yourself.” But Asahel refused to stop.
translation_verse: Abenɛɛ zele ye kɛ, “Mmafoa me ko; to ɛ nye fema anzɛɛ bɛne zo na kye ɛlɔnema ne mɔ ko na sa ye die debie biala mɔɔ ɔlɛ la.” Noko Asahɛle angyakyi ye ɛvoanlɛ.

english_verse: Abner said, “If you don't turn back, I'll have to kill you! Then I could never face your brother Joab again.”
translation_verse: Abenɛɛ eza zele Asahɛle kɛ, “Mmafoa me ko; duzu ati a ɛgyegye me wɔamaa meahu wɔ a? Kɛ ɔkɛyɛ na meahola ɛ diema Dwowabe anyunlu nea ɛ?”

english_verse: But Asahel would not turn back, so Abner struck him in the stomach with the back end of his spear. The spear went all the way through and came out of his back. Asahel fell down and died. Everyone who saw Asahel lying dead just stopped and stood still.
translation_verse: Noko Asahɛle amkponle na ɔvoanle Abenɛɛ ndinlizo. Abenɛɛ dole ye atwɛ ne abo ne ɔ nzi wɔle Asahɛle akunlu manle atwɛ ne vindele ɔ nzi. Asahɛle dɔle aze na ɔwule. Menli mɔɔ rale ɛleka mɔɔ Asahɛle honle dɔle la gyinlanle ɛkɛ ne koonwu.

english_verse: But Joab and Abishai went after Abner. Finally, about sunset, they came to the hill of Ammah, not far from Giah on the road to Gibeon Desert.
translation_verse: Na Dwowabe nee Abehyae bɛdabɛ bɛbelele bɛzile Abenɛɛ zo, na mɔɔ ɔka ekyii na sɛnzɛne ne adɔ la, bɛdwule Amaa boka ne mɔɔ wɔ Gaya aduduleɛ wɔ Gebɛyɔn fienemgbole nu adenle zo la azo.

english_verse: Abner brought the men of Benjamin together in one group on top of a hill, and they got ready to fight.
translation_verse: Bɛngyaman abusua ekpunli ne anu amra boɔboale bɛ nloa zuanle Abenɛɛ anzi, bɛyɛle ɛlɔne ko na bɛhɔvole boka bie azo.

english_verse: Abner shouted to Joab, “Aren't we ever going to stop killing each other? Don't you know that the longer we keep on doing this, the worse it's going to be when it's all over? When are you going to order your men to stop chasing their own relatives?”
translation_verse: Akee Abenɛɛ deanle nu vɛlɛle Dwowabe na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Anzɛɛ ɔnle kɛ konle dadeɛ ne da koonwu ɔ? Anzɛɛ ɛnze kɛ konle nzi lɛ ɛkpɔlɛ ɔ? Kenlenzu yɛɛ ɛkɛmaa wɔ ɛlɔnema ne kɛgyakyi bɛ mediema ne mɔ mgbaliko ɛdulɛ a?”

english_verse: Joab shouted back, “I swear by the living God, if you hadn't spoken, my men would have chased their relatives all night!”
translation_verse: Na Dwowabe zele kɛ, “Meka tease Nyamenle ne kɛ, saa wɔanga ɛ nloa edwɛkɛ a anrɛɛ me ɛlɔnema ne badu mediema ne mɔ mgbaliko toonwo ɛhyema nwonlomɔ.”

english_verse: Joab took his trumpet and blew the signal for his soldiers to stop chasing the soldiers of Israel. At once, the fighting stopped.
translation_verse: Akee Dwowabe wule aweɛne tendenle nu na ɛlɔnema ne gyakyile Yizilayɛma mgbaliko ɛdulɛ yɛɛ bɛ nee bɛ ango bieko.

english_verse: Abner and his troops marched through the Jordan River valley all that night. Then they crossed the river and marched all morning until they arrived back at Mahanaim.
translation_verse: Aledwolɛ ne kɔsɔɔti Abenɛɛ nee ye ɛlɔnema ne diale vale Dwɔdan Bɔnza hɔpɛle Azule Dwɔdan ne. Alehyenlɛ ne anu eza bɛdiale toonwo na nzinlii bɛradwule Meehaneeyem.

english_verse: As soon as Joab stopped chasing Abner, he got David's troops together and counted them. There were
translation_verse: Dwowabe gyakyile Abenɛɛ ɛvoanlɛ, na mɔɔ bɛboɔboale menli ne anloa la, saa ɛye Asahɛle nu a, ɛnee Devidi ɛlɔnema ne mɔɔ ɛmboka nwo la le bulu nee ngɔnla.

english_verse: Joab and his troops carried Asahel's body to Bethlehem and buried him in the family burial place. Then they marched all night and reached Hebron before sunrise.
translation_verse: Dwowabe nee ɔ sa zo ne mɔ vale Asahɛle funli ne na bɛziele ye wɔ ɔ ze nla ne anu wɔ Bɛtelɛhɛm. Bɛdiale nɔe ne toonwo mɔɔ aleɛ kahye la ɛnee bɛwɔ Hibulɔn.

english_verse: As the war went on between the families of David and Saul, Abner was gaining more power than ever in Saul's family.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Devidi ɛlɔnema ne nee Sɔɔlo ɛlɔnema ne konle ne anu yɛle se la, Abenɛɛ tumi ne akee yɛle kpole kpalɛ wɔ Sɔɔlo abo zo amra ne avinli.

english_verse: He had even slept with a wife of Saul by the name of Rizpah the daughter of Aiah. But Saul's son Ishbosheth told Abner, “You shouldn't have slept with one of my father's wives!”
translation_verse: Ɛnee Sɔɔlo lɛ ye mgbɔnla bie, bɛfɛlɛ ye Relezepa; ɔ ze a le Eyiya. Kenle ko Sɔɔlo ara Yehyebɔhyɛte vale zile Abenɛɛ anyunlu kɛ, “Duzu ati a wɔva ɛ sa wɔha egya mgbɔnla ne a?”

english_verse: Abner was very angry because of what Ishbosheth had said, and he told Ishbosheth: Am I some kind of worthless dog from Judah? I've always been loyal to your father's family and to his relatives and friends. I haven't turned you over to David. And yet you talk to me as if I've committed a crime with this woman.
translation_verse: Edwɛkɛ ɛhye manle Abenɛɛ vale ɛya kpole manle ɔhanle kɛ, “Ɛdwenle kɛ mehakyi me nzi mezi Sɔɔlo ɔ? Anzɛɛ ɛdwenle kɛ melɛsonle Dwuda? Ɔvi mɔlebɛbo ne, meli nɔhalɛ memaa ɛ ze Sɔɔlo, ɔ mediema nee ɔ gɔnwo mɔ; melie wɔ mevi Devidi asa anu, meammaa yeanli ɛ nwo zo konim; ɛnɛ ɛlɛto me ɛzonle wɔagua me nyunlu aze wɔ raalɛ duma nu.

english_verse: God said that he wouldn't let anyone in Saul's family ever be king again and that David would be king instead. He also said that David would rule both Israel and Judah, all the way from Dan in the north to Beersheba in the south.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma bɔle Devidi ɛwɔkɛ kɛ ɔbalie belemgbunli maanle ne yeavi Sɔɔlo nee ɔ bo zo amra asa anu, na yeazie Devidi Yizilayɛ nee Dwuda belemgbunli, ɔvi maanle ne ati mɔɔ kɔdwu ɔ bo la. Saa meannea meammaa ɛwɔkɛ ɛhye anyɛ zɔhane a Nyamenle ɛhu me.”

english_verse: Ishbosheth was so afraid of Abner that he could not even answer.
translation_verse: Yehyebɔhyɛte zulole Abenɛɛ, yemɔti yeangola edwɛkɛ kpɔkɛ ko bɔbɔ ka.

english_verse: Abner sent some of his men to David with this message: “You should be the ruler of the whole nation. If you make an agreement with me, I will persuade everyone in Israel to make you their king.”
translation_verse: Abenɛɛ zoanle menli wɔ Devidi anwo wɔ Hibulɔn manle bɛhɔzele ye kɛ, “Azɛlɛ ne, nwane ɛdeɛ ɔ? Maa yɛyɛ ngyehyɛlɛ na menwɔboa wɔ menwɔmaa ɛkɛlie Yizilayɛ maanle ne kɔsɔɔti.”

english_verse: David sent this message back: “Good! I'll make an agreement with you. But before I will even talk with you about it, you must get Saul's daughter Michal back for me.”
translation_verse: Devidi zele ye kɛ, “Mede; meyɛ wɔ mo. Memaa wɔ mɛla ko ɛhye. Saa ɛkola zolɛ di a me nee wɔ kɛyɛ ngyehyɛlɛ ne. Mɛla ne a le kɛ, mmamaa menwu ɛ nyunlu, mɔɔ mekanwu ɛ nyunlu la ɛnee ɛ nee me ye Maekale, Sɔɔlo ara raalɛ ne, ɛra.”

english_verse: David sent a few of his officials to Ishbosheth to give him this message: “Give me back my wife Michal! I killed
translation_verse: Akee Devidi zoanle menli wɔ Sɔɔlo ara Yehyebɔhyɛte ɛkɛ ne manle bɛhɔzele ye kɛ, “Maa me sa ɛha me ye Maekale mɔɔ menvale Filisitia mrenya ɛya ko atoa ati nwoma menzule ɔ ti asoa la ndɛndɛ.”

english_verse: Ishbosheth sent some of his men to take Michal away from her new husband, Paltiel the son of Laish.
translation_verse: Yehyebɔhyɛte zoanle manle bɛhɔzale Paleteɛle mɔɔ ɛnee gya Maekale la bɛliele ɔ ye ne bɛvile ɔ sa nu. Paleteɛle ɔ ze a le Leyihye.

english_verse: Paltiel followed Michal and the men all the way to Bahurim, crying as he walked. But he went back home after Abner ordered him to leave.
translation_verse: Na mɔɔ bɛ nee Maekale kɔ la, ɔ hu vale ɛzunlɛ doale ye toonwo ɔhɔdwule Bahulem. Na Abenɛɛ zele ye kɛ, “Sia ɛ nzi!” Na Paleteɛle ziale.

english_verse: Abner talked with the leaders of the tribes of Israel and told them, “You've wanted to make David your king for a long time now.
translation_verse: Akee Abenɛɛ nee Yizilayɛ mgbanyima hanle bɛ ti kpulale nwolɛ zele kɛ, “Mekɛ tendenle mɔɔ ɛraze ɛhɔ la, ɛnee bɛlɛkpondɛ Devidi bɛamaa yeali bɛ belemgbunli.

english_verse: So do it! After all, God said he would use his servant David to rescue his people Israel from their enemies, especially from the Philistines.”
translation_verse: Kɛkala, mekɛ ne akee ɛdwu, ɔluakɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛbɔ Devidi ɛwɔkɛ kɛ, ‘Mebalua me sonvolɛ Devidi anwo zo mealie me menli Yizilayɛma meavi Filisitiama nee bɛ kpɔvolɛma mɔɔ ɛha la asa anu.’ ”

english_verse: Finally, Abner talked with the tribe of Benjamin. Then he left for Hebron to tell David everything that the tribe of Benjamin and the rest of the people of Israel wanted to do.
translation_verse: Abenɛɛ eza dendɛle hilele Bɛngyaman abusua ekpunli ne anu amra. Akee ɔtelele zolɛ ɔhɔle Hibulɔn kɛ ɔkaha debie mɔɔ Yizilayɛma nee Bɛngyaman abusua ekpunli ne ɛlie ɛdo nu kɛ bɛyɛ la yeahile Devidi.

english_verse: soldiers with him, and when they got to Hebron, David gave a big feast for them.
translation_verse: Abenɛɛ nee mgbanyima abulanwiɔ ne dwule Hibulɔn la Devidi dole bɛ ɛkponle kpole bie.

english_verse: After the feast, Abner said, “Your Majesty, let me leave now and bring Israel here to make an agreement with you. You'll be king of the whole nation, just as you've been wanting.” David told Abner he could leave, and he left without causing any trouble. Joab Kills Abner
translation_verse: Abenɛɛ zele Devidi kɛ, “Nana, mekɔ meahɔboɔboa Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti anloa meamaa wɔ. Bɛ muala bɛ nee wɔ bayɛ ngyehyɛlɛ na bɛalie bɛado nu kɛ ɛle bɛ belemgbunli na wɔazie maanle ne kɔsɔɔti kɛmɔ ɛkpondɛ la.” Yemɔti Devidi manle Abenɛɛ adenle manle ɔhɔle anzonudwolɛ nu. Bɛhu Abenɛɛ

english_verse: Soon after Abner had left Hebron, Joab and some of David's soldiers came back, bringing a lot of things they had taken from an enemy village.
translation_verse: Nzinlii Dwowabe nee Devidi mgbanyima ne bie mɔ vi ɛleka mɔɔ bɛhɔtetale menli bɛwuale bɛ ninyɛne la rale. Bɛ nee anwonyia dɔɔnwo rale. Ɛnee Abenɛɛ ɛnle Devidi anwo ɛkɛ wɔ Hibulɔn, ɔboalekɛ Devidi ɛgua ye adenle ɛmaa yehɔ na yebɔ ye ɛwɔkɛ kɛ bɛbabɔ ɔ nwo bane.

english_verse: Right after they arrived, someone told Joab, “Abner visited the king, and the king let him go. Abner even left without causing any trouble.”
translation_verse: Dwowabe nee ye ɛlɔnema ne rale la, bɛdele kɛ Abenɛɛ rale belemgbunli ɛkɛ na yezia yehɔ anzonudwolɛ nu.

english_verse: Joab went to David and said, “What have you done? Abner came to you, and you let him go. Now he's long gone!
translation_verse: Dwowabe hɔle belemgbunli ɛkɛ ne hɔbizale ye kɛ, “Nana, na duzu debie a wɔyɛ la? Abenɛɛ rale ɛ nwo ɛke; duzu ati a wɔmaa yehɔ anzonudwolɛ nu a?

english_verse: You know Abner—he came to trick you. He wants to find out how strong your army is and to know everything you're doing.”
translation_verse: Ɛze kɛ Abenɛɛ rabɛlɛbɛlale wɔ, dole wɔ agyiba, amaa yeanwu wɔ ɛhɔlɛ nee wɔ ɛralɛ nu na yeanwu adenle biala mɔɔ ɛfa nuhua la.”

english_verse: Joab left David, then he sent some messengers to catch up with Abner. They brought him back from the well at Sirah, but David did not know anything about it.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Dwowabe vi Devidi anwo ɛkɛ ne vindele la, ɔzoanle ɔmanle bɛkpole Abenɛɛ, bɛhɔhyele ye wɔ Saela bula ne azo bɛ nee ye rale; noko Devidi ande nwolɛ bie fee.

english_verse: When Abner returned to Hebron, Joab pretended he wanted to talk privately with him. So he took Abner into one of the small rooms that were part of the town gate and stabbed him in the stomach. Joab killed him because Abner had killed Joab's brother Asahel. Abner's Funeral
translation_verse: Bɛ nee Abenɛɛ rale Hibulɔn la, Dwowabe vale ye vindele anlenkɛ kpole ne anzi lɔ kɛ asɛɛ ɔka edwɛkɛ yeahile ye, na ɔwɔle ye dadeɛ ɔ kunlu ɔhunle ye. Bɛhunle Abenɛɛ, ɔboalekɛ yehu Dwowabe adiema Asahɛle.

english_verse: David heard how Joab had killed Abner, and he said, “I swear to the Lord that I am completely innocent of Abner's death!
translation_verse: Nzinlii mɔɔ Devidi dele la, ɔhanle kɛ, “Medame nee me belemgbunli maanle ye ɛnli fɔlɛ wɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlu wɔ Abenɛɛ mogya nwo.

english_verse: Joab and his family are the guilty ones. I pray that Joab's family will always be sick with sores and other skin diseases. May they all be cowards, and may they die in war or starve to death.”
translation_verse: Ye mogya ne ɛgua Dwowabe nee ɔ ze awuke nu amra kɔsɔɔti ati zo. Wɔ awolɛndoazo biala anu, ye busuanli bie ɛva raalɛ nwo ewule, anzɛɛ kokobɛ ɛdila ye. Kyesɛ mraalɛ gyima ala na yeahola ye yɛ anzɛɛ bɛhu ye bie wɔ konle nu anzɛɛ ɔ nloa anu aleɛ ɛbɔ ye.”

english_verse: Joab and his brother Abishai killed Abner because he had killed their brother Asahel in the battle at Gibeon.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Dwowabe nee ɔ diema Abehyae zenrale Abenɛɛ kɛ ɔhunle bɛ diema Asahɛle wɔ Gebɛyɔn konle ne anu la. Bɛzie Abenɛɛ

english_verse: David told Joab and everyone with him, “Show your sorrow by tearing your clothes and wearing sackcloth! Walk in front of Abner's body and cry!” David walked behind the stretcher on which Abner's body was being carried.
translation_verse: Akee Devidi zele Dwowabe nee menli mɔɔ nee ye lua la kɛ, “Bɛsuosua bɛ adɛladeɛ ne mɔ anu. Bɛheda ɛrele na bɛzu Abenɛɛ.” Belemgbunli ɔdaye mumua ne ɔlile funli ɛlɛka ehwili ne anzi.

english_verse: Abner was buried in Hebron, while David and everyone else stood at the tomb and cried loudly.
translation_verse: Bɛziele Abenɛɛ wɔ Hibulɔn; belemgbunli dukuele nu zunle wɔ azie ne azo na zɔhane ala yɛɛ menli mɔɔ hale la zunle a.

english_verse: Then the king sang a funeral song about Abner: Abner, why should you have died like an outlaw?
translation_verse: Devidi zunle Abenɛɛ yele awolɛ zele kɛ, “Abenɛɛ, anzɛɛ ɔwɔ kɛ ɛwu kɛ koasea la ɔ?

english_verse: No one tied your hands or chained your feet, yet you died as a victim of murderers. Everyone started crying again.
translation_verse: Bɛankyekye ɛ sa, bɛangua ɛ gyakɛ nwɔnzɔnwɔnzɔ; Kɛmɔ sonla si wu maamɔvoma asa anu la, zɔhane ala yɛɛ wɔwu a.” Na menli ne kɔsɔɔti eza zunle Abenɛɛ bieko.

english_verse: Then they brought some food to David and told him he would feel better if he had something to eat. It was still daytime, and David said, “I swear to God that I won't take a bite of bread or anything else until sunset!”
translation_verse: Alehyenlɛ ne anu, menli ne bodole Devidi kɛ ɔli debie, na ɔzele kɛ, “Nyamenle ɛdua me kakɛ ɛgua me bie zo kɛ menwɔli debie kolaa na sɛnzɛne adɔ a.”

english_verse: Everyone noticed what David did, and they liked it, just as they always liked what he did.
translation_verse: Kɛmɔ debie biala mɔɔ belemgbunli yɛle la yɛle bɛ anyelielɛ la, menli ne kɔsɔɔti nwunle nyɛleɛ ɛhye na bɛ nye liele nwolɛ.

english_verse: Now the people of Judah and Israel were certain that David had nothing to do with killing Abner.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Devidi menli ne amuala nee Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti nwunle ye kenle ko ne kɛ belemgbunli ne ɛnlɛ adwenle ɛtane biala kɛ ɔku Abenɛɛ.

english_verse: David said to his officials, “Don't you realize that today one of Israel's great leaders has died?
translation_verse: Belemgbunli zele ye mgbanyima ne kɛ, “Bɛnze kɛ belemgbunli ra nee sonlakpole ɛwu Yizilayɛ maanle ye anu ɛnɛ kenle ye ɔ?

english_verse: I am the chosen king, but Joab and Abishai have more power than I do. So God will have to pay them back for the evil thing they did.”
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛyila me ɛzie me belemgbunli, noko ɛnɛ kenle ye, me sa ɛhondo aze. Zɛluaya amra mrenya ne mɔ te me ɛbolɛ somaa. Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛdua ɛtanevolɛma kakɛ mɔɔ ɔfɛta bɛ amumuyɛ ne mɔ la.”

english_verse: Ishbosheth felt like giving up after he heard that Abner had died in Hebron. Everyone in Israel was terrified.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Yehyebɔhyɛte dele kɛ bɛhu Abenɛɛ wɔ Hibulɔn la, ɔ nwo bubule ye, Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti zulole.

english_verse: Ishbosheth had put the two brothers Baanah and Rechab in charge of the soldiers who raided enemy villages. Rimmon was their father, and they were from the town of Beeroth, which belonged to the tribe of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Yehyebɔhyɛte lɛ menli nwiɔ mɔɔ nea nwule ekpunli ekpunli ne mɔ anwo zo a. Bɛfɛlɛ ko Beeyana yɛɛ bɛfɛlɛ ko ne Rilikabe. Bɛ ze a le Relemɔn mɔɔ vi Biyɛlo la yɛɛ ɔvi Bɛngyaman abusua ekpunli ne anu. (Bɛtia Biyɛlo bɛboka Bɛngyaman maanle ne anwo.

english_verse: The people who used to live in Beeroth had run away to Gittaim, and they still live there.
translation_verse: Biyɛlo amra nriandile hɔle Geteeyem, na ɛkɛ ne a bɛdɛnla toonwo yeradwu ɛnɛ a.)

english_verse: Saul's son Jonathan had a son named Mephibosheth, who had not been able to walk since he was five years old. It happened when someone from Jezreel told his nurse that Saul and Jonathan had died. She hurried off with the boy in her arms, but he fell and injured his legs.
translation_verse: Sɔɔlo ara Dwɔnatan ɛnee lɛ ɔ ra nrenya mɔɔ agyakɛ ɛbubu a. Bɛfɛlɛ ye Mɛfebɔhyɛte. english_verse: One day about noon, Rechab and Baanah went to Ishbosheth's house. It was a hot day, and he was resting
translation_verse: Relemɔn amra mrenya ne mɔ, Rilikabe nee Beeyana, zile nu ewia henlema hɔle Yehyebɔhyɛte sua nu. Bɛhɔdwule la ɛnee yela ɔlɛdie ye ɛnwomenle.

english_verse: Finally they turned west and went to Hebron. They went in to see David and told him, “Your Majesty, here is the head of Ishbosheth, the son of your enemy Saul who tried to kill you! The Lord has let you get even with Saul and his family.”
translation_verse: bɛvale bɛrɛlɛle Devidi wɔ Hibulɔn. Bɛzele belemgbunli ne kɛ, “Sɔɔlo, wɔ kpɔvolɛ ne mɔɔ ɛnee ɛlɛkpondɛ wɔ ahu wɔ la ara Yehyebɔhyɛte ati ne ɛne. Nana, Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛzenra Sɔɔlo nee ɔ bo zo amra ɛdua bɛ kakɛ ɛnɛ demua ye ɛmaa wɔ.”

english_verse: David answered: I swear that only the Lord rescues me when I'm in trouble!
translation_verse: Devidi buale Rilikabe nee ɔ diema Beeyana kɛ, “Meka tease Nyamenle ne mɔɔ ɛlie me ɛvi munzule kɔsɔɔti anu la!

english_verse: When a man came to Ziklag and told me that Saul was dead, he thought he deserved a reward for bringing good news. But I grabbed him and killed him.
translation_verse: Ɛbɔfoɔ ne mɔɔ rahanle hilele me wɔ Zekelage kɛ Sɔɔlo ɛwu la dwenlenle kɛ ɔlɛ amaneɛ fɛlɛko ɔlɛbɛlɛ me. Memanle bɛhyele ye bɛhunle ye. Ɛhye a le kakɛ mɔɔ menvale menduale ye wɔ ye amaneɛ fɛlɛko ne anwo a.

english_verse: You evil men have done something much worse than he did. You've killed an innocent man in his own house and on his own bed. I'll make you pay for that. I'll wipe you from the face of the earth!
translation_verse: Duzu ati yɛɛ amumuyɛma mɔɔ kɛhu tenlenenli wɔ ɔdaye ye sua nu, wɔ nafelɛ nu la, bɛnrɛdua bɛ kakɛ molozo ɛ? Mebalie ye mogya meavi bɛ lɔ na meaye bɛ zo meavi aleɛabo.”

english_verse: Then David said to his troops, “Kill these two brothers! Cut off their hands and feet and hang their bodies by the pool in Hebron. But bury Ishbosheth's head in Abner's tomb near Hebron.” And they did.
translation_verse: Devidi manle ye mgbavolɛ ne mɔ hunle bɛ. Bɛpepɛle bɛ sa nee bɛ gyakɛ na bɛhendɛhendanle bɛ wɔ mbaka zo wɔ Hibulɔn nzubula ne anwo. Akee bɛvale Yehyebɔhyɛte ati ne na bɛziele ye wɔ Abenɛɛ nla ne anu wɔ Hibulɔn.

english_verse: King Hiram of Tyre sent some officials to David. Carpenters and stone workers came with them, and they brought cedar logs so they could build David a palace.
translation_verse: Taya Belemgbunli Helam zoanle menli wɔ Devidi anwo ɛkɛ. Ɔmanle kapentama nee suazilɛma vale sida mbaka nee awolɛ hɔzile sua manle ye.

english_verse: He lived in Hebron for the first seven and a half years and ruled only Judah. Then he moved to Jerusalem, where he ruled both Israel and Judah for
translation_verse: Ɔdɛnlanle Hibulɔn ɔziele Dwuda ɛvolɛ nsuu siane nsia, yɛɛ ɔdɛnlanle Gyɛlusalɛm ɔziele Yizilayɛ nee Dwuda maanle ne amuala ɛvolɛ abulasa nee nsa.

english_verse: The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, and David led his army there to attack them. The Jebusites did not think he could get in, so they told him, “You can't get in here! We could keep you out, even if we couldn't see or walk!”
translation_verse: Belemgbunli Devidi nee ye ɛlɔnema hɔtetale Gyɛlusalɛm. Gyibɛsema mɔɔ lɛ maanle ne la dwenlenle kɛ Devidi ɛnrɛhola suakpole ne anwo zo konim di, yemɔti bɛzele ye kɛ, “Ɛ gyakɛ ba ɛnrɛtia sua ye azo. Anyenzinliravolɛma nee abuburama a baha wɔ ado ɛbɔ nu a.”

english_verse: David became a great and strong ruler, because the Lord All-Powerful was on his side.
translation_verse: Akee Devidi anwo yɛle ɛzulolɛ kpole kpalɛ, ɔboalekɛ Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle ne nee ye lua.

english_verse: David knew that the Lord had made him king of Israel and that he had made him a powerful ruler for the good of his people. David's Sons Born in Jerusalem (
translation_verse: Akee Devidi nwunle ye wienyi kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛzie ye Yizilayɛ belemgbunli bɔkɔɔ, na ye menli Yizilayɛma ati yekpogya ye belemgbunlililɛ ne zo.

english_verse: After David left Hebron and moved to Jerusalem, he married many women from Jerusalem, and he had a lot of children.
translation_verse: Devidi vi Hibulɔn rale Gyɛlusalɛm la, ɔgyale mraalɛ dɔɔnwo, eza ɔvale mgbɔnla dɔɔnwo na ɔwole mralɛ mrenya nee mralɛ mraalɛ dɔɔnwo.
