english_verse: The Philistines heard that David was now king of Israel, and they came into the hill country to try and capture him. But David found out and went into his fortress.
translation_verse: Filisitiama dele kɛ bɛzie Devidi Yizilayɛ belemgbunli, yemɔti bɛ kɔsɔɔti bɛhɔle ye ɛhyelɛ. Devidi dele nwolɛ bie na ɔhɔle ye sua ne mɔɔ bɛbɔ nwolɛ bane la azo.

english_verse: So the Philistines camped in Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: Filisitiama rale na bɛrakpondenle Relɛfeeyem bɔnza ne anu.

english_verse: David asked the Lord, “Should I attack the Philistines? Will you let me win?” The Lord told David, “Attack! I will let you win.”
translation_verse: Devidi bizale Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ, “Mengɔ mengɔteta Filisitiama ɔ? Ɛkɛye bɛ ɛkɛmaa me ɔ?” Ɛdɛnkɛma zele ye kɛ, “Kɔ na mebaye Filisitiama ne meamaa wɔali bɛ nwo zo konim.”

english_verse: David attacked the Philistines and defeated them. Then he said, “I watched the Lord break through my enemies like a mighty flood.” So he named the place “The Lord Broke Through.”
translation_verse: Yemɔti Devidi hɔle Beeyale Pɛleezem na ɔlile Filisitiama anwo zo konim. Ɔzele kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛbɔ me kpɔvolɛma asande wɔ me nyunlu kɛ azule mɔɔ ɛyi ɛbu aze la.” Yemɔti bɛfɛlɛ ɛleka zɔhane Beeyale Pɛleezem.

english_verse: David and his troops also carried away the idols that the Philistines had left behind.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Filisitiama gua ɛbɔ nu la, bɛgyakyile bɛ mmonle ne mɔ bɛ nzi, na Devidi nee ye menli ne mɔ sesale hɔle.

english_verse: Some time later, the Philistines came back into the hill country and camped in Rephaim Valley.
translation_verse: Eza Filisitiama ziale rale rakpondenle Relɛfeeyem bɔnza ne anu bieko.

english_verse: David asked the Lord what he should do, and the Lord answered: Don't attack them from the front. Circle around behind and attack from among the balsam trees.
translation_verse: Na Devidi bizale Ɛdɛnkɛma la, ɔzele ye kɛ, “Mmakɔ ɛ nyunlu; bu bɛ nzi, ɛleka mɔɔ nee ‘belesam’ mbaka ne mɔ anye bɔ zo la.

english_verse: Wait until you hear a sound in the treetops like marching troops. Then attack quickly! That sound will mean I have marched out ahead of you to fight the Philistine army.
translation_verse: Saa ɛte kilikili kɛ asɛɛ menli ɛlɛtia mbaka ne mɔ ati zo a, ɛnee kɔteta bɛ ɛ nee bɛ ɛho, ɔboalekɛ ɛnee Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛlumua ɛ nyunlu ɛhɔli Filisitiama anwo zo konim.”

english_verse: David obeyed the Lord and defeated the Philistines. He even chased them all the way from Geba to the entrance to Gezer.
translation_verse: Na Devidi yɛle, kɛmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma zele ye la na ɔbɔle ye Giba ɔhunle Filisitiama toonwo ɔhɔdwule Gizɛ.

english_verse: The people carrying the chest walked six steps, then David sacrificed an ox and a choice cow.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ menli mɔɔ zo Ɛdɛnkɛma Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne la dule bɛ gyakɛ nsia la, Devidi manle bɛgyinlanle na ɔvale ɛnlankɛ nyinli nee ɛnlankɛ mɔɔ ɛhye kpalɛ la ɔbɔle azu ɔmanle Ɛdɛnkɛma.

english_verse: He was dancing for the Lord with all his might, but he wore only a linen cloth.
translation_verse: Devidi wulale Nyamenlezonlenlɛ tɛladeɛ ne mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye “Yifɔdo” la na ɔvale ye anwosesebɛ kɔsɔɔti ɔzile agole ɔwulale Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlunyia.

english_verse: He and everyone else were celebrating by shouting and blowing horns while the chest was being carried along.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Devidi nee Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti vale aweɛnebɔlɛ, edwɛnedolɛ, agolezilɛ nee fɛlɛkolilɛ vale Ɛdɛnkɛma Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne hɔle Devidi Suakpole zo.

english_verse: Saul's daughter Michal looked out her window and watched the chest being brought into David's City. But when she saw David jumping and dancing for the Lord, she was disgusted.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne dwule Devidi Suakpole zo la, Sɔɔlo ara raalɛ Maekale wulale ɔ ti nvɛnzɛlɛ ne anu nleanle. Ɔnwunle kɛ Belemgbunli Devidi ɛlɛdi wulupe si agole wɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlu; ye adwenle zɛkyele Devidi anwo na ye ahonle yele ye bɔkɔɔ.

english_verse: They put the sacred chest on a new ox cart and started bringing it down the hill from Abinadab's house. Abinadab's sons Uzzah and Ahio were guiding the ox cart,
translation_verse: Bɛyele Ɛlɛka ne wɔ Abenadabe sua nu wɔ boka ne azo na bɛvale bɛziele ehwili fofolɛ zo. Abenadabe amra Ɛza nee Ahayo a ɛnee ɛlɛka ehwili ne mɔɔ Ɛlɛka ne gyi zolɛ la a.

english_verse: led them to Baalah in Judah, which was also called Kiriath-Jearim. They were going there to get the sacred chest and bring it back to Jerusalem. The throne of the Lord All-Powerful is above the winged creatures on top of this chest, and he is worshiped there.
translation_verse: Ɔ nee bɛ hɔle Beeyala mɔɔ wɔ Dwuda la kɛ bɛkava Nyamenle Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne mɔɔ Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma duma a la zo, mɔɔ ye belemgbunli ebia a gyi abɔdeɛ ne mɔ mɔɔ lɛ ndɛbalɛ la azo la bɛara.

english_verse: with Ahio walking in front of it.
translation_verse: Ahayo a li Ɛlɛka ne anyunlu a.

english_verse: Some of the people of Israel were playing music on small harps and other stringed instruments, and on tambourines, castanets, and cymbals. David and the others were happy, and they danced for the Lord with all their might.
translation_verse: Na Devidi nee Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti bubule nya vale bɛ anwosesebɛ dole edwɛne, zile agole, bɔle getaa, akɛya, aweɛne, sɔnwosɔnwo yɛɛ ahenle yele Ɛdɛnkɛma ayɛlɛ.

english_verse: But when they came to Nacon's threshing-floor, the oxen stumbled, so Uzzah reached out and took hold of the sacred chest.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ bɛradwule Neekɔn ma ɛwozolɛ ɛleka ne la, mgbɔnwɔ ne mɔ mɔɔ ehwili ne henda bɛ la agyakɛ wuanenle bɛ na Ɛza dendenle ɔ sa zɔle Nyamenle Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne anu.

english_verse: The Lord God was very angry with Uzzah for doing this, and he killed Uzzah right there beside the chest.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma vale Ɛza anwo ɛya kpole na ɔhunle ye ɛkɛ ne ala, ɔboalekɛ ɔvale ɔ sa ɔhanle Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne. Ɛza wule lale Ɛlɛka ne anwo.

english_verse: David got angry with God for killing Uzzah. He named that place “Bursting Out Against Uzzah,” and that's what it's still called.
translation_verse: Devidi ahonle futule, ɔboalekɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛva ɛya ɛdua Ɛza kakɛ; na toonwo mɔɔ yeradwu ɛnɛ la bɛfɛlɛ ɛleka zɔhane “Ɛza Ndeanlɛ Ɛleka.”

english_verse: David was afraid of the Lord and thought, “Should I really take the sacred chest to my city?”
translation_verse: Na kenle ko ne Devidi zulole Ɛdɛnkɛma, na ɔhanle kɛ, “Kɛ ɔkɛyɛ na Ɛdɛnkɛma Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne adwu me nwo ɛke ɛ?”

english_verse: He decided not to take it there. Instead, he turned off the road and took it to the home of Obed Edom, who was from Gath.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Devidi angulo kɛ ɔkɛva Ɛdɛnkɛma Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne ɔkɛhɔ Devidi Suakpole zo , na ɔvale ɔhɔle Obɛde Yidɔm mɔɔ vi Gate la sua nu.

english_verse: The chest stayed there for three months, and the Lord greatly blessed Obed Edom, his family, and everything he owned. Then someone told King David, “The Lord has done this because the sacred chest is in Obed Edom's house.” At once, David went to Obed Edom's house to get the chest and bring it to David's City. Everyone was celebrating.
translation_verse: Na bɛrahanle bɛhilele Belemgbunli Devidi kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛyila Obɛde Yidɔm, ye awuke nu amra nee debie biala mɔɔ ɔlɛ la, ɔboalekɛ Nyamenle Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne wɔ ye ɛkɛ.” Yemɔti Devidi vale fɛlɛkolilɛ hɔyele Nyamenle Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne vile Obɛde Yidɔm sua nu hɔle Devidi Suakpole zo.

english_verse: They put the chest inside a tent that David had set up for it. David worshiped the Lord by sacrificing animals and burning them on an altar,
translation_verse: Bɛvale Ɛdɛnkɛma Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne bɛraziele ɛleka mɔɔ ɛnee Devidi ɛziezie wɔ Ndanlɛ Sua ne anu ɛmaa ye la. Akee Devidi bɔle ɛyelalɛ nee anzonudwolɛ azu manle Ɛdɛnkɛma.

english_verse: then he blessed the people in the name of the Lord All-Powerful.
translation_verse: Ɔwiele azu ne bɔ la, ɔyilale menli ne mɔ wɔ Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma duma nu.

english_verse: He gave all the men and women in the crowd a small loaf of bread, some meat, and a handful of raisins, then everyone went home. Michal Talks to David
translation_verse: Na ɔvale ahyɛlɛ ninyɛne ɔmanle Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti, mraalɛ nee mrenya. Ɔmanle awie biala kpanwo ko, nane ndondo sinli nee vanye ma welera ndɛlamoa ko. Akee awie biala hɔle sua nu.

english_verse: David went home so he could ask the Lord to bless his family. But Saul's daughter Michal went out and started yelling at him. “You were really great today!” she said. “You acted like a dirty old man, dancing around half-naked in front of your servants' slave-girls.”
translation_verse: Nzinlii Devidi hɔle kɛ ɔkayila ye awuke nu amra, na Sɔɔlo ara raalɛ Maekale rayiale ye na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Yizilayɛ belemgbunli ne ɛlie duma kpole ɛmaa ɔ nwo ɛnɛ. Yeye ɔ nwo yehile ye sonvolɛma sonvolɛ mraalɛ anyiemgba nu bie kɛ koasea la.”

english_verse: David told her, “The Lord didn't choose your father or anyone else in your family to be the leader of his people. The Lord chose me, and I was celebrating in honor of him.
translation_verse: Na Devidi zele Maekale kɛ, “Menzile agole, menyele Ɛdɛnkɛma ne mɔɔ vale ɛ ze nee ye abusua ne ziele ahane, na ɔziele me ye menli Yizilayɛma belemgbunli la ayɛlɛ. Na mebahɔ zolɛ meazi agole meawula Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlunyia dahuu.

english_verse: I'll show you just how great I can be! I'll even be disgusting to myself. But those slave-girls you talked about will still honor me!”
translation_verse: Mebagua me nyunlu aze mɔɔ tɛla ɛhye bɔbɔ la meamaa ye. Wɔmɔ, ɛ nye zo a menzɔho ɛhwee, noko sonvolɛ mraalɛ mɔɔ ɛlɛdi bɛ edwɛkɛ la bawula me anyunlunyia kpalɛ kpalɛ.”

english_verse: Michal never had any children.
translation_verse: Na Sɔɔlo ara raalɛ Maekale anwo ralɛ fee na yeawu.

english_verse: But I will never put an end to my agreement with him, as I put an end to my agreement with Saul, who was king before you.
translation_verse: Menrɛye me nye ɔ nwo zo, kɛmɔ menyele menvile Sɔɔlo anwo zo la, menvale ye menziele ahane, amaa wɔali belemgbunli la.

english_verse: Then one day, as David was talking with Nathan the prophet, David said, “Look around! I live in a palace made of cedar, but the sacred chest has to stay in a tent.”
translation_verse: Na belemgbunli ne akee zele Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ Neetan kɛ, “Mame mede mbaka sua nu na Nyamenle Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne gyi ndanlɛ sua nu.”

english_verse: Nathan replied, “The Lord is with you, so do what you want!”
translation_verse: Na Neetan zele belemgbunli ne kɛ, “Kɔ na kɔyɛ debie biala mɔɔ wɔ wɔ ahonle nu la, ɔluakɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma nee wɔ lua.”

english_verse: That night, the Lord told Nathan
translation_verse: Na kenle ko ne nɔe ne, Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Neetan kɛ,

english_verse: to go to David and give him this message: David, you are my servant, so listen to what I say. Why should you build a temple for me?
translation_verse: “Kɔ kɔze me sonvolɛ Devidi kɛ, ‘Kɛ medame Ɛdɛnkɛma mese la ɛne: Wɔmɔ yɛɛ ɛsi sua wɔamaa meadɛnla nu ɔ?

english_verse: I didn't live in a temple when I brought my people out of Egypt, and I don't live in one now. A tent has always been my home wherever I have gone with them.
translation_verse: Sumunli kɛ menyele Yizilayɛma menvile Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo mɔɔ yeradwu ɛnɛ la, metɛtɛnlanle sua nu ɛlɛ. Meli tutɛnla wɔ ndanlɛ azua nu.

english_verse: I chose leaders and told them to be like shepherds for my people Israel. But did I ever say anything to even one of them about building a cedar temple for me?
translation_verse: Ɛleka kɔsɔɔti mɔɔ me nee Yizilayɛma ɛhɔ la, meanga edwɛkɛ kpɔkɛ ko bɔbɔ meangile Yizilayɛ mgbanyima mɔɔ menyele bɛ kɛ bɛli Yizilayɛma ati la kɛ, duzu ati a bɛtɛfale sida mbaka bɛtɛsile sua bɛtɛmanle me ɛ?’

english_verse: David, this is what I, the Lord All-Powerful, say to you. I brought you in from the fields where you took care of sheep, and I made you the leader of my people.
translation_verse: “Yemɔti ka kile me sonvolɛ Devidi kɛ, medame Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma mese, ‘Menyele wɔ menvile mboane ɛnleanlɛ zo wɔ fiene ne anu kɛ ɛrali me menli Yizilayɛma belemgbunli;

english_verse: Wherever you went, I helped you and destroyed your enemies right in front of your eyes. I have made you one of the most famous people in the world.
translation_verse: yɛɛ adenle biala anu me nee wɔ ɛlua. Meli wɔ kpɔvolɛma kɔsɔɔti anwo zo konim memaa wɔ; mebamaa wɔalie duma kpole, kɛmɔ mgbolema mɔɔ wɔ aleɛabo la lɛ ye la.

english_verse: I'll choose one of your sons to be king when you reach the end of your life and are buried in the tomb of your ancestors. I'll make him a strong ruler,
translation_verse: Saa mekɛ dwu na ɛsia ɛkɔ wɔ ɛkɛla nzi, na bɛwula wɔ mrɛlatɛlɛ nu wɔ wɔ mgbanyinli avinli a, mebakpogya ɛ bo zo amra ne mɔ ko zo na meakyekye ye belemgbunli maanle ne kpundii meamaa ye.

english_verse: and no one will be able to take his kingdom away from him. He will be the one to build a temple for me.
translation_verse: Yemɔ yɛɛ ɔbazi ɛzonlenlɛ sua yeamaa me a, na mebanlea kɛ ye belemgbunli maanle ne ɛgyinla kpundii dahuu.

english_verse: I will be his father, and he will be my son. When he does wrong, I'll see that he is corrected, just as children are corrected by their parents.
translation_verse: Mebayɛ ɔ ze, na ɔdaye ɔbayɛ me ra. Saa ɔyɛ ɛtane a mebadea ye, kɛmɔ selɛ tea ɔ ra la.

english_verse: After all, you really are Israel's God, the Lord All-Powerful. You've told me that you will let my descendants be kings. That's why I have the courage to pray to you like this, even though I am only your servant.
translation_verse: Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, Yizilayɛ Nyamenle, melɛ akɛnrazilɛ yɛɛ melɛyɛ nzɛlɛlɛ ɛhye a, ɔboalekɛ wɔye ɛhye mɔ kɔsɔɔti wɔhile wɔ sonvolɛ Devidi kɛ ɛbayɛ ɔ bo zo amra arelemgbunli.

english_verse: David went into the tent he had set up for the sacred chest. Then he sat there and prayed: Lord All-Powerful, my family and I don't deserve what you have already done for us,
translation_verse: Akee Belemgbunli Devidi hɔle Ndanlɛ Sua ne anu hɔdɛnlanle Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlu na ɔzɛlɛle kɛ, “O Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, me nee me awuke nu amra, mɔɔ wɔyɛ wɔmaa yɛ la, yɛnfɛta.

english_verse: and yet you have promised to do even more. Is this the way you usually treat people?
translation_verse: Noko ɛhye le ɛ nye zo debie ekyi bie; yɛɛ mɔɔ akee ɛlɛyɛ bɔbɔ la bo zolɛ. O Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, wɔbɔ me bo zo amra ɛwɔkɛ wɔ mekɛ tendenle mɔɔ bara la.

english_verse: I am your servant, and you know my thoughts, so there is nothing more that I need to say.
translation_verse: O Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, na duzu bieko bɔbɔ yɛɛ mame Devidi melɛ meka a? Ɔluakɛ ɛze wɔ sonvolɛ.

english_verse: You have done this wonderful thing, and you have let me know about it, because you wanted to keep your promise.
translation_verse: O Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, ɔlua wɔ ɛwɔkɛ ne ati nee wɔ ahunlunyele kpole ne ati yɛɛ wɔyɛ nyɛleɛ kpole ɛhye wɔmaa wɔ sonvolɛ ɛnwu ye a.

english_verse: Lord All-Powerful, you are greater than all others. No one is like you, and you alone are God. Everything we have heard about you is true.
translation_verse: O Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle, ɛle kpole; nyamenle bieko ɛnle ɛkɛ mɔɔ le kɛ ɛdawɔ a, yɛɛ nyamenle bieko ɛnle ɛkɛ mɔɔ yɛdayɛ yɛde ye yɛ nzo nu kɛ ɛ ngome ala.

english_verse: And there is no other nation on earth like Israel, the nation you rescued from slavery in Egypt to be your own. You became famous by using great and wonderful miracles to force other nations and their gods out of your land, so your people could live here.
translation_verse: Maanle biala ɛnle aleɛabo kɛ wɔ menli Yizilayɛma mɔɔ ɛkpɔnenle bɛ na ɛyɛle bɛ wɔ menli la. Ninyɛne mgbole nee nwanwane ninyɛne mɔɔ ɛyɛle ɛmanle bɛ la ɛmaa wɔ duma ɛkponde aleɛabo ɛleka biala. Mekɛ mɔɔ wɔ menli mɔɔ ɛyele bɛ ɛvile Yigyibiti la kɔ bɛ nyunlu la, ɛdule maanle maanle nee bɛ awozonle ne mɔ.

english_verse: You have chosen Israel to be your people forever, and you have become their God.
translation_verse: Wɔyɛ Yizilayɛma wɔ menli wɔ melɛ mɔɔ ɛnlɛ awieleɛ, na wɔmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma wɔyɛ bɛ Nyamenle.

english_verse: And now, Lord God, please do what you have promised me and my descendants.
translation_verse: “Na kɛkala, O Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle, kɛmɔ ɛdawɔ wɔha wɔ wɔ sonvolɛ ye nee ɔ bo zo amra anwo la, moa zolɛ na maa ɔyɛ zɔhane;

english_verse: Then you will be famous forever, and everyone will say, “The Lord God All-Powerful rules Israel, and David's descendants are his chosen kings.”
translation_verse: na bɛkɛbɔ wɔ duma bɛkɛze kɛ, ‘Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma le Yizilayɛ Nyamenle’, na wɔ sonvolɛ Devidi belemgbunlililɛ ne ɛnrɛbɔ aze ɛlɛ wɔ ɛ nyunlu.

english_verse: Lord All-Powerful, you are God. You have promised me some very good things, and you can be trusted to do what you promise.
translation_verse: “O Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle, ɛle Nyamenle bɔkɔɔ; wɔ edwɛkɛ le nɔhalɛ, yɛɛ wɔbɔ wɔ sonvolɛ ye ɛwɔkɛ kpalɛ ɛhye.

english_verse: Please bless my descendants and let them always be your chosen kings. You have already promised, and I'm sure that you will bless my family forever.
translation_verse: Yemɔti mesɛlɛ wɔ kɛ yila me bo zo amra amaa dahuu ɛ nye ala bɛ nwo zo. Wɔmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle yɛɛ wɔbɔ ɛwɔkɛ ɛhye a, yemɔti yila me bo zo amra wɔ melɛ mɔɔ ɛnlɛ awieleɛ.”

english_verse: Benaiah the son of Jehoiada was the commander of David's bodyguard. David's sons were priests.
translation_verse: Gyɛhɔyada ara Bɛnaya a nea Devidi sinzavolɛma ne anwo zo a yɛɛ Devidi amra mrenya ne mɔ le sɛlɛvolɛma.

english_verse: David set out for the Euphrates River to build a monument there. On his way, he defeated the king of Zobah, whose name was Hadadezer the son of Rehob.
translation_verse: Devidi eza lile Rilihɔbo ara Hadadizɛ, Zoba belemgbunli ne, anwo zo konim wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ Hadadizɛ ɛnee ɛlɛkɔ Azule Yufileti sɔlɔ kɛ ɔkava ɛkɛ ne maanle ne la.

english_verse: When troops from the Aramean kingdom of Damascus came to help Hadadezer, David killed
translation_verse: Seleama mɔɔ wɔ Dɛmasekɛse la rale kɛ bɛbaboa Zoba Belemgbunli Hadadizɛ na Devidi hunle bɛ nuhua apenle ngoko abulanwiɔ nee nwiɔ.

english_verse: He left some of his soldiers in Damascus, and the Arameans had to accept David as their ruler and pay taxes to him. Everywhere David went, the Lord helped him win battles.
translation_verse: Akee Devidi yɛle ye ɛlɔnema azokoɛleɛ dɔɔnwo wɔ maanle ne anu na Seleama yɛle Devidi ngɛkɛlɛ na bɛduale adwule bɛmanle ye.

english_verse: Hadadezer's officers had carried their arrows in gold cases hung over their shoulders, but David took these cases and brought them to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Na Devidi yeyele nvutuke enyinlike ne mɔ mɔɔ Hadadizɛ mgbanyima ne mɔ lɛ la amuala hɔle Gyɛlusalɛm.

english_verse: He also took a lot of bronze from the cities of Betah and Berothai, which had belonged to Hadadezer.
translation_verse: Belemgbunli Devidi vale kɔbele dɔɔnwo kpalɛ wɔ Bita nee Bilotae; ɛhye mɔ le azuamgbole mɔɔ Hadadizɛ ɛnee sie bɛ la.

english_verse: King Toi of Hamath and King Hadadezer had been enemies. So when Toi heard that David had attacked and defeated Hadadezer's whole army, he sent his son Joram to praise and congratulate David. Joram also brought him gifts made of silver, gold, and bronze.
translation_verse: ɔzoanle ɔ ra nrenya Dwolam kɛ ɔhɔbiza ye ahye na ɔyɛ ye mo kɛ yeli Hadadizɛ mɔɔ ɔdaye Towae ɔ nee ye ɛho fane dɔɔnwo la anwo zo konim a. Dwolam vale ezukoa nvutuke, dwɛtɛ fufule nee kɔbele ahyɛlɛdeɛ hɔmanle Devidi.

english_verse: David gave these to the Lord, just as he had done with the silver and gold that he had captured from
translation_verse: Belemgbunli Devidi dule ahyɛlɛdeɛ ne nee mɔɔ ɔnyianle bɛ wɔ maanle maanle mɔɔ ɔlile bɛ nwo zo konim la anu la manle Ɛdɛnkɛma.

english_verse: Edom, Moab, Ammon, Philistia, Amalek, and from King Hadadezer of Zobah.
translation_verse: Ɔnyianle ninyɛne ne ɔvile Yidɔm, Mowabe, Amɔn, Filisitia, Amalɛke yɛɛ ɔnyianle bie noko ɔvile Zoba Belemgbunli Hadadizɛ ɛkɛ.

english_verse: Zadok the son of Ahitub, and Abiathar the son of Ahimelech, were the priests. Seraiah was the secretary.
translation_verse: Ahaetɛbe ara Zeedɔko nee Abayata ara Ahemɛlɛke a le sɛlɛvolɛma a; Sɛlaya le kɔɔto kɛlɛhɛlɛvolɛ;

english_verse: David ruled all Israel with fairness and justice.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Devidi ziele Yizilayɛ maanle ne kɔsɔɔti. Ɔvale nɔhalɛlilɛ nee pɛlepɛlelilɛ ɔziele menli ne.

english_verse: Joab the son of Zeruiah was the commander in chief of the army. Jehoshaphat the son of Ahilud kept the government records.
translation_verse: Zɛluaya ara Dwowabe a nea ɛlɔnema ne anwo zo a; Gyɛhɔhyafate mɔɔ ɔ ze a le Ahaelɛde la a le maanle ne kɛlɛhɛlɛvolɛ a;

english_verse: One day, David thought, “I wonder if any of Saul's family are still alive. If they are, I will be kind to them, because I made a promise to Jonathan.”
translation_verse: Kenle ko Devidi bizale kɛ, “Awie tɛbɔ Sɔɔlo abusua ne anu mɔɔ Dwɔnatan ati ɔwɔ kɛ meyɛ ahunlunyele memaa ye ɔ?”

english_verse: David called in Ziba, one of the servants of Saul's family. David said, “So you are Ziba.” “Yes, Your Majesty, I am.”
translation_verse: Ɛnee sonvolɛ bie wɔ Sɔɔlo awuke nu, bɛfɛlɛ ye Zaeba. Bɛvɛlɛle ye bɛmanle Devidi, na belemgbunli ne bizale ye kɛ, “Wɔmɔ a bɛfɛlɛ wɔ Zaeba la ɔ?” Ɔzele kɛ, “Nana, medame ɔ. Mele wɔ sonvolɛ.”

english_verse: David asked, “Are any of Saul's family still alive? If there are, I want to be kind to them.” Ziba answered, “One of Jonathan's sons is still alive, but he can't walk.”

translation_verse: Ɛyɛle wɔ ɛtane ɛdeɛ ne fealera nu, na mebamaa ɛhye azi ewiazo meamaa Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti anwu ye.’ ”

english_verse: David said, “I have disobeyed the Lord.” “Yes, you have!” Nathan answered. “You showed you didn't care what the Lord wanted. He has forgiven you, and you won't die. But your newborn son will.”
translation_verse: Kɛmɔ wɔanli Ɛdɛnkɛma eni fee na wɔyɛ nyɛleɛ ɛhye la, ɛ ra ne mɔɔ bɛbawo ye la bawu.”

english_verse: Then Nathan went back home. David's Young Son Dies The Lord made David's young son very sick.
translation_verse: Na Neetan hɔle sua nu. Devidi ara ne ewule Ɛdɛnkɛma manle Devidi ara ne mɔɔ ɔ nee Yulaya aye ne wole la anwo dole ye kpole kpalɛ.

english_verse: So David went without eating to show his sorrow, and he begged God to make the boy well. David would not sleep on his bed, but spent each night lying on the floor.
translation_verse: Devidi zɛlɛle Nyamenle kɛ kakula ne kɛde kpɔkɛ; ɔhyele ɛhɔne na nɔɔzo biala ɔlale aze wɔ ye sua ne anu.

english_verse: His officials stood beside him and tried to talk him into getting up. But he would not get up or eat with them.
translation_verse: Ye mgbanyima ne mɔ hɔbodole ye kɛ ɔdwazo azɛlɛ ne anwo, noko yeandwazo yɛɛ ɔ nee bɛ ando ɛsalɛ.

english_verse: After the child had been sick for seven days, he died, but the officials were afraid to tell David. They said to each other, “Even when the boy was alive, David wouldn't listen to us. How can we tell him his son is dead? He might do something terrible!”
translation_verse: Ye kenle nsuu ne azo, kakula ne wule, na ɛnee akee mgbanyima ne mɔ sulo kɛ bɛkɛbɔ Devidi amaneɛ. Bɛhanle kɛ, “Mɔɔ kakula ne ɛtɛwule bɔbɔ la, yɛka edwɛkɛ a ɔndie; nienwu bɔbɔ yɛɛ akee yɛpe na yɛabɔ ye amaneɛ kɛ kakula ne ɛwu a? Wɔannea a ɛnee yeyɛ ɔ nwo debie yeyɛ yɛ.”

english_verse: David noticed his servants whispering, and he knew the boy was dead. “Did my son die?” he asked his servants. “Yes, he did,” they answered.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Devidi nwunle kɛ mgbanyima ne mɔ ɛlɛtu bɛ nwo azukue ngoko la, ye adwenle vale manle ye kɛ kakula ne ɛwu. Yemɔti ɔbizale bɛ kɛ, “Kakula ne ɛwu ɔ?” Bɛbuale ye kɛ, “Ɛhɛe, yewu.”

english_verse: His officials said, “What are you doing? You went without eating and cried for your son while he was alive! But now that he's dead, you're up and eating.”
translation_verse: Akee ye mgbanyima ne mɔ zele ye kɛ, “Nana, yɛnde ɛhye mɔɔ wɔyɛ la abo; mɔɔ kakula ne ɛtɛnyianle ɛtɛwule la, ɛzunlɛ ala a ɛnee ɛsu a, wɔanli debie; na ɔwule ala la ɛdwazole ɛlile debie.”

english_verse: David answered: While he was still alive, I went without food and cried because there was still hope. I said to myself, “Who knows? Maybe the Lord will have pity on me and let the child live.”
translation_verse: Devidi buale kɛ, “Mɔɔ kakula ne de aze la mengyele ɛhɔne menzunle; ɔluakɛ mendwenlenle kɛ, ‘Nwane a ze a? Bie a ɛnee Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛnwu me anwunvɔne na yemaa yede kpɔkɛ.’

english_verse: But now that he's dead, why should I go without eating? I can't bring him back! Someday I will join him in death, but he can't return to me. Solomon Is Born
translation_verse: Na kɛkala mɔɔ yewu la, duzu ati a ɔwɔ kɛ mekye ɛhɔne a? Anzɛɛ menwɔhola menwɔdwazo ye menwɔra ngoane nu ɔ? Mame yɛɛ kenle bie mebahɔ ɛleka mɔɔ ɔwɔ la a, na yemɔ, ɔnzia ɔmba me nwo ɛke.” Bɛwo Sɔlɔmɔn

english_verse: David comforted his wife Bathsheba and slept with her. Later on, she gave birth to another son and named him Solomon. The Lord loved Solomon
translation_verse: Akee Devidi kyekyele ɔ ye Batehyɛba arɛle. Ɔ nee ye lale na ɔwole ralɛ nrenya na Devidi donle ye Sɔlɔmɔn. Ɛdɛnkɛma hulole kakula ne,

english_verse: David called the rest of the army together and attacked Rabbah. He captured the city
