english_verse: David made the people of Rabbah tear down the city walls with iron picks and axes, and then he put them to work making bricks. He did the same thing with all the other Ammonite cities. David went back to Jerusalem, and the people of Israel returned to their homes.
translation_verse: na Devidi manle ezuavolɛ ne vale sɛlada, bulalɛ ahoanlɛ nee bulalɛ akuma yɛle gyima, na eza ɔmanle bɛguale belekese. Ɔmanle Amɔnoma mɔɔ wɔ azua gyɛne gyɛne zo la yɛle gyima zɔhane bie. Akee Devidi nee ye ɛlɔnema ne ziale hɔle Gyɛlusalɛm.

english_verse: David had a beautiful daughter named Tamar, who was the sister of Absalom. She was also the half sister of Amnon, who fell in love with her.
translation_verse: Devidi ara nrenya Abesalɛm lɛ ɔ diema raalɛ anwo fɛlɛko ko. Bɛfɛlɛ ye Teemaa. Devidi lɛ ɔ ra nrenya bieko, bɛfɛlɛ ye Amenɔn. Na Amenɔn kulo Teemaa kpole kpalɛ.

english_verse: But Tamar was a virgin, and Amnon could not think of a way to be alone with her. He was so upset about it that he made himself sick.
translation_verse: Amenɔn hulole Teemaa toonwo ɔmanle ɛhulolɛ ne bɔle ye anwonyane, ɔboalekɛ, kɛmɔ ɛnee Teemaa le belamunli na ɔnze nrenya la ati, Amenɔn nwunle kɛ, ɔyɛ se kɛ ɔkɛhola ye debie yɛ.

english_verse: Amnon had a friend named Jonadab, who was the son of David's brother Shimeah. Jonadab always knew how to get what he wanted,
translation_verse: Amenɔn lɛ ɔ gɔnwo bie, bɛfɛlɛ ye Dwɔnadabe. Ɔ ze a le Devidi adiema Hyemɛya. Dwɔnadabe le sonla mɔɔ ze adwenle mgbole bɔ a.

english_verse: and he said to Amnon, “What's the matter? You're the king's son! You shouldn't have to go around feeling sorry for yourself every morning.” Amnon said, “I'm in love with Tamar, my brother Absalom's sister.”
translation_verse: Ɔzele Amenɔn kɛ, “Ɛle belemgbunli ra, noko dahuu biala ɛnee wɔyɛ ɛ nwo alɔbɔlɛ alɔbɔlɛ. Ka deɛ holɛ ko mɔɔ ɛlɛgyegye wɔ la kile me.” Amenɔn zele ye kɛ, “Mekulo me diema raalɛ Teemaa, mɔɔ le Abesalɛm ɔ nli ara ɛdeɛ ne.”

english_verse: Jonadab told him, “Lie down on your bed and pretend to be sick. When your father comes to see you, ask him to send Tamar, so you can watch her cook something for you. Then she can serve you the food.”
translation_verse: Dwɔnadabe zele ye kɛ, “Da na kpati yɛ kɛ ɛnde kpɔkɛ fee la. Saa wɔ papa ba kɛ ɔbakpɔla wɔ a ka kile ye kɛ, ‘Maa me diema raalɛ Teemaa ɛramaa me debie menli. Maa ɔrado deɛ ne wɔ ɛke na meanlea nu, na eza yeasesa yeawula me nloa anu.’ ”

english_verse: So Amnon went to bed and pretended to be sick. When the king came to see him, Amnon said, “Please, ask Tamar to come over. She can make some special bread while I watch, and then she can serve it to me.”
translation_verse: Yemɔti Amenɔn lale na ɔkpatile ɔyɛle kɛ asɛɛ yewu yewie ala ɛne. Mɔɔ belemgbunli ne rale kɛ ɔbakpɔla ye la, Amenɔn zele ye kɛ, “Mesɛlɛ wɔ, maa me diema Teemaa ɛrɛla ɛrayɛ debie ɛmaa me wɔ me nwo ɛke na ɔdaye mumua ne ɔsesa ɔwula me nloa anu.”

english_verse: David told Tamar, “Go over to Amnon's house and fix him some food.”
translation_verse: Yemɔti Devidi zoanle manle bɛhɔzele Teemaa kɛ, “Kɔ ɛ diema Amenɔn sua nu lɔ kɔdo debie maa ye.”

english_verse: When she got there, he was lying in bed. She mixed the dough, made the loaves, and baked them while he watched.
translation_verse: Teemaa hɔle na ɔhɔnwunle kɛ yela. Ɔvale ɛdɔkɛ ɔfetele ɔloale wɔ ɔ nyunlu ɛkɛ.

english_verse: Then she took the bread out of the pan and put it on his plate, but he refused to eat it. Amnon said, “Send the servants out of the house.” After they had gone,
translation_verse: Ɔvale ɔhɔziele Amenɔn anyunlu ɛkɛ, noko yeanli. Amenɔn zele ye kɛ, “Maa awie biala ɛvinde.” Yemɔti awie biala vindele.

english_verse: he said to Tamar, “Serve the food in my bedroom.” Tamar picked up the bread that she had made and brought it into Amnon's bedroom.
translation_verse: Akee Amenɔn zele Teemaa kɛ, “Fa aleɛ ne bɛla sua kunlu ɛke. Dɛ ye ɛ sa nu maa menli.” Teemaa vale aleɛ ne hɔmanle ye wɔ sua kunlu lɔ.

english_verse: But as she was taking it over to him, he grabbed her and said, “Come to bed with me!”
translation_verse: Mɔɔ ɔvale ɔbikyele ye kɛ ɔli la, ɔzɔle ye nu na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Me diema raalɛ, maa me nee wɔ ɛla.”

english_verse: She answered, “No! Please don't force me! This sort of thing isn't done in Israel. It's disgusting!
translation_verse: Ɔbuale ye kɛ, “Me diema, kyɛkyɛ, mmafa anwosesebɛ, ɛkye me mialera nu ɛ nee me yɛ debie biala, ɔluakɛ ɛbɛla zɛhae, bɛmbɔ ye fee wɔ Yizilayɛ maanle ye anu. Mmabɔ munzule ɛbɛla ɛhye.

english_verse: Think of me. I'll be disgraced forever! And think of yourself. Everyone in Israel will say you're nothing but trash! Just ask the king, and he will let you marry me.”
translation_verse: Nyiane kpole ɛhye, nienwu a mefa meabɔ me ti a? Na wɔmɔ, bɛkɛva ye kɛ Yizilayɛ sɛnvolɛma ne mɔ ko a le wɔ. Mesɛlɛ wɔ, fa ɛhye to belemgbunli anyunlu na ɔkɛva me ɔkɛmaa wɔ.”

english_verse: But Amnon would not listen to what she said. He was stronger than she was, so he overpowered her and raped her.
translation_verse: Noko Amenɔn amkponle; kɛmɔ ɔ nwo yɛ se tɛla ye la ati, ye anwosesebɛ ne bole Teemaa anwo zo, yemɔti ɔhyele ye mialera nu ɔvale ye.

english_verse: Then Amnon hated her even more than he had loved her before. So he told her, “Get up and get out!”
translation_verse: Amenɔn anye zo tetele ye la akee ɔkpɔle Teemaa ɔdɛlale kɛ ɔzile ɔhulole ye la. Na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Dwazo, finde kɔ.”

english_verse: She said, “Don't send me away! That would be worse than what you have already done.” But Amnon would not listen.
translation_verse: Teemaa zele ye kɛ, “Me diema, ɛvoanlɛ mɔɔ ɛlɛfoa me la akee le ɛtane kpole tɛla mɔɔ wɔyɛ la.” Noko Amenɔn andie ye.

english_verse: He called in his servant and said, “Throw this woman out and lock the door!”
translation_verse: Ɔvɛlɛle kpavolɛ ne mɔɔ sonle ye la na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Ye raalɛ ɛhye fi me nye zo ɛke, na to anlenkɛ ne anu.”

english_verse: The servant made her leave, and he locked the door behind her. The king's unmarried daughters used to wear long robes with sleeves.
translation_verse: Yemɔti ye sonvolɛ ne vindele ye na ɔdole anlenkɛ ne anu. Mekɛ ne anu ɛnee Teemaa wula tɛladeɛ tendenle asa ndendenle bie, ɔluakɛ tete ne, ɛnee adɛladeɛ mɔɔ belemgbunli amra mraalɛ mɔɔ ɛtɛkɔle agyalɛ ɛlɛ la wula la ɛne.

english_verse: Tamar tore the robe she was wearing and put ashes on her head. Then she covered her face with her hands and cried loudly as she walked away. Absalom Kills Amnon
translation_verse: Teemaa suosuanle tɛladeɛ ne mɔɔ ɔwula la anu na ɔvulale nzonle ɔguale ɔ ti zo. Ɔvale ɔ sa ɔguale ɔ ti zo na ɔzunle. Mɔɔ ɔlɛkɔ la ɛnee ɔlɛsu.

english_verse: Tamar's brother Absalom said to her, “How could Amnon have done such a terrible thing to you! But since he's your brother, don't tell anyone what happened. Just try not to think about it.” Tamar soon moved into Absalom's house, but she was always sad and lonely.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ ɔ diema Abesalɛm nwunle ye la, ɔbizale ye kɛ, “Amenɔn ɛfunlofunla wɔ ɔ? Me diema, mmasu. Ɛdawɔ ɛ diema ɔ; debie biala mɔɔ yeyɛ wɔ la mmafa ɛsie ɛ ti anu yɛɛ mmaka ɛkile awie biala.” Yemɔti Teemaa vale alɔbɔlɛ nee nyane dɛnlanle Abesalɛm sua nu ɛkɛ.

english_verse: Absalom treated Amnon as though nothing had happened, but he hated Amnon for what he had done to his sister Tamar.
translation_verse: Abesalɛm ɛdeɛ, yeambuke ɔ nloa yeanga ɛhwee yeangile Amenɔn; ɔluakɛ ɛnee akee ɔkyi ye, ɔboalekɛ yeva anwosesebɛ yehye ɔ diema raalɛ ne mialera nu yeva ye. Abesalɛm di nzenralɛ

english_verse: Two years later, Absalom's servants were cutting wool from his sheep in Baal-Hazor near the town of Ephraim, and Absalom invited all of the king's sons to be there.
translation_verse: Ɛvolɛ nwiɔ pɛle nu la, Abesalɛm pepɛle mboane nwo enrinli wɔ Beeyale Heezɔ mɔɔ zua Yifelaem la na ɔdole nwolɛ ɛkponle. Ɔdole ɛsalɛ ɔvɛlɛle belemgbunli amra mrenya ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti.

english_verse: Then he went to David and said, “My servants are cutting the wool from my sheep. Please come and join us!”
translation_verse: Abesalɛm eza hɔle belemgbunli ɛkɛ ne hɔzele ye kɛ, “Nana, melɛpepɛ me mboane ne mɔ anwo enrinli. Mesɛlɛ wɔ, Nana, ɛ nee wɔ mgbanyima ne mɔ bɛrɛla nwolɛ ɛkponledolɛ ne abo.”

english_verse: David answered, “No, my son, we won't go. It would be too expensive for you.” Absalom tried to get him to change his mind, but David did not want to go. He only said that he hoped they would have a good time.
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne zele ye kɛ, “Kyɛkyɛ, me ra, yɛ muala yɛkɔ a ɔnrɛyɛ boɛ; ɛ nwo kɛhyele wɔ.” Abesalɛm yɛle mɔɔ kɛyɛ boɛ, noko belemgbunli angɔ. Na ɔyileyilale ye kosoɛɛ kɛ ɔhɔ.

english_verse: Absalom said, “If you won't go, at least let my brother Amnon come with us.” David asked, “Why should he go with you?”
translation_verse: Akee Abesalɛm hanle hilele ye kɛ, “Mesɛlɛ wɔ, saa ɛnrɛnyia adenle ɛnrɛra ɛdeɛ a ɛnee maa me diema Amenɔn ɛrɛla.” Belemgbunli bizale ye kɛ, “Duzu ati ɔ?”

english_verse: But Absalom kept on insisting, and finally David let Amnon and all his other sons go with Absalom. Absalom prepared a banquet fit for a king.
translation_verse: Noko Abesalɛm hanle toonwo ɔmanle ɔ ze manle ɔ nee Amenɔn nee ɔ mediema mrenya ne mɔ amuala hɔle.

english_verse: But he told his servants, “Keep an eye on Amnon. When he gets a little drunk from the wine and is feeling relaxed, I'll give the signal. Then kill him! I've commanded you to do it, so don't be afraid. Be strong and brave.”
translation_verse: Na Abesalɛm zele ye sonvolɛma ne mɔ kɛ, “Bɛdie, saa bɛnwu kɛ Amenɔn ɛbo kpalɛ kpalɛ na mese bɛ kɛ, ‘Bɛyɛ bɛmaa Amenɔn’ a, bɛhu ye. Bɛmmasulo; medame a mese a. Bɛzi ahonle na bɛli mrenyasɛm.”

english_verse: Absalom's servants killed Amnon, just as Absalom had told them. The rest of the king's sons quickly rode away on their mules to escape from Absalom.
translation_verse: Kɛmɔ Abesalɛm zele bɛ la, sonvolɛma ne mɔ yɛle ye zɔhane ala. Na Devidi amra ne mɔ mɔɔ hale la vole bɛ mgbɔnwɔ ne mɔ azo nriandile hɔle.

english_verse: While they were on their way to Jerusalem, someone told David, “Absalom has killed all of your sons! Not even one is left.”
translation_verse: Mɔɔ bɛlua adenle zo la, nrɛlaleɛ dole Devidi kɛ, “Abesalɛm ɛhu belemgbunli amra ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti, ko bɔbɔ anga.”

english_verse: David got up, and in his sorrow he tore his clothes and lay down on the ground. His servants remained standing, but they tore their clothes too.
translation_verse: Belemgbunli manle ɔ nwo zo, ɔsuosuanle ye tɛladeɛ ne anu na ɔweweɛle ɔ nwo aze. Ye sonvolɛma mɔɔ nee ye wɔ ɛkɛ ne la noko suosuanle bɛ adɛladeɛ ne mɔ anu.

english_verse: Then David's nephew Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, not all of your sons were killed! Only Amnon is dead. On the day that Amnon raped Tamar, Absalom decided to kill him.
translation_verse: Na Devidi adiema Hyemɛya ara Dwɔnadabe hanle kɛ, “Nana, bɛtɛkunle ɛ mra ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti. Amenɔn angomekye a ɛwu a. Ɔluakɛ sumunli kɛ Amenɔn hyele Abesalɛm adiema raalɛ Teemaa mialera nu vale ye la yɛɛ ɔbɔle ye ɛhunlɛ nwo adwenle ɔdole ɛkɛ a.

english_verse: Don't worry about the report that all your sons were killed. Only Amnon is dead,
translation_verse: Yemɔti Nana, mmadwenle kɛ ɛ mra ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti ɛwu; Amenɔn ala a ɛwu a.”

english_verse: and Absalom has run away.” One of the guards noticed a lot of people coming along the hillside on the road to Horonaim. He went and told the king, “I saw some men coming along Horonaim Road.”
translation_verse: Akee Abesalɛm nriandile. Mekɛ ne anu ala, ɛlɔnenli ne mɔɔ ɛlɛsinza la dole ɔ nye, na ɔnwunle kɛ menli dɔɔnwo vi Hɔlɔneeyem adenle zo ɛlɛtolo boka ne ara.

english_verse: Jonadab said, “Your Majesty, look! Here come your sons now, just as I told you.”
translation_verse: Na Dwɔnadabe zele belemgbunli ne kɛ, “Nana, kɛmɔ wɔ sonvolɛ menganle la, yeyɛ zɔhane, ɛ mra ne mɔ ɛra.”

english_verse: No sooner had he said it, than David's sons came in. They were weeping out loud, and David and all his officials cried just as loudly.
translation_verse: Ɔ nloa ampe bɔbɔ ɛnee belemgbunli amra ne mɔ ɛvinde ɛkɛ. Bɛdukuele nuhua bɛzunle bɛmanle belemgbunli nee menli mɔɔ wɔ ɛkɛ ne la amuala zunle bie.

english_verse: David was sad for a long time because Amnon was dead. David Lets Absalom Come Home Absalom had run away to Geshur, where he stayed for three years with King Talmai the son of Ammihud.
translation_verse: Abesalɛm nriandile la ɔhɔle Gihyɛ Belemgbunli Talemae mɔɔ ɔ ze a le Amehɛde la anwo lɔ. Ɔdɛnlanle nehane ɛvolɛ nsa. Devidi zunle ɔ ra Amenɔn hyɛle.

english_verse: David still felt so sad over the loss of Amnon that he wanted to take his army there and capture Absalom.
translation_verse: Na mɔɔ akee Devidi arɛle vile Amenɔn ewule ne la, ɔ nwo lɔle ɔ ra Abesalɛm.

english_verse: Joab knew that David couldn't stop thinking about Absalom,
translation_verse: Akee Zɛluaya ara Dwowabe nwunle kɛ Belemgbunli Devidi anwo ɛlɛdɔ Abesalɛm kpole,

english_verse: The woman from Tekoa went to David. She bowed very low and said, “Your Majesty, please help me!”
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Tɛkowa raalɛ ne hɔle belemgbunli ne ɛkɛ ne la, ɔdule ɔdɔle ɔ gyakɛ anu enililɛ nu na ɔhanle kɛ, “Nana, mesɛlɛ wɔ, boa me.”

english_verse: David asked, “What's the matter?” She replied: My husband is dead, and I'm a widow.
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne bizale ye kɛ, “Duzu a ɛhyia wɔ a?” Ɔbuale ye kɛ, “Nana, mele kunlanvolɛ, me hu ɛwu.

english_verse: I had two sons, but they got into a fight out in a field where there was no one to pull them apart, and one of them killed the other.
translation_verse: Wɔ sonvolɛ raalɛ, melɛ mralɛ mrenya nwiɔ; bɛlile butule wɔ ɛbɔ nu, bɛannyia awie amkpɔda bɛ, yemɔti ko bɔle ɔ gɔnwo debie hunle ye.

english_verse: Now all of my relatives have come to me and said, “Hand over your son! We're going to put him to death for killing his brother.” But what they really want is to get rid of him, so they can take over our land. Please don't let them put out my only flame of hope! There won't be anyone left on this earth to carry on my husband's name.
translation_verse: Kɛkala, me nwo amra kɔsɔɔti ɛhɔ afoa na bɛze me kɛ, ‘Fa sonla ne mɔɔ hunle ɔ diema ne la bɛla maa yɛhu ye bie.’ Saa bɛyɛ ɛhye a ɛnee ɔkile kɛ bɛnlua me anyevinli ala ɛne. Me hu ɛnrɛnyia ye kɔliagya yɛɛ ye duma baminli ewiade ye anu.”

english_verse: “Go on home,” David told her. “I'll take care of this matter for you.”
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne zele raalɛ ne kɛ, “Kɔ sua nu na mebanlea meaziezie wɔ edwɛkɛ ne.”

english_verse: The woman said, “I hope your decision doesn't cause any problems for you. But if it does, you can blame me.”
translation_verse: Na Tɛkowa raalɛ ne hanle hilele belemgbunli ne kɛ, “Nana, mɔɔ ɛkɛyɛ la biala anwo fɔlɛlilɛ ne ɛgua me nee egya awuke nu amra yɛ ti zo. Belemgbunli nee ye dehelɛ abusua ne ɛnli fɔlɛ.”

english_verse: He said, “If anyone gives you trouble, bring them to me, and it won't happen again!”
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne zele kɛ, “Awie biala mɔɔ kɛnwunlonwunla wɔ la, baha kile me na ɔnrɛyɛ zɔhane bieko ɛlɛ.”

english_verse: “Please,” she replied, “swear by the Lord your God that no one will be allowed to kill my son!” He said, “I swear by the living Lord that no one will touch even a hair on his head!”
translation_verse: Raalɛ ne hanle kɛ, “Nana, ka Ɛdɛnkɛma wɔ Nyamenle ne kɛ menli mɔɔ di mogya nzenralɛ la ɛnrɛha mogya ɛnrɛgua bieko, amaa me ra ne anyia ɔ ti.” Belemgbunli ne hanle kɛ, “Meka tete Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ, ɛ ra nrenya ne ati enrinli ko bɔbɔ ɛnrɛde ɛnrɛdɔ aze.”

english_verse: Then she asked, “Your Majesty, may I say something?” “Yes,” he answered.
translation_verse: Akee raalɛ ne zele kɛ, “Nana, mesɛlɛ wɔ, wɔ sonvolɛ raalɛ, mekulo kɛ meka edwɛkɛ kpɔkɛ ko.” Belemgbunli ne zele ye kɛ, “Tendɛ.”

english_verse: The woman said: Haven't you been hurting God's people? Your own son had to leave the country. And when you judged in my favor, it was the same as admitting that you should have let him come back.
translation_verse: Raalɛ ne hanle kɛ, “Na duzu ati yɛɛ wɔyɛ ɛtane ɛhye wɔtia Nyamenle menli ne a? Edwɛkɛ ɛhye mɔɔ wɔha la kile kɛ wɔbu ɛ nwo fɔlɛ. Duzu ati a ɛnrɛmaa ɛ ra nrenya ne mɔɔ ɛdɔ ɛbɔ nu la ɛnrɛzia ɛnrɛra ɛ?

english_verse: We each must die and disappear like water poured out on the ground. But God doesn't take our lives. Instead, he figures out ways of bringing us back when we run away.
translation_verse: Ɔwɔ nuhua kɛ yɛ muala yɛbawu. Yɛle kɛ nzule mɔɔ ɛbɔ ɛkponde azɛlɛ nwo la, ɛsa ye bieko a ɔnyɛ boɛ. Nyamenle ɛngu sonla, na ɔfa adenle bie azo ɔmaa sonla mɔɔ ɔdaye Nyamenle yevoa ye la ɛnga ye sonlamgbane nu. Sonla mɔɔ ɛva sulosulo ɛdɔ ɛbɔ nu la noko, belemgbunli kola maa ɔsia ɔba sua nu bieko.

english_verse: Your Majesty, I came here to tell you about my problem, because I was afraid of what someone might do to me. I decided to come to you, because I thought you could help.
translation_verse: Mera kɛ mebaha edwɛkɛ ɛhye meahile wɔ, Nana, ɔboalekɛ menli ne ɛha me ɛzulolɛ; yɛɛ melɛ anyelazo kɛ ɛkɛyɛ me ɛbizalɛdeɛ ɛkɛmaa me.

english_verse: In fact, I knew that you would listen and save my son and me from those who want to take the land that God gave us.
translation_verse: Meze kɛ belemgbunli badie me na yealie me yeavi ahenle ne mɔɔ kpondɛ kɛ ɔku me nee me ra nrenya ne na ɔye yɛ aluma ɔfi azɛlɛ ye mɔɔ Nyamenle ɛva ɛmaa ye menli la azo la asa anu.

english_verse: I can rest easy now that you have given your decision. You know the difference between right and wrong just like an angel of God, and I pray that the Lord your God will be with you.
translation_verse: Wɔ sonvolɛ raalɛ, menyianle adwenle kɛ me awulae belemgbunli baha me ahonle ado azule nu, ɔluakɛ me awulae belemgbunli le kɛ Nyamenle soanvolɛ la, ɔze kpalɛ, ɔze ɛtane. Ɛdɛnkɛma wɔ Nyamenle ne nee wɔ ɛlua.”

english_verse: Then David said to the woman, “Now I'm going to ask you a question, and don't try to hide the truth!” The woman replied, “Please go ahead, Your Majesty.”
translation_verse: Na belemgbunli ne zele raalɛ ne kɛ, “Mmafa debie biala ɛfea me. Edwɛkɛ mɔɔ mebiza wɔ la, kpakye nuhua wienyi ka kile me.” Raalɛ ne hanle kɛ, “Nana, tendɛ.”

english_verse: David asked, “Did Joab put you up to this?” The woman answered, “Your Majesty, I swear by your life that no one can hide the truth from you. Yes, Joab did tell me what to say,
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne bizale ye kɛ, “Ɛnee Dwowabe a ɛha edwɛkɛ ɛhye ɛhile wɔ a?” Raalɛ ne buale kɛ, “Meka meka kɛ, mekoati wɔ kpuyia ye anwo fee a ɔnyɛ boɛ. Nana, kɛmɔ ɛdawɔ wɔha la, wɔ sonvolɛ Dwowabe yɛɛ bɔle adwenle ɛhye a. Yemɔ yɛɛ ɔhilele me mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ meyɛ nee mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ meka la amuala a.

english_verse: but only to show you the other side of this problem. You must be as wise as the angel of God to know everything that goes on in this country.”
translation_verse: Na ɔyɛle ɛhye kɛ ɔfa yeamaa boɛ adoa boɛ. Nana ze nrɛlɛbɛ kɛ Nyamenle soanvolɛ, ɔze aleɛabo edwɛkɛ biala.”

english_verse: David turned to Joab and said, “It seems that I have already given my decision. Go and bring Absalom back.”
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne zele Dwowabe kɛ, “Mekponle wɔ nzuzulɛ ne azo. Kɔ na kɔva Abesalɛm bɛla.”

english_verse: Joab bowed very low and said, “Your Majesty, I thank you for giving your permission. It shows that you approve of me.”
translation_verse: Na Dwowabe dule dɔle belemgbunli agyakɛ anu enililɛ nu na ɔhanvole ye ɔzele kɛ, “Ɛnɛ demua ye, wɔ sonvolɛ, menwu ye wienyi kɛ Nana kulo me edwɛkɛ, yemɔti yɛɛ wɔkponle me ɛbizalɛdeɛ ye wɔmaa me a.”

english_verse: Joab went to Geshur to get Absalom. But when they came back to Jerusalem,
translation_verse: Na Dwowabe hanle ɔ nwo hɔle Gihyɛ hɔvale Abesalɛm rale Gyɛlusalɛm.

english_verse: David told Joab, “I don't want to see my son Absalom. Tell him to stay away from me.” So Absalom went to his own house without seeing his father. Absalom Was Handsome
translation_verse: Na belemgbunli ne zele kɛ, “Mmamaa ɔba suakunlu ɛke. Maa ɔdɛnla ɔdaye ye sua nu. Memkpondɛ kɛ me nye nwu ye.” Yemɔti Abesalɛm angɔ belemgbunli suakunlu ɛkɛ, ɔdɛnlanle ɔdaye ye sua nu. Devidi fa Abesalɛm anwo edwɛkɛ ahyɛ ye

english_verse: His hair grew so thick and heavy that when he got it cut once a year, it weighed over two kilograms.
translation_verse: Ɔ ti enrinli le buzuu yɛɛ nuhua pi. Yemɔti ɛvolɛ biala ɔpepɛ, amaa yeanyɛ ɛnlomboɛ somaa yeammaa ye. Ɔpepɛ enrinli ne na ɔsuzu a ɔto tone nu kilo nwiɔ, kɛmɔ belemgbunli nzuzudeɛ ne kile la.

english_verse: Absalom had three sons. He also had a daughter named Tamar, who grew up to be very beautiful. Absalom Finally Sees David
translation_verse: Abesalɛm wole mralɛ mrenya nsa yɛɛ ralɛ raalɛ ko, bɛfɛlɛ ye Teemaa na ye anwofɛlɛko ne bo zolɛ.

english_verse: Absalom lived in Jerusalem for two years without seeing his father.
translation_verse: Abesalɛm dɛnlanle Gyɛlusalɛm toonwo ɛvolɛ nwiɔ, noko ɔ nye annwu belemgbunli anyunlu ɛlɛ.

english_verse: He wanted Joab to talk to David for him. So one day he sent a message asking Joab to come over, but Joab refused. Absalom sent another message, but Joab still refused.
translation_verse: Yemɔti ɔzoanle ɔmanle bɛhɔvɛlɛle Dwowabe kɛ ɔrava ye ɔhɔ belemgbunli ɛkɛ; na Dwowabe angɔ. Ɔzoanle bieko, na Dwowabe angɔ.

english_verse: Finally, Absalom told his servants, “Joab's barley field is right next to mine. Go set it on fire!” And they did.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Abesalɛm zele ye sonvolɛma ne kɛ, “Bɛhɔ ɛbɔ ne anu; bɛbanwu kɛ Dwowabe ma ɛya avule ne zua me ɛdeɛ ne. Bɛhɔdo senle nu bɛyela ye.” Na Abesalɛm sonvolɛma ne hɔdole senle ɛya ne anu yelale ye.

english_verse: Joab went to Absalom's house and demanded, “Why did your servants set my field on fire?”
translation_verse: Dwowabe zile nu hɔle Abesalɛm sua nu hɔbizale ye kɛ, “Duzu ati a wɔ sonvolɛma ne ɛhɔdo senle me ɛya ne anu ɛ?”

english_verse: Absalom answered, “You didn't pay any attention when I sent for you. I want you to ask my father why he told me to come back from Geshur. I was better off there. I want to see my father now! If I'm guilty, let him kill me.”
translation_verse: Abesalɛm buale ye kɛ, “Mengɛlale wɔ nrɛlaleɛ kɛ ɛrɛla, amaa meazoa wɔ wɔ belemgbunli ɛkɛ meamaa wɔahɔbiza ye kɛ, ‘Duzu ati a wɔmaa mevi Gihyɛ mera ɛ? Ɔle kpalɛ kɛ anrɛɛ mendɛnlanle nehane.’ Yemɔti mekpondɛ kɛ ɛ nee me kɔ belemgbunli ɛkɛ ne. Saa medi fɔlɛ a ɔhu me.”

english_verse: Joab went to David and told him what Absalom had said. David sent for Absalom, and Absalom came. He bowed very low, and David leaned over and kissed him.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Dwowabe hɔle belemgbunli ɛkɛ ne na ɔhɔbɔle ye amaneɛ. Belemgbunli zoanle manle bɛhɔvɛlɛle Abesalɛm, na Abesalɛm rale. Ɔdwule ɛkɛ ne la, ɔbutule azɛlɛ ne anwo ɔbɔle ɔ ti aze ɔmanle ye na belemgbunli ne vale Abesalɛm bɔle ye ɛbolɛ.

english_verse: Some time later, Absalom got himself a chariot with horses to pull it, and he had
translation_verse: Ɛhye anzi, Abesalɛm nyianle ye konle ehwili nee nwolɛ mgbɔnwɔ yɛɛ sinzavolɛma abulanlu.

english_verse: He would get up early each morning and wait by the side of the road that led to the city gate. Anyone who had a complaint to bring to King David would have to go that way, and Absalom would ask each of them, “Where are you from?” If they said, “I'm from a tribe in the north,”
translation_verse: Alehyenlɛ biala nwonlomɔ mangyee ne Abesalɛm kɔgyinla suakpole ne anlenkɛ kpole ne anloa. Na saa awie lɛ ye edwɛkɛ kamaa belemgbunli aziezie a ɛnee ɔbiza ye kɛ, “Ɛvi suakpole boni azo?” Na saa ɔka kɛ, “Wɔ sonvolɛ, mevi Yizilayɛ abusua ekpunli zɛhae anu” a,

english_verse: Absalom would say, “You deserve to win your case. It's too bad the king doesn't have anyone to hear complaints like yours.
translation_verse: ɛnee Abesalɛm ɛha ɛhile ye kɛ, “Nea, wɔ edwɛkɛ yɛ fɛ bɔkɔɔ na belemgbunli ɛnlɛ awie kpaziwɔkɛ biala mɔɔ di wɔ edwɛkɛ ne amaa wɔ a.”

english_verse: I wish someone would make me the judge around here! I would be fair to everyone.”
translation_verse: Eza ɔfa ɔsɔ zolɛ kɛ, “Me kunlu a anrɛɛ mame a mele maanle ye ndɛnebuavolɛ a! Anrɛɛ awie biala mɔɔ kɛva ye edwɛkɛ kɛrɛlɛ me la menwɔli ye nɔhalɛ nu menwɔmaa ye.”

english_verse: Whenever anyone came to Absalom and started bowing down, he would reach out and hug and kiss them.
translation_verse: Saa ahenle bikye ye kɛ ɔbabɔ ɔ ti aze yeamaa ye a ɛnee yezɔ ahenle yeyɛ ye atuu.

english_verse: That's how he treated everyone from Israel who brought a complaint to the king. Soon everyone in Israel liked Absalom better than they liked David.
translation_verse: Ɛhye yɛɛ Abesalɛm yɛle manle Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti mɔɔ rale belemgbunli ɛkɛ ne kɛ ɔziezie bɛ edwɛkɛ ɔmaa bɛ la a. Ɛhye manle Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti hulole Abesalɛm edwɛkɛ.

english_verse: Four years later, Absalom said to David, “Please, let me go to Hebron. I have to keep a promise that I made to the Lord,
translation_verse: Ɛvolɛ nna pɛle nu la Abesalɛm zele belemgbunli ne kɛ, “Nana, mesɛlɛ wɔ, maa me adenle maa mengɔ Hibulɔn mengɔnye me ɛwɔkɛ mɔɔ membɔle Ɛdɛnkɛma la.

english_verse: when I was living with the Arameans in Geshur. I promised that if the Lord would bring me back to live in Jerusalem, I would worship him in Hebron.”
translation_verse: Mekɛ mɔɔ mewɔ Gihyɛ mɔɔ wɔ Arelam la, membɔle ɛwɔkɛ kɛ, ‘Saa Ɛdɛnkɛma boa me maa mesia meba Gyɛlusalɛm a, menwɔhɔzonle ye wɔ Hibulɔn.’ ”

english_verse: David gave his permission, and Absalom went to Hebron.
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne zele ye kɛ, “Kɔ anzonudwolɛ nu.” Yemɔti Abesalɛm hɔle Hibulɔn.

english_verse: A messenger came and told David, “Everyone in Israel is on Absalom's side!”
translation_verse: Ɛbɔfoɔ rale Devidi ɛkɛ razele ye kɛ, “Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti ɛkpo wɔ na bɛva bɛ ahonle bɛmaa Abesalɛm.”

english_verse: David's officials were in Jerusalem with him, and he told them, “Let's get out of here! We'll have to leave soon, or none of us will escape from Absalom. Hurry! If he moves fast, he could catch us while we're still here. Then he will kill us and everyone else in the city.”
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Devidi dele la ɔzele ye mgbanyima kɔsɔɔti mɔɔ nee ye wɔ Gyɛlusalɛm ɛkɛ ne la kɛ, “Bɛha bɛ nwo bɛmaa yɛye yɛ nwo zo na anrɛɛ Abesalɛm kɛbɔ yɛ bo zo bɔkɔɔ. Bɛha bɛ nwo na anrɛɛ ɔkɛbu yɛ nyunlu ɔkɛmaa munzule kɛdo yɛ na ɔkɛbɔ suakpole ye tɔɔ!”

english_verse: Then David stood there and watched while his regular troops and his bodyguards marched past. The last group was the
translation_verse: Ye mgbanyima ne mɔ razenle, na bɛgyinlanle ye foa ko. Ye sinzavolɛma ne mɔ zenle lumuale ɔ nyunlu. Ɛlɔnema ɛya nsia ne mɔɔ ɔ nee bɛ vi Gate la noko zenle lumuale ɔ nyunlu.

english_verse: David spoke to Ittai and said, “You're a foreigner from the town of Gath. You don't have to leave with us. Go back and join the new king!
translation_verse: Akee belemgbunli ne zele Yeteeyae mɔɔ nea bɛ nwo zo la kɛ, “Duzu ati a ɛdawɔ noko ɛboka yɛ nwo a? Sia kɔ kɔdɛnla belemgbunli fofolɛ ne anwo ɛkɛ, ɔluakɛ ɛle ɛyɛvolɛ, yɛɛ eza ɛvi wɔ maanle nu a wɔnriandi wɔradane a.

english_verse: You haven't been with me very long, so why should you have to follow me, when I don't even know where I'm going? Take your soldiers and go back. I pray that the Lord will be kind and faithful to you.”
translation_verse: Anoma ala a ɛdwule ɛke a. Duzu ati a ɔwɔ kɛ mefa wɔ mekɔduolua nu wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɛleka mumua ne mɔɔ melɛkɔ la, medame menze la a? Fa ɛ mediema ne mɔ sia kɔ. Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛhile ye ɛhulolɛ kpole ne ɛmaa wɔ na ɔ nee wɔ ɛlua kɛnlɛma.”

english_verse: Ittai answered, “Your Majesty, just as surely as you and the Lord live, I will go where you go, no matter if it costs me my life.”
translation_verse: Na Yeteeyae buale belemgbunli ne kɛ, “Nana, meka tease Ɛdɛnkɛma metane wɔ kɛ, ɛleka biala mɔɔ me awulae belemgbunli ne kɔ la, saa ewule nu o, ngoane nu o, wɔ sonvolɛ, me nee wɔ bahɔ.”

english_verse: “Then come on!” David said. So Ittai and all his men and their families walked on past David. David Sends the Sacred Chest Back to Jerusalem
translation_verse: Na Devidi zele Yeteeyae kɛ, “Baze kɔ ɛ.” Yemɔti Yeteeyae nee ɔ sa zo ne mɔ, mgbanyinli nee ngakula kɔsɔɔti zenle hɔle.

english_verse: The people of Jerusalem were crying and moaning as David and everyone with him passed by. He led them across Kidron Valley and along the road toward the desert.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ menli ne mɔ kɔ la ezuavolɛ ne kɔsɔɔti zunle. Belemgbunli ne hɔpɛle azudenle Kedelɔn ne; menli ne kɔsɔɔti noko pɛle na bɛbɔle bɛ ti fienemgbole ne anu lɔ.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar the priests were there along with several men from the tribe of Levi who were carrying the sacred chest. They set the chest down, and left it there until David and his followers had gone out of the city.
translation_verse: Abayata rale bie, Zeedɔko nee Livaema mɔɔ zo Nyamenle Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne la noko rale. Bɛzokoɛle bɛziele ye aze hɔkpulale mekɛ mɔɔ menli ne amuala wiele se la.

english_verse: Then David said: Zadok, take the sacred chest back to Jerusalem. If the Lord is pleased with me, he will bring me back and let me see it and his tent again.
translation_verse: Akee belemgbunli ne zele Zeedɔko kɛ, “Bɛva Nyamenle Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne bɛzia bɛhɔ suakpole ne azo. Saa ɔyɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛhulolɛ a, ɔbamaa meazia mearanwu ye bieko nee ye Ndanlɛ Sua ne;

english_verse: But if he says he isn't pleased with me, then let him do what he knows is best.
translation_verse: na saa ɔse kɛ ɔ nye ɛnlie me nwo a, debie biala mɔɔ ɔkulo la ɔva ɔyɛ me.”

english_verse: Zadok, you are a good judge of things, so return to the city and don't cause any trouble. Take your son Ahimaaz with you. Abiathar and his son Jonathan will also go back.
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne eza zele sɛlɛvolɛ Zeedɔko kɛ, “Fa ɛ ra nrenya Ahaemaze nee Abayata ara nrenya Dwɔnatan sia kɔ suakpole ne azo anzonudwolɛ nu.

english_verse: I'll wait at the river crossing in the desert until I hear from you.
translation_verse: Mebahendɛ azule ne anloa, ɛleka mɔɔ bɛpɛ la wɔ fienemgbole ye anu kɔkpula mekɛ mɔɔ menwɔde ɛ nloa anu nrɛlaleɛ la.”

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar took the sacred chest back into Jerusalem and stayed there.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Zeedɔko nee Abayata vale Nyamenle Ngyekyeleɛ Ɛlɛka ne ziale hɔle Gyɛlusalɛm na bɛhɔdɛnlanle ɛkɛ.

english_verse: David went on up the slope of the Mount of Olives. He was barefoot and crying, and he covered his head to show his sorrow. Everyone with him was crying, and they covered their heads too.
translation_verse: Devidi vole hɔle Ɔlivi Boka ne azo. Ɔkɔ la ɛnee ɔlɛsu, ɔ gyakɛ gua aze na yeheda ɔ ti zo, na bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛ nee ye lua la noko hedɛhedale bɛ ti zo. Bɛhɔle boka ne azo; bɛkɔ la ɛnee bɛlɛsu.

english_verse: Someone told David, “Ahithophel is helping Absalom plot against you!” David said, “Please, Lord, keep Ahithophel's plans from working!” David Sends Hushai Back as a Spy
translation_verse: Bɛhanle bɛhilele Devidi kɛ, “Ahetɔfɛle boka maamɔvoma mɔɔ nee Abesalɛm lua la anwo.” Na Devidi zele kɛ, “O Ɛdɛnkɛma, mesɛlɛ wɔ, maa Ahetɔfɛle folɛdulɛ biala ɛyɛ mgbane.”

english_verse: When David reached the top of the Mount of Olives, he met Hushai the Archite at a place of worship. Hushai's robe was torn, and dust was on his head.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Devidi dwule boka ne azo, ɛleka mɔɔ bɛsonle Nyamenle la, Akaenli Huhyae rayiale ye, ɛnee yesuosua ye tɛladeɛ ne anu na yeva ndɛtɛlɛ yeyɛ ɔ ti zo.

english_verse: David told him: If you come with me, you might slow us down.
translation_verse: Devidi zele ye kɛ, “Saa ɛ nee me kɔ a ɛbayɛ ngyegyelɛ wɔamaa me.

english_verse: Go back into the city and tell Absalom, “Your Majesty, I am your servant. I will serve you now, just as I served your father in the past.” Hushai, if you do that, you can help me ruin Ahithophel's plans.
translation_verse: Sia kɔ suakpole ne azo na kɔze Abesalɛm kɛ, ‘O belemgbunli, mele wɔ sonvolɛ; mekɛ bie mɔɔ ɛze ɛhɔ la, menzonlenle ɛ ze, zɔhane ala yɛɛ mera mebazonle wɔ a.’ Ye zɛhae, yemɔ ɛbahola wɔazɛkye Ahetɔfɛle maamɔvo adwenle biala mɔɔ ɔkɛbɔ la.

english_verse: Zadok and Abiathar the priests will be there with you, and you can tell them everything you hear in the palace.
translation_verse: Zeedɔko nee Abayata a le sɛlɛvolɛma mɔɔ bɛ nee bɛ wɔ lɔ a. Edwɛkɛ biala mɔɔ bɛkɛha wɔ belemgbunli suakunlu ɛkɛ ne la baha kile bɛ.

english_verse: Then they can send their sons Ahimaaz and Jonathan to tell me what you've heard.
translation_verse: Bɛ mra mrenya nwiɔ ne, Zeedɔko ara Ahaemaze nee Abayata ara Dwɔnatan wɔ lɔ. Edwɛkɛ biala mɔɔ kɛzi la, bɛzoa bɛ bɛmaa bɛraha bɛhile me.”

english_verse: David's advisor Hushai slipped back into Jerusalem, at just about the same time Absalom was coming in.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Devidi agɔnwo Huhyae ziale hɔle suakpole ne azo wɔ mekɛ ko ne ala mɔɔ ɛnee Abesalɛm ɛlɛba aravo Gyɛlusalɛm la.

english_verse: David had started down the other side of the Mount of Olives, when he was met by Ziba, the chief servant of Mephibosheth. Ziba had two donkeys that were carrying
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Devidi hɔle ɔ nyunlu ekyii wɔ boka ne azo la, ɔ nee Mɛfebɔhyɛte sonvolɛ Zaeba yiale arɛlevilɛ nu. Ɔlɛ asoaso nwiɔ mɔɔ bɛva bɛ bɛbɔ nwo la, na yeva kpanwo ahunguma ɛya nwiɔ, vanye ma welera siakɛ ɛya ko, bakama amolɛ siakɛ ɛya ko yɛɛ nwanye kodoku ko yekyekye asoaso ne mɔ anzi.

english_verse: “What's all this?” David asked. Ziba said, “The donkeys are for your family to ride. The bread and fruit are for the people to eat, and the wine is for them to drink in the desert when they are tired out.”
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne bizale Zaeba kɛ, “Duzu ati a wɔva ninyɛne ɛhye mɔ kɔsɔɔti wɔra a?” Zaeba buale ye kɛ, “Asoaso ne mɔ le belemgbunli awuke nu amra ɛdeɛ kɛ bɛdɛnla zolɛ, kpanwo ne nee ma amolɛ ne le mgbavolɛ ne mɔ ɛdeɛ, yɛɛ nwanye ne le bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛ nwo kɛbɛlɛ bɛ wɔ fienemgbole ne anu la ɛdeɛ.”

english_verse: “And where is Mephibosheth?” David asked. Ziba answered, “He stayed in Jerusalem, because he thinks the people of Israel want him to rule the kingdom of his grandfather Saul.”
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne bizale ye kɛ, “Na ɛ menle ara nrenya ne wɔ nienwu?” Zaeba buale ye kɛ, “Ɔwɔ Gyɛlusalɛm; ɔse, ‘Ɔze ye wienyi kɛ Yizilayɛma bava ɔ ze belemgbunli maanle ne amaa ye.’ ”

english_verse: David then told him, “Everything that used to belong to Mephibosheth is now yours.” Ziba said, “Your Majesty, I am your humble servant, and I hope you will be pleased with me.” Shimei Curses David
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne zele Zaeba kɛ, “Nea, debie biala mɔɔ le Mɛfebɔhyɛte ɛdeɛ la le wɔ ɛdeɛ.” Zaeba zele kɛ, “Mele wɔ sonvolɛ; dahuu mebayɛ mɔɔ belemgbunli ne kpondɛ la.” Devidi nee Hyemɛyae

english_verse: David was near the town of Bahurim when a man came out and started cursing him. The man was Shimei the son of Gera, and he was one of Saul's distant relatives.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Belemgbunli Devidi dwule Bahulem la, Sɔɔlo abo zo amra ne mɔ ko, mɔɔ le Gila ara Hyemɛyae, rayiale ye. Ɔba kɔsɔɔti la ɛnee ɔ ne la zo ɔlɛbɔ Devidi sasa.

english_verse: He threw stones at David, at his soldiers, and at everyone else, including the bodyguards who walked on each side of David.
translation_verse: Hyemɛyae kpale Devidi nee ye mgbanyima ne mɔ awolɛ wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɛnee ye mgbanyima nee ye sinzavolɛma ɛbɔ ɛyia ye la.

english_verse: Shimei was yelling at David, “Get out of here, you murderer! You good-for-nothing,
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Hyemɛyae bɔ sasa ne la ɔzele kɛ, “Dwazo ɛkɛ ne, kɔ nehane, kɔdiawu, sonlamgbane!

english_verse: the Lord is paying you back for killing so many in Saul's family. You stole his kingdom, but now the Lord has given it to your son Absalom. You're a murderer, and that's why you're in such big trouble!”
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛdua wɔ kakɛ kɛ ɛvale Sɔɔlo belemgbunli maanle ne na ɛhanle ɔ bo zo amra mogya ɛguale a. Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛlie belemgbunli maanle ne ɛmaa ɛ ra Abesalɛm. Wɔ munzule doa wɔ, kɔdiawu!”

english_verse: Abishai said, “Your Majesty, this man is as useless as a dead dog! He shouldn't be allowed to curse you. Let me go over and chop off his head.”
translation_verse: Zɛluaya ara Abehyae zele belemgbunli ne kɛ, “Duzu ati bɔbɔ yɛɛ twea funli ɛhye kɛbɔ Nana aholoba ɛ? Nana, maa mengɔnli ɔ ti ne antɛnlɛma memaa ye.”

english_verse: David replied, “What will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? If Shimei is cursing me because the Lord has told him to, then who are you to tell him to stop?”
translation_verse: Na belemgbunli ne zele Abehyae nee ɔ diema Dwowabe kɛ, “Bɛmɛ Zɛluaya amra, ɛhye ɛnle bɛ edwɛkɛ. Saa Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛɛ ɛze ye kɛ ɔbɔ Devidi sasa a ɛnee nwane a lɛ adenle kɛbiza ye kɛ, ‘Duzu ati a wɔyɛ ɛhye ɛ?’ ”

english_verse: Then David said to Abishai and all his soldiers: My own son is trying to kill me! Why shouldn't this man from the tribe of Benjamin want me dead even more? Let him curse all he wants. Maybe the Lord did tell him to curse me.
translation_verse: Akee Devidi zele Abehyae nee ye mgbanyima ne mɔ amuala kɛ, “Me kunlu ralɛ bɔbɔ ɛlɛpɛ me nwo adenle yeahu me, na Bɛngyamanenli ye ɛdeɛ mɔɔ ɛlɛyɛ la yɛɛ yɛ bɛ azibɛnwo a. Bɛgyakyi ye bɛmaa ɔbɔ me sasa. Ɛdɛnkɛma a se ɔyɛ a.

english_verse: But if the Lord hears these curses and sees the trouble I'm in, maybe he will have pity on me instead.
translation_verse: Bie a ɛnee Ɛdɛnkɛma banwu kɛ mezi meyɛ anwunvɔne la na yeamaa me nyilalɛ yeazie sasa ye mɔɔ ɛnɛ bɛlɛbɔ me la abo zo.”

english_verse: David and the others went on down the road. Shimei went along the hillside by the road, cursing and throwing rocks and dirt at them.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Devidi nee ye menli ne zɔle bɛ adendulɛ ne azo. Mɔɔ bɛlɛkɔ la ɛnee Hyemɛyae lua boka ne anye anwo ɔlɛ sasabɔlɛ ne ɔzi ye zo, ɔkpa ye awolɛ na ɔfuandi anwea ɔgua bɛ nwo.

english_verse: When David and those with him came to the Jordan River, they were tired out. But after they rested, they felt much better. Hushai Meets Absalom
translation_verse: Na belemgbunli ne nee menli ne gyi zolɛ toonwo bɛhɔdwule Dwɔdan ne anloa; ɛnee akee bɛvɛ, bɛ nwo ɛyɛ bɛ bɛtɛɛ, yemɔti ɛkɛ ne yɛɛ bɛliele bɛ ɛnwomenle bie a. Abesalɛm wɔ Gyɛlusalɛm

english_verse: By this time, Absalom, Ahithophel, and the others had reached Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Abesalɛm nee Yizilayɛma mɔɔ nee ye lua la hɔvole Gyɛlusalɛm; Ahetɔfɛle ɔdaye ɔboka nwolɛ bie.

english_verse: David's friend Hushai came to Absalom and said, “Long live the king! Long live the king!”
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Devidi agɔnwo Akaenli Huhyae rale Abesalɛm ɛkɛ ne la, ɔdeanle nuhua kɛ, “Belemgbunli ɛnyi ɛhyɛ! Belemgbunli ɛnyi ɛhyɛ!”

english_verse: But Absalom asked Hushai, “Is this how you show loyalty to your friend David? Why didn't you go with him?”
translation_verse: Abesalɛm bizale ye kɛ, “Asoo wɔ nɔhalɛ ne mɔɔ ɛdi ɛmaa ɛ gɔnwo Devidi la, yemɔ ɛne? Duzu ati a ɛ nee ye angɔ a?”

english_verse: Hushai answered, “The Lord and the people of Israel have chosen you to be king. I can't leave. I have to stay and serve the one they've chosen.
translation_verse: Huhyae zele Abesalɛm kɛ, “Kyɛkyɛ, sonla ne mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma nee ye menli ne nee mɔɔ Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti ɛkpa nu ɛye ye la, yemɔ yɛɛ mewɔ ye afoa a.

english_verse: Besides, it seems right for me to serve you, just as I served your father.” Ahithophel's Advice
translation_verse: Saa meanzonle me menle ara ne a ɛnee nwane bieko a ɔwɔ kɛ mesonle ye a? Kɛ mezi mezonle ɛ ze la, zɔhane ala yɛɛ mebazonle wɔ a.”

english_verse: Absalom turned to Ahithophel and said, “Give us your advice! What should we do?”
translation_verse: Akee Abesalɛm zele Ahetɔfɛle kɛ, “Fa wɔ adwenle bɛla; duzu debie a ɔwɔ kɛ yɛyɛ a?”

english_verse: Ahithophel answered, “Some of your father's wives were left here to take care of the palace. You should have sex with them. Then everyone will find out that you have publicly disgraced your father. This will make you and your followers even more powerful.”
translation_verse: Ahetɔfɛle zele Abesalɛm kɛ, “Ɛ ze mgbɔnla ne mɔ mɔɔ yegyakyi bɛ kɛ bɛzinza suakunlu ɛkɛ ne la, ɛ nee bɛ kɔsɔɔti ɛla. Ɛhye bamaa Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti anwu kɛ ɛ nee ɛ ze bɛpɛ amodinli nu, na menli mɔɔ li ɛ nzi la banyia akɛnrazilɛ.”

english_verse: Absalom had a tent set up on the flat roof of the palace, and everyone watched as he went into the tent with his father's wives.
translation_verse: Yemɔti bɛzile ndanlɛ sua wɔ suakunlu azua ne mɔ ko ati zo, na Abesalɛm nee ɔ ze mgbɔnla ne mɔ lale ngoko ngoko wɔ Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti anye zo.

english_verse: Ahithophel gave such good advice in those days that both Absalom and David thought it came straight from God.
translation_verse: Mekɛ ne anu, folɛ biala mɔɔ Ahetɔfɛle kɛdu la le kɛ asɛɛ Nyamenle a ɛha a. Yemɔti Devidi nee Abesalɛm lile Ahetɔfɛle folɛdulɛ biala azo.

english_verse: and we will all go to fight David wherever he is. We will fall on him just as dew falls and covers the ground. He and all his soldiers will die!
translation_verse: Ɛleka biala mɔɔ ɔvea la yɛbahɔvinde ɔ nwo zo, na yɛava konle yɛadoa ye yɛanlua ye kɛ nzule nua senle la; na ɔdaye o, ye ɛlɔnema o, kokye bɔbɔ ɛnrɛha.

english_verse: while he is tired and discouraged. He will panic, and everyone with him will run away. I won't kill anyone except David,
translation_verse: Mebahɔfofo ɔ nwo zo wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɛnee yevɛ na ɔ rɛle ɛbɔ la. Ɔ nye zo bada ye kpole bie na menli mɔɔ li ɔ nzi la banriandi agua ɛbɔ nu.

english_verse: since he's the one you want to get rid of. Then I'll bring the whole nation back to you like a bride coming home to her husband. This way there won't be a civil war. Hushai Fools Absalom
translation_verse: Mebahu belemgbunli ne angomekye na meava menli mɔɔ li ɔ nzi la kɔsɔɔti mearɛlɛ wɔ kɛ atɔfolɛ raalɛ mɔɔ ɛlɛba ɔ hu sua nu la. Sonla kokye ala a ɛkpondɛ kɛ ɔwu a, na menli mɔɔ ɛha la amuala ɔwɔ kɛ sia ba sua nu anzonudwolɛ nu.”

english_verse: Absalom and all the leaders of the tribes of Israel agreed that Ahithophel had a good plan.
translation_verse: Folɛdulɛ ɛhye yɛle Abesalɛm nee Yizilayɛ mgbanyima ne mɔ fɛ kpole.

english_verse: Then Absalom said, “Bring in Hushai the Archite. Let's hear what he has to say.”
translation_verse: Akee Abesalɛm zele kɛ, “Bɛvɛlɛ Huhyae bɛmaa yɛdie ɔdaye noko.”

english_verse: Hushai came in, and Absalom told him what Ahithophel had planned. Then Absalom said, “Should we do what he says? And if we shouldn't, can you come up with anything better?”
translation_verse: Huhyae rale la Abesalɛm zele ye kɛ, “Ahetɔfɛle folɛ mɔɔ ɛdu yɛ la ɛne, na ɛnea a ɔle kpalɛ kɛ yɛkɛyɛ ye zɔhane ɔ? Saa ɔnle kpalɛ a ɛnee ɛdawɔ fa wɔ adwenle bɛla.”

english_verse: Hushai said: This time Ahithophel's advice isn't so good.
translation_verse: Huhyae zele Abesalɛm kɛ, “Adwenle ɛhye mɔɔ ɛnɛ Ahetɔfɛle ɛva ɛra la ɛnle kpalɛ.

english_verse: You know that your father and his followers are real warriors. Now they are as fierce as a mother bear whose cubs have just been killed. Besides, your father has a lot of experience in fighting wars, and he won't be spending the night with the others.
translation_verse: Ɛdawɔ ɛze ye wienyi kɛ ɛ ze nee ye ɛlɔnema ne le menli mɔɔ ze konle nye zo kpole kpalɛ a. Kɛkala, bɛ ahonle ɛfutu kɛ ezile mɔɔ bɛhye ɔ mra la. Fa ɛhye sie ahane. Ɛ ze le ɛlɔnenli mɔɔ bɛto ye sɛbe a, yɛɛ nɔɔzo ɔ nee ye ɛlɔnema ne ɛnrɛla ɛleka ko.

english_verse: He has probably already found a hiding place in a cave or somewhere else. As soon as anyone hears that some of your soldiers have been killed, everyone will think your whole army has been destroyed.
translation_verse: Kɛkala bɔbɔ, kabezɛ ɔvea bolɛ bɔne bie anu anzɛɛ ɛleka gyɛne bie. Na saa menli mɔɔ dumua ahɔteta Devidi la di akɔhoatɔ a, menli mɔɔ bade la baze kɛ, ‘Bɛbɔ Abesalɛm ɛdoavolɛma abo zo bɔkɔɔ.’

english_verse: Then even those who are as brave as a lion will lose their courage. All Israel knows what a great warrior your father is and what brave soldiers he has.
translation_verse: Saa ɔba ye zɛhae a menli bɔbɔ mɔɔ lɛ ahonle kɛ awenade la bazulo. Ɔluakɛ Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti ze kɛ ɛ ze le nrenya katakyie, yɛɛ zɔhane ala a ye ɛlɔnema mɔɔ ɔ nee bɛ lua la de a.

english_verse: My advice is to gather all the fighting men of Israel from the town of Dan in the north down to the town of Beersheba in the south. You will have more soldiers than there are grains of sand on the seashore. Absalom, you should lead them yourself,
translation_verse: Me folɛdulɛ a le kɛ, maa bɛboɔboa Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti anloa, ɔvi Dan ɔhɔkpula Biyɛhyiba; bɛ somaa bayɛ kɛ ɛnweazo anwea la, na ɛdawɔ mumua ne nea bɛ nwo zo ɛ nee bɛ ɛhɔ konle ne.

english_verse: If they go into a walled town, we will put ropes around that town and drag it into the river. We won't leave even one small piece of a stone.
translation_verse: Saa ɔnriandi ɔkɔfea suakpole bie azo a, Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti bava samgbenle nyɛma akyekye suakpole zɔhane na yɛahwe ye yɛahɔdo bɔnza ne anu. Yɛnrɛgyakyi bolɛ ekyi ko bɔbɔ wɔ boka ne azo.”

english_verse: Absalom and the others liked Hushai's plan better than Ahithophel's plan. This was because the Lord had decided to keep Ahithophel's plan from working and to cause trouble for Absalom. Jonathan and Ahimaaz Tell David the News
translation_verse: Abesalɛm nee Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti hanle kɛ, “Huhyae adwenle ne le kpalɛ tɛla Ahetɔfɛle folɛdulɛ ɛdeɛ ne.” Ɔluakɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛhyehyɛ kɛ ɔsɛkye Ahetɔfɛle folɛdulɛ ɛdeɛ ne, amaa yeamaa munzule ado Abesalɛm. Devidi anzoteyɛlɛ nee ye ɛnriandilɛ

english_verse: At once, Hushai went to Zadok and Abiathar. He told them what advice Ahithophel had given to Absalom and to the leaders of Israel. He also told them about the advice he had given.
translation_verse: Akee Huhyae zele sɛlɛvolɛma, Zeedɔko nee Abayata kɛ, “Folɛ mɔɔ Ahetɔfɛle dule Abesalɛm nee Yizilayɛ mgbanyima la ɛne. Medame noko me ɛdeɛ mɔɔ mendule bɛ la ɛne.

english_verse: Then he said, “Hurry! Send someone to warn David not to spend the night on this side of the Jordan. He must get across the river, so he and the others won't be wiped out!”
translation_verse: Yemɔti bɛha bɛ nwo, bɛzoa menli ndɛndɛ bɛmaa bɛhɔha bɛhile Devidi kɛ, ɛnɛ nɔe, ɔmmada azule ne anloa ɛleka mɔɔ bɛpɛ la wɔ fienemgbole ne anu. Na ɔbɔ mɔdenle ɔpɛ Dwɔdan ne ɔhɔ ɔ nzi moa, amaa bɛ sa anga belemgbunli ne nee ye ɛlɔnema ne na bɛahu bɛ.”

english_verse: Jonathan and Ahimaaz had been waiting at Rogel Spring because they did not want to be seen in Jerusalem. A servant girl went to the spring and gave them the message for David.
translation_verse: Ɛnee Dwɔnatan nee Ahaemaze ɛlɛkendɛ nzubula Ɛnlɔgɛle ne anloa wɔ Gyɛlusalɛm kandiba. Sonvolɛ raalɛ bie a kɔka edwɛkɛ mɔɔ ɛlɛsi la kile bɛ a na bɛdabɛ bɛahɔha bɛahile Belemgbunli Devidi, ɔluakɛ ɔnle kɛ bɛnwu bɛ kɛ bɛhɔ suakpole ne azo.

english_verse: But a young man saw them and went to tell Absalom. So Jonathan and Ahimaaz left and hurried to the house of a man who lived in Bahurim. Then they climbed down into a well in the courtyard.
translation_verse: Kenle ko kakula nrenya bie nwunle bɛ. Ɔhɔhanle ɔhilele Abesalɛm, yemɔti bɛ mu nwiɔ bɛnriandile bɛhɔle nrenya bie mɔɔ wɔ Bahulem la sua nu. Ɔlɛ bula bie wɔ ye awuke ne anu na bɛdwule nuhua.

english_verse: The man's wife put the cover on the well and poured grain on top of it, so the well could not be seen.
translation_verse: Nrenya ne aye ne vale debie hedale bula ne azo na ɔrɛlɛle ma zolɛ. Yemɔti awie biala andwenle kɛ debie wɔ ɛkɛ.

english_verse: Absalom's soldiers came to the woman and demanded, “Where are Ahimaaz and Jonathan?” The woman answered, “They went across that stream.” The soldiers went off to look for the two men. But when they did not find the men, they went back to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Abesalɛm sonvolɛma ne rale raalɛ ne sua nu la, bɛbizale ye kɛ, “Ahaemaze nee Dwɔnatan wɔ nienwu?” Raalɛ ne buale bɛ kɛ, “Bɛpɛle azule ne bɛhɔle ɔ nzi lɔ.” Mɔɔ bɛkpondɛle bɛ toonwo na bɛannwu bɛ la bɛziale bɛhɔle Gyɛlusalɛm.

english_verse: After the soldiers had gone, Jonathan and Ahimaaz climbed out of the well. They went to David and said, “Hurry! Get ready to cross the river!” Then they told him about Ahithophel's plan.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ bɛziale bɛhɔle la, Ahaemaze nee Dwɔnatan vi bula ne anu vindele na bɛhɔbɔle Belemgbunli Devidi amaneɛ. Bɛzele ye kɛ, “Dwazo, ka ɛ nwo kɔpɛ azule ne ndɛndɛ, ɔluakɛ Ahetɔfɛle folɛ mɔɔ ɛdu menli ne la ɛne.”

english_verse: David and the others got ready and started crossing the Jordan River. By sunrise all of them were on the other side. Ahithophel Kills Himself
translation_verse: Na Devidi nee ye ɛlɔnema ne kɔsɔɔti hɔpɛle Dwɔdan ne. Mɔɔ maanle nu katete la ɛnee bɛ muala bɛwie Dwɔdan ne pɛ.

english_verse: When Ahithophel saw that Absalom and the leaders of Israel were not going to follow his advice, he saddled his donkey and rode back to his home in Gilo. He told his family and servants what to do. Then he hanged himself, and they buried him in his family's burial place. Absalom Puts Amasa in Charge of the Army
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Ahetɔfɛle nwunle kɛ bɛanva ye folɛdulɛ ne la, ɔvole ye asoaso ne azo na ɔhɔle ɔdaye ye sua zo. Ɔtotole ninyɛne boɛ na ɔbɔle ɔ nwo akɔnvo. Bɛziele ye wɔ ɔ ze nla ne anu.

english_verse: David went to the town of Mahanaim, and Absalom crossed the Jordan River with the army of Israel.
translation_verse: Akee Devidi rale Meehaneeyem. Abesalɛm nee Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti pɛle Dwɔdan ne.

english_verse: The Israelites under Absalom's command set up camp in the region of Gilead. Friends Bring Supplies to David
translation_verse: Na Yizilayɛma nee Abesalɛm yɛle bɛ azokoɛleɛ wɔ Geleade azɛlɛ zo.

english_verse: After David came to the town of Mahanaim, Shobi the son of Nahash came from Rabbah in Ammon, Machir the son of Ammiel came from Lo-Debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite came from Rogelim.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Devidi dwule Meehaneeyem la, Neehahye ara Hyobae mɔɔ vi Relaba mɔɔ wɔ Amɔnoma maanle nu la, Abeɛle ara Meekɛ mɔɔ vi Lodɛbaa yɛɛ Bazeleeyae mɔɔ vi Wulogɛlem mɔɔ wɔ Geleade la rayiale ye adenle.

english_verse: Here is a list of what they brought: sleeping mats, blankets, bowls, pottery jars, wheat, barley, flour, roasted grain, beans, lentils, honey, yogurt, sheep, and cheese. They brought the food for David and the others because they knew that everyone would be hungry, tired, and thirsty from being out in the desert.
translation_verse: Bɛvale ɛkpa, ahyɛnze nee mbuakɛ, ma, esamo, ma ngyehye, aluba akpatala nee alubandenra , wolɛ, kyiisi yɛɛ mboane bɛrɛlɛle Devidi nee ye ɛlɔnema ne kɛ bɛli, ɔluakɛ bɛnwunle kɛ ɛnee ɛhɔne ɛlɛku menli ne na bɛvɛ, yɛɛ nzuhɔne noko ɛhu bɛ toonwo wɔ fienemgbole ne anu.

english_verse: He sent out one third of his army under the command of Joab, another third under the command of Abishai the son of Zeruiah, and the rest under the command of Ittai from Gath. He told the soldiers, “I'm going into battle with you.”
translation_verse: Ɔvale ekpunli ko ɔwulale Dwowabe asa anu; ɔvale ekpunli ne mɔɔ tɔ zo nwiɔ la ɔwulale Dwowabe adiema nrenya Zɛluaya ara Abehyae asa anu yɛɛ ɔvale ekpunli ne mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nsa la ɔwulale Gatenli Yetae asa anu. Akee belemgbunli ne zele menli ne kɛ, “Medame mumua ne me nee bɛ bahɔ.”

english_verse: But the soldiers said, “No, don't go into battle with us! It won't matter to our enemies if they make us all run away, or even if they kill half of us. But you are worth
translation_verse: Na menli ne zele ye kɛ, “Nana, ɛngɔ bie. Ɔluakɛ yɛmɛ, saa ɔkyele zolɛ na yɛnriandi bɔbɔ a, menli ɛnrɛdwenle yɛ nwo. Saa bɛbu yɛ nuhua nwiɔ na bɛku ko a, bɛnrɛdwenle yɛ nwo. Na wɔmɔ, ɛsonle bolɛ ɛtɛla yɛ nuhua apenle kɛyɛ bulu; yemɔti ɔle kpalɛ kɛ ɛkɛdɛnla suakpole ye azo na ɛkɛrɛlɛ yɛ moalɛ ala.”

english_verse: and one of them went and told Joab, “I saw Absalom hanging in a tree!”
translation_verse: Nrenya bie nwunle ye na ɔrabɔle Dwowabe amaneɛ kɛ, “Yɛmenle, menwunle kɛ Abesalɛm zinze oku baka bie azo.”

english_verse: Battles were being fought all over the forest, and David's soldiers were winning. Twenty thousand soldiers were killed that day, and more of them died from the dangers of the forest than from the fighting itself.
translation_verse: Konle ne dɛlɛle kpɔkɛ ne anu ɛleka biala, na menli dɔɔnwo wule kpɔkɛ ne anu dɛlale menli mɔɔ dɔle dadeɛ nloa la.

english_verse: Absalom was riding his mule under a huge tree when his head caught in the branches. The mule ran off and left Absalom hanging in midair. Some of David's soldiers happened by,
translation_verse: Arɛlevilɛ nu ala, Abesalɛm hɔkponzale Devidi ɛlɔnema ne bie mɔ. Ɛnee ɔde ɛkpɔnwɔndua zo, na ɛkpɔnwɔndua ne nriandile hɔvale baka kpole bie mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye oku la abo, na Abesalɛm akɔme hɔtosale baka ne ngane ne bie takola avinli manle ɔzinzele anwomanyunlu, na ɛkpɔnwɔndua ne wɔlɔle ɔ nwo hɔle.

english_verse: Joab said, “You saw Absalom? Why didn't you kill him? I would have given you ten pieces of silver and a special belt.”
translation_verse: Dwowabe zele nrenya ne kɛ, “Duzɔne! Ɛdawɔ ɛnwunle ye ɛ nye zo? Duzu ati a wɔangu ye ɛkɛ ne ala ɛ? Anrɛɛ menwɔva fɛlɛkolilɛ ngome menwɔmaa wɔ dwɛtɛ fufule ngoko bulu nee akyeso.”

english_verse: He always finds out what's going on. I would have been risking my life to kill Absalom, because you would have let me take the blame.”
translation_verse: Saa meandie belemgbunli ne aneɛ yɛɛ mengunle ye a anrɛɛ kɛ ɔkɛyɛ biala la ɔbade, na ɛnrɛpepɛ ɛnrɛlie me noko.”

english_verse: Joab said, “I'm not going to waste any more time on you!” Absalom was still alive, so Joab took three spears and stuck them through Absalom's chest.
translation_verse: Dwowabe zele kɛ, “Menlɛ ɛ nwo alagye.” Ɔvale atwɛ nsa ɔhɔwowɔle Abesalɛm akɛnra azo wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɛnee ɔ nye gyi zo na ɔtɛsinze oku baka ne azo la.

english_verse: Ten of Joab's bodyguards came over and finished him off.
translation_verse: Na mgbavolɛ bulu mɔɔ soa Dwowabe konle ninyɛne ne mɔ la bɔle yiale Abesalɛm na bɛbobɔle ye bɛhunle ye.

english_verse: Then Joab blew a trumpet to signal his troops to stop chasing Israel's soldiers.
translation_verse: Akee Dwowabe wule aweɛne nu manle ɛlɔnema ne mɔ gyakyile Yizilayɛma ne mɔ ɛvoanlɛ na bɛziale bɛrale.

english_verse: They threw Absalom's body into a deep pit in the forest and put a big pile of rocks over it. Meanwhile, the people of Israel had all run back to their own homes.
translation_verse: Bɛyele Abesalɛm funli ne na bɛvuandinle ye bɛdole kuma kpole bie anu wɔ kpɔkɛ ne anu. Bɛhuohuanle awolɛ edukue kpole bie ɔ nwo zo. Na Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti guale ɛbɔ nu. Ko biala hɔle ɔdaye ye sua zo.

english_verse: When Absalom was alive, he had set up a stone monument for himself in King's Valley. He explained, “I don't have any sons to keep my name alive.” He called it Absalom's Monument, and that is the name it still has today. Ahimaaz Wants To Tell David
translation_verse: Mekɛ mɔɔ Abesalɛm de aze la, ɔkpɔnlanle mpila wɔ Belemgbunli Bɔnza ɔvale ɔyɛle ɔdaye ye ngakyelɛ deɛ. Ye edwɛkɛ a le kɛ, “Meanwo ralɛ nrenya na bɛava bɛahakye me.” Yemɔti ɔvale mpila ne ɔdonle ɔ nwo, na ɛnɛ nee ɛnɛ ala, bɛtɛfɛlɛ ye Abesalɛm Ngakyedeɛ . Bɛbɔ Devidi amaneɛ kɛ Abesalɛm ɛwu

english_verse: Ahimaaz the son of Zadok said, “Joab, let me run and tell King David that the Lord has rescued him from his enemies.”
translation_verse: Akee Zeedɔko ara Ahaemaze zele kɛ, “Bɛmaa menriandi waa mengɔmbɔ belemgbunli amaneɛ kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛye ye ɛvi ye kpɔvolɛma asa anu.”

english_verse: Joab answered, “You're not the one to tell the king that his son is dead. You can take him a message some other time, but not today.”
translation_verse: Dwowabe buale ye kɛ, “Kyɛkyɛ, ɛnva nrɛlaleɛ biala ɛngɔ ɛnɛ. Maa ɔyɛ na kenle fofolɛ, ɔboalekɛ ɛnɛ kenle ye, belemgbunli ara nrenya ɛwu.”

english_verse: Someone from Ethiopia was standing there, and Joab told him, “Go and tell the king what you have seen.” The man knelt down in front of Joab, then got up and started running.
translation_verse: Akee Dwowabe zele Sudanenli akɛlɛ ne kɛ, “Kɔ na kɔha mɔɔ wɔnwu ye la kile belemgbunli.” Sudanenli akɛlɛ ne bɔle ɔ ti aze na ɔdɔle adenle zo.

english_verse: Ahimaaz spoke to Joab again, “No matter what happens, I still want to go. And besides, the Ethiopian has already left.” Joab said, “Why should you go? You won't get a reward for the news you have!”
translation_verse: Eza Ahaemaze zele Dwowabe bieko kɛ, “Mɔɔ ɔba la ɛrɛla, medame noko mekpo Sudanenli ne.” Dwowabe bizale ye kɛ, “Me ra, duzu ati a ɛkulo kɛ ɛfɛ ɛvɛlɛ mgbane ɛhye a, ɔluakɛ ɛze ye wienyi kɛ ɛnrɛnyia amaneɛbɔlɛ ɛhye anwo nganvolɛ biala.”

english_verse: “I'll run no matter what!” Ahimaaz insisted. “All right then, run!” Joab said. Ahimaaz took the road through the Jordan Valley and outran the Ethiopian.
translation_verse: Ahaemaze zile zolɛ kɛ, “Kɛ ɔkɛyɛ biala la, ɔwɔ kɛ mekɔ.” Dwowabe zele ye kɛ, “Ɛnee kɔ ɛ!” Na Ahaemaze hanle guale ye, ɔvale Dwɔdan Bɔnza ɔhɔzenle Sudanenli ne anwo.

english_verse: Meanwhile, David was sitting between the inner and outer gates in the city wall. One of his soldiers was watching from the roof of the gate-tower. He saw a man running toward the town
translation_verse: Ɛnee Devidi de suakpole ne anuhɔlɛ nlenkɛ mgbole nwiɔ ne mɔɔ ko wɔ ɔ kunlu, ko wɔ ɔ nzi la avinli. Sinzavolɛ ne luale bane ne anwo vole hɔle anuhɔlɛ ne ati zo. Na mɔɔ ɔmanle ɔ nye zo la, ɔnwunle kɛ nrenya ko lɛ ɛnriandilɛ ɛlɛba.

english_verse: and shouted down to tell David. David answered, “If he's alone, he must have some news.” The runner was getting closer,
translation_verse: Sinzavolɛ ne manle ɔ ne zo na ɔbɔle belemgbunli amaneɛ. Na belemgbunli ne zele kɛ, “Saa ɔdaye ɔ ngome ɛdeɛ a ɛnee ɔ nee amaneɛ fɛlɛko lua.” Na ɛnee ahenle lɛ ɛnriandilɛ kpalɛ a ɛlɛba a, na yebikye.

english_verse: when the soldier saw someone else running. He shouted down to the gate, “Look! There's another runner!” David said, “He must have some news too.”
translation_verse: Sinzavolɛ ne eza kanlea la ɛnee sonla fofolɛ ɔdaye ɔlɛ ɛnriandilɛ ɔlɛba; ɔdendenle ɔ nloa anlenkɛ kpole ne anu na ɔzele kɛ, “Nana, sonla fofolɛ ɔdaye ɔlɛ ɛnriandilɛ ɔlɛba!” Belemgbunli ne zele kɛ, “Ɔdaye noko ɔ nee amaneɛ fɛlɛko lua.”

english_verse: The soldier on the roof shouted, “The first one runs just like Ahimaaz the son of Zadok.” This time David said, “He's a good man. He must have some good news.”
translation_verse: Sinzavolɛ ne zele kɛ, “Ahenle mɔɔ lumua la zɔho Zeedɔko ara Ahaemaze.” Na belemgbunli ne zele kɛ, “Ɔle sonlakpalɛ, yemɔti ɔ nee nrɛlaleɛ kpalɛ lua.”

english_verse: Ahimaaz called out, “We won! We won!” Then he bowed low to David and said, “Your Majesty, praise the Lord your God! He has given you victory over your enemies.”
translation_verse: Akee Ahaemaze deanle nuhua zele belemgbunli kɛ, “Debie biala ɛhɔ boɛ!” Ɔdule ɔdɔle belemgbunli agyakɛ anu na ɔzele kɛ, “Ayɛlɛyelɛ ɛha Ɛdɛnkɛma wɔ Nyamenle ne kɛ yeye wɔ kpɔvolɛma mɔɔ hakyile bɛ nzi zile wɔ la yemaa a.”

english_verse: “Is my son Absalom all right?” David asked. Ahimaaz said, “When Joab sent your personal servant and me, I saw a noisy crowd. But I don't know what it was all about.”
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne bizale ye kɛ, “Kakula Abesalɛm anwo kɔlɔnwo ɔ?” Ahaemaze buale ye kɛ, “Mɔɔ Dwowabe zoanle me la, menwunle kɛ ɛnee ɛkɛ ne ɛyɛ begyebegye zɛhae, noko meangola meannwu deɛ holɛ ko ne.”

english_verse: David told him, “Stand over there and wait.” Ahimaaz went over and stood there.
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne zele kɛ, “Twe ɛ nwo kɔgyinla nehane.” Yemɔti ɔhɔgyinlanle ahane.

english_verse: The Ethiopian came and said, “Your Majesty, today I have good news! The Lord has rescued you from all your enemies!”
translation_verse: Akee Sudanenli akɛlɛ ne ɔdaye ɔrale na ɔrahanle kɛ, “Melɛ amaneɛ fɛlɛko melɛbɛlɛ me awulae belemgbunli. Ɔluakɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛlie wɔ ɛvi kpɔvolɛma mɔɔ honle tiale wɔ la asa anu ɛnɛ.”

english_verse: “Is my son Absalom all right?” David asked. The Ethiopian replied, “I wish that all Your Majesty's enemies and everyone who tries to harm you would end up like him!” David Cries for Absalom
translation_verse: Belemgbunli bizale Sudanenli ne kɛ, “Kakula Abesalɛm anwo kɔlɔnwo ɔ?” Sudanenli ne zele kɛ, “Nana, me kunlu a anrɛɛ wɔ kpɔvolɛma nee menli mɔɔ honle tiale wɔ kɛ bɛkpondɛ wɔ nee munzule la kɔsɔɔti aha agua kɛ kpavolɛ ɛhye la.”

english_verse: David started trembling. Then he went up to the room above the city gate to cry. As he went, he kept saying, “My son Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! I wish I could have died instead of you! Absalom, my son, my son!”
translation_verse: Nyane hanle belemgbunli ne kpole kpalɛ. Ɔhɔle ekpumgbunli ne mɔɔ wɔ anuhɔlɛ kpole ne ati zo la anu na ɔhɔzunle. Mɔɔ ɔkɔ kɔsɔɔti la ɛnee ɔlɛsu kɛ, “O me ra Abesalɛm, me ra, me ra Abesalɛm! Ɛnee ɛmmaa mame menwu, o me ra, me ra Abesalɛm.”

english_verse: Someone told Joab, “The king is crying because Absalom is dead.”
translation_verse: Bɛhanle bɛhilele Dwowabe kɛ, “Devidi ɛlɛdi nyane na ɔlɛsu ɔ ra Abesalɛm.”

english_verse: David's army found out he was crying because his son had died, and their day of victory suddenly turned into a day of sadness.
translation_verse: Yemɔti kenle ko ne konimlilɛ ne hakyile nyanelilɛ manle menli ne kɔsɔɔti, ɔluakɛ bɛdele kɛ, “Belemgbunli ɛlɛdi ɔ ra ne ewule ne anwo nyane.”

english_verse: The troops were sneaking into Mahanaim, just as if they had run away from a battle and were ashamed.
translation_verse: Ɛlɔnema ne ziale hɔle suakpole ne azo koonwu kɛ ɛlɔnema mɔɔ bɛli bɛ nwo zo konim na bɛva nyiane bɛlɛnriandi la.

english_verse: David covered his face with his hands and kept on crying loudly, “My son, Absalom! Absalom, my son, my son!”
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne hedale ɔ nye na ɔdukuele nuhua ɔzunle kɛ, “O me ra Abesalɛm, O Abesalɛm, me ra ye o!”

english_verse: Joab went to the house where David was staying and told him: You've made your soldiers ashamed! Not only did they save your life, they saved your sons and daughters and wives as well.
translation_verse: Dwowabe rale belemgbunli sua nu ɛkɛ ne na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Ɛnɛ wɔmaa nyiane ɛhu wɔ mgbanyima kɔsɔɔti mɔɔ ɛlie wɔ ngoane, na bɛlie ɛ mra mrenya nee mraalɛ, wɔ mraalɛ nee wɔ mgbɔnla ngoane la.

english_verse: You're more loyal to your enemies than to your friends. What you've done today has shown your officers and soldiers that they don't mean a thing to you. You would be happy if Absalom was still alive, even if the rest of us were dead.
translation_verse: Ɔboalekɛ yɛnwu kɛ ɛkulo bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛkpɔ wɔ la na ɛkpɔ bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛkulo wɔ la. Ɛnɛ wɔmaa yela ali wienyi kɛ safohyenlema nee ɛlɔnema ɛnle ɛhwee wɔ ɛ nye zo. Ɛnɛ wɔhile wɔmaa menwu ye wienyi kɛ, saa Abesalɛm anwu yɛɛ yɛmɛ ɛlɔnema ne kɔsɔɔti yɛwule a anrɛɛ ɛ kunlu dwo.

english_verse: Now get up! Go out there and thank them for what they did. If you don't, I swear by the Lord that you won't even have one man left on your side tomorrow morning. You may have had a lot of troubles in the past, but this will be the worst thing that has ever happened to you!
translation_verse: Dwazo na kɔdendɛ ɛdendɛlɛ kɛnlɛma kile wɔ menli ne. Na anrɛɛ meka Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ, saa wɔangɔ a, ɛnɛ nɔe toonwo mɔɔ aleɛ kahye la sonla kokye bɔbɔ ɛnrɛha ɛ nwo ɛke. Na anrɛɛ ɛhye bayɛ munzule kpole adɛla munzule mɔɔ sumunli kɛ ɛbɔle ye wɔ mgbavolɛ nu bɛra ɛ nwo zo la amuala.”

english_verse: David got up and went to the town gate and sat down. When the people heard that he was sitting there, they came to see him. Israel and Judah Want David Back After Israel's soldiers had all returned home,
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne dwazole na ɔhɔdendɛle suakpole ne anlenkɛ kpole ne anloa. Bɛhɔhanle bɛhilele menli ne mɔ kɛ, “Belemgbunli ne de anlenkɛ kpole ne anloa.” Na menli ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti hɔbɔle yiale ye. Devidi sia ahɔ Gyɛlusalɛm Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti ɛnriandi. Ko biala ɛhɔ ɔdaye ye sua zo.

english_verse: When David found out what they were saying, he sent a message to Zadok and Abiathar the priests. It said: Say to the leaders of Judah, “Why are you the last tribe to think about bringing King David back home?
translation_verse: Na belemgbunli vale nrɛlaleɛ ɛhye hɔmanle sɛlɛvolɛma, Zeedɔko nee Abayata kɛ bɛha bɛhile Dwuda mgbanyima kɛ, “Duzu ati a bɛanlumua bɛanga ye kɛ bɛmaa yɛhɔva belemgbunli yɛrɛla sua nu ɛ? Ɔluakɛ mɔɔ Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti ɛha wɔ me ɛralɛ nwo la, mede ɔ muala.

english_verse: He is your brother, your own relative! Why haven't you done anything to bring him back?”
translation_verse: Bɛmɛ Dwudama, bɛle me nwo amra, mogya ne mɔɔ wɔ me nuhua la, ko ne ala bie a wɔ bɛ nu a. Duzu ati a bɛkɛha amozi wɔ me ɛvalɛ nu ɛ?

english_verse: And tell Amasa, “You're my nephew, and with God as a witness, I swear I'll make you commander of my army instead of Joab.”
translation_verse: Bɛze Ameesa kɛ, ɔle me nwo sonla. Saa meandu Dwowabe, meanva ɔdaye Ameesa meanyɛ me Safohyenlema Kpanyinli mɔɔ nea me ɛlɔnema ne anwo zo la a, Nyamenle ɛdua me kakɛ ɛgua me bie zo.”

english_verse: Soon the tribe of Judah again became followers of David, and they sent him this message: “Come back, and bring your soldiers with you.” David Starts Back for Jerusalem
translation_verse: Devidi edwɛkɛ ne hanle Dwudama kɔsɔɔti ahonle na bɛmanle bɛhɔzele belemgbunli ne kɛ, “Ɛ nee wɔ mgbanyima ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti bɛzia bɛrɛla sua nu.”

english_verse: Shimei the son of Gera was there with them. He had hurried from Bahurim to meet David. Shimei was from the tribe of Benjamin, and
translation_verse: Gila ara Hyemɛyae mɔɔ le Bɛngyamanenli na ɔvi Bahulem la nee Dwudama a rale rayiale Belemgbunli Devidi a.

english_verse: Then they brought David's family and servants back across the river, and they did everything he wanted them to do. Shimei Meets with David Shimei crossed the Jordan River and bowed down in front of David.
translation_verse: Bɛpɛle azule ne na bɛboale belemgbunli anwo amra bɛmanle bɛpɛle azule ne na bɛyɛle mɔɔ belemgbunli kpondɛ la bɛmanle ye. Devidi yɛ atiakunlukɛnlɛma amaa Hyemɛyae Mɔɔ belemgbunli ne ɛlɛboɔboa ɔ nwo apɛ Dwɔdan ne la, Gila ara Hyemɛyae radule dɔle belemgbunli ne agyakɛ anu,

english_verse: David said, “Abishai, what will I ever do with you and your brother Joab? Is it your job to tell me who has done wrong? I've been made king of all Israel today, and no one will be put to death!”
translation_verse: Na Devidi zele kɛ, “Bɛmɛ Zɛluaya amra, duzu adwenle a me nee bɛ yɛva mɔɔ bɛyɛ bɛahwe ngyegyelɛ bɛamaa me a? Ɛnɛ le mekɛ mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ bɛku sonla wɔ Yizilayɛ ɔ? Anzɛɛ bɛnze kɛ ɛnɛ mele Yizilayɛ belemgbunli ɔ?”

english_verse: Then David promised Shimei that he would not be killed. Mephibosheth Meets with David
translation_verse: Akee belemgbunli ne hanle ndane na ɔzele Hyemɛyae kɛ, “Bɛnrɛhu wɔ.” Devidi yɛ atiakunlukɛnlɛma amaa Mɛfebɔhyɛte

english_verse: He answered, “Your Majesty, you know I can't walk. I told my servant to saddle a donkey for me so I could go with you. But my servant left without me, and
translation_verse: Ɔbuale ye kɛ, “O me awulae, me belemgbunli, me sonvolɛ ne bɛlɛbɛlale me. Menzele ye kɛ, ‘Boɔboa me asoaso ne maa me maa me nee belemgbunli ɛhɔ,’ na yeanyɛ. Kɛmɔ ɛdawɔ ɛze la, mele abubura.

english_verse: then he lied about me. You're as wise as an angel of God, so do what you think is right.
translation_verse: Ɔdoanle me ɔmanle wɔ, Nana. Noko, awulae me belemgbunli le kɛ Nyamenle soanvolɛ la; yemɔti debie biala mɔɔ fɛta la fa yɛ me.

english_verse: After all, you could have killed my whole family and me. But instead, you let me eat at your own table. Your Majesty, what more could I ask?”
translation_verse: Nana, anrɛɛ ɛnee ɔwɔ kɛ bɛku egya abusua ne anu amra kɔsɔɔti, noko ɛvale wɔ sonvolɛ, medame, ɛbokale menli mɔɔ kpula bɛ sa wɔ wɔ ɛkponle ne anwo la anwo. Na ɛnee akee duzu bieko bɔbɔ yɛɛ mekpondɛ wɔ belemgbunli ɛkɛ a?”

english_verse: David answered, “You've said enough! I've decided to divide the property between you and Ziba.”
translation_verse: Na belemgbunli ne zele ye kɛ, “Ɔngyia kɛ ɛkɛha edwɛkɛ biala. Mezi ye pi kɛ, ɛdawɔ nee Zaeba bɛbahyɛ ɛ ze Sɔɔlo azɛlɛ ne.”

english_verse: Mephibosheth replied, “He can have it all! I'm just glad you've come home safely.” Barzillai Returns Home
translation_verse: Na Mɛfebɔhyɛte hanle kɛ, “Sumunli kenle ala mɔɔ Nana ɛzia ɛra sua nu anzonudwolɛ nu la, maa Zaeba ɛva azɛlɛ ne amuala.” Devidi yɛ atiakunlukɛnlɛma amaa Bazeleeyae

english_verse: Barzillai came from Rogelim in Gilead to meet David at the Jordan River and go across with him.
translation_verse: Geleadenli Bazeleeyae vi Wulogɛlem rale na ɔ nee belemgbunli hɔle kɛ ɔkaboa ye yeamaa yeapɛ Dwɔdan ne.

english_verse: David said to him, “Cross the river and go to Jerusalem with me. I will take care of you.”
translation_verse: Na belemgbunli ne zele Bazeleeyae kɛ, “Maa yɛhɔ Gyɛlusalɛm na mebanlea wɔ kpalɛ.”

english_verse: Barzillai answered: Your Majesty, why should I go to Jerusalem? I don't have much longer to live.
translation_verse: Bazeleeyae hanle kɛ, “Medame mumua ne, yeha me kenle nyɛ mɔɔ me nee me belemgbunli kɔ Gyɛlusalɛm a?

english_verse: I'll cross the river with you, but I'll only go a little way on the other side. You don't have to be so kind to me.
translation_verse: Nana, me nee wɔ yɛbahɔdwu Dwɔdan ne anloa ala. Duzu ati a ɔwɔ kɛ Nana wula me anyunlunyia kpole ɛhye a?

english_verse: Just let me return to my hometown, where I can someday be buried near my father and mother. My servant Chimham can go with you, and you can treat him as your own.
translation_verse: Mesɛlɛ wɔ, maa menzia mengɔ me sua zo na mengɔnwu menla egya nee ɔmɔ akunlu. Wɔ sonvolɛ Kyemeham ɛne, maa ɔ nee Nana ɛhɔ; debie biala mɔɔ ɛkulo la, fa ye yɛ.”

english_verse: David said, “I'll take Chimham with me, and whatever you ask me to do for him, I'll do. And if there's anything else you want, I'll also do that.”
translation_verse: Na belemgbunli ne buale ye kɛ, “Me nee Kyemeham bahɔ, mebayɛ debie biala mɔɔ fɛta la meamaa ye. Eza debie biala mɔɔ ɛkɛbiza la, mebayɛ meamaa wɔ.”

english_verse: David's soldiers went on across the river, while he stayed behind to tell Barzillai goodbye and to wish him well. Barzillai returned home, but
translation_verse: Na menli ne kɔsɔɔti pɛle Dwɔdan ne, belemgbunli ne ɔdaye ɔpɛle. Belemgbunli vole Bazeleeyae anvoka anwo na ɔyileyilale ye kosoɛ kosoɛ. Na Bazeleeyae ziale hɔle sua nu. Dwudama nee Yizilayɛma su belemgbunli ne anwo kpolera

english_verse: Chimham crossed the river with David. Israel and Judah Argue All of Judah's army and half of Israel's army were there to help David cross the river.
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne hɔle Gelegale; Kyemeham nee ye a hɔle a. Dwudama kɔsɔɔti nee Yizilayɛma anu foa ko lile ɔ nzi hɔzɔhonle ye.

english_verse: The soldiers from Israel came to him and said, “Why did our relatives from Judah secretly take you and your family and your soldiers across the Jordan?”
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti rale belemgbunli ɛkɛ ne rabizale ye kɛ, “Nana, duzu ati a yɛ mediema Dwudama ɛrava wɔ nee ɛ nwo amra nee wɔ ɛlɔnema ne ɛpɛ Dwɔdan ye a?”

english_verse: The people of Judah answered, “Why are you so angry? We are the king's relatives. He didn't give us any food, and we didn't take anything for ourselves!”
translation_verse: Na Dwudama buale Yizilayɛma kɛ, “Ɔboalekɛ belemgbunli ne le yɛ nwo sonla. Duzu ati a bɛva edwɛkɛ ɛhye anwo ɛya a? Yebɔ yɛ aleɛlilɛ nwo kakɛ anzɛɛ yehyɛ yɛ nwolɛ debie ɔ?”

english_verse: Those from Israel said, “King David belongs to us ten times more than he belongs to you. Why didn't you think we were good enough to help you? After all, we were the first ones to think of bringing him back!” The people of Judah argued more strongly than the people of Israel.
translation_verse: Na Yizilayɛma buale Dwudama kɛ, “Kanza ɔvi bɛ nu bɔbɔ a yɛ nwo zonle tɛla bɛ fane bulu. Duzu ati a bɛambu yɛ bie a? Tɛ yɛmɛ a yɛlumuale yɛhanle kɛ yɛkava ye yɛara ɔ?” Noko akee Dwudama mgbolehanlɛ ne bole Yizilayɛma anwo zo.

english_verse: A troublemaker from the tribe of Benjamin was there. His name was Sheba the son of Bichri, and he blew a trumpet to get everyone's attention. Then he said, “People of Israel, David the son of Jesse doesn't belong to us! Let's go home.”
translation_verse: Ɛnee sonlamgbane bie wɔ Gelegale. Bɛfɛlɛ ye Hyiba. Ɔ ze a le Bekelae mɔɔ vi Bɛngyaman abusua ekpunli ne anu la. Ɔwule aweɛne nu na ɔdeanle nuhua kɛ, “Yɛ nee Devidi ɛnlɛ ɛhwee ɛnyɛ. Yɛnli Gyɛsi ara agya. Yizilayɛma e! Awie biala ɛhɔ ye sua nu.”

english_verse: So they stopped following David and went off with Sheba. But the people of Judah stayed close to David all the way from the Jordan to Jerusalem. David's Ten Wives
translation_verse: Yemɔti Yizilayɛma kpole Devidi na bɛlile Hyiba anzi. Na Dwudama lile bɛ belemgbunli ne anzi vi Dwɔdan ne anloa hɔle Gyɛlusalɛm.

english_verse: David had left ten of his wives in Jerusalem to take care of his palace. But when he came back, he had them taken to another house, and he placed soldiers there to guard them. He gave them whatever they needed, but he never slept with any of them again. They had to live there for the rest of their lives as if they were widows. The Army Goes after Sheba
translation_verse: Akee Devidi hɔle ye sua nu wɔ Gyɛlusalɛm. Belemgbunli ne manle ye mgbɔnla bulu ne mɔɔ ɔgyakyile bɛ ɔ nzi kɛ bɛzinza ye suakunlu ɛkɛ ne la sua na ɔmanle bɛzinzale bɛ. Ɔnleanle bɛ gyɛlɛɛnye, noko yeanva ɔ nwo yeanga biala fee. Bɛwulale bɛ sua nu na bɛmanle bɛyɛle kɛ asɛɛ bɛle ahunlanvolɛ mraalɛ la toonwo bɛwule.

english_verse: David said to Amasa, “Three days from now I want you and all of Judah's army to be here!”
translation_verse: Akee belemgbunli ne zele Ameesa kɛ, “Memaa wɔ kenle nsa, boɔboa Dwudama kɔsɔɔti anloa na ɛdawɔ noko boka nwolɛ bɛrɛla.”

english_verse: Amasa started bringing the army together, but it was taking him more than three days.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Ameesa hɔboɔboale Dwudama anloa, noko kenle nsa ne mɔɔ bɛhilele ye la kpale nwolɛ.

english_verse: So David said to Abishai, “Sheba will hurt us more than Absalom ever did. Take my best soldiers and go after him. We don't want him to take over any walled cities and get away from us.” Joab Kills Amasa
translation_verse: Na Devidi zele Abehyae kɛ, “Bekelae ara Hyiba bayɛ maamɔvo adɛla Abesalɛm. Fa me ɛlɔnema ne toa ye ndinlizo, saa ɔnyia azuamgbole mɔɔ bɛlie nwolɛ la bie azo ɔfea a ɔbayɛ ngyegyelɛ yeamaa yɛ.”

english_verse: Abishai left Jerusalem to try and capture Sheba. He took along Joab and his soldiers, as well as David's bodyguard and best troops.
translation_verse: Na Dwowabe ɛlɔnema ne, belemgbunli sinzavolɛma nee ɛlɔnema mɔɔ ɛha la lile Abehyae anzi bɛvi Gyɛlusalɛm bɛhɔle Bekelae ara Hyiba ɛhyelɛ.

english_verse: They had gone as far as the big rock at Gibeon when Amasa caught up with them. Joab had a dagger strapped around his waist over his military uniform, but it fell out as he started toward Amasa.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ bɛhɔdwule bolɛ kpole ne mɔɔ wɔ Gebɛyɔn la anwo la, Ameesa rayiale bɛ adenle. Dwowabe wula konle tɛladeɛ, ɔhye akyeso na konle dadeɛ mɔɔ wɔ boa nu la zia nuhua. Mɔɔ ɔkɔ ɔ nyunlu la, ɔyele dadeɛ ne ɔvile ye boa ne anu.

english_verse: Joab said, “Amasa, my cousin, how are you?” Then Joab took hold of Amasa's beard with his right hand, so that he could greet him with a kiss.
translation_verse: Na Dwowabe bizale Ameesa kɛ, “Me diema, wɔ agbɔkɛ nu ɛ?” Dwowabe vale ɔ sa fema ne zɔle Ameesa akɛsa kɛ asɛɛ ɔfo ɔ nloa anwo.

english_verse: Amasa did not see the dagger in Joab's other hand. Joab stuck it in Amasa's stomach, and his insides spilled out on the ground. Joab only struck him once, but Amasa was dying. Joab and his brother Abishai went off to chase Sheba.
translation_verse: Ameesa annwu dadeɛ ne mɔɔ wɔ Dwowabe asa bɛne ne anu la, yemɔti Dwowabe vale dadeɛ ne wɔle Ameesa akunlu tulule ye anyalɛ manle ɔwule. Yeanwɔ ye fane nwiɔ. Akee Dwowabe nee ɔ diema Abehyae hɔle zolɛ voanle Hyiba.

english_verse: One of Joab's soldiers stood by Amasa and shouted, “If any of you are for Joab and David, then follow Joab!”
translation_verse: Dwowabe menli ne mɔ ko gyinlanle Ameesa funli ne anwo na ɔdeanle nuhua kɛ, “Awie biala mɔɔ kulo Dwowabe nee awie biala mɔɔ wɔ Devidi afoa la ɛdoa Dwowabe.”

english_verse: Amasa was still rolling in his own blood in the middle of the road. The soldier who had shouted noticed that everyone who passed by would stop, so he dragged Amasa off the road and covered him with a blanket.
translation_verse: Ɛnee Ameesa funli ne mɔɔ mogya ɛbia ye takaa la la ademgbole ne anu. Yemɔti ɛnee awie biala mɔɔ kɛdwu ɛkɛ ne la gyinla. Na Dwowabe sonvolɛ ne nwunle kɛ awie biala ɛlɛgyinla anlea funli ne la, ɔmanle ye zo ɔhɔdole kpɔkɛ ne anu na ɔdule kundu ɔguale ɔ nwo zo.

english_verse: After this, no one else stopped. They all walked straight past him on their way to help Joab capture Sheba. Sheba Hides Out in the Town of Abel
translation_verse: Mɔɔ bɛyele funli ne ademgbole ne anu la, menli ne mɔ amuala doale Dwowabe kɛ bɛfoa Hyiba bɛahɔhye ye.

english_verse: Sheba had gone through all of the tribes of Israel when he came to the town of Abel Beth-Maacah. All of his best soldiers met him there and followed him into the town.
translation_verse: Na Hyiba luale Yizilayɛ mbusua ekpunli ekpunli ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti avinli hɔle suakpole Ebɛle Bɛte Meeyaka azo, na Bekelae anwo amra ne kɔsɔɔti doale ye wɔ suakpole ne azo.

english_verse: Joab and his troops came and surrounded Abel, so that no one could go in or come out. They made a dirt ramp up to the town wall and then started to use a battering ram to knock the wall down. A Wise Woman Saves the Town
translation_verse: Dwowabe ɛlɔnema ne dele Hyiba nganeɛ, yemɔti bɛrabɛnrale bɛyiale suakpole Ebɛle Bɛte Meeyaka. Bɛvunvunle bane ne mɔ abo kɛ bɛyɛ bɛamaa yeaha yeagua. Eza bɛhuohuanle ndɛtɛlɛ wɔ suakpole ne bane ne mɔ anzi na bɛzile bane ne anzi kɛ bɛbubu ye bɛagua aze.

english_verse: A wise woman shouted from the top of the wall, “Listen to me! Listen to me! I have to talk to Joab! Tell him to come here!”
translation_verse: Raalɛ nrɛlɛbɛvolɛ bie wɔ suakpole ne azo. Ɔdeanle nuhua ɔzele kɛ, “Bɛdie, bɛdie! Bɛha bɛhile Dwowabe kɛ ɔrɛla ɔmaa menga edwɛkɛ mengile ye.”

english_verse: When he came, the woman said, “Are you Joab?” “Yes, I am,” he answered. She said, “Please, listen to what I have to say.” “All right,” he said. “I'll listen.”
translation_verse: Dwowabe bikyele ye. Raalɛ ne bizale ye kɛ, “Wɔmɔ a bɛfɛlɛ wɔ Dwowabe la ɔ?” Dwowabe buale ye kɛ, “Ɛhɛe, medame ɔ.” Raalɛ ne zele ye kɛ, “Yɛmenle, tie me.” Dwowabe zele ye kɛ, “Melɛtie wɔ.”

english_verse: She said, “Long ago people used to say, ‘If you want good advice, go to the town of Abel to get it.’ The answers they got here were all that was needed to settle any problem.
translation_verse: Akee raalɛ ne zele kɛ, “Tete ne ɛnee bɛka ye kɛ, ‘Bɛhɔ Ebɛle Bɛte Meeyaka bɛhɔbiza’, kolaa na bɛahola edwɛkɛ biala di.

english_verse: We are Israelites, and we want peace! You can trust us. Why are you trying to destroy a town that's like a mother in Israel? Why do you want to wipe out the Lord's people?”
translation_verse: Anzonudwolɛ menli nee menli mɔɔ di nɔhalɛ wɔ Yizilayɛ la ko a le me. Ɛkpondɛ kɛ ɛbɔ suakpole ɛhye mɔɔ le tete wɔ Yizilayɛ la ɔ? Ɛkpondɛ kɛ ɛsɛkye debie mɔɔ le Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛdeɛ la ɔ”

english_verse: Joab answered, “No, no! I'm not trying to wipe you out or destroy your town!
translation_verse: Dwowabe buale ye kɛ, “Nyamenle ɛkpa ɛgua kɛ menwɔzɛkye suakpole ye.

english_verse: That's not it at all. There's a man in your town from the hill country of Ephraim. His name is Sheba, and he is the leader of a rebellion against King David. Turn him over to me, and we will leave your town alone.” The woman told Joab, “We will throw his head over the wall.”
translation_verse: Ɔnle nɔhalɛ. Tɛ yɛ adwenle mɔɔ yɛlɛ ye la ɛne. Nrenya bie mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye Hyiba mɔɔ vi Yifelaem awoka ne mɔ azo lɔ la ɛbɔ ɔ bo kɛ ɔko yeatia Belemgbunli Devidi na yenriandi yeravea ɛke. Bɛye ɔ ngomekye ala bɛmaa me na menwɔye me nwo wɔ suakpole ye azo.” Raalɛ ne zele Dwowabe kɛ, “Nea, bɛbavuandi ɔ ti ne bɛado bane ne anzi bɛamaa wɔ.”

english_verse: She went to the people of the town and talked them into doing it. They cut off Sheba's head and threw it to Joab. Joab blew a signal on his trumpet, and the soldiers returned to their homes. Joab went back to David in Jerusalem. Another List of David's Officials
translation_verse: Raalɛ ne vale ye adwenle ne manle ezuavolɛ ne, na bɛpɛle Hyiba ati bɛvuandinle bɛmanle Dwowabe wɔ bane ne anzi lɔ.
