translation_verse: Akee Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne ara raalɛ ne mɔɔ Sɔlɔmɔn gyale ye la vile Devidi suakpole ne azo dule hɔdɛnlanle sua ne mɔɔ ɔ hu Sɔlɔmɔn zile manle ye la anu. Sɔlɔmɔn akee manle bɛzoale anwea bɛduale kuma ne mɔɔ la suakpole ne aduduleɛ la.

english_verse: Three times a year, Solomon burned incense and offered sacrifices to the Lord on the altar he had built. Solomon had now finished building the Lord's temple.
translation_verse: Ɛvolɛ biala Sɔlɔmɔn ku nane yela bɛ bɔ azu na ɔbɔ anzonudwolɛ azu fane nsa ɔmaa Ɛdɛnkɛma wɔ ye azukponle ne mɔɔ yezi la azo. Eza ɔyelale ɛyɛlɛ noko ɔmanle Ɛdɛnkɛma. Ɛnee kɛ Sɔlɔmɔn zile yɛle sua ne anwo gyima dwulale la ɛne.

english_verse: He also had a lot of ships at Ezion-Geber, a town in Edom near Eloth on the Red Sea.
translation_verse: Belemgbunli Sɔlɔmɔn bobɔle meli dɔɔnwo wɔ Yizeɔngibɛ mɔɔ zua Yilate la, wɔ Akaba Ebolo ne anu wɔ Yidɔm maanzinli nu.

english_verse: King Hiram let some of his experienced sailors go to the country of Ophir with Solomon's own sailors, and they brought back about
translation_verse: Bɛ nee bɛ hɔle Ofɛ maanle nu na bɛnyianle ezukoa nvutuke mɔɔ bo kilo apenle ngoko ɛya nna la bɛrɛlɛle Belemgbunli Sɔlɔmɔn.

english_verse: He answered every question, no matter how difficult it was.
translation_verse: Na Sɔlɔmɔn yeyele bɛ kɔsɔɔti anloa; ko bɔbɔ ɛnle nu mɔɔ hyele Belemgbunli Sɔlɔmɔn ekyii a.

english_verse: The Queen was amazed at Solomon's wisdom. She was breathless when she saw his palace, the food on his table, his officials, his servants in their uniforms, the people who served his food, and the sacrifices he offered at the Lord's temple.
translation_verse: Akee ɔnwunle aleɛ mɔɔ bɛdi wɔ sua nu ɛkɛ nee ye mgbanyima ne mɔ tɛnlabelɛ nu, kɛ ye sonvolɛma si sonle ye, bɛ adɛladeɛ mɔɔ bɛwula, ye nzasuvolɛma nee ɛyelalɛ azu mɔɔ Sɔlɔmɔn bɔ wɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu la, ɔzinle ɔ nwo na ɔ nwo bubule ye.

english_verse: She said: Solomon, in my own country I had heard about your wisdom and all you've done.
translation_verse: Ɛhye ati ɔhanle ɔhilele Sɔlɔmɔn kɛ, “Ayi, bɛle nɔhalɛ bɔkɔɔ. Edwɛkɛ mɔɔ fane ɛ nwo nee wɔ nrɛlɛbɛ ne anwo mɔɔ mendele wɔ me maanle nu lɔ la le nɔhalɛ kɔsɔɔ.

english_verse: But I didn't believe it until I saw it with my own eyes! And there's so much I didn't hear about. You are wiser and richer than I was told.
translation_verse: Saa mese kɛ alumua ne mendele la menliele menlile a ɛnee mebɔ adalɛ; meradwu ɛke la yɛɛ melie meli a. Nɔhalɛ, mɔɔ bɛhanle bɛhilele me la ɛndwu mɔɔ medame meranwu ye me nye zo la foa ko bɔbɔ.

english_verse: Your wives and officials are lucky to be here where they can listen to the wise things you say.
translation_verse: Wɔ mraalɛ anwo ɛyɛ moavolɛ, wɔ sonvolɛma ati ɛyɛ boɛ kɛ dahuu bɛtie wɔ, bɛsonle wɔ na bɛte wɔ nrɛlɛbɛ edwɛkɛ ne mɔ a.

english_verse: The back of the throne was rounded at the top, and it had armrests on each side. There was a statue of a lion on both sides of the throne, and there was a statue of a lion at both ends of each of the six steps leading up to the throne. No other throne in the world was like Solomon's.
translation_verse: Bɛze awenade nwiɔ bɛziezie ɔ sa nwiɔ ne mɔ azo: ko gyi bɛne zo yɛɛ ko gyi fema zo. Akee awenade bulu nee nwiɔ gyigyi ebia ne kpolike ne mɔ azo; kpolike ko biala ati nee ɔ ti lɛ awenade nwiɔ. Ebia zɛhae, bie ɛnle ewiade ye anu belemgbunli maanle gyɛne biala anu.

english_verse: Solomon had a lot of seagoing ships. Every three years he sent them out with Hiram's ships to bring back gold, silver, and ivory, as well as monkeys and peacocks.
translation_verse: Ɔlɛ meli dɔɔnwo wɔ Tahyehye nyevile zo mɔɔ nee Helam meli ne mɔ a kɔ gualilɛ a. Bɛkɔ a ɛvolɛ nsa biala bɛsia bɛ nee ezukoa nvutuke, dwɛtɛ fufule, ɛzɛlɛ, motimo yɛɛ ahomu ba sua nu.

english_verse: Year after year people came and brought gifts of silver and gold, as well as clothes, weapons, spices, horses, or mules.
translation_verse: Awie biala mɔɔ rale Sɔlɔmɔn ɛkɛ ne la vale ye ahyɛlɛdeɛ mɔɔ le dwɛtɛ fufule nee ezukoa nvutuke, adɛladeɛ, konle ninyɛne, ninyɛne evuanlɛ mɔɔ bɛfa bɛto aleɛ, alufuanlɛ, mgbɔnwɔ nee mgbɔnwɔndua la rale. Ɛhye hɔle zolɛ ɛvolɛ biala.

english_verse: While he was king, there was silver everywhere in Jerusalem, and cedar was as common as ordinary sycamore trees in the foothills.
translation_verse: Belemgbunli Sɔlɔmɔn mekɛ zo, ɔmanle dwɛtɛ fufule yɛle kɛ awolɛ la wɔ Gyɛlusalɛm, yɛɛ ɔmanle sida mbaka bule kɛ sikamɔ mbaka.

english_verse: Solomon's merchants bought his horses and chariots in the regions of Musri and Kue. They paid
translation_verse: Bɛtɔ konle ehwili ko dwɛtɛ fufule ɛya nsia wɔ Yigyibiti yɛɛ ɛkpɔnwɔ ko dwɛtɛ fufule ɛya ko abulanlu na belemgbunli ne gualilɛma ne azia adɔne bɛ amaa Hɛte nee Selea arelemgbunli.

english_verse: Solomon also worshiped Astarte the goddess of Sidon, and Milcom the disgusting god of Ammon.
translation_verse: Sɔlɔmɔn hakyile zonlenle Saedɛnema bozonle raalɛ ne mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye Asetate la nee Amɔnoma bozonle anwo ɛzulolɛ ne mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye Molɛke la.

english_verse: Solomon's father had obeyed the Lord with all his heart, but Solomon disobeyed and did what the Lord hated.
translation_verse: Sɔlɔmɔn yɛle ɛtane tiale Ɛdɛnkɛma; yeanli Ɛdɛnkɛma anzi nɔhalɛ nu, kɛmɔ ɔ ze Devidi yɛle la.

english_verse: Solomon built shrines on a hill east of Jerusalem to worship Chemosh the disgusting god of Moab, and Molech the disgusting god of Ammon.
translation_verse: Ɔzile Mowabe bozonle anwo ɛzulolɛ ne mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye Kimɔhye la yɛɛ Amɔn bozonle anwo ɛzulolɛ ne mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye Molɛke la mmonle azua wɔ boka ne mɔɔ wɔ Gyɛlusalɛm aduduleɛ la azo.

english_verse: In fact, he built a shrine for each of his foreign wives, so all of them could burn incense and offer sacrifices to their own gods.
translation_verse: Zɔhane ala yɛɛ Sɔlɔmɔn yɛle manle ye nyɛvolɛ mraalɛ ne mɔ amuala a. Ɔsisile azua ɔmanle bɛyelale ɛyɛlɛ bɛzonlenle bɛ maanle nu awozonle ne mɔ.

english_verse: The Lord God of Israel had appeared to Solomon two times and warned him not to worship foreign gods. But Solomon disobeyed and did it anyway. This made the Lord very angry,
translation_verse: ɛha ɛhile ye kɛ ɔmmasonle nyamenle gyɛne bie ɔboka ɔ nwo la. Sɔlɔmɔn anli Ɛdɛnkɛma mɛla zo.

english_verse: and he said to Solomon: You did what you wanted and not what I told you to do. Now I'm going to take your kingdom from you and give it to one of your officials.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Sɔlɔmɔn kɛ, “Kɛmɔ wɔandie me ne na ɛdawɔ ɛ nye fuu wɔbulu me ngyekyeleɛ nee me mɛla mɔɔ meva memaa wɔ la azo la ati, mebalie me maanle ne ɛ sa nu na meava meamaa wɔ sonvolɛma ne mɔ bie.

english_verse: But because David was your father, you will remain king as long as you live. I will wait until your son becomes king, then I will take the kingdom from him.
translation_verse: Noko ɔlua ɛ ze Devidi ati, menrɛlie maanle ne wɔ wɔ mekɛ zo; mebalie ye wɔ ɛ ra nrenya asa anu.

english_verse: When I do, I will still let him rule one tribe, because I have not forgotten that David was my servant and Jerusalem is my chosen city. Hadad Becomes an Enemy of Solomon
translation_verse: Eza bɔbɔ menrɛlie maanle ne amuala ɛ sa nu; ɔlua me akɛlɛ Devidi ati nee Gyɛlusalɛm maanle mumua ne mɔɔ mekpa nu meye la ati, mebava Yizilayɛma anu ekpunli ko meamaa ɛ ra nrenya azie bɛ.” Sɔlɔmɔn kpɔvolɛma

english_verse: Hadad was from the royal family of Edom, and here is how the Lord made him Solomon's enemy:
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma manle Yidɔm amra ne anu ko mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye Heedade la dwazole Sɔlɔmɔn anwo zo.

english_verse: Hadad and his wife had a son named Genubath, and the queen let the boy grow up in the palace with her own children.
translation_verse: Taapɛnize adiema raalɛ ne nee Heedade wole ralɛ nrenya na bɛdonle ye Gɛnubɛte, na Taapɛnize lile ye adane wɔ Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne sua nu ɛkɛ bokale belemgbunli ne amra mrenya ne mɔ anwo.

english_verse: When Hadad heard that David and Joab were dead, he said to the king, “Your Majesty, please let me go back to my own country.”
translation_verse: Mekɛ mɔɔ Heedade dele ye wɔ Yigyibiti kɛ Belemgbunli Devidi ɛhɔ ayile nu na ye safohyenle kpanyinli Dwowabe ɔdaye noko yewu la, Heedade nwunle Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Maa me adenle maa mengɔ me maanle nu.”

english_verse: “Why?” asked the king. “Do you want something I haven't given you?” “No, I just want to go home.” Rezon Becomes an Enemy of Solomon
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne bizale ye kɛ, “Duzu ati ɔ? Wɔhyia debie nwo meanyɛ meammaa wɔ ati a ɛkulo kɛ ɛkɔ a?” Heedade buale belemgbunli ne kɛ, “Wɔmɔ maa mengɔ me maanle nu.” Nzinlii Heedade yɛle belemgbunli wɔ Yidɔm na ɔyɛle Yizilayɛma anwo ɛlɔne kpole kpalɛ.

english_verse: Here is how God made Rezon son of Eliada an enemy of Solomon: Rezon had run away from his master, King Hadadezer of Zobah.
translation_verse: Nyamenle eza manle Yilayada ara nrenya Rilizɔn dwazole Sɔlɔmɔn anwo zo. Ɛnee Rilizɔn ɛnriandi ɔ menle Hadadizɛ mɔɔ le Zoba belemgbunli ne.

english_verse: He formed his own small army and became its leader after David had defeated Hadadezer's troops. Then Rezon and his army went to Damascus, where he became the ruler of Syria and an enemy of Israel. Both Hadad and Rezon were enemies of Israel while Solomon was king, and they caused him a lot of trouble. The Lord Makes a Promise to Jeroboam
translation_verse: Ɔyɛle Yizilayɛma kpɔvolɛ wɔ Belemgbunli Sɔlɔmɔn mekɛ zo, ɔyɛle ninyɛndane kɛmɔ Heedade yɛle la; ɔhyile Yizilayɛma bɔkɔɔ wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɔdi Selea ebia ne la. Nyamenle ɛwɔkɛ ne mɔɔ ɔbɔle Gyɛlɔbowam la

english_verse: Jeroboam was from the town of Zeredah in Ephraim. His father Nebat had died, but his mother Zeruah was still alive. Jeroboam was one of Solomon's officials, but even he rebelled against Solomon.
translation_verse: Sonla ko mɔɔ ɔdaye ɔhakyile ɔ nzi ɔzile Belemgbunli Sɔlɔmɔn la a le ye sonvolɛma ne mɔ ko mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye Gyɛlɔbowam mɔɔ le Nibate ara nrenya ne. Nibate le Yifelaemnli; ɔvi Zɛlɛda. Ɔ nli le kunlanvolɛ raalɛ, bɛfɛlɛ ye Zɛlua.

english_verse: Here is how it happened: While Solomon's workers were filling in the land on the east side of Jerusalem and repairing the city walls,
translation_verse: Deɛ mɔɔ yemɔti Gyɛlɔbowam kpɔle Sɔlɔmɔn la ɛne. Sɔlɔmɔn tua Gyɛlusalɛm aduduleɛ kuma kpole ne yealie suakpole ne anwo bane la,

english_verse: Solomon noticed that Jeroboam was a hard worker. So he put Jeroboam in charge of the work force from Manasseh and Ephraim.
translation_verse: ɛnee Gyɛlɔbowam le kpavolɛ katakyie mɔɔ anwo yɛ se a. Sɔlɔmɔn nwunle ye zɛhae la ɔvale ye ɔziele kpanyinli mɔɔ nea Dwosefi sua nu amra mɔɔ ɛlɛyɛ mialeranu gyima la anwo zo.

english_verse: But Solomon will still rule one tribe, since he is the son of David my servant, and Jerusalem is my chosen city.
translation_verse: Ɔlua me akɛlɛ Devidi nee Gyɛlusalɛm mɔɔ ɔle suakpole mɔɔ mekpa nu meye ye kɛ ɔle me ɛdeɛ la ati, mebava ekpunli ko meamaa Sɔlɔmɔn.

english_verse: “Solomon and the Israelites are not like their ancestor David. They will not listen to me, obey me, or do what is right. They have turned from me to worship Astarte the goddess of Sidon, Chemosh the god of Moab, and Milcom the god of Ammon.
translation_verse: Ɔboalekɛ Sɔlɔmɔn ɛkpo me yehɔzonle Saedɛn bozonle raalɛ Asetate nee Mowabe bozonle Kimɔhye nee Amɔn bozonle Melekɔn ne. Sɔlɔmɔn ɛdu me nloa ɛdo. Yeyɛ ɛtane, kɛmɔ ɔ ze Devidi yɛle la.

english_verse: “Solomon is David's son, and David was my chosen leader, who did what I commanded. So I will let Solomon be king until he dies.
translation_verse: Noko ɔlua me akɛlɛ Devidi mɔɔ memkpale nu menyele ye na ɔdaye noko ɔdiele me edwɛkɛ la ati, memaa yeali belemgbunli toonwo yeawu, menrɛlie maanle ne amuala menrɛvi Sɔlɔmɔn asa anu.

english_verse: but Solomon's son will still rule one tribe. This way, my servant David will always have a descendant ruling in Jerusalem, the city where I have chosen to be worshiped.
translation_verse: Mebamaa Sɔlɔmɔn ara nrenya ne azie abusua ekpunli ko ala na dahuu meanyia me akɛlɛ Devidi abo zo amra ne bie ali ebia wɔ Gyɛlusalɛm. Suakpole ɛhye yɛɛ mekpa nu meye kɛ bɛzonle me wɔ zolɛ a.

english_verse: “You will be king of Israel and will rule every nation you want.
translation_verse: Gyɛlɔbowam, mebamaa wɔazie Yizilayɛma nee maanle biala mɔɔ ɛkɛhulo kɛ ɛkɛzie bɛ la.

english_verse: I'll help you if you obey me. And if you do what I say, as my servant David did, I will always let someone from your family rule in Israel, just as someone from David's family will always rule in Judah. The nation of Israel will be yours.
translation_verse: Saa ɛyɛ tieyɛ ɛmaa me bɔkɔɔ, ɛdi me mɛla zo, na ɛyɛ mɔɔ menwɔze wɔ la, ɛsɔ me nye, kɛmɔ me akɛlɛ Devidi yɛle la a, me nee wɔ badɛnla dahuu; ɛbazie Yizilayɛma na ɛ mra ali ebia ne, kɛmɔ menyɛle memanle Devidi la.

english_verse: “I will punish the descendants of David, but not forever.”
translation_verse: Sɔlɔmɔn ninyɛndane ne ati mebahwe Devidi abo zo amra anzo, noko ɔnrɛyɛ kpole biala.’ ”

english_verse: Everything else Solomon did while he was king is written in the book about him and his wisdom.
translation_verse: Akee Sɔlɔmɔn ɛbɛla mɔɔ ɔbɔle nee mɔɔ ɔyɛle nee ye nrɛlɛbɛ ne, bɛhɛlɛ bɛ wɔ Sɔlɔmɔn anwo Tetedwɛkɛ Buluku ne anu.

english_verse: After he had ruled
translation_verse: Sɔlɔmɔn dɛnlanle Gyɛlusalɛm ziele Yizilayɛma ɛvolɛ abulanla.

english_verse: he died and was buried there in the city of his father David. His son Rehoboam then became king.
translation_verse: Ɔhɔle ayile nu na bɛwulale ye mrɛlatɛlɛ nu wɔ ɔ ze Devidi suakpole zo, na ɔ ra Rilihɔbowam lile ebia ne.

english_verse: But the people from the northern tribes of Israel sent for him. Then together they went to Rehoboam and said,
translation_verse: Mbusua ekpunli ne bie mɔ manle bɛhɔvɛlɛle Gyɛlɔbowam bɛrale, na bɛ muala bɛhɔle Rilihɔbowam ɛkɛ ne bɛhɔzele ye kɛ,

english_verse: “Give me three days to think about it,” Rehoboam replied, “then come back for my answer.” So the people left.
translation_verse: Ɔbuale bɛ kɛ, “Bɛhɔ na ɔdi kenle nsa a bɛzia bɛradie nwolɛ mualɛ.” Yemɔti menli ne ziale hɔle.

english_verse: Rehoboam went to some leaders who had been his father's senior officials, and he asked them, “What should I tell these people?”
translation_verse: Belemgbunli Rilihɔbowam yele edwɛkɛ ne dole mgbanyima mɔɔ boale ɔ ze Sɔlɔmɔn wɔ ye mekɛ zo la anyunlu na ɔbizale bɛ kɛ, “Duzu mualɛ a menva memaa menli ne a?”

english_verse: They answered, “If you want them to serve and obey you, then you should do what they ask today. Tell them you will make their work easier.”
translation_verse: Mgbanyima ne mɔ zele ye kɛ, “Saa ɛto ɛ nwo aze ɛmaa menli ne mɔ, ɛbu bɛ bie, na ɛtendɛ kɛnlɛma ɛkile bɛ a, bɛbazonle wɔ dahuu.”

english_verse: But Rehoboam refused their advice and went to the younger men who had grown up with him and were now his officials.
translation_verse: Rilihɔbowam anli mgbanyima ne mɔ edwɛkɛ ne anwo bie; ɔhɔyiale ɔdaye ɔ gɔnwo mɔ mgbavolɛ mɔɔ ɔ nee bɛ dule la

english_verse: He asked, “What do you think I should say to these people who asked me to make their work easier?”
translation_verse: na ɔbizale bɛ kɛ, “Menli ne se mende bɛ ɛvɛlɛ zo ekyii, na kɛ bɛ adwenle se bɛ ɛ?”

english_verse: Rehoboam ignored the advice of the older advisors.
translation_verse: Rilihɔbowam anva mgbanyima ne mɔ adwenle ɛdeɛ ne,

english_verse: He spoke bluntly and told them exactly what his own advisors had suggested: “My father made you work hard, but I'll make you work even harder. He punished you with whips, but I'll use whips with pieces of sharp metal!”
translation_verse: ɔlile ɔ gɔnwo mɔ mgbavolɛ ne mɔ folɛdulɛ ne azo na ɔdendɛle ɛtane ɛtane ɔhilele ye menli ne mɔ kɛ, “Saa egya zoale bɛ adesoa ɛnlomboɛ a, mame, mebazoa bɛ ye molozo. Saa egya bilale bɛ nɛnemile a, mame, mebava empele a meabila bɛ a.”

english_verse: When the Israelites heard that Jeroboam was back, they called everyone together. Then they sent for Jeroboam and made him king of Israel. Only the people from the tribe of Judah remained loyal to David's family. Shemaiah Warns Rehoboam (
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma amuala dele kɛ Gyɛlɔbowam ɛzia ɔ nzi vi Yigyibiti ɛra la bɛvɛlɛle ye wɔ bɛ ayia bo na bɛvale ye bɛziele Yizilayɛ belemgbunli. Biala anli Devidi abo zo amra ne anzi kɛ Dwuda abusua ekpunli ne anu amra ne mɔ ala. Hyɛmaya Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ ne (

english_verse: Meanwhile, God told Shemaiah the prophet
translation_verse: Na Nyamenle zoanle ye kpɔmanvolɛ Hyɛmaya kɛ

english_verse: to give Rehoboam and everyone from Judah and Benjamin this warning:
translation_verse: ɔva nrɛlaleɛ ɔhɔmaa Rilihɔbowam yɛɛ Dwuda nee Bɛngyaman mbusua ekpunli ne mɔ anu amra kɛ,

english_verse: “Don't go to war against the people from Israel—they are your relatives. Go home! I am the Lord, and I made these things happen.” Rehoboam and his army obeyed the Lord and went home. Jeroboam Makes Religious Changes
translation_verse: “Bɛmmafa konle bɛtoa bɛ mediema Yizilayɛma; bɛzia bɛhɔ sua nu. Medame Ɛdɛnkɛma a memaa ɛhye ɛzi a.” Bɛdiele Ɛdɛnkɛma nrɛlaleɛ ne na bɛhɔle sua nu. Gyɛlɔbowam kakyi ɔ nzi azi Ɛdɛnkɛma

english_verse: Jeroboam rebuilt Shechem in Ephraim and made it a stronger town, then he moved there. He also fortified the town of Penuel.
translation_verse: Akee Belemgbunli Gyɛlɔbowam kyekyele Hyikɛm sua ne mɔɔ wɔ Yifelaem awoka ne mɔ azo la kpalɛ na ɔdɛnlanle ɛkɛ; nzinlii ɔdule ɛkɛ ɔhɔkyekyele Pɛnuwɛle sua ne.

english_verse: One day, Jeroboam started thinking, “Everyone in Israel still goes to the temple in Jerusalem to offer sacrifices to the Lord. What if they become loyal to David's family again? They will kill me and accept Rehoboam as their king.”
translation_verse: Ɔhanle ye ɔ ti anu kɛ, “Saa meannea boɛ na me menli ye amuala kɔ Gyɛlusalɛm kɛ bɛkazonle Ɛdɛnkɛma wɔ Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu a bɛbahakyi bɛ adwenle na bɛazonle Belemgbunli Rilihɔbowam mɔɔ wɔ Dwuda la na bɛarahu me.”

english_verse: One day, Jeroboam was standing at the altar in Bethel, ready to make an offering. translation_verse: Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ ne hilele sɛkɛlɛneɛ ɛhye na ɔhanle kɛ, “Amaa wɔanwu kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma a ɛlɛtendɛ la, Ɛdɛnkɛma se, ‘Azukponle ɛhye bagolo agua, na zolɛ nzonle babɔ asande.’ ”

english_verse: The altar split in half, and the ashes fell to the ground, just as the prophet had warned.
translation_verse: Azukponle ne golole guale aze na zolɛ nzonle ne bɔle zandele, kɛmɔ Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ ne sɛkɛlɛneɛ ne mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma hilele la kile la.

english_verse: “Come home with me and eat something,” Jeroboam said. “I want to give you a gift for what you have done.”
translation_verse: Na belemgbunli ne hanle hilele Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ ne kɛ, “Maa yɛhɔ sua nu kɔnlo nzule, di debie, na mɔɔ wɔyɛ la, ɔwɔ kɛ meyɛ wɔ nyele.”

english_verse: “No, I wouldn't go with you, even if you offered me half of your kingdom. I won't eat or drink here either.

translation_verse: Akee ɔdule ɔ nla Meeyaka ɔvile Ɛhyenlema dibilɛ ne azo, ɔboalekɛ ɛnee yeyɛ bozonle raalɛ Ahyela ne ananze mɔɔ le kyibadeɛ la, na ɔsonle ye. Esa bubule Ahyela ananze ne na ɔhɔyelale ye wɔ Azule Kedelɔn ne anloa.

english_verse: Abijam became king of Judah in Jeroboam's eighteenth year as king of Israel,
translation_verse: Yizilayɛ belemgbunli Nibate ara Gyɛlɔbowam lile ɛvolɛ bulu nee mɔtwɛ wɔ ebia zo la yɛɛ Abaegya bɔle ebialilɛ bo wɔ Dwuda maanle nu a.

english_verse: Asa ordered everyone in Judah to carry away the stones and wood Baasha had used to strengthen the town of Ramah. Then he used these same stones and wood to fortify the town of Geba in the territory of Benjamin and the town of Mizpah.
translation_verse: Belemgbunli Esa bɔle nolo wɔ Dwuda maanle ne anu amuala kɛ awie biala ɛhɔzoa awolɛ nee mbaka mɔɔ ɛnee Beeyahya lɛ ɛlɛkyekye Releema la ɛrɛla Dwuda. Na Belemgbunli Esa vale awolɛ nee mbaka ɛhye mɔ kyekyele Giba wɔ Bɛngyaman maanle nu nee Mezepa.

english_verse: Abijam did not truly obey the Lord his God as his ancestor David had done. Instead, he was sinful just like his father Rehoboam.
translation_verse: Ɔvale ɔ ze agyakɛ na ɔyɛle ɛtane mɔɔ ɔ ze yɛle la amuala bie. Yeanli Ɛdɛnkɛma ye Nyamenle ne mɛla zo nɔhalɛ nu, kɛmɔ ɔ nlenya Devidi lile la.

english_verse: David had always obeyed the Lord's commands by doing right, except in the case of Uriah. And since Abijam was David's great-grandson, the Lord kept Jerusalem safe and let Abijam have a son who would be the next king.
translation_verse: Ɔboalekɛ Devidi nyɛleɛ zɔle Ɛdɛnkɛma anye yɛɛ ɔyɛle debie biala mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma zele ye la. Ɛleka mɔɔ ɔvonle la a le edwɛkɛ ne mɔɔ fane Hɛtenli Yulaya anwo la ala.

english_verse: The war that had broken out between Rehoboam and Jeroboam continued during the time that Abijam was king. Everything else Abijam did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Konle ne mɔɔ Rilihɔbowam nee Gyɛlɔbowam bɔle ɔ bo la dɔle Abaegya asa azo na ɔdaye noko ɔ nee Gyɛlɔbowam honle. Bɛhɛlɛ debie biala mɔɔ Abaegya yɛle wɔ ye mekɛ zo la wɔ Dwuda Arelemgbunli Tetedwɛkɛ Buluku ne anu.

english_verse: Abijam died and was buried in Jerusalem, and his son Asa became king. King Asa of Judah (
translation_verse: Abaegya hɔle ayile nu na bɛwulale ye mrɛlatɛlɛ nu wɔ Devidi suakpole zo. Ɔ ra nrenya Esa a lile ebia ne a. Dwuda Belemgbunli Esa (

english_verse: He placed in the temple all the silver and gold objects that he and his father had dedicated to the Lord.
translation_verse: Ɔhwenle ninyɛne mɔɔ ɔ ze dule ziele ɛkɛ manle Ɛdɛnkɛma nee ezukoa nvutuke nee dwɛtɛ fufule ninyɛne mɔɔ ɔdaye yeyɛ na yedu yemaa Ɛdɛnkɛma la amuala ɔrale Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu.

english_verse: Asa was always at war with King Baasha of Israel.
translation_verse: Konle amkpa Dwuda Belemgbunli Esa nee Yizilayɛ Belemgbunli Beeyahya avinli ɛlɛ.

english_verse: Asa obeyed the Lord, as David had done.
translation_verse: Esa ɛbɛla zɔle Ɛdɛnkɛma anye kɛ ɔ nlenya Devidi ɛdeɛ ne la.

english_verse: Asa became king of Judah in the twentieth year of Jeroboam's rule in Israel,
translation_verse: Bɛvale Esa bɛziele Dwuda belemgbunli wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɛnee Yizilayɛ Belemgbunli Gyɛlɔbowam ɛli ɛvolɛ abulanwiɔ wɔ ebia zo la.

english_verse: He forced the prostitutes at the shrines to leave the country, and he got rid of the idols his ancestors had made.
translation_verse: Ɔduale mrenya tuutuu ɛbɛla ɛbɔlɛ wɔ ɛleka ɛleka mɔɔ bɛsonle la wɔ maanle ne anu na ɔvuandinle awozonle mɔɔ ɔ ze mɔ zieziele la amuala ɔguale.

english_verse: As long as Asa lived, he was completely faithful to the Lord, even though he did not destroy the local shrines.
translation_verse: Esa anzɛkye mmonle azua ne mɔ amuala bɔbɔ ɛdeɛ, noko ɔvale ye ahonle muala ɔzonlenle Ɛdɛnkɛma wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɔde aze la.

english_verse: One time, Baasha invaded Judah and captured the town of Ramah. He started making the town stronger, so he could put troops there to stop people from going in and out of Judah.
translation_verse: Yizilayɛ Belemgbunli Beeyahya vale konle doale Dwudama na ɔkyekyele Releema, amaa yeadua adenle mɔɔ awie ɛngɔ Dwuda yɛɛ awie vi Dwuda ɛnvinde ɛngɔ ɛleka biala la.

english_verse: When Asa heard about this, he took the silver and gold from his palace and from the Lord's temple. He gave it to some of his officials and sent them to Damascus with this message for King Benhadad of Syria:
translation_verse: Esa vale dwɛtɛ fufule nee ezukoa nvutuke mɔɔ wɔ Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu la nee mɔɔ wɔ belemgbunli sua nu ɛkɛ ne la amuala manle ye sonvolɛma ne mɔ kɛ bɛva bɛhɔmaa Bɛneheedade, mɔɔ le Selea belemgbunli ne mɔɔ de Dɛmasekɛse la. Bɛneheedade ɔ ze a le Tabelamɔn yɛɛ ɔ nlenya a le Hizeɔn. Esa manle bɛhɔzele Bɛneheedade kɛ,

english_verse: “Our fathers signed a peace treaty. Why don't we do the same thing? This silver and gold is a present for you. So, would you please break your treaty with Baasha and force him to leave my country?”
translation_verse: “Maa yɛyɛ mediema, yɛhye yɛ nwo file, kɛmɔ yɛ ze mɔ yɛle la. Mefa dwɛtɛ fufule nee ezukoa nvutuke ɛhye mekyɛ wɔ. Bɔ mɔdenle te ɛ nwo fi Yizilayɛ Belemgbunli Beeyahya anwo, amaa yeaye ye ɛlɔnema ne wɔ me azɛlɛ ye azo.”

english_verse: Benhadad did what Asa asked and sent the Syrian army into Israel. They captured the towns of Ijon, Dan, and Abel-Bethmaacah, and the territories of Chinneroth and Naphtali.
translation_verse: Bɛneheedade liele Belemgbunli Esa nzuzulɛ ne dole nu na ɔmanle ye ɛlɔnema hɔdoale Yizilayɛ azuamgbole ne bie mɔ bɛ nee bɛ honle. Ɔhonle ɔvale Ayedwɔn nee Dan nee Ebɛle Bɛte Meeyaka nee azuamgbole ne mɔ mɔɔ wɔ Galeli Tandane ne anloa la nee Nafetalae maanle ne amuala.

english_verse: When Baasha heard about it, he left Ramah and went back to Tirzah.
translation_verse: Belemgbunli Beeyahya dele edwɛkɛ ɛhye la ɔgyakyile Releema sua ne ɛkyekyelɛ na ɔhɔdɛnlanle Tɛza.

english_verse: Everything else Asa did while he was king, including his victories and the towns he rebuilt, is written in The History of the Kings of Judah. When he got older, he had a foot disease.
translation_verse: Bɛhɛlɛ mɔdenle mɔɔ Belemgbunli Esa bɔle, ye akɛnrasesebɛ nee ye tumi nee azua mɔɔ ɔkyekyele la amuala anwo edwɛkɛ wɔ Dwuda Arelemgbunli Tetedwɛkɛ Buluku ne anu. Esa yɛle kpanyinli kpalɛ na nzinlii ɔ gyakɛ hunle ye manle ɔyɛle abubura.

english_verse: Nadab son of Jeroboam became king of Israel in Asa's second year as king of Judah, and he ruled two years.
translation_verse: Belemgbunli Esa lile ɛvolɛ nwiɔ wɔ Dwuda ebia ne azo la yɛɛ Gyɛlɔbowam ara Needabe ɔdaye ɔralile Yizilayɛ ebia ne a; ɔziele Yizilayɛma ɛvolɛ nwiɔ.

english_verse: Nadab disobeyed the Lord by following the evil example of his father, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Ɔvale ɔ ze agyakɛ, ye ɛbɛla anzɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma anye. Ɔmanle Yizilayɛma yɛle ɛtane ko ne ala mɔɔ ɔ ze manle bɛyɛle la bie.

english_verse: The Lord's prophet Ahijah had earlier said, “Not one man or boy in Jeroboam's family will be left alive.” And, as soon as Baasha became king, he killed everyone in Jeroboam's family,
translation_verse: Beeyahya dɛnlanle ebia ne azo ala la yɛɛ ɔbɔle Gyɛlɔbowam abo zo amra ɛhunlɛ bo a; yeangyakyi sonla ko bɔbɔ. Ɔhunle bɛ kɔsɔɔti, kɛmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma edwɛkɛ ne mɔɔ ɔluale ye akɛlɛ Ahaegya mɔɔ vi Hyaelo la anwo zo hanle la se la.

english_verse: because Jeroboam had made the Lord God of Israel angry by sinning and causing the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Gyɛlɔbowam manle Ɛdɛnkɛma, Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne vale ɛya wɔ ɛtane mɔɔ ɔdaye Gyɛlɔbowam ɔyɛle, na eza ɔmanle Yizilayɛma amuala yɛle bie la anwo. Ɛhye ati a bɛbɔle ɔ bo zo bɔkɔɔ a.

english_verse: Everything else Nadab did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Bɛhɛlɛ mɔdenle mɔɔ Needabe bɔle la wɔ Yizilayɛ Arelemgbunli Tetedwɛkɛ Buluku ne anu.

english_verse: King Asa of Judah and King Baasha of Israel were always at war. King Baasha of Israel
translation_verse: Yizilayɛ Belemgbunli Beeyahya nee Belemgbunli Esa honle mekɛ biala. Yizilayɛ Belemgbunli Beeyahya

english_verse: Baasha son of Ahijah became king of Israel in Asa's third year as king of Judah, and he ruled
translation_verse: Belemgbunli Esa lile ɛvolɛ nsa wɔ Dwuda ebia ne azo la ɛnee Ahaegya ara Beeyahya de Tɛza na yebɔ ɔ bo ɔlɛsie Yizilayɛ maanle ne. Ɔlile ebia ne ɛvolɛ abulanwiɔ nee nna.

english_verse: Baasha also disobeyed the Lord by acting like Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Beeyahya ɛbɛla anzɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma anye. Ɔyɛle Gyɛlɔbowam ɛtane ne mɔ mɔɔ ɔyɛle la bie, na ɔmanle Yizilayɛma yɛle ɛtane.

english_verse: The Lord sent Jehu son of Hanani to say to Baasha:
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma luale Gyihu mɔɔ le Hananae ara ne anwo zo vale nrɛlaleɛ hɔmanle Beeyahya kɛ,

english_verse: Nobody knew who you were until I, the Lord, chose you to be the leader of my people Israel. And now you're acting exactly like Jeroboam by causing the Israelites to sin. What you've done has made me so angry
translation_verse: “Ɛdawɔ Beeyahya, anrɛɛ awie ɛnze wɔ. Noko memkpogyale wɔ zo menvale wɔ menziele me menli Yizilayɛma belemgbunli. Na kɛkala, wɔva Gyɛlɔbowam agyakɛ wɔmaa me menli Yizilayɛma ɛyɛ ɛtane ɛtia me.

english_verse: that I will destroy you and your family, just as I did the family of Jeroboam.
translation_verse: Zɔhane ati mebabɔ ɛ bo zo meamaa wɔ awuke ne abɔ kɛ Nibate ara Gyɛlɔbowam ɛdeɛ ne la.

english_verse: Dogs will eat the bodies of your relatives who die in town, and vultures will eat the bodies of those who die in the country.
translation_verse: Wɔ sua nu amra biala mɔɔ kɛwu suakpole zo la, ahwea bali ye nwonane, yɛɛ mɔɔ kɛwu ɛbɔ nu noko la, nloma basuso ye nwonane.”

english_verse: Baasha made the Lord very angry, and that's why the Lord gave Jehu this message for Baasha and his family. Baasha constantly disobeyed the Lord by following Jeroboam's sinful example—but even worse, he killed everyone in Jeroboam's family! Everything else Baasha did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. Baasha died and was buried in Tirzah, and his son Elah became king. King Elah of Israel
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma vale nrɛlaleɛ zoanle ye kpɔmanvolɛ Gyihu mɔɔ le Hananae ara ne manle ɔhɔmanle Beeyahya nee ye sua nu amra wɔ ɛtane mɔɔ bɛyɛle bɛtiale ye la anwo. Beeyahya hanle Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛya, ɔluakɛ ɔyɛle ɛtane ɔtiale ye, kɛmɔ Gyɛlɔbowam yɛle la; yeanga ɛhye angome, ɔdaye Beeyahya a ɔhunle Gyɛlɔbowam abo zo amra amuala a. Yizilayɛ Belemgbunli Yila

english_verse: Omri did more evil things than any king before him.
translation_verse: Ɔmelae yɛle debie mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma kyi la, bɔbɔ akee ɔdɛlale alumua arelemgbunli ne mɔ.

english_verse: Zimri commanded half of Elah's chariots, and he made plans to kill Elah. One day, Elah was in Tirzah, getting drunk at the home of Arza, his prime minister,
translation_verse: Ye sonvolɛ Zemelae mɔɔ nea ye ɛlɔnema mɔɔ ka konle ehwili ne mɔ anu foa ko anwo zo la bɔle adwenle yɛle ɔ nwo ɛlɔne. Kenle ko Yila wɔ ye sonvolɛ Aaza mɔɔ nea belemgbunli awuke nu ɛkɛ ne la sua nu wɔ Tɛza ɔlɛno nza na asɛɛ yewie bo la,

english_verse: when Zimri went there and killed Elah. So Zimri became king in the twenty-seventh year of Asa's rule in Judah.
translation_verse: Zemelae rawolole awuke ne anu, ɔtiale ye ɔdole aze, ɔhunle ye na ɔdaye ɔlile ebia ne.

english_verse: As soon as Zimri became king, he killed everyone in Baasha's family. Not one man or boy in his family was left alive—even his close friends were killed.
translation_verse: Zemelae lile ebia ne ala la yɛɛ ɔhunle Beeyahya sua nu amra kɔsɔɔti a. Yeangyakyi kakula nrenya ekyi ko bɔbɔ ɛkɛ. Ɔ gɔnwo mɔ bɔbɔ, ɔhunle bɛ muala, ɔbɔle bɛ bo zo.

english_verse: Baasha's family was completely wiped out, just as the Lord's prophet Jehu had warned.
translation_verse: Yemɔti ɔlua Ɛdɛnkɛma anloa edwɛkɛ mɔɔ ɔvale ɔzoanle ye kpɔmanvolɛ Gyihu la azo, Zemelae bɔle Beeyahya awuke ne tɔɔ.

english_verse: Baasha and Elah sinned and caused the Israelites to sin, and they made the Lord angry by worshiping idols.
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ Beeyahya nee ɔ ra Yila bɛ mu nwiɔ bɛmanle ɛya hunle Ɛdɛnkɛma wɔ bɛ awozonle ezonlenlɛ ti. Bɛyɛle ɛtane na bɛmanle Yizilayɛma noko yɛle bie.

english_verse: Everything else Elah did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Zimri of Israel
translation_verse: Bɛhɛlɛ Yila nyɛleɛ nee ɛbɛla mɔɔ ɔbɔle la anwo edwɛkɛ wɔ Yizilayɛ Arelemgbunli Tetedwɛkɛ Buluku ne anu. Yizilayɛ Belemgbunli Zemelae

english_verse: Zimri became king of Israel in Asa's twenty-seventh year as king of Judah, but he ruled only seven days from Tirzah. Israel's army was camped near Gibbethon in Philistia under the command of Omri. The soldiers heard that Zimri had killed Elah, and they made Omri their king that same day.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ menli mɔɔ ɛhɔ nzia ne la dele kɛ Zemelae ɛbɔ adwenle ɛhu belemgbunli ne la, bɛvale ɛlɔnema kpanyinli Ɔmelae bɛziele Yizilayɛ belemgbunli ɛkɛ ne ala wɔ ɛleka mɔɔ bɛhɔ nzia ne la.

english_verse: At once, Omri and his army marched to Tirzah and attacked.
translation_verse: Bɛyɛle ɛhye ɔwiele la Ɔmelae nee ye ɛlɔnema ne mɔ yele bɛ nwo wɔ Gebɛtɔn na bɛhɔvale Tɛzama aze.

english_verse: When Zimri saw that the town was captured, he ran into the strongest part of the palace and killed himself by setting it on fire.
translation_verse: Zemelae nwunle kɛ ɛlɔne ɛva bɛ aze la, ɔhɔveale belemgbunli sua ne anu akunlu nehane na ɔdole senle sua ne anu ɔyelale ye ɔguale ɔ ti zo ɔhunle ɔ nwo.

english_verse: Zimri had disobeyed the Lord by following the evil example of Jeroboam, who had caused the Israelites to sin.
translation_verse: Ɔlua ye ɛtane mɔɔ ɔyɛle ɔtiale Ɛdɛnkɛma la ati a ɔwule ewule ɛhye a; ɔbɔle ye ɛbɛla, kɛmɔ Gyɛlɔbowam mɔɔ lumuale ɔ nyunlu la bɔle la. Ɔyɛle ɛtane na ɔmanle Yizilayɛma amuala yɛle bie.

english_verse: Everything else Zimri did while he was king, including his rebellion against Elah, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel. King Omri of Israel
translation_verse: Bɛhɛlɛ Zemelae nyɛleɛ mɔɔ ɔyɛle, nee ye kɔdiawu adwenle mɔɔ ɔbɔle la anwo edwɛkɛ wɔ Yizilayɛ Arelemgbunli Tetedwɛkɛ Buluku ne anu. Yizilayɛ Belemgbunli Ɔmelae

english_verse: After Zimri died, some of the Israelites wanted Tibni son of Ginath to be king, but others wanted Omri.
translation_verse: Nzinlii Yizilayɛma anu kpakyele nwiɔ. Ɛnee foa ko kulo kɛ bɛfa Tebenae mɔɔ le Gaenate ara ne bɛsie ebia ne, yɛɛ foa ko noko gyi Ɔmelae anzi.

english_verse: in the thirty-first year of Asa's rule in Judah. Omri ruled Israel for twelve years. The first six years he ruled from Tirzah,
translation_verse: Belemgbunli Esa dɛnlanle Dwuda ebia ne azo na ɔnyianle ɛvolɛ abulasa nee ko la yɛɛ Ɔmelae bɔle ɔ bo kɛ ɔsie Yizilayɛma a. Ɔlile ebia ne ɛvolɛ bulu nee nwiɔ; ɔlile nuhua ɛvolɛ nsia wɔ Tɛza.

english_verse: He acted just like Jeroboam and made the Lord God of Israel angry by causing the Israelites to sin and to worship idols.
translation_verse: Ɔboalekɛ Nibate ara Gyɛlɔbowam ɛbɛla ne mɔɔ ɔbɔle a ɔmanle Yizilayɛma yɛle ɛtane la bie yɛɛ ɔbɔle a. Ɔdoale awozonle ɛzonlenlɛ, ɔmanle Ɛdɛnkɛma, Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne vale ɔ nwo ɛya.

english_verse: Everything else Omri did while he was king, including his brave deeds, is written in The History of the Kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Bɛhɛlɛ Ɔmelae nyɛleɛ nee ye mɔdenle mɔɔ ɔbɔle la wɔ Yizilayɛ Arelemgbunli Tetedwɛkɛ Buluku ne anu.

english_verse: Omri died and was buried in Samaria, and his son Ahab became king. King Ahab of Israel
translation_verse: Ɔmelae hɔle ayile nu na bɛwulale ye mrɛlatɛlɛ nu wɔ Samɛlea, na ɔ ra Ehabe lile ebia ne. Yizilayɛ Belemgbunli Ehabe

english_verse: Ahab son of Omri became king of Israel in the thirty-eighth year of Asa's rule in Judah, and he ruled
translation_verse: Ɔmelae ara Ehabe kali Yizilayɛ belemgbunli la ɛnee Dwuda Belemgbunli Esa ɛli ɛvolɛ abulasa nee mɔtwɛ wɔ Dwuda ebia ne azo. Ɔmelae ara Ehabe lile ebia ne ɛvolɛ abulanwiɔ nee nwiɔ.

english_verse: Ahab did more things to disobey the Lord than any king before him.
translation_verse: Akee Ehabe ɛtane ɛdeɛ mɔɔ ɔyɛle la, bɛbɔ zolɛ a ɔmbɔ; ɔdɛlale arelemgbunli mɔɔ lumuale la kɔsɔɔti ɛtane ɛdeɛ ne mɔ.

english_verse: He acted just like Jeroboam. Even worse, he married Jezebel the daughter of King Ethbaal of Sidon and started worshiping Baal.
translation_verse: Ɔ nye liele Nibate ara Gyɛlɔbowam ɛbɛla ɛtane ne mɔ mɔɔ ɔbɔle ɔtiale Ɛdɛnkɛma la anwo na ɔvale ɔ gyakɛ. Ehabe hɔgyale Gyɛzɛbɛle mɔɔ le Saedɛn Belemgbunli Ɛtebeeyale ara raalɛ, na ɔhɔhotole bozonle Beeyale ɔzonlenle ye.

english_verse: Ahab built an altar and temple for Baal in Samaria
translation_verse: Ɔzile bozonle sua ɔmanle bozonle Beeyale na ɔzile azukponle wɔ nuhua ɔmanle bozonle ne wɔ Samɛlea.

english_verse: and set up a sacred pole for worshiping the goddess Asherah. Ahab did more to make the Lord God of Israel angry than any king of Israel before him.
translation_verse: Ehabe yɛle bozonle raalɛ Ahyela ne ananze ziele ye aze. Ɔhanle Ɛdɛnkɛma, Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne ɛya ɔdɛlale Yizilayɛ belemgbunli biala.

english_verse: While Ahab was king, a man from Bethel named Hiel rebuilt the town of Jericho. But while Hiel was laying the foundation for the town wall, his oldest son Abiram died. And while he was finishing the gates, his youngest son Segub died. This happened just as the Lord had told Joshua to say many years ago.
translation_verse: Ye mekɛ zo a Hayɛle mɔɔ vi Bɛtɛle la kyekyele suakpole Gyɛleko bieko a. Kɛmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma vale luale Dwɔhyua anwo zo hanle la, amgba Hayɛle vale ye belamunli ralɛ nrenya Abaelam wulale Gyɛleko sua ne abo, yɛɛ ɔ ra kazima ne, mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye Sigɛbe la a bɛvale bɛwulale sua ne anuhɔlɛ kpole ne abo a.

english_verse: Elijah was a prophet from Tishbe in Gilead. One day he went to King Ahab and said, “I'm a servant of the living Lord, the God of Israel. And I swear in his name that it won't rain until I say so. There won't even be any dew on the ground.”
translation_verse: Akee Yilaegya mɔɔ vi Tehyebi mɔɔ wɔ Geleade maanle nu la hanle hilele Ehabe kɛ, “Meka Ɛdɛnkɛma, Yizilayɛ tease Nyamenle ne mɔɔ mesonle ye la, kɛ ɛbɔlɛ anzɛɛ ezule ɛnrɛdɔ ɛvolɛ kɛyɛ nsa ye anu kɔkpula mekɛ mɔɔ menwɔye me nloa la.”

english_verse: Later, the Lord said to Elijah,
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Yilaegya kɛ,

english_verse: “Leave and go across the Jordan River so you can hide near Cherith Creek.
translation_verse: “Ye ɛ nwo ɛke kɔ aduduleɛ kɔvea azule Kilete mɔɔ la Azule Dwɔdan ne aduduleɛ lɔ la anloa.

english_verse: You can drink water from the creek, and eat the food I've told the ravens to bring you.”
translation_verse: Ɛbanlo azule ne bie; eza meyɛ ye kɛ ahɔhɔsɛlɛ ɛrɛlɛ wɔ aleɛ wɔ ɛkɛ.”

english_verse: Elijah obeyed the Lord and went to live near Cherith Creek.
translation_verse: Zɔhane ati ɔhɔyɛle mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma zele ye la: ɔhɔveale azule Kilete ne anloa wɔ Dwɔdan ne aduduleɛ lɔ,

english_verse: Ravens brought him bread and meat twice a day, and he drank water from the creek.
translation_verse: ɔnlonle azule ne bie, yɛɛ ahɔhɔsɛlɛ rɛlɛle ye aleɛ nee nane nwonlomɔ nee nɔsolɛ.

english_verse: But after a while, it dried up because there was no rain. Elijah Helps a Widow in Zarephath
translation_verse: Na kɛmɔ ɛnee ezule ɛndɔ la ati, yeandwu mekɛ biala yɛɛ azule ne sesanle a. Yilaegya nee Zalefate kunlanvolɛ raalɛ ne

english_verse: The Lord told Elijah,
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Yilaegya kɛ,

english_verse: “Go to the town of Zarephath in Sidon and live there. I've told a widow in that town to give you food.”
translation_verse: “Dwazo kɔ Zalefate mɔɔ wɔ Saedɛn maanzinli nu la kɔdɛnla ɛkɛ. Meyɛ ye kɛ kunlanvolɛ raalɛ bie mɔɔ de ɛkɛ ne maanle ne anu la ɛmaa wɔ aleɛ.”

english_verse: When Elijah came near the town gate of Zarephath, he saw a widow gathering sticks for a fire. “Would you please bring me a cup of water?” he asked.
translation_verse: Yemɔti ɔhɔle Zalefate. Ɔdwule sua ne kandiba la, ɔnwunle kunlanvolɛ raalɛ bie kɛ ɔlɛsesa ngeleka; ɔvɛlɛle ye na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Bɛlɛ me nzule ekyi maa meno.”

english_verse: As she left to get it, he asked, “Would you also please bring me a piece of bread?”
translation_verse: Raalɛ ne hakyile ɔ nwo mɔɔ ɔkɔ la, Yilaegya zele ye kɛ, “Anrɛɛ bɛlɛ me aleɛ ekyi noko.”

english_verse: The widow answered, “In the name of the living Lord your God, I swear that I don't have any bread. All I have is a handful of flour and a little olive oil. I'm on my way home now with these few sticks to cook what I have for my son and me. After that, we will starve to death.”
translation_verse: Raalɛ kunlanvolɛ ne buale ye kɛ, “Meka Ɛdɛnkɛma wɔ Nyamenle ne kɛ menlɛ kpanwo nretee zɛ wɔ ɛkɛ. Yeha me ɛdɔkɛ ekyi bie wɔ me kpule ne abo yɛɛ nwole ekyi wɔ toba bo. Yemɔ yɛɛ melɛkpondɛ nwolɛ ngeleka kɛyɛ nwiɔ meahɔwuda senle meado na me nee me ra nrenya ne yɛava yɛazɔ yɛ ɛbolɛ a. Saa yɛdi na ɔwie a ɛnee yɛze kɛ yɛ awieleɛ ne ala ɛne; ɛhɔne yɛɛ bahu yɛ a, ɔluakɛ ɛnee yɛnlɛ aleɛ bieko.”

english_verse: Elijah said, “Everything will be fine. Do what you said. Go home and fix something for you and your son. But first, please make a small piece of bread and bring it to me.
translation_verse: Yilaegya zele kunlanvolɛ raalɛ ne kɛ, “Mmadwenle nwolɛ. Wɔmɔ kɔnlea yɛ mɔɔ wɔha la. Noko akee dumua te ekyi doa tata maa me kolaa na wɔado ɛ nee ɛ ra nrenya ne bɛ ɛdeɛ ne.

english_verse: The Lord God of Israel has promised that your jar of flour won't run out and your bottle of oil won't dry up before he sends rain for the crops.”
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma, Yizilayɛ Nyamenle ne se, ‘Ɛdɔkɛ ne abo ɛnrɛdu kpule ne abo, yɛɛ nwole ne ɛnrɛwie toba ne abo ɛlɛ, kɔkpula mekɛ mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛmaa ezule kɛdɔ bieko kɛgua azɛlɛ ye azo la.’ ”

english_verse: The widow went home and did exactly what Elijah had told her. She and Elijah and her family had enough food for a long time.
translation_verse: Kunlanvolɛ raalɛ ne hɔyɛle ye kɛmɔ Yilaegya hilele ye la, na ɔdaye nee Yilaegya nee ye sua nu amra nyianle aleɛ lile dahuu.

english_verse: The Lord kept the promise that his prophet Elijah had made, and she did not run out of flour or oil. Elijah Brings a Boy Back to Life
translation_verse: Ɛdɔkɛ ne anwie kpule ne anu, yɛɛ nwole ne noko abo andu toba ne abo, kɛmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma luale Yilaegya anwo zo hanle la.

english_verse: Several days later, the son of the woman who owned the house got sick, and he kept getting worse, until finally he died.
translation_verse: Ɛhye anzi kunlanvolɛ raalɛ ne, mɔɔ le awuke menle ne, ara nrenya ne anwo dole ye. Anwondolɛ ne hakyile anwonyane kpole, na nzinlii ɔwule.

english_verse: The woman shouted at Elijah, “What have I done to you? I thought you were God's prophet. Did you come here to cause the death of my son as a reminder that I've sinned against God?”
translation_verse: Raalɛ ne hanle hilele Yilaegya kɛ, “Nyamenle sonla, duzu edwɛkɛ a le ɛhye? Medwenle kɛ ɛrale ɛke kɛ ɛfa saleɛ wɔarɛlɛ me; amuanrɛɛ ɛrale kɛ ɛbaza me ɛtane ne mɔ wɔagua zolɛ na wɔamaa me ra ye awu.”

english_verse: “Bring me your son,” Elijah said. Then he took the boy from her arms and carried him upstairs to the room where he was staying. Elijah laid the boy on his bed
translation_verse: Yilaegya zele raalɛ ne kɛ, “Fa kakula ne maa me.” Ɔliele kakula ne mɔɔ ɛnee la raalɛ ne asa azo la. Ɔvale ye ɔvole ɛbolɔnsam ne azo na ɔ nee ye hɔle ɛleka mɔɔ ɔdaye Yilaegya ɔda la ɔhɔdole ye wɔ ye mgba ne azo.

english_verse: and prayed, “Lord God, why did you do such a terrible thing to this woman? She's letting me stay here, and now you've let her son die.”
translation_verse: Akee ɔmanle ɔ ne zo ɔzɛlɛle kɛ, “O Ɛdɛnkɛma, me Nyamenle, duzu munzule a akee wɔmaa yerado raalɛ ye mɔɔ merazokoɛ ye la na wɔmaa ɔ ra nrenya ye ɛwu a?”

english_verse: Elijah stretched himself out over the boy three times, while praying, “Lord God, bring this boy back to life!”
translation_verse: Yilaegya zanle ɔ nwo fɔɔnwo wɔ kakula ne anwo zo fane nsa na ɔzɛlɛle kɛ, “O Ɛdɛnkɛma, me Nyamenle, maa kakula ye ɛrɛla ngoane nu bieko.”

english_verse: The Lord answered Elijah's prayer, and the boy started breathing again.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma diele Yilaegya nzɛlɛlɛ, kakula ne liele ɛnwomenle na ɔdwazole.

english_verse: Elijah picked him up and carried him downstairs. He gave the boy to his mother and said, “Look, your son is alive.”
translation_verse: Ɔvale kakula ne ɔdwule aze ɔrɛlɛle ɔ nli na ɔzele kɛ, “Ɔmɔ, nea, ɛ ra ne ɛde kpɔkɛ!”

english_verse: “You are God's prophet!” the woman replied. “Now I know that you really do speak for the Lord.”
translation_verse: Raalɛ ne hanle hilele Yilaegya kɛ, “Kɛkala menwu kɛ ɛle Nyamenle sonla, na Ɛdɛnkɛma dua ɛ nwo zo tendɛ.”

english_verse: For three years no rain fell in Samaria, and there was almost nothing to eat anywhere. The Lord said to Elijah, “Go and meet with King Ahab. I will soon make it rain.” So Elijah went to see Ahab.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Yilaegya zile nu hɔle kɛ ɔlɛ ɔ nwo ɔkahile Ehabe. Mekɛ ne anu ɛnee Samɛlea ɛhɔne ɛdeɛ ne akee anu ɛyɛ se kpole kpalɛ.

english_verse: At that time Obadiah was in charge of Ahab's palace, but he faithfully worshiped the Lord. In fact, when Jezebel was trying to kill the Lord's prophets, Obadiah hid
translation_verse: Mekɛ mɔɔ Gyɛzɛbɛle kuhu Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛma ne mɔ la, Obadaya liele bɛ nuhua ɛya ko ngoane. Ɔvale bɛ abulanlu abulanlu ɔveɛveale awolɛ mbɔne nu na ɔmanle bɛ aleɛ nee nzule.)

english_verse: and said, “We have to find something for our horses and mules to eat. If we don't, we will have to kill them. Let's look around every creek and spring in the country for some grass.
translation_verse: Ehabe zele Obadaya kɛ, “Kɔkpɔsa azudenle ne mɔ nee mbɔnza mɔɔ wɔ maanle ye la anu kɛ yɛkɛnyia nya nya bie yɛkɛmaa yɛ mgbɔnwɔ nee yɛ mgbɔnwɔndua ne mɔ na bɛanwu.”

english_verse: You go one way, and I'll go the other.” Then they left in separate directions.
translation_verse: Ɔlua zo bɛlile mgbakyelɛ nu; Ehabe vale ɛleka ko yɛɛ Obadaya ɔdaye ɔbɔle ɔ ti ɛleka fofolɛ.

english_verse: As Obadiah was walking along, he met Elijah. Obadiah recognized him, bowed down, and asked, “Elijah, is it really you?”
translation_verse: Obadaya dɔle adenle zo la ɔrayiale Yilaegya; ɔnwunle ye sonla holɛ, yemɔti ɔhotole ye na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Me menle Yilaegya, wɔmɔ ɛ?”

english_verse: Obadiah replied: King Ahab would kill me if I told him that. And I haven't even done anything wrong.
translation_verse: Obadaya buale ye kɛ, “Duzu ɛtane a meyɛ, mɔɔ yemɔti ɛye me wɔamaa Ehabe ahu me a?

english_verse: I swear to you in the name of the living Lord your God that the king has looked everywhere for you. He sent people to look in every country, and when they couldn't find you, he made the leader of each country swear that you were not in that country.
translation_verse: Meka Ɛdɛnkɛma wɔ Nyamenle ne kɛ, mennwu maanle ko nee sua biala mɔɔ Ehabe ɛtɛsoanle menli wɔ zolɛ kɛ bɛhɔkpondɛ wɔ a. Saa menli mɔɔ kɛhɔ wɔ ɛkpondɛlɛ la kɔto belemgbunli biala na ɔka kɛ ɛnle ɛkɛ a, Ehabe maa belemgbunli ne ka ye maanle ne anu ndane kɛ amgba ɔ nye ambɔ ɛ nwo zo fee.

english_verse: Do you really want me to tell him you're here?
translation_verse: Kɛkala, ɛlɛsoa me kɛ mengɔnga mengile me menle Ehabe kɛ, ‘Yilaegya ɛra’.

english_verse: What if the Lord's Spirit takes you away as soon as I leave? When Ahab comes to get you, he won't find you. Then he will surely kill me. I have worshiped the Lord since I was a boy.
translation_verse: Kɛ metu me bo la ɛnee Nyamenle Sunsum ne ɛye wɔ ɛvi ɛke ɛhɔ ɛleka mɔɔ menze a. Ehabe ba badwu ɛke na ɛnle ɛke a, ɔbahu me. Kakye kɛ ɔvi me ngakula nu, mezonle Ɛdɛnkɛma dedee a yeradwu ɛnɛ a.

english_verse: Elijah said, “I'm a servant of the living Lord All-Powerful, and I swear in his name that I will meet with Ahab today.”
translation_verse: Yilaegya buale ye kɛ, “Meka tease Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma mɔɔ megyi ɔ nyunlu ɛke la kɛ, megyinla me gyakɛ anu ɛke; Ehabe banwu me ɛnɛ kenle ko ye.”

english_verse: Obadiah left and told Ahab where to find Elijah. Ahab went to meet Elijah,
translation_verse: Zɔhane ati Obadaya hɔhanle hilele Ehabe na Ehabe hɔle kɛ ɔkayia Yilaegya.

english_verse: and when he saw him, Ahab shouted, “There you are, the biggest troublemaker in Israel!”
translation_verse: Ehabe anye bobɔle Yilaegya ala la, ɔbizale ye kɛ, “Ɛnee ɛdawɔ Yilaegya, mɔɔ wɔgyegye Yizilayɛ maanle ye kpole la ɛhye ɔ?”

english_verse: Elijah answered: You're the troublemaker—not me! You and your family have disobeyed the Lord's commands by worshiping Baal.
translation_verse: Yilaegya buale kɛ, “Tɛ mame a megyegye Yizilayɛma a. Wɔmɔ, nee ɛ ze sua nu amra a ɛgyegye Yizilayɛma a. Ɔluakɛ bɛzie Nyamenle mɛla ne ahane na bɛhɔli awozonle Beeyale ne mɔ anzi.

english_verse: Ahab got everyone together, then they went to meet Elijah on Mount Carmel.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Ehabe vɛlɛle Yizilayɛma nee ahɔmenle ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti manle bɛrayiale Kamɛle Boka ne azo.

english_verse: Elijah stood in front of them and said, “How much longer will you try to have things both ways? If the Lord is God, worship him! But if Baal is God, worship him!” The people did not say a word.
translation_verse: Yilaegya rale ɛlɔne ne amuala anyunlu na ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Duzu ati a bɛ adwenle ɛngya na bɛyɛ bɛ adwenle nwiɔ nwiɔ ɛ? Saa Ɛdɛnkɛma a le Nyamenle a, bɛdoa ye; na saa bɛkɛzonle bozonle Beeyale noko a, ɛnee bɛdoa ye.” Na menli ne mɔ ampili ye.

english_verse: Bring us two bulls. Baal's prophets can take one of them, kill it, and cut it into pieces. Then they can put the meat on the wood without lighting the fire. I will do the same thing with the other bull, and I won't light a fire under it either.
translation_verse: Bɛmaa yɛ nlankɛ nyinli nwiɔ na bɛmaa bozonle Beeyale ahɔmenle ne mɔ ɛva ko ɛpepɛ ɛgua ɛyɛzinli mɔɔ bɛkpula la azo. Bɛmmafa senle bɛgua nu. Medame noko mebabia ɛnlankɛ ko ne na meagua ye ɛyɛzinli mɔɔ bɛkpula la azo; menrɛdo senle nu.

english_verse: The prophets of Baal will pray to their god, and I will pray to the Lord. The one who answers by starting the fire is God. “That's a good idea,” everyone agreed.
translation_verse: Saa yɛyɛ ɛhye na ɔwie a akee bɛvɛlɛ bɛ nyamenle ne, na medame mebavɛlɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma me Nyamenle ne, na Nyamenle ne mɔɔ kɛrazɔ senle kɛyela nane ne la, yemɔ a le Nyamenle a.” Menli ne kɔsɔɔti zulole zolɛ kɛ “Ɛhɛe, yɛdie yɛto nuhua. Ɔdaye ne ala ɛne”

english_verse: Elijah said to Baal's prophets, “There are more of you, so you go first. Pick out a bull and get it ready, but don't light the fire. Then pray to your god.”
translation_verse: Yilaegya zele Beeyale ahɔmenle ne mɔ kɛ, “Bɛlumua bɛva nlankɛ ne mɔ ko na bɛbia ye, ɔluakɛ bɛmɛ a bɛ nwo zonle a. Bɛmmafa senle bɛgua bɛ ɛyɛzinli ne mɔɔ bɛhua la anu. Bɛzɛlɛ bɛ nyamenle ne bɛmaa ɔdo senle nu.”

english_verse: They chose their bull, then they got it ready and prayed to Baal all morning, asking him to start the fire. They danced around the altar and shouted, “Answer us, Baal!” But there was no answer.
translation_verse: Bɛvale bɛ ɛnlankɛ ne, bɛwiele ye bia, na bɛguale ye azukponle ne azo; bɛzɛlɛle bozonle Beeyale ne sumunli nwonlomɔ dedee ɔhɔkpulale sɛnzɛngyinla. Bɛvɛlɛle ye kɛ, “O Beeyale, tie yɛ ɛ!” Na bɛande ɛnelɛ biala, yɛɛ awie biala anzulo zolɛ. Bɛwuluwulule bɛbɔle azukponle ne anwo mgbɔlɔka, noko awie ambua bɛ.

english_verse: At noon, Elijah began making fun of them. “Pray louder!” he said. “Baal must be a god. Maybe he's daydreaming or using the toilet or traveling somewhere. Or maybe he's asleep, and you have to wake him up.”
translation_verse: Ɔdwule sɛnzɛngyinla la, Yilaegya golole bɛ nwo kɛ, “Bɛdea bɛvɛlɛ ye kpalɛ! Se ɔle nyamenle o! Ɔkɛyɛ kɛ ɔlɛdwenle anzɛɛ ɔlɛsɔho ɔ gyakɛ, anzɛɛ yedu adenle. Bie noko a ɛnee nafelɛ a ɛva ye kpole a, yemɔti ɔwɔ kɛ bɛtunwue ye.”

english_verse: The prophets kept shouting louder and louder, and they cut themselves with swords and knives until they were bleeding. This was the way they worshiped,
translation_verse: Amgba noko ahɔmenle ne mɔ deɛdeanle nuhua kpalɛ; bɛvale dadeɛ nee ɛtweneɛ bɛbodɛbodale bɛ nwo, kɛmɔ bɛ maamɛla ne se la, bɛmanle bɛ nwo amuala yɛle mogya ngome takaa zɛhae.

english_verse: and they kept it up until time for the evening sacrifice. But there was no answer of any kind.
translation_verse: Sɛnzɛne ne kpalile la, bɛdeɛdeanle nuhua mgbole mgbole bie, noko bɛanyia mualɛ, bɛande nganeɛ yɛɛ awie ampili bɛ toonwo kɛyɛ sɛnzɛngyinla nee aledwolɛ muleɛ nu.

english_verse: Elijah told everyone to gather around him while he repaired the Lord's altar.
translation_verse: Akee Yilaegya zele ɛlɔne ne amuala kɛ, “Bɛbikye me nwo ɛke.” Menli ne bikyele ye. Ɔyɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma azukponle ne mɔɔ bɛzɛkyele ye la boɛ.

english_verse: He placed the wood on the altar, then they cut the bull into pieces and laid the meat on the wood. He told the people, “Fill four large jars with water and pour it over the meat and the wood.” After they did this,
translation_verse: Ɔhanle ɛyɛzinli ne mɔ ɔkpulale nwolɛ wɔ azukponle ne azo na ɔpepɛle nane ne ɔguale ɛyɛne ne azo. Na ɔzele menli ne kɛ, “Bɛsesa nzule mbuakɛ nna tetɛkɛɛ bɛgua ɛyɛne ne nee nane ne mɔɔ bɛbayela la azo.”

english_verse: until finally, the water ran down the altar and filled the ditch.
translation_verse: Nzule ne akee bule ɛyɛzinli ne abo na ɔdenrɛle ɔhɔguale kuma ne anu ɔyile ye tɛkɛɛ.

english_verse: When it was time for the evening sacrifice, Elijah prayed: Our Lord, you are the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel. Now, prove that you are the God of this nation, and that I, your servant, have done this at your command.
translation_verse: Ɔdwule mekɛ mɔɔ bɛfa bɛyɛ ewiazo nzɛlɛlɛ la, Yilaegya rale azukponle ne anwo na ɔzɛlɛle kɛ, “O Ɛdɛnkɛma, Ebileham, Ayezeke nee Yizilayɛ Nyamenle, maa bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛyia ɛke la ɛnwu ye ɛnɛ kenle ye kɛ wɔmɔ a ɛle Nyamenle wɔ Yizilayɛ a, yɛɛ wɔ sonvolɛ a le me, yɛɛ ɛdawɔ a wɔzoa me kɛ menyɛ ninyɛne ɛhye mɔ a.

english_verse: Please answer me, so these people will know that you are the Lord God, and that you will turn their hearts back to you.
translation_verse: Bua me, O Ɛdɛnkɛma! Bua me, maa menli mɔɔ ɛyia ɛke la ɛnwu kɛ wɔmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma a ɛle Nyamenle a, na ɛkulo kɛ ɛ nee bɛ sia ba sua nu.”

english_verse: The Lord immediately sent fire, and it burned up the sacrifice, the wood, and the stones. It scorched the ground everywhere around the altar and dried up every drop of water in the ditch.
translation_verse: Na ɛkɛ ne ala Ɛdɛnkɛma manle senle vi anwuma radɔle azubɔdeɛ ne anu yelale nane ne, ɛyɛne ne, awolɛ ne mɔ nee azɛlɛ ne manle nzule ne mɔɔ gyi kuma ne anu la sesanle bɔkɔɔ.

english_verse: When the crowd saw what had happened, they all bowed down and shouted, “The Lord is God! The Lord is God!”
translation_verse: Menli ne amuala nwunle ɛhye la bɛbutubutule na bɛzele kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma, yemɔ a ɔle Nyamenle a; Ɛdɛnkɛma, yemɔ a ɔle Nyamenle a.”

english_verse: Just then, Elijah said, “Grab the prophets of Baal! Don't let any of them get away.” So the people captured the prophets and took them to Kishon River, where Elijah killed every one of them. It Starts To Rain
translation_verse: Akee Yilaegya zele kɛ, “Bɛhye bozonle Beeyale ahɔmenle ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti, bɛmmamaa ko bɔbɔ fi ɛsalɛ.” Bɛnwinwinle bɛ ɛkɛ ne na Yilaegya vale bɛ rale azule Kaehyɔn ne anloa, na ɔhunle bɛ muala. Ɛdɛnkɛma maa ezule adɔ

english_verse: Elijah told Ahab, “Get something to eat and drink. I hear a heavy rain coming.”
translation_verse: Akee Yilaegya zele Ehabe kɛ, “Kɔli na no, ɔboalekɛ mede nganeɛ mɔɔ kile kɛ ezule ɛlɛba aradɔ a.”

english_verse: Ahab left, but Elijah climbed back to the top of Mount Carmel. Then he stooped down with his face almost to the ground
translation_verse: Yemɔti Ehabe hɔle kɛ ɔkali debie. Yilaegya vole hɔle Kamɛle Boka ne azo, ɔkponle ɔ nwo na ɔvale ɔ ti ɔzianle ɔ gyakɛ avinli.

english_verse: and said to his servant, “Look toward the sea.” The servant left. And when he came back, he said, “I looked, but I didn't see anything.” Elijah told him to look seven more times.
translation_verse: Akee ɔzele ye sonvolɛ ne kɛ, “Kɔ ɛ nyunlu na to ɛ nye nyevile nu.” Sonvolɛ ne hɔle na ɔrahanle kɛ, “Mennwu debie wɔ nehane.” Yilaegya zele ye kɛ, “Kɔ zɔhane fane nsuu.”

english_verse: After the seventh time the servant replied, “I see a small cloud coming this way. But it's no bigger than a fist.” Elijah told him, “Tell Ahab to get his chariot ready and start home now. Otherwise, the rain will stop him.”
translation_verse: Na sonvolɛ ne hɔle mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ fane nsuu ne la, ɔrahanle ɔhilele Yilaegya kɛ, “Menwu amungu ekyi bie mɔɔ ye kpole le kɛ sonla sa taakɛ la kɛ ɔlɛmaa ɔ nwo zo wɔ nyevile nu lɔ.” Yilaegya zele ye sonvolɛ ne kɛ, “Ka ɛ nwo kɔze Belemgbunli Ehabe kɛ, ɔziezie ye konle ehwili ne mɔɔ ɔtɛnla nu la na ɔmaa ɔ nwo ɛyɛ ndɛ ɔhɔ sua nu na anrɛɛ ezule kɛbo ye.”

english_verse: Ahab told his wife Jezebel what Elijah had done and that he had killed the prophets.
translation_verse: Belemgbunli Ehabe hanle nyɛleɛ mɔɔ Yilaegya yɛle la amuala hilele Gyɛzɛbɛle, nee kɛ ɔzile ɔhunle ahɔmenle ne mɔ la.

english_verse: She sent a message to Elijah: “You killed my prophets. Now I'm going to kill you! I pray that the gods will punish me even more severely if I don't do it by this time tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Ɛhye ati Gyɛzɛbɛle zoanle manle bɛhɔhanle bɛhilele Yilaegya kɛ, “Ɛhunlɛ mɔɔ wɔhu ahɔmenle ne mɔ la, saa ɛhyema bekezɛ ɛnee metɛkunle ɛdawɔ noko a awozonle ne mɔ ɛdua me kakɛ ɛgua me bie zo.”

english_verse: Elijah was afraid when he got her message, and he ran to the town of Beersheba in Judah. He left his servant there,
translation_verse: Na ɛzulolɛ hanle Yilaegya manle ɔ nee ye sonvolɛ ne bɛnriandile bɛhɔle Biyɛhyiba mɔɔ wɔ Dwuda la. Ɔgyakyile ye sonvolɛ ne wɔ Biyɛhyiba

english_verse: then walked another whole day into the desert. Finally, he came to a large bush and sat down in its shade. He begged the Lord, “I've had enough. Just let me die! I'm no better off than my ancestors.”
translation_verse: na ɔdiale kenle ko adenle ɔhɔle fienemgbole ne anu lɔ, ɔhɔdɛnlanle baka bie abo na ɔzɛlɛle kɛ, “O Ɛdɛnkɛma, akee yeyɛ boɛ. Maa menwu na menle kpalɛ mendɛla egya mɔ.”

english_verse: Then he lay down in the shade and fell asleep. Suddenly an angel woke him up and said, “Get up and eat.”
translation_verse: Ɔhale baka ne abo ɔlafele; Nyamenle soanvolɛ radunwuele ye na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Dwazo na di debie.”

english_verse: Elijah looked around, and by his head was a jar of water and some baked bread. He sat up, ate and drank, then lay down and went back to sleep.
translation_verse: Ɔmanle ɔ ti zo la ɔnwunle kɛ tata nee nzule dwora ko gyi ɔ ti sɔlɔ ɛkɛ. Ɔlile debie, ɔnlonle nzule ne na ɔdole ɔ ti ɛkɛ ne ɔlafele bieko.

english_verse: So Elijah sat up and ate and drank. The food and water made him strong enough to walk
translation_verse: Yemɔti Yilaegya dwazole, ɔlile debie na ɔnlonle nzule; aleɛ zɔhane manle ye anwosesebɛ manle ɔdiale nɔɔzo nee ewiazo kenle abulanla ɔhɔdwule Nyamenle Boka ne mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye Saenae la azo,

english_verse: and he spent the night there in a cave. The Lord Appears to Elijah While Elijah was on Mount Sinai, the Lord asked, “Elijah, why are you here?”
translation_verse: na ɔhɔveale bolɛ bɔne bie anu ɔlale. Arɛlevilɛ nu ala Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle na ɔbizale Yilaegya kɛ, “Yilaegya, duzu yɛɛ ɛyɛ ye ɛke a?”

english_verse: He answered, “Lord God All-Powerful, I've always done my best to obey you. But your people have broken their solemn promise to you. They have torn down your altars and killed all your prophets, except me. And now they are even trying to kill me!”
translation_verse: Ɔbuale kɛ, “Melɛtwe ɛdawɔ Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle ɛ ti nungule, ɔluakɛ Yizilayɛma ɛgyakyi wɔ edwɛkɛ ne anzi ɛlilɛ, bɛbubu wɔ azukponle ne mɔ, na bɛhu wɔ kpɔmanvolɛma ne mɔ amuala; me ngomekye ala yɛɛ meha a, yɛɛ eza bɛlɛkpondɛ medame noko bɛahu me.”

english_verse: “Go out and stand on the mountain,” the Lord replied. “I want you to be there when I pass by.” All at once, a strong wind shook the mountain and shattered the rocks. But the Lord was not in the wind. Next, there was an earthquake, but the Lord was not in the earthquake.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Yilaegya kɛ, “Finde bagyinla me nyunlu wɔ boka ne azo.” Ɛdɛnkɛma akee razenle ɛkɛ, na anwoma bɔle na ahumu dule kpole bie manle awolɛ kpukekpukele, noko ɛnee Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛnle anwoma ne anu; ahumu ne anzi, azɛlɛ kpusule, noko ɛnee Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛnle azɛlɛkpusulɛ ne anu.

english_verse: Then there was a fire, but the Lord was not in the fire. Finally, there was a gentle breeze,
translation_verse: Senle vindele azɛlɛ ɛkpusulɛ ne anzi, Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛnle senle ne anu. Na senle ne anzi akee ɛnelɛ nretee bie dendɛle.

english_verse: and when Elijah heard it, he covered his face with his coat. He went out and stood at the entrance to the cave. A voice asked, “Elijah, why are you here?”
translation_verse: Yilaegya dele ɛnelɛ ne la ɔvale ye aguzo ne ɔkyikyile ɔ nyunlu, na ɔhɔgyinlanle bɔne ne anloa. Ɔdele kɛ ɛnelɛ bie ɛlɛtendɛ ahile ye kɛ, “Yilaegya, duzu yɛɛ ɛyɛ ye ɛke a?”

english_verse: Elijah answered, “Lord God All-Powerful, I've always done my best to obey you. But your people have broken their solemn promise to you. They have torn down your altars and killed all your prophets, except me. And now they are even trying to kill me!”
translation_verse: Yilaegya buale kɛ, “Melɛtwe ɛdawɔ Tumivolɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle ɛ ti nungule, ɔluakɛ Yizilayɛma ɛkpo wɔ ngyekyeleɛ ne, bɛbubu wɔ azukponle ne mɔ na bɛhu wɔ kpɔmanvolɛma ne mɔ amuala; me ngomekye ala a meha a, yɛɛ eza bɛkpondɛ medame noko bɛahu me.”

english_verse: The Lord said: Elijah, you can go back to the desert near Damascus. And when you get there, appoint Hazael to be king of Syria.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele ye kɛ, “Sia ɛ nzi kɔ Dɛmasekɛse fienemgbole ne anu lɔ, kɔkpokpa Hazeeyɛle nwole kɛ yemɔ a ɔbali belemgbunli wɔ Selea a.

english_verse: Then appoint Jehu son of Nimshi to be king of Israel, and Elisha son of Shaphat to take your place as my prophet.
translation_verse: Kpokpa Gyihu, Nemehyae ara nrenya ne noko nwole kɛ ɔbali Yizilayɛ belemgbunli, na kpokpa Hyeefate mɔɔ vi Ebɛle Mɛhola la ara nrenya Yilaehya ɔdaye nwole maa ɔyɛ Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ ɔli wɔ agya.

english_verse: Hazael will start killing the people who worship Baal. Jehu will kill those who escape from Hazael, and Elisha will kill those who escape from Jehu.
translation_verse: Awie biala mɔɔ kɛnriandi kɛvi Hazeeyɛle abo la Gyihu bahu ye, mɔɔ kɛnriandi kɛvi Gyihu abo la Yilaehya bahu ye;

english_verse: Elijah left and found Elisha plowing a field with a pair of oxen. There were eleven other men in front of him, and each one was also plowing with a pair of oxen. Elijah went over and put his own coat on Elisha.
translation_verse: Yilaegya vi ɛkɛ ne la ɔhɔnwunle Hyeefate ara Yilaehya kɛ ɔlɛso ɛya. Ɔlɛ nlankɛ ekpunli ekpunli bulu nee nwiɔ mɔɔ ngyela mbaka gyelegyela bɛ la kɛ bɛlɛwuduwudu azɛlɛ ne, na ɔdaye mumua ne ɔdoa nlankɛ ekpunli ne mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ bulu nee nwiɔ la. Yilaegya yɛle kɛ ɔse ɔ nwo la na ɔdole ye aguzo ne ɔguale Yilaehya anwo zo,

english_verse: Elisha stopped plowing and ran after him. “Let me kiss my parents goodbye, then I'll go with you,” he said. “You can go,” Elijah said. “But remember what I've done for you.”
translation_verse: na Yilaehya gyakyile ye nlankɛ ne mɔ ɛkɛ na ɔnriandile ɔdoale Yilaegya ɔhanle ɔhilele ye kɛ, “Maa mengɔngɛla ɔmɔ nee egya na mearadoa wɔ.” Yilaegya buale ye kɛ, “Sia ɛ nzi ɛ. Mensisi ɛ nwo zo.”

english_verse: Elisha left and took his oxen with him. He killed them and boiled them over a fire he had made with the wood from his plow. He gave the meat to the people who were with him, and they ate it. Then he left with Elijah and became his assistant.
translation_verse: Yilaehya ziale na ɔrahunle ye nlankɛ ne mɔ na ɔvale ngyela mbaka ne mɔ ɔyɛle ɛyɛne ɔdonle nlankɛ ne mɔ ɔmanle menli ne lile. Akee ɔvile ɛkɛ na ɔhɔdoale Yilaegya kɛ ye boavolɛ.

english_verse: They dressed in sackcloth and put ropes on their heads, then they went to Ahab and said, “Your servant Benhadad asks you to let him live.” “Is he still alive?” Ahab asked. “Benhadad is like a brother to me.”
translation_verse: Yemɔti bɛhedale ɛrele, bɛbɔle file bɛguale bɛ kɔme. Akee bɛhɔhanle bɛhilele Yizilayɛ belemgbunli ne kɛ, “Wɔ akɛlɛ Bɛneheedade se ɔkpa wɔ kyɛlɛ na ɛmmaku ye.” Ehabe bizale kɛ, “Bɛneheedade tɛte aze ɔ? Ɔle me diema!”

english_verse: Benhadad sent a messenger to tell King Ahab of Israel,
translation_verse: Ɔzoanle menli wɔ Samɛlea kɛ bɛhɔha bɛhile Yizilayɛ Belemgbunli Ehabe kɛ, “Medame Bɛneheedade, mese,

english_verse: Later, Benhadad sent another messenger to say to Ahab, “I already told you to give me your silver and gold, your wives, and your children.
translation_verse: Soanvolɛma ne mɔ ziale razele Yizilayɛ belemgbunli ne kɛ, “Bɛneheedade se, ‘Menzoanle menli memanle bɛrazele wɔ kɛ ɛye wɔ dwɛtɛ fufule, wɔ ezukoa nvutuke, wɔ mraalɛ ngɛnlɛma ne mɔ nee ɛ mra ɛrɛlɛ me.’

english_verse: But tomorrow at this time, I will send my officials into your city to search your palace and the houses of your officials. They will take everything else that you own.”
translation_verse: Noko akee ɛhyema, kɛyɛ bekezɛ, mebazoa me sonvolɛma meamaa bɛaranleɛnlea wɔ sua nu nee wɔ mgbanyima ne mɔ azua nu, na debie biala mɔɔ bɛ sa kɛdɔ zolɛ na bɛnea a ɔhyia la bɛava bɛarɛlɛ me.”

english_verse: “Don't listen to him!” they answered. “You don't have to do what he says.”
translation_verse: Ye mgbanyima ne mɔ nee ye ezuavolɛ ne amuala zele ye kɛ, “Mmapili ye bɔbɔ na ɔ nwo ayɛ ye fɛ. Mmakponle!”

english_verse: So Ahab sent someone to tell Benhadad, “Your Majesty, I'll give you my silver and gold, and even my wives and children. But I won't let you have anything else.” When Benhadad got his answer,
translation_verse: Yemɔti ɔhanle ɔhilele Belemgbunli Bɛneheedade soanvolɛma ne kɛ, “Bɛhɔha bɛhile Nana, me belemgbunli ne kɛ, medie mɔɔ ɔlumuale ɔbizale la meto nu na nzinlii ɛdeɛ mɔɔ ɔlɛbiza la, ɔnrɛnyia ye.” Bɛneheedade soanvolɛma ne ziale hɔbɔle ye amaneɛ na bɛziale bɛrahanle bɛhilele Yizilayɛ belemgbunli ne kɛ,

english_verse: he replied, “I'll completely destroy Samaria! There won't even be enough of it left for my soldiers to carry back in their hands. If I don't do it, I pray that the gods will punish me terribly.”
translation_verse: “Bɛneheedade se, ‘Saa me nee wɔ anli, meanva menli meammaa bɛambanzɛkye Samɛlea a, awozonle mɔɔ wɔ me maanle ye anu la ɛdua me kakɛ ɛgua me bie zo.’ ”

english_verse: Ahab then answered, “Benhadad, don't brag before the fighting even begins. Wait and see if you live through it.”
translation_verse: Yizilayɛ belemgbunli ne buale kɛ, “Bɛhɔze Bɛneheedade kɛ ɔho konle ne na ɔwie a yeadu ɔ nloa anu.”

english_verse: Meanwhile, Benhadad and the other kings had been drinking in their tents. But when Ahab's reply came, he ordered his soldiers to prepare to attack Samaria, and they all got ready.
translation_verse: Mekɛ ne anu ɛnee Bɛneheedade nee ye arelemgbunli ne mɔ ɛlɛno nza wɔ avanye. Ɔdele nrɛlaleɛ ne la ɔhanle ɔhilele ye ɛlɔnema ne kɛ, “Awie biala ɛzia ɛhɔ ye ɛlɔne nu na bɛhɔva suakpole ne.”

english_verse: At that very moment, a prophet ran up to Ahab and said, “You can see that Benhadad's army is very strong. But the Lord has promised to help you defeat them today. Then you will know that the Lord is in control.”
translation_verse: Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ bie rale Ehabe anwo ɛkɛ ne razele ye kɛ, “Ehabe, kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma se la ɛne, ‘Wɔnwu ɛlɔne pinopino ɛhye ɔ? Mebaye bɛ meamaa wɔ ɛnɛ kenle ye, amaa wɔalie wɔado nuhua kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a.’ ”

english_verse: “Who will fight the battle?” Ahab asked. The prophet answered, “The young bodyguards who serve the district officials.” “But who will lead them into battle?” Ahab asked. “You will!” the prophet replied.
translation_verse: Ehabe bizale ye kɛ, “ Ɛnee nwane mɔ a di bɛ ti ahɔho ali konim ne a?” Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ ne buale kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma se, ‘Mgbavolɛ mɔɔ wɔ maanzinli ne mɔ safohyenle mgbanyinli ne mɔ abo la a baho ali konim ne a.’ ” Eza Ehabe bizale kɛ, “Nwane a le safohyenle kpanyinli mɔɔ balumua ado etu a?” Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ ne buale kɛ, “Ɛdawɔ ɔ.”

english_verse: At noon, King Ahab and his Israelite army marched out of Samaria, with the young soldiers in front. King Benhadad of Syria and the
translation_verse: Mgbavolɛ mɔɔ wɔ maanzinli ne mɔ safohyenle mgbanyinli ne mɔ abo la lumuale vindele. Bɛneheedade zoanle menli kɛ bɛhɔkpɔla adenle zo na ye menli mɔɔ ɔzoanle bɛ la ziale rahanle hilele ye kɛ, “Nana, ɛlɔne ɛkpuke Samɛlea ɛlɛba.”

english_verse: “Take them alive!” Benhadad ordered. “I don't care if they have come out to fight or to surrender.”
translation_verse: Na ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Saa bɛlɛba ye anzonudwolɛ nu o, bɛlɛba ye konle zo o, bɛhye bɛ anyewɔzo.”

english_verse: The young soldiers led Israel's troops into battle,
translation_verse: Maanzinli ne mɔ anu mgbavolɛ ɛlɔnema ne bɔle konle ne abo na Yizilayɛma rabokale bɛ.

english_verse: and each of them attacked and killed an enemy soldier. The rest of the Syrian army turned and ran, and the Israelites went after them. Benhadad and some others escaped on horses,
translation_verse: Biala hunle ye Selea sonla ɛdeɛ ne mɔɔ ɔ nee ye bɔle ye zo la. Seleama ne mɔ angola nuhua sɔ na bɛnriandile. Yizilayɛma voanle bɛ. Bɛneheedade dɛnlanle ye ɛkpɔnwɔ zo ɔ nee ɛkpɔnwɔ zo tɛnlavolɛma ne bie mɔ nriandile.

english_verse: but Ahab and his soldiers followed them and captured their horses and chariots. Ahab and Israel's army crushed the Syrians.
translation_verse: Yizilayɛ Belemgbunli Ehabe voanle bɛ ndinlizo, ɔhyele mgbɔnwɔ nee konle ehwili ne bie mɔ ɔzɛkyele bɛ na ɔhunle Seleama dɔɔnwo kpalɛ.

english_verse: Later, the prophet went back and warned Ahab, “Benhadad will attack you again next spring. Build up your troops and make sure you have some good plans.” Syria Attacks Israel Again
translation_verse: Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ ne hwenle bikyele Yizilayɛ belemgbunli ne na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Sia kɔboɔboa ɛ nwo; nea wɔ ɛlɔnema ne mɔ maa bɛboɔboa bɛ nwo. Ɔluakɛ Selea belemgbunli ne bava konle aradoa wɔ wɔ nyenyensuo mekɛ ne anu.” Seleama konle mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nwiɔ

english_verse: Meanwhile, Benhadad's officials went to him and explained: Israel's gods are mountain gods. We fought Israel's army in the hills, and that's why they defeated us. But if we fight them on flat land, there's no way we can lose.
translation_verse: Selea mgbanyima ne hanle hilele bɛ belemgbunli ne kɛ, “Deɛ mɔɔ yemɔti yeangola Yizilayɛma la a le kɛ, bɛ nyamenle ne mɔ le awoka zo nyamenle. Maa yɛ nee bɛ ɛbɔ ye zo wɔ azɛlɛ sɛsɛ zo na ɛbanwu kɛ bɛnrɛhola yɛ.

english_verse: Then get more soldiers, horses, and chariots, so your army will be as strong as it was before. We'll fight Israel's army on flat land and wipe them out. Benhadad agreed and did what they suggested.
translation_verse: Akee kpondɛ ɛlɔnema mɔɔ kɛyɛ kɛ mɔɔ yɛminli bɛ la abo zo, mgbɔnwɔ nee konle ehwili mɔ amuala, na akee maa yɛhɔzɔ bɛ wɔ azɛlɛ mɔɔ la aze la azo na ɛbanwu kɛ yɛbabila bɛ teledede zɛhae.” Belemgbunli Bɛneheedade kponlenle na ɔlile ye mgbanyima ne mɔ ɛdeɛ ne azo.

english_verse: In the spring, Benhadad got his army together, and they marched to the town of Aphek to attack Israel.
translation_verse: Wɔ nyenyensuo mekɛ ne mɔlebɛbo, Bɛneheedade boɔboale ye ɛlɔnema anloa na ɔhɔdoale Yizilayɛma wɔ suakpole Efɛke azo kɛ bɛ nee bɛ kaho.

english_verse: The prophet went to Ahab and said, “The Syrians think the Lord is a god of the hills and not of the valleys. So he has promised to help you defeat their powerful army. Then you will know that the Lord is in control.”
translation_verse: Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ rahanle hilele Yizilayɛ belemgbunli ne kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma se, ‘Seleama se mame mele awoka zo Nyamenle na menle azɛlɛ mɔɔ la aze la Nyamenle.
