english_verse: He then grabbed his oldest son who was to be the next king and sacrificed him as an offering on the city wall. The Israelite troops were so horrified that they left the city and went back home.
translation_verse: Yemɔti ɔvale ɔ ra nrenya kpanyinli ne mɔɔ di ye agya la, ɔmanle bɛyelale ye bɛbɔle azu wɔ azukponle ne bane ne anwo. Ɛhye manle Yizilayɛma ahonle dule; munzule kpole zile Yizilayɛma anwo zo; ɔlua zo bɛhwenle bɛ nzi na bɛziale bɛhɔle bɛ maanle nu.

english_verse: One day the widow of one of the Lord's prophets said to Elisha, “You know that before my husband died, he was a follower of yours and a worshiper of the Lord. But he owed a man some money, and now that man is on his way to take my two sons as his slaves.”
translation_verse: Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛma asa azo ne mɔ anu sonla ko mɔɔ ɛwu la aye hɔzele Yilaehya kɛ, “Me hu ɛwu. Kɛmɔ ɛdawɔ ɛze la, ɛnee ɔsulo Nyamenle kpole kpalɛ, noko kɛkala, awie mɔɔ yɛtua ye kakɛ la ɛra kɛ ɔbava me mra mrenya nwiɔ ne yeahɔzie nu awoba.”

english_verse: “Maybe there's something I can do to help,” Elisha said. “What do you have in your house?” “Sir, I have nothing but a small bottle of olive oil.”
translation_verse: Yilaehya bizale ye kɛ, “Duzu a ɛkpondɛ kɛ meyɛ memaa wɔ a? Duzu a ɛlɛ ye wɔ sua nu a? Ka mɔɔ ɛlɛ ye la kile me.” Kunlanvolɛ raalɛ ne zele ye kɛ, “Menlɛ ɛhwee. Yeha me nwole buakɛ ko.”

english_verse: Elisha told her, “Ask your neighbors for their empty jars. And after you've borrowed as many as you can,
translation_verse: Yilaehya zele ye kɛ, “Finde kɔ, kɔzɛlɛzɛlɛ mbuakɛ mgbane dɔɔnwo wɔ ɛ gɔnwo mɔ ɛkɛ ne

english_verse: go home and shut the door behind you and your sons. Then begin filling the jars with oil and set each one aside as you fill it.”
translation_verse: Akee kɔ na ɛ nee ɛ mra ne mɔ bɛdo bɛ nwo anlenkɛ nu na bɔ ɔ bo kɛ ɛwola nwole ne wɔagua mbuakɛ ne mɔ anu; ko biala mɔɔ kɛyi la ɛnee wɔye wɔzie ahane.”

english_verse: The woman left. Later, when she and her sons were back inside their house, the two sons brought her the jars, and she began filling them.
translation_verse: Yemɔti raalɛ ne hɔle na ɔ nee ɔ mra ne mɔ hɔdole bɛ nwo anlenkɛ nu, yɛɛ mɔɔ ɔbubu nwole ne la ɛnee bɛlɛtwe bɛkɔsie na bɛfa mbuakɛ fofolɛ bɛba.

english_verse: At last, she said to one of her sons, “Bring me another jar.” “We don't have any more,” he answered, and the oil stopped flowing from the small bottle.
translation_verse: Mbuakɛ ne mɔ yiyile la ɔbizale bɛ kɛ saa buakɛ bieko tɛbɔ ɛkɛ ne a. Na ɔ mra ne mɔ ko buale kɛ, “Bieko ɛnle ɛkɛ.” Na ɛkɛ ne ala nwole ne abo pɛle.

english_verse: After she told Elisha what had happened, he said, “Sell the oil and use part of the money to pay what you owe the man. You and your sons can live on what is left.” Elisha Brings a Rich Woman's Son Back to Life
translation_verse: Raalɛ ne hɔle Yilaehya ɛkɛ ne hɔbɔle ye amaneɛ na Yilaehya zele ye kɛ, “Kɔdɔne nwole ne fa bie tua wɔ kakɛ ne na ɛ nee ɛ mra ne mɔ bɛva mɔɔ ɛha la bɛnlea bɛ nwo.” Yilaehya nee raalɛ sukoavolɛ ne mɔɔ vi Hyunɛm la

english_verse: Once, while Elisha was in the town of Shunem, he met a rich woman who invited him to her home for dinner. After that, whenever he was in Shunem, he would have a meal there with her and her husband.
translation_verse: Kenle ko Yilaehya hɔle Hyunɛm na raalɛ sukoavolɛ bie mɔɔ wɔ ɛkɛ ne la vɛlɛle ye manle ɔrakpulale ɔ sa. Ɛhye ati kenle biala mɔɔ ɔkɛva ɛkɛ ne adenle zo la, ɔmakyi ɛkɛ ne ɔdi debie.

english_verse: Some time later the woman said to her husband, “I'm sure the man who comes here so often is a prophet of God.
translation_verse: Raalɛ ne hanle hilele ɔ hu kɛ, “Yɛmenle, menwu kɛ nrenya ye mɔɔ ba ɛke dahuu la le Nyamenle sonla mɔɔ anwo te a.

english_verse: Why don't we build him a small room on the flat roof of our house? We can put a bed, a table and chair, and an oil lamp in it. Then whenever he comes, he can stay with us.”
translation_verse: Maa yɛzi sua ekpumgbunli ekyi ko wɔ sua ye ati zo lɔ na yɛva ɛsokpa, ɛkponle, ebia nee kɛnlaneɛ yezie nuhua amaa kenle biala mɔɔ ɔkɛra ɛke la yeahɔla ɛkɛ.”

english_verse: The next time Elisha was in Shunem, he stopped at their house and went up to his room to rest.
translation_verse: Kenle ko Yilaehya hɔle Hyunɛm na ɔhɔle ye sua ne anu kɛ ɔkadenrɛ ɔ nwo.

english_verse: He said to his servant Gehazi, “This woman has been very helpful. Have her come up here to the roof for a moment.” She came, and Elisha told Gehazi to say to her, “You've gone to a lot of trouble for us, and we want to help you. Is there something we can request the king or army commander to do?” The woman answered, “With my relatives nearby, I have everything I need.”
translation_verse: ɔzele Gɛheezae kɛ, “Ka kile raalɛ ye kɛ yevɛ yɛ nwo somaa. Duzu yɛɛ ɔkpondɛ kɛ yɛyɛ yɛmaa ye a?” Ɛkɛhulo kɛ yɛkɛnwu belemgbunli anzɛɛ safohyenlema kpanyinli ne yɛkɛmaa wɔ ɔ? Raalɛ ne buale kɛ, “Me tɛnlabelɛ nu le kpalɛ, mewɔ medame me maanle nu.”

english_verse: “Then what can we do for her?” Elisha asked Gehazi. Gehazi replied, “I do know that her husband is old, and that she doesn't have a son.”
translation_verse: Yilaehya bizale Gɛheezae kɛ, “Ɛnea a duzu a ɔwɔ kɛ yɛyɛ yɛmaa ye a?” Gɛheezae zele ye kɛ, “Ɔnlɛ ralɛ nrenya yɛɛ ɔhu noko ɛyɛ kpanyinli.”

english_verse: “Ask her to come here again,” Elisha told his servant. He called for her, and she came and stood in the doorway of Elisha's room.
translation_verse: Yilaehya zele kɛ, “Fɛlɛ ye maa me.” Raalɛ ne ragyinlanle sua ne anlenkɛ ne anloa,

english_verse: Elisha said to her, “Next year at this time, you'll be holding your own baby son in your arms.” “You're a man of God,” the woman replied. “Please don't lie to me.”
translation_verse: na Yilaehya zele ye kɛ, “Ɛvolɛ bieko bekezɛ ɛnee ɛvia ralɛ nrenya.” Raalɛ ne buale kɛ, “Yɛmenle, Ɛle Nyamenle sonla, mmabɛlɛbɛla me.”

english_verse: But a few months later, the woman got pregnant. She gave birth to a son, just as Elisha had promised.
translation_verse: Na kɛmɔ Yilaehya hanle ala la, raalɛ ne nrenzɛle na ɔwole ralɛ nrenya wɔ nyenyensuo mekɛ ne anu.

english_verse: One day while the boy was still young, he was out in the fields with his father, where the workers were harvesting the crops.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ kakula ne dule zo ekyii la, kenle ko ɔ nee ɔ ze, nee ɔ ze ɛkpama ne hɔle ye ɛya nu lɔ kɛ bɛkade bɛyɔba.

english_verse: Suddenly he shouted, “My head hurts. It hurts a lot!” “Carry him back to his mother,” the father said to his servant.
translation_verse: Na ɔzele ɔ ze kɛ, “O me ti, me ti.” Ɔ ze zele ye sonvolɛ ne kɛ, “Dwu ye kɔmaa ɔ nli.”

english_verse: loaves of bread made from the first barley that was harvested. Elisha said, “Give it to the people so they can eat.”
translation_verse: Sonvolɛ ne vale kakula ne hɔmanle ɔ nli. Raalɛ ne vale kakula ne dole ɔ gyakɛ azo na ɔkadwu sɛnzɛngyinla la, kakula ne wule.

english_verse: She carried him upstairs to Elisha's room and laid him across the bed. Then she walked out and shut the door behind her.
translation_verse: Raalɛ ne vale funli ne hɔdole Nyamenle sonla ne ɛsokpa ne azo na ɔdole anlenkɛ ne anu ɔvindele.

english_verse: The woman called to her husband, “I need to see the prophet. Let me use one of the donkeys. Send a servant along with me, and let me leave now, so I can get back quickly.”
translation_verse: Akee ɔzele ɔ hu kɛ, “Maa me sonvolɛma ne mɔ ko nee asoaso maa mengɔ Nyamenle sonla ne ɛkɛ ne ndɛndɛ menzia membɛla.”

english_verse: “Why do you need to see him today?” her husband asked. “It's not the Sabbath or time for the New Moon Festival.” “That's all right,” she answered.
translation_verse: Ɔ hu bizale ye kɛ, “Duzu ati a ɛkɔ Nyamenle sonla ne ɛkɛ ne ɛnɛ ɛ? Ɛnɛ ɛnle ɛnwomenlelielɛ kenle yɛɛ siane ɛtɛfile.” Raalɛ ne buale kɛ, “Tɛ debie ɔ.”

english_verse: She saddled the donkey and said to her servant, “Let's go. And don't slow down unless I tell you to.”
translation_verse: Akee ɔvole asoaso ne azo na ɔzele ye sonvolɛ ne kɛ, “Maa nane ne ɛhɔ ndɛndɛ. Mmamaa ɔto ye ɛnriandilɛ ne anu, kyesɛ mese wɔ kɛ ɛdo nu.”

english_verse: She left at once for Mount Carmel to talk with Elisha. When Elisha saw her coming, he said, “Gehazi, look! It's the woman from Shunem.
translation_verse: Yemɔti ɔzile nu na ɔhɔle Nyamenle sonla ne ɛkɛ wɔ Kamɛle Boka. Mɔɔ Yilaehya nwunle kɛ raalɛ ne ɛlɛba la, ɔzele Gɛheezae kɛ, “Nea nehane, Hyunɛm raalɛ ne a ɛlɛba la.

english_verse: Run and meet her. And ask her if everything is all right with her and her family.” “Everything is fine,” she answered Gehazi.
translation_verse: Nriandi kɔyia ye na biza ye kɛ, ‘Kɛ ɛ nwo de ɛ? Ɛ hu te kpɔkɛ ɔ? Ɛ ra ne te kpɔkɛ ɔ?’ ” Na ɔzele Gɛheezae kɛ, “Yɛ muala yɛte kpɔkɛ.”

english_verse: But as soon as she got to the top of the mountain, she went over and grabbed Elisha by the feet. Gehazi started toward her to push her away, when Elisha said, “Leave her alone! Don't you see how sad she is? But the Lord hasn't told me why.”
translation_verse: Na mɔɔ ɔdwule Yilaehya anwo ɛkɛ ne wɔ boka ne azo la ɔhotole ɔbɔle ɔ ti aze, ɔzɔle Yilaehya agyakɛ. Gɛheezae rale kɛ ɔbahwe ye ahane na Yilaehya zele ye kɛ, “Gyakyi ye na nyane kpole ɛha ye, yemɔ a Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛva ɛvea me mɔɔ yeanga yeangile me la.”

english_verse: The woman said, “Sir, I begged you not to get my hopes up, and I didn't even ask you for a son.”
translation_verse: Raalɛ ne zele ye kɛ, “Me menle, menzele wɔ kɛ ɛmaa menwo ralɛ nrenya ɔ? Se menganle mengilele wɔ kɛ ɛmmabɛlɛbɛla me.”

english_verse: “Gehazi, get ready and go to her house,” Elisha said. “Take along my walking stick, and when you get there, lay it on the boy's face. Don't stop to talk to anyone, even if they try to talk to you.”
translation_verse: Yilaehya zele Gɛheezae kɛ, “Ka ɛ nwo na die me kpɔma ye kɔ. Saa ɛ nee awie yia a, mmabiza ye ahye, yɛɛ saa awie biza wɔ ahye a mmagyinla ɛdie zolɛ, na fa me kpɔma ye kɔdo kakula ne anwoma azo.”

english_verse: But the boy's mother said to Elisha, “I swear by the living Lord and by your own life that I won't leave without you.” So Elisha got up and went with them.
translation_verse: Raalɛ ne zele Yilaehya kɛ, “Meka Ɛdɛnkɛma nee ɛdawɔ kɛ menrɛgyakyi wɔ ɛlɛ.” Yemɔti bɛ mu nwiɔ bɛdwazole bɛhɔle.

english_verse: Gehazi ran on ahead and laid Elisha's walking stick on the boy's face, but the boy didn't move or make a sound. Gehazi ran back to Elisha and said, “The boy didn't wake up.”
translation_verse: Gɛheezae lumuale bɛ nyunlu vale kpɔma ne hɔdole kakula ne anwoma azo, noko kakula ne anzu yɛɛ yeanga ɔ nwo. Zɔhane ati ɔziale kɛ ɔkabɔ amaneɛ na ɔyiale ye la, ɔzele Yilaehya kɛ, “Kakula ne andunwue.”

english_verse: Elisha arrived at the woman's house and went straight to his room, where he saw the boy's body on his bed.
translation_verse: Yilaehya dwule sua nu ɛkɛ ne la ɔnwunle kɛ kakula ne ɛwu na bɛdo ye wɔ ye ɛsokpa ne azo.

english_verse: He walked in, shut the door, and prayed to the Lord.
translation_verse: Yemɔti ɔwolole sua ne anu, ɔdole anlenkɛ ne anu na ɔhale ye nee kakula ne ala na akee ɔzɛlɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma.

english_verse: Then he got on the bed and stretched out over the dead body, with his mouth on the boy's mouth, his eyes on his eyes, and his hand on his hands. As he lay there, the boy's body became warm.
translation_verse: Akee ɔhɔvole ɔdenrɛle ɔ nwo wɔ kakula ne funli ne azo, ɔvale ɔ nloa ɔkpulale kakula ne anloa, ɔvale ɔ nye ɔbutule kakula ne anye zo, ɔvale ɔ sa ɔguale kakula ne asa azo. Ɔbutule ɔ nwo zo zɛhae la kakula ne anwo yɛle wuluwulu.

english_verse: Elisha got up and walked back and forth in the room, then he went back and leaned over the boy's body. The boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.
translation_verse: Ɔdwazole ɔkpɔsale sua ne anu ekyii na eza ɔhɔbutule kakula ne anwo zo bieko. Kakula ne nwuasinle fane nsuu na ɔbukele ɔ nye.

english_verse: Elisha called out to Gehazi, “Ask the boy's mother to come here.” Gehazi did, and when she was at the door, Elisha said, “You can take your son.”
translation_verse: Akee Yilaegya vɛlɛle Gɛheezae kɛ ɔvɛlɛ Hyunɛm raalɛ ne ɔmaa ye. Ɔvɛlɛle ye na ɔrale la, Yilaehya zele ye kɛ, “Die ɛ ra ne, yede kpɔkɛ.”

english_verse: She came in and bowed down at Elisha's feet. Then she picked up her son and left. Elisha Makes Some Stew Taste Better
translation_verse: Raalɛ ne radule dɔle ɔ gyakɛ anu ɛkɛ, ɔbɔle ɔ ti azɛlɛ nwo na ɔdwazole ɔvale ɔ ra ne ɔhɔle. Nwanwane sɛkɛlɛneɛ nwiɔ bieko

english_verse: Later, Elisha went back to Gilgal, where there was almost nothing to eat, because the crops had failed. One day while the prophets who lived there were meeting with Elisha, he said to his servant, “Prepare a big pot of stew for these prophets.”
translation_verse: Ɛhɔne zile maanle ne anu, azɛlɛ ne azo, na Yilaehya rale Gelegale. Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛma asa azo ne bie mɔ radɛnlanle ɔ nwo ɛkɛ na ɔzele ye sonvolɛ ne kɛ, “Fa ɛzɛne kpole ne sie senle zo na to aleɛ maa Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ asa azo ne mɔ.”

english_verse: One of them went out into the woods to gather some herbs. He found a wild vine and picked as much of its fruit as he could carry, but he didn't know that the fruit was very sour. When he got back, he cut up the fruit and put it in the stew.
translation_verse: Bɛ nuhua ko dwazole hɔle kɛ ɔkatete nwolɛ nya nya, na ɔnwunle vanye nyinli bie la ɔtetele ye nya ne dɔɔnwo na ɔrapepɛle ɔguale aleɛ ne anu. Ɛnee ɔnze kɛ awa nyinli nya ɔ.

english_verse: The stew was served, and when the prophets started eating it, they shouted, “Elisha, this stew tastes terrible! We can't eat it.”
translation_verse: Na bɛyeyele bɛmanle bɛ kɛ bɛli. Bɛdi la bɛdeanle nu kɛ, “O Nyamenle sonla, debie mɔɔ ku sonla la wɔ nu.” Yemɔti bɛanli.

english_verse: “Bring me some flour,” Elisha said. He sprinkled the flour in the stew and said, “Now serve it to them.” And the stew tasted fine. Elisha Feeds One Hundred People
translation_verse: Na Yilaehya zele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛva aleɛ ne bɛrɛlɛ me.” Ɔvale aleɛ ne ɔguale siase ne anu na ɔzele kɛ, “Bɛyeye bie bɛmaa bɛli.” Na ɔyɛle kpalɛ bɔkɔɔ mɔɔ bɛdi a bɛnwu a.

english_verse: So the servant served the bread and grain to the people. They ate and still had some left over, just as the Lord had promised.
translation_verse: Yemɔti ɔvale ɔmanle bɛlile na bie dɔɔnwo hale kɛmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma hanle ala la.

english_verse: Naaman was the commander of the Syrian army. The Lord had helped him and his troops defeat their enemies, so the king of Syria respected Naaman very much. Naaman was a brave soldier, but he had leprosy.
translation_verse: Nrenya bie, bɛfɛlɛ ye Neeman; ɔle safohyenle kpanyinli mɔɔ nea Selea ɛlɔnema ne anwo zo a. Selea belemgbunli ne bu ye kpalɛ eza ɔkulo ye edwɛkɛ, ɔboalekɛ ɔlua Neeman anwo zo Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛmaa Seleama ɛli Yizilayɛma anwo zo konim. Neeman le katakyie, noko ɔle kokobɛvolɛ.

english_verse: One day while the Syrian troops were raiding Israel, they captured a girl, and she became a servant of Naaman's wife.
translation_verse: Bɛ nee Yizilayɛma konle konle ne mɔ ko anu, Seleama hɔle Yizilayɛma anwo zo na bɛhyele kakula bɛlɛra bie bɛhɔle bɛ maanle nu, na bɛyɛle kɛ ɔzonle Neeman aye ne.

english_verse: the king replied, “Go ahead! I will give you a letter to take to the king of Israel.” Naaman left and took along
translation_verse: Na Belemgbunli ne zele kɛ, “Ɛnee kɔ ɛ. Mekɛlɛ kɛlata meamaa wɔahɔmaa Yizilayɛ belemgbunli ne.” Yemɔti Neeman vale dwɛtɛ fufule apenle ngoko abulasa, ezukoa nvutuke apenle nsia yɛɛ ɛvoyialilɛ adɛladeɛ ngakyile bulu na ɔzile nu ɔhɔle.

english_verse: He also carried the letter to the king of Israel. It said, “I am sending my servant Naaman to you. Would you cure him of his leprosy?”
translation_verse: Na belemgbunli ne vale kɛlata manle ye kɛ ɔva ɔhɔmaa Yizilayɛ belemgbunli ne. Kɛlata ne se, “Saa ɛ sa ka kɛlata ɛhye a, ɛnee nwu ye kɛ medame yɛɛ mezoa me Safohyenlema Kpanyinli ne ɛ nwo ɛkɛ a, amaa wɔayɛ ye kokobɛ ne ayile.”

english_verse: Elisha sent someone outside to say to him, “Go wash seven times in the Jordan River. Then you'll be completely cured.”
translation_verse: Na Yilaehya zoanle ye sonvolɛma ne mɔ ko manle ɔrazele ye kɛ, “Kɔbia Azule Dwɔdan ne anu fane nsuu na ɛ nwo baza na wɔ nwonane ne ayɛ kɛ ye dɛba ne ala la.”

english_verse: When the king of Israel read the letter, he tore his clothes in fear and shouted, “That Syrian king believes I can cure this man of leprosy! Does he think I'm God with power over life and death? He must be trying to pick a fight with me.”
translation_verse: Yizilayɛ belemgbunli ne asa hanle kɛlata ne na ɔgengale la, nyane ngome manle ɔsuosuanle ye tɛladeɛ ne mɔɔ ɔwula la anu na ɔzele kɛ, “Na mele Nyamenle ɔ, mɔɔ mekola meku sonla eza metunwue ye mɔɔ yemɔti, bɛva nrenya ɛhye bɛrɛlɛ me kɛ menyɛ ye kokobɛ ayile a? Ɛhye kile kɛ konle ala yɛɛ ɔfa yearadoa me a.”

english_verse: As soon as Elisha the prophet heard what had happened, he sent the Israelite king this message: “Why are you so afraid? Send the man to me, so that he will know there is a prophet in Israel.”
translation_verse: Na mɔɔ Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ Yilaehya dele edwɛkɛ ne nee kɛ belemgbunli ne zile suosuanle ye tɛladeɛ mɔɔ ɔwula la anu la, ɔzoanle ɔmanle bɛhɔzele ye kɛ, “Na duzu ati yɛɛ wɔsuosua wɔ tɛladeɛ ne anu a? Maa ɔrɛla me nwo ɛke amaa yeanwu kɛ Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ wɔ Yizilayɛ.”

english_verse: Naaman left with his horses and chariots and stopped at the door of Elisha's house.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Neeman dɛnlanle ye konle ehwili ne anu na ɔ nee ye mgbɔnwɔ ne mɔ amuala hɔgyinlanle Yilaehya sua nu ɛkɛ ne anuhɔlɛ ne.

english_verse: But Naaman stormed off, grumbling, “Why couldn't he come out and talk to me? I thought for sure he would stand in front of me and pray to the Lord his God, then wave his hand over my skin and cure me.
translation_verse: Neeman vale ɛya na ɔzele kɛ, “Medwenle kɛ ɔfinde yeara, yearagyinla yeavɛlɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ye Nyamenle ne, na yeava ɔ sa yeawɔza me ewule ne azo yeayɛ me kokobɛ ne ayile.

english_verse: What about the Abana River or the Pharpar River? Those rivers in Damascus are just as good as any river in Israel. I could have washed in them and been cured.”
translation_verse: Na Azule mgbole mɔɔ le kɛ Abana nee Fapa mɔɔ gua Dɛmasekɛse la ɛnle kpalɛ ɛndɛla azule mɔɔ wɔ Yizilayɛ la ɔ? Duzu ati a mengɔmbia bɛmɛ anu mende kpɔkɛ ɛ?” Yemɔti ɔhakyile ɔ nwo kɛ ɔkɔ.

english_verse: His servants went over to him and said, “Sir, if the prophet had told you to do something difficult, you would have done it. So why don't you do what he said? Go wash and be cured.”
translation_verse: Na ye sonvolɛma ne mɔ hɔle ɔ nwo ɛkɛ ne na bɛzele ye kɛ, “Yɛmenle, saa Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ ne zele wɔ kɛ ɛyɛ debie ɛsesebɛ bie a anrɛɛ ɛnrɛyɛ ɔ? Duzu ati yɛɛ akee ɛnrɛhɔdɔ Azule ne anu fane nsuu ne na ɛnrɛde kpɔkɛ ɛ?”

english_verse: Naaman walked down to the Jordan; he waded out into the water and stooped down in it seven times, just as Elisha had told him. At once, he was cured, and his skin became as smooth as a child's.
translation_verse: Na Neeman hɔle Dwɔdan ne anloa na ɔdɔle nu fane nsuu kɛmɔ Yilaehya zele ye la, na ɔdele kpɔkɛ bɔkɔɔ. Ye nwonane ne yɛle kɛnlɛma kɛ adɔma nwonane la.

english_verse: Naaman and his officials went back to Elisha. Naaman stood in front of him and announced, “Now I know that the God of Israel is the only God in the whole world. Sir, would you please accept a gift from me?”
translation_verse: Yemɔti ɔziale ɔrale Yilaehya ɛkɛ ne na ɔhanle kɛ, “Kɛkala, akee menwu kɛ Nyamenle ɛnle ɛleka biala kɛ Yizilayɛ ala; zɔhane ati, yɛmenle, die me sa nu ahyɛlɛdeɛ.”

english_verse: “I am a servant of the living Lord,” Elisha answered, “and I swear that I will not take anything from you.” Naaman kept begging, but Elisha kept refusing.
translation_verse: Yilaehya buale kɛ, “Meka tease Nyamenle ne mɔɔ mesonle ye la kɛ, menrɛlie ahyɛlɛdeɛ biala.” Neeman hanle biala, na Yilaehya anlie ahyɛlɛdeɛ ne.

english_verse: Finally Naaman said, “If you won't accept a gift, then please let me take home as much soil as two mules can pull in a wagon. Sir, from now on I will offer sacrifices only to the Lord.
translation_verse: Na Neeman zele ye kɛ, “Saa ye zɛhae ɛdeɛ a ɛnee mebodo wɔ, maa me adenle maa menva ɛke ɛnwea mɔɔ mgbɔnwɔndua nwiɔ kɛhola ye soa la mengɔ, ɔluakɛ ɔvi ɛnɛ mɔɔ kɔ la, menrɛva ɛyelalɛ azubɔdeɛ menrɛmaa kɛ bɛva bɛbɔ azu yɛɛ menrɛbɔ azu menrɛmaa nyamenle biala kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma ala.

english_verse: But I pray that the Lord will forgive me when I go into the temple of the god Rimmon and bow down there with the king of Syria.”
translation_verse: Na ɛhye yɛɛ mesɛlɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma a, saa me nee me belemgbunli ne yɛkɔ Selea bozonle Rileemɔn amonle sua ne anu na mebɔ me ti aze mesonle ye bie a, ɔva ɔhyɛ me.”

english_verse: “Go on home, and don't worry about that,” Elisha replied. Then Naaman left. Elisha Places a Curse on Gehazi After Naaman had gone only a short distance,
translation_verse: Na Yilaehya zele ye kɛ, “Kɔ anzonudwolɛ nu.” Na Neeman hɔle. Mɔɔ Neeman hɔle moa ekyii la,

english_verse: Gehazi said to himself, “Elisha let that Syrian off too easy. He should have taken Naaman's gift. I swear by the living Lord that I will talk to Naaman myself and get something from him.”
translation_verse: Yilaehya sonvolɛ Gɛheezae, hanle kɛ, “Nea, me menle ɛgyakyi Seleanli Neeman; yeanlie ninyɛne mɔɔ ɔ nee bɛ rale la anu ko bɔbɔ. Meka tease Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ, menriandi meadoa ye meahɔlie debie wɔ ye ɛkɛ.”

english_verse: So he hurried after Naaman. When Naaman saw Gehazi running after him, he got out of his chariot to meet him. Naaman asked, “Is everything all right?”
translation_verse: Yemɔti ɔnriandile ɔdoale Neeman. Neeman dole ɔ nye na ɔnwunle kɛ awie lɛ ɛnriandilɛ doa ye la, ɔvi ye ehwili ne anu ɔdwule ɔhɔyiale ye na ɔbizale ye kɛ, “Edwɛkɛ bie ɔ?”

english_verse: “Yes,” Gehazi answered. “But my master has sent me to tell you about two young prophets from the hills of Ephraim. They came asking for help, and now Elisha wants to know if you would give them
translation_verse: Gɛheezae buale kɛ, “Tɛ edwɛkɛ bie ɔ, edwɛkɛ biala ɛnle ɛkɛ. Na me menle ɛzoa me kɛ membaze wɔ kɛ, ‘Ɛyele ɛ nwo ɛkɛ ne ala la yɛɛ Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛma asa azo ne mɔ mɔɔ wɔ Yifelaem awoka ne mɔ azo lɔ la anu nwiɔ rale a. Yemɔti fa dwɛtɛ fufule apenle nsa yɛɛ ɛvoyialilɛ adɛladeɛ ngakyile nwiɔ maa memaa bɛ.’ ”

english_verse: “Sure,” Naaman replied. “But why don't you take twice that amount of silver?” He convinced Gehazi to take it all, then put the silver in two bags. He handed the bags and the clothes to his two servants, and they carried them for Gehazi.
translation_verse: Neeman buale kɛ, “Die dwɛtɛ fufule apenle nsia kɔmaa bɛ.” Ɔgyinlanle zo kɛ ɔlie, na ɔwulale dwɛtɛ fufule ne wɔ ahodoku nwiɔ anu ɔkyekyele na ɔvale ɛvoyialilɛ adɛladeɛ ngakyile nwiɔ ɔbokale nwolɛ ɔvale ɔzoale ye sonvolɛma nwiɔ kɛ bɛva bɛ nee Gɛheezae ɛhɔ.

english_verse: When they reached the hill where Gehazi lived, he took the bags from the servants and placed them in his house, then sent the men away. After they had gone,
translation_verse: Bɛhɔdwule boka ne mɔɔ Yilaehya wɔ zo la abo la, Gɛheezae liele ninyɛne ne na ɔvale ɔhɔguale ye sua ne mɔɔ ɔda nu la anu na ɔmanle menli ne mɔ ziale.

english_verse: Gehazi went in and stood in front of Elisha, who asked, “Gehazi, where have you been?” “Nowhere, sir,” Gehazi answered.
translation_verse: Akee ɔziale ɔhɔle sua nu na Yilaehya bizale ye kɛ, “Gɛheezae, ɛhɔle nienwu?” Gɛheezae buale kɛ, “Meangɔ ɛleka.”

english_verse: Elisha asked, “Don't you know that my spirit was there when Naaman got out of his chariot to talk with you? Gehazi, you have no right to accept money or clothes, olive orchards or vineyards, sheep or cattle, or servants.
translation_verse: Na Yilaehya zele ye kɛ, “Me sunsum nee wɔ a hɔle a. Mɔɔ nrenya ne vi ye ehwili ne anu dwule aze kɛ ɔbayia wɔ la ɛnee mewɔ ɛkɛ. Ɛnea a ɛnee mekɛ mɔɔ bɛfa bɛdie ezukoa, adɛladeɛ, ɔlivi nee vanye egyinli, mboane nee nlankɛ, yɛɛ sonvolɛ mrenya nee mraalɛ la a le ɛhye ɔ?

english_verse: Because of what you've done, Naaman's leprosy will now be on you and your descendants forever!” Suddenly, Gehazi's skin became white with leprosy, and he left.
translation_verse: Zɔhane ati Neeman kokobɛ ne badila wɔ nee ɛ bo zo amra dahuu.” Gɛheezae vindele la ɛnee kokobɛ ne ɛdila ye, ɔ nwo ɛyɛ nzelabenle.

english_verse: One day the prophets said to Elisha, “The place where we meet with you is too small.
translation_verse: Kenle ko Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛma asa azo ne mɔɔ Yilaehya a nea bɛ nwo zo la hanle hilele ye kɛ, “Ɛleka mɔɔ yɛde la le ekyi maa yɛ.

english_verse: Why don't we build a new meeting place near the Jordan River? Each of us could get some wood, then we could build it.” “That's a good idea,” Elisha replied, “get started.”
translation_verse: Maa yɛ adenle maa yɛhɔ Dwɔdan ne anloa lɔ yɛhɔpɛ mbaka yɛrabu awuke yɛdɛnla nuhua.” Na Yilaehya zele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛhɔ.”

english_verse: “Aren't you going with us?” one of the prophets asked. “Yes, I'll go,” Elisha answered,
translation_verse: Bɛ nuhua ko zele Yilaehya kɛ, “Yɛbodo wɔ, maa yɛhɔ.” Na ɔkponlenle zolɛ

english_verse: and he left with them. They went to the Jordan River and began chopping down trees.
translation_verse: ɔ nee bɛ hɔle. Bɛrale Dwɔdan ne anloa na bɛpɛle mbaka dɔɔnwo.

english_verse: “Where did it fall in?” Elisha asked. The prophet pointed to the place, and Elisha cut a stick and threw it into the water at that spot. The ax head floated to the top of the water.
translation_verse: Yilaehya bizale ye kɛ, “Nienwu a ɔdɔle a?” Nrenya ne hilele ye ɛleka mɔɔ ɔdɔle la. Yilaehya pɛle baka ekyi ko vuandinle dole azule ne anu na akuma tile ne tulule.

english_verse: “Now get it,” Elisha told him. And the prophet reached in and grabbed it. Elisha Stops an Invasion of the Syrian Army
translation_verse: Yilaehya zele ye kɛ, “Tende ɛ sa fa.” Na nrenya ne vale. Bɛli Selea ɛlɔnema anwo zo konim

english_verse: Time after time, when the king of Syria was at war against the Israelites, he met with his officers and announced, “I've decided where we will set up camp.”
translation_verse: Mekɛ bie mɔɔ ɛnee Selea belemgbunli ne zo konle doa Yizilayɛma la, ɔ nee ye mgbanyima yiale nuhua na bɛvale adwenle bɛhilele ɛleka mɔɔ bɛbayɛ bɛ azokoɛleɛ ne la.

english_verse: Each time, Elisha would send this warning to the king of Israel: “Don't go near there. That's where the Syrian troops have set up camp.”
translation_verse: Na Yilaehya zoanle manle bɛhɔdinle Yizilayɛ belemgbunli ne aze amaa yeangɔ ɛleka mɔɔ bɛwɔ la.

english_verse: So the king would warn the Israelite troops in that place to be on guard.
translation_verse: Na Yizilayɛ belemgbunli ne noko manle menli mɔɔ wɔ ɛkɛ ne afoa nu la lale bɛ nwo zo. Ɛhye hɔle zo fane dɔɔnwo manle Yizilayɛma nyianle bɛ ti.

english_verse: The king of Syria was furious when he found out what was happening. He called in his officers and asked, “Which one of you has been telling the king of Israel our plans?”
translation_verse: Ɛhye manle Selea belemgbunli ne adwenle zɛkyele dɔɔnwo manle ɔvɛlɛle ye mgbanyima ne na ɔbizale bɛ kɛ, “Bɛ nuhua boni a wɔ Yizilayɛ belemgbunli ne anzi a?”

english_verse: “None of us, Your Majesty,” one of them answered. “It's an Israelite named Elisha. He's a prophet, so he can tell his king everything—even what you say in your own room.”
translation_verse: Mgbanyima ne mɔ ko buale kɛ, “Nana, yɛ nuhua biala ɛnle ɔ nzi na Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ Yilaehya ne mɔɔ wɔ Yizilayɛ ɛkɛ ne la yɛɛ edwɛkɛ mɔɔ ɛkɛvea wɔ sua ne akunlu bɔbɔ ɛkɛha la, ɔka ɔkile Yizilayɛ belemgbunli ne a.”

english_verse: “Find out where he is!” the king ordered. “I'll send soldiers to bring him here.” They learned that Elisha was in the town of Dothan and reported it to the king.
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne zele kɛ, “Bɛhɔkpondɛ ye bɛnwu ɛleka mɔɔ ɔde la na menzoa menli memaa bɛhɔhye ye.” Bɛhɔle na bɛrahanle bɛhilele ye kɛ ɔde Dotan.

english_verse: He ordered his best troops to go there with horses and chariots. They marched out during the night and surrounded the town.
translation_verse: Yemɔti belemgbunli ne manle ɛlɔnema mɔɔ tɛnla mgbɔnwɔ zo nee mɔɔ tɛnla ehwili nu ko la dɔɔnwo nee ɛlɔnema dɔɔnwo kpalɛ rale nɔɔzo na bɛrabɔle bɛyiale suakpole ne.

english_verse: When Elisha's servant got up the next morning, he saw that Syrian troops had the town surrounded. “Sir, what are we going to do?” he asked.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ ne sonvolɛ ne dwazole nwonlomɔ mangyee ne na ɔtudu agyakɛ la, ɔnwunle kɛ ɛlɔne ɛva sua ne. Na ɔbizale Yilaehya kɛ, “O, me menle, na duzu yɛɛ yɛkɛyɛ a? Yɛwu bɔkɔbɔkɔ.”

english_verse: “Don't be afraid,” Elisha answered. “There are more troops on our side than on theirs.”
translation_verse: Yilaehya zele ye kɛ, “Mmasulo, ɛlɔnema mɔɔ nee yɛ lua la zonle tɛla bɛ.”

english_verse: Then he prayed, “Lord, please help him to see.” And the Lord let the servant see that the hill was covered with fiery horses and flaming chariots all around Elisha.
translation_verse: Akee ɔzɛlɛle kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma, buke me sonvolɛ ye anye maa ɔnwu debie.” Ɛdɛnkɛma diele nzɛlɛlɛ ne na ɔbukele kpavolɛ ne anye na ɔnwunle kɛ ɛlɔnema mɔɔ de senle mgbɔnwɔ zo nee senle ehwili nu la ɛbɔ ɛyia Yilaehya na bɛ somaa ɛva boka ne amuala.

english_verse: As the Syrian army came closer, Elisha prayed, “Lord, make those soldiers blind!” And the Lord blinded them with a bright light.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Selea ɛlɔnema ne dule kɛ bɛba bɛ nwo zo la, Yilaehya zɛlɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ, “Mesɛlɛ wɔ, bili menli ɛhye mɔ anye zo.” Yemɔti ɔbilile bɛ nye zo, kɛmɔ Yilaehya zɛlɛle ala la.

english_verse: Elisha told the enemy troops, “You've taken the wrong road and are in the wrong town. Follow me. I'll lead you to the man you're looking for.” Elisha led them straight to the capital city of Samaria.
translation_verse: Yilaehya hɔle bɛ nwo ɛkɛ na ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Ayi mɔ, bɛminli. Tɛ adenle ne ɛne yɛɛ tɛ suakpole ne mɔɔ bɛkɔ zo la ɛne. Bɛdoa me na me nee bɛ ɛhɔ ahenle mɔɔ bɛkpondɛ ye la ɛkɛ ne.” Na ɔlile bɛ nyunlu ɔ nee bɛ hɔle Samɛlea.

english_verse: When all the soldiers were inside the city, Elisha prayed, “Lord, now let them see again.” The Lord let them see that they were standing in the middle of Samaria.
translation_verse: Bɛdwule Samɛlea ala la Yilaehya zɛlɛle bieko kɛ, “O Ɛdɛnkɛma, maa bɛ nye zo ɛtete bɛ na bɛnwu ɛleka mɔɔ bɛwɔ la.” Yemɔti Ɛdɛnkɛma manle bɛ nye zo tetele bɛ na bɛnwunle kɛ bɛwolo bɛra Samɛlea suakpole ne azo.

english_verse: The king of Israel saw them and asked Elisha, “Should I kill them, sir?”
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Yizilayɛ belemgbunli ne nwunle Selea ɛlɔnema ne la, ɔbizale Yilaehya kɛ, “Egya, mengu bɛ ɔ? Mengu bɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: “No!” Elisha answered. “You didn't capture these troops in battle, so you have no right to kill them. Instead, give them something to eat and drink and let them return to their leader.”
translation_verse: Yilaehya buale kɛ, “Saa ɛhyele bɛ donvula wɔ konle nu bɔbɔ a anrɛɛ ɛnrɛhu bɛ. Yemɔti mmaku bɛ. Maa bɛ debie bɛli, maa bɛ nzule bɛnlo na gyakyi bɛ maa bɛhɔ bɛ menle anwo lɔ.”

english_verse: The king ordered a huge meal to be prepared for Syria's army, and when they finished eating, he let them go. For a while, the Syrian troops stopped invading Israel's territory. King Benhadad of Syria Attacks Samaria
translation_verse: Yemɔti belemgbunli ne manle bɛdole bɛ ɛkponle kpole bie. Bɛlile debie bɛ ko yile na bɛnlonle nza la, akee ɔmanle bɛ adenle bɛziale bɛhɔle Selea belemgbunli ne ɛkɛ. Ɔvi mekɛ zɔhane Seleama anli bɛ edwɛkɛ ambɔ Yizilayɛma anwo zo ɛralɛ bieko. Selea teta Samɛlea

english_verse: They kept up the attack until there was nothing to eat in the city. In fact, a donkey's head cost
translation_verse: Ɔlua ɛhye ati aleɛ wiele na ɛhɔne rale suakpole ne azo manle bɛdɔle asoaso tile dwɛtɛ fufule abulatwɛ yɛɛ bɛ anweɛ nyinli ngyikyi bie mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye “Kaabe” la ɛkyɛ nu nna a bɛtɔ ko dwɛtɛ fufule nnu.

english_verse: One day as the king of Israel was walking along the top of the city wall, a woman shouted to him, “Please, Your Majesty, help me!”
translation_verse: Kenle ko Yizilayɛ belemgbunli ne lua suakpole ne bane ne sinli nyunlu ɛlɛtudu agyakɛ la, raalɛ bie vɛlɛle ye hanle kɛ, “O Nana, boa me.”

english_verse: “Let the Lord help you!” the king said. “Do you think I have grain or wine to give you?”
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne buale kɛ, “Saa Ɛdɛnkɛma amboa wɔ a ɛnee kɛ mame mesi meboa wɔ memaa ɔyɛ boɛ ɛ? Menlɛ awule yɛɛ menlɛ nwanye.

english_verse: Then he asked, “What's the matter anyway?” The woman answered, “Another woman and I were so hungry that we agreed to eat our sons. She said if we ate my son one day, we could eat hers the next day.
translation_verse: Duzu debie a ɛkpondɛ kɛ meyɛ memaa wɔ a?” Raalɛ ne buale kɛ, “Ɛkenle bie raalɛ ɛhye zele me kɛ menva me ra nrenya ne memaa yɛhu ye yɛli wɔ demua ne na kenle fofolɛ yɛahu ɔdaye noko ye ɛdeɛ ne yɛali.

english_verse: So yesterday we cooked my son and ate him. But today when I went to her house to eat her son, she had hidden him.”
translation_verse: Yemɔti yɛhunle me ra nrenya ne yɛdonle yɛlile. Akee ye alehyenlɛ nu menzele ye kɛ ɔhu ɔ ra nrenya ne ɔmaa yɛdo yɛli a, ɔse ɔnrɛyɛ, yeva ɔ ra ne yehɔvea.”

english_verse: The king tore off his clothes in sorrow, and since he was on top of the city wall, the people saw that he was wearing sackcloth underneath.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Belemgbunli ne dele ɛhye la, ɛya ngome manle ɔsuosuanle ye tɛladeɛ ne mɔɔ ɔwula la anu. Na menli mɔɔ bikye ɛkɛ ne la nwunle kɛ ɛnee ɔwula ɛrele tɛladeɛ wɔ ɔ bo.

english_verse: He said, “I pray that God will punish me terribly, if Elisha's head is still on his shoulders by this time tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Na ɔzele kɛ, “Saa ɛnɛ kenle ye meammaa bɛanye Hyeefate ara Yilaehya ati ne bɛanvi zo a, Nyamenle ɛdua me kakɛ ɛgua me bie zo.”

english_verse: Then he sent a messenger to Elisha. Elisha was home at the time, and the important leaders of Israel were meeting with him. Even before the king's messenger arrived, Elisha told the leaders, “That murderer is sending someone to cut off my head. When you see him coming, shut the door and don't let him in. I'm sure the king himself will be right behind him.”
translation_verse: Na ɔzoanle sonla kɛ ɔhɔva Yilaehya ɔrɛlɛ ye. Mekɛ ne anu ɛnee Yilaehya nee mgbanyima bie mɔɔ ɛra ye ɛkpɔlalɛ la gua ɛlɛdi adwelie wɔ ye sua ne anu. Na ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛnlea, kɔdiawu ne ɛzoa kɛ bɛrahu me. Saa ɔdwu ɛke a bɛdo anlenkɛ ne anu bɛzua ɔ nzi kpundii; bɛmmamaa ɔwolo ɔba ɛke. Belemgbunli mumua ne li ɔ nzi ɛlɛba.” Yilaehya hanle ɛhye kolaa na sonla ne mɔɔ belemgbunli ne zoanle ye la ara.

english_verse: Before Elisha finished talking, the messenger came up and said, “The Lord has made all these terrible things happen to us. Why should I think he will help us now?”
translation_verse: Ɔ nloa ampe bɔbɔ yɛɛ belemgbunli mumua ne yele ɔ nyunlu a, na ɔzele kɛ, “Ngyegyelɛ ɛhye vi Ɛdɛnkɛma. Duzu ati a ɔwɔ kɛ eza mekendɛ dedee ɛ?”

english_verse: Elisha answered, “I have a message for you. The Lord promises that tomorrow here in Samaria, you will be able to buy a large sack of flour or two large sacks of barley for almost nothing.”
translation_verse: Yilaehya buale kɛ, “Tie edwɛkɛ mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛha la. Ɔse, Ɛhyema kabezɛ ala, bɛbadɔne abɛlɛ ɛdɔkɛ kilo nsa anzɛɛ baale kilo nsia dwɛtɛ fufule ko wɔ Samɛlea ɛke.”

english_verse: The chief officer there with the king replied, “I don't believe it! Even if the Lord sent a rainstorm, it couldn't produce that much grain by tomorrow.” “You will see it happen, but you won't eat any of the food,” Elisha warned him. The Syrian Army Stops Its Attack
translation_verse: Na belemgbunli sonvolɛ ne mɔɔ nee ye lua la zele Yilaehya kɛ, “Ɛhye, yemɔ tafela. Saa Ɛdɛnkɛma mumua ne tukuedukue anwuma nvɛnzɛlɛ bɔbɔ a, ɔnrɛzi zɔhane ɛlɛ.” Yilaehya buale kɛ, “Ɛ nye banwu ye na ɛnrɛli bie.” Selea ɛlɔnema nriandi avi Samɛlea

english_verse: About the same time, four men with leprosy were just outside the gate of Samaria. They said to each other, “Why should we sit here, waiting to die?
translation_verse: Menli nna bie mɔɔ kokobɛ ɛdila bɛ la ɛnee de Samɛlea suakpole ne anuhɔlɛ kpole ne anzi. Na bɛhanle bɛhilele bɛ nwo ngoko kɛ, “Duzu ati a yɛtɛnla ɛke dedee yɛawu ɛ?

english_verse: There's nothing to eat in the city, so we would starve if we went inside. But if we stay out here, we will die for sure. Let's sneak over to the Syrian army camp and surrender. They might kill us, but they might not.”
translation_verse: Saa yɛse kɛ yɛkɔ suakpole ne azo lɔ a, ɛhɔne wɔ lɔ, yɛbawu; yɛɛ saa yɛde ɛke noko a ewule ko ne ala ɔ. Zɔhane ati bɛmaa yɛhɔ Selea ɛlɔnema ne azokoɛleɛ lɔ. Saa bɛnwu yɛ anwunvɔne a, yɛ ti ngoane ɔ, saa bɛku yɛ noko a, ɔ muala wie ewule ko ne ala.”

english_verse: They said to each other, “This isn't right. Today is a day to celebrate, and we haven't told anyone else what has happened. If we wait until morning, we will be punished. Let's go to the king's palace at once and tell the good news.”
translation_verse: Na akee bɛzele kɛ, “Yɛnyɛ ye boɛ; ɛnɛ kenle ye nee edwɛkɛ fɛlɛko lua. Saa yɛfea zolɛ toonwo ɔdwu alehyenlɛ a, yɛbanyia ndeanlɛ. Zɔhane ati bɛmaa yɛhɔbɔ belemgbunli mgbanyima ne mɔ sua nu amra amaneɛ.

english_verse: They went back to Samaria and shouted up to the guards at the gate, “We've just come from the Syrian army camp, and all the soldiers are gone! The tents are empty, and the horses and donkeys are still tied up. We didn't see or hear anybody.”
translation_verse: Yemɔti bɛrale na bɛhanle bɛhilele anlenkɛ kpole sinzavolɛma ne kɛ: Yɛhɔle Seleama azokoɛleɛ lɔ na yɛnwunle kɛ awie biala ɛnle ɛkɛ. Anloma nee akɔlɛ bɔbɔ, yeande bie nganeɛ kɛ bɛ mgbɔnwɔ nee bɛ asoaso ne mɔ mɔɔ bɛhendɛhenda bɛ la a yɛnwunle bɛ a, yɛɛ bɛ ndanlɛ azua ne mɔ noko bɛanyɛ bɛ ɛhwee.”

english_verse: The guards reported the news to the king's palace.
translation_verse: Anlenkɛ Kpole sinzavolɛma ne bɔle edwɛkɛ ne nolo na bɛhɔhanle edwɛkɛ ne wɔ belemgbunli suakunlu ɛkɛ.

english_verse: The king got out of bed and said to his officers, “I know what those Syrians are doing. They know we're starving, so they're hiding in the fields, hoping we will go out to look for food. When we do, they can capture us and take over our city.”
translation_verse: Na belemgbunli dwazole nɔe ne na ɔzele ye mgbanyima ne mɔ kɛ, “Bɛdie, bɛze mɔɔ Seleama ne ɛyɛ la ɔ? Bɛze kɛ ɛhɔne ɛlɛku yɛ, yemɔti bɛ nye fuu bɛvi bɛ azokoɛleɛ ne bɛhɔvea fienemgbole ne anu lɔ; bɛ adwenle a le kɛ, yɛvi suakpole ye azo yɛbavinde na bɛarahye yɛ na bɛava suakpole ye.”

english_verse: One of his officers replied, “We have a few horses left—why don't we let some men take five of them and go to the Syrian camp and see what's happening? We're going to die anyway like those who have already died.”
translation_verse: Ye mgbanyima ne mɔ ko zele ye kɛ, “Ewule ɛbɔ sua ye ɛwie; yemɔti ɔsi ɛkɛ ne ko ne ala. Bɛmaa yɛzoa menli yɛmaa bɛva mgbɔnwɔ mɔɔ ɛha la anu nnu bɛhɔnlea ye bɛ nye zo.”

english_verse: They found two chariots, and the king commanded the men to find out what had happened to the Syrian troops.
translation_verse: Yemɔti bɛyele menli nwiɔ mɔɔ tɛnla mgbɔnwɔ zo ko la na belemgbunli zoanle bɛ kɛ bɛhɔnlea.

english_verse: The men rode as far as the Jordan River. All along the way they saw clothes and equipment that the Syrians had thrown away as they escaped. Then they went back to the king and told him what they had seen.
translation_verse: Menli nwiɔ zɔhane dinle Seleama toonwo hɔdwule Dwɔdan ne anloa, na bɛnwunle kɛ, ye ndɛndɛ mɔɔ bɛkpondɛ la ati, Seleama nriandi ahɔ la ɛnee bɛlɛwɔlɔwɔlɔ bɛ adɛladeɛ na bɛfuandi bɛ konle ninyɛne bɛgua. Na soanvolɛma ne ziale rabɔle belemgbunli amaneɛ.

english_verse: At once the people went to the Syrian camp and carried off what was left. They took so much that a large sack of flour and two large sacks of barley sold for almost nothing, just as the Lord had promised.
translation_verse: Na menli ne vindele na bɛhɔfonyianle Seleama ndanlɛ azua ne mɔ anu bɛsesale bɛ debie biala. Yemɔti bɛdɔnenle abɛlɛ ɛdɔkɛ kilo nsa yɛɛ baale kilo nsia dwɛtɛ fufule ngoko, kɛmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma hanle ala la.

english_verse: The king of Israel had put his chief officer in charge of the gate, but he died when the people trampled him as they rushed out of the city.
translation_verse: Ɔrale ye zɛhae la, belemgbunli ne yɛle kɛ safohyenle ne mɔɔ nee ye lua la ɛhɔnlea suakpole ne anlenkɛ kpole sinzavolɛma ne anwo zo, na menli ne tietiale ɔ nwo zo manle ɔwule kɛmɔ Yilaehya hanle dole ɛkɛ ne, wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɔ nee belemgbunli bɛrale ɔ nwo zo la.

english_verse: Earlier, when the king was at Elisha's house, Elisha had told him that flour or barley would sell for almost nothing.
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ mɔɔ Yilaehya zele belemgbunli kɛ, “Bɛbadɔne abɛlɛ ɛdɔkɛ kilo nsa yɛɛ baale kilo nsia dwɛtɛ fufule ngoko ɛhyema kabezɛ wɔ Samɛlea ɛke la,”

english_verse: But the officer refused to believe that even the Lord could do that. So Elisha warned him that he would see it happen, but would not eat any of the food.
translation_verse: safohyenle ne buale ye kɛ, “Saa Ɛdɛnkɛma mumua ne tukuedukue anwuma nvɛnzɛlɛ bɔbɔ a ɔnrɛzi zɔhane ɛlɛ.” Na Yilaehya zele ye kɛ, “Ɛ nye banwu ye na ɛnrɛli bie.”

english_verse: And that's exactly what happened—the officer was trampled to death.
translation_verse: Na ɔyɛle zɔhane. Menli ne tietiale ɔ nwo zo wɔ anlenkɛ kpole ne anloa manle ɔwule.

english_verse: Then she returned to Israel and immediately begged the king to give back her house and property.
translation_verse: Ɛvolɛ nsuu ne awieleɛ, raalɛ ne vi Filisitiama maanle nu ziale rale sua nu na ɔhɔle kɛ ɔkanwu belemgbunli wɔ ye sua ne nee ye azɛlɛ ne mɔ anwo.

english_verse: Meanwhile, the king was asking Gehazi the servant of Elisha about the amazing things Elisha had been doing.
translation_verse: Mekɛ ne anu ɛnee belemgbunli nee Yilaehya sonvolɛ Gɛheezae ɛlɛdi adwelie na yebiza ye kɛ, “Ka ninyɛne mgbole mɔɔ Yilaehya ɛyɛ la amuala kile me.”

english_verse: Some time later Elisha went to the capital city of Damascus to visit King Benhadad of Syria, who was sick. And when Benhadad was told he was there,
translation_verse: Akee Yilaehya rale Dɛmasekɛse. Selea Belemgbunli Bɛneheedade ɛnee ɛnde kpɔkɛ na bɛhanle bɛhilele ye kɛ, Yilaehya ɛra ɛkɛ.

english_verse: Hazael left with forty camel loads of the best things made in Damascus as a gift for Elisha. He found the prophet and said, “Your servant, King Benhadad, wants to know if he will get well.”
translation_verse: Yemɔti Hazeeyɛle vale Dɛmasekɛse ninyɛne dɔɔnwo wulowulale bɛ ahodoku nu zoale afunlumu abulanla na ɔvale ɔhɔyiale Yilaehya kɛ, “Wɔ dehelɛ, Belemgbunli Bɛneheedade ɛnde kpɔkɛ, na yezoa me kɛ membambiza saa ɔkɛde kpɔkɛ a.”

english_verse: “Tell him he will,” Elisha said to Hazael. “But the Lord has already told me that Benhadad will definitely die.”
translation_verse: Yilaehya buale kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛye ɛhile me kɛ ɔbawu noko kɔze ye kɛ, ɔbade kpɔkɛ bɔkɔɔ.”

english_verse: Elisha stared at him until Hazael was embarrassed, then Elisha began crying.
translation_verse: Akee Yilaehya nleanle Hazeeyɛle anyunlu dedee ɔmanle Hazeeyɛle ati zile aze, na Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ ne zunle.

english_verse: “Sir, why are you crying?” Hazael asked. Elisha answered, “Because I know the terrible things you will do to the people of Israel. You will burn down their walled cities and slaughter their young men. You will even crush the heads of their babies and rip open their pregnant women.”
translation_verse: Na Hazeeyɛle bizale ye kɛ, “Duzu ati a me menle akee ɛlɛsu a?” Yilaehya buale kɛ, “Ɔboalekɛ menwu ɛtane mɔɔ ɛbali wɔamaa Yizilayɛma la. Ɛbado senle wɔ bɛ aranemgbole ne mɔ anu, wɔahuhu bɛ mgbavolɛ nee ngakula kɔsɔɔti, na wɔatulutulu mraalɛ mɔɔ ɛva ɛkolɛ la anyalɛ.”

english_verse: “How could I ever do anything like that?” Hazael replied. “I'm only a servant and don't have that kind of power.” “Hazael, the Lord has told me that you will be the next king of Syria.”
translation_verse: Hazeeyɛle zele kɛ, “Medame, na mele duzu? Twea ralɛ mɔɔ le kɛ medame mɔɔ mendo ɛhwee la, mefa nienwu na meayɛ ɛhye?” Yilaehya buale kɛ, “Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛye ɛhile me kɛ wɔmɔ yɛɛ ɛbali belemgbunli wɔ Selea a.”

english_verse: Hazael went back to Benhadad and told him, “Elisha said that you will get well.”
translation_verse: Hazeeyɛle vi Yilaehya anwo ɛkɛ ne hɔle na belemgbunli ne bizale ye kɛ, “Duzu edwɛkɛ a Yilaehya hanle hilele wɔ a?” Hazeeyɛle buale ye kɛ, “Ɔzele me kɛ, ɛbade kpɔkɛ.”

english_verse: But the very next day, Hazael got a thick blanket; he soaked it in water and held it over Benhadad's face until he died. Hazael then became king. King Jehoram of Judah (
translation_verse: Noko aleɛ hyenle la, Hazeeyɛle vale kundu bɔle nzule nu vale hedale belemgbunli ne ati zo manle ye ɛbolɛ kpunle toonwo ɔwule. Na Hazeeyɛle lile Selea ebia ne. Dwuda Belemgbunli Gyɛhɔlam (

english_verse: So Jehoram and his cavalry marched to Zair, where the Edomite army surrounded him and his commanders. During the night he attacked the Edomites, but he was defeated, and his troops escaped to their homes.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Gyɛhɔlam vale ye ɛlɔnema mɔɔ fa ehwili ko la hɔle Zeeyɛ na nɔe ne bɛdwazole bɛhanle Yidɔmma mɔɔ ɛnee ɛbɔ ɛyia bɛ la senle manle bɛnriandile bɛhɔle bɛ azua nu.

english_verse: While Jehoram was king, the people of Edom rebelled and chose their own king.
translation_verse: Gyɛhɔlam mekɛ zo, Yidɔmma dele atua kɛ bɛnle Dwudama abo bieko; bɛdabɛ bɛziele bɛ belemgbunli na bɛlile bɛ ti anwo.

english_verse: Jehoram son of Jehoshaphat became king of Judah in Joram's fifth year as king of Israel, while Jehoshaphat was still king of Judah.
translation_verse: Yizilayɛ Belemgbunli Ehabe ara Dwɔlam lile ɛvolɛ nnu wɔ Yizilayɛ ebia ne azo la yɛɛ Gyɛhɔhyafate ara Gyɛhɔlam bɔle ɔ bo kɛ ɔdi belemgbunli wɔ Dwuda a.

english_verse: Jehoram disobeyed the Lord by doing wrong. He married Ahab's daughter and was as sinful as Ahab's family and the kings of Israel.
translation_verse: Ɔvale Yizilayɛ arelemgbunli agyakɛ na ɔbɔle Ehabe sua nu amra ɛbɛla ne bie, ɔluakɛ ɛnee ɔgya Ehabe ara raalɛ. Na ɔyɛle ɛtane ɔtiale Ɛdɛnkɛma.

english_verse: But the Lord refused to destroy Judah, because he had promised his servant David that someone from his family would always rule in Judah.
translation_verse: Noko ɛnee ɔnle Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛhulolɛ kɛ ɔkɛzɛkye Dwudama, ɔboalekɛ yebɔ ye akɛlɛ Devidi ɛwɔkɛ kɛ ɔ bo zo amra a bali ebia ne dahuu a.

english_verse: Everything else Jehoram did while he was king is written in The History of the Kings of Judah.
translation_verse: Nyɛleɛ mɔɔ Gyɛhɔlam yɛle nee gyima mɔɔ ɔlile la bɛhɛlɛ bɛ muala wɔ Dwuda Arelemgbunli Tetedwɛkɛ Mbuluku ne mɔ anu.

english_verse: Jehoram died and was buried beside his ancestors in Jerusalem. His son Ahaziah then became king. King Ahaziah of Judah (

english_verse: Ahaziah son of Jehoram became king of Judah in the twelfth year of Joram's rule in Israel.

english_verse: They quickly grabbed their coats and spread them out on the steps where Jehu was standing. Someone blew a trumpet, and everyone shouted, “Jehu is king!” Jehu Kills Joram and Ahaziah
translation_verse: Ɛkɛ ne ala Gyihu agɔnwo safohyenlema ne yeyele bɛ adɛladeɛ ne mɔ guale ɔ gyakɛ anu kɛ ɔtietia zolɛ. Akee bɛbɔle aweɛne ndendenle nu na bɛzele kɛ, “Bɛyɛ Gyihu belemgbunli!” Bɛhu Yizilayɛ Belemgbunli Dwɔlam

english_verse: When the guard in the watchtower at Jezreel saw Jehu and his men riding up, he shouted to the king, “I see a large group of men coming this way.” Joram ordered, “Send someone out to ask them if this is a friendly visit.”
translation_verse: Sinzavolɛ bie ɛnee gyi Gyɛzɛlii tawa ne azo na ɔnwunle Gyihu nee ye ɛlɔne ne mɔɔ ɛlɛba la. Ɔzele kɛ, “Menwu kɛ menli bie ɛlɛba.” Dwɔlam zele kɛ, “Maa sonla mɔɔ ze ɛkpɔnwɔ ka la ɛhɔyia bɛ na ɔbiza bɛ saa bɛlɛba ye anzonudwolɛ nu a.”

english_verse: One of the soldiers rode out and said to Jehu, “King Joram wants to know if this is a friendly visit.” “What's it to you?” Jehu asked. “Just stay behind me with the rest of my troops!” About the same time the guard in the watchtower said, “Your Majesty, the rider got there, but he isn't coming back.”
translation_verse: Yemɔti sonla vole ɛkpɔnwɔ zo yiale Gyihu na ɔbizale ye kɛ “Belemgbunli se membambiza bɛ saa bɛlɛba ye anzonudwolɛ nu a.” Gyihu zele ye kɛ, “Se di me nzi. Anzonudwolɛ a le duzu?” Sinzavolɛ ne manle belemgbunli dele kɛ, “Ahenle mɔɔ bɛzoanle ye la ɛdwu menli ne anwo lɔ, noko mennwu kɛ ɔlɛba.”

english_verse: So Joram sent out another rider, who rode up to Jehu and said, “The king wants to know if this is a friendly visit.” “What's it to you?” Jehu asked. “Just get behind me with the rest of my troops!”
translation_verse: Eza belemgbunli zoanle sonla fofolɛ na ɔdaye noko ɔyiale Gyihu nee ye ɛlɔne ne na ɔbizale bɛ saa bɛlɛba ye anzonudwolɛ nu a. Na Gyihu zele ye kɛ, “Se di me nzi. Anzonudwolɛ a le duzu?”

english_verse: The guard in the watchtower said, “Your Majesty, the rider got there, but he isn't coming back either. Wait a minute! That one man is a reckless chariot driver—it must be Jehu!”
translation_verse: Sinzavolɛ ne eza manle belemgbunli dele kɛ ahenle mɔɔ bɛzoanle ye la ɛdwu noko ɔmba. Akee ɔzele kɛ, “Ahenle mɔɔ nee ɛlɔne ne ɛlɛba la zɔho Gyihu, ɔluakɛ ɔlɛka ye konle ehwili ne kpole kpalɛ.”

english_verse: Joram commanded, “Get my chariot ready.” Then he and Ahaziah got in their chariots and rode out to meet Jehu. They all met on the land that had belonged to Naboth.
translation_verse: Belemgbunli Dwɔlam zele kɛ, “Bɛva me konle ehwili ne bɛrɛlɛ me.” Ɔvole nu yɛɛ Dwuda Belemgbunli Ehazaya ɔdaye ɔvole ye ɛdeɛ ne anu na bɛzile nu bɛhɔyiale Gyihu. Bɛyiale ye wɔ Neebɔto mɔɔ vi Gyɛzɛlii la egyinli ne anloa.

english_verse: Joram asked, “Jehu, is this a peaceful visit?” “How can there be peace?” Jehu asked. “Your mother Jezebel has caused everyone to worship idols and practice witchcraft.”
translation_verse: Dwɔlam bizale Gyihu kɛ, “Ɔle bɛtɛɛ ɔ?” Na Gyihu buale ye kɛ, “Kɛ ɔsi ɔyɛ bɛtɛɛ ɛ, wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɛ nli Gyɛzɛbɛle ɛva ye ayɛne nee awozonle ɛzonlenlɛ nu tuutuulilɛ ɛbɛla ɛyɛ maanle ye totɔɔ zɛhae la?”

english_verse: Jehu shot an arrow. It hit Joram between his shoulders, then it went through his heart and came out his chest. He fell over dead in his chariot.

english_verse: Ahaziah saw all of this happen and tried to escape to the town of Beth-Haggan, but Jehu caught up with him and shouted, “Kill him too!” So his troops shot Ahaziah with an arrow while he was on the road to Gur near Ibleam. He went as far as Megiddo, where he died.

english_verse: Ahaziah had become king of Judah in the eleventh year of the rule of Ahab's son Joram. Jehu Kills Jezebel
translation_verse: Ehazaya kali Dwuda ebia ne la ɛnee Dwɔlam ɛli ɛvolɛ bulu nee ko wɔ Yizilayɛ ebia ne azo. Bɛhu Belemgbunli Raalɛ Gyɛzɛbɛle

english_verse: Jehu headed toward Jezreel, and when Jezebel heard he was coming, she put on eye shadow and brushed her hair. Then she stood at the window, waiting for him to arrive.
translation_verse: Gyihu rale Gyɛzɛlii. Ɛnee Gyɛzɛbɛle ɛde mɔɔ ɛzi la ati ɔdole ɔ nye anzi na ɔyɛle ɔ ti kɛnlɛma bie na ɔ nye gyi nvɛnzɛlɛ ne anu ɔlɛnea gua ne azo lɔ.

translation_verse: Yemɔti kpanyinli ne mɔɔ nea belemgbunli awuke ne azo, mgbanyima ne mɔ yɛɛ menli mɔɔ nea Ehabe abo zo amra ne la bɔle nu zoanle manle bɛhɔzele Gyihu kɛ, “Yɛwɔ ɛ bo, yemɔti yɛbayɛ debie biala mɔɔ ɛkɛze yɛ la. Yɛnrɛzie awie biala belemgbunli, yɛ mɔɔ ɛdawɔ ɛnea a ɔle kpalɛ la.”

translation_verse: Gyihu zele ye ɛlɔnema mɔɔ ɔ nee bɛ lua la kɛ, “Bɛhye bɛ.” Bɛhyele bɛ na bɛ nee bɛ hɔle kuma bie mɔɔ zua azokoɛleɛ ne la anloa bɛhɔhunle bɛ muala. Bɛlua menli abulanla nee nwiɔ. Bɛangyakyi ko bɔbɔ. Bɛhu Ehabe anwo amra mɔɔ ɛha la amuala

translation_verse: Gyihu zile nu bieko kɛ ɔkɔ. Ɔlua adenle zo la Rilikabe ara Dwɔnadabe rayiale ye. Gyihu bizale ye ahye na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Wɔmɔ, yɛ mu nwiɔ yɛ adwenle le ko.
