translation_verse: Menli baka ninyɛne kpalɛ mɔɔ Tobaya ɛyɛ la anwo edwɛkɛ kile me na bɛahɔha mɔɔ menwɔha la bɛahile ye. Na ɔhɔle zolɛ ɔhɛlɛhɛlɛle me ngɛlata ɔbɔle me apo.

english_verse: Although Jerusalem covered a large area, not many people lived there, and no new houses had been built.
translation_verse: Gyɛlusalɛm le suakpole kpalɛ mɔɔ wale yɛɛ ɔtɛlɛ, noko menli mɔɔ wɔ zolɛ la anzo, yɛɛ azua dɔɔnwo ɛnle zolɛ.

english_verse: These are the names of the families of temple workers whose descendants returned: Ziha, Hasupha, Tabbaoth, Keros, Sia, Padon, Lebana, Hagaba, Shalmai, Hanan, Giddel, Gahar, Reaiah, Rezin, Nekoda, Gazzam, Uzza, Paseah, Besai, Meunim, Nephushesim, Bakbuk, Hakupha, Harhur, Bazlith, Mehida, Harsha, Barkos, Sisera, Temah, Neziah, and Hatipha.
translation_verse: Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua nu gyimayɛvoma mbusua ekpulike ekpulike mɔɔ vi nlɔnu ziale rale la ɛne: Zaeha, Hasufa, Tabeeyo, Kilɔso, Saya, Peedɔn, Lɛbeena, Hagaba, Hyalemae, Heenan, Gedɛle, Geehaa, Riliaya, Rilizen, Nɛkoda, Gazam, Ɛza, Pasia, Bisae, Mɛyunem, Nɛfɛhyɛsem, Bakebɛke, Hakufa, Haahɛ, Bazelete, Mɛhaeda, Haahya, Baakɔso, Sesɛla, Teema, Nɛzaya, Hataefa.

english_verse: Here are the names of Solomon's servants whose descendants returned: Sotai, Sophereth, Perida, Jaala, Darkon, Giddel, Shephatiah, Hattil, Pochereth Hazzebaim, and Amon.
translation_verse: Sɔlɔmɔn sonvolɛma abo zo amra mbusua ekpulike ekpulike mɔɔ vi nlɔnu ziale rale la ɛne: Soteeyae, Sofɛlɛte, Pɛlaeda, Gyeeyala, Daakɔn, Gedɛle, Hyɛfataya, Hatele, Pokɛlɛte, Hazɛbeeyem yɛɛ Amɔn.

english_verse: The families of Hobaiah, Hakkoz, and Barzillai could not prove they were priests. The ancestor of the family of Barzillai had married the daughter of Barzillai from Gilead and had taken his wife's family name. But the records of these three families could not be found, and none of them were allowed to serve as priests.
translation_verse: Sɛlɛvolɛma mbusua ekpulike ekpulike ɛhye mɔ hɔkpondɛle bɛ nlenya mɔ aluma wɔ mbusua mbuluku ne mɔ anu na bɛannwu bɛ aluma nuhua, yemɔti bɛyele bɛ bɛvile sɛlɛvolɛlilɛ ne anu, ɔluakɛ bɛ nwo ɛnde. Bɛmɛ a le Hɔbaya, Hakɔzo yɛɛ Bazileeyae .

english_verse: In fact, the governor told them, “You cannot eat the food offered to God until he lets us know if you really are priests.”
translation_verse: Dwuu amɛnlado ne zele bɛ kɛ ɔnle kpalɛ kɛ bɛdi Nyamenle aleɛ nwuanzanwuanza ne bie kɔkpula kɛ sɛlɛvolɛ bie mɔɔ kola fa “Yulem nee Tɛmem” ne yɛ gyima la kɛra la.

english_verse: And so, by the seventh month, priests, Levites, temple guards, musicians, workers, and many of the ordinary people had settled in the towns of Judah.
translation_verse: Na akee Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti, sɛlɛvolɛma, Livaema, Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne sinzavolɛma, edwɛndolɛma, Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua nu sonvolɛma yɛɛ Yizilayɛma mɔɔ hale la amuala hɔdɛnlanle aze wɔ bɛ azua ne mɔ azo.

english_verse: Ezra stood on a high wooden platform that had been built for this occasion. Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Uriah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah were standing to his right, while Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hash Baddanah, Zechariah, and Meshullam were standing to his left.
translation_verse: Ɛzela gyinlanle sɛlɛdwee bie mɔɔ ayia ne ati bɛva ndaboa bɛbo la azo a gengale Mɛla ne a. Matetaya, Hyima, Anaya, Yulaya, Helekaya yɛɛ Meeyasaya gyinlanle ɔ sa fema zo, yɛɛ Pɛdaya, Maehyeeyɛle, Malekaya, Hahyɛm, Hahyebadeena, Zɛkalaya, yɛɛ Mɛhyɛlam gyinlanle ye bɛne zo.

english_verse: Ezra was up on the high platform, where he could be seen by everyone, and when he opened the book, all the people stood up.
translation_verse: Ɛzela gyinlanle sɛlɛdwee ne azo la ɛnee ɔ nwo zo ɛhɔ anwuma ɛdɛla bɛ. Mɔɔ ɔbukele Mɛla Buluku ne anu ala la, bɛ kɔsɔɔti bɛdwazole bɛgyinlanle.

english_verse: Ezra praised the great Lord God, and they lifted their hands, shouting “Amen! Amen!” Then they bowed with their faces to the ground and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Na Ɛzela zele kɛ, “Bɛye Ɛdɛnkɛma, Nyamenle Bedevinli ne ayɛlɛ.” Menli ne kɔsɔɔti manle bɛ sa zo na bɛliele zolɛ, “Amen, Amen.” Akee bɛbɔle bɛ ti aze na bɛbutubutule bɛ nye aze bɛyeyɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma.

english_verse: After this, the Levites Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodiah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, and Pelaiah went among the people, explaining the meaning of what Ezra had read.
translation_verse: Bɛgengale buluku ne mɔɔ Nyamenle Mɛla ne wɔ nu la bɛhilele menli ne; bɛhilehilele nuhua wienyi bɛhilele bɛ, amaa bɛade ɔ bo kpalɛ.

english_verse: The people started crying when God's Law was read to them. Then Nehemiah the governor, Ezra the priest and teacher, and the Levites who had been teaching the people all said, “This is a special day for the Lord your God. So don't be sad and don't cry!”
translation_verse: Mɔɔ menli ne dele mɔɔ Mɛla ne se la, debie hwenle bɛ nu na bɛzunle. Na Sɛlɛvolɛ Nihɛmaya, mɔɔ le amɛnlado ne, nee mɛla kilehilevolɛ Ɛzela, nee Livaema mɔɔ hilehilele menli ne la zele bɛ kɛ, “Ɛnɛ kenle ye le nwuanzanwuanza maa Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne. Bɛmmasu yɛɛ bɛmmadi nyane biala.”

english_verse: Nehemiah told the people, “Enjoy your good food and wine and share some with those who didn't have anything to bring. Don't be sad! This is a special day for the Lord, and he will make you happy and strong.”
translation_verse: Akee Nihɛmaya zele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛhɔ sua nu na bɛhɔlie bɛ nye; bɛli debie mɔɔ yɛ fɛ na bɛnlo nwanye fɛlɛko. Bɛmaa menli mɔɔ ɛnlɛ bie la bie. Ɔluakɛ ɛnɛ le Ɛdɛnkɛma kenle nwuanzanwuanza. Bɛmmadi nyane, ɔluakɛ fɛlɛkolilɛ ne mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma fa maa la le bɛ anwosesebɛ.”

english_verse: The Levites encouraged the people by saying, “This is a sacred day, so don't worry or mourn!”
translation_verse: Na Livaema ne gogole menli ne amuala ahonle zele kɛ, “Bɛyɛ ngungoonwu, ɔluakɛ ɛnɛ kenle ye le kenle nwuanzanwuanza; bɛmmadi nyane.”

english_verse: When the people returned to their homes, they celebrated by eating and drinking and by sharing their food with those in need, because they had understood what had been read to them. Celebrating the Festival of Shelters
translation_verse: Yemɔti menli ne kɔsɔɔti hɔle sua nu hɔlile debie na bɛnlonle nwanye. Bɛ nee menli mɔɔ ɛnlɛ bie la hyɛle mɔɔ bɛlɛ la na bɛlile fɛlɛko, ɔboalekɛ bɛdele edwɛkɛ ne mɔɔ bɛgengale bɛhilele bɛ la abo. Kpɔda Bo Ɛdɛnlanlɛ Ɛvoyia ne

english_verse: On the second day of the seventh month, the leaders of all the family groups came together with the priests and the Levites, so Ezra could teach them the Law
translation_verse: Ye kenle nwiɔ ne azo, mbusua mgbanyinli, sɛlɛvolɛma, yɛɛ Livaema bɔle nu hɔle sɛlɛvolɛ Ɛzela ɛkɛ ne kɛ bɛkazukoa mɛla ne.

english_verse: that the Lord had given to Moses. They learned from the Law that the people of Israel were to live in shelters when they celebrated the festival in the seventh month of the year.
translation_verse: Na bɛnwunle kɛ mɛla ne mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma luale Mosisi anwo zo vale manle bɛ la, bɛhɛlɛ ye nuhua kɛ, saa siane nsuu Ɛvoyia ne dwu a ɔwɔ kɛ Yizilayɛma tɛnlɛdɛnla kpɔda kpɔda bo,

english_verse: They also learned that they were to go into the woods and gather branches of leafy trees such as olives, myrtles, and palms for making these shelters.
translation_verse: na bɛbɔ ye nolo wɔ Gyɛlusalɛm nee azuamgbole nee ngyikyi kɔsɔɔti azo kɛ, “Bɛhɔ awoka ne mɔ azo bɛhɔbubu ɔlivi nya, ɛbɔ nu ɔlivi nya, mbaka nya mɔɔ kola maa alubo, yɛɛ arɛlɛ nee mraalɛ kukue mrɛlakɛ bɛrasisi kpɔda kpɔda, kɛmɔ bɛhɛlɛ ye wɔ Mɛla ne anu la.”

english_verse: So the people gathered branches and made shelters on the flat roofs of their houses, in their yards, in the courtyard of the temple, and in the open areas around the Water Gate and Ephraim Gate.
translation_verse: Yemɔti menli ne hɔpɛle mrɛlakɛ, bɛbubule nya nya bɛrasisile kpɔda kpɔda wɔ bɛ azua ne mɔ ati zo, wɔ bɛ awuke ne mɔ anu, wɔ Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne alie wienyi ne anwo yɛɛ ɛleka kpatawienyi ne mɔ mɔɔ wɔ Nzule Anlenkɛ Kpole ne nee Yifelaem Anlenkɛ Kpole ne mɔ anyunlu la.

english_verse: Everyone who had returned from Babylonia built shelters. They lived in them and joyfully celebrated the Festival of Shelters for the first time since the days of Joshua son of Nun.
translation_verse: Bɛ kɔsɔɔti mɔɔ bɛvi nlɔnu bɛrale la sisile kpɔda dɛnlanle ɔ bo. Ɔvi Nɛn ara Dwɔhyua mekɛ zo toonwo mɔɔ radwule mekɛ zɔhane la, bɔ zo mɔɔ bɛyɛ ɛhye bie ɔ. Yemɔti awie biala anwo zandele ye na ɔ nye liele.

english_verse: On each of the first seven days of the festival, Ezra read to the people from God's Law. Then on the eighth day, everyone gathered for worship, just as the Law had said they must.
translation_verse: Ɔvi kenle ko zɔhane, alehyenlɛ biala Ɛzela gengale Nyamenle Mɛla buluku ne hilele menli ne. Bɛlile ɛvoyia ne kenle nsuu. Ye kenle mɔtwɛ ne azo, kɛmɔ mɛla ne se la, bɛyiale bɛyɛle nzɛlɛlɛ na bɛvale ɛvoyialilɛ ne bɛrale awieleɛ.

english_verse: On the twenty-fourth day of the seventh month, the people of Israel went without eating, and they dressed in sackcloth and threw dirt on their heads to show their sorrow.
translation_verse: Siane ko ne ala anu, ye kenle abulanwiɔ nee nna ne azo, Yizilayɛma hedale ɛrele, vale mgbane wɔzale bɛ nwo, na bɛyiale nu bɛhyele ɛhɔne bɛlile bɛ ɛtane ne mɔ anwo nyane.

english_verse: They refused to let foreigners join them, as they met to confess their sins and the sins of their ancestors.
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma ne hwenle bɛ nwo vile nyɛvolɛ ne mɔ avinli na bɛhanle bɛ ɛtane ne mɔ nee bɛ ze mɔ ninyɛndane ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti bɛdole gua.

english_verse: For three hours they stood and listened to the Law of the Lord their God, and then for the next three hours they confessed their sins and worshiped the Lord.
translation_verse: Bɛgyinlanle nzisi bɛgengale Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne Mɛla ne bɛhilele bɛ kɛyɛ dɔnehwele nsa. Bɛvale dɔnehwele nsa noko bɛhanle bɛ ɛtane ne mɔ na bɛyeyɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne.

english_verse: Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani stood on the special platform for the Levites and prayed aloud to the Lord their God.
translation_verse: Livaema sɛlɛdwee ne, menli mɔɔ gyinlanle zolɛ la a le ɛhye mɔ: Gyɛhyua, Beenae, Kademeɛle, Hyɛbanaya, Bɛnae, Hyɛlibaya, Beenae yɛɛ Kɛneenae. Bɛvale ɛnelɛ kpole bɛzɛlɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne.

english_verse: Then the Levites Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabneiah, Sherebiah, Hodiah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah said: “Stand and shout praises to your Lord, the eternal God! Praise his wonderful name, though he is greater than words can express.” The People Pray
translation_verse: Akee Livaema ɛhye mɔ: Gyɛhyua, Kademeɛle, Beenae, Hahyabenaya, Hodaya, Hyɛlibaya, Hyɛbanaya yɛɛ Pɛtahaya zele kɛ, “Bɛdwazo bɛye Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne ayɛlɛ; bɛye ye ayɛlɛ dahuu! Kanza dasanli biala ayɛlɛyelɛ le ekyi bɔbɔ a, awie biala ɛye ye duma nwuanzanwuanza ne ayɛlɛ.” Ɛtanehanlɛ nzɛlɛlɛ ne

english_verse: You alone are the Lord, Creator of the heavens and all the stars, Creator of the earth and those who live on it, Creator of the ocean and all its creatures. You are the source of life, praised by the stars that fill the heavens.
translation_verse: Na Yizilayɛma amuala yɛle nzɛlɛlɛ ɛhye: “Wɔmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma, ɛ ngomekye ala yɛɛ ɛle Ɛdɛnkɛma a; wɔmɔ yɛɛ ɛbɔle anwuma nee anwomanyunlu nwɔlɔra a. Wɔmɔ yɛɛ ɛbɔle azɛlɛ nee zolɛ ninyɛne, nyevile nee nuhua ninyɛne a; wɔmɔ yɛɛ ɛmanle bɛ kɔsɔɔti ngoane a. Anwuma tumivolɛma kɔsɔɔti bɔ bɛ ti aze sonle wɔ.

english_verse: You are the Lord our God, the one who chose Abram— you brought him from Ur in Babylonia and named him Abraham.
translation_verse: Wɔmɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma Nyamenle yɛɛ ɛyele Ebelam, ɛyele ye ɛvile Yule mɔɔ wɔ Babelonia na ɛhakyile ye duma ɛvɛlɛle ye Ebileham.

english_verse: Because he was faithful, you made an agreement to give his descendants the land of the Canaanites and Hittites, of the Amorites and Perizzites, and of the Jebusites and Girgashites. Now you have kept your promise, just as you always do.
translation_verse: Ɛnwunle kɛ ɔdi nɔhalɛ ɔmaa wɔ, na ɛ nee ye yɛle ngyekyeleɛ. Ɛbɔle ye ɛwɔkɛ kɛ ɛkɛva Keenama, Hɛtema, yɛɛ Amɔlema, Pɛlɛzema nee Gyibɛsema, yɛɛ Gɛgahyema azɛlɛ ne mɔ ɛkɛmaa ɔ bo zo amra. Ɛlile wɔ ɛwɔkɛ zo, ɔboalekɛ ɛdi nɔhalɛ.

english_verse: When our ancestors were in Egypt, you saw their suffering; when they were at the Red Sea, you heard their cry for help.
translation_verse: “Ɛnwunle kɛ yɛ mgbanyinli zile nwunle amaneɛ wɔ Yigyibiti, ɛdele bɛ ɛzunlɛ wɔ Ndɔ Nyevile ne anloa na ɛliele bɛ.

english_verse: You knew that the King of Egypt and his officials and his nation had mistreated your people. So you worked fearsome miracles against the Egyptians and earned a reputation that still remains.
translation_verse: Ɛyɛle nwanwane ninyɛne ɛhilele Yigyibiti belemgbunli ne, ɛyɛle bie ɛhilele ye mgbanyima nee menli mɔɔ wɔ azɛlɛ ne azo la, ɔboalekɛ ɛze kɛ bɛzile bɛsisile wɔ menli ne la. Na ɛliele duma ne mɔɔ ɛnɛ nee ɛnɛ ɛtɛdɛ la.

english_verse: You divided the deep sea, and your people walked through on dry land. But you tossed their enemies in, and they sank down like a heavy stone.
translation_verse: Ɛkpakyele adenle ɛdole nyevile ne anu, na ɛmanle bɛluale azɛlɛ resee zo bɛpɛle; menli mɔɔ ɛlɛfoa bɛ la wule azule buma ne anu, bɛnlomanle kɛ bolɛ wɔ nyevile ne mɔɔ ɛzɛkye la anu.

english_verse: Each day you led your people with a thick cloud, and at night you showed the way with a flaming fire.
translation_verse: Ɛvale amungu bolomolo ɛlile bɛ nyunlu alehyenlɛ, ɛvale senle bolonwonwo ɛhilele bɛ adenle aledwolɛ.

english_verse: At Sinai you came down from heaven, and you gave your people good laws and teachings that are fair and honest.
translation_verse: Ɛvi anwuma ɛdwule Boka Saenae azo, ɛdendɛle ɛhilele wɔ menli ne wɔ boka ne azo; ɛmanle bɛ nɔhalɛ mɛla nee ngyehyɛlɛ na ɛhilehilele bɛ kɛ bɛli zo.

english_verse: You commanded them to respect your holy Sabbath, and you instructed your servant Moses to teach them your laws.
translation_verse: Ɛhilele bɛ kɛ bɛzie Ɛnwomenlelielɛ Kenle ne nwuanzanwuanza, na ɛluale wɔ sonvolɛ Mosisi anwo zo ɛvale mɛla ne ɛmanle bɛ.

english_verse: When they were hungry, you sent bread from heaven, and when they were thirsty, you let water flow from a rock. Then you commanded them to capture the land that you had solemnly promised. *
translation_verse: “Ɛhɔne hunle bɛ, ɛmanle bɛ anwuma kpanwo, nzuhɔne hunle bɛ, ɛmanle bɛ bolɛ nu nzukpa. Ɛzele bɛ kɛ bɛhɔva azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ ɛhanle ndane ɛvale ɛmanle bɛ la.

english_verse: Our stubborn ancestors refused to obey— they forgot about the miracles you had worked for them, and they were determined to return to Egypt and become slaves again.
translation_verse: Noko yɛ mgbanyima yɛle mgbanyizonle nee anzosesebɛ, na bɛkpole kɛ bɛnrɛli wɔ mɛla ne mɔ azo.

english_verse: not even when they made an idol shaped like a calf and insulted you by claiming, “This is the god who rescued us from Egypt.”
translation_verse: Bɛyɛle ɛnlankɛ ananze, na bɛzele kɛ ɔle bɛ nyamenle; kɛ yemɔ a ɔyele bɛ ɔvile Yigyibiti a. Bɛhanle wɔ ɛya kpole!

english_verse: Because of your great mercy, you never abandoned them in the desert. And you always guided them with a cloud by day and a fire at night.
translation_verse: Noko wɔamkpo bɛ wɔ fienemgbole ne anu, ɔluakɛ wɔ anwunvɔnezelɛ ne le kpole, Wɔanye amungu bolomolo ne anzɛɛ senle bolonwonwo ne mɔɔ hilele bɛ adenle ewiazo nee nɔɔzo la.

english_verse: Your gentle Spirit instructed them, and you gave them manna to eat and water to drink.
translation_verse: Wɔ kpalɛ ti ɛvale wɔ Sunsum ne ɛhilehilele bɛ, ɛvale mana ɛlile bɛ adane, ɛmanle bɛ nzukpa bɛnlonle.

english_verse: You took good care of them, and for forty years they never lacked a thing. Their clothes didn't wear out, and their feet were never swollen.
translation_verse: Ɛvolɛ abulanla, wɔ fienemgbole ne anu, ɛmanle bɛ debie biala mɔɔ bɛhyianle nwolɛ la; bɛ ndanlɛ antete yɛɛ bɛ gyakɛ amkpomgba ɛlɛ.

english_verse: You brought them into the land that you had promised their ancestors, and you blessed their nation with people that outnumbered the stars in the sky.
translation_verse: Ɛmanle bɛ mralɛ dɔɔnwo kɛ anwomanyunlu nwɔlɔra, na ɛmanle bɛhonle bɛvale maanle ne mɔɔ ɛvale ɛbɔle bɛ nlenya mɔ ɛwɔkɛ la.

english_verse: Then their descendants conquered the land. You helped them defeat the kings and nations and treat their enemies however they wished.
translation_verse: Bɛlile Keenama anwo zo konim bɛvale azɛlɛ ne, ɛvole menli mɔɔ wɔ ɛkɛ ne la akɔme zo; ɛmanle wɔ menli ne tumi bɛvale Keena arelemgbunli nee menli bɛyɛle mɔɔ bɛdabɛ bɛkulo la.

english_verse: They captured strong cities and rich farmland; they took furnished houses, as well as cisterns, vineyards, olive orchards, and numerous fruit trees. They ate till they were satisfied, and they celebrated your abundant blessings.
translation_verse: Wɔ menli ne mɔ honle vale ninyɛne ɛhye mɔ: azuamgbole mɔɔ bɛhye nwolɛ, azɛlɛ mɔɔ kye aleɛ, azua mɔɔ anwonyia ɛyiyi bɛ, bula mɔɔ bɛbɔ, ɔlivi mbaka, mbaka mɔɔ so ma, yɛɛ vanye tola. Bɛlile debie biala mɔɔ bɛkulo la na bɛyɛle mbelane, bɛlile ninyɛne kpalɛ mɔɔ ɛmanle bɛ la kɔsɔɔti anwo fɛlɛko.

english_verse: In spite of this, they rebelled and disobeyed your laws. They killed your prophets, who warned them to turn back to you, and they cursed your name.
translation_verse: “Wɔ menli ne dele ɛ nwo atua na bɛandie wɔ aneɛ, bɛhakyile bɛ nzi bɛzile wɔ mɛla ne. Bɛhunle Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛma mɔɔ bɔle bɛ kɔkɔ, na bɛzele bɛ kɛ bɛzia bɛdoa wɔ la; bɛbɔle munzule kpole!

english_verse: So you handed them over to their enemies, who treated them terribly. But in their sufferings, they begged you to help. From heaven you listened to their prayers and because of your great mercy, you sent leaders to rescue them.
translation_verse: Yemɔti ɛmanle bɛ kpɔvolɛma lile bɛ nwo zo konim, na bɛziele bɛ. Wɔ bɛ amaneɛnwunlɛ nu, bɛzɛlɛle wɔ moalɛ, na ɛliele zolɛ wɔ anwuma lɔ. Wɔ anwunvɔnezelɛ ne kpole ti, ɛmanle bɛ mgbanyima ɛmanle bɛlile bɛ ti, na bɛliele bɛ bɛvile bɛ kpɔvolɛma asa anu.

english_verse: But when they were at peace, they would turn against you, and you would hand them over to their enemies. Then they would beg for help, and because you are merciful, you rescued them over and over again.
translation_verse: Anzonudwolɛ rale, na bɛyɛle ɛtane bɛtiale wɔ bieko, na eza ɛmanle bɛ kpɔvolɛma lile bɛ nwo zo konim. Noko mɔɔ bɛvule bɛ nwo na bɛzɛlɛle la, ɛdele bɛ ne wɔ anwuma lɔ, na mekɛ dɔɔnwo ne ala ɔlua wɔ anwunvɔnezelɛ ne kpole ne ati, ɛliele bɛ.

english_verse: You warned them to turn back and discover true life by obeying your laws. But they stubbornly refused and continued to sin.
translation_verse: Ɛbɔle bɛ kɔkɔ kɛ bɛli wɔ ngilehilelɛ ne mɔ azo, na mgbanyizonle nu ala bɛkpole wɔ mɛla nee wɔ ngyehyɛlɛ ne mɔ; noko wɔ mɛla zo ɛlilɛ ne a le ngoane adenle ne a. Adubɛnwo nee anzosesebɛ nu, bɛkpole kɛ bɛnrɛli zolɛ.

english_verse: For years, you were patient, and your Spirit warned them with messages spoken by your prophets. Still they refused to listen, and you handed them over to their enemies.
translation_verse: Ɛbɔle bɛ kɔkɔ abotane nu ɛvolɛ biala, ɛluale wɔ Sunsum ne azo ɛmanle wɔ kpɔmanvolɛma dendɛle, na wɔ menli ne yɛle ateakpaso; yemɔti ɛmanle maanle maanle lile bɛ nwo zo konim.

english_verse: But you are merciful and kind, and so you never forgot them or let them be destroyed.
translation_verse: Noko, kɛmɔ wɔ anwunvɔnezelɛ ne le kpole la ati, wɔamkpo bɛ yɛɛ wɔanzɛkye bɛ. Ɛle ɛlolɛ nee anwunvɔnezelɛ Nyamenle.

english_verse: Our God, you are powerful, fearsome, and faithful, always true to your word. So please keep in mind the terrible sufferings of our people, kings, leaders, priests, and prophets, from the time Assyria ruled until this very day.
translation_verse: “O Nyamenle, yɛ Nyamenle, ɛle kpole! Ɛ nwo yɛ ɛzulolɛ, ɛle tumivolɛ! Ɛsie wɔ ngyekyeleɛ ɛwɔkɛ ne mɔ nɔhalɛ nu. Ɔvi mekɛ mɔɔ Aselea arelemgbunli sisile yɛ badwu ɛnɛ, yɛnwu amaneɛ dɔɔnwo! Yɛ arelemgbunli, yɛ mgbanyima, yɛ sɛlɛvolɛma nee yɛ Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛma, Yɛ mgbanyinli nee yɛ menli ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti ɛnwu amaneɛ. Kakye yɛ na yɛnwu amaneɛ somaa!

english_verse: You have always been fair when you punished us for our sins.
translation_verse: Ɛdi benle kɛ wɔhwe yɛ nzo a; yɛyɛ ɛtane bɔbɔ ɛdeɛ, noko wɔli nɔhalɛ.

english_verse: Our kings and leaders, our priests and ancestors have never obeyed your commands or heeded your warnings.
translation_verse: Yɛ arelemgbunli, yɛ mgbanyima nee yɛ sɛlɛvolɛma, yɛɛ yɛ mgbanyinli anli wɔ mɛla ne azo. Bɛandie wɔ mɛla ne mɔ yɛɛ bɛande wɔ kɔkɔbɔlɛ ne.

english_verse: You blessed them with a kingdom and with an abundance of rich, fertile land, but they refused to worship you or turn from their evil.
translation_verse: Bɛanzonle wɔ wɔ bɛ maanle ye anu. Bɛannwu boɛ kpole ne mɔɔ ɛyɛle bɛ la, na yeayɛ azɛlɛ kpandaanwo ne mɔɔ kye aleɛ la, yɛɛ bɛandwe bɛ nwo bɛanvi ɛtane nwo.

english_verse: Now we are slaves in this fruitful land you gave to our ancestors.
translation_verse: Ɛnɛ yɛyɛ ahanra wɔ maanle mɔɔ ɛvale ɛmanle yɛ nlenya mɔ la anu, wɔ azɛlɛ ye mɔɔ kye aleɛ maa yɛ la azo.

english_verse: Its plentiful harvest is taken by kings you placed over us because of our sins. Our suffering is unbearable, because they do as they wish to us and our livestock. The People Make an Agreement
translation_verse: Aleɛ mɔɔ azɛlɛ ne maa la kɔ arelemgbunli ne mɔ mɔɔ sie yɛ la ɛkɛ, ɔboalekɛ yɛyɛ ɛtane. Bɛfa yɛ nee yɛ nlankɛ bɛyɛ mɔɔ bɛdabɛ bɛkulo la, yɛwɔ nyane nu kpole!” Menli ne yɛ ngyehyɛlɛ

english_verse: And so, a firm agreement was made that had the official approval of the leaders, the Levites, and priests.
translation_verse: Ɔlua ninyɛne ɛhye mɔ kɔsɔɔti mɔɔ ɛsisi la ati, yɛdayɛ Yizilayɛma, yɛyɛ ngyehyɛlɛ ɛhye, na yɛ mgbanyima, yɛ Livaema nee yɛ sɛlɛvolɛma ava bɛ sa awula ɔ bo.

english_verse: Seraiah, Azariah, Jeremiah, Pashhur, Amariah, Malchijah, Hattush, Shebaniah, Malluch, Harim, Meremoth, Obadiah, Daniel, Ginnethon, Baruch, Meshullam, Abijah, Mijamin, Maaziah, Bilgai, and Shemaiah.
translation_verse: Sɛlɛvolɛma: Sɛlaya, Azalaya, Gyɛlɛmaya, Pahyɛ, Amalaya, Malekaya, Hatɛhye, Hyɛbanaya, Malɛke, Hɛlem, Mɛlɛmo, Obadaya, Daneɛle, Genɛtɔn, Bɛlɛke, Mɛhyɛlam, Abaegya, Maegyamen, Meeyazaya, Belegeeyae, yɛɛ Hyɛmaya.

english_verse: All of us, including priests, Levites, temple guards, singers, temple workers and leaders, together with our wives and children, have separated ourselves from the foreigners in this land and now enter into an agreement with a complete understanding of what we are doing. And so, we now place ourselves under the curse of the Lord our God, if we fail to obey his laws and teachings that were given to us by his servant Moses.
translation_verse: yɛ nee yɛ mgbanyima yɛbɔ nuhua yɛdi amonle, kɛ saa yɛbulu zolɛ a munzule ɛha yɛ, na yɛse kɛ, yɛbali Nyamenle Mɛla ne mɔɔ ɔluale ye sonvolɛ Mosisi anwo zo ɔvale ɔmanle yɛ la azo; yɛbali mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma, yɛ Awulae ne kɛze yɛ biala la, yɛɛ yɛbali mɛla ne nee ngyehyɛlɛ ne mɔ azo.

english_verse: We won't buy goods or grain on the Sabbath or on any other sacred day, not even from foreigners. Every seven years we will let our fields rest, and we will cancel all debts.
translation_verse: Saa menli zɔhane mɔ bie fa bɛ ninyɛne adɔne ba gua wɔ Ɛnwomenlelielɛ Kenle ne anzɛɛ kenle nwuanzanwuanza nu a, yɛnrɛdɔ. Ɛvolɛ mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nsuu la biala yɛnrɛzo ɛya wɔ azɛlɛ ye azo, yɛɛ yɛbapɛ kakɛ biala mɔɔ wɔ ɛkɛ ne la anu.

english_verse: Once a year we will each donate a small amount of silver to the temple of our God.
translation_verse: Ɛvolɛ biala yɛ nuhua ko biala ɔwɔ kɛ tua dwɛtɛ fufule tone nu gelamo nnu, amaa bɛava bɛanlea Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne.

english_verse: This is to pay for the sacred bread, as well as for the daily sacrifices and special sacrifices such as those offered on the Sabbath and during the New Moon Festival and the other festivals. It will also pay for the sacrifices to forgive our sins and for all expenses connected with the worship of God in the temple.
translation_verse: Yɛbava ninyɛne yɛara yɛamaa bɛava bɛayɛ ɛhye mɔ wɔ Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu bɛamaa Nyamenle: kpanwo nwuanzanwuanza ne, dahuu aleɛ ma azubɔdeɛ ne, nane mɔɔ kenle ko biala bɛbayela bɛabɔ azu la, Ɛnwomenlelielɛ Kenle ne azubɔlɛ ninyɛne, Siane Fofolɛ ɛvoyialilɛ ninyɛne, yɛɛ azubɔlɛ nwuanzanwuanza mɔɔ ɛha la anwo ninyɛne, azubɔlɛ mɔɔ bɛfa bɛanrinzi Yizilayɛma ɛtane ne mɔ la anwo ninyɛne, yɛɛ debie biala mɔɔ bɛhyia nwolɛ wɔ Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu la.

english_verse: We have decided that the families of priests, Levites, and ordinary people will supply firewood for the temple each year, so that sacrifices can be offered on the altar, just as the Lord our God has commanded.
translation_verse: Ɛvolɛ biala, yɛdayɛ Yizilayɛma, sɛlɛvolɛma, yɛɛ Livaema, yɛbagua nzeleba yɛanwu mbusua mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ fa ɛyɛne ba maa bɛfa bɛyela nyɛmoa mɔɔ bɛfa bɛabɔ azu bɛamaa Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛ Nyamenle ne, kɛmɔ mɛla ne kile la.

english_verse: Each year we will bring to the temple the first part of our harvest of grain and fruit.
translation_verse: Ɛvolɛ biala yɛbava abɛlɛ mɔɔ yɛkɛlumua yɛkɛbu nee ma biala mɔɔ yɛkɛlumua yɛkɛde la yɛahɔ Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu kɛ azubɔdeɛ.

english_verse: We will bring our first-born sons and the first-born males of our herds and flocks and offer them to the priests who serve in the temple, because this is what is written in God's Law.
translation_verse: Belamunli ralɛ nrenya biala mɔɔ yɛkɛwo ye la, yɛbava ye yɛahɔ Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu yɛahɔmaa sɛlɛvolɛma ne yɛamaa bɛadu ye bɛamaa Nyamenle, kɛmɔ Mɛla ne kile la. Eza yɛbadu yɛ ɛnlankɛ, boane, yɛɛ abɔnkye ralɛ biala mɔɔ bɛkɛlumua bɛkɛwo ye la yɛamaa Nyamenle.

english_verse: To the priests in the temple of our God, we will bring the bread dough from the first harvest, together with our best fruit, and an offering of new wine and olive oil. We will bring ten percent of our grain harvest to those Levites who are responsible for collecting it in our towns.
translation_verse: Ɛvolɛ biala yɛbava abɛlɛ mɔɔ bɛkɛlumua bɛkɛbu la ɛdɔkɛ nee nwolɛ ninyɛne mɔɔ le kɛ nwanye, ɔlivi nwole yɛɛ ma ngakyile yɛahɔmaa sɛlɛvolɛma mɔɔ wɔ Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu la yɛamaa bɛava bɛabɔ azu. Livaema mɔɔ dielie ninyɛne ngyɛnu bulu ɛkpɔ ngoko wɔ namunamu ɛya avule ne mɔ anu la, yɛbava yɛ bɛyɔba ngyɛnu bulu ɛkpɔ ngoko ne mɔ yɛahɔmaa bɛ.

english_verse: A priest from the family of Aaron must be there when we give this to the Levites. Then the Levites will put one tenth of this part in the temple storeroom,
translation_verse: Saa bɛlɛdielie ngyɛnu bulu ɛkpɔ ngoko ne mɔ a, ɔwɔ kɛ sɛlɛvolɛma mɔɔ le Aalɔn abo zo amra la nee Livaema dua nwolɛ, yɛɛ ɔwɔ kɛ Livaema fa Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu ngyɛnu bulu ɛkpɔ ko ne kɔsie Ɛzonlenlɛ sua ne ninyɛnezielɛ ɛleka ne.

english_verse: which is also the place for the sacred objects used by the priests, the temple guards, and the singers. Levites and everyone else must bring their gifts of grain, wine, and olive oil to this room. We will not neglect the temple of our God.
translation_verse: Ɔwɔ kɛ Yizilayɛma nee Livaema fa abɛlɛ, nwanye yɛɛ ɔlivi nwole mɔɔ bɛ nee ye kɛra la kɔ ninyɛnezielɛ ɛleka ne mɔɔ bɛsie Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne ahyɛnze ne mɔ nu la nee ɛleka mɔɔ sɛlɛvolɛma mɔɔ wɔ gyima nu, Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne sinzavolɛma nee edwɛndolɛma ne mɔ wɔ la. Yɛnrɛbu yɛ nye yɛnrɛgua yɛ Nyamenle Sua ne azo.

english_verse: The nation's leaders and their families settled in Jerusalem. But there was room for only one out of every ten of the remaining families, and so they asked God to show them who would live there.
translation_verse: Dwuu mgbanyima ne mɔ dɛnlanle Gyɛlusalɛm, na menli mɔɔ hale la, bɛguale nzeleba, amaa bɛahyɛ abusua biala anu ekpunli bulu bɛamaa ekpunli ko adɛnla Gyɛlusalɛm suakpole nwuanzanwuanza ne azo, na ekpunli ngɔnla ne noko adɛnlɛdɛnla azua nee namunamu mɔɔ ɛha la azo.

english_verse: Then everyone else asked God to bless those who were willing to live in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Na menli ne hanvole menli mɔɔ bɛdabɛ bɛ ahonle nu bɛyele bɛ nwo bɛmanle kɛ bɛmɛ bɛtɛnla Gyɛlusalɛm la.

english_verse: Some of the people of Israel, the priests, the Levites, the temple workers, and the descendants of Solomon's servants lived on their own property in the towns of Judah. But the leaders of the province lived in Jerusalem with their families. The Judah Tribe
translation_verse: Wɔ azua nee azuamgbole ne mɔ azo, Yizilayɛma, sɛlɛvolɛma, Livaema, Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua nu gyimayɛvoma, yɛɛ Sɔlɔmɔn sonvolɛma abo zo amra ne mɔ dɛnlanle bɛdabɛ bɛ azua nee bɛ azɛlɛ zo. Dwudama nee Bɛngyamanema bie mɔ dɛnlanle Gyɛlusalɛm.

english_verse: From the Benjamin tribe, three leaders settled in Jerusalem. The first was Sallu son of Meshullam, and the others were Gabbai and Sallai. Sallu's ancestors were Joed, Pedaiah, Kolaiah, Maaseiah, Ithiel, and Jeshaiah. Altogether, there were
translation_verse: Gabeeyae nee Saleeyae le Salu anwo amra fɔɔnwo. Bɛngyaman abo zo amra mɔɔ dɛnlanle Gyɛlusalɛm la le ɛya ngɔnla abulanwiɔ nee mɔtwɛ.

english_verse: Joel son of Zichri was their leader, and Judah son of Hassenuah was second in command. Priests
translation_verse: Zekelae ara Dwowɛle a le bɛ kpanyinli a, yɛɛ Dwuda mɔɔ le Hasɛnua ara nrenya ne la le suakpole ne azo neavolɛ mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ nwiɔ.

english_verse: The second priest to settle there was Seraiah son of Hilkiah. His ancestors were Meshullam, Zadok, Meraioth, and Ahitub, who had been a high priest.
translation_verse: Helekaya ara Sɛlaya, ɔle Mɛhyɛlam anlɔnra. Ye mgbanyima ne bie mɔ a le Zeedɔko, Mɛlayo yɛɛ Ahaetɛbe mɔɔ le Sɛlɛvolɛ Kpanyinli ne.

english_verse: Several Levites settled in Jerusalem. First, there was Shemaiah son of Hasshub. His ancestors were Azrikam, Hashabiah, and Bunni.
translation_verse: Livaema: Hahyɛbe ara Hyɛmaya, ɔle Azelaekam anlɔnra. Ye mgbanyima ne bie mɔ a le Hahyabaya nee Bɛnae.

english_verse: Next, there were Shabbethai and Jozabad, the Levite leaders in charge of the work outside the temple.
translation_verse: Hyabɛtae nee Dwozabade le Livaema titile. Bɛmɛ a bɛnea gyima mɔɔ bɛyɛ ye wɔ Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anwo la azo a.

english_verse: Then there was Mattaniah son of Mica. His ancestors were Zabdi and Asaph. Mattaniah led the temple choir in the prayer of praise. Bakbukiah, who also settled in Jerusalem, was his assistant. Finally, there was Abda son of Shammua; his grandfather was Galal, and his great-grandfather was Jeduthun.
translation_verse: Maeka ara Matanaya, ɔle Zabedae anlɔnra yɛɛ ɔle Esafe abo zo sonla. Yemɔ yɛɛ ɔlumuale ɔgyinlanle Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua nu edwɛndolɛma ati ɔmanle bɛdole moyɛlɛ nzɛlɛlɛ edwɛne ne a. Bakebukaya a ɛnee le Matanaya boavolɛ a. Hyamua ara Abeda, ɔle Geelale anlɔnra yɛɛ Gyɛdutɛn abo zo sonla ɔ.

english_verse: One hundred seventy-two temple guards settled in Jerusalem; their leaders were Akkub and Talmon.
translation_verse: Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne sinzavolɛma: Akɛbe, Talemɔn nee bɛ nwo amra kɔsɔɔti le ɛya ko abulasuu nee nwiɔ.

english_verse: The rest of the Israelites, including priests and Levites, lived on their own property in the other towns of Judah.
translation_verse: Yizilayɛma, sɛlɛvolɛma, yɛɛ Livaema mɔɔ hale la dɛnlanle bɛdabɛ bɛ azua nee bɛ azuamgbole zo wɔ Dwuda maanle nu.

english_verse: But the temple workers lived in the section of Jerusalem known as Ophel, and the two men in charge of them were Ziha and Gishpa.
translation_verse: Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne gyimayɛvoma ne dɛnlanle Gyɛlusalɛm awɔdenle ne mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye Ofɛle la azo. Zaeha nee Gehyepa a nleanle bɛ nwo zo a.

english_verse: Uzzi son of Bani was the leader of the Levites in Jerusalem. His grandfather was Hashabiah, his great-grandfather was Mattaniah, and his great-great-grandfather was Mica. He belonged to the Asaph clan that was in charge of the music for the temple services,
translation_verse: Sonla mɔɔ nleanle Livaema mɔɔ dɛnlanle Gyɛlusalɛm la anwo zo la a le Beenae ara Ɛzae, ɔle Hahyabaya anlɔnra. Ye mgbanyima ne bie mɔ a le Matanaya nee Maeka. Ɔbɔ Esafe abusua ekpulike ne bie; bɛmɛ a Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu edwɛndolɛ nwo ngyehyɛlɛ wɔ bɛ sa nu a.

english_verse: though the daily choice of music and musicians was decided by royal decree of the Persian king.
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ belemgbunli yɛle ngyehyɛlɛ mɔɔ kile kɛ mbusua ekpulike ne mɔ ɛrado edwɛne bɛ ti bɛ ti ɛboa ɛzonlenlɛ. Mekɛ biala mɔɔ bɛyɛ nzɛlɛlɛ la ɔwɔ kɛ abusua ekpulike ko bato edwɛne boa.

english_verse: The people of Israel were represented at the Persian court by Pethahiah son of Meshezabel from the Zerah clan of the Judah tribe. The People in the Other Towns and Villages
translation_verse: Pɛtahaya, Mɛhyɛzabɛle ara ne mɔɔ vi Zila abusua ekpulike nu na ɔbɔ Dwuda abusua ekpunli ne bie la a gyinlanle Yizilayɛma agyakɛ anu wɔ Pɛhyea Maanle Maanle Belemgbunli ne suakunlu ɛkɛ a. Menli mɔɔ wɔ azua nee azuamgbole gyɛne zo la

english_verse: Some of the people of Judah lived in the following towns near their farms: Kiriath-Arba, Dibon, Jekabzeel,
translation_verse: Menli ne mɔ dɔɔnwo dɛnlanle ɛleka mɔɔ bɛ egyinli wɔ la. Bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛvi Dwuda abusua nu la dɛnlanle Keleate Aaba, Daebɔn, yɛɛ Gyɛkabezile nee namunamu mɔɔ zuozua bɛ la azo.

english_verse: The people of Benjamin lived in the towns of Geba, Michmash, Aija, Bethel with its nearby villages,
translation_verse: Bɛngyaman abusua ekpunli ne anu amra dɛnlanle Giba, Mekemahye, Eyae, Bɛtɛle nee namunamu mɔɔ zuozua bɛ la azo;

english_verse: Anathoth, Nob, Ananiah,
translation_verse: Anato, Nɔbo, Ananaya,

english_verse: Hazor, Ramah, Gittaim,
translation_verse: Heezɔ, Releema, Geteeyem,

english_verse: Hadid, Zeboim, Neballat,
translation_verse: Heedede, Zɛboyem, Nɛbalate,

english_verse: Lod, and Ono, as well as in Craft Valley.
translation_verse: Lɔɔdo, yɛɛ Ono nee Dwinvolɛma Bɔnza ne anu.

english_verse: Several groups of Levites from the territory of Judah were sent to live among the people of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Bɛmanle Livaema ekpunli ekpunli bie mɔɔ anrɛɛ de Dwuda maanle nu la nee Bɛngyaman asa azo ne bie mɔ dɛnlanle.

english_verse: Many priests and Levites had returned from Babylonia with Zerubbabel and Joshua as their leaders. Those priests were Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra,
translation_verse: Sɛlɛvolɛma nee Livaema mɔɔ nee Hyialeteɛle ara Zɛlɛbabɛle nee Sɛlɛvolɛ Kpanyinli Dwɔhyua vi nlɔnu ziale rale la ɛne:

english_verse: Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, and another Jedaiah. These were the leading priests and their assistants during the time of Joshua.
translation_verse: Sɛlɛvolɛma: Sɛlaya, Gyɛlɛmaya, Ɛzela, Amalaya, Malɛke, Hatɛhye, Hyɛkanaya, Rilihɛm, Mɛlɛmo, Yedo, Genɛtowae, Abaegya, Maegyamen, Meeyadaya, Belega, Hyɛmaya, Dwɔyalebe, Gyɛdaya, Salu, Emɔko, Helekaya, yɛɛ Gyɛdaya. Menli ɛhye mɔ a le sɛlɛvolɛma ne mɔ mgbanyima wɔ Dwɔhyua mekɛ zo a.

english_verse: The Levites who returned were Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah. They and their assistants were responsible for the songs of praise,
translation_verse: Livaema: Menli ɛhye mɔ a nea moyɛlɛ edwɛndolɛ zo a: Gyɛhyua, Benuwae, Kademeɛle, Hyɛlibaya, Dwuda, yɛɛ Matanaya.

english_verse: while Bakbukiah and Unno, together with their assistants, were responsible for the choral responses. Descendants of Joshua the High Priest
translation_verse: Menli ɛhye mɔ a le edwɛndolɛma ekpunli ne mɔɔ die edwɛne ne mɔ azo la a; Bakebukaya, Ɛno, yɛɛ bɛ gɔnwo mɔ Livaema. Sɛlɛvolɛ Kpanyinli Dwɔhyua abo zo amra

english_verse: Joshua was the father of Joiakim, the grandfather of Eliashib, and the great-grandfather of Joiada.
translation_verse: Dwɔhyua le Dwɔyakem ɔ ze; Dwɔyakem le Yilayahyebe ɔ ze; Yilayahyebe le Dwɔyada ɔ ze;

english_verse: Joiada was the father of Jonathan and the grandfather of Jaddua. Leaders of the Priestly Clans
translation_verse: Dwɔyada le Dwɔnatan ɔ ze, yɛɛ Dwɔnatan le Gyadua ɔ ze. Sɛlɛvolɛma mbusua mgbanyinli

english_verse: During the time of the high priests Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua, and including the time that Darius was king of Persia, a record was kept of the heads of the Levite and priestly families.
translation_verse: Wɔ sɛlɛvolɛ mgbanyinli Yilayahyebe, Dwɔyada, Dwɔnatan, yɛɛ Gyadua mekɛ zo, bɛhɛlɛle Livaema nee sɛlɛvolɛma mbusua mgbanyinli aluma bɛziele. Bɛyɛle ɛhye toonwo ɔhɔdwule Pɛhyea Maanle Maanle Belemgbunli Dalayɛse mekɛ zo.

english_verse: However, no official record was kept of the heads of the Levite clans after the death of Johanan, the grandson of Eliashib.
translation_verse: Livaema mbusua mgbanyinli aluma ɛdeɛ ne mɔ, bɛhɛlɛle bɛwulale Edwɛkɛsisilɛ Mbuluku ne mɔ anu ɔhɔkpulale Yilayahyebe anlɔnra Dwɔnatan mekɛ zo ala. Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu gyima nwo ngyehyɛlɛ

english_verse: Hashabiah, Sherebiah, Jeshua son of Kadmiel, and their assistants organized two choirs of Levites to offer praises to God, just as King David, the man of God, had commanded.
translation_verse: Livae mgbanyinli ɛhye mɔ: Hahyabaya, Hyɛlibaya, Gyɛhyua, Benuwae, yɛɛ Kademeɛle a nleanle manle bɛhyɛle Livaema anu ekpunli ekpunli a. Mekɛ ko biala ekpunli nwiɔ to ayɛlɛyelɛ nee moyɛlɛ edwɛne maa Nyamenle, kɛmɔ Nyamenle sonla Belemgbunli Devidi hyehyɛle la.

english_verse: Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were responsible for guarding the storerooms near the temple gates.
translation_verse: Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne sinzavolɛma ɛhye mɔ a zinzale azua mɔɔ wɔ Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne nlenkɛ mgbole ne mɔ anloa mɔɔ bɛfa ninyɛne bɛsiezie nuhua la a: Matanaya, Bakebukaya, Obadaya, Mɛhyɛlam, Talemɔn, yɛɛ Akɛbe.

english_verse: All of these men lived during the time of Joiakim and during the time that I was governor and Ezra, a teacher of the Law of Moses, was priest. Nehemiah Dedicates the City Wall
translation_verse: Menli ɛhye mɔ mɔɔ bɛbobɔ bɛ aluma la ɛnee de aze wɔ Dwɔyakem, Dwɔhyua ara nrenya ne mɔɔ le Gyɛhozadake anlɔnra ne nee Amɛnlado Nihɛmaya yɛɛ sɛlɛvolɛ Ɛzela, mɔɔ le mɛla kilehilevolɛ la mekɛ zo. Nihɛmaya tu suakpole ne bane ne amaa Nyamenle

english_verse: When the city wall was dedicated, Levites from everywhere in Judah were invited to join in the celebration with songs of praise and with the music of cymbals, small harps, and other stringed instruments.
translation_verse: Mekɛ dwule mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ akee bɛbuke Gyɛlusalɛm bane ne na bɛtu bɛmaa Nyamenle la, bɛkpondɛle Livaema mɔɔ wɔ ɛleka biala la abo zo bɛ nee bɛ rale Gyɛlusalɛm, amaa bɛ kɔsɔɔti bɛava fɛlɛkolilɛ bɛabɔ nuhua bɛava sɔnwosɔnwo, getaa mgbole nee ngyikyi, moyɛlɛ, nee edwɛndolɛ bɛali ɛvoyia ne.

english_verse: The priests and Levites held special ceremonies to make themselves holy, and then they did the same for the rest of the people and for the gates and walls of the city.
translation_verse: Sɛlɛvolɛma nee Livaema bule amaamuo nluanle bɛ nwo, menli ne, nlenkɛ mgbole ne mɔ nee bane ne.

english_verse: I brought the leaders of Judah to the top of the city wall and put them in charge of the two groups that were to march around on top of the wall, singing praises to God. One group marched to the right in the direction of Garbage Gate.
translation_verse: Memboɔboale Dwuda mgbanyima ne mɔ anloa wɔ bane ne sinli nyunlu anwuma na menvale bɛ menziele menli ekpunli mgbole nwiɔ anloa kɛ bɛnlea bɛmaa bɛva ayɛlɛyelɛ edwɛne bɛkpɔsa suakpole ne azo na bɛyɛ Nyamenle mo. Ekpunli ne mɔɔ lumua la luale bane ne sinli nyunlu hɔle fema zo mɔɔ di kɔ Ewula Anlenkɛ Kpole ne anwo la.

english_verse: and his relatives, Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani. They played musical instruments like those that had been played by David, the man of God. And they marched behind Ezra, the teacher of the Law.
translation_verse: Akee mbusuafoɔ mɔɔ hale la doale zolɛ. Bɛmɛ a le Hyɛmaya, Azali, Melalae, Gelalae, Meeyae, Nɛtanile, Dwuda, yɛɛ Haneenae. Ɛhye mɔ ko biala lɛ agolebɔlɛ ninyɛne mɔɔ le kɛ mɔɔ ɛnee Nyamenle sonla Belemgbunli Devidi bɔ la bie. Mɛla kilehilevolɛ Ɛzela a lile ekpunli ɛhye ati a.

english_verse: When they reached Fountain Gate, they climbed the steps to David's City and went past his palace, before stopping at the Water Gate near the eastern wall of the city.
translation_verse: Bɛdwule Nzufeanvea Anlenkɛ Kpole ne anwo la, bɛluale kpolike ne mɔ mɔɔ kɔ Devidi suakpole ne azo la azo bɛpɛle nuhua wɔ Devidi Anlenkɛ Kpole ne anwo wɔ suakpole ne aduduleɛ afoa nu.

english_verse: The second group of singers marched along the wall in the opposite direction, and I followed them, together with the other half of the leaders of Judah. We went past Oven Tower, Broad Wall,
translation_verse: Ekpunli ko ne mɔɔ bɛdabɛ bɛluale bane ne sinli nyunlu anwuma na bɛvale moyɛlɛ bɛmanle Nyamenle la hɔle bɛne zo. Menvale menli ne foa ko mendoale bɛ. Yɛdole ɛlɔnwɔne yɛpenle Fonlomo Tawa ne anwo yɛhɔle Bane Tɛtɛlɛ ne anwo;

english_verse: where we stood in front of the temple with the other group, praising God. In the group with me were half of the leaders,
translation_verse: Yemɔti moyɛlɛ edwɛndolɛ ekpunli nwiɔ ɛhye rale Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu. Saa ɛye mgbanyinli ne foa ko mɔɔ ɛnee nee me lua la a

english_verse: as well as the priests Eliakim, Maaseiah, Miniamin, Micaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah, who were blowing trumpets.
translation_verse: sɛlɛvolɛma ɛhye mɔ noko boka nwo: Yilayakem, Meeyasaya, Menayamen, Maekaya, Ɛleyoyinae, Zɛkalaya, yɛɛ Hanahaya;

english_verse: Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer also stood there, as Jezrahiah led the singers.
translation_verse: menli ɛhye mɔ noko doa bɛ, Meeyasaya, Hyɛmaya, Ɛlieza, Ɛzae, Gyihoheenan, Malekaegya, Yilam, yɛɛ Yizɛ. Edwɛndolɛma mɔɔ Gyɛzelahaya li bɛ ti la a dole edwɛne ne kpole kpalɛ a.

english_verse: God had made the people very happy, and so on that day they celebrated and offered many sacrifices. The women and children joined in the festivities, and joyful shouts could be heard far from the city of Jerusalem. Preparation for Worship
translation_verse: Kenle ko ne bɛbɔle azu fane dɔɔnwo. Menli ne anye liele kpalɛ, ɔboalekɛ Nyamenle manle bɛlile fɛlɛko. Mraalɛ nee mbɛda kɔsɔɔti bokale ɛvoyialilɛ ne anwo, na anyelielɛ ne manle Gyɛlusalɛm kpudwule na ye nganeɛ dwule moa. Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu ɛzonlenlɛ nwo ngyehyɛlɛ

english_verse: On that same day, some leaders were appointed to be responsible for the safekeeping of gifts for the temple and to be in charge of receiving the first part of the harvest and the ten percent of the crops and livestock that was offered to God. These same leaders also collected the part of crops that the Law of Moses taught was to be given to the Levites. Everyone was pleased with the work of the priests and Levites,
translation_verse: Mekɛ ne anu bɛyele menli mɔɔ nea Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne ninyɛnezielɛ azua ne mɔ azo la. Ninyɛne mɔɔ kɔ azua zɔhane mɔ anu la a le debie biala mɔɔ bɛkɛnyia ye, abɛlɛ, nee ma mɔɔ bɛkɛlumua bɛkɛde ye ɛvolɛ biala anu la, yɛɛ ngyɛnu bulu ɛkpɔ ngoko ne mɔɔ bɛkɛva bɛkɛra la. Menli ɛhye mɔ a nea dielie ninyɛne ne fi ɛyazonlɛma ne mɔ mɔɔ zuozua azuamgbole ne mɔ la ɛkɛ a. Bɛfa ninyɛne ɛhye mɔ bɛnea sɛlɛvolɛma nee Livaema, kɛmɔ mɛla ne se la. Na Dwudama kɔsɔɔti anye liele sɛlɛvolɛma nee Livaema anwo.

english_verse: when they performed the ceremonies to make people acceptable to worship God. And the singers and the temple guards did their jobs according to the instructions given by David and his son Solomon.
translation_verse: Ɔboalekɛ bɛyɛle ɛnluanlɛ gyima ne nee gyima mɔɔ hale la kɔsɔɔ, kɛmɔ Nyamenle kpondɛ la. Zɔhane ala yɛɛ Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu edwɛndolɛma nee sinzavolɛma yɛle bɛ gyima ne a, kɛmɔ Belemgbunli Devidi nee ɔ ra Sɔlɔmɔn hyehyɛle la.

english_verse: In fact, ever since the days of David and Asaph, there had been song leaders and songs of praise and worship.
translation_verse: Mekɛ tendenle mɔɔ ɛze ɛhɔ la, ɔvi Belemgbunli Devidi nee edwɛnekilevolɛ Esafe mekɛ zo ɛnee bɛle edwɛndolɛma mgbanyinli yɛɛ edwɛndolɛma ne ɛdo ayɛlɛyelɛ nee moyɛlɛ edwɛne ɛmaa Nyamenle toonwo a yeradwu ɛnɛ a.

english_verse: During the time that Zerubbabel and I were in charge, everyone in Israel gave what they were supposed to give for the daily needs of the singers and temple guards from the Levi tribe. Then the Levites would give the priests their share from what they had received.
translation_verse: Wɔ Zɛlɛbabɛle nee Nihɛmaya mekɛ zo, Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti vale ahyɛlɛ ninyɛne manle bɛvale bɛnleanle Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu edwɛndolɛma nee sinzavolɛma ne mɔ. Menli vale azubɔlɛ ninyɛne mɔɔ anwo te la manle Livaema, na Livaema ne noko vale sɛlɛvolɛma ne afoa nu ɛdeɛ manle bɛ.

english_verse: On that day when the Law of Moses was read aloud to everyone, it was discovered that Ammonites and Moabites were forbidden to belong to the people of God.
translation_verse: Kenle ko ne mɔɔ bɛlɛkenga Mosisi Mɛla ne bɛahile menli ne la, bɛradwule kpɔkɛ bie mɔɔ se ɔnle kɛ bɛmaa Amɔnonli anzɛɛ Mowabenli biala adenle bɛmaa ɔboka Nyamenle menli ne anwo la,

english_verse: This was because they had refused to give food and water to Israel and had hired Balaam to call down a curse on them. However, our God turned the curse into a blessing.
translation_verse: ɔboalekɛ mekɛ mɔɔ Yizilayɛma vi Yigyibiti ɛlɛba la, Amɔnoma nee Mowabema ammaa bɛ aleɛ na yeayɛ nzule. Mɔɔ bɛyɛle la a le kɛ bɛduale ezukoa bɛmanle Beelam wale Yizilayɛma amonle, na Nyamenle manle amowa ne hakyile nyilalɛ.

english_verse: Following the reading of the Law of Moses, the people of Israel started sending away anyone who had any foreign ancestors. Nehemiah Makes Other Changes
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Yizilayɛma dele Mɛla ɛhye la bɛhwenle bɛ nwo bɛvile menli mɔɔ ɛnle Dwuuma la anwo. Nzenzaleɛ mɔɔ Nihɛmaya yɛle la

english_verse: The priest Eliashib was a relative of Tobiah and had earlier been put in charge of the temple storerooms.
translation_verse: Sɛlɛvolɛ Yilayahyebe mɔɔ ɛnee nea Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne ekpumgbunli ne mɔ mɔɔ bɛsie ninyɛne nuhua la azo la nee Tobaya vale ɛdulɛ la ɛhyɛ.

english_verse: So he let Tobiah live in one of these rooms, where all kinds of things had been stored—the grain offerings, incense, utensils for the temple, as well as the tenth of the grain, wine, and olive oil that had been given for the use of the Levites, singers, and temple guards, and the gifts for the priests.
translation_verse: Ɔlua zolɛ ɔmanle Tobaya adenle ɔmanle ɔdɛnlanle ekpumgbunli kpole ko anu. Zɔhane ekpumgbunli ne bɛfa aleɛ mɔɔ bɛfa bɛbɔ azu, ɛyɛlɛ, Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu ninyɛne, abɛlɛ ngyɛnu bulu ɛkpɔ ko ne, nwanye yɛɛ ɔlivi nwole mɔɔ bɛfa bɛmaa sɛlɛvolɛma la a bɛgua nu a.

english_verse: This happened in the thirty-second year that Artaxerxes ruled Babylonia. I was away from Jerusalem at the time, because I was visiting him. Later I received permission from the king
translation_verse: Mekɛ mɔɔ ɛhye mɔ ɛlɛkɔ zolɛ la, ɛnee menle Gyɛlusalɛm, ɔboalekɛ mɔɔ Atazɛzɛse lile ɛvolɛ abulasa nee nwiɔ wɔ Babelɔn belemgbunli ebia ne azo la, ɛnee mehɔ mekadu me kolakola meahile ye. Mekɛ guale nu ekyii la menzɛlɛle ye adenle menziale membale Gyɛlusalɛm.

english_verse: to return to Jerusalem. Only then did I find out that Eliashib had done this terrible thing of letting Tobiah have a room in the temple.
translation_verse: Na ɛkɛ ne yɛɛ menwunle munzule ɛbɛla mɔɔ Tobaya ati, Yilayahyebe ɛbɔ la, kɛ yeziezie Nyamenle Sua ne anu ekpumgbunli ko anu yemaa ye.

english_verse: It upset me so much that I threw out every bit of Tobiah's furniture.
translation_verse: Me ahonle futule kpole na menvuandinle Tobaya ninyɛne ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti menguale.

english_verse: Then I ordered the room to be cleaned and the temple utensils, the grain offerings, and the incense to be brought back into the room.
translation_verse: Akee memanle bɛnluanle sua ne anu na bɛvale Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu ninyɛne ne mɔ, mɔɔ le ahyɛnze, ma azubɔdeɛ, nee ɛyɛlɛ mɔ la bɛrale nuhua.

english_verse: I also found out that the temple singers and several other Levites had returned to work on their farms, because they had not been given their share of the harvest.
translation_verse: Eza menwunle kɛ bɛnva aleɛ mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ Livaema asa ka ye la bɛmmaa bɛ. Ɔlua zolɛ Livaema nee edwɛndolɛma bie mɔ mɔɔ yɛ gyima ne la ɛzia ɛhɔ bɛ ɛya avule ne mɔ anu.

english_verse: I called the leaders together and angrily asked them, “Why is the temple neglected?” Then I told them to start doing their jobs.
translation_verse: Yemɔti mendwile mgbanyima ne mɔ anyunlu kɛ bɛmaa Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne ɛdɔ mgbane a. Akee memboɔboale Livaema ne nee edwɛndolɛma ne anloa na me nee bɛ rale Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu kɛ bɛrayɛ bɛ gyima ne.

english_verse: After this, everyone in Judah brought a tenth of their grain, wine, and olive oil to the temple storeroom.
translation_verse: Na menli ne kɔsɔɔti bɔle ɔ bo bieko na bɛvale bɛ abɛlɛ, nwanye nee ɔlivi nwole bɛrale Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne ninyɛnezielɛ ɛleka ne.

english_verse: Finally, I appointed three men with good reputations to be in charge of what was brought there and to distribute it to the others. They were Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the teacher of the Law, and Pedaiah the Levite. Their assistant was Hanan, the son of Zaccur and the grandson of Mattaniah.
translation_verse: Na menyele menli ɛhye mɔ kɛ bɛnlea zolɛ; Sɛlɛvolɛ Hyɛlimaya, Mɛla Kilehilevolɛ Zeedɔko yɛɛ Pɛdaya mɔɔ le Livaema ne mɔ ko la. Menyɛle Zakɛ ara nrenya Heenan, mɔɔ le Matanaya anlɔnra ne kɛ ɔyɛ bɛ boavolɛ. Ɔluakɛ bɛdi nɔhalɛ yɛɛ medie bɛ medi kɛ bɛbahyɛ ninyɛne ne mɔ sɛsɛ bɛamaa mediema ne mɔ.

english_verse: I pray that my God will remember these good things that I have done for his temple and for those who worship there. The Sabbath
translation_verse: O me Nyamenle, kakye me wɔ ninyɛne ɛhye mɔ kɔsɔɔti mɔɔ meyɛ memaa wɔ Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ye nee nuhua ɛzonlenlɛ la ati.

english_verse: I also noticed what the people of Judah were doing on the Sabbath. Not only were they trampling grapes to make wine, but they were harvesting their grain, grapes, figs, and other crops, and then loading these on donkeys to sell in Jerusalem. So I warned them not to sell food on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Mekɛ ne anu menwunle Dwudama bie mɔ kɛ bɛlɛyɛ nwanye wɔ Ɛnwomenlelielɛ Kenle ne. Bie mɔ noko ɛlɛsoa abɛlɛ, nwanye, vanye ma, feege, yɛɛ ninyɛne ngakyile akyekye bɛ wɔ bɛ asoaso ne mɔ anzi bɛ nee bɛ ahɔ Gyɛlusalɛm, na membɔle bɛ kɔkɔ ɛsesebɛ kɛ bɛmmatɔne debie biala wɔ Ɛnwomenlelielɛ Kenle ne.

english_verse: People who had moved to Jerusalem from the city of Tyre were bringing in fish and other things to sell there on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Menli bie mɔɔ vi Taya mɔɔ bɛwɔ suakpole ne azo la vale fɛlɛ nee ninyɛne ngakyile dɔɔnwo radɔnenle bɛ wɔ Ɛnwomenlelielɛ kenle ne manle Dwudama nee Gyɛlusalɛmma.

english_verse: I got angry and said to the leaders of Judah, “This evil you are doing is an insult to the Sabbath!
translation_verse: Na mendwile mgbanyima ne mɔ anyunlu kɛ, “Duzu munzule ɛbɛla yɛɛ bɛlɛbɔ la? Bɛlɛto Ɛnwomenlelielɛ Kenle ne mɛla ne.

english_verse: Didn't God punish us and this city because our ancestors did these very same things? And here you are, about to make God furious again by disgracing the Sabbath!”
translation_verse: Bɛ mgbanyima yɛle ɛhye mɔ la, yɛ Nyamenle ne ɛmaa bɛzɛkye suakpole ye ɛmaa bɛ munzule ɛbɔ bɛ ti. Noko bɛtɛgua zolɛ bɛtɛyɛ, bɛlɛto Ɛnwomenlelielɛ Kenle ne mɛla ne, bɛyɛ bɛahwe ndeanlɛ bɛagua Yizilayɛma ati zo.”

english_verse: I ordered the gates of Jerusalem to be closed on the eve of the Sabbath and not to be opened until after the Sabbath had ended. Then I put some of my own men in charge of the gates to make certain that nothing was brought in on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Yemɔti menlile mɛla kɛ nɔsolɛ biala mɔɔ le Ɛnwomenlelielɛ Kenle ne abobɔlɛ la, bɛmmatukuedukue Gyɛlusalɛm nlenkɛ mgbole ne mɔ kɔkpula kɛ Ɛnwomenlelielɛ Kenle ne kɛpɛ nu la. Eza memanle me sonvolɛma ne bie mɔ zinzale nlenkɛ mgbole ne mɔ, amaa bɛanva ninyɛne adɔne bɛamba suakpole ne azo Ɛnwomenlelielɛ Kenle ne.

english_verse: Once or twice some merchants spent the night outside Jerusalem with their goods.
translation_verse: Akee gualilɛma ne hale Gyɛlusalɛm bane ne anzi lale fane kɛyɛ nwiɔ.

english_verse: But I warned them, “If you do this again, I'll have you arrested.” From then on, they did not come on the Sabbath.
translation_verse: Membɔle bɛ kɔkɔ menzele bɛ kɛ, “Duzu ati yɛɛ bɛda bane ne anzi a? Saa bɛyɛ zɔhane bieko a, mebahwi bɛ ɛza.” Na ɔvi mekɛ zɔhane mɔɔ kɔ la, bɛamba gualilɛ wɔ Ɛnwomenlelielɛ Kenle ne bieko.

english_verse: I ordered the Levites to make themselves holy and to guard the gates on the Sabbath, so that it would be kept holy. God is truly merciful, and I pray that he will treat me with kindness and bless me for doing this. Mixed Marriages
translation_verse: Na menzele Livaema ne kɛ bɛdu bɛ nwo bɛmaa na bɛrazinza nlenkɛ mgbole ne mɔ bɛmaa bɛzie Ɛnwomenlelielɛ Kenle ne nwuanzanwuanza. O me Nyamenle, kakye me wɔ ɛhye noko ati na die me, kɛmɔ wɔ ɛhulolɛ kpole ne mɔɔ ɛmbɔ aze ɛlɛ la de la.

english_verse: I discovered that some Jewish men had married women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.
translation_verse: Mekɛ ko ne ala anu, menwunle kɛ Dwuuma bie mɔ ɛgyigya Ahyedɔdo, Amɔn yɛɛ Mowabe mraalɛ,

english_verse: About half of their children could not speak Hebrew—they spoke only the language of Ashdod or some other foreign language.
translation_verse: na bɛ mra ne mɔ anu foa ko ka Ahyedɔdo aneɛ ne bie nee aneɛ gyɛne bie mɔ, na bɛngola Dwuda aneɛ ne ka.

english_verse: So in my anger, I called down curses on those men. I had them beaten and even pulled out the hair of some of them. Then I made them promise: In the name of God we solemnly promise not to let our sons and daughters marry foreigners.
translation_verse: Mendwile bɛ nyunlu na menwale bɛ amonle. Membole bɛ nuhua bie mɔ na mendwewhenle bie mɔ ati enrinli mendudule ye. Memanle bɛhanle ndane kɛ kenle bie maanle nu, “Bɛnrɛva bɛ mra mraalɛ bɛnrɛmaa menli zɔhane mɔ amra mrenya agyalɛ, anzɛɛ bɛnrɛmaa bɛ mra mrenya ɛnrɛgya bɛ mra mraalɛ, yɛɛ bɛdabɛ mumua ne bɛnrɛgya menli zɔhane mɔ bie ɛlɛ.”

english_verse: So we will obey you and not rebel against our God by marrying foreign women.
translation_verse: Na mebiza bɛ kɛ, yemɔti yɛnlea bɛdabɛ bɛ ɛdeɛ ne mɔɔ bɛlɛyɛ la azo yɛyɛ bie na yɛde yɛ Nyamenle ne anwo atua, yɛgya nyɛvolɛ mraalɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: Jehoiada, the son of the high priest Eliashib, had a son who had married a daughter of Sanballat from Horon, and I forced his son to leave.
translation_verse: Dwɔyada le Sɛlɛvolɛ Kpanyinli Yilayahyebe ara nrenya. Dwɔyada amra mrenya ne mɔ ko gya Sanebalate mɔɔ vi Bɛte Hɔlɔn la ara raalɛ, yemɔti mendule ye menvile Gyɛlusalɛm.

english_verse: I pray that God will punish them for breaking their priestly vows and disgracing the Levi tribe.
translation_verse: O me Nyamenle, kakye bɛ kɛ bɛgua sɛlɛvolɛlilɛ ne nee sɛlɛvolɛma nee Livaema ngyekyeleɛ ne anwo evinli a.

english_verse: Then I made sure that the people were free from every foreign influence, and I assigned duties for the priests and Levites.
translation_verse: Akee menuanle menli ne wɔ nyɛleɛ biala mɔɔ ɛnle yɛ maamɛla la anwo, na mengyɛle sɛlɛvolɛma nee Livaema gyima ne memanle bɛ.

english_verse: I also arranged for the people to bring firewood to the altar each day and for them to bring the first part of their harvest to the temple. I pray that God will bless me for the good I have done.
translation_verse: Mengyehyɛle mekɛ mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ bɛfa bɛyela nyɛmoa bɛbɔ azu la, nee mekɛ mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ menli fa abɛlɛ mɔɔ bɛkɛlumua bɛkɛbu nee ma mɔɔ bɛkɛlumua bɛkɛde la ba la. O me Nyamenle, kakye ɛhye mɔ kɔsɔɔti na yila me.

english_verse: During the third year of his rule, Xerxes gave a big dinner for all his officials and officers. The governors and leaders of the provinces were also invited, and even the commanders of the Persian and Median armies came.
translation_verse: Ɔlile ɛvolɛ nsa wɔ ebia ne azo la ɔdole ye mgbanyima nee sonvolɛma, Pɛhyea nee Midea sogya mgbanyinli, menli mɔɔ di munli nee amɛnladoma mɔɔ nea maanle maanle ne mɔ azo la ɛkponle,

english_verse: At the end of this time, King Xerxes gave another dinner and invited everyone in the city of Susa, no matter who they were. The eating and drinking lasted seven days in the beautiful palace gardens.
translation_verse: Ɛhye anzi, belemgbunli ne dole Susa suakpole ne azo amra ɛkponle toonwo kenle kɔkɔlɛ nsuu wɔ ye suakunlu alie kpandaanwo ne anwo. Sukoavolɛma nee koahweabanema kɔsɔɔti hɔle ɛkponledolɛ ne bie.

english_verse: The area was decorated with blue and white cotton curtains tied back with purple linen cords that ran through silver rings fastened to marble columns. Couches of gold and silver rested on pavement that had all kinds of designs made from costly bright-colored stones and marble and mother-of-pearl.
translation_verse: Bɛvale ninyɛne ngɛnlɛma ngakyile dɔɔnwo bɛzieziele suakunlu ɛkɛ ne: mgbɛnu ndanlɛ fufule nee buluwu mɔɔ bɛva lenen ndanlɛ kɔkɔlɛ ndenrɛndenra ngɛnlɛma bɛbobɔ bɛ avinli, na dwɛtɛ fufule ngɛba sosɔ bɛ nloa la hendɛhenda mpila mɔɔ bɛvale awolɛ memeamemea mɔɔ sonle bolɛ la a bɛsisile la. Mbia mɔɔ gyigyi alie nwo ɛkɛ ne la, bɛvale ezukoa nvutuke nee dwɛtɛ fufule a bɛyɛle a. Azɛlɛ ne anwo bɔbɔ, bɛvale awolɛ memeamemea mɔɔ sonle bolɛ la a bɛdole a.

english_verse: The guests drank from gold cups, and each cup had a different design. The king was generous
translation_verse: Nza mɔɔ bɛnlonle la, bɛzule ye ezukoa nvutuke ahanrɛlɛ ngakyile nu, yɛɛ belemgbunli ne ɔdaye ye ahunlunyele nu ala ɔhwenle ye nwanye kpalɛ mɔɔ ɔlɛ la ɔvindele.

english_verse: While the men were enjoying themselves, Queen Vashti gave the women a big dinner inside the royal palace.
translation_verse: Mekɛ ɛhye anu ala Belemgbunli Raalɛ Vahyetae ɔdaye ɔdole mraalɛ ne mɔ ɛkponle wɔ Belemgbunli Zɛzɛse suakunlu ɛkɛ ne.

english_verse: By the seventh day, King Xerxes was feeling happy because of so much wine. And he asked his seven personal servants, Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carkas,
translation_verse: Kenle nsuu ne azo, mɔɔ ɛnee belemgbunli ne ɛlɛno nza na ɔ nye ɛlie kpalɛ kpalɛ la, ɔzoanle ɔmanle bɛhɔvɛlɛle ɔdaye Belemgbunli Zɛzɛse ɔ ti anwo sonvolɛma nsuu ne mɔɔ di ɔ nzi la ɔmanle bɛrale. Bɛmɛ a le Mɛhuman, Bezeta, Haabona, Begeta, Abageta, Zita, yɛɛ Kaakase.

english_verse: to bring Queen Vashti to him. The king wanted her to wear her crown and let his people and his officials see how beautiful she was.
translation_verse: Ɔzele bɛ kɛ bɛhɔze Belemgbunli Raalɛ Vahyetae kɛ ɔzoa ye belemgbunli kyɛlɛ ne na ɔ nee bɛ ɛlua nwolɛ ɛrɛla. Ɔyɛle ɛhye amaa saa ɔba a yeanyia adenle yeava belemgbunli raalɛ ne anwofɛlɛko ne yeadu ɔ nloa anu wɔ menli ne anyunlu, ɔluakɛ ɛnee belemgbunli raalɛ ne anwo yɛ fɛ kpole kpalɛ.

english_verse: The king's servants told Queen Vashti what he had said, but she refused to go to him, and this made him terribly angry.
translation_verse: Na Belemgbunli Raalɛ Vahyetae dule ɔ gye. Ɛhye ati belemgbunli ne ahonle futule na ɔvale ɛya.

english_verse: The king called in the seven highest officials of Persia and Media. They were Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan. These men were very wise and understood all the laws and customs of the country, and the king always asked them what they thought about such matters.
translation_verse: Mgbanyima ne mɔ a le Kaahyina, Hyita, Ademeeta, Tahyehye, Milɛse, Maasina, yɛɛ Mɛmukan. Bɛmɛ a bɛle Pɛhyea nee Midea maanle ne mɔ anu mgbanyima nsuu mɔɔ lumuale wɔ maanle ne ɛbulɛ nu a.

english_verse: The king said to them, “Queen Vashti refused to come to me when I sent my servants for her. What does the law say I should do about that?”
translation_verse: Belemgbunli Zɛzɛse bizale mgbanyima ne mɔ kɛ, “Kɛ mɛla ne se ɛ, duzu a ɔwɔ kɛ bɛfa bɛyɛ Belemgbunli Raalɛ Vahyetae a? Menzoanle kɛ bɛhɔvɛlɛ ye la, ɔdule ɔ gye. Yeamba!”

english_verse: Then Memucan told the king and the officials: Your Majesty, Queen Vashti has not only embarrassed you, but she has insulted your officials and everyone else in all the provinces.
translation_verse: Na Mɛmukan vale dole belemgbunli nee ye mgbanyima ne mɔ anyunlu kɛ, “Debie mɔɔ Belemgbunli Raalɛ Vahyetae ɛyɛ la, tɛ belemgbunli angomekye yɛɛ yegua ɔ nyunlu aze a, na yegua mgbanyima nee menli kɔsɔɔti mɔɔ wɔ Belemgbunli Zɛzɛse maanle maanle ne mɔ anu la amuala anyunlu aze.

english_verse: The women in the kingdom will hear about this, and they will refuse to respect their husbands. They will say, “If Queen Vashti doesn't obey her husband, why should we?”
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ mraalɛ kɔsɔɔti bade belemgbunli raalɛ ye nyɛleɛ mɔɔ yeyɛ la na ɔlua zolɛ bɛnrɛbu bɛ hu mɔ bie. Bɛbaha kɛ, ‘Belemgbunli Zɛzɛse zoanle kɛ bɛhɔvɛlɛ Belemgbunli Raalɛ Vahyetae kɛ ɔrɛla la, yeampili ye.’

english_verse: Before this day is over, the wives of the officials of Persia and Media will find out what Queen Vashti has done, and they will refuse to obey their husbands. They won't respect their husbands, and their husbands will be angry with them.
translation_verse: Ɛnɛ kenle ye, Pɛhyea nee Midea mraalɛ mɔɔ ɛde belemgbunli raalɛ ne subane mɔɔ ɛhile la anwo bie la baha ahile bɛ hu mɔ kolaa na sɛnzɛne adɔ, na ɛyavalɛ dɔɔnwo nee mgbane mgbane ɛyɛlɛ bara, ɔluakɛ mraalɛ anye ɛnrɛzɔ bɛ hu mɔ.

english_verse: Your Majesty, if you agree, you should write for the Medes and Persians a law that can never be changed. This law would keep Queen Vashti from ever seeing you again. Then you could let someone who respects you be queen in her place.
translation_verse: Nana, saa ɛkɛkponle a anrɛɛ mese ɛmaa bɛhɛlɛ mɛla ɛhye bɛboka Pɛhyeama nee Mideama maamɛla ne anwo mɔɔ bɛngakyi ye ɛlɛ a, kɛ ɔvi ɛnɛ mɔɔ kɔ la, Vahyetae agyakɛ ba ɛnrɛtia Belemgbunli Zɛzɛse anwo ɛkɛ ne bieko ɛlɛ; na fa ye dehelɛ gyinlabelɛ ne maa raalɛ mɔɔ lɛ subane kpalɛ la.

english_verse: When the women in your great kingdom hear about this new law, they will respect their husbands, no matter if they are rich or poor.
translation_verse: Saa bɛbɔ mɛla ɛhye nolo wɔ belemgbunli ne maanle maanle ne mɔ anu a, mraalɛ muala bava enililɛ amaa bɛ hu mɔ, mɔɔ ɔnva nwolɛ kɛ bɛ hu mɔ le mgbolema anzɛɛ koahweabanema a.”

english_verse: King Xerxes and his officials liked what Memucan had said,
translation_verse: Folɛdulɛ ɛhye yɛle belemgbunli nee ye mgbanyima ne mɔ fɛ kpole na belemgbunli ne yɛle, kɛmɔ Mɛmukan zuzule la.

english_verse: and he sent letters to all of his provinces. Each letter was written in the language of the province to which it was sent, and it said that husbands should be in charge of their wives and children.
translation_verse: Ɔhɛlɛle ngɛlata ɔhɔle ye maanle maanle ne mɔ amuala anu, maanle ko biala ɔdaye ye aneɛ nu kɛ, “Wɔ awuke biala anu, nrenya ne a le kpanyinli a, yɛɛ ɔ nloa edwɛkɛ, bɛndu bɛndo.”

english_verse: After a while, King Xerxes got over being angry. But he kept thinking about what Vashti had done and the law that he had written because of her.
translation_verse: Nzinlii mɔɔ Belemgbunli Zɛzɛse ɛya ne dwole la, ɛnee ɔtɛkakye debie mɔɔ Vahyetae ɛyɛ la nee ɔdaye Zɛzɛse ye mɛla ne mɔɔ yebɔ ye nolo wɔ Vahyetae anwo wɔ ɛleka biala la.

english_verse: Then the king's personal servants said: Your Majesty, a search must be made to find you some beautiful young women.
translation_verse: Yemɔti belemgbunli ne folɛdulɛma ne bie mɔ mɔɔ bikye ye kpalɛ la zuzule hilele ye kɛ, “Duzu ati a ɛmkpondɛ mbɛlɛra mɔɔ anwo yɛ fɛ kpalɛ la bie ɛ?

english_verse: You can select officers in every province to bring them to the place where you keep your wives in the capital city of Susa. Put your servant Hegai in charge of them since that is his job. He can see to it that they are given the proper beauty treatments.
translation_verse: Yeye mbɔlɔba wɔ maanle ye maanzinli ne mɔ anu maa bɛva mbɛlɛra mɔɔ anwo yɛ fɛ la amuala bɛrɛla Susa suakpole ye azo na fa bɛ wula Higae, mɔɔ le sonvolɛ nrenya ne mɔɔ nea wɔ mraalɛ ne mɔ anwo zo la asa anu; na bɛbɔ ɔ bo kɛ bɛkeha bɛ.

english_verse: Then let the young woman who pleases you most take Vashti's place as queen. King Xerxes liked these suggestions, and he followed them.
translation_verse: Na akee fa bɛ nuhua ko mɔɔ ɛ nye die ɔ nwo la yɛ ye belemgbunli raalɛ sie Vahyetae agyakɛ anu.” Nzuzulɛ ɛhye zɔle belemgbunli ne anye, zɔhane ati ɔliele ɔdole nu na ɔyɛle.

english_verse: At this time a Jew named Mordecai was living in Susa. His father was Jair, and his grandfather Shimei was the son of Kish from the tribe of Benjamin.
translation_verse: Dwuunli bie wɔ suakpole Susa azo, bɛfɛlɛ ye Mɔdekae. Ɔ ze a le Gyeeyɛɛ, Gyeeyɛɛ ɔ ze a le Hyemɛyae, yɛɛ Hyemɛyae ɔ ze a le Kɛhye mɔɔ vi Bɛngyaman abusua ekpunli ne anu la.

english_verse: Kish was one of the people that Nebuchadnezzar had taken from Jerusalem, when he took King Jeconiah of Judah to Babylonia.
translation_verse: Mekɛ mɔɔ Belemgbunli Nɛbukadenɛza hyele Dwuda Belemgbunli Gyɛhɔyaken nee menli bie nuokɛ wɔ Gyɛlusalɛm na ɔ nee bɛ hɔle Babelɔn la, Mɔdekae boka nwolɛ.

english_verse: Mordecai had a very beautiful cousin named Esther, whose Hebrew name was Hadassah. He had raised her as his own daughter, after her father and mother died.
translation_verse: Mɔdekae awuvuanyi ara raalɛ a le Ɛseta mɔɔ eza bɛfɛlɛ ye Hadasa wɔ Hibulu nu la. Ɛseta le raalɛ mɔɔ anwo yɛ fɛ a, yɛɛ eza ɔgyi zolɛ sengɔɔnwo. Ɔ nli nee ɔ ze wule la, Mɔdekae a lile ye adane a, na ɔvale ye ɔyɛle kɛ ɔ kunlu ralɛ.

english_verse: When the king ordered the search for beautiful women, many were taken to the king's palace in Susa, and Esther was one of them. Hegai was put in charge of all the women,
translation_verse: Mekɛ mɔɔ belemgbunli ne nolo ne dwule maanle maanle ne mɔ anu ɛleka biala na bɛ nee mbɛlɛra ne mɔ ba Susa la, bɛvale Ɛseta noko bɛbokale nwolɛ. Ɔdaye noko bɛliele ye wɔ belemgbunli sua nu ɛkɛ na bɛvale ye bɛwulale Higae, mɔɔ nea belemgbunli sua nu ɛkɛ ne mraalɛ nu la asa anu.

english_verse: and from the first day, Esther was his favorite. He began her beauty treatments at once. He also gave her plenty of food and seven special maids from the king's palace, and they had the best rooms.
translation_verse: Higae anye liele Ɛseta anwo kpole na ɛkɛ ne ala ɔbɔle ye ɛhehanlɛ bo. Eza ɔmanle ye nwolɛ aleɛ kpalɛ. Higae eza manle ye ɛleka kpalɛ wɔ belemgbunli sua nu ɛkɛ ne mraalɛ nu, na ɔkpale nu ɔyele mbɛlɛra nsuu wɔ suakunlu ɛkɛ ne kɛ bɛzonle Ɛseta.

english_verse: Mordecai had warned Esther not to tell anyone that she was a Jew, and she obeyed him.
translation_verse: Mɔdekae bɔle Ɛseta anloa, yemɔti Ɛseta angile ɔ nwo kɛ ɔle Dwuunli.

english_verse: He was anxious to see how Esther was getting along and to learn what had happened to her. So each day he would walk back and forth in front of the court where the women lived.
translation_verse: Na Mɔdekae lile belemgbunli sua nu ɛkɛ ne mraalɛ nu anuhɔlɛ ne anyunlu akɔneaba dahuu, kɛ ɔnea kɛ Ɛseta te kpɔkɛ nee debie mɔɔ bazi ɔ nwo zo la.

english_verse: The young women were given beauty treatments for one whole year. The first six months their skin was rubbed with olive oil and myrrh, and the last six months it was treated with perfumes and cosmetics. Then each of them spent the night alone with King Xerxes.
translation_verse: Bɛvale siane bulu nee nwiɔ a bɛhehanle mbɛlɛra ne mɔ a. Bɛvale siane nsia bɛkpokpale bɛ aabɛya nwole yɛɛ bɛvale siane nsia bɛkpokpale bɛ sakyeɛ. Mekɛ ne dwule la, bɛvale mbɛlɛra ne mɔ bɛhɔle Belemgbunli Zɛzɛse ɛkɛ ne ngoko.

english_verse: When a young woman went to the king, she could wear whatever clothes or jewelry she chose from the women's living quarters.
translation_verse: Saa bɛlɛra ne bahɔ belemgbunli ne ɛkɛ a, ɔsiezie ɔ nwo, kɛmɔ ɔdaye ɔkulo la na ɔvi belemgbunli sua nu ɛkɛ ne mraalɛ nu yeahɔ suakunlu ɛkɛ.

english_verse: In the evening she would go to the king, and the following morning she would go to the place where his wives stayed after being with him. There a man named Shaashgaz was in charge of the king's wives. Only the ones the king wanted and asked for by name could go back to the king.
translation_verse: Ɔkɔ nɔsolɛ nu na ɔba nwonlomɔ a, bɛfa ye bɛkɔ ɛleka mɔɔ belemgbunli mgbɔnla ne mɔ wɔ la. Ɛleka ɛhye, sonvolɛ mɔɔ nea ɛkɛ ne la a le Hyeeyahyegaze. Saa bɛlɛra mɔɔ kɛhɔ belemgbunli ɛkɛ ne la sia ba a, ɔngɔ bieko, kyesɛ belemgbunli ne anye liele ɔ nwo. Saa ɔba ye zɔhane a belemgbunli ne soa maa bɛkɔfɛlɛ ye.

english_verse: Xerxes had been king for seven years when Esther's turn came to go to him during Tebeth, the tenth month of the year. Everyone liked Esther. The king's personal servant Hegai was in charge of the women, and Esther trusted Hegai and asked him what she ought to take with her.
translation_verse: Belemgbunli Zɛzɛse lile ɛvolɛ nsuu wɔ ebia ne azo la, ye siane ne mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ bulu mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye “Tibɛte” la anu yɛɛ bɛvale Ɛseta bɛhɔle ye suakunlu ɛkɛ ne a.

english_verse: Xerxes liked Esther more than he did any of the other young women. None of them pleased him as much as she did, and he immediately fell in love with her and crowned her queen in place of Vashti.
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne hulole Ɛseta dɛlale mbɛlɛra ne mɔ amuala, na ɔhulole ye edwɛkɛ ɔdɛlale raalɛ biala mɔɔ ɛra ye suakunlu ɛkɛ ne la. Yemɔti ɔvale belemgbunli kyɛlɛ ne ɔzoale ye na ɔyɛle ye Belemgbunli Raalɛ ɔziele Vahyetae agyakɛ anu.

english_verse: In honor of Esther he gave a big dinner for his leaders and officials. Then he declared a holiday everywhere in his kingdom and gave expensive gifts. Mordecai Saves the King's Life
translation_verse: Akee Belemgbunli Zɛzɛse dole ɛkponle kpole bie manle Ɛseta na ɔdole ɛsalɛ ɔvɛlɛle ye maanle mgbanyima nee ye mbɔlɔba ne mɔ amuala. Mekɛ ne anu belemgbunli ne gyakyile ye adwule mɔɔ ɔdie ɔfi ye maanle maanle ne mɔ lɔ la anu ekyii na ɔvale ahyɛlɛdeɛ dɔɔnwo ɔmanle menli. Mɔdekae die belemgbunli ne ngoane

english_verse: When the young women were brought together again, Esther's cousin Mordecai had become a palace official.
translation_verse: Mekɛ dwule mɔɔ bɛboɔboale mbɛlɛra mɔɔ ɛnze mrenya la anloa bieko la, ɛnee Mɔdekae wɔ belemgbunli ne gyima nu,

english_verse: He had told Esther never to tell anyone that she was a Jew, and she obeyed him, just as she had always done.
translation_verse: noko Ɛseta ɛdeɛ ɛnee ɔtɛkilele ɔ nwo yɛɛ ɔtɛkilele maanle holɛ ko nee menli mɔɔ ɔvi bɛ nuhua la. Ɔyɛle ɛhye, ɔluakɛ ɛnee Mɔdekae ɛbɔ ɔ nloa yɛɛ Ɛseta noko yɛle tieyɛ manle Mɔdekae, kɛmɔ ɔde na yeara belemgbunli sua nu la.

english_verse: Bigthana and Teresh were the two men who guarded King Xerxes' rooms, but they got angry with the king and decided to kill him.
translation_verse: Mekɛ mɔɔ ɛnee Mɔdekae wɔ gyima nu la, sinzavolɛma nwiɔ mɔɔ nea nwolodo ne mɔɔ kɔ belemgbunli suakunlu ɛkɛ ne la hɔle Belemgbunli Zɛzɛse ati akpamo kɛ bɛku ye. Sinzavolɛma nwiɔ ne a le Begeteena nee Tilɛhye.

english_verse: Mordecai found out about their plans and asked Queen Esther to tell the king what he had found out.
translation_verse: Mɔdekae dele ɛhye anwo bie, ɔfetele zolɛ ɔhilele Belemgbunli Raalɛ Ɛseta, na Ɛseta hanle hilele belemgbunli ne.

english_verse: King Xerxes learned that Mordecai's report was true, and he had the two men hanged. Then the king had all of this written down in his record book as he watched.
translation_verse: Belemgbunli Zɛzɛse manle bɛnleɛnleanle edwɛkɛ ne anu, na bɛnwunle kɛ amgba edwɛkɛ ne le nɔhalɛ. Zɔhane ati bɛhunle sinzavolɛma nwiɔ ne na bɛhɛlɛle mɔɔ zile la buluku nu bɛdole ɛkɛ.

english_verse: Later, King Xerxes promoted Haman the son of Hammedatha to the highest position in his kingdom. Haman was a descendant of Agag,
translation_verse: Nzinlii Belemgbunli Zɛzɛse yɛle nrenya bie mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye Heeman, mɔɔ vi Agage abusua nu na ɔ ze a le Hamɛdeeta la sonvolɛ kpanyinli ɔmanle ɔdɛlale ye suakunlu ɛkɛ ne mgbanyima ne mɔ amuala.

english_verse: and the king had given orders for his officials at the royal gate to honor Haman by kneeling down to him. All of them obeyed except Mordecai.
translation_verse: Sonvolɛma mɔɔ wɔ suakunlu ɛkɛ ne la amuala bɔle bɛ ti aze manle ye, kɛmɔ belemgbunli ne hanle kɛ bɛyɛ la. Na Mɔdekae ɛdeɛ, yeangoto Heeman ɛlɛ.

english_verse: When the other officials asked Mordecai why he disobeyed the king's command,
translation_verse: Sonvolɛma mɔɔ wɔ suakunlu ɛkɛ ne la bizale Mɔdekae kɛ, “Duzu ati a ɛnli belemgbunli ne mɛla ne azo a?”

english_verse: he said, “Because I am a Jew.” They spoke to him for several days about kneeling down, but he still refused to obey. Finally, they reported this to Haman, to find out if he would let Mordecai get away with it.
translation_verse: Bɛbizale ye nwolɛ edwɛkɛ fane dɔɔnwo, noko yeandɛne bɛ zo. Dahuu ye edwɛkɛ a le kɛ, “Mame, mele Dwuunli.” Ɛhye ati bɛbɔle Heeman amaneɛ, amaa bɛanlea kɛ saa edwɛkɛ ne kɔda Heeman anyunlu a Mɔdekae kɛva ɔ nwo dwɔɔ.

english_verse: Haman was furious to learn that Mordecai refused to kneel down and honor him.
translation_verse: Heeman nwunle kɛ Mɔdekae amgba ɛmbɔ ɔ ti aze ɛmmaa ye, na ɛya hunle ye kpole.

english_verse: And when he found out that Mordecai was a Jew, he knew that killing only Mordecai was not enough. Every Jew in the whole kingdom had to be killed.
translation_verse: Noko yeangulo kɛ ɔkɛhu Mɔdekae angome. Kɛmɔ bɛmaa yede kɛ Mɔdekae le Dwuunli la ati, ɔhulole kɛ ɔkɛhu Dwuuma amuala mɔɔ wɔ Belemgbunli Zɛzɛse maanle ne anu la.

english_verse: Then Haman went to the king and said: Your Majesty, there are some people who live all over your kingdom and won't have a thing to do with anyone else. They have customs that are different from everyone else's, and they refuse to obey your laws. We would be better off to get rid of them!
translation_verse: Akee Heeman hanle hilele Belemgbunli Zɛzɛse kɛ, “Menli bie mɔɔ bɛdabɛ asolo bɛ amaamuo la ɛde ɛkponde wɔ maanle maanle mɔɔ ɛsie bɛ la amuala anu. Bɛnli wɔ mɛla ɛdeɛ ne azo. Ɛhye ati ɔnle kpalɛ kɛ belemgbunli kɛlie bɛ wɔ ye maanle ye anu.

english_verse: Why not give orders for all of them to be killed? I can promise that you will get tons of silver for your treasury.
translation_verse: Saa ɛ nee me kɛyɛ adwenle a, anrɛɛ mese ɛyɛ ye mɛla ɛmaa bɛhu bɛ muala. Ɛkponle ɛhye azo a, mebadua dwɛtɛ fufule ‘talɛnte’ apenle bulu meamaa menli mɔɔ nea belemgbunli ne gyima zo la, amaa bɛava bɛagua wɔ gya ne anu.”

english_verse: The king handed his official ring to Haman, who hated the Jews, and the king told him,
translation_verse: Yemɔti belemgbunli ne yele ɔ sa kpɔdelera ne mɔɔ ɔfa ɔsi kɛlata zo ɔyɛ mɛla la ɔmanle Agagenli Heeman, mɔɔ le Hamɛdeeta ara nrenya ne mɔɔ kpɔ Dwuuma la,

english_verse: “Do what you want with those people! You can keep their money.”
translation_verse: na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Menli ne wɔ ɛ sa nu. Ezukoa ne le wɔ ɛdeɛ. Mɔɔ ɛnea a ɔfɛta bɛ la, fa yɛ bɛ.”

english_verse: On the thirteenth day of Nisan, Haman called in the king's secretaries and ordered them to write letters in every language used in the kingdom. The letters were written in the name of the king and sealed by using the king's own ring. At once they were sent to the king's highest officials, the governors of each province, and the leaders of the different nations in the kingdom of Xerxes.
translation_verse: Wɔ siane ne mɔɔ lumua la anu, ye kenle bulu nee nsa ne azo, Heeman manle bɛyiale belemgbunli ne kɛlɛhɛlɛvolɛma ne mɔ na ɔmanle bɛhɛlɛle mɛla mɔɔ yeli la anwo ngɛlata kɛ bɛva bɛhɔmaa mgbanyima mɔɔ le kɛ safohyenlema, amɛnladoma, yɛɛ arane mbɔlɔba mgbanyima ne mɔ amuala. Maanle ko biala anu amra kɛlata ɛdeɛ ne bɛhɛlɛle ye wɔ bɛdabɛ bɛ aneɛ nee bɛ ɛhɛlɛndenle nu. Bɛhɛlɛle ngɛlata ne mɔ wɔ Belemgbunli Zɛzɛse duma nu.

english_verse: The letters were taken by messengers to every part of the kingdom, and this is what was said in the letters: On the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month, all Jewish men, women, and children are to be killed. And their property is to be taken.
translation_verse: Bɛvale ngɛlata ne mɔ bɛzoanle menli mɔɔ kola nriandi kpalɛ la a hɔle a. Ngɛlata ne mɔ kile kɛ bɛhu Dwuuma, ngakula nee mgbanyinli, yɛɛ mraalɛ kɔsɔɔti na bɛbɔ bɛ bo zo, na bɛve bɛ ninyɛne. Ngɛlata ne kile kɛ bɛva kenle ko ala a bɛyɛ ɛhye mɔ a, na bɛyɛ ye wɔ siane bulu nee nwiɔ ne mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye “Eda” la ye kenle ne mɔɔ tɔ zolɛ bulu nee nsa ne la azo.

english_verse: King Xerxes gave orders for these letters to be posted where they could be seen by everyone all over the kingdom. The king's command was obeyed, and one of the letters was read aloud to the people in the walled city of Susa. Then the king and Haman sat down to drink together, but no one in the city could figure out what was going on.
translation_verse: Menli mɔɔ bɛzoanle bɛ la manle bɛ nwo yɛle ndɛ bɛhɔle na eza bɛbɔle mɛla ne nolo wɔ Susa mɔɔ le maanle maanle ne suakpole la azo. Akee belemgbunli ne nee Heeman dɛnlanle aze nlonle, liele bɛ nye, noko wɔ Susa suakpole ne azo ɛdeɛ, ɛnee menli adwenle ɛzɛkye kpalɛ.

english_verse: When Mordecai heard about the letter, he tore his clothes in sorrow and put on sackcloth. Then he covered his head with ashes and went through the city, crying and weeping.
translation_verse: Mekɛ mɔɔ Mɔdekae dele edwɛkɛ mɔɔ ɛzi la, ɔsuosuanle ye tɛladeɛ ne mɔɔ ɔwula la anu, na ɔvale ɛrele ɔhedale, na ɔvale nzonle ɔbɔle ɔ nwo, na akee ɔvale ɛzunlɛ ɔyele awolɛ ɔdudule gua toonwo ɔhɔdwule suakpole ne avinli lɔ.

english_verse: But he could go only as far as the palace gate, because no one wearing sackcloth was allowed inside the palace.
translation_verse: Ɔhɔle toonwo ɔhɔle belemgbunli ne anuhɔlɛ kpole ne anloa, noko yeanwolo nu, ɔluakɛ bɛngeda ɛrele bɛngɔ suakunlu ɛkɛ ne.

english_verse: In every province where the king's orders were read, the Jews cried and mourned, and they went without eating. Many of them even put on sackcloth and sat in ashes.
translation_verse: Maanle ne anu ɛleka biala mɔɔ bɛkɛde belemgbunli ne nolo ne la, Dwuuma mɔɔ wɔ ɛkɛ ne la di nyane kpalɛ, bɛdi buada, na bɛsu bɛye awolɛ. Bɛ nuhua dɔɔnwo bɔbɔ fa nzonle bɔ bɛ nwo na bɛkeda ɛrele bɛda.

english_verse: When Esther's servant girls and her other servants told her what Mordecai was doing, she became very upset and sent Mordecai some clothes to wear in place of the sackcloth. But he refused to take them.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Ɛseta sonvolɛ mraalɛ nee mrenya ne mɔ nwunle mɔɔ Mɔdekae ɛlɛyɛ la, bɛhanle bɛhilele ye, na ye adwenle zɛkyele. Ɛhye ati ɔvale adɛladeɛ kɛ bɛva bɛhɔmaa Mɔdekae ɛwula na ɔkpa ɛrele ne ɔgua, noko Mɔdekae anlie.

english_verse: Esther had a servant named Hathach, who had been given to her by the king. So she called him in and said, “Find out what's wrong with Mordecai and why he's acting this way.”
translation_verse: Akee Ɛseta vɛlɛle Hatakye, mɔɔ le sonvolɛ nrenya mɔɔ belemgbunli ne ɛye ye kɛ ɔzonle Ɛseta la, na ɔzoanle ye kɛ ɔhɔbiza Mɔdekae deɛ holɛ ko mɔɔ ɔlɛyɛ la abo, nee kɛ ɔyɛle mɔɔ ɔrale ye zɔhane la.

english_verse: Hathach went to Mordecai in the city square in front of the palace gate,
translation_verse: Hatakye hɔle Mɔdekae anwo ɛkɛ wɔ suakpole ne ɛleka wienyi ne mɔɔ bɛyia la, wɔ belemgbunli sua ne anyunlu ɛkɛ.

english_verse: and Mordecai told him everything that had happened. He also told him how much money Haman had promised to add to the king's treasury, if all the Jews were killed.
translation_verse: Mɔdekae hanle mɔɔ ɛzi ɔ nwo zo la amuala hilele ye nee ezukoa mɔɔ Heeman ɛbɔ ɛwɔkɛ kɛ saa bɛku Dwuuma amuala a ɔkɛdua ɔkɛgua belemgbunli ne gya nu la ɔhilele ye.

english_verse: Mordecai gave Hathach a copy of the orders for the murder of the Jews and told him that these had been read in Susa. He said, “Show this to Esther and explain what it means. Ask her to go to the king and beg him to have pity on her people, the Jews!”
translation_verse: Mɔdekae eza vale nolobɔlɛ kɛlata ne mɔɔ bɛva bɛdo gua wɔ Susa mɔɔ kile kɛ bɛhu Dwuuma bɛbɔ bɛ bo zo la bie manle Hatakye kɛ ɔva ɔhɔmaa Ɛseta, na ɔhile nuhua ɔhile ye. Ɔzele Hatakye kɛ ɔze Ɛseta kɛ ɔdaye noko ɔhɔnwu belemgbunli na ɔbodo ye ɔmaa ɔnwu ye menli ne anwunvɔne.

english_verse: there is a law about going in to see the king, and all his officials and his people know about this law. Anyone who goes in to see the king without being invited by him will be put to death. The only way that anyone can be saved is for the king to hold out the gold scepter to that person. And it's been thirty days since he has asked for me.”
translation_verse: “Mɛla mɔɔ wɔ suakunlu ɛke la a le kɛ, awie biala, nrenya o, raalɛ o, mɔɔ bɛanvɛlɛ ye na ɔkɛwolo belemgbunli suakunlu ɛkɛ ne kɛ ɔkanwu ye la, ɔwɔ kɛ bɛku ye. Awie biala, ɛbɔ ye belemgbunli folɛdulɛma anwo zo toonwo badwu menli mɔɔ wɔ maanle ye maanzinli ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti anu la, ze mɛla ɛhye.
