Kyesɛ sonla mɔɔ belemgbunli ne kɛkpogya ye tumi nvutuke kpɔma ne zo kɛhile ye la, yɛɛ kɛnyia ɔ ti a. Na mame noko, ye siane ko ɛne, belemgbunli ɛtɛfɛlɛle me.”

english_verse: When Mordecai was told what Esther had said,
translation_verse: Mɔdekae dele Ɛseta nrɛlaleɛ ne la,

english_verse: he sent back this reply, “Don't think that you will escape being killed with the rest of the Jews, just because you live in the king's palace.
translation_verse: ɔmanle bɛhɔbɔle ye kɔkɔ: ɔse, “Mmadwenle kɛ ɛwɔ belemgbunli sua nu la ati, mɔɔ bazi Dwuuma anwo zo la bakpa ɛ ti.

english_verse: If you don't speak up now, we will somehow get help, but you and your family will be killed. It could be that you were made queen for a time like this!”
translation_verse: Saa ɛyɛ koonwu wɔ mekɛ ɛhye anu a, moalɛ vi anwuma bara amaa Dwuuma anyia bɛ ti, noko wɔmɔ, ɛbawu na ɛ ze abusua ne abɔ tɔɔ. Noko akee, nwane a ze a? Bie a ɛnee edwɛkɛ mɔɔ le kɛ ɛhye mɔ la ati yɛɛ wɔrayɛ belemgbunli raalɛ a.”

english_verse: Esther sent a message to Mordecai, saying,
translation_verse: Ɛseta vale mualɛ hɔmanle Mɔdekae kɛ,

english_verse: “Bring together all the Jews in Susa and tell them to go without eating for my sake! Don't eat or drink for three days and nights. My servant girls and I will do the same. Then I will go in to see the king, even if it means I must die.”
translation_verse: “Kɔ na kɔboɔboa Dwuuma mɔɔ wɔ Susa ɛke la amuala anloa, maa bɛhye ɛhɔne na bɛzɛlɛ bɛmaa me. Bɛmmadi debie biala yɛɛ bɛmmano nzule toonwo kenle nsa. Me nee me sonvolɛ mraalɛ ne mɔ yɛdayɛ yɛbayɛ zɔhane ala. Ɛhye anzi, mebahɔ belemgbunli ɛkɛ. Ɛhye tia mɛla ne bɔbɔ ɛdeɛ, noko saa ɔlua ɛhye ati na ɔwɔ kɛ mewu a, menwɔwu.”

english_verse: Mordecai did everything Esther told him to do.
translation_verse: Akee Mɔdekae hɔle na ɔhɔyɛle debie biala mɔɔ Ɛseta zele ye la.

english_verse: Three days later, Esther dressed in her royal robes and went to the inner court of the palace in front of the throne. The king was sitting there, facing the open doorway.
translation_verse: Kenle nsa ne dwule la, Ɛseta wulale ye belemgbunli raalɛ tɛladeɛ ne na ɔhɔgyinlanle suakunlu ɛkɛ ne alie ne anwo, ɛleka mɔɔ nee belemgbunli asalo kpole ne anye bɔ zolɛ la. Mekɛ ne anu ɛnee belemgbunli ne de ye ebia nu wɔ ye sua ne anu, ɛleka mɔɔ nee suakunlu ɛkɛ ne anuhɔlɛ ne anye bɔ zolɛ la.

english_verse: He was happy to see Esther, and he held out the gold scepter to her. When Esther came up and touched the tip of the scepter,
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne nwunle Belemgbunli Raalɛ Ɛseta kɛ ɔgyi alie ne anwo la, ɔ nye liele, na ɔkpogyale ye tumi ezukoa nvutuke kpɔma ne ati zo ɔhilele ye. Ɛseta dudule agyakɛ hɔle ɔ nyunlu na ɔvale ɔ sa ɔhɔhanle belemgbunli tumi kpɔma ne ati.

english_verse: the king said, “Esther, what brings you here? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne bizale ye kɛ, “Belemgbunli Raalɛ Ɛseta, duzu ɔ? Duzu a ɛkpondɛ a? Saa ɛkpondɛ me maanle ye foa ko bɔbɔ a, ɛ sa baha ye.”

english_verse: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please come with Haman to a dinner I will prepare for you later today.”
translation_verse: Ɛseta buale ye kɛ, “Nana, mesɛlɛ wɔ, saa mekola ye ka a anrɛɛ mese saa ɛkulo a ɛ nee Heeman bɛrɛla me ɛkɛ ɛnɛ nɔsolɛ na meyɛ debie mezie wɔ na bɛrakpula bɛ sa.”

english_verse: The king said to his servants, “Hurry and get Haman, so we can accept Esther's invitation.” The king and Haman went to Esther's dinner,
translation_verse: Belemgbunli zele kɛ, “Bɛhɔvɛlɛ Heeman bɛmaa ɔrɛla ndɛndɛ, na yɛhɔ Ɛseta ɛvɛlɛlɛ ne.” Zɔhane ati belemgbunli ne nee Heeman hɔle Ɛseta ɛkponle ne mɔɔ ɔdole ɔmanle belemgbunli ne la abo.

english_verse: and while they were drinking wine, the king asked her, “What can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom.”
translation_verse: Mekɛ mɔɔ ɛnee bɛwɔ zolɛ bɛlɛno nwanye la, belemgbunli bizale Ɛseta kɛ, “Duzu a ɛkpondɛ a? Debie mɔɔ ɛkpondɛ la, mebayɛ meamaa wɔ. Duzu a ɛkpondɛ a? Saa ɛkulo me belemgbunli maanle ye foa ko bɔbɔ a, mebava meamaa wɔ.”

english_verse: Esther replied, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to do what I want, please come again tomorrow with Haman to the dinner I will prepare for you. At that time I will answer Your Majesty's question.” Haman Plans To Kill Mordecai
translation_verse: saa me nyunlu ɛra anyia wɔ Nana anyunlu, na mɔɔ mekulo na mekpondɛ kɛ Nana yɛ maa me la ɔkɛyɛ ɛdeɛ a, ɛnee ɛhyema nɔsolɛ Nana nee Heeman bɛrɛla bɛrakpula bɛ sa wɔ ɛke na menye edwɛkɛ ne mɔɔ Nana ɛbiza me la anloa.” Heeman fa adwenle kɛ ɔku Mɔdekae

english_verse: Haman was feeling great as he left. But when he saw Mordecai at the palace gate, he noticed that Mordecai did not stand up or show him any respect. This made Haman really angry,
translation_verse: Kenle ko zɔhane Heeman vale anyelielɛ nee fɛlɛko ngome a hɔle a. Na mɔɔ ɔkɔ na ɔnwunle Mɔdekae wɔ suakunlu ɛkɛ ne anuhɔlɛ ne, na yeandwazo, yɛɛ ye ahonle amkputi ye bɔbɔ la, ɔvale Mɔdekae anwo ɛya kpole.

english_verse: but he did not say a thing. When Haman got home, he called together his friends and his wife Zeresh
translation_verse: Noko Heeman zɔle ɔ nwo, yeanga edwɛkɛ biala na ɔhɔle sua nu. Ɔdwule sua nu la, ɔzoanle ɔmanle bɛhɔvɛlɛle ɔ gɔnwo mɔ nee ɔ ye Zilɛhye.

english_verse: and started bragging about his great wealth and all his sons. He told them the many ways that the king had honored him and how all the other officials and leaders had to respect him.
translation_verse: Bɛrale la, Heeman sosɔle zolɛ hanle ɔ nwo mɔɔ yenyia ye kpole, ɔ mra dodo mɔɔ yewo bɛ, yɛɛ ɔ nyunlu mɔɔ belemgbunli ne ɛmaa yenyia wɔ gyima nu yeva yewula ɔdaye Heeman anyunlunyia la amuala ɔhilele bɛ. Eza ɔhanle kɛ belemgbunli ɛzi ɛmaa ye dibilɛ yedɛla amɛnladoma nee sonvolɛma amuala mɔɔ wɔ suakunlu ɛkɛ ne la ɔhilele bɛ.

english_verse: Haman added, “That's not all! Besides the king himself, I'm the only person Queen Esther invited for dinner. She has also invited the king and me to dinner tomorrow.
translation_verse: Akee ɔvale ɔzɔle zolɛ kɛ, “Belemgbunli Raalɛ Ɛseta ammaa awie biala adenle ammaa ɔ nee belemgbunli ne amba ɛkponledolɛ ne bie kɛ medame me ngomekye ala. Eza yedo ɛsalɛ yevɛlɛ me nee belemgbunli ne kɛ ɛhyema yɛrɛla.

english_verse: But none of this makes me happy, as long as I see that Jew Mordecai serving the king.”
translation_verse: Noko ɛhye mɔ amuala biala ɛnyɛ me fɛ, ɔluakɛ Dwuunli Mɔdekae ɔdaye kɛ dahuu ɔde suakunlu anuhɔlɛ ɛkɛ ne ala ɛne.”

english_verse: That night the king could not sleep, and he had a servant read him the records of what had happened since he had been king.
translation_verse: Kenle ko ne nɔe ne belemgbunli ne angola da. Yemɔti ɔzele kɛ bɛva buluku ne mɔɔ bɛhɛlɛ ninyɛne kpalɛ mɔɔ menli ɛyɛ la wɔ nuhua la bɛrɛla. Bɛvale bɛrale na bɛgengale bɛhilele ye.

english_verse: the king asked, “What has been done to reward Mordecai for this?” “Nothing, Your Majesty!” the king's servants replied.
translation_verse: Na belemgbunli ne bizale kɛ, “Duzu a bɛyɛ bɛmaa Mɔdekae wɔ ɛhye anwo a?” Belemgbunli sonvolɛma ne hanle kɛ, “Bɛtɛyɛle ɛhwee bɛtɛmanle ye.”

english_verse: About this time, Haman came in to ask the king to have Mordecai hanged on the gallows he had built. The king saw him and asked, “Who is that man waiting in front of the throne room?”
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne bizale kɛ, “Na nwane a wɔ ɛkɛ ne a?” Mekɛ ne anu ala ɛnee Heeman ɛra suakunlu ɛkɛ ne alie ne anwo kɛ ɔbaha Mɔdekae ɛhunlɛ nwo edwɛkɛ yeahile ye. Ɛnee Heeman ɛziezie ɛleka mɔɔ bɛbazinze Mɔdekae bɛahu ye la ɛwie.

english_verse: The king's servants answered, “Your Majesty, it is Haman.” “Tell him to come in,” the king commanded.
translation_verse: Sonvolɛma ne hanle hilele belemgbunli ne kɛ, “Heeman a wɔ ɛkɛ a, na ɔkulo kɛ ɔnwu wɔ.” Belemgbunli ne zele kɛ, “Bɛze ye kɛ ɔrɛla.”

english_verse: When Haman entered the room, the king asked him, “What should I do for a man I want to honor?” Haman was sure that he was the one the king wanted to honor.
translation_verse: Heeman wolole sua ne anu ala la, belemgbunli ne bizale ye kɛ, “Duzu debie yɛɛ ɔwɔ kɛ bɛyɛ bɛmaa sonla mɔɔ belemgbunli anye ɛlie ɔ nwo na ɔkulo kɛ ɔdi ye eni la a?” Heeman hanle ye ɔ ti anu kɛ, “Ɛnee nwane ala bɔbɔ yɛɛ belemgbunli kɛli ye eni kɛdɛla me a? Medame ala ɔ!”

english_verse: get someone to bring him one of your own robes and one of your own horses with a fancy headdress.
translation_verse: Na Heeman hanle kɛ, “Saa belemgbunli kulo kɛ ɔwula awie anyunlunyia a, ɛnee ɔmaa bɛva belemgbunli adɛladeɛ mɔɔ ɛdawɔ wɔwula ye ɛlɛ la bɛrɛla, bɛva ɛkpɔnwɔ mɔɔ belemgbunli ɛdɛnla zolɛ na bɛzoa ye belemgbunli kyɛlɛ la bɛrɛla,

english_verse: The king replied, “Hurry and do just what you have said! Don't forget a thing. Get the robe and the horse for Mordecai the Jew, who serves as one of the king's officials!”
translation_verse: Na belemgbunli ne zele Heeman kɛ, “Ka ɛ nwo kɔva belemgbunli adɛladeɛ ne mɔ bie nee ɛkpɔnwɔ, kɛmɔ ɛdawɔ wɔha la, na yɛ mɔɔ wɔha la maa Dwuunli Mɔdekae mɔɔ de suakunlu ɛke anuhɔlɛ ne la. Debie biala mɔɔ wɔha la, mmagyakyi bie nuhua.”

english_verse: Haman got the king's robe and put it on Mordecai. He led him through the city on the horse and shouted as he went, “This is how the king honors a man!”
translation_verse: Yemɔti Heeman hɔvale adɛladeɛ ne nee ɛkpɔnwɔ ne. Ɔzieziele Mɔdekae, ɔvale ye ɔdɛnlanle ɛkpɔnwɔ ne azo na ɔvale ye ɔdudule gua wɔ suakpole ne azo ɛleka wienyi ne mɔɔ ɔyɛ a bɛyia la, ɔbɔle nolo kɛ, “Kɛ ɔwɔ kɛ bɛyɛ sonla ne mɔɔ belemgbunli kulo kɛ ɔwula ye anyunlunyia la ɛne!”

english_verse: Afterwards, Mordecai returned to his duties in the king's palace, and Haman hurried home, hiding his face in shame.
translation_verse: Akee Mɔdekae ziale hɔdɛnlanle ɔ bo zo ne wɔ belemgbunli ne anuhɔlɛ ne. Na Heeman hedale ɔ ti zo na ɔvale nyane nee nyiane ɔhɔle sua nu ndɛndɛ.

english_verse: Haman told his wife and friends what had happened. Then his wife and his advisors said, “If Mordecai is a Jew, this is just the beginning of your troubles! You will end up a ruined man.”
translation_verse: Heeman hanle mɔɔ ɛzi ɔ nwo zo la amuala hilele ɔ ye Zilɛhye nee ɔ gɔnwo mɔ amuala. Na ye menli ne mɔɔ tu ye folɛ la nee ɔ ye Zilɛhye zele ye kɛ, “Saa Mɔdekae mɔɔ kɛkala wɔbɔ ɔ bo kɛ ɛlɛtu ɛtɔ ɔ nyunlu la le Dwuunli ɛdeɛ a, ɛnee noko ɛnrɛhola ye, ɔbali ɛ nwo zo konim.” Bɛku Heeman

english_verse: They were still talking, when the king's servants came and quickly took Haman to the dinner that Esther had prepared.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Heeman agɔnwo mɔ nee ɔ ye anloa wɔ zolɛ bɛ nee ye ɛlɛtendɛ la, yɛɛ belemgbunli ne sonvolɛma rale a, na bɛvale ye bɛ nee ye hɔle ɛkponle ne mɔɔ Ɛseta ɛdo ɛmaa belemgbunli ne la abo.

english_verse: and drinking wine during the second dinner, when the king again said, “Esther, what can I do for you? Just ask, and I will give you as much as half of my kingdom!”
translation_verse: Na ye kenle nwiɔ ne azo, mekɛ mɔɔ ɛnee bɛlɛno nwanye la, belemgbunli ne eza bizale Ɛseta kɛ, “Belemgbunli Raalɛ Ɛseta, duzu a ɛkulo kɛ meyɛ memaa wɔ a? Duzu a ɛkpondɛ a? Debie biala mɔɔ ɛkulo la ka na mebava meamaa wɔ. Saa ɛkpondɛ me maanle ye foa ko bɔbɔ a, ɛ sa baha ye.”

english_verse: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, if you really care for me and are willing to help, you can save me and my people. That's what I really want,
translation_verse: Belemgbunli Raalɛ Ɛseta yele ɔ nloa kɛ, “Nana, saa mezɔ ɛ nye na ɔyɛ Nana ɛhulolɛ kɛ ɔkɛyɛ mɔɔ mekpondɛ la amgba a ɛnee Nana, mesɛlɛ wɔ, die me nee me menli ne fi ewule nu.

english_verse: because a reward has been promised to anyone who kills my people. Your Majesty, if we were merely going to be sold as slaves, I would not have bothered you.”
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ bɛdɔne me nee me menli ne bɛmaa kɛ bɛhu yɛ bɛbɔ yɛ bo zo bɔkɔɔ. Saa bɛdɔnenle yɛ kɛ ahanra mrenya nee mraalɛ ala a, anrɛɛ ɔnvane me nwo. Ɔluakɛ yɛ kpɔvolɛ ne ɛhunlɛ mɔɔ ɔbamaa bɛahu yɛ la ɛnrɛhola ɛnrɛzie mɔɔ belemgbunli ne baminli ye la abo zo.”

english_verse: “Who would dare to do such a thing?” the king asked.
translation_verse: Belemgbunli Zɛzɛse bizale Belemgbunli Raalɛ Ɛseta kɛ, “Ɛnee nwane a ɔdaye yehola yeyɛ debie zɛhae a, yɛɛ ahenle wɔ nienwu?”

english_verse: Esther replied, “That evil Haman is the one out to get us!” Haman was terrified, as he looked at the king and the queen.
translation_verse: Ɛseta buale ye kɛ, “Kpɔvolɛ ne mɔɔ ɛwie yɛ yɛ la a le Heeman amumuyɛ ɛhye!” Heeman ahonle dule na ɔ nye hale belemgbunli ne nee Belemgbunli Raalɛ Ɛseta anyunlu.

english_verse: The king was so angry that he got up, left his wine, and went out into the palace garden. Haman realized that the king had already decided what to do with him, and he stayed and begged Esther to save his life.
translation_verse: Na ɛkɛ ne ala belemgbunli ne vale ɛya, na ɔdwazole ɛkponle ne anwo, ɔhɔle suakunlu ɛkɛ ne tola ne anu. english_verse: Just as the king came back into the room, Haman got down on his knees beside Esther, who was lying on the couch. The king shouted, “Now you're even trying to rape my queen here in my own palace!” As soon as the king said this, his servants covered Haman's head.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Heeman dule dɔle ebia ne mɔɔ Ɛseta la nu la azo kɛ ɔkpa ye kyɛlɛ. Mekɛ ne anu ala yɛɛ belemgbunli ne vindele ɛkɛ ne a, na ɔzele kɛ, “Wio o! Akee eza me nyunlu ɛke ala, wɔ me gyakɛ azo ɛke yɛɛ Heeman akee bafunlofunla belemgbunli raalɛ ye a?” Belemgbunli ne anloa ampe bɔbɔ yɛɛ sonvolɛma ne mɔ hedale Heeman ati zo a.

english_verse: At once, Haman was hanged on the gallows he had built to hang Mordecai, and the king calmed down.
translation_verse: Na bɛvale Heeman bɛhɔzinzele ɛhuleka ne mɔɔ ɔmanle bɛzieziele kɛ ɔbava yeahu Mɔdekae la azo. Na akee belemgbunli ne akunlu dwole fɔɔnwo.

english_verse: Before the end of the day, King Xerxes gave Esther everything that had belonged to Haman, the enemy of the Jews. Esther told the king that Mordecai was her cousin. So the king made Mordecai one of his highest officials
translation_verse: Kenle ko zɔhane Belemgbunli Zɛzɛse vale Heeman mɔɔ le Dwuuma kpɔvolɛ ne la debie biala manle Belemgbunli Raalɛ Ɛseta. Akee Mɔdekae nyianle adenle wɔ belemgbunli sua nu ɛkɛ ne, ɔluakɛ ɛnee Ɛseta ɛha ɛhile belemgbunli ne kɛ ye awie a le Mɔdekae.

english_verse: and gave him the royal ring that Haman had worn. Then Esther put Mordecai in charge of Haman's property.
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne vale ye kpɔdelera ne mɔɔ ɔfa ɔsi kɛlata zo, mɔɔ ɔliele ɔvile Heeman ɛkɛ ne la manle Mɔdekae. Na Ɛseta yɛle Mɔdekae kpanyinli mɔɔ nea debie biala mɔɔ Heeman lɛ la azo.

english_verse: Once again Esther went to speak to the king. This time she fell down at his feet, crying and begging, “Please stop Haman's evil plan to have the Jews killed!”
translation_verse: Akee Ɛseta dule dɔle belemgbunli ne agyakɛ anu, na ɔvale ɛzunlɛ ɔbodole ye kɛ ɔbɔ mɔdenle ɔye munzule kpole ne mɔɔ Agage anlɔnra Heeman ɛhyehyɛ ɛva Dwuuma amuala akɔme ɛwula nu la wɔ bɛ ti.

english_verse: King Xerxes held out the golden scepter to Esther,
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne kpogyale ye tumi ezukoa nvutuke kpɔma ne ati zo hilele Ɛseta,

english_verse: and she got up and said, “Your Majesty, I know that you will do the right thing and that you really love me. Please stop what Haman has planned. He has already sent letters demanding that the Jews in all your provinces be killed,
translation_verse: na Ɛseta dwazole gyinlanle. Na ɔzele kɛ, “Awulae, mesɛlɛ wɔ, mmafa ɛya. english_verse: King Xerxes then said to Esther and Mordecai, “I have already ordered Haman to be hanged and his house given to Esther, because of his evil plans to kill the Jews.
translation_verse: Na Belemgbunli Zɛzɛse zele Belemgbunli Raalɛ Ɛseta nee Dwuunli Mɔdekae kɛ, “Bɛdie, meva debie biala mɔɔ le Heeman ɛdeɛ la memaa Ɛseta na memaa bɛzinze Heeman bɛhu ye, wɔ ye adwenle ɛtane ne mɔɔ ɔvale kɛ ɔku Dwuuma la ati.

english_verse: I now give you permission to make a law that will save the lives of your people. You may use my ring to seal the law, so that it can never be changed.”
translation_verse: Na ɛdawɔ noko ɛze kɛ kɛlata mɔɔ bɛkɛva belemgbunli ne duma bɛkɛhɛlɛ na bɛkɛva ye kpɔdelera ne bɛkɛzi zolɛ la, bɛndwe bɛnzia, yɛɛ bɛmpɛ nuhua. Zɔhane ati bɛdabɛ bɛva belemgbunli ne duma bɛhɛlɛ mɔɔ bɛdabɛ bɛnea a bɛkulo kɛ Dwuuma yɛ la, bɛva belemgbunli ne kpɔdelera ne bɛzi zolɛ na bɛva bɛhɔmaa bɛ.”

english_verse: They were written in the name of King Xerxes and sealed with his ring. Then they were taken by messengers who rode the king's finest and fastest horses.
translation_verse: Mɔdekae manle bɛvale Belemgbunli Zɛzɛse duma a bɛhɛlɛle ngɛlata ne mɔ a, yɛɛ bɛvale belemgbunli ne kpɔdelera ne bɛsisile ngɛlata ne mɔ azo. Belemgbunli sonvolɛma mɔɔ tɛnla mgbɔnwɔ mɔɔ anwo yɛ ndɛ na bɛyɛne bɛ wɔ belemgbunli ne ɔdaye ye tunli nu la azo a hɔle a.

english_verse: In these letters the king said: On the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month, the Jews in every city and province will be allowed to get together and defend themselves. They may destroy any army that attacks them, and they may kill all of their enemies, including women and children. They may also take everything that belongs to their enemies. A copy of this law is to be posted in every province and read by everyone.
translation_verse: Ɔwɔ kɛ bɛyɛ kɛlata ne mɔɔ bɛ sa baha ye maanzinli ne mɔ anu la anu edwɛkɛ ne mɛla; ɔwɔ kɛ bɛbɔ edwɛkɛ ne nolo bɛkile menli ne amuala na bɛmaa Dwuuma adenle bɛmaa bɛboɔboa bɛ nwo bɛ nee kpɔvolɛma ko die bɛ nwo.

english_verse: Then the king ordered his messengers to take their fastest horses and deliver the law as quickly as possible to every province. When Mordecai left, he was wearing clothes fit for a king. He wore blue and white robes, a large gold crown, and a cape made of fine linen and purple cloth. After the law was announced in Susa, everyone shouted and cheered,
translation_verse: Akee Mɔdekae vi belemgbunli sua nu finde a ɔwula belemgbunli tɛladeɛ buluwu nee fufule, na ɔsoa belemgbunli ezukoa nvutuke kyɛlɛ, na yeava dwɛsɛ ɛdanlɛ anye nwohyee nee kɔkɔlɛ kɛnlɛma bie yeagua zolɛ. Ɔvi belemgbunli sua nu ɔfinde a ɛnee awie biala anye ɛlie.

english_verse: and the Jews were no longer afraid. In fact, they were very happy and felt that they had won a victory.
translation_verse: Dwuuma mɔɔ wɔ suakpole ne azo la anwo dɔle bɛ, bɛlile fɛlɛko, bɛ nye liele, na awie biala lile bɛ eni.

english_verse: In every province and city where the law was sent, the Jews had parties and celebrated. Many of the people in the provinces accepted the Jewish religion, because they were now afraid of the Jews.
translation_verse: Wɔ maanzinli biala anu anzɛɛ suakpole biala azo mɔɔ belemgbunli ne kɛlata ne nee ye mɛla ne kɛdwu la, Dwuuma anye die, bɛdi fɛlɛko, bɛsie kenle bɛdie bɛ ɛnwomenle na bɛto ɛkponle. Menli dɔɔnwo noko mɔɔ wɔ maanle ne anu la zulole Dwuuma, na ɔlua zolɛ bɛhakyile bɛyɛle Dwuuma.

english_verse: The first law that the king had made was to be followed on the thirteenth day of Adar, the twelfth month. This was the very day that the enemies of the Jews had hoped to do away with them. But the Jews turned things around,
translation_verse: Siane bulu nee nwiɔ ne mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye “Eda” la, ye kenle bulu nee nsa ne azo yɛɛ belemgbunli ne mɛla ne nee ye ngɛlata ne mɔ anu edwɛkɛ ne mekɛ dwule a, na mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ si la si. Kenle ko ne yɛɛ bɛhyehyɛ kɛ ɔwɔ kɛ bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛngulo Dwuuma edwɛkɛ la dwazo bɛ nwo zo na bɛku bɛ a. Noko ɛhye anyɛ zɔhane. Ɔyɛle kenle mɔɔ Dwuuma lile bɛ kpɔvolɛma anwo zo konim a.

english_verse: and in the cities of every province they came together to attack their enemies. Everyone was afraid of the Jews, and no one could do anything to oppose them.
translation_verse: Dwuuma mɔɔ wɔ azuamgbole mɔɔ wɔ maanle mɔɔ Belemgbunli Zɛzɛse sie bɛ la azo la boɔboale bɛ nloa na bɛhonle bɛliele bɛ nwo bɛvile awie biala mɔɔ rale bɛ nwo zo kɛ ɔbahu bɛ la asa anu. Na awie biala angola bɛ nyunlu gyinla, ɔluakɛ ɛnee bɛ nwo ɛzulolɛ ɛyɛ debie ɛdɔ menli ne kɔsɔɔti anwo zo.

english_verse: The leaders of the provinces, the rulers, the governors, and the court officials were afraid of Mordecai and took sides with the Jews.
translation_verse: Arane mbɔlɔba mgbanyinli, amɛnladoma, maanzinli zo neavolɛma, yɛɛ arane mbɔlɔba kɔsɔɔti lile boale Dwuuma, ɔluakɛ ɛnee bɛsulo Mɔdekae kpole kpalɛ.

english_verse: The Jews took their swords and did away with their enemies, without showing any mercy.
translation_verse: Na Dwuuma hunle bɛ kpɔvolɛma bɛzɛkyele bɛ na bɛyɛle bɛ kɛmɔ bɛdabɛ bɛkulo la.

english_verse: Later that day, someone told the king how many people had been killed in Susa.
translation_verse: Kenle ko ne ala bɛhanle menli mɔɔ bɛhu bɛ wɔ suakpole Susa angome azo la bɛhilele belemgbunli ne.

english_verse: Then he told Esther, “Five hundred people, including Haman's ten sons, have been killed in Susa alone. If that many were killed here, what must have happened in the provinces? Is there anything else you want done? Just tell me, and it will be done.”
translation_verse: Na belemgbunli ne zele Belemgbunli Raalɛ Ɛseta kɛ, “Wɔ Susa sua bɔdenle ye azo angome, Dwuuma ɛhu menli ɛya nnu. Heeman amra mrenya bulu ne boka nwolɛ. Na menea a maanzinli ne mɔ anu ɛdeɛ ne kɛyɛ ɛzulolɛ. Kɛkala duzu yɛɛ akee ɛkpondɛ a? Mɔɔ ɛkpondɛ la, ɛ sa baha ye. Duzu bieko a ɛkpondɛ a? Ka, na mebayɛ meamaa wɔ.”

english_verse: Esther answered, “Your Majesty, please let the Jews in Susa fight to defend themselves tomorrow, just as they did today. And order the bodies of Haman's ten sons to be hanged in public.”
translation_verse: Na Ɛseta buale kɛ, “Nana, mesɛlɛ wɔ, anrɛɛ mese ɛmaa Dwuuma mɔɔ wɔ Susa ɛke la adenle ɛmaa ɛhyema bɛyɛ mɔɔ ɛnɛ kenle ye bɛyɛ la bieko, na maa bɛva nyɛma bɛsosɔ Heeman amra bulu ne akɔme bɛhendɛhenda bɛ.”

english_verse: King Xerxes did what Esther had requested, and the bodies of Haman's sons were hung in Susa.
translation_verse: Zɔhane ati belemgbunli ne manle adenle manle bɛyɛle ɛhye, na bɛlile mɛla wɔ Susa, bɛmanle bɛhendɛhendanle Heeman amra bulu ne.

english_verse: On the thirteenth day of Adar, the Jews in the provinces had come together to defend themselves. They killed
translation_verse: Bɛyɛle ɛhye mɔ wɔ siane “Eda” ne ye kenle bulu nee nsa ne azo. Bɛliele bɛ ɛnwomenle wɔ kenle bulu nee nna ne azo, bɛliele bɛ nye na bɛlile fɛlɛko, bɛdole nwolɛ ɛkponle.

english_verse: On the fifteenth day of the month the Jews in Susa held a holiday and celebrated, after killing their enemies on the thirteenth and the fourteenth.
translation_verse: Na Dwuuma mɔɔ wɔ Susa la lile ahua na bɛhonle kenle bulu nee nsa ne nee kenle bulu nee nna ne azo na bɛliele bɛ ɛnwomenle wɔ kenle bulu nee nnu ne azo, bɛlile fɛlɛko na bɛdole ɛkponle bɛlieliele bɛ nye.

english_verse: This is why the Jews in the villages now celebrate on the fourteenth day of the month. It is a joyful holiday that they celebrate by feasting and sending gifts of food to each other. The Festival of Purim
translation_verse: Ɛhye ati yɛɛ Dwuuma mɔɔ wɔ namunamu ne mɔ nee azua ngyikyi zo la die bɛ ɛnwomenle wɔ siane “Eda” ne ye kenle bulu nee nna ne azo la. Ɔdwu zolɛ a, bɛ nye die, bɛdi fɛlɛko na bɛto ɛkponle, bɛfa aleɛ ahyɛlɛdeɛ bɛmemaa bɛ nwo ngoko ngoko. Pulem ɛvoyia ne

english_verse: Mordecai wrote down everything that had happened. Then he sent letters to the Jews everywhere in the provinces
translation_verse: Mɔdekae hɛlɛle ninyɛne ɛhye mɔ mɔɔ sisile la amuala wɔ ngɛlata zo na ɔvale ɔhɔmanle Dwuuma mɔɔ wɔ Belemgbunli Zɛzɛse maanle maanle ne mɔ anu la amuala.

english_verse: and told them: Each year you must celebrate on both the fourteenth and the fifteenth of Adar,
translation_verse: Wɔ ye ngɛlata ne mɔ anu, ɔzele Dwuuma kɛ bɛzie ɛvolɛ biala siane “Eda” ne ye kenle bulu nee nna nee ye kenle bulu nee nnu ne

english_verse: the days when we Jews defeated our enemies. Remember this month as a time when our sorrow was turned to joy, and celebration took the place of crying. Celebrate by having parties and by giving to the poor and by sharing gifts of food with each other.
translation_verse: kɛ bɛle kenle mɔɔ bɛvale bɛnyianle bɛ ti bɛvile bɛ kpɔvolɛma asa anu a. Siane zɔhane anu yɛɛ bɛ nyane nee bɛ arɛlebɔlɛ hakyile fɛlɛkolilɛ nee anyelielɛ a. Bɛ nwo dɔle bɛ na bɛliele bɛ ɛnwomenle. Ɔwɔ kɛ bɛdie bɛ nye na bɛto ɛkponle wɔ mekɛ ɛhye anu, na bɛfa ninyɛne bɛkyɛ bɛ nwo ngoko ngoko, na bɛfa ahyɛlɛdeɛ bɛmaa ehyianvolɛma.

english_verse: They followed Mordecai's instructions and set aside these two days every year as a time of celebration. The Reason for the Festival of Purim
translation_verse: Zɔhane ati Dwuuma lile Mɔdekae ngyehyɛlɛ ne azo, na bɛhɔle zolɛ bɛyɛle kenle ne ɛvoyia mɔɔ ɛvolɛ biala bɛdi a.

english_verse: Haman was the son of Hammedatha and a descendant of Agag. He hated the Jews so much that he planned to destroy them, but he wanted to find out the best time to do it. So he cast lots.
translation_verse: Agagenli Heeman, mɔɔ le Hamɛdeeta ara nrenya ne mɔɔ kpɔ Dwuuma kɛ debie la, vale Dwuuma amuala anwo adwenle kɛ ɔbɔ bɛ bo zo. Ɔlua zolɛ ɔhwenle nwolɛ adunyi, mɔɔ Hibulu nu bɛfɛlɛ ye “Pulu” la, kɛ ɔkpondɛ kenle mɔɔ ɔkɛva ɔkɛli zɔhane gyima ne la.

english_verse: Esther went to King Xerxes and asked him to save her people. Then the king gave written orders for Haman and his sons to be punished in the same terrible way that Haman had in mind for the Jews. So they were hanged.
translation_verse: Na Ɛseta hɔle belemgbunli ne anyunlu, na belemgbunli ne manle bɛhɛlɛle ngɛlata na ɔmanle adwenle ɛtane ne mɔɔ Heeman vale la hakyile dɔle ɔ nwo zo. Ɔlua zolɛ bɛzinzele ye nee ɔ mra mrenya bulu ne amuala bɛhunle bɛ.

english_verse: Mordecai's letter had said that the Jews must celebrate for two days because of what had happened to them. This time of celebration is called Purim, which is the Hebrew word for the lots that were cast.
translation_verse: Ɛhye ati a bɛfɛlɛ zɛhae ɛnwomenlelielɛ kenle ye “Pulem” a, ɔlua adunyi anzɛɛ “Pulu” ne mɔɔ bɛhwenle la ati. Zɔhane ala yɛɛ ɔlua mɔɔ Mɔdekae hɛlɛle, nee mɔɔ sisile bɛ nwo zo, nee mɔɔ bɛnwunle ye la ati,

english_verse: Now every year the Jews set aside these two days for having parties and celebrating, just as they were told to do.
translation_verse: Dwuuma ziele kenle ɛhye mɔ na bɛzɔle nu kɛ bɛdabɛ, bɛ nlɔnra, yɛɛ awie biala mɔɔ bokale bɛ la, kɛli ɛvoyia ɛhye ɛvolɛ biala mɔɔ ɔmkpa nwolɛ fee a, kɛmɔ bɛhɛlɛ bɛdo ɛkɛ ne la.

english_verse: Queen Esther, daughter of Abihail, wanted to give full authority to Mordecai's letter about the Festival of Purim, and with his help she wrote a letter about the feast.
translation_verse: Akee Belemgbunli Raalɛ Ɛseta mɔɔ le Abeheli ara raalɛ ne nee Dwuunli Mɔdekae hɛlɛle kɛlata hɔzile amozi kɛlata ne mɔɔ fane ɛvoyia “Pulem” ne anwo la pi.

english_verse: You and your descendants must always remember to celebrate Purim at the time and in the way that we have said. You must also follow the instructions that we have given you about mourning and going without eating.
translation_verse: kɛ ɛvoyia ɛhye mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye “Pulem” la dwu zolɛ a, bɛli, kɛmɔ Dwuunli Mɔdekae nee Belemgbunli Raalɛ Ɛseta ɛhyehyɛ ɛmaa Dwuuma kɔsɔɔti la. Bɛhyehyɛle ɛhye bɛmanle bɛdabɛ bɛ nwo nee bɛ mra nee bɛ bo zo amra amuala, kɛ bɛli zolɛ kɛmɔ bɛlile nyanelilɛ nee ɛhɔnehyelɛ ngyehyɛlɛ ne azo la.

english_verse: These laws about Purim are written by the authority of Queen Esther.
translation_verse: Belemgbunli Raalɛ Ɛseta a hyehyɛle zɛhae “Pulem” ɛvoyia ne a, yɛɛ bɛhɛlɛle bɛdole ɛkɛ a.

english_verse: King Xerxes made everyone in his kingdom pay taxes, even those in lands across the sea.
translation_verse: Akee Belemgbunli Zɛzɛse dele adwule manle bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛwɔ maanle ne anu ɛnweazo nee ɛbɔ nu la amuala.

english_verse: All the great and famous things that King Xerxes did are written in the record books of the kings of Media and Persia. These records also tell about the honors that the king gave to Mordecai.
translation_verse: Belemgbunli ne tumi nee ye ninyɛne mgbole mɔɔ ɔyɛle, nee eni mɔɔ ɔlile Mɔdekae ɔmanle ye zo wɔ ye gyima nu la, bɛhɛlɛ bɛ muala wɔ Midea nee Pɛhyea arelemgbunli edwɛkɛ mɔɔ sisile bɛ mekɛ zo la buluku ne anu.

english_verse: Next to the king himself, Mordecai was the highest official in the kingdom. He was a popular leader of the Jews, because he helped them in many ways and would even speak to the king on their behalf.
translation_verse: Ɛnee saa ɛye Belemgbunli Zɛzɛse a, Dwuunli Mɔdekae a wɔ ɛkɛ a. Mɔdekae nyianle ɔ nyunlu na Dwuuma nee ɔ gɔnwo mɔ amuala hulole ye edwɛkɛ na bɛlile ye eni. Mɔdekae eza kpondɛle Dwuuma kpalɛyɛlɛ na ɔmanle bɛ nzo nu dwole bɛ.

english_verse: Many years ago, a man named Job lived in the land of Uz. He was a truly good person, who respected God and refused to do evil.
translation_verse: Ɛnee nrenya bie wɔ Ɛɛze maanle nu. Bɛfɛlɛ ye Dwobu. Nrenya ɛhye anwo ɛnlɛ dɛne biala yɛɛ ɔle sonla fɔɔnwo, ɔdi nɔhalɛ ɔmaa Nyamenle, yɛɛ ɔkyi ɛtane.

english_verse: the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?” Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma bizale Seetan kɛ, “Na ɛvi nienwu yɛɛ wɔra ɛke a?” Seetan buale Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ, “Mewɔ akpɔsa nu wɔ aleɛabo. Ewiade anu ala yɛɛ medi ye akɔneaba a.”

english_verse: Job's sons took turns having feasts in their homes, and they always invited their three sisters to join in the eating and drinking.
translation_verse: Ɔ mra ne mɔ to ɛkponle bɛ ti ngoko. Saa ko biala mekɛ ɛdeɛ ne dwu a, ɔto ɛkponle na ɔfɛlɛvɛlɛ ɔ mediema mrenya ne mɔ nee bɛ mediema mraalɛ ne mɔ na bɛ nee bɛ di, no, dielie bɛ nye.

english_verse: After each feast, Job would send for his children and perform a ceremony, as a way of asking God to forgive them of any wrongs they may have done. He would get up early the next morning and offer a sacrifice for each of them, just in case they had sinned or silently cursed God. Angels, the Lord, and Satan
translation_verse: Saa bɛto ɛkponle ne toonwo na ɔyia bɛ ti a, Dwobu fɛlɛ bɛ na ɔnua bɛ. Ɔdwazo aleɛbahye na ɔbɔ bɛ ti ngoko ɔfa nane ɔyela ɔbɔ azu, ɔluakɛ Dwobu edwɛkɛ a le kɛ, “Wɔannea a ɛnee me mra ne mɔ ɛyɛ ɛtane wɔ bɛ ahonle nu na bɛdendɛ ɛtane bɛtia Nyamenle.” Dwobu yɛle ɛhye mekɛ biala.

english_verse: One day, when the angels had gathered around the Lord, and Satan was there with them,
translation_verse: Kenle ko Nyamenle anzɛɛ Anwuma amra hɔle Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlu kɛ bɛkava bɛ nwo bɛahile ye, na Seetan ɔdaye ɔhɔle ɛkɛ ne bie.

english_verse: Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil.”
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Seetan kɛ, “Wɔnwu me sonvolɛ Dwobu, awie biala mɔɔ le kɛ ɔdaye la ɛnle aleɛabo, ɛtane biala ɛnle ɔ nwo yɛɛ ɔdi nɔhalɛ. Ɔsulo Nyamenle yɛɛ ɔtwe ɔ nwo ɔfi ɛtane nwo.”

english_verse: “Why shouldn't he respect you?” Satan remarked.
translation_verse: Seetan buale Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ, “Na mgbane ala yɛɛ Dwobu sulo Nyamenle a?

english_verse: “You are like a wall protecting not only him, but his entire family and all his property. You make him successful in whatever he does, and his flocks and herds are everywhere.
translation_verse: Wɔbɔ ɔdaye, ɔ mra nee debie biala mɔɔ ɔlɛ la anwo bane. Dahuu ɛsinza ye, ye abusua ne nee debie biala mɔɔ ɔlɛ la. Wɔyila ɔ sa anloa gyima zo yɛɛ dahuu ye anwonyia ne, kpole ala a ɔyɛ a.

english_verse: Try taking away everything he owns, and he will curse you to your face.”
translation_verse: Saa ɛkulo a die debie biala mɔɔ ɔlɛ la fi ɔ sa nu na ɛkɛde mgbole mɔɔ ɔkɛheha ɔkɛtietia wɔ la.”

english_verse: The Lord replied, “All right, Satan, do what you want with anything that belongs to him, but don't harm Job.” Then Satan left. Job Loses Everything
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Seetan kɛ, “Nea, debie biala mɔɔ ɔlɛ la wɔ ɛ sa nu, noko mmafa ɛ sa ɛka Dwobu ɛleka biala fee.” Akee Seetan vi Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlu ɛkɛ ne hɔle. Dwobu amra nee ye anwonyia ɛzɛkye

english_verse: Job's sons and daughters were having a feast in the home of his oldest son,
translation_verse: Kenle ko mɔɔ Dwobu amra ne mɔ, mrenya nee mraalɛ yiale ralɛ nrenya kpanyinli ne sua nu na bɛlɛdi, bɛno nwanye la,

english_verse: when someone rushed up to Job and said, “While your servants were plowing with your oxen, and your donkeys were nearby eating grass,
translation_verse: ɛbɔfoɔ rale Dwobu ɛkɛ razele ye kɛ, “Mɔɔ nlankɛ ne mɔ ɛlɛfundu azɛlɛ ne na asoaso ne mɔ noko ɛlɛdidi bɛ nwo ɛkɛ ne la,

english_verse: a gang of Sabeans attacked and stole the oxen and donkeys! Your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: arɛlevilɛ nu ala, Sabima ralile yɛ nvunu hyehyele nlankɛ ne mɔ na bɛhunle sonvolɛma ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti. Me ngomekye ala a meha mɔɔ menriandi mera mebabɔ wɔ amaneɛ a.”

english_verse: That servant was still speaking, when a second one came running and said, “God sent down a fire that killed your sheep and your servants. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: Mɔɔ ɔ nloa wɔ zolɛ ɔlɛtendɛ la, ɛbɔfoɔ fofolɛ vindele ɛkɛ razele ye kɛ, “Nyamenle ɛkpakye ɛsɛnlɛmanye ɛhu mboane ne nee sonvolɛma ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti na yeyela bɛ wee. Me ngomekye ala a mevi nu mɔɔ mera mebabɔ wɔ amaneɛ a.”

english_verse: Before that servant finished speaking, a third one raced up and said, “Three gangs of Chaldeans attacked and stole your camels! All of your other servants were killed, and I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: Ɔ nloa ampe ɛnee ɛbɔfoɔ bieko anyunlu ɛne. Ɔse, “Kaledima ɛhyɛ bɛ nu ekpunli nsa ɛrali yɛ nvunu, ɛhye afunlumu ne mɔ amuala ɛhɔ, na bɛhu sonvolɛma ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti. Me ngomekye ala a meha mɔɔ mera mebabɔ wɔ amaneɛ a.”

english_verse: That servant was still speaking, when a fourth one dashed up and said, “Your children were having a feast and drinking wine at the home of your oldest son,
translation_verse: Mɔɔ ɔ nloa wɔ zolɛ ɔlɛtendɛ la, ɛbɔfoɔ bieko vindele ɛkɛ razele ye kɛ, “Ɛ mra mrenya nee mraalɛ ne mɔ wɔ bɛ diema nrenya kpanyinli ne sua nu, bɛlɛdi, bɛno nwanye.

english_verse: when suddenly a windstorm from the desert blew the house down, crushing all of your children. I am the only one who escaped to tell you.”
translation_verse: Na nea, ahumu kpole bie vi fienemgbole ne anu lɔ ɛdu ɛrabu sua ne ɛgua bɛ nwo zo, ɛhu bɛ muala. Me ngomekye ala a mevi nu mɔɔ mera mebabɔ wɔ amaneɛ a.”

english_verse: When Job heard this, he tore his clothes and shaved his head because of his great sorrow. He knelt on the ground, then worshiped God
translation_verse: Akee Dwobu dwazole, ɔsuosuanle tɛladeɛ mɔɔ ɔwula la anu, ɔkpale ɔ ti, ɔdule ɔdɔle aze na ɔyeyɛle Nyamenle.

english_verse: and said: “We bring nothing at birth; we take nothing with us at death. The Lord alone gives and takes. Praise the name of the Lord!”
translation_verse: Ɔse, “Meanva bie meamba na mekɔ a meava bie meahɔ. Ɛdɛnkɛma a vale manle me a, yɛɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma a ɛlie ye debie a. Ayɛlɛyelɛ ɛha Ɛdɛnkɛma duma ne.”

english_verse: In spite of everything, Job did not sin or accuse God of doing wrong.
translation_verse: Anwubɛnyunlu ɛhye mɔ kɔsɔɔti anu, Dwobu anyɛ ɛtane biala yɛɛ yeanvu Nyamenle.

english_verse: When the angels gathered around the Lord again, Satan was there with them,
translation_verse: Kenle ko eza Nyamenle anzɛɛ Anwuma amra hɔle Ɛdɛnkɛma anyunlu kɛ bɛkava bɛ nwo bɛahile ye, na Seetan eza hɔle ɛkɛ ne bie.

english_verse: and the Lord asked, “Satan, where have you been?” Satan replied, “I have been going all over the earth.”
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma bizale Seetan kɛ, “Na wɔmɔ, ɛvi nienwu yɛɛ wɔra ɛke a?” Seetan buale Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ, “Mewɔ akpɔsa nu wɔ aleɛabo. Ewiade anu ala yɛɛ medi ye akɔneaba a.”

english_verse: Then the Lord asked, “What do you think of my servant Job? No one on earth is like him—he is a truly good person, who respects me and refuses to do evil. And he hasn't changed, even though you persuaded me to destroy him for no reason.”
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Seetan kɛ, “Wɔnwu me sonvolɛ Dwobu, awie biala mɔɔ le kɛ ɔdaye la ɛnle aleɛabo, ɛtane biala ɛnle ɔ nwo, ɔdi nɔhalɛ, ɔsulo Nyamenle na ɔtwe ɔ nwo ɔfi ɛtane nwo. Wɔyɛ anrɛɛ ɛmaa meazɛkye ye, wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɔtɛyɛle ɛhwee la, noko wɔnwu ye wienyi kɛ Dwobu gyi ɔ gyakɛ anu kpundii.”

english_verse: Satan answered, “There's no pain like your own. People will do anything to stay alive.
translation_verse: Na Seetan buale Ɛdɛnkɛma kɛ, “Ɔle zɔhane, na ye nwonane ne noko ɛ! Sonla kɛhulo kɛ ɔkɛdɛnla ngoane nu tɛla kɛ ɔkɛminli anwonyia biala mɔɔ ɔlɛ la.

english_verse: Try striking Job's own body with pain, and he will curse you to your face.”
translation_verse: Wɔmɔ, ɛkulo a fa ɛ sa ka ye maa ɔde nyane ekyii, na ɛkɛde mgbole mɔɔ ɔkɛheha ɔkɛtietia wɔ la.”

english_verse: “All right!” the Lord replied. “Make Job suffer as much as you want, but just don't kill him.”
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma zele Seetan kɛ, “Ɔwɔ ɛ sa nu, na anrɛɛ mmafa ɛ sa ɛka ye ngoane ne.”

english_verse: Satan left and caused painful sores to break out all over Job's body—from head to toe.
translation_verse: Yemɔti Seetan vi Ɛdɛnkɛma anwo ɛkɛ ne hɔle na ɔhɔdele nganlɛ mgbole ɔkpondenle Dwobu anwo. Ɔvi ɔ ti zo mɔɔ dwu ɔ gyakɛ akunlu la yɛle nganlɛ ngome.

english_verse: his wife asked, “Why do you still trust God? Why don't you curse him and die?”
translation_verse: Na ɔ ye zele ye kɛ, “Ɛnɛ nee ɛnɛ ala ɛtɛgyi ɛ gyakɛ anu, ɛtɛtoa Nyamenle abo zo. Tendɛ ɛtane tia Nyamenle na wu ɛ.”

english_verse: Job replied, “Don't talk like a fool! If we accept blessings from God, we must accept trouble as well.” In all that happened, Job never once said anything against God. Job's Three Friends
translation_verse: Dwobu buale ye kɛ, “Ɛtendɛ kɛ mraalɛ ahɔnwɔne ne mɔ anu ko tendɛ la. Saa Nyamenle kyɛ yɛ ninyɛne kpalɛ a, yemɔ yɛdie. Na saa anwubɛnyunlu to yɛ a, ɛnee duzu ati a ɔwɔ kɛ yɛkpo ye amunli a?” Wɔ amaneɛnwunlɛ ɛhye mɔ amuala anu Dwobu anloa anvula edwɛkɛ ɛtane antia Nyamenle. Dwobu agɔnwo mɔ ba

english_verse: Eliphaz from Teman, Bildad from Shuah, and Zophar from Naamah were three of Job's friends, and they heard about his troubles. So they agreed to visit Job and comfort him.
translation_verse: Mekɛ mɔɔ Dwobu agɔnwo mɔ nsa ne, Ɛlaefaze mɔɔ vi suakpole Tima, Beledade mɔɔ vi Hyua maanle nu, yɛɛ Zofaa mɔɔ vi Neeyama maanle nu la dele ye anwubɛnyunlu ne nganeɛ la, bɛhɛlɛhɛlale bɛ nwo na bɛhilele kenle bɛrale kɛ bɛbakpɔla ye, bɛayɛ ye gyakɔ na bɛakyekye ɔ rɛle.

english_verse: When they came near enough to see Job, they could hardly recognize him. And in their great sorrow, they tore their clothes, then sprinkled dust on their heads and cried bitterly.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ bɛlua adenle zo moa ekyii na bɛnwunle Dwobu la, bɛannwu ye sonla holɛ. Na bɛradole ye la, bɛzunle bɛyele awolɛ. Bɛsuosuanle bɛ adɛladeɛ mɔɔ bɛwula la anu, bɛvale nzonle bɛbɔle bɛ nwo na bɛlile nyane.

english_verse: For seven days and nights, they sat silently on the ground beside him, because they realized what terrible pain he was in.
translation_verse: Bɛkpofokpofole azɛlɛ nwo ɛkɛ ne bɛ nee ye dɛnlanle ewiazo nee nɔɔzo toonwo kenle nsuu. Bɛ biala ambuke ɔ nloa anga edwɛkɛkpɔkɛ ko bɔbɔ, ɔboalekɛ bɛnwunle kɛ ɛnee ɔlɛnwu amaneɛ kpole.

english_verse: Finally, Job cursed the day of his birth
translation_verse: Nzinlii Dwobu bukele ɔ nloa na ɔwale kenle ko ne mɔɔ bɛwole ye la amonle. Dwobu

english_verse: by saying to God:
translation_verse: Dwobu hanle kɛ,

english_verse: Blot out the day of my birth and the night when my parents created a son.
translation_verse: “O Nyamenle, maa abule ɛbu kenle ko ne mɔɔ bɛwole me la; abule ɛbu nɔe ne mɔɔ bɛnrenzɛle me ralɛ nrenya la!

english_verse: and send thick, gloomy shadows to fill it with dread.
translation_verse: Maa awozinli kabii nee awozinli mindomindo ɛva ye. Maa amungu ɛheda zo; maa alehyenlɛ ne anu awozinli ɛha ɛzulolɛ.

english_verse: Don't let children be created or joyful shouts be heard ever again in that night.
translation_verse: Maa nɔɔzo zɔhane ɛyɛ diinyi, mmamaa bɛte anyelielɛ ɛnelɛ biala.

english_verse: Let those with magic powers place a curse on that day.
translation_verse: Maa amowama ɛbɔ kenle ne sasa, ɛwa ye amonle; bɛmɛ yɛɛ bɛze kɛ bɛsi bɛmaa nyevizonle maa ɔ nwo zo a.

english_verse: Darken its morning stars and remove all hope of light,
translation_verse: Mmamaa ye aleɛbahye nwɔlɔra ne mɔ ta; mmamaa nɔɔzo zɔhane mangyee si.

english_verse: because it let me be born into a world of trouble. Why Didn't I Die at Birth?
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ yeando ɔmɔ awodeɛ ne anu, na ɔyele me ɔmanle nyanenwunlɛ.

english_verse: Why was I accepted and allowed to nurse at my mother's breast?
translation_verse: Duzu ati a ɔmɔ dedɛle me ɔ gyakɛ azo a? Duzu ati a ɔmanle me nyɛfonlɛ a?

english_verse: Now I would be at peace in the silent world below
translation_verse: Saa menwule a, anrɛɛ mela melie me menle koonwu; anrɛɛ mela melie me menle bie

english_verse: with kings and their advisors whose palaces lie in ruins,
translation_verse: kɛ ewiade arelemgbunli nee nrɛlɛbɛvoma mɔɔ kyekyele awuke mgbole manle bɛ nwo la.

english_verse: and with rulers once rich with silver and gold.
translation_verse: Anrɛɛ mela kɛ arelemgbunli mralɛ mrenya mɔɔ vale ezukoa nvutuke nee dwɛtɛ fufule yile bɛ azua la.

english_verse: I wish I had been born dead and then buried, never to see the light of day.
translation_verse: Anrɛɛ ɔmɔ ako kpɔnenle, na meanyɛ sonla, anzɛɛ kɛ adɔma mɔɔ wule ɔ nli akunlu.

english_verse: In the world of the dead, the wicked and the weary rest without a worry. *
translation_verse: Funli kuma nu yɛɛ amumuyɛma gyakyi ninyɛndane, na menli mɔɔ ɛvɛ la nyia ɛnwomenlelielɛ a.

english_verse: where captives and slaves are free at last. Why Does God Let Me Live?
translation_verse: Mgbolema nee ahoahweabane wɔ ɛkɛ, na kanranli nyia ɔ ti fi ɔ menle asa anu.

english_verse: Why does God let me live when life is miserable and so bitter?
translation_verse: “Duzu ati a ɛmaa menli mɔɔ de anwunvɔne nu la nwu wienyi a? Duzu ati a ɛmaa menli mɔɔ te nyane la ngoane ɛ?

english_verse: I keep longing for death more than I would seek a valuable treasure.
translation_verse: Bɛ nwo dɔ ewule, noko ewule ɛmba; bɛkpondɛ ewule bɛtɛla anwonyia biala.

english_verse: Nothing could make me happier than to be in the grave.
translation_verse: Kenle mɔɔ bɛkɛwu na bɛkɛzie bɛ la, ɛnee bɛ nye ɛlie.

english_verse: Why do I go on living when God has me surrounded, and I can't see the road?
translation_verse: Duzu ati a sonla mɔɔ ɛnze ye kenlebie la, Nyamenle ɛbɔ ɔ nwo bane a?

english_verse: Moaning and groaning are my food and drink,
translation_verse: Me aleɛ a le me ɛzunlɛ, yɛɛ me nzule a le me ɛkponlenlɛ.

english_verse: I have no peace or rest— only troubles and worries.
translation_verse: Menlɛ anzonudwolɛ, yɛɛ ɛdendɛlɛ ɛdɔ me nwo; menlɛ ɛnwomenlelielɛ, yɛɛ me anwubɛnyunlu ɛnlɛ awieleɛ.”

english_verse: Eliphaz from Teman said:
translation_verse: Ɛlaefaze buale ye kɛ,

english_verse: Please be patient and listen to what I have to say. *
translation_verse: “Dwobu, saa awie ka edwɛkɛ a ɛkɛva ɛya ɔ? Sonla ɛnrɛhola ɛnrɛdɛnla ɛke koonwu zɛhae.

english_verse: But now you feel discouraged when struck by trouble.
translation_verse: Na kɛkala mɔɔ yedo wɔ la, ɛnnyia nwolɛ abotane; yeha wɔ la, wɔ adwenle ɛbɔ nu.

english_verse: You respect God and live right, so don't lose hope!
translation_verse: Wɔ Nyamenle ɛzulolɛ manle wɔ adwenle zile pi, yɛɛ wɔ ndenle kpalɛ zo ɛvalɛ manle wɔ anyelazo.

english_verse: No truly innocent person has ever died young.
translation_verse: Dwenle nwo, nwane a ɛnze nwolɛ bie na ɔwule, anzɛɛ nienwu yɛɛ bɛhunle tenlenema a?

english_verse: In my experience, only those who plant seeds of evil harvest trouble,
translation_verse: Mɔɔ meze la a le kɛ, menli mɔɔ so ninyɛndane ɛya, na bɛdua amumuyɛ la bu munzule.

english_verse: and then they are swept away by the angry breath of God.
translation_verse: Nyamenle ɛnwomenle ɛgulɛ ku bɛ, na ye ɛya ne bɔ bɛ bo zo bɔkɔɔ.

english_verse: They may roar and growl like powerful lions. But when God breaks their teeth,
translation_verse: Amumuyɛma kpo na bɛtea kɛ awenade, na Nyamenle tudu bɛ gye na ɔmaa bɛyɛ koonwu.

english_verse: they starve, and their children are scattered. A Secret Was Told to Me
translation_verse: Bɛle kɛ awenade mɔɔ ɛnnyia debie ɛngu ɛnli, bɛwu na bɛ mra ne mɔ bɔ asande.

english_verse: A secret was told to me in a faint whisper—
translation_verse: “Mekɛ bie ɛnelɛ bie hanle nrɛlaleɛ hilele me, ɛnelɛ ne dule me azukue.

english_verse: I was overcome by sleep, but disturbed by dreams;
translation_verse: Ɔrale kɛ ɛlalɛ ɛzulolɛ bie, mɔɔ menli ka wɔ bɛ nafelɛ nu la.

english_verse: and my hair stood on end, as a wind blew past my face.
translation_verse: Debie pɛle me nye zo, na me nwo bɔle me nyee.

english_verse: It stopped and stood still. Then a form appeared— a shapeless form. And from the silence, I heard a voice say,
translation_verse: Deɛ ne gyinlanle koonwu, na meannwu ye sɔhovolɛ; ɛnee debie gyi me nyunlu ɛkɛ; ɛkɛ ne yɛle diinyi, akee mendele ɛnelɛ, ɔse:

english_verse: “No humans are innocent in the eyes of God their Creator.
translation_verse: Asoo sonla kola yɛ tenlene tɛla Nyamenle anzɛɛ ɔ nwo kɛde kɛdɛla ye Bɔvolɛ?

english_verse: He finds fault with his servants and even with his angels.
translation_verse: Ye sonvolɛma bɔbɔ, ɔnlie bɛ ɔnli, yɛɛ anwuma soanvolɛma bɔbɔ, ɔnyia bɛ nwo nvonleɛ.

english_verse: Humans are formed from clay and are fragile as moths, so what chance do you have?
translation_verse: Na akee bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛvale ndɛtɛlɛ a bɛbɔle bɛ, mɔɔ bɛvi ndɛtɛlɛ nu, na bɛti bɛ kɛ ngɛkɛba la!

english_verse: Born after daybreak, you die before nightfall and disappear forever.
translation_verse: Ɔvi nwonlomɔ kɔdwu aledwolɛ, bɛsɛkye bɛ, bɛ bo zo minli bɔkɔɔ, awie ɛngakye bɛ.

english_verse: Your tent pegs are pulled up, and you leave this life, having gained no wisdom.”
translation_verse: Saa bɛ ahonle nyɛma te a, ɛnee bɛwu, bɛwu mɔɔ nrɛlɛbɛ biala ɛnle nu a.

english_verse: Envy and jealousy will kill a stupid fool.
translation_verse: Nɔhalɛ, ɛya ku koasea, yɛɛ anyebolo ku kɔnwɔne.

english_verse: I have seen fools take root. But God sends a curse, suddenly uprooting them
translation_verse: Menwu kɛ koasea ɛzɔ ndinli, noko arɛlevilɛ nu, membɔle ye awuke ne sasa.

english_verse: Then hungry and greedy people gobble up their crops and grab their wealth.
translation_verse: Menli mɔɔ ɛhɔne ku bɛ la di bɛ bɛyɔba ne, kanza bɛgua mbowule nu bɔbɔ a, bɛbu, yɛɛ anyeboloma anye bolo bɛ anwonyia.

english_verse: Our suffering isn't caused by the failure of crops;
translation_verse: Anwubɛnyunlu ɛnvi azɛlɛ nwo, yɛɛ ngyegyelɛ ɛnfifi ndɛtɛlɛ nu.

english_verse: it's all part of life, like sparks shooting skyward.
translation_verse: Bɛwo sonla bɛmaa ngyegyelɛ, ɔle kɛ senle mɔɔ tudu kɔ anwuma la.

english_verse: Job, if I were you, I would ask God for help.
translation_verse: “Saa medame a, anrɛɛ mebadoa Nyamenle abo zo, na meava me edwɛkɛ meawula ɔ sa nu;

english_verse: His miracles are marvelous, more than we can count.
translation_verse: yemɔ mɔɔ ɔyɛ ninyɛne mgbole, mɔɔ ɛnlɛ nvedenu, ye nwanwane nyɛleɛ ɛnlɛ ɔ nloa.

english_verse: God sends showers on earth and waters the fields.
translation_verse: Ɔmaa ezule tɔ azɛlɛ ye azo na ɔgugua nzule wɔ ɛbɔ ne mɔ azo.

english_verse: He protects the sorrowful and lifts up those who have been disgraced. *
translation_verse: Ɔmaa bɛlɛvoma zo, na ɔye nyanelilɛma ɔfi nyane nu.

english_verse: God swiftly traps the wicked
translation_verse: Ɔsɛkye agyibatovoma mɛlɛbɛla, na ɔmaa bɛfua asakpane.

english_verse: in their own evil schemes, and their wisdom fails.
translation_verse: Ɔkye nrɛlɛbɛvolɛma wɔ bɛdabɛ bɛ agyibadolɛ nu, na agyibadolɛma ngyehyɛlɛ ne mɔ pɛ sinli ndɛndɛ.

english_verse: Darkness is their only companion, hiding their path at noon.
translation_verse: Awozinli fa bɛ alehyenlɛ nu, na bɛdi nvuovua ewiazo ketekete kɛ nɔɔzo.

english_verse: God rescues the needy from the words of the wicked and the fist of the mighty.
translation_verse: Ɔdie menli mɔɔ ɛhyia la ɔfi dadeɛ nloa, na ɔdie bɛ ɔfi mgbolema asa anu.

english_verse: The poor are filled with hope, and injustice is silenced. Consider Yourself Fortunate
translation_verse: Yemɔti ehyianvolɛma lɛ anyelazo, na menli mɔɔ ɛnli pɛlepɛle la ka bɛ nloa to nu.

english_verse: Consider yourself fortunate if God All-Powerful chooses to correct you.
translation_verse: “Nyilalɛ ɛha sonla ne mɔɔ Nyamenle twi ɔ nyunlu la, yemɔti mmakpo Nyamenle Bɛdevinli ne ndeanlɛ.

english_verse: He may cause injury and pain, but he will bandage and heal your cuts and bruises.
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ ɔbo wɔ a, ɔsia ɔdwu wɔ, yɛɛ ɔtea wɔ a, ɔfa wɔ ɔbɔ ye ɛbolɛ.

english_verse: God will protect you from harm, no matter how often trouble may strike.
translation_verse: Ɔbaye wɔ yeavi ngyegyelɛ fane nsia anu, nsuu ne azo, munzule biala ɛnrɛdo wɔ.

english_verse: In times of war and famine, God will keep you safe.
translation_verse: Wɔ ɛhɔne nu, ɔbaye wɔ yeavi ewule nu; wɔ konle nu, ɔbaye wɔ yeavi dadeɛ nloa.

english_verse: You will be sheltered, without fear of hurtful words or any other weapon.
translation_verse: Ɔbaye wɔ yeavi dumanzɛkyelɛ nu, yɛɛ saa ewule ba a ɛnrɛzulo.

english_verse: You will laugh at the threat of destruction and famine. And you won't be afraid of wild animals—
translation_verse: Ɛbazele ewule nee ɛhɔne, yɛɛ ɛnrɛzulo aleɛabo nanemgbole biala.

english_verse: they will no longer be fierce, and your rocky fields will become friendly.
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ ɛ nee ɛbɔ nu awolɛ mgbole bali ngitanwo, na aleɛabo nanemgbole nee wɔ adɛnla anzonudwolɛ nu.

english_verse: Your home will be secure, and your sheep will be safe.
translation_verse: Ɛbanwu kɛ anzonudwolɛ wɔ wɔ sua nu, yɛɛ ɛnrɛminli debie biala wɔ wɔ mboane tunli nu.

english_verse: You will have more descendants than there are blades of grass on the face of the earth.
translation_verse: Eza ɛbanwu kɛ ɛ bo zo amra bada, na ɛ kunlu mralɛ anyenle kɛ ɛbɔ nu ndile.

english_verse: You will live a very long life, and your body will be strong until the day you die.
translation_verse: Ɛbayɛ nwosonwoso kolaa na wɔawu, kɛmɔ ɛlobɔ dwu na bɛava ma bɛahɔ ma ɛwozolɛ ɛleka la.

english_verse: Our experience has proven these things to be true, so listen and learn.
translation_verse: Nea, yɛvedevede ɛhye anu, na ɔle nɔhalɛ. Yemɔti Dwobu, tie na die to nu.”

english_verse: It's impossible to weigh my misery and grief!
translation_verse: “O, anrɛɛ bɛazuzu me nyane ne, nee me amaneɛnwunlɛ ne wɔ tone zo!

english_verse: They outweigh the sand along the beach, and that's why I have spoken without thinking first.
translation_verse: Anrɛɛ bɛkɛnwu kɛ ɔyɛ ɛnlomboɛ ɔtɛla ɛnweazo ɛnwea, ɛhye ati a me mgbolehanlɛ ne ɛyɛ nwanwane a.

english_verse: The fearsome arrows of God All-Powerful have filled my soul with their poison.
translation_verse: Tumivolɛ Nyamenle ne ɛda mbaka ne ɛwowɔ me, na ye bɔlɔ ɛwie me wolowolo, yɛɛ Nyamenle ɛya mgbole ne mɔ ɛra me nwo zo.

english_verse: Do oxen and wild donkeys cry out in distress unless they are hungry?
translation_verse: “Asoo asoaso nyia ndile na ɔlɛdi a ɔsu, anzɛɛ ɛnlankɛ gyi aleɛ nwo a ɔsu?

english_verse: What is food without salt? What is more tasteless than the white of an egg?
translation_verse: Asoo aleɛ tatabɛ, bɛdi a ɔdi? Asoo kolonvia aleɛ fufule ne yɛ fɛ?

english_verse: That's how my food tastes, and my appetite is gone. *
translation_verse: Me tiakunlu ɛmba zo bɔbɔ; bɛle aleɛ mɔɔ ka me ya.

english_verse: How I wish that God would answer my prayer
translation_verse: “O, anrɛɛ meanyia mɔɔ mebiza la, na Nyamenle akponle mɔɔ mekpondɛ la azo!

english_verse: Then I would be comforted, knowing that in all of my pain I have never disobeyed God.
translation_verse: Anrɛɛ ɛhye bakyekye me rɛle; na meali fɛlɛko wɔ me nyane nu, ɔluakɛ metɛtule Nwuanzanwuanza Ko ne anloa.

english_verse: Why should I patiently hope when my strength is gone?
translation_verse: Duzu anwosesebɛ a melɛ, mefa mekendɛ a? Yɛɛ kɛ menwɔwie ye mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ mesi abotane a?

english_verse: I am not strong as stone or bronze,
translation_verse: Ɛnee me anwosesebɛ le kɛ awolɛ ɔ? Anzɛɛ me nwonane le kɔbele ɔ?

english_verse: and I have finally reached the end of my rope. My Friends, I Am Desperate
translation_verse: Nɔhalɛ nu, menlɛ anwosesebɛ biala me nu, yɛɛ menlɛ ɛleka mɔɔ moalɛ vi bara a.

english_verse: My friends, I am desperate, and you should help me, even if I no longer respect God All-Powerful. *
translation_verse: “Awie biala mɔɔ ɛnyɛ atiakunlukɛnlɛma la ɛnzulo Tumivolɛ Nyamenle ne.

english_verse: like streams that swell with melting snow,
translation_verse: na ezukɔtweaba kɔfea nu yɛ azule ne anye fii, kyengye ye.

english_verse: then suddenly disappear in the summer heat.
translation_verse: Wuluwulu melɛ nu bɛkolo, na bɛ bo zo minliminli bɔkɔɔ.

english_verse: I am like a caravan, lost in the desert while searching for water.
translation_verse: Adenduvoma di ɛkɛ ne akɔneaba bɛkɔkpondɛ nzule ne toonwo bɛwu.

english_verse: Caravans from Tema and Sheba
translation_verse: Tima adenduvoma neɛnlea, Hyiba adenduvoma anye da.

english_verse: thought they would find water. But they were disappointed,
translation_verse: Bɛ anyelazo bɔ bɛ, ɔboalekɛ ɛnee bɛdie bɛdi; bɛkɛhɔdwu la, ɛnee nzule ne ɛsesa.

english_verse: just as I am with you. Only one look at my suffering, and you run away scared. What Have I Done Wrong?
translation_verse: Zɛhae yɛɛ bɛle bɛmaa me a; bɛnwu me anwubɛnyunlu la, ɛzulolɛ ɛha bɛ.

english_verse: Have I ever asked any of you to give me a gift
translation_verse: Meha kɛ bɛhyɛ me debie ɔ? Anzɛɛ bɛva bɛ anwonyia ne bie bɛdua me ti ndoloboa ɔ?

english_verse: What have I done wrong? Show me, and I will keep quiet.
translation_verse: “Bɛhilehile me, na menwɔyɛ koonwu; bɛmaa menwu ɛtane mɔɔ meyɛ la.

english_verse: The truth is always painful, but your arguments prove nothing.
translation_verse: Nɔhalɛ edwɛkɛ nu mia! Na bɛ ndeanlɛ ye, duzu anwo ndeanlɛ ɔ?

english_verse: Here I am desperate, and you consider my words as worthless as wind.
translation_verse: Ɛnee bɛdwenle kɛ bɛkola bɛtea edwɛkɛ ɔ, wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ sonla mɔɔ ɛnlɛ anyelazo la edwɛkɛ ɛhanlɛ le anwoma la?

english_verse: Why, you would sell an orphan or your own neighbor!
translation_verse: Bɛnyia arisa a, bɛkɛgua ɔ ti nzeleba, na bɛkɛdɔne agɔnwolɛma.

english_verse: Look me straight in the eye; I won't lie to you.
translation_verse: Na kɛkala, mebodo bɛ, bɛnlea me, ɔluakɛ menrɛbɔ adalɛ wɔ bɛ nyunlu.

english_verse: Stop accusing me falsely; my reputation is at stake.
translation_verse: Mebodo bɛ, bɛgyakyi, bɛmmabua me mgbɔvodɛne; bɛgyakyi, na medi benle.

english_verse: I know right from wrong, and I am not telling lies.
translation_verse: Anzɛɛ meha ɛtane ɔ? Menze kpalɛ menze ɛtane ɔ?

english_verse: Why is life so hard? Why do we suffer?
translation_verse: “Sonla ɛbɛlabɔlɛ yɛ se wɔ azɛlɛ ye azo, sonla mekɛ kɔsɔɔti le kɛ ɛkpanli.

english_verse: We are slaves in search of shade; we are laborers longing for our wages.
translation_verse: Ɔle kɛ kanranli mɔɔ kpondɛ alubo nu adɛnla, ɔle kɛ ɛkpanli mɔɔ anye la ye ahatualɛ zo.

english_verse: God has made my days drag on and my nights miserable.
translation_verse: Zɔhane ala yɛɛ bɛhyehyɛ mekɛ mgbane nee aledwolɛ anu nyane bɛmaa me a.

english_verse: I pray for night to end, but it stretches out while I toss and turn.
translation_verse: Saa meda a mebiza kɛ, ‘Kenlenzu yɛɛ mebadwazo a?’ Aledwolɛ ne wale, mekɔsɔ mekɔ, mekɔsɔ meba, mepe toonwo alehyenlɛ.

english_verse: My parched skin is covered with worms, dirt, and sores,
translation_verse: Melɔ azonlɛ, me nwo ɛzi bile, me nwo nwoma di wulate.

english_verse: and my days are running out quicker than the thread of a fast-moving needle. Don't Forget!
translation_verse: Me mekɛ se ndɛndɛ tɛla ɛdanlɛnwovolɛ agbuyiaba, na ɔba awieleɛ mɔɔ anyelazo ɛnle nu a.

english_verse: I beg you, God, don't forget! My life is just a breath, and trouble lies ahead.
translation_verse: “Kakye kɛ me ngoane le anwoma; me nye ɛnrɛnwu debie kpalɛ bieko.

english_verse: I will vanish from sight, and no one, including you, will ever see me again.
translation_verse: Ɛnyelɛ mɔɔ nwu me la ɛnrɛnwu me bieko; mɔɔ bɛ nye dua me ala la, mebado ɛbɛla ne aze.

english_verse: I will disappear in the grave or vanish from sight like a passing cloud.
translation_verse: Kɛmɔ amungu kpa na ɔpɛ nu ɔse la, zɔhane ala yɛɛ mɔɔ kɔ Ɛbolɔ la ɛnzia ko a.

english_verse: Never will I return home; soon I will be forgotten.
translation_verse: Ɔnzia ɔmba ye awuke nu bieko, yɛɛ ye awuke nu amra ɛnze ye ko.

english_verse: And so, I cry out to you in agony and distress.
translation_verse: Yemɔti menrɛmua me nloa; mebaha mɔɔ wɔ me kunlu la; mebaha mɔɔ wɔ me ahonle nu la.

english_verse: Am I the sea or a sea monster? Is that why you imprison me?
translation_verse: “Mele nyevile, anzɛɛ nyevizonle, mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ bɛmaa me sinzavolɛ a?

english_verse: but you torture me with terrible dreams. *
translation_verse: ɛnee bɛfa ɛlalɛ bɛnwunlonwunla me, na bɛfa ɛnyelɛzodeɛnwunlɛ bɛka me ɛzulolɛ.

english_verse: I'd rather choke to death than live in this body.
translation_verse: Yemɔti menwɔhulo kɛ bɛkɛmia me kɔmenzia bɛkɛhu me tɛla kɛ ɔkɛha me mbowule.

english_verse: Leave me alone and let me die; my life has no meaning.
translation_verse: Mekpo me ngoane; menrɛhakyi bolɛ. Bɛgyakyi me, ɔluakɛ kɛkala, me ngoane ɛnle ɛhwee.

english_verse: Why do you test us from sunrise to sunset?
translation_verse: Mɔɔ nwolomɔ biala ɛkpɔla ye, na mekɛ biala ɛsɔ ye ɛnea ɛ?

english_verse: Won't you look away just long enough for me to swallow?
translation_verse: Kenlenzu yɛɛ ɛkɛye ɛ nye me nwo, anzɛɛ ɛkɛgyakyi me ɛkɛmaa menwɔme nyɛlɛ a?

english_verse: Why do you watch us so closely? What's it to you, if I sin? Why am I your target and such a heavy burden?
translation_verse: Saa meyɛ ɛtane a, ɛnee duzu a meyɛ wɔ a, wɔmɔ menli sinzavo? Duzu ati a ɛ nye gyi me nyunlu zɛhae a? Duzu ati a meyɛ adesoa memaa wɔ a?

english_verse: Why do you refuse to forgive? Soon you won't find me, because I'll be dead.
translation_verse: Duzu ati a ɛnrɛva me mɛladonlɛ ɛnrɛhyɛ me, na ɛnrɛva me amumuyɛ ɛnrɛhyɛ me ɛ? Ɔluakɛ mebala azɛlɛ ye abo; ɛbakpondɛ me, na ɛnrɛnwu me.”

english_verse: Bildad from Shuah said:
translation_verse: Na Beledade hanle kɛ,

english_verse: How long will you talk and keep saying nothing?
translation_verse: “Na kenlenzu a ɛkɛwie tendɛ a? Ɛ nloa edwɛkɛ le kɛ anwoma kpole bie la.

english_verse: Does God All-Powerful stand in the way of justice?
translation_verse: Ɛnea a ɛnee Nyamenle kyi nɔhalɛ, anzɛɛ Tumivolɛ ne kyi pɛlepɛlelilɛ ɔ?

english_verse: He made your children pay for their sins.
translation_verse: Saa ɛ mra ɛyɛ ɛtane ɛtia ye a, yeye bɛ yemaa bɛdabɛ bɛ ɛtane.

english_verse: So why don't you turn to him
translation_verse: Saa ɛkɛkpondɛ Nyamenle abo zo, na ɛkɛbodo ɛkɛzɛlɛ Tumivolɛ ne,

english_verse: and start living right? Then he will decide to rescue and restore you to your place of honor.
translation_verse: saa ɛmaa ɛ nwo te na ɛbɔ ɛbɛla mɔɔ tenrɛ, nɔhalɛ, ɔbaheha ɔ nwo na yeakyekye wɔ awuke ne bieko,

english_verse: Your future will be brighter by far than your past. Our Ancestors Were Wise
translation_verse: amaa saa mɔlebɛbo ne ɛle ekyi a, wɔ awieleɛ nu wɔayɛ sonlakpole.

english_verse: Our own time has been short, like a fading shadow, and we know very little.
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ anoma ala a bɛwo yɛ a, yɛnze ɛhwee, yɛ mekɛ wɔ azɛlɛ ye azo le kɛ ɛlawolɛ.

english_verse: But they will instruct you with great understanding.
translation_verse: Bɛbahilehile wɔ, na bɛaha mɔɔ bɛnwunle ye la bɛahile wɔ.

english_verse: and if the water dries up, they die sooner than grass.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ bɛkɛgyinla dedɛkɛɛ na bɛtɛpepɛle bɛ la, bɛkyengye bɛwu kolaa na baka biala awu.

english_verse: Such is the hopeless future of all who turn from God
translation_verse: Kɛ menli mɔɔ arɛle fi Nyamenle la ndenle nu de la ɛne; sonla mɔɔ ɛnze Nyamenle la anyelazo bawie.

english_verse: and trust in something as frail as a spider's web—
translation_verse: Ye adwenle ɛnzi pi, yɛɛ ye diedi le kɛ kɛdɛba ndenda.

english_verse: they take hold and fall because it's so flimsy.
translation_verse: Ɔtudu ɔkisia ye sua, noko sua ne golo; ɔsɔ nuhua, noko sua ne ɛngyinla.

english_verse: Sinful people are like plants with spreading roots and plenty of sun and water.
translation_verse: “Sɛnzɛne ne ɛtɛtudule a ɔnyi ɔtoto ɔ sa, na ɔtende ɔgua ye tola ne bane ne mɔ azo.

english_verse: They wrap their roots tightly around rocks.
translation_verse: Ye ndinli beba awolɛ edukue ne, na ɔgyinla awolɛ ne mɔ avinli.

english_verse: But once they are pulled up, they have no more place;
translation_verse: Saa bɛtu ye bɛfi ɔ bo zo ne a, ɔkpo ye na ɔka kɛ, ‘Metɛnwunle wɔ ɛlɛ!’

english_verse: their life slips away, and other plants grow there.
translation_verse: Ɛhɛe, kɛ ye fɛlɛkolilɛ adenle ne de la ɛne; bie mɔ noko fifi ɔ bo zo ne.

english_verse: We know God doesn't reject an innocent person or help a sinner.
translation_verse: “Noko, Nyamenle ɛnrɛkpo mɔɔ ɛnze nwolɛ bie la, yɛɛ ɔnrɛzɔ ɛtanevolɛma asa.

english_verse: And so, he will make you happy and give you something to smile about.
translation_verse: Ɔbamaa ɛ nloa anwo ayɛ ɛzelekɛ ɛzelekɛ, na wɔava fɛlɛkolilɛ wɔadeɛdea nu.

english_verse: But your evil enemies will be put to shame and disappear forever.
translation_verse: Menli mɔɔ kpɔ wɔ la baheda anyiemgba ɛdanlɛ, na amumuyɛma awuke ne mɔ abɔ tɔɔ.”

english_verse: What you say is true. No human is innocent in the sight of God.
translation_verse: “Nɔhalɛ, meze kɛ ɔle zɔ. Noko nwane a di benle wɔ Nyamenle anyunlu a?

english_verse: Not once in a thousand times could we win our case if we took him to court.
translation_verse: Saa awie se kɛ ɔ nee ye yeye ɛnloanlɛ a, ɔnrɛhola ye kpuyia apenle ko anu ko bɔbɔ anloa ye.

english_verse: God is wise and powerful— who could possibly oppose him and win?
translation_verse: Ɔle nrɛlɛbɛvolɛ, yɛɛ ye anwosesebɛ le bedevinli; nwane a nee ye ɛdwudwu na yenyia gyinlagyakɛ a?

english_verse: When God becomes angry, he can move mountains before they even know it.
translation_verse: Saa ɔfa ɛya a ɔdwulu awoka, na ɔtudu bɛ mɔɔ ɔngakye awie a.

english_verse: God can shake the earth loose from its foundations
translation_verse: Ɔkpusu azɛlɛ ɔtudu ye ɔ bo zo ne, na ɔmaa ye mpila ne mɔ kpusu.

english_verse: or command the sun and stars to hold back their light.
translation_verse: Ɔsisi sɛnzɛne ne anwo zo, ɔmmaa ɔndudu, na ɔkeda nwɔlɔra nyunlu.

english_verse: God alone stretched out the sky, stepped on the sea,
translation_verse: Ɔdaye ɔ ngome a ɔbɔle anwomanyunlu tɛtɛlɛ ye, na ɔtietiale nyevile azɛlɛkye zo a.

english_verse: and set the stars in place— the Big Dipper and Orion, the Pleiades and the stars in the southern sky.
translation_verse: Ɔbɔle nwɔlɔra Ɛrelera nee ɔ mra nee Apeansa, Nwɔlɔra Nsuu nee nyiakɛ nwɔlɔra.

english_verse: Of all the miracles God works, we cannot understand a one.
translation_verse: Ɔyɛ ninyɛne mgbole mɔɔ bo sonla ndelebɛbo zo, ɔyɛ nwanwane ninyɛne mɔɔ ɛnlɛ ɔ nloa a.

english_verse: God walks right past me, without making a sound.
translation_verse: “Nea, ɔse me nwo ɛkɛ, noko mennwu ye; ɔlɛkɔ bɔbɔ a mennwu ɔ nwo.

english_verse: And if he grabs something, who can stop him or raise a question?
translation_verse: Saa Nyamenle ɛlɛfa debie a, nwane a kɛhola ye aze si a? Nwane a kɛhola kɛbiza ye kɛ, ‘Duzu a ɛlɛyɛ la?’

english_verse: When God showed his anger, the servants of the sea monster fell at his feet.
translation_verse: Nyamenle ɛnrɛhwe ye ɛyavalɛ ne ɛnrɛzia; Releehabe boavolɛma bɔ bɛ ti aze ɔ nyunlu.

english_verse: How, then, could I possibly argue my case with God? Though I Am Innocent
translation_verse: Ɛnee kɛ menzi membua ye ɛ, duzu edwɛkɛkpɔkɛ a meka a?

english_verse: Even though I am innocent, I can only beg for mercy.
translation_verse: Menli fɔlɛ, noko menrɛhola ye bua; ɔwɔ kɛ mesɛlɛ me ndɛnebuavolɛ ne anwunvɔnezelɛ.

english_verse: And if God came into court when I called him, he would not hear my case.
translation_verse: Saa menvɛlɛle ye yɛɛ ɔliele me zo a, anrɛɛ menrɛlie menrɛli kɛ yedie me ne.

english_verse: He would strike me with a storm and increase my injuries for no reason at all.
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ ɔfa ahumu ɔbɛlɛ me aze, na mgbane ne ala ɔmaa me nwo nganlɛ yɛ dɔɔnwo.

english_verse: Before I could get my breath, my miseries would multiply.
translation_verse: Ɔmmaa menlie me ɛnwomenle, na ɔmaa ɛbɛlabɔlɛ yɛ ɛnwonle.

english_verse: God is much stronger than I am, and who would call me into court to give me justice?
translation_verse: Saa ɔba anwosesebɛ ɛzulɛ a, ɔle bedevinli; saa ɔba pɛlepɛlelilɛ a, nwane a kɛhola ye a?

english_verse: Even if I were innocent, God would prove me wrong.
translation_verse: Menze nwolɛ bie, medi nɔhalɛ, noko me nloa bua me ewule fɔlɛ; menli fɔlɛ, noko yehile kɛ menle kpalɛ.

english_verse: I am not guilty, but I no longer care what happens to me.
translation_verse: Menli fɔlɛ; membu me nwo; me kunlu bɔbɔ a anrɛɛ mewu.

english_verse: What difference does it make? God destroys the innocent along with the guilty.
translation_verse: Ɔ muala wie ko; yemɔti mese, ɔsɛkye kpalɛma, ɔsɛkye amumuyɛma.

english_verse: When a good person dies a sudden death, God sits back and laughs.
translation_verse: Saa esiane fa arɛlevilɛ nu ewule ba a, ɔsi anzenwolɛbiema anwubɛnyunlu amgbu.

english_verse: And who else but God blindfolds the judges, then lets the wicked take over the earth? My Life Is Speeding By
translation_verse: Bɛva azɛlɛ ye bɛwula amumuyɛma asa anu; ɔkedɛheda ndɛnebuavolɛma anyunlu, na saa tɛ ye a, ɛnee nwane ɔ?

english_verse: My life is speeding by, without a hope of happiness.
translation_verse: “Me mekɛ se waa tɛla sonla mɔɔ ɛlɛnriandi la; ɔse ɔkɔ, ɔnnwu kpalɛ biala.

english_verse: Each day passes swifter than a sailing ship or an eagle swooping down.
translation_verse: Ɔpɛ nu ɔkɔ kɛ ndɔ mɔɔ la azule nye, ɔto kɛ kɔleɛ ɛlɛto ahye nane.

english_verse: Sometimes I try to be cheerful and to stop complaining,
translation_verse: Saa meka kɛ, ‘Memaa me rɛle avi me nyane, meagyakyi me nyunlu alɔbɔlɛ ɛyɛlɛ, meamaa me nye alie’ a,

english_verse: but my sufferings frighten me, because I know that God still considers me guilty.
translation_verse: me nyanenwunlɛ ne ka me ɛzulolɛ, ɔluakɛ meze kɛ ɛbabua me fɔlɛ.

english_verse: So what's the use of trying to prove my innocence?
translation_verse: Bɛbabua me ewulefɔlɛ, duzu ati a ɔwɔ kɛ mefonla me nwo a?

english_verse: Even if I washed myself with the strongest soap,
translation_verse: Saa mefa saminla mebia, na mefa anatele meyɛ me sa anwo a,

english_verse: God would throw me into a pit of stinking slime, leaving me disgusting to my clothes.
translation_verse: ɛbavuandi me wɔado ewula nu, na medame me nwo ndanlɛ bɔbɔ bahyi me.

english_verse: God isn't a mere human like me. I can't put him on trial.
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ ɔnle sonla kɛ medame la na meabua ye, na yɛ mu nwiɔ yɛaye ndɛne.

english_verse: Who could possibly judge between the two of us?
translation_verse: Kpɔdavolɛ biala ɛngyi yɛ avinli, mɔɔ kɛkpɔda yɛ mu nwiɔ a.

english_verse: Can someone snatch away the stick God carries to frighten me?
translation_verse: Bɛmaa ɔva me nwo empele ne ɔhɔ, na ɔmmafa ɔ nwo ɛzulolɛ ne ɔnwunlonwunla me.

english_verse: Then I could speak up without fear of him, but for now, I cannot speak.
translation_verse: Amaa meanzulo ye na meandendɛ, ɔluakɛ menle kɛ mɔɔ bɛmɛ bɛdwenle kɛ mele la.

english_verse: I am sick of life! And from my deep despair, I complain to you, my God.
translation_verse: “Me kunlu a anrɛɛ mewu; akee mebaha me nyane kɔsɔɔti; mebaha me ahonle nu nyane muala.

english_verse: Why do you take such delight in destroying those you created and in smiling on sinners?
translation_verse: Anzɛɛ ɛ kunlu dwo kɛ ɛkɛsisi me, kɛ ɛkɛkpo ɛ sa anloa gyima, na ɛ nye kɛlie amumuyɛma ɛbɛla nwo ɔ?

english_verse: Do you look at things the way we humans do?
translation_verse: Asoo ɛ nye le kɛ sonla ɛdeɛ ne, na ɛnea debie kɛ sonla la?

english_verse: Is that why you are so quick to find fault with me?
translation_verse: mɔɔ ɛneɛnlea me nu wɔanwu me munzule mɔɔ mebɔ, na wɔaza me ɛtane ne mɔ wɔagua zo a?

english_verse: You know I am innocent, but who can defend me against you?
translation_verse: Ɛze kɛ menli fɔlɛ, yɛɛ awie biala ɛngola ɛnlie me ɛnvi ɛ sa nu.

english_verse: Remember that you molded me like a piece of clay. So don't turn me back into dust once again.
translation_verse: Kakye kɛ ɛvale ndɛtɛlɛ a ɛbɔle me a; na eza ɛmaa meazia meahɔ ndɛtɛlɛ nu bieko ɔ?

english_verse: As cheese is made from milk, you created my body from a tiny drop.
translation_verse: Na wɔanwola me kɛ meleke, wɔambɔ me kunguma kɛ kyiisi ɔ?

english_verse: Then you tied my bones together with muscles and covered them with flesh and skin.
translation_verse: Ɛvale mbowule nee ndinli ɛbɔle me, na ɛvale nwonane nee nwoma ɛhedale zo.

english_verse: You, the source of my life, showered me with kindness and watched over me. You Have Not Explained
translation_verse: Wɔmaa me ngoane nee ɛhulolɛ kpundii, yɛɛ wɔli me sunsum ne adane.

english_verse: but you catch and punish me each time I sin.
translation_verse: Saa meyɛ ɛtane a, ɛnee wɔva wɔzie, ɛnva me nvonleɛ ɛngyɛ me.

english_verse: No matter how hard I try, you keep hunting me down like a powerful lion.
translation_verse: Saa memaa me nwo zo a, ɛfoa me kɛ awenade, na ɛyɛ nwanwane ninyɛne ɛtia me.

english_verse: You never stop accusing me; you become furious and attack over and over again.
translation_verse: Dahuu ɛlɛ alasevolɛ ka tia me, me nwo ɛya mɔɔ wɔ ɛ kunlu la dahuu yɛ kpole, yɛɛ dahuu ɛfa ɛlɔnema fofolɛ ɛba me nwo zo.

english_verse: Why did you let me be born? I would rather have died before birth
translation_verse: “Duzu ati a ɛmanle bɛwole me a? Me kunlu a anrɛɛ menwule kolaa na ɛnyelɛ anwu me.

english_verse: and been carried to the grave without ever breathing.
translation_verse: Anrɛɛ mevi ɔmɔ akunlu ala la bɛ nee me hɔle aziezo.

english_verse: I have only a few days left. Why don't you leave me alone? Let me find some relief, *
translation_verse: Me mekɛ mɔɔ ɛha la le ezinraa. Bɛgyakyi me, amaa me rɛle akyekye ekyii.

english_verse: of darkness and despair, the place of no return.
translation_verse: maanle anu kisii, anu begyebegye ne, mɔɔ ye wienyi le kɛ awozinli.”

english_verse: Zophar from Naamah said:
translation_verse: Zofaa hanle kɛ,

english_verse: Your words have silenced others and made them ashamed; now it is only right for you to be put to shame.
translation_verse: Ɛ nloa beɛbeɛ, awie mmaka bie ɔ, yɛɛ wɔ amgbuzilɛ ne, ɛngulo kɛ bɛtwi ɛ nyunlu ɔ?

english_verse: You claim to be innocent and argue that your beliefs are acceptable to God.
translation_verse: Ɛse wɔ ngehanleɛ ne le fɔɔnwo, yɛɛ ɛ nwo te wɔ Nyamenle anyunlu.

english_verse: But I wish God would speak
translation_verse: Anrɛɛ Nyamenle adendɛ, na yeabuke ɔ nloa wɔ ɛ nwo,

english_verse: and let you know that wisdom has many different sides. You would then discover that God has punished you less than you deserve.
translation_verse: anrɛɛ ɔkɛze wɔ kɛ nrɛlɛbɛ ndenle zonle; ninyɛne dɔɔnwo wɔ ɛkɛ mɔɔ dasanli ɛnde bɛ bo a. Nwu ye kɛ Nyamenle ɛndua wɔ kakɛ, kɛmɔ ɛfɛta la.

english_verse: Can you understand the mysteries surrounding God All-Powerful?
translation_verse: “Ɛkɛhola ɛkɛnwu Nyamenle abo ɔ? Ɛkɛhola ɛkɛnwu Tumivolɛ ne awieleɛ ɔ?

english_verse: They are higher than the heavens and deeper than the grave. So what can you do when you know so little,
translation_verse: Ye tumi ne kpole wɔ anwuma tɛla anwomanyunlu, duzu a ɛkɛhola ɛkɛyɛ a? Yɛɛ ɔle kuloonwu ɔtɛla Ɛbolɔ kuma, na wɔmɔ, ɛkɛhola ɛkɛnwu ye ɔ?

english_verse: and these mysteries outreach the earth and the ocean?
translation_verse: Ɔwale ɔtɛla azɛlɛ ye, yɛɛ ɔtɛlɛ ɔtɛla nyevile.

english_verse: If God puts you in prison or drags you to court, what can you do?
translation_verse: Saa ɔba, ɔse kɛ ɔgua menli efiade, ɔ nee bɛ kɔ ndɛnebualɛ ɛleka a, nwane a kɛhola ɔ nwo zo sisi a?

english_verse: God has the wisdom to know when someone is worthless and sinful,
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ ɔze kpamgbanvolɛma ne mɔ; saa ɔnwu ɛtane a, ɔnrɛdwenle nwo ɔ?

english_verse: but it's easier to tame a wild donkey than to make a fool wise. Surrender Your Heart to God
translation_verse: Saa bɛwo asoaso kokonyinli sonla a, ahɔnwɔne bɔbɔ bade ɔ bo.

english_verse: Surrender your heart to God, turn to him in prayer,
translation_verse: “Saa ɛfa wɔ ahonle ɛmaa Nyamenle a, ɛbamaa ɛ sa zo wɔamaa ye.

english_verse: and give up your sins— even those you do in secret.
translation_verse: Saa ɛle ɛtanevolɛ a, gyakyi ɛtaneyɛlɛ, mmadie amumuyɛ azie wɔ wɔ awuke nu.

english_verse: Then you won't be ashamed; you will be confident and fearless.
translation_verse: Ɛhye bamaa wɔamaa ɛ ti zo, ɛnrɛze nyiane; bɛbabɔ ɛ nwo bane na ɛnrɛzulo.

english_verse: Your troubles will go away like water beneath a bridge,
translation_verse: Ɛ rɛle bavi wɔ anwubɛnyunlu ne; ɛbahakye ye ala kɛ azuyilɛ mɔɔ ɛhwe.

english_verse: and your darkest night will be brighter than noon.
translation_verse: Na wɔ ɛbɛla bada adɛla ewiazo sɛnzɛne; nuhua awozinli ne bayɛ kɛ nwonlomɔ sɛnzɛne.

english_verse: You will rest safe and secure, filled with hope and emptied of worry.
translation_verse: Wɔ adwenle bagyinla, ɔboalekɛ ɛlɛ anyelazo; bɛbabɔ ɛ nwo bane, amaa wɔalie wɔ ɛnwomenle anzonudwolɛ nu.

english_verse: You will sleep without fear and be greatly respected.
translation_verse: Ɛbala koonwu, yɛɛ awie biala ɛnrɛha wɔ ɛzulolɛ; na menli dɔɔnwo babiza wɔ moalɛ.

english_verse: But those who are evil will go blind and lose their way. Their only escape is death!
translation_verse: Amumuyɛma ɛnrɛnwu ɛhwee; ɛnriandilɛ adenle biala baminli bɛ nye zo, bɛ anyelazo a le ewule.”

english_verse: Job said to his friends:
translation_verse: Dwobu buale ye kɛ,

english_verse: You think you are so great, with all the answers.
translation_verse: “Ɔnyɛ nwanwane, menli ne a le bɛmɛ, yɛɛ bɛ nee nrɛlɛbɛ bawu.

english_verse: But I know as much as you do, and so does everyone else.
translation_verse: Noko melɛ ndelebɛbo kɛ bɛdabɛ ala la; mendɔ sinli wɔ bɛ nu. Nwane a ɛnze ninyɛne ɛhye mɔ a?

english_verse: I have always lived right, and God answered my prayers; now friends make fun of me.
translation_verse: Me nwo ɛyɛ me gɔnwo mɔ ɛzelekɛ; medame mɔɔ menvɛlɛle Nyamenle memanle ɔliele me zo, sonlakpalɛ mɔɔ me nwo ɛnlɛ ngehanleɛ, ɛnɛ medo ɛzelekɛ aleɛ.

english_verse: It's easy to condemn those who are suffering, when you have no troubles.
translation_verse: Sonla mɔɔ arɛle ɛdɔ aze la adwenle nu a anwubɛnyunlu ɛnle debie biala; ɔwɔ ɛkɛ ɔmaa bɛdabɛ mɔɔ ɔngyɛ na bɛatele bɛadɔ la.

english_verse: Robbers and other godless people live safely at home and say, “God is in our hands!” If You Want To Learn
translation_verse: Anzonudwolɛ wɔ nwule awuke nu, yɛɛ bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛka Nyamenle ɛya la anwo kɔlɔnwo, bɛmɛ, bɛ nyamenle a le bɛ anwosesebɛ.

english_verse: If you want to learn, then go and ask the wild animals and the birds,
translation_verse: “Na biza nane ne mɔ, na bɛkɛhilehile wɔ; biza anwomanyunlu nloma, na bɛkɛze wɔ;

english_verse: Any of them can tell you what the Lord has done.
translation_verse: Na ɛhye mɔ, bɛ nuhua boni a ɛnze kɛ Ɛdɛnkɛma a ɛyɛ ɛhye a?

english_verse: Every living creature is in the hands of God.
translation_verse: Abɔdeɛ biala ngoane wɔ ɔ sa nu, yɛɛ dasanli biala ngoane wɔ ɔ sa nu.

english_verse: We hear with our ears, taste with our tongues,
translation_verse: Ɛnzonlɛ te edwɛkɛ, kɛmɔ ɛtafinlimalɛ sɔ aleɛ nea la.

english_verse: and gain some wisdom from those who have lived a long time.
translation_verse: “Nrɛlɛbɛ hale mgbanyinli, yɛɛ ɛkyɛ a ɛnyia ndelebɛbo.

english_verse: But God is the real source of wisdom and strength.
translation_verse: Nyamenle lɛ nrɛlɛbɛ, ɔlɛ tumi; folɛdulɛ nee ndelebɛbo le ye ɛdeɛ.

english_verse: No one can rebuild what he destroys, or release those he has imprisoned.
translation_verse: Saa ɔbubu debie a, awie ɛngola ye boɛ yɛ bieko; saa ɔto sonla efiade a, awie ɛngola ye tukue.

english_verse: God can hold back the rain or send a flood,
translation_verse: Saa ɔsisi ezuledɔlɛ zo a, azule sesa; saa ɔtukue ezule a, azɛlɛ sia.

english_verse: just as he rules over liars and those they lie to.
translation_verse: Anwosesebɛ nee nrɛlɛbɛ le ye ɛdeɛ; mɔɔ bɛlɛbɛla nee mɔɔ bɛbɛlɛbɛla ye la le ye ɛdeɛ.

english_verse: God shames counselors, turns judges into fools,
translation_verse: Ɔsa folɛdulɛma ɔdie nrɛlɛbɛ, na ɔmaa ndɛnebuavolɛma yɛ ahɔnwɔne.

english_verse: and makes slaves of kings.
translation_verse: Ɔsa arelemgbunli ɔdie bɛ abɔtile, na ɔmo bɛ abɛlako.

english_verse: God removes priests and others who have great power—
translation_verse: Ɔkpolo sɛlɛvolɛma adɛladeɛ na ɔfoa bɛ, na ɔbɛlɛ mgbolema aze.

english_verse: puts mighty kings to shame, and takes away their power.
translation_verse: Ɔbɔ arelemgbunli mralɛ mrenya anyiemgba, na ɔdie anwosesebɛma anwosesebɛ.

english_verse: God strikes their rulers senseless, then leaves them to roam through barren deserts,
translation_verse: Ɔdie azɛlɛ ye azo arelemgbunli ndelebɛbo, na ɔmaa bɛduolua ye ɔ nye ɔ nye.

english_verse: lost in the dark, staggering like someone drunk.
translation_verse: Bɛdi nvuovua wɔ awozinli nu, na ɔmaa bɛtotɔ kɛ nzanli.

english_verse: I know and understand every bit of this.
translation_verse: “Nea, me nye ɛnwu ɛhye mɔ amuala, me nzo ɛde na mede ɔ bo.

english_verse: None of you are smarter than I am; there's nothing you know that I don't.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ bɛmɛ bɛze la, medame noko meze; mendɔ sinli wɔ bɛ nu.

english_verse: But I prefer to argue my case with God All-Powerful—
translation_verse: Me nee Tumivolɛ ne badendɛ, mekulo kɛ mekilehile edwɛkɛ nu mekile Nyamenle.

english_verse: you are merely useless doctors, who treat me with lies.
translation_verse: Na bɛmɛ, bɛfa adalɛ bɛkye bɛ nwo ɛhane, bɛ muala bɛle ninsivoma mɔɔ anwo ɛnlɛ nvasoɛ a.

english_verse: The wisest thing you can do is to keep quiet
translation_verse: Saa bɛyɛ koonwu a, anrɛɛ ɛnee bɛze nrɛlɛbɛ.

english_verse: Are you telling lies for God
translation_verse: Bɛbɔ adalɛ bɛamaa Nyamenle, na bɛabɛlɛbɛla ye ɔ?

english_verse: and not telling the whole truth when you argue his case?
translation_verse: Bɛdi bɛahɔ Nyamenle anzi ɔ? Bɛka Nyamenle tendile bɛamaa ye ɔ?

english_verse: If he took you to court, could you fool him, just as you fool others?
translation_verse: Saa ɔneɛnlea bɛ nuhua a, bɛkɛvi nu ɔ? Asoo bɛkɛhola ye bɛlɛbɛla kɛ bɛbɛlɛbɛla sonla la?

english_verse: If you were secretly unfair, he would correct you,
translation_verse: Kanza bɛwɔ ye afoa awozinli nu bɔbɔ a, ɔbahwi bɛ nyunlu.

english_verse: and his glorious splendor would make you terrified.
translation_verse: Asoo ye tumi ne ɛnrɛha bɛ ɛzulolɛ, yɛɛ ɔ nwo ɛzulolɛ ne ɛnrɛdɔ bɛ nwo zo?

english_verse: Your wisdom and arguments will blow away like dust. Be Quiet While I Speak
translation_verse: Bɛ mrɛlɛbulɛ le mgbane kɛ nzonle, bɛ nwo banebɔlɛ le kɛ ndɛtɛlɛ.

english_verse: Be quiet while I speak, and we'll see what happens.
translation_verse: Bɛyɛ ngungoonwu, na metendɛ, bɛmaa mɔɔ ba me nwo zo la ɛrɛla.

english_verse: I will be responsible for what happens to me.
translation_verse: “Melɛ me ngoane ne me sa nu, mebava me nwonane ne meado nzeleba.

english_verse: God may kill me, but still I will trust him and offer my defense.
translation_verse: Ɛhɛe, ɔbahu me, menlɛ anyelazo; noko mebahɔha me edwɛkɛ meahile ye.

english_verse: This may be what saves me, because no guilty person would come to his court.
translation_verse: Ɛhye bayɛ me ngoanelielɛ, ɔluakɛ sonla mɔɔ ɛnze Nyamenle la ɛnrɛra ɔ nyunlu.

english_verse: I have prepared my case well, and I am certain to win.
translation_verse: Bɛnlea, meziezie me edwɛkɛ ne pɛpɛ, meze kɛ me nwo bavi nu.

english_verse: If you can prove me guilty, I will give up and die. Job Prays I Ask Only Two Things
translation_verse: “Nwane bɔbɔ a kɛhola kɛze me kɛ meyɛ ɛtane a? Anrɛɛ menwɔyɛ koonwu na menwɔwu.

english_verse: I ask only two things of you, my God, and I will no longer hide from you—
translation_verse: Maa membiza wɔ ninyɛne nwiɔ, na menrɛvea me nwo wɔ ɛ nyunlu.
