translation_verse: Ɛ mediema Sodɔm nee ye namunamu ne mɔ bazia akpazi. Samɛlea nee ye namunamu ne mɔ bazia akpazi, yɛɛ ɛdawɔ noko ɛ nee ɛ mra mraalɛ bazia akpazi.

english_verse: But now everyone has learned how wicked you really are. The countries of Syria and Philistia, as well as your other neighbors, hate you and make insulting remarks.
translation_verse: Kɛkala, wɔyɛ kɛ ɔdaye la. Wɔyɛ agolobɛnwo debie wɔmaa Yidɔmma nee namunamu mɔɔ zuozua bɛ la, yɛɛ Filisitiama nee maanle maanle mɔɔ ɛbɔ ɛyia bɛ na bɛkpɔ bɛ la.

english_verse: You must pay for all the vulgar and disgusting things you have done. I, the Lord, have spoken. The Lord Makes a Promise to Jerusalem The Lord said:
translation_verse: Wɔ anyiemgba nee munzule ɛbɛla mɔɔ wɔbɔ la doa wɔ. Medame Ɛdɛnkɛma a mese a.” Ngyekyeleɛ mɔɔ ɛntulu ɛlɛ la

english_verse: Jerusalem, you deserve to be punished, because you broke your promises and ignored our agreement.
translation_verse: Awulae Nyamenle ne se, “Ɛhɛe, mɔɔ wɔyɛ la mebadua wɔ nwolɛ kakɛ kɛ wɔdo ndane na wɔtulu ngyekyeleɛ ne.

english_verse: But I remember the agreement I made with you when you were young, and so I will make you a promise that will last forever.
translation_verse: Noko akee mebahakye ngyekyeleɛ ne mɔɔ wɔ ngakula nu me nee wɔ kyekyele la, na me nee wɔ ayɛ ngyekyeleɛ mɔɔ ɛntulu ɛlɛ a.

english_verse: When you think about how you acted, you will be ashamed, especially when I return your sisters to you as daughters, even though this was not part of our agreement.
translation_verse: Ɛbahakye wɔ ndenle mɔɔ ɛluale nuhua la, na saa mefa ɛ mediema mraalɛ, ngakula nee mgbanyinli memaa wɔ kɛ bɛle ɛ mediema mraalɛ a anyiemgba aha wɔ. Mebamaa bɛayɛ ɛ mra mraalɛ, noko tɛ ngyekyeleɛ ne mɔɔ me nee wɔ kyekyele la ati ɔ.

english_verse: I will keep this solemn promise, and you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Me nee wɔ bayɛ ngyekyeleɛ, na wɔanwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a.

english_verse: I will forgive you, but you will think about your sins and be too ashamed to say a word. I, the Lord God, have spoken.
translation_verse: Ɛbahakye mɔɔ wɔyɛ la na ɔbayɛ wɔ nyiane, amaa saa mefa wɔ ninyɛndane mɔɔ wɔyɛ la mekyɛ wɔ a, wɔambuke ɛ nloa, ɔboalekɛ nyiane ɛbia wɔ. Medame, Awulae Nyamenle a mese a.”

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele me.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Israel the following story,
translation_verse: Ɔse, “Sonla ra, dwenle agyebɛ bie anwo na bu Yizilayɛma ɛrɛlɛ.

english_verse: so they will understand what I am saying to them: A large eagle with strong wings and beautiful feathers once flew to Lebanon. It broke the top branch off a cedar tree,
translation_verse: Ka kile bɛ kɛ, Ɛdɛnkɛma se: Kɔleɛ kpole bie mɔɔ lɛ ndɛbalɛ mgbole ndendenle, na ye ndɛkɛ le ngakyile ngakyile ngɛnlɛma la rale Lɛbanɔn radɛnlanle sida baka bie azo.

english_verse: then carried it to a nation of merchants and left it in one of their cities.
translation_verse: Ɔbule baka ne ati dɛkɛdɛkɛ ne na ɔvale ɔhɔle maanle bie mɔɔ bɛdi gua nu la anu, na ɔdole ye wɔ suakpole bie mɔɔ gualilɛma wɔ zolɛ la azo.

english_verse: The eagle also took a seed from Israel and planted it in a fertile field with plenty of water, like a willow tree beside a stream.
translation_verse: Akee ɔvale azɛlɛ ne azo ma ne mɔ bie na ɔluale ye wɔ azɛlɛ mɔɔ nzule dɔɔnwo wɔ nu, na ɔkye aleɛ la azo.

english_verse: The seed sprouted and grew into a grapevine that spread over the ground. It had lots of leaves and strong, deep roots, and its branches grew upward toward the eagle.
translation_verse: Ɔfifile na ɔyɛle vanye baka ɔdɛlɛdɛlɛle. Ye ndinli hɔle aze kpalɛ na ye ngane ne mɔ hyibale bɛ nwo doale kɔleɛ ne. Yemɔti ɔyɛle vanye baka, ɔkpakyele ngane dɔɔnwo na ɔyele nya dɔɔnwo.

english_verse: There was another eagle with strong wings and thick feathers. The roots and branches of the grapevine soon turned toward this eagle, hoping it would bring water for the soil.
translation_verse: “Kɔleɛ kpole ko noko mɔɔ lɛ ndɛbalɛ mgbole na ɔ nwo ndɛkɛ zonle la ɔdaye ɔrale. Vanye baka ɛhye denrɛdenrɛle ye ngane nee ye ndinli ne mɔ wɔ kɔleɛ ɛhye anwo, amaa yeanyia nzule dɔɔnwo kpalɛ.

english_verse: But the vine was already growing in fertile soil, where there was plenty of water to produce healthy leaves and large grapes.
translation_verse: Noko ɛnee bɛlua ye wɔ azɛlɛ kpalɛ mɔɔ nzule wɔ zolɛ la azo, amaa yeabua, yeakpakye ngane, yeazo, na yeayɛ vanye baka mɔɔ anwo yɛ fɛ a.

english_verse: Now tell me, Ezekiel, do you think this grapevine will live? Or will the first eagle pull it up by its roots and pluck off the grapes and let its new leaves die? The eagle could easily kill it without the help of a large and powerful army.
translation_verse: “Na medame, Awulae Nyamenle, mebiza kɛ: Asoo vanye baka ɛhye bayɛ kpalɛ? Asoo alumua kɔleɛ ne ɛnrɛdu vanye baka ne ɔ bo, ɔnrɛkpolo ye ma ne mɔ amuala ɔnrɛgua, na ɔnrɛpepɛ ye ngane ne mɔ anu ɔnrɛmaa bɛnrɛgyengye? Ɔnrɛhyia anwosesebɛ kpole biala anzɛɛ maanlema dɔɔnwo na bɛadu ye bɛado.

english_verse: The grapevine is strong and healthy, but as soon as the scorching desert wind blows, it will quickly wither. The Lord Explains the Story
translation_verse: Eza nea, asoo saa bɛtu bɛdua bɔbɔ a, ɔbayɛ kpalɛ? Asoo aduduleɛ anwoma ne bɔ ye a ɔnrɛnwoso ɔnrɛwu wɔ ɛleka mɔɔ bɛkɛlua ye la?” Bɛhile ɛrɛlɛ ne abo

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Akee Ɛdɛnkɛma zele me kɛ,

english_verse: Ezekiel, ask the rebellious people of Israel if they know what this story means. Tell them that the king of Babylonia came to Jerusalem, then he captured the king of Judah and his officials, and took them back to Babylon as prisoners.
translation_verse: “Biza atuadelɛma ɛhye mɔ kɛ, asoo bɛte ɛrɛlɛ ne abo? Ka kile bɛ kɛ, bɛnlea, Babelonia belemgbunli rale Gyɛlusalɛm na ɔravale Dwuda belemgbunli nee ye mgbanyima ne mɔ amuala ɔhɔle Babelonia.

english_verse: He chose someone from the family of Judah's king and signed a treaty with him, then made him swear to be loyal. He also led away other important citizens,
translation_verse: Ɔvale suakunlu ɛkɛ ne alehelɛ ne mɔ ko na ɔ nee ye yɛle ngyehyɛlɛ, na ɔmanle ɔhanle ndane ɔhyele ɔ bo. Ɔhyele menli titile mɔɔ wɔ maanle ne anu la nuokɛ ɔhɔle,

english_verse: so that the rest of the people of Judah would obey only him and never gain control of their own country again.
translation_verse: amaa maanle ne angola ɔ nwo zo kpogya bieko; na saa bɛdi ye ngyehyɛlɛ ne azo a, maanle ne agyinla.

english_verse: But this new king of Judah later rebelled against Babylonia and sent officials to Egypt to get horses and troops. Will this king be successful in breaking the treaty with Babylonia? Or will he be punished for what he's done?
translation_verse: Noko Dwuda belemgbunli ne dele atua na ɔzoanle ɛbɔfoɔma wɔ Yigyibiti, amaa Yigyibitima amaa bɛ mgbɔnwɔ nee ɛlɔnema dɔɔnwo. Na ɛnee ɛnea a, asoo belemgbunli ɛhye bayɛ kpalɛ? Asoo sonla mɔɔ yɛ ninyɛne ɛhye mɔ la fi ɛsalɛ? Asoo ɔbahola yeatulu ngyekyeleɛ ne na yeava ɔ nwo dwɔɔ?

english_verse: As surely as I am the living Lord God, I swear that the king of Judah will die in Babylon, because he broke the treaty with the king of Babylonia, who appointed him king.
translation_verse: “Suzuamgba ala mɔɔ medame a mele tease Awulae Nyamenle ne la, mese, ɛleka holɛ ko ne mɔɔ belemgbunli ne mɔɔ ɔdonle ye ndane ne, na ɔtulule ye ngyehyɛlɛ ne la de, wɔ Babelonia suakpole ne azo la, ɛkɛ ne yɛɛ ɔbawu a.

english_verse: Even the king of Egypt and his powerful army will be useless to Judah when the Babylonians attack and build towers and dirt ramps to destroy the cities of Judah and its people.
translation_verse: Yigyibiti belemgbunli nee ye ɛlɔnema pemgbenleamgbe ne bɔbɔ ɛnrɛhola ɛnrɛboa ye wɔ konle nu, wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ Babeloniama kɛrateta ye, kɛbɛnra suakpole ne kɛyia, bɛkɛpɛ ahuma bɛkɛdeda nuhua kɛ bɛku menli dɔɔnwo la.

english_verse: The king of Judah broke his own promises and ignored the treaty with Babylonia. And so he will be punished!
translation_verse: Kɛmɔ ɔdonle ndane ne na ɔtulule ngyehyɛlɛ ne la ati, kɛmɔ ɔkponlenle ngyehyɛlɛ ne azo na akee ɔziale ɔyɛle ninyɛne ɛhye mɔ la ati, ɔ nwo ɛnrɛvi nu.”

english_verse: He made a promise in my name and swore to honor the treaty. And now that he has broken that promise, my name is disgraced. He must pay for what he's done.
translation_verse: Zɔhane ati Awulae Nyamenle ne se, “Suzuamgba ala mɔɔ medame a mele tease Nyamenle ne la, me ndane ne mɔɔ yedo, na yetulu me ngyekyeleɛ ne la, mebakpokpo meagua ɔ ti zo.

english_verse: I will spread out a net to trap him. Then I will drag him to Babylon and see that he is punished for his unfaithfulness to me.
translation_verse: Mebagua ye asawu, na meahye ye me ɛhane nu. Mebava ye meahɔ Babelonia na me nee ye ali ye pɛsɛɛ, wɔ ɛkɛ ne, wɔ ye maamɔvo ɛbɛla ne mɔɔ yebɔ yetia me la anwo.

english_verse: His best troops will be killed in battle, and the survivors will be scattered in every direction. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Bɛbahu ye ɛlɔnema kpalɛ ne mɔ amuala, na bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛkɛvi ɛsalɛ la babɔ asande ahɔ ɛleka ɛleka, na bɛanwu kɛ medame Ɛdɛnkɛma a meha a.” Nyamenle anyelazo ɛwɔkɛ ne

english_verse: Someday, I, the Lord, will cut a tender twig from the top of a cedar tree, then plant it on the peak of Israel's tallest mountain,
translation_verse: Awulae Nyamenle ne se: “Medame mumua ne mebahɔ sida baka bie azo, na meahɔbu ɔ ti dɛkɛdɛkɛ ne. Mebahɔlua ye wɔ boka tendenle bie azo,

english_verse: where it will grow strong branches and produce large fruit. All kinds of birds will find shelter under the tree, and they will rest in the shade of its branches.
translation_verse: wɔ Yizilayɛ awoka ndendenle ne mɔ anu. Ɔbakpakye ngane na yeazo ma, na yeayɛ sida baka kɛnlɛma kpalɛ. Nane ngakyile kɔsɔɔti baradɛnla ɔ bo; nloma ngakyile kɔsɔɔti baradɛnla ye ngane ne mɔ anu, na bɛayɛ bɛ sane wɔ ɛkɛ.

english_verse: Every tree in the forest will know that I, the Lord, can bring down tall trees and help short ones grow. I dry up green trees and make dry ones green. I, the Lord, have spoken, and I will keep my word.
translation_verse: Mbaka mɔɔ wɔ azɛlɛ ne azo la amuala banwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a. Meka mbaka ndendenle aze, na memaa mbaka nzinrenzinra nyi ndendenle. Memaa mbaka amolɛ kyengye, na memaa mbaka wulera yɛ amolɛ. Medame Ɛdɛnkɛma a mese a; mebayɛ mɔɔ meha kɛ meyɛ la.”

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele me kɛ,

english_verse: Ezekiel, I hear the people of Israel using the old saying, “Sour grapes eaten by parents leave a sour taste in the mouths of their children.”
translation_verse: “Ɛrɛlɛ ɛhye mɔɔ Yizilayɛma ta bu la abo a le duzu? ‘Nenya mɔ ɛli vanye ma nyinyianlera ɛmaa nlɔnra gye ɛnyia.’ ”

english_verse: Now tell them that I am the Lord God, and as surely as I live, that saying will no longer be used in Israel.
translation_verse: Awulae Nyamenle se, “Suzuamgba ala mɔɔ medame a mele tease Nyamenle ne la, bɛnrɛbu ɛrɛlɛ ɛhye bieko wɔ Yizilayɛ.

english_verse: The lives of all people belong to me—parents as well as children. However, only those who sin will be put to death.
translation_verse: Bɛnwu ye kɛ awie biala ngoane le me ɛdeɛ. Bɛ nlenya mɔ ngoane ne le me ɛdeɛ, yɛɛ ngakula ne mɔ ngoane le me ɛdeɛ. Awie biala mɔɔ kɛyɛ ɛtane la, bawu.

english_verse: Suppose there is a truly good man who always does what is fair and right.
translation_verse: “Saa sonla tenlene bie wɔ ɛkɛ, ɔyɛ mɔɔ tenrɛ na ɔkɔ mɛla nu,

english_verse: He refuses to eat meat sacrificed to foreign gods at local shrines or to worship Israel's idols. He doesn't have sex with someone else's wife or with a woman having her monthly period.
translation_verse: na ɔnzonle Yizilayɛma awozonle ne mɔ bie, yɛɛ ɔnli bɛ azu ne mɔɔ bɛbɔ ye awoka ne mɔ azo la bie, ɔnva awie aye, yɛɛ ɔnva raalɛ mɔɔ ɛhɔ amozi la,

english_verse: He never cheats or robs anyone and always returns anything taken as security for a loan; he gives food and clothes to the poor
translation_verse: ɔnsisi awie, awie fa debie wula ye awoba a ɔye ɔmaa ye, ɔnwua, ɔmaa mɔɔ ɛhɔne ɛlɛku ye la aleɛ na ɔmaa mɔɔ ɛngeda bie la ɛdanlɛ,

english_verse: and doesn't charge interest when lending money. He refuses to do anything evil; he is fair to everyone
translation_verse: ɔbɔ awie bosea a ɔnlie nzinwo, yɛɛ ɔnlie bie ɔmboka nwolɛ, ɔnle amumuyɛ, ɔfa pɛlepɛlelilɛ ɔdi awie mɔ avinli edwɛkɛ,

english_verse: and faithfully obeys my laws and teachings. This man is good, and I promise he will live.
translation_verse: ɔdi me mɛla zo na ɔnea ɔdi me ngyehyɛlɛ ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti azo a, sonla zɛhae, ɔle tenlenenli, ɔbadɛnla ngoane nu, medame Awulae Nyamenle a mese a.

english_verse: But suppose this good man has an evil son who is violent and commits sins
translation_verse: “Saa sonla zɛhae wo ralɛ nrenya, na kakula ne yɛ awule, ɔyɛ kɔdiawu,

english_verse: his father never did. He eats meat at local shrines, has sex with someone else's wife,
translation_verse: na ɔyɛ ninyɛne zezɛhae mɔ bie, ɔdi azu mɔɔ bɛbɔ bɛmaa awozonle la aleɛ ne bie, ɔfa ɔ gɔnwo mɔ mraalɛ,

english_verse: cheats the poor, and robs people. He keeps what is given to him as security for a loan. He worships idols, does disgusting things,
translation_verse: ɔsisi ehyianvolɛma nee menli mɔɔ yɛ anwunvɔne la, ɔsonle awozonle, ɔbɔ bɛkyi ɛbɛla,

english_verse: and charges high interest when lending money. An evil man like that will certainly not live. He is the one who has done these horrible sins, so it's his own fault that he will be put to death.
translation_verse: ɔbɔ bosea ɔdie nzinwo, anzɛɛ ɔfa bie ɔgua zolɛ a, ɛnee ɛnea a ɔwɔ kɛ sonla zɛhae nyia ngoane ɔ? Ɔwɔ kɛ bɛku ye. Yebɔ munzule ɛbɛla; ɔwɔ kɛ ɔwu, yɛɛ ye mogya gua ɔdaye ɔ ti zo.

english_verse: But suppose this evil man has a son who sees his father do these things and refuses to act like him.
translation_verse: “Saa sonla ɛhye wo ralɛ nrenya, mɔɔ nwu ɔ ze ɛtane mɔɔ yeyɛ la, na ɔsulo, na yeanyɛ ɔ ze ninyɛndane ne mɔ bie,

english_verse: He doesn't eat meat at local shrines or worship Israel's idols, and he doesn't have sex with someone else's wife.
translation_verse: ɔnli aleɛ mɔɔ bɛdo bɛmaa bozonle la yɛɛ ɔnzonle Yizilayɛ awozonle ne mɔ bie, ɔnva ɔ gɔnwo mɔ mraalɛ,

english_verse: He never cheats or robs anyone and doesn't even demand security for a loan. He gives food and clothes to the poor
translation_verse: ɔnyɛ awie ɛtane, awie fa debie wula ye lɔ awoba a ɔye ɔmaa ye, ɔnwua, ɔmaa mɔɔ ɛhɔne ɛlɛku ye la aleɛ, ɔmaa mɔɔ ɛngeda bie la ɛdanlɛ,

english_verse: and refuses to do anything evil or to charge interest. And he obeys all my laws and teachings. Such a man will live. His own father sinned, but this good man will not be put to death for the sins of his father.
translation_verse: ɔnle amumuyɛ, ɔmbɔ bosea ɔnlie nzinwo, yɛɛ ɔnlie bie ɔmboka nwolɛ, na ɔdi me mɛla nee me ngyehyɛlɛ ne mɔ azo a, ɔnle kɛ ɔ ze ɛtane ne mɔ mɔɔ ɔyɛle la ati ɔwu. Ɔwɔ kɛ ɔnyia ngoane.

english_verse: It is his father who will die for cheating and robbing and doing evil.
translation_verse: Ɔ ze ɛdeɛ, kɛmɔ ɔlile amile, ɔwuale ɔ mediema, na ɔbɔle ɛbɛla ɛtane wɔ ye menli ne avinli la, ye ɛtane ne ati, ɔbawu.

english_verse: You may wonder why a son isn't punished for the sins of his father. It is because the son does what is right and obeys my laws.
translation_verse: “Noko bɛmɛ bɛbiza kɛ, ‘Duzu ati a ɔnle kɛ ralɛ nrenya nwu amaneɛ wɔ ɔ ze ɛtane ne mɔ mɔɔ ɔkɛyɛ la anwo ɛ?’ Suzuamgba ala mɔɔ ralɛ nrenya ne ɛyɛ mɔɔ le kpalɛ na ɔkɔ mɛla nu, na yenlea boɛ yeli me mɛla ne mɔ azo la, ɔwɔ kɛ ɔnyia ngoane.

english_verse: Only those who sin will be put to death. Children won't suffer for the sins of their parents, and parents won't suffer for the sins of their children. Good people will be rewarded for what they do, and evil people will be punished for what they do.
translation_verse: Sonla biala mɔɔ kɛyɛ ɛtane la, bawu. Ralɛ nrenya ɛnrɛnwu amaneɛ wɔ ɔ ze ɛtane ne mɔ ati, yɛɛ selɛ ɛnrɛnwu amaneɛ wɔ ralɛ nrenya ɛtane ne mɔ ati. Sonlakpalɛ biala banyia ye kpalɛyɛlɛ nwo ahatualɛ, yɛɛ amumuyɛnli biala banyia ye amumuyɛ nwo ahatualɛ.

english_verse: Suppose wicked people stop sinning and start obeying my laws and doing right. They won't be put to death.
translation_verse: “Na saa amumuyɛnli twe ɔ nwo fi ye amumuyɛ ne mɔ mɔɔ yeyɛ la anwo, ɔdi boɛ, ɔsie me mɛla ne mɔ na ɔdi zolɛ a, ɔbanyia ngoane; ɔnrɛwu.

english_verse: All their sins will be forgiven, and they will live because they did right.
translation_verse: Bɛnrɛhakye ye mɛla ne mɔ mɔɔ yedo la biala. Ye kpalɛ mɔɔ yeyɛ la ati, ɔbanyia ngoane.

english_verse: I, the Lord God, don't like to see wicked people die. I had much rather see them turn back from their sins and live.
translation_verse: Medame Awulae Nyamenle, me nye ɛnlie amumuyɛnli ewule nwo. Mɔɔ mekulo la a le kɛ ɔkɛvi ye ɛtane ne mɔ anwo na ɔkɛnyia ngoane.

english_verse: But when good people start sinning and doing disgusting things, will they live? No! All their good deeds will be forgotten, and they will be put to death because of their sins.
translation_verse: “Na saa tenlenenli twe ɔ nwo fi ye kpalɛ mɔɔ yeyɛ la anwo, ɔyɛ ɛtane na ɔyɛ bɛkyi ninyɛne ne mɔ mɔɔ amumuyɛnli ne yɛ la bie a, ɔbawu. Bɛnrɛhakye ye kpalɛ biala mɔɔ yeyɛ la. Munzule ne mɔɔ yebɔ la anwo fɔlɛlilɛ nee ye ɛtane ne mɔ mɔɔ yeyɛ la ati, ɔbawu.

english_verse: You people of Israel accuse me of being unfair! But listen—I'm not unfair; you are!
translation_verse: “Noko bɛmɛ bɛse, ‘Awulae ɛnli pɛlepɛle.’ Yizilayɛma, bɛdie! Menli pɛlepɛle ɔ? Asoo tɛ bɛmɛ yɛɛ bɛnli pɛlepɛle a?

english_verse: If good people start doing evil, they must be put to death, because they have sinned.
translation_verse: Saa sonlakpalɛ twe ɔ nwo fi ye kpalɛyɛlɛ nwo na ɔyɛ ɛtane a, ye ɛtane ne ati, ɔbawu.

english_verse: They will think about what they've done and stop sinning, and so they won't be put to death.
translation_verse: Kɛmɔ ɔdwenlenle nwolɛ na ɔhwenle ɔ nwo ɔvile ye mɛladonlɛ ne mɔ anwo la ati, ɔbanyia ngoane, ɔnrɛwu.

english_verse: But you still say that I am unfair. You are the ones who have done wrong and are unfair!
translation_verse: Noko bɛmɛ Yizilayɛma bɛse, ‘Awulae ɛnli pɛlepɛle!’ O Yizilayɛma, menli pɛlepɛle ɔ? Bɛmɛ yɛɛ bɛnli pɛlepɛle a.

english_verse: I will judge each of you for what you've done. So stop sinning, or else you will certainly be punished.
translation_verse: “Zɔhane ati Yizilayɛma, medame Awulae Nyamenle mese: Mebabua bɛ ndɛne, kɛmɔ sonla ko biala nyɛleɛ si de la. Bɛnlu bɛ nwo na bɛhwe bɛ nwo bɛvi bɛ mɛladonlɛ kɔsɔɔti anwo na yeanyɛ munzule wɔ bɛ adenle nu.

english_verse: Give up your evil ways and start thinking pure thoughts. And be faithful to me! Do you really want to be put to death for your sins?
translation_verse: Bɛgyakyi bɛ mɛladonlɛ ne mɔ na bɛnyia ahonle fofolɛ nee subane fofolɛ. Duzu ati a bɛkulo kɛ bɛwu ɛ, Yizilayɛma?

english_verse: I, the Lord God, don't want to see that happen to anyone. So stop sinning and live!
translation_verse: Me nye ɛnlie awie biala ewule nwo. Yemɔti medame Awulae Nyamenle, mese, bɛhakyi na bɛnyia ngoane.”

english_verse: Ezekiel, sing a funeral song for two of Israel's leaders:
translation_verse: Akee Nyamenle zele me kɛ mendo alɔbɔlɛ edwɛne ɛhye memaa arelemgbunli mɔɔ wɔ Yizilayɛ la:

english_verse: Your mother was a brave lioness who raised her cubs among lions.
translation_verse: Bɛ nli le awenade belɛ wɔ awenade avinli! Ɔlile ɔ mra adane wɔ awenade nyinli anwo ɛzulolɛ avinli.

english_verse: She taught one of them to hunt, and he learned to eat people.
translation_verse: Ɔlile ɔ ra ko adane, ɔhilele ye kɛ bɛsi bɛdi ɛbɔlɛ la, na ɔhyele menli ɔlile.

english_verse: When the nations heard of him, they trapped him in a pit, then they used hooks to drag him to Egypt.
translation_verse: Maanle maanle bɔle ɔ nwo twoobue, na bɛzuale ye kuma nu ɛhane bɛhyele ye. Bɛvale koba bɛzɔle ye na bɛ nee ye hɔle Yigyibiti.

english_verse: His mother waited for him to return. But soon she lost all hope and raised another cub, who also became fierce.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ ɔ nli hendɛle toonwo na ye anyelazo wiele la, ɔvale ɔ mra ne mɔ ko ɔtetele ye, na ɔyɛle awenade anwo ɛzulolɛ kpole kpalɛ.

english_verse: He hunted with other lions and learned to eat people.
translation_verse: Ɔwiele nyi la, ɔ nee awenade ne mɔ dule, ɔdaye noko ɔzukoale ɛbɔlɛlilɛ na ɔlile menli.

english_verse: Nations plotted to kill him, and people came from all over to spread out a net and catch him in a trap.
translation_verse: Maanle maanle boɔboale bɛ nloa zuale ye ɛhane; bɛguale ye asawu, na bɛhyele ye wɔ bɛ ɛhane nu.

english_verse: They put him in a cage and took him to Babylonia. The lion was locked away, so that his mighty roar would never again be heard on Israel's hills.
translation_verse: Bɛvale koba bɛsosɔle ye bɛdole ye tunli nu, bɛvale ye bɛhɔmanle Babelonia belemgbunli; bɛhyele ye nuokɛ bɛziele, amaa bɛande ɔ ne bieko wɔ Yizilayɛ awoka ne mɔ azo.

english_verse: Your mother was a vine like you, growing near a stream. There was plenty of water, so she was filled with branches and with lots of fruit.
translation_verse: Ɛnee bɛ nli le kɛ vanye baka mɔɔ bɛlua ye wɔ azule nloa. Ɔnyia nzule dɔɔnwo la ati, ɔwula nya dɔɔnwo, ɔso ma dɔɔnwo.

english_verse: Her strong branches became symbols of authority, and she was taller than all other trees— everyone could see how strong and healthy she was.
translation_verse: Ye baka ɛsesebɛ ne, rayɛle belemgbunli ɛhɔtɔlɔ. Vanye baka ne nyinle hɔle anwuma kpalɛ; awie biala nwunle ye tendenle nee ye buzuu.

english_verse: But in anger, I pulled her up by the roots and threw her to the ground, where the scorching desert wind dried out her fruit. Her strong branches wilted and burned up.
translation_verse: Noko bɛdule vanye baka ne ɛya nu. Aduduleɛ anwoma ne manle ɔgyengyenle, ye ma ne mɔ kpolole guale. Ye baka ɛsesebɛ ne wule, na bɛdole ye senle nu bɛyelale ye.

english_verse: Then she was planted in a hot, dry desert,
translation_verse: Kɛkala akee bɛhɔlua ye ɛsɛlɛ zo, wɔ azɛlɛ mɔɔ nzule ɛnle nu na yehwe la azo.

english_verse: where her stem caught fire, and flames burned her branches and fruit. Not one strong branch is left; she is stripped bare. This funeral song must be sung with sorrow.
translation_verse: Senle ɛdɔ ye baka ne anu; yeyela ye ngane nee ye ma ne mɔ amuala. Baka ne anwo ɛnyɛ se ko, bɛfa bɛyɛ belemgbunli ɛhɔtɔlɔ a ɔnyɛ boɛ. Ɛhye le nyanelilɛ edwɛne, yɛɛ bɛdo toonwo a yeradwu ɛnɛ a.

english_verse: Seven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, some of Israel's leaders came to me on the tenth day of the fifth month. They sat down and asked for a message from the Lord.
translation_verse: Bɛ nee yɛ hɔle nlɔnu la, ye ɛvolɛ nsuu ne, siane nnu ne na ye kenle bulu ne azo, Yizilayɛ mgbanyima bie rale me ɛkɛ radɛnlanle aze kɛ bɛbabiza Ɛdɛnkɛma edwɛkɛ.

english_verse: Just then, the Lord God said:
translation_verse: Na Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele me.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, these leaders have come to find out what I want them to do. As surely as I live, I will not give them an answer of any kind.
translation_verse: Ɔse, “Sonla ra, ka kile Yizilayɛ mgbanyima ne mɔ kɛ, kɛ medame Awulae Nyamenle mese la ɛne: Bɛbabiza me edwɛkɛ la, yemɔti a bɛra a. Suzuamgba ala mɔɔ medame a mele tease Nyamenle ne la, bɛmbiza me edwɛkɛ biala. Medame Awulae Nyamenle a mese a.

english_verse: Are you willing to warn them, Ezekiel? Then remind them of the disgusting sins of their ancestors.
translation_verse: “Sonla ra, bua bɛ ndɛne na maa bɛnwu bɛ ze mɔ ninyɛndane mɔɔ bɛyɛle la.

english_verse: Tell them that long ago I, the Lord God, chose Israel to be my own. I appeared to their ancestors in Egypt and made a solemn promise that I would be their God and the God of their descendants.
translation_verse: Ka kile bɛ kɛ, medame Awulae Nyamenle mese: Kenle mɔɔ memkpale nu menyele Yizilayɛma la, menganle ndane mengilele Gyekɔbo abo zo amra ne, na mengilele bɛ kɛ mesi mede la wɔ Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo. Menganle ndane na menganle kɛ mame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne a.

english_verse: I swore that I would rescue them from Egypt and lead them to a land I had already chosen. This land was rich with milk and honey and was the most splendid land of all.
translation_verse: Kenle ko zɔhane menganle ndane kɛ meye bɛ meavi Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo na meava bɛ meahɔ azɛlɛ kpalɛ mɔɔ kye aleɛ, na ɔle azɛlɛ kpalɛ ɔtɛla azɛlɛ kɔsɔɔti, mɔɔ mekpondɛ mezie ɛkɛ memaa bɛ la azo.

english_verse: I told them to get rid of their disgusting idols and not to sin by worshiping the gods of Egypt. I reminded them that I was the Lord their God,
translation_verse: Na menganle mengilele bɛ kɛ, bɛvuandi ninyɛne ɛtane ɛtane ne mɔ mɔɔ mekyi na bɛva bɛ nye bɛzie nwolɛ la bɛgua, bɛmmasonle Yigyibiti awozonle ne mɔ bie bɛgua bɛ nwo evinli, ɔboalekɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma bɛ Nyamenle ne a.

english_verse: but they still rebelled against me. They refused to listen and kept on worshiping their idols and foreign gods. In my anger, I decided to punish the Israelites in Egypt.
translation_verse: Noko bɛandie me edwɛkɛ ne na bɛdele me nwo atua. Bɛ nuhua ko bɔbɔ anvuandi ye bɛkyi ninyɛne ne mɔ angua, yɛɛ bɛ rɛle anvi Yigyibiti awozonle ne mɔ ɛzonlenlɛ. Menyɛle kɛ mewola me ɛya ne meagua bɛ nwo zo, na mealua me ɛya ne azo meadea bɛ wɔ Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo.

english_verse: But that would have made me look like a liar, because I had already promised in front of everyone that I would lead them out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Noko amaa meanzɛkye me duma wɔ maanle maanle ne mɔ mɔɔ bɛde bɛ avinli la anyunlu la, mengilele bɛ kɛ mesi mede la na menyele bɛ menvile Yigyibiti.

english_verse: So I brought them out and led them into the desert.
translation_verse: “Yemɔti menyele bɛ menvile Yigyibiti azɛlɛ zo na me nee bɛ rale fienemgbole ne anu.

english_verse: I gave them my laws and teachings, so they would know how to live right.
translation_verse: Menvale me mɛla ne memanle bɛ na mengilehilele bɛ me ngyehyɛlɛ ne mɔ mɔɔ sonla di zolɛ a ɔnyia ngoane la.

english_verse: And I commanded them to respect the Sabbath as a way of showing that they were holy and belonged to me.
translation_verse: Eza menvale me Ɛnwomenlelielɛ Kenle ne mɔ memanle bɛ, kɛ ɔle sɛkɛlɛneɛ mɔɔ la me nee bɛ avinli a, amaa bɛanwu kɛ medame Ɛdɛnkɛma a mete bɛ nwo a.

english_verse: But the Israelites rebelled against me in the desert. They refused to obey my laws and teachings, and they treated the Sabbath like any other day. Then in my anger, I decided to destroy the Israelites in the desert once and for all.
translation_verse: Noko Yizilayɛma dele me nwo atua wɔ fienemgbole ne anu. Bɛanli me mɛla ne mɔ azo, bɛkpole me ngyehyɛlɛ ne mɔ mɔɔ bɛdi zolɛ a bɛkɛnyia ngoane la, yɛɛ bɛambu me Ɛnwomenlelielɛ Kenle ne mɔ bie. Menyɛle me adwenle kɛ mewola me ɛya ne meagua bɛ nwo zo wɔ fienemgbole ne anu, na meabɔ bɛ bo zo bɔkɔɔ.

english_verse: But that would have disgraced me, because many other nations had seen me bring the Israelites out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Noko me duma ne ati, mengakyile me adwenle, amaa me duma anzɛkye wɔ maanle maanle ne mɔ mɔɔ menyele bɛ menvile bɛ avinli me nee bɛ rale la anyunlu.

english_verse: Instead, I told them in the desert that I would not lead them into the beautiful, fertile land I had promised.
translation_verse: Yemɔti menganle ndane mengilele bɛ wɔ fienemgbole ne anu kɛ me nee bɛ ɛnrɛra azɛlɛ kpalɛ ne mɔɔ kye aleɛ, na ɔle azɛlɛ kpalɛ ɔtɛla azɛlɛ kɔsɔɔti, mɔɔ meva memaa bɛ la azo.

english_verse: I said this because they had not only ignored my laws and teachings, but had disgraced my Sabbath and worshiped idols.
translation_verse: Menganle ndane ne, ɔboalekɛ bɛkpole me ndenle ne mɔ, bɛanli me mɛla ne mɔ azo, yɛɛ bɛambu me Ɛnwomenlelielɛ Kenle ne mɔ bie, ɔluakɛ bɛlile bɛ awozonle nzi.

english_verse: Yet, I felt sorry for them and could not let them die in the desert.
translation_verse: “Noko akee menwunle bɛ anwunvɔne. Meanzɛkye bɛ yɛɛ meambɔ bɛ bo zo wɔ fienemgbole ne anu.

english_verse: So I warned the children not to act like their parents or follow their evil ways or worship their idols.
translation_verse: Na menganle mengilele bɛ mra wɔ fienemgbole ne anu kɛ, ‘Bɛmmafa bɛ ze mɔ agyakɛ, bɛmmadua bɛ ndenle ne mɔ anu, yɛɛ bɛmmasonle bɛ awozonle ne mɔ na bɛgua bɛ nwo evinli.

english_verse: I reminded them that I was the Lord their God and that they should obey my laws and teachings.
translation_verse: Medame Ɛdɛnkɛma, mame a mele bɛ Nyamenle ne a. Bɛli me mɛla ne mɔ azo, na bɛnlea boɛ bɛli me ngyehyɛlɛ ne mɔ azo,

english_verse: I told them to respect my Sabbath to show that they were my people and that I was the Lord their God.
translation_verse: bɛde me Ɛnwomenlelielɛ Kenle ne mɔ anwo, amaa yeayɛ sɛkɛlɛneɛ yeala me nee bɛ avinli, na bɛanwu kɛ medame Ɛdɛnkɛma a mele bɛ Nyamenle a.’

english_verse: But the children also rebelled against me. They refused to obey my laws and teachings, and they treated the Sabbath as any other day. I became angry and decided to punish them in the desert.
translation_verse: “Noko bɛ awolɛndoazo zɔhane dele me nwo atua. Bɛanli me mɛla ne mɔ azo, yɛɛ bɛanli me ngyehyɛlɛ ne mɔ mɔɔ bɛdi zolɛ a bɛkɛnyia ngoane la azo. Eza bɛambu me Ɛnwomenlelielɛ Kenle ne mɔ bie. Menyɛle me adwenle kɛ mewola me ɛya ne meagua bɛ nwo zo, na meazɛkye bɛ wɔ fienemgbole ne anu.

english_verse: But I did not. That would have disgraced me in front of the nations that had seen me bring the Israelites out of Egypt.
translation_verse: Noko mendwenlenle nwolɛ bieko wɔ me duma ne ati, amaa me duma anzɛkye maanle maanle mɔɔ me nee bɛ ɛra bɛ avinli la anyunlu.

english_verse: So I solemnly swore that I would scatter the people of Israel across the nations,
translation_verse: Yemɔti eza menganle ndane wɔ fienemgbole ne anu kɛ mebɔ bɛ asande na meakponde bɛ wɔ maanle maanle ne mɔ anu,

english_verse: because they had disobeyed my laws and ignored my teachings; they had disgraced my Sabbath and worshiped the idols their ancestors had made.
translation_verse: ɔboalekɛ bɛanli me ngyehyɛlɛ ne mɔ azo, na bɛkpo me mɛla ne mɔ yɛɛ bɛambu me Ɛnwomenlelielɛ Kenle ne mɔ bie. Bɛvale bɛ ti bɛzɔle bɛ ze mɔ mmonle ne mɔ.

english_verse: I gave them laws that bring punishment instead of life,
translation_verse: “Yemɔti memanle bɛ mɛla mɔɔ ɛnle kpalɛ nee ngyehyɛlɛ mɔɔ bɛdi zolɛ a, bɛnrɛnyia ngoane la.

english_verse: and I let them offer me unacceptable sacrifices, including their first-born sons. I did this to horrify them and to let them know that I, the Lord, was punishing them.
translation_verse: Memanle bɛvale bɛ belamunli mralɛ bɛyelale bɛ bɛbɔle azu, na bɛluale bɛ ahyɛlɛ ninyɛne zo bɛzɛkyele bɛ nwo. Menyɛle ɛhye menganle bɛ ɛzulolɛ, amaa bɛanwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a.

english_verse: by offering sacrifices, incense, and wine to gods on every hill and under every large tree. I was very angry, because they did these things in the land I had given them!
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ mɔɔ me nee bɛ radwule azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ menganle ndane kɛ mefa meamaa bɛ la azo la, ɛnee akee ɛleka biala mɔɔ bɛkɛnwu boka tendenle biala anzɛɛ baka buzuu biala la, ɛkɛ ne a bɛbɔ azu ne mɔ, na bɛye bɛ ahyɛlɛdeɛ ne mɔ, bɛyela bɛ azubɔlɛ ninyɛne ne mɔ na bɛgua bɛ nza ne mɔ a.

english_verse: I asked them where they went to worship those gods, and they answered, “At the local shrines.” And those places of worship are still called shrines.
translation_verse: Membizale bɛ kɛ, ‘Na ɛleka ɛhye mɔ mɔɔ bɛkɔsonle la noko ɛ?’ Yemɔti ɛnɛ nee ɛnɛ ala, bɛtɛfɛlɛ ɛkɛ ne Beema.

english_verse: Then ask the Israelites why they are following the example of their wicked ancestors
translation_verse: Yemɔti ka kile Yizilayɛma kɛ, medame Awulae Nyamenle, melɛbiza bɛ kɛ: Bɛfa bɛ ze mɔ agyakɛ, bɛaminli adenle bɛayɛ bɛkyi ninyɛne ne mɔ bɛagua bɛ nwo evinli ɔ?

english_verse: by worshiping idols and by sacrificing their own children as offerings. They commit these sins and still think they can ask me for a message. As surely as I am the living Lord God, I will give them no answer.
translation_verse: Bɛhu bɛ mra mrenya bɛyela bɛ bɛbɔ azu bɛmaa awozonle bɛgua bɛ nwo evinli toonwo a yeradwu ɛnɛ a. Yizilayɛma, na akee mame yɛɛ bɛbabiza me bɛanwu mɔɔ ɔwɔ kɛ bɛyɛ la ɔ? Suzuamgba ala mɔɔ medame a mele Awulae Nyamenle ne la, mese, menrɛmaa adenle menrɛmaa bɛnrɛbiza me edwɛkɛ biala.

english_verse: They may think they can be like other nations and get away with worshiping idols made of wood and stone. But that will never happen! The Lord Promises To Restore Israel The Lord said to the people of Israel:
translation_verse: Mɔɔ wɔ bɛ adwenle nu la ɛnrɛyɛ zɔhane ɛlɛ. Bɛ adwenle a le kɛ, bɛkulo kɛ bɛyɛ kɛ maanle maanle ne mɔ, nee mbusua ekpunli ekpunli mɔɔ wɔ maanle ne mɔ anu la na bɛsonle mbaka nee awolɛ. Na ɔnrɛyɛ zɔhane ɛlɛ. Nyamenle tea sonla na ɔfa ɔkyɛ ye

english_verse: As surely as I am the living Lord God, I will rule over you with my powerful arm. You will feel my fierce anger
translation_verse: “Suzuamgba ala mɔɔ medame a mele Awulae Nyamenle ne la, medame a mele tease Nyamenle ne a. Mebava ɛya nee tumi kpole meazie bɛ na meali bɛ belemgbunli.

english_verse: and lead you into a desert surrounded by nations. I will meet you there face to face. Then I will pass judgment on you
translation_verse: Mebava bɛ meara ‘Maanle Maanle Ɛsɛlɛzo,’ na ɛkɛ ne yɛɛ mebaye me nyunlu meadea bɛ a.

english_verse: and punish you, just as I punished your ancestors in the desert near Egypt.
translation_verse: Kɛ menzile mendeanle bɛ ze mɔ wɔ Saenae Fienemgbole nu la, zɔhane ala yɛɛ mebadea bɛdabɛ noko a. Medame Awulae Nyamenle a mese a.

english_verse: I will force each of you to obey the regulations of our solemn agreement.
translation_verse: “Mebanlea bɛ boɛ na meaholo bɛ nwo zo meamaa bɛali me ngyekyeleɛ ne azo.

english_verse: I will separate the sinful rebels from the rest of you, and even though I will bring them from the nations where they live in exile, they won't be allowed to return to Israel. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Mebakpa bɛ nuhua meaye atuadelɛma nee bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛto me mɛla ne la wɔ bɛ avinli. Mebaye bɛ meavi azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ bɛde zolɛ kɛkala la azo, noko bɛ gyakɛ ba ɛnrɛtia Yizilayɛ azɛlɛ zo. Na akee bɛbanwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a.”

english_verse: Go ahead and worship your idols for now, you Israelites, because soon I will no longer let you dishonor me by offering gifts to them. You will have no choice but to obey me!
translation_verse: Na Awulae Nyamenle ne zele kɛ, “Bɛmɛ Yizilayɛma, bɛhɔ zolɛ. Saa bɛnrɛdie me a, ɛnee awie biala ɛbɔ ɔ bo ɛnɛ nee dahuu ɔzonle ye mmonle ne mɔ. Noko bɛmmafa bɛ ahyɛlɛ ninyɛne nee bɛ mmonle ne mɔ bɛsɛkye me duma.

english_verse: When that day comes, everyone in Israel will worship me on Mount Zion, my holy mountain in Jerusalem. I will once again call you my own, and I will accept your sacred offerings and sacrifices.
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ medame Awulae Nyamenle ne, mese, wɔ me boka nwuanzanwuanza ne azo, wɔ Yizilayɛ azɛlɛ zo awoka ne mɔ anu, ɛkɛ ne yɛɛ Yizilayɛma kɔsɔɔti bazonle me a. Ɛkɛ ne yɛɛ mebalie bɛ meado nu a, yɛɛ ɛkɛ ne a mebalie bɛ ahyɛlɛ ninyɛne kpalɛ ne nee bɛ azubɔlɛ ninyɛne nwuanzanwuanza ne mɔ a.

english_verse: When I bring you home from the places where you are now scattered, I will be pleased with you, just as I am pleased with the smell of the smoke from your sacrifices. Every nation on earth will see that I am holy,
translation_verse: Saa me nee bɛ vi menli ngakyile nee maanle maanle mɔɔ mendole bɛ memkpondenle nu la anu sia ba a, mebalie bɛ kɛ azubɔlɛ evuanlɛ, na meahile me nwuanzanwuanzayɛlɛ ne wɔ bɛ avinli meamaa maanle maanle kɔsɔɔti anwu ye.

english_verse: and you will know that I, the Lord, am the one who brought you back to Israel, the land I promised your ancestors.
translation_verse: Saa mefa bɛ meba Yizilayɛ azɛlɛ zo maanle ne mɔɔ menvale membɔle bɛ ze mɔ ɛwɔkɛ la anu a, bɛbanwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a.

english_verse: Then you will remember your wicked sins, and you will hate yourselves for doing such horrible things. They have made you unacceptable to me,
translation_verse: Bɛbahakye bɛ ndenle mɔɔ bɛluale nu nee nyɛleɛ ɛtane ɛtane mɔɔ bɛyɛle bɛvale bɛzɛkyele bɛ nwo la, na bɛavu bɛ nwo wɔ bɛ ninyɛndane mɔɔ bɛyɛle la amuala anwo.

english_verse: so you deserve to be punished. But I will treat you in a way that will bring honor to my name, and you will know that I am the Lord God. Fire from the South
translation_verse: O Yizilayɛma, me nee bɛ ɛnrɛli kɛmɔ bɛ ninyɛndane anzɛɛ bɛ munzule ɛbɛla ne mɔ si de la, amaa bɛanwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a. Medame, Awulae Nyamenle ne a mese a.” Nyiakɛ senle ne

english_verse: The Lord said,
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele me.

english_verse: that I, the Lord God, will start a fire that will burn up every tree, whether green or dry. Nothing will be able to put out the blaze of that fire as it spreads to the north and burns everything in its path.
translation_verse: Ka kile nyiakɛ kpɔkɛ ne kɛ bɛdie Ɛdɛnkɛma edwɛkɛ ne: Awulae Nyamenle ne se, ‘Mebado senle wɔ bɛ avinli meamaa yeayela baka amolɛ nee baka wulera biala mɔɔ wɔ bɛ avinli la. Awie ɛnrɛhola senle ne mɔɔ ɛlɛsɔ la nua; ɔbayelɛyela awie biala anyunlu, ɔvi nyiakɛ yeahɔdwu sɔlɔ.

english_verse: Everyone will know that I started it, and that it cannot be stopped.”
translation_verse: Menli kɔsɔɔti banwu kɛ medame Ɛdɛnkɛma a mendole senle ne a. Awie biala ɛnrɛhola ye nua.’ ”

english_verse: But I complained, “Lord God, I don't want to do that! People already say I confuse them with my messages.”
translation_verse: Na menganle kɛ, “Aa, O Awulae Nyamenle! Bɛlɛkeha ye wɔ me nwo kɛ, ‘Asoo tɛ nwɔra a ɔlɛto yeahile yɛ la?’ ”

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele me.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, condemn the places in Jerusalem where people worship. Warn everyone in Israel
translation_verse: Ɔse, “Sonla ra, kakyi ɛ nye wɔ Gyɛlusalɛm na ka Nyamenle edwɛkɛ tia ɛleka nwuanzanwuanza ne mɔ. Ka Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ ne mɔɔ tia Yizilayɛ azɛlɛ ne la

english_verse: that I am about to punish them. I will pull out my sword and have it ready to kill everyone, whether good or evil.
translation_verse: na ka kɛ, Ɛdɛnkɛma se: Bɛnlea, mele bɛ kpɔvolɛ, mebahwe me dadeɛ ne wɔ ye boa ne anu, na meahu amumuyɛma nee tenlenema amuala.

english_verse: From south to north, people will die,
translation_verse: Mebahu awie biala, kpalɛ o, amumuyɛnli o, ɔvi nyiakɛ yeahɔdwu sɔlɔ.

english_verse: Ezekiel, groan in sorrow and despair so that everyone can hear you.
translation_verse: “Sonla ra, gu ɛnwomenle, kponle ɛ bo kɛ ɛlɛdi nyane kpole bie la wɔ bɛ nye zo ɛkɛ ne.

english_verse: When they ask why you are groaning, tell them you have terrifying news that will make them faint and tremble in fear and lose all courage. These things will happen soon. I, the Lord God, make this promise! A Sword Is Ready To Attack Israel
translation_verse: Na saa bɛbiza wɔ kɛ, ‘Duzu ati a wɔgu ɛnwomenle kpole ɛhye’ a, ka kile bɛ kɛ nrɛlaleɛ ne mɔɔ ɛlɛba la ati ɔ. Saa nrɛlaleɛ ne ba a, awie biala ahonle badu. Bɛ sa nu batuto, bɛ nwo bagolo bɛ, na bɛ gyakɛ agbɔkɛ abili kɛ atɛ. Bɛdie, kɛ ɔlɛba ɛ, na ɔbayɛ zɔhane noko. Medame Awulae Nyamenle a mese a.”

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele me.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Jerusalem: I have sharpened my sword to slaughter you; it is shiny and will flash like lightning! Don't celebrate— punishment is coming, because everyone has ignored my warnings.
translation_verse: Bɛzi kɛ bɛfa bɛahu menli, bɛhwi nwolɛ, amaa yeapɛ kɛ ɛsɛnlɛmanye. Anyelielɛ biala ɛnle ɛkɛ ne ko, ɔluakɛ me ra nrenya ne ɛkpo me kɔkɔbɔlɛ, nee nwolɛ ndeanlɛ ne.

english_verse: Groan in sorrow, Ezekiel; the sword is drawn against my people and their leaders. They will die! So give up all hope.
translation_verse: Sonla ra, su ye awolɛ, ɔluakɛ dadeɛ ne ɛlɛkɔ me menli ne nee Yizilayɛ arelemgbunli anwo zo. Bɛye Yizilayɛ arelemgbunli nee menli ne amuala bɛmaa kɛ bɛhu bɛ wɔ dadeɛ nloa. Fa nyane bɔ ɛ sa ati.

english_verse: I am testing my people, and they can do nothing to stop me. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: “ ‘Ɛhye ɛnle sɔnea edwɛkɛ, saa bɛkpo me kɔkɔbɔlɛ ne a, ɛnee duzu a li ɔ nzi a?’ Medame Awulae Nyamenle a mebiza bɛ a.

english_verse: Ezekiel, warn my people, then celebrate my victory by clapping your hands. My vicious sword will attack again and again, killing my people with every stroke.
translation_verse: “Zɔhane ati sonla ra, ka Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ ne. Bɔ ɛ sa nu maa dadeɛ ne mɔɔ ku menli ne la ɛrɛla na eza ɔrɛla bieko, fane nsa bɔbɔ. Ɔle dadeɛ mɔɔ bahu menli dɔɔnwo yeaha bɛ ɛzulolɛ a,

english_verse: They will lose all courage and stumble with fear. My slaughtering sword is waiting at every gate, flashing and ready to kill.
translation_verse: amaa bɛ ahonle adu na dɔɔnwo adɔ anlenkɛ kpole ne anloa. Meva dadeɛ ne mɔɔ anwo ɛlɛta la memaa; ɔfede kɛ ezule. Bɛhwi nwolɛ kɛ bɛva bɛhu menli.

english_verse: It will slash right and left, wherever the blade is pointed.
translation_verse: To wɔ dadeɛ ne fema zo nee bɛne zo, to ye ɛleka biala mɔɔ ɔ nye kɛli la.

english_verse: Then I will stop being angry, and I will clap my hands in victory. I, the Lord, have spoken. The King of Babylonia and His Sword
translation_verse: Medame noko mebabɔ me sa nu na akee me ɛya ne adwo. Medame a mese a.” Babelonia belemgbunli ne dadeɛ ne

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele me.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, mark two roads for the king of Babylonia to follow when he comes with his sword. The roads will begin at the same place, but be sure to put up a signpost where the two roads separate and go in different directions.
translation_verse: Ɔse, “Sonla ra, kile ndenle nwiɔ mɔɔ Babelonia belemgbunli ne bava ye dadeɛ ne alua nuhua ara la. Ɔwɔ kɛ ndenle nwiɔ ne fi maanle ko ne ala anu a ba a. Akee yɛ sɛkɛlɛneɛ baka maa ɔhile adenle mɔɔ bɛfa nu bɛkɔ suakpole ne azo la.

english_verse: Clearly mark where the two roads lead. One goes to Rabbah, the capital of Ammon, and the other goes to Jerusalem, the fortified capital of Judah.
translation_verse: Kile adenle mɔɔ dadeɛ ne balua nuhua ara Amɔnoma sua ne mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye Relaba la azo, maa ɔlua ɛkɛ ɔrɛla Dwuda na ɔhɔ suakpole Gyɛlusalɛm mɔɔ bɛhye nwolɛ ɛhane la azo.

english_verse: When the Babylonian king stands at that signpost, he will decide which way to go by shaking his arrows, by asking his idols, and by carefully looking at the liver of a sacrificed animal.
translation_verse: Babelonia belemgbunli ne bagyinla nwɔnda ne azo, wɔ ndenle nwiɔ ne ati, na yeabiza nwolɛ, ɔbabili ye ɛda mbaka ne mɔ, yeado yeabiza ye amonle ne, na yeanlea nane ne mɔɔ bɛhu ye la ɛvovoa.

english_verse: His right hand will pull out the arrow marked “Jerusalem.” Then he will immediately give the signal to shout the battle cry, to build dirt ramps up to the top of the city walls, to break down its walls and gates with large wooden poles, and to kill the people.
translation_verse: Ɛbizalɛ ne babɔ Gyɛlusalɛm, na ɔkile kɛ ɔhɔ na ɔhɔva konle ɔdoa Gyɛlusalɛm, ɔbɛnra ɔyia sua ne, ɔva mbaka mgbole ɔsisi Gyɛlusalɛm nlenkɛ mgbole ne mɔ na ɔvu kuma wɔ suakpole ne anwo ɔbɛnra ɔyia.

english_verse: Everyone in Jerusalem had promised to be loyal to Babylonia, and so none of them will believe that this could happen to them. But Babylonia's king will remind them of their sinful ways and warn them of their coming captivity.
translation_verse: Noko Gyɛlusalɛm amra ɛdeɛ, bɛbadwenle kɛ, kɛmɔ bɛli amonle la ati, ɛhye ɛnrɛyɛ zɔhane. Nyamenle bamaa bɛ ɛtane ne mɔ ala ali na nyɛvolɛ ɛlɔnema ali bɛ nwo zo konim.

english_verse: Ezekiel, tell the people of Jerusalem and their ruler that I, the Lord God, am saying: Everything you do is wicked and shows how sinful you are. You are guilty and will be taken away as prisoners.
translation_verse: Yemɔti medame Awulae Nyamenle, mese: Kɛmɔ bɛmaa bɛ ɛtane ne mɔ ɛla ali, na bɛ mɛladonlɛ ne mɔ ɛza ɛgua zolɛ, na bɛ nyɛleɛ ɛtane ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti ɛla ali wienyi la, bɛbadea bɛ na bɛaye bɛ bɛamaa bɛ kpɔvolɛma.

english_verse: And now, you evil and wicked ruler of Israel, your day of final punishment is almost here.
translation_verse: “Wɔmɔ Yizilayɛ belemgbunli, amumuyɛnli mɔɔ anwo ɛnde a, wɔ kɔpo ne ɛyi, na yedwu mɔɔ akee ɔwɔ kɛ bɛsɛkye wɔ bɔkɔɔ a.

english_verse: I, the Lord God, command you to take off your royal turban and your crown, because everything will be different. Those who had no power will be put in charge, and those who now rule will become nobodies.
translation_verse: Medame Awulae Nyamenle mese: Bɛdu ɔ ti abɔtile ne, na bɛdu zolɛ kpɔba kpoonwu ne. Debie biala ɛnrɛyɛ kɛ ye dɛba ne la bieko. Debie biala bahakyi. Maa mɔɔ le bɛlɛvo la zo, na bɛlɛ mɔɔ memaa ɔ nwo zo la aze.

english_verse: I will leave Jerusalem in complete ruins like no one has ever seen until my chosen one comes to punish this city. Judgment against Ammon
translation_verse: Munzule o, munzule! Mebamaa munzule ado suakpole ne na meayɛ ye suadu. Noko ɛhye ɛnrɛzi, kyesɛ ahenle mɔɔ ɔle ye ɛdeɛ la ba, na yemɔ yɛɛ mebava meamaa ye a. Amɔnoma nee dadeɛ

english_verse: The Lord God said: Ezekiel, son of man, the Ammonites have insulted Israel, so condemn them and tell them I am saying: A sword is drawn, ready to slaughter; it is polished and prepared to kill as fast as lightning.
translation_verse: “Na wɔmɔ, sonla ra, ka Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ ne na ka mɔɔ medame Awulae Nyamenle, melɛka meahile wɔ, mɔɔ fane Amɔnoma nee bɛ ɛralɛ mɔɔ bɛlɛba Yizilayɛma anwo zo la anwo edwɛkɛ kile bɛ. Ka kile bɛ kɛ, ‘Dadeɛ, bɛhwe dadeɛ kɛ bɛku menli; bɛhwi nwolɛ, amaa yeapɛ kɛ ɛsɛnlɛmanye.

english_verse: You wicked Ammonites see false visions and believe untrue messages. But your day of punishment is coming soon, and my sword will slaughter you!
translation_verse: Ɛnyelɛzodeɛnwunlɛ biala mɔɔ bɛnwu la ɛnle nɔhalɛ, yɛɛ bɛ abisadeɛ edwɛkɛ biala mɔɔ bɛka la le adalɛ, na ɔbakpomgbolo amumuyɛma mɔɔ anwo ɛnde na bɛ mekɛ ɛdwu kɛ ɔwɔ kɛ bɛsɛkye bɛ la akɔme.

english_verse: Your days to punish others are over, so put your swords away. You will be punished in the land of your birth.
translation_verse: “ ‘Bɛva bɛ dadeɛ ne bɛwula ye boa ne anu. Mebabua bɛ ndɛne wɔ ɛleka mɔɔ bɛbɔle bɛ, wɔ azɛlɛ ne mɔɔ bɛwole bɛ bɛguale zolɛ la azo.

english_verse: My furious anger will scorch you like fire, and I will hand you over to cruel men who are experts in killing.
translation_verse: Mebawola me ɛya ne meagua bɛ nwo zo, na meava ɛya mɔɔ le kɛ senle la meazɛkye bɛ. Mebaye bɛ meawula menli mɔɔ ati yɛ se na bɛze menli ɛhunlɛ nye zo kpalɛ la asa anu.

english_verse: You will be burned and will die in your own land. Then you will be forgotten forever. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Bɛbayɛ kɛ ɛyɛne, bɛayela bɛ senle nu. Bɛbaha bɛ mogya bɛagua maanle ne anu, yɛɛ awie ɛnrɛhakye bɛ bieko, ɔluakɛ medame Ɛdɛnkɛma a mese a.’ ”

english_verse: Some time later, the Lord said:
translation_verse: Eza Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele me.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, are you ready to condemn Jerusalem? That city is filled with murderers, so remind the people of their sins
translation_verse: Ɔse, “Na wɔmɔ, sonla ra, asoo ɛbabua suakpole ne mɔɔ ahɔdiawu ɛyi ye tɛkɛɛ la ndɛne? Ɛnee fa ye bɛkyi nyɛleɛ ne mɔ si ɔ nyunlu.

english_verse: and tell them I am saying: Jerusalem, you have murdered many of your own people and have worshiped idols. You will soon be punished!
translation_verse: Ka kile ye kɛ medame Awulae Nyamenle, mese: Ɔle suakpole mɔɔ bɛka mogya bɛgua ye awɔdenle zo, na bɛva awozonle ɛzonlenlɛ bɛzɛkye bɛ nwo a, bɛ kɔpo ne bayi!

english_verse: Those crimes have made you guilty, and the idols have made you unacceptable to me. So your final punishment is near. Other nations will laugh at you and make insulting remarks,
translation_verse: Bɛdi fɔlɛ wɔ mogya mɔɔ bɛha bɛgua, nee bɛ awozonle mɔɔ bɛdabɛ bɛyɛ la ɛzonlenlɛ nwo. Bɛmaa bɛ mekɛ ne ɛbikye, bɛ mekɛ mɔɔ bɛhilele la ɛdwu. Yemɔti meyɛ bɛ mɔɔ maanle maanle kɔsɔɔti bakpɔ bɛ na bɛagolo bɛ nwo.

english_verse: None of you honor your parents, and you cheat foreigners, orphans, and widows.
translation_verse: Bɛmbu selɛ na yeayɛ ninli, bɛbɔ nyɛvolɛ apo bɛdie bɛ ninyɛne, yɛɛ bɛsisi mɔɔ ɛnlɛ ɔ ze nee ahunlanvolɛ mraalɛ.

english_verse: You show no respect for my sacred places and treat the Sabbath just like any other day.
translation_verse: Bɛkpo me ninyɛne nwuanzanwuanza ne mɔ, yɛɛ bɛnzie me Ɛnwomenlelielɛ Kenle ne.

english_verse: Some of your own people tell lies, so that others will be put to death. Some of you eat meat sacrificed to idols at local shrines, and others never stop doing vulgar things.
translation_verse: Menli wɔ bɛ avinli mɔɔ pɛ nwondomgbɔ na bɛka mogya bɛgua a; menli wɔ bɛ avinli mɔɔ bɔ azu maa awozonle na bɛdidi awoka ne mɔ azo lɔ a, yɛɛ menli wɔ bɛ avinli mɔɔ ɛnze nyiane wɔ adwɔmane ɛbɛla mgbane mgbane ɛbɔlɛ nwo a.

english_verse: Men have sex with their father's wife or with women who are having their monthly period
translation_verse: Mrenya wɔ bɛ avinli mɔɔ fa bɛ ze mɔ mraalɛ, yɛɛ bie mɔ fa mraalɛ mɔɔ ɛhɔ amozi la.

english_verse: or with someone else's wife. Some men even sleep with their own daughter-in-law or half sister.
translation_verse: Bie mɔ fa bɛ gɔnwo mɔ mraalɛ; bie mɔ ɛnze bɛ mra mrenya mraalɛ nyiane na bɛfa bɛ; bie fa ɔ diema raalɛ mɔɔ ɔ nee ye bɛ ze ko la.

english_verse: Others of you accept money to murder someone. Your own people charge high interest when making a loan to other Israelites, and they get rich by cheating. Worst of all, you have forgotten me, the Lord God.
translation_verse: Menli wɔ bɛ avinli mɔɔ die ndoloboa ku awie mɔ, bɛdie nzinwo, bɛdie bie bɛboka nwo na bɛsisi awie mɔ bɛfa bɛnyia bɛ nwo. Bɛ rɛle ɛvi me bɔkɔɔ, medame Awulae Nyamenle a mese a.

english_verse: I will shake my fist in anger at your violent crimes.
translation_verse: “Yemɔti bɛnlea, meva me sa mebɔ bɛ awule nvasoɛ ne mɔ mɔɔ bɛnyia la anu medua bɛ ahɔdiawu ɛbɛla ne mɔ.

english_verse: When I'm finished with you, your courage will disappear, and you will be so weak that you won't be able to lift your hands. I, the Lord, have spoken and will not change my mind.
translation_verse: Asoo mekɛ dwu na mese kɛ me nee bɛ di a, bɛ sa nu kɛyɛ se, bɛkɛhola gyinla? Medame Ɛdɛnkɛma a mese a, yɛɛ mebayɛ noko.

english_verse: I will scatter you throughout every nation on earth and put a stop to your sinful ways.
translation_verse: Mebakponde bɛ maanle maanle zo, na meazande bɛ wɔ maanle maanle ne mɔ anu, meamaa bɛagyakyi bɛ ninyɛne ɛtane ɛtane ne mɔ ɛyɛlɛ.

english_verse: You will be humiliated in the eyes of other nations. Then you will know that I, the Lord God, have done these things. Jerusalem Must Be Purified
translation_verse: Maanle maanle ne mɔ banwu kɛ bɛwie mgbane yɛ, na akee bɛanwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a.” Nyamenle debie nu evinlidulɛ fonlomo ne

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele me kɛ,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, I consider the people of Israel as worthless as the leftover metal in a furnace after silver has been purified.
translation_verse: “Sonla ra, Yizilayɛma ɛyɛ ewula wɔ me nye zo. Bɛ kɔsɔɔti bɛyɛ kɛ dwɛtɛ fufule nee kɔbele, kyɛnze nee bulalɛ nee sumi mɔɔ bɛholo bɛ fonlomo nu toonwo bɛhakyi ewula la.

english_verse: So I am going to bring them together in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Yemɔti medame Awulae Nyamenle, mese: Kɛmɔ bɛ muala bɛyɛ ewula la, mebahuohua bɛ kɔsɔɔti bɛ nloa wɔ Gyɛlusalɛm.

english_verse: like silver in a furnace. Then they will know that I, the Lord, have punished them in my anger. Everyone in Jerusalem Is Guilty
translation_verse: Kɛ bɛsi bɛkolo dwɛtɛ fufule wɔ fonlomo nu la, zɔhane ala yɛɛ mebaholo bɛdabɛ a, na akee bɛanwu kɛ medame Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛɛ mewola me ɛya ne megua bɛ nwo zo a.” Ɛtane mɔɔ Yizilayɛ mgbanyima yɛle la

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Eza Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele me.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the people of Israel that their country is full of sin, and that I, the Lord, am furious!
translation_verse: Ɔse, “Sonla ra, ka kile Yizilayɛ kɛ ɔle azɛlɛ mɔɔ zolɛ ɛnde a, anzɛɛ sumunli kɛ bɛvale ɛya bɛdeanle ye la zolɛ ɛtɛtele.

english_verse: Their leaders are like roaring lions, tearing apart their victims. They put people to death, then steal everything of value. Husbands are killed, and many women are left as widows.
translation_verse: Arelemgbunli mɔɔ wɔ maanle ne anu la le kɛ awenade mɔɔ ɛnyia nane na ɔlɛkpo yeatete ye la. Bɛli menli nwonane, bɛve anwoneɛ nee ninyɛne mɔɔ sonle bolɛ, yɛɛ bɛmaa ahunlanvolɛ mraalɛ ɛzo dɔɔnwo wɔ bɛ avinli.

english_verse: The priests of Israel ignore my Law! Not only do they refuse to respect any of my sacred things, but they don't even teach the difference between what is sacred and what is ordinary or between what is clean and what is unclean. They treat my Sabbath like any other day, and so my own people no longer honor me.
translation_verse: Bɛ sɛlɛvolɛma ɛvuandi me mɛla ne ɛdo na bɛgua me ninyɛne nwuanzanwuanza ne mɔ anwo evinli. Bɛammaa ngakyile anla ninyɛne mɔɔ le nwuanzanwuanza nee mɔɔ ɛnle nwuanzanwuanza la avinli, yɛɛ bɛangile ngakyile mɔɔ la ninyɛne mɔɔ anwo te nee mɔɔ anwo ɛnde la avinli. Bɛambu me Ɛnwomenlelielɛ Kenle ne mɔ, yemɔti bɛgua me nwo evinli wɔ bɛ avinli.

english_verse: Israel's officials are like ferocious wolves, ripping their victims apart. They make a dishonest living by injuring and killing people.
translation_verse: Arelemgbunli mɔɔ wɔ maanle ne anu la le kɛ bɛdi mɔɔ ɛlɛtete nane la. Bɛka mogya bɛgua, bɛsɛkye ngoane na bɛfa bɛnyia awule nvasoɛ.

english_verse: And then the prophets in Israel cover up these sins by giving false visions. I have never spoken to them, but they lie and say they have a message from me.
translation_verse: Bɛ Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛma ɛnyelɛzodeɛnwunlɛ ɛnle nɔhalɛ, bɛka adalɛ abisadeɛ edwɛkɛ na bɛava kisane bɛagua zolɛ bɛaze kɛ, ‘Kɛ Awulae Nyamenle ne se la ɛne’, wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma ɛtɛbukele ɔ nloa la.

english_verse: The people themselves cheat and rob; they abuse the poor and take advantage of foreigners.
translation_verse: Menli mɔɔ wɔ maanle ne anu la ɛzukoa apobɔlɛ, yɛɛ bɛyɛ bɛ nwo nwule. Bɛsisi ehyianvolɛ nee mɔɔ ɛhyia la; bɛsisi nyɛvolɛ bɛwua bɛ, yɛɛ bɛngakyi bɛ ɛbɛla ne.

translation_verse: Wɔ adwɔmane ɛbɛla mgbane mgbane ne a le nrɛnlana ne mɔɔ andu la. Kɛmɔ anrɛɛ ɔwɔ kɛ metu ɛ nwo evinli ne amuala, noko ɛ nwo anvie, na ɛ nwo evinli ne bie tɛbɔ ɛkɛ ne la, ɛ nwo ɛnrɛvie ɛlɛ, kyesɛ mewola me ɛya kpole ne megua ɛ nwo zo na me kunlu adwo.

english_verse: That time will certainly come! And when it does, I won't show the people of Jerusalem any pity or change my mind. They must be punished for the evil they have done. I, the Lord God, have spoken. Ezekiel's Wife Dies
translation_verse: Medame Ɛdɛnkɛma a mese a, mebayɛ mɔɔ meha la. Menrɛzia me nzi, menrɛze anwunvɔne yɛɛ menrɛvu me nwo. Mebadea bɛ, kɛmɔ bɛ nyɛleɛ nee bɛ ndenle ne mɔ si de la. Medame, Awulae Nyamenle a mese a.” Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ ne aye ne ewule

english_verse: The Lord said,
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele me kɛ,

english_verse: “Ezekiel, son of man, I will suddenly take the life of the person you love most. But I don't want you to complain or cry.
translation_verse: “Sonla ra, nea, mefa kɛlɛ kokye meaye ɛ ye ne mɔɔ ɛkulo ye kɛ debie la meavi ɛ nye zo, noko ɔnle kɛ ɛsu ye anzɛɛ ɛdi nyane, yɛɛ ɔnle kɛ ɛsuosua wɔ adɛladeɛ nu.

english_verse: Mourn in silence and don't show that you are grieving. Don't remove your turban or take off your sandals; don't cover your face to show your sorrow, or eat the food that mourners eat.”
translation_verse: Ɛbagu ɛnwomenle, noko ɔnle kɛ awie te, yɛɛ mmakile kɛ ɛlɛdi nyane. Fa wɔ abɔtile ne bɔ ɛ ti na fa wɔ mgbɔlaboa ne wula, mmakeda ɛ nyunlu yɛɛ mmadi aleɛ mɔɔ kile kɛ ɛlɛdi nyane la.”

english_verse: One morning, I was talking with the people as usual, and by sunset my wife was dead. The next day I did what the Lord had told me,
translation_verse: Yemɔti nwonlomɔ ne menganle mengilele menli ne, na ye nɔsolɛ nu me ye wule. Aleɛ hyenle bieko na ye nwonlomɔ ne menyɛle mɔɔ Ɛdɛnkɛma zele me la.

english_verse: and when people saw me, they asked, “Why aren't you mourning for your wife?”
translation_verse: Na menli ne bizale me kɛ, “Ɛnrɛhile ninyɛne ɛhye mɔ mɔɔ ɛlɛyɛ la abo ɛnrɛhile yɛ ɔ?”

english_verse: he is ready to destroy the temple in which you take such pride and which makes you feel so safe. Your children who now live in Jerusalem will be killed.
translation_verse: Awulae Nyamenle ne se: Bɛnlea, mebagua me Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anwo evinli. Ɔle debie mɔɔ bɛfa bɛtu bɛ nwo a, bɛ nye ɛralɛ mɔɔ bɛ nye kuku nwolɛ a. Bɛ mra mrenya nee bɛ mra mraalɛ mɔɔ bɛgyakyile bɛ bɛ nzi la badɔ dadeɛ nloa.

english_verse: Then you will do the same things I have done. You will leave your face uncovered and refuse to eat the food that mourners usually eat.
translation_verse: Na bɛbayɛ mɔɔ meyɛ la bie: bɛnrɛheda bɛ nyunlu yɛɛ bɛnrɛli aleɛ mɔɔ kile kɛ bɛlɛdi nyane la.

english_verse: You won't take off your turbans and your sandals. You won't cry or mourn, but all day long you will go around groaning because of your sins.
translation_verse: Bɛbabɔ bɛ abɔtile ne mɔ, bɛawula mgbɔlaboa; bɛnrɛzu yɛɛ bɛnrɛli nyane. Bɛ ninyɛndane ne mɔ bamaa bɛanwa na bɛazu bɛ kunlu bɛakponle bɛahile bɛ nwo ngoko.

english_verse: I am a warning sign—everything I have done, you will also do. And then you will know the Lord God has made these things happen.
translation_verse: Yizikeɛle bayɛ sɛkɛlɛneɛ amaa bɛ, na mɔɔ yeyɛ la, bie yɛɛ bɛdabɛ noko bɛbayɛ a. Na saa ɛhye mɔ sisi a, yɛɛ bɛbanwu kɛ medame a mele Awulae Nyamenle ne a.”

english_verse: The Lord said, “Ezekiel, I will soon destroy the temple that makes everyone feel proud and safe, and I will take away their children as well.
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele kɛ, “Na wɔmɔ, Sonla ra, kenle ne mɔɔ mebaza bɛ mealie bɛ aranemgbole ne, bɛ anyelielɛ nee bɛ anyunlunyia, bɛ nye ɛralɛ ne, nee mɔɔ bɛ nye kuku nwolɛ, bɛ mra mrenya nee mraalɛ la,

english_verse: On that same day, someone will escape from the city and come to tell you what has happened.
translation_verse: kenle ko zɔhane mɔɔ mebayɛ ɛhye la, awie mɔɔ vile ɛsalɛ la yɛɛ baraha ahile wɔ a.

english_verse: Then you will be able to speak again, and the two of you will talk. You will be a warning sign to the people, and they will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_verse: Kenle ko ne ɛ nloa bade na wɔadendɛ wɔahile ahenle ne mɔɔ vile ɛsalɛ la. Ɛbadendɛ, ɛnrɛdɔ mumule bieko. Yemɔti ɛbayɛ sɛkɛlɛneɛ wɔamaa bɛ, na bɛanwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a.”

english_verse: Now I am going to let you be conquered by tribes from the eastern desert. They will set up their camps in your land and eat your fruit and drink your milk.
translation_verse: melɛye bɛ meamaa menli ne mɔɔ wɔ Aduduleɛ la meamaa bɛava bɛ bɛayɛ bɛ ɛdeɛ bɔkɔɔ. Bɛbadɛnla bɛ avinli na bɛasisi bɛ azua wɔ bɛ avinli. Bɛbali bɛ mbaka ma ne mɔ na bɛanlo bɛ nlankɛ nyɛfonzule.

english_verse: And so I will hand you over to enemies who will rob you. I will completely destroy you. There won't be enough of your people left to be a nation ever again, and you will know that I, the Lord, have done these things. Judgment on Moab
translation_verse: bɛnlea, meva bɛ nwo ɛya kpole, na mebaye bɛ meamaa maanle maanle ne mɔ, na bɛava bɛ kɛ konle nu afedeɛ. Mebaye bɛ meavi menli avinli na meaminli bɛ bo zo wɔ maanle maanle avinli. Mebazɛkye bɛ bɔkɔɔ, na bɛanwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a.” Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ mɔɔ tia Mowabe la

english_verse: The Lord God said, “The people of Moab thought Judah was no different from any other nation.
translation_verse: Awulae Nyamenle ne se, “Kɛmɔ Mowabe hanle kɛ, Dwudama ɛyɛ kɛ maanle maanle gyɛne ne mɔ la ati,

english_verse: So I will let Moab's fortress towns along its border be attacked, including Beth-Jeshimoth, Baal-Meon, and Kiriathaim.
translation_verse: mebamaa bɛaho bɛava azuamgbole mɔɔ wɔ Mowabe maanle ne ɛweɛne zo, mɔɔ bɔ maanle ne anwo bane la amuala, Bɛte Gyɛhyemo, Beeyale Mɛyɔn, yɛɛ Keleateeyem boka nwolɛ.

english_verse: The same eastern desert tribes that invade Ammon will invade Moab, and just as Ammon will be forgotten forever,
translation_verse: Mebaye Mowabe maanle ne meaboka Amɔnoma maanle ne meamaa maanle maanle mɔɔ wɔ aduduleɛ la ayɛ bɛ ɛdeɛ, amaa bɛangakye ye bieko wɔ maanle maanle ne mɔ avinli.

english_verse: Moab will be punished. Then the people there will know that I am the Lord.” Judgment on Edom
translation_verse: Mebadea Mowabema, na bɛanwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a.” Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ mɔɔ tia Yidɔm la

english_verse: The Lord God then said, “The people of Edom are guilty of taking revenge on Judah.
translation_verse: Awulae Nyamenle ne se, “Kɛmɔ Yidɔm vale atisesebɛ lile Dwudama nzenralɛ, na bɛvonle wɔ nzenralɛlilɛ ne anu la ati, Mal

english_verse: So I will punish Edom by killing all its people and livestock. It will be an empty wasteland all the way from Teman to Dedan.
translation_verse: kɛ medame Awulae Nyamenle ne mese la ɛne: Mebadea Yidɔmma, na meahu menli nee nyɛmoa mɔɔ wɔ maanle ne anu la amuala, na meamaa maanle ne adɔ mgbane. Menli mɔɔ wɔ maanle ne anu la amuala, ɔvi Timan mɔɔ kɔdwu Didan la badɔ dadeɛ nloa.

english_verse: I will send my own people to take revenge on the Edomites by making them feel my fierce anger. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord God.” Judgment on Philistia
translation_verse: Mebamaa Yizilayɛma aha Yidɔm senle meava meali nzenralɛ. Bɛbayɛ Yidɔmma, kɛmɔ me ɛya ne kpole si de la, na bɛanwu me nzenralɛlilɛ ne deɛ holɛ, medame, Awulae Nyamenle a mese a.” Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ mɔɔ tia Filisitia la

english_verse: The Lord God said, “The cruel Philistines have taken revenge on their enemies over and over and have tried to destroy them.
translation_verse: Awulae Nyamenle ne se, “Filisitiama le abolɛ yɛɛ bɛvale ɛkpɔlɛ mɔɔ ɛnlɛ awieleɛ la a bɛlile bɛ nzenralɛ ne a.

english_verse: Now it's my turn to treat the Philistines as my enemies and to kill everyone living in their towns along the seacoast.
translation_verse: Yemɔti medame Awulae Nyamenle mese, mebadea Filisitiama nee Kɛlɛtema, meabɔ bɛ bo zo bɔkɔɔ, na meazɛkye bɛ menli mɔɔ ɛha mɔɔ wɔ ɛnweanloa la.

english_verse: In my fierce anger, I will take revenge on them. And when I punish them, they will know that I am the Lord.”
translation_verse: Mebava ɛya ndeanlɛ kpole kpalɛ a meali nzenralɛ ne a, na bɛanwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a.”

english_verse: Eleven years after King Jehoiachin and the rest of us had been led away as prisoners to Babylonia, the Lord spoke to me on the first day of the month. He said:
translation_verse: Bɛhyele yɛ bɛhɔle nlɔnu la, ye ɛvolɛ bulu nee ko ne anu, siane ko ne kenle ne mɔɔ lumua la azo, Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele me.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, the people of the city of Tyre have celebrated Jerusalem's defeat by singing, “Jerusalem has fallen! It used to be powerful, a center of trade. Now the city is shattered, and we will take its place.”
translation_verse: Ɔse, “Sonla ra, Taya ɛha Gyɛlusalɛm anwo edwɛkɛ kɛ, ‘Ɛhɛe, bɛbubu menli ne anlenkɛ kpole ne; akee yela nwolɛ wanaanwo yemaa me. Kɛkala mɔɔ yedɔ mgbane la, me sa baha mɔɔ meminlinle ye la amuala.’

english_verse: Because the people of Tyre have sung that song, I have the following warning for them: I am the Lord God, and I am now your enemy! I will send nations to attack you, like waves crashing against the shore.
translation_verse: “Yemɔti medame Awulae Nyamenle mese, ɛdawɔ Taya, meyɛ wɔ kpɔvolɛ, na mebamaa maanle maanle dɔɔnwo ara ɛ nwo zo, kɛmɔ nyevile azɛlɛkye bu la.

english_verse: They will tear down your city walls and defense towers. I will sweep away the ruins until all that's left of you is a bare rock,
translation_verse: Bɛbazɛkye Taya bane ne mɔ, na bɛabubu ye tawa ne mɔ bɛagua aze. Mebadu ye ɛnwea ne kɔsɔɔti meagua, meamaa yeaha ye bolɛ tandane ne mɔɔ la azɛlɛ ne abo la.

english_verse: where fishermen can dry their nets along the coast. I promise that you will be robbed
translation_verse: Ɔbayɛ ɛleka mɔɔ fɛlɛhyelɛma rɛlɛ bɛ avonle a, wɔ nyevile ne avinli. Medame Awulae Nyamenle a mese a. Ɔbayɛ afedeɛ yeamaa maanle maanle dɔɔnwo.

english_verse: and that the people who live in your towns along the coast will be killed. Then you will know that I am the Lord.
translation_verse: Bɛbahu menli mɔɔ wɔ azuamgbole ne mɔ azo la, na bɛbanwu kɛ medame a mele Ɛdɛnkɛma a.”

english_verse: King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylonia is the world's most powerful king, and I will send him to attack you. He will march from the north with a powerful army, including horses and chariots and cavalry troops.
translation_verse: Awulae Nyamenle ne se, “Mebava belemgbunli kpole mɔɔ bo bɛ kɔsɔɔti bɛ nwo zo, Babelonia belemgbunli Nɛbukadenɛza meavi sɔlɔ nehane, meamaa yeava mgbɔnwɔ, konle ehwili, ɛlɔnema mɔɔ tɛnla mgbɔnwɔ zo nee ɛlɔnema dɔɔnwo kpalɛ yeara Taya anwo zo.

english_verse: First, he will attack your towns along the coast and kill the people who live there. Then he will build dirt ramps up to the top of your city walls and set up rows of shields around you.
translation_verse: Ɔbahu bɛ mra mraalɛ wɔ bɛ azɛlɛ ne azo; ɔbamaa ye ɛlɔnema abɛnra ayia bɛ, bɛbavunvu ahuma, bɛahuohua ɛnwea edukue edukue, na bɛava enyinlike bɛalie bɛ nwo bane bɛaho bɛatia bɛ.

english_verse: He will command some of his troops to use large wooden poles to beat down your walls, while others use iron rods to knock down your watchtowers.
translation_verse: Ɔbamaa bɛava mbaka mgbole bɛasisi bɛ azuamgbole bane ne mɔ kɛ bɛbubu bɛ bɛagua, na yeamaa bɛava akuma bɛagologolo bɛ tawa ne mɔ bɛagua.

english_verse: He will have so many horses that the dust they stir up will seem like a thick fog. And as his chariots and cavalry approach, even the walls will shake, especially when he proudly enters your ruined city.
translation_verse: Ye mgbɔnwɔ ne mɔ bazo dɔɔnwo kpalɛ mɔɔ bɛ nzi munlutu bɔbɔ baheda bɛ nwo zo a. Ye ɛlɔnema mɔɔ ka mgbɔnwɔ nee konle ehwili ne mɔ la agyakɛ abo nee bɛ ne bakpusu bɛ azuamgbole bane ne mɔ, wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ ɔkɛze kɛ akee ɔfo azua ne mɔ azo kɛ sonla mɔɔ ɛli konim la.

english_verse: His troops will ride through your streets, killing people left and right, and your strong columns will crumble to the ground.
translation_verse: Ye ɛlɔnema mɔɔ ka mgbɔnwɔ la barava bɛ azuamgbole gua ne mɔ, bɛbahu bɛ menli ne mɔ, na bɛ mpila mgbole ne mɔ babubu agua.

english_verse: The troops will steal your valuable possessions; they will break down your walls, and crush your expensive houses. Then the stones and wood and all the remains will be dumped into the sea.
translation_verse: Ɛlɔnema ne bave bɛ nwo ninyɛne kɔsɔɔti, bɛ anwonyia nee bɛ ninyɛne adɔne, bɛbabubu bɛ azuamgbole bane ne mɔ nee bɛ azua ngɛnlɛma ne mɔ bɛagua. Bɛbavuandi bɛ awolɛ, dubinli nee ɛnwea bɛagua azule ne mɔ anu.

english_verse: You will have no reason to sing or play music on harps,
translation_verse: Mebamaa bɛagyakyi bɛ edwɛne mɔɔ bɛto la, na awie ɛnrɛde bɛ getaa ne mɔ ane bieko.

english_verse: because I will turn you into a bare rock where fishermen can dry their nets. And you will never rebuild your city. I, the Lord God, make this promise.
translation_verse: Mebayɛ bɛ kɛ bodane mɔɔ ɛhwee ɛnle zolɛ la, na bɛayɛ kɛ ɛleka mɔɔ bɛrɛlɛ avonle la. Bɛnrɛkyekye bɛ azua ne mɔ bieko, ɔluakɛ medame Ɛdɛnkɛma yɛɛ meha a.”

english_verse: The people of the nations up and down the coast will shudder when they hear your screams and moans of death.
translation_verse: Awulae Nyamenle hanle ɛhye hilele Taya amra. Ɔse, “Saa bɛba kɛ bɛbahu bɛ a, bɛ menli mɔɔ ɛbodɛboda la ɛkponlenlɛ nee bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛho bɛgua la azedɔlɛ bakpusu bɛ ɛnweanloa azua ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti.

english_verse: The kings will step down from their thrones, then take off their royal robes and fancy clothes, and sit on the ground, trembling. They will be so shocked at the news of your defeat that they will shake in fear
translation_verse: Akee arelemgbunli mɔɔ wɔ ɛnweanloa maanle maanle ne mɔ anu la vi bɛ ebia ne mɔ anu badwazo; bɛbayeye bɛ arelemgbunli adɛladeɛ ne mɔ, na bɛayeye bɛ adɛladeɛ ne mɔ nee bɛ adɛladeɛ mɔɔ bɛnwo bɛ nloa la. Bɛ nwo bawozo bɛ; bɛbakpofokpofo aze na bɛ nwo awozo mekɛ biala, na bɛ rɛle abɔ bɛmɛ bɛ nwo.

english_verse: But now Tyre is in ruins, and the people on the coast stare at it in horror and tremble in fear.”
translation_verse: Kenle mɔɔ bɛhonle bɛdɔle la, mbɔra ne mɔ wozole. Ɛhɛe, mbɔra mɔɔ wɔ nyevile nu la arɛle bɔle wɔ bɛ ɛzɛkyelɛ nwo.”

english_verse: I, the Lord God, will turn you into a ghost-town. The ocean depths will rise over you
translation_verse: Awulae Nyamenle ne se, “Saa meyɛ bɛ suakpole ne suadu kɛ azuamgbole mɔɔ awie ɛnde zolɛ la, memaa nyevile ne bu fa bɛ nwo zo, na azɛlɛkye ne mɔ keda bɛ nwo zo a,

english_verse: and carry you down to the world of the dead, where you will join people of ancient times and towns ruined long ago. You will stay there and never again be a city filled with people.
translation_verse: akee meavuandi bɛ meamaa bɛahɔboka bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛkɔ ewule kuma nu la anwo, mebaye bɛ meamaa bɛahɔboka mɔmoane amra anwo, meamaa bɛahɔboka bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛwɔ ɛbolɔ maanle nu na bɛde alɔbɔlɛ nu la anwo, amaa bɛannyia ɛleka bɛandɛnla anzɛɛ bɛannyia ɛleka wɔ teasema azɛlɛ zo.

english_verse: You will die a horrible death! People will come looking for your city, but it will never be found. I, the Lord, have spoken.
translation_verse: Mebamaa bɛ awieleɛ ayɛ ɛzulolɛ na bɛ bo zo aminli bɔkɔɔ. Bɛbakpondɛ bɛ bo zo, na bɛnrɛnwu bɛ.” Awulae Nyamenle ne a se a.

english_verse: The Lord said:
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma zele me kɛ,

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, sing a funeral song for Tyre,
translation_verse: “Akee wɔmɔ, sonla ra, ye Taya awolɛ, na ka kile ye kɛ,

english_verse: the city that is built along the sea and that trades with nations along the coast. Tell the people of Tyre that the following message is from me: Tyre, you brag about your perfect beauty,
translation_verse: Wɔmɔ mɔɔ bɛkyekye wɔ nyevile nloa, menli mɔɔ wɔ ɛnwea ɛnwea gualilɛ ɛleka, kɛ Awulae Nyamenle se la ɛne: O Taya, wɔmɔ wɔha kɛ, wɔ anwofɛlɛko di munli.

english_verse: and your control of the sea. You are a ship built to perfection.
translation_verse: Wɔ ɛweɛne ne mɔ wɔ nyevile kunlu lɔ; menli mɔɔ kyekyele wɔ la kyekyele wɔ kɛnlɛma.

english_verse: Builders used cypress trees from Mount Hermon to make your planks and a cedar tree from Lebanon for your tall mast.
translation_verse: Bɛvale Hɛmɔn Boka mbaka ɛsesebɛ bɛyɛle mgbunla, bɛvale Lɛbanɔn sida mbaka bɛyɛle wɔ meli avela mbaka.

english_verse: Oak trees from Bashan were shaped into oars; pine trees from Cyprus were cut for your deck, which was then decorated with strips of ivory.
translation_verse: Beehyan mbaka ɛsesebɛ a bɛvale bɛzele bɛ ndahoma a; bɛvale Saepelɛse ɛnweanloa mbaka bɛzɛle wɔ meli ne mɔ anu, na bɛvale ɛzɛlɛ bɛduoduale nu.

english_verse: The builders used fancy linen from Egypt for your sails, so everyone could see you. Blue and purple cloth from Cyprus was used to shade your deck.
translation_verse: Bɛvale Yigyibiti lenen ɛdanlɛ kɛnlɛma mɔɔ bɛnwo ɔ nloa la bɛyɛle bɛ meli ne mɔ avela, bɛhilele kɛ ɔle bɛ sɛkɛlɛneɛ. Bɛvale Saepelɛse ndanlɛ kɔkɔlɛ nee buluwu bɛbole kpɔda bɛdɛnlanle ɔ bo; bɛbole belandane bɛ meli ne mɔ anu.

english_verse: Men from Sidon and Arvad did the rowing, and your own skilled workers were the captains.
translation_verse: Saedɛnema nee Avadema a hanle meli ne mɔ a; ɛdawɔ wɔ menli mɔɔ ze nyevile nye zo la lile bɛ ɛlɛne bo hanle meli ne mɔ.

english_verse: Experienced men from Byblos repaired any damages. Sailors from all over shopped at the stores in your port.
translation_verse: Bebolɔsoma mɔɔ ze adwinli kpalɛ, duoduale bɛ meli ayiazo ne mɔ, Nyevile nye meli nee nuhua menli kɔsɔɔti nee bɛ ralile gua.

english_verse: Brave soldiers from Persia, Lydia, and Libya served in your navy, protecting you with shields and helmets, and making you famous.
translation_verse: “Sogyama vi Pɛhyea, Ledea, yɛɛ Lebeya rayɛle gyima wɔ wɔ ɛlɔnema anu. Bɛ nee bɛ dɛnlanle, bɛvale bɛ ahyɛlɛ nee bɛ enyinlike bɛhendɛhendanle bɛ azua nu; bɛlile konim bɛmanle bɛ, bɛmanle bɛ nyunlu rale anyia.

english_verse: Your guards came from Arvad and Cilicia, and men from Gamad stood watch in your towers. With their weapons hung on your walls, your beauty was complete.
translation_verse: Ɛlɔnema mɔɔ vi Avade nee Hilɛke la zinzale bɛ bane ne mɔ, yɛɛ ɛlɔnema mɔɔ vi Gamade la zinzale bɛ tawa ne mɔ. Bɛhendɛhendanle bɛ enyinlike ne mɔ wɔ bɛ bane ne mɔ anwo na bɛmanle bɛ anwofɛlɛko ne lile munli.

english_verse: Merchants from southern Spain traded silver, iron, tin, and lead for your products.
translation_verse: “Wɔ ninyɛne ngɛnlɛma dɔɔnwo ne ati, Sepeenema nee wɔ lile gua na bɛvale bɛ dwɛtɛ fufule, bulalɛ, kyɛnze, yɛɛ sumi bɛmanle wɔ bɛliele ninyɛne.

english_verse: The people of Greece, Tubal, and Meshech traded slaves and things made of bronze,
translation_verse: Gilikima, Tubalema, yɛɛ Mihyɛkema nee wɔ lile gua na bɛdɔnenle menli nee kɔbele ninyɛne bɛmanle wɔ bɛliele ninyɛne bɛvile wɔ ɛkɛ.

english_verse: and those from Beth-Togarmah traded work horses, war horses, and mules.
translation_verse: Bɛte Togama amra dɔnenle bɛ mgbɔnwɔ, konle mgbɔnwɔ, yɛɛ mgbɔnwɔndua manle wɔ liele ninyɛne.

english_verse: You also did business with people from Rhodes, and people from nations along the coast gave you ivory and ebony in exchange for your goods.
translation_verse: Menli mɔɔ wɔ Didan la nee wɔ lile gua; menli mɔɔ de ɛnweanloa la rɛlɛle wɔ ɛzɛlɛ nee mbaka ɛsesebɛ bie mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye ɛbɔni la liele ninyɛne.

english_verse: Judah and Israel gave you their finest wheat, fancy figs, honey, olive oil, and spices in exchange for your merchandise.
translation_verse: Dwudama nee Yizilayɛma nee wɔ lile gua. Bɛrɛlɛle wɔ hwiiti, ɔlivi, feege, wolɛ, nwole, yɛɛ ɛnlomedazia na bɛliele wɔ ninyɛne ne mɔ bie.

english_verse: The people of Damascus saw what you had to offer and brought you wine from Helbon and wool from Zahar.
translation_verse: Wɔ ninyɛne ngakyile dɔɔnwo ne mɔ ati, Dɛmasekɛsema nee wɔ lile gua na bɛdɔnenle Hɛlebɔn nwanye, mboane enrinli fufule,

english_verse: The people of Dedan supplied you with saddle blankets,
translation_verse: Didan nee wɔ lile gua dɔnenle ɛkpɔnwɔ zo ndanlɛ manle wɔ.

english_verse: Merchants from Sheba and Raamah gave you excellent spices, precious stones, and gold in exchange for your products.
translation_verse: Hyibama nee Releemama nee wɔ lile gua; bɛdɔnenle bɛ aleɛdonlɛ ninyɛne evuanlɛ kpalɛ, ezukoa awolɛ kpalɛ kpalɛ, yɛɛ ezukoa nvutuke bɛmanle wɔ bɛliele wɔ ninyɛne kpalɛ kpalɛ ne mɔ bie.

english_verse: You also did business with merchants from the cities of Haran, Canneh, Eden, Sheba, Asshur, and Chilmad,
translation_verse: Hɛlan, Kani, Yidɛn, Ahyɔɔ, yɛɛ Kelemade nee wɔ lile gua.

english_verse: and they gave you expensive clothing, purple and embroidered cloth, brightly colored rugs, and strong rope.
translation_verse: Bɛ nee wɔ lile ndakpa gua, yɛɛ akee ndanlɛ buluwu, ninyɛne mɔɔ bɛnwo, kapɛte futufutu mɔɔ bɛva nyɛma bɛkyekye bɛmia nu la amuala.

english_verse: Large, seagoing ships carried your goods wherever they needed to go. You were like a ship loaded with heavy cargo
translation_verse: Meli vi Tahyehye yɛɛ batwe wɔ ninyɛne kɔ a. “Yemɔti ɛnee ɛle kɛ meli mɔɔ la nyevile nye, mɔɔ ninyɛne ɛyi ye tɛkɛɛ la.

english_verse: and sailing across the sea, but you were wrecked by strong eastern winds.
translation_verse: Menli mɔɔ ka wɔ la ɛva wɔ ɛdo nyevile nye. Aduduleɛ anwoma ɛnloma wɔ nyevile buma nu.

english_verse: The shouts of your drowning crew were heard on the shore.
translation_verse: Wɔ menli mɔɔ nea wɔ meli ne mɔ azo la ɛzunlɛ dielie maanle ne anu amuala.

english_verse: Every ship is deserted; rowers and sailors and captains all stand on shore,
translation_verse: “Menli mɔɔ ka meli ne la fo gua ndahoma zo weɛ azule ba ɛnweazo. Bɛ muala bɛbagyinla ɛnwea ne anloa,

english_verse: mourning for you. They show their sorrow by putting dust on their heads and rolling in ashes;
translation_verse: bɛsu alɔbɔlɛ ɛzunlɛ, bɛye awolɛ. Bɛfula anwea bɛgua bɛ ti zo, bɛweweɛ bɛ nwo nzonle nu.

english_verse: they shave their heads and dress in sackcloth as they cry in despair.
translation_verse: Wɔmɔ ati, bɛkpa bɛ ti, bɛkeda ɛrele, na bɛfa nyane bɛsu alɔbɔlɛ ɛzunlɛ.

english_verse: In their grief they sing a funeral song for you: “Tyre, you were greater than all other cities. But now you lie in silence at the bottom of the sea.
translation_verse: Bɛye awolɛ wɔ bɛ ɛzunlɛ nu, na bɛye awolɛ kɛ: ‘Suakpole boni a wɔ nyevile avinli mɔɔ bɛzɛkye ye bɛdɛla Taya a?

english_verse: “Nations that received your merchandise were always pleased; kings everywhere got rich from your costly goods.
translation_verse: Mekɛ mɔɔ wɔ ninyɛne adɔne vi nyevile nzi ba la, ɛmanle menli dɔɔnwo anye liele; wɔ anwonyia nee wɔ ninyɛne adɔne manle azɛlɛ ye azo arelemgbunli nyianle bɛ nwo.

english_verse: But now you are wrecked in the deep sea, with your cargo and crew scattered everywhere.
translation_verse: Wɔmɔ a nyevile ne ɛbɔ ɛ bo zo wɔ azule buma ne anu lɔ la; wɔ ninyɛne adɔne nee menli mɔɔ ka meli ne la, nee wɔ ɛnloma gbodogbodo.’

english_verse: People living along the coast are shocked at the news. Their rulers are horrified, and terror is written across their faces.
translation_verse: “Wɔ anwubɛnyunlu ne ɛmaa awie biala mɔɔ de ɛnweanloa la ahonle ɛdu; na ɛzulolɛ ɛmaa bɛ arelemgbunli nyunlu ɛdo.

english_verse: The merchants of the world can't believe what happened. Your death was gruesome, and you are gone forever.”
translation_verse: Gualilɛma mɔɔ wɔ menli ne anu la ahonle dule kɛ wɔ awieleɛ ɛwie ɛzulolɛ zɛhae, na ɛnrɛkpazi bieko ɛlɛ na aloa abɔ a.”

english_verse: The Lord God said:
translation_verse: Ɛdɛnkɛma dendɛle hilele me.

english_verse: Ezekiel, son of man, tell the king of Tyre that I am saying: You are so arrogant that you think you're a god and that the city of Tyre is your throne. You may claim to be a god, though you're nothing but a mere human.
translation_verse: Ɔse, “Sonla ra, ka kile Taya belemgbunli ne kɛ, medame Awulae Nyamenle mese: Kɛmɔ ɛtu ɛ nwo la ati, wɔha mgbole kɛ, ‘Medame, mele nyamenle, mede nyamenle ne mɔ kɔsɔɔti ebia nu, wɔ nyevile kunlu nehane,’ noko ɛle sonla, ɛnle nyamenle. Ɛyɛ ɛ nwo kɛ ɛze nrɛlɛbɛ kɛ nyamenle bie,

english_verse: You think you're wiser than Daniel and know everything.
translation_verse: na ɛze nrɛlɛbɛ bɔbɔ ɛtɛla Daneɛle, yemɔti debie biala ɛnvea wɔ.

english_verse: Your wisdom has certainly made you rich, because you have storehouses filled with gold and silver.
translation_verse: Wɔ nrɛlɛbɛ nee wɔ ndelebɛbo ti wɔnyia ɛ nwo, na wɔboɔboa ezukoa nvutuke nee dwɛtɛ fufule dɔɔnwo anloa wɔ wɔ gya ne mɔ anu.

english_verse: You're a clever businessman and are extremely wealthy, but your wealth has led to arrogance!
translation_verse: Wɔ gualilɛ nu nrɛlɛbɛ kpole ne mɔɔ ɛlɛ la ati, wɔ anwonyia ɛzo dɔɔnwo, na ɔmaa ɛmemaa ɛ nwo zo.

english_verse: You compared yourself to a god, so now I, the Lord God,
translation_verse: “Yemɔti kɛ medame, Awulae Nyamenle mese la ɛne: Kɛmɔ wɔyɛ ɛ nwo kɛ ɛze nrɛlɛbɛ kɛ nyamenle bie la ati,

english_verse: will make you the victim of cruel enemies. They will destroy all the possessions you've worked so hard to get.
translation_verse: nea, mebamaa nyɛvolɛ maanle anwo ɛzulolɛ bie ara ɛ nwo zo. Bɛbahwe dadeɛ bɛazɛkye wɔ nrɛlɛbɛ ninyɛne ngɛnlɛma ne mɔ, bɛamaa ɛ nyunlu adɔ aze abɔ.

english_verse: Your enemies will brutally kill you, and the sea will be your only grave.
translation_verse: Bɛbavuandi wɔ bɛado ewule kuma ne anu, na wɔawu dadeɛ nloa wɔ nyevile kunlu nehane.

english_verse: When you face your enemies, will you still claim to be a god? They will attack, and you will suffer like any other human.
translation_verse: Asoo ɛbaha kɛ, ‘Mele nyamenle,’ wɔ menli mɔɔ ɛlɛku wɔ la anyunlu? Ɛle sonla, ɛnle nyamenle wɔ menli mɔɔ ɛlɛbodɛboda wɔ la asa anu.

english_verse: Foreigners will kill you, and you will die the death of those who don't worship me. I, the Lord, have spoken. A Funeral Song for the King of Tyre
