translation_verse: Mɔɔ Saelase nee Temɔte vi Masidonea rale la ɛnee Pɔɔlo ɛva ye mekɛ muala ɛlɛka Edwɛkpa ne ali daselɛ ahile Dwuuma ne kɛ, Mɛzaya ne a le Gyisɛse.

english_verse: Finally, they turned against him and insulted him. So he shook the dust from his clothes and told them, “Whatever happens to you will be your own fault! I am not to blame. From now on I am going to preach to the Gentiles.”
translation_verse: Nzinlii mɔɔ bɛtiale mɔɔ ɔlɛka la, bɛhehanle ɛtane dɔɔnwo bɛhilele ye. Ɛhye ati Pɔɔlo kpokpole ye tɛladeɛ ne anu munlutu guale na ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Saa bɛminli a, nwolɛ ɛzonle ɛnzo me. Bɛdabɛ bɛ ɛminlinlɛ nwo ɛzonle zo bɛ! Ɔvi ɛnɛ mɔɔ kɔ la mebahɔ bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛnle Dwuuma la anu meahɔha Edwɛkpa ne.”

english_verse: Paul then moved into the house of a man named Titius Justus, who worshiped God and lived next door to the synagogue.
translation_verse: Na Pɔɔlo vi ɛleka mɔɔ ɔde la dule na ɔhɔle nrenya bie mɔɔ ɛnle Dwuunli, na ɔsonle Nyamenle la sua nu. Nrenya ne bɛfɛlɛ ye Taeteɛse Gyɛsetɛse; ye sua nu bikye Dwuuma nyianu sua ne.

english_verse: Crispus was the leader of the synagogue. He and everyone in his family put their faith in the Lord. Many others in Corinth also heard the message, and all the people who had faith in the Lord were baptized.
translation_verse: Kelesepɛse mɔɔ nea nyianu sua ne azo la nee ye sua nu amra liele Awulae lile, yɛɛ Kɔlentema dɔɔnwo mɔɔ dele Edwɛkpa ne la liele lile na bɛmanle bɛzɔnenle bɛ.

english_verse: One night, Paul had a vision, and in it the Lord said, “Don't be afraid to keep on preaching. Don't stop!
translation_verse: Kenle ko nɔɔzo Pɔɔlo nwunle Awulae wɔ ɛlalɛ nu kɛ ɔlɛka yeahile ye kɛ, “Pɔɔlo, mmasulo; kɔ zolɛ ka Edwɛkpa ne, mmagyakyi

english_verse: I am with you, and you won't be harmed. Many people in this city belong to me.”
translation_verse: na mezua ɛ nzi. Awie biala ɛnrɛhola wɔ ɛhwee yɛ, ɔluakɛ menli dɔɔnwo wɔ sua ye azo mɔɔ bɛle me ɛdeɛ a.”

english_verse: Paul stayed on in Corinth for a year and a half, teaching God's message to the people.
translation_verse: Na Pɔɔlo dɛnlanle ɛkɛ ne toonwo ɛvolɛ ko nee foa, ɔhanle Nyamenle edwɛkɛ ne ɔhilele menli ne mɔ.

english_verse: While Gallio was governor of Achaia, some of the Jewish leaders got together and grabbed Paul. They brought him into court
translation_verse: Na mɔɔ bɛvale Galeyo bɛyɛle Wulomu amɛnlado mɔɔ nea Giliki maanzinli ne azo la, Dwuuma ne mɔ yɛle ko na bɛhwenle Pɔɔlo bɛhɔle kɛ ɔli ye edwɛkɛ.

english_verse: and said, “This man is trying to make our people worship God in a way that is against our Law!”
translation_verse: Bɛ ɛzonle mɔɔ bɛdonle ye la a le kɛ, “Sonla ɛhye ɛlɛbɔ mɔdenle yeamaa menli azonle Nyamenle wɔ adenle bie mɔɔ tia yɛ Dwuuma mɛla ne la azo.”

english_verse: Even before Paul could speak, Gallio said, “If you were charging this man with a crime or some other wrong, I would have to listen to you.
translation_verse: Pɔɔlo yɛle kɛ ɔsa ɔ ne la, Galeyo zele Dwuuma ne mɔ kɛ, “Saa edwɛkɛ ɛhye yɛle debie mɔɔ tia mɛla anzɛɛ fane nyɛleɛ ɛtane bie anwo a anrɛɛ menwɔdie.

english_verse: But since this concerns only words, names, and your own law, you will have to take care of it yourselves. I refuse to judge such matters.”
translation_verse: Na kɛmɔ yehɔyɛ edwɛkɛ nu ngilehilelɛ nee duma yɛɛ bɛdabɛ Dwuuma bɛ mɛla nwo edwɛkɛ la, ɛnee bɛdabɛ bɛhɔnlea na bɛziezie. Edwɛkɛ zɛhae mɔ menrɛdɛnla menrɛli.”

english_verse: Then he sent them out of the court.
translation_verse: Na ɔyele bɛ ali wɔ kɔɔto ɛkɛ ne.

english_verse: The crowd grabbed Sosthenes, the Jewish leader, and beat him up in front of the court. But none of this mattered to Gallio. Paul Returns to Antioch in Syria
translation_verse: Bɛvindele la, bɛhɔle Sɔsotɛnize mɔɔ nea nyianu sua ne azo la anwo zo na bɛbole ye dwɛɛ wɔ kɔɔto sua ne anyunlu ɛkɛ ne, noko ɛhye anvane Galeyo anwo nretee zɛhae bɔbɔ. Pɔɔlo sia ara Anteɔko

english_verse: After Paul had stayed for a while with the Lord's followers in Corinth, he told them goodbye and sailed on to Syria with Aquila and Priscilla. But before he left, he had his head shaved at Cenchreae because he had made a promise to God.
translation_verse: Pɔɔlo lile mekɛ ekyi wɔ diedima ne mɔ anwo ɛkɛ ne la, nzinlii ɔ nee Pelesela nee Akoyela bɛvile ɛkɛ bɛvale azule nye kɛ bɛkɔ Selea. Bɛdwule Sɛnkilia la Pɔɔlo bɔle ɛwɔkɛ manle Nyamenle, yemɔti ɔmanle bɛkpale ɔ ti.

english_verse: The three of them arrived in Ephesus, where Paul left Priscilla and Aquila. He then went into the synagogue to talk with the people there.
translation_verse: Bɛdwule Ɛfɛsɛse la, Pɔɔlo gyakyile Pelesela nee Akoyela. Ɔhɔle Dwuuma nyianu sua ne anu ɔ nee bɛ hɔdendɛle.

english_verse: They asked him to stay longer, but he refused.
translation_verse: Menli mɔɔ liele lile la bodole ye kɛ ɔ nee bɛ ɛdɛnla ɛhyɛ, na yeamkponle.

english_verse: He told them goodbye and said, “If God lets me, I will come back.”
translation_verse: Ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Saa ɔyɛ Nyamenle ɛhulolɛ a mebazia meara.” Na ɔvi Ɛfɛsɛse ɔvale ɛlɛne ɔhɔle.

english_verse: Paul sailed to Caesarea, where he greeted the church. Then he went on to Antioch.
translation_verse: Ɔradwule Sizalia la ɔbɔle hwii ɔhɔle Gyɛlusalɛm ɔhɔkpɔlale asɔnema ne mɔ na ɔpɛle nu ɔhɔle Anteɔko.

english_verse: After staying there for a while, he left and visited several places in Galatia and Phrygia. He helped the followers there to become stronger in their faith. Apollos in Ephesus
translation_verse: Ɔlile mekɛ ekyi wɔ ɛkɛ ne la, ɔvile ɛkɛ ne na ɔhɔkpɔsale Galeehyea nee Felegyea maanzinli ne mɔ anu ɔmanle diedima ne mɔ anwosesebɛ. Apɔlɔso bɔ Edwɛkpa ne nolo wɔ Ɛfɛsɛse nee Kɔlente

english_verse: A Jewish man named Apollos came to Ephesus. Apollos had been born in the city of Alexandria. He was a very good speaker and knew a lot about the Scriptures.
translation_verse: Dwuunli bie mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye Apɔlɔso, mɔɔ bɛwole ye Alɛzandelea, na ɔ nloa ɛde, eza ɔze Nyamenle Edwɛkɛ ne kpalɛ la rale Ɛfɛsɛse.

english_verse: He also knew much about the Lord's Way, and he spoke about it with great excitement. What he taught about Jesus was right, but all he knew was John's message about baptism.
translation_verse: Bɛtete ye wɔ Awulae Adenle ne anu, yemɔti ɔkola ɔka Gyisɛse anwo edwɛkɛ ne fɔɔnwo kpalɛ. Noko Dwɔn ɛzɔnenlɛ ɛdeɛ ne ala a ɔze a.

english_verse: Apollos started speaking bravely in the synagogue. But when Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him to their home and helped him understand God's Way even better.
translation_verse: Ɔdendɛle akɛnrasesebɛ zo kpalɛ wɔ Dwuuma nyianu sua ne anu. Pelesela nee Akoyela nwunle ye la, bɛvɛlɛle ye bɛ sua nu na bɛhilehilele ye Awulae Adenle ne anwo edwɛkɛ fɔɔnwo.

english_verse: Apollos decided to travel through Achaia. So the Lord's followers wrote letters, encouraging the followers there to welcome him. After Apollos arrived in Achaia, he was a great help to everyone who had put their faith in the Lord Jesus because of God's gift of undeserved grace.
translation_verse: Apɔlɔso yɛle ye adwenle kɛ ɔkaluolua Akaya yeaha Nyamenle edwɛkɛ ne, zɔhane ati mediema ne mɔ boale ye na bɛhɛlɛle kɛlata bɛmanle ɔhɔmanle mediema mɔɔ wɔ nehane la, kɛ bɛlie ye kɛnlɛma gyɛlɛɛnye. Ɔhɔdwule la ɔyɛle moalɛ kpole ɔmanle bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛlua Nyamenle ɛlolɛ zo bɛrayɛ diedima la.

english_verse: He got into fierce arguments with the Jewish people, and in public he used the Scriptures to prove that Jesus is the Messiah.
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ ɔka Dwuuma ne mɔ ɔgua mekɛ biala mɔɔ bɛkɛyia kɛ bɛyɛ ngilehilelɛ la na ɔfa Nyamenle Edwɛkɛ ne ɔkilehile nu wienyi kɛ Mɛzaya ne a le Gyisɛse.

english_verse: While Apollos was in Corinth, Paul traveled across the hill country to Ephesus, where he met some of the Lord's followers.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Apɔlɔso wɔ Kɔlente la, Pɔɔlo hɔle maanzinli ne anu akpɔsa toonwo ɔravindele Ɛfɛsɛse, na ɔranwunle ɛdoavolɛma bie wɔ ɛkɛ.

english_verse: He asked them, “When you put your faith in Jesus, were you given the Holy Spirit?” “No!” they answered. “We have never even heard of the Holy Spirit.”
translation_verse: Ɔbizale bɛ kɛ, “Bɛliele bɛlile la, bɛnyianle Sunsum Nwuanzanwuanza ne ɔ?” Bɛzele ye kɛ, “Yɛtɛtele bɔbɔ kɛ Sunsum Nwuanzanwuanza bie wɔ ɛkɛ.”

english_verse: “Then why were you baptized?” Paul asked. They answered, “Because of what John taught.”
translation_verse: Ɔbizale bɛ kɛ, “Ɛnee ɛzɔnenlɛ ne boni a bɛnyianle a?” Bɛbuale kɛ, “Dwɔn ɛzɔnenlɛ ne ɔ.”

english_verse: Paul replied, “John baptized people so they would turn to God. But he also told them someone else was coming, and they should put their faith in him. Jesus is the one that John was talking about.”
translation_verse: Na Pɔɔlo zele bɛ kɛ, “Dwɔn zɔnenle menli mɔɔ nlunle bɛ nwo wɔ bɛ ɛtane nwo la; na ɔzele Yizilayɛma kɛ bɛva bɛ rɛle bɛwula mɔɔ ɔli ɔ nzi ɛlɛba la anu. Na sonla zɔhane a le Gyisɛse.”

english_verse: After the people heard Paul say this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.
translation_verse: Bɛdele ɛhye la, bɛmanle bɛzɔnenle bɛ wɔ Awulae Gyisɛse duma nu.

english_verse: Then Paul placed his hands on them. The Holy Spirit was given to them, and they spoke unknown languages and prophesied.
translation_verse: Pɔɔlo vale ɔ sa guale bɛ nwo zo, bɛnyianle Sunsum Nwuanzanwuanza ne na bɛhanle ɛdendɛlɛ ngakyile bɛhanle Nyamenle nrɛlaleɛ ne.

english_verse: There were about twelve men in this group.
translation_verse: Bɛ muala bɛkɛyɛ bulu nee nwiɔ.

english_verse: For three months Paul went to the synagogue and talked bravely with the people about God's kingdom. He tried to win them over,
translation_verse: Pɔɔlo hɔle nyianu sua ne anu na ɔdendɛle akɛnrasesebɛ zo ɔhilele Dwuuma ne mɔ toonwo siane nsa kɛ ɔmaa bɛanwu Nyamenle Belemgbunlililɛ ne.

english_verse: but some of them were stubborn and refused to believe. In front of everyone they said terrible things about God's Way. Paul left and took the followers with him to the lecture hall of Tyrannus. He spoke there every day
translation_verse: Na kɛmɔ bie mɔ ahonle ɛsolo la ati, bɛ muala bɛanlie bɛanli. Bie mɔ dendɛle ɛtane tiale Awulae Adenle ne wɔ menli somaa ne anyunlu. Zɔhane ati Pɔɔlo gyakyile bɛ na ɔ nee diedima ne mɔ akee kɔtendɛ na ɔkilehile bɛ wɔ Taelanɛse sukulu sua ne anu alehyenlɛ biala.

english_verse: for two years, until every Jew and Gentile in Asia had heard the Lord's message. The Sons of Sceva
translation_verse: Ɛhye hɔle zolɛ ɛvolɛ nwiɔ. Yemɔti ɔmanle bɛdabɛ mɔɔ ɛnee bɛwɔ Ehyea maanzinli ne anu la, Dwuuma nee bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛnle Dwuuma la, amuala dele Awulae anwo Edwɛkpa ne. Siva amra mrenya ne mɔ

english_verse: God gave Paul the power to work great miracles.
translation_verse: Nyamenle luale Pɔɔlo anwo zo yɛle nwanwane ninyɛne mɔɔ yɛ ɛzulolɛ a.

english_verse: People even took handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched Paul's body, and they carried them to everyone who was sick. All of the sick people were healed, and the evil spirits went out.
translation_verse: Saa bɛfa ye hameteduku anzɛɛ ahedazo bɛkɔgua awuleravolɛ nwo zo a, bɛte kpɔkɛ, na sunsum ɛtane ne mɔ fi bɛ nwo nriandi.

english_verse: Some Jewish men started going around trying to force out evil spirits by using the name of the Lord Jesus. They said to the spirits, “Come out in the name of that same Jesus that Paul preaches about!”
translation_verse: Dwuuma bie mɔ noko mɔɔ bɛdabɛ bɛluolua nu bɛtu sunsum ɛtane la yɛle kɛ bɛfa Awulae Gyisɛse duma bɛayɛ bie. Bɛzele sunsum ɛtane ko kɛ, “Melua Gyisɛse ne mɔɔ Pɔɔlo bɔ ɔ nwo nolo la duma nu mese wɔ kɛ ɛvi ɔ nwo tu.”

english_verse: Seven sons of a high priest named Sceva were doing this,
translation_verse: Debie zɛhae, Dwuunli sɛlɛvolɛ kpanyinli bie mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye Siva la amra mrenya nsuu a yɛle a.

english_verse: when an evil spirit said to them, “I know Jesus! And I have heard about Paul. But who are you?”
translation_verse: Na sunsum ɛtane ne zele bɛ kɛ, “Meze Gyisɛse, yɛɛ meze Pɔɔlo, na bɛmɛ noko ɛ?”

english_verse: Then the man with the evil spirit jumped on them and beat them up. They ran out of the house, naked and bruised.
translation_verse: Na sonla ne mɔɔ sunsum ɛtane ne gyi ɔ nwo la dele dɔle bɛ nwo zo na ɔhanle bɛ senle dwɛɛ ɔmanle bɛlɛle bɛ nwo zɔhane bɛnriandile bɛvile sua ne anu bɛhɔle, bɛbodɛboda zɛhae ala.

english_verse: When the Jews and Gentiles in Ephesus heard about this, they were so frightened that they praised the name of the Lord Jesus.
translation_verse: Dwuuma nee bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛnle Dwuuma, mɔɔ wɔ Ɛfɛsɛse la amuala dele mɔɔ zile la; bɛ muala bɛzulole, na ɔmanle bɛlile Awulae Gyisɛse duma ne eni kpole kpalɛ.

english_verse: Many who were followers now started telling everyone about the evil things they had been doing.
translation_verse: Na menli somaa ne ala mɔɔ liele lile la rale bagua nu rahanle ɛtane mɔɔ bɛyɛ bɛvea la amuala.

english_verse: Some who had been practicing witchcraft even brought their books and burned them in public. These books were worth about
translation_verse: Ngonyiama dɔɔnwo ne ala vale bɛ mbuluku mɔɔ bɛfa bɛyɛ bɛ gyima la rale manle bɛyelale bɛ wɔ bagua nu. Bɛsesenle mbuluku ne mɔ awolɛ la, bɛ muala bɛ nloa dole dwɛtɛ fufule apenle ngoko abulanlu.

english_verse: So the Lord's message spread and became even more powerful. The Riot in Ephesus
translation_verse: Na ɔlua zɛhae adenle zo Awulae edwɛkɛ ne dɛlɛle na ɔlile konim dɔɔnwo. Ɛfɛsɛsema di nzaka

english_verse: After all this had happened, Paul decided to visit Macedonia and Achaia on his way to Jerusalem. Paul had said, “From there I will go on to Rome.”
translation_verse: Ɛhye anzi, akee Pɔɔlo yɛle ye adwenle kɛ ɔkɔ Masidonea nee Akaya na yeava lɔ yeahɔ Gyɛlusalɛm, na ɔhanle ɔzɔle zolɛ kɛ, “Saa mevi ɛkɛ a mebahɔ Wulomu noko.”

english_verse: So he sent his two helpers, Timothy and Erastus, to Macedonia. But he stayed on in Asia for a while.
translation_verse: Zɔhane ati ɔmanle ye boavolɛma ne mɔ nwiɔ, Temɔte nee Yilasetɛse lumuale Masidonea, na yemɔ ɔdɛnlanle Ehyea maanzinli ne anu ekyii.

english_verse: At that time there was serious trouble because of the Lord's Way.
translation_verse: Mekɛ ɛhye anu ala Awulae Adenle ne ngilehilelɛ ne ati nzaka zile Ɛfɛsɛse.

english_verse: A silversmith named Demetrius had a business that made silver models of the temple of the goddess Artemis. Those who worked for him earned a lot of money.
translation_verse: Dwɛtɛ dwinvolɛ bie wɔ ɛkɛ, bɛfɛlɛ ye Dimiteleɛse. Ɔfa dwɛtɛ fufule ɔyɛ bozonle raalɛ Aatɛmese ananze ɔtɔne ye. Zɛhae gyima maa dwinvolɛma nyia ezukoa kpalɛ.

english_verse: Demetrius brought together everyone who was in the same business and said: Friends, you know we make a good living at this.
translation_verse: Kenle ko Dimiteleɛse vɛlɛle ɔ gɔnwo dwinvolɛma manle bɛyiale na ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Ayi mɔ, bɛdabɛ bɛze kɛ yɛ ɛkpazilɛ gyi yɛ gyima ye azo.

english_verse: But you have surely seen and heard how this man Paul is upsetting a lot of people, not only in Ephesus, but almost everywhere in Asia. He claims that the gods we humans make are not really gods at all.
translation_verse: Na bɛdabɛ bɛnwu ye yɛɛ eza bɛde nyɛleɛ mɔɔ Pɔɔlo ye ɛlɛyɛ la; asɛɛ yehakyi bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛwɔ Ɛfɛsɛse ɛke, nee Ehyea maanzinli ye anu la amuala adwenle kɛ ananze mɔɔ sonla ɛva ɔ sa ɛyɛ la ɛnle nyamenle fee.

english_verse: Everyone will start saying terrible things about our business. They will stop respecting the temple of the goddess Artemis, who is worshiped in Asia and all over the world. Our great goddess will be forgotten!
translation_verse: Ɛhye kile kɛ yɛ gyima bazɛkye na bozonle raalɛ kpole Aatɛmese ɛzonlenlɛ sua kpole ne adɔ mgbane, mɔɔ ɔnrɛhyɛ biala na ye ɛzonlenlɛ wɔ Ehyea maanzinli ye anu nee ewiade amuala abɔ aze a.”

english_verse: When the workers heard this, they got angry and started shouting, “Great is Artemis, the goddess of the Ephesians!”
translation_verse: Mɔɔ dwinvolɛma ne mɔ dele Dimiteleɛse edwɛkɛ ne la, bɛ muala bɛvale ɛya na bɛdeɛdeanle nuhua kɛ, “Aatɛmese, Ɛfɛsɛsema bozonle raalɛ ne le kpole!”

english_verse: Soon the whole city was in a riot, and some men grabbed Gaius and Aristarchus, who had come from Macedonia with Paul. Then everyone in the crowd rushed to the place where the town meetings were held.
translation_verse: He-e-e ko mɔɔ bɛyɛle la pɛle sua bɔdenle ne. Na nzakama ne mɔ dule twi kokye la ɛnee bɛwɔ Masidoneama nwiɔ, Gayɛse nee Alesetaakɛse mɔɔ nee Pɔɔlo a lua la anwo zo nwee. Bɛhwenle bɛ bɛ nee bɛ hɔle ɛleka mɔɔ ɔyɛ a bɛyia la.

english_verse: Paul wanted to go out and speak to the people, but the Lord's followers would not let him.
translation_verse: Pɔɔlo yɛle kɛ ɔkɔ bagua ne anu yeahɔdendɛ yeahile bɛ, na diedima ne mɔ amkponle ye.

english_verse: A few of the local officials were friendly to Paul, and they sent someone to warn him not to go.
translation_verse: Maanzinli ne anu mgbanyima ne bie mɔ, mɔɔ le Pɔɔlo agɔnwo mɔ la noko zoanle manle bɛhɔzele ye kɛ ɔmmaye ɔ nyunlu wɔ ɛlɔne ne anu.

english_verse: Some of the people in the meeting were shouting one thing, and others were shouting something else. Everyone was completely confused, and most of them did not even know why they were there.
translation_verse: Mekɛ ne anu ɛnee ɛwudolɛ ala a ɛlɔne ne ɛlɛwudo a. Bie mɔ ɛlɛka edwɛkɛ ko la, ɛnee bie mɔ noko ɛlɛka edwɛkɛ fofolɛ, na ayia sua ne anu yɛle wadawada zɛhae ala, ɔluakɛ bie mɔ dɔɔnwo mɔɔ rale ɛkɛ ne la ɛngola ɛnnwu deɛ holɛ ko mɔɔ ɔlua zolɛ bɛrayia la.

english_verse: Several of the Jewish leaders pushed a man named Alexander to the front of the crowd and started telling him what to say. He motioned with his hand and tried to explain what was going on.
translation_verse: Bɛ nuhua bie mɔ dwenlenle kɛ Alɛzanda a di nzakadolɛ ne anwo ɛzonle a, ɔluakɛ Dwuuma bie mɔ mɔɔ wɔ ɛkɛ ne la ɛzuhuzuhu ye dedee bɛmaa yeragyinla ɛlɔne ne anyunlu. Alɛzanda bobole bɛ kɛ bɛyɛ koonwu, na ɔyɛle kɛ ɔtendɛ yeahile bɛ.

english_verse: But when the crowd saw that he was Jewish, they all shouted for two hours, “Great is Artemis, the goddess of the Ephesians!”
translation_verse: Na mɔɔ bɛnwunle kɛ ɔle Dwuunli la, bɛ muala bɛdeɛdeanle nuhua bɛwudole dedee asɛɛ dɔnehwele nwiɔ bɛhanle kɛ, “Aatɛmese, Ɛfɛsɛsema bozonle raalɛ ne le kpole!”

english_verse: Finally, a town official made the crowd be quiet. Then he said: People of Ephesus, who in the world doesn't know that our city is the center for worshiping the great goddess Artemis? Who doesn't know that her image which fell from heaven is right here?
translation_verse: Nzinlii, maanle abɔlɔba ne nleanle manle ɛlɔne ne yɛle koonwu na ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Ɛfɛsɛsema, awie biala ze kɛ suakpole Ɛfɛsɛse a nea bozonle raalɛ kpole Aatɛmese amonle sua ne nee ye dehelɛ bolɛ ne mɔɔ vi anwuma radɔle aze la azo a.

english_verse: No one can deny this, and so you should calm down and not do anything foolish.
translation_verse: Awie biala ɛnzu ɛhye anwo kpolera kɛ yemɔ ɔnze. Yemɔti, bɛha bɛ ahonle bɛgua azule nu, na bɛmmayɛ bɛsɛkye debie.

english_verse: You have brought men in here who have not robbed temples or spoken against our goddess.
translation_verse: Bɛva menli ɛhye mɔ bɛra ɛke wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ bɛtɛwuale bozonle debie yɛɛ bɛtɛkanle munzule edwɛkɛ biala bɛtɛtiale yɛ bozonle raalɛ ne la.

english_verse: If Demetrius and his workers have a case against these men, we have courts and judges. Let them take their complaints there.
translation_verse: Saa Dimiteleɛse nee ɔ gɔnwo mɔ lɛ edwɛkɛ bie tia awie a, kɔɔto wɔ ɛkɛ yɛɛ edwɛkɛdivolɛma ne noko wɔ ɛkɛ mekɛ biala. Bɛkola bɛ nee bɛ kɔ lɔ.

english_verse: But if you want to do more than that, the matter will have to be brought before the city council.
translation_verse: Na saa bɛnea na debie gyɛne bieko wɔ nu mɔɔ yemɔti ɔwɔ kɛ bɛdi ye baguafutu a, ɛnee ɔwɔ kɛ bɛyɛ ye kɛmɔ ngyehyɛlɛ ne kile la.

english_verse: We could easily be accused of starting a riot today. There is no excuse for it! We cannot even give a reason for this uproar.
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ saa yɛannea boɛ a yɛbali ɛzonle wɔ nzakadolɛ ɛhye mɔɔ ɛra ɛnɛ la anwo, ɔboalekɛ mɔɔ bɛlɛyɛ la ɛnlɛ ngilenu biala.”

english_verse: After saying this, he told the people to leave.
translation_verse: Ɔhanle ɛhye la ɔmanle bɛzandele.

english_verse: When the riot was over, Paul sent for the followers and encouraged them. He then told them goodbye and left for Macedonia.
translation_verse: Nzinlii mɔɔ nzakadolɛ ne guale la, Pɔɔlo vɛlɛle ɛdoavolɛma ne na ɔmanle bɛ akɛnrazilɛ, ɔ nee bɛ lile nrɛlaleɛ na ɔhɔle Masidonea.

english_verse: As he traveled from place to place, he encouraged the followers with many messages. Finally, he went to Greece
translation_verse: Ɔvale maanzinli ne mɔ anu na ɔhɔdendɛle ɔzile ɛdoavolɛma ne mɔ ahonle na akee ɔrale Akaya.

english_verse: and stayed there for three months. Paul was about to sail to Syria. But some of the Jewish leaders plotted against him, so he decided to return by way of Macedonia.
translation_verse: Ɔlile siane nsa wɔ Akaya. Na mɔɔ ɔhuohuanle ɔ nwo kɛ ɔkɔ Selea la, ɔnwunle kɛ Dwuuma ne ɛhɔ ɔ ti akpamo. Yemɔti ɛkɛ ne ala ɔyɛle ye adwenle kɛ ɔpe aze yealua Masidonea yeazia.

english_verse: With him were Sopater, son of Pyrrhus from Berea, and Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica. Gaius from Derbe was also with him, and so were Timothy and the two Asians, Tychicus and Trophimus.
translation_verse: Na Sosepatɛ, mɔɔ le Pelɛse ara nrenya ne mɔɔ vi Bɛlia, yɛɛ Alesetaakɛse nee Sɛkɛndɛse, mɔɔ vi Tɛsalonaeka, Gayɛse mɔɔ vi Dɛbi, yɛɛ Temɔte, akee Tekekɛse nee Tulofemɛse mɔɔ vi Ehyea maanzinli nu la nee ye a hɔle a.

english_verse: They went on ahead to Troas and waited for us there.
translation_verse: Menli ɛhye mɔ lumuale yɛ nyunlu hɔhendɛle yɛ wɔ Tulowase.

english_verse: After the Festival of Thin Bread, we sailed from Philippi. Five days later we met them in Troas and stayed there for a week. Paul's Last Visit to Troas
translation_verse: Na mɔɔ Angye Ɛvoyia ne pɛle nu la, yɛvale ɛlɛne yɛvile Felepae; ye kenle nnu ne azo yɛhɔdole bɛ wɔ Tulowase na yɛlile dapɛne ko wɔ ɛkɛ. Pɔɔlo kakpɔla diedima mɔɔ wɔ Tulowase la

english_verse: On the first day of the week we met to break bread together. Paul spoke to the people until midnight because he was leaving the next morning.
translation_verse: Dapɛne ne anu kenle ne mɔɔ lumua la nɔsolɛ nu, yɛyiale nu yɛlile Awulae aleɛ ne, na Pɔɔlo dendɛle hilele diedima ne mɔ, ɔluakɛ ɛnee ye alehyenlɛ nu ɔbahɔ, na ɔhɔle zolɛ ɔdendɛle dedee alevinli mu nwiɔ avinli.

english_verse: In the upstairs room where we were meeting, there were a lot of lamps.
translation_verse: Ahɛnlaneɛ dɔɔnwo wɔ esanwu ne ekpumgbunli ne mɔɔ yɛwɔ nu la anu.

english_verse: A young man by the name of Eutychus was sitting on a window sill. While Paul was speaking, the young man got very sleepy. Finally, he went to sleep and fell three floors all the way down to the ground. When they picked him up, he was dead.
translation_verse: Na kpavolɛ bie mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye Yutekɛse, mɔɔ ɛnee de nvɛnzɛlɛ ne mɔ ko azo la bɔle ngɔsɔkɛ, na nzinlii ɔlafele kpole na ɔvi esanwu nzɛzo nsa ne azo ɔdɔle aze. Bɛhɔmanle ye zo la, ɛnee yewu bɔkɔɔ.

english_verse: Paul went down and bent over Eutychus. He took him in his arms and said, “Don't worry! He's alive.”
translation_verse: Pɔɔlo dwule aze hɔbutule ɔ nwo zo, ɔbɛlale ye na ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛgyakyi mɔɔ bɛlɛyɛ la na ɔtɛwule.”

english_verse: After Paul had gone back upstairs, he broke bread, and ate with us. He then spoke until dawn and left.
translation_verse: Pɔɔlo ziale hɔle esanwu ne azo bieko na ɔhɔlile debie. Nzinlii eza Pɔɔlo dendɛle hilele menli ne toonwo alehyenlɛ, akee ɔhɛlale bɛ na ɔhɔle.

english_verse: Then the followers took the young man home alive and were very happy. The Voyage from Troas to Miletus
translation_verse: Na bɛ nee kpavolɛ ne hɔle sua nu arɛlekyekyelɛ nu mɔɔ ɛnee ɔte kpɔkɛ bɔkɔɔ a. Pɔɔlo vi Tulowase kɔ Maelitɛse

english_verse: Paul decided to travel by land to Assos. The rest of us went on ahead by ship, and we were to take him aboard there.
translation_verse: Na yɛmɛ yɛvale ɛlɛne yɛlumuale Asɔso kɛ yɛkava Pɔɔlo wɔ ɛkɛ; ɔluakɛ ɛnee ɔ nee yɛ ɛhyehyɛ kɛ ɔpe aze yealumua lɔ.

english_verse: When he met us in Assos, he came aboard, and we sailed on to Mitylene.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ ɔ nee yɛ yiale Asɔso la, ɔravole ɛlɛne ne anu na yɛtelele zolɛ yɛhɔle Metelin.

english_verse: The next day we came to a place near Chios, and the following day we reached Samos. The day after that we sailed to Miletus.
translation_verse: Yɛvi ɛkɛ ne la ye alehyenlɛ nu yɛradwule Kayɔso. Aleɛ hyenle bieko la yɛrale Seemɔso, ye alehyenlɛ nu ɛnee yɛwɔ Maelitɛse.

english_verse: Paul had decided to sail on past Ephesus, because he did not want to spend too much time in Asia. He was in a hurry and wanted to be in Jerusalem in time for Pentecost. Paul Says Goodbye to the Church Leaders of Ephesus
translation_verse: Pɔɔlo yɛle ye adwenle kɛ ɔnrɛgyinla Ɛfɛsɛse na ɔpɛ nu yeahɔ, amaa yeanzɛkye mekɛ dɔɔnwo wɔ Ehyea maanle ne anu na ɔ nwo ayɛ ndɛ, amaa saa ɔyɛ na ɔkɛyɛ boɛ a, yeadwu Gyɛlusalɛm wɔ Pɛntekɔso kenle ne. Pɔɔlo nee Ɛfɛsɛse asɔne mgbanyima di nrɛlaleɛ

english_verse: From Miletus, Paul sent a message for the church leaders at Ephesus to come and meet with him.
translation_verse: Pɔɔlo dole Ɛfɛsɛse asɔne mgbanyima ne mɔ nrɛlaleɛ kɛ bɛyia ye wɔ Maelitɛse.

english_verse: When they got there, he said: You know everything I did during the time I was with you when I first came to Asia.
translation_verse: Bɛrale la ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Bɛdabɛ bɛnwu kɛ mezi mebɔ me ɛbɛla, ɔvi kenle mɔɔ membandwule Ehyea maanle ye anu toonwo mɔɔ ɛradwu ɛnɛ la.

english_verse: Some of the Jews plotted against me and caused me a lot of sorrow and trouble. But I served the Lord and was humble.
translation_verse: Wɔ Dwuuma akpamo ne mɔ mɔɔ bɛvale wɔ me ti la amuala anu, mendole me nwo aze menvale monle nee amaneɛnwunlɛ menyɛle me gyima kɛ Awulae akɛlɛ.

english_verse: When I preached in public or taught in your homes, I didn't hold back from telling anything that would help you.
translation_verse: Bɛze kɛ meanva debie biala mɔɔ kɛyɛ moalɛ kɛmaa bɛ la meanvea bɛ, na menzile me ahonle mengilehilele bɛ wɔ bagua nu nee bɛ azua nu.

english_verse: I told Jews and Gentiles to turn to God and have faith in our Lord Jesus.
translation_verse: Mengakyele Dwuuma nee bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛnle Dwuuma la amuala kɛ bɛnlu bɛ nwo wɔ bɛ ɛtane ne mɔ mɔɔ bɛyɛ bɛtia Nyamenle la anwo na bɛlie yɛ Awulae Gyisɛse bɛli.

english_verse: I don't know what will happen to me in Jerusalem, but I must obey God's Spirit and go there.
translation_verse: Kɛkala melɛkɔ Gyɛlusalɛm, kɛmɔ Sunsum ne ɛhile la. Menze mɔɔ bazi me nwo zo wɔ ɛkɛ ne a,

english_verse: In every city I visit, I am told by the Holy Spirit that I will be put in jail and will be in trouble in Jerusalem.
translation_verse: mɔɔ meze la a le kɛ Sunsum Nwuanzanwuanza ne ɛhakye me wɔ sua biala azo kɛ efiadedolɛ nee esiane yɛɛ ɛlɛkendɛ me a.

english_verse: But I don't care what happens to me, as long as I finish the work the Lord Jesus gave me to do. And this work is to tell the good news about God's gift of undeserved grace.
translation_verse: Noko me ngoane ɛdeɛ, mendwenle nwolɛ, amaa meahola meawie Awulae Gyisɛse gyima ne mɔɔ yeva yemaa me kɛ membɔ Edwɛkpa ne mɔɔ fane Nyamenle ɛlolɛ ne anwo la nolo.

english_verse: I have gone from place to place, preaching to you about God's kingdom, but now I know that none of you will ever see me again.
translation_verse: “Mekpɔsa bɛ nwo zo meha Nyamenle Belemgbunlililɛ ne anwo edwɛkɛ mehile bɛ. Kɛkala, bɛ biala ɛnrɛnwu me nyunlu bieko.

english_verse: I tell you today I am no longer responsible for any of you!
translation_verse: Ɛhye ati memaa bɛade ɔ bo wienyi ɛnɛ kenle ye kɛ saa bɛ nuhua biala minli a, menli nwolɛ ɛzonle.

english_verse: I have told you everything God wants you to know.
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ meanva debie biala mɔɔ fane Nyamenle ngyehyɛlɛ ne anwo la meanvea bɛ.

english_verse: Look after yourselves and everyone the Holy Spirit has placed in your care. Be like shepherds to God's church. It is the flock he bought with the blood of his own Son.
translation_verse: Bɛnlea bɛ nwo boɛ na bɛnlea mboane ne mɔ mɔɔ Sunsum Nwuanzanwuanza ne ɛva bɛ ɛwula bɛ sa nu la boɛ. Bɛnlea Nyamenle asɔne ne mɔɔ yeva ɔ Ra ne mogya a yekpondɛ la azo boɛ.

english_verse: I know that after I am gone, others will come like fierce wolves to attack you.
translation_verse: Meze kɛ saa mekɔ a, bɛdi anwo ɛzulolɛ baragua mboane ne mɔ avinli, na bɛnrɛze bɛ anwunvɔne fee.

english_verse: Some of your own people will tell lies to win over the Lord's followers.
translation_verse: Mekɛ bara mɔɔ menli vi bɛ avinli badwazo araha edwɛkɛ adalɛ ahwe diedima ne bie mɔ ahɔli bɛ nzi a.

english_verse: Be on your guard! Remember how day and night for three years I kept warning you with tears in my eyes.
translation_verse: Yemɔti bɛnlea boɛ, na bɛhakye kɛ mendwinle monle ɛvolɛ nsa a mengilehilele bɛ wɔ nɔɔzo nee ewiazo a.

english_verse: I now place you in God's care. Remember the message about his gift of undeserved grace! This message can help you and give you what belongs to you as God's people.
translation_verse: “Kɛkala mefa bɛ mewula Nyamenle nee ye edwɛkɛ ne mɔɔ ɛlolɛ wɔ nu la asa anu. Ɔdo bɛ ngoane nu na ɔva ye nyilalɛ ne mɔɔ yeva yezie ye menli ne ɛkɛ ne la ɔmaa bɛ.

english_verse: I have never wanted anyone's money or clothes.
translation_verse: Me nye ambolo awie biala ezukoa nvutuke, dwɛtɛ fufule anzɛɛ ndanlɛ.

english_verse: You know how I have worked with my own hands to make a living for myself and my friends.
translation_verse: Bɛdabɛ bɛze kɛ medame me sa anloa gyima mɔɔ meyɛ la yɛɛ meva menlea me nwo nee me gɔnwo mɔ a.

english_verse: By everything I did, I showed how you should work to help everyone who is weak. Remember that our Lord Jesus said, “More blessings come from giving than from receiving.”
translation_verse: Mehilehile bɛ wɔ debie biala anu kɛ ɔlua gyima ɛsesebɛ ɛyɛlɛ zo yɛɛ bɛkɛhola bɛkɛboa menli mɔɔ ɛnlɛ anwosesebɛ la a. Bɛhakye Awulae Gyisɛse edwɛkɛ ne mɔɔ ɔhanle la. Ɔse, ‘Nyilalɛ dɔɔnwo wɔ ɛmanlɛ nu tɛla ɛlielɛ.’ ”

english_verse: After Paul had finished speaking, he knelt down with all of them and prayed.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Pɔɔlo wiele la, ɔ nee bɛ bɛ muala bɛhotole na bɛyɛle nzɛlɛlɛ.

english_verse: They were especially sad because Paul had told them, “You will never see me again.” Then they went with him to the ship.
translation_verse: Debie mɔɔ manle bɛ nwo bubule bɛ kpalɛ bɔbɔ la a le ye edwɛkɛ kpɔkɛ ne mɔɔ ɔhanle kɛ bɛnrɛnwu ye bieko la. Na bɛhɔzɔhonle ye wɔ ɛlɛne ne anwo.

english_verse: After saying goodbye, we sailed straight to Cos. The next day we reached Rhodes and from there sailed on to Patara.
translation_verse: Yɛ nee bɛ lile nrɛlaleɛ wiele la yɛvi ɛkɛ ne yɛdule yɛluale zo yɛhɔle Kɔɔso; aleɛ hyenle la ɛnee yɛ nyunlu a le Wulodise. Yɛvi ɛkɛ ne la yɛhɔle Patala.

english_verse: We found a ship going to Phoenicia, so we got on board and sailed off.
translation_verse: Ɛkɛ ne yɛɛ yɛvale ɛlɛne mɔɔ ɛlɛkɔ Fonehyea la yɛhɔle a.

english_verse: We came within sight of Cyprus and then sailed south of it on to the port of Tyre in Syria, where the ship was going to unload its cargo.
translation_verse: Yɛradwule ɛleka bie mɔɔ ɛnee yɛ nye dua Saepelɛse la yɛwɔnenle yɛ ti nyiakɛ yɛpɛle yɛdɔle Selea. Yɛradwule Taya, na kɛmɔ ɛkɛ ne yɛɛ ɛlɛne ne tu ye ninyɛne ne agua la ati, yɛdwule aze yɛhɔle sua zo.

english_verse: But when the week was over, we started on our way again. All the men, together with their wives and children, walked with us from the town to the seashore. We knelt on the beach and prayed.
translation_verse: Noko yɛ mekɛ mɔɔ yɛdi ye bɛ nwo ɛkɛ ne la wiele la, yɛvile ɛkɛ ne na yɛzɔle yɛ adendulɛ ne azo. Bɛ muala bɛ nee bɛ ye mɔ nee bɛ mra bɛhɔzɔhonle yɛ wɔ suakpole ne kandiba, na yɛ muala yɛhotole ɛnwea ne azo yɛyɛle nzɛlɛlɛ.

english_verse: Then after saying goodbye to each other, we got into the ship, and they went back home.
translation_verse: Akee yɛlile nrɛlaleɛ na yɛhɔvole ɛlɛne ne anu, na bɛdabɛ noko bɛziale bɛhɔle sua nu.

english_verse: We sailed from Tyre to Ptolemais, where we greeted the followers and stayed with them for a day.
translation_verse: Yɛzɔle yɛ adendulɛ ne azo, yɛvi Taya yɛhɔle Tɔlɛmeeyese, yɛhɔkpɔlale diedima mɔɔ wɔ ɛkɛ ne la na yɛlale ɛkɛ ne.

english_verse: The next day we went to Caesarea and stayed with Philip, the preacher. He was one of the seven men who helped the apostles,
translation_verse: Ye alehyenlɛ nu yɛvi ɛkɛ ne yɛrale Sizalia. Yɛhɔzokoɛle Felepe mɔɔ kpɔsa bɔ Nyamenle Edwɛkɛ ne nolo la sua nu na yɛ nee ye dɛnlanle. Felepe boka menli nsuu ne mɔɔ bɛkpale nu bɛyele bɛ wɔ Gyɛlusalɛm la anwo.

english_verse: and he had four unmarried daughters who prophesied.
translation_verse: Ɔlɛ mralɛ mraalɛ nna mɔɔ ɛtɛkɔle agyalɛ ɛlɛ la wɔ ɛkɛ, bɛle Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛma.

english_verse: We had been in Caesarea for several days, when the prophet Agabus came to us from Judea.
translation_verse: Yɛlile kenle ekyi ɛkɛ ne la, Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛ bie mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye Agabɛse la vi Dwudiya rale.

english_verse: He took Paul's belt, and with it he tied up his own hands and feet. Then he told us, “The Holy Spirit says that some of the Jewish leaders in Jerusalem will tie up the man who owns this belt. They will also hand him over to the Gentiles.”
translation_verse: Ɔrale yɛ nwo ɛkɛ ne na ɔvale Pɔɔlo akyeso ne ɔkyekyele ɔdaye ɔ ngome ɔ sa nee ɔ gyakɛ na ɔhanle kɛ, “Kɛ Sunsum Nwuanzanwuanza ne se la ɛne: Sonla ne mɔɔ lɛ akyeso ɛhye la, Dwuuma bakyekye ye zɛhae wɔ Gyɛlusalɛm, na bɛava ye bɛawula bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛnle Dwuuma la asa anu.”

english_verse: After Agabus said this, we and the followers living there begged Paul not to go to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Yɛdele ɛhye la, yɛ nee menli mɔɔ wɔ ɛkɛ ne la amuala yɛkpale Pɔɔlo kyɛlɛ kɛ ɔmmakɔ Gyɛlusalɛm.

english_verse: But Paul answered, “Why are you crying and breaking my heart? I am not only willing to be put in jail for the Lord Jesus, but I am even willing to die for him in Jerusalem!”
translation_verse: Na ɔbizale yɛ kɛ, “Na ɛzunlɛ ye abo ɛ? Duzu ati a bɛyɛ bɛabɔ me rɛle ɛ? Meziezie me nwo kɛ tɛ ɛkyekyelɛ mɔɔ bɛkyekye me la angome, na kɛ menwɔwu wɔ Gyɛlusalɛm wɔ Awulae Gyisɛse duma ne ati.”

english_verse: Since we could not get Paul to change his mind, we gave up and prayed, “Lord, please make us willing to do what you want.”
translation_verse: Yɛyɛle biala, na yeamkponle, yemɔti yɛgyakyile ye na yɛzele kɛ, “Awulae ɛhulolɛdeɛ ɛyɛ ɛkɛ.”

english_verse: Then we got ready to go to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Yɛlile mekɛ ekyi wɔ ɛkɛ ne la, yɛhuohuanle yɛ nwo na yɛhɔle Gyɛlusalɛm.

english_verse: Some of the followers from Caesarea went with us and took us to stay in the home of Mnason. He was from Cyprus and had been a follower from the beginning. Paul Visits James
translation_verse: Na ɛdoavolɛma bie mɔɔ wɔ Sizalia la nee yɛ hɔle, na yɛhɔzokoɛle diedinli Meneesen mɔɔ vi Saepelɛse mɔɔ mɔlebɛbo ne ala ɔliele Gyisɛse ɔlile la sua nu. Pɔɔlo kakpɔla Gyemise

english_verse: When we arrived in Jerusalem, the Lord's followers gladly welcomed us.
translation_verse: Yɛradwule Gyɛlusalɛm la, mediema diedima ne mɔ liele yɛ anyelielɛ nu.

english_verse: Paul went with us to see James the next day, and all the church leaders were present.
translation_verse: Aleɛ hyenle la Pɔɔlo nee yɛ hɔle Gyemise ɛkɛ ne kɛ yɛ nee ye kadendɛ; yɛhɔle la ɛnee asɔne mgbanyima ne mɔ amuala wɔ ɛkɛ.

english_verse: Paul greeted them and told how God had used him to help the Gentiles.
translation_verse: Pɔɔlo bizale ahye na ɔhanle gyima mɔɔ Nyamenle ɛlua ɔ nwo zo ɛli wɔ bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛnle Dwuuma la avinli la amuala ɔhilele bɛ.

english_verse: Everyone who heard this praised God and said to Paul: My friend, you can see how many tens of thousands of our people have become followers! And all of them are eager to obey the Law of Moses.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ bɛdiele ye bɛwiele la, bɛyɛle Nyamenle mo na bɛzele Pɔɔlo kɛ, “Adiema Pɔɔlo, tie yɛ ɛ! Yɛlɛ Dwuuma apenle apenle mɔɔ ɛlie Edwɛkpa ne ɛli, noko bɛli Mosisi mɛla ne anzi kpalɛ kpalɛ a.

english_verse: But they have been told that you are teaching those who live among the Gentiles to disobey this Law. They claim that you are telling them not to circumcise their sons or to follow our customs.
translation_verse: Bɛha bɛhile bɛ kɛ ɛlɛkilehile Dwuuma mɔɔ wɔ maanle zo la kɛ bɛgyakyi Mosisi mɛla ne anzi ɛlilɛ, na wɔze bɛ kɛ bɛmmayɛ bɛ mrenyanu nzonlɛ anzɛɛ bɛmmadi Dwuuma maamɛla ne mɔ azo.

english_verse: What should we do now that our people have heard you are here?
translation_verse: Kɛ ɔkɛyɛ biala la bɛbade kɛ wɔra. Zɔhane ati ɛnee kɛ yɛkɛyɛ ye ɛ?

english_verse: Please do what we ask, because four of our men have made special promises to God.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ yɛkpondɛ kɛ ɛyɛ la ɛne. Yɛlɛ mgbavolɛ nna mɔɔ ɛbɔ ɛwɔkɛ wɔ Nyamenle anyunlu la wɔ ɛke.

english_verse: Join with them and prepare yourself for the ceremony that goes with the promises. Pay the cost for their heads to be shaved. Then everyone will learn that the reports about you are not true. They will know you do obey the Law of Moses.
translation_verse: Ɛ nee bɛ ɛhɔ maa bɛhɔkpa bɛ ti, bɛdu bɛ nwo evinli na tua bɛ ti kakɛ biala maa bɛ. Ɛhye a kɛmaa awie biala kɛnwu kɛ edwɛkɛ mɔɔ bɛhanle wɔ ɛ nwo la amuala ɛnle nɔhalɛ a, na ɛdawɔ mumua ne, ɛdi Dwuu maamɛla ne nee Mosisi mɛla ne mɔ azo.

english_verse: Some while ago we told the Gentile followers what we think they should do. We instructed them not to eat anything offered to idols. They were told not to eat any meat with blood still in it or the meat of an animal that has been strangled. They were also told not to commit any terrible sexual sins.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ fane bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛnle Dwuuma, na bɛlie bɛli la anwo, yɛhɛlɛ kɛlata yɛhɔmaa bɛ kɛ bɛmmadi debie biala mɔɔ bɛva bɛkpa munzule bɛmaa bozonle nee nane mɔɔ bɛlofo ye bɛhu ye la; eza bɛmmadi mogya, na bɛhwe bɛ nwo bɛvi adwɔmane ɛbɔlɛ nwo.”

english_verse: The next day Paul took the four men with him and got himself ready at the same time they did. Then he went into the temple and told when the final ceremony would take place and when an offering would be made for each of them. Paul Is Arrested
translation_verse: Yemɔti Pɔɔlo vale menli ne, na aleɛ hyenle la ɔ nee bɛ hɔle bɛhɔnluanle bɛ nwo. Akee ɔhɔle Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu ɔhɔhilele kenle mɔɔ evinli ɛdulɛ ne kɛwie na bɛabɔ awie ko biala ati azu ne la. Bɛhye Pɔɔlo wɔ Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu

english_verse: When the period of seven days for the ceremony was almost over, some of the Jewish people from Asia saw Paul in the temple. They got a large crowd together and started attacking him.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ ɔka ekyii na kenle nsuu ne adwu la, Dwuuma bie mɔɔ vi Ehyea maanle nu rale la nwunle Pɔɔlo wɔ Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu. Bɛzɛkyele menli dɔɔnwo adwenle wɔ Pɔɔlo anwo na bɛmanle bɛhɔnwinwinle ye wɔ Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu,

english_verse: They were shouting, “Friends, help us! This man goes around everywhere, saying bad things about our nation and about the Law of Moses and about this temple. He has even brought shame to this holy temple by bringing in Gentiles.”
translation_verse: bɛdeɛdeanle nu kɛ, “Yizilayɛma e, bɛrɛla o na sonla ne mɔɔ luolua nuhua ɛlɛkilehile menli atia Yizilayɛma nee Mosisi mɛla ne nee Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ye la, yemɔ ɛne! Eza noko yehɔva menli bie mɔɔ ɛnle Dwuuma la yera Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ye anu yemaa evinli ɛha ɛleka nwuanzanwuanza ɛhye.”

english_verse: The whole city was in an uproar, and the people turned into a mob. They grabbed Paul and dragged him out of the temple. Then suddenly the doors were shut.
translation_verse: Suakpole ne azo fonyianle, na menli ne mɔ razɔle Pɔɔlo hwenle ye vile Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu vindele, na ɛkɛ ne ala bɛtotole Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne nlenkɛ ne mɔ amuala anu.

english_verse: The people were about to kill Paul when the Roman army commander heard that all Jerusalem was starting to riot.
translation_verse: Menli ne mɔ akee nyianle adwenle kɛ bɛku Pɔɔlo. Na nrɛlaleɛ hɔdole Wulomu sogyama kpanyinli ne kɛ nzaka ɛzi Gyɛlusalɛm.

english_verse: So he quickly took some soldiers and officers and ran to where the crowd had gathered. As soon as the mob saw the commander and soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
translation_verse: Yemɔti sogyama kpanyinli ne vale ye sogya mgbanyinli ne bie mɔ nee sogyama hanle bɛ nwo waa hɔle ɛlɔne ne anu. Mɔɔ menli ne mɔ nwunle sogyama kpanyinli ne nee sogyama mɔɔ doa ye la, bɛgyakyile Pɔɔlo ɛbolɛ.

english_verse: The army commander went over and arrested him and had him bound with two chains. Then he tried to find out who Paul was and what he had done.
translation_verse: Sogyama kpanyinli ne hɔzɔle Pɔɔlo, na ɔmanle bɛvale nwɔnzɔnwɔnzɔ nwiɔ bɛguale ye. Akee ɔbizale kɛ, “Na nwane a le ɛhye, yɛɛ duzu ɛtane a yeyɛ a?”

english_verse: Part of the crowd shouted one thing, and part of them shouted something else. But they were making so much noise that the commander could not find out a thing. Then he ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress.
translation_verse: Na menli ne mɔ annwu mɔɔ bɛka a. Bie mɔ ɛlɛka edwɛkɛ ɛhye la, ɛnee bie mɔ noko ɛlɛka edwɛkɛ ngakyile. Yemɔti ɛnee sogyama kpanyinli ne ɛngola ɛnnwu edwɛkɛ kpɔkɛ mɔɔ ɛmaa ɛhye ɛzi la. Yemɔti ɔzele bɛ kɛ bɛva Pɔɔlo bɛhɔ aranemgbole ne anu lɔ.

english_verse: As they reached the steps, the crowd became so wild that the soldiers had to lift Paul up and carry him.
translation_verse: Bɛ nee ye hɔle hɔdwule aranemgbole ne kpolike ne anloa la, ɛnee akee ɔwɔ kɛ sogyama ne soa ye bɛ kɔme zo na bɛava ye bɛahɔ, ɔluakɛ ɛnee akee menli ne mɔ anye ɛbolo kpalɛ.

english_verse: The crowd followed and kept shouting, “Kill him! Kill him!” Paul Speaks to the Crowd
translation_verse: Bɛ muala bɛdoale bɛ ndinlizo na bɛdeɛdeanle nuhua kɛ, “Bɛhu ye bɛye ye ɛkɛ ne!” Pɔɔlo sa ɔ ne

english_verse: When Paul was about to be taken into the fortress, he asked the commander, “Can I say something to you?” “How do you know Greek?” the commander asked.
translation_verse: Bɛ nee Pɔɔlo kɔ ahɔwolo aranemgbole ne anu la, ɔzele sogyama kpanyinli ne kɛ, “Maa me adenle maa menga edwɛkɛ mengile wɔ.” Na sogyama kpanyinli ne zele kɛ, “Hwio, ɛdawɔ mumua ne ɛka Giliki.

english_verse: “No!” Paul replied. “I am a Jew from Tarsus, an important city in Cilicia. Please let me speak to the crowd.”
translation_verse: Pɔɔlo buale ye kɛ, “Mele Dwuunli. Bɛwole me wɔ Taasɛse mɔɔ wɔ Selesea la. Mevi suakpole kpalɛ zo. Mekpa wɔ kyɛlɛ, maa mendendɛ ekyii mengile menli ne mɔ.”

english_verse: The commander told him he could speak, so Paul stood on the steps and motioned to the people. When they were quiet, he spoke to them in Aramaic:
translation_verse: Na sogyama kpanyinli ne manle ye adenle kɛ ɔdendɛ. Na Pɔɔlo gyinlanle kpolike ne azo, ɔmanle ɔ sa zo ɔbobole menli ne. Mɔɔ bɛ muala bɛyɛle koonwu kpalɛ la, Pɔɔlo dendɛle Hibulu aneɛ nu hilele bɛ zele kɛ,

english_verse: When the crowd heard Paul speak to them in Aramaic, they became even quieter. Then Paul said:
translation_verse: Mɔɔ bɛdele kɛ ɔlɛtendɛ yeahile bɛ wɔ Hibulu aneɛ nu la, bɛ muala akee bɛyɛle koonwu. Na Pɔɔlo hɔle zolɛ hanle kɛ,

english_verse: I am a Jew, born in the city of Tarsus in Cilicia. But I grew up here in Jerusalem where I was a student of Gamaliel and was taught to follow every single law of our ancestors. In fact, I was just as eager to obey God as any of you are today.
translation_verse: “Mele Dwuunli, bɛwole me wɔ Taasɛse mɔɔ wɔ Selesea maanle nu la. Bɛtetele me wɔ Gyɛlusalɛm ɛke wɔ nwomanli Gameeleɛle sukulu ne anu. Menzukoale yɛ nlenya mɔ mɛla ne nee amaamuo ne kpalɛ, na mendule me nwo memanle Nyamenle, kɛmɔ kɛkala bɛde la.

english_verse: I made trouble for everyone who followed the Lord's Way, and I even had some of them killed. I had others arrested and put in jail. I didn't care if they were men or women.
translation_verse: Mengyele menli mɔɔ lua Adenle ɛhye azo la dɔɔnwo, mraalɛ nee mrenya, memanle bɛguale bɛ efiade na bɛhunle bɛ.

english_verse: The high priest and all the council members can tell you this is true. They even gave me letters to the Jewish leaders in Damascus, so that I could arrest people there and bring them to Jerusalem to be punished.
translation_verse: Sɛlɛvolɛ Kpanyinli ne nee ayia mgbanyima ne mɔ amuala di daselɛ kɛ mɔɔ melɛka la le nɔhalɛ. Menliele ngɛlata wɔ bɛ lɔ kɛ melɛ mekamaa mediema Dwuuma mɔɔ wɔ Dɛmasekɛse la. Na menzile nu kɛ mekahye menli ɛhye mɔ meagua bɛ anga na meava bɛ meara Gyɛlusalɛm, amaa bɛadea bɛ, kɛmɔ ɔfɛta la. Pɔɔlo ka kɛ ɔzile ɔrayɛle diedinli la (Gyi

english_verse: One day about noon I was getting close to Damascus, when a bright light from heaven suddenly flashed around me.
translation_verse: “Mɔɔ melua adenle zo melɛkɔ na ɔka ekyii medwu Dɛmasekɛse la, kɛyɛ sɛnzɛngyinla mekɛ nu, arɛlevilɛ nu ala wienyi kpole bie vi anwuma dale bɛnrale yiale me.

english_verse: I fell to the ground and heard a voice asking, “Saul, Saul, why are you so cruel to me?”
translation_verse: Mempɛle menfinle na mendele kɛ ɛnelɛ bie se, ‘Sɔɔlo, Sɔɔlo! Duzu ati a ɛyɛ me kpɔdekpɔde zɛhae ɛ?’

english_verse: “Who are you?” I answered. The Lord replied, “I am Jesus from Nazareth! I am the one you are so cruel to.”
translation_verse: Na membizale kɛ, ‘Awulae, ɛdawɔ nwane ɔ?’ Na ɔzele me kɛ, ‘Medame a mele Gyisɛse mɔɔ vi Nazalɛte, mɔɔ wɔdu ɛ nye wɔzie me nyunlu ɛlɛyɛ me kpɔdekpɔde la.’

english_verse: Those who were traveling with me saw the light, but did not hear the voice.
translation_verse: Menli mɔɔ nee me lua la nwunle wienyi ne, na bɛande ɛnelɛ ne mɔɔ dendɛle hilele me la.

english_verse: I asked, “Lord, what do you want me to do?” Then he told me, “Get up and go to Damascus. When you get there, you will be told what to do.”
translation_verse: Na membizale kɛ, ‘Awulae, duzu a menyɛ a?’ Na Awulae zele me kɛ, ‘Dwazo na kɔ Dɛmasekɛse, na ɛkɛ ne yɛɛ bɛbaha debie mɔɔ Nyamenle ɛhyehyɛ kɛ ɔmaa wɔayɛ la bɛahile wɔ a.’

english_verse: The light had been so bright that I couldn't see. And the others had to lead me by the hand to Damascus.
translation_verse: Wienyi ne kɛ zile dale la manle me nye zinle. Ɛhye ati me gɔnwo mɔ mɔɔ nee me lua la sosɔle me sa vale me hɔle Dɛmasekɛse.

english_verse: In that city there was a man named Ananias, who faithfully obeyed the Law of Moses and was well liked by all the Jewish people living there.
translation_verse: “Nrenya bie wɔ Dɛmasekɛse ɛkɛ, bɛfɛlɛ ye Ananayase, ɔdi mɛla ne azo kpalɛ, yɛɛ Dwuuma mɔɔ wɔ Dɛmasekɛse la amuala bu ye.

english_verse: He came to me and said, “Saul, my friend, you can now see again!” At once I could see.
translation_verse: Ɔrale ɛleka mɔɔ mewɔ la, ɔragyinlanle me nwo ɛkɛ na ɔzele me kɛ, ‘Adiema Sɔɔlo, nwu debie bieko.’ Na ɛkɛ ne ala me nye zo dele na menwunle debie bieko na meneanle ɔ nyunlu.

english_verse: Then Ananias told me, “The God that our ancestors worshiped has chosen you to know what he wants done. He has chosen you to see the One Who Obeys God and to hear his voice.
translation_verse: Na ɔhanle kɛ, ‘Yɛ nlenya mɔ Nyamenle ne ɛye wɔ ɛzie ɛkɛ kɛ ɛnwu ye ɛhulolɛdeɛ na ɛnwu ye Fɔɔnwonli sonvolɛ ko ne, na ɛde ɔ ne.

english_verse: You must tell everyone what you have seen and heard.
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ ɛbali ɔ nwo daselɛ wɔaha mɔɔ wɔde nee mɔɔ wɔnwu ye la wɔahile ewiade amra amuala.

english_verse: What are you waiting for? Get up! Be baptized, and wash away your sins by praying to the Lord.”
translation_verse: Na duzu ati a akee ɛlɛkendɛ bieko ɛ? Dwazo na sɛlɛ maa bɛzɔne wɔ bɛnrinzi wɔ ɛtane ne mɔ bɛgua.’ Ɔwɔ kɛ Pɔɔlo bɔ Edwɛkpa ne nolo kile bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛnle Dwuuma la

english_verse: After this I returned to Jerusalem and went to the temple to pray. There I had a vision
translation_verse: “Menziale mengɔle Gyɛlusalɛm na mɔɔ mewɔ Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu melɛyɛ nzɛlɛlɛ la, me nye hɔle dɔɔnwo,

english_verse: of the Lord who said to me, “Hurry and leave Jerusalem! The people won't listen to what you say about me.”
translation_verse: na menwunle Awulae kɛ ɔlɛtendɛ yeaze me kɛ, ‘Maa ɛ nwo ɛyɛ ndɛ fi Gyɛlusalɛm. Ɔluakɛ menli mɔɔ wɔ ɛke la ɛnrɛdie daselɛ ne mɔɔ ɛlɛdi ye me nwo la.’

english_verse: I replied, “Lord, they know that in many of our synagogues I arrested and beat people who had faith in you.
translation_verse: Na menganle kɛ, ‘Awulae, bɛdabɛ bɛze ye wienyi kɛ medame a anrɛɛ ɛnee mekye menli mɔɔ die wɔ di la, mebo bɛ, metwenle bɛ aze wɔ nyianu azua ne mɔ anu a.

english_verse: Stephen was killed because he spoke for you, and I stood there and cheered them on. I even guarded the clothes of the men who murdered him.”
translation_verse: Mekɛ mɔɔ bɛku wɔ dasevolɛ Sitivin la, ɛnee medame mewɔ ɛkɛ, me kunlu dwole ye ɛhunlɛ nwo na menliele menli mɔɔ hunle ye la ndanlɛ menlɛle bɛ.’

english_verse: But the Lord told me to go, and he promised to send me far away to the Gentiles.
translation_verse: Na Awulae zele me kɛ, ‘Kɔ, mesoa wɔ wɔ maanle zo moa moa wɔ menli mɔɔ ɛnle Dwuuma la avinli.’ ”

english_verse: The crowd listened until Paul said this. Then they started shouting, “Get rid of this man! He doesn't deserve to live.”
translation_verse: Menli ne mɔ diele Pɔɔlo toonwo na mɔɔ ɔhanle edwɛkɛ kpɔkɛ ɛhye la bɛ muala bɛ ahonle futule na bɛdeɛdeanle nu kɛ, “Bɛye ye wɔ ɛkɛ ne! Bɛhu ye! Ɔle musuofoɔ!”

english_verse: They kept shouting. They waved their clothes around and threw dust into the air. Paul and the Roman Army Commander
translation_verse: Bɛtea la ɛnee bɛlɛfuandivuandi bɛ ndanlɛ anwuma, na bɛfula anwea bɛsande ye anwomanyunlu, kɛ bɛndie edwɛkɛ biala.

english_verse: The Roman commander ordered Paul to be taken into the fortress and beaten with a whip. He did this to find out why the people were screaming at Paul.
translation_verse: Zɔhane ati Wulomu sogyama kpanyinli ne zele ye menli ne mɔ kɛ bɛva Pɔɔlo bɛwolo aranemgbole ne anu, na bɛbila ye empele bɛmaa ɔha deɛ holɛ ko mɔɔ ɔlua zo a Dwuuma doa ye ɛlɛwudo la.

english_verse: While the soldiers were tying Paul up to be beaten, he asked the officer standing there, “Is it legal to beat a Roman citizen before he has been tried in court?”
translation_verse: Na mɔɔ bɛkyekyele ye kɛ bɛbila ye empele ne la, Pɔɔlo bizale sogya kpanyinli ko mɔɔ gyi ɔ nwo ɛkɛ ne la kɛ, “Asoo ɔfa mɛla adenle zo kɛ bɛkɛbo Wulomunli mgbane wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ bɛtɛdile ye edwɛkɛ bɛtɛbuale ye fɔlɛ kɛ yedo mɛla la ɔ?”

english_verse: When the officer heard this, he went to the commander and said, “What are you doing? This man is a Roman citizen!”
translation_verse: Sogya kpanyinli ne dele ɛhye la, ɔhɔle sogyama kpanyinli ne ɛkɛ ne na ɔhɔbizale ye kɛ, “Duzu debie a ɛlɛyɛ la? Nea, sonla ne le Wulomunli.”

english_verse: The commander went to Paul and asked, “Tell me, are you a Roman citizen?” “Yes,” Paul answered.
translation_verse: Na sogyama kpanyinli ne rale Pɔɔlo anwo ɛkɛ rabizale ye kɛ, “Na ɛle Wulomunli ɔ?” Pɔɔlo buale ye kɛ, “Ɛhɛe.”

english_verse: The commander then said, “I paid a lot of money to become a Roman citizen.” But Paul replied, “I was born a Roman citizen.”
translation_verse: Na sogyama kpanyinli ne zele ye kɛ, “Mame, menduale ezukoa kpole kpalɛ yɛɛ menyianle zɔhane gyinlabelɛ a.” Pɔɔlo buale ye kɛ, “Mame, bɛwole me Wulomunli.”

english_verse: The men who were about to beat and question Paul quickly backed off. And the commander himself was frightened when he realized that he had put a Roman citizen in chains. Paul Is Tried by the Council
translation_verse: Na ɛkɛ ne ala menli mɔɔ rale kɛ bɛbabizebiza Pɔɔlo edwɛkɛ la vi ɔ nwo ɛkɛ hwenle bɛ nwo. Mɔɔ sogyama kpanyinli ne nwunle kɛ Pɔɔlo le Wulomunli na yegua ye nwɔnzɔnwɔnzɔ la ye ahonle dule. Pɔɔlo gyi ayia ne anyunlu

english_verse: The next day the commander wanted to know the real reason why the Jewish leaders had brought charges against Paul. So he had Paul's chains removed, and he ordered the chief priests and the whole council to meet. Then he had Paul led in and made him stand in front of them.
translation_verse: Ɛnee sogyama kpanyinli ne kpondɛ kɛ ɔnwu deɛ holɛ ko mɔɔ yemɔti Dwuuma ne ɛlɛto Pɔɔlo ɛzonle la ati, aleɛ hyenle la ɔmanle bɛyele Pɔɔlo nwɔnzɔnwɔnzɔ ne na ɔmanle sɛlɛvolɛ mgbanyinli ne nee ayiama ne mɔ amuala yiale na ɔvale Pɔɔlo ɔragyinlanle bɛ nyunlu ɛkɛ.

english_verse: Paul looked straight at the council members and said, “My friends, to this day I have served God with a clear conscience!”
translation_verse: Pɔɔlo nleanle bagua ne na ɔzele bɛ kɛ, “Mediema Yizilayɛma, me adwenle ɛmbu me fɔlɛ wɔ me ɛbɛlabɔlɛ nu wɔ Nyamenle anyunlu toonwo a yeradwu ɛnɛ a.”

english_verse: Then Ananias the high priest ordered the men standing beside Paul to hit him on the mouth.
translation_verse: Sɛlɛvolɛ Kpanyinli Ananayase dele ɛhye la ɔhanle kɛ bɛbɔ ɔ nloa ne azo.

english_verse: Paul turned to the high priest and said, “You whitewashed wall! God will hit you. You sit there to judge me by the Law of Moses. But at the same time you order men to break the Law by hitting me.”
translation_verse: Pɔɔlo zele ye kɛ, “Ɛ kunlu le bile, Nyamenle babɔ wɔ bie adua, kɛ ɛde ɛkɛ ne kɛ ɛfa mɛla wɔali me edwɛkɛ, noko wɔbulu mɛla ne azo ɛse bɛbɔ me la.”

english_verse: The men standing beside Paul asked, “Don't you know you are insulting God's high priest?”
translation_verse: Menli mɔɔ gyi Pɔɔlo anwo ɛkɛ ne la zele ye kɛ, “Hɛe, ɛyɛ Nyamenle Sɛlɛvolɛ Kpanyinli ne aholoba ɔ?”

english_verse: Paul replied, “Oh! I didn't know he was the high priest. The Scriptures do tell us not to speak evil about a leader of our people.”
translation_verse: Pɔɔlo buale bɛ kɛ, “Mediema Yizilayɛma, menze kɛ ɔle Sɛlɛvolɛ Kpanyinli. Nyamenle Edwɛkɛ ne se, ‘Mmaka wɔ kpanyinli mɔɔ nea wɔ menli nwo zo la anwo edwɛkɛ ɛtane.’ ”

english_verse: When Paul saw that some of the council members were Sadducees and others were Pharisees, he shouted, “My friends, I am a Pharisee and the son of a Pharisee. I am on trial simply because I believe that the dead will be raised to life.”
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Pɔɔlo nwunle kɛ menli mɔɔ ɛrayia la bie mɔ boka Sadusiima fane ne anwo na foa ko dɔɔnwo noko boka Falasiima fane ne anwo la, ɔdeanle nu ɔzele kɛ, “Mediema Yizilayɛma! Mele Falasiinli, yɛɛ Falasiinli a wole me a. Bɛ nee me ɛra ɛke kɛ bɛbali me edwɛkɛ, ɔboalekɛ melɛ anyelazo kɛ bɛbadwazo mɔwuamra bɛara ngoane nu bieko.”

english_verse: As soon as Paul said this, the Pharisees and the Sadducees got into a big argument, and the council members started taking sides.
translation_verse: Ɔhanle ɛhye ala la, Falasiima ne nee Sadusiima ne mɔ bɔle ɔ bo kɛ bɛdi butule, na ɛlɔne ne lile abunwiɔ.

english_verse: and so there was a lot of shouting. Some of the teachers of the Law of Moses were Pharisees. Finally, they became angry and said, “We don't find anything wrong with this man. Maybe a spirit or an angel really did speak to him.”
translation_verse: Bɛdeanle kpalɛ, na mɛla kilehilevolɛma bie mɔ mɔɔ boka Falasiima fane ne anwo la dwazole hanle kɛ, “Yɛnnwu ɛtane biala wɔ sonla ne anwo! Ɔkɛyɛ zɔhane kɛ Nyamenle soanvolɛ bie anzɛɛ sunsum bie ɛdendɛ ɛhile ye amgba.”

english_verse: The argument became fierce, and the commander was afraid that Paul would be pulled apart. So he ordered the soldiers to go in and rescue Paul. Then they took him back into the fortress.
translation_verse: Nzinlii akee ɛdeanlɛ ne bole zolɛ na sogyama kpanyinli ne zulole kɛ bɛkɛhu Pɔɔlo la ati, ɔmanle sogyama ne mɔ dwule aze hɔle bagua ne anu hɔyele Pɔɔlo wɔ ayiama ne avinli bɛ nee ye hɔle aranemgbole ne anu bieko.

english_verse: That night the Lord stood beside Paul and said, “Don't worry! Just as you have told others about me in Jerusalem, you must also tell about me in Rome.” A Plot To Kill Paul
translation_verse: Kenle ko ne nɔe ne, Awulae ragyinlanle Pɔɔlo anwo ɛkɛ ne na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Gyinla kpundii! Wɔli me nwo daselɛ bɔkɔɔ wɔ Gyɛlusalɛm ɛke, na ɔwɔ kɛ ɛyɛ ye zɔhane noko wɔ Wulomu.” Bɛkɔ Pɔɔlo ati akpamo

english_verse: The next morning more than
translation_verse: Bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛvale adwenle ɛhye la bo abulanla.

english_verse: Then some of them went to the chief priests and the nation's leaders and said, “We have promised God that we would not eat a thing until we have killed Paul.
translation_verse: Na bɛhɔle Sɛlɛvolɛ Kpanyinli ne nee mgbanyima ne mɔ ɛkɛ, na bɛzele bɛ kɛ, “Yɛli amonle kɛ yɛnrɛli aleɛ yɛɛ yɛnrɛnlo nzule kyesɛ yɛku Pɔɔlo kolaa.

english_verse: You and everyone in the council must go to the commander and pretend that you want to find out more about the charges against Paul. Ask for him to be brought before your court. Meanwhile, we will be waiting to kill him before he gets there.”
translation_verse: Yemɔti, bɛ nee ayiama ne ɛbɔ nu na bɛzoa bɛmaa bɛhɔze Wulomu sogyama kpanyinli ne kɛ ɔmaa bɛva Pɔɔlo bɛrɛla na bɛkpondɛ kɛ bɛbizebiza ye edwɛkɛ ne anu kpalɛ. Na kɛ ɔkɛyɛ biala la toonwo mɔɔ ɔkadwu ɛke la ɛnee yɛhu ye.”

english_verse: When Paul's nephew heard about the plot, he went to the fortress and told Paul about it.
translation_verse: Pɔɔlo awozoa nrenya ne dele ɛhye anwo bie. Zɔhane ati ɔhɔle aranemgbole ne anu ɔhɔfetele zolɛ ɔhilele Pɔɔlo.

english_verse: So Paul said to one of the army officers, “Take this young man to the commander. He has something to tell him.”
translation_verse: Na Pɔɔlo vɛlɛle sogya kpanyinli ko na ɔzele ye kɛ, “Fa kpavolɛ ye kɔ sogyama kpanyinli ne ɛkɛ na ɔlɛ edwɛkɛ ɔka yeahile ye.”

english_verse: The officer took him to the commander and said, “The prisoner named Paul asked me to bring this young man to you, because he has something to tell you.”
translation_verse: Sogya ne vale kpavolɛ ne hɔle bɛ kpanyinli ne ɛkɛ ne na ɔzele kɛ, “Pilizanli Pɔɔlo vɛlɛle me na ɔzele me kɛ menva kpavolɛ ye membɛlɛ wɔ na ɔlɛ edwɛkɛ ɔka yeahile wɔ.”

english_verse: The commander took the young man aside and asked him in private, “What do you want to tell me?”
translation_verse: Na sogyama kpanyinli ne zɔle kpavolɛ ne asa, ɔvale ye ɔhɔle ahane, na ɔbizale ye kɛ, “Duzu edwɛkɛ a ɛ nee ye rale a?”

english_verse: He answered, “Some men are planning to ask you to bring Paul down to the Jewish council tomorrow. They will claim they want to find out more about him.
translation_verse: Kpavolɛ ne zele ye kɛ, “Dwuu mgbanyima ne ɛli bɛ nloa kɛ ɛhyema bɛbaraha bɛahile wɔ kɛ ɛva Pɔɔlo ɛrɛla bagua ne anyunlu ɛmaa bɛdie ye edwɛkɛ ne kpalɛ.

english_verse: The commander sent the young man away after saying to him, “Don't let anyone know you told me this.” Paul Is Sent to Felix the Governor
translation_verse: Na sogyama kpanyinli ne zele ye kɛ, “Mede. Mmabɔ zolɛ ɛkile awie biala kɛ wɔraha ɛhye wɔhile me.” Na ɔmanle ɔhɔle. Bɛva Pɔɔlo bɛhɔmaa Amɛnlado Filekese

english_verse: Get a horse ready for Paul and make sure he gets safely through to Felix the governor.”
translation_verse: Bɛziezie ɛkpɔnwɔ ko noko bɛmaa Pɔɔlo ɛdɛnla zolɛ na bɛva ye gyɛlɛɛnye bɛhɔmaa amɛnlado Filekese.”

english_verse: The commander wrote a letter that said:
translation_verse: Na sogyama kpanyinli ne hɛlɛle kɛlata ɛhye manle bɛhɔle:

english_verse: Greetings from Claudius Lysias to the Honorable Governor Felix:
translation_verse: “Medame Kolɔdeɛse Lesease a melɛkɛlɛ kɛlata ɛhye mearɛlɛ Amɛnlado Filekese a, mebiza wɔ ahye.

english_verse: Some Jews grabbed this man and were about to kill him. But when I found out that he was a Roman citizen, I took some soldiers and rescued him.
translation_verse: Dwuuma zɔle nrenya ɛhye nu mɔɔ anrɛɛ bɛku ye a. Na mendele kɛ ɔle Wulomunli la ati menvale sogyama mengɔnliele ye.

english_verse: I wanted to find out what they had against him. So I brought him before their council
translation_verse: Memkpondɛle kɛ menwɔnwu ye nvoleɛ, yemɔti menvale ye mengɔle bɛ ayia ne anyunlu kɛ mekadie nu kpalɛ.

english_verse: and learned that the charges concern only their religious laws. This man isn't guilty of anything for which he should die or even be put in jail.
translation_verse: Na menwunle kɛ ɔtɛyɛle debie mɔɔ fɛta ɛhunlɛ anzɛɛ efiade ɛdolɛ bɔbɔ a. Bɛ ɛzonledonlɛ ne fane bɛdabɛ bɛ mɛla nwo.

english_verse: As soon as I learned that there was a plot against him, I sent him to you and told their leaders to bring charges against him in your court.
translation_verse: Eza mede kɛ bɛvua kɛ bɛnyia ye a bɛkɛhu ye, yemɔti meyɛ kɛ bɛva ye bɛrɛlɛ wɔ. Meze menli mɔɔ donle ye ɛzonle la noko kɛ bɛva bɛ edwɛkɛ ne bɛrado ɛ nyunlu.”

english_verse: The soldiers obeyed the commander's orders, and that same night they took Paul to the city of Antipatris.
translation_verse: Sogyama ne yɛle bɛ gyima ne kɛmɔ bɛhilele bɛ la na nɔe ne ala bɛvale Pɔɔlo bɛ nee ye hɔle toonwo bɛhɔdwule Antepatelese.

english_verse: The next day the foot soldiers returned to the fortress and let the soldiers on horseback take him the rest of the way.
translation_verse: Aleɛ hyenle la sogyama ne mɔɔ dua aze la ziale rale aranemgbole ne anu na sogyama ne mɔɔ tɛnla ɛkpɔnwɔ zo la vale Pɔɔlo hɔle.

english_verse: When they came to Caesarea, they gave the letter to the governor and handed Paul over to him.
translation_verse: Bɛ nee ye hɔdwule Sizalia la bɛyele kɛlata ne bɛmanle amɛnlado ne na bɛvale Pɔɔlo noko bɛwulale ɔ sa nu.

english_verse: The governor read the letter. Then he asked Paul and found out that he was from Cilicia.
translation_verse: Amɛnlado ne gengale kɛlata ne wiele la, ɔbizale Pɔɔlo maanzinli mɔɔ ɔvi nu la. Mɔɔ ɔdele kɛ ɔvi Selesea la

english_verse: The governor said, “I will listen to your case as soon as the people come to bring their charges against you.” After saying this, he gave orders for Paul to be kept as a prisoner in Herod's palace.
translation_verse: ɔzele ye kɛ, “Saa menli mɔɔ ɛdo wɔ ɛzonle la ba a mebanlea wɔ edwɛkɛ ne anu.” Na ɔzele kɛ bɛva Pɔɔlo bɛhɔzie Hɛlɔdo aranemgbole ne anu ɛleka mɔɔ ɔdaye amɛnlado ye gyima ne abo wɔ la na bɛzinza ye.

english_verse: Five days later Ananias the high priest, together with some of their leaders and a lawyer named Tertullus, went to the governor to present their case against Paul.
translation_verse: Ɛhye anzi kenle nnu Sɛlɛvolɛ Kpanyinli Ananayase nee mgbanyima ne bie mɔ yɛɛ bɛ kamaavolɛ ko mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye Tɛtɛlɛse la rale Sizalia. Bɛvale ɛzonle mɔɔ bɛvale bɛdole Pɔɔlo anwo zo la bɛradole amɛnlado ne anyunlu.

english_verse: So Paul was called in, and Tertullus stated the case against him: Honorable Felix, you have brought our people a long period of peace, and because of your concern our nation is much better off.
translation_verse: Bɛvale Pɔɔlo bɛragyinlanle ɛkɛ, na Tɛtɛlɛse bɔle Pɔɔlo ɛzonledonlɛ ne abo zɛhae. “Nana, ɛle kpanyinli nrɛlɛbɛvolɛ la ati, yɛ nzo nu ɛdwo yɛ toonwo yeradwu ɛnɛ. Na ɔlua zolɛ maanzinli ye ɛnyia anyunluhɔlɛ.

english_verse: All of us are always grateful for what you have done.
translation_verse: Yɛ nye sɔ mɔɔ wɔyɛ la amuala, yɛyɛ wɔ mo somaa.

english_verse: I don't want to bother you, but please be patient with us and listen to me for just a few minutes.
translation_verse: Mengulo kɛ mesɛkye wɔ mekɛ biala, yemɔti mesɛlɛ wɔ, tie yɛ edwɛkɛ sikalɛ ɛhye.

english_verse: This man has been found to be a real pest and troublemaker for our people all over the world. He is also a leader of a group called Nazarenes.
translation_verse: Yɛnwu kɛ sonla ɛhye le agyegyeamra kpalɛ, ɔlɛtwehwe manzonle yeado Dwuuma mɔɔ wɔ aleɛabo la amuala avinli. Ɔli fane ne mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye Nazalin la ati.

english_verse: When he tried to disgrace the temple, we arrested him. If you question him, you will find out for yourself that our charges are true.
translation_verse: na ɔhanle kɛ saa yɛlɛ edwɛkɛ bie a ɛnee yɛrɛla ɛ nyunlu.] Saa ɛdawɔ ɛbizebiza sonla ye edwɛkɛ ne anu a ɛkɛnwu kɛ mɔɔ yɛlɛka la le nɔhalɛ.”

english_verse: The Jewish crowd spoke up and agreed with what Tertullus had said. Paul Defends Himself
translation_verse: Dwuuma ne mɔ amuala nee ye yɛle adwenle na bɛhanle kɛ mɔɔ yeha la amuala le nɔhalɛ. Pɔɔlo sa ɔ ne wɔ Filekese anyunlu

english_verse: The governor motioned for Paul to speak, and he began: I know that you have judged the people of our nation for many years, and I am glad to defend myself in your court.
translation_verse: Amɛnlado ne yɛle kɛ Pɔɔlo ɛdendɛ, na Pɔɔlo hanle kɛ, “Meze kɛ ɛvale edwɛkɛlilɛ wɔ maanle ɛhye anu la ɛhyɛ, yemɔti menzulo kɛ menwɔha me edwɛkɛ menwɔhile wɔ.

english_verse: It was no more than twelve days ago that I went to worship in Jerusalem. You can find this out easily enough.
translation_verse: Kɛmɔ ɛdawɔ ɛkola ɛnwu ye la, kenle bulu nee nwiɔ ɛne yɛɛ mengɔle Gyɛlusalɛm kɛ mekayɛ nzɛlɛlɛ a.

english_verse: Never once did the Jews find me arguing with anyone in the temple. I didn't cause trouble in the synagogues or in the city itself.
translation_verse: Dwuuma ye annwu me wɔ Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu kɛ me nee awie ɛlɛdi butule, anzɛɛ melɛkilehile menli debie ɛtane wɔ bɛ nyianu sua ne anu, anzɛɛ ɛleka biala wɔ suakpole ne azo.

english_verse: I admit that their leaders think the Lord's Way which I follow is based on wrong beliefs. But I still worship the same God that my ancestors worshiped. And I believe everything written in the Law of Moses and in the Prophets.
translation_verse: Ko mɔɔ medie meto nu la a le kɛ melua Awulae Adenle ye mɔɔ bɛmɛ bɛse ɔnle nɔhalɛ la azo yɛɛ mesonle yɛ nlenya mɔ Nyamenle ne a. Noko eza medie mɔɔ bɛhɛlɛ ye wɔ Mosisi mɛla ne anu, nee Nyamenle kpɔmanvolɛma mbuluku ne mɔ anu la medi.

english_verse: I am just as sure as these people are that God will raise from death everyone, good or evil.
translation_verse: Me anyelazo mɔɔ melɛ wɔ Nyamenle anu la le kɛ mɔɔ bɛdabɛ bɛlɛ ye ala la, kɛ menli kɔsɔɔti, ɛtanevolɛma nee kpalɛyɛlɛma badwazo ara ngoane nu.

english_verse: And because I am sure, I try my best to have a clear conscience in whatever I do for God or for people.
translation_verse: Ɛhye ati yɛɛ mebɔ mɔdenle kɛ menwɔnyia adwenle mɔɔ nuhua te la wɔ Nyamenle nee menli nyunlu a.

english_verse: After being away for several years, I returned here to bring gifts for the poor people of my nation and to offer sacrifices.
translation_verse: “Kɛmɔ menvile Gyɛlusalɛm la ɛvolɛ dɔɔnwo ɛze la ati, mengɔle ɛkɛ ne kɛ melɛ ezukoa nee azubɔlɛ ninyɛne mekamaa me menli ne mɔ.

english_verse: This is what I was doing when I was found going through a ceremony in the temple. I wasn't with a crowd, and there was no uproar.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ mewɔ ɛhye azo la yɛɛ bɛnwunle me wɔ Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne anu a, mekɛ ne anu ɛnee melɛtu me nwo evinli. Menli dɔɔnwo biala ɛnle ɛkɛ yɛɛ basabasa biala anzi.

english_verse: Some Jews from Asia were there at that time, and if they have anything to say against me, they should be here now.
translation_verse: Na Dwuuma bie mɔ bɔbɔ mɔɔ vi Ehyea maanle nu na bɛwɔ ɛkɛ ne bie la, bɛmɛ yɛɛ saa bɛlɛ edwɛkɛ bɛka bɛtia me a ɛnee ɔwɔ kɛ bɛba ɛ nyunlu na bɛbaka bɛ edwɛkɛ mɔɔ bɛ nee me lɛ ye la a.

english_verse: Or ask the ones who are here. They can tell you that they didn't find me guilty of anything when I was tried by their own council.
translation_verse: Anzɛɛ maa bɛdabɛ mɔɔ bɛwɔ ɛke kɛkala la bie ɛha ɛtane holɛ ko mɔɔ bɛnwunle ye me nwo wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ megyi bagua ne anyunlu la.

english_verse: The only charge they can bring against me is what I shouted out in court, when I said, “I am on trial today because I believe that the dead will be raised to life!”
translation_verse: Bɛannwu ɛhwee kɛ edwɛkɛ kpɔkɛ ko ne ala mɔɔ menganle wɔ mekɛ mɔɔ megyi bɛ nyunlu wɔ bagua ne anu la kɛ, ‘Bɛva me bɛra bɛ nyunlu ɛke, ɔluakɛ medie medi kɛ bɛbadwazo mɔwuamra bɛara ngoane nu bieko.’ ”

english_verse: Felix knew a lot about the Lord's Way. But he brought the trial to an end and said, “I will make my decision after Lysias the commander arrives.”
translation_verse: Filekese ze Awulae Adenle ɛhye anwo bie kpalɛ, yemɔti ɔdule edwɛkɛ ne ɔziele na ɔzele kɛ, “Saa sogyama kpanyinli Lesease ba a mebanwu mɔɔ meka ye wɔ bɛ edwɛkɛ ne anwo a ɔkɛyɛ boɛ la.”

english_verse: He then ordered the army officer to keep Paul under guard, but not to lock him up or to stop his friends from helping him. Paul Is Kept under Guard
translation_verse: Akee ɔzele sogya kpanyinli ne mɔɔ Pɔɔlo wɔ ɔ sa nu la kɛ ɔnlea ye boɛ, na ɔmaa ɔnyia adenle ɔkpundi ɔ nwo, na ɔmaa ɔ gɔnwo mɔ adenle ɔmaa bɛva ninyɛne mɔɔ ɔhyia nwo la bɛrɛlɛ ye. Pɔɔlo gyi Filekese nee Dulusela anyunlu

english_verse: Several days later Felix and his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish, went to the place where Paul was kept under guard. They sent for Paul and listened while he spoke to them about having faith in Christ Jesus.
translation_verse: Kenle ekyi guale nu la Filekese nee ɔ ye Dulusela mɔɔ le Dwuunli la rale. Ɔzoanle ɔmanle bɛhɔvale Pɔɔlo na ɔmanle ɔhanle diedi wɔ Gyisɛse Kelaese anu anwo edwɛkɛ ɔmanle ɔdiele bie.

english_verse: But Felix was frightened when Paul started talking to them about doing right, about self-control, and about the coming judgment. So he said to Paul, “That's enough for now. You may go. But when I have time I will send for you.”
translation_verse: Pɔɔlo noko hɔle zolɛ, na mɔɔ ɔka boɛlilɛ, bɛ nwo zo ɛhomonlɛ, yɛɛ Ndɛnebualɛ Kenle ne mɔɔ bara la anwo edwɛkɛ la, Filekese ahonle dule na ɔzele kɛ, “Yeyɛ boɛ, kɔ. Saa menyia alagye a mebazoa meamaa bɛarava wɔ bieko.”

english_verse: After this, Felix often sent for Paul and talked with him, because he hoped that Paul would offer him a bribe.
translation_verse: Na ɛnee eza ye adwenle ko noko a le kɛ Pɔɔlo kɛmaa ye ezukoa. Ɛhye ati ɔmanle bɛhɔle ye ɛvalɛ wazowazo ɔ nee ye dendɛle.

english_verse: Two years later Porcius Festus became governor in place of Felix. But since Felix wanted to do the Jewish leaders a favor, he kept Paul in jail.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ ɛvolɛ nwiɔ pɛle nu la, Pɔseɛse Fɛsetɛse ralile amɛnlado Filekese agyakɛ anu. Na kɛmɔ ɛnee Filekese kulo kɛ ɔnyia ɔ nyunlu wɔ Dwuuma anyunlu la ati, ɔmanle Pɔɔlo hale efiade ne.

english_verse: Three days after Festus had become governor, he went from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Fɛsetɛse radwule maanzinli ne anu la, ye kenle nsa yɛɛ eza ɔvi Sizalia ɔhɔle Gyɛlusalɛm a.

english_verse: There the chief priests and some Jewish leaders told him about their charges against Paul. They also asked Festus
translation_verse: Sɛlɛvolɛ mgbanyinli ne mɔ nee Dwuu mgbanyima ne mɔ radonle Pɔɔlo ɛzonle bieko wɔ ɛkɛ ne. Bɛkpale Fɛsetɛse kyɛlɛ kɛ

english_verse: if he would be willing to bring Paul to Jerusalem. They begged him to do this because they were planning to attack and kill Paul on the way.
translation_verse: ɔli ɔboa bɛ na ɔva Pɔɔlo ɔrɛla Gyɛlusalɛm, ɔluakɛ ɛnee bɛlɛ adwenle kɛ bɛtɛ ye wɔ adenle nu bɛahu ye.

english_verse: But Festus told them, “Paul will be kept in Caesarea, and I am soon going there myself.
translation_verse: Na Fɛsetɛse buale bɛ kɛ, “Pɔɔlo la efiade wɔ Sizalia, yɛɛ medame mumua ne ɔnrɛhyɛ na meazia meahɔ ɛkɛ.

english_verse: If he has done anything wrong, let your leaders go with me and bring charges against him there.”
translation_verse: Yemɔti saa bɛnea na yeyɛ bɛ ɛtane bie a ɛnee bɛmaa bɛ menli mɔɔ li bɛ ti la nee me ɛhɔ Sizalia na bɛhɔha bɛ edwɛkɛ ne.”

english_verse: Festus stayed in Jerusalem for eight or ten more days before going to Caesarea. Then the next day he took his place as judge and had Paul brought into court.
translation_verse: Fɛsetɛse lile kenle kɛyɛ mɔtwɛ mɔɔ kɔ bulu la wɔ Gyɛlusalɛm kolaa na yeazia yeahɔ Sizalia. Aleɛ hyenle ala la ɔhɔdɛnlanle ye ebia nu kɛ bɛva Pɔɔlo bɛrɛla ɔ nyunlu.

english_verse: As soon as Paul came in, the leaders from Jerusalem crowded around him and said he was guilty of many serious crimes. But they could not prove anything.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ Pɔɔlo rale la, Dwuuma mɔɔ vi Gyɛlusalɛm rale la radonle ye ɛzonle mgbole bie mɔɔ akee bɛdabɛ bɔbɔ bɛngola bɛngilehile nu a.

english_verse: Then Paul spoke in his own defense, “I have not broken the Law of my people. And I have not done anything against either the temple or the Emperor.”
translation_verse: Pɔɔlo zale ɔ ne kɛ, “Metɛyɛle ɛtane biala metɛtiale Dwuuma mɛla ne anzɛɛ Ɛzonlenlɛ Sua ne na yeayɛ Wulomu Maanle Maanle belemgbunli ne.”

english_verse: Festus wanted to please the leaders. So he asked Paul, “Are you willing to go to Jerusalem and be tried by me on these charges?”
translation_verse: Na kɛmɔ Fɛsetɛse kpondɛ ɔ nyunlu wɔ Dwuuma anyunlu la ati, ɔbizale Pɔɔlo kɛ, “Ɛkɛhulo kɛ ɛkɛhɔ Gyɛlusalɛm na ɛkɔhɔye ɛzonledonlɛ ɛhye mɔ anloa wɔ me nyunlu ɔ?”

english_verse: Paul replied, “I am on trial in the Emperor's court, and that's where I should be tried. You know very well I have not done anything to harm the Jewish nation.
translation_verse: Pɔɔlo buale ye kɛ, “Megyi Wulomu Maanle Maanle belemgbunli ɔdaye ye ndɛnebualɛ ebia nyunlu, yɛɛ ɛke a ɔwɔ kɛ bɛdi me edwɛkɛ a. Metɛyɛle Dwuuma ɛtane biala, kɛmɔ ɛdawɔ wɔnwu ye la.

english_verse: If I had done something deserving death, I would not ask to escape the death penalty. But I am not guilty of any of these crimes, and no one has the right to hand me over to these people. I now ask to be tried by the Emperor himself.”
translation_verse: Saa medo mɛla bie mɔɔ maa mefɛta ewule a menzulo kɛ bɛkɛhu me. Na saa nɔhalɛ biala ɛnle bɛ ɛzonledonlɛ ne anu ɛdeɛ a, ɛnee noko ɔnle kɛ awie biala ye me maa bɛ. Zɔhane ati medo me edwɛkɛ ne memaa Maanle Maanle belemgbunli ne.”

english_verse: After Festus had talked this over with members of his council, he told Paul, “You have asked to be tried by the Emperor, and to the Emperor you will go!” Paul Speaks to Agrippa and Bernice
translation_verse: Fɛsetɛse nee ye mgbanyima ne mɔ hanle bɛ ti kpulale nwolɛ, na Fɛsetɛse buale Pɔɔlo kɛ, “Saa wɔdo wɔ edwɛkɛ ne wɔmaa Maanle Maanle belemgbunli ne a ɛnee ɛkɛ ne ala a ɛkɛhɔ a.” Pɔɔlo gyi Agelepa nee Bɛnaesi anyunlu

english_verse: A few days later King Agrippa and Bernice came to Caesarea to visit Festus.
translation_verse: Mekɛ guale nu la Belemgbunli Agelepa mɔɔ tɔ zo nwiɔ la nee ɔ ye Bɛnaesi rale Sizalia kɛ bɛbakpɔla Fɛsetɛse bɛayɛ ye akoaba.

english_verse: They had been there for several days, when Festus told the king about the charges against Paul. He said: Felix left a man here in jail,
translation_verse: Na nzinlii mɔɔ bɛlile kenle ekyi wɔ ɛkɛ ne la Fɛsetɛse hanle Pɔɔlo edwɛkɛ ne hilele belemgbunli ne kɛ, “Filekese gyakyile awie bie wɔ efiade ɛkɛ.

english_verse: and when I went to Jerusalem, the chief priests and the Jewish leaders came and asked me to find him guilty.
translation_verse: Na mekɛ mɔɔ mengɔle Gyɛlusalɛm la, Dwuuma sɛlɛvolɛ mgbanyinli nee Dwuu mgbanyima ne mɔ radonle ye ɛzonle hilele me kɛ menli ye edwɛkɛ membua ye ewule fɔlɛ.

english_verse: I told them it isn't the Roman custom to hand a man over to people who are bringing charges against him. He must first have the chance to meet them face to face and to defend himself against their charges.
translation_verse: Na menzele bɛ kɛ ɔnle Wulomu mɛla kɛ bɛkɛye awie biala mɔɔ bɛkɛdo ye ɛzonle kɛ yedo mɛla la bɛkɛmaa kyesɛ ɔ nee menli mɔɔ donle ye ɛzonle ne la yia nu bɛka bɛmaa ɔdaye ɔnyia adenle ɔsa ɔ ne wɔ nwolɛ.

english_verse: So when they came here with me, I wasted no time. On the very next day I took my place on the judge's bench and ordered him to be brought in.
translation_verse: Yemɔti bɛ muala bɛrale ɛke, na meanva meando aze. Ye alehyenlɛ nu ala yɛɛ mendɛnlanle aze kɛ medi edwɛkɛ ne a.

english_verse: But when the men stood up to make their charges against him, they did not accuse him of any of the crimes that I thought they would.
translation_verse: Menli ne mɔ dwazole la, bɛangola bɛanga edwɛkɛ kpaziwɔkɛ biala bɛando ɔ nwo zo kɛ yedo mɛla kpole bie, kɛmɔ mendwenlenle la.

english_verse: Instead, they argued with him about some of their beliefs and about a dead man named Jesus, who Paul said was alive.
translation_verse: Mɔɔ bɛyɛle ala la a le bɛ nyamenlezonlenlɛ nwo kpolerazulɛ yɛɛ awie bie mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye Gyisɛse, mɔɔ ɛwu, na Pɔɔlo kile kɛ ɔde aze la anwo kpolerazulɛ.

english_verse: Since I did not know how to find out the truth about all this, I asked Paul if he would be willing to go to Jerusalem and be put on trial there.
translation_verse: Kɛmɔ ɛnee mengola mennwu adenle mɔɔ mefa zolɛ a menwɔnwu edwɛkɛ ɛhye anu kpalɛ la, membizale Pɔɔlo saa ɔkɛhulo kɛ ɔkɛhɔ Gyɛlusalɛm na bɛahɔli edwɛkɛ ɛhye wɔ ɛkɛ a.

english_verse: But Paul asked to be kept in jail until the Emperor could decide his case. So I ordered him to be kept here until I could send him to the Emperor.
translation_verse: Na Pɔɔlo buale kɛ memaa bɛva edwɛkɛ ne bɛhɔ Maanle Maanle belemgbunli ne ɔdaye ɔ nyunlu. Yemɔti memaa bɛva ye bɛzie kɔkpula mekɛ mɔɔ bɛ nee ye kɛhɔ la.”

english_verse: Then Agrippa said to Festus, “I would also like to hear what this man has to say.” Festus answered, “You can hear him tomorrow.”
translation_verse: Na Belemgbunli Agelepa zele Fɛsetɛse kɛ, “Mekulo kɛ metie sonla ɛhye edwɛkɛ ne bie.” Fɛsetɛse buale kɛ, “Ɛhyema ɛkɛdie ye.”

english_verse: The next day Agrippa and Bernice made a big show as they came into the meeting room. High ranking army officers and leading citizens of the town were also there. Festus then ordered Paul to be brought in
translation_verse: Yemɔti aleɛ hyenle la Agelepa nee Bɛnaesi zieziele bɛ nwo kpalɛ na bɛ nee sogya mgbanyinli nee suakpole ne azo adile adile hɔle ɛleka mɔɔ bɛdi edwɛkɛ la, na Fɛsetɛse manle bɛhɔvale Pɔɔlo bɛrale.

english_verse: and said: King Agrippa and other guests, look at this man! Every Jew from Jerusalem and Caesarea has come to me, demanding for him to be put to death.
translation_verse: Fɛsetɛse zele kɛ, “Belemgbunli Agelepa, nee bɛdabɛ mgbanyima mɔɔ bɛ nee yɛ wɔ ɛke la amuala, nrenya ɛhye, Dwuuma amuala mɔɔ wɔ Gyɛlusalɛm nee ɛke la ɛrado ye ɛzonle ɛhile me, na bɛkile kɛ ɔnle kɛ ɔtɛnla ngoane nu bieko.

english_verse: I have not found him guilty of any crime deserving death. But because he has asked to be judged by the Emperor, I have decided to send him to Rome.
translation_verse: Me afoa nu ɛdeɛ, menleɛnlea edwɛkɛ ne anu la menwu kɛ ɔtɛyɛle debie mɔɔ maa ɔfɛta ewule a. Na kɛmɔ ɔdaye mumua ne ɔse ɔfa ye edwɛkɛ ne yeahɔ Maanle Maanle belemgbunli ne anyunlu la, meyɛ kɛ memaa bɛava ye bɛahɔ.

english_verse: I have to write some facts about this man to the Emperor. So I have brought him before all of you, but especially before you, King Agrippa. After we have talked about his case, I will then have something to write.
translation_verse: Noko mennwu edwɛkɛ kpaziwɔkɛ mɔɔ megyinla zolɛ meahɛlɛ meahɔmaa Maanle Maanle belemgbunli ne a. Yemɔti me nee ye ɛra bɛ nyunlu ɛke, bɔbɔ wɔmɔ Belemgbunli Agelepa, amaa wɔanleɛnlea ye edwɛkɛ ne anu boɛ, na meanyia edwɛkɛ kpalɛ meahɛlɛ meahɔ.

english_verse: It makes no sense to send a prisoner to the Emperor without stating the charges against him.
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ menea a ɔnwie nrɛlɛbɛ yɛ kɛ melɛ pilizanli melɛkɔ na menlɛ ɔ nwo ɛzonledonlɛ kpalɛ biala a.”

english_verse: King Agrippa, I am glad for this chance to defend myself before you today on all these charges my own people have brought against me.
translation_verse: “Belemgbunli Agelepa, ɔyɛ me fɛ kpole kɛ mesa me ne wɔ ɛ nyunlu ɛnɛ wɔ ɛzonle mɔɔ Dwuuma ɛva ɛdo me nwo zo la anwo a.

english_verse: You know a lot about our religious customs and the beliefs that divide us. So I ask you to listen patiently to me.
translation_verse: Ɔluakɛ wɔmɔ, ɛze Dwuuma maamɛla ne kpalɛ. Yemɔti, mesɛlɛ wɔ, nyia abotane na tie me.

english_verse: All the Jews have known me since I was a child. They know what kind of life I have lived in my own country and in Jerusalem. And if they were willing, they could tell you I was a Pharisee, a member of a group that is stricter than any other.
translation_verse: Bɛze, yɛɛ saa bɛdi nɔhalɛ a, anrɛɛ bɛkola bɛdi daselɛ kɛ mɔlebɛbo ne amuala ɛnee meboka ɛzonlenlɛ fane ɛsesebɛ ne mɔɔ bɛfɛlɛ ye Falasii la anwo.

english_verse: Day and night our twelve tribes have earnestly served God, waiting for his promised blessings. King Agrippa, because of this hope, some of our leaders have brought charges against me.
translation_verse: Ɛwɔkɛ ne ati yɛɛ yɛ mbusua ekpunli bulu nee nwiɔ ye gua ɛzonlenlɛ zo alehyenlɛ nee aledwolɛ, kɛ saa bɛkɛnyia ye a. Na anyelazo ɛhye ala ati, Nana, yɛɛ Dwuuma ɛlɛto me ɛzonle zɛhae a.

english_verse: Why should any of you doubt that God raises the dead to life?
translation_verse: Na duzu ati yɛɛ bɛmɛ Dwuuma bɛnlie bɛnli kɛ Nyamenle badwazo mɔwuamra ɛ?

english_verse: I did this first in Jerusalem, and with the authority of the chief priests I put many of God's people in jail. I even voted for them to be killed.
